children.text: śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūḥ
children.translated_text: The Glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>

children.text: pūrva-campūḥ
children.translated_text: The First <s>Campū</s> (Earlier Part)

children.text: prathamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: The First Completion (<s>Pūraṇam</s>)

children.text:
śrī-śrī-rādhā-ramaṇāya namaḥ
śrī-śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanyāya namaḥ
children.translated_text:
Obeisance to the glorious <s>Rādhā-ramaṇa</s> (the Beloved of Rādhā)!
Obeisance to the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>!

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, together with <s>Sanātana</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>,

children.text: gopāla raghunāthāpta-vraja vallabha pāhi mām ||JGc_1,1.1||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gopāla</s>, O beloved of <s>Vraja</s> attained by <s>Raghunātha</s> — protect me! ||1.1||

children.text: tad evam ārambhasambhavadantarmahasā sahasā vilikhya tad idam ullikhyate | kim idam? madiṣṭadevasya, madanviṣṭadayāśiṣṭatadbhakta-samudayasya ca kramataḥ smaraṇam āvirbhūtam | kiṃ vā, kevalasya madiṣṭa-devasya; kiṃ vā, tadviśiṣṭasya | āṃ āṃ, tantratas tat trayam api svatantratayā labhyate | tatra prathamaṃ tāvat prathamataḥ prathayāmi | atra śrī padam anyad anyad api kiñcid anuṣṭupchandaḥparacchandatayā pūrvatra ca paraparatra ca yatra na dattaṃ, tatra ca sandhātavyam |
children.translated_text: Thus, having hastily sketched this with the inner majesty arising at the commencement, this is now outlined. What is this? A remembrance has appeared, in sequence, of my chosen deity, and of the assembly of his devotees blessed by his most esteemed grace. Or rather, of my chosen deity alone; or rather, of him together with his distinguished [devotees]. Yes, yes — according to the system, all three are independently obtained. Of these, I shall first set forth the first. Here, wherever the word <s>Śrī</s> (auspicious prefix) and other similar words are not given, whether in the preceding or subsequent passages, due to the constraint of the <s>anuṣṭubh</s> meter, they should be mentally supplied.

children.text: yathā: he śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmnātidhanya! sarva-mūrdhanya! he śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya! sarva-śarmada-kīrtanya! he mahita-śrī-sanātana-sahita-śrī-rūpa-nāmadheya, man-mūrdhany ādheya! he śrī-gopāla-bhaṭṭākhyā-pravṛddha-bhaṭṭārakatā-samṛddha! he śrī-raghunātha-dāsa! nāma-dhāmatayātiprasiddha-parama-bhakti-bharāviddha! he teṣām evāpta-vrajatāsiddha-varṇana-sat-karṇa-garbhābharaṇa-śrī-bhūgarbhādi-sañjñādhikaraṇa! he śrī-vallabha! prāg-bhavīya-durlabha-sukṛta-sandhīyamāna-madīya-śaraṇa-pitṛ-caraṇa!
children.translated_text: As follows: O one exceedingly blessed by the name <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! Supreme among all! O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>! Whose fame is to be celebrated as the giver of all happiness! O one bearing the name <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> accompanied by the honored <s>Śrī Sanātana</s>, to be placed upon my head! O one called <s>Śrī Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s>, enriched with an abundantly grown lordly status! O <s>Śrī Raghunātha Dāsa</s>! Well-known as an abode of names, pierced by the fullness of supreme devotion! O designation of <s>Śrī Bhūgarbha</s> and others — jewel-ornaments for the ears of the worthy, whose descriptions have been proved through their attainment of <s>Vraja</s>-nature! O <s>Śrī Vallabha</s>! O feet of my shelter-father, joined by the rare merit of a previous life!

children.text: kiṃ vā, he śrī-raghunāthasyāptān vrajaty anuvrajatīti tattayā sarva-vallabha! śrīvallabha! māṃ pāhi! nijacaraṇacchāyayā matpratipālakatām āyāhi | yathā kaṃsārāter āśu sukhavilāsaṃ śaṃsantī, sahāyatayā ca lasantī ca priyasakhīyate, na tadvad anyo dhanyo' pi janaḥ sambhavati |
children.translated_text: Or rather: O <s>Śrī Vallabha</s>, beloved of all, because you go to and follow after the <s>Vraja</s> attained by <s>Śrī Raghunātha</s>! Protect me! Come to protect me with the shade of your own feet! Just as [<s>Rādhā</s>], quickly proclaiming the delightful pastimes of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and shining forth as a companion, becomes a dear female friend — no other person, however blessed, can be so.

children.text: atha dvitīyam api pratīyamānaṃ nirmāmi: śrī-kṛṣṇa iti | śrīr atra rādhā | eṣā hi śrīpradhānatayā sādhayiṣyamāṇatāyāṃ nirābādhā | tad-anantara-kṛṣṇa-śabdaś cātra śabda-brahma-gūdha-para-brahma nanda-nandana-vācakatāyāṃ rūḍhaḥ | tena, "he śrī-rādhākhya-svarūpa-śakti-yukta-kṛṣṇa" ity arthaś ca nirvyūdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now I also fashion a second [interpretation]: '<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>' — <s>Śrī</s> here means <s>Rādhā</s>. For she is unobstructed in the primacy of <s>Śrī</s>-ness that is to be established. The word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' following it, here has its established usage as denoting <s>Nanda-nandana</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>), the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> concealed within the word-<s>Brahman</s>. Thus the meaning 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, endowed with <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> as your inherent <s>Svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential energy)' is also fully established.

children.text: kṛṣṇa iti:
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>':—

children.text: kṛṣir bhū-vācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛtivācakaḥ |
children.translated_text: The syllable <s>kṛṣ</s> denotes 'existence' (<s>bhū</s>), and <s>ṇa</s> denotes 'bliss' (<s>nirvṛti</s>);

children.text: tayor aikyaṃ paraṃ brahma kṛṣṇa ity abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: the unity of these two is called the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text:
iti pramāṇa-jñāta-caraḥ kṛṣṇa-śabdas tv atra yoga-puraskṛta-rūḍhitayā tat-paraḥ | bhūr iti
bhāvakvibantatākaraḥ | sa cāyaṃ bhāva-śabdavad dhātv-artha-mātratā-dharaḥ | dhātvarthaś cātrākarṣaṇam, tad eva sphuṭam āptatayāptamanasām ākarṣaṇam | tataś ca bhinna-padārthatayāvagatayor dayitayor iva tayor aikyaṃ yoga eveti tad-yukta ānandaḥ sarvākarṣakānanda ity artha evāmandaḥ; paraṃ brahma iti, | ṇarākṛti paraṃ brahma iti hi prasiddhiḥ | yoga-puraskṛta-rūḍhatopagūdhatayāpi śrī-nandanandanam eva vakti tac-chabda-śaktir iti vyakti-siddhiś ca | tad etad abhidhīyate cābhidhīyate iti | tasmād eva tadīya-svabhāva-viśeṣa-bhāvanārtham eva punar-uktir iyaṃ yuktiṃ yunakti |
children.translated_text: Thus the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>', whose nature is known through authoritative evidence, here has its conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) preceded by etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>), and is directed toward Him. '<s>Bhū</s>' is productive of a <s>bhāva</s>-verbal affix form. And this, like the word <s>bhāva</s>, bears only the meaning of the verbal root. The root-meaning here is 'attraction' (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>), and that very thing is clearly the attraction of the minds of those who have attained [Him]. Thus, the unity of these two — understood as separate word-meanings, like a pair of lovers — is indeed etymological derivation (<s>yoga</s>); and the bliss joined with that is the bliss that attracts everything — this meaning is indeed abundant. 'Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — for indeed the established tradition is that '<s>Ṇa</s>-shaped [entity] is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.' The word-power, even when concealed by the conventional usage preceded by etymological derivation, speaks only of <s>Śrī Nanda-nandana</s> — thus the establishment of the referent [is proven]. And this 'is called' — is indeed called. Therefore, this repetition serves the purpose of contemplating the particular nature that belongs to Him, and is thus fitting.

children.text: caitanya iti | "he sarvaprakāśaka! sadrūpatayā sarvāśrayasvarūpa!" tadrūpatā ca vipaścidbhir avagatā, sac-cid-ānanda-rūpāya kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭa-karmaṇe iti tāpanīya-nāndīni-śamanāt | tvayy eva nitya-sukhabodha-tanau iti śrī-bhāgavatīya-brahma-stave nigamanāc ca |
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>Caitanya</s>': 'O all-illuminating one! O one whose essential nature is the foundation of all, being of the nature of pure existence (<s>sat</s>)!' That nature has been understood by the wise, from the <s>Tāpanīya Upaniṣad</s> [pacifying] the opening benediction: 'To <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of the form of <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), of unhindered action.' And from the conclusion in the hymn of <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>: 'In you alone, whose body is eternal bliss and consciousness.'

children.text: sa-sanātana-rūpaka iti, "he sanātanena sadātanena śvasvarūpam anubhavadbhir api sunirūpaṇa rūpeṇa saha vartamāna! tena svabhaktivittacittam anuvartamāna!"
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>sa-sanātana-rūpaka</s>': 'O one who exists together with <s>Sanātana</s>, the eternal one, who, even as [others] experience your own nature through description of a form that is beautiful and well-delineated, are accompanied by him! O one who follows the hearts enriched by the wealth of his own devotion!'

children.text: gopāla-raghunāthāpta-vraja-vallabha iti, "gopāleṣu ye raghavo laghavo, ye ca nāthā mukhyā iti vikhyātagāthās, tair āptasya vrajasya ballava-tallaja-vrajasya vallabha!" kiṃ vā, "gopālānāṃ laghur iṣṭaḥ, sa ca nāthaś ca yas, tasya sambodhanam triṣv iṣṭe' lpe laghur iti nānārthavargalabdhabodhanam | āptavrajavallabha iti "āptavrajānāṃ svajanasamūhānāṃ vallabha! pareṣām alabhya ṃsatprabha!"
children.translated_text: Regarding '<s>gopāla-raghunāthāpta-vraja-vallabha</s>': 'O beloved of <s>Vraja</s> — the cowherd community — attained by those among the cowherds who are <s>raghu</s> (swift/humble) and those who are <s>nātha</s> (lords/chief), whose fame is well-known!' Or alternatively: 'The one who is humble and dear among the cowherds, and who is also their lord — that is the form of address, in the vocative for the desired one. <s>Āptavrajavallabha</s> means: O beloved of the assemblies of one's own people! O one of excellent radiance, unattainable for others!'

children.text: atha tṛtīyam api sambhṛtīkaravāṇi: he śrī-kṛṣṇa iti | śrīr atra ca paramapreyasīṣu śreyasī rādhā, tatas "tadyuktatayā madhuralīlāyām asaṃkīrṇa! he kṛṣṇa-caitanyākhya-bhaktāvatāra! tādātmyāpannatayāvatīrṇa! he sanātana-rūpābhyāṃ paramānurakta-subhaktābhyāṃ saha vidyamāna! he gopāla-raghunāthābhyāṃ tat-tan-nāmābhyām api subhaktābhyām āptaḥ prāpto yo vrajas, tasya vallabhatayā sarva-vidyamānaṃ! māṃ pāhi, mat-pālakatāṃ yāhīti |
children.translated_text: Now I shall also bring forth a third [interpretation]: '<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>' — <s>Śrī</s> here too is <s>Rādhā</s>, the best among the most beloved; then: 'O one unmixed in sweet pastimes through union with her! O <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, the devotee-incarnation of that very name! Descended through identity [with Him]! O one present together with <s>Sanātana</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>, the two supremely devoted devotees! O one whose <s>Vraja</s> has been attained by <s>Gopāla</s> and <s>Raghunātha</s>, two excellent devotees bearing those respective names — as the beloved of that [<s>Vraja</s>], you are all that exists! Protect me, come to be my protector!'

children.text: atha grantha-sūcanā-
children.translated_text: Now, the indication of the text —

children.text: tad evam maṅgalaṃ saṅgamayya kāryaṃ vicāryate |
children.translated_text: Thus, having joined this auspicious [invocation], the work is considered.

children.text:
yan mayā kṛṣṇasandarbhe siddhāntāmṛtam ācitam |
tad eva rasyate kāvyakṛtiprajñā-rasajñayā ||JGc_1,1.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
That very nectar of established doctrine which was gathered by me in the <s>Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s>,
that same [nectar] is tasted by one whose poetic intelligence discerns <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor). ||1.2||

children.text:
so' haṃ kāvyasya lakṣyeṇa mano nirmāmi tādṛśam |
tan mahānto yad īkṣeraṃs tadā hemni cito maṇiḥ ||JGc_1,1.3|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
I, that very person, fashion my mind toward that goal through the aim of poetry;
if the great ones would look upon it, then it would be a gem set in gold. ||1.3||

children.text:
pūrvottaratayā campū-dvayī seyaṃ trayī trayī |
pṛthak pṛthag grantha-tulyā yathecchaṃ sadbhir īkṣyatām ||JGc_1,1.4|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
This <s>campū</s>-pair, divided into earlier and later parts, is a triad of triads;
each separately is equal to a [full] treatise — let the wise view it as they wish. ||1.4||

children.text:
śrī-gopāla-gaṇānāṃ gopālānāṃ pramodāya |
bhavatu samantād eṣā nāmnā gopāla-campūr yā ||JGc_1,1.5|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
For the delight of the cowherd communities (<s>gopāla-gaṇas</s>) of <s>Śrī Gopāla</s>,
may this [work], named <s>Gopāla-campū</s>, prevail everywhere! ||1.5||

children.text:
yadyapi ciram antardhā jātā śrī-gokula-sthānām |
tadapi mahātmasu teṣāṃ vyūha-samūhaḥ puraḥ sphuran jayati ||JGc_1,1.6|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
Although the inhabitants of <s>Śrī Gokula</s> have long been hidden,
nevertheless the array of their manifestations, shining before us among those great souls, is victorious! ||1.6||

children.text:
asti kila vṛndāvana-nāma-dheyaṃ bhāga-dheyam iva subhagaṃ vanam avanī-devyāḥ | yad aho, vanam apy avanāya kalpate sakala-lokasya | prasaṅga-mātrataḥ pavamānam api tatra kṣipratā-pratāpataḥ pavamānatām apy atikrāmati | parama-tri-varga-dāne nirargalam api sarvadāpavargam apavarjayati | mukti-sandha-sambandha-gandham api svabandha-nirbandha-nibandhanaṃ bhavati | sadā sadāvalīśasya bhakti-pradam api kadāpi na dadāti tad-bhaktim | brahmaṇātmani yad anañcitam api matvā janma vāñchitam, tena tat paramañcitaṃ matam iti nija-hita-mahita-mahimārambham upalambhayati | tad evaṃ gahana-caryā-paryākulatayā virodhālaṅkāravad viruddhāyamānam apy artham anuruddhatayā paryavasānataḥ pariṇamayati | tasmin kavīnām akavitāyām api kavitā śambhāvitā bhavitā | tasminn eva ca paramodāra-sāratāvagamyate
| tadd hi taddhitatayā muhur avatīrṇasya sarvasyāpy ānandanasya śrīman-nanda-nandanasya sarvam ānanda-parva sarvadā parvati |
children.translated_text: There exists a forest called <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, like a blessed portion belonging to the goddess Earth. For, O wonder, though it is a forest, it serves for the protection of all people. Merely by association, even the wind (<s>pavamāna</s>), which is inherently purifying, transcends even its purifying nature through the power of its swiftness there. In the bestowal of the supreme three goals of life (<s>tri-varga</s>), even while being ungated [in generosity], it always sets aside liberation. It becomes the very basis of the insistent bond of its own attachment, even [eclipsing] the mere fragrance of the connection and association of <s>mukti</s> (liberation). Though it bestows devotion to the Eternal Lord of <s>Sadāvalī</s>, it never grants devotion of that [particular] kind. Even <s>Brahmā</s>, having considered that birth [there] was desirable though [this place] was not honored by him in himself, thereby reveals the beginning of the greatness of its own honored welfare — thus it is regarded as supremely honored. In this way, though appearing contradictory like the figure of speech called <s>virodhālaṅkāra</s> (paradox) due to being overwhelmed by its dense, mysterious conduct, it ultimately transforms [all] meanings through accommodation. In it, even the non-poetry of poets becomes esteemed as poetry. In it alone is comprehended the supremely generous essential nature. For there, all the festival of bliss of <s>Śrīman Nanda-nandana</s> (the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s>), the delighter of all, who has repeatedly descended for its welfare, always reaches its summit.

children.text: asti ceha śrī-śukasyāpi sukha-camatkāra-kāraṇaṃ padyam-
children.translated_text: And here there is a verse of <s>Śrī Śuka</s> himself, which is the cause of delightful wonder —

children.text:
vṛndāvanaṃ govardhanaṃ yamunā-pulināni ca |
vīkṣyāsīd uttamā prītī rāma-mādhavayor nṛpa ||iti | (BhP 10.11.36)
children.translated_text:
'O King, seeing <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Govardhana</s>, and the sandy banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
a supreme joy arose in <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.' (BhP 10.11.36)

children.text: tatra govardhanas tu purastād evaṃ prastūyate -
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>Govardhana</s> is praised first as follows —

children.text:
yad gokuleśvara iti prathitiḥ purāṇe
kṛṣṇasya tad bhavati gokulam asya dhāma |
govāsatā ca kila gokulatā-nidānaṃ
govardhanas tad iha sarva-nidhānam eva ||JGc_1,1.7|| [vasanta-tilaka]
tatra cāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ -
children.translated_text: And here is a particular point —

children.text:
tri-jagati mānasa-gaṅgā govardhanam api vibhindatī viditā |
aham iha manye kṛṣṇa- snehaja-dhārā tad-antaraṃ viśati ||JGc_1,1.8|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
In the three worlds, the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>, which is known to split <s>Govardhana</s>, flows [through it];
I think that the stream born from the affection for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> enters into its interior. ||1.8||

children.text:
kiṃ ca,
tasmin śrī-hari-rādhayor yugalitaṃ yad bhāti kuṇda-dvayaṃ
saṃsaṅgena parasparaṃ parimalān manye tayos tan-miṣam |
premāsīt prakaṭaṃ yataḥ śvasanakaiḥ kampānvitaṃ jādya-yug
bhaktārdra-sthiti-kṛc ca tad ghana-rasākāraṃ darīdṛśyate ||JGc_1,1.9|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
On it, the pair of ponds (<s>kuṇḍa-dvayam</s>) of <s>Śrī Hari</s> and <s>Rādhā</s> that shines forth as a couple —
I think their mutual association and fragrances are but a pretext.
Since love was manifest there, trembling through breaths, the pair [of ponds] became inert,
and that [love], causing a state moistened with devotion, is seen in the caves as a form of dense essence. ||1.9||

children.text: yamunāyāṃ cāyam atiśayaḥ-
children.translated_text: And regarding the <s>Yamunā</s>, this is its extraordinary quality —

children.text:
snāna-jāta-sukṛtān na kevalāt
sphūrtidā muraripo raveḥ sutā |
vīkṣaṇād api yato bibharti sā
śyāma-dhāma-vara-mādhurī-dhurām ||JGc_1,1.10|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
Not merely from the merit born of bathing, the daughter of the Sun
gives inspiration regarding the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>);
for even through [mere] sight she bears
the burden of the excellent sweetness of the dark-hued abode. ||1.10||

children.text: tasyāṃ cotprekṣante-
children.translated_text: And regarding her, they conjecture —

children.text:
śva-snigdha-vṛnda-viṣaya-priyatā-mahimnā
svedāṃśa eva kim u kṛṣṇatanor visārī |
vṛndasya kṛṣṇa-viṣaya-priyataiva kiṃ vā
tad-bhāva-bhāvita-gatir bhavati sma kṛṣṇā ||JGc_1,1.11|| [[vasantatilakā]]
children.translated_text:
By the greatness of her love directed toward the dear community of her own beloveds,
is she perhaps the spreading perspiration of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> body?
Or is the love of the community directed toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> itself [the cause] —
whose course is imbued with that very state, [and so] she became dark? ||1.11||

children.text: pulināni ca tasyā mahā-premollāsam āviṣkurvanti | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: And her sandy banks also reveal the great ecstasy of love. Thus —

children.text:
adyāpi yāni vibudhān avaloka-mātrāt
puṣṇanti kṛṣṇa-kṛta-rāsa-rasaṃ vibhāvya |
tāny atra kiṃ vara-rasāyana-divya-cūrṇair
abhyāsataḥ sva-pulināni cinoti saurī? ||JGc_1,1.12|| [[vasantatilakā]]
children.translated_text:
Even today, those [banks] which, from a mere glance, nourish the gods
by evoking the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor) of the <s>rāsa</s>-dance performed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
does the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) here strew her own sandy banks
repeatedly with divine powders of excellent elixir? ||1.12||

children.text: bhāṇdīras tu sa no mano vyākulayati | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: But the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> [tree] agitates our minds. Thus —

children.text:
bhāṇdīrasya sphuṭam adhihari prema kiṃ varṇanīyaṃ
sāntardhānaṃ sthitavati harau bādham antardadhe yaḥ |
yāntu svāṃśena ca viṣayatām atra govardhanādyā
loke snigdhā racayitum idaṃ na kṣamaḥ syām itīva ||JGc_1,1.13|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
The love of <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> for <s>Hari</s> — what need to describe it?
When <s>Hari</s> disappeared, it too indeed disappeared;
let <s>Govardhana</s> and the rest become objects [of description] through their own portions —
'I am not capable of composing this among the loving ones in the world,' as it were. ||1.13||

children.text: aho premagambhīryam asya paśya vṛndāvanasya! yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Behold the depth of love of this <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! For —

children.text:
kutra kutracid agasya dambhataḥ
stambham eti tad idaṃ harer vanam |
prāyaśaś cala-dalasya kampratām
aṅkurasya pulakāni sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,1.14|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
Here and there, from the pretense of the <s>Agastya</s> [star's rising],
this forest of <s>Hari</s> becomes stiff [as if in renunciation];
but for the most part, the trembling of its quivering leaves
is the horripilation of its sprouts everywhere. ||1.14||

children.text:
āvirvrajati ca tasmin sa-vraja-vāsi-jana-vraje vraja-rāja-tanūje kiṃ kiṃ vā tad vyañjijiṣayā
nāvirvrajati? tac ca yuktam evotpaśyāmaḥ; vrajapadam hi sarva-samīcīna-samūham ūhayati ||
children.translated_text: And in that [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>], with the community of <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers, in the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> — what indeed does not manifest with the desire to express itself? And we rightly perceive this; for the word <s>Vraja</s> suggests the entire assemblage of all that is excellent.

children.text: asti ceha śrī-bhāgavatīyaṃ padyam,
children.translated_text: And here there is a verse from the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> —

children.text:
tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarvasamṛddhimān |
harer nivāsātmaguṇai ramākrīdam abhūn nṛpa! ||iti | [BhP 10.5.18]
children.translated_text:
'From that time onward, O King, the <s>Vraja</s> of <s>Nanda</s> became endowed with all prosperity;
through the qualities of <s>Hari's</s> presence, it became a playground of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī).' (BhP 10.5.18)

children.text: teṣām āvirbhāvasya pādma-purāṇa-sandarbhānusāreṇa pratikalpam analpa-sukha-kalpaka-sampad-udanta-dantavakra-vadhānte sarvato' py ekānte kānte yatra praveśasya nirdeśaḥ prathayiṣyate, tasmād bhava-jana-manaḥ-kāya-nikāya-sparśa-virahitād vārāhādi-saṃkīrtita-pravara-kīrti-kadambādi-mayāt pādma-skāndādi-gatāsaṃkīrṇa-varṇākarṇita-tat-tat-sanātana-śīla-tārāmasa-rāma-go-gopa-gopāla-līlā-nidhānād vṛndāvanasyaiva vaibhava-viśeṣād aśeṣaṃ bhavati, prakṛti-sthitim atīto hi yaḥ |
children.translated_text: The description of their manifestation, in accordance with the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>'s context, will be elaborated — [namely, that] at the end of every <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle), after the destruction of <s>Dantavakra</s> through the narration of abundant bliss-granting prosperity, there is entry into that solitary, beloved [realm] in all respects. Therefore, from <s>Vṛndāvana</s> alone — which is untouched by the minds, bodies, and assemblages of worldly people, which consists of the excellent fame extolled by <s>Vārāha</s> and others, whose kadamba-grove is made of that [fame], from which the eternal conduct, the darkness-removing <s>Rāma</s>, the cows, cowherds, and cowherd-sports found in the <s>Pādma</s>, <s>Skānda</s>, and other [purāṇas] are heard in their unmingled glory — from the particular magnificence of that [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>] alone, everything arises, for he who transcends the state of <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature) [is there].

children.text: bṛhad-gautamīya-stha-śrī-kṛṣṇa-vacane tu tat-tat-saṃkṣepārtha-nikṣepaḥ prekṣyate |
children.translated_text: In the statement of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> found in the great <s>Gautamīya</s>, one finds the deposit of the summarized meaning of each [topic]:

children.text: idaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ mama dhāmaiva kevalam |
children.translated_text: "This <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is delightful — it is indeed my abode alone.

children.text: atra me paśavaḥ pakṣi-mṛgāḥ kīṭā narāmarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Here my animals, birds, deer, insects, humans, and immortals —

children.text: ye vasanti mamādhiṣṇye mṛtā yānti mamālayam ||
children.translated_text: those who dwell in my domain, upon dying, go to my abode.

children.text: atra yā gopa-kanyāś ca nivasanti mamālaye |
children.translated_text: And those cowherd girls who reside here in my abode —

children.text: yoginyas tā mayā nityaṃ mama sevā-parāyaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are <s>yoginīs</s>, eternally devoted to my service.

children.text: pañca-yojanam evāsti vanaṃ me deha-rūpakam |
children.translated_text: This forest of five <s>yojanas</s> is my bodily form.

children.text: kālindīyaṃ suṣumnākhyā paramāmṛta-vāhinī ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) is the <s>suṣumnā</s> channel, carrying the supreme nectar.

children.text: atra devāś ca bhūtāni vartante sūkṣma-rūpataḥ |
children.translated_text: Here gods and beings exist in subtle form.

children.text: sarva-deva-mayaś cāhaṃ na tyajāmi vanaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: I, who am the embodiment of all gods, never abandon this forest.

children.text:
āvirbhāvas tirobhāvo bhaven me' tra yuge yuge |
tejo-mayam idaṃ ramyam adṛśyaṃ carma-cakṣuṣā ||iti |
children.translated_text: Manifestation and disappearance of mine occur here age after age. This luminous, delightful [place] is invisible to the eyes of flesh." Thus it is stated.

children.text:
yaṃ khalu vaibhava-viśeṣaṃ sarva-sāreṇa yathā-sthānaṃ prakāśayiṣyamāṇa-vyākhyā-viśeṣāvatāreṇa śrīmad-bhāgavatānusāreṇa gopānāṃ svaṃ lokaṃ varuṇālayād āgataḥ karuṇā-varuṇālayaḥ svayaṃ bhagavān akrūrāya vaikuṇṭha-viśeṣa-lakṣaṇa-sva-vaibhava-vyañjanayā sukha-prade brahma-hrade majjanena tasmād unmajjanena ca taj-jana-kautuka-jananād anantaraṃ chandaḥ-stūyamānenātmanāvitrā vicitram atraiva vṛndāvane tadīya-nara-līlā-veśena sādhāraṇam anyebhyas tebhyaḥ sandarśayāmāsa; yaṃ prati sampraty api prapadyamānā vidvāṃsaś cetasāpi sākṣād iva tal-līlāḥ pratipadyante; yaṃ pari hari-vaṃśe govindābhiṣeka-sampad-aṃśe mahendraḥ śrīmad-vrajendra-tanūja-tanuvad vyāpakatāṃ satyāṃ pratyāyayāmāsa; yaṃ
punar vṛndāvana-stha-samasta-samabhyarṇam api tat-tad-varṇanānusāreṇa kecit prakṛty-āvaraṇataḥ parama-viyad-ūrdhvaṃ nirvarṇayanti; ataeva līlānurūpa-rūpatayā bhūmānam abhūmānaṃ ca prapadyante yad bhūmayaḥ | eṣa eva śeṣa-nirviśeṣatayā brahma-sākṣāt-kārākāratayā ca brahma-saṃhitādiṣu bṛṃhitaṃ bṛhadbhir varṇayāmāse | tatra ca prakaṭāprakaṭa-prakāśa-mayasya vṛndāvanasya bahu-vidha-saṃsthānatayā bahu-vidha-śāstra-śrutasyāprakaṭa-prakāśa-maya-vaibhava-viśeṣa eva samprati varṇanīyaḥ | sa ca gokula-pradhāna eveti sva-vivakṣita-hitā brahma-saṃhitānu-saṃhitā kriyate | tad-vacanāni tu bodha-kramāya kramam atikramyānukramyante, yathā-
children.translated_text: Indeed, this particular magnificence — which will be revealed in its proper place through the descent of detailed commentary in all its essential aspects, in accordance with the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> — was shown by the Blessed Lord himself, the ocean of compassion, who, having come from the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s> to the cowherds' own world, displayed to <s>Akrūra</s> the particular grandeur of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> marked with his own magnificence, through the pleasure-giving immersion in and emergence from <s>Brahmahrada</s> (the lake of <s>Brahman</s>), and thereby generated wonder in those people. Immediately afterwards, being praised by hymns, he himself, the invisible one, displayed right here in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — in an ordinary manner, through his human sport-form, to those and others — [his glory]. And those learned ones who even now take refuge [in this], perceive his sports as if directly with their minds. Regarding this, in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, in the section on <s>Govinda's</s> consecration, the great <s>Indra</s> confirmed the all-pervasiveness [of this realm], as if [it were] the body of the glorious son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>. Yet some, following the various descriptions, though everything in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is close to everything else there, describe it as being above the supreme sky due to the covering of <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature). Therefore, as [his] form corresponds to [his] sports, the realms accept both limited and unlimited [dimensions]. This very [truth] was elaborately described by the great ones in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> and other [texts], in the form of the direct realization of <s>Brahman</s>, without distinction from the remainder. And there, of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — which consists of both manifest and unmanifest radiance, and which has been heard of in various <s>śāstras</s> in its manifold configurations — it is the particular magnificence of the unmanifest-radiant aspect that is now to be described. And since that pertains primarily to <s>Gokula</s>, the exposition is composed following the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>, as intended. The verses from that [text] are cited in order for progressive understanding, transcending sequential order, as follows —

children.text: bhaje śvetadvīpaṃ tam aham iha goloka iti yaṃ
children.translated_text: "I worship that <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (White Island), which is known here as <s>Goloka</s>

children.text: vidantas te santaḥ kṣiti-virala-cārāḥ katipaye |
children.translated_text: by those few saintly persons of rare conduct on earth.

children.text: śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ kalpa-taravaḥ
children.translated_text: The beloveds of <s>Śrī</s> are the beloved ones, the supreme person is their lover, the <s>kalpa</s>-trees

children.text: drumā bhūmiś cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-mayī toyam amṛtam ||
children.translated_text: are the trees, the ground is made of assemblages of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems), the water is nectar.

children.text: kathā gānaṃ nāṭyaṃ gamanam api vaṃśī priya-sakhī
children.translated_text: Conversation is song, walking is dance, and the flute is the dear companion,

children.text: cid-ānanda-jyotiḥ param api tad āsvādyam api ca |
children.translated_text: the light is of <s>cit-ānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss), and that supreme [reality] is also to be relished.

children.text: sa yatra kṣīrābdhiḥ sarati surabhibhyaś ca sumahān
children.translated_text: Where the ocean of milk flows abundantly from the <s>surabhī</s> cows,

children.text: nimeṣārdhākhyo vā vrajati na hi yatrāpi samayaḥ ||[bra.saṃ. 5.57-58]
children.translated_text: and where not even a half-moment's worth of time passes" [<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.57-58].

children.text: kiṃ ca, īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ ity upakramyāha-
children.translated_text: Furthermore, beginning with "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the supreme Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>)," [the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>] says —

children.text: ṣahasra-patra-kamalaṃ gokulākhyaṃ mahat padam |
children.translated_text: "The thousand-petaled lotus named <s>Gokula</s> is the great abode.

children.text: tat-karṇikāraṃ tad-dhāma tad-anantāṃśa-sambhavam |
children.translated_text: Its pericarp is that abode, born of an infinite portion of it.

children.text: tat-kiñjalkaṃ tad-aṃśānāṃ tat-patrāṇi śriyām api ||
children.translated_text: Its filaments are the portions of that; its petals are [the abodes] of the <s>Śrīs</s> (goddesses of fortune) also.

children.text: catur-asraṃ tat-paritaḥ śvetadvīpākhyam adbhutam |
children.translated_text: Surrounding it on four sides is the wondrous [place] called <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>,

children.text: catur-asraṃ catur-mūrteś catur-dhāma catuṣ-kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: four-sided, of the four-fold form, four-fold abode, four-fold made.

children.text: caturbhiḥ puruṣārthaiś ca caturbhir hetubhir vṛtam |
children.translated_text: Surrounded by the four <s>puruṣārthas</s> (goals of life) and the four causes,

children.text: śūlair daśabhir ānaddham ūrdhvādho-dig-vidikṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: bound by ten tridents in the upper, lower, cardinal, and intermediate directions.

children.text: aṣṭabhiḥ nidhibhir juṣṭam aṣṭabhiḥ siddhibhis tathā |
children.translated_text: Attended by eight treasuries and likewise by eight <s>siddhis</s> (powers),

children.text: manu-rūpaiś ca daśabhir dik-pālaiḥ parito vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: surrounded on all sides by ten guardians of the directions in human forms.

children.text: śyāmair gauraiś ca raktaiś ca śuklaiś ca pārṣada-rṣabhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By dark, fair, red, and white foremost attendants,

children.text: śobhitaṃ śaktibhis tābhir adbhutābhiḥ samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: adorned on all sides with those wondrous powers."

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And further,

children.text:
cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa-
lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhīr abhipālayantam |
lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||ity ādi |
children.translated_text: "In residences made of heaps of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gems, enclosed by hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling trees), tending the <s>surabhī</s> cows, served with eagerness by hundreds of thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s> — I worship <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval person." — and so on.

children.text:
bṛhad-vāmane-
ratna-dhātu-mayaḥ śrīmān yatra govardhano giriḥ |
ratna-baddhobhaya-taṭā kālindī saritāṃ varā ||ity ādi cānyatra |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bṛhad-vāmana</s> [Purāṇa] — "The glorious mount <s>Govardhana</s> there is made of jewel-substrata; the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā), the best of rivers, has both banks set with jewels" — and so on, elsewhere also.

children.text: tad etad-anusāreṇa prathamaṃ tāvat kāvyasya nidhānaṃ vastu-mātraṃ sa-pramāṇaṃ prakāśyate, citrasya phalakam iva | [22] tathā hi--yasya khalu lokasya golokatayā go-gopa-vāsa-rūpasya, śvetadvīpatayā cānanya-spṛṣṭa-parama-śuddhatā-samudbuddha-svarūpasya
children.translated_text: Therefore, in accordance with all this, the subject matter alone — the foundation of the poem — is first set forth with supporting evidence, like a canvas for a painting. [22] Thus indeed — this world, which in its nature as <s>Goloka</s> has the form of the dwelling of cows, cowherds, as <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> has a nature awakened to supreme purity untouched by anything else —

children.text: tādṛśa-jñāna-maya-katipaya-mātra-prameya-gātratayā tat-tat-paramatā matā, parama-golokaḥ parama-śvetadvīpa iti | [23] tad eva yuktam uktaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: because only a few whose bodies are formed of such knowledge can comprehend it, the supremacy of each [aspect] is acknowledged; [it is called] the supreme <s>Goloka</s>, the supreme <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>. [23] This alone is properly stated.

children.text: yatra hi svacchandatānanda-prada-bahu-vacanārthā gopī-padārthāḥ śriyaḥ śrayante | nānya-vaikuṇṭhavat tad-eka-vacanārthatākuṇṭhāḥ | tāsāṃ tat-padārthatā ca tan-mahā-vāg-artha-sārākarṣa-yantre mahā-mantre ballavī-vallabhatayā tasya japam upadiśantīti sidhyati |
children.translated_text: Where indeed the <s>gopī</s>-principles — as <s>Śrīs</s> (goddesses of fortune) — take shelter, [being] of the nature of many words conveying the bliss of spontaneous freedom. Not as in the other <s>Vaikuṇṭhas</s>, where there is no limitation to their singular meaning. Their identity as such [<s>gopī</s>-principles] is established by the fact that, in the great <s>mantra</s> — the machine that draws forth the essence of the great word-meaning — it instructs the <s>japa</s> (recitation) of him as the beloved of the cowherd women (<s>ballavī-vallabha</s>).

children.text:
atra na kevalaṃ tasya dvi-varṇa-padasya vṛttāv eva rūḍhim avalambāmahe, api tu dhyāne' pi | kintu, nāyaṃ śriyo' ṅga iti śukānuvādaḥ sāmānya-lakṣmī-vijayaṃ vyanakti | lakṣmī-sahasra iti viriñci-vāṇī lakṣmī-viśeṣatvam urīkaroti, yasmād atra kuru-pāṇdava-śabdavad yathāvasaraṃ khaṇdākhaṇda-vācakatā matā | tad evaṃ sati, tatrāpi rādhā parameti
pādma-skāndādivārāha-vimiśra-mātsye | govinda-vṛndāvana-nāma-tantre' py abhāṣi yat, tat katham anyathā syāt?
lakṣmīr abhitaḥ stritamā gopyo lakṣmītamāḥ prathitāḥ |
rādhā gopitamā ced asyāḥ kā vā samā rāmā? ||JGc_1,1.15|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
Here we rely not only on the conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) of that two-syllabled word in practice, but also in meditation. However, <s>Śuka's</s> statement "not these <s>Śrīs</s>, dear one" indicates [merely] the victory over ordinary <s>Lakṣmī</s>. <s>Brahmā's</s> statement "a thousand <s>Lakṣmīs</s>" confirms their status as special <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, since, like the words <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, partial and complete denotation is accepted as occasion requires. This being so, "<s>Rādhā</s> is supreme" is what was stated in the <s>Pādma</s>, <s>Skānda</s>, <s>Vārāha</s>, <s>Vimiśra</s>, <s>Mātsya</s>, the <s>Govinda-Vṛndāvana-nāma-tantra</s>, and other [texts] — how can it be otherwise? 
[Verse:] "<s>Lakṣmī</s> is the most womanly of all; the <s>gopīs</s> are the most <s>Lakṣmī</s>-like, it is proclaimed. If <s>Rādhā</s> is the most <s>gopī</s>-like, what woman could be her equal?" [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.1.15]

children.text:
tad evaṃvidhānāṃ tāsām api sarvāsām eka eva ramanas, tata eva gokuladhāmā govindanāmā pratyekam ekām ekāṃ ramāṃ ramayatāṃ ramā-ramaṇanāmnāṃ
purupuruṣāṇāṃ paramaḥ | [27] yat tu madhye māyayā pratyāyitam aupapatyaṃ, tat khalv avāstavatvāt parastād avadhvastam iti śrīparamapuruṣaśabdābhyāṃ pramitam | kathāyāṃ tu pramāṇa-viśeṣagrathanayā prathamiṣyāmaḥ | [28] evaṃ śiṣṭaḥ śrīrāmo' py atidiṣṭaḥ |
[29] kiṃ ca, aśeṣā evataravaḥ kalpataravaḥ saṅkalpadānabalāt kevalān, na tu mānyatā-dhanya-sāmānya-viśeṣāt | teṣu ca jātyā kalpa-taravas tu vilakṣaṇa-tayā kṛta-lakṣaṇā eva |
children.translated_text: Thus, of all such [<s>gopīs</s>], there is but one lover, and therefore he, named <s>Govinda</s>, whose abode is <s>Gokula</s>, is the supreme among those supreme persons named <s>Ramā-ramaṇa</s> (delighter of <s>Ramā</s>), who delight each and every <s>Ramā</s> (goddess of fortune). [27] As for the paramour relationship (<s>aupapatya</s>) projected in the midst through <s>māyā</s> (illusion), since it is unreal it is dispelled beyond; this is understood from the words <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Parama-puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person). In the narrative, however, we shall elaborate with a specific arrangement of proofs. [28] Thus, the remaining <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (Balarāma) is also appointed. [29] Furthermore, all trees without exception are wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-taravas</s>) solely by the power of their willed generosity, not by any difference of ordinary or special honor. And among them, those that are <s>kalpa-taravas</s> by species are distinguished by their distinctive characteristics.

children.text:
kiṃ ca, ādarśanibhasvacchavibhavanānādarśasparśādimayabhūmikā bhūmiś ca kānter uta kānter vṛṣṭisṛṣṭikāriṇī cintāmaṇīyate | [31] āstāṃ tāvad uttaram anu tāratamya-ramyatā-gamya-mahimā gṛhādiṣu mahā-cintāmaṇi-mayī, yasmād udbhinnās tad-udbhidaś ca
tadīya-śobhām ātmany udbhāvayanti | yatra ca,
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the ground — which has surfaces made of mirror-like clarity, transparent substance, and touch — produces showers upon showers of beauty, [being itself] made of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems). [31] Let us leave aside the further magnificence that is to be appreciated through graduated beauty in the residences and other [structures], which are made of great <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gems, since the plants springing from them manifest that beauty within themselves. And where,

children.text:
dṛṣṭi-śravaṇam ayātās tad-gocaritāś ca jāti-rūpābhyām |
naga-mṛga-pakṣi-viśeṣās tatratyānāṃ ca citram ādadhati ||JGc_1,1.16|| [gīti]
children.translated_text: [Verse:] "The special kinds of trees, animals, birds — which have come within the sight and hearing [of that realm], and which are of that nature in their species and form — create wonder even among the inhabitants of that place." [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.1.16]

children.text: kiṃ ca, toyam apy amṛtāyate, kim utāmṛtam? kiṃ ca, kathāpi yathā gānaṃ tathā karṇayoḥ pānakāyate, kim uta svayam eva gānam? kiṃ ca, gamanam api nṛtya-cāturī-dhurīṇatām urīkaroti, nṛtyaṃ punar atīvādṛtyam | kiṃ ca, vaṃśī yathā kaṃsārāter āśu sukha-vilāsaṃ śaṃsantī, sahāyatayā ca lasantī ca priya-sakhīyate, na tadvad anyo dhanyo' pi janaḥ sambhavati |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, even the water becomes like nectar — what then of the actual nectar? Moreover, even conversation becomes like song to the ears, like a drink — what then of song itself? Walking, too, assumes the mastery of dance-skill — and dancing itself is to be most highly esteemed. Moreover, the flute, as it quickly proclaims the blissful sport of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and as it shines as a companion, becomes a dear friend — and no other fortunate person can match it.

children.text: kiṃ ca, cidānanda eva kevalaṃ svarūpānatirikta-śakti-vyakti-vaśād vyakti-viśeṣatayā vyaktībhavan, gokula-śabda-bala-labdha-lokaval-līlā-kaivalya-kalanāya puṣpavad-ādi-lakṣaṇa-prakāśakatayā tat tat prakāśya puṣpādi-lakṣaṇāsvādyatayā ca lāpaṃ kalayantīnām ālīnāṃ nija-nija-yūtha-varūthapāyāḥ paramāpūrva-pūrva-pūrvānurāgādi-kathānikāyaṃ gāyantīnāṃ madhu-madhura-kākalī-kulāni tatrakīyaṃ sarvaṃ tarv-antam ārdrīkurvanti, kim uta bahu-kaṣṭa-sṛṣṭatayā mithunī-bhūtaṃ tat tan mithunam |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>cit-ānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss) alone, becoming manifest as a particular manifestation through the expression of power inseparable from its own nature, and thereby manifesting each [element] with the characteristics of flowers and the like for the purpose of the exclusive experience of the world-sport obtained by the power of the word <s>Gokula</s> — the sweet, honey-sweet cooing-sounds of the groups of companion <s>gopīs</s>, who sing the narrative-mass of supremely unprecedented, former-and-prior love (<s>pūrvānurāga</s>) of the chief of each group's own troupe, these [sounds] moisten everything there up to the trees. How much more, then, each couple united together, created through great labor!

children.text: tathā ca, hāyaśīrṣa-pañcarātre pañca-tattva-nirūpaṇe vaikuṇṭha-stha-dravya-tattvaṃ nirūpitam -
children.translated_text: Accordingly, in the <s>Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>, in the determination of the five <s>tattvas</s>, the <s>dravya-tattva</s> (material principle) residing in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is described —

children.text: gandha-rūpaṃ svāda-rūpaṃ dravyaṃ puṣpādikaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: "That which has the form of fragrance, the form of taste, and is material such as flowers and the like,

children.text: rasavad bhautikaṃ dravyam atra syād rasa-rūpakam ||
children.translated_text: material substance possessing <s>rasa</s> (flavor) here would be of the form of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text:
heyāṃśānām abhāvāc ca rasa-rūpaṃ bhavec ca tat |
tvag-bījaṃ caiva heyāṃśaṃ kaṭhināṃśaṃ ca yad bhavet |
tat sarvaṃ bhautikaṃ viddhi na hi bhūtamayaṃ hi tat ||ity ādi |
children.translated_text: And that [substance] would be of the form of <s>rasa</s> due to the absence of objectionable parts. The skin, seeds, and whatever objectionable and hard parts there are — know all that to be material, for it is not made of [spiritual] elements." And so on.

children.text: tathāpi,
children.translated_text: Nevertheless,

children.text: prapañcaṃ niṣprapañco' pi vidambhayasi bhūtale |
children.translated_text: "Though you are free from the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>), you imitate the phenomenal world on earth,

children.text: prapanna-janatānanda-sandohaṃ prathituṃ prabho ||[BhP 10.14.37]
children.translated_text: in order to spread the flood of bliss among the people who have surrendered, O Lord" [<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.14.37].

children.text: iti brahmavacanānusāreṇa kṛta-prapañcānukāre līlā-sāre tasya tat-prapanna-janasya ca yathāveśaḥ syāt, na tathā ñityākāre' pīti labhyate |
children.translated_text: Thus, in accordance with <s>Brahmā's</s> statement, in the essence of sport (<s>līlā-sāra</s>) that imitates the phenomenal world, the experience of those surrendered people is as it should be — but it is obtained that it is not so even in the eternal form.

children.text:
heyāṃśānām abhāvāc ca rasarūpaṃ bhavec ca tat | tvag
 bījaṃ caiva heyāṃśaṃ kaṭhināṃśaṃ ca yad bhavet | tat
sarvaṃ bhautikaṃ viddhi na hi bhūtamayaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: "And that [substance] would be of the form of <s>rasa</s> due to the absence of objectionable parts. The skin, seeds, and whatever objectionable and hard parts there are — know all that to be material, for it is not made of [spiritual] elements."

children.text: tataḥ pūrvatra tasya tasya cāveśaḥ paratra ca praveśaḥ syāt | [37] tataś ca, tad-icchā-vaśāl līlā-śaktiḥ paratra ca prāyaḥ sarvaṃ vyaktīkarotīti vivektavyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the former [realm], there is the experience of each [element], and in the latter [realm], there is entry. [37] Therefore, by [the Lord's] will, the <s>līlā-śakti</s> (sport-power) generally makes everything manifest in the latter [realm] also — this should be understood.

children.text: kiṃ ca, murajin-muralī-kalī-khuralī ca sva-mādhurī-pradugdha-mugdha-surabhi-dugdhānāṃ surabhīnām ūdho-giritaḥ saritaḥ prasārayantī paritaḥ parikhāyamāṇaṃ kṣīra-vāridhiṃ visphārayati | tatra kāmadhenutayā nikāmam eva snuvatīnāṃ kṣīra-vāhitāpi
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the melody of <s>Murahari's</s> (Kṛṣṇa's) flute causes rivers to flow from the udders of the <s>surabhī</s> cows — charming cows whose milk has been drawn forth by its own sweetness — spreading an ocean of milk all around, expanding on every side. There, as the wish-fulfilling cows flow abundantly with milk at their pleasure, even the flowing of milk

children.text: prācuryeṇaiva paryavasāyyate | [39] tato nānā-rasā api tā nadyaḥ pratipadyante vidyā-vadbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: is fully concluded. [39] Then those rivers of various <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic flavors) are also recognized by the learned. |

children.text:
kiṃ ca, yatra ca tat-kaiśorānurūpārdha-vārdhaka-yauvana-nava-yauvanādi-vayasa
eva tat-pitṛ-bhrātṛ-sakhi-prabhṛtayas te nikhila-vargā nānyām avasthām āśritā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, where the ages of those — such as half-old-age corresponding to adolescence, fresh youth, and new youth — are those of his fathers, brothers, friends, and others; all those groups do not take any other state. |

children.text:
anyac ca, yasya ca golokasya madhyam adhyāsya sphuṭatarāneka-sahasra-patrī-paricitam ajasram eva khalv amalaṃ mahā-maṇi-kamalaṃ gokula-nāmatayā nija-rūpaṃ nirūpayati, "go-gopāvāsa-vraja-rūpa-vraja evāham asmi" iti |
[42] nyāya-vinyastam eva ca khalv idam, rūḍhir yogam apaharati iti | yathā jalaja-śabdenāpsavya-mātraṃ nocyate, kintu kamalam eva | rūḍhitām eva khalv ākhyā-grahaṇam
āviṣkaroti | [43] śrī-śuka-devenāpy etad-apekṣayoktaṃ, bhagavān gokuleśvaraḥ iti | varaṭ-pratyayaḥ khalv atra śīlārthatā-paraḥ | tad eva cāmnātaṃ gokulaṃ vana-vaikuṇṭham iti |
children.translated_text:
Furthermore, occupying the center of that <s>Goloka</s>, there is a great jeweled lotus, eternally pure, adorned with manifestly numerous thousands of petals, which by the name <s>Gokula</s> reveals its own form, [saying:] 'I am indeed the settlement (<s>vraja</s>) in the form of a <s>vraja</s> (encampment) where cows and cowherds dwell.' |
[42] And this is indeed established according to logic, [the rule that] conventional meaning overrides etymological meaning. Just as by the word <s>jalaja</s> (water-born) not merely anything born in water is meant, but the lotus specifically. The conventional usage indeed reveals the meaning of the name. [43] <s>Śrī Śukadeva</s> also said with reference to this: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, the Lord of <s>Gokula</s>.' The suffix <s>varaṭ</s> here denotes habitual nature. And that very [place] is traditionally known as '<s>Gokula</s> — the forest <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.' |

children.text: atha śrīmad-vraja-rāja-tanūjatā-śīla-līlasya mahā-bhagavatas tadīya-karṇikāṃ-madhyam adhikṛtya nānā-varṇa-dhāmatayā nirvarṇita-maṇi-maya-mahā-dhāma nikāmam udbhrājate, yad eva svayam anantāṃśa-sambhūtam iti sphuṭam anantadhā prakāśate |
children.translated_text: Now, the greatly blessed Lord, whose play is the nature of being the son of the King of <s>Vraja</s>, occupying the center of that [lotus's] pericarp, blazes forth abundantly as a great jeweled abode distinguished by rays of various colors, which itself, born from infinite portions, clearly manifests in infinite ways. |

children.text:
yasmin kesara-visarān prācīrāṅgān samantataḥ samayā |
sadayā dāyādāyāḥ sopāsīnā vasanti gopālāḥ ||JGc_1,1.17|| [gīti]
children.translated_text: In which, surrounding the filaments and the walls on all sides, | the <s>Gopālas</s> (cowherds), who are compassionate heirs, dwell seated nearby. || (JGc 1,1.17) [gīti meter]

children.text: gokulatābalatas tad api saṃvalate | tathā hi,
children.translated_text: That too is understood from the character of <s>Gokula</s>. Namely,

children.text:
aṃśā bhāgā dāyās tad-dhita-yogena dāyavantaś ca |
tat kila jāter bhāgā bakajiti te santi dāyavantaś ca ||JGc_1,1.18|| [gīti]
tasminn aṃśo yeṣām iti vā gamyo bahu-vrīhiḥ |
vrīhi-nibhas tat-premā teṣāṃ vṛttau tad-āśrayo yuktaḥ ||JGc_1,1.19|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
Portions, shares, inheritances — and by the use of the suffix <s>tad-dhita</s>, 'possessors of inheritance'; | those are indeed the shares of the [same] class, O <s>Bakajit</s> (Conqueror of the crane-demon), they are possessors of inheritance. || (JGc 1,1.18) [gīti]
Or it may be construed as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'those in whom there is a portion of that'; | their love resembles rice (<s>vrīhi</s>) — in their conduct, dependence on Him is fitting. || (JGc 1,1.19) [udgīti]

children.text: tad evam eṣāṃ tajjātitvam evoktaṃ śrī-śukena-
children.translated_text: Thus, their being of the same class (<s>tajjātitva</s>) was stated by <s>Śrī Śuka</s> —

children.text:
evaṃ kakudminaṃ hatvā stūyamānaḥ svajātibhiḥ |
viveśa goṣṭhaṃ sabalo gopīnāṃ nayanotsavaḥ ||iti | (BhP 10.36.15)
children.translated_text: 'Having thus slain <s>Kakudmin</s> (the bull-demon Ariṣṭa), being praised by his own kinsmen (<s>svajāti</s>), | He entered the cow-settlement (<s>goṣṭha</s>) with <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma), a festival for the eyes of the <s>Gopīs</s>.' || (BhP 10.36.15)

children.text:
patrāṇi tatra kamale kamalālayānām
aṃśena keli-vipināni bhavanti yeṣu |
cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa-
lakṣāvṛteṣu nibhṛtaṃ ramate mukundaḥ ||JGc_1,1.20|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: The petals of that lotus become, by portions, the pleasure-groves of the dwellers of the lotus (<s>Kamalālaya</s>), | in which, in mansions built of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) jewels, surrounded by millions of <s>kalpa-vṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees), | <s>Mukunda</s> (Kṛṣṇa) sports in seclusion. || (JGc 1,1.20) [vasantatilakā meter]

children.text:
tatrādhirājyaṃ kila rādhikām anu
prattaṃ priyeṇeti purāṇa-viśrutam |
ahaṃ tu manye punar-uktam eva tad
guṇena tasyāḥ sa ca yad vaśaṃ-gataḥ ||JGc_1,1.21|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: There, sovereignty is said to have been bestowed upon <s>Rādhikā</s> by her Beloved — so it is renowned in the <s>Purāṇas</s>; | but I consider that to be merely a tautology, | since He is already under Her sway by virtue of Her qualities. || (JGc 1,1.21) [upajāti meter]

children.text:
iha ca pūrvaṃ yad eva śrī-parama-puruṣa-śabdābhyām adhyavasitaṃ, tad evādhyavasīyate | tāsu kevalāsu vraja-rāja-suta-vadhū-bhāvasya labdha-prasiddhitāṃ vinā
vraja-kamala-sakala-patrāvaly-ādhipatyaṃ na prasidhyatīti |
children.translated_text: And here, what was previously established by the terms '<s>Śrī</s>' and '<s>Parama-puruṣa</s>' (Supreme Person) is now reaffirmed. Without the well-established status of being the bride of the son of <s>Vraja-rāja</s> (King of Vraja) among those [gopīs] exclusively, sovereignty over all the petals of the <s>Vraja</s>-lotus cannot be established. |

children.text:
atha kiñcit-kuñcita-kamala-patravad-unnata-pārśva-dvayāvayavatayā bahir
durlaṅgha-śṛṅga-maṇi-mayālavāla-śobhā-matrāṇāṃ patrāṇām antarāleṣu keśarād avatīrṇāni vistīrṇāni pṛthak pṛthag upaniṣkarāṇi virājante | teṣām agrima-sandhiṣu sphuṭam adhimadhya-madhyam adhyasta-samasteśa-goṣṭhāni goṣṭhāni vibhrājante |
ataeva tatparyantasya tasya gokulatāvakalitā |
children.translated_text: Now, on account of the slightly-curled lotus petals having two elevated side-portions, in the intervals between the petals — whose outer beauty consists of impassable peaks of jeweled basins — the sub-settlements (<s>upaniṣkara</s>) that have descended from the filament spread out extensively, each distinct. At the foremost junctions of those, clearly in the very center, the main cow-settlements (<s>goṣṭha</s>) where the master of all is presided over shine forth. | Therefore, the <s>Gokula</s>-nature of that periphery is established. |

children.text:
tatrāpi doha-samayaṃ samayā samena
go-vṛnda-pāla-valayena niviśya paśyan |
cintāmaṇi-pracita-sadmasu kalpa-śākhi-
padmāvṛteṣu surabhīr abhipāti kṛṣṇaḥ ||JGc_1,1.22|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: There too, at milking time, with propriety, | entering with a circle of cowherds attending the herds, watching, | in mansions composed of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems, surrounded by <s>kalpa</s>-trees and lotuses, | <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> tends the <s>Surabhī</s> (wish-fulfilling) cows. || (JGc 1,1.22) [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
yasya ca samīpagānām ālaya-rūpasya kamalasya sarvataś caturasraṃ bhavati, tad idaṃ sarvaṃ vṛndāvanam iti vadanti | tad-bahir-antaraṃ samasta-dīpāyamānaḥ sa
mahā-dvīpāyamānaḥ parama-suveśaḥ sarvaś ca deśaḥ śvetadvīpa ity ācakṣate goloka iti ca | yas tu bahir-bhāgaḥ sāgaravad aparicchedyas tatra vigata-śokā dhāritra-nibha-vicitra-lokāḥ salokā vidyante | patra-sthitāni tu vanāni keli-vṛndāvanānīti bhaṇanti | yathoktaṃ
pāñcarātre - mahāvṛndāvanaṃ tatra kelivṛndāvanāni ca iti |
children.translated_text: And that which is square on all sides in the form of the dwelling-lotus near Him — all that they call <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. The inner and outer expanse of that, wholly radiant, that great island-expanse, supremely well-adorned, the entire region — they declare it to be <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), and also <s>Goloka</s>. But the outer part, immeasurable like the ocean — there exist grief-free beings of worlds variegated like the earth's surface. The forests situated on the petals, they call pleasure-<s>Vṛndāvanas</s>. As stated in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>: 'The great <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is there, and also the pleasure-<s>Vṛndāvanas</s>.' |

children.text: atha caturasram anu kamalāt patayālutayā paritaḥ sravantīr madhu-dhārāḥ pibanta iva punar uparata-tat-pānāya vamanta iva ca dakṣiṇa-paścimayoḥ sarvataḥ parvataḥ parvata-ṣaṭ-padā dṛśyante | yatra ca tatrāpi mahā-maṇi-maya-kūṭa-ghanaḥ śrī-govardhanaḥ kuṭī-bhūta-mahā-nidhivad akharvam ānanda-garvaṃ sarvādhipater apy āvirbhāvayati |
children.translated_text: Now, around the square [area], as if drinking the streams of honey flowing all around from the lotus with eagerness, and as if disgorging [them] again for renewed drinking, on the south and west [and] on all sides, mountains — the 'mountain-bees' — are seen. And there, among them, dense with peaks of great jewels, the glorious <s>Govardhana</s> reveals an undiminished pride of bliss even for the Lord of all, like a treasure-house that has become a cottage. |

children.text:
śrī-govardhana-nāmā cāyaṃ ramaṇīya-maṇi-śilābhiḥ samāsanam āsanam,
khagāvali-kalita-kākalībhiḥ svāgataṃ svāgatam,
śyāmāka-dūrvābja-viṣṇukrāntāparyag-ākrānta-tiryag-nirjharibhir niṣpādyaṃ pādyam,
cañcan-mṛga-caraṇa-nyañcad-akṣata-darbhānantāṅkuraiḥ samarghyam arghyam,
tīra-sanīḍa-jātī-lavaṅga-kakkola-saṅgata-pallalair alam ācamanīyam ācamanīyam,
nava-nava-nava-prasūta-gavī-navīna-snuta-kṣīra-pariṇata-dadhi-tat-prasṛta-ghṛta-śabalanais tarūpahṛta-madhuparkaṃ madhuparkam,
śikhara-śekhara-śilāsara-prakhara-dhārā-pātair anukṛta-snapana-paricaryā-prīti-majjanaṃ majjanam,
dukūlavad-anukūla-saṃśleṣa-svarṇa-varṇa-vṛkṣa-viśeṣa-valkalaiḥ kalita-sukha-vasanaṃ vasanam,
svabhāvānubandha-gandha-sugandha-śilā-śata-pariṇata-hari-candana-gaura-gairikaiś carcātiśayaṃ carcātiśayam,
praphulla-māla-mālatī-latādibhir nandita-sumanasaḥ sumanasaḥ,
gavyākhuravyāhati-jātāguru-dāru-dhūmair vyāhata-sarva-dhūpaṃ dhūpam,
divāpi vidyoti-maṇi-nikara-jyotibhiḥ sarva-sampad-uddīpaṃ dīpam,
mañjula-guñjāpiñchā-divi ncholīvāñchita-nirmāṇaiḥ kṛta-suṣamā-bharaṇam ābharaṇam,
abhilāṣānukūla-phala-mūla-valayaiḥ sarva-sukha-samāhāraṃ samāhāram,
puṣpa-vāsita-śītala-jala-valayita-punar-ācamanam anu vimala-parimalātula-tulasikā-pallavādibhir mukha-vāsanaṃ mukha-vāsanam,
marud-uccala-sphuṭa-puṣpa-sampac-campaka-dīpāvalyā sphuṭam ārātrikam ārātrikam,
ghana-kisalaya-valaya-saṅkula-bakula-mukha-śākhā-nikaraiḥ śobhāntaratamātapatram ātapatram,
malaya-marul-lava-calat-pallava-viśāla-śālair nandita-bhavya-janaṃ vyājanam,
nija-svara-vivekināṃ kekinām anekāṅga-kekābhiḥ kalilāsyaṃ lāsyam,
hari-veṇu-dhvani-bhram-kīcaka-kala-krama-ktākarsa-vanitānvita-śayyāyamāna-puspa-pāta-paryāyaiḥ kta-sarvātiśayanaṃ śayanam,
kākalī-kalila-kala-kokila-kulair labdha-saṅgānaṃ saṅgānam api hariṃ parikalayan pūrva-pūrva-siddha-nija-hari-dāsa-varyatāṃ paryāpayann āste |
children.translated_text: And this one named <s>Śrī Govardhana</s> — with its beautiful jeweled stones it offers a seat as a seat (<s>āsana</s>), with the cries of rows of birds it offers a welcome as a welcome, with cascading streams on all sides covered with <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet), <s>dūrvā</s> (sacred grass), lotuses, and <s>viṣṇukrānta</s> plants it offers water for washing feet as foot-water (<s>pādya</s>), with unbroken blades of <s>darbha</s> grass and endless sprouts from the hooves of wandering deer it offers a respectful offering as an offering (<s>arghya</s>), with clusters of <s>jātī</s> (jasmine), <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove), and <s>kakkola</s> (cardamom) growing in nests on its banks it offers mouth-rinsing water as mouth-rinsing water (<s>ācamanīya</s>), with the ever-newly born cows' fresh-flowing milk, ripened yogurt, and the clarified butter produced from it, brought by the trees, it offers the honey-mixture as a honey-mixture (<s>madhuparka</s>), with the fierce cascades of waterfalls from the rocky summit-crests it offers a bath of loving service as a bath (<s>majjana</s>), with bark-garments of golden-colored special trees clinging favorably like silk cloth it offers comfortable garments as garments (<s>vasana</s>), with the naturally fragrant sandal-paste and yellow ochre ripened from hundreds of fragrant stones it offers an excess of anointing as anointing (<s>carcā</s>), with blooming garlands of <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) creepers and the like it offers delightful flowers as flowers (<s>sumanas</s>), with the smoke of <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) ignited by the striking of cow-hooves it offers all-surpassing incense as incense (<s>dhūpa</s>), with the lights of clusters of gems that glow even by day it offers all-prosperous illumination as a lamp (<s>dīpa</s>), with charming ornamental creations of <s>guñjā</s> (berries) and peacock feathers it offers an abundance of beauty as ornaments (<s>ābharaṇa</s>), with circles of fruits and roots agreeable to desire it offers a feast of all happiness as a feast (<s>samāhāra</s>), and after the renewed mouth-rinsing with cool water perfumed with flowers, with incomparably fragrant <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil) shoots and the like it offers mouth-freshening as mouth-freshening (<s>mukha-vāsana</s>), with the wind-stirred <s>campaka</s> flower-wealth blossoming openly it offers a clear evening-worship with lamps as evening-worship (<s>ārātrika</s>), with dense rows of branches headed by <s>bakula</s> trees thick with circles of young leaves it offers the most beautiful parasol as a parasol (<s>ātapatra</s>), with wide leaves of <s>śāla</s> trees whose shoots sway in the breeze from <s>Malaya</s> it offers a fan delighting noble people as a fan (<s>vyājana</s>), with the manifold cries of peacocks who distinguish by their own voices it offers a charming dance-performance as a dance (<s>lāsya</s>), with layers of flower-showers that make a bed for ladies attracted by the melodious sequence of bamboos resonating with the sound of <s>Hari's</s> flute it offers the supreme resting-place as a resting-place (<s>śayana</s>), and with flocks of cuckoos full of soft <s>kākalī</s> notes it offers music of companionship as music (<s>saṅgāna</s>) — thus attending upon <s>Hari</s>, [Govardhana] fulfills its pre-established supreme status as <s>Hari's</s> chief servant. |

children.text: kṛta-haridāsa-varya-saṅgā mānasa-gaṅgā ca sarva-sukha-sthemani kṛṣṇa-premaṇi mānasa-drava-mayīti kila tan-nāmatayā tāṃ varṇayanty upaślokayanti ca-
children.translated_text: And <s>Mānasa-Gaṅgā</s> (the mental Ganges), associated with the chief servant of <s>Hari</s>, rests in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-love, the abode of all happiness, being of the nature of mental liquefaction — they describe and eulogize it by that very name —

children.text:
svalpenāghajid-aṃśa-vāmana-pada-sparśena gaṅgā sadā
sarvāgha-praśamany abhūd api śivasyārūḍha-mūrdhājani |
svenaivāghajitā sadā viharatā brahmeśa-lakṣmī-jayi-
prāśastyena saha vrajena militā gaṅgāparā kiṃ punaḥ ||JGc_1,1.23|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text: By the mere touch of the foot of the <s>Vāmana</s>-portion of <s>Aghajit</s> (the Conqueror of Sin, i.e. Kṛṣṇa), the <s>Gaṅgā</s> always | became the pacifier of all sins and rose to the head of <s>Śiva</s>; | but [this] <s>Gaṅgā</s>, united with <s>Vraja</s> where <s>Aghajit</s> himself always sports, | with a glory surpassing <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva), and <s>Lakṣmī</s> — what more need be said of this other <s>Gaṅgā</s>? || (JGc 1,1.23) [śārdūlavikrīḍita meter]

children.text: atha yatrāpy uttara-pūrvayoḥ kasyānanda-vraja-rūpasya vrajasyālindād adūrabhaveti kila kālindīti-nāmnī yamunā vilasati | yā khalu-
children.translated_text: Now, in the northeast, not far from the veranda of that <s>Vraja</s> of the nature of <s>Ānanda-vraja</s> (the settlement of bliss), there gleams the <s>Yamunā</s>, known by the name <s>Kālindī</s>. She indeed —

children.text:
kadācid dhārābhir vahati hari-ratna-drava-nibhā
kadācit stabdhāṅgī sphurati hari-ratna-kṣitir iva |
kramād veṇau tasmin na nadati nadaty arka-tanayā
jalasthalyoḥ śarma prasavati hareḥ sevana-vidhau ||JGc_1,1.24|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: Sometimes she flows with currents resembling the liquid essence of sapphire (<s>Hari-ratna</s>), | sometimes she stands motionless, shining like a surface of sapphire; | gradually, when that flute does not sound, the daughter of the Sun (<s>Arka-tanayā</s>, Yamunā) does not flow — | on water and land she produces happiness in the service of <s>Hari</s>. || (JGc 1,1.24) [śikharinī meter]

children.text:
paśyantī jalajekṣaṇā ghana-rasāvarta-śrutiḥ śṛṇvatī
jighrantī jhaṣa-nāsikā tarala-dor āliṅganaṃ kurvatī |
jalpantīva ca haṃsa-cakra-vadanā nīrātmanā kṛṣṇa-bhāg
yā kṛṣṇā bata sātha kīdṛg asakṛd devyātmanā ceṣṭate ||JGc_1,1.25|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text: With lotus-eyes she is seeing, with whirlpools of dense <s>rasa</s> (flavor) as ears she is hearing, | with fish as her nose she is smelling, with restless arms she is embracing, | with mouths of swans and <s>cakravāka</s> birds she is as if speaking — through her watery nature she partakes of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; | she who is dark (<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>) — ah, how often she acts in the role of a goddess toward Him! || (JGc 1,1.25) [śārdūlavikrīḍita meter]

children.text: yatra ca sarvatra sarāṃsi caivam utprekṣyante-
children.translated_text: And everywhere there the lakes are imagined thus —

children.text:
vraja-vipina-vibhāge niścalo yasya vāsaḥ
svayam ayam apareṣāṃ poṣako jañjanīti |
kalaya vara-sarāṃsi srotasām atra vṛndair
vidadhati yamunādi-dvīpinīḥ shīta-toyāḥ ||JGc_1,1.26|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text: He whose stationary abode is in a portion of the <s>Vraja</s> forest, | who himself nourishes the others, moving about freely — | consider the excellent lakes here: with clusters of streams | they create the <s>Yamunā</s> and other island-rivers of cool waters. || (JGc 1,1.26) [mālinī meter]

children.text:
yatra ca-
kāścit paṅka-kairavāvali-lasat-srotasvatī-prāntagā
nānā-puṣpa-vanī-virājad avanī-madhya-sthitāḥ kāścana |
kekā-jhaṅkṛti-mat-kuhū-madhuritāḥ kāntāṅga-carcācitā
nāsādṛk-śravasaḥ sadāpi sukhadā rāsāṅkitā bhūmayaḥ ||JGc_1,1.27|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text: And where — | some grounds are at the edges of streams bright with rows of white water-lilies in the mud, | some are situated in the middle of the earth resplendent with groves of various flowers, | some are sweetened with the cries, buzzing, and cooing [of peacocks, bees, and cuckoos], anointed with beautiful limbs, | always giving pleasure to the ears and the like, marked with the <s>Rāsa</s>-dance. || (JGc 1,1.27) [śārdūlavikrīḍita meter]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
bhāṇḍīras taraṇi-padaṃ samunnater na
prāyātaḥ param iha kintu vistṛteś ca |
tac-chākhāḥ pariviharann avāra-pāre
kālindyā muhur abhiyāti gopa-saṅghaḥ ||JGc_1,1.28|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text: Moreover — | The <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> (banyan tree) is not a station of the sun on account of height — | rather, it is primarily on account of breadth; | sporting among its branches, on this side and the far side | of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā), the company of cowherds constantly comes and goes. || (JGc 1,1.28) [praharṣiṇī meter]

children.text:
tathā-
kvacit sadmābhāsa-prakaṭa-balavat-koṭara-ghaṭaḥ
kvacit palyaṅkābha-prathita-pṛthu-śākhā-sukhatamaḥ |
kvacid dolātulya-grathita-latikā-pāli-valitaḥ
sadāsau bhāṇḍīraḥ kam iva hari-keliṃ na tanute ||JGc_1,1.29|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: Likewise — | In some places, with strong hollows resembling the appearance of houses, | in some places, supremely comfortable with broad branches famed as resembling couches, | in some places, swaying with rows of creepers entwined like swings — | this <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> (banyan) — what sport of <s>Hari</s> does it not facilitate? || (JGc 1,1.29) [śikharinī meter]

children.text:
tad-udīcīm anudeśaḥ
prathayati saukhyāni rāma-ghaṭṭākhyaḥ |
yatra ca rāmaṃ kurvan
sukhayati rāmaḥ sarāmatām añcan ||JGc_1,1.30|| [gītiḥ]
children.translated_text: To its north, a region | known as <s>Rāma-ghaṭṭa</s> (Balarāma's bathing place) spreads its delights; | where, performing the <s>Rāma</s> (pleasure), | <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) gladdens, manifesting supreme delight. || (JGc 1,1.30) [gīti meter]

children.text: atha tasya lokasya loaka-pālair varaṇīyāni vimāna-cāriṇāṃ varāṇyāvaraṇāni sura-vartmani varīvṛtati | yatra ca vāsudevādi-saṃjñaṃ svayam eva caturvyūha-vṛndaṃ loka-pālāyamānaṃ senā-vyūhatām urarīcarīkarīti | tatra ca puruṣārthādayaḥ ke varākāḥ ?
children.translated_text: Now, in that world, the coverings of the sky-chariots, worthy of being chosen by the world-protectors, revolve in the celestial path. And there, the fourfold <s>Vyūha</s> group, itself bearing the names <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the rest, assumes the role of world-protectors, taking on the form of an army formation. And there — what are the wretched goals of human life (<s>puruṣārthas</s>) [compared to this]? |

children.text: tad evaṃ sati goloka-nāmāyaṃ lokaḥ parama-mānyaḥ sāmānyatayāpi kena varṇyatām ? yaḥ khalv amṛta-sindhur ity amṛtāndhasaḥ, yaśasaḥ savayā iti kavayaḥ, vicitrī-dharmākṛtir iti viśvakarmāṇaḥ, ānandānāṃ brahma-sākṣād iti brahmānubhavinaḥ, premā svayaṃ vyakta iti bhagavad-bhaktā manyanta ity aneka-mata-parāmṛṣṭatayā dṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: This being so, this world named <s>Goloka</s>, supremely worthy of honor — by whom can it be described even in general terms? Those who [say it is] an ocean of nectar [call it] nectar-food; the poets [call it] the companion of fame; the cosmic architects [call it] a form of wondrous principles; those who experience <s>Brahman</s> [call it] the direct <s>Brahman</s> of blisses; the devotees of the Lord consider it to be love itself made manifest — thus it is perceived through many viewpoints. |

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
kiṃ tejaḥ kiṃ nu citraṃ kim uta naṭa-kalā kintarāṃ ko' pi lokaḥ
kiṃ vā premā sa sākṣād iha kalita-vapur yaḥ śukena pragītiḥ |
itthaṃ tal-lokapāla-pramukha-diviṣadāṃ saṃhatis tarkayantī
tasmin govinda-dhāmni pratidinam ayate sambhramaṃ ca bhramaṃ ca ||JGc_1,1.31|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
Moreover —
What is this brilliance? What is this marvel? Is it indeed some art of dance? What world beyond? Or is it some person?
Or is it love itself, having assumed a body here, being hymned by a parrot?
Thus, the assembly of <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Protectors) and other gods, led by their chiefs, speculating,
arrives at that abode of <s>Govinda</s> day after day, in both agitation and bewilderment. // [<s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ buddha-paddhatim apy atītavān asau lokaḥ prasabhaṃ buddhi-madhyam adhyārohati | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, that world, having surpassed even the path of the enlightened, forcefully ascends to the very center of intelligence. For —

children.text:
ye ye prītiṃ dadati viṣayā ye ca tat-tad-vidūrās
teṣūtkaṇṭhā mama nahi kadāpy atra satyaṃ karomi |
kṛṣṇe snehaṃ bata vitanute yaś ca yatrāpi kṛṣṇaḥ
śaśval-lokaṃ sa tu sarabhasaṃ māṃ didṛkṣuṃ karoti ||JGc_1,1.32|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
Whatever objects give pleasure, and those that are far removed from them —
I never feel longing for those here; this I declare truly.
But the love that expands toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and wherever <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is —
that world constantly, eagerly, makes me desire to see it. // [<s>mandākrāntā</s>]

children.text:
yasyākarṇanam apy apūrvam amita-brahmāṇḍa-koṭi-vraje
vaikuṇṭheṣv api vāñchitaṃ kim aparaṃ yal-lālasā śrīr api |
goloke sa tu bāndhavāgrimatayā vibhrājate sarvadā
yeṣāṃ tan-madhurimṇi hanta mama hṛn majjan muhuḥ sajjati ||JGc_1,1.33|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text:
The very hearing of which is unprecedented among the multitude of countless billions of universes,
which is desired even in the <s>Vaikuṇṭhas</s> (heavens of Viṣṇu) — what more could be wished? — for which even <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) yearns,
yet in <s>Goloka</s> he always shines forth with the intimacy of the closest kinsman —
alas! My heart, sinking repeatedly into his sweetness, becomes entangled again and again. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: hanta kiṃ karavāṇi ? sahasaivārabdhavān etad varṇanam | nirvāhaṃ tu na paśyāmi | [59] yataḥ prathamataś caturasra-pari-hari-carita-cārutā-praṇidhāna evedṛśatā dṛśyate, yathā-
children.translated_text: Alas, what shall I do? I have suddenly begun this description! But I do not see how to bring it to completion. [59] For, in the first place, such beauty is seen only in the devoted contemplation of the all-encompassing charm of <s>Hari's</s> deeds, as follows —

children.text:
gavāṃ kṣepaś cāraṃ prati sakhibhir ākrīḍa-paratā
muhus tāsāṃ dūre gamanam anusambhālana-vidhiḥ |
tad-āhvānaṃ tāsu kramam anuvisṛṣṭiḥ savayasāṃ
punaḥ krīḍāveśaḥ smṛti-padatayā kṣobhayati ||JGc_1,1.34|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
The driving of the cows toward pasture, the delight in play with friends,
the repeated watching over them as they wander far away,
the calling of those [cows], the gradual release [to pasture] with companions,
and then again the rapture of play — [all this] agitates [my mind] by way of remembrance. // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text:
tatrāpi-
kva cāpi kṛṣṇa-rāmau tau kara-baddha-karau mithaḥ |
hasantau hāsayantau ca kurvāte cittam ākulam ||JGc_1,1.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And there too —
Somewhere <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, hand clasped in hand with each other,
laughing and making others laugh — they confound the mind. // [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
vṛkṣān aṅkurayantu vidruta-daśām adrīn nayantu drutaṃ
stambhaṃ cāmbhasi lambhayantu saritāṃ kiṃ vā pratīcīnatām |
veṇu-dhvāna-ghaṭā yato' tinikaṭāḥ kasmād akasmād balāt
karṇābhyarṇa-gatā iva sphuṭam amūn dhunvanti tad-dhyāyinaḥ ||JGc_1,1.36|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text:
Moreover —
Let the trees sprout forth, let the mountains be reduced to a flowing state,
let the rivers acquire motionlessness in their waters, or even flow backward!
For the torrents of the sound of the flute, being so very near, somehow, suddenly, forcefully,
as if having reached the very vicinity of the ears, clearly shake those who meditate upon him. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: yatas tad-anubhavināṃ sukhaṃ tu manasi sphurad api na vaktum īśyate |
children.translated_text: For the happiness of those who experience that, even as it flashes in the mind, cannot be expressed in words.

children.text:
yasmin harir yāti vihāra-hetos
tasmin mudā phullati cet kuṭo' pi |
na tatra pṛcchā na ca vaktṛtā tan
na pṛcchyam etan na ca vācyam asti ||JGc_1,1.37|| [upajāti]
children.translated_text:
In the place where <s>Hari</s> goes for the sake of his pastimes,
if even a hut blooms with joy,
there is no question and no speaking about it —
it is not to be asked about, nor is it to be described. // [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: idaṃ ca sujana-matim atīvākarṣati |
children.translated_text: And this exceedingly attracts the minds of good people.

children.text:
gāyanti tatra dhavalāḥ paripālayantaḥ
pārāvatīṃ madhura-rāgavatīm udasrāḥ |
janmādi-kṛṣṇa-caritāni ciraṃ gatāni
smṛtvā yataḥ sapadi muhyati sarva eva ||JGc_1,1.38|| [vasanta]
children.translated_text:
There the white [cows] sing as they are tended,
offering their sweet, melodious, tear-filled lowing.
Recalling the deeds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> beginning from his birth, long past,
everyone at once becomes bewildered. // [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: aho kutaḥ kuto vā manaḥ saṃyamanīyam, yato goṣṭhāni ca tāni draṣṭuṃ manaḥ prasabham utkaṇṭhayanti | yathā-
children.translated_text: Ah! From where, from where should the mind be restrained? For those cow-pens make the mind forcefully long to see them. As follows —

children.text:
virājat-kastūrī-dyuti-parimalair gomaya-maya-
sphurac-cūrṇaiḥ sadma-pratikṛti-vapubhis taru-varaiḥ |
divā nūtnair vatsair niśi surabhijidbhiḥ surabhibhiḥ
samanād goṣṭhānii pratimati diśanti smṛti-śatam ||JGc_1,1.39|| [*2] [śikhariṇī]
[*2] The two latter lines are also found at the end of GC (uttara-campū 37v55).
children.translated_text:
With powders of cow-dung, shining and fragrant, possessing the luster and perfume of gleaming musk,
with excellent trees having the forms of house-replicas,
by day with fresh calves, and by night with fragrant cows conquering all scents —
the cow-pens in every direction bestow a hundred memories. // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text:
sandhyayos tu-
vatsān mocayatāṃ dhanāni duhatāṃ dugdhāni sañcinvatāṃ
gāḥ sambhālayatāṃ gṛhān pracalatāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ puraḥ kurvatām |
tal-līlāḥ parigāyatāṃ pulakitām aśrāṇi cātanvatāṃ
gopānāṃ bata cittam uccita-madaṃ mac-cittam ākrāmati ||JGc_1,1.40|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text:
And at the two twilights —
Of those releasing the calves, of those milking the wealth [of cows], of those collecting the milk,
of those tending the cows, of those walking toward their homes, of those placing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> before them,
of those singing his pastimes, covered in goosebumps, shedding tears —
the mind of those cowherds, overflowing with rapture, overwhelms my mind. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: sadā caitāni rāja-vartmāni tat-kīrtana-catvarāṇīva prasabhaṃ mac-cittam ākarṣanti | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: And always these royal pathways, like arenas for celebrating him, forcefully attract my mind. For indeed —

children.text:
rāmaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmau ca kṛṣṇaḥ
kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇa ity eṣa jalpaḥ |
yātāyātaṃ kurvatāṃ sarvadāpi
svairālāpe śrūyate tatra tatra ||JGc_1,1.41|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'<s>Rāma</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>Rāma</s>! And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' — such is the chatter
of those constantly coming and going,
heard here and there in free conversation. // [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa-pramadānāṃ pramadānāṃ pramada-vana-pātrāṇi patrāṇi tu varṇyamānāni kavīnām apatrapām eva bibhrati, yatas tatratyaṃ sarvam eva citram iti duṣpratyāyatāṃ prāpnoti | yeṣu hi-
children.translated_text: The pleasure gardens of the joyful women of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — even their leaves, when described, bring nothing but shame to poets, for everything there is so wondrous that it reaches the point of incredibility. In those [gardens] indeed —

children.text:
kvacit kuñjāḥ sadma-bhramakara-rucais tair avayavaiḥ
kvacic citraiḥ sadmāny api tulita-kuñjāni śataśaḥ |
jalāni kvāpy udyat-kamala-valitāni pratipadaṃ
sthalāny apy evaṃ kvāpy atha kim iva kiṃ nirṇaya-padam ||JGc_1,1.42|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Somewhere there are bowers with branches whose beauty causes confusion with houses,
and somewhere there are houses by the hundreds that rival the bowers with their marvels;
somewhere waters are adorned with emerging lotuses at every step,
and somewhere dry lands too are just so — what then is the basis for any determination? // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text:
sakhīnāṃ sāraṇya-tridaśa-sudṛśāṃ gāna-valanāṃ
muhuḥ prodyan-mūrcchāṃ madhu-madhura-rāga-praṇayinīm |
hari-premārta-strī-prathama-racitāṃ śṛṇvati jane
sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vety avakalayituṃ kaḥ prabhavati ||JGc_1,1.43|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
The female companions, equal in beauty to the celestial women of the divine grove, singing songs
whose rising modulations are lovingly devoted to honeyed, sweet <s>rāgas</s> (melodies),
first composed by women anguished with love for <s>Hari</s> — when people hear them,
who is able to determine whether it is pleasure or pain? // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text:
kvacid gānaṃ sūkṣmaṃ kvacid api ca tauryatrika-kalā
kvacit premṇā goṣṭhī kvacid api mahā-keli-kalahaḥ |
iti sphāraṃ tābhiḥ praṇaya-maya-sāraṃ viharaṇaṃ
harer dhyāyan nānā bhavati kavi-cittaṃ muhur api ||JGc_1,1.44|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Somewhere there is subtle singing, somewhere the threefold art of music,
somewhere affectionate conversation, somewhere a great sportive quarrel;
thus, meditating on the widely expansive, love-filled play of <s>Hari</s> with them,
the poet's mind becomes agitated again and again. // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text:
premā kāmati tat-kriyā kalahati stambhādi-bhāvāvalī
sakhyāṃ sañcarati śrutaṃ ca caritaṃ sarva-śrutaṃ laṅghati |
itthaṃ keli-kalā-kalāpa-kalitaṃ vṛndāvanāntar-vane
dampatyor nikhilaṃ vicāra-padavīm uddhūya vibhrājate ||JGc_1,1.45|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Love desires, its activities quarrel, the series of states like <s>stambha</s> (stupefaction) and others
wander among the <s>sakhīs</s> (female friends), and the heard narrative surpasses all that is heard;
thus, the entire [display] adorned with the clusters of arts of amorous play in the inner forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
of the divine couple, transcending the path of analysis, shines resplendent. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
akuṇṭhām utkaṇṭhāṃ vahati harir āsu pratipadaṃ
harāv apy etā yad vyatimilana-saukhyaṃ vijayate |
aho yasmād asmin nirupadhi sakhī-vṛndam ubhaya-
prakṛṣṭotkaṇṭhitvaṃ viśati tad idaṃ hanta kim iva ||JGc_1,1.46|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
<s>Hari</s> bears unblunted longing toward them at every step,
and in these [<s>gopīs</s>] too, the bliss of meeting with <s>Hari</s> prevails.
Ah! Since in this, the group of <s>sakhīs</s>, without any motive, enters
into the state of intense longing of both — what then is this wonder? // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text:
api sundaratāṃ prati tāḥ, sundaratāṃ kila vahanti gopālyaḥ |
yan nirdūṣaṇa-bhūṣaṇa-, bhūṣaṇa-kṛṣṇe vibhūṣaṇāyante ||JGc_1,1.47|| [udgītiḥ]
children.translated_text:
And regarding their beauty — the cowherd women indeed bear such beauty
that they serve as ornaments to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is himself the ornament beyond reproach. // [<s>udgīti</s>]

children.text:
na bhajati lakṣmīs tulanām, iti kiṃ stutaye ghaṭeta rādhāyāḥ |
yā lakṣmīm api jetrīḥ, sva-rucā gopīḥ pṛthak kurute ||JGc_1,1.48|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
