<s>Lakṣmī</s> does not bear comparison — so what praise could be fashioned for <s>Rādhā</s>?
She who, by her own radiance, distinguishes the <s>gopīs</s> even from those who surpass <s>Lakṣmī</s>. // [<s>āryā</s>]

children.text: tasmād asāmpratāya tu sāmpratāya mad-vidhāya svaṃ varṇayituṃ kim uta nirvarṇayitum-
children.translated_text: Therefore, for one such as myself — untimely yet timely — to describe, or rather to fully describe:

children.text:
ravy-ādi-dyuti-jiṣṇu-divya-dharaṇi-kṣauṇī-ruhāntargata-
prāsāda-sthita-siṃha-pīṭha-mahasi cchannānya-dṛṣṭi-tviṣi |
spaṣṭātmīya-dṛśi prakīrṇaka-vikīrṇālī-hitālī-vṛtā
rādhā-mādhava-mādhurī-vara-sudhā tṛṣṇāṃ mudhā yacchati ||JGc_1,1.49|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
In the splendor of a lion-throne situated within a palace hidden among divine trees on the divine earth,
a splendor that conquers the radiance of the sun and others, concealed from the sight of all others,
clearly visible only to her own gaze, surrounded by rows of buzzing bees scattered about —
the supreme nectar of the sweetness of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa) gives thirst in vain. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: tad evam ānanda-satra-patrādi-sthitānām upari sāndra-śākhābhir alakṣya-talānām analpa-kalpa-vṛkṣa-lakṣāṇām adhimadhyaṃ rāja-samāja-virājamānāṃ varṇita-mañju-kiñjalka-karṇikām adhivasantaḥ sadā lasataḥ sa-parivāra-vāra-surabhī-pāla-bhūpāla-kumārasya tasya sarva-cintātīta-cintāmaṇi-mayam akṣāmaṃ sapta-kakṣyārāmaṃ dhāma nikāmaṃ dhāma vistārayan netrāṇi vistārayati | tatra ca bhāsamānaṃ tad āvāsam abhitaḥ satatam upaparārdhe gaṇanīyānāṃ sajātīyānām advitīyā vasatiḥ | seyam abhisnihya vandibhiḥ sandihyate |
children.translated_text: Thus, amidst those countless wish-fulfilling trees whose dense branches conceal the ground below, standing like leaves and canopies of a feast of bliss, in the center of a royal assembly, upon the described beautiful pericarp with charming filaments — there, forever radiant, expanding the abode of that supreme prince, the protector of cows, the wish-fulfilling jewel surpassing all thought, the expansive seven-gated abode, that realm — he widens the eyes. And there, on all sides of that shining dwelling, constantly in numbers to be counted in the hundreds of trillions, stands the unrivaled habitation of his equals. This is spoken of with wonder by bards:

children.text:
abjaṃ tad āliṅgitum abja-bandhor
bandhur yayau kiṃ pariveṣa eṣaḥ |
gopālayānāṃ valayāvalir vā
gopeśa-veśmābhita evam asti ||JGc_1,1.50|| iti | [indravajrā]
children.translated_text:
Has the sun gone to embrace that lotus?
Is this its halo?
Or is it a circle of bracelets of the abodes of cowherds?
Such is the sight around the dwelling of the chief of cowherds. // [<s>indravajrā</s>]

children.text:
tad-vāsinas tv evaṃ stūyante-
arthāḥ sarva-janārthanām atigatāḥ kāmā nikāmāgrimā
dharmāḥ karmaṭha-deva-dharma-mahitā mokṣāś ca mokṣātigāḥ |
teṣāṃ tatra vasanti sevakatayā kṛṣṇāya tṛṣṇā-juṣāṃ
yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tat-kṛte ||JGc_1,1.51|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text:
And its residents are praised thus —
Wealth surpassing the purposes of all people, desires that are the foremost of all desires,
<s>dharmas</s> honored beyond the <s>dharma</s> of diligent gods, and liberations surpassing liberation itself —
all these dwell there in servitude for the sake of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, among those who are filled with longing for him,
for whom their abode, wealth, friends, beloveds, their own selves, children, and very life-breaths exist for his sake. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
netraṃ śrotraṃ cittam apy anyad anyat
tucchaṃ yasmin bhāti kṛṣṇaṃ vinā tu |
ghoṣe tasmiṃś cakṣuṣaś cakṣur evaṃ
śrautī vārtā paśya dṛśyā vibhāti ||JGc_1,1.52|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
The eye, the ear, the mind — each and every [sense]
appears empty without <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
in that cow-settlement, the very eye of the eye —
thus the heard report appears as something visible. // [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text:
vibhrājante sūtra-sañcāra-vidyā
pāñcālyaḥ kiṃ viśva-vismāyanāya |
kiṃ vā gopāḥ svāntare kṛṣṇa-bhāvair
baddhāḥ santas tatra tatra bhramanti ||JGc_1,1.53|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Do the puppets of the art of string-manipulation shine forth
for the amazement of the world?
Or are the cowherds, bound within by feelings for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
wandering here and there? // [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
pitāyaṃ māteyaṃ pitṛ-sahaja-vargaḥ svayam asau
tathaivānye cānya-prathita-hita-sambandha-mahitāḥ |
vraje khyātir yaiṣā bakaripu-gaṇe bhāti khalu tāṃ
kvacit tulyaḥ premā pathikam anu śaśvad bhramayati ||JGc_1,1.54|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Moreover —
'This is [my] father, this is [my] mother, this is the group of paternal kinsmen, he himself is such,
and likewise others honored by their well-known, beneficial relationships' —
this is the fame that shines in the clan of the enemy of <s>Baka</s> (Kṛṣṇa) in <s>Vraja</s>;
the love, which is everywhere equal, constantly bewilders the traveler. // [<s>śikharīṇī</s>]

children.text: athānyad api kim api vibhāvya sambhāvyate | tad yadi satām anubhavam apy anubhavitā, tadā bhavyam eva khaly bhavyam, na cen navya-kāvyatā tu na vyabhicaritā | athavā, tathāpi yat kiñcid api teṣāṃ vāñchitaṃ syād eveti sarva añcitam eva manyāmahe |
children.translated_text: Now, something else too is conceived and esteemed. If even a good person experiences their experience, then it is truly auspicious; and if not, then at least the novelty of the poetry is not violated. Or rather, even so, whatever they may desire — all of it we consider to be honored.

children.text:
tat tu sambhāvanaṃ, yathā-atha gopāvāsābhyantare tādṛśām eva sabhyānāṃ labhyā sabhāvalir upalabhyate,
yatra bhūri-vaicitrī-dhurāṇi mahā-gopurāṇi purāṇīva virājante,
yeṣāṃ panthānaḥ kila kiñjalka-valaja-paryantāḥ samastād vibhrājante,
yatra ca parasparam abhimukhāḥ sumukhā mahāntas te gṛhā mithaḥ pṛthula-śobhā loka-spṛhā iva vimṛśya dṛśyante,
yatra ca siṃha-saṃhananānāṃ puruṣa-siṃhānāṃ niścalāṅghrīṇi mahā-siṃhāsanāni vicitratayā netrāṇāṃ paribṛṃhaṇatām aṃhante,
yatra ca parāvara-kakṣyā-vāsi-loka-lakṣāṇi samam eva samakṣāṇi santi, mithaḥ sukha-śatāni varṣanti,
yatra caikatrāsīnānām anyatrāpi rūpaka-kāvya iva pratirūpāṇi rūpāṇi pratīyante-na ca tāni kevalāni, api tu pratidhvanayaś ca dhvani-kāvya iva dhvanitayā vibhāvyante, yataḥ svacchāntaḥ-karaṇā mahāntaḥ khalu para-guṇāntarāṇy api āyacchantīti prathitiḥ prathīyasī; yadā ca tathā prathīyante vibhāvyante ca, tadā hy āgantukā nānā-janās tat-tad-rūpāṇāṃ jānānāḥ paritaḥ parihāsyante;
yatra ca kutrāpi yadā sadā paramānanda-syanda-sandoha-dohana-kānti-kandalī-lambhita-sukha-tandraḥ śrīman-nanda-kula-candraḥ svayam āloka-sudhayā loka-cakṣuś-cakora-vārapārāṇām āpūrayati, tadā tūtsavānām api mahān utsavaḥ sphurati |
children.translated_text:
And that conception is as follows — Now, within the cowherd settlement, assemblies of such refined persons are found,
where great gateways bearing the mark of abundant variety shine like ancient edifices,
whose pathways gleam on all sides, bordered by pollen-laden enclosures,
where those great houses, facing one another, fair-faced, appear upon consideration to embody the mutual desire of the world with their broad beauty,
where magnificent lion-thrones of unshakable foundation, belonging to those lion-among-men of leonine build, delight the eyes with their varied splendor,
where the multitudes dwelling in the inner and outer precincts are all equally visible to one another, showering hundreds of happinesses upon each other,
where the forms of those seated in one place appear as mirror-images even elsewhere, like a visual drama — and these are not mere forms, but their echoes too are perceived with resonance, like the suggestive style (<s>dhvani</s>) of poetry, for the well-known truth is that those of pure inner disposition draw forth even the hidden virtues of others; and when they are thus perceived and envisioned, then the various visitors, recognizing those forms in every direction, are put to shame;
and wherever, at whatever time, that moon of the glorious <s>Nanda</s> family, drowsy with the happiness obtained from the ever-flowing flood of supreme bliss and its cascading beauty, himself fills with the nectar of his sight the <s>cakora</s>-birds that are the eyes of the world to overflowing — then even among festivals, a great festival blazes forth.

children.text: atha sabhā-valayam antarā ca kakṣyā-pañcakatayā labdha-bodhaḥ sarva-cittāvarodhaḥ sa tu vraja-nṛpāvarodhaḥ samudbhrājate | tatra tam eva hi saha-mātara-pitarādi-vṛndaḥ śrī-govindaḥ svayam āvasati | yatra sabhā-valayāntar-antaḥ paritaḥ parītaś catasro' py antaḥ pṛthag-avarodha-lakṣāḥ kakṣyā lakṣyante | anyā ca pañcamī dhanyā sarva-madhya-labdha-nyāsatayā yatra citrīyate, yasyāṃ tu mahā-prāṅgaṇa-saṅginyāṃ pratīcīm anu svāntara-aṅgam aṅgaṇam aṅgaṇaṃ parito nikāyānāṃ nikāyaḥ sarvato' pi śreyasyā śrīmad-vraja-nara-deva-preyasyā samāśriyate | udīcīm anu sukha-mayūkha-rohiṇyā rohiṇyā | prācīm anu samasta-kṛta-sevena śrīmad-vraja-naradevena | avācīm anu svajana-sabhājana-bhojanāpavarjana-prayojana-sāmagryā |
children.translated_text: And within the circle of the assembly hall, the inner quarters (<s>avarodha</s>) of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, which captivates all minds, shines forth, made known by the five-fold enclosures (<s>kakṣyā</s>). There, <s>Śrī Govinda</s> himself resides, together with the host of his mother, father, and others. Within the innermost part of the assembly circle, on all sides, four separate inner enclosures numbering one <s>lakṣa</s> each are visible. And a fifth, the blessed one, is depicted as having obtained its place in the very center of all, in which, along the great courtyard, to the west, the body of bodies of assemblies is served on all sides — of the most auspicious, glorious beloved of the king of <s>Vraja</s>. To the north, by <s>Rohiṇī</s>, whose rays are of happiness. To the east, by the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, served by all. To the south, with the provisions for the purposes of honoring, feeding, and dismissing one's own people.

children.text: atha tad-bahir bahir antaḥ-pura-prayuta-vibhāga-pracurāṇāṃ parama-santuṣṭa-jana-puṣṭānāṃ catuṣṭayīnāṃ ca kakṣyāṇāṃ paścān niścita-paścimādi-kakubhaṃ śubhāṃ rītim avalambya sakala-śarma-dṛśvarī śrīmad-vrajeśvarī rāma-ghaṭṭābhirāmaḥ śrīmad-balarāmaḥ sarva-loka-gatiḥ śrīmad-vrajādhipatiḥ sa ca govardhanānandanaḥ śrīmad-vrajādhipati-nandanaḥ patir atīva rājate |
children.translated_text: Then, beyond those four enclosures, outside, abundant with the divisions employed in the inner quarters, filled with supremely contented people, following the auspicious course established in the western and other directions, there shines forth: the sovereign mistress of all happiness, the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s>; the glorious <s>Balarāma</s>, delightful at <s>Rāma-ghaṭṭa</s>; the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, the refuge of all people; and that son of <s>Govardhana's</s> delight, the glorious son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — the master reigns supreme.

children.text: tatra cāharahar aviraha-rahaḥ-keli-kalita-tṛṣṇayo rāma-kṛṣṇayor vikhyāta-tat-tan-nāmasu madhyama-kakṣyā-dvaya-dhāmasu parama-ramā-gaṇa-śreyasīnāṃ preyasīnām āvāsa-prāsādāvalir udbhāsate; [73] yatra cāveśanam anu sāveśaṃ nānā-kalā-kalāpaṃ kalayantīnām ālīnāṃ nija-nija-yūtha-varūthapāyāḥ paramāpūrva-pūrva-pūrvānurāgādi-kathānikāyāṃ gāyantīnāṃ madhu-madhura-kākalī-kulāni tatrakīyaṃ sarvaṃ tarv-antam ārdrīkurvanti, kim uta bahu-kaṣṭa-sṛṣṭatayā mithunī-bhūtaṃ tat tan mithunam |
children.translated_text: And there, day after day, for <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose thirst is mingled with the secret sports of uninterrupted union, rows of palace-residences of the beloveds — the most excellent among the hosts of supreme <s>Lakṣmīs</s> — shine forth in those well-known abodes of the middle two enclosures bearing their respective names. [73] Where, upon entering with passion, the sweet cuckoo-like voices of the <s>sakhīs</s> (companions), who display various arts and accomplishments, singing to their respective group-leaders about the narrative of supremely unprecedented earlier loves and the like — those voices moisten everything there down to the trees' ends — how much more then the couples who have become united, being created through much longing!

children.text: tayor dvayor āvaraṇatayā lakṣye ye cānyatare pratyantara-kakṣyam eka-bhūma-dvi-bhūmatādi-prakāreṇādhika-bhūmikā-racanābhir uccatara-rītikāyāḥ samāna-māna-gṛha-sva-sva-vīthikāyā dhāriṇī goloka-dharaṇī-loka-hāriṇī bhavati | tatra sarvās tu gṛha-lekhā-maṇi-bhitti-sambadhya-madhya-rekhā-labdha-dvaividhyā samantād ubhayataḥ-sthita-dvāratayā paraspara-sammukhatā-śobhānandita-dig-antāḥ kaimutyam āsādayanti |
children.translated_text: Those which are perceptible as covering both of them, in the other inner enclosure, with constructions of additional stories in the manner of one-storied, two-storied, and so forth, of an elevated design, bearing the street of equal-honor houses — the earth of <s>Goloka</s>, the bearer, the enchantress of the world. There, all the house-lines, having obtained duality through the central line joined to gem-walls, on all sides, with doors standing on both sides, delighted by the beauty of mutual facing in all directions, arrive at the argument <s>a fortiori</s>.

children.text: yatra ca sarva-madhyamāvarodhasyādhimadhyaṃ bṛhat-prāṅgaṇam adhikṛtyākhaṇḍa-puṭa-bhedana-mukuṭa-bhaṅgī-laṅginaṃ niśreṇi-śreṇi-miśrāntaḥ-śvabhra-śubhra-laghu-laghu-dvāra-sukhāroha-sañcāra-merv-ākāra-cārv-aṅga-kuṭṭimād upari paritaḥ stambha-vāra-saṅgatam agāram ekaṃ sarvataś calat-patākam avalokyate | [77] yadā ca tasya sarva-kakudam udañcitasya dhiṣṇyasya purūpari cālaṅkariṣṇutayā śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ vartiṣṇur bhavati, tadā sarva-jiṣṇu-tad-uparicariṣṇu-jiṣṇu-nīla-maṇir iva kaṃ vā tal-loka-bhaviṣṇu-lokaṃ kānti-kandalībhir na puṣṇāti?
children.translated_text: Where, in the supreme center of the middle inner quarters, dominating the great courtyard, above the beautiful-limbed <s>Meru</s>-shaped pavement with easy ascent, having rows of stairs mixed with bright, light, light openings and shafts, surmounting the unbroken dome-cap-crown-style tier, a single chamber surrounded by rows of pillars is seen on all sides, with banners waving everywhere. [77] And when <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, in his adorning nature, abides upon the very top of that elevated throne rising above all directions — then, like a blue sapphire all-conquering and roaming above, what world of beings that will exist does he not nourish with his bursts of radiance?

children.text:
yā ceyaṃ karṇikāyām upari purī, tad-adhastād anyāpi samantād asti, kintu sā prati-kṛṣṇa-kāntā-dhāmany eva nijāṅgana-nibha-patra-paṅkti-sīmany eva cāyantrita-dvāra-gaṇeti pareṣām ajñātā, dyumaṇivan-maṇi-gaṇa-samujjvalālaya-kalāpā, vātānīta-sujāta-parimala-sampātā, nirjanatā-janita-svairatānārata-rati-pradā, śayyāsana-cchatra-cāmarādi-sāmagrīti-bahula-śatī-prītidā-nānā-krīḍā-bhāṇḍa-maṇḍala-maṇḍitākhaṇḍa-maṇḍapā, tat-tac-ceṣṭādhiṣṭhāna-nara-mṛga-pakṣi-pratikṛti-lakṣa-vilakṣitā preyasīṣu vibhakta-pradeśa-viśeṣā śeṣālayāyate | yatratyena pathā yathāvat preyasī-nāmānandanaḥ śrīmān nanda-nandanas tatra patra-samudyad-udyāna-vṛndam amūbhir anuvindann atīva nandati | tasmād udyānād antar-dvāreṇa caturasraṃ
pratyudyānam api vindati |
children.translated_text: And this city that is above, on the pericarp — beneath it there is also another on all sides; but it is unknown to others, because the rows of doors are controlled in the domain of each of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> beloveds, within the boundary of leaf-rows resembling their own courtyards. It is an array of dwellings brilliant with sun-like gem-clusters, receiving the fragrant breezes brought by the wind, giving pleasure through the uninterrupted freedom of solitude's amorous sport, with undivided pavilions adorned with circles of various playthings — hundreds of provisions including beds, seats, parasols, fly-whisks, and the like — marked with a <s>lakṣa</s> of likenesses of men, animals, and birds who are the presiding figures of each activity, with special places distributed among the beloveds — it becomes the abode of all the rest. Through the path there, the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s>, the delight of the beloveds, finding there the garden-groves rising with leaves, delights exceedingly with them. From that garden, through an inner door, he also finds a square counter-garden.

children.text: evaṃ śrī-balarāmasya rāma-ghaṭṭākhya-nija-krīḍā-vana-gamanaṃ ca tala-vartmanaiva vartate, kintu saṃkṣiptatayā nihitena patrāvali-paryantāla-vāla-pihitena mantavyam |
children.translated_text: Thus the going of <s>Śrī Balarāma</s> to his own pleasure-grove called <s>Rāma-ghaṭṭa</s> proceeds along the lower path; but it should be understood as concealed by the bordering leaf-rows placed in abbreviated form.

children.text: tām etām uparigatāṃ śrīmad-vrajeśvara-purīṃ pari tu ślokāḥ parigīyante-
children.translated_text: About this upper city of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, these verses are sung:

children.text:
yastāṃ patākā mṛdu-vāta-kampitā
nānāmukhībhāvam itāḥ punaḥ punaḥ |
saurabhyam āyāti yadā yatas tadā
vivṛtya paśyanti diśām amūm iva ||JGc_1,1.55|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: Those banners, swayed by the gentle breeze, assuming the appearance of many faces again and again — when fragrance comes, and from wherever it comes, then opening up, they seem to gaze upon the directions!

children.text:
nityaṃ sudhā-dhāmaja-dhāma-saṅgataḥ
pūrṇāṅgatām aṅgala-saṅgatiṃ gatāḥ |
yatrāpi kumbhā vidhu-kānta-sambhavāḥ
kūṭāntaratva-mukuṭā iva sthitāḥ ||JGc_1,1.56|| [indravaṃśā]
children.translated_text: Always joined with the abode born of the moon's dwelling, having attained full-bodiedness in auspicious conjunction — where even the water-pots, made of moonstone, stand like crowns within the pinnacles!

children.text:
yatrānvitā kumbhā vidhukānta-sambhavāḥ
kūṭāntaratna-mukuṭā iva sthitāḥ |
yatrānvitā svacchatayā vibhātayā
hīrādi-ratna-cchadir ālir īkṣyate ||JGc_1,1.57|| [indravaṃśā]
children.translated_text: Where the water-pots made of moonstone are joined, standing like crowns of pinnacle-gems — where, endowed with transparency and splendor, a row of canopies of diamond and other jewels is seen!

children.text:
mayūra-pārāvata-kokilādyā
vasatni yasyāṃ tu vināpi yatnam |
śabdāyamānā vipinasya tair ye
vivāda-saṃvādavad ācaranti ||JGc_1,1.58|| [upajāti 11]
vicitra-ratnāvali-citra-carcitā
sauvarṇa-bhittiḥ paritaś cakāsatī |
gopāla-bālyādii-vilāsa-mādhurīḥ
sākṣād ivālakṣayate śiśūn api ||JGc_1,1.59|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: Peacocks, doves, cuckoos, and others dwell in it without any effort; the sounds they make are like those of the forest itself, as if conducting a dispute and response! The golden walls, beautifully painted with variegated jewel-garlands, shining all around, seem to directly display the sweetness of <s>Hari's</s> childhood pastimes and even the infants themselves!

children.text:
vistāritotsaṅga-nibhair alindaiḥ
śliṣyanti kṛṣṇaṃ bhavanāni nityam |
yeṣāṃ sadāntar nivasanti te tad-
bhaktā amī tādṛśatāṃ vrajanti ||JGc_1,1.60|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: With balconies resembling outstretched laps, the houses constantly embrace <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; those who always dwell within them — his devotees — attain that very nature!

children.text:
prāṅgaṇāni maṇi-darpaṇa-cchavīny
ullasanti sadanāvalīm anu |
yeṣu nūtana-vadhūr bakāntakaṃ
vrīḍa-namra-vadanāpi vīkṣate ||JGc_1,1.61|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: Courtyards with the luster of gem-mirrors sparkle along the row of houses, in which even the new bride, with face bowed in modesty, beholds the slayer of <s>Baka</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!

children.text:
candrakānta-maṇi-baddha-bhūtale
palvalāni ca lasanti sarvataḥ |
rādhikādi-mukha-kānti kandalī
yāni pūrayanti hanta sarvadā ||JGc_1,1.62|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: And pools set in floors of moonstone glitter everywhere — which the radiance of the faces of <s>Rādhikā</s> and others, alas, always fills to the brim!

children.text:
lokaḥ śrīnātha-loka-pratiruci-vijayī kānanaṃ śrī-spṛhājid-
vāsaḥ śrī-rājadhānī-nikhila-śubha-rucāṃ vāsinas te ta eva |
bhoktā kṛṣṇaḥ sa bhogyaḥ praṇaya-madhurimā śaśvad ity evam asmin
pratyekaṃ sarvam antaḥkaraṇam atigataṃ kas tad-antaṃ labheta ||JGc_1,1.63|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: The world is victorious over the splendor of the world of <s>Śrīnātha</s> (Viṣṇu's heaven); the forest conquers the longing for <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī); the dwelling surpasses all auspicious beauties of the royal capital; and those residents are those very ones. The enjoyer is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; the object of enjoyment is the sweetness of love, always — thus in this [realm], each and everything has transcended the inner faculty of understanding; who could reach its end?

children.text: tat-prema-śarmaṇāṃ sarvātiśayi-dharmatāyām aham api marma-vettā, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: In the nature of the supreme excellence of all those joys of love, even I am a knower of their essence, for:

children.text:
harir gopa-kṣauṇī-pati-mithunam anye ca vibudhā
na naḥ krūraṃ cittaṃ mṛdulayitum īśā lavam api |
aho teṣāṃ premā vilasati harau yas tu balavān
harer vā yas teṣu drutayati sa eva pratipadam ||JGc_1,1.64|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, the couple who are king and queen of the cowherds, and the other wise ones — they are unable to soften our hard heart even a bit. Ah! That love of theirs which sports in <s>Hari</s>, which is so mighty, or that of <s>Hari</s> toward them — that alone melts at every step!

children.text: ataḥ sarvataḥ kṣemāṇāṃ sa eva premā sarvatra sphurati | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Therefore, from all sides of auspiciousness, that very love shines everywhere. Thus:

children.text:
hariḥ premā sākṣād iva bhavati kiṃ vā vraja-janas
tayor ekasmiṃś ca sphurati sa hi śaśvat sphurati naḥ |
idaṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ vidhi-śiva-surarṣi-prabhṛtayaḥ
sphuṭaṃ kartuṃ śaktiṃ dadhati natarāṃ yat kiyad api ||JGc_1,1.65|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> seems to be love incarnate; or is it the people of <s>Vraja</s>? In either one of them, that [love] indeed always shines for us. <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the gods, and sages and others, time and again, possess only so much power to make this manifest — not at all!

children.text: sa tu paramāścarya-caryaḥ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And that [love] is of supremely wondrous conduct, for:

children.text:
tadīyānāṃ premā yad api kṛti-caryātiga-sukhaas
tathāpy uccair hetur bhavati hari-sāhāyaka-vidhau |
jagat-kārye yadvac chruti-mata-para-brahma nitarām
acintyo yo bhāvaḥ sa hi na hi vitarkaṃ viṣahate ||JGc_1,1.66|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: Although the love of those [<s>Vraja</s>-folk] is a happiness that transcends the conduct of the meritorious, nevertheless it becomes an exalted cause in the arrangement of <s>Hari's</s> help. Just as in the cosmic purpose, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, according to the view of the <s>Śruti</s>, is utterly inconceivable — that very nature indeed does not admit of speculation.

children.text: yasmād evaṃ sa eva cittam ākarṣati, tasmāt-
children.translated_text: Since that [love] alone captivates the mind, therefore:

children.text:
jñātvā karma svayam uta parāt kṛṣṇa-tṛṣṇānukūlaṃ
tasminn antar bahir api sadā gopa-rājāvarodhe |
yātāyātaṃ muhur atitarāṃ kurvatām ādṛtānām
apy utkaṇṭhācalita-manasāṃ mānasaṃ bhāvam īhe ||JGc_1,1.67|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: Knowing their duty, either by themselves or from another, favorable to the thirst for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, within and without that inner court of the cowherd-king, always making their comings and goings most frequent, of those who are honored yet whose minds are agitated with longing — I contemplate the inner disposition of their minds!

children.text: tatratyānāṃ samūhāvalokanaṃ tu parama-paramādbhutam, tathā hi-
children.translated_text: And the sight of the assemblages of those who dwell there is supremely, supremely wondrous; thus:

children.text:
udghūrṇante priya-parijanāḥ snigdha-bhāvā yathā-svaṃ
gopa-kṣauṇī-patim anugatās tasya cātma-dvitīyām |
yau premākhya-prabala-raśanā-yantranāt kṛṣṇa-kānti-
jyotiś-cakre ravi-śaśi-tanū ye ca nakṣatra-saṅghāḥ ||JGc_1,1.68|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: The beloved attendants, of affectionate nature, each in their own way, whirl about following the king of the cowherd-land and his other self (consort) — like the sun and moon bodies, and the hosts of stars, in the luminous wheel of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> beauty, [bound] by the powerful cord-mechanism called love!

children.text: gānaṃ tu pratigaṇaṃ sādhāraṇam api kañcid viśeṣaṃ vahati, yathā-
children.translated_text: And the singing, though common to each group, carries a certain distinction; thus:

children.text:
janmādy-arbhakatā hareḥ pravayasāṃ madhye-sabhaṃ prāyaśaḥ
paugaṇḍādiṣu nirjarāri-vijiteḥ prāyaḥ suhṛn-maṇḍale |
kāliyāidiṣu durjaneṣv api kṛpā-bhakta-vraje' nalpaśaḥ
prāyenātmani rāga-rītir abhitaḥ kāntā-gaṇe gīyate ||JGc_1,1.69|| [śārdūlā]
children.translated_text: The birth and infancy of <s>Hari</s>, mostly in the full assembly of the elders; the <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (boyhood) and other [periods] of the conqueror of the enemies of the gods, mostly in the circle of friends; compassion even toward the wicked such as <s>Kāliya</s> and others, in the devotee-<s>Vraja</s> abundantly; the style of passionate attachment, mostly about himself, is sung among the host of beloveds, on all sides!

children.text: tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And there:

children.text:
saṅgāne ced bhajati murajid-bhakta-mātraṃ vimohaṃ
śarmāśarmāpy anumiti-miyān tarhi na prekṣakāṇām |
śāntir dāsyaṃ sahacara-daśā vatsalatvaṃ tathānyad
gacched eṣāṃ hṛdi katham iha kṣīra-vār-vad vivekam ||JGc_1,1.70|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: If in their singing, the devotees of the drum-player (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) attain mere bewilderment, then the happiness and sorrow of the spectators, measured by inference, are beyond comprehension. How could peace, servitude, companionship, parental love, and other [sentiments] of these [Vraja-folk] attain discrimination in the heart, like milk and water?

children.text: hanta! padya-dvayam idam ālole manasi udbhūya tad evāndolayati | yathā-
children.translated_text: Ah! These two verses, having arisen in my swaying mind, rock it further; thus:

children.text:
mātar mātar janani mama tad dehi dehīti śabdair
vatsāyuṣman suta vadasi kiṃ prāṇa-lālyeti cārdraiḥ |
nānālāpa-praṇaya-valitā māṃ balāt sneha-mudrā
tasmin goṣṭhe smarayatitarāṃ tau savitrī-kumārau ||JGc_1,1.71|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'O Mother, Mother, my mother, give that, give that!' — with such words; 'O child, long-lived one, son, what do you say? O darling of my life!' — and with such tender [words]; variegated with the affectionate speech of many conversations, the seal of love forcefully — in that cowpen, those two, mother and son, make me remember intensely!

children.text:
geheśi tvaṃ carita-sukṛtā hanta vatsas tvad-agre
vakti psāti prathayati ruciṃ yācate jāhasīti |
ardhād evaṃ sthagita-vacanaṃ sneha-pūrād vrajeśaṃ
dhyāyed vṛttiṃ bata na labhate man-mano bambhramīti ||JGc_1,1.72|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'You are the lord of the house, O one of meritorious conduct! Ah, the child before you speaks, crawls, shows delight, begs, laughs!' — Thus, with speech half-stopped by the flood of affection, about the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — one would contemplate, but alas, does not attain the state of mind — 'my mind wanders!'

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
śrī-goloka-rūpa-nirūpaṇaṃ nāma
prathamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopālacampū</s>, this is the description of the form of <s>Śrī Goloka</s>, called
the First Chapter.

children.text: atha dvitīyaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Second Chapter.

children.text: śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ namaḥ |||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!

children.text: atha kathā-prathanāya grathanam idam ārabhyate | [2] svabhajana-lasan-mānasa-san-mānada-janmādi-līlā-bhavyāya bhuvy āvirbhāvitasya tasya nija-vraja-loka-cakrasya dantavakraṃ hatavatā śrī-bhagavatā tatra vigata-sarva-śoke goloke punar api saṃśleṣaḥ sādhita iti campū-dvayasya pratisampūrti-vakṣyamāṇa-sapramāṇa-kathā-lakṣyatayā viviktam eva vyaktīkariṣyate |
children.translated_text: Now the composition for the narration of the story begins. [2] It will be clearly manifested — as the stated purport of the narrative with proofs, to be described in the completion of the two <s>campūs</s> — that by the glorious Lord who manifested on earth the circle of his own <s>Vraja</s>-folk, who bestow honor upon the devoted mind shining with its own worship, and whose birth-pastimes and other līlās are glorious — by that Lord who slew <s>Dantavakra</s> — reunion was accomplished with them once again in <s>Goloka</s>, free from all sorrow.

children.text:
siddhe tatra tu saṃśleṣe kutrāpi rātriviśeṣe śeṣe golokādvandva-mahendra-dvāri hāri dundubhi-dvandvam unnanāda | nāda-viśeṣa-miṣeṇānandam evedam ujjagāreti matvā, loko' py ujjajāgāra | na ca sa eva kevalaḥ, kintu kṛṣṇāvaloka-tṛṣṇayā saha, yathā kamala-samūhaḥ parimala-dhārayā | atha nija-nija-vṛndinaḥ sūta-māgadha-vandinaḥ śrīman-nanda-rāja-pura-virājamāna-bṛṃhita-siṃha-dvāri sarvordhvaṃ vindamānāṃ candra-śālikām adhiruhya, nūtanāni pūtanādi-dantavakrānta-durbuddhi-śakrāri-cakra-vadha-sambaddhāni virudādi-cchandāṃsi svacchandatayā naṭanta ivāparyantaṃ paṭhantaḥ samantād eva jana-sandoham ānanda-dohaṃ lambhayāmāsuḥ | sānurāga-rāgāvali-vibhāga-laṅgima-saṅgīta-saṅgi-tal-līlā-kathākulam apy ākalayāmāsuḥ
|
children.translated_text: When this union was accomplished, at a certain late hour of the night, at the gate of <s>Goloka's</s> supreme <s>Indra</s>-pair, a pair of charming kettledrums resounded. Thinking, 'This has poured forth joy itself under the pretext of this special sound,' the people too awoke — and not merely that, but along with a thirst for the sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, just as a cluster of lotuses [opens] with a stream of fragrance. Then the bards, eulogists, and panegyrists of their respective groups, ascending the moon-pavilion that towered above everything at the lion-gate adorned and magnified at the palace of the glorious King <s>Nanda</s>, reciting without end in complete freedom — as if dancing — new compositions in the <s>viruda</s> and other meters, related to the killing of <s>Pūtanā</s> and other [demons] up to <s>Dantavakra</s>, the wicked ally of <s>Śakra's</s> enemy — they caused the crowd of people everywhere to receive a milking of bliss. They also performed the narrative of those very pastimes, interwoven with melodious music distinguished by sequences of affectionate <s>rāgas</s> (musical modes).

children.text: tadā muhur api harer avadāna-gānato labdha-toṣa-poṣā ghoṣādhipati-dampati-mukhāḥ parama-sukhād atiśasta-vastrālaṅkāra-bhāraṃ tebhyaḥ svayam īhayā vihāpayāmāsuḥ | kintu śravaṇe' pi tṛptir na kptim avāpa, kathaṃ vā tatrāvaśyam eva vaśanīyā sātiḥ sātim āsīdatu? tad anu ca samudbhūta-prema-rasa-rāśir vraja-vāri-rāśiḥ svayam eva nija-nija-hṛdayaṅgama-vraja-maṅgala-śyāmalāṅga-saṅgāna-taraṅga-saṅgha-saṅgitayā viśva-vismaya-kāritāṃ saṅgatavān | tatra ca, gīyamānatayā sannidhīyamānasya tadīya-yaśasaś candramasaḥ samatām anumimīmahe |
children.translated_text: Then, the chieftain and his wife, led by them, and the other leaders of the cowherd settlement, whose nourishment was the satisfaction gained from the repeated singing of <s>Hari's</s> exploits, out of supreme happiness, of their own accord distributed to them a weighty load of praised garments and ornaments. But even in hearing, satisfaction did not reach completion — how indeed could that satiety, which must certainly be mastered there, subside to contentment? And thereafter, the ocean of the cowherd community, in which had arisen masses of the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic essence) of <s>prema</s> (divine love), itself attained a wonder that astonished the universe, through the assemblage of waves of songs about the dark-limbed one — the auspicious one of <s>Vraja</s>, dear to every heart. And there, we infer the equality of his fame, which becomes present as it is being sung, with the moon.

children.text: yadā tu śrīla-gopāla-līlā-gāna-grahilā mahilā gātum ārabdhās tadā sarva eva satṛṣṇās tūṣṇīm āsan, kṛṣṇa-muralī-kākalīm anu kokilā iva | yad eva gānaṃ vaidagdhī-digdha-kaṅkanādi-jhaṅkārālaṅkṛta-manthāna-nirghoṣaḥ svara-tālādi-dānam iva kurvāṇaḥ sva-poṣaṃ pupoṣa |
children.translated_text: But when the women, absorbed in singing the pastimes of the glorious <s>Gopāla</s>, began to sing, everyone became silent with longing — like cuckoos following the melody of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> flute. That very song, whose self-sustenance was nourished by the churning-sound adorned with the jingling of bangles and other [ornaments] anointed with artistry, as if making an offering of melody and rhythm and the like.

children.text:
tad evaṃ sati, sarvataḥ-sāreṇa sapramāṇa-varṇayitavyānusāreṇāpagatāpara-pati-bhramāḥ sarvā eva vraja-ramā māravāṇa-dalita-marmāṇas tad-eka-sevā-
dharmyeṣu nija-nija-harmyeṣu samam eva labdhāgamanaṃ tam ekam eva ramaṇaṃ ramaṇatāṃ gamayamānā na virāmam icchantīti sakhībhir eva prābhātikarāgamaya-gāna-narmaṇā tasmād uparamayāmāsire |
children.translated_text: This being so, all the ladies of <s>Vraja</s> — essentially valuable in every way, in accordance with the authoritative descriptions that are to be set forth with evidence, their delusion of [any] other husband having departed — with their vital points pierced by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (Desire), entertaining that one and only lover in their respective mansions devoted exclusively to his service, not wishing to stop, were made to cease from him by their <s>sakhīs</s> (female friends) alone, through the play of singing morning <s>rāgas</s>.

children.text: tac ca na sahasā, kintu kramaśaḥ | tathā hi,
children.translated_text: And that [cessation occurred] not suddenly, but gradually. As follows:

children.text:
bāhū viślathitau ślathīkṛtam uro vaktraṃ daracyāvitaṃ,
talpād utthitam ekadā vinimayenālambya yatnān muhuḥ |
yābhyāṃ sparśasukhāgraho' pi damitas tābhyāṃ haripreyasī
vyaktibhyāṃ bata soḍham atra sahasākraṣṭuṃ na dṛṣṭiṃ mithaḥ ||JGc_1,2.1|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitā]
[7] hanta, tāsu ca sarvādhikā yā tu rādhikā, sā khalu tad-ārambha-sambhavād eva prāyaḥ sarvadā mūrcchām ṛcchati | yatra ca,
children.translated_text:
The arms loosened, the chest relaxed, the face slightly turned away;
once risen from the bed, supporting each other in exchange, with repeated efforts —
those two, by whom even the seizing of the pleasure of touch was restrained — by those very two,
the beloved of <s>Hari</s>, alas, was suddenly endured to be dragged away from each other's gaze. ||2.1||
[7] Ah, among all of them, she who is the foremost is indeed <s>Rādhikā</s> — she, from the very onset of that [union], almost always falls into a swoon. And there,

children.text:
"pūrvānurāga-galitāṃ mama lambhane' pi
  lokāpavāda-dalitām atha mad-viyuktau |
  dāvānala-jvalita-jāti-vanī-sadṛkṣām
  etāṃ kathaṃ katham ahaṃ bata sāntvayāmi?" ||JGc_1,2.2|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
"Even when I obtain her, whose former deep love has melted [into mine],
whose [reputation] has been shattered by the censure of the world, and who in separation from me
resembles a grove of jasmine set ablaze by a forest fire —
how, O how, alas, can I console this one?" ||2.2||

children.text: iti sadā bhāvayantaṃ, samprati cātivyagrībhavantaṃ vraja-yuvarājaṃ prati samāśvāsanayā viśvāsanayā ca tāṃ vyavahitāṃ kurvāṇāḥ, prāṇa-tulyāḥ paramālyas tadīya-tāmbūlodgārādi-saṃvalanayā cetanām ālambayanti; samantād api sāntvitām atha pṛcchanti ca, "hanta, keyaṃ tava rītiḥ?" iti |
children.translated_text: Thus he, the young prince of <s>Vraja</s>, who always contemplates [thus] and who now becomes exceedingly anxious — making her concealed from him through consolation and reassurance, [her] friends, dear as life itself, of supreme garlands, restore her consciousness by fanning her with the exhaled fragrance of his <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel-leaf) and the like; and having consoled [her] all around, they also ask, 'Alas, what is this behavior of yours?'

children.text:
sā punaḥ sāsram āśrāvayati,
  "na mūrkha-dhīr asmi na vā durāgrahā
  śarīra-bhogeṣu na vātilālasā |
  kintu vrajādhīśa-sutasya te guṇā
  balād apasmāra-daśāṃ nayanti mām ||JGc_1,2.3|| [vaṃśasthavilā]
children.translated_text:
She again tearfully declares:
'I am not of foolish mind, nor of stubborn attachment,
nor am I excessively greedy for bodily pleasures;
but the virtues of the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>
forcibly bring me to a state of unconsciousness.' ||2.3||

children.text: "kiṃ kurmahe? yayā marma-pīḍayā kvacana ca śarma na labhāmahe vayam" iti |
children.translated_text: 'What shall we do? From this inner torment, we find no peace anywhere.'

children.text:
atha punar vyākulī-bhavantī sā śubhra-dantī rasāntareṇa tābhiḥ sāntvitī-kriyate | tad-dine tu tad idam ācacakṣe: "aśeṣa-maṅgala-saṅgatācaraṇānāṃ śrī-vrajeśa-gṛhiṇī-caraṇānām ādeśa-praveśa āsīt, æhanta, sarvā evārvācīna-vayasaḥ samāgatāḥ, mat-prāṇādhikā rādhikā katham adhunāpi nāgatā?' iti |" tad evam avadhāritavatī śrī-rādhāpi sāvadhānī-bhavantī, śīghram eva prātar aucitīṃ vidhāya, sarvābhir evopaśāya-viśāya-valitābhiḥ kalyam ākalya militābhir lalitā-viśākhādi-sakhibhiḥ sārdhaṃ śrī-vrajādhīśvaryā dhāma jagāma | gatvā ca, parama-kānta-sva-kānti-kandalībhir antima-gatābhīra-kāntāḥ samantād apy antar-bahir api devayāmāsa | [11] yatra tāsāṃ nirnimeṣatā ca jātā | sambhāvanāvatī bhāvanā ceyaṃ,
  "adhi-vidhu nīlāmbuja-yugam api tila-puṣpaṃ sabandhūkam |
  yasyāṃ kanaka-latāyāṃ seyaṃ kṛṣṇāṅganā citram ||JGc_1,2.4|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
Then, becoming agitated again, she of the bright teeth is consoled by them with a different <s>rasa</s> (sentiment). And on that day, she recounted this: 'There was a command-entry from the feet of the wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, whose conduct is attended by all auspiciousness: "Alas! All of the young women have arrived — how is it that my <s>Rādhikā</s>, dearer than my own life-breath, has still not come?"' Having thus resolved, <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> too, becoming attentive, quickly performed her morning duties, and together with all [her friends] — <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and other <s>sakhīs</s> (companions) — who had assembled in the early morning, attended and surrounded [by them], she went to the abode of the queen of <s>Vraja</s>. And having gone, with the splendor of her own most beloved beauty, she delighted the cowherd women who had reached the final [degree of charm], both inside and out, on all sides. [11] And there, their unblinking gaze was born. And this is the reverential contemplation:
'Upon [a vine] more beautiful than the moon, even a pair of blue lotuses [become like] sesame flowers along with <s>bandhūka</s> blossoms —
upon this golden vine, she is indeed the dark-complexioned woman — how wondrous!' ||2.4||

children.text: atha bhakti-tṛṣṇaṅ-manāḥ kṛṣṇa-jananīm anu mānanīyatayā nijam ānanam avanīm avanīya nanāma | sā ca tāṃ saha-sabhyānandam abhyanandat | tatra ca,
children.translated_text: Then, with a mind thirsting for devotion, she bowed her face to the ground after [bowing before] <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother, who was to be honored. And she [<s>Yaśodā</s>] greeted her together with [her] companions' joy. And there:

children.text:
asau caraṇayor natā śirasi hastam ādhatta sāpy
  asau bhuvi tathā sthitā kacam ajighrad utthāpya sā |
  asau kucita-vigrahā bhuja-tale nidhāyātha sā
  sa-bāṣpakam udaikṣata dvayam aho dvayoh kiṃ bruve? ||JGc_1,2.5|| [pṛthvī]

tad evam api rohiṇī-prabhṛtīnām ādarāya bhṛta-nibhṛta-saṅkocām ālocayantī rājñī tām anujajñe, "putri, vandasva vandana-yogyāḥ" iti | sā ca ramya-guṇā puru-nipuṇā bhakti-pūrataḥ sarvā eva gurūr avanamya dūra-deśa eva niveśaṃ vinata-vaktram āsasāda |
children.translated_text: Even so, the queen, perceiving her restrained modesty maintained for the sake of respect toward <s>Rohiṇī</s> and the others, gave her leave: 'Daughter, pay homage to those worthy of homage.' And she, of charming qualities and great skill, having bowed to all the elders with fullness of devotion, took her seat at a distance, with face bowed.

children.text: atha lalitādis tad-āli-pālir api tāsu guru-vanitāsu tadvad eva kṛta-varivasyā tasyā eva sadeśam upaviveśa | [15] tataś ca śrī-rāma-prasūḥ spaṣṭam ācaṣṭa, "vrajeśvari, sarva-sukha-rohiṇī rohiṇī-tārādya vidyate | tad ādiśyatām: iyaṃ sad-bhāva-dhūta-sarva-diśya-vadhū-naipuṇyā, pākādi-sādguṇyāya pūrvam eva somābhānulomatayā yā rasavatīṃ pratītāḥ samam anyā dhanyā maṅgalādyā maṅgalārāma-rāmānuja-rāmās, tathā yāḥ parāpara-nāmānaḥ kalyāṇārāma-rāma-rāmāḥ samantād apy amūr amūm evānuvartantām | lalitādyāḥ punar asyāḥ kāya-nikāya-rūpā eveti, na sāhāyakāyāsmābhir niyojanīyāḥ |"
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lalitā</s> and the rest of her company of friends, having likewise performed service to those senior ladies, sat down in that very place beside her. [15] And then the mother of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (Balarāma) [i.e., <s>Rohiṇī</s>] clearly spoke: 'O Queen of <s>Vraja</s>, all happiness-bestowing <s>Rohiṇī</s>-star is auspicious today. Therefore, please give the order: this one [<s>Rādhā</s>], whose skill surpasses that of all young brides of every region through her genuine goodness, let her — who has already gained the reputation of being a master of flavors through her concordance with the moon — together with other blessed women led by <s>Maṅgalā</s> and others — the <s>Rāmās</s> (women) of <s>Maṅgalārāma</s> and the younger brothers of <s>Rāma</s>, as well as the <s>Rāmās</s> bearing names both higher and lower — of <s>Kalyāṇārāma</s> and <s>Rāma</s>'s <s>Rāmās</s> — let all of them follow her on all sides. As for <s>Lalitā</s> and the others, they are like the very body-assembly of hers — they need not be assigned by us as helpers.'

children.text: atha tayāpi tathādiṣṭā śiṣṭāṅganā-gaṇa-gaṇeya-guṇā śiro namayitvā sakhīṣu tirobhūya tat-kālam eva cacāla |
children.translated_text: Then, thus instructed by her, the noble woman — foremost in the count of the assembly of refined women — bowing her head, disappeared among the <s>sakhīs</s> and departed that very moment.

children.text: atha prasaṅgam anyam api saṅgataṃ prathayāmaḥ | [18] atha dhṛta-praṇaya-naya-sārā vayasā mahasā sahasā ca kṛta-savayasaḥ sabhānukārāḥ, svakula-paramparā-gata-paricāraka-śūdrābhīra-kumārāḥ svāvasara-visara-prāptāvasaratayā prātar eva mohanāgāra-dvāra-sāram āvrajantaḥ samaṃ virājante sma |
children.translated_text: Now we shall also relate another fitting incident. [18] The servant-boys of the <s>Śūdra</s>-cowherd class — who had come through the generations of their own families, who had adopted the ways of affectionate conduct, who by their age, grandeur, and swiftness had made themselves equals of the same age, and were courteous — having obtained their proper occasion and opportunity, arriving at the very entrance of the enchanting palace early in the morning, shone together.

children.text: tataś ca snānīyādi-ramya-karais taiḥ kiṅkarair anugamyatayā sa tu vara-kiśora-vayā nikhila-trātā rāma-bhrātā prātar-ācārā-caraṇāya sadeśam upaveśa-pradeśaṃ pūrvam eva viveśa |
children.translated_text: Then, accompanied by those servants performing charming services such as bath-preparation and the like, that excellent youth — protector of all, brother of <s>Rāma</s> — first entered the assigned sitting area for the performance of the morning rituals.

children.text: tatra ca narma-maya-śarmada-praṇayā vaiśyābhīra-tanayāḥ sakhāyaḥ subalādayaḥ samam eva samagaṃsata | taiḥ saṅgataiḥ saha tu vilamba-kathantā-kathāvalambena mithaḥ parihāsa-vilāsa-kautukī varāsanam adhyāsāmāsa | te sarve premṇā paricaryāyāṃ param āścarya-caryāḥ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And there, the <s>Vaiśya</s>-cowherd sons — friends like <s>Subala</s> and others, whose affection was playful, bliss-giving, and loving — arrived together. And sitting with them on an excellent seat, through the support of leisurely conversation and mutual jesting, he delighted in play and amusement. They were all supremely wonderful in their loving service, for —

children.text:
ādeyādhārādi-bhāvena bhedāt
  prāṇā bhinnāḥ prāṇinaḥ santi bhinnāḥ |
  ye kṛṣṇādyāḥ snigdhatā-śarma-bhājaḥ
  prāṇā jñeyās te mithaḥ prāṇinaś ca ||JGc_1,2.6|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Through the distinction of being the vessel, foundation, and other such relations,
life-breaths are distinct, and living beings are distinct;
but those like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and his [companions], who share in the happiness of affection —
know them to be [each other's] life-breaths and living beings mutually.' ||2.6||

children.text: prabhāte ca prabhāte, tādṛśānām madhye tādṛśasya tasya tu,
children.translated_text: And morning after morning, among such [companions], the [routine] of that particular one who is such:

children.text:
śrīmad-vaktra-karāṅghri-dhāvana-kalā tailādibhir mardanaṃ
snānaṃ gātra-mṛjāṃśuka-dvaya-dhṛtiḥ sācāma-puṇḍra-kriyā |
prātar dharmaga-karma divya-vasanaṃ ratnāvalī-maṇḍanaṃ
vaṃśī-śṛṅga-śikhaṇḍa-daṇḍa-kalanā mac-cittam ākarṣati ||JGc_1,2.7|| [śārdūla]
[22] teṣu ca keṣucid aṅga-sevakeṣu viśeṣaḥ śeṣa-vacasām api śeṣasya viṣayāyate | yataḥ,

saurabhyaṃ śirasaḥ padāmbujayugaṃ bāhuprasārādikaṃ
labdhvā-śleṣaviśeṣatāṃ dadhati ye kṛṣṇasya tṛṣṇānvitāḥ |
vātsalye pariṣevaṇe sakhipade kānta-sthitāv apy amī
saukhyaṃ yat tad aśeṣam eva dadhate premṇā tadabhyaṅginaḥ ||JGc_1,2.8|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'Those who, filled with longing, receive the fragrance of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> head,
the lotus-pair of his feet, the extension of his arms, and the special quality of embrace —
in parental affection, in attendance, in the station of friendship, and even in the position of a lover —
whatever happiness they hold, they hold it entirely through love, being anointed thereby.' ||2.8||

children.text: atha tasmāt taiḥ parivītaḥ pīta-vasanaḥ svāṅgana-praveśam aṅgīkurvan sadeśa-samavayaskābhiḥ samaṃ, jananyā jīva-nyāsa iva pratimayā labhyate sma | tatra ca,
children.translated_text: Then, surrounded by them, wearing yellow garments, accepting entry into his own courtyard, together with his companions of the same age at the appointed place, he was received by his mother like a deposit of her life-breath, as if [seeing] an idol. And there:

children.text:
"āgacchaj jayatād aho madhuratā nirmañchanadravyatāṃ
gaccheyaṃ, mama dṛgdvayasya bhavatād atrātipakṣmāsthitiḥ |"
itthaṃ kañjavilocanasya kalayann ākasmikīm āgatiṃ
citraṃ citrajanaḥ sadā bhajati ced āsāṃ tu kiṃ tad bruve? ||JGc_1,2.9|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'"Come! Let the sweetness be victorious! Ah, I would go to the state of being the very substance for wiping [my eyes]!
May there be a most steady placement of eyelashes upon my pair of eyes here!"
Thus, perceiving the unexpected arrival of the lotus-eyed one,
it is wonderful if a painter always worships — but what shall I say of these [cowherd women]?' ||2.9||

children.text: atha guravaś ca tā rajanijanitatadvirahajvālākalitasnehapūravaśatayā muhur agurutām āsādyānavadyāmodam āviṣkurvatyaḥ pūrvadiṅmukhamahā-mandirālindād avateruḥ | tatra pūrvaṃ mātā vatsam iva mātā vatsaṃ militavatī, yatra rohiṇy api rohiṇīvad ūhāñcakre lokacakreṇa | [25] śrī-govindaś ca dvayor api tayoḥ padāravindaṃ kramād vanditvā nanditvā, mānyānām anyāsām api yathānyāyaṃ mānam unnamayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then the elders — the mothers, by the force of the fullness of affection produced by the flames of separation from him born during the night, having quickly assumed lightness, revealing their faultless fragrance — descended from the balcony of the great east-facing palace. There, the mother first met her calf like a cow meets her calf, where <s>Rohiṇī</s> too exchanged [glances] like [the constellation] <s>Rohiṇī</s>, with the wheel of people. [25] And <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, having worshipped the lotus-feet of both of them in turn, and having rejoiced, raised the honor of the other venerable women also, as was proper.

children.text: tadaiva ca śrīnīlāmbaram anu samāgatikarāḥ sahacarāḥ śrīdāma-sudāmādayaḥ śrīharisahavihārivitatayas, tathā sarvavidyāpaṭavaḥ purohita-baṭavas, tathā kāścid anyās tatprasūsamānamānanīya-tanmānanīyādi-varāṅganāsu gaṇyās, tathā sarvasukhadohāḥ svasṛsvasrīyādisnigdha-sambandhinīsandohās tatpradeśaṃ viśanti sma | [27] vāraṃ vāraṃ pratyekam utthānādyabhāvārthaṃ tathaiva hi sarvair maryādā paryāpitāsti |
children.translated_text: And at that very time, following <s>Śrī Nīlāmbara</s>, [his] companions who had come together — <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, and others — extended ranks of those who sport with <s>Śrī Hari</s>; likewise, the officiating young <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, adept in all learning; likewise some other excellent women, counted among those venerable ladies who were to be honored following his mother; likewise, assemblies of affectionate relatives such as sisters and sisters' [families], milkers of all happiness — they all entered that area. [27] For the purpose of [his] not rising repeatedly for each one, propriety was indeed observed by all in the same manner.

children.text: atha khalu siddhānāṃ pariṣadi yogamāyeti prasiddhā bhakti-siddhānta-sad-bhāva-rate śrīmad-bhāgavate ca yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ ity ādinā bhagaval-līlādhikāritayā siddhā svarūpa-śaktiḥ svābhivyaktim antareṇa rūpāntareṇa tāpasīti vyavasīyate, yasyāḥ paurṇamāsīti nāma-vyāhāra-vyavahāra āsīt | tasyām āgatāyām agarveṇa sarve' pi sa-sambhramam abhramaṃ namaḥ samam akurvata | tayā cānandād āśīrbhiḥ sphuṭam abhyanandiṣata |
children.translated_text: Now, in the assembly of the perfected ones (<s>siddhas</s>), the one well-known as <s>Yogamāyā</s> — devoted to the true principles of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) — and who in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> is established as having authority over the Lord's sports through [the statement] "having taken shelter of <s>yoga-māyā</s>" and the like — that <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential power), perfected in herself, without her own direct manifestation, is determined to have assumed another form as a female ascetic, whose name in conventional usage was <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>. When she arrived, all, without pride, with eagerness and without confusion, made obeisance together. And she joyously blessed them clearly with benedictions.

children.text: atha yaś ca sarva-vidyā-niṣṇātas tasyāḥ snātakaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya rahasya-narmāṇi baddha-tṛṣṇatayā tad-vayasyatāṃ vaśyatām āninye, yaś cāvidūṣaṇa-bhāva-rūṣita eva devarṣi-prakṛtitayā tasya kautuka-kṛte vidūṣakatām api vibhūṣayati sma, sa khalu madhumaṅgala-nāmā narmaṇā marma-sparśi-kutuka-racanair āśīr-vacanaiḥ sarvān amandam ānandayāmāsa, nidhim iva hari-sannidhiṃ cānañca |
children.translated_text: Now, the one who was proficient in all sciences, her initiated student, who, through intense longing for the confidential and humorous pastimes of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, had brought himself to the status of his companion and obedient friend, and who, though himself of the nature of a divine sage, though actually embodying faultless disposition, adorned even the role of the jester (<s>vidūṣaka</s>) for [Kṛṣṇa's] amusement — he, indeed, the one named <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, through his wit, with heart-touching, curiosity-arousing benedictory words, delighted everyone exceedingly, and he approached the presence of <s>Hari</s> as if approaching a treasure.

children.text: tataś ca parasparaṃ kara-baddha-karau sitāsita-kumāra-varau mātṛbhyām
children.translated_text: Then, with hands clasped in each other's hands, the two excellent young princes — one fair and one dark — by their mothers

children.text: ubhayataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pradatta-hastau smita-vaśaṃvada-vadana-śastau mandaṃ mandaṃ tad evāmandam alindam avindatām | [31] suvarṇa-svarṇa-kirmīrita-prayatna-nirmita-pṛthu-ratna-pīṭham abhi pṛthak pṛthaṅ niviṣṭavantau sudhā-vṛṣṭim iva ca sarveṣūpaviṣṭeṣu dṛṣṭiṃ sṛṣṭavantau |
children.translated_text: with hands placed on their backs from both sides, with faces obediently smiling, slowly, slowly found that very delightful verandah. [31] They sat down separately upon a broad jeweled throne, carefully crafted with efforts of golden inlay, and cast their gaze — like a shower of nectar — upon all those who were seated.

children.text: atha pratimāsyā seyam āsyā janma-tārā-gamana-mayīti śrī-yaśodā-yaśo-dātus tasya tadā tad-ācāryāṇām arbhakā darbhakāgrīya-nīrābhiṣekaṃ vivekātirekavantaḥ śantama-mantra-pravacana-sacanayā racayāmāsuḥ | tataś ca,
children.translated_text: Then, at the occasion of her birthday star — "This is indeed her birth-star" — the <s>ācāryas</s> (preceptors) of that time, of <s>Śrī Yaśodā</s>, the bestower of glory to her son, performed the sprinkling ablution of the infant with the tips of <s>darbha</s> grass and water, with supreme discernment, accompanied by the chanting of most auspicious <s>mantras</s>. And then,

children.text:
mantrā gītāni vādyāny api ca jaya-ravāḥ kṛṣṇa-śobhās tadīya-
preyo-vargāti-citra-praṇaya-vilasitānīti parvaṇy amuṣmin |
pratyekaṃ tat tad ekībhavanam api tadā prāpa rucyatvam uccaiḥ
śṛṅgārādyo raso vā kavi-kṛtir athavā ṣāḍavo vāpi yadvat ||JGc_1,2.10|| [srāgdharā]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "<s>Mantras</s>, songs, music, and victory-cries, the beauties of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
and the most wonderfully varied affectionate pastimes of his beloved company —
at this festival, each and every one of these, even when merged together,
attained great charm, just as the erotic and other <s>rasas</s>, or poetic art, or a <s>ṣāḍava</s> dish [taste better when combined]." [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.10, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text:
tasmin nīrāja-nirmañchana-bhavika-padārthāli-saṃsparśanānām
ājyādarśādi-darśa-dvija-nija-janatārcādikānāṃ śubhānām |
kṛṣṇo gotrādir āsīt pravara-vara-daśāṃ tāni jagmuḥ samantād
yebhyo' nye ca prathante śubha-śata-nivahasyānvayāḥ sarva-loke ||JGc_1,2.11|| [srāgdharā]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "In that [ceremony], of the objects for the lustration-rites — the <s>nīrājana</s> (waving of lights), wiping, auspicious items to be touched —
and of the auspicious acts such as offering mirrors with ghee, honoring twice-born priests and one's own people —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was the <s>gotra</s>-initiator (the foremost); those [rites] attained their most excellent and exalted condition all around;
and from those [rites], others too, the lineages of hundreds of auspicious deeds, spread throughout the entire world." [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.11, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text:
brāhmaṇyas tv adhikacam acyutasya dūrvā
pūrvāṇi nyadhiṣata tatra maṅgalāni |
yady āśīrvacanam ihārurodha bāṣpaḥ
kalyāṇaṃ bata bhavatān manorathasya ||JGc_1,2.12|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "The <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (priest's wife) placed upon <s>Acyuta</s> (the infallible one) the foremost of auspicious items, the <s>dūrvā</s> grass.
If [at that moment] tears blocked her benedictory words —
alas! How auspicious was that [obstruction] for the fulfillment of their hearts' desires!" [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.12, <s>praharṣiṇī</s>]

children.text:
dṛgambhaḥ-stambha-ruddhāpi kurvatī tilakaṃ prasūḥ |
kuryāt kiṃ yadi sāhāyyaṃ nākariṣyata rohiṇī? ||JGc_1,2.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "Even as the mother, applying the <s>tilaka</s> mark, was blocked by the dam of tears in her eyes —
what would she have done if <s>Rohiṇī</s> had not come to her aid?" [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.13, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
mātuḥ pitus tasya ca tatra mātṛ-
bhāvānvitā-bhrātṛ-vadhū-svasṝṇām |
upāyanaṃ puṇḍram itīyatī gīr
āsīt tadīyārtha-caye mitir na ||JGc_1,2.14|| [upajāti]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "Of his mother's, father's, and also of those bearing the sentiment of motherhood —
sisters-in-law and sisters — the gifts, marked as auspicious (<s>puṇḍra</s>),
were described only by the word 'this much' — there was no measure for the aggregate of their offerings." [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.14, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: atha prācī-gata-dvitīya-prakoṣṭhād āgamya ramya-kumāraḥ kaścid ācaṣṭa, yaḥ khalv etad-artham eva pūrvaṃ visṛṣṭaḥ | "śrīman vraja-rāja-kumāra, śrīmad-vraja-rāja-sabhāyāṃ sarva eva parvaṇīha saṃvalitā vartante, kintu bhavad-yātrā-dvāra-mātrāvalokinaḥ | yāni ca sarvārādhana-dhanāni śrīmad-vraja-rāja-caraṇa-rājīva-parisarāya sajjitāni bhavad-visarjitāni tāmbūla-dukūlādīni, tāni cādhunāpi mūrdhānaṃ dhunānā nopayuñjate sma |"
children.translated_text: Then, coming from the second antechamber facing east, a certain handsome young man announced — one who had indeed been sent earlier for this very purpose: "O glorious prince of <s>Vraja</s>, in the court of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, everyone indeed has assembled for the festival here, but they are looking only toward the gateway awaiting your procession. And the gifts for the worship of all — the <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), fine cloths, and other items dispatched by you for the lotus-feet of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> — those they are still not using, shaking their heads [in refusal]."

children.text: atha so' pi tad avadhārayann eva, tad evāvadhārayan mātaram anu kātara iva niṣkramaṇa-klama-samanujñā-yācanam anusandhāya, praṇāmādinā paurṇamāsīm uṭaja-gṛhāya vihāya, śrī-rāmam agre vidhāya, śrīdāmādīn parito nidhāya, paścimāgrima-prema-dolāyamāna-svāntas tato niṣkrāntaḥ; sahasā mahasā vṛtaḥ sabhyālibhir abhyālokayāñcakre |
children.translated_text: Then he too, while taking note of that very message, and noting it further, feeling anxious about his mother, devised a request for permission to depart from the fatigue [of ceremony]. Having taken leave of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> with obeisance and the like, dismissing her to her hermitage, placing <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (Balarāma) before him, positioning <s>Śrīdāma</s> and others around him, with his inner self swaying on the swing of hesitation between staying and going — he departed from there. Suddenly, enveloped by a halo of majesty, he was beheld by the assemblage of courtier-friends.

children.text: atha sodita-meghāś cātakā iva, labdha-candrāś cakorā iva, saṅgata-jalā jala-janmāna iva, samunmīlita-prāṇā dehā iva, sarve' py ānanda-garveṇa vandi-vṛndādi-kalita-kolāhalena ca samam eva samuttasthuḥ | [36] kintūtkalikā-kalita-manaso' pi sva-sva-maryādayāparyāpitā iva labdha-stambhārambhās tatra tatra kevalaṃ sthitavantaḥ | yuktam eva ca tat proktaṃ, yatas tasmin khalv asmākaṃ śrī-nanda-vraja-rāja-grāme tat-tat-prema-viśeṣa-rīti-nītir eva grāmaṇīr iva vartate | [37] tathā hi, kadācit kasyacit kañcit prati vacanam,
children.translated_text: Then, like <s>cātaka</s> birds at the appearance of clouds, like <s>cakora</s> birds finding the moon, like lotus-born beings meeting with water, like bodies whose life-breath has been fully restored — all of them, with pride of joy and with the tumultuous sound made by the throngs of bards and others, rose up together. [36] Yet, even though their minds were filled with excitement, they merely stood in their respective places, restrained as if seized by the staff of their own propriety — having obtained the beginning of a pillar-like stillness. And that was indeed proper, for in this our village of <s>Śrī Nanda</s>, the king of <s>Vraja</s>, the specific etiquette and protocol of each kind of love reigns as the headman, as it were. [37] As someone once said to someone about that,

children.text:
"tau śubhra-dyuti-nīrada-dyuti-harāv indrāśma-hema-prabhā
hṛd-vastrau sita-kañja-nīla-kamala-śrī-cori-cārv-ānanau |
cañcat-khañjana-gañjanākṣi-yugalau dantīndrajid-vikramau
tān astambhayatāṃ janān yad akhilāṃs tan mitra citraṃ na hi ||JGc_1,2.15|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "Those two — one stealing the radiance of white clouds, the other stealing the radiance of dark clouds,
with garments of topaz and gold splendor, with beautiful faces stealing the beauty of white and blue lotuses,
with eyes that rival fluttering wagtails, with the prowess of lords of elephants —
that those two made all those people motionless — O friend, that is no wonder!" [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.15, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: yadā ca dakṣiṇe sarvānarvācīna-māhātmya-guravo guravo babhūvuḥ; te ca sarve pūrva-pūrvataḥ pūrvajā eva tasthuḥ | yatra purohitāḥ svayam anargham arghyaṃ dadhānāḥ sarvataḥ pūrve bhavantaḥ sva-nāma-niruktim iva vyaktīkurvanti sma, "puro dhīyante" iti | tad etad api yuktaṃ, śleṣeṇa ca prathamato hitās ta eva hi bhaṇyante |
children.translated_text: And when to the right, the weighty elders — teachers of unexcelled greatness — were present, and they all stood in order of seniority. Where the family priests, themselves offering priceless <s>arghya</s> (water-offering), standing foremost on all sides, manifested the etymology of their own name, as it were — "they are placed in front" (<s>puro dhīyante</s>). And this too is fitting, for by the device of double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>), they who are beneficial are indeed described first.

children.text: atha tādṛśa-nija-kula-candra-premānandāmṛta-tundilitatayā kila śrīmad-upanandābhinanda-nanda-sananda-nandanādi-nāmānaḥ prabala-nandana-sneha-madhura-dhāmānas, tān anu ca premṇā samyag-bandhutā-bandhinaḥ sambandhinaḥ parāpara-nāmānas tan-milanam anusandhāya sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, swollen with the nectar of love's bliss for such a moon of their own clan, those named <s>Upananda</s>, <s>Abhinanda</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, and others — whose sweet abodes were [filled with] powerful filial affection — stood waiting to meet [him], and after them, the relatives, whose names were various, bound by the bonds of proper kinship through love.

children.text: atha vāme' pi tathaivālaghu-premṇā laghūbhavanto laghavaḥ samavatasthire | [41] sarve caite yathā-pūrvaṃ yathā-yathaṃ sarva-cittārāmeṇa rāmeṇa saha hāriṇā hariṇā militāḥ samunmīlita-bhāvā babhūvuḥ, candramasaṃ vindamānāḥ kumuda-sandohā iva |
children.translated_text: And on the left too, the juniors, becoming humble through their no-small love, likewise took their positions. [41] And all of them, as before, in their own ways, meeting with the charming <s>Hari</s> and the delightful <s>Rāma</s>, who captivates all hearts — they became manifest in their feelings, like clusters of night-lotuses finding the moon.

children.text: tataś ca kṣaṇa-katipayād akṣīṇānanda-vṛndārpita-satvara-visṛtvara-mohād unmagneṣu teṣu tadīya-śrīman-mukha-nirīkṣaṇa-lagneṣu śrīmān vraja-rājas taṃ vyājahāra, "tāta, tavādya vidyate sarva-sampan-mayī janma-tārā | tasmād vraja-dhāma svayam ā madhyāhnam adhyāsitavyam | go-sambhālana-pālanāya punaḥ prātar eva mayā samayāsthitā yuktā niyuktāḥ santi | svayam atha prathama upaviśya dṛśyatāṃ svajana-vrajaḥ" iti |
children.translated_text: Then, after a few moments, when those [elders], immersed in the bewilderment of hastily bestowed and abundantly overflowing undiminished bliss, had emerged [from that reverie] — fixed upon gazing at his glorious face — the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> addressed him: "Dear son, today you have a birthday star endowed with all prosperity. Therefore, <s>Vraja-dhāma</s> (the abode of <s>Vraja</s>) itself should be personally attended to until midday. For the care and protection of the cows, I have already appointed those who are properly designated, in keeping with established protocol, from early morning. Now, being the first to be seated yourself, behold your assembled kinfolk."

children.text: atha so' py avācīnatā-samīcīna-śiraskatayā rājñāṃ tām ājñāṃ mālām iva śirasi nidhāya, śrī-rāma-mukha-tāmarasam avadhāya, svajana-vraja-sahitatayā sahitam adhiruhya catuṣka-deśa-gataṃ puṣkalam upaveśa-veśma valita-smitaṃ tārā-patir iva pūrva-parvatam adhyāsitavān | viprādi-sampradānatayā yathā-yathaṃ gavādikam api sātavān | tataś ca tasminn upaviśya, punas tāmbulādi-saṃvibhāga-sukha-saṃvalanayā sambandhibhir mitho narma-saṃvāda-sambandhi-sandhi-kutūhalaṃ kalayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And he, with the propriety of a humble head-bowing befitting one receiving commands, placed the king's instruction on his head like a garland. Observing the lotus-face of <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, accompanied by the assembly of his own kinfolk, he mounted the ample, delightful reception-hall situated in the quadrangular court with a gentle smile — like the lord of stars (the moon) ascending the eastern mountain. Through gifts to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, he also distributed cows and other [gifts] as appropriate. Then, having seated himself there, he engaged in the pleasure of distributing <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) and the like, and enjoyed the curiosity of humorous conversations connecting with relatives.

children.text: muhūrtād atha kaścid antaḥ-pura-sāraḥ kumāraḥ samāgamya sāmyenopaviṣṭayor jyāyaḥ-kaniṣṭhayoḥ sambandhi-nivahārādhanāya dhṛta-tṛṣṇayoḥ śrī-rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ karṇābhyarṇaṃ lagitavān, tābhyām anumataḥ punas tad-rūpa-taś citrībhavituḥ śrīmad-vraja-dharitrīśituḥ | tena ca "adya śrīvatsa-vatsa-prasāda-labdhasya vatsasya śubha-sampan-maya-janma-rkṣam" iti vinaya-sandhena kevalenāñjali-bandhena vyañjanayā bhojanāya yācitāḥ santo' ti-santoṣād vyativīkṣya yugapad utthitavantas te prasthitavantaś cāntaḥ-puram |
children.translated_text: After a moment, a certain refined young man of the inner apartments came and whispered into the ears of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who were seated equally and who held the desire to honor the assembly of kinsmen — [he was] approved by both and then [went] to the king of the earth of <s>Vraja</s>, who was to be made a portrait of wonder. By him, [the message was conveyed that] "today is the auspicious birthday star of the calf obtained by the grace of the glorious <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-marked one's child" — and through a mere gesture of folded hands, with only the bond of courtesy, the saintly ones were invited to the feast. They rose simultaneously with supreme satisfaction and exchanged glances, and proceeded toward the inner apartments.

children.text: athāgrataḥ-sareṇa tena sukumāreṇa kumāreṇa prāṅgaṇataḥ pratiruddha-saṅgamanāsu śuddhānta-saṅgatāṅganāsu praviṣṭās te kaṃsajid-iṣṭā gṛhādi-śobhekṣaṇa-spṛhātaḥ kṣaṇam āviṣṭāḥ, kramaśo bhojanālayāya kalayām-babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, led in front by that delicate young man, when the women of the inner quarters — connected with the pure inner chamber — were prevented from the pathway at the courtyard, [the guests] entered — those beloved of the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — and, momentarily captivated by the desire to behold the beauty of the residences and other [structures], gradually made their way toward the dining hall.

children.text: rāma-kṛṣṇau tu gavālokana-satṛṣṇau tad-aṅgaṇa-saṅgata-merv-ākāra-mahāgāram āruhya, mahī-mahita-māheyī-sthāneṣu pīyūṣa-vṛṣṭīr iva dṛṣṭīr vidhāya, vidheyair vidūra-deśān nideśayāmāsatuḥ, "bho bho gopa-gaṇāḥ, vartmanaḥ savyāpasavyayor eva pātavyā gavyāḥ" iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, eager to see the cows, climbed the great <s>Meru</s>-shaped hall adjacent to that courtyard, and casting their gazes — like showers of nectar — upon the stations of the earth-honored cows, directed their attendants to the distant regions: "Ho, ho, company of cowherds! The herds are to be driven only along the right and left sides of the path!"

children.text: athāvatīrṇābhyām ābhyām abhyāgatair api,
children.translated_text: Then, when those two had descended and [others] had also arrived,

children.text:
aguruja-guru-dhūpaḥ śubhratā ratna-pīṭhā-
vali-mad-aśana-pātrāsaṅgi-bhṛṅgāra-saṅghaḥ |
niyata-saciva-lokaḥ sādara-prema cāsīd
iti diśi diśi dharmyaṃ bhoga-harmyaṃ vyaloki ||JGc_1,2.16|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "Incense of <s>aguru</s> (agarwood) fragrance not born of elder [trees], the bright splendor of jeweled thrones,
clusters of pitchers clinging to vessels of intoxicating food,
the constant retinue of ministers, and affectionate love —
thus in every direction, the righteous banquet-hall was beheld." [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.16, <s>mālinī</s>]

children.text:
"aṅghri-kṣālana-mārjane iha bhavān jīyād" iti prārthanā,
samyag vījanam antarā pramadasūhāsa-prasū-sūktayaḥ |
rucyānāṃ pariveṣaṇaṃ muraripor dṛṣṭi-prasādāmṛtaṃ
yatraivaṃ suhṛdāṃ sabhojana-vidhiḥ sūte na kiṃ vā sukham? ||JGc_1,2.17|| [śārdūla]

tatrānupayukta-yukta-bhoktṝṇāṃ viprāṇāṃ paṅktir ekatra, sagdhi-digdhānām asandigdha-snigdhānāṃ vaiśya-vaṃśyānām anyatra | tatra tatra ca vṛddha-madhyama-nava-yauvanānāṃ pṛthak pṛthag iti viyutāv api, mitho yathāsvaṃ parihāsa-vilāsena saṃyutir iva vīkṣyate sma | na ca kevalena tena, tad-avalocana-samunmīlita-locana-rocana-vilāsālāpa-līlā-rasa-vāridher vrajendra-kula-sudhā-nidher asakṛd anubhava-yaugapadyena ca |
children.translated_text: There, the row of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, who eat only suitable and proper food, was in one place; in another, the undoubtedly affectionate ones of the <s>Vaiśya</s> lineage, anointed with togetherness. And there, though separated into distinct groups of the aged, middle-aged, and youthful — yet through mutual jesting and playfulness as befitted each, a unity, as it were, was seen. And not by that alone, but also through the simultaneous experience of the ocean of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight) of the playful conversation, illuminated by gazes awakened by observing him — the nectar-treasure of the family of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — repeatedly.

children.text: yatra ca sa eva sarva-rasa-satram amatram ekam āsīt | tatra ca,
children.translated_text: Where he alone was the one, immeasurable, complete sacrificial feast of all <s>rasas</s> (flavors). And there,

children.text:
parasparasya sphuṭa-hāsa-vārtāṃ
sañcārayantaḥ parito harau ca |
ṣaṇṇāṃ rasānāṃ pariveṣakā ye
te saptamasyāpi babhūvur atra ||JGc_1,2.18|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
[Verse:] "Those who served the six flavors, while circulating throughout
clear jesting conversation among one another and about <s>Hari</s> —
they became the servers of a seventh [flavor] as well, here!" [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.2.18, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: yatra parihāsa-bījaṃ ca pṛthag-dig-deśa-loka-prasiddhānām atraiva cānyathā-siddhānāṃ temanādīnāṃ nāma nāmnātuṃ śakyate, nāmāntareṇa vāmnāyate, sad-āmnāya-janmabhir api bandhu-sambandhibhir ity ādi lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: Where the seed of jesting was such that the names of <s>Temana</s> and others — famous in various regions and countries of the world, and here established differently — cannot [even] be named; they are conveyed only by another name, by kinsmen and relatives born of the true tradition, and so forth — such is the mark that is observed.

children.text:
kiṃ ca, tatra madhumaṅgalaḥ kautukena kenacit prahitena nija-hitena śrīmad-vrajeśaṃ sandideśa, "rāja-vara, tad etad asmākaṃ brāhmaṇā nivedayanti: æśaukla-nāma-dheyaṃ prathamam eva janma tāvad asmādṛśāṃ bhṛśa-śarmaṇe cakpe | yad dvitīye sāvitrākhye janmani labdha-sva-kulaiśya-vaiśya-dvijatayā rājanyavad brāhmaṇa-bhojya-pakvānnair api bhavadbhir vidūra-vibhakta-paṅktāv eva niveśitā vayaṃ na pratīmaḥ, tatra kiṃ kiṃ pariveṣitam atra vā kim iti | tasmād goṣṭhādhipatinā sva-dṛṣṭi-niṣṭaṅkitī-kṛtāny asmat-kṛte punaḥ prathamataḥ sarvāṇy eva temanāni pariveṣyantām | yāny eva vārṣabhānavy-ādi-sva-hasta-prayastatayā paktāni parama-śastāny uttara-tāpany-anusāreṇa pūrvaṃ durvāsasāpi krodha-durvāsanāṃ nirvāsayatā prasādam api
bhāsayatā rasanayābhyastānīti nikhila-miṣṭatāviśiṣṭatayā kila vartmany eva pariveśakaiś coraṃ coram urvaritāni, parāṇy api dṛśaiva bhukta-pūrvāṇi santi, tāni ca bhuktvā vaiṣṇava-yajñāya śruti-smṛti-vihita-hita-pratīkāra-mayaṃ daikṣasam ākhyaṃ tṛtīyam api janma drutam urīkariṣyate' iti |"
children.translated_text: Moreover, there <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, sent by some well-wishing curiosity, conveyed a message to the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>: 'O best of kings! Our <s>brāhmaṇas</s> report the following: 'The first birth, named <s>Śaukla</s> (the white/pure), was indeed perfectly suited for our great happiness. But in the second birth called <s>Sāvitrī</s>, we — having obtained our own clan's lordship as <s>Vaiśya</s> twice-born — were seated by you in a row far removed, like <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, even with food cooked fit for <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and we do not understand: what was served there and what here? Therefore, let the lord of the cowherd settlement cause all the food-preparations to be served to us again from the beginning, marked by his own glance. The very ones that were cooked by the hands of <s>Vārṣabhānavī</s> (Rādhā) and others, supremely praised, following the Uttara-Tāpanī [Upaniṣad] — even <s>Durvāsas</s>, banishing his wrath's evil disposition and displaying grace, had savored them with his tongue — and due to their excellence of supreme sweetness, they were secretly kept back by the servers on the path, and others were consumed merely by sight. Having eaten those, the third birth too, called <s>Daikṣa</s>, consisting of the beneficial remedies ordained by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> for the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> sacrifice, will be swiftly undertaken!''

children.text: tad etad ākalayya kalitaṃ hāsa-kolāhalaṃ, gokula-kuleśvarī gṛhād avakalayantī svayam anala-pakva-tulitāni sūrya-pakvāni bahūny anupa-bhukta-carāṇi vihāpayāmāsa, yena bahulam eva sahāsa-kutūhalaṃ nikhilaḥ kalayām-babhūva |
children.translated_text: Understanding this, a tumultuous burst of laughter arose. The queen of the <s>Gokula</s> clan, perceiving from the house, herself had many sun-ripened items, matched with fire-cooked ones, and items not yet partaken of as appetizers, brought out — whereby the entire [company] experienced abundant curiosity mixed with laughter.

children.text: tad evam udara-pūraṇa-mātreṇa tṛptā, na tu tat-tad-bahula-rasa-pūra-kutūhalena, natarāṃ tat-tad-ānanda-mūlena sad-ānukūla-pīta-dukūlena prati-ruci-nava-navāyamānatā hi tatrāyatā, tathāpi balād iva parimala-ramaṇīyam ācamanīyaṃ dattam | gaty-antareṇāsamāpanīya-spṛhaṇīyatā hi tatra bṛhatī | tataś ca,
children.translated_text: Thus they were satisfied merely by the filling of the belly, but not by the curiosity for the abundance of various flavors, and certainly not by the root of those various joys, the favorable yellow silk worn by the auspicious one — for the charm of ever-renewed relish was extended there. Nevertheless, as if by force, the delightfully fragrant mouth-rinsing water was given — for the desirability that could not be completed by any other means was vast there. And then,

children.text:
divya-tāmbūla-cārcikya
vastra-mālya-vibhūṣaṇaiḥ |
arcitā bandhavaḥ sarve
dakṣiṇābhiś ca bhūsurāḥ ||JGc_1,2.19|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: All the kinsmen were honored with divine betel, cosmetic preparations, garments, garlands, and ornaments, and the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). //

children.text: lakṣitāyāṃ ca dakṣiṇāyāṃ, madhumaṅgalaḥ sa tu narma-śarmāmṛtam adugdha | "bho vraja-mahanīyāḥ, nāsyām akṣīṇāyām api dakṣiṇāyām īrṣayā vayaṃ vīkṣaṇīyāḥ | bhavatāṃ bhuñjānānām ekaika-vyañjana-mūlya-tulyatayāsmākaṃ samastāpi sā na prastāvayati |"
children.translated_text: And when the gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) were noticed, that <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> milked the nectar of playful delight: 'O revered ones of <s>Vraja</s>! Even though this <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is undiminished, we are not to be regarded with envy! For even our entire [share] does not match the value of each single condiment that you have consumed!'

children.text: tad evaṃ bahala-hāsa-kolāhala-kutūhale nivṛtte pitaram upetya sarva-sukha-pālaḥ śrīla-gopālaḥ śanaiḥ saniṃ praṇayan sa-vinayam ālalāpa, "arvāg eva sarvān ādāya sabhālaya-valayaṃ svayaṃ tatra-bhavantaḥ samayantu | vayaṃ tu śrī-rāma-dāma-sudāmādayaḥ samāgata-prāyāḥ |" tad evaṃ mātṛ-gṛham upetya tām apy uvāca, "mātar, mātṝṇāṃ sambhālanārtham anuyātṝṇ asmān anumanyasva |"
children.translated_text: Thus, when the commotion of abundant laughter and curiosity subsided, the protector of all happiness, the glorious <s>Gopāla</s> (Kṛṣṇa), approached his father and spoke gently, with affection and humility: 'Let the venerable ones themselves lead everyone and proceed to the circle of the assembly hall. We — <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, <s>Dāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, and others — have mostly assembled.' Having thus gone to the mother's house, he said to her too: 'Mother, give us, the followers, your permission for the sake of attending to the mothers.'

children.text: mātā ca kṣarat-kṣīra-kula-kuca-mukulam ālalāpa, "āyuṣman, yuṣmad-eka-prāṇā vayaṃ, tasmān na vilambanīyam" iti |
children.translated_text: And the mother, from whose breasts the milk-buds were flowing, spoke: 'O long-lived one! We whose sole life is you — therefore, you must not delay!'

children.text: tataś ca tasyāḥ savayasaḥ pravayasaś ca sarvāḥ saṅghaśaḥ sāsram ūcuḥ, "vatsa, nāmnaiva tā mātaraḥ, eṣā tu tava mātaiva, tasmād asyāṃ kathaṃ na vilakṣaṇaṃ pakṣapātam āpātayasi?" sa ca nata-vadanaḥ sāsra-smita-vācam uvāca, "mātaraḥ, kiṃ kurmaḥ? tās tu paśu-jātayo na vivekam ekam api labhante, yato māṃ vinā tṛṇam api na tṛṇvanti |"
children.translated_text: Then all her companions, both of the same age and older, said together in groups, tearfully: 'O child! Those are mothers in name only; this one alone is truly your mother! So why do you not let fall upon her an extraordinary partiality?' And he, with bowed face, spoke with tearful smiling words: 'O mothers! What shall we do? Those [cow] creatures do not attain even a single discernment, since without me they do not even graze on a blade of grass!'

children.text: mātovāca, "samyag āha vatsaḥ, yato dharma evāsmākaṃ marmabhedī babhūva, yeṣāṃ dhanāni tanayāś ca sadā vanāni nilayān kurvanti |"
children.translated_text: Mother said: 'The child speaks rightly, for <s>dharma</s> itself has become the piercer of our innermost hearts — they whose wealth and sons always make the forests their abode!'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sahāsam- āha sma, "mātar, atra vane na ko' pi trāsaḥ | sa tu samūlakāsaṃ kaṣitānāṃ keśiprabhṛtīnāṃ saṅgata eva gataḥ |"
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a laugh: 'Mother, in this forest there is no fear whatsoever! That [fear] has departed along with <s>Keśī</s> and the others who were thoroughly crushed root and all!'

children.text: mātovāca, "tarhi kim ākarṇyate, yad adyāpi kiñcit teṣām auddhatyaṃ vidyate, pretānām api tattadākāratayā sadyaḥ pretatāṃ prāptānām iva |"
children.translated_text: Mother said: 'Then why is it heard that even today some of their arrogance exists, of those who seem to have immediately obtained the state of ghosts in those very forms — like ghosts themselves?'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sahāsam- āha sma, "mātar, na te pretajātitām avāptāḥ | kintu, bhavaccaraṇareṇugaṇaguṇitabhūmim anu maraṇapratāpavargād apavargam eva gatāḥ | vayaṃ tu māyāmayatatpratikṛtiprapañcasañcayam añcantaḥ sukhasantānāya madhye madhye līlām adhyasyāmaḥ; yathā nilāyanaiḥ setubandhair markaṭotplavanādibhiḥ kauśalyeyalīlām |"
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a laugh: 'Mother, they have not attained the state of ghosts! Rather, following the earth sanctified by the host of merits of the dust of your feet, they have attained liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) from the category of the glory of death! We, however, extending the phenomenal array of illusory (<s>māyā</s>) likenesses, superimpose play (<s>līlā</s>) from time to time for the continuation of happiness — just as through hiding-places, bridge-building, monkey-leaping, and the like, we [superimpose] the <s>līlā</s> of the son of <s>Kausalyā</s> (Rāma).'
