children.text: tataś ca sarvāsu gata-sandehāsu snehātiśayāt kṛṣṇa-mātā savyena pāṇinā pṛṣṭham, apasavyena cibukaṃ spṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇajyeṣṭhaṃ prati sabāṣpam ācaṣṭa, "vatsa nīlāmbara, taveyam ambā mama samakṣaṃ bālyād eva tvayi nātīva vātsalyam ullāsayati, kintu svayam udāsīnavad āsīnā bhavati | tat khalu mama tāralyaṃ katham iva vairalyāya kalyatām? tasmād aham eva tvām upadiśāmi: pītāmbareṇa samam avilambam evālambanīyaṃ vrajavartma" iti |
children.translated_text: Then, when all doubts had departed from all, <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother, from an excess of affection, touching the back with her left hand and the chin with her right, said tearfully to <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> elder brother: 'O child of the blue garment! This mother of yours, in my presence, from childhood itself does not display overflowing maternal love toward you; rather, she sits as if indifferent. How then can my fickleness be considered steadfastness? Therefore, I myself instruct you: with the yellow-garmented one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), without delay, take to the path of <s>Vraja</s>!'

children.text: atha rāmānujaṃ hitavatī rohiṇy abhihitavatī, "tāta, yaśodāmāta, bālyād eva lālya-bhāvān mātur upadeśaṃ jātu na ca manyase | mama tu taṃ na matāntaram ātanoṣi | tataḥ sakṛd api mama nideśam asakṛd iva manyasva | mātur manas-tāpa-vistārān nistārāya nija-vadanāṃśu-sudhāṃ vistāraya tvaritam" iti |
children.translated_text: Then the well-wishing <s>Rohiṇī</s> addressed <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>): 'Dear child, O <s>Yaśodā</s>-mother! From childhood itself, because of your nature as the pampered one, you never heed mother's instruction. But you do not extend a different opinion to me! Therefore, consider my single command as though it were given many times. To deliver your mother from the expanse of mental anguish, spread quickly the nectar-moonlight of your face!'

children.text: atha tāsāṃ caraṇa-pātācaraṇāya kṛta-rocane nirmala-kamala-locane sarvābhir anarvācīnābhiḥ saha gṛhaṃ hitvā tat-pāṇiṃ gṛhītvā prāṅgana-saṅgitāṃ gatāyāṃ gopa-pati-pati-vratāyāṃ, sarvataḥ śreyasyas tat-preyasyaḥ sagavākṣa-bhitti-bhittīkṛta-nija-vilokanā vilokayāmāsuḥ | tathā hi,
children.translated_text: Then, when the one of pure lotus-eyes was inclined to fall at their feet, the devoted wife of the cowherd-lord, taking his hand, left the house with all those venerable ladies and went to the courtyard. And from all sides, the most excellent beloveds beheld through the windows of the walls, making their own gazing a screen upon the walls. Thus:

children.text:
autsukyaṃ priya-mādhurī-madhu-madaṃ premātipāta-bhramaṃ
viśleṣāgama-bhītim apy anugatā lajjātiparyākulāḥ |
gocārāya vanāya gacchati harau tasyāṅganānāṃ gaṇāś
citrāṇīva nirīkṣya tasthur abhito dvitra-kṣaṇaṃ bhittiṣu ||JGc_1,2.20|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: Eagerness, the intoxication of the honey of the beloved's sweetness, the bewilderment of love's excess, and even the fear of separation's approach — following all these, yet overwhelmed by excessive modesty — when <s>Hari</s> went to the pasture, to the forest, the hosts of his women stood like paintings on the walls for two or three moments, gazing from all sides! // [<s>śārdūla</s>]

children.text:
tatra sati,
acyutasya nayana-dvayam āsāṃ
tṛṣṇag apy atihriyā nimimīla |
asya mānasam amūr atigūḍhaṃ
paśyatīti milituṃ tad ivecchu ||JGc_1,2.21|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: Thereupon: The pair of <s>Acyuta's</s> eyes, though thirsting for these [women], closed from excessive shyness. 'He sees their innermost hearts with his mind!' — as if desiring to meet that [mind], those [eyes] wished to close! // [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text:
yadā ca tāsāṃ sphuraṇaṃ jagāma tan-
manas tad āśaṅkata tāsu rādhayā |
"aho gurūṇāṃ purato vikāritāṃ
labheya cet kiṃ kara-vaitarām" iti ||JGc_1,2.22|| [vaṃśasthavilā]
children.translated_text: And when the flash of those [women] subsided, his mind apprehended <s>Rādhā</s> among them: 'Ah! If I were to display emotional changes before the elders, what crossing of the river of consequence would there be!' // [<s>vaṃśasthavila</s>]

children.text:
tatra mātṛ-gaṇataḥ krama-pūrvaṃ
prāpya yan baka-śamanaḥ samanujñām |
ambakāny aharata pratibimba-
vyājataḥ svatanugāny akhilānām ||JGc_1,2.23|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: There, having obtained permission step by step from the group of mothers, the subduer of <s>Baka</s> stole all their reflections — on the pretext of [receiving their] reflected images — their own body-followers! // [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text: athāmara-durlabha-cchatra-cāmara-paṭa-puṭa-tāmbūla-sampuṭādi-ghaṭita-karāḥ savayasaḥ karma-karāḥ śrī-rāma-dāmādibhiḥ saha gacchantaṃ tam anvagacchan |
children.translated_text: Then, the companions of the same age, the attendants, carrying in their hands parasols, fly-whisks, cloth-wrappings, betel-boxes, and other items — rare even for the gods — together with <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, <s>Dāma</s>, and others, followed him as he went.

children.text:
atha tatabhāyāṃ parama-sabhāyāṃ
pitṛ-mukha-lokān sphurad-avalokān |
children.translated_text: Then, in that supreme assembly before his father's face and the people there, whose gazes sparkled,

children.text:
sukhayitu-kāmaḥ saha-sakhi-rāmaḥ
samadhura-veśaḥ sapadi viveśa ||JGc_1,2.24|| [kusumavicitrā]
children.translated_text: wishing to delight them, <s>Rāma</s> together with his friend, in sweetly beautiful attire, entered at once! // [<s>kusumavicitrā</s>]

children.text:
tat-tad-vṛndaiḥ kṛta-pariveṣaḥ
kṣoṇī-pṛṣṭha-sthita-vidhur eṣaḥ |
kramato dṛṣṭi-bhramaṇābhreṣa-
sthiti-kṛtam akhilān api viśiśeṣa ||JGc_1,2.25|| [mātrāsamaka]
children.translated_text: Attended by the various groups, served by them, this one, like the moon standing on the earth's surface,

children.text:
rahita-nimeṣa-prathitonmeṣa-
svaka-dṛk-preṣa-pracitānveṣaḥ |
abhavad aśeṣa-cchavi-saviśeṣa-
sva-tanu-śleṣaḥ śrī-harir eṣaḥ ||JGc_1,2.26|| [mātrāsamaka]
children.translated_text: by the unerring revolution of his gaze as he walked, distinguished all! // [<s>mātrāsamaka</s>]

children.text:
tad evaṃ labdha-paramānanda-majjaneṣu sarva-sajjaneṣu kula-paramparā-varāvāryaḥ kaścana sūtācāryaḥ katicid ātmīyān parivārya peśala-veśau kāka-pakṣa-keśau kaucid bālakau purataḥ sandhārya tatra prāṭa, pāṭhayāmāsa ca tāv āśīrvāda-virudam | tau ca cātakānām antas-taḍitvantam iva sāgarāṇāṃ vāri-nidhim iva, dhana-cintācitānāṃ cintāmaṇim iva, jyotir-maṇḍalānāṃ vyoma-maṇḍalam iva, teṣām āśrayaṃ tam ekaṃ śrī-vraja-rāja-kumāram ālokayām āsatuḥ | tataś ca tau sa-parivāram eva taṃ pārāvāra-rahita-śobhāvāra-vārāṃ-nidhiṃ nidhyāya kṣaṇa-katipayam anudhyāya ca svajana-stambhita-patanārambhau mūrcchā-prāyam ṛcchataḥ sma | tad-upariṣṭād eva kathañcid viśiṣṭatām āviṣṭau sagadgadaṃ jagadatuḥ,
"jayāśeṣa-cintā-ratna-nīla-ratnākara vraja-dharaṇī-dhara! jaya dharaṇī-bhārāvatāra-vitīrṇa-dharaṇī-dhara-śeṣa-paryantāśeṣa-sukha-samāja vraja-yuvarāja! jaya nija-vaṃśāgra-vraja-kīrti-dhvaja-samāna-śubhra-dhāma śrī-balarāma! jaya jaya!" iti |
children.translated_text:
Thus, while all the good people were immersed in supreme bliss, a certain chief bard (<s>sūtācārya</s>), the crest-jewel of all bards, irreproachable in the succession of hereditary families, surrounding some of his own retinue, presenting before him two boys of delicate dress and locks of hair like crow's-wing, came there and had them recite a benedictory poem. And those two gazed upon that sole refuge, the glorious prince of <s>Vraja</s>, as <s>cātaka</s> birds gaze upon the lightning-bearing [cloud] within, as [thirsty ones gaze upon] the ocean's reservoir, as those anxious about wealth gaze upon a wish-fulfilling gem, as the celestial spheres gaze upon the firmament. And then, having contemplated that ocean of beauty without limit or far shore, together with his retinue, meditating for a few moments, they nearly fainted, their fall arrested by their own people, and attained a swoon-like state. Just barely recovering from above that state and attaining distinction, they stammered:
'Victory, O mine of the blue sapphire that is the jewel of all thought, O upholder of the earth of <s>Vraja</s>! Victory, O prince of <s>Vraja</s>, session of complete bliss extending to the end of <s>Śeṣa</s> (the infinite serpent), who is the upholder of the earth descended to relieve the earth's burden! Victory, O <s>Śrī Balarāma</s>, of white radiance equal to the banner of the fame of <s>Vraja</s> — the foremost of your own dynasty! Victory, victory!'

children.text:
punaś ca kamala-locanaṃ vilocantāv ūcatuḥ,
  "rohiṇy-udyad-vidhuḥ pakṣa iva kṛṣṇaḥ sva-janmanaḥ |
  so' yaṃ yaśodānandaḥ san yaśodānanda-nandanaḥ ||JGc_1,2.27|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And again, gazing at the lotus-eyed one, they said:
'The dark (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) fortnight is like the moon rising from <s>Rohiṇī</s>, of his own birth — that very one, being the joy of <s>Yaśodā</s>, is the son of <s>Yaśodā's</s> joy (<s>Nanda</s>)!' // [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: punaś ca sāścaryam,
children.translated_text: And again, with wonder:

children.text:
"yaśaḥ praśaṃsanti budhā mudhāgiraḥ
sarvatra śaśvad viśadaṃ bhaved iti |
aho, yaśodā yad asūta sā yaśas
tat kṛṣṇa-rūpaṃ purato vilokyatām" ||JGc_1,2.28|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: 'The wise praise fame in vain, saying that everywhere it should always be spotless! Ah! That fame which <s>Yaśodā</s> gave birth to — behold it before us in the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' // [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: tataḥ śrīmān vraja-rājaḥ supralāpaṃ lalāpa, "sarva-sūta-cūḍā-ratna, ratnacūḍa, kāv etau sukumārau kumārau?"
children.translated_text: Then the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> spoke eloquently: 'O crest-jewel of all bards, <s>Ratnacūḍa</s>, who are these two delicate youths?'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "sarva-sampad-virājamāna, śrīmad-vraja-rāja, mama bhāgineyau |"
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'O glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, radiant with all prosperity — they are my sister's sons.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca, "katamāyā bhaginyā bhāga-dheya-rūpāv etau?"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Of which fortunate sister are these two, in the form of [her] good fortune?'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "asapatna-ratna-garbhā-pate! ratnavatyāḥ | sā caiṣā bhavad-apūrva-pūrva-puruṣa-puṇya-darśanāya kṛta-parāmarśā samāgatāsti | namaskaroti ceyam |"
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'O lord of the gem-womb with no rival! Of <s>Ratnavatī</s>. She has come with deliberate intention to behold your venerable ancestors of unprecedented [glory]. And she pays her respects.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca, "bhagini, bhāgadheyena vardhasva |"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'O sister, may you flourish by [your] good fortune!'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "deva, mama bhaginī-patir apy ayaṃ sumati-nāmā |"
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'O lord, this one is the husband of my sister, named <s>Sumati</s>.'

children.text:
vrajarājaḥ sasmitam uvāca, "bālye dṛṣṭo' yaṃ nātīva niṣṭaṅkituṃ śakyate |"
[75] taṃ ca satkṛtyovāca, "mānya, svayam agrataḥ samagram ehi" iti pṛṣṭavāṃś ca, "samprati bhavatāṃ kutra bhavanam?"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said with a smile: 'He was seen in childhood — it is not very easy to recognize him [now].' [75] And honoring him, he said: 'O revered one, come forward yourself with everyone,' and asked: 'Where is your home at present?'

children.text: sa uvāca, "rājavīra, nīradhitīra eva |"
children.translated_text: He said: 'O heroic king, on the bank of <s>Nīra</s> (a river).'

children.text: upananda uvāca, "tarhi dūrād abhyāgato' yam abhyāgataḥ |"
children.translated_text: <s>Upananda</s> said: 'Then this one has come as a guest from afar!'

children.text: atha vadana-sudhā-karāṃśu-sudhā-snapita-dṛgantaḥ smita-madhurādharāvṛta-kunda-koraka-dantaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam iva pṛṣṭavān, "kiṃ-nāmānāv etau?"
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, with the corners of his eyes bathed in the nectar-rays of his moonlike face, with jasmine-bud teeth covered by sweet-smiling lips, asked as if with thirst: 'What are the names of these two?'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "prāṇi-koṭi-nirmañchanīya-nakha-koṭe, madhukaṇṭha-snigdhakaṇṭha-nāmānau |"
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'O you whose nail-tips are to be worshipped by tens of millions of beings! Their names are <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> (Honey-throat) and <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> (Tender-throat).'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca, "samāna-nāmānau dṛśyete |"
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'They appear to have identical names.'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "sahajāv etau sahajāv eva |"
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'These two are innately identical, innately indeed.'

children.text: upananda uvāca, "ratnacūḍa, kiṃ khalu bhavad-vidyām anavadyād adhītavantāv etau?"
children.translated_text: <s>Upananda</s> said: '<s>Ratnacūḍa</s>, have these two indeed learned their faultless learning from you?'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "atha kim, ākasmikatayā vismāyakau guṇa-viśeṣāv apy anayoḥ staḥ |"
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'Why not? Yet there are also two qualities in them that are surprisingly spontaneous.'

children.text: upananda uvāca, "kau tau?"
children.translated_text: <s>Upananda</s> said: 'What are those two?'

children.text: ratnacūḍa uvāca, "sarvajñatā tad-avitā kavitā ca |" iti | [86] tataś ca sarve sāścaryaṃ paśyanti sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> said: 'Omniscience, and its guardian — poetic power.' [86] Then all gazed upon them with wonder.

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca, "mānya sumate, kuta etat-prabhāva-bhāvitav etau?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'O venerable <s>Sumati</s>, from where have these two acquired such a manifest power?'

children.text: sumatir uvāca, "viśva-pāvana, svaccha-kīrte, pṛcchyetām etāv eva |"
children.translated_text: <s>Sumati</s> said: 'O purifier of the universe, O you of spotless fame! Let these two themselves be asked.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca, "āyuṣmantau, yuṣmad-vṛttenāsmākaṃ cittaṃ vismayam evāviveśa, tasmād apanīyatām ayam |"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Long-lived ones! By your conduct, our mind has entered nothing but amazement; therefore, please dispel this [wonder].'

children.text: tau ca sāñjali-vacasā vyānañjatuḥ, "śrī-goloka-loka-deva, śrī-guru-prasāda eva sarvatra durvāraṃ kāraṇam iti tatrabhavanta evānubhavanti |"
children.translated_text: And the two, with palms joined in salutation, declared: 'O God of the people of glorious <s>Goloka</s>! The grace of the glorious <s>Guru</s> is everywhere an irresistible cause — this your lordships themselves experience.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca, "ke khalv īdṛśa-mahā-mahimānas te?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Who indeed are those of such great glory?'

children.text: atha tau punar ghaṭita-kara-puṭāv ūcatuḥ, "sugṛhīta-nāma-dheyā mad-vidha-bhāga-dheya-rūpāḥ sarva-sukha-varṣi-śrī-devarṣi-caraṇāḥ |"
children.translated_text: Then those two, with hands folded again, said: 'The venerable feet of the divine sage <s>Śrī Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), who showers all happiness, whose name is well-known, and who is the very destiny of people such as ourselves.'

children.text: atha sarve' py ūcuḥ, "tarhi nāścaryam idam |"
children.translated_text: Then all said: 'Then this is not surprising!'

children.text: punaḥ tāv ūcatuḥ, "samprati ca yad-upadeśād vṛndāvana-deśam āgatā vayam | nūnaṃ yat-prasādād eva deva-varga-durgama-samadhigamasya bhavābhibhava-bhāvana-bhāvanasya tad etad bhavadīya-vaibhava-pradeśasya praveśe sadeśa-rūpatāṃ yātāḥ sma |" [94] punaś ca sarve sāścaryam idaṃ paśyanti sma |
children.translated_text: Again those two said: 'And now, it is by his instruction that we have come to the region of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. Surely, by his grace alone, having attained the fitness for entering this domain of your Lordship's majesty — which is inaccessible to the hosts of gods, and which subdues the condition of worldly existence — we have arrived.' [94] And again all gazed upon this with wonder.

children.text: tataś ca śrī-kṛṣṇaś cintitavān, "āṃ āṃ, cirān mamāpy anayor āgamanaṃ sphuraṇa-mayam āsīt" iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> reflected: 'Ah yes! For a long time their arrival had been appearing in my consciousness as a flash of intuition.'

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇānumatānugatatayā śrī-rāmas tu samīpam āgamya vraja-rājam uvāca, "bṛhat-tāta, tayor anayoḥ kautukaṃ draṣṭum utkaṇṭhitāḥ smaḥ |"
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (Balarāma), following <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa's</s> consent, came near and said to the King of <s>Vraja</s>: 'Dear elder father, we are eager to see the wondrous skill of those two!'

children.text: tad anumodya punar vrajarāja uvāca, "ratnacūḍa, adya dinam ārūḍham | prāghuṇāś ca ta ete ghuṇākṣara-nyāyenopalabdhāḥ, tad eṣām ātitheya-vastubhir avitatham ātithyam evādya vidhīyatām |" pārśva-vartinaś cādiṣṭavān, "dīyatām ebhyo varṣaṃ yāvad bhogyā varīyasī samagrā sāmagrī, sā ca yathaivāsmākaṃ tathaiva | prātar ārabhya tu sabhyāḥ samāhūyantāṃ kautukāvalokāya |"
children.translated_text: Approving that, the King of <s>Vraja</s> again said: '<s>Ratnacūḍa</s>, today the day has begun. And these honored guests have been obtained as if by the maxim of the chance formation of letters by wood-worms (<s>ghuṇākṣara-nyāya</s>) — therefore, let true hospitality be arranged for them today with the proper provisions of hospitality.' And he instructed those nearby: 'Give them the entire most excellent collection of provisions for enjoyment for a full year, and that to be just as for ourselves. And from tomorrow morning, let the assembly be convened for the viewing of their art.'

children.text: atha puraskṛtopanandeṣu vrajajana-vṛndeṣu tatra jñāpita-nijānandeṣu tathā teṣu sūteṣu ca kṛta-sarva-kleśa-varjaneṣu bhojya-bhogya-yogya-vastubhiḥ prastuta-visarjaneṣu madhyāhnaḥ so' yam ahnāya vyatīta iti rājñe vijñāpya vijñāta-sakala-tattvaḥ śrīmān mahā-sattvaḥ śrīpatir api śrī-rāmādi-sahita-gatis tat-tan-namanādi-kramān niṣkramya prasthitavān | tatra ca,
children.translated_text: Then, with the groups of <s>Vraja</s>-folk led by <s>Upananda</s>, their own joy made known there, and those bards too being relieved of all hardship, with provisions of food and enjoyment duly presented and concluded — that midday of the day having passed — after informing the king, the glorious one of great power, the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, himself knowing all truths, together with <s>Śrī Rāma</s> and others, having completed the sequence of bowing and such, departed and set forth. And there:

children.text:
buddhir eva suhṛdām anumene
taṃ gavānugataye na manas tu |
sā hi mantra-sacivaṃ suvicāraṃ
pāti tat tu rahitārgala-kāmam ||JGc_1,2.29|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: It was only intelligence that guided the friends regarding his going to follow the cows — not the mind; | for that [intelligence] guards the minister of counsel, wise deliberation, | while the mind [guards only] desire with its barriers open. || (JGc 1,2.29) [svāgatā meter]

children.text:
atho vanaṃ prati calitaḥ sahāgrajaḥ
samitrakaḥ pṛthu muralīm anādayat |
yataḥ śrutād bata puratas tu tasthuṣāṃ
supūrṇatābhavad atiśūnyatānyataḥ ||JGc_1,2.30|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: Then, setting out toward the forest together with his elder brother, | accompanied by friends, he sounded forth his broad flute | upon a path graced by the playful branch-tips of fruit-laden trees; | from which sound, those standing before became supremely full, | and from elsewhere, supremely empty! || (JGc 1,2.30) [rucirā meter]

children.text:
tadā guru-vyavahitim āgatā mudā
parasparaṃ paśupa-sutāḥ karair yutāḥ |
sabhāgataṃ jahasur adhītya kasyacid
vacas tadā skhalitam anūdya cāpare ||JGc_1,2.31|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: Then, having come out of the elders' supervision with joy, | the cowherd boys, hand in hand with one another, | laughed at the speech of someone who had recited with a mistake, | and others then repeated the stumble. || (JGc 1,2.31) [rucirā meter]

children.text: hāse coparatābhāse rāma uvāca, "bhaṅgura, madhumaṅgala, mātṛbhir asmāsu vinīyamāneṣu bhavān kim avispaṣṭam ācaṣṭa, ævrajeśvari, kathayiṣyāmy ahaṃ rahaḥ' iti | kintu tābhir āveśavaśān nāvakalitam |"
children.translated_text: When the laughter seemed to subside, <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) said: 'O rogue <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>! While our mothers were instructing us, what did you say rather indistinctly? — "O queen of <s>Vraja</s>, I shall tell it in private!" But they did not notice it in their excitement.'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uccair vihasya nimīlya ca maunam ālalambe | kṣaṇād uvāca ca, "hanta, śantamam api tad vismṛtam iva |"
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, laughing loudly and then closing his eyes, assumed silence. After a moment he said: 'Alas! Even that most peaceful [secret] seems to have been forgotten.'

children.text: rāma uvāca, "priyasakha, śapathaṃ prathayāni, tathyaṃ kathyatāṃ: kiṃ tat?"
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said: 'Dear friend, I shall make you take an oath! Let the truth be told: what was that?'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca, "yajñopavītāya śape, nānyathā prathayāni | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'I swear by my sacred thread — I shall not speak otherwise! For:"

children.text:
"dāntena damitaḥ so' haṃ śamitaḥ śānta-cetasā |
jñaptena jñapitaḥ pūrṇenācāryeṇāsmi pūritaḥ ||JGc_1,2.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
tena channena cābhūvaṃ chāditānṛta-vāk punaḥ |
kathaṃ vā spāśitān kuryāṃ guṇāṃs tān spaṣṭam iṣṭadān" ||JGc_1,2.33|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Trained by the self-controlled one, tamed by the peaceful-minded, | instructed by the knowledgeable, I was filled by the complete <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher). || (JGc 1,2.32) [anuṣṭubh]
By him who was secretive, I too became one whose false speech was concealed; | how then could I make visible those qualities which clearly grant what is desired?' || (JGc 1,2.33) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: "kintu yuvayor vadhūnāṃ cājñām ājñāya paraṃ vijñāpanīyaṃ tāsu, tan na cen na |"
children.translated_text: 'But recognizing the command of your brides as well, I should report [only] to them — if not [to them], then not [at all].'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca, "unmatta, prathamam āvayor āvedaya |"
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'O madman! First report to us two!'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca, "yadi na khidyāthe |"
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'If you won't be upset.'

children.text: ubhāv ūcatuḥ, "nahi nahi |"
children.translated_text: Both said: 'Not at all! Not at all!'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca, "evam uccaiḥkāram api vivakṣāmi, tayor anayor yathāsvaṃ preyasībhiḥ saha sā sā śreyasī vidyā nādyāpi vicchidyamānā vidyate, yan muhur ārabhyata eva vanābhyantare keli-kalaha-pralāpa-kalāpaḥ" iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'Then I shall speak even at the top of my voice: that excellent knowledge of those two with their respective beloveds has not yet been interrupted — namely, within the forest, a series of amorous quarrels, babbling, and prattling is constantly being initiated!'

children.text: tataś ca kṛṣṇaḥ savyena pāṇinā tad-apasavyaṃ bāhuṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭha-madhyamābhyāṃ tad-adhara-puṭaṃ mṛdu niṣpīḍya smayamāna uvāca, "suṣṭhu ghuṣṭa-paṭṭa-ḍorakeṇa tad idaṃ sīvyate cen, munitām āpadyate viprakīrṇa-buddhir ayaṃ yan mitra-vipraḥ |" madhumaṅgalas tu tadvan mudrita-mukha evāmbū-kṛta-nirasta-grasta-vacanatayā vyaktavān, "tathā ced antar-lobhanam anyatra tu durlabhaṃ nija-gṛhān matsyaṇḍī-khaṇḍa-cayam ādāyākhaṇḍa-kālam eva man-mukhaṃ pūrayathaḥ | tataḥ kathaṃ vā kim-arthaṃ vā vāṇī-vyayaṃ karavāṇi? tad etad api sevanam eva bhaṇyate |"
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seizing his left arm with his right hand, and gently pinching his lower lip between the right thumb and middle finger, said with a smile: 'If this is sewn shut with a well-tied cord of silk, then this friend-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> of scattered wits will attain silence.' But <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, his mouth similarly sealed, unable to speak with his words swallowed and blocked, managed to say: 'If so, then as an inner bribe — something otherwise hard to obtain from one's own home — you must fill my mouth ceaselessly with heaps of <s>matsyaṇḍī</s> (sugar-candy) chunks! Then why and for what purpose should I expend speech? That too is indeed called service!'

children.text: rāmaḥ sasmitam uvāca, "utkocaś cāmiṣam eva bhaṇyate, tad api brāhmaṇāḥ kāmayeran?"
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) said with a smile: 'A bribe is indeed called meat — would even <s>brāhmaṇas</s> desire that?'

children.text: tad evaṃ sakhi-sabhāsatsu hasatsu svayaṃ sa tu narma-paṭur baṭuḥ sa-tṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṣaṇam āliṅgya preṅkholayan prakaṭaṃ jahāsīti sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, while the friends sitting in the assembly laughed, that witty student (<s>baṭu</s>), himself a master of humor, eagerly embraced <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> for a moment, rocking him playfully, and laughed openly.

children.text: atha sarva-guṇa-śālī vanamālī bahala-kutūhala-kalita-cittatayā calitaḥ, sakhibhir valitaḥ, phalita-śākhi-śākhā-śikhā-lalitenādhvanā dhenūr labdhvā veṇu-dhvanim udbhāvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then the garlanded one (<s>Vanamālī</s>, Kṛṣṇa), adorned with all virtues, his mind filled with abundant curiosity, set out, surrounded by friends, and upon reaching the cows on a path graced by the charming branch-tips of fruit-laden trees, produced the sound of his flute.

children.text: tataś ca dhenūpalakṣaṇatayā sarvāṇi yadākṛkṣanta, tadā sāścaryaṃ nabhasthaḥ kaścid āha sma,
children.translated_text: When, with the cows as the pretext, everything was attracted, then someone in the sky said with wonder:

children.text:
"sarvaḥ pravāhaḥ sarvatra
svānukūlyena karṣakaḥ |
veṇu-dhvani-pravāhas tu
prātikūlyena karṣati |" ||JGc_1,2.34|| [anuṣṭubh] iti |
children.translated_text: 'Every stream everywhere draws [things] | in its own favorable direction; | but the stream of the flute-sound | draws in the adverse direction!' || (JGc 1,2.34) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
anantaraṃ ca--
gāvaḥ svān ṛṣabhān bhujaṅgama-bhujaḥ ṣaḍjān pikāḥ pañcamān
anye ca pratipadya tān nija-nijān suṣṭhu svarān veṇutaḥ |
āścaryeṇa vikarṣaṇaṃ muhur aho mohaṃ tathā bhejire
sarve ced asakṛt kva sāntvana-vidhiṃ kurvantu ke vā tadā? ||JGc_1,2.35|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: And then — | The cows [drew] their own bulls, the serpent-armed one [drew] the <s>ṣaḍja</s> notes, the cuckoos the <s>pañcama</s> notes, | and others too, receiving their own respective notes from the flute, | were repeatedly drawn away with amazement — ah! They fell into such a trance! | If all [are entranced] more than once, who then can perform the act of reviving them? || (JGc 1,2.35) [śārdūlavikrīḍita meter]

children.text:
svayam api mohaṃ bheje yadi nija-veṇu-dhvanau kṛṣṇaḥ |
syād urvaritaḥ ko vā, jīvaḥ sa hi sarva-jīvasya ||JGc_1,2.36|| [upagīti] iti |
children.translated_text: If <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself also fell into a trance at his own flute-sound, | then who would remain? — For He is the very life of all that lives! || (JGc 1,2.36) [upagīti]

children.text: kintu hanta, veṇu-rava-śravaṇa-sukha-vistāra eva tatra nistārāya babhūva | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: But alas! The very expansion of the joy of hearing the flute-melody became the means of deliverance there. For:

children.text:
mohe' pi svapna-kalitaṃ niśamya muralī-kalam |
parasparaṃ jāgratas te paśyanti sma sa-vismayam ||JGc_1,2.37|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Even in their trance, hearing as if in a dream the melody of the flute, | they awoke and looked at one another with wonder. || (JGc 1,2.37) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś ca svasthī-bhūteṣu teṣu samutthiteṣu gāḥ prati prasthiteṣu ca madhur madhura-smitam uvāca, "brāhmaṇān prati duranudhyānasya phalaṃ sadya eva jātaṃ nidhyātam | yad aho mama mūkatvam anudhyātaṃ sarva-madhyam adhyāsīnenaikena, sarvasyaiva tu mūkatvaṃ jātam |"
children.translated_text: Then, when they had recovered, risen, and set out toward the cows, <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Madhumaṅgala</s>) said with a sweet smile: 'The fruit of improper meditation upon <s>brāhmaṇas</s> has been immediately produced — just witness it! For ah, my muteness was meditated upon by one seated in the midst of all, and the muteness of everyone was produced!'

children.text:
evam eva tena saha hasantas te māthura-deśa-deśa-rūpa-go-nideśa-
vacanatayā,
children.translated_text: Thus, laughing with him, they led the cows toward the <s>Yamunā</s> with the herding-calls of the <s>Māthura</s> country's dialect:

children.text:
sambodhane hihīty ūcuḥ kṣepe jihijihīti tu |
dhīrīha iti viṣkambhe gāṃ netuṃ yamunām amī ||JGc_1,2.38|| [anuṣṭubh]
cokāraṃ pāthasaḥ pāne jhiri-kāraṃ viyojane |
tasmāt payasa utthāne cakrus tiritirīti te ||JGc_1,2.39|| [anuṣṭubh]
stambhayitvāmbhasas tīre go-saṅkhyā go-gaṇān atha |
sambhālya sambhṛtānandāḥ kṛta-snānādikā jaguḥ ||JGc_1,2.40|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
For calling they said '<s>hihī</s>'; for reproach '<s>jihijihī</s>'; | for restraining '<s>dhīrīha</s>' — [thus] these [boys] led the cows to the <s>Yamunā</s>. || (JGc 1,2.38) [anuṣṭubh]
For drinking water they used '<s>co</s>'; for separating [from water] '<s>jhiri</s>'; | for making them rise from water, they made the sound '<s>tiritirī</s>'. || (JGc 1,2.39) [anuṣṭubh]
Having stopped [the cows] on the water's bank, | counting the herds of cows, | overflowing with joy, having bathed and performed other duties, they sang. || (JGc 1,2.40) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
prahāpitaṃ pratiśiśu mātṛbhis tadā
subhojanaṃ surabhita-yojanaṃ mudā |
hariḥ sakhīn pari pariveṣayan hasan
parīkṣitaṃ sakṛd akṛta svajihvayā ||JGc_1,2.41|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: The food sent by the mothers for each child then, | well-prepared, fragrant, [spreading its scent] a <s>yojana</s> far — with joy | <s>Hari</s>, laughing, serving the friends all around, | tasted it once with his own tongue. || (JGc 1,2.41) [rucirā meter]

children.text: tataś cācaritācāmaḥ śrīdāma-dāma-sudāma-vasudāmādibhiḥ saha karpūra-pūrita-khapurānukūla-svarṇa-varṇa-parṇa-śubhratāvakīrṇa-cūrṇa-maya- tāmbūla-pūrṇa-kapola-lola-kuṇḍala-maṇḍanānana-lakṣmīkaś cakṣur-vijita-nālīkaḥ svajanāvaloka-nābhīkaḥ śrīla-gopālaḥ svālayāya cacāla | yathā,
children.translated_text: Then, having performed the mouth-rinsing, together with <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Dāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, <s>Vasudāma</s> and others, the glorious <s>Gopāla</s> (Kṛṣṇa) — with cheeks filled with betel leaf made of camphor-filled powder of golden-colored leaves of pleasing purity, with swaying earrings adorning his face's beauty, with eyes surpassing lotuses, with a glance at his own folk that was like a nave [hub], set forth toward his own abode. As follows:

children.text:
śanaiḥ śanaiḥ sarabhasam anya-vanyayā
sa tarṇayan surabhi-tṛṇāni saurabham |
vraja-sthitān prati virahākulībhavan
bakāntakaḥ praticalati sma taiḥ saha ||JGc_1,2.42|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: Gradually, gradually, with haste, making the fragrant <s>Surabhī</s> cows | cross with different forest-cows [and] fragrant grasses, | growing restless with longing toward those situated in <s>Vraja</s>, | the slayer of <s>Baka</s> was returning along with them. || (JGc 1,2.42) [rucirā meter]

children.text:
vidhāya gā gokula-sammukhīnā,
mahā-taru-cchāyam upāsya kṛṣṇaḥ |
devopadeva-stuti-gīta-vādyaṃ
śṛṇvan muhuḥ prāpa taṭaṃ vrajasya ||JGc_1,2.43|| [upajāti]
children.translated_text: Having directed the cows toward <s>Gokula</s>, | having rested under the shade of a great tree, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, | hearing the music, songs, and praises of gods and demigods, | again and again reached the edge of <s>Vraja</s>. || (JGc 1,2.43) [upajāti meter]

children.text:
gīr-vāṇair divya-yānaiḥ pathi pathi munibhir mantra-yogādi-siddhair
gavyābhir ghrāṇa-dṛgbhis tad-anugata-narair dṛṣṭi-deśe saradbhiḥ |
goṣṭha-sthair unnata-sthaiḥ praṇihita-vadana-śrīmayūkhaḥ samantān
netrābja-prānta-lakṣmī-kalita-sukha-kulaḥ pūrṇa-veṇur viveśa ||JGc_1,2.44|| [srāgdharā]
children.translated_text: By the gods in divine chariots, on each path by sages accomplished in <s>mantra</s>-yoga and other <s>siddhis</s>, | by the cows through [their] noses and eyes, by the men following them with glances at the horizon, | by those in the cow-settlement standing in elevated places, with faces directed [toward him] — with radiant beauty in all directions, | the beauty of the lotus-petal corners of his eyes gracing the happy lineages, he entered with his full flute. || (JGc 1,2.44) [sragdharā meter]

children.text:
hambā-rāvaḥ paśūnāṃ pramada-kala-kalaḥ pāśupālya-vrajānāṃ
stotrāsāraḥ surāṇāṃ nigama-samudayāvṛtti-ghoṣas tv ṛṣīṇām |
itthaṃ sāṃrāviṇānta-vadhira-sama-daśām āgate sarva-loke
veṇoḥ sūkṣmo' pi nādaḥ sa jayati nitarāṃ yaḥ samastaṃ bhinatti ||JGc_1,2.45|| [srāgdharā]
children.translated_text:
The lowing of the cattle, the melodious warbling of the cowherd communities,
the ceaseless hymns of the gods, the chanting of the entire collection of <s>Vedas</s> by the sages —
thus, when the entire world has reached a state as if deafened by all these sounds,
the subtle note of the flute prevails supremely, for it pierces through everything. // [<s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text: atha vana-kula-gokulābhyāṃ mithaḥ sukham abhimukham āgatayor mahatāṃ samūhayor mahodadhi-tulyayoḥ saṅgamaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; yathā nityam eva tathānubhavinām api divaukasāṃ camatkṛtir ajāyata; yatra śrī-govinda eva svayam indavati sma, svayam eva ca veṇu-śikṣayā dheṇūḥ pṛthak pṛthag avātastambhat |
children.translated_text: Then, of the two great hosts — the forest community and the <s>Gokula</s> community — coming face to face with mutual happiness, a confluence occurred, like that of two great oceans. As always, even the celestial beings who constantly experience it were struck with wonder. There, <s>Śrī Govinda</s> himself led the way, and by the instruction of his flute alone, he brought each cow to a standstill, one by one.

children.text: tatra goṣṭhād bahir lambhita-muhur-upaṣṭambhānāṃ dohanādi-karmaṇā gavāṃ tarṇakādīnām api śarma nirmāya, dugdhāya janān puro vidhāya, savayobhiḥ savayobhir āvṛtau sarveṣāṃ madhya-vṛttau suvṛttau gopuram āvrajantau gṛhāya vrajantau, svakula-yaśodādi-purandhrī-rāji-nīrājitau rājitau lājādibhir abhivṛṣṭau samam eva samasta-nayana-dṛṣṭau, goṣṭhābhyantaraṃ praviṣṭau samam eva nija-nija-preyasī-samākṛṣṭi-paṭu-dṛṣṭi-viśiṣṭau nihata-danujau rāma-rāmānujau caraṇa-mārjana-vījanādibhir viśaśramatuḥ |
children.translated_text: There, having first ensured the comfort of the cows, calves, and others through the milking and other tasks performed outside the cow-settlement with constantly renewed support, having set the people before him for the sake of the milk, the two — surrounded by companions of their own ages, moving in the midst of all, of noble conduct — entered through the great gateway toward home, going to their residence. Greeted with <s>nīrājana</s> (lamp-waving ceremony) by the line of ladies led by <s>Yaśodā</s> and others of their own clan, resplendent, showered with parched rice and the like, beheld equally by the eyes of all — having entered the inner cow-settlement, equally distinguished by the keen glances attracting their respective beloveds, the two slayers of demons, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), rested through foot-washing, fanning, and the like.

children.text: tatra kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ jananī-janita-lālana-nirmāṇa-śarmānubhūya, snāna-dhāmani sambhūya nija-sevā-kṛj-jana-kārita-majjanādibhiḥ, suveśatayā vibhūya, punar jananī-sanīḍam evājagmatuḥ |
children.translated_text: There, having experienced for a few moments the happiness created by their mother's caressing, entering the bathing chamber and being bathed and attended to by their personal servants, having become splendidly dressed, they returned again to the very nest of their mother.

children.text: tataś ca sandhyāṃ gamayitvā janakādibhiḥ saha bhojana-līlāṃ janayitvā bahiḥ-sabhā-bhāgam āgamya nānā-bandhu-janatayā samāgamya tad-viśiṣṭau sūpaviṣṭau babhūvatuḥ, [121] yatra nānā-guṇi-śateṣu samāgateṣu tābhyāṃ sukumāratā-prabhūtābhyāṃ kumāra-sūtābhyāṃ saha sumati-ratnacūḍāv āvavrajatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having passed the twilight hour, having engaged in the play of dining together with their father and others, having come to the outer hall and gathered with various kinsmen, the two, distinguished among them, were well-seated. [121] There, when hundreds of accomplished persons had assembled, the two tender princes — <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Ratnacūḍa</s> — arrived together with them.

children.text: tataḥ śrīmatā goloka-sāmrājyavatā bhojanādikaṃ pṛṣṭayos tayoḥ parama-hṛṣṭayoḥ, śrīyuta-rāmānujas tu nijānuja-vad eva tau sūta-tanūjāv āhūya bhūyasā snehena sadeśam upaveśayāmāsa | nija-vraja-vāsi-sūtādīnāṃ prabhūtānāṃ bhavyāni kāvyāni tair eva śrāvayāmāsa ca | tataś ca tau parama-hṛṣṭau santau sva-guṇa-kalāpaṃ saphalayituṃ balavad utkaṇṭhitavantau |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the sovereign of <s>Goloka</s>, having inquired about their dining and so forth — both of them being supremely delighted — summoned those two sons of the <s>sūta</s> (bard) as if they were his own younger brothers, and with great affection seated them at a place of honor. He had them recite the excellent poems of the distinguished bards dwelling in his own <s>Vraja</s>. And then, those two, being supremely delighted, intensely desired to bring their own array of talents to fruition.

children.text:
atha prahara-mātrāyāṃ rātrāv ācarita-yātrāyāṃ nandita-sarva-samājena śrī-vraja-rājena samajyā-pradhāneṣu prātar navya-kāvya-śravaṇa-nimantraṇam
apavarjya visṛjyamāneṣu, taṃ nija-janakam anujñāpya kanaka-vasanas tau sukumārau sūta-kumārau kare gṛhītvā spṛhāntaraṃ hitvā mātṛ-gṛhāntaḥ saṅgatavān | mātaraṃ prati tayoḥ prasaṅgaṃ saṅgamitavāṃś ca |
children.translated_text: Then, when a <s>prahara</s> (three hours) of the night had been spent in festivities, the king of <s>Vraja</s>, having delighted the entire assembly, extended to the foremost assembly-members an invitation for the hearing of new poetry on the following morning, and as they were being dismissed, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having taken leave of his father, took the two delicate bard-princes by the hand, dressed in golden garments, and abandoning other desires, entered his mother's quarters. He brought about the meeting of those two with his mother.

children.text: tatas tu tāṃ sarva-stutāṃ tau kumāra-santau sukha-sāraṃ sambhavantau vividham evaṃ vicāritavantau, "kim iyam asya gokula-kula-candrasya kṣīra-nīradhi-gambhīra-velā? kiṃ vā pūrṇa-tad-udayākara-rākā-sākāratayā labdha-mad-vidha-dṛṣṭi-melā? kiṃ vā prācī dig evam ānandanayā racita-tanayā? vastutas tu tanaya-viṣaya-dayā kila sphurad evam udayatayā śītalī-kṛta-loka-samudayā" iti |
children.translated_text: Then, those two youthful princes, experiencing the essence of happiness in meeting that universally praised one, contemplated in various ways: 'Is this the deep shore of the milk-ocean that is the moon of the <s>Gokula</s> clan? Or has she, by assuming the full-moon form of its rising source, attained the union of the gaze of ones such as us? Or is the eastern direction itself thus fashioned with a son made of bliss? In truth, the compassion that relates to the son, by manifesting thus as a rising [moon], has cooled the entire multitude of the world!'

children.text: atha sā ca parama-ramaṇīya-caritā madhureṇa vyavahārādinābhy-avahārādinā vastrālaṅkārādinā ca pracurataram eva snehaṃ tayor ācaritavatī |
children.translated_text: And she, of supremely charming conduct, with sweet behavior, manner, garments, ornaments, and the like, displayed her affection toward those two most abundantly.

children.text: tataś ca tayor maṅgalāya mātaram āśiṣaś citvā, vāsasam āsādanāya cānujñā-vitaraṃ yācitvā svayam api snehāveśa-maya-tan-nideśa-vaśatayā viśramāya saṃveśa-veśma praviśan sarva-sukha-sāraḥ śrī-gopādhipati-kumāras tau sūta-sutau svena yutau vidhāya śrī-rādhikā-sadeśam āsāditau cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then, having offered blessings to their mother for the welfare of those two, and having requested her permission to retire for sleep, he himself — the prince of the chief of cowherds, the essence of all happiness, entering the sleeping chamber for rest by the force of her instruction imbued with loving emotion — arranged those two sons of the bard to be together with him, and brought them to a place near <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>.

children.text: āsannau ca tau vidyud-āvaliṣu tad-adhidevatām iva, kamalinīṣu kamalālayām iva, sarva-sampattiṣu sad-anukampām iva, guṇa-śreṇiṣu sa-vinaya-nītim iva, hari-rati-jātiṣu mahā-bhāva-sampadam iva, nikhila-sakhīṣu śrī-rādhām īkṣāmāsatuḥ |
children.translated_text: And as they drew near, they beheld <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> as if she were: among rows of lightning, their presiding goddess; among lotus-groves, the dweller of the lotus (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); among all fortunes, true compassion; among chains of virtues, disciplined conduct; among the species of love for <s>Hari</s>, the treasure of <s>mahābhāva</s> (the highest ecstasy); and among all <s>sakhīs</s> (companions), <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> herself.

children.text: atha tāṃ paśyantāv eva prema-vaśyaṃ tāv ātmānam ajānantāv ātmanā kṛṣṇa eva sāntvayāmāsa, sāntvitau ca tau taṃ ca tāṃ ca nicāyya cintayāmāsatuḥ,
children.translated_text: Then, as they were gazing at her, those two, overcome by love, not knowing themselves, were themselves soothed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. And being soothed, they contemplated both him and her:

children.text:
"indranīla-ruci-jīvanaṃ mahaḥ
svarṇa-varṇa-nikarākara-prabhā |
yac ca yā ca cayanaṃ tayor idaṃ
dvandvam ādi-rasa-sāra-kāraṇam ||JGc_1,2.46|| [rathoddhatā] iti |
children.translated_text:
'A radiance that is the life of the luster of a sapphire,
and a splendor that is the source of a mass of golden hue —
he and she, and this coupling of the two,
is the cause of the essence of the primordial <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).' // [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text: atha kaṃsa-ripuṇā paricāyitayoś ca tayor eṣā sa-kautukaṃ bāladeva-rayor iva kumāra-varayoḥ saśarma sanarma ca puraskāraṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then, when those two were introduced by the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), she, with curiosity, honored those two excellent princes — like <s>Baladeva</s> and his companion — with both comfort and playfulness.

children.text: tataḥ saṅginaḥ pradāpya mātula-gṛham eva tau prasthāpya śrī-govindaḥ sva-mohana-mandiraṃ praviveśa saṃviveśa ca | tatra,
children.translated_text: Then, having sent his companions away and dispatched those two to the maternal uncle's house, <s>Śrī Govinda</s> entered his own enchanting palace and lay down to rest. There:

children.text:
āyāte ramaṇe sasambhramam upāgamyāsanādi-kriyām
ācarya vyajanādibhiḥ svayam asau sevāvadhānaṃ dadhe |
śayyāyāṃ tvaritaṃ gate punar iyaṃ līnā sakhīyācitāpy
āsīt kvāpi kadāpi tatparicitā nāsmītivad vyañjatī ||JGc_1,2.47|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[131] tatra sakhīnāṃ vacanam,
"adṛṣṭe darśanotkaṇṭhāṃ dṛṣṭe tu tvam apahnutim |
sarvadā kurvatī kṛṣṇe kīdṛśīti na lakṣyase ||JGc_1,2.48|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
When the beloved arrived, she hastily approached and performed the duties of offering a seat and the like,
and with fan and other implements, she herself devoted attention to his service.
When he quickly went to bed, she, though entreated by her <s>sakhīs</s> (friends), remained hidden
somewhere, sometimes, as if indicating 'I am not the one familiar with him!' // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
[131] There, the words of the <s>sakhīs</s>:
'When he is unseen, you bear longing to see him; when seen, you feign indifference.
Always acting thus toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — what kind of woman are you? No one can discern!' // [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
tataḥ sakhībhyāṃ sugṛhīta-bāhur
nītāpi madhye-gṛham āyatākṣī |
stambhena bāhyena tathāntareṇa,
kṛtāvalambā cakṛṣe priyeṇa ||JGc_1,2.49|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
Then, though led by two friends who firmly grasped her arms
to the center of the room, the wide-eyed one,
supported outwardly and inwardly by pillars of <s>stambha</s> (stupefaction),
was drawn by her beloved. // [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text:
balena kṛṣṭā hariṇāpy analpaṃ
talpaṃ gatāsīn milituṃ ca lolā |
tathāpi nāyād ṛjutāṃ tu kintu
karākariprāyatayā sasañja ||JGc_1,2.50|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
Forcefully drawn by <s>Hari</s>, she went to the not-insignificant bed,
eager to unite with him;
yet she would not come to straightforwardness, but rather
clung to him with the manner of one feigning resistance. // [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text:
amilana-haṭha-kṛd yadāmilad vā
harim atha bhedayiteyam āśu kena |
dvayam api caritaṃ na citram asyā
yad alam asau rasa-rūpatām ayāsīt ||JGc_1,2.51|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
When she stubbornly refused to close her eyes, or when she did close them —
who could then separate her from <s>Hari</s>?
Both behaviors of hers are not surprising,
for she had become the very embodiment of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). // [<s>puṣpitāgrā</s>]

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, accompanied by <s>Sanātana</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>!

children.text: gopāla raghunāthāpta- vraja-vallabha pāhi mām ||JGc_1,2.52||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gopāla</s>! O beloved of <s>Vraja</s>, dear to <s>Raghunātha</s> — protect me! //

children.text:
iti śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
goloka-vilāsa-vikāsanaṃ dvitīyaṃ pūraṇam |
||2||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopālacampū</s>,
the second chapter, called 'The Blossoming of <s>Goloka</s> Pastimes.'
||2||

children.text: pūrṇaḥ śrī-goloka-vilāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrī Goloka-vilāsa</s> (Sports of Goloka) is complete.

children.text: atha tṛtīyaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Third Chapter.

children.text:
kṛta-pūraṇa-varti-tṛṣṇa-
śrī-kṛṣṇa-janma-sampan-mayam
children.translated_text:
Filled with the wealth of the birth of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,
whose thirsting is in the wick of fulfillment.

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, accompanied by <s>Sanātana</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>!

children.text: gopāla raghunāthāpta-vraja vallabha pāhi mām ||JGc_1,3.1||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gopāla</s>! O beloved of <s>Vraja</s>, dear to <s>Raghunātha</s> — protect me! //

children.text: tad evaṃ praśasta-śāstrāvalokataḥ śrīmān golokaḥ prastutaḥ | yatra lokābhivyakta-tad-abhivyakta-vaibhava-bhedād dvidhāpi vṛndāvana-vaibhavaṃ vibhāvitam | yatra ca lokānabhivyakta-vaibhave cintāmaṇi-maya-kamalākāra-gokula-prakāraś cāvikalam avakalitaḥ | yatra ca sapta-prakoṣṭhā goṣṭhādhipati-purī varṇanābhir urīkṛtā | yatra ca prātar aucitī-cita-kṛti-prabhṛti śrī-hari-caritaṃ pracāritam | yatra ca gopa-rāja-rājita-sakala-bhājita-sabhāyāṃ bhavya-kāvya-vijña-sarvajñatātimanojña-prajña-sūta-vaṃśa-prasūta-kumāra-dvayāgamanam anavadyaṃ varṇitam | yatra ca vraja-rājādibhis tat-kathā-śuśrūṣā prathayāñcakre ity api nigaditam | tad-anantaram atra tu tat-kathā vitāyate |
children.translated_text: Thus, the glorious <s>Goloka</s> has been presented through the examination of the authoritative scriptures. There, the glory of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> has been envisioned in two aspects, distinguished by the difference between its splendor manifest to the world and its splendor not manifest. There, in the glory not manifest to the world, the form of <s>Gokula</s> as a lotus made of wish-fulfilling gems has been fully discerned. There, the seven-gated city of the chief of the cow-settlement has been depicted in descriptions. There, <s>Śrī Hari's</s> pastimes beginning from the morning have been narrated according to propriety. And there, the arrival of the two princes born of the <s>sūta</s> (bard) lineage in the assembly graced by the king of <s>Vraja</s> — all-knowing, charming, learned in the auspicious poetry — has been described as faultless. And there, the eagerness to hear their narrative by the king of <s>Vraja</s> and others has been stated. After that, here, that narrative is unfolded.

children.text: anthānyedyur brāhma-muhūrtam ārabhya pūrvavad eva pūrvaja-rāmaḥ sarvaṃ parvati sma | bhojanaṃ punar aikāntikam eva nityam iva tad-dine jātam | yathā jñāpayanti sma śrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇāḥ - "tāta! prātar eva gobhiḥ śobhiṣyamāṇatāṃ sambhavatā bhavatā tābhyaḥ samagrānuttama-grāsān prādeśya mad-ādeśyatayā yat kiñcid upayujya svayam añcitavyam |" iti |
children.translated_text: Now, on the next day, beginning from the <s>Brāhma-muhūrta</s> (the hour before dawn), <s>Rāma</s>, the elder, celebrated everything as before. The meal, however, was entirely private that day, as it always was. As the glorious father's feet instructed: 'My son! In the morning, having displayed your splendor with the cows, having offered all the best morsels to them by my command, having partaken of something yourself as directed by me, you should proceed.'

children.text:
bhojanaṃ, yathā-
agrye sadmani ratna-pīṭha-mahitau rāmājitau tad-vadhū-
hastebhyaḥ parigṛhya mātṛ-yugalenānnādi paryāpitam |
bhuñjānau sakhibhiḥ sunarma-valitaṃ prasmāyayantau ca tad-
yugmaṃ tena ca parvaṇā parijanaṃ sarvaṃ sukhācakratuḥ ||JGc_1,3.2|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
The meal, as follows:
In the foremost hall, honored upon jeweled platforms, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, receiving food and the like
from the hands of their two wives and the two mothers — were served to satisfaction.
Eating, and while making their companions laugh with fine wit,
that pair, and he, and by that festive occasion, they made the entire retinue happy. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: bjhojanānantaraṃ tu sāsraṃ nibhālayantyāḥ sasmitaṃ cākarṇayantyāḥ śrīmatyā mātṛ-dvitīyāyāḥ purastād agrajena sakhibhiś ca sukhada-nānā-vārtāṃ vartayati śrī-vraja-rāja-kumāre vraja-nareśādeśaḥ praviveśa-"vatsa! sabhāsadaḥ sabhāyāṃ sabhājitāḥ śobhante | tau ca sūta-sutau svasampradāyam ādāya vartete" iti |
children.translated_text: After the meal, before the glorious mother accompanied by her co-mother — who was gazing with tearful eyes and listening with a smile — while the prince of <s>Vraja</s> was conversing with his elder brother and companions about various pleasant news, the command of the king of the cowherd settlement arrived: 'My child! The assembly-members are honored and adorned in the assembly hall. And the two sons of the bard are ready with their own tradition.'

children.text: tadā ca-
sa tu jananīm anujānatīṃ praṇamya
children.translated_text: He bowed to his mother who gave her consent,

children.text: drutam anurāmam iyāya sabhya-vṛndam |
children.translated_text: and swiftly, accompanied by <s>Rāma</s>, went to the assembly of the refined.

children.text: dvayam api tad atha prakāśa-yuktaṃ
children.translated_text: Both [<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], endowed with radiance,

children.text: kumuda-suhṛt kumudākarāyate sma ||JGc_1,3.3||
children.translated_text: became like the moon turning a bed of night-lotuses into a lake of lotuses. //
And then —

children.text: tatrābhyantaraḥ sabhā-valaya-praveśa-dvāraṃ paritaḥ stambha-paṅkti-sakta-gṛhākāraṃ yat pañcamaṃ loka-sahasrādhāratā-samucitākāraṃ pūrva-dig-gataṃ pūr-dvāraṃ, tasya bahir-antaratayā ghaṭita-sūkṣa-jāla-randhra-jālena kuḍyena dvidhā-vibhakta-dīrghatā-vidhānasya tiryaktayā madhya-sthitena nimna-vartmanā bahira-antar-labdha-kuṭṭima-catuṣṭayasya bahiḥ-kuṭṭima-dvaya-valita-ratna-pīṭha-ghaṭāsu yathāyatham upaviṣṭā mudāviśiṣṭās te vibhrājante sma |
children.translated_text: There, within the inner assembly-circle, at the entrance gateway, shaped like a house with rows of pillars attached on all sides, which was the fifth [gateway], of a form suitable to support thousands of people, facing east — as the eastern gate — its length divided in two by a wall fitted with a network of fine lattice-work openings on both its outer and inner sides, with a sunken path running through the middle crosswise, having obtained four pavements on the outer and inner sides — upon the rows of jeweled seats arranged along the outer pair of pavements, those who were seated, distinguished by joy, shone resplendent.

children.text: yasminn udīcī-kuṭṭima-taṭa-ghaṭitām avācī-mukhatayā vibhrājinīṃ rājim adhikṛtya virājamānaḥ śrī-vraja-rājas tasya tu savya-tat-taṭa-ghaṭitāṃ prācī-mukhatayā śrī-nidhānāṃ śreṇim āśritya datta-sukha-samājaḥ śrī-vraja-yuva-rājas tathāpasavyatas tat-taṭa-gata-kuḍya-sanīḍa-ghaṭitāṃ prācīmukhatayā sukha-karīm āvalim āsādya param ahitaḥ kṣiti-surottama-samūha-sahitaḥ purohitaḥ samya-virājate sma | tatrāvācī-kuṭṭima-gatāś ca kecid ābhīra-vīrā virājante sma |
children.translated_text: In which, presiding over a row arranged along the northern pavement-border, shining with a southward orientation, the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> was resplendent. On his left, along the border of that same pavement, with an eastward-facing row sheltering the treasury of <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), bestowing happiness upon the assembly, the glorious young prince of <s>Vraja</s> [was seated]. And on the right, along the wall bordering that same pavement, upon a comfortable row arranged with an eastward orientation, the supreme earth-born priest (<s>purohita</s>), supremely beneficial, accompanied by an assembly of the best among earthly <s>suras</s> (brāhmaṇas), shone resplendent. And upon the southern pavement were seated certain valiant cowherd warriors.

children.text: tataś ca tayoḥ kuṭṭimayor madhya-bhāgaś ca prāṅgaṇāt kramata unnataḥ | svayaṃ tu vistīrṇatayā nātinimnatayā ca kuṭṭima-sthānāṃ suṣṭhu dṛṣṭi-saṅgataḥ san vibhrājate sma | śrī-bhājaṃ goloka-samrājam abhimukhīkṛtya tayoḥ kuṭṭimayor madhyasthau puṭitāgra-hastau tau sūta-sutau tu saha sahāyam utthāna-yutau vartete sma | yayoś ca savyāpasavyataḥ sarve vrajasthāḥ sūtādiṣu sphurad-arhad-avasthā-viśiṣṭam upaviṣṭā vistīrṇatāsāṅga-prāṅgaṇe tu pare śiṣṭāḥ |
children.translated_text: And the middle portion between those two pavements was progressively elevated from the courtyard. It itself, by its breadth and moderate depth, being well-suited to the view of those standing on the pavements, shone resplendent. Facing the glorious sovereign of <s>Goloka</s>, the two sons of the <s>sūta</s> (bard), standing in the middle of those two pavements with palms joined at the tips, remained ready to rise together with their attendants. And to their left and right, all <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers were seated, distinguished by their respective positions of eminence among the bards and others; while those who remained on the broad courtyard connected to [the assembly] were refined [people].

children.text: iti sthite-
sarvasmād uccamāne maṇi-janita-mahā-siṃha-pīṭhe niviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Seated upon the great lion-throne made of jewels, elevated above all,

children.text: sādhviṣṭaḥ sat-prakīrṇādy-upavalita-karair bhrātṛ-madhyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: the most excellent one, having entered the midst of [his] brothers, with hands folded by [attendants] scattering fine [flowers] and the like,

children.text: dṛṣṭiṃ pīyūṣa-vṛṣṭiṃ vinidadhad asakṛt kṛṣṇa-vaktre sa-tṛṣṇaṃ
children.translated_text: placing his gaze — a shower of nectar — repeatedly upon <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> face with longing,

children.text: śrīmān goloka-rājaḥ sa-sadasi dadṛśe rājamānaḥ prajābhiḥ ||JGc_1,3.4||
children.translated_text: the glorious king of <s>Goloka</s> was beheld in his assembly, resplendent among his subjects. ||3.4||
This being established —

children.text:
śrī-śubhrāsana-tulikopari-milat-kāyādharāṃśo manāg
ālambād upadhāna-candra-valayasyeṣat tiro-vartanaḥ |
dhinvan sasmitayā dṛśā pariṣadaṃ śrī-rāma-dāmādimān
śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ samayātra sāmpratam api pratyakṣaval lakṣyate ||JGc_1,3.5||[7] tatra ca tasya varṇādikam evaṃ varṇyate-
children.translated_text:
Upon the cushion of the glorious white seat, with the lower part of his body resting lightly, slightly turned behind the crescent-shaped backrest-pillow, enlivening the assembly with a smiling glance — <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, accompanied by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Dāma</s>, and others, appears even now as if directly visible at that assembly-gathering. ||3.5||
[7] And there, his complexion and other [features] are described thus:

children.text: śyāme śyāma-daśām avāpa sahasā śoṇe tathā śoṇatāṃ
children.translated_text: In the dark, darkness suddenly attained [deeper] darkness; in the red, redness likewise;

children.text: pīte rociṣi pīta-dhāma vividhe vaividhyam āgād iti |
children.translated_text: in yellow radiance, a yellow abode — in the variegated, variegation was reached.

children.text: aṅgopāṅga-rucā harer jana-dṛśāṃ vīthir gatā tat-kṣaṇān
children.translated_text: The pathway of people's eyes, through the radiance of <s>Hari's</s> limbs and sub-limbs, in those moments

children.text: nānā-rūpa-gatīr naṭānupajahāseva smita-vyaṅgataḥ ||JGc_1,3.6||
children.translated_text: seemed to laugh at the various movements of an actor, through the hints of his smile. ||3.6||

children.text: kiṃ ca-
candro' yaṃ śyāma eṣa prthama-jaladharaḥ kāntibhir viśva-dīpaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This is the moon!' 'This dark one is the primordial cloud!' 'With his radiance, he is the lamp of the universe!'

children.text: śobhante vidyutas tā iha sapadi jahatyātma-sattām amūs tu |
children.translated_text: 'Those lightnings shine here, but instantly they abandon their own existence!'

children.text: nakṣatrāṇīha līnāny api bata kumate no nabhaḥ sā sabhāsāv
children.translated_text: 'The stars here have merged!' 'Fool, this is not the sky — this is the assembly!'

children.text: ity anyonyaṃ vinodād vivadanam udabhūt tatra śaśvat kavīnām ||JGc_1,3.7||
children.translated_text: Thus, a perpetual dispute arose there among the poets, debating with each other in jest. ||3.7||
Moreover:

children.text: tatraiva kasyacid anyasya kavitā-
children.translated_text: There, the poetry of yet another poet:

children.text: upari madhukarāvalī tadīyaṃ
children.translated_text: Above, a row of black bees — that belongs to him;

children.text: talam anu sasmita-nīla-vāri-jātam |
children.translated_text: below, a smiling blue lotus cluster;

children.text: tad anu ravi-sutācchavāri-pūraṃ
children.translated_text: and below that, a flood of water reflecting the Sun's daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>) —

children.text: sphurati sakhe kim iyaṃ sabhā navāsti ||JGc_1,3.8||
children.translated_text: friend, does this assembly shine anew? ||3.8||

children.text: athātma-sthāne yuktaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-rāmābhyāṃ prayuktaḥ prasiddha-nāmā śrīdāmā śrībhājaṃ vraja-rājam āvedya sadyaḥ pura-madhyam āsādya kṛtī śrī-vrajarājñī-prabhṛtir bahiḥ kuṭṭimāt kiñcid unnata-kuṭṭimam anu maryādām aṃśam apy aticarya sphuṭam upary upari ghaṭita-gātraṃ labdha-sannikṛṣṭi-dṛṣṭi-mātra-pātraṃ śreṇitayālaṅkṛtam aneka-nīrandhra-jāla-randhra-jālaṃ samayā samānīya pratīhāraṃ sapratīhāraṃ praṇīya dṛg-bhaṅgi-kalayā tāsām antaḥ-sabhā-saṅgitām abhinīya punas tayor aviprakṛṣṭa evopaviṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Śrīdāma</s>, of well-known name — appointed at his own place, engaged by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> — having informed the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, the receptacle of <s>Śrī</s>, and having immediately reached the center of the city, the capable one, leading the queen of <s>Vraja</s> and others from outside to a pavement slightly elevated from the [main] pavement, exceeding even the boundary of that section, bringing clearly into view a lattice-screen with tightly fitted body[-shaped windows], arranged in rows, which was merely a vessel for close-range viewing — having brought an inner passage with a doorkeeper, having conveyed their participation in the assembly through a gesture of the eyes, he sat down again at a place not far from the two [brothers].

children.text: yatra śrīmatāṃ mitrāṇāṃ saṅgatau madhumaṅgalo' pi raṅga iva tat-tat-prasaṅgena narma-bhaṅgibhiḥ śarma dātum aṅgīkurvann iva niviveśa |
children.translated_text: There, at the gathering of the glorious friends, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> too entered as if at an arena, undertaking to give delight through playful gestures on each successive topic.

children.text: tatra śrī-vraja-rājñī-
children.translated_text: There, the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: maṇi-maya-vara-pīṭhe yātṛ-mukhyāntarāle
children.translated_text: Upon an excellent jeweled throne, in the midst of the foremost visitors,

children.text: tanaya-nava-vadhūbhiḥ sevitārāt-pradeśā |
children.translated_text: attended in the surrounding area by the new brides of her son,

children.text: suta-mukha-vidhu-kāntiṃ sā gavākṣāt pibantau
children.translated_text: she, <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother, drinking from the lattice-window the moon-like radiance of her son's face,

children.text: suta-sucarita-tṛṣṇak kṛṣṇa-mātā vyarājīt ||JGc_1,3.9||
children.translated_text: thirsting for the noble deeds of her son, shone resplendent. ||3.9||

children.text: atha rājñā vrajasya madhuram ājñāpyate sma-"aye madhukaṇṭha-snigdhakaṇṭhau! vayam utkaṇṭhitāḥ smaḥ | tataḥ kiñcid uṭṭaṅkyatām |"
children.translated_text: Then the king of <s>Vraja</s> sweetly commanded: 'O you of honey-throated and sweet-throated [voices]! We are eager. Therefore, let some [performance] be commenced.'

children.text: tau ca sāñjalau vyānñjatuḥ-"deva! kiṃ prakramitavyam avalambya saṃvādavahe?"
children.translated_text: And those two, with palms joined, asked: 'O lord! What should we undertake as the basis for our discourse?'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"bhavantu sarvajñāv iti vijñāpanāyāsmadīya-kathābhibhir evāsmān vismāyayetām |"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Since you are all-knowing, astonish us with narratives that are our own!'

children.text: tāv ūcatuḥ-"yathā śiṣṭiḥ śiṣṭāgraṇī-caraṇānām | kintu śāvayor āvayor ekataraḥ samājñāpyatāṃ, yathānyataraḥ śrotā bhavati |"
children.translated_text: They said: 'As commanded by the feet of the foremost among the noble! However, of us two, who are but young [performers], let one be designated [to speak], so that the other may be the listener.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"dinam ekam ekam antarā pratyekam api tat-tad-rūpatām āpnotu | prakrāntā punar jyāyān eva jyāyān vidhīyate |"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Let each one, day by day alternately, assume each respective role. But the one who has begun shall continue as the elder [speaker] — the elder is thus appointed.'

children.text: tataś ca dhṛtotkaṇṭhaḥ sapadi madhukaṇṭhaḥ kṛtāñjalitayā nāndīṃ paṭhann akhilam ānandayati sma | yathā-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> (Honey-throat), holding his eagerness, immediately delighted everyone by reciting the <s>nāndī</s> (benediction) with joined palms. As follows:

children.text: śrīmān yo bhagavān svayaṃ vijayate brahmā surarṣir mahān
children.translated_text: The glorious Blessed Lord himself, who is victorious — <s>Brahmā</s>, the great divine sage,

children.text: vyāsas tat-prabhavaḥ parīkṣid api yāv ugraśravaḥ-śaunakau |
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s> who is his emanation, <s>Parīkṣit</s> too, and the pair <s>Ugraśravas</s> and <s>Śaunaka</s> —

children.text: śrīmad-bhāgavata-prathā-praṇayinas tān viśva-nistāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: those propagators of the glory of the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, the deliverers of the universe,

children.text: śrī-goṣṭhasya mahiṣṭhatāṃ prathayituṃ kamrān namaskurmahe ||JGc_1,3.10||
children.translated_text: to establish the supreme greatness of the glorious cow-settlement — we bow to those charming ones! ||3.10||

children.text: tataś ca-
paścād alpaṃ tāla-yugmaṃ gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: Thereafter, having taken a pair of small cymbals,

children.text: gāyantau dvau pārśvayor maḍḍu-vijñau |
children.translated_text: two [musicians] skilled in the <s>maḍḍu</s> (drum) singing on either side,

children.text: śrotā bhrātā yasya savyetarāgre
children.translated_text: the listener being the brother at the left-front —

children.text: so' yaṃ vaktā sarvam uccair didhinva ||JGc_1,3.11||
children.translated_text: this one, the speaker, enlivened everything loudly. ||3.11||
And then:

children.text: iti prakāre labdha-sāre punar madhukaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭhaṃ gāyan nṛtyan tat-tad-bhāvābhinayaṃ praṇayan kathām abhyādade |
children.translated_text: Thus, having obtained the essence in this manner, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, singing with eagerness, dancing, producing the dramatic representation of each emotion, took up the narrative.

children.text: atha kathārambhaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the narrative.

children.text:
yathā-atha sarva-śruti-purāṇādi-kṛta-praśaṃsasya vṛṣṇi-vaṃśasya vataṃsaḥ śrī-devamīḍha-nāmā parama-guṇa-dhāmā madhurāmadhyāsāmāsa | tasya cāryāṇāṃ śiromaṇer bhāryā-dvayam āsīt | prathamā dvitīya-varṇā, dvitīyā tu tṛtīya-varṇeti | tayoś ca krameṇa yathāvad āhvayaṃ putra-dvayaṃ prathamaṃ babhūva śūraḥ parjanya iti | tatra śūrasya śrī-vasudevādayaḥ samudayanti sma | śrīmān parjanyas tu mātṛvad varṇa-saṅkaraḥ iti nyāyena vaiśyatām evāviśya gavām evaiśyaṃ vaśyaṃ cakāra | bṛhad-vana eva ca vāsam ācacāra | sa cāyaṃ bālyād eva brāhmaṇa-darśaṃ pūjayati, manoratha-pūraṃ deyāni varṣati, vaiṣṇava-vedaṃ snihyati, yāvad vedaṃ vyavaharati, yāvaj-jīvaṃ harim arcayati sma | tasya mātur vaṃśaś ca vyāpta-sarva-diśāṃ
viśāṃ vataṃsatayā paraṃ śaṃsanīyaḥ | ābhīra-viśeṣatayā sadbhir udīraṇād eṣa hi viśeṣaṃ bhajate sma |
children.translated_text: As follows: Now, the crest-jewel of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> dynasty — praised by all <s>Śrutis</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like — named <s>Śrī Devamīḍha</s>, the supreme abode of virtues, dwelt in <s>Mathurā</s>. And that crown-jewel of the noble had two wives: the first was of the second <s>varṇa</s> (class, i.e. <s>Kṣatriya</s>), and the second was of the third <s>varṇa</s> (i.e. <s>Vaiśya</s>). Of those two, in due order, a pair of sons named respectively <s>Śūra</s> and <s>Parjanya</s> was first born. Of these, from <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> and others arose. But the glorious <s>Parjanya</s>, like his mother, by the principle of 'mixed <s>varṇa</s>,' entered the <s>Vaiśya</s> status and made the lordship and governance of cows his own. And he dwelt in <s>Bṛhadvana</s> (the great forest). And from his very childhood, he worshipped the sight of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, showered gifts that fulfilled desires, loved the <s>Vaiṣṇava Veda</s>, conducted himself according to the <s>Veda</s>, and worshipped <s>Hari</s> for as long as he lived. His mother's lineage too, as the crown-ornament of the <s>Vaiśya</s> people spread through all directions, is supremely praiseworthy. As he was specially identified by the wise as being of the <s>Ābhīra</s> (cowherd) kind, he was specially honored.

children.text: tathā ca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Manu</s> [says]:

children.text: brāhmaṇād ugra-kanyāyām āvṛto nāma jāyate |
ābhīro' mbaṣṭa-kanyāyām āyogavyāṃ tu dhigvaṇaḥ ||[Manu 10.15] iti |
children.translated_text: an <s>Ābhīra</s> from a daughter of an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>; and from an <s>Āyogavī</s>, a <s>Dhigvaṇa</s>.' [Manu 10.15]
'From a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and a daughter of an <s>Ugra</s>, one called <s>Āvṛta</s> is born;

children.text: ambaṣṭhas tu viśaḥ putryāṃ brāhmaṇāj jāta ucyate iti cānyatra | ataḥ pādme sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍādau yajñaṃ kurvatā brahmaṇāpy ābhīra-paryāya-gopa-kanyāyāḥ patnītvena svīkāraḥ prasiddhaḥ | eṣa eva ca gopa-vaṃśaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlāyāṃ saṃvalanam āpsyatīti | sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa eva tatra spaṣṭīkṛtam asti | tasmāt parama-śaṃsanīya evāsau vaiśyāntaḥ-pāti-mahābhīra-dvija-vaṃśa iti |
children.translated_text: And elsewhere: 'An <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> is said to be born from a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and a <s>Vaiśya</s> daughter.' Therefore, in the <s>Pādma Purāṇa</s>, in the beginning of the creation-section, the acceptance of a cowherd (<s>gopa</s>) girl — who is a synonym for <s>Ābhīra</s> — as wife by <s>Brahmā</s> himself while performing a sacrifice is well-known. And it is this cowherd lineage that will serve as the accompaniment in the pastimes of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. This is clearly stated in that very creation-section. Therefore, that great <s>Ābhīra</s>-<s>dvija</s> (twice-born) lineage within the <s>Vaiśya</s> [class] is indeed supremely praiseworthy.

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhena cāntaś cintitam-evam api kecid aho eṣāṃ dvijatāyāṃ sandeham api dehayisyanti | ye khalu śrīmad-bhāgavate kuru dvijāti-saṃskāram [10.8.10] iti gargaṃ prati śrī-vrajarāja-vacane, vaiśyas tu vārtayā jīvet ity ārabhya,
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> (Smooth-throat) thought inwardly: 'Even so, some will cast doubt upon their twice-born status! Those indeed [who note] in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, in the words of <s>Śrī Vraja-rāja</s> (Nanda) to <s>Garga</s>: "Perform the sacrament of the twice-born" [10.8.10]; and beginning with "A <s>Vaiśya</s> should live by trade":',

children.text: kṛṣi-vāṇijya-go-rakṣā kusīdaṃ tūryam ucyate |
children.translated_text: 'Agriculture, commerce, cow-protection — and the fourth is called usury;

children.text: vārtā caturvidhā tatra vayaṃ go-vṛttayo' niśam ||[BhP 10.24.20-21]
children.translated_text: trade is of four kinds — and we are perpetually engaged in cow-livelihood.' [BhP 10.24.20-21]

children.text: iti vrajarājaṃ prati śrī-kṛṣṇa-vacane, agny-arkātithi-go-vipraḥ [BhP 10.46.12] iti śrī-śuka-kṛta-gopāvāsa-varṇane, vyatirekatas tu dharma-rāja-caratāyām api vidurasya śūdra-garbhodbhavatayānyathā-vyavahāra-śravaṇe' py adhikaṃ viadhirāyiṣyante iti |
children.translated_text: In the words of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> to the king of <s>Vraja</s>; [and] in <s>Śrī Śuka's</s> description of the cowherd settlement: 'fire, sun, guest, cow, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' [BhP 10.46.12]; and even in hearing about the otherwise-treatment of <s>Vidura</s>, who was of <s>Śūdra</s>-womb birth, despite his conduct being that of a <s>dharma-rāja</s> — [such people] will raise further objections.'

children.text: atha sphuṭam ūce-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then he spoke openly: 'Then what [happened]?'

children.text:
madhukaṇṭha uvāca-sa ca śrīmān parjanyaḥ saujanya-varyeṇārjitena nijaiśvaryeṇāpi vaiśyāntara-sādhāraṇyam atīyāya, tac ca nāścaryam | yataḥ svāśrita-deśa-pālakatā-mānyatayā vadānyatayā kṣīra-vaibhava-plāvita-sarva-janatā-labdha-prādhānyatayā ca parjanya-sāmānyatām āpa ; yaḥ khalu prahlādaḥ śravasi, dhruvaḥ pratiśruti, pṛthur mahimaṇi, bhīṣmo durhṛdi, śaṅkaraḥ suhṛdi, svayambhūr garimaṇi, haris tejasi babhūva | yasya ca sarvair api kṛta-guṇanena guṇa-gaṇane vaśitāḥ sahasra-saṅkhyābhir apy anavasitā mātāmaha-mahā-vaṃśa-prabhavāḥ sarvathā prabhavante gopāḥ sopādhyāyāḥ svayam eva samāśritā babhūvuḥ | tat-sambandhāni ca vṛndaśaḥ yaṃ khalu śrīmad-ugrasenāgrīya-yadu-saṃsad-agraṇyas te samagra-guṇa-garimaṇy
agragaṇyam avalokayantaḥ sakala-gopa-loka-rāja-rājatā-sambalakena tilakena sambhāvayāmāsuḥ | yasya ca preyasī sakala-guṇa-varīyasī varīyasīnām āsīt | yasya ca śrīmad-upanandādayaḥ pañca-nandanā jagad evānandayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'And that glorious <s>Parjanya</s>, through the excellence of his noble character and by his own lordship earned thereby, surpassed even the ordinary status among the <s>Vaiśyas</s> — and that is not surprising. For, by his honor as protector of the region under his care, by his generosity, and by his preeminence through flooding all people with the wealth of milk, he attained equality with <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god). He in whom <s>Prahlāda</s> manifested in hearing, <s>Dhruva</s> in obedience, <s>Pṛthu</s> in grandeur, <s>Bhīṣma</s> in steadfastness, <s>Śaṅkara</s> in friendship, <s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā) in gravity, and <s>Hari</s> in splendor. And by the enumeration of his virtues made by all, even thousands in number could not exhaust [them] — [those] cowherds sprung from the great lineage of the maternal grandfather, capable in every way, accompanied by their preceptors, themselves became his dependents. And the groups related to him — those who were foremost in the assembly of the <s>Yadus</s> headed by the glorious <s>Ugrasena</s>, beholding him as the foremost in the gravity of all virtues, honored him with the <s>tilaka</s> (mark of distinction) signifying the sovereignty of all the cowherd people. And his beloved was the most excellent of all excellent women of all virtues. And his five glorious sons, beginning with <s>Upananda</s>, delighted the entire world.'

children.text: tathā ca vandinas tasya ślokaṃ ślokatām ānayanti-
children.translated_text: And his panegyrists bring this verse to fame:

children.text:
anyas tu jala-parjanyaḥ sukha-parjanya eṣa tu |
sadā yo dhinute sṛṣṭair upanandādibhir janam ||JGc_1,3.12||parjanyaḥ kṛṣi-vṛttīnāṃ bhuvi lakṣyo vyalakṣyata |
tad etan nādbhutaṃ sthūla-lakṣyatāṃ yad asau gataḥ ||JGc_1,3.13||

children.translated_text:
'Another is the rain-<s>parjanya</s> (cloud); this one, however, is the happiness-<s>parjanya</s>:
he who always delights people with his creations — <s>Upananda</s> and others.' ||3.12||
'<s>Parjanya</s> was observed on earth as the foremost among those of agricultural livelihood;
that this is not amazing is [only] because he has attained the state of being broadly visible.' ||3.13||

children.text: upamānti ca-
children.translated_text: And they compare:

children.text: upanandādayaś caite pituḥ pañcaiva mūrtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'These, <s>Upananda</s> and others, are the five very forms of their father,

children.text: yathānandamayasyāmī vedānteṣu priyādayaḥ ||JGc_1,3.14||
children.translated_text: just as, in <s>Vedānta</s>, <s>Priya</s> and the others [are forms] of the Blissful One (<s>Ānandamaya</s>).' ||3.14||

children.text: utprekṣante ca-
children.translated_text: And they imagine:

children.text: upanando' bhinandaś ca nandaḥ sannanda-nandanau |
children.translated_text: '<s>Upananda</s>, <s>Abhinanda</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Sannanda</s>, and <s>Nandana</s> —

children.text: ity ākhyāḥ kurvatā pitrā nander arthaḥ sudaṇḍitaḥ ||JGc_1,3.15||
children.translated_text: by the father who made [them bear] these names, the meaning of "<s>nanda</s>" (joy) has been well-wielded!' ||3.15||

children.text: tad evaṃ satīṣu sarva-sampattiṣu tasya putra-sampattis tu parama-ramaṇīyatām avāpa | nepathya-sampattiṣu vāsaḥ-sampattir iva | tatrāpi madhyama-suta-sampattiḥ sutarām aiśvaryāṇām avicchinna-sampatti-paṅktim anu madhyama-sampattir iva |
children.translated_text: Thus, amid all these various prosperities of his, his prosperity in sons attained supreme beauty — like the prosperity of garments among the prosperities of costume. And among those, the prosperity of the middle son was even more so — like the middle [jewel] prosperity in an unbroken row of prosperities of wealth.

children.text: atra kecid arjunam upamānīkurvanti | vayaṃ tu tasya madhya-sambadhyamānasya sarvānandanasya śrīmat-parjanya-nandanasya bālaka-paryāyeṇa tena pāṇḍu-tanayenopamānaṃ na manyāmahe | api ca paramodāreṣu ca sahodareṣu teṣu na kevalaṃ janmanā tāvan madhya-vartitayā so' yaṃ vartate | api tu sneha-sampadām āspadatayāpi na ca kevalaṃ teṣām kintu sarveṣām api | yena tasmin pitror apy adhikā sneharddhikāyā vardhiṣṇutā bhrātṝnām api sadā sukha-saṃvardhanī babhūva, na jātu spardhanī | na caitāvān udbhūtaḥ suguṇas tasminn udbhūtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, some propose <s>Arjuna</s> as a comparison. But we do not consider the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> to be a fitting comparison for the middle-related one, the delighter of all, the glorious son of <s>Parjanya</s>, even by the synonym '<s>bālaka</s>' (boy). Moreover, among those supremely generous brothers, he stands not merely in the middle position by birth, but also as the abode of the wealth of affection — and not merely of theirs, but of everyone's. By which, even the overflowing increase of affection for him from his parents, even more than [for the others], was always a fosterer of his brothers' happiness, never a cause of rivalry. Nor was such an abundant virtue born [in anyone else] as was born in him.

children.text: bhavati hi svayaṃ bhagavati tasya bhakti-viśeṣa-vyaktiḥ-yasyāsti bhaktir bhagavaty akiñcanā sarvair guṇais tatra samāsate surāḥ iti hi bhagavatī śrī-bhāgavata-gīr-devī |
children.translated_text: For there is indeed a specific manifestation of devotion in the Blessed Lord himself — 'One who has unflinching devotion to the Lord, in whom all virtues along with the gods reside' — for such is the Blessed Goddess <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, the divine speech.

children.text: tad etan madhukaṇṭhataḥ śrutvā śrīmad-upanandaḥ śrīmad-abhinandaṃ nīcair uvāca-vijñātā kathāṃ prakurvāṇasya kim asya para-hṛdaya-vijñatā ?
children.translated_text: Having heard this from <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, the glorious <s>Upananda</s> said softly to the glorious <s>Abhinanda</s> — 'Is it his knowledge of others' hearts that makes this narrator so knowing?'

children.text: athābhinandas tad avadhārya sāścaryaṃ madhukaṇṭham uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Abhinanda</s>, pondering that, said with wonder to <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> — 'And then? And then?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tad evaṃ sati nāmnā sumukhena kenacana gopānāṃ mukhena tasmai parama-dhanyā kanyā dattā | yā khalu sva-guṇa-vaśīkṛta-svajanā yaśāṃsi dadāti śṛṇvantyaḥ, kim uta paśyadbhyaḥ, kim utatarām bhaktimadbhyaḥ | tataś ca tayoḥ sāmpratam eva dāmpatyena sarveṣām api sukha-sampattir ajāyata, kim uta mātara-pitarādīnām |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'This being so, a supremely blessed maiden was given to him by a certain <s>gopa</s> (cowherd) named <s>Sumukha</s>, through the mouth [proposal] of the cowherds. She who, by her own virtues, had won over her own people, bestows fame upon those who merely hear of her — what then of those who see her, and what more of those who are devoted to her! And through the marriage of those two, just now, the wealth of happiness of everyone was born — what then of [the happiness of] the mother, father, and others!'

children.text: tad evam ānandita-sarva-janyu-vigata-manyuḥ parjanyaḥ sarvato dhanyaḥ svayam api bhūyaḥ sukham anubhūya cābhyāgārikatāyām abhyāgataṃ-manyaḥ śrī-govinda-padāravinda-bhajana-mātrānvitāṃ deha-yātrām abhīṣṭāṃ manyamānaḥ sarva-jyāyase jyāyase svaka-kula-tilakatāṃ dātuṃ tilakaṃ dātum iṣṭavān | śrī-vasudevādi-naradeva-gargādi-bhūdeva-kṛta-prabhāṃ sabhāṃ kṛtvā dattavāṃś ca |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, <s>Parjanya</s> — who had delighted all people, who was free from anger, blessed in every way — having himself experienced further happiness, and regarding a life devoted solely to the worship of the lotus-feet of <s>Śrī Govinda</s> as the desired course in household life — desired to bestow the <s>tilaka</s>-mark of headship of his own clan upon the eldest among all the eldest. Having convened an assembly graced by <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> and other <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Garga</s> and other <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he bestowed it.'

children.text: sa punaḥ pitur ājñām aṅgīkṛtya kṛta-kṛtyas tasyām eva śrī-vasudevādi-saṃvalita-mahānubhāvānāṃ sabhāyām āhūya sabhāvam utsaṅga-saṅginaṃ vidhāya madhyamam eva nijānujaṃ tena tilakena gokula-rājatayā sabhājayāmāsa |
