children.translated_text: 'He, having accepted his father's command and feeling his purpose fulfilled, in that very assembly — composed of those of great stature who had gathered, such as <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> and others — summoned [his son], and placing his own younger brother as the intimate one seated on his lap, making him the middle one, he honored that very younger brother of his with that <s>tilaka</s> [mark of kingship] over <s>Gokula</s>.'

children.text: atha tatrānuje saṅkucati sarvatra ca jane vismayaṃ sacamāne pitari ca rocamāna-locane sa covāca-mayedaṃ nāvicāram ācaritam, yataḥ sarva eva sneha-paramparāyāḥ parādhīnaḥ | sā ca sādguṇyasya, tac ca sarva-samañjasatāyāḥ | sā cātra yathā tathā na mad-vidhe | saiva ca khalu sarva-vaśīkāritāyāṃ svairitām arhati |
children.translated_text: 'Then, when the younger brother shrank back, and all the people marveled, and the father's eyes shone with approval, he spoke thus: "I have not done this inconsiderately, for everyone is subordinate to the chain of affection. And that [affection] is subordinate to genuine virtue, and that to perfect fitness for all. And such [fitness] is not found in one such as myself, not as it is here. And that [fitness] alone deserves freedom in the domain of universal mastery."'

children.text: kiṃ ca, sarvāntaryāmy apy enam evorarīcarīkarīti | dṛśyatām asyāṃ bhāsamānāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ sarveṣāṃ netra-paṭalī-ṣaṭpadaval-līlāyamānā kevalam asya mukhaṃ kamalam iva saṃvalate | tathā prathamata eva tad-ānukūlyam atrākalpyate | parikalpyatām apīdaṃ mama nāmnaiva | tasmād asmākam ayam eva rājeti |
children.translated_text: '"Furthermore, even the inner controller of all favors this one alone. See — in this shining assembly, the row of bee-like eyes of everyone, like a vine of play, settles only upon his lotus-face. Therefore, from the very first, favorable disposition toward him is established here. Let this be considered as [done] in my name alone. Therefore, he alone is our king!"'

children.text: athābhavat kusumaka-vṛṣṭibhiḥ samaṃ
children.translated_text: Then there arose, together with showers of flowers,

children.text: sphuṭa-dhvanir divam anu sādhu sādhv iti |
children.translated_text: a clear sound throughout the sky — 'Well done! Well done!'

children.text: sabhāsadām iha ca vikāsi-dṛṣṭibhir
children.translated_text: And here among the assembly-members, with blossoming gazes,

children.text: yathāsphuraj jaya-jaya-śabda-maṅgalam ||JGc_1,3.16||
children.translated_text: the auspicious sound of 'Victory! Victory!' burst forth! [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.3.16]

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-madhukaṇṭha-kṛta-jagad-utkaṇṭha-śrīman-madhukaṇṭha ! śrīmad-upananda-nandanayos traya eva madhyamā iti ko' yaṃ madhyamaḥ | kīdṛśī vā tasya samañjasateti sodāharaṇam ucyatām |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'O glorious <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, who through <s>Madhukaṇṭha's</s> narration has created longing in the world! Of the glorious <s>Upananda</s> and <s>Nandana</s>, the three middle brothers — who is this middle one? And what is his fitness like? Tell us with examples!'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-ekaṃ tāvad bhavan-manaḥ-prahlannatā-samucitaṃ pravahlikā-padyam idam anavadyaṃ pūryatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'First, let this one faultless riddle-verse, appropriate for delighting your mind, be completed by you.'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-kāmam |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'Gladly!'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said —

children.text: ākṛṣya mat-putram anena putrī-
children.translated_text: 'Having attracted my son, this one who has been adopted as a son

children.text: kṛtena bhūtiṃ bhajate sa eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: now enjoys prosperity.'

children.text: iti svayaṃ vetti na tena maitrīṃ
children.translated_text: 'He himself does not know the friendship [that motivates this]; so who

children.text: bhinatti ko' yaṃ vadane vadeti ||JGc_1,3.17||
children.translated_text: is this one who speaks thus on [another's] face?' [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.3.17]

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭhatayā śīghram eva sānandam uvāca-nanda eva iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, with eagerness, quickly and joyfully said — 'It is <s>Nanda</s> himself!'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-bhavatā jñātm evedam iti | tad etac chrūyatām-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'You have understood this correctly.' Now hear this —

children.text: svenālpena guṇena vāñchati nije pūjā-sukhe bhūyasī
children.translated_text: 'The world that, through its own small virtue, desires more honor-happiness for itself,

children.text: loko yas tu mahīyasāpi khalu tenaivānyadīye sadā |
children.translated_text: but through a greater person's virtue, always bestows it upon another's child —

children.text: so' yaṃ śrī-vrajarāja eva yad asau śūrāṅgajaṃ dhinvituṃ
children.translated_text: this is the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> himself, who, in order to nourish the son of <s>Śūra</s> (Vasudeva),

children.text: tat-tad-dhānim asoḍha sakhyam abhinnālpaṃ ca tasyāntaram ||JGc_1,3.18||
children.translated_text: bore his friend's wealth unselfishly — and the difference between himself and that friend was insignificant.' [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.3.18]

children.text: tataś ca tad etan madhukaṇṭha-sūkta-sudhākaram āsādya ratnākara ivocchalad-aṅga-taraṅgas tad-antar-bahiraṅga-sabhya-saṅghas tad-upari-hṛdayaṅgama-ratnāvaliṃ vikīrṇavān hṛdayāvaliṃ vā vitīrṇavān iti svayam api na bhidāṃ vidāmbabhūva |
children.translated_text: 'Then, having reached that nectar-moon of <s>Madhukaṇṭha's</s> well-spoken words, the assembly of inner and outer courtiers — like an ocean with surging waves of excitement — scattered a garland of heart-ravishing jewels over those words, or rather, bestowed a chain of hearts — and even Madhukaṇṭha himself did not perceive any distinction between the two.'

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'And then? And then?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tataḥ śrīmān asau dhanyaḥ parjanyaḥ śrī-govinda-padāravinda-bhajanāya vṛndāvanaṃ praviśan samāsata eva samasta-śāstra-sāraṃ pṛcchataḥ putrān upadideśa, yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'Then that glorious and blessed <s>Parjanya</s>, entering <s>Vṛndāvana</s> for the worship of the lotus-feet of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, in brief, instructed his sons who asked for the essence of all scriptures, as follows —

children.text:
kiṃ bhaya-mūlam adṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ śaraṇaṃ śrī-harer bhaktaḥ |
kiṃ prārthyaṃ tad-bhaktiḥ kiṃ saukhyaṃ tat-para-prema ||JGc_1,3.19|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'What is the root of fear? The unseen. What is refuge? The devotee of <s>Śrī Hari</s>. What is to be sought? Devotion to him. What is happiness? Supreme love for him.' [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.3.19]

children.text: tad evaṃ saha-bhārye vṛndāvanaṃ gate tasminn ārye śrīmān upanandaḥ sva-nāmānurūpaṃ śrīman-nanda-vraja-mahendra-sabhāyām ayantrita-mantritayā sthitavān | vicitravīrya-sabhāyāṃ bhīṣma iva | so' pi mantra-miṣeṇa viśeṣeṇa tad-ājñām eva gṛhṇan sarvaṃ sarva-kālaṃ surājā prajā-kulaṃ pālayati sma |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, when that noble one, together with his wife, had departed to <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the glorious <s>Upananda</s>, true to his own name, remained in the court of the great lord <s>Śrī Nanda</s>, king of <s>Vraja</s>, with unrestricted counsel-authority — like <s>Bhīṣma</s> in the assembly of <s>Vicitravīrya</s>. He too, under the pretext of counsel, received Nanda's commands especially, and ruled the clan of subjects well at all times, like a good king.'

children.text: tatra ceyaṃ caryācaritāścaryā babhūva, yathā-
children.translated_text: 'And there, this wonder of conduct transpired, as follows —'

children.text: maryādāṃ pitur ayam āvad eva sarvāṃ
children.translated_text: 'This one maintained all the propriety of his father completely,

children.text: dharmādir na vipadam eti yatra cārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: and where <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and others did not decline, wealth too did not suffer misfortune.

children.text: sampattir na punar abhūd amuṣya vaśyā
children.translated_text: Yet prosperity did not become subservient to this one,

children.text: yenāsau prasabham avāpa vṛddhim eva ||JGc_1,3.20||
children.translated_text: by which he forcefully attained only growth.' [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.3.20]

children.text: tad evaṃ sarva-samṛddhi-vṛddhi-siddhim āyāte rājanvati vraja-jana-jāte kalikāyamānā kācid utkalikā krameṇa vikāsam ayāmāsa | sarveṣāṃ prāṇa-tulyasya nija-kulyasya rājñas tasya santatir na jāyata iti | kālātyaye cāśā-vyatyayāt sarvaṃ janam atīva kṛcchram ānarccha | agrajādīṃs tu sutarām | śrīmad-vrajapati-jampatī tu prajāśāṃ pūrvata eva sandigdhi-digdhām api kurvāte sma, uttaratas tu viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, when all prosperity, growth, and accomplishment had arrived in the royal <s>Vraja</s> lineage, a certain bud of anxiety gradually blossomed. The offspring of that king — who was dear as life itself to all, of their own clan — was not being born. And as time passed, through the reversal of hope, all the people were greatly distressed — especially the elder brothers and others. But the glorious royal couple of <s>Vraja</s> had been daubing their hope for progeny with doubt even from before, and especially afterwards.'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-kathaṃ tat-preṣṭhāḥ putreṣṭyādikaṃ nānuṣṭhāpitavantaḥ ? kathaṃ vā vidagdhayor api tayoḥ sandigdhatā jātā | tathāpi parameśa-parayoḥ kathantarāṃ vā tad-āśā ? uttaratas tu viśeṣataḥ kathantamām ?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'How is it that those dearest kinsmen did not have the <s>putreṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for obtaining a son) and such rites performed? And how did doubt arise even in those two who are so wise? Moreover, for those two who are devoted to the Supreme Lord, how could there even be such hope? And why especially afterwards?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-anuṣṭhāpitam api tat tan na pratiṣṭhām āsasāda |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'Even what was performed did not attain fulfillment.'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-kathaṃ tat ? kathaṃ vānyad anyat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'How so? And how about the other things?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tathā hi, tat tad aśeṣa-sampattyor api dampatyo rahasi saṃvādo' yaṃ babhūva | yathā śrīmān patir uvāca-kuṭumbini! kim avalambī mama sanānāya vitānādi vitānayati śoka-vaśo' yaṃ lokaḥ ? yato mama saṅkalpa-kalpanā-samaye yādṛśāya sarvato vicitrāya putrāya cittaṃ kalpate | sa tu parama evāpūrvaḥ katham apūrva-viṣayatāṃ prāpnotu ? tata punar anyatra vacana-gocaraṃ racayituṃ saṅkucaty eva ceto-vṛttiḥ | yato yat khalu mayi dayā-parāyaṇasya śruti-pārāyaṇa-phalasya śrī-nārāyaṇasya rūpaṃ tato' pi madhurataraṃ katarad vā bhavet, parijāta-kusumād ākāśa-kusumam iva |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'Accordingly, despite the complete prosperity of both, the couple had this private conversation. The glorious husband spoke thus: "O mistress of the household! For what reason does this world, overcome by grief, prepare festival-canopies and the like for my bathing? For at the time when I form my wish, my mind conceives of a son who is entirely wonderful in every respect. But he is supremely unprecedented — how can the unprecedented be attained? Therefore, the activity of mind shrinks from fashioning such a wish into the domain of words. For what form could be sweeter than that of <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is devoted to compassion toward us, who is the fruit of studying the Vedas? — like a sky-flower compared to a <s>pārijāta</s> blossom."'

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhaś cintayāmāsa-asya tato' pi madhurataratvaṃ nāyuktam | yata etad uddiśya śrī-bhāgavata-padyam-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> reflected — 'That he should be even sweeter than that Nārāyaṇa is not unreasonable. For, with reference to this, there is the verse from the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>:'

children.text:
yan martya-līlaupayikaṃ sva-yoga-
māyā-balaṃ darśayatā gṛhītam |
vismāpanaṃ svasya ca saubhagarddheḥ
paraṃ padaṃ bhūṣaṇa-bhūṣaṇāṅgam ||[BhP 3.2.12] iti |
children.translated_text: the supreme abode, astonishing even to himself by the richness of its beauty — a body that is the ornament of ornaments.' [<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 3.2.12]
'That form which was assumed, displaying the power of his own <s>yoga-māyā</s>, suitable for his human sport,

children.text: atha sphuṭaṃ papraccha-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then he asked clearly — 'And then? And then?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-atha śrīmatī tat-patnī covāca-kīdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ tad iti kathyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'Then his glorious wife also said: "What kind of form is that? Let it be described."'

children.text: sa uvāca-
children.translated_text: He said —

children.text: śyāmaś cañcala-cāru-dīrgha-nayano bālas tavāṅka-sthale
children.translated_text: 'Dark-complexioned, with charming, restless, long eyes — a child on your lap,

children.text: dugdhodgāri-payodhare sphuṭam asau krīḍan mayālokyate |
children.translated_text: on your breast overflowing with milk — clearly playing — is beheld by me!

children.text: svapnas tat kim u jāgaraḥ kim athavety etan na niścīyate
children.translated_text: Is it a dream or is it waking? — this cannot be determined.

children.text: satyaṃ brūhi sadharmiṇi sphurati kiṃ so' yaṃ tavāpy antare ||JGc_1,3.21||
children.translated_text: Tell me truly, O wife: does he also flash before you within?' [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.3.21]

children.text: sovāca-śrīman ! mamāpīyam eva mano-vṛttir mati-vṛttim ativartamānā vartate | kevala-vilajjayā taj jātu bhavantaṃ na nivedayāmi | tasmād asmād asambhava-manorathān nivṛtti-śāstra-vicāram udyacchantau mana eva saṃyacchevahi |
children.translated_text: She said — 'O glorious one! This very same mental activity of mine also persists, surpassing even the activity of reason. It is solely out of shyness that I have never disclosed it to you. Therefore, from this impossible desire, let us undertake the study of the scriptures of renunciation and restrain the mind alone.'

children.text: sa uvāca-yadyapi mayāpy etad eva madhye madhye sphuṭam adhyavasīyate, tathāpy astoko vaśita-viśvodreko mahān sahāyaḥ śrīman-nārāyaṇa-deva eva śaraṇam iti citta-vṛttiḥ parivartate-yo' smākam adṛṣṭāśrutam idaṃ dṛṣṭam iva karoti | sa sarvaṃ kṛta-pūrvī tad api kurvīta |
children.translated_text: He said — 'Although I too arrive at this very conclusion clearly from time to time, nevertheless, the mental inclination turns thus: the great helper, the supreme lord <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s> alone — whose mastery surpasses the universe — is the refuge, who makes this unseen and unheard vision of ours appear as if seen. He who has done all things before could do even this.'

children.text: sovāca-deva ! tasya devasya kām api sevāyogyām evātra yogyām upalabhāmahe |
children.translated_text: She said — 'O Lord! For the service of that God, we find here one who is fit, indeed fit.'

children.text: sa uvāca-bāḍham | kintu kīdṛśī sā ?
children.translated_text: He said — 'Indeed! But what kind of service is that?'

children.text: sovāca-dvādaśī-vrata-rūpā |
children.translated_text: She said — 'In the form of the <s>Dvādaśī</s>-<s>vrata</s> (twelfth-day observance).'

children.text: sa sānandam uvāca-saṅgataṃ bravīṣi | mamāpy utkaṇṭhāṅkuritaṃ sphuritam etad evāsīt | tasmād adyārabhya samārabhyatām eṣa vrata iti |
children.translated_text: He said joyfully — 'You speak aptly! For this very resolve, sprouting from longing, had already flashed within me too. Therefore, let this vow be undertaken from today!'

children.text: tad evaṃ sampravadamānayor udbhavan deva-dundubhi-nādaḥ sarvam aticakrām |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, as the two were conversing, the sound of divine <s>dundubhi</s> drums surpassed everything.'

children.text: atha tayā vṛtta-sva-citta-vṛtti-prathayā tat-kathayā ślathitavāntaḥ śrī-vraja-dharitrī-kāntaḥ kānta-nijālaṅkāra-vāraṃ sūta-kumārāya vitatāra | śrīmatī vrajapati-patnī ca mahā-nīlamaṇi-maya-nāyakaṃ hāraṃ vihāpayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: 'Then the glorious lord of the earth of <s>Vraja</s>, his heart softened by that conversation which had manifested the activity of her own mind, extended to the son of the bard a set of his own dear ornaments. And the glorious queen of the king of <s>Vraja</s> had him wear a great necklace with a centerpiece of sapphire.'

children.text: atha sotkaṇṭhaṃ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tarhi kiṃ jātam ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said eagerly — 'Then what happened?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tena vratena pūrṇe varṣe bṛṃhite ca tarṣe yugapad eva deva-devaḥ svapne tayor āvirbabhūva, covāca ca-aho ! mayy atisaktau bhaktau kathaṃ nirvidya khidyāthe ? yo' sāv atasī-kusuma-suṣamaḥ sukumāraḥ kumāraḥ śaśvad evānubhavator bhavatoḥ kumāratayā sphurati | sa tu sadā bhavator evānugataḥ pratikalpaṃ svabhakti-pravartanāya divi mat-pravartita-droṇa-dharā-rūpa-kalāṃśa-kalāvatoḥ tad bhūri bhāgyaṃ ity ādi-rītyā brahmādy-alabhya-sākṣāt-tat-phala-sākṣātkārāya svayam eva pṛthivyāṃ bhavator bhavator eva bhavaṃ labhata eva æ acirād eva ca rucirā rucireṣā yuvayoḥ saphalatāṃ valitā |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'When a year had been completed through that vow, and their longing had intensified, the God of gods appeared to them both simultaneously in a dream and said: "Ah! How, being so deeply attached devotees to me, can you become despondent and distressed? That boy — dark as the flax flower, delicate — who constantly appears to you both, in your experience, as a child — he indeed always follows you! In every cosmic age, for the propagation of my own devotion, he descends in the artistic portion of a celestial cloud-form set in motion by me in heaven. Your great fortune manifests in this way" — and so forth. Thus, for the direct realization of the fruit unattainable even by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, he himself will take birth on earth, of you, as your very own — he shall indeed obtain birth soon! And this beautiful desire of yours shall be soon fulfilled with delight.'

children.text: tad evaṃ śrāvitābhihite tirohite ca paramahite bhagavati labdha-jāgarāv upalabdhāmṛta-sāgarāv iva ca mithas tad eva saṅkathayantau prathayantau ca parama-camatkāra-nivahaṃ vahataḥ sma |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, when the Blessed Lord — having been heard, having spoken, and having disappeared — the supreme benefactor was gone, the two, having awakened, finding themselves as if having obtained an ocean of nectar, narrating that very dream to each other and proclaiming it, bore a flood of supreme wonder.'

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ svagataṃ cintayāmāsa-tad evaṃ jātāny eva mama praśnānām uttārāṇi | tatra ca bhavator eveti yuktam evoktaṃ śrī-bhagavatā--prāg ayaṃ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ [10.8.14] iti vadato' py avyabhicāra-vacaḥ-pracāra-sargasya muneḥ śrī-gargasya prāyaḥ so' yam abhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> (Smooth-Throated) thought to himself: 'Thus the answers to my questions have already arisen. And in that regard, the Blessed Lord's statement, 'he is your son' — this was most fittingly said. For even the sage <s>Śrī Garga</s>, whose utterances are unerring, when saying 'Sometime before, this [child] was born as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>' [BhP 10.8.14] — his intention was likely this.'

children.text: śrī-bhagavatā saha sambandhaḥ kila kevala-prema-nibandhanaḥ-bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ [BhP 11.14.11] ity ādeḥ | atas tad-viśeṣasya tad-viśeṣa eva hetuḥ-ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmy aham [Gītā 4.11] ity ādeḥ | tatas tasmin vatsatāṃ satāṃ vātsalyābhidha eva premā pramāpayati |
children.translated_text: The relationship with the Blessed Lord is founded solely on pure love — as stated in 'I am grasped by devotion alone' [BhP 11.14.11] and similar texts. Therefore, the specific quality of that [devotion] is the cause of that specific [relationship] — as stated in 'As they surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly' [Gītā 4.11] and similar texts. Thus, in them, their calf-like tenderness confirms the love called <s>vātsalya</s> (parental affection).

children.text: tatra śrī-vasudevasya tad-aiśvaryālocanena vātsalyasya tāralyaṃ sāralyaṃ cāsāditam | śrī-vrajarājasya punas tad-vātsalyaṃ śaśvad udbuddhaṃ śuddham eva ca prasiddham | pitṛbhyāṃ putratayā tad-dhāraṇe kāraṇaṃ ca munibhir mana eva manyate | āviveśāṃśa-bhāgena mana ānakadundubheḥ [BhP 10.2.26] ity ādeḥ | dadhāra sarvātmakam ātma-bhūtaṃ kāṣṭhā yathānanda-karaṃ manastaḥ [BhP 10.2.18] ity ādeś ca | śrī-vraja-rājābhyām api manasā dhāraṇaṃ tasya kāryānyathānupapatti-siddhena bhakti-svābhāvyenaiva sambhāvyate | tatra ca sati sāmprataṃ tu viśeṣata eva sāmprataṃ parāvasthām anu kṛtāsaktau hi bhaktau tad-udayaḥ syāt | tasmāt tavaivātmajas tasya vasudevasya tu kvacit kārye nimitte jātaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: There, in <s>Śrī Vasudeva's</s> case, due to his perception of the Lord's divine majesty, his parental love attained both agitation and simplicity. But the parental love of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>) is well-known as eternally awakened and pure. The sages consider that the cause of both fathers bearing him as their son is the mind itself — as stated in 'He entered in partial form into the mind of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>)' [BhP 10.2.26] and 'She bore the all-encompassing one, who was her very self, in her mind, like the eastern direction bears the bliss-giving [moon]' [BhP 10.2.18]. The bearing of him in the mind by the royal couple of <s>Vraja</s> too is to be understood through the natural character of devotion itself, established by the logical impossibility of any other explanation. And in that case, his appearance would occur in devotion that has presently attained its supreme state with specific attachment. Therefore, 'He is your son; but for <s>Vasudeva</s>, he was born on some occasion, for some purpose.'

children.text: atha prakaṭam uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then he said aloud: 'And then? What happened next?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tad evaṃ paramārter upakaṇṭhatāṃ prāptāyām utkaṇṭhāyām ekadā sarve' narvācīnā vraja-vāsinaḥ sabhāvāḥ sabhāyāṃ militāḥ | militvā ca tad eva sotkaṇṭhaṃ suṣṭhu pratuṣṭuvuḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> (Honey-Throated) said: 'Thus, when the intense longing born of supreme anguish reached its peak, one day all the ancient inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s>, together with the assemblies, gathered in the assembly hall. And having gathered, they praised that [expected arrival] most ardently, with great longing.'

children.text: tadā ca tatraikā tāpasī kenacana snātakena samam āyātā | tāṃ ca mahā-prabhāva-lakṣaṇāṃ lakṣayitvā sarve samutthāyātithyam āvitathyena vidhāya vijñāpayāmāsuḥ-sākṣād bhagavato yogamāyeva kā tvam asi ? śrīman-nāradasyābhinava-tanur ivāyaṃ vā kaḥ ?
children.translated_text: And then, a certain female ascetic arrived there together with a <s>snātaka</s> (graduated student). Perceiving her as bearing the marks of great power, all rose, offered hospitality in truth, and asked: 'Who are you — as if the divine <s>Yogamāyā</s> (Illusive Power) of the Blessed Lord in person? And who is this — like a new form of the glorious <s>Nārada</s>?'

children.text: sā ca sahāsam āha sma-paurṇamāsī-nāmnī kātyāyanī ca kumāra-śramaṇā ca pārikāṅkṣiṇī cekṣaṇikā cāsmi | ayaṃ ca madhumaṅgala-nāmā snātakaḥ śrī-nārada-prakṛtiḥ | āvāṃ ca vidyā-viśeṣeṇaitad-vayaskāv eva sadā vidyāvahe |
children.translated_text: And she, smiling, said: 'I am named <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, and I am <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, and <s>Kumāraśramaṇā</s>, and <s>Pārikāṅkṣiṇī</s>, and <s>Cekṣaṇikā</s>. And this <s>snātaka</s> is named <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, who is of the nature of <s>Śrī Nārada</s>. And we two, by a special power of knowledge, always appear to be of this [youthful] age while bearing great learning.'

children.text: te ūcuḥ-etāvatī kṛpā kṛpaṇeṣu katham asmāsu kṛtā ?
children.translated_text: They said: 'How has such mercy been bestowed upon wretched ones like us?'

children.text: sovāca-bhavatāṃ kim api vaibhavaṃ sambhāvya |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Having esteemed a certain glory of yours.'

children.text: sarve ūcuḥ-kiṃ tat ?
children.translated_text: All said: 'What is that?'

children.text: sovāca-bhavatāṃ prāṇa-kandasya śrīman-nandasya jagadānandaḥ sa khalu nandanaḥ sambhaviteti |
children.translated_text: She said: 'That son of your <s>Śrīmān Nanda</s>, who is the root of your lives, whose delight is the joy of the world — he is about to be born!'

children.text: sarve sa-bāṣpa-pulaka-kulam ūcuḥ-bṛhad-vanam asmākam ida bṛhat-tīrthaṃ bhavati | tasmād asmabhyaṃ datta-viśrāntike kṛṣṇāntike sphuṭam uṭajaṃ tava ghaṭayāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: All said, with tears and waves of goosebumps: 'This <s>Bṛhadvana</s> (Great Forest) of ours becomes a great holy place because of you! Therefore, at a resting-place granted by you, near the <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (Yamunā), we shall build a hermitage for you.'

children.text: sovāca-upaśrutir eṣā śruti-veṣā navyāpi na vyabhicaritā | yataḥ kṛṣṇāyā iti vivakṣitam api kṛṣṇasyeti lakṣitaṃ karoti | kṛṣṇa-nāmā hi bhavitāsau | mahā-prabhāvavati yasmin jātavati nirdānavatā pṛthivyāṃ bhaviṣyati | tadīya-guṇe tu sadā navatā, saguṇatā vidyādi-prabandhe tat-sambandhe tu nirguṇatā | sakiñcanatā viṣaya-sampattau tad-bhaktau tu niṣkiñcanatā ity ādikaṃ viruddhāyamānam api sarvair anuruddhaṃ kariṣyati | tasmād asmākam atra sthātum āgraha eva bhavatām anugrahāya sampannaḥ |
children.translated_text: She said: 'This prophecy, though clothed in the garb of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture), is novel yet not contradicted. For even when the intended meaning is 'born of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>' (the Yamunā), it points to 'of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' For his name shall be <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. When that one of great power is born, there shall be generosity upon the earth. In his qualities there is always novelty; in possessing qualities there is excellence in learning and such pursuits, but in relation to him there is freedom from qualities; in worldly possessions there is wealth, but in devotion to him there is utter poverty — thus, though seemingly contradictory, all these will be harmonized by everyone. Therefore, our insistence on staying here has been accomplished for the blessing of all of you.'

children.text:
atha tāṃ sarve sānandaṃ vandamānās tayā samam indīvara-ruci-nindīhita-kālindīṃ vindamānāḥ parṇa-mandiraṃ pūrṇayantas tatra vāsayāmāsuḥ |
[80] tasminn eva divase' pagata-doṣe pradoṣe samudbhaṭa-kaṃsa-roṣeṇa jāta-citta-śoṣeṇa kṛta-paridevena vasudevena prahitā vraja-hitā baḍavārohiṇī rohiṇī guptam ājagāma | yasyām āgatāyāṃ parama-pativratāyāṃ sarva eva vraja-rāja-rāja-samājaḥ śubha-śakuna-saṅkula-śakunādi-samajena samam ullalāsa | tatra cānanda-mohinyau śrī-yaśodā-rohiṇyau yamunā-gaṅge iva saṅgata-saṅge parasparaṃ parebhyaś ca sukha-samūham ūhatuḥ |
children.translated_text:
Then, all of them joyfully worshipping her, together with her finding the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) whose dark beauty shames the luster of blue lotuses, filling a leafy hermitage to perfection, they made her dwell there.
[80] On that very day, at the flawless twilight hour, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the wife of great <s>Vasudeva</s>, was secretly sent by <s>Vasudeva</s> — whose mind was parched by the erupting wrath of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who was in lamentation — to the benefit of <s>Vraja</s>, and she arrived in secret. Upon the arrival of that supremely devoted wife, the entire royal assembly of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, together with an assembly of auspicious omens and birds, rejoiced. And there, the two — <s>Śrī Yaśodā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>, bestowers of bliss and enchantment — like the <s>Yamunā</s> and <s>Gaṅgā</s> at their confluence, mutually and toward others, bore forth a mass of happiness.

children.text: vraja-rāja-patnī ca tasyā jyaiṣṭham avaṣṭabhya māsa-traya-jātam antarvatnītvaṃ paryālocya svābheda-vedanenaiva śāta-jātaṃ prāpa |
children.translated_text: And the queen of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, grasping the seniority of that one [<s>Rohiṇī</s>], contemplating her three-month pregnancy, experienced joy as if it were the very perception of her own non-difference [from her].

children.text: atha māgha-māsi cāsita-pratipadi kṛta-sarva-sukha-prasara-janyāṃ rajanyāṃ sā vraja-rājaṃ sevyamānā tandrāparatantrāyamāṇā svapna-tulyatā-saṃcitaṃ kiñcid añcitaṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: Then, in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, on the first day of the dark fortnight, on a night that produced the flow of all happiness, she, being attended upon by the king of <s>Vraja</s>, becoming drowsy, beheld something slightly curved, gathered together like a dream.

children.text: yathā sa eva bālaḥ sarvatas tad-āvaraṇa-kārikayā kayācic divya-kumārikayātmānaṃ pidhāya vraja-rāja-hṛdayān nija-hṛdayaṃ praviśya dṛśyavad eva sthita iti | tataś ca so' yaṃ hṛdaya-kamala-madhym adhyāsāmāsa | seyaṃ tu jaṭhara-madhyam iti | vrajarājaś ca nirantara-svāntara-tat-praveśāveśaṃ durnideśaṃ ciram anubhūya dūyamānatāṃ vidhūya tathaivānubhūtavān |
children.translated_text: Namely, that very child, concealing himself by means of some divine maiden who created a covering around him on all sides, having entered her heart from the heart of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, stood there as if visible. And then he took his seat in the center of her heart-lotus. And she [perceived it] as the center of her womb. And the king of <s>Vraja</s>, having experienced for a long time the indescribable rapture of his continuous entry into his own inner self, dispelling his distress, experienced it in the same way.

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ svānte cintayati sma-satyam etad ata eva sad-vāṇī-guṇibhir muhur anayor ātmaja iti matam | mayā ca suvicāratas tad eva pūrvaṃ niścitam ācaritam iti | uvāca ca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> thought within himself: 'This is true! That is why those endowed with the qualities of good speech repeatedly hold the view that he is the son of these two. And I too, upon careful reflection, had previously determined and established this very thing.' And he said: 'And then? What happened next?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca - atha tad ārabhya garbha-lakṣaṇam upalabhya sambhūta-bhavyānāṃ sabhyāṅganā-gaṇānāṃ gokula-kula-pātrī sukha-dātrī babhūva | yathā -
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, from that time, recognizing the signs of pregnancy, she became the bestower of happiness, the fit vessel of the <s>Gokula</s> clan, for the hosts of noble women who had become pregnant with auspicious expectations. As follows:'

children.text: mukham āpāṇḍu kucāgraṃ sphītaṃ jaṭharaṃ darottuṅgam |
children.translated_text: Her face became slightly pale, her breasts swelled, her belly rose prominently high;

children.text: abhajata karṇejapatāṃ garbhe vṛtte yaśodāyāḥ ||JGc_1,3.22||
children.translated_text: the state of having earrings dangling — <s>Yaśodā</s> attained this when her pregnancy advanced. //

children.text: yathā ca -
children.translated_text: And as follows:

children.text: vraja-rājñyāṃ sphuritātmā kṛṣṇaḥ sphurati sma loke' pi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose being stirred within the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, stirred also in the world;

children.text: dīpaḥ sphaṭika-ghaṭī-bhāg antar bahir api vibhāti tat-tulyaḥ ||JGc_1,3.23||
children.translated_text: like a lamp inside a crystal vessel, he shone both within and without. //

children.text: kintu -
children.translated_text: However —

children.text: jita-rasanā rasa-dhairyā gāmbhīryādi-pravīṇāpi |
children.translated_text: Though one who had conquered her tongue, steady in taste, skilled in gravity and other virtues,

children.text: spṛhitaṃ kiñcit kiñcid vraja-nṛpa-gṛhiṇī tadā cakre ||JGc_1,3.24||
children.translated_text: the wife of the king of <s>Vraja</s> then developed certain small, particular longings. //

children.text: yathā -
children.translated_text: As follows —

children.text: aihata dohadam eṣā kṛṣṇāveśāviśat tṛṣṇā |
children.translated_text: She had a pregnancy-craving — a thirst infused with the spirit of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.text: tulasī-saṃskṛta-ghṛta-yuk sa-sitaṃ sita-kānti-gandhi paramānnam ||JGc_1,3.25||
children.translated_text: for the finest rice-preparation, mixed with <s>tulasī</s>-consecrated ghee, white, with the fragrance and radiance of whiteness. //

children.text: atha yogamāyā rohiṇyāḥ sāptamāsikaṃ garbhaṃ srastaṃ vidhāya devakyās tad-vidhaṃ taṃ tasyāṃ niyojayāmāsa | tataś ca labdha-sarva-samaya-sampad-daśe caturdaśe māsi śrāvaṇataḥ prāk śravaṇa-rkṣe samasta-sukha-rohiṇī rohiṇī guṇa-gaṇanayā suṣamaṃ sita-suṣamaṃ sutaṃ susrāva | sāndra-śubhratā-vibhrājamānatayā paurṇamāsī candramasam iva, darśita-vikrama-kramatayā siṃha-vadhūḥ śāvakam iva, nirmala-parimala-dhārādhāratayā nava-kamalinī dhavala-kamalam iva, sarva-śravaṇa-saṅgha-maṅgalatayā niravadya-vidyatā yaśaḥ-stomam iva ca |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yogamāyā</s>, having caused the seventh-month embryo of <s>Rohiṇī</s> to slip out, and from <s>Devakī</s> transferred one of the same kind into her. Then, when the fourteenth month from <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> had attained the full occasion of all auspicious tidings, under the asterism of <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s> — the one who makes everything auspicious — gave birth beautifully to a fair, beautiful son: like the full-moon night [giving birth to] the moon with its dense whiteness shining forth; like a lioness [giving birth to] a cub displaying the progression of prowess; like a fresh lotus-pond [giving birth to] a white lotus as the support of streams of pure fragrance; like faultless learning [giving birth to] a mass of fame auspicious to all who hear.

children.text: kiṃ ca -
śubhrāṃśu-vaktraṃ taḍid-āli-locanaṃ
children.translated_text: With a face like the bright moon, with eyes like a row of lightning,

children.text: navābda-keśaṃ śarad-abhra-vigraham |
children.translated_text: with hair like a fresh cloud, with a body like an autumn cloud,

children.text: bhānu-prabhāvaṃ tam asūta rohiṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> gave birth to him of sun-like power —

children.text: tat tac ca yuktaṃ sa hi divya-bālakaḥ ||JGc_1,3.26||
children.translated_text: and all this was fitting, for he was a divine child. //
Moreover —

children.text: sa eṣa ca asita-varṣmā sita-varṣmā sad-anujaḥ sūdita-danujaḥ, pālita-dhenuko dalita-dhenukaḥ, pralamba-bāhuḥ pralamba-ghātayitā, svayaṃ rāma-nāmā rāma-ramita-dvivida-vidārayitā ca bhavitā iti jyotirvidbhir udbhāvitam |
children.translated_text: And this one — of dark complexion yet also of fair complexion, a true younger brother yet a slayer of demons, a protector of <s>Dhenuka</s> (cows) yet a slayer of <s>Dhenuka</s> (the demon), of long arms yet the destroyer of <s>Pralamba</s>, himself named <s>Rāma</s> yet the future destroyer of <s>Dvivida</s> who was delighted by <s>Rāma</s> — thus was it divined by astrologers.

children.text: asya jātakarmādikaṃ ca marmagair eva śarmāntanāmabhir guptam eva paryāptam akāri ānaka-dundubhi-mantraṇā-paratantratayā | kintu tatraikaṃ duḥkham ivāsit | [89] yataḥ sa tu janmata evānuja-janma yāvat jaḍa evādṛśyata | tatra pratīkāraś caika evāsīt yathāntardhṛta-nijāvarajaṃ vrajeśvary-aṅkam eva kevalaṃ valamānaḥ samullasitaval lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: His birth-rites and other ceremonies were performed secretly, with names that conveyed hidden auspicious meanings, under the direction of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>). But there was one seeming sorrow: [89] for from birth until the birth of his younger brother, he appeared simply inert. And there was only one remedy for this: merely lying in the lap of the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, as if internally holding his own younger brother, he was seen to suddenly become animated.

children.text: tad evaṃ dina-katipaye labdha-vyatyaye garbha-sandarbhāt spaṣṭam aṣṭa-māsi tad-avarajanma-janmanaḥ samārambhaḥ sambhavati sma | yathā cādhunāpi varṇayanti --
children.translated_text: Thus, with the passage of a few days and with variation from the sequence of the [first] pregnancy, the onset of the birth of his younger brother clearly became possible in the eighth month. As they describe even now —

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśa-catur-yuge kali-śiraḥ saṃmardya vaivasvate
children.translated_text: In the twenty-eighth <s>caturyuga</s> (four-age cycle), in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> [<s>Manvantara</s>], crushing the head of <s>Kali</s>,

children.text: bhādrāntar-bahulāṣṭamīm anu vidhoḥ putre vidhor udgame |
children.translated_text: on the eighth day of the dark half within the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, at the rising of the Moon's son (Mercury), under the Moon's rising,

children.text: yoge harṣaṇa-nāmni śuddha-vidhibhe purṇaḥ paraḥ śrī-vidhur
children.translated_text: in the <s>yoga</s> named <s>Harṣaṇa</s> (Rejoicing), under the pure <s>Vidhi-bha</s> (Rohiṇī nakṣatra), the full, supreme, glorious Moon [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]

children.text: nandan nanda-vadhū-mude svayam udaid ahnāya dhunvaṃs tamaḥ ||JGc_1,3.27||
children.translated_text: himself rose, dispelling darkness, for the delight of <s>Nanda's</s> wife, shining for the day! //

children.text: yathā ca -
children.translated_text: And as follows —

children.text: tadā yugādi devās te sva-sva-smapad-upāyanam |
children.translated_text: Then the gods of the beginning of the age, each bearing the offering of their own prosperity,

children.text: ādāya kṛṣṇa-janmarkṣa-niśām āśu siṣevire ||JGc_1,3.28||
children.translated_text: quickly served the night of the asterism of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> birth. //

children.text: yathā hi -
children.translated_text: As indeed —

children.text: vibabhūva vinā satyaṃ dhyānaṃ tretāṃ vinā makhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Meditation flourished without truth (<s>Satya</s> age); sacrifice without <s>Tretā</s> age;

children.text: vinā dvāparam abhyarcā harer nāma kaliṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: worship without <s>Dvāpara</s> age; <s>Hari's</s> name without <s>Kali</s> age;

children.text: vinā madhuṃ saptalādi vinoṣṇaṃ pākimāmratā |
children.translated_text: the <s>saptalā</s> and other [flowers] without honey; the mango's ripeness without heat;

children.text: vinā śarad-ambu-śrīḥ śālis tasyāḥ paraṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: the beauty of waters without autumn; the rice without that [autumn] further;

children.text: śiśireṇa vinā māghyaṃ vināhnāmbuja-vistṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Māgha</s> month's [festival] without winter; the lotus's expanse without day;

children.text: vinā jyotiṣa-śāstreṇa grahāṇāṃ śubhadā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the auspicious position of planets without the science of astrology;

children.text: vinā guru-prabhāveṇa sarvatra sphuraṇaṃ hareḥ |
children.translated_text: the manifestation of <s>Hari</s> everywhere without the power of the <s>guru</s>;

children.text: vinā sūti-pratītyā ca prasūto' sau yaśodayā ||JGc_1,3.29||
children.translated_text: and without the experience of childbirth, he was born from <s>Yaśodā</s>! //

children.text: tad idam agre vyaktīkariṣyate | kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: This will be clarified further ahead. Moreover —

children.text: madhye tārāvāra-sāraṃ nabhas tat-
children.translated_text: In the midst, the sky with the essence of the multitude of stars;

children.text: prānte sindhūrdhvaṃ dhvanan-megha-bandhu |
children.translated_text: at its edge, the ocean roaring upward, the companion of clouds;

children.text: itthaṃ varṣādhāmatarṣā śarac-chrīs
children.translated_text: thus, the rainy season's abode, the thirst [quenched by it], and the beauty of autumn —

children.text: tasyāṃ tithyāṃ tathyam ātithyam āpa ||JGc_1,3.30||
children.translated_text: on that <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), truly received hospitality. //

children.text:
kiṃ ca -
jātibhiḥ saha mādhavyaḥ ketakyaḥ ketakaiḥ samam |
kumūdyāny ambujaiḥ sārdhaṃ sphuṭanti smeti dig yadā ||JGc_1,3.31||tadā tad api nāścaryam ācāryaiḥ paricīyate |
sarvāścarya-nidhiḥ so' pi janma-caryāṃ yato gataḥ ||JGc_1,3.32||
children.translated_text: For he who is the treasury of all wonders has entered the course of birth. //

Moreover —
When <s>mādhavī</s> flowers bloom together with jasmine, <s>ketakī</s> flowers with <s>ketaka</s>,
night-lotuses with day-lotuses — thus when even this direction [of impossibility occurs] //
then even that is not considered a wonder by the teachers.

children.text:
tathā hi etad-uttaraṃ bhāvi-tad-vilokānāṃ lokānāṃ bhāvitānam -
[93] mukham asya lasita-smitāsita-kamalānām adhipam iva vilokyate,
netra-yugalaṃ sūkṣma-bhramara-citra-kairavāntaḥ-patrāṇām,
ghrāṇaṃ nīla-nīrada-cchavi-ladha-kīla-tila-prasūnānām,
oṣṭhādharaṃ sindūra-girijani-javā-badnhūka-bimba-goṣṭhīnām,
karṇa-dvandvam añjana-bhūmija-śyāmalatā-potānām,
kara-prāntatā-kānta-bhuja-yugalaṃ sa-nava-pallava-nava-tāla-śākhānām,
śrīvatsa-sindhu-vatsākhya-lekhā-sahita-vatsaṃ dhṛta-dakṣiṇāvarta-dyuti-viśeṣa-kṛta-sthira-vidyud-āśleṣa-megha-khaṇḍānām iti |

kiṃ ca mukhena mahāpadmaṃ vijetā,
nayanābhyāṃ padmam,
nāsikayā makaram,
smitena kundam,
kaṇṭhena śaṅkham,
caraṇayoḥ pṛṣṭābhyāṃ kacchapam,
rucā nīlam,
sarvair eva ca sarveṣāṃ kharvam |
kiṃ bahunā, svena mukundam apīti yugapad atra tat-tad-avasara-prasavādīnāṃ tathā durlabha-sannidhīnāṃ nidhīnām api sannipatanaṃ nāsambhāvyam |
atha tasya janmani ko' pi viśeṣaḥ, yathā -
children.translated_text: Now, there is a special feature of His birth, namely —

children.text: tadā tatra māyā milad-bālya-kāyā
children.translated_text: Then there <s>Māyā</s> (the divine illusory power), with a body mingling with infancy,

children.text: tadīyānukūlyaṃ kṛpā-mātra-mūlyam |
children.translated_text: rendering His favor, whose price is compassion alone,

children.text: sadā kurvatī taṃ samastān atītaṃ
children.translated_text: always making Him transcend everything,

children.text: vidhāyāgrajātaṃ svayaṃ prāpa jātam ||JGc_1,3.33||
children.translated_text: having made [<s>Balarāma</s>] the first-born, she herself attained birth. || (JGc 1,3.33)

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhena bhāvitaṃ sa-pramāṇaḥ khalv idam - adṛśyatānujā viṣṇoḥ sāyudhāṣṭa-mahābhujā [BhP 10.4.9] iti śrī-bhāgavatād, tac ca nandas tv ātmaja utpanne jātāhlādo mahā-manāḥ [BhP 10.5.1] ity ādiṣv ātmaja-padaiḥ sthāpanā-vyapadeśataḥ sadeśa-rūpam eva nirūpyate | kintu tad idam apracchannaṃ vivicya pṛcchāmaḥ yatheha sandehaḥ sarveṣāṃ śāmyati | [97] spaṣṭam apy ācaṣṭa - aho ārya tarhi kathaṃ vasudeva-devakī-putratayā so' yam avadhāryate ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> reflected — this indeed has authority — 'There appeared the younger sister of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, eight-armed, bearing weapons' (BhP 10.4.9) — from the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>; and that [is reconciled] by the terms '<s>ātmaja</s>' (own-born son) in passages such as 'And <s>Nanda</s>, when his own son was born, became great-minded, overflowing with joy' (BhP 10.5.1) and so forth — it is demonstrated to be fitting through the pretext of establishment. But let us openly investigate and ask this in detail, so that the doubt of all may be pacified. [97] He spoke clearly — 'O venerable one! Then how is He regarded as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>?'

children.text: tad īdṛg-vacasi sati snigdhakaṇṭhe vacasi kiñcit-kuṇṭhena madhukaṇṭhena manasi bhāvitam - śrīmatā devarṣiṇedam āvāṃ praty atiharṣeṇādiṣṭaṃ - yadi kadācic chrīmati mahā-premavati vraje kṛta-vrajanayoḥ kathā-yogo bhavatoḥ sambhāvyate, tadā śrī-kṛṣṇa-devasya sarvato varṣyam aiśvaryaṃ gopanīyam ity ato munivarga-prasiddha-garga-siddhāntam evālambya saṃvadiṣyāvahe | sa cāmībhiḥ śruta eveti nāścaryāya paryavasiṣyatīti |
children.translated_text: At such speech, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, somewhat hesitant at <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha's</s> words, reflected in his mind — 'The glorious <s>Devarṣi</s> (Nārada) instructed us two with great delight: if ever the occasion for a narrative should arise for you two in the glorious <s>Vraja</s>, which abounds in great love, then the universal majesty of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-deva</s> must be concealed; therefore, we shall speak in accordance with the well-known <s>Garga</s>-doctrine established among the sages. And since that [doctrine] has been heard by these [Vraja-folk], it will not end in surprise.'

children.text: prakaṭaṃ covāca - atra khalv idam asya śrī-vraja-rāja-tanūjasya rahasyam udbhāvayato mama samatikramaḥ svayam amunaiva bāḍhaṃ soḍhavyaḥ | tathā hi asmin sarvato labdhātirekakā saṃsiddhiḥ khalv ekā vartate | yad atikrānta-sarveha-sneha-maya-hṛdaya eva sadā vartamānaḥ snighdatā-digdha-janānāṃ bhāva-mudrayā parokṣaṃ kṛtayāpi svahṛdi pratibimbatatayā mudrito bhavati | asya svarūpeṇāvirbhāvaś ca sneha-maya-sphūrti-pūrti-vaśībhāvata eva sarvathā, na tv anyathā | putratayāvirbhāve ca bījaṃ pitṛ-bhāva-maya-sneha eva nānyeṣām ivānyat | jāte ca kutracit putratayāvirbhāve tat-tat-sambandha-maya-sneha-kṛta-caya-sphūrtir eva tathā tathā bhāvenāvirbhāve nibandhanaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: And he spoke openly — 'Herein, the transgression committed by me in revealing the secret of the son of the glorious King of <s>Vraja</s> must indeed be endured by him himself. For in him, who has obtained supremacy over all, there abides one settled attainment: namely, he who always remains with a heart drenched in love transcending all worldly affection, is sealed in his own heart by the emotional stamp of those anointed with tenderness, even though they have sealed him indirectly as a reflection. And his manifestation in his essential nature is entirely by the force of the overflowing fullness of love-born intuition, and not otherwise. And in his manifestation as a son, the seed is solely the parental love — not something else as for others. And whenever there is a manifestation as a son somewhere, the surge of love made of that particular relationship becomes the occasion for such and such a manifestation in a corresponding emotion.'

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite sarvataḥ samudbuddha-śuddha-pitrādi-bhāva-vicitrāṇāṃ vraja-nṛpati-prabhṛtīnāṃ bhṛti-bhuk-paryantānāṃ vraja-janānāṃ yeṣām adhimadhyaṃ prati-dviparārdhaṃ pratikalpam āvirbhavati, vṛddhi-jīvikānām iva teṣām eva prema-sañcaya-paryudañcana-prapañcam añcaṃs tad-vṛddher aparicchedyatābuddhyā pratidātum adhyavasāyaṃ muñcan sadā putrāditayā sa eṣa virājate, nānye tu tatra kila tilam apy avakāśa-kālaṃ labhante |
children.translated_text: This being established, among the <s>Vraja</s>-folk — from the King of <s>Vraja</s> and others down to the servants — whose pure parental and other emotions are fully awakened in every way, for whom He manifests every half-<s>parārdha</s> (cosmic half-cycle), every <s>kalpa</s>, in the very center — like those whose livelihood is nourishment — embracing the elaborate outpouring of accumulated love, releasing the resolve to repay it due to the understanding that such growth is unlimited, He always shines forth as their son and so on; and others there obtain not even a sesame seed's worth of opportunity or time. |

children.text: etad evoktaṃ brahmaṇā eṣāṃ ghoṣa-nivāsinām uta bhavān kiṃ deva rāteti naḥ [BhP 10.14.35] ity ādinā | etad eva ca śrī-nārāyaṇa-devena samādiṣṭaṃ - yo' sāv atasī-kusuma-suṣamaḥ sukumāraḥ kumāraḥ ity ādinā | tataś ca -
children.translated_text: This very thing was stated by <s>Brahmā</s>: 'Of these dwellers of the cowherd settlement, are You, O Lord, a kinsman or what?' (BhP 10.14.35) and so forth. And this very thing was instructed by <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa-deva</s>: 'He who has the beauty of an <s>atasī</s> (flax) blossom, that delicate boy...' and so forth. From which —

children.text: tasmān nandātmajo 'yaṃ te nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore this son of <s>Nanda</s>, your [charge], is equal to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in qualities;

children.text: śriyā kīrtyānubhāvena gopāyasva samāhitaḥ ||[BhP 10.8.19]
children.translated_text: protect him with <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), fame, and power, with a concentrated mind.' (BhP 10.8.19)

children.text:
iti garga-vacanānusāreṇedam utprekṣyāmahe - etad-rūpa-svaputra-mātra-paryāpta-sarva-svārthena śrīmad-vraja-mahendreṇa mahīyamānasya yasya mahābhagavato yā yogamāyākhyā durghaṭa-ghañanī svarūpa-śaktiḥ śāstreṇa vaktīkriyate | tena kila dattā sā tvat-putre śrī-kṛṣṇa eva paryavasyati sma | sā ceha svajana-sneha-nikṣipta-cittasya yadyapy asya tat-putrasya prāyo' vadhānaṃ na prāpnoti | tathāpi tasmād anyasmāc ca parokṣam anukṣaṇam anugatiṃ līlā-sahāyakaṃ ca prapañcati | yathā ca yogamāyā tathā tad-anugatā māyādayo' pīti | yadyapy evaṃ tathāpi tvat-prabhu-pratta-śaktim enaṃ tvam eva nija-śrī-prabhṛti-śaktibhir gopāyasveti gargo vyañjitavān | tad evaṃ sati bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te [BhP 10.8.15] ity api tad-uktir udriktīsyāt |yataḥ sva-snigdha-jana-bhajana-rasāveśitāveśatayā
sadā virājamānasya śrīmad-vraja-rājātmajasya khalv asya sva-snigdha-jana-bhāva-svabhāva-viśeṣa-vinodam anumodamānasya tad-bhāva-rūpānurūpaṃ rūpaṃ yadṛcchāvaśād ekadhānekadhā ca samīpator'samīpato' py āvirbhavati tirobhavati ca |
children.translated_text: Following the words of <s>Garga</s>, we speculate thus: Of this most blessed Lord, magnified by the glorious great <s>Indra</s> of <s>Vraja</s> whose entire purpose is fully satisfied by his own son of that very form — His <s>Yogamāyā</s>-named essential power, the accomplisher of the impossible, is declared by scripture. What was given by Him indeed culminates in <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> alone as 'your son.' And she here, though the attention of him whose mind is placed in the love of his own people mostly does not reach that son, yet she secretly, from him and from others, moment by moment extends her following and her assistance in His pastimes. And as <s>Yogamāyā</s>, so too <s>Māyā</s> and others who follow her. Even though this is so, <s>Garga</s> hinted: 'You yourself, protect him with the powers of your own <s>Śrī</s> and other potencies, this one endowed with power granted by your Lord.' This being so, even the statement 'Many are the names and forms of your son' (BhP 10.8.15) would be elevated. For, of the glorious son of the King of <s>Vraja</s>, who always shines resplendent, immersed in the rapture of passionate devotional worship by his own beloved people — as he delights in the special play of the natural emotions of his own dear folk — a form corresponding to that emotional nature appears, whether as one or as many, whether near or far, by the force of spontaneity, and also disappears.

children.text: tataḥ śrī-vasudeva-devakyor antar yac caturbhujam asya rūpaṃ sphurati, tad eva hi bahir āvirbhavati sma | phalena phala-kāraṇam anumīyate iti nyāyena | tenaiva ca nyāyena śrī-vrajeśvaryos tu paraṃ dvibhuja-mūrtitayā sphūrtir āsīt |
children.translated_text: Then, the four-armed form of His that flashed within <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s> — that indeed manifested externally. By the maxim 'the cause is inferred from the effect.' And by that same maxim, for the glorious Lord and Lady of <s>Vraja</s>, the manifestation was as the supreme two-armed form.

children.text: tataḥ prāg ayaṃ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ [BhP 10.8.14] iti dhṛta-tapo-vargasya gargasya vacanam anusṛtya parāmṛśyate | yadā nṛśaṃsa-kaṃsa-bhiyā svāvirbhūta-caturbhuja-rūpācchādana-pūrvaka-dvibhuja-rūpāvirbhāvanāya śrī-devakīcchā jātā, tadā tasya yad apūrvaṃ dvibhuja-rūpaṃ pūrvaṃ māyayā saha śrī-yaśodāyāḥ svāntaram āyātaṃ, tad eva tatra sannidhānam avāpya caturbhujaṃ rūpam antarbhāvya svayam āvirbabhūva | yatra sākāratayā mātṛ-garbha-sthitāpi māyā nirākāratayā tūrdhva-gatyā tanvā tad-vāhanatām āgatā | gandavāha-śreṇī nīla-kamala-dalam iva tatra sarvālakṣitatayā tat prāpitavatī | yā khalu pūrvaṃ tad-ākarṣeṇa dharṣeṇa paraṃ mātaram api mohena mlāpitavatī |
children.translated_text: Then, following the words of <s>Garga</s>, who had performed austerities — 'This one was born previously as a son of <s>Vasudeva</s> somewhere' (BhP 10.8.14) — we consider: When the wish of the glorious <s>Devakī</s> arose, out of fear of the cruel <s>Kaṃsa</s>, for the manifestation of a two-armed form by concealing the self-manifested four-armed form, then that unprecedented two-armed form which had previously entered the interior of the glorious <s>Yaśodā</s> along with <s>Māyā</s>, having obtained proximity there by incorporating the four-armed form within itself, manifested on its own. Where <s>Māyā</s>, though residing in the mother's womb in embodied form, in disembodied form, through upward movement with a subtle body, assumed the role of a vehicle. Like a line of wind-bearers carrying a blue lotus petal, she brought it there completely unperceived by anyone. She who, earlier, by the force of that attraction, had stupefied even the mother with delusion.

children.text: atha punas tena garbhasthenākāreṇa mātuḥ prasūti-bhramaṃ ca samprathayya bahir ātmanaṃ saṃvalayya prasūti-śayyām evādhiśayya sthitavatī | yā khalu śrī-devakītaḥ śrī-rohiṇyāṃ saṅkarṣaṇa-saṅkramaṇe' pi tathā prakramate sma iti |
children.translated_text: Then again, by that in-womb form, having produced the illusion of childbirth in the mother, and having wrapped herself externally, having lain upon the birthing-bed, she remained. She who indeed had proceeded in the same way even during the transfer of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (Balarāma) from <s>Śrī Devakī</s> to <s>Śrī Rohiṇī</s>.

children.text: atra ca snigdhakaṇṭhenāntaś cintitam - satyam evāha sma nūnaṃ athāham aṃśabhāgena [BhP 10.29] iti hi māyāṃ prati śrī-bhagavad-vākyam ādiṣṭā prabhuṇāṃśena kāryārthe sambhaviṣyati [BhP 10.1.25] iti ca devān prati brahma-vacanam | atra aṃśabhāgena caturbhuja-rūpeṇākāra-bhedeneti bhagavad-abhiprāyaḥ | kāryārthe tat-tan-mohanāya aṃśena sambhaviṣyati śrī-kṛṣṇasya dvibhuja-rūpeṇākāra-bhedena saha miliṣyati seti brahmaṇo' bhiprāyaḥ | tad evam eva hi vyākhyātam anyatra śrī-bhāgavata-tattvavidbhiḥ avatīrṇau jagaty-arthe svāṃśena bala-keśavau [BhP 10.38.32] ity atra svāṃśena mūrti-bhedeneti |
children.translated_text: Here <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> reflected internally — 'Truly indeed is the Lord's statement to <s>Māyā</s>: "And I, by a portion" (BhP 10.29), and <s>Brahmā's</s> words to the gods: "Commanded by the Lord, she will be born as a portion for the sake of the task" (BhP 10.1.25). Here, "by a portion" means "in the four-armed form, by a difference of appearance" — this is the Lord's intention. "For the sake of the task" — for the purpose of deluding them respectively — "she will be born as a portion" means "she will merge with the two-armed form of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, by a difference of appearance" — this is <s>Brahmā's</s> intention. This indeed has been explained elsewhere by those who know the reality of the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>: "<s>Bala</s> and <s>Keśava</s> descended to the world for its sake, by their own portion" (BhP 10.38.32) — here "by their own portion" means "by a difference of bodily form."'

children.text: api ca śrī-vrajeśvara-sambandha-nibandhanā yā kṛṣṇe yogamāyābhivyaktir uktā sā siddhāntato' pi siddhatām āsīdati | bhagavataḥ khalu priyajanecchām evānugacchati sarva-śakti-vyaktir na tu yadṛcchām iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, the manifestation of <s>Yogamāyā</s> in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — which is described as based on His relationship with the glorious Lord of <s>Vraja</s> — that is established even from the doctrinal standpoint. For the manifestation of all powers of the Lord follows solely the wish of His beloved people, not arbitrary will.

children.text:
atha sarve sāścaryam ūcuḥ - bhavatu nāma tat tat | kintu tataḥ kim anantaraṃ jātam ?
[107] madhukaṇṭha uvāca - anantaraṃ tu caturbhujatāvirbhāvānurūpyataḥ pravyakta-yogamāyasya tasya prāg-upadeśataḥ śrī-vasudevaḥ sarvatra māyika-śāyikāyāṃ jātāyāṃ pūrva-deva-bhiyā dvibhujam atrakīyaṃ bālakam atrānīya tayā bālikayā vimilitavān | so' yaṃ tu teneśvaratā-pratyāyakena caturbhuja-rūpeṇopadeśena ca na tatra jātakatāṃ vyañjitavān iti putratāṃ sandehitavān | atra tu dvibhuja-rūpeṇa vacanādi-śakter vyakter abhāvena ca tām eva vyajya putratām eva nidehitavān | śrīmān ānakadundubhis tu tad idaṃ sarvaṃ nānusadadhau iti |
children.translated_text:
Then all said with wonder — 'So be it regarding all that. But what happened next?'
[107] <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'Next, in accordance with the four-armed manifestation, when <s>Yogamāyā</s> had become manifest and by His prior instruction, <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s>, when everywhere the <s>Māyā</s>-sleep had occurred, and out of prior fear of the god [Kaṃsa], brought the two-armed infant from there [Mathurā] to here [Vraja] and exchanged him with that baby girl. But He, by that instruction through the sovereignty-demonstrating four-armed form, did not indicate birth there — so [<s>Vasudeva</s>] doubted His sonship. But here, through the two-armed form and the absence of manifested speech-power and the like, He revealed just that — and confirmed His sonship. The glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (Vasudeva) did not recall all of this afterwards.'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca - nānusandadhātu nāma | tathāpi yāṃ tanayām atrakīyām apamāya svayam apanināya tasyāḥ pratidānasyāpi sad-bhāvābhāvāt katham iva nyaste' py asminn ātmīyatāṃ pratyapadyata ? āgamādāv api yasya nandanandana-nandātmaja-nandaja-nandatanaya-ballavīnandanādi-nāmāni tat-tad-abhīṣṭa-pradatayā nirdiṣṭānīti |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'Let him not recall it. Still, having removed the daughter who was from here, and having taken her away himself — when there was no reality of any return-gift — how could he claim ownership even over this one who was deposited? Even in authoritative texts, names such as <s>Nanda-nandana</s> (Joy of Nanda), <s>Nandātmaja</s> (Son of Nanda), <s>Nandaja</s> (Born of Nanda), <s>Nandatanaya</s> (Child of Nanda), <s>Ballavīnandana</s> (Delight of the Cowherd-woman) are designated as granting the desired [meaning] of each.'

children.text: punaḥ sa-hāsam āha sma - yasya nandanandana iti nāma viparītatayā paṭhatāpi krama-parītatayānubhūyate | tasmād evam apy asman-nṛpater eva pūrva-vyañjitaṃ samañjasaṃ sañjanam añjasā tasya labhyatvāyopapalabhyata iti |
children.translated_text: Again he said with a laugh — 'Whoever reads the name <s>Nanda-nandana</s> even in reverse order experiences it in sequential order. Therefore, even so, for our king alone, the previously indicated, proper, straightforward birth of Him is easily comprehended.'

children.text: hasitvā punar uvāca - atha sa vraja-deva-sutasya vasudevasyāgamana-prakāras tu varṇyatām |
children.translated_text: Having laughed, he spoke again — 'Now, let the manner of the arrival of <s>Vasudeva</s> at the [dwelling of] the son of the Lord of <s>Vraja</s> be described.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca -
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said —

children.text: aṅghryor bandho vyadālīd aśayiṣata janā dvāra-rodhā vidīrṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The fetters on his feet were split open; the people, who were barriers at the door, fell asleep;

children.text: śeṣaś chatraṃ babhūva dyumaṇijani-nadī prāpya kedāra-bhāvam |
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> (the cosmic serpent) became an umbrella; the river born of the Sun-jewel assumed the form of a rice-paddy;

children.text: āgopādhīśa-gehaṃ vṛti-rahitam abhūd gokulaṃ kṛṣṇa-vāhaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Gokula</s>, without any obstacle, became the bearer of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, up to the house of the chief of cowherds —

children.text: prāpya śrī-śūra-putraṃ yad iha tad akhilaṃ kasya kiṃ brūhi tat tu ||JGc_1,3.34||
children.translated_text: Having brought the glorious son of <s>Śūra</s> (Vasudeva) here — all that which [happened] here — tell me, to whom [does it belong]? || (JGc 1,3.34)

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca - tad akhilaṃ goparājasya bhāgyam iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said — 'All that is the good fortune of the King of Cowherds.'

children.text: tad evaṃ labdha-prathāyāṃ kathāyām -
children.translated_text: Thus, as the narrative gained currency —

children.text: tayor māyā-jāla-prathana-tulayā saṅkathanayā
children.translated_text: When that <s>līlā</s> of <s>Hari</s>, weighed on the scale of the spreading of the net of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and told as a story,

children.text: hareḥ sā sā līlā nayanam iva yātā kila yadā |
children.translated_text: came, as it were, before the eyes —

children.text: tadā bāṣpa-stambhaa-pralaya-mukha-bhāvāḥ pratipadaṃ
children.translated_text: then the states of tears, stupefaction, dissolution, and others arose at every step

children.text: babhūvur ye vā te kati kati ca varṇyā vrajasadām ||JGc_1,3.35||
children.translated_text: among the residents of <s>Vraja</s> — how many and how many of them could be described? //

children.text: tataś ca taṃ ratna-nidhāyaṃ nidhāya gate śrī-vasudeve kāraṇābhāvāt pracalāyitatā-pracaya-dohaṃ maoham apahṛtya ca gatāyāṃ māyāyāṃ śrī-vraja-rāja-jāyā punaḥ sambhūtaṃ sutaṃ sākṣād eva dadarśa | yathā viṣṇu-purāṇe --
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> had deposited that treasure and departed, and when <s>Māyā</s> (the illusory power), having removed the delusion — which was the milking of the accumulated drowsiness — for want of cause had also departed, the queen of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> beheld her son reborn, directly before her. As in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: dadṛśe ca prabuddhā sā yaśodā jātam ātmajam |
nīlotpala-dala-śyāmaṃ tato' tyarthaṃ mudaṃ yayau ||[ViP 5.5.22] iti |
children.translated_text: dark as the petal of a blue lotus — she then attained extreme joy. //
And <s>Yaśodā</s>, having awakened, saw her son born,

children.text: yathā ca -
children.translated_text: And as follows:

children.text: bālaṃ divyāti-divyāsita-maṇi-vapuṣaṃ candrajic candra-vaktraṃ
children.translated_text: The child, of a divine, supremely divine dark-jewel body, his moon-face conquering the moon,

children.text: lokātītābja-netraṃ dyu-taru-nava-dalollaṅghi-śobhāṅghri-pāṇim |
children.translated_text: his lotus-eyes transcending the world, his feet and hands of beauty surpassing the new leaves of the divine tree,

children.text: kiñcic cañcat-karādi-mradima-madhurita-krandanād viśva-mohaṃ
children.translated_text: enchanting the universe with his crying sweetened by the slight waving of his hands and other tender motions —

children.text: paśyantī gopa-rājñī tanujam amanuta svaṃ tadā citra-kalpam ||JGc_1,3.36||
children.translated_text: the queen of cowherds, beholding her son, considered her own self like a miraculous age! //

children.text: sāmrājyaṃ śyāma-bhāsāṃ nidhir api tad idaṃ rūpa-ratnākarāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The sovereignty of dark radiances, the very treasure of oceans of beautiful jewels,

children.text: bhāgyaṃ lāvaṇya-bhājāṃ vilasita-nigamas tat-tad-aṅgāvalīnām |
children.translated_text: the fortune of possessors of charm, the revealed scripture of each row of his limbs —

children.text: evaṃ mīmāṃsamānā vrajapati-dayitā yāvad āste sma tāvat
children.translated_text: while the beloved of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> was thus contemplating, just then

children.text: krandann om om itītthaṃ nava-śiśur asakau tad dhruvaṃ svīcakāra ||JGc_1,3.37||
children.translated_text: the new infant, crying 'Om, Om' in this manner, instantly claimed her at both [breasts]! //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā putram asau vrajeśa-gṛhiṇī sadyaḥ prajātaṃ sakhīr
children.translated_text: The wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, seeing her son just born, though she called her companions,

children.text: āhūtā na śaśāka kartum api ced āstāṃ paraṃ ceṣṭitam |
children.translated_text: was unable even to perform — let alone any further action —

children.text: asrair āvṛtam akṣi-kaṇṭham atha yat stabdhaṃ ca tasyā vapus
children.translated_text: her eyes and throat were covered with tears, and her body was paralyzed;

children.text: tasmin lālana-lālasā-vaśatayā cātmātmanā vyagritaḥ ||JGc_1,3.38||
children.translated_text: due to her subjection to the desire to caress him, she was agitated with her own self. //

children.text:
kiṃ ca -
yadā māyā gatā tarhi vraje mohaṃ jahau janaḥ |
kadā yadā hy āvirāsīt tatra śrī-puruṣottamaḥ ||JGc_1,3.39||tadā vyavahitānām apy eṣa prākāśayan manaḥ |
kumudvatīnāṃ sumano-gaṇaṃ vā śīta-dīdhitiḥ ||JGc_1,3.40||sphurati sma paraṃ mātuḥ śayyāyāṃ na sa bālakaḥ |
snigdhānām api citteṣu svaccheṣu pratibimbavat ||JGc_1,3.41||sphurati sma yadā bālas tāsāṃ vyavahito' pi saḥ |
taṃ drutaṃ tās tadā jagmuḥ sāraṅgyo vā ghanāgamam ||JGc_1,3.42||rohiṇyādibhir etābhiḥ samam āloki bālakaḥ |
udayat-pūrṇa-candro vā cakorībhiḥ samantataḥ ||JGc_1,3.43||stambhe' pi smera-netrābhyāṃ paśyantīṃ sutam eva tām |
pratikāryāṃ vicāryāmūḥ paryālocanta taṃ tataḥ ||JGc_1,3.44||
children.translated_text: considering what should be done for her, they then contemplated him from all around. //

Moreover: When <s>Māyā</s> departed, then the people of <s>Vraja</s> abandoned their delusion. When? When <s>Śrī Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person) manifested there. Then, even for those who were separated [by walls], he illuminated their minds — as the moon illuminates the blossoming of night-lotuses and the hosts of flowers. The infant shone forth supremely — not [merely] on his mother's bed, but in the hearts of the affectionate ones, as a reflection in clear [mirrors]. When the infant shone forth for them, though separated [from them], they rushed swiftly toward him — like <s>cātaka</s> birds toward the approaching cloud. The child was beheld by <s>Rohiṇī</s> and these others — like the rising full moon beheld by <s>cakorī</s> birds on all sides. Even in her paralysis, she who beheld her son with smiling eyes —

children.text: tā etā manasā dṛśā kalitam apy atrāsitaṃ bālakaṃ
children.translated_text: All those women, though having beheld this dark-colored child with their mind and eyes,

children.text: sandehāspadatām anaiṣur asakṛd yat tat tu yogyaṃ matam |
children.translated_text: arrived at a state of doubt repeatedly — and that is deemed fitting.

children.text: yad vastu prathitaṃ sudurlabhatayā tad daivato labhyatāṃ
children.translated_text: For what is renowned as extremely rare, let it be obtained by divine fortune;

children.text: kintv etat prathamaṃ pratīti-padavīṃ nātmany alaṃ yacchati ||JGc_1,3.45||
children.translated_text: but this at first does not adequately grant the path of conviction in oneself! //

children.text: tad yathā -
navyendīvaram-mālyam asti kim idaṃ kiṃ śakra-nīlaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Is this a garland of fresh blue lotuses? Or is it a great sapphire?

children.text: kiṃ vaidūryam aho tad etad atulaṃ jñātuṃ na yac chakyate |
children.translated_text: Or is it a <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl) gem? Ah, that incomparable thing which cannot be known!

children.text: paśyāmaḥ kila bālakasya tu tanuṃ sarvendriyāṇāṃ kṛtiṃ
children.translated_text: Let us behold the body of this child — an achievement of all the senses,

children.text: rundhānā khalu yā tanoti nayana-dvandvasya nirdvandvatām ||JGc_1,3.46||
children.translated_text: which, blocking [all else], indeed bestows upon the pair of eyes their freedom from duality! //
That is as follows:

children.text: tatra ca - nirmitaṃ kila mṛgamada-saurabha-tamāla-dala-sāreṇa, abhyaktaṃ kila nikhila-vilambaka-lāvaṇyena, udvartitaṃ kila nija-deha-tejasā, snātaṃ kila nija-mukha-niryat-kānti-sudhayā, anuliptaṃ kila jananī-dṛṣṭi-karpūra-labdha-saṃghṛṣṭi-bhadra-śriyā, bhūṣitaṃ kila sahaja-śubhatā-rūṣita-nijākāreṇa iti sadyo-jātaṃ tad apatyaṃ vitarkya mithaḥ-kṛta-samāgamāḥ sarvāḥ punas taṃ bālaṃ labdha-tamāla-patra-bhoga-mṛga-bheda-mṛgamada-sāra-paṅkam iva komalāṅgam, nija-kara-cūrṇitatama iva cūrṇa-kuntalam, vahan-mukha-vidhu-bimbam īkṣayantaṃ sarva-manāṃsy ākraṣṭum iva karau muṣṭīkurvantaṃ, taraṇijā-nijāguru-taraṅgam iva kara-caraṇa-kamalaṃ cālayantaṃ vilokayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: And there: 'It is as if anointed with the essence of <s>tamāla</s>-leaf mixed with the fragrance of musk, as if smeared with the charm that surpasses all, as if rubbed with the radiance of its own body, as if bathed in the nectar of beauty streaming from its own face, as if anointed with the auspicious beauty obtained from the friction of the camphor of the mother's gaze, as if adorned by its own form beautified by innate auspiciousness' — thus imagining the newly-born child, all having assembled together, they again beheld that infant — whose tender body was like a lump of musk from the enjoyment of the <s>tamāla</s>-leaf-like pattern of a deer, whose curling locks were as if powdered fine by its own hand, bearing the moon-disc of its face, as if clenching its fists to attract all minds, moving the lotuses of its hands and feet like the waves of its own agalloch-scented [river]!

children.text: tad evaṃ vilokya ca -
children.translated_text: And having thus beheld:

children.text: sarvās tāḥ kalakalam eva moda-yuktāḥ
children.translated_text: All those women, joined with delight, making nothing but a tumult,

children.text: kurvatyaḥ param avidur na tatra kṛtyam |
children.translated_text: knew no duty to perform there beyond that.

children.text: ekā tu drutam atha suṣṭhu-dhīra-cittā
children.translated_text: But one of them, swiftly, of truly steady mind,

children.text: taṃ kampre kara-yugale dadhaty apaśyat ||JGc_1,3.47||
children.translated_text: placed him in the cradle of her pair of hands and gazed! //

children.text: tataś ca pum-apatya-cihnam ahnāyāvagatya tāsāṃ pratyekam api samīhitam | yathā -
children.translated_text: Then, having ascertained the mark of a male offspring that day, the desire of each of them [was expressed]. As follows:

children.text: aho śirasi dhāraye nayanayor muhuḥ sparśaye
children.translated_text: 'Ah! I would bear him on my head! I would touch him to my eyes again and again!

children.text: hṛdi pracuram arpaye hṛdaya-madhyamāveśaye |
children.translated_text: I would place him abundantly in my heart! I would install him in the center of my heart!'

children.text: idaṃ vividha-bhāvanaṃ bhṛśam atītya vīcikṣiṣā
children.translated_text: This manifold imagination, greatly overcoming the desire to see,

children.text: balād vara-dṛśāṃ dṛśāṃ viṣayatām anaiṣīd amum ||JGc_1,3.48||
children.translated_text: forcefully brought him to become the object of the eyes of the beautiful-eyed ones! //

children.text: tatra ca -
muhur aho tanayaṃ nayanaṃ gataṃ
children.translated_text: Again and again, ah! The son came before the eyes,

children.text: pramadataḥ praṇayanty api nātṛpat |
children.translated_text: yet even as she placed him there with great delight, the mother was not satisfied.

children.text: ghana-rucir jananī-stana-yugmajām
children.translated_text: She of cloud-like radiance produced a rain of nectar from the pair of mother's breasts,

children.text: amṛta-vṛṣṭim adhād api dṛṣṭijām ||JGc_1,3.49||
children.translated_text: and also [a rain] born from her eyes! //
And there:

children.text: tataś cātyarvāg arha-śiśu-snapanādi-parvānusandhānataḥ sarvāsāṃ sāvadhānatā-vidhāne jāte -
children.translated_text: Then, when all had been set to attentiveness through the investigation of the proper occasions for the bathing of the worthy child and other celebrations:

children.text: rohiṇyājñām anu pati-suta-śreyasī vṛddha-viprā
children.translated_text: An aged <s>brāhmaṇa</s> lady, the most excellent for the welfare of husband and son, by <s>Rohiṇī's</s> command,

children.text: vṛttaṃ vijñāpayitum atulānandam eti sma nandam |
children.translated_text: went to <s>Nanda</s> to convey the news of the event, bringing incomparable joy.

children.text: vaktrollāsāt palita-valanād ambarāc chubhra-dhāmā
children.translated_text: From the radiance of her face, from the movement of her grey hair, from her garment of white splendor,

children.text: dhāmnāṃ hāsa-prathiti-tulitā yā javān nirjagāma ||JGc_1,3.50||
children.translated_text: she who emerged swiftly was like the spreading laughter of luminaries! //

children.text: atha tad etat-paryante vṛtte vṛtte, jāta-tat-tad-bhāva-sampadaḥ sabhāsadaḥ pratikṛtāñjalitayā sthitayor madhukaṇṭha-snighdakaṇṭhayor madhukaṇṭhaḥ prāha sma -
children.translated_text: Then, when all this had duly transpired, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> spoke to <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, who stood with palms reverently joined, both of honey-smooth, affectionate voices, while the assembly-members had attained the wealth of those sentiments:

children.text:
vrajendra so' yaṃ putras te sadaḥ-sādbhuta-sampadaḥ |
janma-mātrāj jana-śreṇyā nandana-śreṇi-janmadaḥ ||JGc_1,3.51|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'O lord of <s>Vraja</s>! This is your son, of wondrous glory among the assembly — who, by mere birth, bestows upon the host of people rows of <s>Nandana</s> (heavenly) gardens!' //

children.text: tataś ca tau nijopakaṇṭhopam anu vraja-rāja ājuhāva | āgatyoś ca tayoḥ śirasi kara-saroruham ādhāya nijālaṅkārair alañcakāra | sarvaṃ ca tat-sampradāyaṃ bahu-sampradānena sampradānam akarot | uvāca ca - adya vāsaḥ samāsādyatāṃ bhojananādy-artham iti | sarvān prati covāca - punar evaṃ prātaḥ prātar āyātavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Then the king of <s>Vraja</s> summoned the two to a place near himself. When they had come, placing his lotus-hand upon their heads, he adorned them with his own ornaments. And he made all the traditional gifts with abundant generosity. And he said: 'Today, lodging should be arranged, for the purpose of meals and the like.' And to all he said: 'You must come again like this, morning after morning.'

children.text: atha go-sambhālanārthaṃ pitaram anujñāṃ samabhyarthya mātaraṃ ca vanya-bhojana-prasthāpanaṃ prārthya sūta-kumāraayoś cātma-saṅgamanaṃ samarthya kṛta-vrāje vraja-yuva-rāje sarve yathā svam āvāsaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having sought his father's permission for tending the cows, having requested his mother to send the forest-meal, having arranged for the meeting with the two bard-princes, when the young prince of <s>Vraja</s> had performed his <s>Vraja</s>-duties, all went to their respective homes.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
kṛta-pūraṇa-vraja-varti-tṛṣṇa-śrī-kṛṣṇa-janma-sampan-mayaṃ
nāma tṛtīyaṃ pūraṇam
||3||
children.translated_text: Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopālacampū</s>, this is the Third Chapter, called 'Filled with the Wealth of the Birth of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose Thirsting is in the Wick of Fulfillment.' ||3||

children.text:
(4)
atha caturtha-pūraṇam
nanda-nandana-parva
children.translated_text: (4) Now the Fourth Chapter: The Festival of <s>Nanda's</s> Son.

children.text: atha pūrvedyur madhukaṇṭhaḥ kṛtī yathācīkṛtat, evam aparedyuś ca vraja-deva-sabhāyāṃ bhāsamānāyāṃ sāvasara-nidigdhaḥ snigdhakaṇṭhas tat-kīrtim acīkīrtat |
children.translated_text: Now, on the previous day, the accomplished <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> narrated as he had narrated; and likewise on the following day, when the assembly of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> was shining, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, steeped in the opportune moment, with affectionate voice, narrated that glory.

children.text: madhukaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭhaṃ papraccha-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> asked with longing:

children.text: prāg yadvac caritaṃ harer arasayad vāg-indriyaṃ tadvad apy
children.translated_text: 'Just as the past deeds of <s>Hari</s> savored the sense of speech, so too

children.text: adyāsvādayituṃ mamecchatitarām udyamya karṇa-dvayam |
children.translated_text: today my pair of ears strains most eagerly to taste them.

children.text: yady apy ekaka eva bhoktṛ-pada-bhāg jīvas tathāpi prati-
children.translated_text: Although the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) alone is the one entitled to enjoy,

children.text: svaṃ cakṣuḥ-prabhṛtīni tāni ca muhur vāñchanti bhoga-prathām ||JGc_1,4.1||
children.translated_text: even so, the eyes and other [senses] individually and repeatedly desire the spreading of that enjoyment!' //

children.text: tathā ca snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-athānanda-samṛddhā sā vṛddhā go-dohanārthaṃ gosthānam adhyavasthitān madhya-sthita-śrīman-nandopanandādīn vindati sma | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke: 'Then she, the aged one, enriched with joy, found the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Upananda</s>, and others stationed in the cow-pen for the purpose of milking, standing in the midst. And there:'

children.text: asta-vyasta-gatiḥ pramoda-madhurā paśyanty amūn agrataḥ
children.translated_text: 'Moving with unsteady gait, sweet with delight, seeing those [men] before her,

children.text: kiñcid vaktum ivodyad āsya-valanā dīrghāyitālpa-kṣitiḥ |
children.translated_text: with face turning as if about to say something, sighing long, occupying little space,

children.text: hasta-nyasta-phalādir evam api sā putrodbhavaṃ vyañjatī
children.translated_text: with fruits and such placed in her hand, thus indicating the birth of a son —

children.text: yat kiñcid vadati sma tat punar avādīd ity amī menire ||JGc_1,4.2||
children.translated_text: whatever little she said, they supposed she said it again and again!' //

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-kim uktavatī sā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'What did she say?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha sasmitam uvāca-asmākaṃ rājādya prajāta-prajāḥ | kathaṃ bhavantas tan-milanāya nāyānti ? iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said with a smile: 'Our king has today become one with a born offspring! Why do you not come for the meeting with him?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha sahāsam uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said with a laugh: 'And then? And then?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca taj-janma-vṛttāmṛta-nava-varṣābhiḥ śikhina iva gopāḥ kolāhalaṃ kalayāmāsuḥ | śrī-gopaty-adhipas tu vānaspatya iva pulakāṅkura-kulākulatayā paraṃ paramānandaṃ vyañjayāmāsa, na tu vacasā |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then the cowherds, like peacocks rejoicing in the showers of the fresh nectar of the story of that birth, raised a tumult! But the great lord of the cowherds, like a tree, displayed only supreme supreme bliss through the agitation of the buds of bristling hair — not through words.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'And then? And then?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca smita-sambhramādara-bhara-karbūritaiḥ sarvair vanditayā nanditayā ca tayā satvarayā paliknī-varayā sa-nijāṅga-jāta eva bhavān maṅgala-saṅgī bhūyād ity apūrvāṃ sukha-pūrvāṃ vācaṃ procya rocanā-kuṅkuma-saṅga-lepa-saṅkula-sad-aṅkura-phala-maṅgale śrīmad-vraja-rājasya kṣemaṅkara-karayor vinyaste tena vilokita-kalpaḥ śrīmān upanandaḥ sānandaṃ jalpati sma-iha dohāya saṃhāya raṃhasāyamānā dhenu-saṅghāḥ kām apy avihāya drutam asyāḥ sagṛhāya vihāpyantām |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, having been bowed to and delighted by all — variegated with smiles, fluster, and the weight of reverence — she, the aged and excellent one, hastily uttering the unprecedented and joyful words "May the lord, born with your own body, be associated with auspiciousness!" — placed a <s>maṅgala</s> (auspicious offering) of good sprouts and fruits mixed with <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment) and saffron paste in the auspiciousness-making hands of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>. Then the glorious <s>Upananda</s>, having attained the sight of a wish-fulfilling tree, spoke joyfully: "Let the herds of cows, which are being swiftly driven here for milking — without excluding any — be quickly brought along with [their gifts] for her!"'

children.text: tatra sarve cāmoda-garveṇa procuḥ-anyad vā yat kiñcid asyā hitaṃ samīhitaṃ bhavati | tataś ca-
