children.translated_text: And there all, with the pride of delight, said: 'Whatever else is desired as beneficial for her — let it be done!' And then:

children.text: āhlādena samaṃ jajñe bālaḥ kiṃ kiṃ sa eva saḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Was the boy born together with joy, or is he that very [joy] himself?' —

children.text: evaṃ viviktuṃ nandasya nāsīn matimatī matiḥ ||JGc_1,4.3||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Nanda</s>, the wise one, had no capacity to discriminate! //

children.text: atha śrīmān vrajeśaḥ svīkṛta-dhārmika-veśas tad api bahulam anyad api bahulādikaṃ dānāya saṃcakpe | yatra sarvaś ca tathābhāvāya kharvaśaś cakpe | saṅkalpya ca gṛhe gantuṃ kṛta-spṛhe dhṛta-veśe ca tat-tad-vṛta-vraja-nareśe śrī-rāma-prasū-samādeśān mahā-gopura-deśād dundubhi-dvandvam unnanāda | tac ca vādya-vidyā-vidura-vyañjitaṃ vādyaṃ vyaktam evedaṃ muhur vakti sma-prādurbhūto nandānanda iti | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, having assumed the attire of religious observance, resolved to give away abundantly yet more — and more in multiples — in charity. Where everyone also resolved to do the same, each in shorter measure. And when, having resolved, the lord of the <s>Vraja</s>-people was eager to go home and had assumed his attire, from the direction of the great gateway, by the command of <s>Rāma's</s> mother, a pair of kettledrums thundered! And that music, played with the skill remote from [ordinary] instrumental art, clearly and repeatedly proclaimed: 'The joy of <s>Nanda</s> has manifested!' And then:

children.text: api śrutam abhūn niśi tridiva-vādya-garjojitaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Was it the sound of celestial music thundering in the night that was heard —

children.text: jitaṃ jitam iti svanaṃ na tu viniścitaṃ kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: the sound "Conquered! Conquered!" — though the cause was not ascertained?

children.text: tadā tad-anuvādi tat kalayatām amīṣāṃ muhur
children.translated_text: When they perceived that [drumming] which echoed that [celestial sound],

children.text: mudā kalakalā-ravaṃ samajani vraja-prāṇinām ||JGc_1,4.4||
children.translated_text: a tumultuous clamor of joy arose among the creatures of <s>Vraja</s>!' //

children.text: atha saṃmadena muhur lambhita-stambhārambhatāyām apy utkaṇṭhayākṛṣṭa iva tatra ca labdha-kampa-sampattāyām api kevalaṃ svakṛta-sevena nārāyaṇa-devena datta-hastāvalamba iva dhairyam avalambamānaḥ svālayaṃ prati vraja-bhūpālaḥ pracacāla | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, though he had repeatedly attained the onset of paralysis through ecstasy, as if drawn by longing — and though he had attained the wealth of trembling — holding onto courage as if supported by the hand of Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who was [now] served solely by himself, the king of <s>Vraja</s> set forth toward his own home. And then:

children.text: tad vṛnde gṛham abhiyāti bandhu-vargā
children.translated_text: 'As he went homeward amidst that assembly, the kinsmen

children.text: dhāvantaḥ krama-militā mithaḥ purogāḥ |
children.translated_text: came running, meeting step by step, going before him —

children.text: ye gaṅgā-jharam anu nirjhara-prabhedā
children.translated_text: like the tributaries following the cascade of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: yadvat tat-tūlitatayānayanta vṛddhim ||JGc_1,4.5||
children.translated_text: who, being swept along by it, brought about its increase!' //

children.text: athāgatāḥ pura-vanitāḥ puraḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: Then the city-women arrived, row upon row,

children.text: sahasraśaḥ kalita-śubhāyutāyutāḥ |
children.translated_text: in thousands, adorned with tens of thousands of auspicious marks;

children.text: vrajeśvaraṃ puru nirarājayan jayan
children.translated_text: they abundantly waved the <s>nīrājana</s> (lamp) before the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, hailing [him]

children.text: navātmaja-prabhavamahe mahehayā ||JGc_1,4.6||
children.translated_text: at the great festival of the birth of the new son, with great royal splendor. ||4.6||

children.text: tataś ca kolāhalibhir vraja-sthitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, accompanied by the jubilant <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers,

children.text: samaṃ gataḥ śrīla-mahā-vrajeśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: the glorious great lord of <s>Vraja</s> went forth;

children.text: svarāṃs tu sālaṅkṛti cārv aśūśubhan
children.translated_text: but along with his ornaments, he himself beautifully shone

children.text: nabhaḥ-sabhaṃ pūrṇa-sudhāṃśuvat prabhuḥ ||JGc_1,4.7||
children.translated_text: like a full moon pervading the sky-assembly. ||4.7||

children.text: yadyapi viprāḥ sahasā
children.translated_text: Although the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> had all

children.text: svayam āgataye kṛtodyamāḥ sarve |
children.translated_text: spontaneously made efforts to come of their own accord,

children.text: tad api tad-ādara-vidhaye
children.translated_text: nevertheless, for the sake of showing them honor,

children.text: rājñāhūtāḥ pṛthak pṛthak prathamam ||JGc_1,4.8||
children.translated_text: they were individually summoned first by the king. ||4.8||

children.text: sukhāviṣṭas tasmin madhuram upaviṣṭaiḥ sadasi tair
children.translated_text: Filled with joy, sweetly seated in that assembly by those

children.text: mahā-snigdhaiḥ śarma-prakara-paridigdhaiḥ parivṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: most affectionate ones, surrounded by [them], anointed with heaps of happiness,

children.text: paṭhadbhiḥ putrāśīr ucita-nigamaṃ bhūsura-varaiḥ
children.translated_text: by the foremost earth-born ones (<s>brāhmaṇas</s>) reciting blessings for the son with appropriate <s>Vedic</s> [mantras],

children.text: kiradbhir dūrvādyaṃ śirasi sukha-pūrvaṃ sa mahitaḥ ||JGc_1,4.9||
children.translated_text: sprinkling <s>dūrvā</s> grass and the like upon his head — he was thus honored with joy. ||4.9||

children.text: sasne yat paricaskare vapur api svasti-śrutiḥ śuśruve
children.translated_text: That he bathed, that he prepared his body, that the blessing-recitations were heard,

children.text: śrīman-nanda-mahātmanā suta-janau tat tat stuve nāparam |
children.translated_text: that the great-souled <s>Śrīman Nanda</s> praised the birth of the son — and nothing more [need be said];

children.text: adyāpi sphuṭam eti sarva-janatā yeṣāṃ śrutād apy aho
children.translated_text: even today, from merely hearing of those [blessings], all people clearly attain [benefit] — ah!

children.text: snānādy apy atigamya satkṛti-phalaṃ yasyāsti nāntaḥ kvacit ||JGc_1,4.10||
children.translated_text: Even transcending the bathing and other [rites], the fruit of their honor has no end anywhere. ||4.10||

children.text: atha jāta-karma bhavyaṃ kartavyam iti gurubhir ādiṣṭena tena tat-pratyutkramaś cakre, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, instructed by the elders that the auspicious birth-rite (<s>jātakarma</s>) must be performed, he carried it out in the following order:

children.text:
ānarcire vrajeśitrā mātṛkā yās tadā tu tāḥ |
mātuḥ kam iva kaṃ yāsām ity artha-vyaktim āgatāḥ ||JGc_1,4.11||atha nāndīmukha-śrāddhaṃ rāddhaṃ gopāla-pālinā |
pitaro hi svayaṃ yasmiṃs te nāndīmukhatāṃ gatāḥ ||JGc_1,4.12||

children.translated_text:
The <s>Mātṛkā</s> goddesses who were then worshipped by the wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> —
for each of them, the meaning 'Whose mother is like whom?' became manifest. ||4.11||
Then the <s>Nāndīmukha-śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite of joy) was accomplished by the protector of the cowherds;
for in that [rite], the ancestors themselves attained the state of joy-faced (<s>nāndīmukha</s>). ||4.12||

children.text: atha veda-vidhāna-paṭubhiḥ sārdham antaḥpuraṃ praviṣṭe bhadra-kumbhādi-bhadra-viśiṣṭa-sūtikā-gṛhāgra-vedy-upaviṣṭe śrī-vraja-kula-mahiṣṭhe parama-manorathārohiṇī rohiṇī tad avadhāya kula-traya-yaśo-dāyi-yaśodā-khaṭṭām antaḥ-paṭena vyavadhāya bālaṃ pidhāya gṛhāvagrahaṇīm ānināya | kintu nava-bālakaṃ vilokayituṃ śarmaṇā narmaṇā ca nijālaṅkṛty-arthaṃ prajāvatyas taṃ pratyabhitaḥ kim api kim apy amūlyatā-paryācitaṃ yācitavatyaḥ pratiśrute tu taṃ vilokayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, when the most eminent chief of the <s>Vraja</s> clan, accompanied by those skilled in <s>Vedic</s> procedures, had entered the inner quarters and was seated on the platform before the auspicious birth-chamber distinguished by blessed water-jars and the like, <s>Rohiṇī</s> — ascending the chariot of supreme desires — having observed this, covered the bed of <s>Yaśodā</s> (whose name grants glory to three lineages) with a curtain, concealed the child, and brought forth the midwife. But the women, eager to see the new baby — with delight and with playful humor, for the sake of their own adornment — having requested something or other of inestimable value from those with children, upon receiving the promise, they then beheld him.

children.text:
sa ca khalv astoka-roka-loka-valaya-bhava-prabala-nava-kuvalaya-kulapati-durlaṅgha-śobhā-saṅghaṃ durlabha-komalāmala-kānti-viśrānti-bhūmiṃ, kalita-marma-prayatana-karma-viśvādbhuta-viśvakarma-nirmita-nirmala-nīla-cintāmaṇi-pratimā-pratipratīkātikrama-parimita-sarvāvayavaṃ, prabala-pravāha-dalita-cara-bāla-vāyaja-samavāyaja-mañjulāñjana-kalita-tala-niścala-jala-kālindī-hrada-jālaja-bāla-śaivālaka-ruci-rucira-rocir-valitārāla-ślakṣṇa-bāla-samudāyaṃ, kamalālayā-kara-kiśalaya-sita-lasita-sita-kamalāntar-valaya-dala-nirmala-vilocanaṃ, vaikuṇṭha-sthita-kalpa-taru-tallaja-pallava-kuṇṭhatākara-kara-caraṇādharaṃ, nipīta-kanaka-ruci-śuci-pītana-pītitāmbarāvaraṇa-rocanaṃ rocanaṃ bālakam ālocayann ātmānaṃ nayana-payaḥ-payasā snapayan vilakṣaṇatayā kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ jalavad āsīt
|
children.translated_text: And he, upon beholding the baby — [that child] who was the domain of a beauty insurpassable even by the chief of the powerful, fresh blue-lotus clusters born of the dark-hued realm from the numerous trembling-world circle; the resting-place of a rare, tender, spotless radiance; whose every limb was proportioned to surpass the likeness of a spotless blue <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) image created by the universally-wondrous divine artist <s>Viśvakarman</s> through the labor of craftsmanship that penetrates to the essence; whose mass of soft, beautiful, curly, fine infant-hair was charming like young dark algae in a pool of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā), upon whose still surface was applied the lovely dark collyrium gathered through the assemblage arising naturally from the powerful current smashing the moving — like the little breezes — [particles]; whose eyes were spotless like the inner petal-circle of a white lotus shining upon the white shoot-like hand of the abode of <s>Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī); whose hands, feet, and lower lip were tinged like the bashful young shoots of the wish-fulfilling trees in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>; whose garment was pleasing — a yellow cloth wrapped [around him], whose yellow hue had drunk the luster of gold — beholding that radiant child, bathing himself with the water of tears from his eyes, he remained for some moments like water, through the state of being [utterly] transfixed.

children.text: yadyapi bahuvidha-bhāvā, jātā goṣṭheśitus tarhi |
children.translated_text: Although many kinds of emotions arose then in the chief of the cowherd settlement,

children.text: tad api ca jāḍyaṃ balavaj jajñe gāmbhīrya-śīlasya ||JGc_1,4.13||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, a powerful stupor was born in him, [a man] of deep and grave temperament. ||4.13||

children.text: atha cirāya dhīra-bhāvaṃ dhāritavatī vraja-dharitrī rājya-śrīmatī tad-ānanda-spṛhiṇī nava-nandanam upananda-gṛhiṇī tad-utsaṅga-saṅginaṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then, after a long while, the earth-[queen] of <s>Vraja</s>, the royal-beauty-possessing one, who had maintained a state of composure, desirous of that bliss — <s>Upananda's</s> wife, the new grandmother — placed the new <s>Nandana</s> (son) upon his lap.

children.text: utsaṅgaṃ vahati śiśuṃ vrajādhirāje
children.translated_text: As the king of <s>Vraja</s> held the infant on his lap,

children.text: sā dūrād adhiśayitā prasūti-śayyām |
children.translated_text: she, lying at a distance upon the birthing-bed,

children.text: āsīt tac-chravaṇaja-bāṣpa-romaharṣa-
children.translated_text: became — by the tears, horripilation, and stupor born from hearing [the child's sounds] —

children.text: stambhādyair vivaśa-tanūr vrajādhirājñī ||JGc_1,4.14||
children.translated_text: the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, with body rendered helpless [by ecstasy]. ||4.14||

children.text: atha tatra medhā-janakaṃ karma śarmānta-nāmabhir nirmame, yatra bhūs tvayi ity-ādikaṃ paṭhitvā hemāntarhitayānāmikayā bālo ghṛta-lavaṃ lehayāmāse | athāyuṣya-kriyā kriyate sma, yatra oṃ divaspati ity ādikena ḍimbhaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ | dik-catuṣṭaye madhye ca oṃ hṛdam annaṃ prāṇāya ity ādibhir bhūmiś cābhimantritā | atha oṃ aśmā bhava ity ādinā punar arbhako' bhimṛṣṭaḥ | tataḥ oṃ iḍāsi ity ādinā tan-mātābhimantritā | punar mātuḥ stana-dvayaṃ oṃ imaṃ stanam iti, oṃ yas te stanam ity ābhyām ṛgbhyāṃ krameṇa prakṣālitam | tataś ca tam uttāna-śāyinaṃ sūtikā-śayyāyāṃ nidhāya tac-chiraḥ-pradeśe oṃ āpo deveṣu ity ādinodapātraṃ nihitam iti |
children.translated_text: Then, the rite for generating intelligence (<s>medhājanana</s>) was performed there, under names ending in '<s>śarman</s>' (happiness), wherein, having recited '<s>bhūs tvayi</s>' and the like, the baby was made to lick a morsel of clarified butter with the ring-finger concealed in gold. Then the life-span rite (<s>āyuṣya-kriyā</s>) was performed, wherein the child was touched with [the <s>mantra</s>] '<s>Oṃ divaspati</s>' and the like. And in the four cardinal directions and the center, the earth was consecrated with [<s>mantras</s> such as] '<s>Oṃ hṛdam annaṃ prāṇāya</s>' and the like. Then again the baby was ritually touched with '<s>Oṃ aśmā bhava</s>' (Be as stone!) and the like. Then his mother was consecrated with '<s>Oṃ iḍāsi</s>' and the like. Then the mother's pair of breasts was washed in order with the two <s>Ṛg</s>-verses '<s>Oṃ imaṃ stanam</s>' and '<s>Oṃ yas te stanam</s>.' Then, having laid him on his back upon the birthing-bed, a water-vessel was placed at the region of his head with [the <s>mantra</s>] '<s>Oṃ āpo deveṣu</s>' and the like.

children.text: tad evaṃ jāta-karma-śarmaṇi nirvṛtte bāla-nābhi-nāle ca prāpta-cchedana-kāle vṛtte paramānanda-sandohenānavahita-prāyā yā saiva tadaiva tad-avadhātrī dhātrī sapulaka-kāyā citram idam iti dvi-tri-vāram idam niveditavatī-rājan ! itaratra nābhi-sarasi nālam eva lakṣyate, na tu nālīkam | atra punar nālīkam eva na tu nālam iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the happiness-giving birth-rite (<s>jātakarma</s>) was completed and the time for cutting the baby's umbilical cord had arrived, the midwife-nurse herself — who at that very moment was largely inattentive due to floods of supreme bliss — her body bristling with horripilation, reported this wondrous thing two or three times: 'O King! Elsewhere, in the navel-pool, only a stalk (<s>nāla</s>) is seen, not a lotus (<s>nālīka</s>). But here, there is indeed a lotus, not [merely] a stalk!'

children.text: kiṃ ca-
aṅghryor vyakta-darāri-vajra-kamalādyāścarya-cihnair alaṃ
children.translated_text: 'On the feet, with wondrous signs clearly [visible] — the enemy-splitting <s>vajra</s>, the lotus, and other marks —

children.text: kamrair ujjvalitāṃ tathā kara-yuge taiḥ kaiścid anyair api |
children.translated_text: beautifully illuminated, and likewise on the pair of hands, with those and certain other [marks],

children.text: paśya śrī-vrajanātha nīrada-rucer bālasya sāmudrako-
children.translated_text: behold, O glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, the body-fold of this cloud-complexioned baby

children.text: llaṅghi-śrī-vibhavasya deha-valanām asmāsu citra-pradām ||JGc_1,4.15||
children.translated_text: whose glorious majesty surpasses the ocean — [it is] a source of wonder for us!' ||4.15||
Moreover:

children.text: tadā ca sarvasminn api vismita-caryā-paryākule baṭavaḥ sahāsa-pāṭavam ūcuḥ-aye ! sarva-śarmada ! nirmala-dharmaṇo bhavataḥ katham aśaucaṃ nāma sāmarthyaṃ samarthayatām ? yato nāḍī-ccheda eva vṛtte tad āmananti sma |
children.translated_text: Then, when everyone was overwhelmed with wonder, the young <s>brāhmaṇa</s> students said with a blend of laughter and skill: 'O bestower of all happiness! How can impurity (<s>aśauca</s>) claim authority over you, whose <s>dharma</s> is spotless? For they recite that [impurity begins] only at the cutting of the cord.'

children.text: tad evam ullasan nikhila-roma-samutphulla-mukha-somaḥ parivārita-baṭu-stomatayā bahir vihita-homa-sthānam āgamya samyag arpita-sarvānandaḥ saṅgi-samarpita-tat-tad-vṛtta-śantama-kandaḥ śrīmān nandas tān dānīya-viprān ānīya pradānārambhaṃ sambhṛtavān |
children.translated_text: Thus, with all body-hair fully blossoming, with a moon-like face shining, surrounded by the multitude of young <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having come outside to the place prepared for the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), having properly offered all his joy, the root of the most auspicious accounts of various occasions presented by his associates — the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, having brought those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> worthy of gifts, commenced the distribution of gifts.

children.text: ārebhe sa ca dātuṃ, lebhe na tulāṃ tu saṅgināṃ teṣām |
children.translated_text: He began to give, but found no balance for them, those associates

children.text: tādṛśa-tat-prasava-śrī-vārtā yair arpitā paritaḥ ||JGc_1,4.16||
children.translated_text: by whom the tidings of such splendor of that birth had been conveyed all around. ||4.16||

children.text:
tathāpi-
ayutaṃ prayutaṃ niyutaṃ bhavati daśānāṃ sahasram ārabhya |
niyute viṃśati-lakṣaṃ tāvad dhenūr adān nandaḥ ||JGc_1,4.17||viṃśati-lakṣaṃ dattvā dhenūḥ sauvarṇa-śṛṅga-saṅgy-aṅgīḥ |
hṛdayam apūrṇatayāsīt tasyānyasmai pradānāya ||JGc_1,4.18||daśabhir daśabhir droṇaiḥ kṛta-tila-saptācalīm adadāt |
yad-vṛti-maṇi-kanakānāṃ tad-adhikatara-bhāratā dvijair mene ||JGc_1,4.19||tebhyaś ca dakṣiṇīyebhyaḥ prattā yā dakṣiṇāmunā |
tayāpy akṣīṇayānyeṣām akṣīṇy āścaryam āyayuḥ ||JGc_1,4.20||bāḍavyānām asaṅkhyānāṃ nāsīt paricitis tadā |
brahma-varcasam evāsmin paricāyakatāṃ yayau ||JGc_1,4.21||
children.translated_text: Brahmanical splendor itself became their attendant. ||4.21||

children.text:
tatra ye vidita-vedābhiprāyā viprā nija-nija-vidyātiśāyakāḥ sūta-māgadha-vandi-kṛśāśvi-gāyakāḥ svacchanda-nānā-śabda-vādakā vādakāś ca, te sarve' pi tasmin parvaṇi saṅginaḥ santaḥ sumaṅgalam eva śabdāyamānāḥ pṛthaktāyām apy apṛthaṅ-nisvanā iva viśvaṃ vismāyayanti sma | yāvad evaṃ vṛttaṃ vṛttam, tāvad vraja-sthalam api hṛṣṭam iva dṛṣṭaṃ, kim uta vrajasthāḥ | yataḥ saṃsṛṣṭatayā vikṣepa-śūnyam iva saṃsiktatayā snigdham iva, cala-citra-dhvajāditayā nṛtyad iva cāsīt | tatra ca yadā go-vṛṣa-vatsānām api svabhāvata eva bhavataḥ sānurāga-snehasya taila-vidrāvita-haridrā-samakti-vyājād bahir api vyaktir āsīt | harṣa-vaicitryasya ca vicitra-dhātu-barha-srak-kāñcana-mālā-vyājāt | tadā kim uta gopānāṃ te hy adyāpi yaśasā
vidyamānā go-pṛthivyāḥ pātāra itīva tathocyante | ye khalu vyañjita-rasa-bhāvatayā vidhṛtālaṅkāratayā ca sva-varṇana-kāvya-granthair abhedam āyayuḥ | ullāsa-vidhṛta-nānā-maṇi-maya-bali-pāṇitayā premaṇi sveṣāṃ vīratāṃ ca vyañjayāmāsuḥ | yadā caivaṃ gopās tadā punar atīva jīvanāyamāna-gokula-kuleśvarī guṇa-gaṇa-digdha-snigdha-hṛdayā gopa-vara-varṇinyaḥ kiyad vā varṇanīyāḥ ?
children.translated_text: There, those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who knew the purport of the <s>Vedas</s>, surpassing in their respective knowledge, the bards, eulogists, panegyrists, <s>Kṛśāśvi</s>-singers, the free-spirited instrumentalists playing various sounds — all of them, being present at that festive occasion, sounding only auspicious [notes], even in their separateness were like those of undivided sound, causing wonder in the entire world. As long as these events transpired, even the ground of <s>Vraja</s> appeared as if delighted — what then of the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers? For it appeared as if moistened through being permeated, as if affectionate through being sprinkled, and as if dancing through the [waving of] moving colorful banners. And there, when even the cows, bulls, and calves — whose natural and affectionate love — had its external manifestation through the pretext of being smeared with oil-dissolved turmeric; and the variety of their joy [expressed] through the pretext of variegated mineral pigments, peacock-feather garlands, and golden necklaces — then what need to speak of the cowherds? For even today they are called 'the ferrymen of the cow-earth,' being present through [their] fame. They indeed, through the display of expressed <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and through wearing ornaments, became one with their own descriptive poetic texts. Through the joy-borne raising of hands holding various gem-laden offerings, they manifested their heroism and their love. And when the cowherds were thus, then the cowherd women — queens of the <s>Gokula</s> clan who were supremely vivified, with hearts affectionately anointed by the multitude of virtues — how much more could they be described?

children.text: yāḥ khalu pūrvaṃ tad-apatya-samapatty-abhāvān nirveda-vedanayā tyakta-prāya-pariṣkārāḥ, samprati tu kiñcic-caraṇa-pravaṇa-tad-apatya-śravaṇa-mātreṇa vidhṛta-vividha-sukha-vikārās tat-parva-rañjanārthaṃ vilambanīyām api pariṣkṛtim urīkṛtya nṛtyantya iva tat-purīṃ prati calitāḥ | yāś ca vyañjijiṣita-maṅgala-saṅgatayā sneha-maya-kāmanā-pariṇāmatayā ca svayam eva mahā-maṇi-mayopāyana-pāṇayo babhūvuḥ | yāsām ānandād anyad eva śobhā-vaibhavam āvirbhavati sma |
children.translated_text: They who previously, from the sorrow of not having offspring of such [quality], with the pain of disenchantment, had nearly abandoned all adornment — but who now, merely from hearing of the birth of that son, somewhat inclined toward their feet, having assumed the transformation of various forms of happiness, and having accepted the adornment that should have been delayed for the sake of festival-beautification, set forth toward his city as if dancing. And they who, with the fullness of a wish to express auspiciousness and with the maturation of affection-filled desires, themselves became bearers of offerings of great jewels in their hands. From whose joy, quite another majesty of beauty would manifest.

children.text: tathā hi-
children.translated_text: As follows:

children.text: jita-kuṅkumam uru ruruce mukha-śaśināṃ rocir etāsām |
children.translated_text: The radiance of the moon-like faces of these women outshone saffron;

children.text: samuditam uditaṃ parvaṇi suta-januṣaḥ śrī-yaśodāyāḥ ||JGc_1,4.22||
children.translated_text: it rose at the festival of the birth of a son to <s>Śrī Yaśodā</s>. ||4.22||

children.text: tatra ca gāyanti-
children.translated_text: And there they sing:

children.text: ajani yaśodā niśi suta-sāram |
children.translated_text: '<s>Yaśodā</s> has given birth to the essence of a son in the night!'

children.text: iti mahilālir itā tad-agāram ||dhru||
children.translated_text: Thus the group of women went to that house. ||refrain||

children.text: sambhrama-viracita-bahu-vidha-veśam |
children.translated_text: 'With many kinds of attire hastily arranged,

children.text: pathi mālya-cyava-pūrita-deśam ||
children.translated_text: on the path, [their] area filled with garlands falling off,

children.text: cala-maṇi-kuṇḍala-valita-kapolam |
children.translated_text: with cheeks framed by moving jeweled earrings,

children.text: aparikalita-galad-aṃśa-nicolam ||
children.translated_text: with garment-ends slipping from their shoulders unnoticed,

children.text: ucchalita-cchavi-capalāhāram |
children.translated_text: with flickering beauty playfully robbing the necklaces,

children.text: citra-vasana-vasa-rasanā-vāram ||
children.translated_text: with the succession of girdle-strings captivating the colorful garments —

children.text:
aparaspara-gati-vijitānyonyam |
sagaṇā vyahasīd iha cānyonyam ||JGc_1,4.23|| iti |
children.translated_text:
surpassing one another in their respective paces,
the group laughed at each other here!' ||4.23||

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
vrajaḥ prakaṭatāṃ yātas tatra kṛṣṇaś ca saṅgataḥ |
ity avādyanta vādyāni vādyādhiṣṭhātṛ-daivataiḥ ||JGc_1,4.24||tasmād ānanda-sandohād upananda-puraḥsarāḥ |
gambhīrās te' pi cābhīrā vijahrur nanṛtur jaguḥ ||JGc_1,4.25||tadā tatrāgatā yoṣās taṃ sadāśīrbhir arbhakam |
nirvarṇya varṇayitvā ca parasparam idaṃ jaguḥ ||JGc_1,4.26||
children.translated_text: having described and praised [him] to one another, sang this: ||4.26||

Moreover:
'<s>Vraja</s> has become manifest, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has joined it!' —
thus the instruments were played by the presiding deities of instruments. ||4.24||
From that flood of bliss, led by <s>Upananda</s>,
even those grave <s>Ābhīras</s> (cowherds) sported, danced, and sang. ||4.25||
Then the women who had come there, having blessed that baby with constant blessings,

children.text: pāhi ciraṃ vraja-rāja-kumāra |
children.translated_text: 'Protect [us] long, O prince of the cowherd-king,

children.text: asmān atra śiśo sukumāra ||dhru||
children.translated_text: protect us here, O tender child!' ||refrain||

children.text: drutatara-vṛddhi-samṛddhi-gatena |
children.translated_text: 'By swiftly growing prosperity,

children.text: śaṃ bhavatād bhavatābhimatena ||
children.translated_text: may there be happiness for you through what is dear to you!

children.text: spṛhayāmas te hasita-mukhāya |
children.translated_text: We long for you, O smiling-faced one,

children.text: aṅgana-saṅgata-riṅga-sukhāya ||
children.translated_text: for the joy of crawling in the company of women!

children.text: go-bālāvali-lūmālambi |
children.translated_text: Clinging to the tails of rows of young cows,

children.text: calanaṃ tava valatām avilambi ||
children.translated_text: may your walking happen without delay!

children.text: saha go-śāvaka-gama-ramaṇena |
children.translated_text: With the delight of going together with young calves,

children.text: sukhayasi hanta kadā kamanena ||
children.translated_text: when, alas, will you make us happy with [your] loveliness?

children.text: go-gaṇa-cāraṇa-viharaṇam asya |
children.translated_text: The roaming and playing [while] herding the multitude of cows — of this one —

children.text: sa tu paśyed vara-bhāgyaṃ yasya ||
children.translated_text: he alone would see the supreme fortune of whom: ||

children.text: duṣṭa-kadala-dada-suṣṭhu-balāya |
children.translated_text: For one who strikes down wicked givers of evil bananas — of great strength, |

children.text: bhava-śiṣṭāli-viśiṣṭa-phalāya ||JGc_1,4.27||
children.translated_text: for one whose fruit is the most distinguished of the polished [ones] of existence. || (JGc 1,4.27)

children.text: iti saṅgīta-saṅginyo raṅgiṇyo maha-sampadi |
children.translated_text: Thus, the singing companions, joyful, in the great festivity, |

children.text: pītā-tailena siñcantyaḥ siñcantyaḥ prayayur bahiḥ ||JGc_1,4.28||
children.translated_text: sprinkling with yellow mustard oil, went outside. || (JGc 1,4.28)

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And then —

children.text: dadhi-dugdhādi-sekena mitho' mī śubhratāṃ gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Drenched with yogurt, milk, and the like, these [cowherds] attained mutual radiance — |

children.text: taraṅgā iva dugdhābdher anṛtyan vara-goduhaḥ ||JGc_1,4.29||
children.translated_text: like waves of the milk-ocean, the excellent milkmen danced! || (JGc 1,4.29)

children.text: atha tās tad avadhāya tad eva gāyanti sma, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then the women, observing that, sang this very [song], as follows —

children.text: paśya sakhī-kula gokula-rājam |
children.translated_text: 'Behold, O company of friends, the king of <s>Gokula</s>!

children.text: putrotsavam anu khelā-bhājam ||dhru||
children.translated_text: Engaged in festive play on the occasion of the son-celebration!' || [refrain]

children.text: udadhi-prabha-dadhi-saṃplava-deśam |
children.translated_text: 'The scene of a flood of yogurt with the radiance of the ocean,

children.text: parito ghūrṇita-mandara-veśam ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by the whirling appearance of the <s>Mandara</s> [mountain],

children.text: madhya-dhaṭī-phaṇi-rāje kṛṣṭam |
children.translated_text: drawn in the middle by the king of serpents upon the churning-rod,

children.text: hṛdya-suhṛdbhir atīva ca hṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: and exceedingly delighted by his charming friends!'

children.text: madhye madhye durlabha-dānam |
children.translated_text: 'In between, giving rare gifts,

children.text: dadataṃ dadhataṃ vismaya-bhānam ||
children.translated_text: bestowing them, displaying a vessel of wonder!'

children.text:
ekaṃ punar alam abhavad apūrvam |
ajani vidhur bata yad itaḥ pūrvam ||JGc_1,4.30|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'One more thing that was unprecedented occurred: | the moon, alas, was born before him!' || (JGc 1,4.30)

children.text: etad api ślokayāmāsuḥ-
children.translated_text: They also composed this verse —

children.text:
neyaṃ dugdha-vikīrṇi-pālir api tu drāg-vāri-dhārā-gatir
neyaṃ syān navanīta-piṇḍa-visṛtir muktās tu muktāmbudāḥ |
neyaṃ dīrṇa-haridra-nīra-vikṛtiḥ kintu prabhā vidyutāṃ
parvaivedam atīva harṣa-mahasā varṣā-vapur nirmame ||JGc_1,4.31|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'This is not the scattering of spilled milk; rather, it is the flow of swift water-streams! | This is not the release of lumps of butter; but rather released pearl-clouds! | This is not the transformation of dissolved turmeric-water; rather, it is the radiance of lightning! | This indeed is a festival; by the greatness of overwhelming joy, a rainy-season form was created!' || (JGc 1,4.31)

children.text: bālasya mātāmaham etya mātulās
children.translated_text: The maternal uncles of the baby, coming to the maternal grandfather,

children.text: tadā gṛhītāḥ kara-corakā iva |
children.translated_text: were then caught like hand-thieves.

children.text: dadhy-ādi-paṅkeṣu muhur vikarṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: From being repeatedly dragged through the puddles of yogurt and the like,

children.text: pitṛvya-vargeṇa vihasya daṇḍitāḥ ||JGc_1,4.32||
children.translated_text: they were laughingly punished by the group of paternal uncles. || (JGc 1,4.32)

children.text: śrīmān nandaś ca-
children.translated_text: And the glorious <s>Nanda</s> —

children.text: mahodāra-cittaś citāneka-vittaṃ
children.translated_text: Of great generous mind, having gathered abundant accumulated wealth,

children.text: samāhūya sarvaṃ guṇājīvi-kharvam |
children.translated_text: having summoned everyone, even the humblest of those who live by virtue,

children.text: vinā tad-vicāraṃ vapuḥ-śakti-sāraṃ
children.translated_text: without any discrimination, casting forth the essence of his bodily strength,

children.text: samutkṣipya ratnaṃ dade sātiyatnam ||JGc_1,4.33||
children.translated_text: he gave jewels with the utmost effort. || (JGc 1,4.33)

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: grahītā yācitāny atra pradātāṅgīkriyā-yutaḥ
children.translated_text: The receiver has what is requested; here the giver is endowed with acceptance; |

children.text: śrīman-nandena dāne tu tatra jāto viparyayaḥ ||JGc_1,4.34||
children.translated_text: but in the giving of the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, there occurred a reversal! || (JGc 1,4.34)

children.text: ataeva-
children.translated_text: Therefore —

children.text: vinā yācñāṃ dadāne tu sarvaṃ vraja-patau tadā |
children.translated_text: When the lord of <s>Vraja</s> was giving everything without being asked, |

children.text: kalpadru-cintāmaṇy-ādyās te' py āsan kṛpaṇā iva ||JGc_1,4.35||
children.translated_text: even the wish-fulfilling tree and wish-fulfilling gem and the like appeared miserly! || (JGc 1,4.35)

children.text: tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And there —

children.text: anena prīyatāṃ viṣṇus tena stān me sute śivam |
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> be pleased by this; by that may auspiciousness abide in my son' — |

children.text: evaṃ prasabham udbhūtā dāne nandasya bhāvanā ||JGc_1,4.36||
children.translated_text: such was the sentiment that spontaneously arose in <s>Nanda</s> during his giving. || (JGc 1,4.36)

children.text: atha sarvā janatā janita-snāna-kāmā samam amunā yamunām ayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then all the people, having generated the desire to bathe, went together to the <s>Yamunā</s> with him.

children.text: tatra cānandena śrī-nandena saha galad-vrīḍāṃ jala-krīḍāṃ santatya nirmala-parimala-parimilana-pūrvakaṃ snānam ātatya divya-vastra-saṃvastraṇaṃ vitatya candra-candana-samālambhaṃ pratatya tatroṭaja-madhyam adhyāsīnāṃ siddha-pratana-prayatanatayā pūrṇa-mānasāṃ paurṇamāsīm anu namanam avatatya vandi-jana-janita-viśrāva-pūrita-śravasā śravasā valitā sā punas tad eva sadanam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: There, with the joyful glorious <s>Nanda</s>, having extended water-sports free from bashfulness, having performed the bath preceded by fragrant mingling of pure perfumes, having spread divine garments as coverings, having applied moon-like sandal-paste, having bowed to <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> who sat within a hermitage there, her mind fulfilled by the efforts of accomplished <s>siddha</s>-worship, and having filled her ears with the fame generated by the panegyrist-folk, she (<s>Yaśodā</s>), accompanied by fame, returned to that very residence again.

children.text: tataḥ śrīmān vrajasya rājā ruci-dānāni racayan bandhu-vṛnda-sindhuṃ pūrayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, arranging delightful gifts, filled the ocean of the kinsmen-multitude.

children.text: atha tasminn ānanda-pīvni pratidīvni śrī-rāma-jananyā śraddhā-yantritatayā nimantritāḥ kṛta-ghṛta-pakva-jemanāḥ sarva eva parva-lakṣmyā pūritāś candrā iva sva-sva-mandiram avindananta | viditvā ca tad-ānandaṃ prati kṛta-pratijāgarāṃ jāgarām eva nṛtya-gītādi-dhanyāyāṃ rajanyām abhajanta |
children.translated_text: Then, on that next blissful day, invited by the mother of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (Balarāma) (<s>Rohiṇī</s>) with devoted sincerity, having eaten meals cooked in clarified butter, everyone, filled with the auspiciousness of the festival like full moons, found their respective homes. And knowing that a vigil was being kept for that joy, they embraced the blessed night of dancing, singing, and other festivities as a sleepless night.

children.text: śrī-rohiṇyā hari-jani-sukhaṃ śakyate kena vaktuṃ
children.translated_text: Who can describe the joy of <s>Śrī Rohiṇī</s> at <s>Hari's</s> birth?

children.text: yasmād veṣaṃ vividham adadhād bhartṛtaḥ proṣitāpi |
children.translated_text: For she assumed various festive attires even though separated from her husband!

children.text: citraṃ citraṃ sukṛta-varimā dṛśyatāṃ viśva-vandyaḥ
children.translated_text: Wonderful, wonderful — let the greatness of her good fortune be seen, honored by the world!

children.text: śrīman-nando' py amanuta nijaṃ bhāgyam āyātim asyāḥ ||JGc_1,4.37||
children.translated_text: Even the glorious <s>Nanda</s> considered his own fortune to be due to her arrival! || (JGc 1,4.37)

children.text: atha so' yaṃ ratnākaro' pi vrajas taṃ harer āvirbhāvam ārabhyāharahar viraha-rahita-tad-viharaṇād vardhiṣṇu-samṛddhiḥ kām api camatkāritāṃ vitene | gopa-samavāyāt kramād āvirbhūtānāṃ prabhūtānāṃ paramāṇāṃ ramāṇāṃ ramaṇa-dhāmatayā tu kim uta ?
children.translated_text: Now this <s>Vraja</s>, though already a mine of jewels, from the day of <s>Hari's</s> manifestation onward, by the daily, ever-growing prosperity from his play free from separation, produced an indescribable wonder. With the abundant supreme delights that gradually appeared from the assemblages of cowherds — as a domain of delight — what more need be said?

children.text: atha madhukaṇṭhena cintanyāñcakre-āṃ śrīmad-bhāgavata-saṃvādaś cātra sambhavati-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> reflected — 'And here, a concordance with the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> also occurs' —

children.text: tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarva-samṛddhimān |
harer nivāsātma-guṇai ramā-krīḍam abhūn nṛpa ||[BhP 10.5.18] iti |
children.translated_text: and became the playground of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), by the self-qualities of <s>Hari's</s> dwelling, O King.' (BhP 10.5.18)
'From that time onward, the <s>Vraja</s> of <s>Nanda</s> became possessed of all prosperity,

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭhas tu vibhāvya punar āha sma-aho mahotsāha-svabhāvatādibhir virājamānatā śrīmad-vrajarājasya | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, having reflected, said again — 'Ah, how resplendent is the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, with his nature of supreme enthusiasm and the like! For:' —

children.text:
tāvan mānaṃ vitaraṇam aho sampadas tāḥ kiyatyas
tāvat saṅkhyaṃ mahasi racanaṃ bhṛtya-vargāḥ kiyantaḥ |
tāvat prāntaṃ jana-sama-vanaṃ katy amuṣyāvadhānāny
evaṃ sarvaṃ vraja-narapateḥ ko nu śakto vivektum ||JGc_1,4.38|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'So much honor, so much distribution — ah, how many were those riches! | So much counting, so much grandeur in arrangement — how many servant-groups! | So far the extent, so much forest equal to the people — how many were his exertions! | Thus, who indeed is able to discern everything about the king of <s>Vraja</s>?' || (JGc 1,4.38)

children.text: samāpayaṃś covāca-
children.translated_text: And concluding, he said —

children.text: īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava goṣṭha-kṣitīśa yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Such a son was born to you, O Lord of the cow-settlement, who,

children.text: lakṣmī-lakṣānvitaṃ kurvan goṣṭhaṃ ninye vilakṣatām ||JGc_1,4.39||
children.translated_text: making the cow-settlement endowed with a hundred-thousand marks of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), led [even prosperity itself] to astonishment!' || (JGc 1,4.39)

children.text:
tad etad vṛtte ca vṛtte pūrva-dinavad akhilā eva nija-nijālayam āsāditavantaḥ śrī-gokula-yuvarājaś ca gavāṃ kulam iti |
iti śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
śrīman-nanda-nandana-parva nāma
caturthaṃ pūraṇam
||4||
children.translated_text:
And so, when this event too was concluded, just as on the previous day, everyone returned to their own respective homes. And the young prince of glorious <s>Gokula</s> [returned] to the community of cows.
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Fourth Chapter, called 'The Festival of the Glorious Son of <s>Nanda</s>.'
||4||

children.text: atha pañcamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Fifth Chapter.

children.text: pūtanā-vadhāvadhāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: The narration of the slaying of <s>Pūtanā</s>.

children.text: athottaredyus tathā dyotamānāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ kaṇṭha-dhvani-kṛta-sarvotkaṇṭhaḥ śubhaṃyur madhukaṇṭhaḥ samācaṣṭa, aye snigdhakaṇṭha, śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, in the similarly shining assembly, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, the auspicious one, whose throat-sounds created universal eagerness, narrated: 'Listen, O <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> —'

children.text: atha tasminn evāpadoṣe pradoṣe samasta-deva-rūpa-śrī-vasudeva-sadeśataḥ sandeśa-haraḥ ko' pi gopitātmā śrī-vrajarāja-caraṇa-rājīva-pīṭha-paryanta-dhāma samājagāma | sa ca śrīmatā tena tadīya-pratna-sevaka-ratnatayā pariciti-yuktaḥ paryanuyukta-kuśala-tatir namaḥ samācarann uvāca-"rakṣāṃsi sarvaṃ bhakṣayituṃ jīvati bhṛśaṃ nṛśaṃse kaṃse kim iva niraṅkuśaṃ kuśalam? tac ca mama veśenaiva vitarkyatām | yad asmākaṃ taraṇyā taraṇaṃ, taraṇau ca sati kutrāpi prasthānaṃ na sambhavatīti bāhubhyām eva santaraṇāt tīrṇa-taraṇijaḥ sārdra-vastraḥ pradoṣe samāgato' smi |"
children.translated_text: 'Now, in that very faultless evening twilight, from the direction of <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s>, who was himself the form of all gods, a certain messenger, having concealed himself, arrived at the domain extending to the lotus-throne of the feet of the glorious King of <s>Vraja</s>. And he, being recognized by the glorious [king] as a jewel among his ancient servants, was questioned about his welfare and, bowing in salutation, said: "When the demons (<s>rākṣasas</s>) live eagerly to devour everything, under the utterly ruthless <s>Kaṃsa</s>, what welfare is there unobstructed? That may be judged by my very appearance. For our crossing of the river [was achieved only because] there was no boat available, and departure to anywhere was not possible — therefore, having crossed by swimming with my own arms, having crossed the river's daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>), I have arrived at dusk with wet garments."'

children.text: vrajarājas tu rukṣaṃ hasann āha, "viśeṣaś cet kathyatām |"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s>, laughing harshly, said: 'If there is something specific, let it be told.'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"kim adhikayā vaivadhikatayā sāmpratam asmākam ajīvanir eva jīvātu-vallī, yayā nijādhīśaṃ tādṛśa-tad-adhīnaṃ na paśyāmaḥ |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Why speak of further elaboration? At present, our very creeper of survival is our life-sustainer, by which we do not behold our own lord, who is so much under that one's (<s>Kaṃsa's</s>) control.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"samprati taṃ prati kim api viśeṣa-vṛttaṃ vṛttam asti?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Has any particular event recently occurred concerning him?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"atha kiṃ? yata eva tadīya-caraṇa-hitaḥ prahitas tenāham ayam asmi |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Indeed! Since I have been sent by him, his servant well-disposed toward his feet — here I am.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"kiṃ tat?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'What is it?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"ānantaryeṇa paryavasitāyā niśāyā niśīthe śrīmad-īśasya tasmin kārāgāra eva śrī-devakī-devītaḥ kācit kanyā jātā |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'At midnight, at the end of a night concluded without interruption, in that very prison, a certain girl was born to the glorious <s>Devakī-devī</s> from the glorious Lord.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"tatas tataḥ?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Then? Then?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"tataḥ sā nava-sutā sutarāṃ guptāpi rudatī rakṣibhir akṣibhir alakṣitāpi viditā, veditā cāntaḥ-purīśaya-sānuśaya-durāśaya-durīśāya | sa ca śrī-devakī-devī-vivāha-gatāham ārabhya nabhaḥ-sabhya-jana-vāṇītaḥ suṣṭhu bhītaḥ satataṃ vyagratayā jāgrad eva tiṣṭhati | tatas tad-vacana-varṇākarṇana-mātreṇa samagra-vyagra-manāḥ vikṣipta-keśaḥ sa bhojeśaḥ sa-karavālaḥ karālaḥ skhalad-gatiḥ kumatiḥ sūtikāgāram āsasāra |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Then that newborn daughter, though extremely well-guarded, crying, though unseen by the eyes of the guards, became known — and was reported to the one lying in the inner palace, regretful, of evil intent, the wicked lord (<s>Kaṃsa</s>). And he, since the wedding of <s>Śrī Devakī-devī</s>, having been well-frightened by the voice of the celestial beings, always remains awake in constant agitation. Then, by the mere hearing of those spoken words, his mind entirely agitated, his hair disheveled, that lord of the <s>Bhojas</s>, sword in hand, terrible, stumbling in gait, evil-minded, rushed to the maternity chamber.'

children.text: vrajarāja sa-bhayam uvāca-"tatas tataḥ?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said with fear: 'Then? Then?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"tataś ca niravagraha-graha-van niranugrahaḥ sahasā raṃhasā sūtikā-śayyām eva sajjan sa nirlajjaḥ prajātāyā jāta-parivedanāyā devyāḥ kroḍataḥ samācchidya, tad vidyamānam eva vikṣiptatām eva vikṣipta-cittaḥ kṣipram eva tāṃ prastarāya prakṣiptavān, yataḥ sarvataḥ sa eva pratikṣiptatām āpa |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Then, that one, without restraint, seizing like a planet, without mercy, suddenly falling upon the very birthing-bed, shameless — from the lap of the goddess who had just given birth and was experiencing the pains of delivery — snatching [the baby], that deranged one, though it existed right there, hurled it toward the stone slab in his frenzy — but from all sides he alone was repulsed.'

children.text: atha vrajarāja sāsram uvāca-"āḥ katham etad durakṣara-mrakṣitam anakṣaram asmāsu śrāvitam? bhavatv, adyāpy avadyam idaṃ madīya-saṃstyāye na prastāvyam | sā tu tad-duḥkha-duḥkhitā śrī-devakī-sakhī tathā tad-virahiṇī śrī-rohinī ca moham āpsyati |"
children.translated_text: Then the King of <s>Vraja</s> said with tears: 'Ah! How has this ill-lettered, besmeared, speechless thing been made audible to us? So be it — even today, this reprehensible deed should not be spoken of in my family circle. But <s>Śrī Rohiṇī</s>, who is the friend of <s>Śrī Devakī</s> — distressed by her distress — and she who is separated from her — will fall into a swoon.'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"deva, śrūyatām avyagram agrimam āścaryam |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'O Lord, hear without agitation the foremost wonder.'

children.text: vrajarājaḥ sa-harṣam ivovāca, "āyuṣman, kathyatāṃ tathyam |"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said, as if with delight: 'Long-lived one, let the truth be told.'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"sā tu kanyā tasyānyāya-bhājo bhojeśasya hastād astāpi prastaram aprāptā, pratyuta tan-mastaka-nyasta-caraṇam ūrdhva-gatyā samutpatyāśu divy anyad eva divyaṃ rūpaṃ smitavatī prakāśitavatī |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'But that girl, though seized from the hand of that unjust lord of the <s>Bhojas</s>, did not reach the stone slab at all; rather, placing her foot upon his head, flying upward, she quickly, smiling, revealed another divine, truly divine form.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"kīdṛśam?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Of what kind?'

children.text:
dūta uvāca,
  "śyāmāṣṭapāṇi-pariveṣṭita-pārśva-yugmā
  cakrādi-śastra-valitā khaga-siṃha-vāhā |
  devādibhiḥ pariṇuta-prasarat-prabhāvā
  sarvaiḥ samunnata-mukhaiḥ parito vyaloki ||JGc_1,5.1|| [vasanta] iti yādṛśam |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: | 'Dark, eight-armed, surrounded on both sides, | adorned with the discus and other weapons, riding an eagle-lion vehicle, | praised by gods and others with their spreading power, | she was beheld on all sides by all with upturned faces.' || (JGc 1,5.1) [vasantatilakā] — of such a kind.'

children.text: vrajarājaḥ sāścaryam uvāca-"kiṃ vadasi?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said with wonder: 'What are you saying?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"deva, nātrānyathā kim apy anyad api kalyam ākalyatām | sā khalv idaṃ sācchūritam accham uvāca,
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'O Lord, nothing other than what is spoken here. Let anything else auspicious be heard. She indeed spoke these clear and bold words:"

children.text:
ære pāpa kaṃsa kim iti tvam ahan mudhā māṃ
  tvat-pūrva-śatrur ajani kvacana pradeśe |
  yasmād upetya nidhanaṃ tava jātu kartā
  tan nānyam apy atiśiśuṃ kvacid iccha hastam ||JGc_1,5.2|| '" [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: 'O wicked <s>Kaṃsa</s>! Why did you strike me in vain? | Your former enemy has been born in a certain place; | since He will come and surely bring about your death, | therefore do not seek any other infant's hand!' || (JGc 1,5.2) [vasantatilakā]'

children.text: vrajarājaḥ sāścarya-smitam uvāca-"nūnaṃ śrī-vasudeva-bhakti-praṇālī-putrī-kṛtā bhadrakālī | sā bhadram idaṃ vadati sma yad adyāvadhi nādhīram avadhīritaḥ so' yaṃ vacasāpi kenacanāpi" iti |
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s>, with a wonder-filled smile, said: 'Surely, <s>Bhadrakālī</s> has been made the daughter of the stream of <s>Śrī Vasudeva's</s> devotion! She spoke this auspicious thing — that even until now, he who is not timid has not been disrespected even by the words of anyone.'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"ārya-kṣitīśa, punaś cedam āścaryam avadhāryatām | sa khalu bhrātṛ-vyapadeśa-bhrātṛvyaḥ svasya bhaginy-aṣṭama-garbham aniṣṭatayā niṣṭaṅkitaṃ kurvatīṃ sura-vartma-vāṇīm api devyādiṣṭaḥ sva-dviṣṭa-sura-kptāṃ matvā, tau kārāgārād āhūya bhūyaḥ, pāda-graha-caryā-paryantāgrahataḥ putra-ṣaṭka-hatyāgas-tyāgaṃ bhūri-visūrita iva vidhitsan nigaḍān mocitavān |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'O noble King of the Earth, hear this further wonder too. That one — a cousin by designation of "brother" — having been addressed by the Goddess, who through the celestial voice was marking the eighth womb of his own sister as unfavorable, and considering it to be something done by the gods hostile to him — having summoned those two (<s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>) from the prison again, out of insistence extending to the service of grasping their feet, greatly aggrieved as if desiring to abandon the sin of slaying the six sons, he released their shackles.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"tatas tataḥ?"
children.translated_text: The King of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Then? Then?'

children.text:
dūta uvāca-"tataś ca madīya-śrīmad-īśvarī putra-ghātiny api tasmin sāralya-doṣād eva roṣān nivivṛte | śrīman-mad-īśitā tu vicāritavān, æpūrvaṃ śuṣka-peṣaṃ piṣṭavān, samprati tu sarpiḥ-peṣaṃ pinaṣṭi so' yam asmān' iti | tad evaṃ tat-kauṭilya-koṭiṃ parikalpyāpi saujaunya-prābalyād iha sāralyam evāvalambitavān | tena pitari-śūreṇa durmatinānumataḥ śūra-nandanaḥ saha-dharmiṇyā saha sva-gṛham āgatavāṃś ca, na punar viśvāsam āśvāsaṃ ca labdhavān | yataḥ,
  jāty-anya-janitaḥ kaṃsaḥ sadā dunvan samāśritān |
  mātaraṃ ca dunoty uccaiḥ śilā-putraḥ śilām iva" ||JGc_1,5.3|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Then my glorious mistress, though she was a slayer of children, withdrew from her anger toward him, due to nothing but the fault of simplicity. But my glorious lord reflected: "Previously he ground dry flour; now he grinds flour with ghee — this fellow wants to grind us!" Thus, even though he conceived the sharpest edge of that one's crookedness, relying on simplicity itself due to the predominance of his gentle nature — the son of <s>Śūra</s>, authorized by the evil-minded <s>Śūra</s>, together with his wife, came to his own house; but he did not obtain trust or reassurance. For: <s>Kaṃsa</s>, born of another species, always tormenting those who depend upon him, loudly oppresses even his mother — like a stone-son grinds a stone!' //

children.text: vrajarājaḥ sahāsam uvāca-"tad-anantaraṃ prātar ārabhya sa punar asabhyaḥ kāṃ kārim akārṣīt?"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said with a laugh: 'After that, starting from the morning, what improper deed did that uncouth one commit again?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"svabhāva-jāṃ kārim eva | tathā hi, prātar asau duṣṭas tv anyad duśceṣṭitam anu ceṣṭitavān |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'An act born of his very nature! For, in the morning, that wicked one performed yet another evil deed.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"hanta, kathaya tat kim?"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Alas! Tell us — what was it?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"prātaḥ sa tu malinī-kṛta-nija-kulaḥ khalinī-patiḥ svadayitān daiteyān ānayāmāsa niśāmayāmāsa ca niśīthinī-vṛttam | te ca bhinna-setavaḥ ketava iva rāhu-nibham etaṃ militā vyaghra-varga-nirghoṣa-prabha-ghargharāyamāṇāṃ goṣṭhīm anuṣṭhitavantaḥ, kiṃ bahunā, tatra mahendrādi-nirjaya-garjana-parya-vasānatas tātparyam idam eva jātam, yad viśvadrīcāṃ viṣṇum anucariṣṇūnāṃ deva-devadryag-bhūdeva-gavādīnāṃ pīḍanenaiva tat-pīḍanam īḍitaṃ, tathā tat-sadhrīcīna-tayā nirdaśā-nirdaśānāṃ bālānāṃ nirdayatayā nirdalanam iti khalyām eva balyām avalambya tatra sa ca saṃvalate sma | tayā ca tadānīṃ bahu samprayacchate sma |"
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'In the morning, that polluter of his own family, the lord of wickedness, summoned his beloved <s>Daityas</s> (demons) and informed them of the night's events. And those treacherous ones, of broken principles, meeting this <s>Rāhu</s>-like [figure], conducted an assembly that roared and growled with the thunderous sounds of tiger-packs. In short, the conclusion arrived at from the roaring of the conquest of <s>Mahendra</s> (Indra) and others was this: that the torment of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — who is followed by the devotees of the universal tree — would be praised through the persecution of gods, demi-gods, earth-gods (<s>brāhmaṇas</s>), cows, and others; and likewise, because of their alignment with him, the merciless destruction of infants of each ten-day period. Relying on nothing but villainy, which is their strength, he [<s>Kaṃsa</s>] gathered his forces there. And by her [<s>Māyā</s>/his sister], much was then surrendered.'

children.text: vrajarājas tu tad idaṃ ruṣad-vacanam avakalayya saruṣas tataḥ satrāsam uvāca-"tatra śrīmad-bhrātā kim apy akliṣṭaṃ mayy upadiṣṭam asti?"
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s>, understanding this wrathful account, spoke with both anger and fear: 'Did my glorious brother convey any instruction to me, free from difficulty?'

children.text: dūta uvāca-"atha kiṃ? yat khalu śīghram evāsmai rāja-vyāja-rākṣasāya saṅgamya balir valayitavyo militavyaś cāham" iti | kiṃ cedam api sandiṣṭam, "bhavan-nandanotpatti-samayaṃ samayā vayam atyutkaṇṭhitās tan-maṅgalena saṅgama-nīyāḥ, tathā bhavat-putra-nirviśeṣasya tasya bāla-viśeṣasya vṛttir vartayitavyā" iti |
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Indeed! The message is: "Go swiftly to this royal-disguised demon (<s>rākṣasa</s>) and present the tribute, and let me be met." Moreover, this too was instructed: "We are extremely eager regarding the time of the birth of your son — let us be brought to that celebration. And the maintenance of that special child, who is no different from your own son, should be arranged."'

children.text: atha tad etad avakalayya saṃśayya ca taṃ bhojanādinā yojayitvā, nijāgrajā-nujān ākārya tad agre punas taṃ tad anu rahasam anuvyāhāritavān |
children.translated_text: Then, having understood all this and deliberated, having provided him with food and the like, [<s>Nanda</s>] summoned his elder brothers and younger ones and, in private, again discussed that [matter] with them in his presence.

children.text: tata upananda uvāca-"yuktam evānakadundubhinā sandiṣṭam | sāmprataṃ kareṇaiva kareṇa rāja-viṣa-dharasya tasya mukha-mudraṇam eva sāmpratam |"
children.translated_text: Then <s>Upananda</s> said: 'What <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) has instructed is indeed appropriate. At present, the sealing of the mouth of that royal poison-bearer must be done with the very hand [of tribute].'

children.text:
atha vrajeśas taṃ sandeśam urasikṛtya prātaḥ-prāyam adhigamya dūtaṃ nidideśa, "saumya, bhavān vyagram agrataḥ prayātu, tad-bālakasya sāṅga-maṅgala-saṅgitāṃ tathā tasya vāñchitam anyam udayan-mudam udantam api sva-mukha-svasti-mukhata eva prathayatu | vayaṃ tu bhrātur ājñayā rājñe karam ācitya prābhṛtaṃ ca paritaḥ pracitya dina-pañcakānantaram āgacchanta eva sma |"
[34] tad evaṃ gate dūte dināntare tu jātaka-mātuḥ snāna-vidhāne kṛta-sandhāne sarva-maṅgala-saṅgatam ahaḥ saṅgatya mahan mahaḥ santatya purohita-sahita-hita-mahita-pañcajana-jana-prapañcaṃ yathā puraḥsaram antaḥ-puram ānāyam ānāyaṃ nava-bālakaṃ gopāla-bhūpālaḥ samālokayāmāsa | tathā hi,
  tasmin puṇyāhavarye vraja-nṛpati-śiśor ādi-vīkṣā-sudhābhiḥ
  satraṃ jajñe tathā tac-chravaṇa-parimalād eva śaktā yathā te |
  ājanma-prāpta-sampan-mṛdutara-tanavo' py ātmanā prīti-dānāny
  ūhur bhārāyamāṇāny uta dadhur amitān sveda-romāñca-bāṣpān ||JGc_1,5.4||[sragdharā]
  śrīmad-gopa-nṛpeṇa nūtana-tanūjātasya vīkṣā-kṛte
  prāgryā eva nimantritā vraja-janāḥ sarve tu tatrāyayuḥ |
  yarhy ambhoja-vanākaraḥ sva-kusuma-vrāta-prakāśa-prathā-
  vyāptaḥ syāt kim u tarhi ṣaṭpada-gaṇān ākārayaty ātmanā ||JGc_1,5.5|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Then the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, having taken that message to heart, approaching the morning hour, instructed the messenger: 'O gentle one! You proceed swiftly ahead. Through the face of your own auspicious words, convey the auspiciousness of that child's full celebration, as well as the other news of rising joy that he desires. We, however, by our brother's command, shall present the tribute to the king, gather gifts on all sides, and arrive within five days.'
[34] Thus, when the messenger had departed, on the following day, at the arrangement of the bathing ceremony of the birth-mother, having conjoined all-auspicious rites, the day being joined [with celebrations], the king of the cowherds, preceded by the priestly entourage of beneficial and honored assembly of the five clans, brought the new infant within the inner quarters and beheld him. As follows:
On that supremely auspicious day, with the nectars of the first gazing upon the child of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, a sacred session was born; and by the mere fragrance of hearing about it, they were so empowered that even those whose bodies were supremely tender, endowed with wealth from birth, bore by their own selves gifts of joy that were becoming burdensome, and held immeasurable perspiration, bristling, and tears! // [<s>sragdharā</s>]
By the glorious cowherd-king, for the viewing of the newly-born son, the very foremost people of <s>Vraja</s> were all invited, and all came. When a lake of lotuses is pervaded by the spreading fame of its own flower-clusters, does it then need to summon the hosts of bees to itself? // [<s>śārdūla</s>]

children.text:
paryag dvāriṇi rāṅkavāsta-racite vistīrṇa-gehe yaśo-
  dādy-agre sthaviropananda-gṛhiṇī-kroḍe vicitraṃ śiśum |
  darśaṃ darśam amī na yadyapi gatās tṛptiṃ tathāpy uccakair
  nāsthuḥ pṛṣṭhy-ajanāvakāśa-vidhaye śīlaṃ hi maryāditā ||JGc_1,5.6|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: In the spacious chamber spread with woolen carpets at the entrance, before <s>Yaśodā</s> and others, in the lap of the elder <s>Upananda's</s> wife, the wondrous child was displayed. Though these [people] did not attain satisfaction from gazing and gazing, still they did not stand high [in front], in order to provide space for those behind — for civility indeed has its limits! // [<s>śārdūla</s>]

children.text:
"aṅka-bhrāji-śiśūpananda-gṛhiṇīm ājñā madīyedṛśī
  yan mā mādṛśa-dṛṣṭi-sambhrama-vaśād utthāta yūyaṃ muhuḥ |"
  ity evaṃ vinigadya yājaka-guruḥ sammoda-sampan-milat-
  kampaḥ sākṣata-pāṇi sāśru-nayanaṃ svasti-śrutīr ūcivān ||JGc_1,5.7|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'My command to you is this: do not repeatedly rise up from [your places], overwhelmed by the fluster of gazes like mine, [just to see] the wife of <s>Upananda</s> with the infant shining in her lap!' — Thus having spoken, the chief priest, trembling with the wealth of delight, with <s>akṣata</s> (sacred rice) in his hand and tears in his eyes, recited the benedictory <s>svasti</s> (blessing) verses! // [<s>śārdūla</s>]

children.text:
āgacchantaḥ sva-gehād abhimukha-militā bāla-vaiśiṣṭhya-pṛcchā-
  vantas tad-bāla-dṛṣṭyā pramudita-hṛdayair ūcire kaiścid evam |
  "śobhā sā dṛṣṭi-gamyā na tu para-vacana-śreṇi-gamye"ti harṣāt
  kuṇṭhat-kaṇṭhair abhāvi prativacasi parais tat tu nāśrāvi cānyaiḥ ||JGc_1,5.8|| [sragdharā]
  ākaiśoraṃ yat pariṣkāra-vastraṃ
  yāvad dhāryaṃ māsa-māsaṃ sutena |
  tasmai tāvat tad-vicāreṇa sarvaiḥ
  prattaṃ pitrā ko' pi koṣo hy anantaḥ ||JGc_1,5.9|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Those coming from their own homes, meeting face to face, asking about the special qualities of the child — their hearts delighted by the sight of that child — some said thus: 'That beauty is to be known only by sight, not through the sequence of others' words!' With throats choked by joy, their replies were made — but those [replies] were not even heard by others! // [<s>sragdharā</s>]
All the garments of adornment that the son would wear month by month up to adolescence — in consideration of each, the father gave away some infinite treasury! // [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text:
śobhāṃ vindan nandajāloka-lokaḥ
  sadmāyāsīt kṛtrimākṛtrimā yā |
  vastrādīnāṃ citratā yatra pūrvā
  netrādīnāṃ citratāsīd apūrvā ||JGc_1,5.10|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: The people who came to behold <s>Nanda's</s> son found a beauty — both artificial and natural — in the house, where the variegation of garments and the like was former, but the variegation of eyes and the like was unprecedented! // [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text:
āgatā nija-gṛhaṃ yadāpy amūr
  nanda-bālam avalokya lobhanam |
  hanta tarhy api dināni kānicit
  menire dṛśi-gataṃ vraja-prajāḥ ||JGc_1,5.11|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: Even when these people of <s>Vraja</s> had returned to their own homes, having beheld <s>Nanda's</s> captivating child — alas, even then for several days they considered him present before their eyes! // [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text: atha mathurā-pathikatāṃ prathayiṣyamāṇaḥ śrī-gokula-kula-rājas tv agrajādīn nija-pratinidhitādi-karmaṇi nirmāya calann antaś cintitavān, "hanta, suhṛdi durhṛdi ca mama mānasaṃ samāna-sambandha-hārda-bandham api prasabhaṃ bhṛśam eva tatra prasajjati nava-jātake, yenāsau pībitā jīvitāśāpi na paricchinnatām icchati | samprati duṣṭasyāviprakṛṣṭam aṭann asmi, nānubhavann asmi kiṃ bhavitā | tasmād vikalatāvikalanāya vilokaṃ vilokam eva taṃ bālakaṃ yadu-nilayaṃ calāni" iti |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious king of the <s>Gokula</s> clan, about to display his journey toward <s>Mathurā</s>, having appointed his elder brothers and others to the duties of his own representatives, while setting out, reflected within: 'Alas! My mind, though bound with equal bonds of affection to both friend and foe, nevertheless clings forcefully and intensely to that newborn infant — by whom even the draining of the hope of life does not wish to be cut short. At present I am going not far from the wicked one; if I do not experience [danger], what will be? Therefore, to avert the state of distress, let me proceed to the abode of the <s>Yadus</s>, gazing and gazing again at that child!'

children.text:
atha gamana-samaye ca,
  utsaṅge nihitasya tasya tu śiśor vaktraṃ muhur dṛṣṭavān
  nāmodaṃ ciram ādade niṭilakād gaṇḍāv acumbīd bhṛśam |
  āśiśleṣatarāṃ vapur na tu tadā tṛptiṃ vrajeśo yayau
  yāṃ pātheyatayā viveda mathurā-prasthānam āsthāya saḥ ||JGc_1,5.12|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And at the time of departure:
He placed that infant on his lap and gazed at his face again and again, he smelled the <s>tilaka</s> on his forehead for a long time, he kissed both his cheeks intensely — he embraced his body ever more closely; yet the lord of <s>Vraja</s> did not attain satisfaction — which he learned as provision for the journey, having undertaken the departure for <s>Mathurā</s>! // [<s>śārdūla</s>]

children.text:
vatse śyāma pitā tavāyam ayituṃ rājñaḥ puraṃ tvat-kṛtā-
  nujñāṃ prārthayate tato vitaratād" ity eṣa dhātrīritaḥ |
  āścaryātula-bāla-bhāva-balād babhre smitaṃ tena ca
śrīmān gopa-janādhipaḥ pracita-dhīḥ prasthānam āsedivān ||JGc_1,5.13|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'O dark-complexioned child! This is your father, who desires to go to the king's city. He seeks your permission given for his sake' — thus prompted by the nursemaid. Through the power of the astonishing, incomparable, child-like nature, he bore a smile — and by that [smile], the glorious chief of the cowherd-folk, with gathered courage, set forth on his journey! // [<s>śārdūla</s>]

children.text:
smāraṃ smāraṃ tan-mukhaṃ susmitāktaṃ
  vyaktaṃ vyaktaṃ gopayan prema-dhāma |
  ānandenānalpa-jalpeṣu gopeṣv
  ātmārāma-prāyatāṃ prāpa nandaḥ ||JGc_1,5.14|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: Remembering and remembering that face touched with a beautiful smile, clearly, clearly protecting the abode of love, <s>Nanda</s>, amidst the cowherds with their abundant conversations, in the abundance of joy, attained a state almost like <s>Ātmārāma</s> (one delighting in the Self)! // [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: atha mathurām āsādya sadya eva karādhikāriṣu karam upasādya tad-dvārā dūrata eva rājānam anujānantaṃ prasādya śakaṭa-ghaṭāvamocanam evānañca, na tu śrī-vasudeva-sadma, kaṃse tena sākaṃ nijānāsañjana-vyañjanāya |
children.translated_text: Then, having reached <s>Mathurā</s>, he immediately presented the tribute to the tax-collectors, through them pleased the king who gave audience from afar, and headed toward the unloading of his carts — but not toward <s>Śrī Vasudeva's</s> residence, to display to <s>Kaṃsa</s> his non-attachment to that [Vasudeva].

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-śiṣṭa-dviṣṭi-viśiṣṭo' pi sañjāta-jātaka-dveṣa-pātako' pi para-dhanāyayā dhanānusandhāna-nirbandha-sandho' pi sa katham asmin nigama-śiṣṭi-saṃsliṣṭe vicitreṇa putrekṣaṇena putra-kṣaṇena ca vismāyita-sakale jagad-vitta-vittā-śakale saralāyate sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Though he was distinguished among the best of the civilized, though he had incurred the sin of hatred toward the newborn, though he was bound in the bond of pursuing others' wealth through the arrival of riches — how was it that this one, in that remarkable moment of seeing the son, in a world amazed at every particle of the world's wealth, became straightforward?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-uktam eva purā yat praguṇatayākhilasamañjasayaśasaḥ śrī-vrajeśacandramasaḥ khalv asya guṇena guṇeneva ko vā baddho na bhavet? it |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'It has already been stated before that — by the virtue of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, the moon of entirely befitting fame, of virtue like a rope — who indeed would not be bound?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tatas tataḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then what happened next?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tato vraja-trātari taṃ bhrātaram anu nirjana-milanāya mantraṃ valayati paryakalitāvasaraḥ sa śrī-śūra-tanūja-varaḥ svayaṃ kevala-sevaka-viśeṣa-saṅgitayā saṃvalate sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, while the protector of <s>Vraja</s> was arranging a stratagem for a private meeting with that brother, the excellent son of <s>Śrī Śūra</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), having seized the opportunity, himself managed to come, accompanied only by special servants.'

children.text: atha tenāvrajita-sadeśaḥ śrīmān vraja-maheśaḥ sahasā mahasāvṛtatayā sābhyutthānam utthāya nyāya-paramaḥ, kṛta-tad-abhigamaḥ svam anujam anuraktaḥ pariṣvaktavān pariṣvaktaś cānena na tu kañcit kaścin natavān, jātāv ekasya jyāyastvam anyasya tu jātāv iti | na ca kevalam etad eva kāraṇatām avalambate, api tu paraspara-praṇayātiśayaś ca, yenānyan nānusandhātuṃ śakyate |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious great lord of <s>Vraja</s>, hearing of his arrival with his attendants, suddenly rose with a formal reception, enveloped by greatness, and being supremely just, having approached him, lovingly embraced his younger brother and was embraced by him; but neither bowed to the other — for one had seniority by birth and the other had [seniority] by birth [of his son]. And it is not this alone that serves as the cause, but also the excess of mutual love, by which nothing else can be pursued.

children.text: etad eva ca dṛṣṭāntena spaṣṭīkṛtaṃ śrī-bādarāyaṇinā--dehaḥ prāṇam ivāgatam [BhP 10.5.21] iti | atra ca deha-sthānīyasya go-sthāna-pater asmad-īśitur evāsaktir atiriktā darśitā | prāṇaḥ khalv anyaṃ dehaṃ sañcarati, dehas tu taṃ vinā na bhavaty eveti | sa tu catura-śiromaṇiḥ svayam eva rāgatas tac-chivirāgatas tenātithivad eva pūjitas tad-vyavahāreṇa jitaḥ | samprati jātayoḥ sva-tanujātayoḥ prasakta-dhīr idam uktavān-
children.translated_text: And this itself was made clear by <s>Śrī Bādarāyaṇi</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) through a simile: '[He embraced him] as the body [embraces] the life-breath that has arrived' [<s>BhP</s> 10.5.21]. And here, the attachment of the master of the cow-station, who stands in the position of the body, to our lord is shown as exceeding. For the life-breath indeed migrates to another body, but the body without it does not exist at all. But that crest-jewel of the clever ones, having come voluntarily out of affection to his encampment, was honored by him like a guest; and [<s>Nanda</s>] was conquered by his conduct. At present, with his mind absorbed in both newborn sons, he said this:

children.text: "diṣṭyā bhrātaḥ pravayasa idānīm aprajasya te |
children.translated_text: 'By good fortune, O brother! Now in your old age, to you who were without offspring,

children.text: prajāśāyā nivṛttasya prajā yat samajāyata || [BhP 10.5.23]
children.translated_text: who had abandoned the hope of progeny — offspring has been born!' // [<s>BhP</s> 10.5.23]

children.text: upādhi-kṛta-hāni-vṛddhiṃ vinā kṛta-sneha-samṛddhi-maya-dehatayā gambhīra-svaratayā ca payaḥ-payodhir ivāyaṃ vrajādhīśvaras tu tasya sarva-stutasya vaṃśān kaṃsa-kṛta-dhvaṃsān anuśocan, karma-vāda-rocanayā dhairyaṃ saṃvarmayann ātmanaś ca tasya ca śarma sūnṛtāmṛta-bhṛta-santarpaṇaṃ kṛtavān |
children.translated_text: Without the growth and diminution caused by limiting conditions, with a body made of the abundance of established affection, and with a deep voice — like a milk-ocean — the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, lamenting the destruction wrought by <s>Kaṃsa</s> upon the dynasties of that universally praised one, maintaining courage through the appeal to the doctrine of <s>karma</s>, provided comfort to both himself and to him, satisfying him with an offering of sweet and truthful nectar.

children.text: tataḥ śrīmān ānakadundubhis taṃ kṛta-kāryam avadhārya bhāvy utpātaṃ vicārya sva-bhavanam eva gantum anumatavān | śrī-vrajarājas tu vastutaś cetasā cetaḥ pracalita eva, samprati tu gehaṃ prati deham evehayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), having ascertained that the task was accomplished, reflecting on future calamities, decided to return to his own home. The king of <s>Vraja</s>, however, in truth had his heart set in motion, but presently he moved only his body toward the house.

children.text:
atha vraja-vṛttam anuvṛttyatām | yathā pūrva-devānāṃ pūrva-mantraṇāyām āmantritā rākṣasa-pakṣiṇī nirdaśāna-nirdaśāṃś ca deśa-deśataḥ śāvakān bakān iva śyenī vinighnatī, kaṃsasya nighnatī vairocani-kanyā rajanyām asyāṃ vraja-pradeśa-sadeśam ājagāma; yā khalu jaṭā-ghaṭā-vighaṭita-prakaṭa-muṇḍā,
viśaṅkaṭa-daṃṣṭrā-saṃsṛṣṭa-daṣṭa-ḍimbha-koṭi-vikaṭa-tuṇḍā netra-garta-vartamāna-vartma-loma-samuddaṇḍa-kuṇḍali-khaṇḍita-brahmāṇḍa-varti-dhairyā pakṣati-dvaya-madhya-sthita-vakṣaḥ-sthala-lambamāna-vakṣoja-yugalodgīrṇa-dugdha-miṣa-viṣa-viṣama-jvālā-sahya-bala-dahyamāna-paryantatayā yantrita-jantu-sthairyā cetyādi-mahā-ghoratāvahā, kiṃ bahunā, pratīka-mātra-prāṇi-pratīkā pṛthukān eva ca pṛthukān iva kurvatī vartate |
children.translated_text: Now, let the events of <s>Vraja</s> be narrated. As the former gods had summoned her in their earlier council, the demoness in bird-form, killing infants in region after region like a she-hawk killing young herons, slaying on behalf of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, that daughter of <s>Virocana's</s> [lineage] — came to the area of <s>Vraja</s> on that very night. She who had exposed her shaved head through the dishevelment of her matted locks, whose terrible beak was joined with terrible fangs that had bitten countless children, whose coiling eyebrow-hairs turning in the hollows of her eye-sockets shattered the fortitude of the world within the cosmic egg, whose pair of breasts hanging from her chest between two wings emitted a terrible blaze of poison in the guise of milk that burned all around with unbearable force, thus destroying the steadfastness of living creatures — and so forth, bearing extreme fearfulness — in short, she was reducing children to mere images of living beings, flattening them flat.

children.text:
atha sā śrī-vraja-kṣitīśa-rakṣita-gīrvāṇa-vāṇa-jña-dhānuṣka-bhiyā duṣkara-svarūpaṃ vihāya hāri-rūpāntaraṃ prātihārikatayā dhṛtavatī, yena khalu sampad-adhidevīyam adhibhūmi sampatantī nijāśraya-viśeṣam anvicchantī ca sarva-sal-lakṣaṇatayā kṛta-lakṣaṇaṃ samprati jātaṃ śrī-vrajarāja-jātam eva samāśrayiṣyatīti matvā tasyā nūtana-vapuḥ pūtanāyāś cākūtam amatvā hārita-hṛdbhī rakṣibhir na nivāritā rakṣiṇībhiś ca nāvadhāritā; yeyaṃ pakṣa-pātinī kaṃsa-pakṣa-pātinī sātvata-bhartuḥ śravaṇa-kīrtanādi-pradeśam anuvartitum asamarthā, tad-bahirmukhānām arbhakān nighnatī tat-pakṣa-pātiny eva lakṣitā | evam apy asyāḥ śrīmad-vrajāgamanādikaṃ tu kautuka-viśeṣāya sādhayituṃ yogamāyā khalu yogam
āyāntī babhūva, yasyāś ca hetor anyatra kutracin netram anādadhatī sarvam atyādadhatī śrīman-nanda-mandira-sthaṃ tam eva bālakam ālokayāmāsa | aṅgāra-dhānī-saṅgata-sphuliṅga-vad aṅgāra-saṅgham iva tamasi pataṅgī taṃ ca yogamāyā-kṛta-prākṛta-bālaka-kalpatākalpanayā yathāvan nānubabhūva, ujjvala-guñjā-puñja-tulanayā prajvalad iṅgalam iva |
children.translated_text: Then she, out of fear of the archers who knew the divine weapons and who guarded the king of <s>Vraja</s>, abandoned her own difficult form and assumed an attractive alternate form as a disguise. By this, she who was like the presiding goddess of prosperity descending upon this supreme land, seeking a special refuge — thinking, 'Having all auspicious marks, he who has just been born, the offspring of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, I shall take refuge in him' — the guards, with their hearts won over by the marks of her beauty, did not stop her, and the female guards too did not scrutinize her; she, a partisan, a supporter of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> faction — unable to follow the practice of hearing, chanting, and other devotions to the Lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — was recognized as a partisan of that [Kaṃsa] faction by those who were hostile, killing their infants. Yet even so, <s>Yogamāyā</s> (the Lord's illusory power) herself came employing her <s>yoga</s> to accomplish a special wonder in her arrival at glorious <s>Vraja</s>. And because of her, <s>Pūtanā</s>, paying no attention anywhere else, seizing everything, gazed upon that very child situated in the glorious mansion of <s>Nanda</s>. Like a moth toward a mass of embers appearing as a spark attached to a coal-box in the darkness — and through <s>Yogamāyā's</s> contrivance of making him appear as an ordinary child, she did not truly perceive him, like a blazing ember [appearing] comparable to a heap of bright <s>guñjā</s> berries.

children.text: ayaṃ tu śrīmān nanda-nandanaḥ sva-tāta-śubhānudhyāna-maya-yogamāyayā sevitatayā janmata eva samasta-jñānādi-sampan-mayatāyāṃ śastaḥ svajana-sneha-vaśaṃvada-bālyādi-līlā-sukhāveśena tatrānādṛtyātula-tad-vyakti-vyatiriktīkṛtas tathāpy avasaram avāpya madhyaṃ madhyaṃ sā sva-sevām adhyavasyantī tatra prādurbhavati | tataḥ samprati ca tām antarvikṛtākṛtim upalabhya bhavya-svabhāva-rocane locane nimīlitavān |
children.translated_text: But this glorious son of <s>Nanda</s>, by the service of <s>Yogamāyā</s> composed of his father's auspicious meditation, though from birth replete with the fullness of all knowledge and other powers — by the joyful absorption in the childhood pastimes governed by his devotees' affection, he remained indifferent there, making the incomparable manifestation of that [power] appear as an exception; yet, finding the occasion, from time to time that [<s>Yogamāyā</s>], intent on her own service, would manifest. And so now, perceiving her internally distorted form, he closed his eyes — beautiful in their auspicious nature.

children.text: tataś ca sahasā parābhāvya-dhiyā bhiyā vinā bhūtā tam aṅkam eva niḥśaṅkam ānītavatī, mūṣika-dhiyā sarpantī sarpī nakulam iva |
children.translated_text: Then, suddenly, with an intellect about to be overcome, without fear, she fearlessly took him into her very lap — like a serpent-woman, thinking herself a mongoose, slithering toward a mongoose.

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-agrajanmaṃs tan-mātarau katham iva tām aparicitāṃ na nivāritavatyau, na ca vicāritavatyau?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Elder brother! How is it that his two mothers did not stop that unfamiliar one, nor did they reflect upon her?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-purastād yogamāyākhyaṃ kāraṇam upanyastaṃ, prakriyāntaraṃ ca tatra tayā kriyate sma | yathā, sā hi tatrāntar-gūḍhāṅga-bhujaṅgī-saṅgatāyāḥ kūṭa-kanaka-maya-payaḥ-kanakālukāyāḥ sāmyāvagamyaṃ rūpaṃ dadhatī, paritaḥ sravad-asra-dhārā-vārājasra-stanya-pravāhān vahantī, snehānukāraka-dehata eva te mohitavatī |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'The reason called <s>Yogamāyā</s> was presented earlier, and another stratagem was also employed by her there. For she, bearing a form comparable to a pot of golden milk with golden lentils concealing a serpent-woman within, streaming unceasing torrents of milk in the form of tears flowing on all sides, by the very naturalness of her body imitating affection — she bewildered them.'

children.text:
punaś cedaṃ sagadgadaṃ jagāda, "ayi yaśode, tvam api haṭhottaratayā kaṭhorāsi, sutarāṃ tu sva-suta-sthita-cittādrohiṇī rohiṇī, yataḥ śayanatala evedṛśa-sukumāraṃ kumāraṃ nidhāya cintām avidhāya nātikṛta-niṣṭhaṃ tiṣṭhathaḥ, na tu hṛdaye | prāṇā api hṛdaya eva rakṣaṇīyāḥ, kim uta prāṇādhiko' yaṃ sutaḥ? tasmād dhig vo rākṣasīto' pi rūkṣa-mānasā mānuṣīḥ | ahaṃ tu sampad-adhiṣṭhātṛ-devī tvayā prasūtaṃ sutaṃ viśva-vilakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇaṃ śrutvā tat-kṣaṇam evāgatānena vasantena vāsantīm iva dṛṣṭiṃ hṛṣṭāṃ kṛtavaty asmi | mama ca stanau sarva-śreyastananau nityam amṛtaṃ kṣarataḥ, yena pītena so' yaṃ niḥsandeha-siddha-dehaḥ syāt | tasmād aham asya sarva-sukha-vidhātrī dhātrī
ca bhaviṣyāmi" iti |
children.translated_text: And she spoke this, with a faltering voice: 'O <s>Yaśodā</s>! You too are hard-hearted, through the stubbornness of your superiority; and all the more so, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, whose mind is not hostile toward the son — for you have placed such a tender child on the sleeping-surface and have remained standing without concern, rather than on your hearts! Even the life-breaths should be protected in the heart itself — how much more so this son who is dearer than life? Therefore, fie upon you human women, more hard-hearted than even a <s>rākṣasī</s> (demoness)! But I am the presiding goddess of prosperity. Having heard that the son born to you bears marks unique in all the world, I have come at that very instant, and with this spring-like [child], I have made my gaze blossom like a <s>vāsantī</s> creeper! And my breasts, the source of all welfare, always flow with nectar; by drinking which, this child shall undoubtedly become one of perfected body! Therefore, I shall become his nurse and the bestower of all happiness!'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tato grahaṇād anantaraṃ kiṃ jātam?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, after she seized him, what happened?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tad evaṃ miṣataḥ sā viṣayoṣā taṃ gṛhītvā vilambaṃ hitvā cūcukopary eva tan-mukha-vāry-udbhavaṃ nidadhe |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Thus, before their very watching eyes, that poisonous woman, having grasped him, without delay, placed his mouth-opening upon the very tip of her nipple.'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha sabhayam uvāca-tatas tataḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said fearfully: 'And then? And then?'

children.text:
madhukaṇṭha sahāsam uvāca- tataḥ sa tu svamātuḥ sākṣāt tasyās tādṛśa-bhṛśa-durnaya-darśanād upajātena tat-prāṇān pibatā roṣa-tejaḥ-saṅghātena tat-stanyasya ca doṣaṃ śoṣayan mātṛ-bhāvābhāsa-sphurad-ullāsa-sva-sparśa-svābhāvyena tu tad-dehe sugandhitā-sugandhitām iva tat-stanye pīyūṣatāṃ rūṣayaṃs cūṣaṇaṃ cakāra |
  kṛṣṇena pūtanā-stanya-pānam itthaṃ virocate |
  yathā gaṅgā-pravāheṇa karmanāśā-jalāhṛtiḥ ||JGc_1,5.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
