<s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said with a smile: 'Then he, by the concentrated fiery energy of his wrath aroused from seeing such extreme wickedness directly against his own mother, drying up the poison of her milk — yet by the naturalness of his own touch, flashing with the semblance of maternal feeling, as if infusing her milk with the fragrance of fragrance itself and reproaching the nectar-nature — he suckled!
The drinking of <s>Pūtanā's</s> breast-milk by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> shines forth thus:
just as the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> [sanctifies] the waters of the <s>Karmanāśā</s> (Sin-Destroying river)! // [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]'

children.text: sā tu rākṣasa-pakṣiṇī "muñca muñca" iti puṣṭa-kruṣṭatayā vyathita-sanīḍāṃ pīḍāṃ prapañcayantī prāṇān api muñcantī saṃskāra-vaśāt taṃ vakṣasy eva nikṣipya pakṣa-vikṣepād vrajād bahiḥ sasāra mamāra ca | yatra hrādinī sā hrādinīty eva tarkyate sma, yatra ca svarūpāvasthitim eva cāsasāra |
children.translated_text: Then that bird-like demoness, crying aloud 'Release! Release!' with full-throated screams, elaborating the agony that distressed her very nest [body], even releasing her life-breaths — by force of [residual] impressions, placing him upon her very breast, she flew out of <s>Vraja</s> by the flapping of her wings, and died. Where <s>Hrādinī</s> (the bliss-giving <s>śakti</s>) — she was speculated to be that very <s>Hrādinī</s>; and there she attained her own essential nature.

children.text:
uḍḍiḍye sapadi yadā tu pakṣiṇī sā
  taṃ bālaṃ hṛdi parigṛhya lambamānaṃ |
  uḍḍīnā drutataram eva mātṛ-yugma-
  prāṇāś ca sphuṭita-hṛdambujād ivāsan ||JGc_1,5.16|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
When that bird-like demoness suddenly flew up,
holding that child dangling upon her breast,
her flight was exceedingly swift — and the life-breaths of the two mothers
were as if they had burst from a shattered heart-lotus! //

children.text:
tasmin hṛte pūtanayā tu bāle
  mātror yadi prāṇa-gaṇo na mūrcchet |
  bhoktuṃ tad ābhīla-kulaṃ tadā te
  kiṃ śaknuyātām? api kintu naiva ||JGc_1,5.17|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text:
When the child was taken by <s>Pūtanā</s>,
if the host of life-breaths of the two mothers had not fainted,
could those two then have consumed that terrible clan [of demons]?
Or could they not? Certainly not! //

children.text:
ākrandād bhidurāṇi pakṣa-pavanāt kalpaṃ bhuvi bhraṃśanād
  bhū-bhraṃśaṃ śava-rūpatā-śavalanād gotrāṅga-paṅktīr api |
  āśāṅkyābhigatā diviṣṭha-paṭalī tat-tad-vijātīyatāṃ
  nirṇīyātha visismiye katipayaṃ kālaṃ bakī-saṃsthitau ||JGc_1,5.18|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
From the shrieking, [the earth was] splitting; from the wind of her wings, shaking [everything] to the end of the <s>kalpa</s>; from the fall to earth,
the earth quaking; from the ashen pallor of her corpse-form, [terror seized] even the mountain ranges;
the host of celestials, approaching with apprehension, examining each strange phenomenon —
then marveled for a brief time at her crane-like posture. //

children.text:
tataś ca pūtanāṃ niścitya,
  tasyāḥ surā vakṣasi lagnam enaṃ
  smeraṃ gṛhītākṛśa-cūcukāgram |
  asya prabhāvāvali-vijña-cittāḥ
  sarve samantāj jahasur vilokya ||JGc_1,5.19|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text:
Then, having identified her as <s>Pūtanā</s>:
The gods, seeing him smiling upon her breast,
grasping the tip of the slender nipple,
their minds knowing the series of his powers —
all around, they laughed upon beholding. //

children.text:
ūcuś ca,
  "abhajad iha yad eṣā parvatākāra-varṣmā,
  kṣayam atitanu-mūrtiṃ prāpya bālaṃ tam etam |
  na hi tad ativicitraṃ prekṣyatām eva sākṣād
  vidhur ayam amṛtāṅgaḥ pūtaneyaṃ viṣāṅgī ||JGc_1,5.20|| [mālinī]
tathā ca,
  "viṣaṃ syād viṣam anyasminn amṛtaṃ tu viṣe viṣam |
  pūtanā-kṛṣṇa-saṅgharṣe dṛśyatām etad eva hi ||JGc_1,5.21|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And they said:
'That she who was of mountain-like body here attained
destruction upon reaching this child of exceedingly delicate form —
that is not at all extraordinary! For behold directly:
this is the Moon with a body of nectar, and this is <s>Pūtanā</s>, whose body is poison!' // [<s>mālinī</s>]
And also:
'Poison would be poison against another, but nectar — that is the true poison against poison!
In the clash between <s>Pūtanā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, let this very thing be seen!' // [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
athavā,
  "nava-nava-rasa-pākād utpalābhoga-dhātrī
  sthalaja-jalaja-padme sarvadā duḥkha-dātrī |
  rajanicara-gaṇānāṃ śaśvad āmoda-pātrī
  prati hari-layam āgāt pūtanā vyāja-rātrī ||JGc_1,5.22|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
Or rather:
'By the ever-new ripening of <s>rasa</s> (sentiment), the sustainer of the enjoyment of lotuses,
always a giver of suffering to land-born and water-born lotuses,
always a vessel of delight for the hosts of night-wanderers —
upon the dissolution into <s>Hari</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, the false night, departed!' // [<s>mālinī</s>]

children.text:
kintu, sva-carita-cāturībhir idam ivāyaṃ sūcayati,
  "stanandhayasya stana eva jīvikā
  dattas tvayā svayam ānane mama |
  mayā ca pīto mriyate yadi tvayā,
  kiṃ vā mamāgaḥ? svayam eva kathyatām ||JGc_1,5.23|| [upajāti 12]
snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-hanta, śrī-vrajeśvary-ādīnāṃ dīnānāṃ kā maryādā dhairyāya jātā? kiṃ vā tat-parijanaiḥ samādhānam adhāyi?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Alas! What limit did the queen of <s>Vraja</s> and the others, being wretched, reach in their fortitude? And what consolation was given by their attendants?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-atha vraje tu mahā-kolāhala-vraje jāte vrajeśvara-gṛhiṇīṃ rohiṇīṃ ca vihāyaṃ vihāyam upary upari paridrutāsu vṛddhā-madhyā-vadhūṣu tāsu tadaiva daiva-niścita-diśaḥ kāścit pṛthu-naga-pṛtanām patitāṃ pūtanāṃ dṛṣṭvāpi vighaṭita-bhayā nikaṭam aṭitā vidhi-ghaṭita-skhalita-bāhu-ghaṭṭam ārūḍhā bāla-bhāvād akutobhayatayā khelantam iva taṃ bāla-gopālam avilambitaṃ gṛhītvā tāṃ saṃvega-jāta-vegatayā sarvaṃ cātihāya gṛhāya dudruvuḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, when a great uproar had arisen in the uproarious <s>Vraja</s>, abandoning the queen of <s>Vraja</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s> [who had fainted], while the old, middle-aged, and young women were running to and fro, higher and higher — at that very moment, certain women, their direction determined by fate, even after seeing <s>Pūtanā</s> fallen like a great mountain-army, with their fear shattered, came near. Climbing up, grasping the child — who, by his child-nature and fearlessness from all quarters, was playing as if at sport, despite the tumbling caused by the fate-decreed stumbling of their arms — they seized that child <s>Gopāla</s> without delay, and with the speed born of urgency, surpassing everything, they ran toward the house.'

children.text: tataś ca tad-avalokenāsaṅkhya-lokena sukha-magnena paścāl-lagnena pariplava-tayā samutplavamānena saha samahaṃ mahāntaḥ-puram āgatā nārī-janā jananyor niśceṣṭitāṃ dṛṣṭvā kartavya-mūḍhatām ūḍhā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having arrived at the great inner quarters, those women — together with countless people who had submerged in happiness at the sight of him, following behind, overflowing and surging with agitation — upon seeing the two mothers lying motionless, were seized by a bewilderment of not knowing what to do.

children.text: atha tathā-lakṣaṇatayā kṣaṇa-katipaye labdha-vyatyaye yatnāntara-pathe ca vitathe, kācid buddhimatī sa-kaśmalayos tayor apy aṅke taṃ bālakam evāvalambayāmāsa | avalambite ca bāle tenaivāmṛteneva kṛta-trāṇeṣu prāṇeṣu, taṃ bālakam avalokamāne te punar anyāṃ mūrcchām ānarcchatuḥ | tataḥ punaḥ punar evaṃ-vidhānāc cid-ādhānena prakṛtim āsedatuḥ, muhur eva jala-saṃvalanena nidāgha-dagdha-bhūmivat |
children.translated_text: Then, after a few moments, when the condition had changed to one of such signs, and other remedial paths having proved futile, a certain wise woman placed the child upon the very laps of the two who were still in a state of distress. And when the child was placed there, as if their life-breaths were saved by that very nectar, as they gazed at the child, they fell into yet another swoon. Then, again and again, through such methods — by the application of consciousness — they returned to their natural state, repeatedly, like ground scorched by summer heat [revived] by repeated sprinkling with water.

children.text:
atha bālakam apy avalokayantyāv ālokana-vacanayoḥ kārābhir ivāśru-dhārābhir atīva vyagratām agrataḥ prāpatuḥ | tataś cānyābhir eva stanyābhimukhīkṛtena tena sukumāreṇa kumāreṇa kramānusāreṇa dhīratāṃ dhārayāmāsatuḥ | tataś ca,
  āśliṣṭaḥ pratidṛṣṭi-cumbita-mukhaḥ sughrāta-mūrdhā dṛgar-
  ṇaḥ-siktaḥ suhṛdāṃ puro bhuvi dhṛtaḥ svenāpi nirmañchitaḥ |
  satyaṃ satyam idaṃ na cānyad iti sa vyaktaṃ viviktīkṛto
  mātṛbhyāṃ na tathāpi saṃhṛta-bhayaṃ dṛṣṭo bakī-mardanaḥ ||JGc_1,5.24|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Then, looking at the child too, through the imprisonment-like streams of tears in their gazing and speech, they attained extreme agitation in his presence. Then, by the effort of others, when that tender prince was directed toward their breasts, gradually they upheld fortitude. And then:
Embraced, his face kissed at every glance, his head well-smelled, drenched
with eye-tears, placed on the ground before kinsmen, and rubbed even by himself —
'This is real! This is real! And nothing else!' — thus clearly was he examined;
yet even so, the two mothers did not see the crusher of the crane-demoness with their fear removed. // [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: atha śrī-vrajeśvarī sa-camatkāram uvāca-"hanta, vilokyatām asau dvitīyo bālaḥ" iti | tad etad uktvā ca tāṃ svayaṃ dhāvitum udyatāṃ vibudhya pratirudhya śrīla-rohiṇī bahula-mahilābhiḥ saha gṛhāntaram avagāhamānā, taṃ maṅgala-saṅgataṃ vilokayantī, saṅginībhir aṅgīkṛta-pālanaṃ vidhāya ca, tad-āgamana-spṛhinīṃ vraja-mahendra-gṛhiṇīṃ saṃhāya sāntvitavatī |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s> said with wonder: 'Ah, behold this second child!' Having said this, and perceiving that she herself was about to rush [toward him], the glorious <s>Rohiṇī</s>, restraining her, entering the inner quarters together with many women, beholding that auspicious one, arranging his care to be undertaken by her companions, she then brought and consoled the wife of the great <s>Indra</s> of <s>Vraja</s>, who was eager for his arrival.

children.text:
pūtanā-hantus tu,
  go-mūtrādyaiḥ snānam ācārya tasya
  premṇā cakrur mantra-rakṣāṃ jananyaḥ |
  śrutvā yasmin śāstra-vijñatvam āsāṃ
  sarve' py uccaiḥ kovidā vismayante ||JGc_1,5.25|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
For the slayer of <s>Pūtanā</s>:
His mothers performed the bathing with cow-urine and the like,
and with love they made the <s>mantra</s>-protection for him;
upon hearing of the scriptural knowledge of these [women],
all the learned ones exclaim in great wonder! ||5.25||

children.text:
atha tādṛśa-mahotpāta-dṛśvarī śrīmatī vrajeśvarī sarvānarvācīnāḥ prati sa-gadgadaṃ jagāda,
  "putro bhaved evam atispṛhā nau
  nāsīd abhūd eṣa tu vaḥ spṛhātaḥ |
  pratyarpi so' yaṃ bata yuṣmakābhir
  asmāsu yuṣmāsu tathāsmakābhiḥ ||JGc_1,5.26|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text:
Then the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s>, she who had witnessed such a great portent, spoke to all her senior women with a faltering voice:
'That a son should be born thus — such was not our intense desire;
but this one has come from your desire.
Therefore this one, alas, has been entrusted by you
to us, and by us to you!' ||5.26||

children.text: iti tāsāṃ caraṇa-parisaraṇam anu bālaṃ namayantī bāṣpaṃ mumoca |
children.translated_text: Thus, making the child bow at the feet-vicinity of those [elder women], she shed tears.

children.text:
tāś ca dhairyaṃ hitvā sa-sambhramaṃ bālakaṃ gṛhītvā procuḥ,
  "asmākaṃ yad akhilam asti puṇya-jātaṃ
  yad vāsmat-pitṛ-jananī-kulānujātam |
  tenāsau bata bhavatād aho yaśode
  putras te niravadhi-maṅgala-pramode ||JGc_1,5.27|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
And they, abandoning composure, taking the baby with haste, said:
'Whatever accumulated merit of ours exists,
or whatever has been born from the families of our fathers and mothers —
by all that, alas, may it be so, O <s>Yaśodā</s>,
that your son [abide] in boundless auspicious delight!' ||5.27||

children.text:
iti sāsram ātmanā taṃ nirmañchayañcakruḥ |
[69] tasyāḥ sāntvanārthaṃ samuditā muditās tatraiva tasthuś ca | tatra ca putanayā kṛtam ajanyaṃ jananyāv anyāś ca sva-svadṛṣṭam anyo' nyaṃ nirdiṣṭavatyaḥ | tathā hi,
  yathāgatā sā yad uvāca yac ca vā
  cakāra tad-grastam amū samūcatuḥ |
  amūḥ samūcuḥ yathā svayaṃ gatā
  yathānvapaśyaṃś ca tathā sa-gadgadam ||JGc_1,5.28|| [vaṃśasthavilā]
children.translated_text:
Thus, with tears, they wiped him (or rubbed him protectively) by their own [hands].
[69] For the purpose of consoling her, having assembled joyfully, they remained right there. And there, the mothers and others reported to each other what was done by <s>Pūtanā</s>, each one what she herself had seen. As follows:
As she came, what she said, and whatever she did —
those two (the mothers) together reported what she had devoured;
the others reported as they themselves had gone,
and as they themselves had observed — with choked voices. ||5.28||

children.text:
śrī-vrajarājādayas tu dūrataḥ kiñcit kiñcid īkṣitvā mithaḥ-kathayā kathantayā tad etad uccāvaca-vacanaṃ racayāmāsuḥ | tathā hi, [71] "samuḍḍīyamānāmāna-vāyasātāyi-samudāyāvivikta-mahā-ghora-rūpaṃ caṇḍa-raśmi-bhasmīkṛta-santam asāv aśiṣṭa-mahiṣṭha-granthi-santatitayopahasitaṃ jhaṭiti niviḍita-vaḍrībhūtāṭavī-khaṇḍa-maṇḍita-pradeśatayā nirdiṣṭaṃ bhūri-dūratayā bhū-lagnavat pratīyamāno' yaṃ toyada-sambhāra iti sambhāvitaṃ śrī-vasudeva-sūcitotpātocitaṃ kiñcin nicitam idam" iti cintitam | punar, "labdha-pakṣatayotpātam ācarann utpatya patito' yam akharva-parvata-viśeṣa" iti vitarkitam | [72] rākṣasākāra-sākṣāt-kāra-vikalpa-kalpanā-janita-jana-caya-bhaya-hāsa-kautuka-visaṃvāda-nādaṃ kṣaṇato
rākṣasa-tāla-kṣaṇālakṣaṇa-viniścita-vrajāpaciti-pracayaṃ svābhimukham āgatāyā janatāyā mukhān naikabheda-vedana-viccheda-kāraṇāvadhāraṇād avadhārita-vedanaṃ naikaṭya-ghaṭyamāna-vaikaṭyatayā vitrasta-samasta-cittaṃ pari vrajāt patitaṃ pūtanā-pudgalam udbhāvayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> and others, however, having glimpsed bits and pieces from a distance, through mutual narration and the passing of stories, composed these various high-and-low utterances. As follows: [71] 'With flocks of crows rising up in agitation and undistinguished masses of terrible, great, fearsome forms — as if the fierce-rayed [sun] had reduced a being to ashes — it was ridiculed as a knotted mass of the most wicked great bindings; suddenly, with an area decorated with a compacted forest-fragment turned into a thicket — designated thus, and appearing as if touching the earth due to its great distance — this mass of clouds was thus conjectured, deemed fitting for the portent indicated by <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s>, certain and accumulated.' Then [it was reconsidered]: 'Having obtained wings, causing a portent, this special, not-small mountain flew up and fell down' — thus it was speculated. [72] From the instantaneous discernment of the <s>rākṣasa</s>-nature through the decisive resolution of the various imaginings, producing the sounds of the people's fear, laughter, curiosity, and contradiction, and from the ascertainment of the cause of cutting through the various pains from the faces of the people coming toward them — having determined the agony, with everyone's minds terrified by the monstrous proximity being manifested — they envisioned the individual of <s>Pūtanā</s> who had fallen outside of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text:
śrutvā pūtanayā sutasya nayanaṃ tasyās tu tasmān mṛtiṃ
  mūrcchann eva tadā vraja-kṣiti-patiḥ samyak prabodhaṃ yayau |
  labdhvā durdhara-kāla-nāga-daśana-troṭaṃ yathā tat-kṣaṇād
  divyaṃ mantram api śrayeta manujaḥ kaścid drutaṃ jīvitum ||JGc_1,5.29|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Hearing that <s>Pūtanā</s> had aimed at his son's [destruction], and then of her death from that —
the lord of the <s>Vraja</s>-land, even while fainting, attained full awakening;
just as a person, having received the bite of the unbearable <s>Kāla-nāga</s> (death-serpent),
would at that very moment resort to a divine <s>mantra</s> in order to quickly survive. ||5.29||

children.text: atha vrajarājas tatrāścarya-pāramparyam idam aśṛṇod adarśayad anvabhūd api | [74] tatrāśṛṇod yathā prathamaṃ tāvat pūtanā-tanur āyāmatas tri-gavyūtiṃ vyāpya patitavatī, vistāratas tu gavyutim, ucchrāyataś ca prāyaḥ krośam iti | [75] sā ca yāma-dvaya-gamyāyāma-tad-ardha-vistāra-vrajāgāra-vrajād bahir eva papāta, tatra ca na prāṇinaḥ pīḍitavatī, kintu drumān eveti |
children.translated_text: Then the king of <s>Vraja</s> heard, saw, and experienced this succession of wonders. [74] He first heard that <s>Pūtanā's</s> body, falling, covered three <s>gavyūtis</s> (about 12 miles) in length, a <s>gavyuti</s> (about 4 miles) in width, and approximately a <s>krośa</s> (about 2 miles) in height. [75] And she fell outside the <s>Vraja</s> settlement — which was itself two <s>yāmas</s> (about 8 miles) in length and half that in width — and there she had not injured any living beings, but only trees.

children.text: athādarśayad yathā, tatra hi kuliśa-tulya-niṣṭhura-mahiṣṭha-kulya-kulākulā-ghanās tad-apaghanāḥ svīya-samājñayā vraja-jana-pṛthak-pṛthag-jana-vrajena jhaṭity eva kaṭhina-kuṭhārair vipāṭitāḥ, pracuratara-sthāna-sthāpitās tato' py ativitatāni nirbandhenendhanāni sandhāya sandagdhāś ceti |
children.translated_text: And he saw the following: The massive limbs — dense with clusters of great, adamantine-hard bones like channels — were quickly split by the <s>Vraja</s>-folk, each group of people separately, with hard axes, by his own command; and having been placed in very large spaces, and having been bound with firewood that was even more extensive, they were burned.

children.text: tad evaṃ tad-vraja-bahir-dhāma-pāmara-carmakārādi-karmākāra-gaṇānām api gaṇanā śakti-samatiriktatā ca na vyaktīkartuṃ śakyate, kim uta gopādīnām iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, the enumeration and the surpassing capacity even of the untouchable workers — leather-workers, craftsmen, and others — outside the domain of that <s>Vraja</s>, cannot be made manifest — what then of the cowherds and others?

children.text: athānvabhūd yathā-
children.translated_text: And he experienced the following:

children.text:
kaṃsāreḥ sumadhurimā pramāṇa-caryāṃ
  na prāpsyaty adhiyuga-koṭi-kūṭito' pi |
  sā rākṣasy api rudhirāśanāpi yasya
  sparśāṃśād vara-surabhitvam āsasāda ||JGc_1,5.30|| [praharṣiṇī]

yataḥ,
  tadā ca dūtā iva pūtanāṅgato
  dagdhād gatā dhūma-gaṇāḥ sugandhayaḥ |
  grāmāntaraṃ yātavatāṃ dināntare
  keṣāñcid āhvāna-kṛtiṃ vinirmamuḥ ||JGc_1,5.31|| iti ||| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
For:
Then, the fragrant smoke-masses that went forth
from the burning body of <s>Pūtanā</s> — like messengers —
for some who had traveled to other villages,
on another day, produced the act of summoning [them back]. ||5.31||

children.text:
athātmajaṃ kalayitum āśu gokula-
  kṣitīśitā vraja-pura-madhyam āyayau |
  gato' ntike pathi patad-aśru-vigrahaḥ
  kṣaṇaṃ sthitaḥ svajana-gṛhīta-dor-yugaḥ ||JGc_1,5.32|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
Then, the lord of the <s>Gokula</s>-land,
in order to quickly see his son, came to the center of <s>Vraja</s>-city;
on the way, near [the house], with a body from which tears were falling,
he stood for a moment, his two arms held by his own people. ||5.32||

children.text: atha dhīratām eva dhārayan parama-dhīra-dhīr asau dvi-tra-mitra-parivṛtatayā bṛhad-gṛhālinda-vedīṃ vindamānaḥ kanakāsana-kṛtāsanaḥ svakula-gokula-kula-purandhrībhiḥ sārdham ardhāṅgena sānandam upananda-vadhū-hasta-vinyastaṃ bālaṃ puraskurvatā purataḥ patir abhijagme | bālaś ca tasyotsaṅga-saṅgī kārayāñcakre | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then, maintaining his composure, that one of supremely steady intellect, surrounded by two or three friends, reaching the platform-terrace of the great house, having taken his seat on a golden throne — together with the principal women of his own <s>Gokula</s> clan — with half his body [turned toward them], joyfully, with the baby placed on the hand of <s>Upananda's</s> wife before him, his wife came to meet him. And the baby was made to rest upon his lap. And there:

children.text:
"kiṃ grahārditatayā sa bālako
  dūnatām agamad eka-rātrataḥ |"
  ity acintayad amuṃ tadenduvat
  sphītam aikṣata punar vrajādhipaḥ ||JGc_1,5.33|| [rathoddhata]
children.translated_text:
'Could it be that the baby has become weak
from affliction by a planet (<s>graha</s>), in just one night?'
Thus the lord of <s>Vraja</s> wondered about him,
then beheld him again, full like the moon. ||5.33||

children.text:
kiṃ ca,
  līḍhaṃ rūpa-madhu prakṛṣya rasitaṃ vaktra-prasādāmṛtaṃ
  samyak svādita eva tulya-rahita-sparśotsavaḥ ko' py asau |
  tasya śyāmala-bāla-komala-tanor mūrdhnas tu tātena tāṃ
  saurabhya-svadanānubhūtim abhito viśvaṃ madād vismṛtam ||JGc_1,5.34|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
The honey of his beauty was drunk, the nectar of his face's grace was drawn out and savored,
the festivity of his touch — incomparable, unequaled — was fully tasted;
of that dark, infant, tender-bodied one's head — by the father, that
experience of savoring the fragrance — by it, the entire world was forgotten in ecstasy! ||5.34||

children.text:
nibhālya ca śrīman mukhaṃ sukham ūce,
  "yadi nārāyaṇena tvaṃ datto' si kṛpaṇāya me |
  tenaiva sarvaṃ nirvoḍhā soḍhā ca mama durnayaḥ ||JGc_1,5.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And having gazed upon that glorious face, he said with happiness:
'If you have been given by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> to wretched me,
then by Him alone will everything be borne,
and my misfortune too will be endured.' ||5.35||

children.text: atha "nirvoḍhā nirvoḍhā" ity anuvadanty atyantābhiniveśād ekenāpy akṛta-nirdeśā pṛṣṭha-deśād ita-praveśā jaṭilita-kacā satya-vacāḥ paurṇamāsī sarvair eva tūrṇam utthāya samanaskāreṇa namaskāreṇa puraścakre, arcayāñcakre cāsanādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, repeating 'He will bear it! He will bear it!' — from extreme absorption, without being announced by anyone, entering from behind, with matted hair, truthful in speech — <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> was swiftly honored by everyone, who rose [to greet her] with mental and bodily salutation, and was offered a seat and other honors.

children.text: tataś ca, svapraśnottara-viṣayīkṛta-tad-viṣa-yoṣā-vṛtti-śeṣā rājñānujñāpayām babhūve pūrvavad apūrva-dānādy-apūrvāya | tac ca tām eva pradhānaṃ vidhāya vidhīyate sma iti |
children.translated_text: Then, she — with the remainder of her account of the story of the poisonous woman (<s>Pūtanā</s>), which had been made the subject of her own questions and answers — was given leave by the king, as before, for the unprecedented giving and other [charitable acts]. And that [giving] was carried out with her as the presiding [authority].

children.text: tad evaṃ pūtanāṃ ghātayitvā samāpanāya punar apīdaṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ paramarṣi-sammatatā-vyañjanayā samuṭṭaṅkitavān-
children.translated_text: Thus, having caused <s>Pūtanā</s> to be killed, for the conclusion once again, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> composed this, revealing the assent of the great sages:

children.text:
īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava gopa-pate yataḥ |
  sā bāla-rākṣasī jajñe nija-saṃsāra-rākṣasī ||JGc_1,5.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Such a son was born to you, O lord of the cow-settlement, for whom
that child-demoness became a demoness of her own <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence)! ||5.36||

children.text:
cetasi cedaṃ viviktavān,
  arbhāsṛg-bhug ajani yat purā yad arvāg-
  dhātrī cābhavad iyam atra nanda-sūnoḥ |
  tat kvādhaspadam atha tac-chiraspadaṃ vā
  kvety antar-hṛdi vimṛśan bhṛśaṃ bhramāmi ||JGc_1,5.37|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
In his mind, he reflected:
That a blood-drinking [demoness] of infants was born before, and that recently
this nurse too appeared here for the son of <s>Nanda</s> —
where then is the lowly state, or where is the exalted state of her head?
Thus, pondering deeply in my inner heart, I am greatly bewildered. ||5.37||

children.text: tad evaṃ vṛtte tad-dine' pi pūrvavad eva kathā rakṣitā yathāyatham api svāvasathādi-pathānugatir ācaritā |
children.translated_text: Thus, on that day too, the narrative was preserved just as before, and the return to their own dwellings and paths was carried out as proper.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
pūtanā-vadhāvadhāraṇaṃ nāma
pañcamaṃ pūraṇam |
||5||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the ascertainment of the slaying of <s>Pūtanā</s>, named
the Fifth Chapter.
||5||

children.text:
atha ṣaṣṭhaṃ pūraṇam
viśaṅkaṭa-śakaṭa-vighaṭṭa-nādi-vicitra-bālya-caritram
children.translated_text:
Now the Sixth Chapter.
The wondrous childhood deeds including the shattering of the formidable cart (<s>Śakaṭa</s>).

children.text: atha tathaivādhare-dyuḥ subhāsamānāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ anumodana-nidigdhaḥ snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭha uvāca-madhu-madhura-kaṇṭha śrī-madhukaṇṭha, śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, in the similarly shining assembly, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, anointed with approbation, eagerly said: 'O <s>Śrī Madhukaṇṭha</s>, of honey-sweet throat! Let it be heard!'

children.text: tataḥ samantād aharahar anyad anyal lāvaṇyam utphullayan vidhuḥ sva-janma-pakṣam ullāsayāmāsa | tatra dig-darśanaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: 'Thereafter, day after day, the moon [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], causing new and ever-new beauty to blossom in all directions, delighted the fortnight of his own birth.' The demonstration of this is as follows:

children.text:
ekā dvitrāś catasro yuta-viyutatayā pañca-ṣāḥ sapta cāṣṭau
paṅktir vā paṅkti-baddhāḥ śiśu-yuvati-jaraty-ardha-vṛddhāḥ samantāt |
āyānti drāg viśanti vraja-nṛpati-gṛhaṃ taṃ ca paśyanti bālaṃ
kṛtvā cuckāra-miśraṃ bahula-vilasitaṃ smāyayantyo hasanti ||JGc_1,6.1|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
One, two or three, four — joined and separated — five and six, seven and eight,
a row, or bound in rows — young women, old ones, half-grown ones, from all sides,
come quickly, enter the house of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, and behold that baby;
having made a loud exclamation mixed with abundant playfulness, smiling, they laugh! ||6.1||

children.text:
yathā ca-
mātrā pitrātha mātā-pitara-kula-bhavair ākulaiś citra-mitrair
netrāṇām añjanābhaṃ śiśum anubhavituṃ santataṃ kañjanābham |
āgamyāgamya ramyākṛti-parivṛtim udvāsya hāsyādi-pūrvaṃ
sparśaṃ sparśaṃ tam uccair aharahar ahaho dṛṅ-maho labhyate sma ||JGc_1,6.2|| [sragdhara]
tataś ca-
  vigalad-alaka-jālālola-dṛk-khañjarīṭaḥ
  prakaṭita-tilaka-śrī-rocanā-kuṅkumābhyām |
  smita-vilasita-vaktraḥ śyāma-dhāmācalāṅghriḥ
  śiśur atiśuśubhe sa prāpya māsaṃ tṛtīyam ||JGc_1,6.3|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
And as follows:
By the mother, by the father, by those born of the mother's and father's families — agitated, with wondrous friends —
to experience the child [who is] collyrium-like [in dark beauty], lotus-like [in softness], continuously,
coming and coming again, casting off the encirclement of beautiful forms, preceded by laughter and the like,
touching and touching him aloud, day after day — ah, ah! — a festival of the eyes was obtained! ||6.2||
And then:
With loosely falling locks of hair, with eyes [darting] like <s>khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail) birds,
with displayed beauty of <s>tilaka</s>, <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), and saffron,
with a smilingly playful face, with feet [dark and] steady as a dark abode,
that infant shone supremely upon reaching the third month. ||6.3||

children.text:
tatra ca-
  snigdhāḥ paśyati seṣmayīti bhujayor yugmaṃ muhuś cālayann
  atyalpaṃ madhuraṃ ca kūjati pariṣvaṅgāya cākāṅkṣati |
  lābhālābha-vaśād amuṣya lasati krandaty api kvāpy asau
  pīta-stanyatayā svapity api punar jāgran mudaṃ yacchati ||JGc_1,6.4||[śārdulavikrīḍitā]
atha kadācin nākṣatra-māsa-trayānte nakṣatreśa-kānte taj-janma-nakṣatre śrīman-mātrā putrābhiṣeka-kautuka-yātrā pravartitā | tadā ca,
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of three <s>nākṣatra</s> (sidereal) months, on the beloved [day] of the lord of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (stars), on the birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation), the glorious mother initiated a festive procession for the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) of the son. And then:

children.text:
bhavanam anu suyatne ratna-paryaṅka-varye
  surabhi-mṛdula-tulī-śubhra-vastra-praśaste |
  hari-maṇi-ruci-bālaḥ śobhate smāsitāmbho-
  ruham iva sura-sindhau kṣīra-sindhau harir vā ||JGc_1,6.5|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
In the well-appointed house, upon the finest jeweled couch,
on soft, fragrant cushions, praised with white cloth,
the baby, with the radiance of a <s>hari-maṇi</s> (emerald/sapphire), shone
like a smiling lotus upon the celestial river, or like <s>Hari</s> upon the milk-ocean! ||6.5||

children.text:
athottāna-śāyī sa sarvātiśāyī
  nijāmbā-yaśodaḥ sva-tāta-pramodaḥ |
  sva-nakṣatra-bhāte babhūva prabhāte
  balenātisāṅgaḥ parāvartitāṅgaḥ ||JGc_1,6.6|| [bhūjaṅgaprayātā]
children.translated_text:
Then, lying on his back, that one who surpassed all,
the glory of his mother <s>Yaśodā</s>, the delight of his father,
on the morning of the shining of his own birth-<s>nakṣatra</s>,
with great strength and firm limbs, turned over! ||6.6||

children.text: tataś ca, śayanaṃ pārśvenopapīḍaṃ śayānam amuṃ sukumāra-kumārāpīḍam akasmād vilokya tad-vṛtte dhātrībhir mātre nivedita-mātre sati sātimātrānanda-kandalitā nija-nandana-maṅgalātiśaya-spṛhiṇī śrīman-nanda-kṣitīśa-gṛhiṇī bhartur ājñāṃ sujñātāṃ sambhūya bhūyaḥ sarvāḥ samāhūya tam eva mahotsavam aho mahotsavaṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then, having suddenly beheld the tender prince lying on his side upon the bed, pressed sideways — when the nurse-maids had reported the matter to the mother — the wife of the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, king of the earth, overflowing with boundless joy, eager for the excess of auspiciousness for her own son, having understood her husband's known wish, gathering everyone again, performed that very great festival — ah, what a great festival!

children.text: tatra kāsāñcid api gṛha-pālanāya sthitānām āhūtir evam anusandheyā;
children.translated_text: There, the summoning of even those who had remained home for house-guarding should be understood thus:

children.text:
lālyasyādya tu janmabhaṃ vijayate tatrāpi cautthānikaṃ
  sarvā eva gatās tvam eva kila kiṃ sadmāvituṃ vartase |
  āgṛhṇāti muhur vrajeśa-gṛhiṇī kiṃ vā vraje moṣakaḥ
  ko' py asti sphuṭam asti vā sa tu śiśur muṣṇāti cetaḥ param ||JGc_1,6.7|| [śārdulavikrīḍitam]
[6] atha tatra citra-vāditra-śubha-rīti-gīti-praśasta-vipra-kula-śasta-svasti-vācana-pūrvaka-vidhim atiricyābhiṣicya, pīta-vāsasā parikṛtyālaṅkṛtya, mantrādibhir abhirakṣyābhilakṣya, tad-uddharṣa-harṣamaya-bahutara-kārya-caryā-maryādāṃ paryāpayitum itas tataś calantī, parijanān api niyojanayā sa-prayojanān janayantī, jananī gehāyamāna-visaṅkaṭa-ghaṭana-mahā-śakaṭādhaḥ kalya eva palyaṅke bālam ālokājira evājire śāyitavatī | tatra kumārayataḥ kumārāṃś ca sthāpitavatī | tatrāvaṣṭambha-stambha-catuṣṭaya-madhyaga-dolākāraḥ sa palyaṅko yathā-
children.translated_text:
'The celebration of the darling's birth-day triumphs today! And there, even the fourth-day ceremony! | All have gone — you alone, it seems, remain to guard the house? | Does the wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> keep summoning you again and again, or is there some thief in <s>Vraja</s>? | Clearly there is — but that infant steals only the mind, nothing else!' || (JGc 1,6.7) [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[6] Then, there, having surpassingly anointed [the child] with auspicious rites of various musical instruments, praises, and songs, and the preliminary recitation of benedictions by the excellent assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having dressed [him] in yellow garments and adorned him, having protected and marked him with <s>mantras</s> and the like, moving here and there to complete the boundaries of the plentiful duties of that excessive delight, setting the attendants too to their purposeful tasks, the mother laid the infant on a cradle beneath a great cart in the spacious yard of the house, in the courtyard at a blessed hour. There she stationed boys as guards around the prince. And that cradle, in the middle of four supporting pillars, in the shape of a swing, was as follows:

children.text:
pravālāṅghrir gārutmata-ghaṭita-paṭṭī-paṭu-rucir
  vahan madhye paṭṭāruṇa-cipiṭa-ḍorī-paṭa-vṛtim |
  dukūlāntas tula-sphurita-vara-tulī-valayito
  darāndolo dolo yad upari vireje śiśu-hariḥ ||JGc_1,6.8|| [sikhariṇī]
tatra ca-
  sthaviṣṭha-paṭṭa-stavakaṃ vicitraṃ
  nibaddham ūrdhvād abhilambamānam |
  spṛśan karābhyām asitaḥ sa kūjann
  uttāna-śāyī muhur ujjahāsa ||JGc_1,6.9|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
With coral legs, with the sharpness of emerald-fitted border-strips, | bearing in the middle a covering of cloth with red crimson-pressed cords, | lined within with fine silk, encircled with an excellent cotton-fiber cushion, | gently swaying — upon that cradle above, the infant <s>Hari</s> shone! || (JGc 1,6.8) [śikharinī]
And there: | A variegated cluster of thick silk-cloth, | bound from above, hanging down — | touching it with his hands, the dark one, cooing, | lying face upward, laughed again and again! || (JGc 1,6.9) [upajāti]

children.text: tataś ca, brāhmaṇādi-pūjāyāṃ pūryamāṇāyāṃ kṛta-samāharaṇena haraṇena sārdhaṃ sārdha-praharaṇe' py atiyāte na kasyacid anyat kiñcid api chidra-mātram āsīt |
children.translated_text: Then, while the worship of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others was being fulfilled, even though one and a half <s>praharas</s> (about four and a half hours) had passed with the collection and distribution [of gifts], there was not the slightest gap for anyone.

children.text: tadā ca pūtanāvan nūtanārbhakāya kaṃsa-prahitaḥ kaścid diviṣad-ahitaḥ samāgamya divi sthita evaṃ cintayāmāsa: "sa pūtanā-pothako' yaṃ poto visaṅkaṭa-śakaṭādhastād āste | sākṣān mantuṃ vidhātuṃ na ko' pi jantur amuṣya śakṣyatīti lakṣyate | chadma-rūpa-sadmatayā ca pūtanā saṃsthitā, tasmād amūrta eva sann atra pūrtaye bhavāni" iti | tataś cāsau śakaṭam aprakaṭam āviṣṭavān |
children.translated_text: Then, just like <s>Pūtanā</s> [had been sent], a certain celestial enemy, sent by <s>Kaṃsa</s> against the newborn infant, arrived and, remaining in the sky, reflected thus: 'This slayer of <s>Pūtanā</s>, this infant, rests beneath the cart outside the house. It is seen that no creature can directly confront or harm him. And <s>Pūtanā</s> had assumed a disguised form as her abode — therefore, let me too, being bodiless, enter here for fulfillment.' Then that one entered the cart invisibly.

children.text: tad-āveśena cāsau bhūmyāṃ praviśac cakratayā vakrībhavad-akṣatayā copari-pāta-parīpāka-prakramaṃ yadā cakre, tadaiva tad-daiva-vaśataḥ kila tasya potasya stana-nidigdha-dugdha-jagdhīcchā jātā | tadā ca mātaram anupalabhya kātara iva nava-kamala-dala-komala-caraṇāsphālanād udghaṭitaṃ nija-śakaṭaṃ pakṣa-vihīnam api kutukād iva rākṣasa-pakṣiṇīvad uḍḍīnaṃ vidhāya vivṛtta-patanatvam āsādayāmāsa sa śāvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: By the force of his possession, when that [cart] began the process of toppling over — as the wheel bent into a crooked axle and pressed into the earth — at that very moment, by the force of that [infant's] divine destiny, a desire for milk arose in that infant, milk smeared upon the breast. And then, not finding his mother, as if distressed, by the striking of his feet — tender as fresh lotus petals — he kicked open his own cart, and [the cart], though wingless, as if out of curiosity, like a <s>rākṣasa</s>-bird, made a flying leap, and that fawn [the baby] brought about its overturned fall.

children.text:
idam eva sāścaryatayānuditaṃ śrīmad-arjunena viṣṇu-dharme:
  tālocchritāgraṃ guru-bhāra-sāram
  āyāma-vistāravad adya jātaḥ |
  pādāgra-vikṣepa-vibhinna-bhāṇḍaṃ
  cikṣepa ko' nyaḥ śakaṭaṃ yathā tvam? ||iti |
children.translated_text: This very thing was spoken with wonder by the glorious <s>Arjuna</s> in the <s>Viṣṇu-dharma</s>: | 'Having the height of a palm tree, heavy and dense in its load, | of great length and breadth, now born — | who else but you could have hurled the cart, | its vessel shattered by the stroke of a foot-tip?' ||

children.text: sa cāsuraḥ svayam evāmūrtatām urīkṛtavān itīva tam apy asāv ākāśa-nīkāśatayā nāśayāmāsa | tad idam aho kākatālīyam eva jātam | so' yam asurāveśa eva brahmāṇḍa-purāṇe śrī-kṛṣṇāṣṭottara-śata-nāma-stotre śakaṭāsura-bhañjana iti nāmnā vyañjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: And that <s>Asura</s> had himself assumed formlessness — as if [for that reason], [the baby] destroyed him too by reducing him to sky-like [nothingness]. Ah, this indeed happened as if by the coincidence of crow and palm-fruit (<s>kākatālīya</s>)! This very demonic possession is indicated in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, in the hymn of 108 names of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, by the name '<s>Śakaṭāsura-bhañjana</s>' (Smasher of the cart-demon).

children.text: atra devāḥ śrīla-gopāla-bhāvam utprekṣāñcakrire, yathā-
children.translated_text: Here the gods imagined the sentiment of the glorious <s>Gopāla</s>, as follows —

children.text:
"śakaṭam idam ihāsti mad-gṛhasya
  svayam aviśastad anena cotpluto' si |
  ruditam anupadaṃ mayā vikīrṇaṃ
  tad api yadi mriyase na tan mamāgaḥ ||JGc_1,6.10|| iti | [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text: '"This cart here belongs to my house; | you yourself entered it, and by it you were thrown up! | The crying was scattered by me moment by moment — | even so, if you die, that is not my fault!"' || (JGc 1,6.10) [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text:
āvirbhavat-kaṭakaṭe śakaṭe' tha sarve
  kiṃ kiṃ kim ity abhita eva bhiyābhiyātāḥ |
  tasyātipātam avalokya vilokya tokaṃ
  krandad-vimūḍha-matitātatimūḍhavantaḥ ||JGc_1,6.11|| [vasantatilaka]
children.translated_text: When the crashing sound arose from the cart, then all, | saying 'What? What? What?' rushed from every side in fear; | seeing its fall and beholding the child, | crying, bewildered in mind, they became utterly bewildered beyond their bewildered father! || (JGc 1,6.11) [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
mātā ca taṃ vivaśitāvayavāpi devā
  viṣṭeva paśyati jane jagṛhe draveṇa |
  paścāt tu kampa-mukha-bhāva-nipīḍitāṅgīṃ
  tāṃ vidrutāḥ paraparāḥ parito' py agṛhṇan ||JGc_1,6.12|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: And the mother, though her limbs were paralyzed, a goddess seemingly helpless, | gazed and seized him with her flowing [tears/emotion]; | afterwards, those who had rushed from every side | held her, whose body was pressed with trembling, facial expressions, and emotions. || (JGc 1,6.12) [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tasminn anasy abdavac-chabde jāte tu,
  kiṃ tat? kiṃ tan nanāda? śruti-kaṭu-śakaṭas tat kathaṃ sa vyaloṭhīt
  kasmāt kasmād? akasmāt kuśala-kuśalam? oṃ vāsudeva-prasādāt |
  itthaṃ praśnottarābhyāṃ vraja-kula-patayaḥ prāpur antaḥ-purāntar
  dṛṣṭvā tat-pātam āsan daśana-tati-śikhād aṣṭa-jihvāś cirāya ||JGc_1,6.13|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: When that thunderous cloud-like sound arose from that [cart]: | 'What was that? What thundered? The cart that was harsh to the ears — how did it overturn? | From what? From what? Suddenly! Is all well? All well? Yes — by the grace of <s>Vāsudeva</s>!' | Thus, through questions and answers, the lords of the <s>Vraja</s> clan entered the inner quarters; | having seen that fall, they became, for a long time, eight-tongued [like fire] from their rows of teeth! || (JGc 1,6.13) [sragdharā]

children.text: tataś ca sahasā bahiḥ-purād antaḥ-pura-pura-sthala-bhājaṃ śrīmad-vraja-rājaṃ nirvarṇya sarve paryāyāgatā dvidhābhūtāḥ pūrato dūrato' vakāśaṃ daduḥ | [15] tato' sau janakas tu jana-kalakalatas tad-vṛttam avakalayann ambālā-galāvalambaṃ bālakam eva sva-pāṇi-talam avalambayāmāsa, vilokayāmāsa ca tasya sarvāvayavān |
children.translated_text: Then, suddenly discerning the glorious King of <s>Vraja</s> coming from the outer quarters to the inner-quarters ground, everyone who had arrived in turn divided into two and gave way in front and at a distance. [15] Then that father, ascertaining the event from the commotion of people, took the infant — who was hanging from <s>Yaśodā's</s> neck — into the palm of his own hand, and examined all his limbs.

children.text: tad anu ca sarva eva śāntatāmāyāntas tad-antaṃ samantataḥ śakaṭa-nikaṭa-saṃvalakān bālakān eva papracchuḥ | te ca tad-eka-nirdeśinyā darśayantas tam eva nirdidiśuḥ | tatraiko lohalo' py agra-vādī nivārita-kolāhalaḥ pralalāpa, "ma ma mama pā pā pā pārśvataḥ śrūyatām, ya ya ya yadā ca ca caraṇa mu mutthāpitavān ayam, ta ta ta tadā te tena spṛṣṭa-mātro ḍi ḍi ḍi ḍi ḍīna ivodvṛttaḥ so' yaṃ śa śa śa śakaṭaḥ" iti |
children.translated_text: Then, when everyone had attained calmness, they questioned only the boys assembled near the cart all around. And those [boys], pointing with a single indicating [finger], pointed to him [the baby] alone. Among them, one iron-bold, forward speaker, his tumult restrained, stammered: 'F-f-from m-m-my s-s-side, listen! Wh-wh-when h-he r-raised his f-foot, th-th-then, th-that [cart], merely touched by it, t-t-tumbled over l-like a b-b-bird — th-that c-c-c-cart!'

children.text: tataś ca, tad-viḍamba-vādiṣu bālādiṣu hasatsu bībhatsita-bāliśa-bhāṣitāḥ parama-vatsalā vicikitsāṃ na dhitsāṃ cakruḥ | pūtanā-vadhāvadhāritānuvāditayā karkaśa-tarka-cakra-niruddha-buddhayas tu cakruḥ | [18] pitā tu punaḥ svasti-vācanābhiṣecanādinā vipra-kula-pratoṣaṇādinā sarvāśī-rāśinā ca taṃ laṅgima-bālaṃ maṅgalena saṅgamayāmāsa mātur utsaṅgena ca | tayā ca sva-bāla-lālanā-kalāpa-mayyā gṛhāntaḥ-śayyāyām evāyaṃ śāyyate sma | gopa-mahendrādibhir mahita-mahā-śakaṭaś ca yathā-sthānaṃ ghaṭayāmāse |
children.translated_text: Then, while the children and others who mocked [his stammering] laughed, those of supreme tenderness, disgusted by the childish speech, made no inquiry — nor had they the intention to. But those whose understanding was blocked by the harsh wheel of logic, checked by the established narration of the slaying of <s>Pūtanā</s>, did make [such inquiry]. [18] The father, however, through benedictions, anointing-baths, and the like, through the gratification of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> community and the like, and through the entire mass of blessings, united that acrobat-infant with auspiciousness and with his mother's lap. And she, full of the arts of fondling her own child, laid him upon the bed within the house. And the great cart, honored by the chief of cowherds and others, was restored to its place.

children.text: atha madhukaṇṭha uvāca-vatsa, bālakena mahā-śakaṭa-samuccāṭanam asambhāvyam iti sambhāvya bhaṇyatām, anyathā hi kaver evānyathātvam āpadyeta |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'O dear one! Considering that the overturning of the great cart by a baby is improbable, please speak — otherwise, the poet himself would fall into inaccuracy.'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-ārya, pūrvam evātrāpūrvatā nivāritāsti, yato yogamāyā khalv asya sambhāvita-yogaṃ nirmāpayatīti punar mā prākṣīḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'O elder! The impossibility in this has already been precluded, for <s>Yogamāyā</s> indeed manufactures the conceived yoga [supernatural feat] for him — so do not ask again.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭhaḥ sa-smitam uvāca-tad-anantaram udantaḥ kaḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said with a smile: 'What is the next episode after that?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-athāgrajānujān anu vrajasya rājā viviveca, "bālaka-yugalam idam apṛthag-ālayālambanatām eva nitarām arhati, yatas tadīya-jananyoḥ svayam eva tal-lālanāya lālasā-dhanyayos, tatra ca paraspara-tad-āsaktayor nānā-spṛha-gṛha-kārya-paryāpaṇa-vyasanayor yugapat tad-yugalasya pṛthag-avakalanaṃ durbalam iti kevalaṃ sudināgamana-vilambatām avalambe | yathā vā bhavatām icchā bhavati" iti śrutvā śrutajñāḥ śrotriyān āśrāvya tadaiva daivānukūlyaṃ nibhālya samam udyad-vādya-parīta-gīta-svasti-vācanādi-praśasti-pūrvakaṃ dvayor apūrva-milanam āśu kalayāmāsuḥ | tac ca yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then the king of <s>Vraja</s>, considering the elder and younger [sons], deliberated: "This pair of boys indeed fully deserves the sheltering of a single, undivided home, because of the two mothers' own eagerness for fondling them, and because, given their mutual attachment there and the distraction of various household duties arising from diverse desires, the separate care of the two [boys] simultaneously would be difficult — therefore I merely await the arrival of the auspicious day. Or, as your wish may be." Having heard this, those knowledgeable in traditions, having made the <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholars) hear, having ascertained divine favor at that very time, simultaneously, preceded by praises of the blessings of rising music and songs, they quickly arranged the unprecedented meeting of the two. And that was as follows:' —

children.text:
mitho lagnā dṛṣṭiḥ samajani ciraṃ mūrtir acalā
  dravac-cittaṃ netrodaka-miṣatayāgād abhimukham |
  iti bhrātror bālye' py asita-sitayoḥ sā prasitatā
  nave vyatyāloke kutukam iha kiṃ vā na tanute? ||JGc_1,6.14|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: Their gazes became mutually locked; for a long time their bodies became motionless; | their melting hearts, under the pretext of tears in the eyes, came face to face. | Thus, even in the childhood of the two brothers, the dark and the fair, that passionate attachment — | in their novel, first mutual seeing — what wonder does it not produce here? || (JGc 1,6.14) [śikharinī]

children.text:
bālye prathamam anyo' nyaṃ milato rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ |
  sitāsitāṃśavaḥ pṛktā jajñire mṛga-lāñchanāḥ ||JGc_1,6.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> first met each other in childhood, | the dark and bright rays, commingled, | produced deer-marks [moon-spots]! || (JGc 1,6.15) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evam eva sarva eva parva vidhāya nija-nija-nūtana-tanūjān gaṇaka-gaṇita-guṇa-gaṇe' hani snehaṃ teṣāṃ teneha sahehamānāḥ sa-maṅgalaṃ saṅgamayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when everyone had performed every celebration, on the day computed by the astrologers as auspicious in the count of virtues, they brought together each person's respective new-born child with affection, performing the confluence with auspiciousness.

children.text:
atha yukti-matyā sad-ukti-sammatyā śrīmad-bhāgavata-kathana-vyutkrameṇāpy upakramyate, yataḥ,
  sarvaiḥ kavibhir anukrama śāli procyate kṛṣṇa-līlādyam |
  śuka-mukha-vacasi prema pramada-maye tad vinā tu citrāya ||JGc_1,6.16|| [gīti]
children.translated_text: Now, with ingenuity, with the approval of good speech, [the narration] is also undertaken in a different order from the narrative of the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, because: | 'All poets speak of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> pastimes in sequential order; | in the speech of <s>Śuka's</s> mouth, however, there is love filled with ecstasy — without that, it would be strange.' || (JGc 1,6.16) [gīti]

children.text:
tad evaṃ dina-śata-pūraṇam adūratām anujasyāgrajasya tu tasmād apy adūratāṃ labdham |
  samyaṅ mātuḥ paricitir abhūd yatra kiñcit pituś ca
  prāptaḥ so' yaṃ svasadana-janaḥ kiṃ na vetthaṃ matiś ca |
  tasmin bālye valayati tayoḥ kāpi śobhā sudhābdhi
  prakhyā goṣṭhaṃ bhūvanam api sā vīcibhiḥ siñcati sma ||JGc_1,6.17|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: Thus, the completion of a hundred days was not far off for the younger [Kṛṣṇa], and for the elder [Balarāma], was already reached even before that. | 'Sufficient acquaintance with the mother was there, and somewhat with the father too; | this one has obtained [the company of] the people of his own home — what [more] does he not know? And his intelligence [has grown]. | In that infancy, some beauty that encircles those two, like the fame of the nectar-ocean, | drenches not only the cow-settlement but also the world with its waves!' || (JGc 1,6.17) [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tad etad adhigatya śīghram eva nāma-karaṇaṃ kartavyam iti sammatya śrīmantaṃ vasudevaṃ prati yadā śrī-vraja-naradevas tan nijam iṣṭaṃ sandiṣṭavān, tadā paramārtha-vicāreṇa mitra-putratārha-samadhika-bahir-vyavahāreṇa cānujasya śatatamaṃ vāsaram eva tad-avasaraṃ niścinvan, śrī-vasudevaḥ śrī-vrajarājaṃ prati yathāvasaraṃ tan nivedayiṣyāma ity aniścinvann iva sandideśa | atha tapo-dhāmānaṃ garga-nāmānam ātmanaḥ parama-hitaṃ kula-purohitaṃ manasi sammatya rahasi saṅgatya nija-tanaya-vinimaya-mayaṃ vṛttaṃ vitatya nivedayāmāsa | sa ca sahāsam āha sma, "tad etad aparam apy ahaṃ nānā-vṛttaṃ jānāmy eva | sampraty atra mat-kṛtyaṃ tv ājñāpyatām |"
children.translated_text: Having understood this, agreeing that the name-giving ceremony should be performed quickly, when the glorious Lord of <s>Vraja</s> sent his desired instruction to the glorious <s>Vasudeva</s>, then [<s>Vasudeva</s>], determining by means of deliberation on ultimate reality and by the external formality that befits a friend's son's [ceremony], fixed exactly the hundredth day of the younger [Kṛṣṇa] as the occasion — and, as if not determining it, sent word to the glorious King of <s>Vraja</s>: 'We shall inform [you] at the proper time.' Then, [<s>Vasudeva</s>], having thought in his mind of <s>Garga</s> by name, that great repository of austerity, his own supremely beneficial family priest, having met him in private, having extended and reported the entire account including the exchange of his own sons, [consulted him]. And he (<s>Garga</s>) said with a laugh: 'I too indeed know all these various events. At present, however, command what my task shall be.'

children.text: vasudeva uvāca-"tatas tatra-bhavatā nanda-vraja-bhūvaṃ vrājaṃ vrājaṃ mithaḥ saṃyutau navyau nija-yajamāna-sutau dvijāti-jāti-samucita-prakāreṇa saṃskāreṇa puraskartavyau, kintūpanayanopayamane yathā tasyāṃ na syātāṃ, tathā prayatanīyam |"
children.translated_text: Vasudeva said: "Therefore, by you, going and going to the land of Nanda's Vraja community, these two new sons of your own patron should be consecrated with the sacraments appropriate to the twice-born caste. However, care must be taken that the upanayana (sacred thread ceremony) and marriage should not take place there."

children.text: munir uvāca-"yuktam uktam, yataḥ sva-pakṣa evāsmābhir apekṣaṇīyaḥ |"
children.translated_text: The sage said: "What you have said is proper, for it is our own side that we must consider."

children.text:
atha tasminn anujasya śatatama eva vāsare, vrajaṃ prati prasthite ca muni-vare, vraja-rājas tu jyāyasas tad-dinātikramāt puṇyataraṃ dināntaram eva dvayor api nāma-karaṇasyādhikaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti niścitya, prātar eva tarṇakānāṃ koṭibhir nṛtya-paripāṭībhir āṭīkamānābhir vicitraṃ sthānaṃ go-gopānāṃ vana-prasthānān nirjanāvasthānaṃ gosthānam anusaṃskārālaṅkāra-sambhālanārtham eka-sevaka-mātra-kṛtānuvrajanatayā kṛta-vrajanaḥ sa-kṛpatayā tān paśyann āsīt | tatraiva ca sarvato' py atirikte vivikte bālyata eva kṛta-sevaṃ nija-devaṃ sarva-sal-lakṣaṇa-nandita-nikhilāyāṃ śrīmal-lakṣmī-nārāyaṇākhya-śālagrāma-śilāyām aṣṭākṣareṇopatiṣṭhamānaś cirād virājate sma | kṛta-samāpane ca sabhājane sarva-sarvajña-gurur muni-pariṣadām
ururvāṇī-vāsita-sāmā śrī-garga-nāmā vāraṃ vāraṃ niṣkrama-dvāraṃ vilokamānena gopa-loka-pradhānena tasmād akasmāt tarṇakānām utkarṇatā-nirvarṇanayā kasyacid āgamanaṃ vitarkayatā turṇam abhyarṇata eva niravarṇi | tadā ca-
children.translated_text: Then, on the very hundredth day of the younger brother's birth, when the foremost sage had set out toward Vraja, the king of Vraja decided that a more auspicious day following the day of the elder — that very different day — would serve as the occasion for the naming ceremony of both. Early in the morning, having gone to the cow-station — the wonderful place where the cows and cowherds had departed for the forest, now deserted — for the purpose of arranging the decorations for the re-consecration, accompanied only by a single servant, he was gazing at them with tenderness. And there, in the most secluded and private of all places, worshipping since childhood his own deity — in the Śālagrāma stone named Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, which delighted all with its auspicious marks — he had been standing in worship with the eight-syllabled mantra for a long time, resplendent. When that worship was completed and the assembly honored, the foremost teacher of all assemblies of sages, whose name was the glorious Garga — whose Sāma Veda chanting was perfumed with divine speech — was discerned quite nearby and suddenly by the chief of the cowherd community, who was looking again and again toward the exit-gate, and who, by noticing the sudden pricking-up of the calves' ears, conjectured someone's arrival. And then —

children.text:
unmīlad-vidhu-varṇam ardha-palitaṃ vaktrādir upānvitaṃ
  kiñcit sthūlam akharvam āyāta-bhūjaṃ viṣvak-prasādākaram |
  śubhra-śrī-vasana-dvayaṃ śruti-karālaṅkāra-dīvyat-prabhaṃ
  putra-prema-vilakṣitākhilam ṛṣiḥ śrī-nandam atraikṣata ||JGc_1,6.18|| [śārdula]
children.translated_text: [Verse:] "Of a complexion like the opening moon, half-grey-haired, with a corresponding face and other features, somewhat stout, not short, with long arms, spreading grace in all directions, wearing a pair of bright, auspicious garments, with splendid radiance from the ornaments of his ears of Vedic learning — the sage beheld Śrī Nanda, in whom everything was distinguished by love for his son." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.18, śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: asya ca muner anena cirād vīpsayābhīpsitam āgamanam āsīt, yataḥ pratīkṣya eva sarvatrāyaṃ pratīkṣyatāṃ vā kathaṃ na labheta?
children.translated_text: And this sage's arrival had been long desired with yearning by this one, for he who is to be awaited — awaited everywhere — how could he not be obtained?

children.text: tad evaṃ, "pratītatayā pratītaḥ so' yam" iti taṃ vrajapatir api nipītāmṛtavat parama-prītaḥ śīghram āsana-pradeśam atītaḥ samatirikta-bhakti-parītaḥ kṛtāñjalitayātivinītaḥ sākṣād adhokṣaja-dhītaḥ praṇanāma | brahma-varcasena carcitam enam ānarcā-śeṣeṇa devārcana-dravya-śeṣeṇa, provāca ca-
children.translated_text: 'Thus — "This is the very one recognized by recognition!" — the king of Vraja too, supremely delighted as if drinking nectar, quickly went beyond his seat, surrounded by surpassing devotion, with folded hands and utmost humility — as if beholding Adhokṣaja (Viṣṇu) directly — he bowed down. He worshipped him, radiant with brahminical splendor, with the remnants of the divine worship — the remaining flowers, sandalwood, and other offerings — and said:',

children.text:
"alam iha kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭvā kuśalaṃ kuśalaṃ bhaved yasmāt |
  kintu svaka-kuśalārthaṃ kuśalaṃ tatra ca vipṛcchyate sadbhiḥ ||JGc_1,6.19|| [udgīti]
  svāgata-pṛcchā dhārṣṭyaṃ bhavati mahiṣṭhe sadeti gīr-yuktā |
  tad api surārcām anu sā yadvan nirmīyate tadvat ||JGc_1,6.20|| [āryā]
  kevala-vacasā toṣo vaibhava-sattve na yujyate nunam |
  kintv idam apūrṇa-viṣayaṃ pūrṇe kiñcin na māty eva ||JGc_1,6.21|| [āryā]
  na sataḥ svārthāpekṣā kintu sadā sā parārthaiva |
  tasmād viharati tasmin para-para-vijñāpanaṃ sukhadam ||JGc_1,6.22|| [upagīti]
  jyotiḥ-śāstraṃ bhavatā kṛtam atha vede' pi niṣṇātam |
  tat tat para-sukha-mātrāpekṣaṃ tad idaṃ nivedyaṃ me ||JGc_1,6.23|| [upagīti]
  bālo yo mama jātas tasmād adhikaś ca vāsudevo yaḥ |
  nija-dṛk-sudhayā taṃ taṃ śīkitum āstāṃ bhavān karuṇaḥ ||JGc_1,6.24|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text: "'Enough of asking about welfare here — [for] welfare would result from welfare! But the wise inquire about welfare only for the sake of one's own welfare. [Gopāla-campū 1.6.19, udgīti] The inquiry about welcome is boldness toward a great one — so the saying goes. Nevertheless, just as it is fashioned after divine worship, so [let it be]. [Gopāla-campū 1.6.20, āryā] Satisfaction by mere words alone is indeed not fitting when the substance of magnificence exists. But this is a matter of incompleteness — in fullness, nothing at all is small. [Gopāla-campū 1.6.21, āryā] A virtuous person has no expectation for his own sake, but his [expectation] is always for the sake of others. Therefore, the informing of the supreme other, who plays in that [realm], is the source of happiness. [Gopāla-campū 1.6.22, upagīti] The science of luminaries (jyotiḥ-śāstra) has been composed by you, and you are also accomplished in the Veda. All of that is concerned solely with the happiness of others — let this be communicated to me. [Gopāla-campū 1.6.23, upagīti] A child has been born who is mine, and one who is greater — who is Vāsudeva's. May you, the compassionate one, remain to sprinkle each of them with the nectar of your gaze." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.24, upagīti]'

children.text:
tad etad āśrutya gargaḥ sa-gadgadaṃ jagāda-
  "yan-manā bhikṣur āyātas tad dātā ditsati svayam |
  tadā bhāgyaṃ kiyad varṇyaṃ bhikṣor dātuś ca kauśalam? ||JGc_1,6.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Having heard all this, Garga spoke with a choked voice: '"The very thing for which the beggar came, the giver himself wishes to give — then how much fortune can be described, of either the beggar or the giver's skill?" [Gopāla-campū 1.6.25, anuṣṭubh]'

children.text:
tad evam ātmane ślāghamāne muni-rāje śrī-vrajarājaḥ sva-niyojyasya karṇe varṇitavān, "evam evaṃ kuru," iti, pravartayāmāsa ca muninā kaṃsa-durvṛtta-vivartita-vasudeva-vṛtta-saṃvādam | [34] sampravadamānayoś ca tayoḥ so' pi tat-prayojanaṃ parāmṛśya śuddhāntaṃ praviśya nija-nijotsaṅga-saṅgatīkṛta-bāle ambāle puro vidhāya gandha-puṣpādi-lasita-cāmīkara-bhājana-karaḥ parama-kiṅkaraḥ sahasā rahasāsasāda |
  vīkṣyātha mātror urasi prasañjitāv
  atyarbhakau dūrata eva tāv ṛṣiḥ |
  javād udasthān maṇi-mantravat prabhoḥ
  prabhāva evādṛtaye na vistṛtiḥ ||JGc_1,6.26|| [upajāti 12]
tataś ca,
  mātṛ-yugma-lalitāṅga-lālitau
  vīkṣya kṛṣṇa-dhavalau sa bālakau |
  nirnimeṣa-daśayā dṛśor jalaṃ
  roddhum aiṣṭa nitarāṃ na tāpasaḥ ||JGc_1,6.27|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'Thus, when the king of sages was praising himself, the king of Vraja whispered in his servant's ear: "Do thus and thus" — and set in motion a conversation with the sage about the circumstances of Vasudeva, brought about by Kaṃsa's wickedness.' [34] 'And while those two were conversing, that servant too, grasping the purpose, entered the inner quarters and, placing before them the two infants — each made intimate upon their respective laps — bearing vessels of golden ware adorned with sandalwood, flowers, and the like, the supreme attendant quickly arrived at the private place. [Verse:] "Then, seeing the two most tender infants attached to the breasts of the two mothers from afar, the sage swiftly rose up — like a jewel or a mantra, it is the Lord's power alone that is honored, not its extent!" [Gopāla-campū 1.6.26, upajāti] And then, [Verse:] "Beholding those two children, dark and fair, being fondled on the graceful limbs of the pair of mothers — with unblinking gaze, the ascetic could not restrain the water of his eyes at all!" [Gopāla-campū 1.6.27, rathoddhatā]'

children.text:
atha saṅkocaṃ vidhāya sannidhāya mātṛbhyām ātmanātmajābhyāṃ ca maunenaivānāmi muni-varaḥ | so' yam uccakair āśīśiṣac ca, yathā,
  "pitroḥ pratisvaṃ kulayos tadīyayoḥ
  sambandhi-bandhu-prakare jagaty api |
  ānanda-dātā bhava nanda-nandana,
  tvaṃ tadvad apy ānakadundubheḥ suta! ||JGc_1,6.28|| [indravaṃśā]
children.translated_text: Then, having composed himself and come near, the foremost sage silently bowed to the mothers and to their sons. He blessed them loudly, as follows: '"O son of Nanda, be a giver of joy to your parents, to the two families of each, to the throng of relatives and kinsmen, and to the world! And you likewise, O son of Ānakadundubhi (Vasudeva)!" [Gopāla-campū 1.6.28, indravaṃśā]'

children.text:
tataś ca, tad-eka-sarge garge vrajeśvara-yācanataḥ svāsanam āgate purataḥ kiñcid dūrataḥ:
  sitāsitaikaika-puṣpa viṣṇukrāntādvaya-prabhe |
  te rohiṇī-yaśodākhye tanayābhyāṃ virejatuḥ ||JGc_1,6.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Then, when Garga, being of that single creative purpose, had come to his seat before [them] at the request of the lord of Vraja, from a little distance: [Verse:] "Resplendent with the radiance of a pair of Viṣṇukrāntā flowers — one white, one dark — those two, named Rohiṇī and Yaśodā, shone with their sons." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.29, anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tato muner ādeśatas te' py upaviviśituś ca | śrī-garge ca tayor āveśita-dhīndriya-varge, vraja-kṣiti-patiḥ kṣaṇaṃ pratīkṣya sāñjali-girābhilaṣitaṃ vyañjitavān-
children.translated_text: Then, by the sage's instruction, they too sat down. And when Garga's mind and senses were fully absorbed in those two, the king of the earth of Vraja, waiting for a moment, expressed his desire with folded hands and voice —

children.text:
"yogya eva para-yogyatākaras
  tādṛśatvam api veda-vedajam |
  tvaṃ tu veda-viduṣāṃ varas tataḥ
  saṃskuru dvija-janus tanū amū ||JGc_1,6.30|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: '"One who is fit is indeed the cause of the fitness of others; such status too is born of the knowledge of the Vedas. But you are the best among those who know the Vedas; therefore, consecrate these two bodies of twice-born birth!" [Gopāla-campū 1.6.30, rathoddhatā]'

children.text: garga uvāca-"bhavanto yadu-bījyatve' pi vaiśyatatījya-mātṛ-vaṃśānvayitayā tad-guru-padavyāgatair eva karma kārayitavyāḥ na tu mayā |"
children.translated_text: Garga said: "You are to be classified as Vaiśyas by maternal lineage, though of Yadu origin. Therefore, the rites should be performed by those who have attained the station of your guru — not by me."

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-"bhaved evaṃ, kintu kvacid utsarge' py apavāda-vargaṃ bādhate' dhikāri-viśeṣa-śleṣam āsādya, yathaivāhiṃsā-nivṛtta-karmaṇi baddha-śraddhaṃ prati yajñe' pi paśu-hiṃsāṃ | tasmād bhavatāṃ brāhmaṇa-bhāvād utsarga-siddhā gurutā śraddhā-viśeṣavatām asmākaṃ kule kathaṃ laghutām āpnotu? tatrāpi bhavataḥ sarva-pramāṇataḥ samadhikatā samadhigatā, tasmād anyathā mā sma manyathāḥ | etad upari nija-purohitānām api hitam apihita-mahasā kariṣyāmaḥ |"
children.translated_text: The king of Vraja said: "That may be so, but sometimes, in the case of a general rule, the class of exceptions overrides it when encountering the special connection of a qualified person — just as in the case of animal-killing in sacrifice, even for one of firm faith in the non-violent, action-renouncing [path]. Therefore, how can your status as guru, established by the general rule due to your being a brāhmaṇa, become diminished in our clan, which possesses special faith? Moreover, your superiority has been ascertained by all authorities. Therefore, do not think otherwise! Above and beyond this, we shall also ensure the welfare of our own family priests, with undimmed glory."

children.text: gargaḥ punar atigopanāya sa-vicāram uvāca-"tatrāpi khalaḥ sa khalu devakī-toka-hantā durmantā devyāḥ śaṃsanena nṛśaṃsaḥ kaṃsaḥ punar āgatāśaṅkaḥ syāt | yasmād yādava-gurutayā puru-prasiddhaḥ so' yam anya-vargajam amuṃ samaskuruta, tasmād eva vasudeva-kṛtopāsanayā nūnam anayā devyā svena vinimitaḥ sa bālas tatra vartate, gīrvāṇa-vāṇīnām amṛṣābhāvād iti | tadā niḥṣamam idam atiduḥṣamaṃ syāt |"
children.translated_text: Garga then spoke deliberatively about the need for secrecy: "Even so, that wicked one — that killer of Devakī's children, the evil-counseled, cruel Kaṃsa — might become suspicious again through the announcement by the Goddess. Because, being well-known as the guru of the Yādavas, if this one [Garga] consecrated a son of another clan, then, 'Surely, through Vasudeva's worship, by this Goddess he was contrived and the child is placed there' — since the words of divine voices are not false. Then this would be unbearable and most grievous."

children.text:
atha vrajarājas tu manāg vimanāyamāna ivāsīt | punar, anena svasti-vācanādike kṛte sarvaṃ śastaṃ bhaved iti vibhāvya provāca-"yasmāt tava saṅga eva sa-maṅgalas tasmāt,
  alakṣito' smin rahasi māmakair api go-vraje |
children.translated_text: Then the king of Vraja was somewhat dismayed. But then, having reflected that if this one performed the svasti-vācana (benedictory rite) and the like, all would be auspicious — he said: "Since your very association is auspicious, therefore,

children.text: kuru dvijāti-saṃskāraṃ svasti-vācana-pūrvakam ||[BhP 10.8.10] iti |
children.translated_text: 'Unobserved, in this secluded cow-settlement, even by my own people, perform the twice-born sacrament preceded by the svasti-vācana (blessing).' [Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.8.10]"

children.text:
garga uvāca-"bhavatu, bhavad-icchayā yadṛcchayā maṅgalaṃ saṅgamayiṣyate | tataḥ samaya-sammatatvād āpātatas tu nāma-karaṇam eva karavāṇi" iti svasti-vācanādy ācarya provāca tatrāgrajam uddiśya, yathā:
  "īryeta praṇayādi-sad-guṇa-gaṇair etaṃ tathā bandhutā
  mukhyaṃ lokam aśeṣam eṣa ramayan rāmo, balitvād balaḥ |
  kiṃ cāyaṃ bhavad-ādi-śūra-tanayādīnāṃ yadūnāṃ gaṇaṃ
  saṅkrakṣyaty ubhayatra bhāva-tulayā svaṃ tena saṅkarṣaṇaḥ ||JGc_1,6.31|| [śārdula]
children.translated_text: Garga said: "So be it. By your will, through divine arrangement, auspiciousness shall be conjoined. Then, since the naming ceremony alone is appropriate by convention at this time, I shall perform just the naming ceremony." Having performed the svasti-vācana and other rites, he spoke regarding the elder [child], as follows: '"By the abundance of qualities such as affection and other virtues, he shall delight the whole of this foremost world of kinship, and being named Rāma, [he shall be called] Bala (the Strong) because of his might. And furthermore, this one shall draw together the host of Yadus — the sons of Śūra and others of your line — in both [realms], by the balance of feeling; therefore, he is Saṅkarṣaṇa (the Drawer-Together)." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.31, śārdūlavikrīḍita]'

children.text:
athānujam uddiśya,
  "śuklo raktaḥ pīta ity ādi-varṇās
  tat-tad-bhāvād asya tat-tad-yugeṣu |
  tat-tan-mūla-śyāmataikātmya-yogāj
  janmany asmin kṛṣṇa-nāmāyam asti ||JGc_1,6.32|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: Then, regarding the younger [child]: '"White, red, yellow — such were his colors in each successive age, according to his respective nature in each. By the union of the essential identity with the dark hue that is the root of each of those — in this birth, he bears the name Kṛṣṇa." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.32, śālinī]'

children.text:
"yuṣmatto janmataḥ pūrvaṃ vasudevāt tavātmajaḥ |
  jāto yasmāt tato vāsudeva ity api gīyate ||JGc_1,6.33|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: '"Before his birth from you, your son was born from Vasudeva; therefore he is also sung as Vāsudeva." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.33, anuṣṭubh]'

children.text:
"nāmāni yāni guṇa-karma-nibandhanāni
  rūpāṇi ca pratidiśaṃ nikhila-stutāni |
  sākalyato nahi vayaṃ yadi tāni vidmo,
  jānanti tarhi na pare tv iti paunaruktyam ||JGc_1,6.34|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: '"The names that are grounded in qualities and deeds, and the forms praised in every direction by all — if we do not know them in their totality, then neither do others — hence it would be mere repetition." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.34, vasantatilakā]'

children.text:
sānandaṃ nanda-rājena tadā munir agadyata: |
  "lagnaṃ hṛdi na lagnaṃ naḥ, sarvajñas tad bhavān gatiḥ ||JGc_1,6.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Then the sage was joyfully addressed by King Nanda: '"The horoscope is fixed in our heart but not understood by us; you, the omniscient one, are our recourse." [Gopāla-campū 1.6.35, anuṣṭubh]'

children.text:
punaś ca-
  "īkṣatāṃ bhagavann asmai bhavān," iti niveditaḥ |
  gargas tasmai rādhyati sma prahasan mahasānvitaḥ ||JGc_1,6.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: And again: '"Please look upon this [child] for his sake, O Blessed One!" — being thus entreated, Garga, laughing, endowed with glory, assented to him. [Gopāla-campū 1.6.36, anuṣṭubh]'

children.text:
"tad etad asmākaṃ khamāṇikyanāmni jyotirgranthe prāg eva nirupitamasti |
  uccasthāḥ śaśibhaumacāndriśanayo lagnaṃ vṛṣo lābhago
  jīvaḥ siṃhatulāliṣu kramavaśāt puṣośanorāhavaḥ |
  naiśīthaḥ samayo' ṣṭamī budhadinaṃ brahmarkṣamatra kṣaṇe
  śrīkṛṣṇābhidhamambujekṣaṇamabhūd āviḥ paraṃ brahma tat ||iti |
children.translated_text: '"That has already been determined in our astrological treatise called Khamāṇikya: The Moon, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are in exaltation; the ascendant is Taurus; Jupiter is in the eleventh house; in Leo, Libra, and Scorpio in order are Puṣya, Saturn, and Rāhu; the time is midnight; the tithi is the eighth; the day is Wednesday; the nakṣatra is Brahma (Rohiṇī); and at that moment, the lotus-eyed one named Śrī Kṛṣṇa manifested — that is the Supreme Brahman!" Thus it is stated.'

children.text:
"vṛṣakanyātulāmīnarājeṣu sphuṭamuccagāḥ |
  somasaumyaśanikṣauṇīsutāstajjanmani sthitāḥ ||JGc_1,6.37|| [anuṣṭubh]
  yasmād viśvāvasau varṣe janma tvajjanmanaḥ śiśoḥ |
  viśvameva vasu śrīmad bhavitāmuṣya tuṣyataḥ ||JGc_1,6.38|| [anuṣṭubh]
  rohiṇyāṃ janmanā rohiṇyayutānāmasau patiḥ |
  vṛṣalagnaṃ ca tatrāsīd vṛṣakoṭīśitā tataḥ ||JGc_1,6.39|| [anuṣṭubh]
  āyatiścāsya bhavitā sadaivāyatimaty ataḥ |
  āyatyāṃ munayo' py asmin kuryurmanasa āyatim ||JGc_1,6.40|| [anuṣṭubh]
  eṣa vakṣyati śāstrāṇi śastrāṇy apy ātmatejasā;
  aniṣṭahṛd amitrāṇāṃ mitrāṇāṃ ca vrajādhipa ||JGc_1,6.41|| [anuṣṭubh]
  bhavatorbhavitā bhavyamasmād iti vṛthā kathā |
  bhāvatkānāṃ ca tad bhavyaṃ bhavasya ca bhavasya ca ||JGc_1,6.42|| [anuṣṭubh]
  asyāścaryā caryā vahati bahunāṃ kutuhalaṃ bahulam |
  sasurān asurān dunvan bhavati surāṇāṃ purāpy asāv avitā ||JGc_1,6.43|| [udgīti]
  sahajapremṇāṃ bhavatām amunā kiṃ tāraṇaṃ citram?
  tān api kṛtrimahārdān sarvān nistārayed eṣaḥ ||JGc_1,6.44|| [āryā]
children.translated_text: 'In [the signs of] Taurus, Virgo, Libra, and Pisces, the planets are clearly exalted; Moon, Mercury, Saturn, and the son of Earth (Mars) are situated in his birth [chart]. // Since [his] birth, O child, was in the year called Viśvāvasu, all wealth, O glorious one, shall be his when he is pleased. // By birth under the star Rohiṇī, he is the lord of [those] accompanied by Rohiṇī — ten thousand [in number]; and the ascendant was Taurus there, hence he is the ruler of ten million cows! // And his future will be always extensive; in the future, even sages shall extend their minds toward him. // This one shall proclaim scriptures and weapons too, by his own radiance; a remover of the undesirable for enemies, and [a joy] for friends, O lord of Vraja! // That auspiciousness shall come to you from him — this is a needless tale! That auspiciousness belongs to your devotees, and to existence itself, and to existence! // His wondrous conduct carries the intense curiosity of many! Tormenting even the gods' demons (asuras), he becomes the protector even of the city of the gods! // For you of innate love, what wonder is deliverance by him? He would deliver even all those of artificial attachment!'

children.text:
"tasmān nandātmajas te yad api hari-samaḥ sarva-sādguṇya-vṛttyā
  sarvatremaṃ tathāpi sva-mahima-vibhava-khyātibhiḥ pālaya tvam |
  vaśyaṃ kurvan sva-devaṃ harim amum api taṃ svāṅgajaṃ nirmimīṣe
  tad vīra tvāṃ vinā na svayam ayam ayate svairatāṃ svāvanāya ||JGc_1,6.45|| [śārdulavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, though your son born of Nanda is equal to Hari in the conduct of all excellent virtues, nevertheless protect him everywhere with the fame of his own majestic glory. Making your own deity, Hari, subject — you have fashioned him as your own son! Therefore, O hero, without you, he himself does not go freely for his own protection!'

children.text: "tad evaṃ bhavadbhiḥ sva-devena tulya-guṇiny asmiṃs tan-nāmāny eva kāmaṃ gaṇanīyānīti saṅkṣepeṇārtha-nikṣepaḥ |"
children.translated_text: 'Thus, in brief, the deposit of meaning is this: the very names of your deity, who is equal in virtues to this one, are to be reverently counted.'

children.text: tad evam ākarṇya joṣaṃ juṣamāṇe tu vraja-rāje, muniḥ punar uvāca-"vraja-rāja, bhavad-icchayā vayam evāgamya cāgamya cānayor dvijāti-saṃskārān kariṣyāmaḥ, kintu karṇa-vedha-cuḍā-karaṇe na sambhavataḥ | paśya cābhyarṇataḥ sukṣmatayā karṇa-cchidram asti, keśa-lavasyāpi lavaḥ sphuṭaṃ na sambhavatīti, tataś cānna-prāśana-mātraṃ bhavadbhir ācaryam | sāvitra-samāvartana-vivāha-vṛttaṃ tu na svayam udyama-pātraṃ kāryaṃ, kintu samaya-jñair asamaya-jñair asmābhir eva" iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the king of Vraja was silently savoring this, the sage spoke again: 'O king of Vraja! By your wish, we ourselves shall come and come again to perform the twice-born sacraments for both of these. However, the ear-piercing and the tonsure ceremony are not possible. Look — from nearby, with subtlety, there is a hole in the ear, and not even a trace of a hair-strand is clearly possible! Therefore, only the first-feeding ceremony is to be performed by you. But the Sāvitrī (sacred-thread), graduation, and marriage ceremonies are not to be made the object of effort by yourselves, but only by us, knowers of the proper and improper times.'

children.text:
tataś ca kṣaṇaṃ munitām eva vyavasyan munis tau paśyan vaśya-manā babhūva | tataś ca,
  yadyapi pitroḥ snehānvaya-maya-bālyaika-tānau tau |
  tad api munis taj jñānaṃ śaṅkitavān saṅkucann āsīt ||JGc_1,6.46|| [upagīti]
  saṅkocād iva gopa prabhum anu sa munir vidhāpayann ājñām |
  calito' py alabhata tasmin sthita iva tat-tat-parisphūrtim ||JGc_1,6.47|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
Then, settling into the state of a sage for a moment, the sage, gazing at those two, became one of captivated mind. And then:
Although those two were solely absorbed in the childishness consisting of the flow of parental affection, even so the sage, apprehending that knowledge, remained contracted [with awe]. // Though he departed following the cowherd chief as if from contraction, he obtained — as if standing still within him — the manifestation of this and that [wonder]. //

children.text: calana-samaye tu śrīmān vrajeśaḥ svayam anuvrajya bālakābhyām abhyavādayata | sa ca, "sa-gave saha-putrāya svasti te' stu vrajāmy aham" iti vyaktam uktavān |
children.translated_text: At the time of departure, the glorious lord of Vraja himself followed and had the two boys bow to him. And he clearly said: 'May all be well with you, together with your cows and sons — I depart.'

children.text:
tataś cātmano mahatā suprajastvena vraja-rājaḥ svāntar evam ātmānam āmantrya vadan nananda,
  "putro labdhaḥ sucirād iṣṭaḥ sa mahadbhir evam ādiṣṭaḥ |
  asmāt pūrṇānandān manuṣva nanu nanda-pūrṇo' smi ||JGc_1,6.48|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
Then the king of Vraja, through his own great state of excellent progeny, thus addressed himself within and spoke joyfully:
'A son, long desired, has been obtained, and thus instructed by the great ones! From this, be filled with complete bliss — am I not indeed Nanda-the-complete?' //

children.text: atha munaye sa dākṣiṇyāya sa-dakṣiṇānāṃ gavām ayutaṃ prayutaṃ ca gopair indragopa-varṇānāṃ svarṇānāṃ parokṣaṃ vihāpayāmāsa, "yathecchaṃ svīya-parakīya-yajña-yogyaṃ kriyatām idam" iti |
children.translated_text: Then, as a courtesy to the sage, he had the cowherds send ten thousand and also ten million cows with gifts, and gold coins of the color of Indragopa (crimson), secretly: 'Let this be used as fitting for one's own and others' sacrificial purposes.'

children.text: atha nija-dvija-svajana-vargān āhūya ca bhūyaḥ prakaṭam eva viśaṅkaṭa-tat-tan-nāma-karaṇa-parvaṇā sarvān ānanditavān iti |
children.translated_text: Then, having summoned the clans of his own brāhmaṇas and kinsmen, he delighted all with the openly celebrated festival of naming, with its grand and manifold designation-ceremonies.

children.text:
tad evam avadhārayan madhukaṇṭhaḥ saha-vismaya-gadgada-kaṇṭham āha sma,
  nāmnā prasiddhim anyasya prasādhayati nāma-kṛt |
  aho kṛṣṇasya tat-kartā gargas tena prasidhyati ||JGc_1,6.49|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Thus contemplating, Madhukaṇṭha spoke with throat choked by wonder:
'The name-giver establishes the fame of another through the name; ah, but the maker of Kṛṣṇa's [name] — Garga — by that [act] himself becomes famous!' //

children.text: atha madhukaṇṭhaś cintayāmāsa, "tasmān nandātmajas te yad api hari-samaḥ" iti yad uktam, tat tu yuktam eva, nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ [BhP 10.8.19] iti hi śrīmad-bhāgavata-sthaṃ tad vākyam apīdṛśaṃ dṛśyate, tat-puruṣa-bahuvrīhibhyāṃ śliṣṭatvād asyādhikatvaṃ ca lakṣyate iti | [54] prakaṭaṃ covāca-nanu nāma-karaṇaṃ viśiṣya na proktam anna-prāśanaṃ tu na kiñcid apīti | tac ca tac ca stūyamānatayā prastūyatām |
children.translated_text: Then Madhukaṇṭha reflected: 'The statement "though your son born of Nanda is equal to Hari" is indeed appropriate, for the phrase "equal to Nārāyaṇa in qualities" [BhP 10.8.19] is found in the glorious Bhāgavata itself, and by the ambiguity of the tatpuruṣa and bahuvrīhi compounds, his superiority is also indicated.' [54] And he said openly: 'Indeed, the naming ceremony was not described in detail, nor the first-feeding ceremony at all! Let both be praised and introduced, as they are objects of celebration.'

children.text:
snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sahāsam āha sma,
  tan nāma-karaṇaṃ cānna-prāśanaṃ ca vraje mahaḥ |
  yātam asman-mano-rājyaṃ na pṛthak stotum īśmahe ||JGc_1,6.50|| iti | [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Snigdhakaṇṭha said with a laugh:
'That naming ceremony and that first-feeding ceremony of Vraja were great celebrations that have gone to the kingdom of our minds — we are unable to praise them separately!' //

children.text: tad idaṃ procya punaḥ sānandam uvāca-tataḥ śrūyatām uttara-vṛttāntaḥ:
children.translated_text: Having said this, he again spoke joyfully: 'Then hear the subsequent events:'

children.text:
yadavadhi gargaḥ prayayau vraja-sadanān nāma nirmāya |
  kramatas tadavadhi pṛthukāv abhimānyete sma tena svaiḥ ||JGc_1,6.51|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text: 'From the time Garga departed from the houses of Vraja, having created the names, from that time onward, those two little ones were gradually cherished with those [names] by their own people.' //

children.text:
yathā-
  utkarṇatā-niśamanaṃ nayanābhimukhyaṃ
  sva-bhrātṛ-nāmni ca nijāhvaya-bhāṇa-rītiḥ |
  tat-tad-viviktim abhi jhaṅkṛti-mādhurī ca
  svān atra kṛṣṇa-balayor balavat pupoṣa ||JGc_1,6.52|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
As follows:
The attentiveness of listening, the facing of the eyes, and the practice of uttering one's own name at the call of the other brother's name — the sweetness of the babbling-response toward each distinction — all this powerfully nourished their own [people] here, in the case of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma! //

children.text:
udīkṣya madhuraṃ mukhaṃ sukha-cariṣṇu kṛṣṇākhyayā
  tadā janaka-diṣṭayā tanayam iṣṭam āhūya tam |
  tadīya-kala-huṅkṛtīr api niśamya ramyākṛtīḥ
  prasūr amṛta-bhṛt-prabhā jagati śarma sā nirmame ||JGc_1,6.53|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text: Gazing at his sweet face, delightfully active, calling by the name 'Kṛṣṇa' — by the father's designation — that beloved son, and hearing even his tender humming sounds, of charming forms — the mother, like the radiance of the nectar-bearer (moon), created happiness in the world! //

children.text:
athāvrajad drutam iva riṅga-raṅgatāṃ
  tayor vrajeśvara-sadanāṅgana-kṣitiḥ |
  sametya tau caraṇa-carārbhakā muhur
  vilebhire sukham abhilebhire tataḥ ||JGc_1,6.54|| [rucirā]
