children.translated_text: Then the ground of the courtyard of the lord of Vraja's mansion attained the state of crawling-play, as it were, swiftly! When those two, toddlers moving on all fours, met, they repeatedly obtained delight and then attained happiness! //

children.text:
atra gāyanti cādyāpi:
  "riṅgana-keli-kule jananī-sukha-kārī | vraja-dṛśi sukṛta-sphurad-avatārī |
  valayita-bālya-vilāsa jaya bala-valita hare! ||dhru||
children.translated_text:
And here they sing even today:
'In the family of crawling-play, the giver of maternal happiness! In the sight of Vraja, the incarnation whose merit shines forth! O you of dancing childhood sports, victory! O Hari, entwined with Bala's strength!' //refrain//

children.text: kiṅkiṇi-gaṇa-raṇane hṛdaye ruci-dhārī | pada-yuga-cālana-kutuka-vihārī ||
children.translated_text: 'In the jingling of hosts of little bells, bearing delight in the heart! Sporting with the curiosity of moving both feet!' //

children.text: gorasa-kīrṇi-bhave paṅke laghu-cārī | vāraṇa-kāraṇa-vāg aticārī ||
children.translated_text: 'Moving lightly in the mud made of spilled milk-products! Transgressing speech that reasons about elephants (prohibition)!' //

children.text: akalita-jana-milane tasmād apasārī | jananīṃ prati gati-cāpala-bhārī ||
children.translated_text: 'Running away from meetings with unfamiliar people! Burdened with the haste of his gait toward mother!' //

children.text: jananī-stana-vasane bhaya-bhāg-anuhārī | tatra payo-rasa-visarāhārī ||
children.translated_text: 'Imitating the share of fear in the garment-fold of mother's breast! There, carrying away the taste of the milk-essence!' //

children.text: vapuṣi mṛdā maline mṛdutām apahārī | jananī-kara-kṛta-mṛjayā hārī ||
children.translated_text: 'Taking away the softness of the body soiled by soft earth! Charming through the washing done by mother's hand!' //

children.text:
api tandrāvalane stanapām anukārī | jananī-smita-patad-amṛtāsārī ||JGc_1,6.55|| iti
 [mātrāsamaka]
tataś ca,
  varṣa-pañcakam anu skhaled vayas
  tat tu tat trayam anu dvayos tayoḥ |
  kintu na skhalati tat-kiśoratā
  yā gatāgami-daśā-tiraskarī ||JGc_1,6.56|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
'Even in the embrace of drowsiness, imitating the drinking of breast-milk! Streaming the nectar-shower of mother's smile!' //
And then:
The stumbling age of about five years, but for those two, that of about three — yet their adolescence, which conceals the states of coming and going, does not stumble! //

children.text: yathānantaram āha-
children.translated_text: As is said afterwards:

children.text: kālenālpena rājarṣe rāmaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca gokule |
aghṛṣṭa-jānubhiḥ padbhir vicakramatur ojasā ||[BhP 10.8.26] iti |
children.translated_text: walked about with power on feet whose knees did not touch the ground!' // [BhP 10.8.26]
'In a short time, O royal sage, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, in Gokula,

children.text:
yathā ca śambara-gṛhāt prathama-vayasaḥ pradyumnasyāgamana-samaye prāha-kṛṣṇaṃ matvā striyo hrītā nililyustatra tatra ha [BhP 10.55.28] iti | tatra ca-
  na navyād yauvanād anyāvasthā tasyeti yan matam |
  varjayaty aṅga-vṛddhiṃ tan, na mādhurya-samarjanam ||JGc_1,6.57|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And as was said at the time of Pradyumna's arrival from the house of Śambara in his first youth: 'The women, mistaking him for Kṛṣṇa, bashfully hid here and there' [BhP 10.55.28]. And there:
'That no other state than perpetual youth is his — this is the view; it excludes the growth of limbs, but not the accumulation of sweetness!' //

children.text:
yataḥ priyajanabhāvabhāvita eva tasyāvirbhāva ity avādi sma | tatra tadbhāvo yathā:
  utkaṇṭhā vaṣṭi tṛptiṃ sthavayitum abhitaḥ sā tu śaśvat kṛśantī
  tām evoccair bakāreḥ sthavayati jhaṭiti prema-bhājāṃ janānām |
  yadyapy evaṃ tathāpi prathamaja-vayasas tūrdhvagāṃ tat-tad-īhāṃ
  noṣṭas te suṣṭhu kintu prasṛmara-madhurimṇy eva tāṃ nirmimāte ||JGc_1,6.58|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
For it was stated that his manifestation is cultivated by the sentiments of his beloved people. There, that sentiment is as follows:
Longing desires to make satisfaction permanent on all sides, but that [satisfaction] is ever diminishing; the enemy of Baka (Kṛṣṇa) swiftly makes it permanent and expansive for people who possess love. Yet even so, those desires — the upward-striving activities of each [age] beginning from the first — he does not stay with them properly, but fashions them only in the ever-flowing sweetness! //

children.text: atha kālenālpena ity ādau līlāyāḥ sādhu-rīti-madhuratāsvādyatām | [62] tatra gati-śikṣā yathā-
children.translated_text: Now, in 'in a short time' and so forth, let the sweetness of the excellent style of the pastimes be savored! [62] There, the teaching of walking, as follows:

children.text:
hasta-tyāga-maye navye saṃstavye gati-śikṣaṇe |
  putre skhalati sā jīyān mātuḥ putrasya ca tvarā ||JGc_1,6.59|| [anuṣṭubh]
  dvitra-kramaṃ gataḥ kṛṣṇaś calitaḥ skhalane rudan |
  putra putreti cumbantīm ambām ālolayan muhuḥ ||JGc_1,6.60|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kiñcid dūraṃ yad ānañca svaka-tejaḥ-prapañcakaḥ |
  sthirībhūya prasū-vaktraṃ sa-smitaṃ sa vyalokata ||JGc_1,6.61|| [anuṣṭubh]
  dūraṃ mātur yadā yāti tadāsau mantharāyate |
  samīpaṃ tu yadā tarhi smayamāno drutāyate ||JGc_1,6.62|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'In the novel walking-lesson of hand-release, when the son stumbled — victorious was the haste of the mother toward the son and of the son [toward her]! // Having gone two or three steps, Kṛṣṇa wobbled; stumbling, crying — and his mother, kissing him, saying "Son! Son!" — he rocked her again and again! // When he advanced somewhat far, that displayer of his own radiance, becoming steady, looked at his mother's face with a smile! // When he goes far from mother, then he becomes slow; but when near, then he speeds up, smiling!' //

children.text:
gīḥ-śikṣā yathā-
prathamam agrajasya tuṇḍa-puṇḍarīke |
kṣarad-akṣara-madhu-madhure jāte ||JGc_1,6.63|| [*3]
[*3] This is not in any recognizable metre. Probably editor's mistake.
children.translated_text:
The teaching of speech, as follows:
First, upon the lotus of the elder brother's mouth, when the honey-sweet flow of syllables arose —

children.text: tad-anujātam api dhātryā lāpayāmāsa | yatra ca-
children.translated_text: Following that [example], the nurse also had him prattle. And there:

children.text:
"mā mā tā tā" iti vacaḥ paṭhan nanda-tanūjanuḥ |
  ānandārtham abhūt pitror vrajasya nikhilasya ca ||JGc_1,6.64|| [anuṣṭubh]
  ardhoditānāṃ dantānām akṣarāṇāṃ tathā tatiḥ |
  citrīyāmāsa kṛṣṇasya yatrācitrīyata prasūḥ ||JGc_1,6.65|| [anuṣṭubh]
  "īśīthāḥ kiṃ jagatyām?" "om" "bandhūn pāsyasi naḥ kim?" "om"
  ity ādi mātṛ-sutayoḥ saṃvādavad abhūd iha ||JGc_1,6.66|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Reciting the words "mā mā tā tā" (mama, papa), the younger son of Nanda became the cause of joy for his parents and for the whole of Vraja! // The array of half-uttered teeth and syllables of Kṛṣṇa was wondrous — where his mother was [herself] amazed! // "Will you be lord of the world?" "Om." "Will you nourish our kinsmen?" "Om." — Thus between mother and son, there was as if a dialogue!' //

children.text:
ajñāta-vācaṃ śukavat paṭhantaṃ
  viśeṣa-pṛcchā-kṛti-tarjanīkam |
  dhātrī-janādhyāpita-vāk-pracāraṃ
  vrajasya bhāgyaṃ paritaḥ smarāmi ||JGc_1,6.67|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text: 'Reciting speech unknowingly, like a parrot, with a pointing forefinger in the manner of special inquiry, the child, whose practice of speech was taught by the nurse-folk — I remember on all sides as the fortune of Vraja!' //

children.text:
nāma-grāhaṃ tadā prāha rāmaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ |
  kṛṣṇo rāmam athāryeti mātṝṇāṃ pariśikṣayā ||JGc_1,6.68|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Then Rāma slowly, slowly called Kṛṣṇa by name; and Kṛṣṇa called Rāma "Ārya" (elder brother) — by the teaching of their mothers.' //

children.text:
tadā ca-
  pṛcchantyā vṛddhayāṅgāni yadā kim api pṛcchyate |
  tadāmbā-śikṣayā bālaḥ sa tāṃ muhur atāḍayat ||JGc_1,6.69|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'And then: When an old woman, touching his limbs, asked him something, then the child, by his mother's teaching, struck her repeatedly!' //

children.text: atha bhrātṛ-dvayam api mithaḥ kiñcid vadati sma, yathā-
children.translated_text: And the two brothers also said something to each other, as follows:

children.text:
"āgaccha khelāṃ gacchāva |" "mātā kopaṃ kariṣyati" |
  "na kuryād," iti tau bālau kṛṣṇa-rāmau samūcatuḥ ||JGc_1,6.70|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: '"Come, let us go to play!" "Mother will be angry." "She won't!" — thus the two boys, Kṛṣṇa and Rāma, said to each other!' //

children.text:
atha bālyacāpalyaṃ cāvakalyatām:
  daṃṣṭrāṃ dhitsati daṃṣṭriṇaḥ phaṇi-pater udyat-phaṇāṃ śṛṅgiṇaḥ
  śṛṅgaṃ prajvalad-arciṣaṃ huta-bhujaḥ koṭiṃ ca khaḍgādinaḥ |
  itthaṃ bhrātṛ-yugaṃ nivartitam api prāgalbhyam evāsadan
  mātros tena samasta-vismṛtir abhūd gehe' pi dehe' pi ca ||JGc_1,6.71|| [śārdula]
children.translated_text:
Now the restlessness of childhood and its immaturity:
He desires the fang of the fanged one, the raised hood of the serpent-lord, the horn
of the horned one, the blazing flame-tip of the fire-god, and the edge of a sword and such;
thus, though the pair of brothers was turned away, they attained only boldness —
and by that, the two mothers forgot everything, both home and body. // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
"dūram añca na hi cañcala sphuṭaṃ
  tatra ko' pi varivarti bhīṣaṇaḥ |"
  evam eṣa jananī-girā punas
  tat-kṛte kutukitāṃ dadhe śiśuḥ ||JGc_1,6.72|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
'Do not go far, O restless one! Clearly,
someone terrifying lurks there!'
Thus, hearing his mother's words, this child
only developed more curiosity on that account! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
śiśunā bhīṣma-grahaṇe sthāne mātur bhayaṃ yato mātā |
  kavayas tv idam anumimate tejasvitvasya bījaṃ tat ||JGc_1,6.73|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
In the child's seizing of fearsome things, the fear is properly the mother's;
but poets infer this: that is the very seed of his heroic splendor. // [āryā]

children.text:
yaṃ yaṃ padārtham atitīvram iyaṃ prayāti
  bhrātṛ-dvayī, sa ca sa ca pratibhāti saumyaḥ |
  atrānumāna-vidurā niranaiṣur etad
  yugmaṃ bhaviṣyati sadā kali-nāśanāya ||JGc_1,6.74|| [vasantatilaka]
children.translated_text:
Whatever object this pair of brothers approaches most intensely,
that very thing appears gentle and benign;
those far-sighted in inference concluded:
'This pair shall forever be for the destruction of Kali!' // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
atha krameṇa mātṛ-vañcanī buddhir apy udbuddhā | yatra yatra sa ca sa ca,
  "naiva naiva cala cañcala re re,"
  vākyam etad avakarṇya jananyāḥ |
  māyayā sma parivṛtya hasitvā
  tāṃ nivartya laṣite varivarti ||JGc_1,6.75|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
Then, gradually, the intelligence for deceiving the mothers was also awakened. Wherever he and his brother were:
'No, no! Don't go, O restless one, hey, hey!' —
hearing this speech of the mother,
by a trick, having circled round and laughed,
having turned her back, he would roam wherever he desired. // [svāgatā]

children.text: alpa-hīna-hāyana-vayastve tu jāte yatra kutracit krīḍanāya nirgacchantau na sambhālayituṃ śakyete | sambhālitau ca tau kuto līyeta iti nāvadhārayituṃ pāryete | [69] atha jananī-dvayam ubhayato vartmāvṛtya paritaś ca dhātrīr avadhāna-vidhātrīr vitatya dravantau tatra-bhavantau gṛhṇāti | [70] tato rudantau hasantau ca tau gṛhāntarānītāv udvartanādinā veṣa-parivartanādinā ca stana-pāyanādinā śāyanādinā ca rocayati |
children.translated_text: But when they had reached the age just short of a year, wherever they went out to play, they could not be watched over. And even when watched, it was impossible to determine where they might hide. [69] Then the two mothers, blocking the paths from both sides and spreading nurses as attentive guardians all around, would catch the two as they ran about. [70] Then, brought inside the house, crying and laughing, she would please them with massage and the like, with changing of clothes and the like, with nursing and the like, and with putting them to sleep and the like.

children.text: tad evaṃ varṇanam ākarṇayatsu sabhāsatsu prahasatsu śrīmad-vraja-purandara-kula-dhurandhara-kiśora-vare cānavarajena saha dara-smita-sundaratara-vadanatayā netrādaraṇīye sati samāpanāya punar uvāca snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, as the assembly-members listened to this description and laughed, while the foremost young prince of the illustrious family of the lord of Vraja was worthy of the eyes' reverence through the more-than-beautiful face bearing a slight smile alongside the unsurpassed one (Balarāma), Snigdhakaṇṭha again spoke to bring it to a conclusion:

children.text:
īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava gopādhināyaka |
  bālyāvalita-cāpalyād api yo muni-mohanaḥ ||JGc_1,6.76|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Such a son has been born to you, O chief of the cowherds,
who, even through the restlessness adorned with childhood, enchants the sages! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha kṛta-sukha-prathāyāṃ kathāyāṃ vṛttāyām, anya-dinavat kathakān sa prasādhanaṃ sedhayāmāsa śubha-caritrī-vraja-dharitrīśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, when the tale that had spread happiness was concluded, the lord of earth of Vraja of auspicious deeds, as on other days, dismissed the narrators with gifts of adornment.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
viśaṅkaṭa-śakaṭa-vighaṭṭanādi-vicitra-bālya-caritraṃ nāma
ṣaṣṭaṃ pūraṇam
 ||6||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the Śrī Śrī Gopālacampū,
the Sixth Chapter, named 'The Marvelous Childhood Deeds including the Shattering of the Cart (<s>Śakaṭa</s>) and other [exploits].'
||6||

children.text: atha saptamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Seventh Chapter.

children.text: bālya-līlā-caurya-śauryaṃ
children.translated_text: The Valor and Thievery of Childhood Pastimes.

children.text: atha dināntaravat prabhātāntaḥ prabhātāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ madhukaṇṭha uvāca-snigdhakaṇṭha, līlāntareṇa nidigdha-citto bhava |
children.translated_text: Then, as on other days, when the assembly had dawned in the morning's dawn, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'O <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, let your mind be steeped in yet another pastime!'

children.text: atha varṣa-jāte jāte nabhasye māsi sarva-sampan-mayaṃ janma-dinam āyātam | tatra ca gargopadeśa-vargopāśrayā kṛṣṇasya janma-tithi-pūjā pūryate sma | yatra ca vraja-kṣiti-patinā praśasta-vācanādi-pūrvakāpūrva-parva pravartayāmāsa | yathā-
children.translated_text:
Now, as each year arrived, in the month of <s>Nabhasya</s> (<s>Bhādrapada</s>), the birthday, full of all prosperity, came. And there, following the instructions of <s>Garga</s> and relying on the cowherd community, the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> birthday <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) was performed in full. And there, the king of <s>Vraja</s> inaugurated the unprecedented festival with auspicious recitations and the like as preliminaries. As follows:
With <s>Vedas</s>, music, songs, the art of dance, consecrations preceded by <s>mantras</s>,
with affectionate giving and receiving, with melodious joyful sounds, with the learned performance of sacrifices,
with six types of sesame offerings and the like, with auspicious anointings of clay, aloe, unguents, and grains and the like,
with the release of fish and others — the birthday festival of the son of the cowherd-king was celebrated! // [sragdharā]
But:
Gradually, the growth of years of <s>Nanda's</s> son's birth
and likewise of his birthday festival was evident — since both were designated the same! // [anuṣṭubh]
The food that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> ate was called '<s>Kṛṣṇa-bhojana</s>'; the garment that covered <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was called '<s>Kṛṣṇa-ācchādana</s>' —
by those very names, the practice [of naming things after him] spread in <s>Vraja</s> from that time. // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
vedair vādyaiḥ pragītair naṭana-paṭimabhiḥ mantra-pūrvābhiṣekaiḥ
  sa-prītyādāna-dānaiḥ pramada-kala-kalair yajña-vijña-prayogaiḥ |
  ṣaṭ-tilyādi-prakārair mṛd-aguru-rasa-dhānyādi-bhavyābhimarśair
  matsyādīnāṃ pramokair ajani jani-tithir gopa-rājāṅgajasya ||JGc_1,7.1|| [sragdharā]
kintu,
  krameṇa vṛddhir varṣāṇāṃ yathā nandātma-janmanaḥ |
  tathā tat-parvaṇo' py āsīt sphuṭaṃ yad-abhidā dvayoḥ ||JGc_1,7.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kṛṣṇa-bhojanam annaṃ yat kṛṣṇācchādanam aṃśukam |
  tat-tan-nāmnā pracāro' bhūt tasya tasya vraje tataḥ ||JGc_1,7.3|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
[3] Thus, as the years were counted with joy, once, when the elder women and men were occupied with their respective tasks, the infant <s>Gopāla</s> (Kṛṣṇa) was being fondled by his mother on her own lap on the veranda of his palace. As follows:
She pressed face to face and kissed it, she told him fanciful tales difficult to comprehend,
she laughed and then he laughed — and there with the child,
the queen of <s>Vraja</s> attained a state drenched with a hundred happinesses! // [rucirā]

children.text:
tad evaṃ harṣeṇa varṣe gaṇite, kadācid varṣiyaḥ-prabhṛtiṣu strī-puṃseṣu tat-tat-kṛti-vyāpṛteṣu nijotsaṅgena bāla-gopālaḥ sva-mandirālinde jananyā lālyate sma, yathā--
  mukhe mukhaṃ lagayati cumbati sma tad
  vṛthā kathāḥ kathayati tena durgamāḥ |
  hasaty atho hasati ca tatra bālake
  vrajeśvarī sukha-śata-siktatām agāt ||JGc_1,7.4|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: Then, the demon <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, sent by <s>Kaṃsa</s> — whose intellect was shattered by the fear born of previous slayings, who was devoid of fortitude — an enemy of the good, standing far away on the celestial path, saw him thus situated and reflected: 'This very one of cloud-complexion, this little child, is on the wide veranda of a great house, I suspect, resting in the lap of his mother.'

children.text: tataś ca pūrva-pūrva-nihiṃsanāt prajāta-mati-bhraṃśena dhairya-rahitatayā kaṃsena prahitaḥ sumanasām ahitaḥ sura-vartmani dūrataḥ sthitas tṛṇāvartas taṃ tathā vartamānaṃ dadarśa vimamarśa ca | so' yam eva toyada-varṇaḥ pṛthukaḥ pṛthu-gṛhālindaṃ vindamānāyā mātur aṅke vartata iti śaṅke |
children.translated_text: 'So now, shaking everything, I shall carry the child along with his guard upon the celestial path! But <s>Pūtanā</s> with her contrivance of a new body, and <s>Śakaṭa</s> with his device of entering the cart in formless form — even they, who wished to deceive, met their destined end by him. Therefore, I shall enter in my own wind-form!' — thus he thought.

children.text: tad evam adhunā sarvaṃ dhunānaḥ sāmbālam eva bālaṃ sura-vartmani vartayāṇi | kintu pūtanā nūtana-tanu-kalanayā, śakaṭaś ca śakaṭāviṣṭāmūrtatā-valanayā chalayitum iṣṭenāpy anena diṣṭāntam āpyate sma | tasmād ahaṃ tad-ubhayetara-vāta-rūpeṇa praviśāmi iti |
children.translated_text: And then <s>Yogamāyā</s>, always following the occasion for that [pastime], having arrived at the arrangement of that embodiment, manifested her own power for the sake of separating him from his mother. By which, his mother — unable to bear the weight even of that one whose body was like a tender blue lotus, and amazed — unable to bear his burden by any other means, suddenly placed him upon the very ground; and she meditated upon the Inner Controller, the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) of the worlds. Extremely frightened, she became agitated in mind, both for warding off that calamity and for propitiating him.

children.text: tadā ca sadā tad-avasaram anusarantī tu yoga-māyā tad-vapur-yogam āyātā, mātuḥ pṛthag-bhāvāya sva-vaibhavam āvirbhāvayāmāsa | yena ca tad-ambā komala-nīla-kamalāyamāna-kalevarasyāpi tasya bhāram asahamānā vismayamānā cānyasya tad-bhārāsahatayā sahasā bhūmāv eva taṃ dhṛtavatī, dhyātavatī ca jagatām antaryāmi-puruṣam | atibhītā ca tad-upadrava-bādhanāya tad-ārādhanāya vyagra-cittā babhūva |

tṛṇāvartas tu vātāvartena vartamānaḥ sura-vartmani taṃ ca vartayan gala-graha-pāśam iva sañjagrāha | goṣṭham api kaṣṭada-karkarādi-vṛṣṭibhir naṣṭa-prāyatayā ghaṭṭayāmāsa | yatra ca trasam atrasam api sarvaṃ vitrastam asti sma | tataś ca,
  tamobhir āvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ bahir eva na kevalam |
  janānām antaraṃ cāsīt tṛṇāvarta-pravartane ||JGc_1,7.5|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Then, when that wicked one was thus causing destruction of the not-insignificant born ones in this combat of the unborn, the terrified people cried out, as follows:

The wind, with speed that causes wounds from flying skull-fragments, with sounds that threaten and roar in the ears and eyes,
in those who are shattered and writhing, with loud cracking noises, halving their life-span —
splitting the settlement and the storehouses, it dances! Alas! Ah! Alas! What has happened there,
where that child lies, his cherished body comparable to a blue lotus petal? // [sragdharā]

children.text: tena tu durjanena tadaivam anyūnānāṃ janyūnām ajanye janyamāne tatra vitrastāḥ prajāḥ prajajalpuḥ, yathā-

utsarpat-karparāṃśa-vraṇa-janaka-javaḥ śrotra-dṛk-tarja-garja-
  dhvānas truṭy-utkuṭheṣu prakaṭa-kaṭa-kaṭeṣv ardhayan vāyur āyuḥ |
  goṣṭhaṃ koṣṭhaṃ ca bhindann naṭati bata hahā hanta kiṃ tatra vṛttaṃ
  yatrāste nīla-paṅkeruha-dala-tulanā lālitāṅgaḥ sa bālaḥ ||JGc_1,7.6|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: In the mansion of the glorious lord <s>Nanda</s>, however:

children.text: śrīman-nanda-deva-mandire tu-
children.translated_text:
In this calamity, the queen of <s>Vraja</s> did not see her son
whom she had placed there;
she, though more tender than a cow, then
by the loss of discernment, attained a likeness to a cow! //
In that flood of destructive wind, when the queen of the cowherds
did not see her son's existence,
alas, what agitation she attained —
if somewhere, someone imagines a mere cow bereft of her calf,
aware of the language of the world — she might imagine that! //

children.text:
upadrave' sminn adhi yad dadhe sutaṃ
  taṃ tatra nāpaśyad asau vrajeśvarī |
  gavādhika-snigdhatarāpi yā tadā
  vicāra-lopād valate sma go-tulām ||JGc_1,7.7|| [upajāti 11]
  upaplava-marut-plave' bhajati tatra putrāstitām
  avīkṣya paśupeśvarī bata jagāma yāṃ vyagratām |
  hahā vigata-tarṇakā budhita-loka-bhāṣādikā
  yadi sphurati naicikī kvacana kācid ūhate tām ||JGc_1,7.8|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text: [9] And then, from her onward, by the continuous chain of people's weeping spreading on all sides, by the intense wailing, the entire <s>Gokula</s> became agitated. [10] And disregarding such an unprecedented calamity, all came running and running, and in the shoreless ocean of unbearable suffering, all drowned. And there:
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was taken by <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, his mother's body became a burden [to herself]

children.text: tadā ca tām ārabhya jana-rodana-paramparayā paritaḥ prasarpaṇād amandena tad-ākrandena sarva-gokulam ākulaṃ babhūva | [10] avigaṇayya ca tādṛśaṃ visadṛśam upadravaṃ sadravam evāgamyāgamyāpāra-duḥkha-vāra-vārāṃ nidhau sarve mamajjuḥ | tatra ca-
children.translated_text:
;
this was so for his people too — and for both [groups], there was a rupture [of composure]. // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tṛṇāvarta-hṛte kṛṣṇe mātur bhārāyitā tanuḥ |
  tadīyānāṃ yathā sāsīd ubhayeṣāṃ yathā truṭiḥ ||JGc_1,7.9|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: [11] Then, while all the women were uniformly entering a state of subjection to weeping: 'O <s>Rohiṇī</s>! O treacherous one! What shall I do? How shall I die without seeing him? Or how shall I turn my face toward the king of <s>Vraja</s>?' — and so on, the lamentation of the mother that reached its uttermost limit, following the final extremity — that complete outpouring of wailing — when contemplated, suddenly melts the heart like ghee! How can it be told? 'Enough of this excessive digression!' — thus <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, apprehending the state of being overcome by helplessness, both his own and everyone's, swiftly narrated:

children.text: tataś ca, sarvāsu nirviśeṣaṃ rodana-vaśatāṃ viśantīṣu, hā rohiṇi, drohiṇi, kiṃ kariṣyāmi? kathaṃ tam anavalokya mariṣyāmi? kathaṃ vā vraja-rāja-diśi mukhaṃ vitariṣyāmi iti paryantaṃ paryanta-daśāvasānam anu yaḥ khalv aśeṣa-vilāpanaḥ prasū-vilāpaḥ | sa punar avakalitaḥ sahasā ghṛtam iva vilālayati hṛdayam | kathaṃ kathayitum īśyate? ity alam atiprasaṅgena iti madhukaṇṭhaḥ svasya sarvasya ca vaivaśya-vaśyatām āśaṅkya maṅkṣu saṅkathayāmāsa,
children.translated_text:
For the kinsmen of that well-born son of the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, carried off by the sky, who were deeply immersed in the unbearable ocean of grief — suddenly a favorable shore drew near. For indeed:
By the nature of childhood, the one born after <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)
forcefully seized the throat of that one (<s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>);
then, when he was squeezed exceedingly tight, the demon
considered those two arms to be the nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s> (the god of bonds). //
Like the squeezing of his arms, the weight of the child also increased;
the lowest of demons could neither bear, nor abandon, nor restrain him! //
And then, by that one who was a garland-thief in an unworthy state:
he attained the state of burden-bearer, and went to the state of life-bearer! //
As follows:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> wound his own body around him —
like a snake [mistaking him] for a garland-string, or like a bear [mistaking him] for a mass of hair;
how could the wind-demon shake him off? //
And as follows:
When <s>Tṛṇāvarta's</s> throat was throttled, his breaths were blocked;
and at that very time, the winds outside [also stopped] — were they perhaps the very same? // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
nabhasā hṛtasya sujātasya śrīman-nanda-jātasya tasya bandhūnām avagāḍha-duḥsaha-sāda-sindhūnāṃ sahasānukūlaṃ kūlam āsannam | tathā hi,
  bālya-svabhāvena balānujanmā
  balān nijagrāha galaṃ tadīyam |
  tadātigāḍhaṃ sa ca pīḍitas tau
  mene bhujau pāśi-bhujaṅga-pāśau ||JGc_1,7.10|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text: Then, from the expanse of the sky, upon the courtyard ground spread with a pavement of flagstones, that body fell with an exceedingly great crash that deafened the settlement. And having fallen, even the embodied form appeared with its joints slackened. And then:

children.text:
bhujāpīḍanavat tasya bhāraś ca vavṛdhe śiśoḥ |
  voḍhuṃ tyaktuṃ ca roddhuṃ ca nāśakad dānavādhamaḥ ||JGc_1,7.11|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tadā ca mālya-haratānarhāvasthena cāmunā |
  sa bhāra-hāratāṃ prāptaḥ sva-prāṇa-haratāṃ gataḥ ||JGc_1,7.12|| [anuṣṭubh]
yathā,
  mālya-buddhyāhival loma-paṭala-bhrāntyā tam ṛkṣavat |
  kṛṣṇo' vaveṣṭad ātmāṅgaṃ vātūlaḥ katham ujjhatu? ||JGc_1,7.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
yathā ca,
  tṛṇāvarte ruddha-kaṇṭhe tac-chvāsā ruddhatāṃ gatāḥ |
  tadaiva ca bahir vātās tat kiṃ tasya ta eva te? ||JGc_1,7.14|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'What is this? Ahahaha! From where has it fallen?' —
thus the cowherd men surrounded it, having approached;
they became afraid; but then, seeing a <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon),
and upon it, the child <s>Hari</s>, being sought — // [puṣpitāgrā]

Seeing the demon-son with eyes rolled up,
and then the infant gazing with watchful eyes —
hastily placing a kick upon that one,
these [women]

children.text: athākāśāvakāśāt prastara-kṛtāstaraṇāyām aṅgaṇa-sthalyām ativistīrṇaṃ mahā-ghoṣa-badhirī-kṛta-ghoṣaṃ tad-vapur nipapāta | nipatya ca mūrtiman mūrtikam api ślatha-sandhi-bandhī-bhūtam adṛśyata | tataś ca, tat tu,
children.translated_text: joyfully brought him to his mother! // [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text:
kim idam ahahahā papāta kasmād
  iti parivavrur upetya gopa-rāmāḥ |
  bhayam adhur atha kaṃ nirīkṣya rakṣas
  tad-upari bāla-hariṃ ca mṛgyamāṇam ||JGc_1,7.15|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
[14] Then, by some words like a <s>mantra</s>, they gradually restored consciousness to those [mothers]. As follows:
'Death has died! The one seized by death now lives!
Therefore receive this one, O you who love your son!' —
with these mantra-like words, placing the child-medicine upon her,
they revived those [mothers]! // [upajāti]

children.text:
danu-sutam alam udvivartitākṣaṃ
  śiśum atha vīkṣya nirīkṣamāṇa-netram |
  tad-upari sahasā nidhāya lattām
  amum upajahrur amūr mudā jananyām ||JGc_1,7.16|| [puṣpitāgrā]

atha mantravat kiñcid vacanāt punar amūr amuṣyāś cetanām ācinvate sma, yathā,
  mṛtyur mṛto, mṛtyu-hṛtas tu jīvitas
  tad etam ādatsva tanūja-vatsale |
  ity ukti-mantrānvita-bālakauṣadhaṃ
  vinyasya tāṃ pratyudajījivann amūh ||JGc_1,7.17|| [upajāti 12]

śiśum upasadya yaśodā danuja-hṛtaṃ drāk ciceta līnāpi |
  varṣājalam upalabhya prāṇiti jātir yathendra-gopānām ||JGc_1,7.18|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
Approaching the child, <s>Yaśodā</s>, though herself faint, quickly perceived [him] snatched by the demon;
as the species of <s>Indra's</s> cowherds revives upon obtaining rainwater! ||7.18|| [<s>gīti</s>]

children.text:
athāgaman vraja-pati-saṅgatā janāḥ
  sa-vismayaṃ sa-bhayam adabhra-sambhramam |
  gṛhāntara-vrajana-vicāraṇā'nyadā
  na tarhy abhūd yad abhavad eka-bhāvatā ||JGc_1,7.19|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
Then the people, accompanied by the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, came
with wonder, with fear, with immense agitation;
the deliberation about entering the interior of the house
had never before occurred — for there was single-minded [devotion]! ||7.19|| [<s>rucirā</s>]

children.text:
paśyann api tṛṇāvartam apaśyann iva taṃ janaḥ |
  kṛṣṇam evāgamad draṣṭuṃ tat-premā hy adbhutādijit ||JGc_1,7.20|| [anuṣṭubh]
  spṛṣṭaḥ kampreṇa hastena dṛṣṭaḥ sāsreṇa cakṣuṣā |
  pitrātha mātur utsaṅgād avitrā śiśur ādade ||JGc_1,7.21|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Even while seeing <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, as if not seeing him, the people
came only to see <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — for love conquers even amazement! ||7.20|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
Touched by a trembling hand, beheld by a tearful eye,
the child was then taken by the father from the mother's lap, the protector! ||7.21|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
tataś ca rākṣasa-sparśaja-kṣatajādi-śaṅkayā,
  nirīkṣitāvayava-gaṇo' pi mātṛbhir
  vilokitaḥ sa tu janakena kṛtsnaśaḥ |
  mameti-dhī-pṛthu-mamatāspadaṃ dṛśā
  svayā paraṃ na tu parayā parīkṣyate ||JGc_1,7.22|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
Then, out of apprehension of blood and such [wounds] caused by the demon's touch:
Though his group of limbs had been examined by the mothers,
he was then beheld by the father in his entirety;
the broad seat of possessiveness in the thought 'He is mine' —
is examined by one's own gaze alone, not by another's! ||7.22|| [<s>rucirā</s>]

children.text: atha vyagrehitā vṛṣabhānv-agresarāḥ parama-hitāḥ parasparam aparasparaṃ kathayāñcakruḥ-
children.translated_text: Then the eager ones, led by <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, the supremely well-wishing [elders], narrated to one another, in fragmentary fashion:

children.text:
kvāyaṃ hatas tīvra-balaḥ palāśanaḥ,
  kva tīrṇavān so' yam atīva bālakaḥ |
  kiṃ vā sva-pāpena vihiṃsyate khalaḥ
  sādhuḥ samatvena bhayāt pramucyate ||JGc_1,7.23|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
'Where was that fierce-powered flesh-eater slain,
and where did this exceedingly [tender] boy survive?
Or is it that the wicked one is destroyed by his own sin,
while the virtuous one is freed from fear through equanimity?' ||7.23|| [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: athavāsmākam eva bhāgyam idam iti yogyam | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: 'Or rather, this is indeed our fortune — and that is fitting! For thus:'

children.text:
kiṃ nas tapaḥ pūrtam aśeṣa-sauhṛdam
  dattaṃ tatheṣṭaṃ hari-tuṣṭaye' jani |
  rakṣo-gṛhītaḥ punar eṣa bālakaḥ
  svayaṃ sva-bandhūn sukhayan yad āgataḥ ||JGc_1,7.24|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
'What austerity of ours was fulfilled, what universal friendship
was given, what sacrifice arose for the satisfaction of <s>Hari</s>,
that this boy, seized by a demon, has again
come back himself, gladdening his own kinsmen?' ||7.24|| [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text:
samastārtha-karī viṣṇu-bhaktiḥ sākṣād vrajeśvare |
  dṛśyatāṃ mṛśyatām anyat kiṃ vā bālaka-maṅgalam ||JGc_1,7.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which accomplishes all purposes, is directly [present] in the lord of <s>Vraja</s>;
let it be seen, let it be considered — what other child-blessing [is needed]? ||7.25|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Since:

children.text:
sarvadā kramate yasya buddhiḥ sad-bhaktaye hareḥ |
  sa sadā kramate tasya lakṣmīś ca kramatetarām ||JGc_1,7.26|| [anuṣṭubh] iti |
children.translated_text:
He whose intellect always proceeds toward true devotion to <s>Hari</s> —
for him, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) always proceeds, and proceeds exceedingly! ||7.26|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: devāś ca sa-kautukam imaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇābhiprāyam utprekṣāṃ cakrire |
children.translated_text: And the gods, with curiosity, conjectured this intention of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text:
bālo' haṃ na paricinomy abhadra-bhadraṃ
  yaḥ kroḍe kalayati tad-galaṃ dadhāmi |
  tena tvaṃ yadi maraṇaṃ prayāsi kaḥ svid
  doṣaḥ syān mama tam atha tvam eva jalpa ||JGc_1,7.27|| [praharṣiṇī] iti |
children.translated_text:
'I am a child — I do not distinguish the auspicious from the inauspicious;
whoever holds me on his lap, I grasp his throat!
If by that you go to death — what
fault would be mine? Tell me that yourself!' ||7.27|| [<s>praharṣiṇī</s>]

children.text: tataś ca sarvānarvācīnābhīra-vīrāṇāṃ seyaṃ mantraṇā jātā, goṣṭham idaṃ duṣṭānām adhiṣṭhānaṃ vṛttam, tasmād gṛha eva gopanīyam idaṃ bāla-yugalam iti |
children.translated_text: Then, among all the cowherd heroes of the present [age], this counsel arose: 'This settlement has become a haunt of the wicked; therefore, this pair of boys must be guarded within the house itself.'

children.text: tataḥ śaṅkātiśaya-mayaṃ dina-katipayaṃ nānā-krīḍanakena krīḍayamānā mātṛ-samānā gopikā gopikā babhūvuḥ | yatra ca bāla-bālikā-kula-pālikādayaḥ sadayaṃ samāgamya ramyaṃ tat-keli-kutūhalaṃ kalayanti, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, for several days filled with excessive apprehension, the cowherd women (<s>gopikās</s>), playing [with the children] with various toys, became like mothers themselves, each a guardian. And there, the guardians of the assembly of boys and girls and such, coming together with affection, experienced that delightful play-curiosity, as follows:

children.text:
krīḍanāni vividhāni taṃ sadā
  darśayanti ca mudā hasanti ca |
  khelayanti ca balena tā iti
  svāntare param amū arakṣiṣuḥ ||JGc_1,7.28|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
They show him various toys always,
and laugh with joy,
and play with vigor — thus
within their hearts, they supremely protected these two! ||7.28|| [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then:

children.text:
bālena samam anyo' nyaṃ prābalyaṃ darśayann iva |
  ūrdhvādho-bhāvam āsādya sarvā hāsayati sma saḥ ||JGc_1,7.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
  mātṝṇām agrato bāhū vikṣipan dhāvati sma saḥ |
  darśayann iva tejaḥ svaṃ hasan pāte ruroda ca ||JGc_1,7.30|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Along with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), as if showing his prowess to one another,
attaining states of [going] up and down,
he made everyone laugh! ||7.29|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
Before the mothers, extending his arms, he would run,
as if displaying his own power;
laughing [first], upon falling, he also cried! ||7.30|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
balaṃ vā jñānaṃ vā kiyad abhavad asyeti vimṛśan
  yadā gopī-saṅghaḥ kim api muhur ānetum adiśat |
  tadā śaktiṃ vyañjan kva ca punar aśaktiṃ kva ca śiśuḥ
  sa paśyaṃs tad-vaktraṃ hasati ca puro hāsayati ca ||JGc_1,7.31|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'How much strength or knowledge does this one possess?' — reflecting thus,
when the host of <s>gopīs</s> repeatedly directed [him] to fetch something,
then, revealing power somewhere, and again incapacity elsewhere, the child,
gazing at their faces, both laughed and made [them] laugh! ||7.31|| [<s>śikhariṇī</s>]

children.text:
nāmādeśaṃ yadā mātā diśate nayanādikam |
  kṛṣṇaś ca kurute bāḍhaṃ cakre tasyā na kiṃ tadā? ||JGc_1,7.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
  rudantam indave mantha-gargaryāṃ pratirūpiṇe |
  piṇḍena nāvanītena vṛddhāgardhayatārbhakam ||JGc_1,7.33|| [anuṣṭubh]
  svasya svalpāpahāre' pi cakranda maṇi-hānivat |
  kṛtvānya-maṇi-hāniṃ ca prāhasīd bāla-kṛṣṇakaḥ ||JGc_1,7.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
When the mother gave the instruction of a name, [pointing to] the eye and such,
and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> performed it eagerly — did he not then conquer her? ||7.32|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
When he cried for the moon, [seeing] its reflection in the churning pot,
the elderly women pacified the infant with a lump of fresh butter! ||7.33|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
Even at the slightest theft from himself, he would cry as if a jewel were lost;
but having caused the loss of another's jewel, baby <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> would laugh! ||7.34|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
nirmañchanaṃ tava bhajāma kuleśalālya
  bālyātimohana balānuja nṛtya nṛtya |
  ity aṅganābhir uditas thi thi thitthi thīti
  kptena tāla-valayena harir nanarta ||JGc_1,7.35|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
'We shall churn for you, O darling of the clan!
O younger brother of <s>Bala</s>, enchanter beyond childhood, dance, dance!'
Thus urged by the women with 'thi thi thitthi thī' —
with the beat of clapping bangles, <s>Hari</s> danced! ||7.35|| [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text:
māṃ nartayata bho vṛddhāḥ, iti tāsāṃ puro gataḥ |
  bhadraṃ nṛtyasi bhadras tvam, iti stotrān nanarta saḥ ||JGc_1,7.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
  vihasantīṣu sarvāsu sauṣṭhavāt pracyavād api |
  nṛtyan vrīḍitavat kṛṣṇo mātur aṅke' palāyata ||JGc_1,7.37|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Make me dance, O elderly ladies!' — thus, going before them,
'You dance well, blessed one!' — praised thus, he danced! ||7.36|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
While all were laughing, even from stumbling in his gracefulness,
dancing, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as if embarrassed, fled to his mother's lap! ||7.37|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ viramya ca ramyānanaḥ stana-dhayanam api tatrārabdhavān, yad darśanam anu saṅkarṣaṇaḥ serṣyam iva nijam utkarṣaṃ vāñchan nija-jananī-stana-pānam ārabdhavān | [22] tadaiva ca tau līlābhiḥ pramīlām āgatau yātṛbhyāṃ mātṛbhyāṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ śayyām adhiśāyyete sma |
children.translated_text: And having paused for a moment, the one with the charming face commenced breast-feeding there too, seeing which <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), as if with jealousy, desiring his own preeminence, commenced drinking at his own mother's breast. [22] And just then, when both had been brought to drowsiness by their play, they were gently laid upon their beds by their traveling mothers.

children.text: tad evaṃ sarāmasya tasya nirodhe vidhīyamāne bahir vijihīrṣite cātīva tad-upajīvana-pīvatām āsann eva yogamāyā tad-anukulyāya kiñcit prapañcitavatī, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the confinement of him — along with <s>Rāma</s> — was being enforced, and when [his] desire to play outside had grown exceedingly — the sustenance thereof being very rich — <s>Yogamāyā</s>, for his accommodation, devised a certain contrivance, as follows:

children.text: ekadārbhakam ādāya svāṅkam āropya bhāvinī |
children.translated_text: Once, having taken the infant and placed him upon her own lap, the divinely-inspired one,

children.text: prasnutaṃ pāyayāmāsa stanaṃ sneha-pariplutā ||
children.translated_text: overflowing with affection, suckled him at her flowing breast.

children.text: pīta-prāyasya jananī sutasya rucira-smitam |
lālayantī mukhaṃ viśvaṃ jṛmbhato dadṛśe idam ||[BhP 10.7.34-5] iti |
children.translated_text: while fondling his beautiful smiling face, saw this — the universe — as he yawned! ||[BhP 10.7.34-35]||
Of the son, mostly done drinking, the mother

children.text: tena ca santataṃ vismayamānāyāṃ nijajāyāyāṃ tasyāṃ kadācit śrīmān vrajarājaḥ papraccha, mayā yad aniṣṭa-bhayād bāla-rodhanam upadiṣṭam, tat kiṃ nirvahati?
children.translated_text: And as she was continuously amazed thereby, the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> once asked his own wife: 'The confinement of the boy that I prescribed out of fear of misfortune — is that being maintained?'

children.text: sā prāha-nirvahaty eva, kintu vṛtheti lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: She said: 'It is being maintained indeed, but it is observed to be futile.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-hanta, katham iva?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Alas, how so?'

children.text: sā prāha-vraja-mātra-vrajanaṃ varjyate | dṛṣṭaṃ tu mṛṣṭa-smitaṃ jṛmbhamānasya bālakasya vadana-dvārā jagad eva iti |
children.translated_text: She said: 'Going to any part of <s>Vraja</s> is prevented. But through the mouth-door of the yawning, bright-smiling baby boy — the world itself has been seen!'

children.text: atha vrajarājaḥ sa-vailakṣyam ālakṣya lakṣmī-jāni-lakṣyatayā maunam ālambya vilambya covāca-yady evam, tadā svajana-parāyaṇasya śrī-nārāyaṇasya vidhitsitam eva sarvaṃ vicikitsitam api cikitsitaṃ kariṣyati | tasyaiva khalv idaṃ vaibhavam iti |
children.translated_text: Then the king of <s>Vraja</s>, observing [this] with embarrassment, adopting silence in recognition of the purpose of <s>Lakṣmī's</s> husband (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), and then pausing, said: 'If so, then the intention of Śrī <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is devoted to his own people, will make even all that is doubtful into a remedy. This is indeed his glory.'

children.text:
evaṃ tad-avadhi tad-vidhinā nātinirodhe vidhīyamāne kvacid api samaye saṃyamanaṃ samayā sarāmaḥ sa rāmānujaḥ śrīdāma-sudāma-vasudāmādibhiḥ samaṃ ramate sma | [30] tatra vinodena mṛdadanaṃ cakrāṇe cakrāṅkita-caraṇe saṅkarṣaṇā-dayaḥ khelāyāṃ kalita-kalahā rahas tan-mātaraṃ nivedayāmāsuḥ, ye khalu tayā tad-vidha-vidhāne' vadhāpitā vidhīyante sma | [31] mātā ca pracchannam āgacchantī bāhuṃ gṛhītvā papraccha, capala, kim idaṃ duścaritam ācaritam?
[32] sa tu sahasā saṅkalitānana-kamalaḥ kātara-matir mātaram uvāca-mātar, na kim api |
children.translated_text:
Thus, from that point onward, when excessive confinement was not being enforced by that method, at some time, checking [his] restraint, that glorious younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, along with <s>Rāma</s>, sported with <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, <s>Vasudāma</s>, and others. [30] There, when the one marked with the discus on his feet was playfully eating mud, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and others, having quarreled in play, secretly informed his mother, and they were indeed employed by her in the enforcement of such a procedure. [31] And the mother, coming secretly, having seized his arm, asked: 'Wayward one, what is this misbehavior you have done?'
[32] And he, suddenly composing his lotus-face, with an anxious mind, said to his mother: 'Mother, nothing at all!'

children.text: mātā prāha-mṛttikām atti sma bhavān |
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'You have been eating mud!'

children.text: suta uvāca-ka idaṃ vadati?
children.translated_text: The son said: 'Who says this?'

children.text: mātā prāha-sarva eva tava savayasaḥ |
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'All of your playmates!'

children.text: suta uvāca-ete khalu nija-nija-vastyān madhura-vastūni muṣṇantaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam atrapam atra parasparam aśnanti, tad anaṅgī-kṛtavataḥ kapāṭita-radane mama vadane prathamaṃ samaṃ balāc chalād api samarpayanti, tac ca tvayi sa-nirvedaṃ nivedayitum icchor mama tucchaṃ sa-vivādaṃ durvādam etam avādiṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: The son said: 'These ones, stealing sweet things from each other's pouches, eat them here shamelessly with longing among themselves; then, forcibly — even by trickery — they stuff [the mud] into the mouth of me, who has not accepted [it], whose teeth were shut tight, and wishing to report this to you with indignation, they uttered this false, worthless, quarrelsome accusation against me!'

children.text: mātā suvismitam ūrdhvam adho mūrdhānam ādhūya sasmitam uvāca-savyāja-rāja! tavāpy agrajaḥ so' yaṃ vyañjayati, tatra kiṃ vadiṣyati?
children.translated_text: The mother, greatly astonished, shaking her head up and down, said with a smile: 'O king of pretexts! Your own elder brother too indicates [the same] — what will he say to that?'

children.text: suta uvāca-ete sarva eva vīthyāṃ vīthyāṃ mithyābhiśaṃsinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The son said: 'All these, in every lane, are false accusers!'

children.text: mātā prāha-sa-cchala-pralapita! bho mat-pitaḥ, balabhadraḥ kim iti pramiti-rahitam abhadraṃ vadatu?
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'O prattler of pretexts! O my father's [darling]! Why would <s>Balabhadra</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) speak something improper and without proof?'

children.text: suta uvāca-ayam apy etad-gaṇa-pātīti tathānyedyur mṛttikām atti sma, tad avadyaṃ nivedayitum udyataṃ mad-vacanaṃ mṛṣodyatām āsādayitum iti |
children.translated_text: The son said: 'He too belongs to their faction, and on another day he [himself] was eating mud; the statement of mine that was ready to report that misdeed — he seeks to bring it to falsehood!'

children.text: mātā tan-mukhaṃ dhṛtvā sahāsam āha sma, kim idaṃ ciraṃ nigirann asi?
children.translated_text: The mother, holding his face, said laughingly: 'What is this you have been swallowing for so long?'

children.text: suta uvāca-uktam eva mama lapane balād galāntaḥ praveśāya kim api nyastaṃ samastaiḥ iti |
children.translated_text: The son said: 'As I have already said — something was forcibly thrust into my gaping [mouth] by all of them!'

children.text: mātā prāha-dhūrta, kathaṃ jānīyām?
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'Rogue! How shall I find out?'

children.text: suta uvāca-sāmprataṃ mama mukham eva nirīkṣyatām |
children.translated_text: The son said: 'Now, let my mouth itself be examined!'

children.text: mātā sa-saṃrambha-smitam uvāca-vyādehi, paśyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The mother said with agitated smile: 'Open wide — let us see!'

children.text: tataś ca bhayena sa eṣa mṛc-cihnitam apy ahnāya vadanaṃ vyādadau | [47] tatas tad-bhayam avadadhānā samādadhānā ca rasāntareṇa mātuḥ kopa-śāntaye tad-antar-yogam āyātā sā yogamāyā punar viśvaṃ darśitavatī |
children.translated_text: Then, in fear, he — concealing the mud-marks — opened his mouth. [47] Then, that <s>Yogamāyā</s>, both concealing his fear and composing [the scene], and with a different <s>rasa</s> (mood) — for the pacification of the mother's anger — having entered his interior through her yogic connection, displayed the universe once more.

children.text: tatra cedaṃ vrajeśvarī parāmamarśe-
children.translated_text: And therein the queen of <s>Vraja</s> reflected:

children.text:
aho bahir ivekṣyate jagad idaṃ mukhābhyantare
śiśos tad anu bhūr iyaṃ bhuvi ca māthuraṃ maṇḍalam |
iha vraja-kulaṃ yad anv api mayā dhṛto bālakaḥ
sa eva tad aho kathaṃ kim iva hanta kiṃ sidhyati ||JGc_1,7.38|| [pṛthvī]

atha punaḥ svapnādikam analpaṃ kalpayitvā paścimam idaṃ niścikāya,
  ahaṃ yaśodāsmi patir vrajādhipaḥ
  sutaḥ sa eṣa svam idaṃ ca gokulam |
  pratīyate' thāpi śiśor mukhe jagad
  yan-māyayetthaṃ kumatiḥ sa me gatiḥ ||JGc_1,7.39|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then, having again imagined much — dreams and such — she finally determined this:
I am <s>Yaśodā</s>, my husband is the lord of <s>Vraja</s>,
this son is he, and this is my own <s>Gokula</s>;
yet the world appears in the child's mouth —
by whose <s>māyā</s> I am thus deluded — he is my refuge! ||7.39|| [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ sa ca nārāyaṇas tad-bhāva-parāyaṇatāṃ tām anu nitāntāṃ vicārayann ātmanaḥ paramābhiruci-paricitāvirbhāve tasminn eva vismiti-nicitaṃ janany-ucita-sneham eva dehayāmāsa, yaṃ khalu nemaṃ viriñci [BhP 10.9.20] vakṣyamāṇānusāreṇa samastāni śāstrāṇi sadā praśastatayā gāyanti |
children.translated_text: Thus, that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, reflecting upon her supreme devotion as the culmination of [all] states, and upon the manifestation of his own supreme delight — upon that very amazement-filled, mother-befitting love — bestowed it [upon her]; which indeed all the scriptures always sing as supremely praiseworthy, in accordance with what will be stated: 'Not even this one, <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)...' [BhP 10.9.20].

children.text: atha kautukāntaraṃ cāntaram ānīyatām | tad evaṃ sarvānandanaḥ śrīman-nanda-nandanaḥ krīṇīhi bhoḥ phalāni iti [BhP 10.11.10] gīti-rīti-rocana-vacanaṃ karṇayor āracayann eva capala-locanaḥ kiñcanāpy ālocayann eva ca laghunāpi pāṇi-yugalena laghutayā puraḥ patita-dhānya-puñjataḥ pūrṇam añjalim ādāya tad-abhimukhaṃ jagāma | kintu drava-vaśād alpakāñjalitaḥ skhalitam idam iti bhidāṃ na vidāñcakāra, kevalam eva kara-yugalaṃ krayya-phala-pūrita-tat-patra-pātropari parivṛttyā ca cālayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Now, let another amusing episode be brought in! Thus, the all-delighting son of the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, the restless-eyed one, arranging upon his ears the charming words of the song-style 'Buy, O sir, fruits!' [BhP 10.11.10], and contemplating something too, with both small hands, lightly, from the heap of grain that had fallen in front, taking a full handful, went toward her [the fruit-seller]. But due to the liquid [flowing out], that this small handful had spilled — he did not notice the loss; he merely turned both his hands over upon the leaf-vessel filled with fruits for purchase, and shook them.

children.text:
tataś ca sā smitavatī smita-digdha-tan-mukha-mādhurī-sādhu-rītibhiḥ snigdha-hṛdayā vyañjita-spṛhāvalīṃ tad-añjaliṃ phala-valayena bhikṣayantī dūrata eva saṅkalana-mudrām api śikṣayantī sakalena tu pūrayituṃ śaśāka | [53] nija-bhājanaṃ phala-riktaṃ babhūva vā na vā kim iti tu na viviktuṃ cakāra | gṛhābhyantareṇāntarite tu tasmin nijaṃ patrajam amatram ayatnatayā ratna-pūritam apy anibhālya bhāram apy asambhālya tan-mādhuryāveśābhiniveśavatī svajanānām api śarma-jananāya bahula-phalāvali-bali-samānayanāya ca nija-nilayam eva jagāma | kintu gṛhaṃ gatvā jñāta-maṇi-tattvāpy akuṇṭhāsakṛd-utkaṇṭhāvahena tan-mukha-śobhābhara-viraheṇa sā dhanyā hārita-mahā-dhanaṃ-manyā babhūva, yata eva sā kṛṣṇa-dṛśvarī viśvam api visasmāra
|
children.translated_text: Then she, smiling, her heart melted by the excellent manner of the sweetness of his smile-anointed face, begging his handful that displayed a row of desires, and teaching him from afar even the gesture of gathering, was able to fill it completely with a circle of fruits. [53] Whether her own vessel became empty of fruits or not — she did not bother to ascertain. And when he had disappeared behind the interior of the house, without even looking at her own leaf-basket, which had effortlessly become filled with gems, and without even feeling its weight, she — possessed by absorption in his sweetness — went to her own dwelling, to generate joy for her own people and to bring back an offering-tribute of abundant rows of fruits. But having gone home and having learned the reality of the jewels, that blessed woman, whose great wealth had been rendered worthless by the unceasing longing produced by separation from the splendor of that face, became supremely honored — for that seer of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> indeed forgot even the entire world.

children.text: sa tu vividha-durvidha-śarma-vidhāna-sannidhānaḥ svayaṃ labdha-nidhānavad atisāvadhāna-pāṇir nṛtyann iva mātuḥ samīpam añcan madhura-cañcalehitas tasyā nicolāñcale nirbandhataḥ sakalāni phalāni babandha |
children.translated_text: And he, the repository of the bestowal of various kinds of improper delights, himself dancing as if with hands that had obtained a treasure, with a sweetly playful gait, reaching his mother's side, insistently tied all the fruits upon the hem of her garment.

children.text: mātā covāca-putra kutra labdhāni tānīmāni?
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'Son, where did you obtain these?'

children.text: sutas tu bālya-bhāvād ardhārdha-varṇaṃ varṇayāmāsa, kadācid ācita-phalā dhānyāni mūlyam ādāya dhanyā mayi cānukūlyam ādhāya samarpitavatī |
children.translated_text: The son, due to his childhood state, described it in half-and-half syllables: 'Once, a blessed woman who had gathered fruits, having taken grains as payment, and having bestowed her kindness upon me, offered [them].'

children.text: mātovāca-vatsa, gṛhajanavat sarvataḥ pratītiṃ mā kṛthāḥ iti |
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'Child, do not trust everyone as though they were members of the household.'

children.text: sutas tu kā khalv apratītir iti ca na vidāñcakāra | [59] kṣaṇataś ca tāṃ gatāṃ nirīkṣya punar āgataḥ sakṣaṇatayā janāya tat-phala-vibhajanāya jananīṃ niyojayāmāsa | [60] mātā cāmandenānandena kṛta-spandena kara-dvandvena tāni vibhajantī tadantīkṛtiṃ nāsasāda | dina-katipayaṃ vismaya-vaśā smayamānā vasati sma | tad-āsvāda-karāś ca labdha-camatkārā na vismaranti sma |
children.translated_text: The son, however, did not understand what distrust was. [59] And in a moment, seeing her gone, he came again and promptly engaged his mother in distributing those fruits to the people. [60] The mother, with a gentle joy that made her hands tremble, distributing those [fruits], could not reach the end of them. For several days she remained smiling in amazement. And those who tasted them, having attained wonder, did not forget.

children.text: atha līlāntaram udbhāvayitum evaṃ vibhāvyate-
children.translated_text: Now, to introduce another pastime, thus it is described:

children.text:
gokuleṣu kila śīlam īdṛśaṃ
  yad divā vanam ayanti gonarāḥ |
  yoṣitaḥ pracura-gavya-saṃskriyāṃ
  krīḍanaṃ rahasi bāla-tarṇakāḥ ||JGc_1,7.40|| [rathoddhatā] iti |
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Gokula</s>, indeed, such is the custom: | by day the cow-lords go to the forest; | the women [attend to] the abundant dairy preparations; | the young calves play in seclusion.' || (JGc 1,7.40) [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
tadā caikadā gṛha-vyaya-payaḥ-kṛte samīpakṛte vatsa-sadmani ruddha-dvārān śakṛt-kari-sārān bāla-hariḥ paritaḥ-sthita-bālaka-jālaḥ kalayāmāsa | tatra ca,
  vatsīr matvā tadā dhenūś chāga-tokāni vatsakān |
  ātmānaṃ go-duhaṃ bālā go-doham anunirmamuḥ ||JGc_1,7.41|| [anuṣṭubh]
  vatsīṣu yarhi gavyanto goduhanti sma te' rbhakāḥ |
  teṣāṃ prahāsajā bhāsaḥ payasyante sma tās tadā ||JGc_1,7.42|| [anuṣṭubh]
  iyeṣa ca yadā dhenu-cāraṇānukṛtiṃ prati |
  mantrayitvā tadā kṛṣṇaḥ prāmuñcan nava-vatsakān ||JGc_1,7.43|| [anuṣṭubh]
  rakṣām icchū vatsa-pucchaṃ gṛhṇānau rāma-keśavau |
  tad-ākṛṣṭatayā goṣṭhe bālair babhramatustarām ||JGc_1,7.44|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then, one day, the young <s>Hari</s>, surrounded by a crowd of boys, observed at the calf-shed nearby — where the doors were shut for the household milk expenditure — the calves that were dung-producing treasures. And there:
'Regarding the mother-cows as cows, and the baby goats as calves, | and themselves as cow-milkers — the boys imitated the milking!' || (JGc 1,7.41) [anuṣṭubh]
'When the boys, desiring dairy products, milked the mother-cows — | the radiance born of their laughter made those [cows] seem to overflow with milk!' || (JGc 1,7.42) [anuṣṭubh]
'And when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> wished to imitate the driving of cows, | having deliberated, they released the young calves!' || (JGc 1,7.43) [anuṣṭubh]
'Desiring to guard [the calves], <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Keśava</s> grasped a calf's tail; | being dragged by it, they wandered exceedingly through the cow-pen with the boys!' || (JGc 1,7.44) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tac ca tarṇakānugatayā tayoḥ prathamam abhyarṇāgamanam ākarṇya nirvarṇya ca vara-varṇinyaḥ skhalad-varṇaṃ varṇayāmāsuḥ | tathā hi gītam-
children.translated_text: And hearing and observing the first approach of the two through following the calves, the excellent women described it in faltering syllables. For thus was the song:

children.text: bala-kṛṣṇau balavalitavilāsau |
children.translated_text: '<s>Bala</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of graces rolling with strength,

children.text: khelata iha sakhi sakhi-kṛta-hāsau ||dhru||
children.translated_text: are playing here, O friend, laughing with their companions!' ||refrain||

children.text: tarṇaka-puccha-dhṛti-vyāpṛtinau |
children.translated_text: 'Engaged in the activity of holding calf-tails,

children.text: praṇaya-kalita-kali-kalane kṛtinau ||
children.translated_text: accomplished in the settling of love-infused quarrels!'

children.text: gṛha-gṛha-vīkṣaṇa-sakṣaṇa-netrau |
children.translated_text: 'With eyes eagerly glancing from house to house,

children.text: dhenu-pāla-tulayā dhṛta-vetrau ||
children.translated_text: holding sticks like cowherd guardians!'

children.text: druta-tarṇakam anuvidrutavantau |
children.translated_text: 'Running after the swift calves,

children.text: śreṇīyita-cala-veṇīmantau ||
children.translated_text: with their moving braids swaying in a line!'

children.text: śārada-vārṣika-vārida-vapuṣau |
children.translated_text: 'With bodies like autumnal and rainy-season clouds,

children.text: cala-locana-ruci-capalāṃśu-juṣau ||
children.translated_text: their darting eyes enjoying flickering radiance!'

children.text: skhalad-alaka-dyuti-valayita-lapanau |
children.translated_text: 'With faces encircled by the luster of tumbling curls,

children.text: ali-lalitāmala-kamala-glapanau ||
children.translated_text: putting to shame the pure, spotless lotuses, delicate as bees!'

children.text:
nīla-kanaka-ruci-śuci-laghu-vasanau |
cañcala-caraṇa-sphuṭa-raṭa-rasanau ||JGc_1,7.45|| iti | [mātrāsamaka]
children.translated_text:
'With garments blue and golden, pure and light, |
with jingling anklets on their restless feet!' || (JGc 1,7.45) [mātrāsamaka]

children.text:
tad evam aṅganād aṅganād vrajāṅganābhir aham-pūrvikayānugamyamānau, vihitākasmika-parva-sukha-dohana-sarva-mohanatayādhigamyamānau,
saṃvāda-vivāda-parīvāda-bandhura-bandhūnām abhyarṇatayā nirvarṇyamānau,
tādṛśākarṇana-nivarṇanam anu parasparaṃ varṇyamānau,
tāsu ca kābhiścid amṛtam anṛtaṃ kurvatā praticarvaṇaṃ sarasena rasa-visareṇa bhojyamānau,
tadvad ekābhir nija-gṛhājīvya-divya-maṇi-hāram upahāram upahāraṃ hāritayopayojyamānau tadvad varṇyamānau,
tāsu ca kābhir api premānugamya-ramya-vacana-pracaya-racanayā kañcana kālaṃ varivasyamānau,
kiṃ cānyābhiḥ samuttambhita-karṇa-tarṇaka-kṛta-kṛṣṭi-dṛṣṭitaḥ śasyamānavat parihasyamānau,
tadvad anyatarābhis tan-madhura-cakura-cikura-cañcuratā-pracura-cañcalatāṃ nicāyya cāturyataś caritam idaṃ bhavan-mātṛ-caraṇeṣu gocarayāmaḥ, iti sūcanayā tasmād varjyamānau,
tābhir eva mātara-pitarāv ārabhya gaṇanālabhya-kulāli-gāli-pālim upalabhya kalita-vyalīkam iva sa-kolāhala-praṇaya-kalita-kalitayā tarjyamānau
bala-gopāla-nāmānau valgu-bālyavayasā samānau khelāṃ kalayāmāsatuḥ |
children.translated_text:
Thus, from courtyard to courtyard, followed by the women of <s>Vraja</s> each vying to be first, being encountered as all-enchanting through the milking of unexpected festive delight,
observed up close by the charming kinsmen of conversations, disputes, and reproaches,
being described to one another upon hearing and observing thus,
being fed by some among them with a relish of savory morsels that makes nectar seem false,
likewise being presented by some with divine jewel-necklaces — the life-wealth of their own homes — as offerings, and being praised accordingly,
being attended for some time by some with an arrangement of loving speech worthy of following with affection,
being mocked as if praised by others whose eyes were drawn by the attraction created by the ear-pricking calves,
likewise being avoided by some others who, having perceived the abundant playfulness of those sweet-eyed, curly-haired ones, skillfully [threatened]: 'We shall report this conduct to your mothers!' —
being threatened by those very ones with a row of affectionate scoldings — of innumerable familial reproaches beginning from mother and father — discovered with feigned displeasure and clamorous loving agitation,
the two named <s>Bala</s> and <s>Gopāla</s>, equal in charming childhood age, played their play.

children.text:
atha mātarāv api jātāv amū kutra yātāv iti kātarāyamāṇa-nayane nirjanatā-janita-svairatā-bhāg-ayane vraja-nīvṛd-ayane ruṣā ninditābhir upamātṛbhir mudā vanditābhir api tad-abhidhātṛ-yātṛbhiḥ samam eva gṛhataḥ kṛta-niryāṇe svayam eva samyag mṛgayamāṇe dara-sarasi-janija-cihna-vigata-nihnava-caraṇa-lakṣaṇa-vilakṣaṇa-vartma-valanena mahilānāṃ kutūhala-kolāha-lāva-kalanena ca samayā samayāñcakrāte | tadā ca nijāgamana-varjanīṃ tarjanīm abhicālya pracchannatayā nibhālya tasmād akasmād anayor bāhū jagṛhatuḥ | bālakās tu sarvataḥ sarva eva dudruvuḥ, mahilāś ca kāścanānukūlyataḥ kāścana prātikūlyata iva ca tayoś cāpalyaṃ lapantyaḥ samam eva mātṛbhyām abhyāyayuḥ | dhātryas tu bālayor atīva sneha-pātryas tarṇakān ādāya
tad-abhyarṇam ājagmuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, the two mothers, their eyes anxious wondering 'Where have these two born [ones] gone?', having set out from the house together with the scolding foster-mothers and the praising informant-guides, themselves searching properly on the pathway of <s>Vraja</s>'s boundary lane — that portion free from people that offered the freedom born of solitude — they caught up [with the boys] by following the trail of footprints bearing the marks of the small-pond-born signs on the distinctive, telltale path where concealment was impossible, and by the tumultuous curiosity of the women. And then, flexing the forbidding forefinger, having secretly observed [them], from that [spot] unexpectedly they seized the arms of those two. The boys all ran away in every direction, and some women accompanied [the mothers] agreeably, while others as if disapprovingly, speaking of the two's mischief, came together with the mothers. And the nurse-maids, supremely affectionate vessels of love for the boys, taking the calves, came near them.

children.text: atha tad ārabhya vīthīṃ vīthīm upalabhya kutukakarmā balānujanmā saha- sahacaraḥ kolāhalaṃ kalayāmāsa | tadā ca kadācin nijatanūjalabhyaprāgalbhya-spṛhiṇī vrajeśagṛhiṇī tadānandabṛṃhiṇībhir vivadamānābhir iva dīyamāna-tadīyamānasamānābhir upālambhasamādhānalambhanavākovākyavyaṅgam avyaṅgam abhyadhāyi |
children.translated_text: Now, from that time onward, finding one lane after another, the mischief-maker born alongside his companion performed clamor. And then, once, the wife of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, who yearned for the boldness difficult to obtain in her own little son, while the women who were quarreling as if [complaining] — giving away his [butter and the like] equating it to their own — a dialogue of reproach and reconciliation was recited, complete in every limb:

children.text: tatra sabhāyāṃ sā yathā-
children.translated_text: There, in the assembly, she [appeared] thus:

children.text:
āsīnā kanakāsane sutayutā śrīmad-vrajādhīśvarī
  pīṭha-śreṇim upāśritā vraja-vadhūr nānātma-bhāva-śriyaḥ |
  kṛṣṇa-prema-sudhā-mahomaya-girām āsvādanād dhinvatī
  tābhiś ca pratidhinvitākhila-sabhā śobhāṅga-yaṣṭir babhau ||JGc_1,7.46|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[68] vākovākyaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text:
'Seated on a golden throne, accompanied by her son, the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s>, | with the women of <s>Vraja</s> seated upon rows of stools, [radiant] with the splendors of various sentiments, | nourishing [all] through the savoring of speeches that are a great flood of the nectar of love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, | and nourished in return by them — the whole assembly, a staff of beauty's limbs, shone!' || (JGc 1,7.46) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[68] The dialogue was as follows:

children.text: tava sūnur muhur anayaṃ kurute |
children.translated_text: 'Your son repeatedly commits mischief!'

children.text: akuruta kiṃ vā vyañjita-kurute ||dhru||
children.translated_text: 'Has he committed it, or is he merely accused of committing it?' ||refrain||

children.text: muñcati vatsān bhrāmaṃ bhrāmam |
children.translated_text: 'He releases the calves, wandering and wandering!'

children.text: sācivyaṃ vaḥ kurute kāmam ||
children.translated_text: 'He does your service willingly!'

children.text: asamaya-mocanam asukha-nidhānam |
children.translated_text: 'Untimely releasing is a repository of unhappiness!'

children.text: kaḥ kiṃ kurute na yadi nidānam ||
children.translated_text: 'Who does anything without a reason?'

children.text: vinā nidānaṃ kurute svāmini |
children.translated_text: 'He does it without reason, O mistress!'

children.text: krośaṃ na kim iva kuruṣe bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: 'Then why don't you scold him, O spirited one?'

children.text: krośe hasati pratyuta so' yam |
children.translated_text: 'When scolded, he laughs in return, that one!'

children.text: dattvā vaśaya sphuṭam api toyam ||
children.translated_text: 'Give him water and subdue him, clearly!'

children.text: atti steyaṃ param iha rucitam |
children.translated_text: 'He eats stolen [butter] — that is what delights him here!'

children.text: ajñe bhānaṃ katham idam ucitam ||
children.translated_text: 'O naive one, how is this accusation proper?'

children.text: steyopāye gurur ayam akhile |
children.translated_text: 'He is a master in all the methods of theft!'

children.text: nārhati sarvaṃ mithyā nikhile ||
children.translated_text: 'He does not deserve all [this blame] — it is entirely false!'

children.text: racayati pīṭhādikam āroham |
children.translated_text: 'He constructs a climbing structure of stools and the like!'

children.text: tad agamyaṃ kuru sarvaṃ doham ||
children.translated_text: 'Then make all the milk-pots inaccessible!'

children.text: dūrāc chidraṃ kalayati pātre |
children.translated_text: 'He discerns a hole in the vessel from afar!'

children.text: asya kathaṃ dhīḥ sati tan-mātre ||
children.translated_text: 'How does he have such intelligence, being only that age?'

children.text: antar-dhiyam anu sa iha viśālaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'In hidden intelligence, he is great here!'

children.text: vakṣi yathāsau na tathā bālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'You say so, but he is not such a [grown] boy!'

children.text: vetti sa kṛtsnaṃ gopana-rītim |
children.translated_text: 'He knows the entire technique of concealment!'

children.text: geha-guhā nahi davayati bhītim ||
children.translated_text: 'The cave of the house does not cause him fear!'

children.text: geha-guhātra vṛthā tanu-dīpe |
children.translated_text: 'The cave of the house is useless when there is a small lamp within!'

children.text: tanur anuliptā kalaya samīpe ||
children.translated_text: 'His body is smeared [with butter] — observe it closely!'

children.text: maṇi-gaṇa-mahasā gaṇayati na tamaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'By the radiance of clusters of gems, he regards no darkness!'

children.text: bhūṣaṇa-rahitas tiṣṭhet katamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Without ornaments, which [boy] would remain [unseen]?'

children.text: api cāśayati balād api kīśam |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, he forcibly feeds even a monkey!'

children.text: manuṣe kiyad amum attum adhīśam ||
children.translated_text: 'How much can a human eat — [this is] the lord's [doing]!'

children.text: tad aśaktau pātraṃ bhedayate |
children.translated_text: 'When unable [to eat more], he breaks the pot!'

children.text: tasyāśaucaṃ vā vedayate ||
children.translated_text: 'Or does he proclaim its impurity?'

children.text: gama-samaye rodayati ca bālām |
children.translated_text: 'At the time of departure, he makes the girl-child cry!'

children.text: prakṣyāmo vara-mahilāmālām ||
children.translated_text: 'We shall ask the garland of excellent women!'

children.text: api bālān mehayate gehe |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, he makes the boys urinate in the house!'

children.text: nahi nahi cūrṇaṃ patitaṃ snehe ||
children.translated_text: 'No, no — powder has fallen into the ghee!'

children.text:
tava purato' yaṃ sthiravan-mūrtiḥ |
āścaryeyaṃ tava vāk-pūrtiḥ ||JGc_1,7.47|| iti | [mātrāsamaka]
children.translated_text:
'Before you, this one stands like a statue! |
Wondrous indeed is this fulfillment of your words!' || (JGc 1,7.47) [mātrāsamaka]

children.text:
punaś ca pratītim āsādayantya ivedaṃ vadanti sma, nāścaryam atrācaryatām | yataḥ,
  indriya-kulam atigūḍhaṃ netrādy-anta-nigūḍham evāsti |
  tan-madhyād api cittaṃ harato nṛ-harer na hāryaṃ kim? ||JGc_1,7.48|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
And again, as if gaining conviction, they said this: 'There is no wonder — let it be revered! For:
'The entire group of senses, most deeply hidden, is concealed within, ending with the eyes. | From the midst of even those, he steals the mind — what then is not to be stolen by <s>Nṛ-hari</s> (the man-lion, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)?' || (JGc 1,7.48) [āryā]

children.text: tad evam abhīṣaṅga-bhaṅgībhir vara-varṇinībhir varṇyamānam ākarṇya capala-dṛṣṭi-parāmṛṣṭi-karṇaṃ jhaṭiti jāta-vilakṣaṇa-varṇaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-mukha-śrī-parṇaṃ nirvarṇya vihasantīṃ tām anu vihasantībhis tābhiḥ śapantībhir iva bhaṇitam-yadi ca vayaṃ sādhu-caritācaritārthatāṃ gatās, tadā bhavatyā bhavane' pi śīghram etat patiṣyati |
children.translated_text: Thus, hearing [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] described by the excellent women with these waves of fond attachment, and observing the face of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — that leaf of beauty — which had suddenly become of an embarrassed hue, its ears touched by restless glances, [<s>Yaśodā</s>] laughed; and following her laughter, those [women], laughing and cursing as it were, said: 'If we have attained the fulfillment of righteous conduct, then this [mischief] will soon befall your house too!'

children.text: hasantī sā covāca-bhadraṃ bhadram, tadaiva vo bhadratvam anubhaviṣyāmaḥ iti | [72] vastutas tu tasyāḥ komalatāyām avakalitāyāṃ, muhur ayam asmad-ālayaṃ valiṣyate iti vicāryaiva caryeyam amūbhir ācaryate sma |
children.translated_text: She (<s>Yaśodā</s>), laughing, said: 'Blessings, blessings! Then indeed we shall experience your blessedness!' [72] In truth, however, when her tenderness was perceived, [the women] actually conducted this behavior with the deliberation that 'again and again he will come to our homes' — that was the practice performed by them.

children.text:
atha samāpanam idaṃ madhukaṇṭha-vacanam,
  adbhutaṃ bālyacaritaṃ tava sūnor vrajeśvara |
  kva tṛṇāvarta-dalanaṃ kva mātur bhaya-bhāvanam? ||JGc_1,7.49|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Now this concluding utterance of <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>:
Wondrous are the childhood deeds of your son, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>!
Where stands the crushing of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, and where the causing of fear to the mother? ||7.49|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ tad-divāvṛtte pūrvavad eva tal-līlā-parvaṇi sākṣād iva vṛtte sarve puraskṛta-vrajeśāḥ sambhṛta-tat-tad-āveśā yathāyatham ātma-pathaṃ pratasthire |
children.translated_text: Thus, when that day had passed, just as before, when that festival of pastimes had transpired as if directly [before them], all — led by the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — filled with their respective absorptions, set out upon their own paths as was fitting.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
bālya-līlā-caurya-śauryaṃ nāma
saptamaṃ pūraṇam
 ||7||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Seventh Chapter, named
'The Theft and Valor of Childhood Pastimes.'
||7||

children.text: athāṣṭamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Eighth Chapter.

children.text: dāmodarānumodaḥ
children.translated_text: The Delight of <s>Dāmodara</s>.

children.text:
athetaradyur api prabhāta eva sabhām upaviśya vibhāteṣu vaiśyajāteṣu snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-kadācid dāmodara-māsi darānvavasāne, sāmodā yaśodā prātar bāla-gopālaṃ śayānam unmīlan-nibha-netra-nīla-nalina-yugalaṃ nibhālya śanair eva kara-kiśalayena palyaṅkād upari talpa eva parilālya punar asūṣupat-kalpam | tasmād alpam alpaṃ niṣkrāmantī cālindaṃ vindamānā prāhṇetarām ahnāya nijālaya-vyaya-sambandhi dadhi katipayaṃ nicita-nicaya-granthir manthitum ārebhe | yasminn ahani saha-nandanāmanda-syandanārohiṇī rohiṇī praṇaya-maya-yantraṇayā nimantraṇayā śrīmad-upananda-mandiraṃ vindamānāsīt | parijana-nāryaś ca svasva-kāryātiśaya-paryāya-paryāpaṇāya gatāḥ | kāryātiśayaś cāyaṃ hāyana-śīrṣāyamāṇa-mārgaśīrṣāgame
jana-varga-mahita-mahendra-mahā-mahaḥ kula-paramparā-vihitaḥ sannihita āsīd iti |
children.translated_text: Then, on the following morning too, having taken his seat in the assembly as the <s>Vaiśya</s> clans shone forth, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke: 'Once, in the month of <s>Dāmodara</s> (Kārttika), near the end of the dark fortnight, the joyful <s>Yaśodā</s>, in the morning, seeing baby <s>Gopāla</s> lying asleep — his pair of blue-lotus eyes appearing as if just opening — gently rocked him on the couch atop the bed itself, and he fell back asleep. Gradually withdrawing from him little by little, finding a corridor, she began to churn some yogurt belonging to her own household for the day's provisions in the forenoon, having tied up its accumulated store in bundles. On that day, <s>Rohiṇī</s> — who mounts the delightful chariot together with <s>Nandana</s> (the son) — had gone, by the compulsion of an affectionate invitation, to the glorious mansion of <s>Upananda</s>. And the attendant women had gone for the conclusion of their successive extraordinary duties. And that extraordinary duty was this: the great festival of the great <s>Indra</s>, honored by the multitude of people, established by family tradition, was approaching as the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> drew near, extending to the summit of the year.'

children.text: tad evaṃ svayam eva sayatnī-bhūya vraja-rāja-patnī dadhi-cayam asakṛd adhimathnatī tasya nidrāyā drāghīyastvāya gāyantī tadeka-tānatayā tad-ānanam eva nicāyantī paritas tadīya-caritam eva jagau | yad uktaṃ śrī-bādarāyaṇinā-
children.translated_text: Thus, the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, having become diligent by herself, repeatedly churning the pile of yogurt, singing for the prolongation of his sleep, gazing intently at his face with single-pointed absorption, sang his deeds all around. As stated by the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva):

children.text:
yāni yānīha gītāni tadbālacaritāni ca |
  dadhinirmanthane kāle smarantī tāny agāyata ||iti | [BhP 10.9.2]
children.translated_text:
'Whatever songs were [composed] here about the childhood deeds of that [child],
she sang them, remembering, at the time of churning the yogurt.' [Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.9.2]

children.text:
atra manthanaṃ yathā,
  śyāmā lola-dukūla-ratna-vilasat-kāñcī-cayenāñcitā
  taj-jhaṅkāra-karambita-dhvani-dhara-śrī-kaṅkaṇālaṅkṛtā |
  paśyantī tanayānanaṃ laghu-laghūnmīlan-nibhākṣi-dvayaṃ
  śrīmad-gopa-maheśvarī cala-bhujāmathnād abhīkṣṇaṃ dadhi ||JGc_1,8.1|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[4] gānaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text:
Here, the churning was as follows:
Dark-complexioned, adorned with clusters of radiant jeweled girdle-chains over her loosely flowing silk garment,
bedecked with the splendid bangles whose sound mingled with the tinkling of those [chains],
gazing at her son's face with the pair of eyes appearing as if gently, lightly opening,
the glorious queen of the great cowherd lord churned the yogurt again and again with moving arms. ||8.1|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[4] The song was as follows:

children.text: gokula-pati-kula-tilaka tvam asīha |
children.translated_text: 'O ornament of the family of the lord of <s>Gokula</s>, you are here!

children.text: kṛta-sukṛta-vraja-racita-sukha-vraja, nayanānandi-samīha ||dhru||
children.translated_text: O you who have fashioned a multitude of joys in <s>Vraja</s> through accumulated merit, O delight of the eyes! ||refrain||

children.text: ānandodbhava-janma-mahotsava-nandita-gopa-samāja |
children.translated_text: O you who have delighted the assembly of cowherds at the great festival of the birth born of supreme bliss!

children.text: pūta-nikāmṛti-nava-maṅgala-kṛti-valayita-gokula-rāja ||a||
children.translated_text: O king of <s>Gokula</s>, encircled by the acts of new auspiciousness of purified overflowing nectar!

children.text: dhairya-nivartana-śakaṭa-vivartanam anu bhavyena parīta |
children.translated_text: After the overturning of the cart (<s>Śakaṭa</s>), which dispelled all courage, you were surrounded by the auspicious!

children.text: satṛṇāvartaka-vāyu-nivartaka-parameśenānīta ||b||
children.translated_text: You were brought by the supreme Lord who reversed the wind of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s> along with [him]!

children.text: madhura-prāṅgaṇa-viracita-riṅgana jalaja-nayana supuṇya |
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one of great merit, who performed crawling in the sweet courtyard!

children.text: nānā-keliṣu nṛtya-kalāliṣu darśita-vara-naipuṇya ||c||
children.translated_text: You who displayed excellent skill in dancing arts amidst various sports!

children.text: tarṇaka-vāladhi-śabalita-tanvadhi-valayita-mañjula-śobha |
children.translated_text: O you of beautiful splendor, entwined about the body variegated by the tails of young calves!

children.text: jaratī-nivahe kautuka-kalahe prabalita-mithyā-lobha ||d||
children.translated_text: You who stirred up playful rivalry and false greed among the old women!

children.text: māṃ mātaram anu sukham udvitanu pratataṃ satataṃ kṛṣṇa |
children.translated_text: O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, extend happiness toward me, your mother, constantly and always!

children.text: drutam urarīkuru tanu-vṛddhiṃ puru-khelāvali-kṛta-tṛṣṇa ||e||
children.translated_text: Quickly accept bodily growth, O you who are thirsting for an abundance of play!

children.text:
tribhuvana-darśana-vismaya-marśana-niścita-vaiṣṇava-māya |
  hari-varivasyā-sukhadatamaḥ syā vigata-jarāmara-kāya ||f|| ||JGc_1,8.2|| | iti | [8 x 8 x 11]
children.translated_text:
O you whose marveling and touching of the vision of the three worlds has confirmed <s>Vaiṣṇava Māyā</s>!
May you be the supreme bestower of the joy of serving <s>Hari</s>, free from old age and death in body!' ||8.2|| Thus. [8 x 8 x 11]

children.text: atha labdha-jāgaraḥ sa nityatā-śāli-lālitya-sāgaraḥ sapadi rudann iva samutthitavān, mātaram itavāṃś ca, yathā,
children.translated_text: Then he, having awakened — that ocean of ever-flowing gracefulness — suddenly rose up as if crying, and went toward his mother, as follows:

children.text:
dīrgha-śvāsaṃ gātra-moṭa-prayuktaṃ
  netre mārjan jāgrad ambeti jalpan |
  krandan mantha-dhvānam ākarṇya bālaḥ
  śrī-gopālaḥ praskhalaṃs tāṃ jagāma ||JGc_1,8.3|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
Heaving deep sighs, employing body-stretching,
rubbing his eyes, babbling 'Mother!' as he awakened,
crying upon hearing the sound of the churning — the child,
the glorious <s>Gopāla</s>, went stumbling toward her. ||8.3|| [rucirā]

children.text: tataś ca mātā bālyatā-ghaṭita-lālyatā-jaṭita-praṇayākula-kāku-lava-saṅkulatayā tena subhagākhaṇḍalena vighaṭite kṣubdha-daṇḍasya gati-maṇḍale svayaṃ payas-tananayoḥ stanayoḥ prasnavaṃ navakaṃ taṃ śāvakaṃ pāyayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then the mother — overwhelmed by the abundance of entreating tones produced by the affection-laden tenderness fashioned by his childhood — when the orbit of the churning-rod's motion was disrupted by that blessed <s>Akhaṇḍala</s> (Indra-like child), she herself suckled that little fawn with the fresh flow from her two milk-bearing breasts.

children.text:
payo varṣati dhārābhir varṣāvan medura-śriyaḥ |
  tasyāḥ payodhare suṣṭhu kṛṣṇaś cātakatāṃ gataḥ ||JGc_1,8.4|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Like a rain-cloud of resplendent beauty raining milk in streams,
her breast poured forth; <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> assumed the nature of a <s>cātaka</s> bird toward it! ||8.4|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: sā tatra gardhenārdhe tena pīte dhanye stanye netrānantara-gṛhāntara-santāpyamāna-payaḥ-santānānām utsekaṃ prati nirvivekatāṃ pratipadya sadya eva taṃ vihāya yad-drutavatī, drava-gamane tasya patana-bhītyā ca na taṃ gṛhītvā gatavatī |
children.translated_text: When, from eagerness, half of the breast-milk had been drunk by him — [the milk] blessed and nourishing — she, arriving at a state of non-discrimination regarding the overflow of the streams of milk from the inner chambers of her eyes being heated on the other side by the fire [of the boiling milk], abandoned him at once and rushed off.
