[She did] not take him along, out of fear that he might fall in the hasty running.

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-kim ittham āttha? tāvan-mātrāya tasyāḥ kathaṃ kṣut-kṣāma-gātrād bāla-putrād anyatra yātrā yukti-pātrāyatām? sā hi vatsa-vatsalānām acchatā-bhāg-upamā |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Why do you say it thus? For such a small reason, how could the departure from a child-son — thin-bodied from hunger — to somewhere else become appropriate for her? For she is the very model of unsullied tenderness among those who love their young!'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sahāsam āha sma, guro, puro' vadhīyatāṃ yad vātsalyavilāsa eva khalv ayam asyāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said with a smile: 'O Guru, attend to what is before us! For this is indeed the very sport of her maternal affection (<s>vātsalya</s>)!'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-katham iva?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'How so?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tathā hi, ye geha-dehādayas taṃ vināstamita-prāyā manyante sma, te tu taj-janmārabhya tan-mamatā-maya-mamatā eva tābhyāṃ pitṛbhyām abhyamanyanta | yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayas tvat-kṛte [BhP 10.14.35] iti brahma-vākye vraja-mātrasyāpi tathā śrūyate, kim uta tayor iti | idaṃ ca mugdhaṃ dugdhaṃ dadhi ca tad-adhika-tat-pradhānatāvadhikam eveti sa-viśeṣatayāvagamyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'For indeed, those things — house, body, and so forth — which were considered nearly eclipsed without him, those very things were, from the time of his birth, regarded by those two parents as nothing but possessiveness made of possessiveness for him. As stated in the words of <s>Brahmā</s>: "Home, wealth, friends, dear ones, self, sons, life-breath — all their purpose is for You" [BhP 10.14.35] — this is heard even of the mothers of <s>Vraja</s>, how much more then of those two [parents]! And this — whether milk, yogurt, or the like — is understood with the special qualification that it has an even greater predominance for him.'

children.text:
tad evaṃ sati tasyāḥ seyaṃ bhāvanā- kleśam api viṣahya spṛhyamāṇāṃ nānā-nija-gṛhya-kriyāṃ sāmprataṃ na jānāti so' yaṃ bālaka iti dayanīyatayāsmadīyam eva khalv etadīya-kṛtyaṃ kṛtyam iti | so' yam evaṃ-vidha-sneha-vividha-vidhis tair eva boddhum adhyavasyate yaiḥ kṛtaṃ tarjana-tāḍanādikam api lālanā-mayatāṃ kalayati, kim utānyat? yataḥ,
  snehataḥ kvacana ruṭ prajāyate
  tasya vardhana-karī ca dṛśyate |
  medure' pi mudire tathā tathā
  vidyud-agnir asakṛd vivartate ||JGc_1,8.5|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
This being so, her reasoning was as follows: 'Enduring even hardship, the various domestic duties that are being desired — he, this child, does not know them at present; therefore, as he is pitiable, this duty for him is indeed our own duty!' Such is this manifold regulation of love of this kind; it is to be understood only by those very ones for whom even scolding and striking constitute forms of fondling — what then of other things? For:
From love, in some case, anger arises,
and that too is seen to be its nourisher;
in a cloud too, dense and wet with beauty,
lightning-fire repeatedly flashes! ||8.5|| [rathoddhatā]

children.text: tathā hi, tayor mitho hitayor ubhayor api caritam | dugdhāya gamana-samaye sā khalu tan-muditatā-nibandhanam idam uditavatī, vatsa, nirmañchanaṃ bhajāmi, kṣaṇaṃ tāvan manthana-gargarī rakṣatām, tvadīyaṃ payo vīkṣya yāvad drutam aham āyāmi iti | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: For indeed, the conduct of those two, mutually well-wishing, was as follows: At the time of going out for the milk, she, on account of his delight, spoke thus: 'Dear child, I am going to churn; guard the churning-pot for a moment, while I quickly return after seeing to your milk!' And then:

children.text:
yāvad vihāya pṛthukaṃ bata manthanāntād
  ambā yayau drutam asau tata āyayau ca |
  tāvat payodhara-yugaṃ hṛdaya-stha-vastra-
  knopaṃ vavarṣa pathi picchilatā yathāsīt ||JGc_1,8.6|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
As soon as the mother left the little one from beside the churning and went quickly, and then came back,
her pair of breasts, with the cloth-knot over her heart, rained [milk] on the path — such was the wetness! ||8.6|| [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tad evam api sa tu nijārthite pratyarthite bhṛśam āvijate sma, yathā-
  tenātha kopa-sphuritāruṇādharaṃ
  sandaśya dadbhyām udasarji rodanam |
  daṇḍāhatāmatram akhaṇḍi cāśmanā
  nālambhi tasmin navanītam aṇv api ||JGc_1,8.7|| [vaṃśastha]
children.translated_text:
Even so, he, having been thwarted in his desire, was greatly agitated, as follows:
Then, biting his quivering reddened lower lip with his teeth in anger,
he let loose a cry;
with a stone he broke just the base of the churning [vessel],
and did not touch even a bit of the butter therein! ||8.7|| [vaṃśastha]

children.text:
atra tu varṇayanti,
  dantendu-lekhāviśad ādharāruṇaṃ
  cakṣuś-cakora-dvayam aśru cādadhe |
  tadā śiśor asya karāmbu-janmanāpy
  ariṣṭam uddhūya balād vijṛmbhitam ||JGc_1,8.8|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Here they describe:
The redness of his lower lip, radiant with the crescent-marks of his teeth,
and his pair of <s>cakora</s>-bird-like eyes took on tears;
then, even by the water born of the child's hands,
the ill-omen was forcefully dispelled and [auspiciousness] blossomed forth! ||8.8|| [upajāti]

children.text: tad evaṃ kalaśāntarīṇe kālaśeye sarvato rīṇe parvāntaram api jātam, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the contents of the pot had completely flowed away and an interval had also occurred, as follows:

children.text:
tato gṛhābhyantara-śikya-lakṣitaṃ
  haiyaṅgavīnaṃ parigṛhya yatnataḥ |
  jaghāsa tatrorvaritaṃ tu pakṣaka-
  dvāreṇa nihnutya jahāra keśavaḥ ||JGc_1,8.9|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then, seizing the <s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> (fresh butter) spotted in a hanging pot inside the house with great effort,
<s>Keśava</s> devoured it; the remainder he stole away through a side door, concealing [his deed]! ||8.9|| [upajāti]

children.text:
sa ca yatno, yathā-
  kuñcīkṣepād argalām antaraṅgām
  alpāṃ muñcan sadma gatvā yuyoja |
  kṛtvā khaṭṭāṃ tatra niḥśreṇikābhāṃ
  kṛtvā sarpir guptam añcann apāgāt ||JGc_1,8.10|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
And that effort was as follows:
Releasing the small inner bolt by tossing a key, going into the chamber, he contrived [an entry];
making a cot there serve as a ladder,
reaching for the hidden butter, he drew it out and departed! ||8.10|| [śālinī]

children.text:
tataḥ kṣaṇād dugdham itaṃ tu mugdhatām
  ādhāya mātā sutam āgamad drutam |
  aprāpya taṃ tasya tu karma tad-vidhaṃ
  buddhvā sa-kopaṃ sa-sukhaṃ jahāsa sā ||JGc_1,8.11|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then, in a moment, the milk having overflowed, the mother, assuming an air of innocence,
came quickly to her son;
not finding him, but perceiving his deed of that kind,
she laughed — with anger and with delight together! ||8.11|| [upajāti]

children.text:
tatra prathamaṃ śaṅkā-saṅkasukāyāṃ tasyāṃ yogamāyā-prakāśitākāśa-vāg eva hāsa-prakāśanasya bodhasya kāraṇaṃ jātam | [19] sā yathā-
  śiśu-madhu-kṛd atakṣan madhv asiddhaṃ pipāsan
  sarasija-mukulādhaś chedam ācarya paśyan |
  drava-vigalana-mātraṃ tatra nirvidya madhye
  kamalam aparam añcan prāpa tasmin madhūni ||JGc_1,8.12|| [mālinī]
kiṃ ca,
  śamayāñcakṛṣe dugdhaṃ
kṣubhitaṃ tat tava sudakṣatā kalitā |
  śamayasi yadi śiśu-kopaṃ
tādṛśam uccais tadā praśasyethāḥ ||JGc_1,8.13|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
There, when she was initially in a state mingled with doubt, a voice from the sky revealed by <s>Yogamāyā</s> itself became the cause of the laughter-revealing knowledge. [19] That [voice] was as follows:
'The child-bee, carving [at] honey, thirsting for unripe honey,
performing the cutting of a lotus-bud below, and looking —
seeing merely the flowing of liquid there, becoming disenchanted midway,
reaching for another lotus, he found honey in that one!' ||8.12|| [mālinī]
Moreover:
'You managed to calm the agitated milk —
your great skill is acknowledged!
If you calm the anger of the child,
then you would be praised most highly indeed!' ||8.13|| [udgīti]

children.text: tad evaṃ śrutvā hasitvā kālaśeya-leśādhyavaseyatānapahnava-caraṇa-cihnam īkṣitvā sādhakatamāntareṇa dvāra-yantraṃ mocayitvā ca sā punar evam ācacāra-
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard [this], having laughed, having observed the foot-prints — the tell-tale marks — of the butter-thief's concealment effort, and having opened the door-mechanism by the most effective means, she then did as follows:

children.text:
gatvā gṛhābhyantaram anyad apy asau
  dṛṣṭvā sutasyātula-cāpalaṃ prasūḥ |
  tadīya-vartmānugamena ca kramād
  ālokayal lola-vilocanaṃ ca tam ||JGc_1,8.14|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Going inside the house, seeing yet another [mischief] — the incomparable mischief of her son — the mother,
following his trail, gradually
beheld him too, with his darting eyes. ||8.14|| [upajāti]

children.text:
tatra lola-vilocanatvam, yathā-
  havir abhihṛtavān ihāsmi dṛśyaḥ
  katham atha mātaram īkṣaṇaṃ nayāni |
  iti nayana-yugaṃ śruti-dvayāntar
  muhur iva veśayati sma bāla-kṛṣṇaḥ ||JGc_1,8.15|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
There, the darting of his eyes was as follows:
'I have taken the butter here and am visible —
how then shall I direct my gaze toward mother?'
Thus, baby <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> repeatedly tucked
his pair of eyes between his two ears, as it were! ||8.15|| [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text:
adho-mukhī-kṛtya balād udūkhalaṃ
  niviśya tasyopari cañcalekṣaṇam |
  kīśāya sarpir dadataṃ prasūḥ sutaṃ
  vīkṣya smitaṃ prāpa tathā ca vismitam ||JGc_1,8.16|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Having forcefully turned a mortar upside-down
and seated upon it — with darting glances —
the mother beheld her son giving butter to a monkey,
and attained both a smile and astonishment! ||8.16|| [upajāti]

children.text:
gūḍhaṃ pratasthe kṛta-moṣam ātmajaṃ
  dhartuṃ prasūr eṣa nirīkṣya cādravat |
  prasiddhir eṣā khalu lokataḥ śataṃ
  dṛśor mataṃ hartari bhartari dvayam ||JGc_1,8.17|| [upajāti 12]
sa khalu dṛptaḥ śākhā-mṛgas tu navanītānāṃ tṛptaḥ paṭa-veṣṭita-yaṣṭim etāṃ dṛṣṭvā drutam eva śākhām ārūḍhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Indeed, the proud monkey, satisfied with the butter, upon seeing this stick wrapped in cloth, quickly climbed up a branch.

children.text:
atha dravantaṃ sutam anvagāt prasūḥ
  prasūna-vṛṣṭi-pratha-keśa-bandhanā |
  kva yāsi re coravareti jalpitā
  nātisphuṭa-krandana-hāsa-sundaram ||JGc_1,8.18|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then the mother pursued her running son,
her hair-binding loosened by the shower of blossoms;
'Where are you going, you thief!' — thus she called,
with an indistinct blend of crying and laughter, beautiful! ||8.18|| [upajāti]

children.text:
tokaṃ dhartuṃ sā samīpe' pi śīghraṃ
  dhāvantī tat prāpa dhāvan na mātā |
  prāgañcantaṃ vāyu-vegāt pratīcī
  stokāmbhodaṃ yadvad ambhoda-vīthī ||JGc_1,8.19|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: She ran swiftly to catch the child even nearby, yet the running mother could not reach that running one — like a bank of clouds [chasing] from the west a small cloud blown ahead by the force of the wind! // [śālinī]

children.text:
atha pura-dvāraṃ na mātur gamana-dvāram iti matvā palāyana-grahilas tad-diśam eva jagrāha | jananī tu tadānīṃ tatrājanatāṃ jānatī tam evānuyātavatī | tataś ca,
  yadādravat pṛṣṭham anīkṣamāṇas
  tadā na lebhe pṛthuko jananyā |
  yadā bhayād vīkṣitavān sa paścāt
  tadā tayāsau jagṛhe kareṇa ||JGc_1,8.20|| [upendravajrā]
children.translated_text:
Then, thinking that the house-gate was not his mother's path of approach, the one eager to flee seized that very direction. But the mother, knowing his unknowing [of her approach], followed him. And then:
When the little one ran without looking back, then he could not be caught by his mother; but when out of fear he looked behind — then she seized him by the hand! // [upendravajrā]

children.text:
sa ca tathāpi-
  akṣiṇī drava-gamāya sākṣiṇī
  rodanaṃ krud-udaya-praṇodanam |
  cālanaṃ vapuṣi dhārṣṭya-pālanaṃ
  sṛṣṭavān avinayaṃ na mṛṣṭavān ||JGc_1,8.21|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
And even then, he —
Eyes as witnesses for the swift escape, weeping as the impeller of rising anger, squirming of the body as the guardian of boldness — he produced all this misbehavior but did not tolerate it! // [svāgatā]

children.text:
nirmame prasabham ambayā mukhaṃ
  sammukhaṃ nijaśiśor yadā yadā |
  sarpir-arpita-vilepanaṃ tadā
  rūkṣaṇāya tad aghukṣad eṣa ca ||JGc_1,8.22|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: Whenever the mother forcibly brought her face close to her child's face, then the ghee-smeared ointment [on his face] — he rubbed it [on her] to make it dry! // [svāgatā]

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And then —

children.text:
vaṣṭi ced bata bhavān gṛha-muṣṭiṃ
  yaṣṭim ākalaya mat-kara-mṛṣṭām |
  ittham uccakitite kamalākṣe
  tāṃ jahau nijajahau vraja-rājñī ||JGc_1,8.23|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: 'If indeed you desire the household goods, O sir, then take this stick polished by my hand!' — When the lotus-eyed one was thus frightened, the queen of <s>Vraja</s> abandoned that [stick] and abandoned her own [anger]! // [svāgatā]

children.text:
mā meti vadatā tena, cora coreti gīḥ-kalim |
  rahasā saha sā rājñī sahasā sahasātanot ||JGc_1,8.24|| [anuṣṭubh]
  aho rājāsi corāṇāṃ, corās tvat-pitṛ-gotrajāḥ |
  ity ādy acakalan mātā śiśunā gavya-coriṇā ||JGc_1,8.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
As he said 'Don't! Don't!' (<s>mā mā</s>), she, the queen, together with a secret [laugh], suddenly created a quarrel of words [by saying] 'Thief! Thief!' (<s>cora cora</s>). // [anuṣṭubh]
'Oh, you are king of thieves! The thieves are born of your father's lineage!' — such and more the mother composed for the child who was a stealer of dairy products! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text:
dadhi-maṇḍaḥ kathaṃ khaṇḍo? daṇḍo' yaṃ parameśituḥ |
  ghṛtaṃ kīśāya kaḥ prādād? asau yena vinirmitaḥ ||JGc_1,8.26|| [anuṣṭubh] iti |
children.translated_text: 'How is the whey broken? This is the staff of the Supreme Lord! Who gave ghee to the monkey? The one by whom he was created!' // [anuṣṭubh] — thus.

children.text:
śaṅke svāduṅkāram itthaṃ sadā tvaṃ
  yajñāṅgīyaṃ lekṣi haiyaṅgavīnam |
  evaṃ coraṅkāram ambā śiśuṃ taṃ
  praty ākrośanty ārdra-cittā babhūva ||JGc_1,8.27|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: 'I suspect that you, always making sweet sounds, will lick up this sacrificial fresh butter!' — Thus the mother, scolding that child as a thief-maker, became tender-hearted. // [śālinī]

children.text: tataḥ sa-saṃrambhaṃ vihasya, sarahasyam ucyatām, dambhaś ca mucyatām iti mātrā pṛṣṭaḥ sṛṣṭa-rodana-netraḥ putra uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, laughing with agitation, when asked by the mother — 'Speak the secret and abandon the pretense!' — the son, with eyes producing tears, said loudly:

children.text:
tvayy udbhaṭaṃ pradravantyām aṅghryāḥ kaṭaka-ghaṭṭanāt |
  asphuṭad dadhi-maṇḍasya ghaṭaḥ, kā mama dhṛṣṭatā? ||JGc_1,8.28|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kīśo' yam īśa-nirdiṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaḥ sadma muṣṭaye |
  kṛṣṭaḥ sarpiḥ-parāmṛṣṭo mayā, kā mama duṣṭatā? ||JGc_1,8.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tathāpi tvām ātta-yaṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭvā dudrava coravat |
  tvaṃ punar māṃ vṛthā bhītam api dudrotha nirdayam ||JGc_1,8.30|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'When you were rushing out impetuously, from the striking of the anklet on [your] foot, the pot of whey cracked — what is my audacity in that? // [anuṣṭubh]
This monkey, directed by the Lord, entered the house to steal; I dragged him away from the ghee he had touched — what is my wickedness in that? // [anuṣṭubh]
Even so, seeing you with stick raised, he fled like a thief; but you then chased even me, though frightened without cause, mercilessly!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha sānutāpam iva mātā prāha-re vāco-yuktimattama corottama! tvaṃ narottama-jāto' pi vānara-priyo vānara-prakṛtir evāsi |
children.translated_text: Then the mother spoke as if with remorse: 'O you most clever with words, O supreme thief! Though born of the best of men (<s>Narottama</s>), you are fond of monkeys and are indeed of monkey-nature!'

children.text: sutas tu sa-bhayaṃ sabhaya-pradānam apy uvāca-tato vanam eva praviśya sthāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: But the son said with fear, offering even fearful gifts: 'Then I shall enter the forest itself and stay there!'

children.text: atha mātā sabhayaṃ cintitavatī, ko jānīyāt, kuryād apīdaṃ mānī | tarhi tan-nibandhanaṃ bandhanam eva sandheyam, yad ekayā mayālaya-bālayor avadhānaṃ durdhānaṃ bhavitā | [29] spaṣṭaṃ tv idam uktavatī-
children.translated_text: Then the mother thought anxiously: 'Who knows — this proud one might actually do this! Then the binding must be arranged on his account, for it would be difficult for me alone to keep watch over the house-children.' [29] And she said this plainly:

children.text:
re caura cañcala-vilola-vilocana-śrī-
  nikṣipta-moha manuṣe vinivāraṇaṃ na |
  baddhvā bhavantam aham āśu calāmi gehaṃ,
  śaktir yadi prathayatāṃ kuru cauryam anyat ||JGc_1,8.31|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: 'O thief of wavering, trembling, beautiful-eyed charm, who casts enchantment upon people — there is no restraining [you]! Having bound you, I shall quickly go about the house — if you have the power, then display it and commit another theft!' // [vasantatilakā]

children.text: bandhodyame ruṣitatā-ruṣitaḥ putraḥ phut-kurvann iva sāsram uccair uvāca-amba, rohiṇi, saha sahajena kva gatāsi? tvayā rahitaṃ mām iyaṃ badhnāti, tad drutam iha samehi |
children.translated_text: When she undertook to bind him, the son, angered at her anger, making a 'phut' sound, said loudly with tears: 'Mother <s>Rohiṇī</s>, where have you gone with [my] elder brother? This one binds me, abandoned by you — so come here quickly!'

children.text: tad etad dūragatayā tayā nāvadhāryate sma, kintu parāḥ pāramparyeṇāvadhārya kṛtopālambha-caryāḥ kāścin nikaṭa-nikāyyā nāryaḥ parivārya militāḥ | sva-vācam iha smārayitum aikāgārikaḥ so' yaṃ bhavad-agāre' pi kāṃ kārim akārṣīt iti sūcayantya iva saha jahasuś ca |
children.translated_text: But that [call] was not heeded by her who had gone far away; however, other women, learning [of it] through hearsay, having performed the customary scolding, some women from the nearby neighborhood surrounded him and gathered. As if to remind him of his own words [said] here, and as if indicating 'this housebreaker — what mischief has he done in your houses too?' — they laughed together with him.

children.text: tatas tad anavadadhatī kuntala-santāna-bandhād vighaṭitāṃ paṭṭa-ḍorīm ekām upasādya, sadyaḥ sadma-dvārāntar upasadyamānam udūkhalam anu vatsa-gala-bandhavad alagnam evāvalagne sa-nirbandhaṃ bandhum udyatavatī, stanandhayaṃ śikṣā-jananī jananī | sā tu dvy-aṅgulāṅga-nyūnājani |
children.translated_text: Then she, not heeding that, unfastening a single silk cord loosened from the binding of [her] hair-braids, approaching the mortar standing near the house-door, undertook to bind it firmly around his waist, attached just as a rope around a calf's neck — the mother who was a disciplining mother for the suckling child. But that [cord] fell short by two finger-breadths of his body.

children.text: tataś ca tasyā dhammillād udvāsyānyasyā vinyastatve' pi tad-avasthatāyāṃ dṛśyamānāyāṃ sāścaryam iva nāry-arpitair manthana-netrair bahubhir api pāraṃ na vavrāja vrajeśvarī | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, even when another [cord] was unwound from her hair-knot and added, and the same state was seen [still too short], the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, wondrously, did not reach the end even with many churning-ropes given by the women. And then —

children.text:
tad-aṅge dvy-aṅgulābhāse sarve labdhāvakāśakāḥ |
  dṛśyante sma vaṭās tatra vidūrādrau ghanā iva ||JGc_1,8.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: In that body appearing [only] two finger-breadths [short], all the ropes found their scope; those ropes were seen there like dense banyan trees on a distant mountain! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad etat paśyantībhiḥ parihasantībhir uktam, vraja-devi, niveditam evāsmābhiḥ; sa eṣa samunnatayā mohanatayā kaphallakam api vellayan loptra-mātra-sukalatānandī parāskandī sandīpyate iti |
children.translated_text: The onlooking, laughing women said: 'O queen of <s>Vraja</s>, we have indeed reported [it]; this one, by his towering enchanting power, shaking even a hood-cap, delighting in the felicity of a mere rope-measure, is a great jumper — he is inflamed [with mischief]!'

children.text: sā prāha-kiṃ jānāty asāv adya-jātaḥ, kintu bhavatīnām eva kāpīyam avadyāvidyā yad antar asya pakṣa-pātinyaḥ samīkṣyadhve, bahir evānyathā vyavahāratayā viharantyaḥ stha |
children.translated_text: She said: 'What does this one know, born just today? Rather, it is some disreputable skill of yours — that inwardly you are seen as his partisans, while outwardly you go about pretending otherwise!'

children.text: sarvāḥ sahāsam ūcuḥ, tatrabhavati, bhavac-caraṇebhyaḥ śapatham ācarāmaḥ, nāsmākaṃ vismāpikeyaṃ vidyā vidyate iti |
children.translated_text: All said with a laugh: 'O revered lady, we swear by your feet — we do not possess this astonishing skill!'

children.text: sā ca cetasi vicāram ācacāra, tarhi garga-vacana-vargavat sakṛt kāpi bhāgavatī śaktir evāmum avaruṇaddhi, na cāyaṃ kiñcid api jānāti |
children.translated_text: And she pondered in her mind: 'Then, as in the collection of <s>Garga's</s> words, some divine <s>Bhāgavatī</s> power alone restrains this one, and he himself knows nothing of it.'

children.text: atheyam asyāścaryasya paryantaṃ paryālocituṃ tābhir eva gṛhād anyāny api manthana-dāmāni muhur muhur ānāyya sanirbandhaṃ bandham ādadhaty api gaty-antaraṃ na prāpa | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then she, attempting to reach the end of this wonder, having them bring yet more churning-ropes from other houses again and again, though binding with determination — found no alternative. And then —

children.text:
badhnatī na tu sutaṃ vrajeśvarī
  pāram āpa tad apāra-karmaṇaḥ |
  gharma-vāri-varimāṇam āvrajad
  vāra-vāram alakāvṛtīr api ||JGc_1,8.33|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: The queen of <s>Vraja</s>, binding but unable to bind the son, did not reach the end of that one of limitless deeds; perspiration flowed in torrents, and even the curls covering [her forehead] came undone again and again! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
tato yāvad eva yādava-deva-kulajasya tasya haṭhavattāyāṃ prayatnādhīr āsīt, tāvat tad-āgraho' pi graha-nigṛhīta ivābhūt | mātṛ-vaikalyena kalyamāna-manastve tu prathama-ḍorikā-dvaya-mātra-sambaddha-gātratayā baddha eva so' yam abudhyata | anyāni tu sarvāṇi dāmāni tasminn urvaritāny evādṛśyanta | [40] yogamāyā-nāminī tat-karma-kāriṇī hi tan-mano' nusāriṇī, yayā tan niṣpādya mātaraṃ praty, api bhrama evāyam iti pratyayaḥ pratyaham āsādyata | [41] atha labdha-sandhaṃ taṃ bandhaṃ dīrghatamayānyayā rajjvābadhya ca tayā tad-udūkhala-madhyaṃ babandha | [42] baddhvā ca mātā śikṣāṃ ghaṭayantī nija-kaṭhinatām eva tasmin haṭhini prakaṭayantī tābhir vihasantībhiḥ saha sa-narma-geha-karmaṇe gacchantī, tat-paripālanāya bālakān paritaḥ sthāpitavatī
|
children.translated_text: Then, just when she was exhausted in her effort at his stubbornness, at that point his own obstinacy too became as if seized by a planet [i.e., subdued]. And through the mother's distress, when his mind became compassionate, being bound with only two initial cords around his body, he himself understood that he was bound. But all the other ropes were seen remaining loose upon him. [40] For the one named <s>Yogamāyā</s>, the agent of that deed, followed his mind — and having accomplished that, she produced in the mother, day after day, the conviction: 'This was merely an illusion.' [41] Then, having obtained a settled binding, she tied him with the longest rope of all and bound him to the middle of that mortar. [42] And having bound him, the mother, applying discipline, displaying her own firmness toward that stubborn one, went together with those laughing women to the housework with playfulness, having stationed young boys around him for his guarding.

children.text: tataś ca gatāsu tāsu kṣaṇaṃ kṛta-rodana-vinodaḥ, paścād bahala-khalaṃ praty udūkhala-nodanāya labdha-modaḥ sa tu baddha eva kevala-bāla-valitatayā prabalita-cāpala-śraddhas taiḥ saha prahasan khelann ulūkhalam etaṃ laghu laghu cālayām āsa, hārayāmāsa ca tair evolbaṇa-hāsatayā śulva-hāriṇīnāṃ labdha-śūnya-sādharmya-harmya-śreṇyā hāri-śikyita-nava-nava-nītādikam āhārayāmāsa ca | kintu, tat-karṣaṇa-maya-harṣa-prada-līlayā na ca kareṇa na cāpareṇa tad-uddāna-mocana-rocanatām avāpa |
children.translated_text: Then, when they had gone, he entertained himself with weeping for a moment; afterwards, filled with delight at pushing the mortar toward the thick thicket, that bound one — with the strength empowered only by childish caprice — laughing and playing with those [boys], slowly, slowly moved the mortar along, and had them steal — by their own outrageous laughter, [giving] them the likeness of the empty houses in a row [whose owners were] rope-givers — the fresh butter and the like hanging in swinging-nets; and he too helped himself! But through his play of dragging [the mortar] with delight, neither by one hand nor the other did he find it pleasing to undo the bonds of the enclosure.

children.text: tatra tu pura-dvāra-purastād-varti vātāvarta-vartita-nartanam iva yamalam arjuna-dvayam asya netra-vartmani vartate sma | krameṇa cāsau tayor antara eva vikramate sma iti |
children.translated_text: There, in front of the house-gate, stood a pair of <s>Arjuna</s> trees, as if dancing whirled by a whirlwind, in the path of his vision. And gradually he was advancing right between those two.

children.text: etāvan mukta-kaṇṭham uṭṭaṅkayan snigdhakaṇṭhas tad-bhañjane kāraṇaṃ harer aiśvarya-pracāraṇam iti tat pratārayan kāraṇāntaram eva vyājahāra- [46] tataḥ sphuṭaṃ jhaṭiti parataḥ paryaṭitum utkaṇṭhayā tan-madhya-sambaddhenaivādhvanā niścakrāma, tad-adhvanas tu saṅkṣiptatayādhaḥ-kṣiptatayā tad udūkhalaṃ pratitaṣṭambhe |
children.translated_text: At this point, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, exclaiming with full throat, proclaiming that the cause of their breaking was the display of <s>Hari's</s> divine majesty — while hinting at that, spoke of another cause entirely: [46] 'Then, manifestly, with the sudden longing to wander beyond, he went out on the very path bound between them [the trees], and because of its being shortened and dragged downward, that mortar became wedged [between them].'

children.text: atha sphuṭam asau vaṭītroṭanecchayā tat kṛṣṭavān | haṭhād ākṛṣṭe ca tasmin-
children.translated_text: Then, clearly, he pulled [the mortar] with the desire to break the rope. And when it was pulled with force —

children.text:
kuṭha-dvayaṃ kaṭakaṭa-śabda-mugja-
  vighaṭṭitaṃ sphuṭam aluṭhad dvayor diśoḥ |
  na dhī-dhṛtiṃ vadhira-vimugdhatām adhi
  vrajann adhi vrajam adadhāt prajā-vrajaḥ ||JGc_1,8.34|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: The two trunks, with cracking, crashing sounds struck apart, fell manifestly in two directions; the host of people in <s>Vraja</s>, going into a state of deafness and bewilderment, could not maintain steadiness of mind or composure! // [rucirā]

children.text:
citraṃ tutroṭa tat tatra vajra-majjārjuna-dvayam |
  na punar mātṛ-vātsalya-nirbandha-maya-bandhanam ||JGc_1,8.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Wondrously, that pair of <s>Arjuna</s> trees with diamond-hard cores broke there, but not the bond made of the force of maternal affection! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: ślokayanti cātra-
children.translated_text: And they compose verses here —

children.text:
śyāmāṅga-dyuti kiṅkiṇi-dhvani-dharaṃ riṅgātiraṅga-pradaṃ
  karṣac chaśvad udūkhalaṃ khara-kharat-kāra-prakāra-pratham |
  visphūrja-pratimārjuna-dvaya-kaṭat-kārārjitāt kautukāt
  paryāvṛtta-nirīkṣaṇaṃ vraja-vadhū-lālyasya bālyaṃ stuve ||JGc_1,8.36|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: Dark-limbed in radiance, bearing the sound of little bells, giving delight in the sport of crawling, constantly dragging the mortar with the spreading clamor of harsh scraping sounds — from the curiosity gained by the crashing fall of the thundering pair of <s>Arjuna</s> trees, looking back with turned gaze — I praise the childhood of the darling of the women of <s>Vraja</s>! // [śārdūla]

children.text: atha tayor atyūrjitena visphūrjitena muhūrtārdham ārtatayā goṣṭhādhiṣṭhānā mūrcchām ṛcchantaḥ sthitāḥ, tan-nikaṭa-saṅghaṭṭinīm arbhaka-ghaṭāṃ vinā | sā tu tal-līlā-mādhurī-dhurīṇatayā citrākṛtir iva mitrāvalī na vitrāsam āsasāda | [50] dūrād api tad-ūrjitaṃ visphūrjitaṃ sambhrama-kāry avadhārya tu vraja-pati-mukhās tarkita-mukhās tad evābhipratasthire | satrā sa-trāsam atrābhidadhire ca-
children.translated_text: Then, by the extremely powerful crashing of those two [trees], the inhabitants of the cow-settlement stood as if fainting with distress for half a <s>muhūrta</s> (24 minutes) — except for the group of little children clinging near him. That [group], by the preeminence of the sweetness of his play, like a circle of friends in a picture, did not experience terror. [50] But those led by the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, perceiving even from afar that powerful crash as cause for alarm, with anxious faces, set forth toward that very place. And there, with trembling, they said:

children.text:
vinā vātaṃ vinā varṣaṃ vidyut-prapatanaṃ vinā |
  vinā hasti-kṛtaṃ doṣaṃ kenemau pātitau drumau? ||JGc_1,8.37|| [anuṣṭubh]
  ajanya-janyam etāvaj jātā nirjanatā kutaḥ? |
  tasmāt tasmān mahā-garjān mūrcchām ārcchan vraje janāḥ ||JGc_1,8.38|| iti |
 [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Without wind, without rain, without the fall of lightning, without damage done by an elephant — by whom were these two trees felled?' // [anuṣṭubh]
'This much destruction, not caused by any known cause — whence came this desolation? From that, from that great thunder, the people of <s>Vraja</s> obtained fainting!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: avadadhire ca tan-nikaṭa-taṭasthaṃ bhāsamāna-hāsa-vilāsa-mukham ulūkhalaṃ karṣantaṃ līlā-sukhaṃ varṣantaṃ bāla-gopālam | tena ca, kathaṃ, kathaṃ? iti kathayantas tam āvṛnvanta evāvatasthire |
children.translated_text: And they perceived the child <s>Gopāla</s>, standing near those [fallen trees], his face shining with the sport of a smile, dragging the mortar, showering the joy of play. And saying 'How? How?' — narrating [events to each other], they stood surrounding him.

children.text: sa tu pitaram anuvindamānam anucakranda | [53] pitā cāntaḥ-sambhrāntaḥ sann api tasya sāntvanāya mukha-mātraṃ hasita-pātram ācarann acirād eva taṃ vipāśayāmāsa | [54] sa-rodana-vadanaṃ vadanaṃ cumban vidann api muhuḥ papraccha ca, putra, kutratyaḥ sa khalu khala-buddhir yena colūkhale nirbandha-janita-baddhas tvam asi? iti |
children.translated_text: He (Kṛṣṇa), finding his father approaching, cried out after him. [53] And the father, though inwardly agitated, merely made his face a vessel of smiling for the child's comfort, and very soon put him at ease. [54] Kissing the tear-stained face, though knowing, he asked again and again: "Son, from where is that wicked-minded one by whom you have been bound, tied to the mortar through forcible constraint?"

children.text: sa tu pitari rataś cirataḥ śliṣṭa-kaṇṭhatayābhyarṇam āgataḥ karṇe varṇayāmāsa, tāta, mātaiva iti |
children.translated_text: But he (Kṛṣṇa), attached to his father, having come near with arms clasped around his neck for a long time, described in his ear: "Father, it was mother herself."

children.text: pitā tu tāṃ pūrvaṃ vigata-saṃvedatayā anantaraṃ tu svata eva jāta-nirvedatayā dūnāṃ veda sma | tata eva na sahasā rahasāpi paribhāṣitum iyeṣa | ajñatayāvajñayā na ca papraccha bālakān, kim idaṃ vṛttam? iti |
children.translated_text: The father, however, understood her — formerly as having lost her composure, and then as having become filled with remorse of her own accord. Therefore he did not wish to reproach her suddenly, even in private. And feigning ignorance, he did not ask the boys with disdain: "What has happened here?"

children.text: te tu svayam evocuḥ, sphuṭam anena kṛta-madhya-gamanena vistīrṇa-khale pura-sthale krīḍituṃ niṣkramya, vikṛṣṭa-tale tiryag-bhāvād acale cāsminn ulūkhale khaṭat-khaṭiti truṭitatām ṛcchat kuṭha-dvayaṃ jhaṭiti luṭhad-bhāvam ānarccha |
children.translated_text: But they themselves said: "Clearly, having gone out to play in the wide threshing-floor of the nearby grounds through this middle passage, and in this immovable mortar on the sloping ground, which was going 'crack-crack' and reaching the state of splitting due to the sideways pulling — a pair of <s>kuṭha</s> trees suddenly reached the state of tumbling down."

children.text: tataś ca khaṇḍitābhyām ābhyāṃ nirgatya kaṭaka-mukuṭa-kuṇḍalādi-maṇḍitau rociṣmad-vapuṣmantau śuṣmāṇau praṇamantau samantād etaṃ kim api santoṣayāmāsatuḥ | tad-uttaram uttarasyāṃ diśi prāsthiṣātām |
children.translated_text: "And then, having emerged from those two broken [trees], two resplendent, powerful beings — adorned with bracelets, diadems, earrings and the like, with shining bodies — bowing down, delighted him (Kṛṣṇa) all around with something indescribable. After that, those two set off in the northern direction."

children.text: tad etad ākalya, bālānāṃ pralāpo' yam iti vatsalāḥ kalayāmbabhūvuḥ | anye tu sāṃśayikatānapeta-cetasaḥ prajātāḥ |
children.translated_text: Understanding this, the affectionate ones considered: "This is the prattle of children." But others were born with minds not free from doubt.

children.text: tataś ca kramād eka-dvy-ādi-prakramān militena vraja-janena samaṃ vraja-bhūpālaḥ sva-bālakenāṅkaṃ sad alaṅkṛtya nitya-kṛtya-kṛte kālindīm anuvindamānas tenānuṣajya nimajya tatraiva vipraiḥ svasti-vācanādikam ācarya, mahā-dānādikaṃ visarjya, nikāyyam āsajya ca, pūrvāhna-bhojanāya sasajja |
children.translated_text: And then, gradually, in one, two and successive steps, the king of <s>Vraja</s>, together with the <s>Vraja</s> folk who had gathered, having adorned his lap with his own child, following the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) river for the daily rites, having accompanied him, having bathed there, having performed the <s>svasti-vācana</s> (benedictory recitation) and the like with the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> right there, having dispensed great gifts and the like, and having taken the bath, he prepared for the forenoon meal.

children.text: taj-jāyā tu taj-jābhyāṃ duḥkha-lajjābhyāṃ sajjatī gṛhād āgrahāc ca na niṣkrāntavatī, na ca gṛhāgatāḥ sambhāṣitavatī | sarvāsv arvāg eva nivṛttāsu, samādhānohinī rohiṇī gaurava-pātrībhiḥ paurogavībhiḥ pariveṣayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: His wife, however, bound by the pair of grief and shame, did not come out of the house even with urging, nor did she speak with those who came to the house. When all the others had returned without success, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, who was a soother of composure, had the food served by the chief women of the household who were objects of respect.

children.text: śrī-vraja-rājas tv avarātmajaṃ rāmam api samānīya tena sutena ca sārdhaṃ tayoḥ snigdha-kala-kolāhala-nidigdhaḥ sagdhim ācaritavān | tābhyāṃ mūrta-paramānanda-pūrtābhyāṃ muhūrtam ekaṃ viśramya ca samyag-īdṛg-auśīra-sukha-dhīra-cetā gavāgamana-ramya-samaye gosthānam āgamya go-dohanādi-kāryaṃ ca kārayati sma | [63] udavasitād atisitāṃ sitām ānāyya tayā sahitaṃ suhitaṃ saha sa-vayobhis tanayau stana-pāna-pratinidhitayā dhāroṣṇaṃ payaḥ pāyayāmāsa ca | śikṣayāmāsa ca tatra patra-puṭī-ghaṭanām |
children.translated_text: The glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, however, bringing the younger son <s>Rāma</s> as well, dined together with that son, immersed in their affectionate soft murmuring. And having rested for a moment with those two who were the embodiment of supreme bliss, with his mind made well, cool, and steady like <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver) — when the pleasant time of the cows' return arrived, he came to the cow-station and had the cow-milking and other tasks carried out. [63] Having brought the pure white cow <s>Sitā</s> from the milking, and together with her, having the two sons, accompanied by their age-mates, drink the warm fresh milk as a substitute for breast-feeding — he also taught them there the folding of leaf-cups.

children.text: atha punar api harmyam āgamya tābhyām ācarita-sāyam-bhojana-sukha-samāje vraja-rāje, saha-rohiṇīkās tadīya-santata-sukhābhīkāḥ svakula-māṇikya-lakṣmyaḥ sarvāḥ prāmāṇikyaḥ samāsādya nivedavatyaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, when he had come again to the mansion and the king of <s>Vraja</s> had concluded the pleasant assembly of the evening meal, <s>Rohiṇī</s> and the ladies of the family — those jewel-treasures of his own clan, all authoritative women who desired the continuous happiness of that household — approached with tidings:

children.text: rājan, kṛṣṇa-janany adya na bhuktavatī, na kenacid uktavatī ca vartate | tām anu sarvāś ca tathā vartante |
children.translated_text: "O King, <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother has not eaten today, nor has she spoken to anyone. And following her, all the others are behaving likewise."

children.text: vrajarājas saha-duḥkha-hāsam uvāca-vayaṃ kiṃ kurmaḥ? roṣam anuvartamānā svayam eva sva-doṣaṃ paśyatu |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said with a laugh mixed with compassion: "What can we do? Let her, following her anger, see her own fault herself."

children.text: sarvāḥ sāsram ūcuḥ, hanta, sā khalv antar bahir apy atikomalā tavedṛśā-lāpena tāpenātimlāsyati |
children.translated_text: All said tearfully: "Alas, she who is exceedingly tender both inside and outside will wilt excessively from the torment of such words from you!"

children.text: vrajarājas tu sa-smitaḥ sutam apṛcchat, sva-mātaraṃ yāsyasi?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s>, however, with a smile, asked his son: "Will you go to your mother?"

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-nahi nahi, kintu tvām eva samayā samayān gamayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "No, no! Rather, I shall spend time after time with you alone."

children.text: atha rāja-jyāyaḥ-prajāvatyaḥ sahāsam ūcuḥ-stanaṃ kasya pāsyasi?
children.translated_text: Then the elder wives of the king, who had children, said with laughter: "Whose breast will you drink?"

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-sitāsambhaviṣṇu dhāroṣṇaṃ payaḥ pāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "I will drink warm fresh milk that does not come from <s>Sitā</s>."

children.text: sarvā ūcuḥ-kena krīḍiṣyasi?
children.translated_text: All said: "With whom will you play?"

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tātenaiva samam | tathā bhrātaram api saṅgaṃ gamayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "With father alone. And I shall have my brother join in too."

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-bhrātur mātaraṃ kathaṃ nānugacchasi?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: "Why do you not follow your brother's mother?"

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-roṣāsram uvāca-māṃ vihāyeyam apīyāya iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with angry tears: "Because she too went away, abandoning me!"

children.text: tad etad ākarṇya sāsrā rohiṇī nīcair uvāca-putra, kathaṃ kaṭhorāyase? mātā tava duḥkhāyate |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, with tears, said softly: "Son, why do you harden yourself? Your mother grieves."

children.text: kṛṣṇas tad etad aśrṇvann iva sāsraṃ pitṛ-mukham īkṣate sma | rohiṇī tu saṅkarṣaṇaṃ tasya saṅkarṣaṇāya sañjñayā jñāpayāmāsa | tena gṛhīta-hastaḥ punar asau nirasta-tad-dhastatayā vidrutya pitur utsaṅga-saṅgī babhūva | tathābhavaṃś ca bhujābhyām avaguṇṭhita-tat-kaṇṭhaḥ kṛta-bāṣpa-vṛṣṭiṃ tad-dṛṣṭim eva paśyaṃs tam atīva vaśyam ācarann āsīt |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as if not hearing that, gazed tearfully at his father's face. <s>Rohiṇī</s> then signaled <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (Balarāma) with a gesture to draw him (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) away. Seized by the hand by him, he again, having broken free of that hand, ran and clung to his father's lap. And with arms wrapped around his father's neck, watching the tear-showered gaze of his father, he remained making him exceedingly submissive.

children.text: vraja-rājas tu mātary antaḥ-sneham asya paryālocya tad abhivyaktaye hastaṃ kiñcid udastaṃ vidhāyābhidadhe-putra, yadi vakṣi, tarhi bāḍhaṃ tāṃ tāḍayāmi |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s>, however, perceiving the inner affection for his mother in him, in order to bring it to expression, raising his hand slightly, declared: "Son, if you say so, then very well — I shall strike her!"

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu tad asahamānas tasya hastaṃ stambhayāmāsa | [79] tato vraja-rājaḥ punar vihasya nija-vatsalatayātīva sadayaṃ tadīya-mātur api hṛdayam adhiyan-putra, tava mātā yady evaṃ bhaviṣyati, tadā kiṃ kariṣyasi? ity anadhātor viruddhārthaṃ prayujya sa-parihāsam āha sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, unable to bear that, stopped his hand. [79] Then the king of <s>Vraja</s>, laughing again, with supreme tenderness born of his own fatherly love, and also reading the heart of the child's mother — "Son, if your mother were to be like this, then what would you do?" — using the word in its contrary meaning from the root 'an' (to breathe/live), he spoke with humor.

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu bālaka-bhāvenājasraṃ mātari sa-tṛṣṇaḥ sāsraṃ, kutra me mātā? tatra gamyatām iti sa-śaṅkaṃ rohiṇy-aṅkaṃ gatavān | [81] tataś ca, prahasita-kalakaleṣu sakaleṣu parama-sukhārohiṇyā rohiṇyānītaḥ so' pi veśma praviśya sa-rodana-modam ambālā-galaṃ lagnavān | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, with a child's nature, constantly longing for his mother, tearfully said: "Where is my mother? Let us go there!" — and anxiously climbed into <s>Rohiṇī's</s> lap. [81] Then, when all burst into peals of delighted laughter, brought by <s>Rohiṇī</s> — who was the ascent of supreme happiness — he too entered the house, and weeping yet joyful, clung to his mother's neck. And then —

children.text:
vatsa-mūrdhni cibukaṃ dadhatī sā
  dhenuvad valita-gharghara-śabdā |
  rodana-prathanayā dravad-ātmā
  rodayat parikarān api sarvān ||JGc_1,8.39|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
Placing her chin upon the calf's head, she,
like a cow with rolling, rumbling sounds,
her soul melting through the spreading of weeping,
made all the attendants weep as well! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.8.39, <s>svāgatā</s>]

children.text: atha tāsāṃ tv aneka-sāntvanayā labdha-śāntiḥ kiñcid vyañjita-mukha-kāntiḥ śrī-sumukha-kanyeyaṃ stanyena tanayaṃ prīṇayāmāsa | bubhuje ca sahāgrajātena tena parama-hitābhiḥ sahitā |
children.translated_text: Then, having gained peace through the many consolations of those women, with her facial radiance somewhat restored, this daughter of the glorious <s>Sumukha</s> pleased her son with her breast-milk. And she ate together with him, accompanied by the elder-born one (Balarāma), surrounded by those who were supremely devoted to her welfare.

children.text: tad ārabhya tu saṅkocaṃ upalabhya vrajarāja-locana-gocaratāṃ vāsara-trayaṃ nāsāditavatī | dināntare tu pitṛ-nideśa-pāla-bāla-gopālenaiva celāñcale gṛhītvā nītā | tad-dinaś ca sa-narmāmodaṃ dāmodaraḥ iti vraja-vadhūbhir āhūyate sma, so' yaṃ śyāma-manoharaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: From that time on, perceiving a withdrawal [from her], she did not come within the range of the king of <s>Vraja's</s> sight for three days. But on the following day, led by the child <s>Gopāla</s> himself — who guarded his father's commands — holding onto the edge of her garment, she was brought. And from that day, with affectionate jesting, the <s>Vraja</s> women called him "<s>Dāmodara</s>" (one bound by a rope around the belly), saying: "This is the dark enchanter!"

children.text:
vrajeśvarīṃ stotum apīha kovidaḥ
  ko vā bhavel lokaga-loka-saṅgrahe |
  brahmāpi sarvo' pi ramāpi yat-kalā-
  kalāṃ ca nāñcīd iti bādarāyaṇiḥ ||JGc_1,8.40|| [upajāti]
children.translated_text:
Who in the world would be competent to praise the queen of <s>Vraja</s>,
even in the gathering of all the people of the worlds?
Even <s>Brahmā</s> in his entirety, even <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) — could not reach
even a fraction of a fraction of her glory — so says <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva)! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.8.40, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: so' yam asyā bādarāyaṇinā ghaṭita-samyag-udghaṭṭanaḥ śrīmān yaśaḥ-paṭaha-śabdas trailokyam eva ślokyatayā paryaṭann asti | tathā hi, nemaṃ viriñciḥ [BhP 10.9.20] ityādi |
children.translated_text: This glorious drum-sound of her fame — whose proper exposition was fashioned by <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> — wanders through the three worlds indeed as worthy of praise. As follows: "Not him did <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā)..." [BhP 10.9.20] and so forth.

children.text: śrī-rāmas tu nijānujaṃ sa-tṛṣṇam āha sma, smarasi, bhrātar, bṛhad-vane vatsyāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Rāma</s> said to his younger brother with longing: "Do you remember, brother, we shall dwell in <s>Bṛhadvana</s> (Vṛndāvana)?"

children.text: anujo' pi sa-smitam āha sma, āṃ āṃ, tatra krīḍām api kariṣyāvaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: The younger brother too said with a smile: "Yes, yes! There we shall play too!"

children.text: atha kathakaḥ samāpanam āha-
children.translated_text: Then the narrator (<s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>) spoke the concluding verse:

children.text:
īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava gopa-maheśvara |
  yau vṛkṣāv api tau svasya divya-bhaktau vinirmame ||JGc_1,8.41|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Such a son has been born to you, O great lord of the cowherds,
who made even those two trees into his own divine devotees! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.8.41, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ vṛtte vṛtte sarve tat-tat-kathāṃ api tat-tat-parvaivānubhūya svaṃ svam āvāsam āsannavantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when each event had transpired, all the assembly-members, having experienced each respective tale at each respective festival, returned to their own respective abodes.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
dāmodarānumodo nāma
aṣṭamaṃ pūraṇam
 ||8||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the Śrī Śrī <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Eighth Chapter named "The Delight of <s>Dāmodara</s>"
||8||

children.text:
(9)
atha navamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text:
(9)
Now the Ninth Chapter.

children.text: śrī-vṛndāvana-deśe praveśaḥ
children.translated_text: The Entry into the Region of Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.

children.text: atha dināntare bhāsamānāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ śrī-vrajarājaḥ paryanuyuktavān, vatsa snigdhakaṇṭha, tau khalu vṛkṣau vraje saṅkalpa-pradatayā devatā-sadṛkṣau | tataḥ prāg-janmani kīdṛśāv, atra vā kasmād āgatau, samprati ca kīdṛśatayā kva gatau?
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, when the assembly was shining, the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> inquired: "Dear <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, those two trees in <s>Vraja</s> — tree-like in their power of granting wishes, resembling deities! So, in their previous birth, what were they like? And why did they come here? And now, in what form have they gone where?"

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-pūrvaṃ dhūrjaṭi-mitrād utpannavantau śrī-devarṣi-varye dhārṣṭyam anuṣṭhitavantau santau, pariṇāmataḥ paramānugraheṇa śrī-devarṣi-varya-kṛta-nigraheṇa vṛkṣatāyām api bhavagad-bhaktatām āgatavantau | pratibhavad-avatāram udbhavatas tasya bṛhadvana-stha-bhavad-gṛhasya tu sadeśe deśe yamalārjuna-veśena sthitavantau | etad-anantaraṃ ca nija-gatim āgatavantau parama-bhagavad-bhaktimantau ca jātavantau | samprati tu tad-bhakti-phala-vyaktim apy ākalayantau vartete |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: "Previously, having been born from <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva)'s friend (Kubera), and having committed an offense against the most excellent glorious divine sage (<s>Nārada</s>), by the culmination of his supreme grace through the restraint imposed by the divine sage, they attained devotion to the Lord even in the state of being trees. Arising at each descent (avatāra) of the Lord, at the site of his house in <s>Bṛhadvana</s>, they stood in the form of twin <s>Arjuna</s> trees. And after this [liberation], they attained their own destination and became supremely devoted to the Lord. And now, they continue to behold the manifestation of the fruit of that devotion."

children.text: vrajarājaḥ sakautukam uvāca-kathyatāṃ tathyaṃ, samprati kutra pratiyātau?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said with curiosity: "Tell the truth — where exactly have they gone now?"

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sva-mukha-kamalaṃ namayitvā tuṣṇīm iva sthitvā ca madhukaṇṭhaṃ kaṭākṣeṇekṣāñcakre |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, bowing his lotus-face, standing as if silent, glanced at <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> with a sidelong look.

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-saṅkucann iva kathaṃ nocitavān asi?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: "Why do you seem to shrink back and not speak as is proper?"

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sa-sambhramam uvāca-deva, vayaṃ kiṃ brūmahe? śrī-caraṇāḥ svayam eva vetsyanti |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said with agitation: "Lord, what shall we say? Your glorious feet will know of their own accord."

children.text:
vrajarājaḥ sasmitam uvāca-satyaṃ bhavad-uktaṃ punar-uktam eva bhavet, yato bhavato maunam evātra bravītīti rīti-vaśāj jñātavanta eva ca vayam | tathāpi, sva-mukhena sukhena yojayatu bhavān asmān |
[8] snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-sarva-sukha-varṣi-śrī-devarṣi-caraṇānāṃ kṛpaṇa-viṣaya-kṛpā-kpta-tad-etad-gatī labdhamatī tāv eva sphuṭam āvām iti |
children.translated_text:
The king of <s>Vraja</s> said with a smile: "What you have said would indeed be redundant, since your very silence speaks here — and by convention we have already understood. Even so, please gladden us with your own mouth."
[8] <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: "Having obtained the understanding through the mercy of the glorious divine sage <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>) — whose feet shower all happiness, and whose compassion for the wretched fashioned their respective destinies — those two are clearly none other than ourselves!"

children.text: tad etad ākarṇya nirvarṇita-tan-mukhāḥ śrī-vrajarāja-pramukhāḥ samāhūya bhūyaḥ sa-kautukaṃ sa-sukhaṃ tau militavantaḥ | madhye samupaveśya nirīkṣitavantaś ceti | [10] punas tu tat-praśnānantaraṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ krama-prāptāṃ kathāṃ prāha, [11] tad evaṃ vicitrāt pūrva-caritrād divasa-pañcakānantaraṃ śrīmān upanandaḥ sva-mandiraṃ vindamānaḥ sva-patnīṃ papraccha, adya sva-devara-nara-deva-gṛhe kiṃ gamana-maṅgalaṃ jagṛhe bhavatyā?
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> and others, having examined their faces, summoned them again with curiosity and delight, and met them. Seating them in their midst, they beheld them. [10] Then, after that inquiry, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> narrated the story that had come in due course. [11] "Thus, five days after that extraordinary previous episode, the glorious <s>Upananda</s>, arriving at his own residence, asked his wife: 'Today, has any auspicious preparation for going to the house of your brother-in-law, the king, been undertaken by you?'"

children.text: patnī prāha-atha kim, ko vā tad gamanaṃ vinā mano mānayituṃ śaknoti, kim uta bhavad-vidha-savidha-sambandhinas te vayam?
children.translated_text: The wife said: "Of course! Who could indeed honor the mind without going there? — how much more so for us, who are relatives intimately connected like your kind!"

children.text: patir āha-viśeṣaś cet kathyatām |
children.translated_text: The husband said: "If there is anything special, let it be told."

children.text: patnī prāha-
children.translated_text: The wife said:

children.text:
yasmin prema-pracuraṃ bhayam api tasmin vibhāvyate pracuram |
  yadvan netraṃ śaṅkā-viṣayas tadvan na karṇādi ||JGc_1,9.1|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
"In whom abundant love [is felt], in him abundant fear too is perceived;
just as the eye is an object of suspicion, so not the ear and the like." // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.9.1, <s>gīti</s>]

children.text: tathā hi, yadyapi niravadyādhāna-vidhātṛ-mātṛ-prabhṛtibhī rakṣyete sabhībhir eva tau, tathāpi khela-velāyāṃ sambhālayitum apāraṇīyatayā sukalam eva vikalayataḥ | tatra cādyatanaṃ vṛttaṃ pratipadyatām-
children.translated_text: For indeed, although those two were guarded by the assembly-members themselves, including the faultless guardians such as mothers and others, even so, because of the impossibility of watching over them during playtime, they easily slipped away. And there, let the events of today be recounted:

children.text: tau bhavad-bhrātṛjau sa-nija-vraja-vrajeśvara-bhojya-sajjanāya janitāmodāyāṃ yaśodāyāṃ tadīya-sāhāyakā-rohiṇyām api rohiṇyām āśaṅkā-pātrīr dhātrīr vañcayitvā vidūraṃ cañcitavantau | yathā,
children.translated_text: Those two nephews of yours, having deceived the nurses — who were objects of suspicion — while <s>Yaśodā</s>, who had produced delight for the worthy food-companions of the king of <s>Vraja</s> and his own cowherd community, and <s>Rohiṇī</s> too, who was her helper, wandered far away. As follows:

children.text:
dhātrīṇām aparatra karmaṇi manāg dattātmanām agrataḥ
  savyāsavya-dṛśor dṛśor aviṣaye sāntarddhi-deśe ca tau |
  krīḍā-dambha-vaśāt kramād apagatau vidrutya dūra-sthitau
  tatrātha sva-suhṛdbhir uddhata-gaṇaiḥ kolāhalaṃ cakratuḥ ||JGc_1,9.2|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: When the nurses' attention was slightly given to other tasks, beyond the range of their sideways and forward gazes, in a place with hiding spots, those two, by the pretext of play-deception, having gradually departed and run far away, then and there, with their bold companions raised in a group, they made an uproar! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
atha tathā nikṛtas tat-pālanādhikṛta-dhātrī-vargaḥ kṣaṇāt kṛtāvadhāna-sargaḥ śīghram eva kṛtānumārgaḥ krameṇa svasyākāraṇam akāraṇatām āsāditam avadhārya nijeśvaryor āvedayāmāsa |
[18] tāvac ca tato' py atidūraṃ gambhīra-sarit-tīraṃ gatāv ākarṇya pūtanā-sūdana-prasū rāmāmbālām eva tayoḥ saṅkalanāya cālayāmāsa | æhanta, na jāne khalv arjuna-yugalavad durjana-preryamāṇatayā kaścid anokaho vā nadyavaroho vā skhalatīti mayi pāka-karma-vipākāvaruddhāyāṃ satvaraṃ tvam eva svayaṃ yāhi' iti |
  sā ca tatra gatā śīghraṃ vyagrī-bhūtāṅga-mānasā |
  sarit-tīra-gataṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhagnārjunam athāhvayat ||JGc_1,9.3|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then the group of nurses appointed for their protection, thus outwitted, within a moment marshaling their attention and swiftly following their trail, gradually ascertaining that their own [negligence] had become causeless, reported to their two masters.
[18] And then, hearing that they had gone even further, to the bank of a deep river, the mother of the slayer of <s>Pūtanā</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>) dispatched the mother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Rohiṇī</s>) herself for their retrieval. 'Alas, I do not know — like the pair of <s>Arjuna</s> trees, whether some impenetrable tree or descent into a river is causing them to stumble, being impelled by wicked ones — while I am detained by the ripening of cooking tasks, you yourself go quickly!'
She, having gone there swiftly, her limbs and mind agitated like a tigress, called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> at the river bank — the one who had broken the <s>Arjuna</s> trees! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś ca krīḍā-raṅgākulatayā tad anaṅgīkartari saṅgīśitari kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇāgraje ca tad-anuga-tṛṣṇe, sā parivṛtya sadmāgatya tasya kiñcid bhaya-sthānaṃ prabhava-sthānam eva prasthāpayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, engrossed in the excitement of the play-arena, did not accept that [summons], and when <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> elder brother (<s>Balarāma</s>), thirsting to follow him [likewise refused], she, turning around and coming home, dispatched the very source of his slight fear — his birthplace itself (his mother <s>Yaśodā</s>).

children.text: tataś ca tan-mātā ca gatvā-
children.translated_text: Then his mother too, having gone —

children.text:
krīḍantaṃ tanayaṃ bālair ativelaṃ sahāgrajam |
  vīkṣya stana-miṣāt snehaṃ varṣantī hūtim ātanot ||JGc_1,9.4|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Seeing her son playing with boys excessively along with his elder brother, she, raining affection under the pretext of offering her breast, extended her call! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: na tu sahasā samīpam āpa tat-palāyana-śaṅkayā | āhūti-mādhurī ceyam āsvāda-dhurīṇatāṃ nīyatām-
children.translated_text: But she did not approach hastily, out of the apprehension that he might flee. And let the sweetness of this calling be savored to the full:

children.text:
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇāravindākṣa
tāta ehi stanaṃ piba |
  alaṃ vihāraiḥ kṣuc-chrāntas
tad bhavān bhoktum arhati ||[BhP 10.11.15] iti |
children.translated_text: you deserve to eat!' // [BhP 10.11.15]

'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O lotus-eyed one!
Dear child, come, drink from the breast!
Enough of playing — you are hungry and tired,

children.text: tathāpi mithaḥ saṅgharṣayataḥ krīḍā-tarṣavantaṃ tam anāgacchantaṃ dharṣayantī, vicchiduratā-vidhur asajātīya-snehasya dvitīya-pātram ādṛta-sva-vacana-mātratayāvaśyam eva vaśyaṃ śrī-bala-bhadram eva sānukrośaṃ cukrośa-
children.translated_text: Even so, as they wrestled with each other, she, scolding that play-thirsty one who would not come, the second vessel of affection unlike her own kind — who was necessarily obedient by the mere regard for her words — she called out affectionately to the glorious <s>Balabhadra</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>):

children.text: he rāmāgaccha tātāśu sānujaḥ kulanandana |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rāma</s>, come quickly, dear child, along with your younger brother, O delight of the family!

children.text: prātar eva kṛtāhāraḥ krīḍāśrānto' pi putraka ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten early in the morning, and now tired from play, O dear son!

children.text: pratīkṣate tvāṃ dāśārha bhokṣyamāṇo vrajādhipaḥ |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> awaits you, O <s>Dāśārha</s>, ready to eat,

children.text: ehy āvayoḥ priyaṃ dhehi, svagṛhaṃ yāta bālakāḥ ||[BhP 10.11.16-7]
children.translated_text: come, do what is dear to us both — go home, O boys!' // [BhP 10.11.16-17]

children.text: tato mātṛ-harṣaṇāya nivartayituṃ kṛṣṇaṃ karṣati saṅkarṣaṇe, sacchala-protsāhanaṃ tam eva bhaṇati sma-
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) was pulling <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to turn back for the delight of their mother, she spoke to him alone with an encouraging pretext:

children.text: dhūli-dhūsaritāṅgas tvaṃ tāta majjanam āvaha |
children.translated_text: 'Your body is covered with dust, dear child — come for a bath!

children.text: janmarkṣaṃ te' dya bhavati viprebhyo dehi gāḥ śuciḥ ||[BhP 10.11.18]
children.translated_text: Today is your birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation) — give cows to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, being purified!' // [BhP 10.11.18]

children.text: punas tadānīm eva gṛhād āgatān bālān ākalayya spṛhāṃ bṛṃhayantī babhāṣe,
children.translated_text: Then, noticing the boys who had just come from home at that very time, stimulating his desire, she spoke:

children.text: paśya paśya vayasyāṃs te mātṛ-mṛṣṭa-svalaṅkṛtān |
children.translated_text: 'Look, look at your playmates, adorned and groomed by their mothers!

children.text: tvaṃ ca snātaḥ kṛtāhāro viharasva svalaṅkṛtaḥ ||[BhP 10.11.19]
children.translated_text: You too, having bathed and eaten, play well-adorned!' // [BhP 10.11.19]

children.text: tad evaṃ bālyam evārabhya vipra-poṣaṇād ātmanas toṣa iti tad ārambhāya stambhamānam āhvānādi-lakṣyeṇa laghu laghu samīpam āsannā sa-rāmaṃ rāmānujaṃ bhujayor gṛhītvā gṛham ānināya |
children.translated_text: Thus, from childhood itself, [illustrating the principle that] satisfaction of the self comes from nourishing <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — she, approaching near step by step through the stratagem of calling and such, targeting his obstinacy at the initiation of that [task], took <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) together in her arms and brought them home.

children.text: tataś ca, janmarkṣaṃ te iti mithyā-kathyamānam api tena gṛhītaṃ nitarām eva gṛhītavatī vrajarāja-gṛhiṇī tat parva, yatra duṣṭa-dṛṣṭi-nivāraṇāya sa-yantrā mantrā muhur vinyāsam ūhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, although 'today is your birth-<s>nakṣatra</s>' was spoken falsely, the wife of the king of <s>Vraja</s> took it as entirely accepted by him, and she took up that festival, where, for the warding off of evil eyes, <s>mantras</s> accompanied by <s>yantras</s> (mystical diagrams) were repeatedly installed.

children.text: tad evam avadhāya sa sarva-darśaḥ śrīmān upanandaḥ parāmamarśa, satyam āśaṅkitaṃ prajāṃ prati prajāvatyor anayoḥ prajāvatyoḥ, yad idaṃ goṣṭha-prakoṣṭham avaduṣṭam iva dṛśyate | bhavatu, vrajarāja-samājam anu vicārayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus observing this, the all-seeing glorious <s>Upananda</s> reflected: 'The anxiety of these two parents regarding their children is indeed justified, for this corner of the cow-settlement appears as if corrupted. So be it — we shall deliberate in the assembly of the king of <s>Vraja</s>.'

children.text: tatpatnī prāha-vicāraḥ punas tatrabhavaty eva sthāsyate |
children.translated_text: His wife said: 'The deliberation will indeed rest with his lordship there.'

children.text: atha prātar eva go-vraja-vrajānta-sthāyāṃ sarvāsthāspada-vrajarāja-samāja-rājamānāyām āsthānyāṃ militā gopālā gopāla-nādi-saukaryaṃ nātreti paryālocayāmāsuḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, early in the morning, in the assembly-hall — the seat of all affairs — of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, resplendent at the outskirts of the cow-settlement, the cowherds gathered and deliberated that there was no longer any comfort for the protection of <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) here.

children.text: ciravāsenotsannatāsanna-vanatayā bṛhadvanasya | tatra tu vayo-jñānābhyāṃ vṛddhaḥ śrī-rāma-kṛṣṇa-premṇā samṛddhaḥ svāṅka-palyaṅkaṃ sad-alaṅkariṣṇunā madhye madhye ca cibukaṃ gṛhītvā vitatha-praśnam ācariṣṇunā tat tadā krīḍanaka-yācñā-satṛṣṇena kṛṣṇena labhyamānānandaḥ śrīmān upanandaḥ prāvocad akhila-rocanam | iha ca vrajarājasya saṅkocam avalocayan bāla-prajā-mātrasya hita-pakṣam upalakṣayāmāsa | yathā-
children.translated_text: Because of the overgrown and nearby forest condition of <s>Bṛhadvana</s> due to long habitation. There, the one who was elder in age and wisdom, enriched by love for the glorious <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, receiving bliss from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who was beautifying the cushion of his own lap like a fine ornament, grasping his chin now and then and asking playful questions, and at that time desirous of playthings with thirst — the glorious <s>Upananda</s> spoke what was pleasing to all. And here, observing the reluctance of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, he indicated only the welfare of the young children. As follows:

children.text:
æiha na stheyam' itītthaṃ vraja-hitam uktaṃ bhavadbhir yat |
  tat punar atibālānāṃ hita-pradhānaṃ mama sphurati ||JGc_1,9.5|| [upagīti]
  sahajani-janite yan mama para-para-yatnena rakṣite' py atra |
  jātaṃ viplava-jātaṃ, tasmāt kiṃ syād ihorvaritam? ||JGc_1,9.6|| [āryā]
  tat-tad-upadrava-jāte kevala-parameśitū rakṣā |
  tasmin bhāraṃ dadyād iti ca na khalu tat-parair iṣṭam ||JGc_1,9.7|| [udgīti]
  calatā dvayam anucintyaṃ: tyājyaṃ gamyaṃ ca yad dhāma |
  tyājyaṃ duḥkha-nidānaṃ, gamyaṃ sukhitā-nidhānaṃ tu ||JGc_1,9.8|| [upagīti]
  sthānaṃ tad apadeyaṃ, yad iha paratra ca ghaṭeta duḥkhāya |
  bṛhad-ākhyaṃ vanam anupadam aihika-duḥkhāya sāmprataṃ jātam ||JGc_1,9.9|| [gīti]
  sthānaṃ tad upadeyaṃ, yad iha paratra ca ghaṭeta saukhyāya |
  vṛndāvanāraṇyaṃ cādaḥ samasta-sukhatamam atīva puṇyaṃ ca ||JGc_1,9.10|| [gīti]
  govardhana iti nāmā yatrāraṇye giriḥ sphurati |
  tat khalu go-jātīnāṃ gopānāṃ cāsti sarvasvam ||JGc_1,9.11|| [upagīti]
  gopāḥ kānana-karadā grāmādīnāṃ viniścayābhāvāt |
  tad apara-kānana-gamane rājñāṃ cājñā svataḥ-siddhā ||JGc_1,9.12|| [āryā]
  sukhato bhayato vā yat kṛtyaṃ kartavyatāṃ yāti |
  śīghraṃ yat khalu kāryaṃ valayati śaṅkām alaṃ vilambas tu ||JGc_1,9.13|| [udgīti]
  utthātavyaṃ tasmād asmāt sadyo na kāryam ālasyam |
  tulitā hy udyama-kalanā kṛtyaṃ yad yad yadā kriyate ||JGc_1,9.14|| [āryā]
  iyam asmākam udīkṣā yuṣmabhyaṃ yadi tu rocamānā syāt |
  para-vīkṣite' pi vastuni bahu-sammatir utsavaṃ dugdhe ||JGc_1,9.15|| [āryā]
  bhavati tu ced iha bhavatāṃ samarthanā tarhi gāvaḥ prāk |
  samyak pāyita-vatsāś carantu vṛndāṭavī-vartma ||JGc_1,9.16|| [upagīti]
  paścāt paṭa-gṛha-śakaṭāny aṭantu gṛhyaṃ samastam ādāya |
  vidhi-vidhi-siddhā seyaṃ vrajanād vrajatā hi goduhāṃ sadane ||JGc_1,9.17|| [gīti]
tataś ca,
  tad vākyaṃ paśupa-samūham ūha-śūnyaṃ
  svārthāya svayam anugamya kalpate sma |
  sādharmya-spṛśi mṛdi paśya bīja-bhedaḥ
  sphītaḥ syāt phalati ca tatra nāparatra ||JGc_1,9.18|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
'We should not stay here' — thus, O cowherds, what was said by you regarding the welfare of <s>Vraja</s>,
that again appears to me as primarily for the welfare of the very young ones! // [upagīti]
In that which was born to me by natural birth, even though protected here with the utmost exertion,
a series of calamities has arisen — so what would be gained by remaining here? // [āryā]
Against this and that calamity, the sole Supreme Lord is the protection;
but to place the burden entirely upon him — that is certainly not desired by those devoted to him! // [udgīti]
When moving, two things must be considered: what is to be abandoned and what destination is to be reached;
what is to be abandoned is the source of suffering, while the destination should be the treasury of happiness! // [upagīti]
That place is to be rejected which would conduce to suffering both here and hereafter;
the forest called <s>Bṛhat</s> (<s>Bṛhadvana</s>) has now at every step become a source of worldly suffering! // [gīti]
That place is to be accepted which would conduce to happiness both here and hereafter;
and that forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> yonder is supremely blissful and exceedingly sacred! // [gīti]
In that forest shines the mountain named <s>Govardhana</s>;
that is indeed the everything of the cow-folk and the cowherds! // [upagīti]
Cowherds are forest-dwelling taxpayers; since there is no fixed rule for villages and such,
in moving to another forest, the permission of kings is self-established! // [āryā]
Whatever duty becomes obligatory, whether from happiness or from fear,
what must be done quickly — delay fully invites doubt! // [udgīti]
Therefore we must rise up from here at once; no laziness should be practiced!
For when the weighing of exertion is balanced — whatever task is done whenever — [it is done well]! // [āryā]
This is our outlook; if it is agreeable to you,
then even in a matter examined by others, the consensus of many yields a festival! // [āryā]
But if there is your approval here,
then let the cows first, well-nursed with their calves,
graze along the path to the <s>Vṛndā</s> forest! // [upagīti]
Afterwards let the tent-houses and carts travel, taking along all household goods;
this is the proper procedure — for the milker's dwelling follows the migration from the cow-pen! // [gīti]
And then:
That speech led the cowherd community, devoid of deliberation,
to follow it of their own accord for their own benefit;
see — in soft soil that shares [the seed's] nature, the seed-splitting
is abundant, and it bears fruit there, not elsewhere! // [praharṣiṇī]

children.text: tad evaṃ paurṇamāsīm api vijñāpya samanujñāpya purataḥ prasthāpya ca śīghram utthāpyatāṃ vrajaḥ iti dundubhi-nirghoṣaṇayā kṛta-poṣaḥ so' yaṃ ghoṣaḥ sva-niruktim evātiriktatayā vyaktavān | gavyānāṃ mānuṣyakānām api kolāhalān mahā-ghoṣāspadatā hi ghoṣatā nirdiṣṭā | yathā,
children.translated_text: Thus, having informed and obtained the permission of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> and sent her ahead, 'Let <s>Vraja</s> be raised quickly!' — by the drum-proclamation that gave nourishment [to the plan], this cowherd settlement itself manifested its own etymology with surpassing clarity. For the uproars of both cattle and humans — hence the designation 'great cowherd settlement' (<s>mahā-ghoṣa</s>) is indeed indicated as the cowherd state (<s>ghoṣatā</s>). As follows:

children.text:
tadā vraje kalakala-koṭir utthitā
  hihī-hihī-jihi-jihi-kāra-miśritā |
  ghaḍad ghaḍad ghaḍad iti śākaṭā-ravaḥ
  sa-vādyakaḥ punar akhilaṃ-gilaḥ sthitaḥ ||JGc_1,9.19|| [*jabhajasaga]
children.translated_text:
Then in <s>Vraja</s>, a crore of clamors arose,
mixed with 'hihī-hihī-jihi-jihi' sounds;
the 'ghaḍad ghaḍad ghaḍad' noise of the carts,
accompanied by musical instruments, stood swallowing everything! // [*jabhajasaga]

children.text:
āropyānasi vṛddhādīn svayam ūḍha-śarāsanāḥ |
  gauraveṇa gavāṃ gopā yayur vikramamāṇatām ||JGc_1,9.20|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Having placed the elders and others upon carts,
themselves bearing bows,
the cowherds, out of reverence for the cows,
proceeded with valorous stride! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tataś ca saṅkrīḍati śakaṭa-varge saṅkrīḍamāne sati,
  śakaṭa-gṛhāṭana-caryāṃ paryākalayan vidūra-go lokaḥ |
  vyatiṣajyāvadad etad grāmaḥ kaścic cariṣṇur astīti ||JGc_1,9.21|| [gīti]
pathi tu,
  eko dhāvati kaścanāhvayati ko' py atrottaraṃ bhāṣate
  kaścit tatra nivṛtya gacchati nijaṃ sambhālayaty anyakaḥ |
  sarvo gāyati kṛṣṇa-bālya-caritaṃ bāṣpāyate stambhate
  svidyaty ejati romaharṣam ayate vaivarṇyam āsīdati ||JGc_1,9.22|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Then, as the multitude of carts played along, making sport,
the people far away, observing the spectacle of carts, houses, and wandering,
exchanged words and said: 'Some wandering village exists here!' // [gīti]
And on the road:
One runs, someone calls out, another answers here and there,
someone turns back and goes, another looks after his own belongings;
everyone sings the childhood deeds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — one weeps, one is stunned,
one perspires, one trembles, one has horripilation, one turns pale! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
ārūḍha-śakaṭā gopyo vyūḍha-navya-pariṣkriyāḥ |
  amandaṃ jagur ānandād ānandān nanda-nandanam ||JGc_1,9.23|| [anuṣṭubh]
yathā,
  nanda-mahī-pati-jāta nanda yaśodā-māta |
  janma-mahā-maha-digdha ramita-samasta-snigdha ||dhru |
sparśādita-viṣa-yoṣa aparicitāpada-doṣa |
children.translated_text: 'Destroyer of the poison-woman by mere touch, one unfamiliar with the blemish of calamity!'

children.text: śakaṭa-vighaṭṭana-śeṣa gokula-puṇya-viśeṣa ||
children.translated_text: 'Remainder of the shattering of the cart, the special merit of <s>Gokula</s>!'

The cowherd women, mounted on carts, arrayed in fresh finery,
sang abundantly out of joy — sang of <s>Nanda-nandana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), [who is] joy itself! // [anuṣṭubh]
As follows:
'O born of king <s>Nanda</s>, O joy, O born of mother <s>Yaśodā</s>!
Smeared with the great festival of birth, delighter of all dear ones!' // [refrain]

children.text: kṛta-nāmabhir abhirāma santata-rāmā-rāma |
children.translated_text: 'Delightful through names well-given, ever the joy of <s>Rāmā</s> (Lakṣmī) and <s>Rāma</s>!'

children.text: riṅga-bhṛtāṅga-naraṅga aṅgīkṛta-sakhi-saṅga ||
children.translated_text: 'One whose crawling limbs are like an orange, one who has accepted the companionship of friends!'

children.text: laṅghita-māruta-cakra nandita-gokula-śakra |
children.translated_text: 'Leaper over the wind-vortex (<s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>), delighter of <s>Gokula's</s> <s>Indra</s> (<s>Nanda</s>)!'

children.text: vatsa-vimocana-moda vraja-jana-śarma-yaśoda ||
children.translated_text: 'Joy of releasing the calves, <s>Yaśodā</s> who is the happiness and fame of the <s>Vraja</s>-folk!'

children.text:
sarvānandana-caurya tasmin darśita-śaurya |
  ayi dāmodara-līla akhila-sukha-prada-śīla ||JGc_1,9.24|| [2 x 3 gaṇas] iti |
children.translated_text:
'Thief of everyone's delight, one who displayed valor in that [encounter]!
O one of <s>Dāmodara</s> pastimes, one whose nature bestows all happiness!' // [2 x 3 gaṇas]

children.text: tad evaṃ gāyantyas tad-darśanasya nāthamānā vyatyatikrāmanti sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, singing and longing for the sight of him, they passed along —

children.text: tadā yaśodā-rohiṇyāv ekaṃ śakaṭam āsthite |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yaśodā</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>, seated upon one cart,

children.text: rejatuḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmābhyāṃ tat-kathā-śravaṇotsuke ||[BhP 10.11.34]
children.translated_text:
shone with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>,
eager to hear their stories! // [BhP 10.11.34]

children.text:
tatra sthitir, yathā:
  maṇi-khacita-suvarṇa-citra-varṇe
  śuci-mṛdu-tulikayānukūla-madhye |
  gṛha-nibha-śakaṭe virejatus te
  suta-ruci-rociṣi rohiṇī-yaśode ||JGc_1,9.25|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
Their appearance there, as follows:
In a cart resembling a house, jewel-studded, golden, of varied colors,
with a soft, pure, comfortable cushion in the pleasant middle —
those two, <s>Rohiṇī</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>, shone
in the radiance of the beauty of their sons! // [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text: tat-kathā tu dvi-vidhā, tat-sambandhinī, tat-kartṛkā ca | pūrvā yathā,
children.translated_text: The tales about them were of two kinds: those relating to them, and those performed by them. The former, as follows:

children.text:
snigdhā nāryaḥ śakaṭam abhito mātarau putrayos tair
  jñātājñātair akhila-caritair dhinvate smāviśeṣāt |
  premṇaḥ seyaṃ prakṛtir akhilāścarya-rūpā yad uccaiḥ
  sarvaṃ svīyaṃ viṣayam amanaḥ-spṛṣṭa-tulyaṃ karoti ||JGc_1,9.26|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'The affectionate women, the mothers of the two sons, on all sides of the cart, | are nourished by those known and unknown deeds of theirs, without distinction; | this is the nature of love, whose form is all-wondrous, that it greatly | renders everything of its own domain equal to that which the mind has never touched.' || (JGc 1,9.26) [mandākrāntā]

children.text: uttarā yathā-
children.translated_text: The sequel was as follows:

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-mātaḥ, kva nu khalu gacchantaḥ sma?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Mother, where indeed are we going?'

children.text: mātā prāha-putra, vṛndāvana-nāmani vana-dhāmani |
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'Son, to the forest-abode named <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-kadā sadanam āyāsyāmaḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'When shall we come back home?'

children.text: mātā sasmitam āha-vatsāsmad-anuṣaṅgata eva saṅgacchamānaṃ tad āste |
children.translated_text: The mother said with a smile: 'Child, it [the home] comes along with us by our very attachment to it.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-kva nu nirūpyatām?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Where may it be pointed out?'

children.text: rāmaḥ prahasann āha-kṛṣṇa, pākādi-nitya-kṛtya-sanniveśa-deśādhaḥ-pradeśān mahā-śakaṭa-veśān gṛhān nikaṭata evāṭataḥ paśya |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, laughing, said: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, look — just nearby, wandering about, [you can see] the houses in the form of great carts, in the lower areas of the places designated for cooking and other daily tasks.'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sāścaryaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrī-rāmaṃ spṛṣṭvā jahāsa, punar uvāca ca, tathyam idaṃ kathyate sma | yasmād vidūra-kṣitigā api kṣiti-ruhās tathā lakṣyante |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, looking with wonder, touching the glorious <s>Rāma</s>, laughed, and said again: 'What is said is true! For even the trees standing far away on the ground appear just so.'

children.text: mātā tu rohiṇyā saha sa-hāsam āha sma, putra, ta ete tu na kutracana ca gacchanti, kintu samprati tathā pratīyante mātram |
children.translated_text: The mother, however, said with laughter together with <s>Rohiṇī</s>: 'Son, those [trees] do not go anywhere at all; rather, they merely appear so at present.'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam uvāca-bhavatu, tad vṛndāvanaṃ kutra?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with longing: 'So be it — then where is <s>Vṛndāvana</s>?'

children.text: rohiṇy āha-putra, yamunāyāḥ pāre |
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> said: 'Son, on the other side of the <s>Yamunā</s>.'

children.text: rāma uvāca-ekā yamunā dūrataḥ paścān nyastā, purataḥ kim anyāpy asti?
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said: 'One <s>Yamunā</s> has been placed behind us in the distance — is there another one ahead too?'

children.text: mātā sahāsam āha-putra, kutracid api manāg api na vicchinna-gamanā sā |
children.translated_text: The mother said with laughter: 'Son, she is nowhere even slightly interrupted in her course.'

children.text: rāmas tu mātṛ-mukhaṃ sāścaryatayā sa-sukha-caryaṃ paśyati sma | [49] kṛṣṇa uvāca-tatra-bhavatā kila na tarkitaṃ, yat khalv ita iva tatrāccha gacchantī sā dṛśyate sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, however, gazed at his mother's face with wonder and joyful curiosity. [49] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'It was not considered by your honor that she was seen going clearly from here to there, just as from here.'

children.text: tad evaṃ tayoḥ sollāsaṃ hāsaṃ bibhratoḥ punaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam uvāca-laghu-mātaḥ, kā tatra śāta-sampad asti yad etāvatā prayāsena prayāsyāmaḥ?
children.translated_text: Thus, as the two bore their joyful laughter, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again said with longing: 'Dear lesser-mother, what cool prosperity is there that we are traveling with so much effort?'

children.text: rohiṇy āha-putra, krīḍā-sthānāni krīḍanakāni ca bahūni santi |
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> said: 'Son, there are many playgrounds and many playthings.'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ saharṣaṃ saṅkarṣaṇa-niṣkalaṅka-vidhor aṅkaṃ nija-śyāma-dhāmnālaṅkurvann eva sāṅga-praṇayatayā samuttānitāṅgas tan-mukham unmukhaṃ paśyan vihasan vilasan muhur luṭhati sma | [53] saṅkarṣaṇas tu tan-mukham anu mukhaṃ nidhāya muhur vihasita-līlāṃ vidhāya cirāya taṃ hāsayati sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, joyfully adorning the lap of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> — the spotless moon — with his own dark radiance, with affectionate whole-bodied eagerness, his body raised up, looking up at his face expectantly, laughing, playing, rolled about again and again. [53] <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, however, placing his face upon his face, fashioning the play of repeated laughter, made him laugh for a long time.

children.text: atha yamunā-taraṅga-saṅgha-saṅgata-māruta-digdha-snigdha-vana-lekheyam āsannā iti mātṛ-yugala-saṃlāpaṃ niśamya samyag utthitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saṅkarṣaṇa-saṅkaraḥ prāg ajñātān jñātān api naga-mṛga-khagān hasantībhiḥ skhalita-dantībhir vivādataḥ sarvān apūrvān iva pṛcchann uttaram āyacchaṃś ca tat-kūlānukūla-vanam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the conversation of the pair of mothers that 'this forest-line, anointed and smooth with the wind mingled with the waves of the <s>Yamunā</s>, is near' — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the companion of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, arose fully. Asking about all the previously unknown and also known trees, animals, and birds from the laughing, gap-toothed [women], questioning all of them disputatiously as if they were unprecedented, and receiving answers, he reached the forest along the bank.

children.text: tatra praśnottare yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the questions and answers were as follows:

children.text:
ko' sau vṛkṣaḥ samantād aniśa-cala-dalaḥ? pippalaḥ | ko' ṇḍa-koṭiṃ
  sūte? soḍumbarākhyaḥ ka iha ghana-jaṭā-vyāpta-mūrtir? baṭaḥ saḥ |
  itthaṃ navyāṃ vanāntar-gatim anu jananī-ḍimba-saṃvāda-jātaṃ
  lokaṃ pīyūṣa-varṣair asukhayad akhilaṃ tatra tatrāticitram ||JGc_1,9.27|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
