'What is that tree with constantly moving leaves on all sides?' 'The <s>Pippala</s> (sacred fig).' 'Which one bears egg-shaped fruits?' 'That one called <s>Udumbara</s> (cluster fig).' 'Which one here has a form pervaded by thick matted roots?' 'That is the <s>Vaṭa</s> (banyan).' |
Thus, following the novel journey into the forest, the dialogue born of mother-and-child conversation | drenched the entire world there and there with showers of nectar, surpassingly wonderful! || (JGc 1,9.27) [sragdharā]

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text:
gaurāḥ kṛṣṇa-pradhānāpluta-gati-paśavaḥ ke ramante? hariṇyaḥ
  ke vāmī sairibhāśva-pratima-tanudharā? rohiṣākhyāḥ prasiddhāḥ |
  ke śṛṅgānekaśākhā-śavalita-vapuṣaḥ? śambarākhyās tad evaṃ
  mātur gīr-jñāta-nāmā sa jayati sa-balo nanda-gopāla-bālaḥ ||JGc_1,9.28|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: 'What are those fair animals that sport with a leaping gait, led by a dark chief?' '<s>Hariṇīs</s> (deer).' | 'What are those that move crookedly with bodies resembling buffalo and horses?' 'They are known as <s>Rohiṣas</s> (nilgai).' | 'What are those with bodies dappled by many-branched horns?' 'They are called <s>Śambaras</s> (sambhur deer).' Thus, | victorious is that child of <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd, <s>Gopāla</s>, together with <s>Bala</s>, who learned the names from his mother's speech! || (JGc 1,9.28) [sragdharā]

children.text:
api ca-
  citraḥ ko' pi? mayūraḥ ka iha mṛdukuhūgāyakaḥ? kokilākhyaḥ
  ko vaktuṃ vaṣṭi vāṇīṃ naravad api? śukaḥ puṣpagaḥ kaś ca? bhṛṅgaḥ |
  itthaṃ mātṛ-dvayena prathama-vana-game saṃlapantau hasantau,
  bālau gopāla-rāmau vraja-kula-mahilāḥ śarmabhiḥ siñcataḥ sma ||JGc_1,9.29|| [sragdharā]
  athāgatās taraṇi-sutā-taṭaṃ vraja-
  prajā-vrajāḥ sa-śakaṭa-dhenu-saṅkaṭam |
  sa-sambhramaṃ taritu-manastayā ca te
  parasparaṃ kalakala-kīrṇam abhraman ||JGc_1,9.30|| [jabhasajaga]
children.translated_text:
And further:
'What is that strange one?' 'A peacock.' 'Which one here sings with a soft cooing sound?' 'The one called <s>Kokila</s> (cuckoo).' | 'Which one wishes to speak words like a human?' 'The <s>Śuka</s> (parrot).' 'And which goes from flower to flower?' 'The <s>Bhṛṅga</s> (bee).' | Thus, conversing and laughing with the pair of mothers on their first forest-visit, | the two boys <s>Gopāla</s> and <s>Rāma</s> drenched the women of the <s>Vraja</s> clan with delights! || (JGc 1,9.29) [sragdharā]
Then the multitudes of <s>Vraja</s> folk arrived at the bank of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), | crowded with carts and cows in close quarters; | and with minds eager to cross, they | wandered about in every direction amidst the tumultuous clamor. || (JGc 1,9.30) [jabhasajaga]

children.text: tataś ca dvāv api bhrātarau mātarau vihāya, paramam unnatatamaṃ vrajeśituḥ pituḥ śakaṭam āgatāv, ūrdhva-sthityā dalad-indīvara-sundaratā-śāli-kālindīṃ prāṇi-vṛnda-prīṇi vṛndāvanam api phulla-dṛśā dadṛśatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the two brothers too, leaving the mothers, climbed upon the supremely lofty cart of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, their father. And from their elevated position, with wide-open eyes, they beheld the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), beautiful as a splitting blue lotus, and <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, which delights all living beings.

children.text:
śrī-vrajeśvarādayas tu parasparam ūcuḥ-aho, rūpam iha pārīṇa-vanyā-sambandhinyā bhāsvat-kanyāyāḥ, yā khalu pratibimba-saṃvalanayā vṛndāvanāntam antar-vahantī vicitra-citra-paṭṭa-paṭavad ācarati | [58] aho madhurīṇāṃ sādhu-rītir asya ca vṛndāvanasya, yat khalu nīlābhaṃ sita-pīta-lohita-prasūnālibhir niḥsarad-āsāra-vidyotamāna-vidyut-kānti-rohita-rohita-nīrada-vad ābhāsamānaṃ dūrato' py amṛta-pūram arpayati | yasya cākṛṣṭa-tripiṣṭapa-pada-ṣaṭpada-padatayā vyakta-daurlabhyaṃ samākarṣi-saurabhyaṃ ghrāṇābhyāgatānāṃ dūram ārabhya pratyudgami sabhājaka-sabhya-vṛndam iva labhyate | [59] yasya ca vicitra-patri-kṛtrima-kala-kalila-kākalī-saṅkula-kolāhala-kulam ākarṣaṇa-mantra ivārtha-grahaṇaṃ vināpi sa-karṇakaṃ janyuṃ nijāśrayābhyarṇam
ākarṣati |
children.translated_text: The glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s> and others said to one another: 'Ah, behold the beauty here of the radiant daughter (the <s>Yamunā</s>) connected with the familiar river-flood, who, carrying reflections, flows within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, behaving like a variegated, painted silk cloth! [58] Ah, the excellent manner of the sweetnesses of this <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, which, though dark in hue, appearing like a rain-cloud whose crimson lightning-radiance flashes forth with emerging showers amid white, yellow, and red flower-blossoms, bestows a flood of nectar even from afar! — whose fragrance, attracting the bees of the celestial realm and thus revealing its rarity, is found by those who arrive at the nose, like a host of assembled welcoming courtiers coming out to greet from a distance, proceeding far ahead. [59] And whose tumultuous noise, filled with the varied, artful, softly warbling sounds of colorful birds — like a charm of attraction — draws [people] near to its own abode, bringing [them] to the ear even without grasping the meaning!'

children.text:
tad evaṃ paśyatoḥ śṛṇvator api sa-tṛṣṇayo rāma-kṛṣṇayor gopāḥ gāḥ pārayituṃ vyāpāraṃ kārayāmāsuḥ,
  nīraṃ taraṇi-kanyāyās tīraṃ ca taraṇe tadā |
  go-mayaṃ gomaya-mayaṃ kṣaṇād ajani sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,9.31|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Thus, even as the longing <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> were watching and listening, the cowherds engaged them in the task of crossing the cows:
'The water of the Sun's daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>), the bank, and the fording | at that time became everywhere covered with cow-products and cow-dung in an instant.' || (JGc 1,9.31) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tīrṇāsu goṣu tathā karṇīrathād avatīrṇāsu parijana-paricchada-sahitāsu gopa-vanitāsu, kāśa-kuśa-śara-vaṃśa-varair alaṅkarmīṇa-nirmita-paraspara-naddha-plava-rājī rāja-paddhatir ivāsambādhatayā sādhitā | [62] tataś ca pārāvārīṇa-bhūmyor ekatāyāṃ kṛtāyām avārīṇam iva pārīṇam madhupurī-kālīya-hradayor antarālaṃ tad vana-bhāgaṃ sarva eva gāyantaḥ prahasantaḥ krīḍantaś ca śakaṭa-ghaṭayāpi praviviśuḥ | tad evam evoktam,
children.translated_text: When the cows had crossed, and likewise the cowherd women had descended from the covered carts together with retinue and belongings, a royal pathway was fashioned without obstruction — like a royal road — consisting of rows of rafts bound to one another, built from the finest <s>kāśa</s>, <s>kuśa</s>, <s>śara</s> reeds, and bamboo. [62] Then, when the lands on both banks had become as one, the intervening forest-portion between <s>Madhupurī</s> (Mathurā) and the pool of <s>Kālīya</s> — as if this bank were the far bank — all entered singing, laughing, and playing, even with the train of carts. Thus indeed it is said:

children.text: vṛndāvanaṃ sampraviśya sarva-kāla-sukhāvaham |
tatra cakrur vrajāvāsaṃ śakaṭair ardha-candravat ||[BhP 10.11.35] iti|
children.translated_text: there they made their <s>Vraja</s>-settlement with carts in a half-moon shape.' || [BhP 10.11.35]
'Having entered <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, which bestows happiness at all times,

children.text: rāma-kṛṣṇāu ca baddha-tṛṣṇāv āsādita-tīropakaṇṭhāv utkaṇṭhayā bhuvi śakaṭād utplutau pluta-samplutāhvānataḥ sukha-samanvitaṃ sakhīn anvag vidhāya pratyagram api pratyagrāyamāṇa-vaicitrī-gahaṇaṃ gahanam avagāhamānau savyāpasavyayoḥ paśyantau caraṇa-cāritām evācaritavantau | tadā ca kim anyad varṇanīyam, samastaṃ vṛndāvanam api kṛṣṇena spṛṣṭaṃ hṛṣṭam eva nirṇīya parāmṛṣṭam | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: And <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bound with longing, having reached the vicinity of the bank, with eagerness leaped from the cart to the ground. Having joyfully dispatched their friends by calling out with splashing invitations, and penetrating the deep forest with its ever-renewing thickets of variety — looking left and right — they performed nothing but the conduct of their feet. And then, what else need be described? It was determined that all of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, touched by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, was simply delighted. For:

children.text:
yad gānaṃ vipinasya kokila-kale nṛtyaṃ latā-vibhrame
  romṇām utthitam aṅkure ca kavitaṃ yogyān nidānādṛte |
  tan mithyā yadi kṛṣṇa-saṅgati-vaśāt tasmiṃs tathā varṇyate
  satyaṃ tarhi sadāpi tat tad akhilaṃ yasmād darīdṛśyate ||JGc_1,9.32|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'If the song of the forest in the cuckoo's art, and the dance in the creeper's bending, | and the poem in the sprouting of the hair-like shoots were all false, | yet described so in that [forest] due to the association with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — | then indeed all that is always true, since it was actually seen!' || (JGc 1,9.32) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: tataś ca tau kvacid vikramaṇena kvacit tu snigdha-jana-skandhādy-ākramaṇena bandhubhir āsvādyamānānavadya-lālityāmṛtau śubha-śakuna-sambhṛtau vatsa-krīḍanābhidha-yamunā-ghaṭṭataḥ saṭṭīkarākhyaṃ pradeśam āsedatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those two, sometimes by their own walking, and sometimes by climbing upon the shoulders and the like of affectionate people — whose tasted, faultless, nectar-like charm was savored by kinsmen, and who were accompanied by auspicious omens — reached from the calf-play <s>ghāṭ</s> of the <s>Yamunā</s> the place called <s>Saṭṭīkarā</s>.

children.text: athāvataraṇa-turya-ghoṣa-jāte rājñā samanujñāte, taṃ paścān nidhāya dakṣiṇa-paścimām agre vidhāya sarve samākīrṇa-vistīrṇa-deśatayāvatīrṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, when the blare of the trumpets of descent was produced and sanctioned by the king, placing that [<s>Saṭṭīkarā</s>] behind and setting the southwestern direction ahead, all descended into the sprawling, spacious terrain.

children.text:
loka-hūti-vyakta-ceṣṭaṃ tadā nandādi-veṣṭitam |
  vṛndāvanam idaṃ reje supta-jāgarita-prabham ||JGc_1,9.33|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tatra cakrur vrajāvāsaṃ śakaṭair ardha-candravat |
  yad-antaḥ-pūritaṃ gobhiḥ krameṇa ghana-rītibhiḥ ||JGc_1,9.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
śrī-hari-vaṃśe ca,
  niveśaṃ vipulaṃ cakre gavāṃ caiva hitāya ca |
  śakaṭāvarta-paryantaṃ candrārdhākāra-saṃsthitam ||iti | [2.9.20-1]
children.translated_text:
'<s>Vṛndāvana</s> then shone, with activities manifest from the calls of the people, | surrounded by <s>Nanda</s> and others, with a radiance as of one asleep and awake!' || (JGc 1,9.33) [anuṣṭubh]
'There they made the <s>Vraja</s> settlement with carts in a half-moon shape, | the interior of which was gradually filled with cows in dense array.' || (JGc 1,9.34) [anuṣṭubh]
And in the <s>Śrī Harivaṃśa</s>:
'He made a vast settlement, for the welfare of the cows too, | surrounded by a perimeter of carts, arranged in the shape of a half-moon.' || [2.9.20-1]

children.text:
evaṃ taddine śakaṭair eva cakruḥ, dināntare tu,
  kaṇṭakībhiḥ pravṛddhābhis tathā kaṇṭakibhir drumaiḥ |
  nikhātocchrita-śākhābhir abhiguptaṃ samantataḥ ||iti | [2.9.22]
children.translated_text:
Thus they did so on that day with carts alone; on the next day, however:
'With thorny bushes that had grown tall, and with thorny trees, | with branches firmly planted and raised high, [the settlement was] guarded on all sides.' || [2.9.22]

children.text:
go-purasya puraḥ kṛtvā govardhana-dharādharam |
  gopa-vāsaḥ sa tatrāsīn nagopa-vasatir yataḥ ||JGc_1,9.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
  paurastya-vastya-tyāge' pi tat-tan-maryādayācitaḥ |
  vrajākāras tathaivāsīt kṛṣṇāpāre yathā sthitaḥ ||JGc_1,9.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Placing <s>Govardhana</s>, the upholder of the earth, before the cow-settlement, | the cowherd dwelling was there, for it was not a settlement without cows!' || (JGc 1,9.35) [anuṣṭubh]
'Even upon leaving the eastern dwelling, adhering to such-and-such customs, | the form of <s>Vraja</s> remained just as it was established on <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> far bank.' || (JGc 1,9.36) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
aṣṭa-krośīm āyataṃ goṣṭham etan
  madhye tasmin vistṛtaṃ cārdham asyāḥ |
  etan mānaṃ cātra lokasya dṛṣṭyā
  śaktyānantācintya-dhāmatvam eva ||JGc_1,9.37|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: 'The cow-settlement extends eight <s>krośas</s> (about sixteen miles) in length, | and in its middle, the width is half of that; | this measurement is by the sight of ordinary people — | by the infinite, inconceivable power [of the Lord], it is indeed a [limitless] abode!' || (JGc 1,9.37) [śālinī]

children.text:
madhye rājñaḥ sadma tat-pārśvatas tad-
  bhrātṝṇāṃ tad-bāhyatas tat pareṣām |
  yadvat premaṇy antaraṅgādi-rītir
  vāse' pi syād aucitī tadvad eva ||JGc_1,9.38|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: 'In the center was the king's mansion, alongside it that of his brothers, | outside that, the [homes] of others; | just as in the hierarchy of love there is an inner-circle and so on, | so too in the dwelling — the propriety was exactly likewise.' || (JGc 1,9.38) [śālinī]

children.text: atha tatra parama-śarmaṇā gamyamāna-samaya-vraje pūrvavad vraje krīḍā-ratayor api tayor vana-didṛkṣā punar atīva vilakṣaṇā jātā | tataś ca pratidinam api gavāvanāya vanāya prayātena tātena samaṃ samantata eva vrajataḥ sma | yatra-
children.translated_text: Now, there in <s>Vraja</s>, where time passed with supreme bliss, while the two were engaged in play as before, a desire to see the forest arose again, extremely extraordinary. And so, every day, they went along in all directions together with their father, who set out for the forest for the daily cow-driving. Where:

children.text:
vṛndāvanaṃ govardhanaṃ yamunā-pulināni ca |
  vīkṣyāsīd uttamā prītī rāma-rāmānujātayoḥ ||JGc_1,9.39|| [BhP 10.11.36]
children.translated_text: '<s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Govardhana</s>, and the sandy banks of the <s>Yamunā</s> — | upon seeing these, supreme delight arose in <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!' || (JGc 1,9.39) [BhP 10.11.36]

children.text:
yathā,
  prādhānyād atidivya-vṛkṣa-vitater vṛndāvanaṃ ratna-bhū-
  palyaṅkānvita-pīṭha-jetṛ-dṛśadāṃ vṛndasya govardhanaḥ |
  glau-cūrṇodbhava-raṅga-bhūmi-vijayi-sthalyāvaler aṃśumat-
  kanyāyāḥ pulinālir utsava-śataṃ dugdhe sma mugdhaṃ tayoḥ ||JGc_1,9.40|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[68] atha madhukaṇṭhaḥ samāpanam idaṃ sāñjalitayā vyānañja,
children.translated_text:
As follows:
'Principally, <s>Vṛndāvana</s> with its rows of supremely divine trees, <s>Govardhana</s> with its multitude of | gem-ground boulders that defeat couches, thrones, and seats, | and the rows of sandy banks of the Sun's daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>), victorious over the stages adorned with | golden-dust-born dye — milked a hundred festivals of delight for those two innocent ones!' || (JGc 1,9.40) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[68] Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> adorned this conclusion with joined hands:

children.text: īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava gopādhināyaka |
children.translated_text: 'Such a son has been born to you, O chief of the cowherds,

children.text: pālyaṃ karoti yo viśvaṃ bālyasya caritād api ||JGc_1,9.41||
children.translated_text: who makes even the world a thing to be nurtured, by the conduct of his childhood alone!' || (JGc 1,9.41)

children.text: tad evaṃ tal-līlānāṃ sākṣāt-prathāyāṃ kathāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ pūrva-vṛttavat tad-dine' pi sarve' py ānandānām akharvāṇāṃ kharveṇa karburitā nija-nijālayaṃ kalayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the story of the direct manifestation of those pastimes had transpired, on that day too — as in the previous occasions — all, variegated by a multitude of undiminished joys, repaired to their respective abodes.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
śrī-vṛndāvana-deśe praveśo nāma
navamaṃ pūraṇam
||9||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the Śrī Śrī <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Ninth Chapter named 'The Entry into the Region of Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s>'
||9||

children.text: atha daśamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Tenth Chapter.

children.text: vatsāsurādy-utsādanam
children.translated_text: The Destruction of <s>Vatsāsura</s> and Others.

children.text: atha prātar api pūrvavat kathā prathate sma |
children.translated_text: Then, the next morning too, the story proceeded as before.

children.text:
yathā snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca- athānayor atibālyād ūrdhva-vilāsam ārabhamāṇaṃ sukumāraṃ kumāratā-śeṣaṃ varṇayiṣyāmaḥ | yathā-
  mukta-stanyam udañcad aṅgavalayaṃ cāñcalya-paryākulaṃ
  khelā-cañcad-akharva-netra-yugalaṃ śaśvat-prahāsānanam |
  nānā-kautuka-bhāvitaṃ sakhijanakrīḍāvilāsāspadaṃ
  vatsekṣā-spṛhi rāma-kṛṣṇa-kalitaṃ kaumāram antar bhaje ||JGc_1,10.1|| [śārdūla]
api ca,
  śubhraśyāmau nīla-pītābha-vastrau
  śṛṅgī-pārīdhvāna-śikṣāsu dakṣau |
  krīḍā-lolau mitra-varge vicitraṃ
  citrīyete rāma-kṛṣṇau kumārau ||JGc_1,10.2|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
As <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Now we shall describe the tender boyhood that remains after early childhood, commencing its upward-rising sport beyond the extreme infancy of these two. As follows:
Weaned from the breast, with limbs swelling upward, restless with agitation, with a pair of full, ever-playful eyes, with a face of constant laughter, filled with manifold curiosities, a dwelling-place of the sportive play with companion-folk, eager for gazing at calves — I worship inwardly the boyhood occupied by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! // [śārdūla]
Moreover:
Fair and dark, wearing garments of blue and yellow luster, skilled in the lessons of horn-playing and flute-blowing, playful in sport, wondrously displayed among the circle of friends — the two boys <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! // [śālinī]'

children.text: etad-avadhi ca vastra-paridhānaṃ krameṇa niścitaṃ jātaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: And from this point onward, the wearing of garments was gradually established, as follows:

children.text:
vastraṃ dadhāti jananī-nihitaṃ prayatnāt
  kṣipraṃ ca bandhana-dhiyā svayam ujjahāti |
  bhūyas tad ardati bibharti ca yasya cārdhaṃ
  vrīḍāṃ vikalpya laghu nityayati sma kṛṣṇaḥ ||JGc_1,10.3|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: The garment placed by the mother he puts on with effort, and quickly removes it himself with the intention of bondage [i.e., thinking it a binding]; again he tears at it, and bears half of it — thus, having devised modesty bit by bit, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> made it permanent! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tatra nityam eva gojātam anuyātena tātena saha yātavantau samantād alaṃ tau bhramataḥ | yathā,
  agacchatāṃ tatra vane janānāṃ
  snehārthināṃ kroḍa-gatau pituś ca |
  apṛcchatāṃ tat-prati-vastu bālāv
  ayacchatāṃ śarma ca rāma-kṛṣṇau ||JGc_1,10.4|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
There, having daily followed the father who accompanied the cow-herds, those two wandered about on all sides amply. As follows:
Wherever those two went in the forest, people seeking affection and riding in their father's lap would ask about each thing — and those two boys, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bestowed happiness! // [upajāti]

children.text: tatra ca nivāryamāṇāv api visphāry-aham-pūrvikayā go-goyugaṃ gogoyuga-yugaṃ go-ṣaḍ-gavam api yugapad vaśayantāv akrīḍatām | anantaram api parasparam aparasparaṃ sadravam eva dravantau vighaṭita-dhenv-anaḍuha-saṅghaṭṭāv uddhatā dhenur vṛṣabhān api śṛṅga-grāhaṃ nivartayataḥ sma | kiṃ ca, pañcakenāpi paśūn gṛhṇītaḥ sma |
children.translated_text: There, though restrained, with expanding 'I-first!' rivalry, they brought under control a pair of cows, a yoke of four cows, even a group of six cows all at once, and played! Subsequently too, running with and without each other at full speed, having scattered the herds of cows and bulls, those impetuous ones even turned back bulls by seizing their horns! Moreover, they would catch animals even with [just] five [fingers].

children.text: dina-katipaye punar evaṃ gata-samaye tad etad upadhārya vrajeśvaryā patiṃ prati praṇaya-sphurad-upālambhaṃ bhaṇitaṃ, kim idam apūrvam iva kurvanti tatra-bhavantaḥ? iti | tena ca lajjātaṅkau sajjatā tau vañcayatā vanaṃ cañcatāmunānumatā taṃ ca taṃ ca sā ca sā ca tan-mātā vana-gamanatas tanayam atipraṇayān niruddhavatī | [7] niruddhau ca tāv utkaṇṭhāviṣṭhāv arodiṣṭām | tatra ca kadācid ahnāya nihnavam ārabhya pitur abhyarṇaṃ gacchantau, savayobhyaḥ sukhaṃ yacchantau vartmāparikalya vrajabahir upaśalya-sthair vatsa-pālyair bālaiḥ kṛta-melantau khelantau tat-pālāyamānau mumudāte |
children.translated_text: Then, after some days had thus passed, the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, having observed all this, addressed her husband with a reproach sparkling with affection: 'What is this unprecedented thing that your honors are doing?' And he, concealing his embarrassment with readiness, deceiving those two — having been permitted by that one [the queen] — each mother restrained her son from going to the forest out of excessive affection. [7] And those two, when restrained, stood filled with longing and wept. And there, sometimes, beginning with a denial [of intent] for the day, going near the father, giving happiness to their age-mates, without knowing the path, reaching the outskirts of <s>Vraja</s>, meeting with the calf-herding boys stationed in the nearby pasture-grounds, playing, tending [calves] — they delighted!

children.text: tad evaṃ tayor asakṛtkṛtim anubhūya bhūyaḥ śrī-vraja-bhūpatī dampatī sukha-sambhūyamānatāyām api bhavya-dūyamāna-manastayā mantrayāmāsatuḥ: yadi go-saṅgāvasthānaṃ vinā na sthātuṃ pārayatas, tarhi vraja-sadeśa-deśe vatsān eva tāvat sañcārayatām iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, having experienced their repeated [escapades], the royal couple of Śrī <s>Vraja</s>, even while experiencing happiness together, with their noble minds pained, deliberated: 'If they cannot remain without being in the company of cows, then let them at least tend calves in the region near <s>Vraja</s> for now.'

children.text: tad etad eva vrajarājaḥ sahajādibhir mantra-vidbhiḥ saha mantra-sahatayā vicārya, tantra-vidbhiḥ puṇya-dinam avadhārya, puṇyāha-vācanādikam api sañcārya tābhyāṃ go-bāla-pālanārambham ācārayāmbabhūva | [10] tābhyām eva saha mahā-gopālā mahaṃ vidhāya manasi ca sukhaṃ nidhāya nija-nija-bālān vatsa-pālān kalayāmāsuḥ | yasya cādau jananī-janitena majjana-sajjanena bhojana-bhajanena vasana-vasanena sad-alaṅkaraṇa-dharaṇena vetra-netra-muralī-gavalānāṃ valanena ca bala-kṛṣṇau śobhāṃ lebhāte |
children.translated_text: This very thing the king of <s>Vraja</s> considered together with <s>Sahaja</s> and other ministers through careful counsel, and having the astrologers determine an auspicious day, and having performed the <s>puṇyāha-vācana</s> (auspicious recitation) and other rites, he had those two inaugurated into the commencement of calf-herding. [10] With those two themselves, the great cowherds performed a grand ceremony, and placing happiness in their hearts, assigned their own respective boys as calf-herders. And at the start of that, by the mother's preparation of bathing and grooming, feeding and dining, dressing and clothing, wearing of fine ornaments, and the handling of sticks, ropes, flutes, and horn-trumpets — <s>Bala</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> obtained splendor.

children.text:
kṛṣṇas tv ānīte upānahau nahi-nahi-kāreṇa bahiś cakāra, kula-paramparā-gata-dhana-godhan-samārādhana-dharma-marma-bādhanaṃ hi tat-prasādhana-vaśād bhavati iti | tataḥ kṛṣṇa-bhāvam anubhavatā rāmeṇāpi tathānumatam | [12] duṣkara-gaṇanāni godhanāni tu nūnaṃ kṛta-tad-avadhānāni tad-ānukūlyāya prakhara-khara-khura-khanana-khuralībhir mṛn-maya-reṇūn api puṣpa-reṇūn iva vidhāya karkarākaṇṭakādikam api khaṇḍaśas tathā sandhāya tadīya-caraṇa-pracāra-bhūmiṃ sukha-sañcāratayā kārayāmāsuḥ | vasudhā ca sudhā-sekam eva tadīya-caraṇa-sañcāreṇa manvānā vṛndayā saha ca yogaṃ tanvānā tad-ānukūlyāvaśeṣaṃ niravaśeṣaṃ cakāra | yathā ca khadira-vanādikam api sukha-sañcārāya samyag adhikaṃ bhavati | [13] yathā ca
sarvatra tadīya-caraṇa-kiśalayālaya-sūkṣma-rekhā-lekhānām udayaḥ sarva-mud-ayanaṃ bhavatīti prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ |
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, when shoes were brought, cast them outside with a 'No! No!' — for the adorning of [feet with] those would violate the essence of the dharma of worshipping the cows and cattle-wealth received through family tradition. Then <s>Rāma</s> too, experiencing the sentiment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, likewise assented. [12] The cattle, countless in number, surely mindful of him, for his convenience, with their sharp, hard hooves' digging, made even the dust-particles into flower-pollen, and even thorns of the <s>karkara</s> plant and the like they arranged in pieces to make the ground of his footsteps easy to traverse. And the earth too, considering his footsteps as a sprinkling of nectar, creating connection with <s>Vṛndā</s> (Tulasī), made whatever remained for his convenience entirely complete. As even an <s>Acacia</s> (<s>khadira</s>) forest and the like become perfectly easy to traverse. [13] As follows:
'The arising of the tender, delicate lines of his lotus-feet's resting-place everywhere — that becomes the abode of all joy' — thus let us follow the main narrative.

children.text:
tad evaṃ mahā-maṅgala-saṅgatatayā vatsa-cāraṇotsavam anukriyamāṇe prayāṇe samudgata-śobha-samudgaka-vicitrac-chatra-cāmara-paṭṭa-paṭādi-nānā-sāmagrī-saṅgraha-vyagrībhūta-karā bhuvana-śubhaṅkarā jita-vṛndākarāḥ kiṅkara-dārakās tāv anusarantaḥ kim apy antaḥ-sukham anubabhūvuḥ | [15] tatra ca mātara-pitarāv ārabhya pratyāgāra-dvāraṃ sarvābhir anarvācīnābhir vara-varṇinībhir mahā-dhanair nirmañchyamānau dīpāyamāna-maṇibhir nīrājyamānau praphulla-surabhi-prasūnair abhivṛṣyamāṇau maṅgala-saṅgha-saṅgata-gītaiḥ saṅgīyamānau yathārhaṃ tad-antika-vacana-kānti-santatibhiḥ santoṣyamāṇau, purastād vikīrṇa-vistīrṇa-nayanair nirvarṇyamānau gurūn abhivādya niravadya-vādya-prasādyamāna-kautuka-pratataṃ pratasthāte
| [16] yatra divya-gaṇāś ca tadvad eva dīvyanti sma | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, with the conjunction of great auspiciousness, as the festival of calf-herding departure was being celebrated — servant boys with hands busy gathering the collection of manifold equipment such as beautifully risen ornamental parasols, resplendent <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), silk banners and the like, making the world auspicious, surpassing clusters of <s>Vṛndā</s> [groves] — following those two, experienced some indescribable inner happiness. [15] There, beginning from the parents, at every house-gate, by all the excellent ladies of unexcelled description, the two were anointed by great riches, consecrated with shining gems, showered with fragrant blossoming flowers, sung to with songs accompanied by auspicious groups, properly gratified by the streams of beautiful words from those nearby, and having bowed to the elders — they set forth, their curiosity gratified by the faultless music, extended broadly before them, eyes scattered wide with wonder. [16] Where divine hosts too sported in just the same manner. And then —

children.text:
veṇu-vetra-dala-śṛṅgavaṭībhiḥ
kanduka-bhramara-dāru-naṭībhiḥ |
  krīḍinau sa-śiśu-go-suta-jāte
nīla-pīta-vasanau rurucāte ||JGc_1,10.5|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: With flutes, sticks, leaf-cups, horn-baskets, with balls, whirligigs, and wooden puppets — those two playful ones, in the company of children and calves, wearing blue and yellow garments, shone forth! // [svāgatā]

children.text: tad anu, dūrataḥ sūratatayā purataḥ paśyadṛśaḥ pitṛtatsadṛśas te kāṃścit prauḍhān ūḍhāvadhānān vidhāya, cārapradeśavicāram abhidhāya ca, kramata eva vyutkramataḥ kramamāṇāḥ sukṛtinaḥ kṛtinaḥ parāvavṛtire | [18] rāma-rāmānujādayaś ca kiñcid añcitvā-
children.translated_text: Then, from afar, with heroic bearing, with forward-looking eyes, the father-like ones — having appointed certain mature and capable guardians, and having communicated the plan for the grazing-area — gradually turning back as they stepped along, those fortunate, accomplished ones returned. [18] And <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), and the others, having saluted slightly —

children.text:
visārya vatsān āvārya paritaḥ śādvale sthale |
  khelāṃ cakrur mitho melād āvelāṃ bhojanāgateḥ ||JGc_1,10.6|| [anuṣṭubh]
yathā,
  veṇuṃ vādayatoḥ phalādi kiratoḥ śiñjat-tulākoṭi-bhāg-
  aṅghribhyāṃ kṣipator vṛṣānukaraṇaiḥ saṃyudhyator etayoḥ |
  bhrātror nirjayinor mitho drava-vaśād uccaiḥ sakhāyaś ca te
  pārṣṇi-grāhatayā yudhaṃ vidadhataḥ kolāhalaṃ cakrire ||JGc_1,10.7|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Having released the calves and corralled them all around on the green meadow, they played together until the time of the meal arrived, from the joy of meeting! // [anuṣṭubh]
As follows:
Of the two playing the flute, scattering fruits and the like, kicking with feet clinking with rows of anklets, fighting mock-battles with imitations of bulls — those two brothers, each victorious, and those companions of theirs too, supporting each [side] from behind, waged [playful] war and created an uproar! // [śārdūla]

children.text: tataś ca tau vatsāṃs tṛṇair āpyāyya jalam āpāyya sarvān vilokitavantau | śrī-kṛṣṇas tu teṣu kasyacid gaṇḍādi-kaṇḍūti-khaṇḍanena bāhu-daṇḍa-kṛta-kaṇṭhāvaguṇṭhanena, mātaraṃ militum icchasi? melayiṣyāmi iti tat-karṇe mithaḥ kapola-melana-pūrvaka-vṛthā-varṇanena ca tam upacarya sukham upalabdhavān |
children.translated_text: Then those two, having nourished the calves with grass and given them water, surveyed them all. Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, attending to one of them by scratching its cheek-itch and the like, wrapping his arm around its neck, and whispering in its ear with face-to-cheek meeting: 'Do you want to meet your mother? I shall bring about the meeting!' — obtained happiness by thus caring for it.

children.text:
atha bhrātarau sakhibhir jalāplavana-kelim ācarya vanya-veśa-viśeṣam apy āsajjya caraṇa-caryayā carantāv apūrva-mṛga-pakṣiṇaḥ samantāl lakṣayantau vailakṣyam āsedatuḥ | tatra ca,
  rutam anukurutas tau līlayā yasya jantoḥ
  samudayati tadīyaṃ jāti-mātraṃ tadāśu |
  bhaṇitam atha vidhattas tad-viruddhasya tasmin
  yadi bhayam anu tasmāl līyate taj javena ||JGc_1,10.8|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
Then the two brothers, having performed the sport of water-splashing with their companions, and having also put on a special forest-costume, moving about on foot, observing novel birds and animals all around — they reached a state of amazement. And there:
Whichever creature's cry those two playfully imitated, that creature's entire species would immediately appear; and then, if they uttered the call of that one's enemy, that [species] would flee from it with speed, in fear! // [mālinī]

children.text:
tataś cāhnāya madhyāhnāśanam ādāya sva-sva-dhāmataḥ samāgatābhis tad-ucitābhir vanitābhir janitānandanaḥ śrīmān nanda-nandanaḥ sakhi-vṛndam ānandayan vāṇīya-māna-veṇu-raṇitenākāraṇayā maṅkṣu saṅkalayāmāsa | saṅkalitāṃś ca sakhīn eṇīdṛśaḥ śreṇīkṛtya cādṛtya ca samupaveśitān suveśitān madhyam adhyāsita-śyāma-rāmān bhojana-kāmān krama-niśāmanayā yām anayā jemayāmāsuḥ | [22] yatra narmaṇā śarma-dānāya kiñcit kaścit kiñcit kaścid viśiślāghe śaślāghe ca | yatra ca tair vivadamānānāṃ saṃvadamānānāṃ cānyāsāṃ vacana-prativacana-śravaṇa-kautukānantaraṃ dhātrī-gaṇa-pātrī kācit tu dāsera-bālakān prati phelā-visarjana-rañjanāya pūrti-vyañjanayā bhojana-vitṛṣṇatām anucariṣṇuṃ
kṛṣṇaṃ prati sa-kāku jagāda-
children.translated_text: Then, at midday, having brought the midday meal from their own homes, the fitting women who arrived — generating delight — the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s>, delighting the circle of companions, quickly assembled them by the unfeigned sound of the flute being played. And the doe-eyed women, having arranged the assembled companions in rows, having honored them, having seated those well-dressed ones — with dark <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> seated in the middle, eager to eat — fed them with gradual attentiveness. [22] Where, for the giving of pleasure through humor, someone praised this one and someone that. And where, after the curiosity of hearing the words and counter-words of those arguing and conversing women, a certain nurse — the chief vessel [of affection] — addressed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who was becoming disinterested in eating, with a coaxing expression of satiation, toward the servant-boys, for the delight of distributing morsels:

children.text:
mayā yatnād etad drava-madhuram ārād upahṛtam
  jananyā rāmasya prayatana-yujā sādhitam idam |
  bhavan-mātrā cāsya svadana-vidhaye datta-śapathaṃ
  muhuḥ sandiṣṭaṃ tan nikhilam upayuṅkṣva trayam api ||JGc_1,10.9|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'This liquid-sweet [food] I brought with effort from afar; this [dish] was prepared by the mother of <s>Rāma</s> with labor; and your own mother gave a sworn command for its savoring — all three, please consume them entirely, again and again!' // [śikharinī]

children.text: tad evaṃ kautuka-viśeṣeṇa jāte bhojana-śeṣe racitācamanaṃ tam ananta-guṇa-kamanaṃ rāma-dāmādibhiḥ sahitaṃ sahitaṃ sā punaḥ karpūra-rasa-pūra-pūrṇa-khapura-pūrita-sacūrṇa-svarṇa-varṇa-parṇa-puṭa-dāna-puraḥ-saram evam avādīt, lālya-pālyamāna-mātṛ-sandeśatayā bālyam apahāya tūrṇam eva vraja-sadanaṃ pūrṇam ācaraṇīyam |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the meal-remainder was completed with special delight, having performed the mouth-rinsing, she spoke to him — that one of infinite desirable qualities, together with <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Dāma</s> and others — preceded by the gift of camphor-juice-filled, powder-dusted, gold-colored leaf-packages, as follows: 'By the message of the mother who is to be fondled and tended, abandoning childhood [play], you must speedily come to the house of <s>Vraja</s> fully [on time].'

children.text: atha kiñcid dūraṃ gatvā tasya teṣāṃ ca khelā-melābhiniveśaṃ matvā grīvāṃ parāvartya nartyamāna-nayanatayā samarthāṃs tat-pālakān bālakān praty uvāca-are re, śīghram evāyaṃ prāṇayanīyo vraja-dharaṇīśa-praṇayinyāḥ prāṇasya prāṇaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then, having gone some distance, perceiving the absorption of his and their play-assembly, turning her neck, with dancing eyes, she said to the capable guardian-boys: 'Come, come — quickly! This one who must be brought with love is the very life of the life of the queen who is devoted to the lord of <s>Vraja</s>!'

children.text: tad evaṃ gatāsu tāsu sāgrajaḥ sa tu duṣparihara-bāṣpa-cchedya-sa-puṣpa- tṛṇa-mukhān vatsān vrajābhimukhān vidhāya śanaiś cārayan gāyan nṛtyan hasan krīḍan divi-carair brāhmaṇair brāhmaṇaiḥ stūyamānaḥ sumanobhiś ca sumanobhir vṛṣyamāṇaḥ svagṛhāya vartma jagṛhe |
children.translated_text: Thus, when those [women] had departed, he, together with his elder brother, having directed the calves — whose faces bore grass and flowers with tears hard to restrain — toward <s>Vraja</s>, slowly driving them, singing, dancing, laughing, playing — praised by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> [both] divine and earthly, and showered with flowers and blessings — he took the path toward his home.

children.text:
tataś ca vatsāvāsaṃ yāvat sāgraja-mitra-vrajatayā yathākramaṃ vikramamānas tatra ca vatsān saṅkṛtya kṛta-kṛtyatayā ramamāṇas tal-lāvaṇya-darśanena harṣamānas tat prāg eva sarvair vraja-vāsibhir upavrajyamānaḥ snānādi-pūrvakaṃ divyam ambaraṃ valayamānaḥ śīghram eva bhojanaṃ bhajamānaḥ punar api go-dohana-bhūmi-gamanena sukhaṃ yajamānas tat-tan-mātṛ-nāmabhir vatsān hvayamānaḥ sambhramatas tad-gamana-vyatikramāt prahāsa-maya-mānaḥ pradugdhāni dugdhāni ca tāni kiṅkara-nikareṇa gṛhaṃ hārayamāṇaḥ punar ālayam āgamya kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ mātaram ānandya tām anu vindamānaś candra-śālikāṃ viśramāya śrayamāṇaḥ punar sarveṣām atiharṣaṃ vavarṣa | prasvāpya ca taṃ ca taṃ ca sā ca sā ca mātā paritaḥ parijana-kumārān
sannidhāpya gṛha-vyavahārāya bṛhad-dhāma jagāma |
children.translated_text: And then, proceeding gradually with his elder brother and the company of friends to the calf-station, and there, having gathered the calves and delighting as one whose task is fulfilled, rejoicing at the sight of their beauty, being approached even beforehand by all the residents of <s>Vraja</s>, donning divine garments preceded by bathing and the like, partaking of food very quickly, again finding happiness by going to the cow-milking grounds, calling the calves by their respective mothers' names, becoming a source of laughter from the comical confusion when they ran the wrong way, having the milked and freshly-milked quantities of milk sent home by the troop of servants, returning again to the residence, delighting his mother for a few moments and then following her to the moon-pavilion to rest — he again showered supreme delight upon all. And having put this one and that one to sleep, this mother and that mother, stationing the attendants' children all around, went to the great hall for the household affairs.

children.text: tad evaṃ dina-katipaye parama-ramaṇena gamita-samaye sa tu nṛśaṃsaḥ kaṃsa-nāmā yathārha-varṇa-kṛta-varṇanataḥ samākīrṇa-tat-tad-vṛndāvanāgamanādi-vṛttāntaḥ svāntaś cintayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Thus, when a few days had passed in supremely delightful time, that cruel one named <s>Kaṃsa</s> — having been filled with the various reports of the arrival at <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and other events, through descriptions rendered in appropriately colored narration — reflected inwardly:

children.text: hanta, satyatā-sāreṇa devyā vacanānusāreṇa nanda-gopa-ḍimbhatā-dambha eva sa ko' pi gopitaḥ sambhāvyate, yena nūtanāvayavenāpi duḥsaha-mahasaḥ pūtanādayaḥ sahasā gāmbhīryāvṛttena vīryātiśayenālambhanīyatāṃ lambhitāḥ | trasyati ca tasya nāma-dhāma-vaśān mama hṛdayam | tasmād asau chalata evotkalanīyaḥ | hanta, chalān apy uttaram uttaram atiriktaṃ yuktam eva te prayuktavantaḥ | tathāpi kadarthitī-bhūya vyarthī-bhūtāḥ iti vicārya, punar api taṃ praṇidhiṃ sannidhiṃ nikāyyataḥ samānāyya papraccha, aye, tvayedam apy avakalitaṃ, jātau kasyāṃ tasyādaraḥ sneha-bharaś ca paramaḥ parāmṛśyate?
children.translated_text: "Alas, in accordance with the truth-bearing words of the Goddess (<s>Devī</s>), that deceitful disguise as a child of the cowherd <s>Nanda</s> is indeed suspected to conceal some hidden one, by whom — even with a novel body — the unbearable powers of <s>Pūtanā</s> and others were suddenly brought to a state of helplessness through valor of depth concealed beneath gravity. And my heart trembles on account of his name and abode. Therefore, he must be uprooted even by deception. Alas, even beyond deception, you (my agents) have employed increasingly excessive stratagems, yet they have been rendered contemptible and futile!" — having reflected thus, he again summoned that spy from nearby and asked: "Say, have you also discerned this — in which born creature does he show the greatest regard and fullness of affection?"

children.text: sa covāca-deva, go-vatseṣu tad-utsekaḥ pratīyate |
children.translated_text: And he replied: "Lord, his excessive fondness is perceived in the calves."

children.text: kaṃsa uvāca-samyag gamyatāṃ nijam eva harmyam | punaś cānyam uvāca-ākāryatāṃ purataḥ sa vatsāsuraḥ | sa ca śacī-pater api klamanaḥ | sa-sambhrama-vikrama-kramatayā tenānīya samarpitaḥ pānīya-lavavad drava-pravaṇatāvastha eva tasthau | tena ca sambandhatām āśaṃsan pāṃśu-saṅghaval labdha-dhvaṃsaḥ kaṃsas tūpāṃśu taṃ sutam iva śaśaṃsa, vatsa vatsāsura, gaccha nandasya vrajam | gatvā ca vatsāṃś cārayataḥ kumārayatas tat-kumārasya sadeśam āsādya nijaṃ vatsa-veśam utpādya tasyāpakāram ārabhasva |
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s> said: "Very well, go to your own quarters." And to another he said: "Bring before me that <s>Vatsāsura</s> (the calf-demon)." He who causes exhaustion even to the lord of <s>Śacī</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — brought with hasty, valorous strides and presented — stood in a state inclined to fluidity like a drop of water. And <s>Kaṃsa</s>, hoping for kinship with him and having been shattered like a mass of dust, praised him like a son: "Dear <s>Vatsāsura</s>, go to the <s>Vraja</s> of <s>Nanda</s>. And going there, approaching the vicinity of that prince who tends and plays with the calves, assuming the disguise of a calf, commence your attack upon him."

children.text: tataḥ sa ca, yathājñāpayanti rājñām ājñāpakāḥ iti tad-vacanānupathātmā tat pratiśāsanād atrāsam eva tatrājagāma | yatra svacche vatsa-krīḍana-nāmani yāmuna-kacche tad-vidha-māraka-karmā vraja-rāja-janmā vatsān mānayan nayana-viṣayaṃ viṣa-dharam iva taṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then he, with the attitude of "as the commanders of kings command" — his soul following the path of that command — by that decree, came here without fear. Where, on the bright bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> called the calf-playground, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, whose work was the slaying of such killers, honoring the calves, made him — a poison-bearer, as it were — the object of his gaze.

children.text: atha matsaratas tata itaḥ saratas tasya gandhānusandhānataḥ kṛtsnān khaṭa-deśam aṭataḥ śakṛtkarīn vyagraṃ paśyataḥ paśyann agrajaṃ vrajarāja-tanūjanū rahaḥ sa-vyājaṃ vyajahāra, bṛhad-bhrātaḥ, prātar anāyātaḥ paricīyate vā ko' yam upatoyaṃ pratīyate vatsaḥ?
children.translated_text: Then, out of rivalry, while that one was roaming hither and thither, tracking by scent the dung-making calves who were wandering all over the threshing-ground area, and watching him intently — watching him, the elder son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> spoke privately to his elder brother with a pretext: "Great brother, who is this calf that appeared this morning without having come [with the herd], and is perceived near the water?"

children.text: rāma uvāca-bhrātar, nahi nahi |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said: "Brother, no, no [I don't recognize him]."

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-nirūpyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "Let him be examined."

children.text: rāma uvāca-bhīṣaṇa-prakṛtir iva pratīyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said: "He appears to be of a terrifying nature."

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-pūrvaja, pūrva-devo' yam |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "Elder brother, this one is a former <s>deva</s> (demon in disguise)."

children.text: rāma uvāca-satyam, yasmād asmāsu vatseṣu cākasmād adṛṣṭijādṛṣṭir asya dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said: "True, since an unnatural, hostile gaze is suddenly seen in him toward us and the calves."

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-yadi bhavad-ādiṣṭaṃ syāt tarhy etaṃ diṣṭāntam āsādayāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "If it is commanded by you, then I shall bring this one to his destined end."

children.text: rāma uvāca-lokataḥ kalaṅkataḥ śaṅke |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said: "I fear blame from the public."

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-maraṇe ditya-patyatā param āgatya pratyakṣī-bhaviṣyaty asya | tataḥ ko' pi nāpavadeta |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "Upon his death, his <s>daitya</s> (demon) nature will become manifest to all. Then no one would reproach us."

children.text: rāmaḥ saharṣam uvāca-dviṣantapa, sacchalam etaṃ sacchalam eva mandaṃ mandam abhyavaskanda |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said with delight: "O tormentor of foes, assail this deceitful one — indeed, the deceitful one — slowly, slowly, with a stratagem!"

children.text: atha śrīvatsa-vakṣāś ca vatsān anyāṃś cucukāreṇa sannidhānaḥ kaṇṭha-gaṇḍa-piciṇḍādau kaṇḍūm apanayamānaḥ, sarvataḥ krīḍan gāyan parva tanvann ivāsīt |
children.translated_text: Then the one bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark on his chest, calling the other calves near with a 'coo-coo' sound, relieving the itching on their throats, cheeks, humps and the like, playing on all sides, singing — was as if weaving a festival.

children.text:
tatas tasyāpi labdha-chidraṃ-manyasya, kūṭa-mayyā sva-kaṇḍūti-vighaṭanecchayā nikaṭam aṭatas, tad akarkaśa-mudrayā sahasā tān hitvā taṃ sa-puccha-pādaṃ gṛhītvā bhramayāmāsa |
  yāvacchaḥ parivartanaṃ bhramayatā vatsasya cakre' munā
  tāvacchaḥ pratipat kramān niragamad rūpāntaraṃ cāgamat |
  krīḍāyāḥ phala-pātanārtham iva ca kṣipte kapitthopari
  jñātṛtvaṃ naṭavat kalāṃ ca pṛthukās te tasya śaślāghire ||JGc_1,10.10|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Then, when that one — who thought he had found an opening — came close with a deceitful approach, desiring to scratch his own itch (i.e., to attack), <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with a gesture that was not harsh, suddenly leaving the others, seized him by the tail and hind legs and whirled him around.
As many times as he whirled the calf around in revolutions,
that many times did he shed his successive forms and assume another appearance;
and when hurled upon a <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) tree as if for the purpose of knocking down the fruits of sport,
the young boys praised his skill and artistry like that of an actor! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.10, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
atha devaiḥ prasūnāni vṛṣṭāni hasitāni ca |
  na nāsayā na ca dṛśā bhinnatāṃ netum īśire ||JGc_1,10.11|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then the gods showered flowers and laughed;
neither through the nose nor through the eye could they manage to separate [laughter from tears]! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.11, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tad anu ca parihāsa-bhāsamāna-hāsaṃ divya-sabhāsadas tad idam avadaṃś ca, nūnam etad eva deva-vairi-vairiṇas tātparyaṃ paryavasyati |
children.translated_text: And then, with laughter sparkling in jest, the divine assembly-members said this: "Surely this is the very purpose in which the enemy of the enemies of the gods culminates!"

children.text:
vayaṃ gāṃ gopālāḥ paricinumahe tad-dviṣam api
  praticchanne rūpe' py anumiti-nidāna-vyatikarāt |
  ato re re vatsākṛti-suraripo mad-vidha-karāt
  kathaṃ te mokṣaḥ syād iha laṣasi cet pretya bhavatu ||JGc_1,10.12|| iti | [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"We cowherds know the cow; even the foe of cows we recognize
in disguised form too, through the cross-application of inferential evidence.
Therefore, O you in the form of a calf, enemy of the gods! From one skilled as I am,
how could you find liberation here? If you desire it, let it be in the hereafter!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.12, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ-
children.translated_text: Thus:

children.text:
tau vatsād api rakṣantau sarvaṃ lokaṃ rarakṣatuḥ |
  yad-arthaṃ prātarāśādi yasmin daitya-vadhādi ca ||JGc_1,10.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Those two, protecting even from the calves, protected the entire world;
for whose sake was the morning meal and such, and in whom was the slaying of demons and such! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.13, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tataś ca tad-dine' pi śrī-kṛṣṇa-rāmayoḥ svadhāma-samāgamanaṃ jātam, kintu tad-vṛttam aniṣṭam iti tad-iṣṭa-gaṇaḥ sarva evāvariṣṭa | tac ca, na jāne kiṃ-vadantī kiṃvadantī syād, iti sacintībhūya |
children.translated_text: And so, on that day too, the homecoming of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> took place; but the entire group of their dear ones suppressed that unpleasant event — having become anxious, thinking: "I know not what kind of rumor this rumor might become."

children.text: kaṃsas tu tasmād vatsapād api vatsāsura-nirvāsanam apasarpa-mukhād viṣam iva karṇa-randhra-sparśa-mātreṇāntaḥ sambhūya bhṛśaṃ dṛśau nimīlayāmāsa | tena daśamīm iva daśāṃ prāpitaḥ | sa tu mantribhiḥ kathañcid bahir avadhāpitaḥ sārdham eva tair idam acāru vicārayāmāsa, hanta sambhāvitā dambhānvitā bahavaḥ prasthāpitāḥ, na tu tair bhadraṃ kiñcid api sañcitam | teṣāṃ dhīpsā-vīpsā hi na hīpsāṃ trātavatī, pratyuta tān eva psātavatī | tataḥ kiṃ kurmaḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s>, however, hearing through the spy's mouth of the destruction of <s>Vatsāsura</s> along with the calves — like poison through the mere touch of the ear-hole — closed his eyes tightly, deeply [shaken]. By that, he was brought to a state like [that of] the tenth [day of the moon — nearly extinguished]. But somehow brought back to external awareness by his ministers, together with them he deliberated this unpleasant matter: "Alas! Many esteemed and deceit-equipped ones have been dispatched, but not a bit of good has been accumulated by them. Their desire to kill and repeated attempts did not protect their desire [to live], but rather destroyed them. So what shall we do?"

children.text: mantriṇa ūcuḥ, deva, kevalaṃ bakam atra balam avalambāmahe, yatas tajjātāv eva dambha-sambhārā gambhīrāyante |
children.translated_text: The ministers said: "Lord, we rely solely on <s>Baka</s> (the crane-demon) as our strength here, for in his very species, the stores of deceit run deep."

children.text: kaṃsa uvāca-āṃ āṃ, mama suhṛttamaḥ sa eva kevalas tatra prasthāpanāya sthāpyatām ity ānāyya tathādiṣṭaḥ sad-aniṣṭaḥ sa duṣṭaḥ kaṃsa-puṣṭaḥ samprati baka-sthala-nāmānaṃ nāndīśvara-giri-samīpa-dhāmānam upasarasaṃ pradeśaṃ bhāvi-kṛṣṇa-praveśam adhigamyābhigamya giri-śṛṅga-bhramārambhaṃ dambhaṃ dadhamānas tasthau | yatra tulya-paryāyatayā dambha eva gahvarāyate sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s> said: "Yes, yes! Let my dearest friend alone be stationed for dispatch there." — thus summoned and so instructed, that wicked one, nourished by <s>Kaṃsa</s>, inauspicious to the good — now standing at the place called <s>Baka-sthala</s>, near the mountain <s>Nāndīśvara</s>, a marshy region destined for <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> future arrival — bearing the pretense of being a mountain-peak while swooping about, he stood. Where, with equal aptness, deceit itself deepened into a cavern.

children.text: tadā ca śrī-gopāla-valitā gopāla-bālā go-bālān pālayantaḥ pānīyaṃ pāyayantaḥ kūlam anusthāpayantaḥ svayam api payaḥ-pānam ayantaḥ parasparaṃ snapayantaḥ samutthāya ca kalāpayantaś cikrīḍuḥ | kalāpayantaś ca puṣpāharaṇāya parataḥ pracāram āceruḥ, tam ācarantaś ca taṃ bakam īkṣāmāsur utprekṣāmāsuś ca: aho, girir ayaṃ dūrata eva kutaḥ? puras tasya śṛṅgam | tataḥ sadya evādaḥ śata-manyunā manyunā śata-koṭi-troṭitam iti ghaṭate | punar nicāyya ca procuḥ, nedaṃ giri-śṛṅgaṃ saṅgacchate, kintu jantu-viśeṣaḥ so' yaṃ mantum iva cikīrṣann amitaśīrṣaṃ vartate, yata ugram-paśyatayā kharatā-cañcu-cuñcutayā ca baka iva parāmṛśyate |
children.translated_text: Then the cowherd boys, accompanied by the glorious <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), tending the young calves, making them drink water, stationing them along the bank, themselves also drinking the water, splashing each other, and then rising and engaging in play — and while playing, they set out further afield for flower-gathering. And as they went about, they beheld that <s>Baka</s> (crane-demon) and conjectured: "Aho! This mountain — from where does it appear so close? Before it is its peak. Therefore, it must have just now been split into a hundred million fragments by the hundred-powered one (<s>Indra</s>) — that makes sense!" But upon looking more carefully, they said: "This doesn't match a mountain peak, but rather it is some special creature, standing with its immeasurable head as if pondering something — since, from its fierce-looking appearance and the sharpness-beak-pointedness, it is perceived to be like a crane."

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-
  ākārāt pakṣitulyaḥ syād vyāpārān na ca pakṣivat |
  bakaḥ kiṃ navakaḥ sākṣāt kūṭavat sthitir īkṣyate? ||JGc_1,10.14|| [anuṣṭubh]

atra tatra jigamiṣann eva samiṣa-śliṣṭatāviśiṣṭaṃ kūṭa-śabdaṃ paṭhitavān | [51] atha samuddaṇḍa-daṇḍa-varaṇḍa-sakhi-maṇḍala-maṇḍitaḥ puṇḍarīka-locanas taṃ jānann apy ajānann iva tasya tuṇḍa-sannidhim eva gamane' vadhiñcakāra | sparśa-viṣa-viṣadhara-viśeṣa-kumāraḥ kautukātireka-vaśād bhekasyeva |
children.translated_text: Here, desiring to go there himself, he recited the word <s>kūṭa</s> — distinguished by its intertwined double meaning ("peak" and "fraud"). [51] Then the lotus-eyed one, adorned by the circle of friends with upraised staffs and goads, though knowing him, as if not knowing, resolved to go right up to his beak. Like a frog impelled by excess of curiosity, that prince among poison-touch-possessing serpents [approached].

children.text:
tataś ca gaṇḍūpadaṃ manyamānaḥ sa ca maṇḍūka iva kuṇḍali-pogaṇḍaṃ taṃ nijagāra, na tu kiñcit kuñcayitum api śaśāka | kintu hanta, hanta, sphūrtiṃ prati santama-sadharmaṇā tena karmaṇā śrī-rāma-dāmādīn prāṇair vikalitāṃ kalayāmāsa |
  sva-bhrātṛ-vīryaṃ januṣā vidann api
  pralamba-kārir baka-ceṣṭite' rditaḥ |
  bhaiṣmīkṛte tasya gatau yathaiva sa
  premā hi sarvaṅgila-bhāvam ṛcchati ||JGc_1,10.15|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then, considering him a worm, that one — like a frog — swallowed the boy <s>Kuṇḍalin</s> (the coiled one, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), but could not constrict him even slightly. But alas, alas! Through that act — which by its effect on the eruption of awareness was equal to the ultimate darkness — <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Dāma</s> and the others were rendered as if bereft of life.
Though knowing by birth his brother's valor,
<s>Rāma</s>, who later destroyed <s>Pralamba</s>, was afflicted by <s>Baka's</s> action;
just as when <s>Bhīṣma's</s> [valor] was countered, that very same he —
for love indeed attains a state that consumes everything! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.15, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: atha bakaḥ sva-kaṇṭhāvaṭe kṛpīṭa-yonivat kapaṭa-tejaskaṃ taṃ jhaṭity ujjagāra | tataś ca, so' yaṃ mama hṛdayam abhrākṣīd iti vibhāvya punas tan nigaraṇa-yogyaṃ nādrākṣīt, kintu tataḥ parāṅ-mukhaḥ sa punar baka iva mūrkhaḥ sura-śātrava-bakas tejo-mātra-gātratayāvagatam api taṃ troṭi-koṭibhyāṃ troṭayitum udayuṅkta | [54] sa tu śauṭīrya-koṭīśvaras tat-troṭī karābhyāṃ vighaṭayaṃs taṃ sa-pāṭavaṃ pāṭayāmāsa, bhīmo jarāsandham iva, bālo vīraṇam iva vā |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Baka</s>, from the hollow of his own throat — like a fire-born creature — suddenly vomited him out, that one of fraudulent brilliance. And then, "He has pierced my heart!" — perceiving thus, he again did not find him fit for swallowing; but then, turning away, that foolish crane-like enemy of the gods attempted to crush him — who was perceived as pure brilliance of body — with the pincers of his beak in a hundred-million-fold crushing. [54] But that lord of the pinnacle of valor, opening those pincers with both hands, split him apart — as <s>Bhīma</s> [split] <s>Jarāsandha</s>, or as a child [splits] a blade of <s>vīraṇa</s> grass.

children.text:
yadā murāriṃ nijagāra kahvas
tadā sakhāyaḥ sabalā mumūrcchuḥ |
  udgīrṇavān yarhi tadānvacetan
svabhāva-jaṃ prema parān apekṣi ||JGc_1,10.16|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
When the crane swallowed <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
then his friends, including <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), fainted;
when he was disgorged, then they regained consciousness —
for inherent love depends upon the other ['s fate]! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.16, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: yatra vṛndārakā dārakāś ca kramān mumudire | yathā-
children.translated_text: There the heavenly beings and the boys gradually rejoiced. As follows:

children.text:
bakāsure vatsasurāri-ghātinā
hate surā nartana-vādya-vartanāḥ |
  te nandanād apy atisetutāṃ gatā
mallyādyam ullūya mudā varīvṛṣuḥ ||JGc_1,10.17|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
When <s>Bakāsura</s> was slain by the slayer of the calf-demon's foe,
the gods, engaged in dance, music, and festivities,
having surpassed even <s>Nandana</s> (Indra's garden) in bliss,
showered garlands and the like, tossing them with delight! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.10.17, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇābhiprāyam utprekṣamāṇāḥ sādbhutaṃ prekṣamāṇā bakam upajahasuś ca | yathā-
children.translated_text: Conjecturing the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> intention, gazing upon <s>Baka</s> with wonder, they also laughed. As follows:

children.text:
prasārayaṃs tvaṃ grasanāya cañcuṃ
sāhāyakaṃ tatra mayāpy akāri |
  vidīrṇam āsīd yadi sarvam aṅgaṃ
mamāsti doṣaḥ kva nu mūḍha kahva? ||JGc_1,10.18|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
'You, extending your beak to devour —
even I rendered assistance there!
If all your limbs were split asunder,
where then is my fault, O fool, O crane?' ||10.18|| [upajāti]

children.text:
tatra ca-
  yasmin bakāsyād udite' pi te' rbhakā
  jijīvur asmin milite bakāntake |
  teṣv aśru-kampa-svara-bhaṅga-saṅgataṃ
  vaivarṇyam ṛcchet kim u varṇanīyatām ||JGc_1,10.19|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
And there:
Those boys who survived when you emerged from <s>Baka's</s> beak,
and now when this slayer of <s>Baka</s> has appeared among them —
would tears, trembling, breaking of voice, and
paleness come upon them — is that even fit for description? ||10.19|| [upajāti]

children.text: atha sarve samaya-vyagratayā śīghram eva tasmin sarasi militvā snātvā taṃ pradeśaṃ hitvā kṛṣṇaṃ gṛhītvā gṛhāya pratasthire |
children.translated_text: Then all of them, with urgency born of the occasion, quickly assembled at that lake, bathed, left that spot, took <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and set out for home.

children.text:
kṛta-gṛhāgamanā vraja-bālakās
tad akhilaṃ khalu vṛttam avarṇayan |
  baka-khagasya tathākṛtitā
tathā śiśu-kṛtā mṛtir evam abhūd iti ||JGc_1,10.20|| [drutavilambitā]
  tad-vārtā-yugalena gokula-bhuvāṃ dagdhaṃ ca siktaṃ ca yat
  pratyaṅgaṃ tad idaṃ layāya bhavitety evaṃ janaiḥ śaṅkitam |
  paścāt pratyuta romaharṣam adadhād yat tat tu yuktaṃ parā
  vārtā tatra varāmṛtād api parā tair evam āsvādyata ||JGc_1,10.21|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
The boys of <s>Vraja</s>, having returned home,
narrated all that had transpired:
'Such was the form of the crane-bird <s>Baka</s>,
and thus was his death accomplished by the child!' ||10.20|| [drutavilambitā]
By that pair of tidings, the people of <s>Gokula</s> were both burned and sprinkled;
that this was leading toward dissolution was feared by the people, limb by limb;
but afterwards, on the contrary, it produced horripilation — and that indeed was fitting, for the
latter tiding, surpassing even the finest nectar, was thus savored by them! ||10.21|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
tataś ca te sarve samudvignam uditāḥ samuditā vitrāsānanda-nispandaṃ śrīman-nanda-mandira-jana-vṛndam anuvindamānāḥ śrī-govinda-vadanāravindam asra-sanditāḥ sandarīdṛśya parāmṛśya ca bakāntānām aśāntānāṃ maraṇe kāraṇaṃ parasparam ūcuḥ-
  asya bālasya kiṃ pūrvaṃ kim apūrvaṃ vrajeśituḥ |
  kim arthaṃ vā pūrvam āgas te cakrus te hatā yataḥ ||JGc_1,10.22|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then all of them, having arisen in great agitation and come together, finding the people of the glorious <s>Nanda's</s> mansion motionless with the tremor of fear and joy, beholding the lotus-face of the glorious <s>Govinda</s> with tear-soaked [eyes], touching and reflecting upon him, they spoke to one another about the cause of the death of the unpeaceful demons ending with <s>Baka</s>:
'Of this child, what was first, and what was unprecedented for the lord of <s>Vraja</s>?
Or what offense had they previously committed, that they were slain?' ||10.22|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ prapañce' vatīrṇānām api śrīman-nandādīnāṃ tad-varṇanānandād adīnānāṃ prapañca-dharmeṇa saṅkīrṇatāṃ na varṇayāmāsuḥ | ūcuś ca śrī-bādarāyaṇi-caraṇāḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, even though the glorious <s>Nanda</s> and others had descended into the phenomenal world, they — undaunted because of the joy of narrating his deeds — did not describe the affliction that is the law of the phenomenal world. And the feet of the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva) said:

children.text: iti nandādayo gopāḥ kṛṣṇa-rāma-kathāṃ mudā |
kurvanto ramamānāś ca nāvindan bhava-vedanām ||[BhP 10.11.58] iti |
children.translated_text: the tales of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> with joy, did not experience the suffering of worldly existence.' [BhP 10.11.58]
'Thus the cowherds, headed by <s>Nanda</s>, delighting in

children.text: tad etad baka-nirgranthanam ugram ugrasena-duṣputraḥ śrotreṇāpīya vyagra-cetā babhūva, bhāvayāmāsa ca-hanta, sarva eva māyātiriktatā-prayoktāras tatra riktī-kṛtāḥ | sarvaṃ lumpantas te culumpāmāsire ca | tarhi vyomābhidhāna-dānava-mātram atra pātraṃ paśyāmaḥ | [61] sarva-māyā-maya-maya-tanayaḥ prakhyāta-bala-valayaḥ sa hi mahīyān iti padmāvatī-jaraṭha-jaṭhara-janmā saṃmānanayā tam ānāyya tat-kāryāya paryāpayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Now, this gruesome dispatch of <s>Baka</s> — the wicked son of <s>Ugrasena</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) drank it in through his ears and became agitated in mind, and reflected: 'Alas, all who were dispatched as agents of supernatural craft have been rendered empty there! All who went plundering have been themselves plundered! Then the only one we see as a fitting vessel for this task is the demon named <s>Vyoma</s>.' [61] <s>Vyoma</s>, son of the all-illusory <s>Maya</s>, of renowned might and prowess — he being the greater one, born from the aged womb of <s>Padmāvatī</s> — <s>Kaṃsa</s> honorably summoned him and charged him with that task.

children.text: sa cāgamya vyoma-nāmā kṛta-vyomāvalambatayā nyakṣeṇa vīkṣamāṇaḥ kāmyakāraṇya-dharaṇī-dhara-sannidhānataḥ samam atyarbhaka-vṛndenātyarbhakatayā nirvrīḍa-krīḍā-sandarbhaṃ śrī-yaśodā-garbha-jātaṃ śrī-rohiṇy-arbhakaṃ vinā samāyātaṃ dadarśa vimamarśa ca-
children.translated_text: He, the one named <s>Vyoma</s>, came and — having assumed an aerial vantage point, gazing downward obliquely — from the vicinity of the <s>Kāmyaka</s> forest mountain, saw along with a group of very young boys, himself appearing as a very young boy, the shameless play-spectacle of the one born from the womb of the glorious <s>Yaśodā</s>, who had come without the son of the glorious <s>Rohiṇī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>). And he reflected:

children.text:
ete khalu bhoḥ dāsyāḥ-putra ! caurasya-kula ! paśyato-hara ! devānāṃ priya ! iti parasparaṃ sambodhayantaḥ krīḍanti | te caite meṣa-tat-poṣaka-tan-moṣakāyamāṇā ramamāṇā lakṣyante | yatra ca meṣā moṣyamāṇā api na bhāṣante | poṣakāś ca teṣāṃ bahalānāṃ sambhālanāya durbalāyante, moṣakās tu nirghoṣatayā pracchannam evāgacchanti | ayaṃ tu tat-poṣakāyamāṇaḥ śyāma-dhāmā kumāraḥ prabhākara-sahasra-prabhāva-bhāvitatayā nāsmad-vidha-sannidheya-sannidhānas tarkyate | tathāpy asmākam ayam evāvasaro varo nāvaro varaṇīyatām anusarati | atra hi tasya niravadhānasya bahiś-cara-prāṇa-tulāṃ valamānā bālakā vinaivārtiṃ hartavyā bhaveyuḥ | tato vyagrībhūtaḥ so' yam agrīyaś ca vinā vigrahaṃ grahītavyatām ṛcchet, sāmikṛtaṃ
tu na svāmine rociṣyate | tad etad vicārayaṃś cora-vad-ācāra-gopa-dāraka-prakāras tadīya-niviḍa-krīḍāyāṃ praviveśa | praviśya ca, niviḍa-kānana-kṛta-praveśatayā poṣakābhiniveśam atikrāmatas tān moṣāyamānān kramaśaś catuḥ-pañcāvaśeṣam apakramayāmāsa | apakramyāpakramya ca giri-guhāyāṃ nigūhayamānaḥ punaḥ punar ayamānaḥ peśaskaritānusārī prastarāstaraṇatas tad-dvāram āvavāra |
children.translated_text: 'These indeed call out to each other — "O son of a maidservant!" "O family of thieves!" "Behold, you thief!" "O beloved of the gods!" — and thus they play. They appear to be delighting in [a game of] sheep, their keepers, and sheep-stealers. In this game, the sheep about to be stolen do not speak; the keepers become weakened in managing those numerous ones; and the stealers come stealthily and silently. But this dark-complexioned boy, who is playing the keeper-role, by his being imbued with the radiance of a thousand suns, is not reckoned as one who should be in the proximity of beings like us. Nevertheless, this is indeed the best opportunity for us, and it follows the path of what is desirable. For here, the boys who are as dear as his external life-breath, being unguarded, could easily be carried off without causing him pain. Then, when he becomes agitated and is without his elder brother, he may be seized without a fight; but making peace will not please the master.' Thus deliberating, adopting the guise of a cowherd thief-boy, he entered into their close-knit play. Having entered, by the manner of one who surpasses the keepers' attention through having entered the dense forest, he gradually removed those being stolen, four or five at a time. And removing them repeatedly, concealing them in a mountain cave, coming again and again, following the footstep-trail, he blocked the entrance of that cave with a boulder.

children.text:
etaj jñātvā nirjarāri-prahārī śiṣṭān kaṣṭantaṃ harantaṃ kumārān vyagrī-bhūtaḥ siṃhavad grāma-siṃhaṃ vidrutyārād agrahīn nyagrahīc ca |
  svāṅga-vyaṅgāt spaṣṭa-bhūmiṣṭhamānaṃ
  kṛṣṭā ḍimbhāṃs taṃ tataḥ kṣauṇī-pṛṣṭhe |
  āpātyātha prāṇa-vartmaṇi rundhan
  vyagrī-kṛtyālambhya-kalpaṃ cakāra ||JGc_1,10.23|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Knowing this, the slayer of the immortals' foe (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), seeing him carrying off the remaining boys with difficulty,
became fierce like a lion against that lion of the village;
rushing from afar, he seized and subdued him!
From the disjointing of his own limbs, he was clearly thrown to the ground;
then, dragging the rascal onto the earth's surface,
falling upon him, blocking his breath-pathway,
making him helpless, he dispatched him as if performing a ritual offering! ||10.23|| [śālinī]

children.text:
tad evaṃ saṃhata-saṃhananam apy etaṃ niḥsandhi-bandhanaṃ visṛjya tat-pada-paddhatiṃ saṃsṛjya tad-gupti-dvāram anusasāra | tataś ca,
  sadyo nirbhidyāpidhānaṃ guhāyās
  tatrāviśya dyotam āviścakāra |
  tasyās teṣāṃ cārbhakāṇāṃ samantād
  ātmālābhād yat tamas taj jahāra ||JGc_1,10.24|| [śālinī]

yeṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ tad-guhā-garta-rodhe
  tadvan nāsīd yadvad etad-viyoge |
  dṛṣṭvākasmād enam ete bakāriṃ
  prāṇān prāntākarṣaṇenaiva jagmuḥ ||JGc_1,10.25|| [śālinī]
  sarve tasmād utthitā rodanārtās
  tadvad ārtaṃ kṛṣṇam ahnāya cakruḥ |
  so' pi kṣmābhṛt tat-pratidhvāna-dambhāt
  krandann āsīd ity amībhir vyabhāvi ||JGc_1,10.26|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Their suffering in being trapped in that cave-pit
was not as great as the suffering of separation from him;
seeing this enemy of <s>Baka</s> suddenly,
they attained their life-breaths by the very act of drawing [breath] to its end! ||10.25|| [śālinī]
All of them, risen up, distressed with weeping,
likewise made <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> appear distressed;
but he — that mountain — through the pretense of echoing [their cries],
was [merely] crying — thus they understood! ||10.26|| [śālinī]

children.text:
tasmāt kṛṣṭās tena taṃ veṣṭayantaḥ
  śaśvat tasya spṛṣṭito naṣṭa-duḥkhāḥ |
  dṛṣṭvā dviṣṭa-prāṇam atyanta-bhīṣmaṃ
  vyomaṃ hṛṣṭā mitra-goṣṭhīm upeyuḥ ||JGc_1,10.27|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Drawn by him, embracing him,
constantly freed of suffering through touching him,
seeing <s>Vyoma</s>, the hateful one, bereft of life and most terrifying,
they joyfully went to the company of their friends! ||10.27|| [śālinī]

children.text:
atha parimilitair vicitra-mitrair
  bhuvi divi deva-gaṇais tadopalambhyaḥ |
  apahṛti-caritaṃ nija-kramāt taiḥ
  kathitam asau kalayan vraje viveśa ||JGc_1,10.28|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
Then, welcomed by his assembled wondrous friends
on earth and in heaven by the hosts of gods,
he, hearing from them the stolen-and-recovered adventure
narrated in proper sequence, entered <s>Vraja</s>, reflecting [upon it]. ||10.28|| [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text: atra vyomaṃ diṣṭānta-daṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā kusuma-vṛṣṭi-kṛdbhir dānava-dveṣṭṛbhir ayaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇābhiprāyaḥ spaṣṭaṃ parāmṛṣṭaḥ-
children.translated_text: Here, seeing <s>Vyoma</s> bitten to his destined end, the enemies of the demons (<s>devas</s>), showering flowers, clearly contemplated the following intention of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text:
krīḍāyām atra corāṇāṃ śvāsa-rodho vidhīyate |
  vyomas tvaṃ vyomatāṃ prāptas tasmāc cet karavāṇi kim? ||JGc_1,10.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'In this game of thieves, choking is prescribed;
you, <s>Vyoma</s>, have attained the state of sky (<s>vyoma</s>) — so what can I do about that?' ||10.29|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
atha kathakaḥ kathā-samāpanam uvāca,
  īdṛk kautukavān putras tava gopa-narādhipa |
  vatsādi-trayam āninye līlayā yas tu pañcatām ||JGc_1,10.30|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then the narrator spoke the conclusion of the tale:
'Such a wonder-working son is yours, O lord of the cow-settlement,
who playfully brought the trio beginning with <s>Vatsa</s> to their destruction!' ||10.30|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evam amī sākṣād iva vyoma-vadham anubhūya bhūyasā sukhena vilasan-mukhena lalitā gṛhāya calitā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, having experienced the slaying of <s>Vyoma</s> as if directly [before them], they — with faces beaming with abundant joy, graceful — set out for home.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
vatsāsurādy-utsādanaṃ nāma
daśamaṃ pūraṇam
 ||10||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Tenth Chapter, named
'The Destruction of <s>Vatsāsura</s> and Others.'
||10||

children.text: athaikādaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Eleventh Chapter.

children.text: agha-brahmāgha-mocanam
children.translated_text: The Liberation from the Sin of <s>Agha</s> and of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: atha pūrvavat prabhātataḥ prabhātāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭham uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, as before, in the morning, when the assembly shone forth, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> spoke with eager longing:

children.text: tad evaṃ pūrvavad eva devana-kutukataḥ pūrvadeva-mārayoḥ kumārayor anayoḥ kaumāram ativṛtta-kalpam āsīt | [3] yau khalu,
children.translated_text: 'Thus, just as before, through the delight of play, the boyhood of these two boys — the previous god and <s>Māyā</s> — was such as to have nearly surpassed [all description]. [3] Those two indeed:

children.text:
śubhra-śyāma-rucī rucīm akurutāṃ paugaṇḍa-lakṣmī-kṛte
  cāpalyena muner api sma kurutaś cittaṃ milac-cāpalam |
  nānā-krīḍita-mādhurī-vara-kalā śikṣā-kalāpaṃ gatau
  veṇūdgāna-sudhāṃ sudhāṃśu-vadanāv ātatya cikrīḍatuḥ ||JGc_1,11.1|| [śārdūla]

atha kadācid atiprātar agrato jāgrato nija-vihārato jagad eva pātuḥ śrī-rāma-bhrātur yādṛcchikīyam icchā jātā | prātar-bhojanam apy adya nirjana-vana eva yojanīyam iti | tataś ca kṛta-prātaḥ-kriyas tat-prārthanāya racita-mātṛ-priyas tad-anujñayā gacchan śṛṅga-rava-sañjñayā sāgrajaṃ sakhi-vrajaṃ jāgarayāmāsa | jhaṭiti cāṭitvā śṛṅgāṭaka-madhyam adhyāsya kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ tat pratīkṣaṇaṃ pratīkṣaṇaṃ vyāpārayāmāsa | [5] śayyotthāyāṃ vidrutya militeṣu savayaḥ-sama-vāyeṣu rāmam āgamayitum ūrdhvaṃ vartamānas tan-mānavena vārtānuvartayāmāse |
children.translated_text: Then once, very early in the morning, while the glorious <s>Rāma</s>, his elder brother — who, by his own sport, sustains the world itself — was still wakeful before him, a spontaneous desire arose [in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]: 'Today, even the morning meal should be arranged in the uninhabited forest itself!' And then, having performed his morning duties, having won his mother's favor by way of soliciting her permission, departing with her leave, he awakened his elder brother and the flock of friends by the signal of a horn-blast. Swiftly running and taking his seat at the center of a crossroads, he occupied a few moments with the expectation of awaiting them at every instant. [5] When his age-mates had hastily risen from bed and assembled, he busied himself conveying the message through <s>Rāma's</s> attendant to bring <s>Rāma</s> along.

children.text: yathā ca provāca tad vācikam asau-hanta bhoḥ, kṛṣṇa, tvayā saha krīḍā-tṛṣṇag apy ahaṃ viruddha-vidhinā niruddha evāsmi, yad akasmāt kasmād api puru-kulajanmā man-mātulaḥ paramātula-nirbandhān mām avalokayitum āgamya harmya eva sthāvara-sādharmyam āsāditavān asti | adya ca tavātīva prātar ātta-jāgaratayā samīhita-viśeṣam ūhitavān asmi | tasmād bhavatā yā līlā bhāvayituṃ bhāvitā, sāvaśyaṃ bhāvayitavyā | navyārambhe viṣkambhaḥ khalv apratibaddha-siddhi-sambhāvanāṃ stambhayati iti |
children.translated_text: And the verbal message he sent was this: 'Ho, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Though I am thirsting for play with you, I am helplessly restrained by an opposing circumstance — that unexpectedly, from somewhere, a maternal uncle of mine, born of a great family, has come by the insistence of the supremely venerable one to see me, and has assumed the immovability of a fixed object in this very mansion! Today, however, by your extremely early awakening, I have inferred that something special is intended. Therefore, whatever pastime you have envisioned to perform, it must certainly be performed! For a hindrance at a new venture indeed blocks the prospect of unobstructed success!'

children.text: atha varṇyamāṇaṃ tad ākarṇya sa ca kamala-savarṇatā-vilasad-ākarṇa-locanaḥ pratipanna-krīḍā-rocanaḥ sakhīn uvāca-bhavatu | bhavanta eva sva-sva-bhavanād vihaṅgikāyāṃ kācam āyojya bhojya-bhakta-bhakta-niyojyajanaṃ prayojya tat tad upayojyam ānāyya vanāya gamanāya tvarayantu | asmaj-jananī ca bhavyānāṃ bhājana-bhṛta-bhojana-dravyāṇāṃ drutam eva sajjana-vargeṇāsmabhyaṃ visarjanam arjayiṣyati iti nijehite tathā vihite, hitepsu-bālaka-samudāya-mudām udāra-ceṣṭaḥ puraskṛta-vatsa-cayeṣṭaḥ kānanaṃ praviṣṭavān | yatra ca vatsa-pāla-bālakāḥ pratighasraṃ sahasraśa eva tena miśratayā viśrūyante | teṣāṃ vatsāś cāyuta-prayuta-niyutādi-saṅkhyā-yutā varṇyante | kṛṣṇa-vatsānāṃ saṅkhyā punar asaṅkhya-sañjñā saṅgīyate | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that described, he — whose eyes extended to his ears, flashing with the luster of golden <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), eager for play — said to his friends: 'So be it! You yourselves, having fitted glass vessels into baskets from your own homes, having dispatched your devoted servants [to prepare] the food to be eaten, bringing whatever provisions are needed, hasten for the departure to the forest! Our mother too will swiftly arrange the dispatch to us, through a group of good servants, of the food-provisions packed in vessels.' When his own wish was thus arranged, he — of magnanimous deeds, eagerness toward the assembled calves — entered the forest. And there, the calf-herding boys are reported to number in the thousands for each [daily outing] through their mingling with him. Their calves are described as numbering tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, millions, and so forth. The number of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> own calves, however, is celebrated as bearing the designation 'innumerable.' And then:

children.text:
āpūrṇa-śṛṅga-muralī-niyutaṃ savatsa-
  yūthāyutāravam udīrita-hūti-miśram |
  kṛṣṇaś calann atha vanāya balasya cittaṃ
  lolaṃ cakāra jagatā saha kautukāya ||JGc_1,11.2|| [vasantatilaka]
children.translated_text:
Filled with ten million flutes and horns, with the clamor of calf-herds by the ten thousands,
mixed with calls that were sent forth,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, setting out for the forest, made the mind of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>)
restless with curiosity, along with the entire world! ||11.2|| [vasantatilakā]

children.text: atha gahanaṃ gāhamānā maṇi-jāta-rūpābhyāṃ suṣṭhu jāta-rūpā api bālāḥ phala-pravālādibhir alaṅkṛtam ātmānaṃ kṛtavantaḥ, yathā nikāyye duryāca-kāca-guñjā-puñjam apy upayuñjate sma | nahi vilāsa-bahulatākulānām idaṃ na tat tulam iti vicāraḥ sañcarati | kārpaṇyam eva khalu paṇyaṃ gaṇyatāṃ nayati, vilāsitā punar dṛśyatām eva parāmṛśya hṛṣyatīti |
children.translated_text: Then, penetrating the dense forest, the boys — already beautifully formed by jewels and gold — adorned themselves with fruits, sprouts, and the like; just as in a necklace they would even use heaps of worthless glass and <s>guñjā</s> berries. Indeed, for those overwhelmed by the abundance of playfulness, the consideration 'this is [suitable], that is not' does not arise. It is miserliness alone that makes merchandise worthy of counting, whereas playfulness simply delights upon touching whatever is seen!

children.text: atha te śikyitānna-pātrāṇi vṛkṣa-śākhāsv avalambita-gātrāṇi vidhāya kṛṣṇa-bhrū-bhaṅga-taraṅga-saṅgata-raṅgatayā cāpalya-viśeṣaṃ śleṣayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, hanging their food-vessels suspended by slings upon the branches of trees, with their bodies dangling, they embraced a special mischievousness through their prancing, which moved in concert with the waves of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> eyebrow-gestures.

children.text:
muṣṇanto' nyo' nya-śikyādīn jñātān ārāc ca cikṣipuḥ |
  tatratyāś ca punar dūrād hasantaś ca punar daduḥ ||[BhP 10.12 |5] iti |
children.translated_text:
Stealing one another's sling-pots and the like, they threw them to acquaintances far away;
and those in turn, from a distance, laughing, gave them back again! // [BhP 10.12.5]

children.text:
tatra cauryādikaṃ, yathā:
  yaṣṭy-āder narmaṇāsann apaharaṇa-karā ye hṛta-svās tathā ye
  dūre ye kṣepakā ye pratiharaṇa-kṛtas te ca te cāśu sarve |
  śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhrū-vidhūti-pratilava-laghutā-śāli-tat-tad-vilāsaiḥ
  pratyekaṃ svīya-yogyaṃ nigamanam avidus tatra naivānyad anyat ||JGc_1,11.3|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
The thievery and such there, as follows:
Those who were near, making theft by jest of staffs and the like, and those whose [things] were stolen,
those far away, those who were throwers, those who made counter-seizure — all of them, all swiftly —
through the various sports bearing the lightness that follows each fragment of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> eyebrow-flash,
each one found only its own fitting conclusion there, and never anything else! // [sragdharā]

children.text:
tad evam eva saṃyogād yathā tad-eka-sukha-yoga eva teṣāṃ bhogas tathā viyogād api, yathā:
  yadi dūraṃ gataḥ kṛṣṇo vana-śobhekṣaṇāya tam |
  ahaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ pūrvam iti saṃspṛśya remire ||[BhP 10.12 |6] iti |
children.translated_text:
Thus indeed, just as by union their enjoyment was solely the yoga of happiness in him alone, so also by separation, as follows:
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had gone far to behold the beauty of the forest,
'I first! I first!' — thus touching him, they delighted! // [BhP 10.12.6]

children.text: asya cārthaḥ samasya darśyate | tatra sparśanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is shown in its entirety. There, the touching, as follows:

children.text:
vatsebhyaḥ preṣya sarvāṃ sakhitatim aghajid vīkṣituṃ vanya-lakṣmīṃ
  dūre' gād kṛṣṭa-dṛṣṭiḥ kramaśa iha tadā sā nivṛttā vidūrāt |
  saurabhyāghrāṇa-netrā madhupa-kula-tulā saṅghaśas taṃ dravantī
  spṛṣṭvāham-pūrvikāyām aham-ahamikayā pṛcchatī cānananda ||JGc_1,11.4|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
Having sent all his companions away to the calves, the slayer of <s>Agha</s>, to behold the woodland splendor,
went far, drawing [their] gazes; then gradually that [group] returned from afar,
with eyes [serving as organs of] fragrance-smelling, comparable to swarms of bees, rushing toward him in crowds,
touching him in an 'I first! I first!' contest, asking questions, they rejoiced! // [sragdharā]

children.text: ramaṇaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: The delighting, as follows:

children.text:
mitho' pi snigdha-bhāvānāṃ kṛṣṇa-kautuka-dattaye |
  āhopuruṣikā teṣām āloki spardhanām iva ||JGc_1,11.5|| [anuṣṭubh]
  jagur eke veṇunā tat-pracchādana-parāḥ pare |
  vādayanto viṣāṇāni hāsayāmāsur acyutam ||JGc_1,11.6|| [anuṣṭubh]
  vyañjayantas tatra kecit pūrveṣāṃ grāmya-rītitām |
  tān nivārya svayaṃ bhṛṅgair jagus tadvat pikaiḥ pare ||JGc_1,11.7|| [anuṣṭubh]
  gopālānāṃ javaḥ ślāghyo gānādyaṃ bhikṣutā-param |
  itthaṃ kecid vyañjayantaḥ pakṣi-cchāyena dudruvuḥ ||JGc_1,11.8|| [anuṣṭubh]
  ke' pi sarvānukartṛtva-sva-guṇādhikya-sūcakāḥ |
  haṃsa-kahva-mayūrāṇāṃ goṣṭhī-madhyaṃ prapedire ||JGc_1,11.9|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kecid vāṃśa-naṭīṃ vidyām ātmano vyañjituṃ mudā |
  viḍambitaiḥ kīśa-ḍimbaiḥ saha śākhāsu babhramuḥ ||JGc_1,11.10|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tatra sarva-kaniṣṭhās tu sva-niṣṭhā-mātra-tat-parāḥ |
  sākaṃ bhekair vilaṅghantaḥ saritaḥ srava-samplutāḥ ||JGc_1,11.11|| [anuṣṭubh]
  vihasantaḥ praticchāyāṃ śapantaś ca pratisvanān | [BhP 10.12 |10]
  hasantaḥ kṛṣṇa-santoṣaṃ lasantaḥ santataṃ daduḥ ||JGc_1,11.12|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kartuṃ pratidhvanau śāpaṃ pratibimbe viḍambanam |
  nudan bālān mudaṃ lebhe pratiśāpādito hariḥ ||JGc_1,11.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Even among those of mutual affection, for the sake of giving curiosity to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
their bravado was seen as if it were rivalry! // [anuṣṭubh]
Some sang; others, intent on imitating him, played flutes;
others, blowing horns, made <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) laugh! // [anuṣṭubh]
