Some, displaying the rustic ways of the elders there,
were stopped by him; they themselves then sang like bees, and others like cuckoos! // [anuṣṭubh]
The speed of the cowherds is praiseworthy, and singing and such is their begging-profession —
thus declaring, some ran in the shadow of birds! // [anuṣṭubh]
Some, indicating the excellence of their own quality of imitating everything,
entered the midst of gatherings of swans, geese, and peacocks! // [anuṣṭubh]
Some, to joyfully display their skill in the art of bamboo-acrobatics,
wandered on branches together with imitated monkey-young! // [anuṣṭubh]
There, the very youngest, devoted solely to their own steadfastness,
jumping along with frogs, were drenched in river-currents! // [anuṣṭubh]
Laughing at [their own] reflections, cursing at echoes, [BhP 10.12.10]
laughing, they continuously gave <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> delight, shining forth! // [anuṣṭubh]
To curse the echo and to mock the reflection —
pushing the boys [toward these], <s>Hari</s> obtained joy, himself counter-cursed! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
eṣā gatir māyika-dṛg-vimohanī
  jñātātmanāṃ bhaktimatāṃ ca dūragā |
  yāsādito kṛṣṇam anuvrajārbhakair
  iti sphuṭaṃ śrī-śuka-deva-niścitiḥ ||JGc_1,11.14|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
'This is the way [of the Lord] that bewilders the vision of the illusioned,
but is far removed from those who know the Self and are endowed with devotion;
which was attained by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, followed by the cowherd boys' —
this is clearly the determination of the glorious <s>Śukadeva</s>! // [upajāti]

children.text: tad evaṃ līlām anyām api titaṃsati kaṃsa-dviṣi dīvyatsu ca sarva-kalā-vidvatsu visaraj-jāleṣu vatsa-pāleṣu bakī-bakayor anujaḥ kaścid agha-nāmā danujas tad-vartmani vartate sma, jyotir-maṇḍaleṣu pracaṇḍa-kāla-jalada iva | yaṃ khalu kaṃsaḥ śaśaṃsa-aye, madīya-mahā-sahāya! vismayam apahāya śrūyatām | tvam ajagara-bhāvena sadā jāgara-rahita eva śāśayyamānatā-niṣṭhaṃ tiṣṭhan na jānāsīti hi tvaṃ jāgarayāmāsiṣe |
children.translated_text: Thus, as the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> desired to extend yet another pastime, and as the calf-herders — masters of all arts — were sporting with their spreading net [of play], a certain younger brother of the crane-demoness (<s>Bakī</s>) and <s>Baka</s>, a demon named <s>Agha</s>, was stationed upon their path, like a fierce storm-cloud upon the sphere of luminaries. <s>Kaṃsa</s> had indeed told him: 'O my great helper! Setting aside amazement, listen! You, in your python-form, always devoid of wakefulness, standing firm in your commitment to lying in sleep — you do not know [what has happened], and so I am awakening you.'

children.text: agha uvāca-jagadīśa, kāmam ādiśyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Agha</s> said: 'Lord of the world, command as you wish!'

children.text: atha devakī-vivāha-gatāha-nabhaḥ-sabhya-vāṇīm ārabhya sarva-kathā-śaṃsana-pūrvakaṃ kaṃsa uvāca-tad evaṃ pratyekaṃ nūtana-nūtanārabdha-miṣa-viṣa-maya-pūtanādiṣu dhūta-phala-prayāsāliṣu sarvaṅgila-līlatayā bhavān adyānavadya-gatiḥ | iha ca rāvaṇasya kumbha ity ardhoktam aśakuna-bhiyācchādya, pūrveṣāṃ pūrva-devānāṃ vṛtra iva ity api pratyākhyāyedam ākhyat-dhruvaṃ dhruvasyeva tava cātra bhrātra-mitra-niryātanam avaśya-vaśyatām arhati iti |
children.translated_text: Then, beginning from the celestial voice at <s>Devakī's</s> wedding journey, after narrating all the stories, <s>Kaṃsa</s> said: 'Thus, as each newly begun [demon] — <s>Pūtanā</s> and the others, with their stratagem of poisonous deception — has had its effort and fruit shaken off, by his all-devouring sport, you are today the one of irreproachable course! And here, concealing the ill-omened fear of [the word] "kumbha" in the half-said [name] "<s>Kumbha</s>(-karṇa)" in reference to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and also rejecting the [comparison] "like <s>Vṛtra</s> among the ancient gods," he declared this: "Surely, like <s>Dhruva</s> himself, you too here — the sacrifice of brother and friend — must necessarily command obedience!"'

children.text: tad evaṃ bhavya-prasavyam apy upalabhya sphuṭam asabhyatayā śīghram asau baka-bhrātṛkaḥ kṛṣṇa-bhrātṛkāṇāṃ teṣāṃ purataḥ pracaran pracura-tarāṅgam uraṅgam arūpam āsthāya sthitaḥ | kintv athāsau tathāsīd yathātma-pathādhikṛta-prathā-calatayā prathayāmāse | narmaṇā nāga-dharmatām upadiśadbhir amībhir ūce ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, even having received what was auspicious [in intent], clearly through its rudeness, that brother of <s>Baka</s>, moving before those brothers of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, assumed a formless serpentine form (<s>uraṅga</s>) with exceedingly long coils, and stood [there]. But he was such that, by the wavering of the reputation established over his path, he spread himself forth. And those [boys], jesting and teaching him the nature of a serpent, said:

children.text:
udyad-garatayā jāgrad vartmany ajagaraḥ puraḥ |
  samagraṃ grasitā tasmād asmān yadi bakiṣyati ||JGc_1,11.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'A python lies before us on the path, its gorge rising up, awake!
If it will swallow us all completely, it will be like <s>Baka</s> [i.e., meet the same fate]!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad etad abhidhāya śrī-kṛṣṇa-mukha-kamalaṃ nidhyāya, bāḍhaṃ kara-tāḍanāl lasanto hasanto mahā-giri-guhāntarvat tad-vaktrāntaraṃ praviviśur, jyotir-valayaḥ paścimācalam iva, yato mayūkhavat samagrā vatsāś ca tad-vartmāyacchanti sma; yatra niṣiṣitsann api śrīvatsa-lakṣmā nāvasaram avāpa, kintu bhāvi-nija-līlā-niścalatayā vismayam āpa, paścāt-tāpam āpad apy asau yena hi teṣāṃ vartmāpy anuvartamānas tatra praviveśa, nīhāra-kujjhaṭikā-ghaṭita-tamaś-cakravāle pracaṇḍa-martaṇḍa-maṇḍalam iva; [19] yatra murāri-prabhāvācaturāḥ surāḥ surārayaś ca muhur ārād ārād api hanta-hanta-kāraṃ cakruḥ; yatra ca teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ tat-tad-varṇataḥ samānam ānana-kula-yugalaṃ tat-tad-varṇataḥ kramād bhayaṃ vijayam udbhāvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Having said this and gazing at the lotus-face of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, 'Indeed!' — clapping their hands, shining and laughing, they entered the interior of his mouth as if it were the interior of a great mountain-cave, like a circle of luminaries [entering] the western mountain; from where all the calves too extended along that path like rays; where even the one marked with <s>Śrīvatsa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) did not find occasion to restrain them, but rather was amazed at the certainty of his own future pastime; [19] where the gods led by <s>Brahmā</s>, standing before on the celestial path, along with the gods and anti-gods, incapable of fathoming the power of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), repeatedly cried out 'Alas! Alas!' even from afar; and where the pair of clusters of faces of both groups [gods and demons], each described by their respective colors, gradually produced fear and [then] triumph in succession.

children.text: baka-ceṣṭām anutiṣṭhatas tasya tu pāpiṣṭhasya kaṇṭhe so' yam akuṇṭha-dhāmā kṛṣṇa-nāmā vraja-nṛpa-tapaḥ-pratāpa-maya-yogamāyā-sahāyatayā keśi-praveśi-sva-bhuja-divya-bhujaṅgamavad vavṛdhe | [21] sa tu jāta-śvāsa-rodhaḥ parityakta-bodhaś ca kṣaṇa-katipayam āsīt | tad-ūrdhvaṃ pāṭita-mūrdhānaṃ prāṇam apahāya pūtanā-śamayituḥ saṅgataḥ pūtaḥ pūtanā-bhrātur ātmā nitya-nūtanāṃ sad-gatim avāptum asya bahir āgamanaṃ pratīkṣate sma |
children.translated_text: As that most sinful one was imitating the behavior of <s>Baka</s>, in his throat this one named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of undiminished splendor, with the aid of <s>Yogamāyā</s> composed of the glory of the austerities of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, expanded like a divine serpent — the weapon-arm of the <s>Keśī</s>-slayer entering [the demon]. [21] He, his breath obstructed and consciousness abandoned, remained so for a few moments. Thereafter, abandoning his life through his split skull, the soul of the brother of <s>Pūtanā</s>, purified by contact with the pacifier of <s>Pūtanā</s>, awaited his emergence outside in order to attain the ever-new blessed destination.

children.text: sa śrīvatsa-vatsas tu tam antar hatya vatsa-vatsapān mūrcchitān amṛta-vṛṣṭi-maya-dṛṣṭi-pracāreṇa sañcarita-cetanān ācarann amībhiḥ samaṃ gamana-vartmanā tasmān nirjagāma svar-bhānu-mukhād amṛta-bhānur iva |
children.translated_text: That <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-marked calf [-herder], having slain him from within, revived the calves and calf-herders who had fainted, restoring their consciousness by the diffusion of his nectar-rain-like glance, and together with them emerged from that [mouth] by the path of passage — like the nectar-sun from the mouth of <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>).

children.text: tataś ca himācalād gāṅga-pravāhānām iva teṣāṃ pravahe jāte tasyātma-jyotir ajitasyāṅga-saṅghān niḥsajjad eva jagaj-janena dṛdaśe caṇḍa-jyotir-jyotiṣi jyotir iva |
children.translated_text: Then, as a stream arose from them like the Gangetic currents from the <s>Himālaya</s>, the self-luminous, unconquered one's body-assemblage, emerging without obstruction, was seen by the world's people — like a light within the fierce luminary's luminous sphere.

children.text: yatra brahma-puraḥsarāḥ surāḥ sura-vartmani purataḥ sthitāḥ sura-taru-puṣpa-stavaka-vṛṣṭibhiḥ stava-kṛta-saṃstava-tauryatrikādi-prastāva-sṛṣṭibhiḥ stava-nīyaṃ vrajarāja-tanūjaṃ pūjayāmāsur, upajahasur apy aghāsuram |
children.translated_text: There, the gods led by <s>Brahmā</s>, stationed upon the celestial path, worshipped the praiseworthy son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> with showers of flower-clusters from wish-fulfilling trees, with elaborate ceremonies of praise-songs, music, dance, and other festivities; and they also laughed at <s>Aghāsura</s>.

children.text:
mama sparśa-mātrād bhavaj-jñāti-mātraṃ
  vinaśyaty akasmāt tamas tejaso vā |
  idaṃ jñātavān apy aghākhyāsura tvaṃ
  kathaṃ mām ayāsīr itīvāha kṛṣṇaḥ ||JGc_1,11.16|| [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
athavā,
  sarvāṃs tvaṃ kharva-koṭīḥ paśu-paśupa-śiśūn grastavān mām tathāpi
  grastaṃ nirmātum aiṣīr iti sukhadatayā prāpam antas tvadīyam |
  saṅkocād gantum icchan bahir atha bhujaga prāṇa-vargas tavāddhā
  man-nirbandho' pi mūrdhnaḥ sphuṭana-kṛtitayā dhig gataḥ kiṃ vidadhyām? ||JGc_1,11.17|| [sragdharā] ity evam |
children.translated_text:
'By the mere touch of me, the entire host of your kinsmen
perishes suddenly — whether of darkness or of light;
knowing this, O demon named <s>Agha</s>,
how did you come to me?' — thus <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> spoke, as it were. // [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
Or rather:
'You swallowed all — billions upon billions of calves, cattle-herders, and boys — yet even so,
you wished to swallow me too, and so in delight I entered your interior;
then, wishing to exit through contraction, O serpent, your host of vital breaths, truly —
by my insistence, departed through the splitting of the skull — alas, what am I to do?' // [sragdharā]

children.text: tataś ca tasmāt kalita-gaṇatayā taruni-cayād ācita-kācita-divya-dīdivitayā cāticapalaṃ calitasya tasya kācanātidūrā bhūr āyata-vana-kalāpa-vimalāpasaro-varāntaratayā varāpy avaratām āsasāda | [26] yām upasādya ca sadyaḥ sukha-vikasita-mukha-paṅkajaḥ padma-locanaḥ svaṃ rocanaṃ vacana-gocaram ācacāra | yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, from him, reckoned among the host [of victims], having been loaded with collected, glittering, divine splendors from the gathered tree-clusters, that exceedingly restless one moved on; and a certain not-too-distant land, beautiful with an expanse of forest groves and a clear, excellent <s>apsaras</s>-pool within, came to a halt as a fine [resting place]. [26] Approaching which, the lotus-eyed one, his lotus-face blossoming with natural happiness, brought his own delight into the range of speech. As follows:

children.text:
bhāsvan-maho yoga-vikāsa-hṛd-gata-
  prabhāmbujātaṃ madhusūdana-prabham |
  paśyantu mitrāṇi sujīvanālayaṃ
  mahan-manas-tulyataraṃ sarovaram ||JGc_1,11.18|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
'Let my friends behold this lake,
resembling the great mind, an abode of excellent life,
shining with great luster, with a heart-dwelling lotus
of yogic expansion, radiant like <s>Madhusūdana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!' // [upajāti]

children.text:
eṣā vanālī sarasī tathā mitho
  guṇena puṣṭā guṇitena sarvadā |
  ādyā rasena dvaya-pūraṇī yataḥ
  prasūna-saurabhya-śatena puṣpate ||JGc_1,11.19|| [upajāti 12]
  sphurati pulinam acchaṃ komalaṃ bālukābhiḥ
  kusuma-phala-vana-kṣmā-prāvṛtaṃ sūkṣma-dūrvam |
  yad iha mṛga-janānāṃ vṛkṣa-lakṣālayānām
  upa vimala-jalāntaṃ bhāti śayyāyamānam ||JGc_1,11.20|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
'This row of forests and this lake — mutually
always nourished by their manifold quality;
the first [the forest] fills both [lake and itself] with <s>rasa</s>,
and blossoms with hundreds of flower-fragrances!' // [upajāti]
'A sandbank shines here, pure and soft with fine sand,
covered with ground of flowers, fruits, and trees, and fine <s>dūrvā</s> grass;
where for the deer-folk and tree-dwelling creatures,
near the clear water, it appears as a resting-bed!' // [mālinī]

children.text:
atra bhoktavyam asmābhir divārūḍhaṃ kṣudhārditāḥ |
  vatsāḥ samīpe' paḥ pītvā carantu śanakais tṛṇam ||[BhP 10.13 |6]
children.translated_text:
'We who are afflicted by hunger should eat here — the day has risen;
let the calves, having drunk water nearby, graze gently on the grass!' // [BhP 10.13.6]

children.text: atha samaṃ bhūmisthitaṃ saṃyujya bhojana-jananārthaṃ racita-majjaneṣu kṛta-mithaḥ-sajjaneṣu teṣu suhṛj-janeṣu prathamatas tāvad evaṃ jātam |
children.translated_text: Then, when those friends, having assembled together on the ground, engaged in bathing prepared for the purpose of producing the meal, and in mutual preparation, at first this happened:

children.text:
kṛṣṇaṃ madhye labdhavantaḥ sakhāyaḥ
  sarvaṃ tat tad vismarantaḥ sva-duḥkham |
  tat-kāntīnāṃ santataṃ pātu-kāmās
  tasthur yadvat pūrṇa-candraṃ cakorāḥ ||JGc_1,11.21|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
The companions, having obtained <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in their midst,
forgetting all their own suffering,
desiring always to drink the beauty of his radiance,
stood like <s>cakora</s> birds before the full moon! // [śālinī]

children.text:
tataś ca tat-pālana-tṛṣṇena kṛṣṇena yatnena yojitabhojaneṣu savayojaneṣu kācid anyā śobhā dhanyāṃ tāṃ vanyāṃ śobhayāmāsa, yathā:
  antarāntara-milad-valayānāṃ
  valgu bālya-vayasām adhimadhyam |
  sarvato' bhimukhatāṃ harir āgāl
  līlayābhramad apūrva-naṭābhaḥ ||JGc_1,11.22|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
Then, when the food of those age-mates was arranged with care by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who thirsted for their protection, another beauty graced that blessed woodland scene, as follows:
In the midst of those of boyhood age, meeting in circle after circle of bangles,
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) attained the state of facing all directions,
and with sport he whirled about — appearing like an unprecedented dancer! // [svāgatā]

children.text:
vibhrad-veṇuṃ jaṭhara-paṭayoḥ śṛṅga-vetre ca kakṣe
  vāme pāṇau masṛṇa-kavalaṃ vyañjanāny aṅgalīṣu |
  tiṣṭhan madhye priya-savayasāṃ hāsayan hāsitas tair
  divye loke kalayati mudā bhuktavān bāla-kṛṣṇaḥ ||JGc_1,11.23|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'Carrying the flute between the folds of the belly-cloth, the horn and stick under the arm, | a soft morsel in the left hand, condiments on the fingers, | standing in the midst of his dear age-mates, making them laugh and being made to laugh by them — | in the divine world, the child <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> joyfully enacts the one who has eaten!' || (JGc 1,11.23) [mandākrāntā]

children.text:
tad evaṃ paramotsva-rateṣu teṣu vatsāḥ kaccha-deśād anaccha-tārṇa-pradeśaṃ praviśya pracchannā babhūvuḥ | [30] pracchanneṣu ca teṣu vicchinna-bhojana-ratīr mitra-tatīḥ svasthayan tad-avastha eva svayaṃ nīrandhra-vanāvanīdhra-madhyam adhyāsitān avīdhra-durga-mārgān vicitya kṛtakṛtyatā-rāhityaṃ pratītya ca nivṛtya tatra ca mitra-vargān aparicitya vaicittya-vaśād ubhayān api sabhayān matvā vicikitsan vicikāya | kāya-kleśataḥ keśavaḥ so' yaṃ kintayā cintayāmāsa ca,
  aho, mātṝṇāṃ yac chiśu-kulam asubhyo' pi dayitaṃ
  sthitiṃ vatsatvena prasajati tathā vatsapatayā |
  tad etan mat-prāṇa-pratikṛti-śarīraṃ kva nu gataṃ
  yad arthaṃ duṣṭāher jaṭharam aviśaṃ hā viṣamayam ||JGc_1,11.24|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Thus, while they were engaged in the supreme festival, the calves entered from the meadow-area into a region of dense grass and became hidden. [30] When those had disappeared, he himself — reassuring the groups of friends whose eating-delight had been interrupted — in that very state, searched the paths of impassable difficulty amid the dense forest-thickets, and not finding [them], perceiving the absence of accomplishment, returning, and not finding his friend-groups there either, and through bewilderment considering both [groups] to be in danger, he searched anxiously, wondering. From bodily exertion, <s>Keśava</s> reflected with worry:
'Ah, the herd of young ones that is dearer to the mothers than their very lives — | they persist in the status of calves and likewise as calf-herders. | Where has this body — the replica of my very life-breath — gone? | For whose sake I entered — alas! — the venomous belly of the wicked serpent!' || (JGc 1,11.24) [śikharinī]

children.text:
tad etad aguṇa-guṇa-guṇagaṇa-nidhānasya tasya niravadhānam api na citram adhyasyati | [32] eṣa hi prema-maya-līlāveśa-vaśyatām āpannaḥ kadācid avaśyaṃ paśyann apaśyann iva bhavati | tadā hi sadya evedaṃ pratyapadyata | āṃ brahmaṇaḥ khalv idaṃ karma | mama punar etāvantaṃ kālaṃ sañjaṅghanya-māna-sakhi-saṅgha-praṇayāsaṅga-vaśāl laṅghita-jñānatayā na tad-anusandhānaṃ jātam | na ca tena virodhitayedam ācaritam, kintu mayi prema-sthema-saṃhitasya tasya vraja-hitasya samprati mad-vaibhavaṃ prati viśeṣa-vīkṣā-pratīkṣā jātety evam evācaritam | yata eva khalu māyā-vaibhavatas tad ananya-sthāna-sthitaṃ-manyam evānyatra vanya-bhūmāv ākṛṣya punas tatraiva puline pratikṛṣya tat-tad-vṛndam anenāgopāyi, tato na virodhi-buddhir asau | virodhiṣu mad-buddhi-vīryayor
nidrāgame' pi jāgarukatā kalitā | tato vayaṃ bhakte tasmin narma-karmaṭhatām eva ghaṭayiṣyāmaḥ | tatra ca prāyaḥ śrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇābhiprāya-mayatayā yā mama yogamāyā sāhāyakam āyāti | yadi tām eva samprati cāvalambeya, tadā svayam eva tat-tad-rūpatāṃ labheya | nānyad dhi mad-dhitānāṃ teṣāṃ sāmyaṃ bhajed iti-[33] yena ca śatānandasya vrajānandasya ca mandatā-mandatāṃ vindeta, tad evaṃ cintayann eva, saha-suhṛl-loka-śokaṃ cintayāmāsa, hanta, hanta, kathaṃ tān māṃ vinā tāntān vinā samayaṃ gamayiṣyāmi? iti | tataś ca,
  yasya yasya ca śucā guṇa-rūpaṃ
  cintayann abhajata svatayātha |
  tasya suṣṭhu dhuta-bhedatayā'sau
  jajñivān prayatanaṃ vyatiricya ||JGc_1,11.25|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
That this unlimited [bewilderment] settles upon him — the repository of the multitudes of qualities of the quality-less — is not strange. [32] For he, having fallen under the sway of his love-filled play-absorption, sometimes, though surely seeing, becomes as if not seeing. At that moment, however, he immediately realized: 'Ah, this indeed is the deed of <s>Brahmā</s>! But for me, for so long, due to the attachment of the affection of the companionship of my friend-groups who are to be embraced, my awareness was overridden and no investigation of that arose. Nor was this done by him in a spirit of hostility, but rather — he who is established in his steadfast love beneficial to <s>Vraja</s> — it was done precisely because he developed a special anticipation-glance toward my sovereignty. For indeed, through his <s>māyā</s>-sovereignty, he pulled those [boys and calves] — who thought themselves fixed in no other place — elsewhere to the forest terrain, and then drew them back to that very bank, and by him those respective groups were concealed. Therefore he is not of hostile intent. Even when my intelligence and valor were directed against his hostilities, | wakefulness was maintained even in the arrival of sleep. Therefore, toward that devotee, we shall arrange nothing but the work of sport. And there, mostly — because of being constituted of the purpose of the feet of my glorious father — my <s>Yogamāyā</s> comes to my aid. If I were to rely upon her alone at present, then I myself would attain the respective forms [of each]. For nothing else could equal those who are my beloved ones.' — [33] And by which [reflection] both the hundred-faced (<s>Brahmā</s>) and the delight of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>) would find their dullness upon dullness — thus reflecting, he reflected upon the grief of his companion-world: 'Alas, alas! How shall I pass the time without them, without those weary ones?' And then:
'Of each one, contemplating the form of whose virtues | with grief, he assumed as his own identity — | for each one, with distinction thoroughly shaken, | he came into being, surpassing [all] effort.' || (JGc 1,11.25) [svāgatā]

children.text:
iti tathānusandhāya svatas tat-tad-bālavatsādi-rūpāṇi sandhāya sarva-samādhāna-nirbandhāya dināntaravad eva vrajāgamana-devanena gehaṃ gehaṃ praveśam āsīnas tāṃ sandhyām abandhyāṃ cakāra | [35] tan-mātaras tu dināntarād apy antaraṅgataram ānandaṃ vindanti sma | tathā hi,
  sute gopeśvaryā nija-nija-suta-pratyaya-mudā
  tathā tan-mitratva-sphuraṇa-sukha-lakṣmyā dvi-guṇitam |
  purāvad vātsalyaṃ vraja-pura-purandhrīr vidadhatīs
  tadīyā saṃsiddhir yad adhinuta tad bhāti tad iva ||JGc_1,11.26|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Thus, having investigated accordingly, having fashioned from himself the respective forms of those boys, calves, and so on, insisting on the complete resolution of all, he — entering house by house with the device of coming to <s>Vraja</s> just as on any other day — made that evening fruitful. [35] The mothers, however, experienced a joy even more intimate than on other days. For thus:
'Since the queen of the cowherd-lord's joy of her own son's conviction, | and doubly so by the radiance of the happiness of friendship shining forth with him — | the motherly affection the women of <s>Vraja</s>-town bestowed as before — | that his accomplished power overwhelmed that [affection] appeared as if identical [to the original]!' || (JGc 1,11.26) [śikharinī]

children.text:
yadyapy eka-svarūpā vraja-nṛpati-sutasyāpare bāla-vatsā
  jātās tarhy apy amī tat-pratima-padam adhus tatra nety eva yuktam |
  tad-rūpaṃ tad-guṇālis tad-amita-vihṛtiś cāśrayaḥ khalv amīṣāṃ
  tasyāpi svasya citra-sthiti-kṛd iti yatas tatra tatrābhyadhāyi ||JGc_1,11.27|| [sragdharā]
[36] tad evaṃ hāna-prāyasya tasya hāyanasya pūraṇāya pañcaṣāṇy ahāni yadā hīnāni, tadā tu kṛṣṇa-viṣayaka-sneha-jātīya-sneham anu sva-para-tat-paratāyās teṣu bālādiṣu samyag avagamyamānatayā rāmo' pi vismitya tena saha praśnottare vinimitya viniścitya ca sthitavān, kintu teṣāṃ sakhīnām akhilānāṃ vipralambha-lambhita-kaṣṭena nijānuje ruṣṭatayā pañcaṣāṇy ahāni tena saha vanaṃ nājighāya |
children.translated_text:
'Although the other young calves that appeared were of a single essential form as the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, | even so, that they attained the status of his likeness is not fitting to say; | his form, his array of qualities, his limitless play — these were indeed the basis of those [forms], | yet even of his own, it was a creator of wondrous states — for that reason, it was proclaimed there and there.' || (JGc 1,11.27) [sragdharā]
[36] Thus, when only five or six days remained to complete that year that was nearly over, then <s>Rāma</s> too, fully perceiving in those boys and calves an affection of the same species as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-directed love — the subordination of self and other to them — was astonished, and having fashioned questions and answers with him, having determined [the truth], he remained [silent]. However, due to the hardship inflicted by the deception upon all those companions, being angry with his younger brother, he did not go to the forest with him for five or six days.

children.text: brahmā tu tatra guptam āgataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇena tarkyate sma, yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, however, who had come there in secret, was surmised by the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows:

children.text:
yasmād eti paraiti paśyati puraḥ paścāt tathā pārśvataḥ
  svātmānaṃ paritaḥ stṛṇoty anupadaṃ sambhrāmyati bhrāmyati |
  loptrā loptrasa-vatsa-vatsapa-gaṇaṃ sandigdham ālokate
  tasmān me pratibhāty asāv anudiśaṃ vaktraṃ dadhat stenakaḥ ||JGc_1,11.28|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'Since he comes and goes, looks ahead and behind and to the sides, | spreads himself all around, step by step grows agitated and wanders, | looks doubtfully at the crowd of calves and calf-herders, both fake and genuine — | therefore, this little thief, bearing faces in every direction, appears to me!' || (JGc 1,11.28) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: atha brahmā teṣām arvācīnānāṃ prācīnānāṃ ca bālādīnāṃ rūpādibhiḥ parasparam abhedam ākalayya cetasāścaryam ācarya cārvācaḥ parivindan, sarvato' py atidṛṣṭa-mahiṣṭhatā-bhūyiṣṭhān dṛṣṭavān | [38] brahmāṇaṃ paśyati śrīdāmādi-mitre tu sva-mitrāṇām evānayanecchā jāteti yadṛcchayā tad-anveṣaṇāvasthā prādurbhūtā, sāmpratikāś cāntarbhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, perceiving the non-difference between the recent and the original boys and calves through their forms and the like, experiencing wonder in his mind and performing reverence, finding [them] most excellent, saw them on all sides as possessing a preponderance of supremely perceived magnificence. [38] While he gazed at <s>Brahmā</s>, however, a desire arose in <s>Śrīdāmā</s> and other friends for the restoration of their own friends, and spontaneously a state of searching for them emerged — while the present [duplicates] were absorbed within.

children.text: tad evaṃ nānā-vaibhavam anubhavataḥ kamala-bhavasya traptatayānutaptatayā ca yā racitāvācīnatā, sā svayaṃ praṇāmāya pariṇamati sma | tatra ca,
children.translated_text: Thus, the discomfiture produced by <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born — who was experiencing the various glories — through his remorse and repentance, itself transformed into prostration. And there:

children.text:
ekam ekam adhaḥ kṛtvā mukhaṃ tatra caturmukhaḥ |
  namann anya-mukhasyordhvī-bhāvāt pūrtiṃ jagāma na ||JGc_1,11.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
  yadyapi na naman mumude vidhir ekāsyānavāg-bhāvāt |
  tadapi harer mukhacandrā-lokālopān mudaṃ lebhe ||JGc_1,11.30|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'Lowering one face at a time, the four-faced one there, | bowing, could not attain the fullness of the upward state of the other face!' || (JGc 1,11.29) [anuṣṭubh]
'Although the Creator, not bowing, did not rejoice, due to one face not going downward, | even so, from the appearances and non-appearances of the moon-faces of <s>Hari</s>, he attained joy!' || (JGc 1,11.30) [upagīti]

children.text: athāpakṛṣṭaṃ-manyaḥ sann ananya-gatitayā sumedhā vedhāḥ stavakeneva stavakeneṣṭavāṃś ca kṛṣṇam | yatra ca caturbhir vaktrair ānuvāna iva nuvann asau sarva-mahān api yat kiñcid gokulānugatānugatim eva prati nijānumatim ātatāna | yathā cāha sma-
children.translated_text: Then the supremely wise Creator, feeling himself to have been humiliated, having no other refuge, extolled <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with a cluster-like cluster of hymns. And there, praising with four mouths as if following a chorus, that all-great one inclined his own assent toward nothing but the path of <s>Gokula</s>. As he also said:

children.text:
tad bhūri bhāgyam iha janma kimapy aṭavyāṃ
  yad gokule' pi katamāṅghri-rajo' bhiṣekam |
  yaj-jīvitaṃ tu nikhilaṃ bhagavān mukundas
tv adyāpi yat-pada-rajaḥ śruti-mṛgyam eva ||[BhP 10.14.34] iti |
children.translated_text: whose entire life is the glorious <s>Mukunda</s> (the giver of liberation), | whose foot-dust even today remains sought by the <s>Vedas</s>!' || [BhP 10.14.34]
'O, how greatly fortunate is birth of any kind in this forest, | where in <s>Gokula</s> one receives the anointing by the foot-dust of some feet or other —

children.text: tad evaṃ vraja-mahi-mahima-kara-kara-nikara-jaḍī-bhūtā vayaṃ nopapatti-pratyāsattiṃ labhāmaha ity alam ativistareṇa |
children.translated_text: Thus, we, rendered inert by the hands of the hands of the greatness of the glory of <s>Vraja</s>'s soil, cannot attain even the proximity of reasoning — enough of excessive elaboration!

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-śrīmad-vraja-yuvarājena tatra kim uktam?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'What did the glorious young prince of <s>Vraja</s> say to him there?'

children.text:
madhukaṇṭhaḥ sa-smitam uvāca-na kim api, kintu tatra stuti-samaye tāvat |
  govindaḥ smitam atanot stuvānam enam
  dṛṣṭvā yat kim api dadarśa tatra citram |
  ekasmin vadati caturmukhe hi tasmiṃś
  catvāro dadhati rutīr iti bhramaḥ syāt ||JGc_1,11.31|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
<s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said with a smile: 'Nothing at all — but at the time of the hymn, at least:
'<s>Govinda</s> spread a smile, seeing him praising [Him], | and beheld something wondrous there: | when one four-faced one speaks, | four [mouths] produce sounds — such might be the illusion!' || (JGc 1,11.31) [praharṣiṇī]

children.text:
stuty-uttara-kālatas tu,
  vayaṃ gopāś cārthavanto brahmā ca tvam anarthavān |
  brūmas tvāṃ kim itīvāyam avadan smitam ātanot ||JGc_1,11.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
After the hymn, however:
'"We are cowherds and wealthy; but you, <s>Brahmā</s>, are penniless! | What shall we say to you?" — thus as if he spoke, he spread a smile.' || (JGc 1,11.32) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-parisedhaty api vedhasi kiṃ kiñcid apy uktam?
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Even when <s>Brahmā</s> was being dismissed, was anything at all said?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-stava-paryāvasāne khalu nija-rūpa-rūpatayā sarva-paryāptimadbhir api paścād āvirbhūtavadbhir bālādibhiḥ paritoṣa-poṣam amanyamānaḥ sa dhanyaḥ svajana-prema-jitaḥ śrīmān ajitas tān vraja-bālādīn evānetuṃ yadā vāñchām ānañca, tadāñjali-bandha-vyañjitāṃ sañjñām anu samanujñāṃ yācamānaṃ viriñciṃ khalv evaṃ lambhita-tad-upālambha-narma-smitam anujñāpayāmāsa-yadi tatra-bhavatām ājñā vijñāyate, tadā tān pūrvam evānusaṃhitān sannihitān ānayāmi iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'At the conclusion of the hymn, when he — not considering even the boys and calves who had appeared afterwards with his own form's beauty to be sufficient for his satisfaction, though they sufficed in every way — that blessed one, the unconquered glorious Lord, conquered by the love of his own people, when he extended his wish to bring back those very original <s>Vraja</s> boys and calves, he then — with a sportive smile that conveyed the reproach — dismissed <s>Brahmā</s>, who was requesting permission with joined palms and a gesture of assent, [saying]: "If your honor's command is understood, then I shall bring back those who were already established and are present."'

children.text: tataś ca viriñciḥ kiñcin namra-niṭilatā-ghaṭita-muni-vrata-sunirūpita-nija-durnītitayānujñāyāḥ karma-kartṛtvaṃ vyaktīkurvan, bhakti-bharāsakti-pṛktīkṛta-pulaka-saṅkulatayā svāparādha-maya-bādhā-vyakulatayā ca triḥ parikramya bahuśaḥ praṇamya ca nija-harmyam eva jagāma |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, with a slightly bowed forehead — fashioning the clear display of his own misconduct, well-ascertained by a sage-like vow — manifesting the agency of the permission, through the agitation pervaded by the horripilation mixed with the attachment of devotion's fullness, and through the distress filled with the injury of his own offense — having circumambulated three times and prostrated many times — went to his own celestial mansion.

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇaś ca manasi tasyāparādhaṃ manāg apy anāgamayann āgamayamānaḥ prāg-diṣṭa-sadiṣṭa-dveṣa-veśa-kriyānatikrami-kramatayāvasthitāṃs tān vatsāṃs tat-sadṛg-avasthair vatsa-pālair melayāmāsa | [49] tathaiva hi teṣāṃ kāla-deśa-viparyayā paryālocanāya druhiṇa-devena sneha-dehany anavadya-vidyeyam udbhāvitā | etad evoktam-
children.translated_text: And the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, not allowing even the slightest trace of his offense to enter his mind, fulfilling [all] — reunited those calves, who had remained in the state of conformity with the previously ordained, well-ordained arrangement of the disguise of enmity, with the calf-herders who were in an identical state. [49] For precisely this purpose, by <s>Brahmā</s> the god, for the contemplation of the reversal of time and place of those [beings], this faultless knowledge born of love was brought forth. This very thing was stated:

children.text: tato' nujñāpya bhagavān sva-bhuvaṃ prāg-avasthitān |
vatsān pulinam āninye yathā pūrva-sakhaṃ svakam ||[BhP 10.14.42] iti |
children.translated_text: brought the calves to the bank, along with his own former companions.' || [BhP 10.14.42]
'Then, having dismissed the self-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>), the Lord, [restoring] those previously stationed [boys and calves],

children.text: atha te,
children.translated_text: Then they,

children.text: ūcuś ca suhṛdaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ, svāgataṃ te' tiraṃhasā |
children.translated_text: said to their friend <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Welcome to you, O greatly swift one!

children.text: naiko' py abhoji kavala, ehītaḥ sādhu bhujyatām ||
children.translated_text: Not even one morsel has been eaten — come here, let us eat well!'

children.text: tato hasan hṛṣīkeśo' bhyavahṛtya sahārbhakaiḥ |
darśayaṃś carmājagaraṃ nyavartata vanād vrajam ||[BhP 10.14.45-46] iti |
children.translated_text: showing them the skin of the python (<s>Aghāsura</s>), returned from the forest to <s>Vraja</s>.' || [BhP 10.14.45-46]
Then <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, laughing, having eaten together with the boys,

children.text: carma cedam etāvantaṃ samayaṃ yathāvad eva yogamāyayāntardhāpitam iti gamyam |
children.translated_text: And this skin — for so long a time it had been properly concealed by <s>Yogamāyā</s> — this should be understood.

children.text: tataś ca saṃvatsara-prasara-vatsa-vatsapāla-bāla-viraha-virahān mahatānandena mahitas tair eva sahitaḥ saṃhita-sampad-vrajaṃ vrajaṃ praviśan, tat-tad-unmaryāda-vatsa-parāvartanāya nidiśan, pūrva-pūrvato' py apūrvaṃ parva parvati sma | tathā hy uktam-
children.translated_text: Then, honored by those very ones with great joy — [joy] that dispelled the separations from the calves, calf-herders, and boys throughout the year's duration — accompanied by them, entering <s>Vraja</s> whose prosperity was well-established, directing the return of the respective calves beyond their boundaries, he celebrated a festival more unprecedented than any before. As has been said:

children.text:
barha-prasūna-vana-dhātu-vicitritāṅgaḥ
  proddāma-veṇu-dala-śṛṅga-ravotsavāḍhyaḥ |
  vatsān gṛṇann anuga-gīta-pavitra-kīrtir
gopī-dṛg-utsava-dṛśiḥ praviveśa goṣṭham ||[BhP 10.14.47] iti |
children.translated_text: a feast for the eyes of the <s>gopīs</s> — he entered the cow-settlement.' || [BhP 10.14.47]

'With body adorned by peacock feathers, flowers, and forest minerals, | enriched with the festive sounds of the exuberant flute, leaf-pipe, and horn, | calling the calves, his holy fame sung by his followers,

children.text: tataś ca pitṛ-sambandhibhir nanda-sūnur iti mātṛ-sambandhibhir yaśodā-sūnur iti tasya nāmānūdya, sadya eva siddham iti cirantanam api tac-caritaṃ jage | tad yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, his name being repeated as 'son of <s>Nanda</s>' through paternal relations and as 'son of <s>Yaśodā</s>' through maternal relations, immediately — as if accomplished just now — even that ancient tale of his deeds spread through the world. That is as follows:

children.text: nanda-tanūjanur adya vyālam | hatavān hṛtavān asmat-kālam ||iti dhru ||
children.translated_text: 'The son of <s>Nanda</s> today [slew] the serpent! | He slew it and reclaimed our time!' ||refrain||

children.text: adya yaśodā-sūnur vyālam | hatavān hṛtavān asmat-kālam ||iti vā ||
children.translated_text: 'Today the son of <s>Yaśodā</s> — a serpent! He has slain, and has stolen our time!' — or thus. //

children.text: oṣṭhādharam iha jalada-taṭāliḥ | dambhāvalir api dantaka-pāliḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The lower lip here is like the edge of a thundercloud! The array of pretense is like the row of little teeth!' //

children.text: śvāsa-bharaḥ kharadāvaja-vātaḥ | jihvā-yugam api vartma-nipātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The heavy breathing is the wind of a raging forest-fire! The pair of tongues is like the fall of a pathway!' //

children.text: ity utprekṣitatama-vividhāṅgān | vyatihāsān ācarataḥ sāṅgān ||
children.translated_text: Thus, performing various limb-by-limb exaggerated comparisons in their complete form, //

children.text: ahim anv ahitāṃ kalpayamānān | girir iti taṃ viśataḥ kṛta-mānān ||
children.translated_text: imagining the snake as hostile, entering it with pride, saying 'it is a mountain,' //

children.text: tad-udara-madhya-kṛtābhyanuveśān | nija-virahādi-vimūrcchita-veśān ||
children.translated_text: having made their entry into the middle of its belly, their appearance swooning from separation from him and the like, //

children.text: sneha-bharād atha svena sametān | svaka-netrāmṛta-vṛṣṭi-sacetān ||
children.translated_text: then, out of the weight of affection, reunited by him, revived by the nectar-rain of his own eyes, //

children.text: tasmād bahir atha niṣkāsitavān | punar iha nikhilaṃ bata darśitavān ||
children.translated_text: and then expelled from it outward, here again he showed everything, alas! //

children.text: prāṇād adhikaḥ so' yaṃ prāṇān | rakṣann asmān kurute trāṇān ||JGc_1,11.33|| [mātrā-samaka]
children.translated_text: He who is dearer than life-breath — this very one — protecting our lives, makes us secure! // [mātrā-samaka]

children.text: iti śrutvā ca te vrajasthāś cintayāmāsuḥ, sādhu-ghātukānāṃ pātukānām āmīṣāṃ katham iva jātu kāmāḥ sidhyeyuḥ? iti |
children.translated_text: And having heard this, those residents of <s>Vraja</s> reflected: 'How could the desires of these slayers of the good, these drinkers [of blood] among them, ever succeed?' //

children.text: tad evaṃ siddhe, sukhānubiddhe teṣāṃ same samāgame prātas tu bṛhad-bhrātaram anugamya praṇaya-maya-ramya-roṣam anunīya dīyamāna-vismayatayā tān ānīya tena caikatra praṇīya śrīvatsa-vatsaḥ pūrvavad eva vatsa-pālanam ārebhe |
children.translated_text: Thus, when that was accomplished, in their joyful coming-together the next morning — he, having followed his elder brother, having appeased his lovingly-angry playful wrath, having brought those [boys] with astonishing power, having been gathered together by him (<s>Rāma</s>) in one place — the calf of <s>Śrīvatsa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) commenced calf-herding just as before.

children.text: atha punar madhukaṇṭhaḥ samāpanāya sa-vismayam ivāha sma-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, as if with wonder, spoke for the conclusion:

children.text:
īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava goṣṭhādhināyaka |
  brahmāṇḍa-grāmaṇīr yasya brahmāpi grāmaṇīr iva ||JGc_1,11.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Such a son has been born to you, O lord of the cow-settlement, the village-chief of the universe — of whom even <s>Brahmā</s> is like a village-chief!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ kathakayoḥ kathāṃ prathayitvā sabhyeṣu sākṣād iva kalita-tat-tat-keli-sandhayoḥ kṛtāñjali-bandhayos tad-dine' pi pūrvavad eva sarve gṛha-vartmani vartamānā nija-nija-spṛhaṇīyaṃ karma nirmimāṇā api tām eva līlāṃ bṛṃhitāṃ hṛdi jagṛhire |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the two narrators had spread the tale among the assembly-members — as if [those events were] directly experienced — the two standing with palms joined in reverence, on that day too, as before, all, while proceeding on the path homeward and performing their own respective desirable tasks, held that very pastime, expanded, in their hearts.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anv
agha-brahmāgha-mocanam nāma
ekādaśaṃ pūraṇam
||11||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the Śrī Śrī <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Eleventh Chapter named 'The Liberation from the Sin of <s>Agha</s> and of <s>Brahmā</s>'
||11||

children.text: atha dvādaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Twelfth Chapter.

children.text: gocāraṇa-pracāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: The Promotion of Cow-Herding.

children.text: atha paredyavi ca kathā prathate sma, [2] yathā snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-yadyapi kālenālpena [BhP 10.8.26] ityādi-rītyā varṣa-traya-traya-paryāyeṇa tayor vayo-gaṇanā nirṇītā, tathāpi kaumāraṃ tu varṣam ekam adhikam adhirūḍham, bāla-vatsānāṃ śrīvatsa-vatsasya ca mitho vatsara-viraha-mayānullāsena vyatīta-kṣaṇa-maya-saṃvatsara-kāla-bāla-vatsānurodhena vā tasya stabdhībhāvāt | [3] tatas tad-bhāvānugāmitayā rāmasya ca tathā vṛttaṃ sutarām eva vṛttam | tad-anantaram akhaṇḍaṃ paugaṇḍaṃ tu varṣa-dvayenaivāpūryata, cirāl labdha-bandhu-saṃvāsena samyag ullāsena jhaṭiti kaiśora-ghaṭanāt | tathā ca prathāṃ karavāma dhenuka-vadhāvama-dhāma-gamanānte | tad evam eva saṅgacchate kālenālpena ityādi |
children.translated_text: And on the following day too, the narrative proceeded. [2] As <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Although by the manner of "in a short time" [BhP 10.8.26] and so forth, the reckoning of their age was determined by the cycle of three years each, nevertheless the boyhood (<s>kaumāra</s>) extended one year longer, either because of the lack of joy arising from the mutual year-long separation of the young calves and the calf of <s>Śrīvatsa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), or because of the freezing of the past-moment-constituted year-period through the young calves' attachment — hence his stasis. [3] Then, by following that state of his, <s>Rāma's</s> case too was certainly the same. Afterwards, the unbroken pre-adolescence (<s>paugaṇḍa</s>) was completed in just two years, because of the swift onset of early adolescence (<s>kaiśora</s>) through the joy of long-attained companionship arising rapidly. And thus, let us narrate the events up to the slaying of <s>Dhenuka</s> and the going to the wicked one's abode. This indeed accords with "in a short time" and so forth.

children.text: tāvad evātmabhūr ātma-mānena truṭy-anehasā |
purovad ābdaṃ krīḍantaṃ dadṛśe sakalaṃ harim ||[BhP 10.13.40] iti |
children.translated_text: '— beheld <s>Hari</s> playing as before for a year, in his complete form.' [BhP 10.13.40] — thus.
'Meanwhile, <s>Brahmā</s>, through self-regard, with the effort of a mere <s>truṭi</s> (instant) —'

children.text: tataś ca paugaṇḍa-vayaḥ-śritau [BhP 10.15.1] ityādi ca |
children.translated_text: And then: 'When they had attained pre-adolescent age' [BhP 10.15.1] — and so forth.

children.text: atha prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ | tad evaṃ viharatoḥ sarveṣāṃ mano harator anayoḥ pañcamaṃ varṣam añcat kaumārataḥ pāra-bhūtaṃ vayaḥ samayāñcakre | yathā-
children.translated_text: Now let us follow the main narrative. Thus, as those two sported, captivating the minds of all, the fifth year dawned — the age that had gone beyond boyhood from the state of childhood. As follows:

children.text:
aiṣamo' bhavad asau parut parāry
  evam ādi nikhilair yadāgaṇi |
  hanta tarhi sahasā bakāntakaḥ
  prāpta-kānti vijahau kumāratām ||JGc_1,12.1|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'This year, last year, the year before that' — when thus counted by all, then suddenly the slayer of <s>Baka</s>, having attained full beauty, left behind his childhood! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
udgacchad-buddhi-śakti-prathama-ruci-jayi-śyāmatā-śubhratā-yuk
  kiñcid-vistīrṇa-vakṣaḥ-prabhṛti valayitāyāma-netrādi-gātram |
  keśaṃ veśaṃ ca pūrvād adhika-mitim ayat keli-śikṣā-pravīṇaṃ
  paugaṇḍaṃ prāg acaṇḍaṃ sphurad alam anayor māṃ didṛkṣuṃ karoti ||JGc_1,12.2|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: With dawning intellectual power, with the first victorious charm of dark and fair complexion, with a somewhat broadened chest and the like, with limbs of extended curved eyes and other features, with hair and attire surpassing the former measure, skilled in the lessons of every sport — the pre-adolescence of these two, gentle at first, clearly manifesting — makes me long to behold it! // [sragdharā]

children.text: tadā ca kadācic chrī-vraja-rājñī sabhāntaḥ prātar āyātā śrīmad-abhinanda-patnī sayatnī-bhavantī tāṃ papraccha-yātaḥ kṛṣṇa-mātar, adya sadyaḥ prātar eva kutra vā bhavaj-jātaḥ prayātaḥ?
children.translated_text: Then, once, the wife of the glorious <s>Abhinanda</s>, having come to the assembly-hall of the queen of Śrī <s>Vraja</s> in the morning, making an effort, asked her: 'O mother of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, where has your son gone today — first thing in the morning, just now?'

children.text:
vraja-rājñī tu sa-hāsam āha sma-hanta, tad etad vartamāna-samaya-paryantaṃ tasyodvartana-snāna-paridhāna-mayāni karmāṇi mayā nirmīyante sma | samprati mad api lajjām āsajjan svaka-savayaḥ-sevaka-priyaḥ pṛthag eva kṛta-tat-kriyaḥ sa mā samayā samāyāti | āgatya ca pratyahaṃ māṃ pitaraṃ yathā-yatham itaraṃ ca guru-janaṃ puru-gauraveṇa namaskāreṇa puraskaroti | [7] kiṃ ca, tad-avadhi yadā sandhyāyāṃ mayā dhyāyamānāgamanaṃ saha-vatsaḥ samāgacchati, tadā tad-upari vāri vāra-trayaṃ bhramayitvā pibantī bhavāmi sma | samprati tu, sa-śapatham edhamāna-yatnavatā tat-pratiṣedhatā tena mama hastau vihastau kriyete | evam eva rauhiṇeyaś ca iti | tad etad arvācīnaṃ tad-varṇanam apūrvatayākarṇya tan-mukhaṃ nirvarṇya sarvā hasanti sma | [8] sā punar uvāca-tad etad abālyam
iva ca tasyāsamaya-mayatvād bālyam eva matvā sukham upalabhāmahe, anena tu duḥkhākriyāmahe |
children.translated_text:
The queen of <s>Vraja</s> said with a laugh: 'Well then, up until the present time, his tasks of anointing, bathing, and dressing were performed by me. But now, attaching even modesty to me, that one who is dear to his own age-mates and servants independently performs those tasks and comes to me on time. And coming, every day he honors me first, then his father as appropriate, and then the other elders with great reverence and salutation. [7] Moreover, from that time onward, when at twilight, as I contemplate his coming, he arrives together with the calves — then I would circle water three times over him and drink it. But now, with sworn and increasing effort, that one who prohibits it renders my hands helpless. And the same with the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s>.' Hearing this recent description of his behavior with the novelty of unprecedented charm, gazing at her face, all laughed. [8] She said again: 'This indeed seems like not-childhood,
but considering its untimeliness, we take it as childhood itself and find happiness; but by this [other matter] we are made unhappy.'

children.text: sarvāḥ sāśaṅkam ūcuḥ-hanta, kiṃ tat?
children.translated_text: All said with anxiety: 'Alas, what is that?'

children.text: sā prāha-svayam acirād eva gavāṃ vicāram antarā cicārayiṣitaṃ yat |
children.translated_text: She said: 'That which he himself desires to do shortly — namely, to tend the cows!'

children.text: sarvā ūcuḥ-nātrāpy anyathā manyasva | gopa-kula-tilakāyamāna-bālakānāṃ sa eṣa eva svabhāvaḥ sarvatra nābhāvam āsīdati | kim uta teṣv api parama-citra-caritrasya tasya iti |
children.translated_text: All said: 'Do not think otherwise about this either! This is indeed the very nature of boys who are the ornaments of the cowherd clan — it does not fail to appear anywhere. How much more so for him, of supremely wondrous conduct, among them!'

children.text: atha vraja-rājasya sadasy api tasya vṛttam idaṃ vṛttam āsīt | yathāha sma sa-smitaṃ samāsannau sannanda-nandanau nandita-samājaḥ śrīman-nanda-rājaḥ-bhoḥ āyuṣmantāv, adya-jāta iva yuṣmad-bhrātṛ-jātaḥ sa yathā samprati yuvāṃ prati vartate, na tathā mām iti lakṣyate | yataḥ kiñcit saṅkucita-vilocanena mām avalocayann ālocyate | yuvābhyāṃ saha tu madhura-vārtāṃ vartayann eva dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: And in the assembly of the king of <s>Vraja</s> too, this same topic was the matter discussed. As the glorious king <s>Nanda</s>, delighting the assembly, said with a smile to the two sons of <s>Sananda</s> and <s>Nanda</s> seated nearby: 'O long-lived ones! Your brother, born as if just today, does not seem to behave toward me the way he presently behaves toward you two. For he is observed gazing at me with somewhat contracted eyes. But with you two, he is seen conducting sweet conversation.'

children.text: sannanda uvāca-sāmpratam evedaṃ, yataḥ sāmprataṃ tatra-bhavatā tatra śikṣā-maya-vīkṣā gāmbhīryam ācaryate | āvābhyāṃ tu kaumāra-kālīne' pi tasminn atiśālīne vidheyatayā paryālocituṃ na pāryate | [14] pāśya paśya
children.translated_text: <s>Sananda</s> said: 'This is just how things are now, for at present your honor practices a depth of disciplinary gaze there. But we two cannot properly observe even that most noble one from his childhood, out of deference. [14] Look, look!

children.text:
prathamaṃ namam iha mātaram atha pitaraṃ tvāṃ tathaivāsmān |
  pratyūṣaḥ pratisuhṛdaṃ sat-kurute' sāv atīva bālye' pi ||JGc_1,12.3|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text: First bowing here to his mother, then to his father, then to you just so, and then to us — at dawn, he properly honors each friend, exceedingly, even in childhood!' // [udgīti]

children.text: atha kramāgateṣu vatsalatayā samāna-mateṣu tad-ākarṇanārtham akiñcidvādiṣu śrīmad-upanandābhinandādiṣu tad-varṇyamānam anya-mukhād ākarṇya sānanda-vikasita-manda-hasita-bhrājiṣu punaḥ sannanda-nandanau prati śrī-vraja-rāja uvāca-bhavantāv ekāntam anubhavantāv anugamya tau ramya-kātarākṣi-prāntāv asakṛt prātar ārabhya prārthitavantāv iva hyaḥ pūrve' hni samantād bhrātarāv atidūrād adṛkṣātām | tat kim ucyatām?
children.translated_text: Then, when the glorious <s>Upananda</s>, <s>Abhinanda</s> and others had gradually arrived — being of like mind out of affection, saying nothing [special], having come to listen to that — hearing that being described from another's mouth, their faces blooming with joy and gentle smiles — the king of Śrī <s>Vraja</s> again said to the two sons of <s>Sananda</s> and <s>Nanda</s>: 'You two, who experience exclusive [companionship], having followed those two of lovely, tender eye-corners, repeatedly since morning as if entreating them — yesterday, the day before, on all sides the two brothers were not seen from a great distance. So what is to be said about this?'

children.text: nandana uvāca-tadānīm eveti kiṃ vaktavyam? kintu cirād eva tayos tad abhirucitam upacitam asti | saṅkucita-bhāvābhyām āvābhyāṃ tu bhavatsu na śrāvitam |
children.translated_text: <s>Nandana</s> said: 'What is there to say about that moment? Rather, that desire has been cultivated in those two for a long time. But we two, being of a contracted disposition, did not report it to your honors.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-kiṃ tat?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'What is that?'

children.text: sannandaḥ sasmitam uvāca-svayam eva gavāṃ sevanam iti yat |
children.translated_text: <s>Sananda</s> said with a smile: 'The tending of cows by themselves — that is what.'

children.text: upananda uvāca-kim ūcatus tau?
children.translated_text: <s>Upananda</s> said: 'What did those two say?'

children.text: sannanda uvāca-āvayoḥ prathama-vayo' tītayos tāta-caraṇānāṃ svayaṃ gocāraṇam anācāratām ācarati iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Sananda</s> said: 'When we two had passed our first youth, the venerable father's own cow-herding was not the proper conduct — thus they said.'

children.text: tad etad varṇyamānam ākarṇya tayor mukhaṃ nirvarṇya sa-vismayaṃ tūṣṇīmbhūṣṇutayā virājamāne vrajeśāne sarve' pi tam ūcuḥ-yadyapy adya-jātāv iva sujātāv amū, tathāpi kramaṃ vinā buddhi-niṣkramasya bala-saṃvalanasya ca sad-bhāvād asmākaṃ vismāyakāv eva bhavataḥ | itas tu na vismāyakau bhavatas tapaḥ-prabhāva eva khalv evaṃ bhāvam āvahatīti | na khalu tat-tat-khalānāṃ yat parimalanaṃ jātam, tatra sahāyatānāṃ sahāyatā kācid api paricitā | tasmān maṅgalam eva saṅgataṃ bhaviṣyati iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing that being described and gazing at their faces, when the lord of <s>Vraja</s> fell wonderfully silent, shining in his taciturnity — all said to him: 'Although these two are as if born today, well-born as they are, nevertheless, without proper sequence, because of the reality of the emergence of intelligence and the growth of strength, they are indeed astonishing to us. But from this side, they are not astonishing — for the power of your austerity indeed brings about such a state. And indeed, the destruction that was wrought by those various wicked ones — no assistance of any kind was noticed [from our side] in that. Therefore, only auspiciousness will result from this conjunction.'

children.text: atha tadā kadācin nija-gṛhiṇyāpi saha rahasi śrī-vraja-rājasya sa eṣa prastāva-viśeṣa āsīt-yatra ca tau putra-prema-yantritatayā tad etan mantritavantau, paśyāmaḥ samaya-viśeṣam iti |
children.translated_text: Then, once, the king of Śrī <s>Vraja</s> had this very special discussion in private with his own wife as well — where those two, being controlled by parental love, deliberated on this matter: 'Let us observe the special occasion [for it].'

children.text: tadā ca dina-katipayānantaraṃ sabhāyāṃ bhāsamānāyāṃ śrī-vraja-rājasya vailakṣyam ālakṣya sarve' narvācīna-gopā mitho nirīkṣya hasanti sma | [24] tatra ca śrī-vraja-rāje kathaṃ katham? iti sa-smitam uktavati vadanti sma, yad asmābhir akasmād vismāyanam anubhūtam, tad eva bhavadbhir apīti sambhāvyate |
children.translated_text: Then, after a few days, when the assembly was shining, all the unexcelled cowherds, perceiving the king of Śrī <s>Vraja's</s> embarrassment, exchanged glances and laughed. [24] And there, when the king of Śrī <s>Vraja</s> said with a smile, 'How, how?' — they said: 'That which we have unexpectedly experienced as astonishment — we surmise that your honor too has [experienced] the same.'

children.text: vraja-rāja uvāca-kathyatāṃ tāvat tathyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Let the truth be told by your honors!'

children.text: sarva ūcuḥ-yadyapi cirata evedaṃ caritam, tathāpi bhavatāpi gocaritena gocaritenātīva racitam, yat khalu sarvaṃ go-jātam na tu bhavaj-jātam antarā padam api padaḥ pradadāti | kathañcit tenaivāgrāvasthitenādya tāḥ prasthāpitāḥ santi |
children.translated_text: All said: 'Although this has been going on for a long time, nevertheless, even by your honor's cow-tending in the manner of cow-tending, it has been exceedingly arranged — that the entire cow-kind does not place even a single step without your offspring. Somehow, by his standing in front alone, today they have been set forth.'

children.text: vrajarāja uvāca-tad idam akasmāt kathaṃ jātam?
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'How has this happened so suddenly?'

children.text:
sarva ūcuḥ-bhavat-putraḥ kutracid yatra snehaṃ vyañjayati, tatra sarvatra caivaṃ dṛśyate |
[29] vraja-rāja uvāca-tarhi kim agarhitam arhitaṃ syāt?
children.translated_text:
All said: 'Wherever your son displays affection, everywhere the same is seen.'
[29] The king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'Then what would be the unobjectionable and proper course?'

children.text: sarva ūcuḥ-yatra gaty-antaraṃ nāsti, tat khalv anantaram eva vidhātuṃ yuktam | yat tu tatra-bhavantas tatra bhītāyante, tat punar vatsa-pālane' pi na tucchāyate | kintu bhavat-tapa eva pratapati pratīpān iti pratīyate | tasmād bhavatād bhavatām anujñā, yā paramparayāpi paraṃ param apy amaṅgalaṃ tāra-yiṣyati |
children.translated_text: All said: 'Where there is no alternative, that indeed must be arranged immediately. As for the fear that your honors have regarding that — well, even in calf-herding it was not slight. But your austerity alone blazes against adversaries — thus it is understood. Therefore, from your honor, the permission that, even by tradition, will carry across the most supreme inauspiciousness beyond and beyond.'

children.text: athedam ākarṇya nirvarṇanata eva jñāpitānujñā-nija-samāje śrīman-nanda-rāje sarvānumati-labdhānandaḥ śrīmān upanandaḥ prathita-samajñān samaya-jñān jijñāsayāmāsa | tair api budha-śravaṇa-sukha-prada-maṅgala-śravaṇa-saṅgata-budha-śravaṇa-viśiṣṭhāyām abahula-bāhulāṣṭamyāṃ bahulā-pālanaṃ bahulam etad iṣṭam ity ādiṣṭam | [32] śrīman-nandādayaś ca sarve dundubhi-nirghoṣeṇa ghoṣe tasmin nirviśeṣam ahas-tritayam ahamahamikayā mahaḥ pracārayantas, tad-vatsa-cāraṇa-bṛhad-utsavam apy aticarantas tat samācaranti sma |
children.translated_text: Now, hearing this, the glorious <s>Upananda</s> — having obtained permission conveyed through examination itself in the assembly of the glorious king <s>Nanda</s>, and having gained the delight of universal consent — consulted the well-known experts who understood the proper times. By them too, the instruction was given that the eighth day of the dark fortnight (<s>Bāhulāṣṭamī</s>) conjoined with the auspicious <s>Budha-śravaṇa</s> (Mercury-<s>Śravaṇa</s>) constellation — which bestows the happiness of hearing what is auspicious — was greatly desired for the abundant tending of the cows (<s>bahulā-pālana</s>). [32] And the glorious <s>Nanda</s> and all the others, by the thunderous sound of <s>dundubhi</s> drums, uniformly spread radiance throughout that cowherd settlement for three days with eager rivalry, and they also surpassed even the great festival of calf-herding in their celebration of it.

children.text:
ekasyaikasya ced vaktur vaktrāṇi syuḥ sadāyutam |
  tadā tad vaktum icchantu yady āyuḥ sarvadāyutam ||JGc_1,12.4|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
If each single speaker were to have ten thousand mouths,
then let them wish to speak of it — if their lifespan were eternally ten thousand [years]! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.4, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
dig-darśanaṃ tu yathā,
  gopālocita-navya-veṣa-valanai rakṣā-vidhānair dvijādy-
  āśībhiḥ sudināha-labhya-racanair vrajyārha-nīrājanaiḥ |
  saṅgānānvita-vādya-nṛtya-nikaraiḥ śaśvaj-jayādy-āravaiḥ
  śrīmān gopa-mahendra-sūnur agamad rāmeṇa dhenūr anu ||JGc_1,12.5|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text:
A glimpse of it, as follows:
With new attire and adornments befitting a cowherd, with protective rites,
with blessings of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, with arrangements obtained on that auspicious day, with lustration ceremonies worthy of the procession,
with multitudes of music, dance, and instrumental accompaniment, with perpetual victory-cries and other sounds,
the glorious son of the great lord of cowherds set forth with <s>Rāma</s>, following the cows! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.5, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: tad anu gati-rītir itīva ca gantavyā-vādya-gīta-maṅgala-parītaṃ purodhasaḥ purodhāya dhenūḥ sannidhāya tāś ca pādyādibhir arcitā vidhāya madhura-grāsais tāsāṃ samagrāṇāṃ tṛptim ādhāya tāsu nati-prabhṛtibhir mānam upadhāya punaś ca pradāna-dakṣiṇābhiḥ purohitādīn akṣīṇānandān sandhāya, śrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇādīn mañjulāñjali-valitam agrato nidhāya sthitavati sāgraje tasminn avaraje, śrīmāṃs tat-pitā vrajarājas tāvan maṇi-maya-lakuṭiṃ tat-kare ghaṭayāmāsa | śrīmatī tan-mātā ca vraja-rājñī bhāle tilakaṃ nidadhe, nidhāya ca sā-
children.translated_text: Then, the manner of proceeding was thus: surrounded by music, song, and auspicious sounds, placing the family priests ahead, assembling the cows, worshipping them with foot-washing and the like, satiating all of them with sweet morsels, showing them respect with bowing and the like, and then filling the <s>purohitas</s> and others with undiminished joy through generous gifts — when the younger son, along with his elder brother, stood before the glorious feet of his father and others with graceful folded hands, the glorious father, the king of <s>Vraja</s>, placed a jewel-studded staff in his hand. And the glorious mother, the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, applied the <s>tilaka</s> mark on his forehead. And having applied it, she —

children.text:
rāma prāg asya paścād bhava subala yuvāṃ śrīla dāman sudāman
  doḥ pārśva-sthau bhavetaṃ diśi vidiśi pare santu cātmīya-bandhoḥ |
  itthaṃ haste vidhṛtya pratiśiśu diśatī tatra kṛṣṇasya mātā
  tat-tat-karmādhikāra-śriyam api dadatī netra-nīrair asikta ||JGc_1,12.6|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
"<s>Rāma</s>, be before him! Behind him, you — <s>Subala</s>! You two, O glorious <s>Dāman</s> and <s>Sudāman</s>,
be stationed at his two sides! In every direction and intermediate direction, let the others of our kinsman be!"
Thus, grasping each child by the hand, assigning them, <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother,
while also bestowing upon each the glory of authority over their respective tasks, was drenched with tears from her eyes! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.6, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text: atha rohiṇī-bṛṃhita-śuci-sampad-upananda-gṛhiṇī-saṃhita-mahita-mahilābhiḥ sahitaṃ yathāyathaṃ saṅgamite nānā-maṅgale, bhuvi divi ca mahā-maha-bahala-kuśala-kutūhalam anu, mātaraṃ pitaraṃ kāṃścid anyāṃś ca namaskṛtya, kṛta-kṛtyatayā jihi-jihi-kāreṇeritāś ca gāvaḥ svābhimukham eva sthitā na prasthitavatya ity anupapattyā pratyāsannān gurūn parāvartya, tāsām purata eva sa-bala-sakhaḥ sa prasthitavān | prasthitavati ca tatra śyāma-varṇe tarṇakāgrimatā-nirvarṇaneneva mandaṃ mandaṃ gacchantaṃ gāvas tam anvagacchan |
children.translated_text: Then, when the various auspicious rites had been duly conducted, accompanied by women headed by <s>Rohiṇī</s>, joined by the wife of <s>Upananda</s> — resplendent with pure prosperity — and other venerable ladies, and following the overwhelming curiosity of auspicious festivities on earth and in heaven — having bowed to his mother, father, and certain others, and when the cows, prompted by the "go, go!" call as if done with their duties, stood facing him and did not set forth — confounded by this anomaly, he turned around to face the elders who were nearby, and then, accompanied by his powerful friends, he set forth before the cows themselves.

children.text: tad evaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-rāmāv etāv atha svānugamana-kamana-manaskān janān kathaṃ katham api tataḥ pathaḥ ślathayitvā, svātmānam api tal-locana-śṛṅkhalā-mocanān mocayitvā, sakhibhir apy akhila-vilambi-lalitair nava-gopa-mahasopavalitaiḥ saha sahasā hasantau lasantau cārāya madhye madhye stabdha-nikhila-gavīkau labdha-mano-gavīkau suvalita-calitaṃ govardhana-diśam uddiśya calataḥ sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> had somehow loosened the people — whose minds longed to follow them — from that path, and having freed even themselves from the chain of those people's gazes, together with their friends — all of whom were charmingly languid and adorned with the dignity of the new cowherd festival — laughing suddenly, shining, pausing the entire herd now and then for the pleasure of tending, having gained their heart's desire, they proceeded with beautifully swaying steps toward the direction of <s>Govardhana</s>.

children.text: yatra gāvaḥ saṅketita-svarādi-viśeṣeṇaiva mithaḥ saṅkīrṇā vikīrṇāś ca bhavanti sma, na tu daṇḍenopaghātaṃ viśīrṇāḥ kriyante sma | yatra ca sakhiṣu tābhyāṃ saha parasparaṃ maṇḍayanteṣu nandayanteṣu krīḍā-janayanteṣu ca parama-kautukam āvirbhavati sma |
children.translated_text: Where the cows, by the particular signal of designated calls and the like, would gather together and disperse among themselves, but were never scattered by being struck with a staff. And where, among the friends adorning each other with those two, playing and generating sport, supreme curiosity manifested.

children.text: tad etan nirvarṇya devair varṇitaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: Having observed this, the gods described it as follows:

children.text:
pratyekaṃ gāva etā bahir api ca hareḥ prāṇa-rūpā yad āsāṃ
  śaśvat tṛptau ca tṛptiṃ kṣudhi ca kalayati kṣud-vikāraṃ sa eṣaḥ |
  ānīyānīya caitā nijahṛdi vidadhad ghrāṇa-saukhyaṃ dadhānaḥ
  śliṣyann uccair vicinvann aśanam upadadat pālayan svena bhāti ||JGc_1,12.7|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
Each of these cows, even externally, is the very life-form of <s>Hari</s>, since
he always feels satisfaction in their satisfaction and the pangs of hunger in their hunger;
bringing them again and again and placing them in his heart, bestowing the pleasure of scent,
embracing them, carefully inspecting their food, providing it, and protecting them by himself — he shines! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.7, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text:
usrāṇāṃ prāṇa-sāmyaṃ vahati harir amūs taṃ vinā rikta-cittāś
  citra-prāyāḥ samantād yad iha vana-tati-śrī-nibhā visphuranti |
  tal-lābhād ghrāṇa-dṛṣṭi-śravaṇa-sarasana-sparśa-yogād valante
  kintu syāc citram etad bahir upavalitaṃ teṣu taṃ svādayanti ||JGc_1,12.8|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
<s>Hari</s> bears an equality of life-breath with the cows; without him, they are empty-hearted,
mostly motionless, manifesting on all sides like the beauty of rows of painted forests;
upon finding him, through the union of scent, sight, hearing, taste, and touch, they flourish;
but this is wondrous — outwardly adorned thus, they relish him within! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.8, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text:
āhūtaṃ kurute hariḥ sakhi-janaṃ, so' py enam evaṃ tathā
  vakti śliṣyati jighrati prahasati skandhaṃ spṛśan karṣati |
  āstāṃ tac ca mahādbhutaṃ śṛṇuta bho yady antaraṃ tarkyate
  naivātmā pṛthag asya tasya ca bhaved ity eva vijñāyate ||JGc_1,12.9|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
<s>Hari</s> calls his group of friends, and they likewise call him;
he speaks, embraces, smells, laughs, touches the shoulder, and pulls!
Leave aside that great wonder — just hear this: if the interval [between them] is examined,
no separate self of his or theirs would be found — thus it is known! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.9, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
vadati sakhi-samūhaḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmāv itīdaṃ
  kvacid api vinimāya prāha tat tac ca yuktam |
  kalayata yad imāv apy ātmanaḥ sthāna eva
  sphuṭam iha vidadhāte yan mithas tatra tatra ||JGc_1,12.10|| [mālinī]

atha tad evaṃ ca sthite, pūrvata eva tadīya-vimala-parimala-mādhurī-dhārā-nandita-vidūraga-vṛndāvana-sthira-cara-jīvāvalībhir jīvātutayājīvyamānau, samprati tu sarvā eva tā devatā-pūrvāḥ paramāpūrva-darśana-sparśanādibhir labdha-parvaṇaḥ kurvāte sma | [40] yāḥ khalu sarvātiyāyi-sukha-dāyitayānyeṣām api puṇyāya puṇya-phalāya naipuṇyam āseduḥ | [41] tatraiva ca sarva-sukha-śaṃsinī vaṃśī sarvam ātmānaṃ ca kṛtārthatāṃ prāpitavatī | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, things being thus, even before this, by the stream of the fragrant sweetness of his stainless perfume, the assemblages of all moving and stationary living beings of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — though far away — had been delighted and were sustained as if by life-breath. But now, all those beings, led by the deities, having obtained the unprecedented festival of seeing, touching, and the like, were making it [come alive]. [40] They who, by bestowing happiness that surpasses all, attained merit and the fruit of merit and excellence for others as well. [41] And right there, the flute that proclaims all happiness brought everything and himself to fulfillment. For:

children.text:
na tad vanaṃ yan na vihāra-maṅgalaṃ
  nāyaṃ vihāraḥ śubha-gīta-bhṛn na yaḥ |
  gītaṃ na tad yan na hi vaṃśīkākṛtaṃ
  vaṃśī na sā kṛṣṇa-mukhānugā na yā ||JGc_1,12.11|| [upajāti 12]
tad-dine tu kāntaḥ so' yaṃ vṛttāntaḥ karṇāntaḥ kriyatām-
children.translated_text: Now, on that day, let this charming account reach the ears:

children.text:
udīrṇa-muralīkalaḥ sva-guṇa-gātṛ-gopāvṛtir
  balena sahitaḥ sphurad-vividha-mādhurī-vistṛtiḥ |
  rasārdram aniśa-smitaṃ tad-atihārda-bhājāṃ gavāṃ
  hitaṃ svajana-cittavad vanam athāviśan mādhavaḥ ||JGc_1,12.12|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
With the melody of the <s>muralī</s> (flute) uplifted, surrounded by cowherd companions who sang his virtues,
accompanied by <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), radiating a spread of manifold sweetness,
with a smile moist with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight), always for the welfare of those cows who are recipients of his deepest affection,
<s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) then entered the forest — [tender] as the mind of his own people! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.12, <s>pṛthvī</s>]

children.text: sa ca nitānta-priya-jana-bhānaḥ kānanāntaḥ-sāra-sarasa-gandha-sarasa-sugandha-gandha-vāha-vāhita-nava-pallava-pāṇibhiḥ sphuran-madhura-sakhi-tatiṃ madhupatim āliṅgann utasaṅga-saṅginaṃ vidhāya, svānuvrata-madhuvrata-khaga-mṛga-mañju-guñjitādi-vyañjanayā khelitum iva protsāhayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And he — the delight of his most intimate people — within the forest, by the hands of fresh sprouts borne on the fragrant and luscious breeze carrying the essence of the forest, making the sweet ranks of friends — who were embracing <s>Madhupati</s> (the lord of spring/<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and placing him upon his lap — he, as it were, encouraged them to play through the charming humming of bees, the songs of birds and deer that were devoted to him.

children.text:
tataś ca kautuka-viśeṣa-lambhanāya vraja-rāja-tanūjaḥ sa-smitam īkṣamāṇaḥ sa-vismayavad utprekṣamāṇaś ca nijāgrajaṃ prati sādara-narma-gandha-prabandhi-vana-varṇanaṃ nirmame, yathā-
  nūnaṃ bhavān viśva-patir namanti yad
  baliṃ gṛhītvā taravaḥ padaṃ tava |
  paśya prasūnādi-śatena tan nata-
  pravāla-śākhā-śikhayā spṛśanti te ||JGc_1,12.13|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then, for the attainment of a special curiosity, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, gazing with a smile and conjecturing with wonder, composed before his elder brother a description of the forest, fragrant with affectionate humor, as follows:
"Surely you are the lord of the universe, for the trees
bend down and, having accepted tribute, bow at your feet!
See — with hundreds of flowers and the like, they touch your [feet]
with their tips of bent sprout-branches!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.13, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text:
tvaṃ rājase deva vane' tra sāmprataṃ
  vayaṃ na paśyāma tathāpi tāmasāḥ |
  itīva cakṣuṣmati janma-lambhanaṃ
  vṛkṣā vṛṇānāś caraṇaṃ tavāśritāḥ ||JGc_1,12.14|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
"You shine here, O Lord, in this forest now;
we do not see [the same] — yet we are ignorant!"
— as if saying thus, the trees, choosing birth
in the presence of one who has eyes, have taken refuge at your feet! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.14, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text:
gāyanti tvāṃ ṣaṭpadāś cānuyāntaḥ
  śrī-rohiṇyāḥ putram antarhitaṃ ca |
  itthaṃ mitrāṇy āhur ūhe' ham evaṃ
  sarveśas tvaṃ na tv amī san-munīśāḥ ||JGc_1,12.15|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
"The bees sing of you and follow you,
and [they sing] of the son of the glorious <s>Rohiṇī</s> who is hidden [within you]!"
Thus the friends say — but I surmise thus:
you are the lord of all, but they are not — they are the lords of the sages! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.15, <s>śālinī</s>]

children.text:
suramyaṃ nṛtyanti pramada-śikhinaḥ sneha-valitaṃ
  hariṇyaḥ paśyanti sphuṭa-mṛdu-kalaṃ bibhrati pikāḥ |
  naṭā rāmāḥ sūkta-prapaṭhana-vidaḥ kānana-sadām
  amī dhanyā yasmād vidadhati tavārād atithitām ||JGc_1,12.16|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
The exquisitely beautiful peacocks dance, the deer gaze with loving tenderness,
the cuckoos produce clear, soft, melodious sounds;
the dancers are the women, the chanters of hymns are the forest-dwellers —
they are blessed because they perform your hospitality! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.16, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text:
aṅghrisparśair dharitrīgiritṛṇasaritas te nakhaśreṇilekha-
  śrīmac-citrair vicitra-druma-samudayaga-dyota-vīrud-vibhedāḥ |
  snigdhekṣābhiś ca dhanyā mṛga-vihaga-gaṇā vakṣasaḥ saṅga-lābhād
  eṣā tatrāpi gopī-vratatir atitarāṃ yat-spṛhā sāpi lakṣmīḥ ||JGc_1,12.17|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
By the touch of your feet, the earth, mountains, grasses, rivers — the varieties of vines
adorning trees of diverse splendor, decorated with the beauty of your toenail-streaks;
by your affectionate glances, the blessed herds of deer and birds; by contact with your chest,
this company of <s>gopīs</s> supremely — and she who longs for that, even <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.17, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text:
pitṛvyān me kṣatrād avataraṇam āptaḥ sa tu bhavān
  pitur gopeśasyātmaja-padam agād dharma-vidhinā |
  atas tvaṃ gopīnāṃ pariṇayanam āptāsi tad iyaṃ
  latā gopī-nāmnī tava hṛdaya-lagnā prathayati ||JGc_1,12.18|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"From my paternal uncle's <s>Kṣatriya</s> [clan], that descent was obtained, but you,
by the law of <s>dharma</s>, attained the position of son of <s>Gopeśvara</s> (the lord of cowherds, <s>Nanda</s>);
therefore you are fit for marriage with the <s>gopīs</s> — and this
vine called '<s>gopī</s>' declares it, clinging to your heart!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.12.18, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: athāgrajaś cānuja-vācam amṛtam ivācamya smitam ācarann uvāca-bhavādṛśa eva tādṛśa-guṇa-gaṇa-bhāg īśvaraḥ katham anyaṃ tatra gaṇyaṃ karoti? iti |
children.translated_text: Then the elder brother, sipping his younger brother's words like nectar and smiling, said: "How could one such as yourself — possessing such a multitude of virtues — the very Lord, consider anyone else there worthy of reckoning?"

children.text: tad evam akhila-sakhibhiḥ saha hasan narmaṇā teṣāṃ śarma sphuṭam uttambhayan, śrīmad-vṛndāvana-vana-śobhām api svam iva tān upalambhayan, paśūn api mānasa-gaṅgā-rodhāṃsi lambhayan svayam apy ayam atitarāṃ reme | tac ca prātyahika-prāyam evaṃ prathayiṣyāmaḥ | yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, laughing with all his friends together, clearly uplifting their joy through humor, making them perceive the beauty of the glorious <s>Vṛndāvana</s> forest as if it were his own self, bringing even the cattle to the banks of the <s>Mānasa Gaṅgā</s>, he himself too sported exceedingly. And we shall describe this as being almost the daily routine. As follows:

children.text: ramate rāmaṃ paritaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ | sakhi-gaṇa-gīta-guṇeṣu sa-tṛṣṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> delights all around with <s>Rāma</s>; thirsting for the virtues sung by the company of friends —

children.text: anugāyati pika-ṣaṭpada-gānam | parijalpati śuka-haṃsa-samānam ||
children.translated_text: He sings in imitation of the cuckoo and the bee; he chatters like a parrot and a swan —

children.text: evaṃ cakra-cakora-bakādi | anurauti sphuṭa-hāsa-vivādi ||
children.translated_text: Thus imitating the <s>cakravāka</s>, <s>cakora</s>, crane and others, he calls out, full of bright laughter and jesting —

children.text: dvīpi-mukhārpita-bhīti paśūnām | rutim iva sṛjati bhayāya śiśūnām ||
children.translated_text: He emits a sound as if for terrifying the young boys, resembling the cry of animals facing a leopard's mouth —

children.text: pakṣi-mṛgādikam aharahar acalam | viracita-nāmabhir āha ca sakalam ||
children.translated_text: Day after day, the birds, deer and other creatures, including the unmoving ones, he addresses all by their assigned names —

children.text: bhramati sakhā yadi tasmin ko' pi | karṣati vihasan paṇam amuto' pi ||
children.translated_text: If any friend strays among them, he pulls him back from there, laughing and claiming a wager —

children.text: dūraga-paśum āhvayati ca nāmnā | kṛta-go-gopa-manorama-sāmnā ||
children.translated_text: He calls distant cattle by name, having composed melodies that delight cows and cowherds —

children.text: gavyāhūtau śikhināṃ hūtiḥ | jātā yad asau ghana-ruti-bhūtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the summoning of cows, the peacocks cry out, for he possesses the glory of a cloud's rumble —

children.text: vyatiyuñjāno bhrātrā sva-karam | śaṃsati hasati sakhī-hita-nikaram ||
children.translated_text: Interlocking his hand with his brother's, he praises and laughs at the host of benefits of friends —

children.text: sakhibhir viśramayann ayam āryam | praṇayati tat-pada-lālana-kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Having his friends give rest to his elder brother, he performs the task of massaging his feet —

children.text: sulalita-pallava-talpa-vidhānaḥ | suhṛd-ūru-sthira-mūrdha-nidhānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Arranging a couch of most lovely sprouts, placing his head firmly on a friend's thigh —

children.text: keli-śramam anu kṛta-śayanehaḥ | puṇyatamair upavījita-deḥaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After the fatigue of play, having made a bed here, his body is fanned by the most blessed ones —

children.text: atra ca kair api lālita-caraṇaḥ | asmat-tṛṇ-mātrada-paricaraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here, with his feet caressed by some, attended even by those who offer [as little as] a blade of our grass —

children.text: yaḥ snigdhānāṃ gāna-vinodaiḥ | nidrām itavān svara-kṛta-modaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who, by the entertainments of song of his affectionate ones, with melodies that create delight, went to sleep —

children.text: smaratāṃ tan naḥ kim api manaḥ-stham | samayaṃ sahate nānyāvastham ||
children.translated_text: Let our minds remember that something which dwells within the heart; the occasion does not bear any other state!

children.text: vayam iha ke vā lubdhaṃ-manyāḥ | lubdhā yasmin śuka-mukha-dhanyāḥ ||JGc_1,12.19|| [mātrā-samaka]
children.translated_text: Who are we here, thinking ourselves greedy? [It is rather they] who are greedy — those blessed ones with parrot-like mouths! ||12.19|| [mātrā-samaka]

children.text:
tad evam eva valgu valayite līlā-valaye pūrvavan nilayād ākalitam iṣṭa-miṣṭānnādikaṃ rasanayā śliṣṭaṃ vidhāya, gavāṃ jālaṃ cālayan pālayan sāgraja-vraja-rāja-tanūjaḥ savayobhir āyatīgavam avasaram avagatya gotrā-mātrāṇāṃ tatiṃ śanair upavrajam anaiṣīt | nītvā ca tārṇaka-vātsaka-bhedānāṃ tathā strī-gavīnāṃ tāsv apy upasāryāsandhinī-praṣṭhauhī-dhenu-baṣkayiṇī-gṛṣṭi-samāṃsamīnā-naicikī-kapilā-vaśā-gopati-prabhṛtīnāṃ tatra ca gaṅgādi-nāmnāṃ tathā puṅgavānāṃ teṣu cārṣabhya-damya-jāta-kakutpūrṇa-kakuj-jātokṣa-mahokṣa-vṛddhokṣa-yugya-prāsaṅgya-śākaṭa-praṣṭhavāṭ-pramukhānāṃ tatra ca haṃsādi-nāmnāṃ paraḥ-koṭīnāṃ kūṭān pṛthak pṛthag avīvasat | tatra tatra
ca nastitān api śivaka-baddhān acīkarat |
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, when the beautiful circle of pastimes had been gracefully rounded, having prepared the desired sweetmeats and other delicacies brought from home as before, savored by the tongue, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> together with his elder brother, driving and tending the herd of cows, understanding with his age-mates the time when the cows would be returning, gradually led the rows of mother-cows toward the cow-settlement. And having led them, he settled the herds separately — of the various kinds of calves and young cattle, and likewise of the female cattle, among which were the <s>upasāryā</s> (about to calve), <s>sandhinī</s> (newly pregnant), <s>praṣṭhauhī</s> (having calved once), <s>dhenu</s> (milch cow), <s>baṣkayiṇī</s> (newly calved), <s>gṛṣṭi</s> (having calved once), <s>samāṃsamīnā</s> (about to calve again), <s>naicikī</s> (of low quality), <s>kapilā</s> (tawny), <s>vaśā</s> (barren), <s>gopati</s> (bull-attended), and the like — among them those named <s>Gaṅgā</s> and so forth — and likewise the bulls, among which were the <s>ārṣabhya</s> (born of a fine bull), <s>damya</s> (to be tamed), <s>jāta-kakut</s> (with emerging hump), <s>pūrṇa-kakut</s> (full-humped), <s>jātokṣa</s> (young bull), <s>mahokṣa</s> (great bull), <s>vṛddhokṣa</s> (old bull), <s>yugya</s> (yoke-worthy), <s>prāsaṅgya</s> (attendant bull), <s>śākaṭa</s> (cart bull), <s>praṣṭhavāṭ</s> (lead bull), and others — among them those named <s>Haṃsa</s> and so forth — numbering tens of millions of herds, he separated them each. And wherever they had been lost, he had them tied with <s>śivaka</s> (halter) ropes.
