children.text: tataś ca pūrva-pūrvasmād apy apūrvatayā maṅgala-vastu-nikara-karaiḥ puraskṛta-kṣiti-deva-nara-deva-puraḥsarair vrajavāsi-varair upavrajya nīrājya ca sapaśu-pāla-balaḥ sa gopālaḥ sadanaṃ sādaram āsādayāmāse | prasādayāmāse ca sulalita-lālanayā janita-sukha-jananī-mukha-purandhrī-janena |
children.translated_text: Then, with an unprecedented novelty surpassing all before, greeted by the eminent <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers preceded by earth-gods (<s>brāhmaṇas</s>) and man-gods (kings) bearing clusters of auspicious objects in their hands, and having been welcomed with the <s>nīrājana</s> (lamp-waving) ceremony, that <s>Gopāla</s>, together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) the protector of animals, reverently reached his dwelling. And he gladdened the women headed by his joy-producing mother through his most graceful fondling.

children.text: atha kṣaṇa-mātraṃ tatra viśramya go-dohanāya nirgamya ramya-doha-pātra-sandohaṃ kiṅkara-nikara-karāhṛtaṃ vidhāya, gavās-thānīm abhinidhāya, mahā-mahima-gopa-samūham anukṛtopaveśaṃ śrī-vraja-nareśam anujñāpya vatsa-mocanam ājñāpya dhenuka-madhya-sthitaḥ svasti-vācanādi-praśastaṃ samasta-citta-mohanaṃ go-dohanaṃ nāma karma prathamaṃ nirmame |
children.translated_text: Then, resting there for just a moment, going out for the cow-milking, having arranged the delightful collection of milking-vessels brought by the hands of groups of servants, having settled them in the cow-station, having obtained permission from the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> who was seated in the manner imitated by the assembly of greatly glorious cowherds, and having ordered the release of the calves, standing in the midst of the milch-cows, he first performed the act called cow-milking — auspicious with the recitation of <s>svasti-vācana</s> (blessings) and the like, captivating the minds of all.

children.text:
tatra ca gṛhān nirgamanaṃ yathā,
  hāṭaka-lakuṭi-pāṇir maṇi-cita-niryoga-rājad-uṣṇīṣaḥ |
  jita-gajarāja-vilāsaḥ sabalaḥ kṛṣṇo yayau goṣṭham ||JGc_1,12.20|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
There, his going forth from the house was as follows:
With a golden staff in hand, with a turban radiant with gem-studded <s>niryoga</s> (ear-ornament) and pearls,
conquering the grace of the lord of elephants, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with <s>Bala</s>, went to the cow-pen! ||12.20|| [āryā]

children.text:
dohanaṃ yathā,
  śrīmat-paṭṭa-vaṭānta-mauktika-lasan-niryoga-rājat-kacau
  gāḍhā-naddha-varāntarīya-rucibhiś citrādharāṅga-śriyau |
  ūrdhvajñū kṣiti-saṃhitāgra-caraṇau jānu-dvayāntaḥ-sthita-
  svarṇāmatra-dharau sitāsita-tanū dhenūr duhāte sma tau ||JGc_1,12.21|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text:
The milking was as follows:
With fine silk headbands, pearls gleaming, ear-ornaments radiant, with lustrous hair,
with tightly bound beautiful inner garments, with resplendent beauty of variegated limbs,
with knees raised, toes touching the ground, with golden vessels placed between the two knees —
those two, of white and dark complexion, milked the cows! ||12.21|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: tataś ca ghaṭodhnīnāṃ tāsāṃ nātidugdhānām api dugdhāni tu pracuraṃ dugdhāni vidhāya gavādi-sambhālanam anu gopān saṃvidhāya tāni ca pituḥ purastān nidhāya karābhyām añjaliṃ sandhāya sthitavantau santau, tena dūratas tadīya-turīya-kakṣā-pūrita-cāturī-nirīkṣaṇa-sukha-sthagitena bhūyo bhūyaś cāhūya savyāpasavyayor upaveśitau | yatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then, although those cows with full udders had not been milked much, nevertheless their milk was abundantly milked. Having arranged the tending of the cows and other [animals] by the cowherds, and having placed those [vessels of milk] before his father, those two stood with palms joined in <s>añjali</s>. And by him — whose joy was concealed by the pleasure of watching the skill that filled the fourth grade [of proficiency] of those two — they were called again and again and seated to his left and right. And there:

children.text:
akṣṇā tasyāpasavyena savyaṃ tac cakṛṣe balāt |
  api savyenāpasavyaṃ rāmaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ didṛkṣuṇā ||JGc_1,12.22|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
His left eye forcefully drew the right [son],
and likewise his right eye drew the left — <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
by the king of <s>Vraja</s> who desired to behold [them both]! ||12.22|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
  eka-hetu-mayam eva locane dve ca bāṣpam aparatra vindataḥ |
  rāma-kṛṣṇa-yugapad-vilokane te tu gopa-nṛpater yathāyatham ||JGc_1,12.23|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
Both eyes, though of a single cause, found tears in two different places;
in the simultaneous beholding of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
those [eyes] of the king of the cowherds [flowed] each in its own fitting way! ||12.23|| [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
tathā hi-
  savyam akṣi tanujād vrajeśitur
  bhrātṛjāt punar asavyam asravat |
  yatra mānasam api svayaṃ dvidhā-
  bhidyatāśru-miṣam ity abudhyata ||JGc_1,12.24|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
For indeed:
The left eye of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> flowed for his son,
and the right flowed for his brother's son;
whereupon his mind itself, splitting itself in two,
understood [the division] under the pretext of tears! ||12.24|| [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  agrimān agrimān kurvann antyān antyān samaiḥ samam |
  so' bhito rāma-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ śobhito gṛham āyayau ||JGc_1,12.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And then:
Making each foremost one still more foremost, each last one equal with the equals,
he — beautified on both sides by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — went home! ||12.25|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tauryātrika-carya-paryākulatayeti śeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: The remainder [of the sentence is]: 'amid the bustle of the festival of music, song, and dance.'

children.text: gṛham āgatya ca sarvām ātma-goṣṭhīṃ miṣṭānnādibhiḥ suṣṭhu tuṣṭām akārṣīt | [54] tataś cānanda-viśiṣṭeṣu visṛṣṭeṣu śiṣṭeṣu rāma-kṛṣṇau nija-nija-dhāma samāgamya ramyatama-śayyām adhiśayya mātṛbhyām upacaryamāṇau paricārakaiḥ paricaryamāṇau sukhaṃ nidadratuḥ |
children.translated_text: Having come home, he fully satisfied all his own company with sweetmeats and the like. [54] Then, when the distinguished ones had been joyfully dismissed, and the select few remained, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having arrived each at his own dwelling, lying down upon the most delightful bed, attended by their mothers and served by their attendants, slept happily.

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ samāpana-digdhaṃ tad idaṃ vākyaṃ sāñjali vyānañja-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, anointing that concluding utterance, said with joined palms:

children.text:
īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava gopa-dharā-pate |
  ātmārāmāś ca yat-kīrtyā yānti drāg ātma-vismṛtim ||JGc_1,12.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
[56] atha śrīdāmādi-camatkāra-sāra-prada-prathanasya tad-etat-kathanasya śravaṇānte, saiveyaṃ līleti bhrānte, tata eva bahir vṛttita upaśānte goloka-dharitrī-kānte jane ca śreṇī-prānte, tau sūta-sutau yathāvad baddhāñjalitayāvasthitau cirata eva pūrva-pūrvavat prīti-dānena vāsaṃ prasthāpitau vidhāya te sarve yathāsvam āvāsādikam āsāditavantaḥ |
children.translated_text:
'Such a son was born to you, O lord of the cow-earth,
by whose fame even the self-delighting ones (<s>ātmārāmas</s>)
swiftly attain self-forgetfulness!' ||12.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
[56] Then, at the conclusion of hearing that narrative — the bestower of the essence of wonder about <s>Śrīdāmā</s> and others — when the assembly was bewildered [thinking] 'This is indeed the very same pastime!', and when the people at the outskirts had quieted down from the outdoor conclusion of that very [narrative], and the people — beloved of the <s>Goloka</s>-earth — were at the edges of the rows, those two bard-sons, standing with properly joined palms for a long time, were dispatched to their lodging with the gift of affection just as before; and then all [the assembly members] reached their own dwellings and such.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
gocāraṇa-pracāraṇaṃ nāma
dvādaśaṃ pūraṇam
 ||12||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Twelfth Chapter, named
'The Propagation of Cow-Herding.'
||12||

children.text: atha trayodaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Thirteenth Chapter.

children.text: kāliya-dava-caṇḍatā-daṇḍanam
children.translated_text: The Chastisement of the Ferocity of <s>Kāliya</s> and of the Forest Fire.

children.text: atha pratiprātar iva śrīmad-vrajarāja-samāje virājamāne kathāṃ kathayituṃ samutkaṇṭho madhukaṇṭho nijāntaś cintayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then, as if every morning, when the glorious assembly of the king of <s>Vraja</s> was resplendent, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, eager to narrate the tale, reflected within himself:

children.text: dhenu-cāraṇārambha-lambhaka-dine dhenukālambhaḥ khalu śrī-bādarāyaṇinā tadīya-cāraṇāvasara-sāmyānusāriṇā pūrvam eva varṇitaḥ | vastutas tu paugaṇḍa-prānta eva paṇḍayā nirṇītaḥ, tad-divasāvasāne veśma-praveśe kaiśorāṃśāveśa-varṇanāt | ataḥ śrī-parāśareṇāpi kāliya-damanānantar-āvasara eva so' yaṃ sāvasaraḥ kṛtaḥ | śrī-hari-vaṃśe ca spaṣṭam eva, damite sarparāje tu kṛṣṇena yamunā-hrade [2.13.1] ity uktvā dhenuka-vadhaḥ samārabdhaḥ | tad eva yuktyāpi vyaktī-bhavati | kārtika-vartamāna-śuklāṣṭamyāṃ gocāraṇārambha-sambhava-dinatayā pādme spaṣṭatayoktir dṛṣṭā | pakva-tāla-phala-kālo bhādra eva, tatra ca dhenuka-nirdhūnana-prasiddhiḥ | tasmāt kāliya-damanam eva prathamaṃ prathayiṣyāmaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: 'The seizure of <s>Dhenuka</s> on the day that marks the beginning of cow-herding was indeed described by the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva) first, following the chronological proximity to the occasion of cow-herding. But in reality, it is determined by the learned to be at the very end of the <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (pre-adolescent) period, since the description of the entry into <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence) occurs at the evening homecoming of that day. Therefore, even by the glorious <s>Parāśara</s> (Viṣṇu Purāṇa), this [Dhenuka episode] was placed at the occasion right after the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s>. And in the glorious <s>Hari-vaṃśa</s> too, it is clearly stated: "When the serpent-king was subdued by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the pool of the <s>Yamunā</s>" [2.13.1] — having said this, the slaying of <s>Dhenuka</s> is begun. This is also confirmed by reasoning. The day of the beginning of cow-herding being the bright <s>aṣṭamī</s> (eighth day) during the month of <s>Kārttika</s> is clearly stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>. The season of ripe palm-fruits is <s>Bhādrapada</s> itself, and in that [month] the renowned shaking-down of <s>Dhenuka</s> [occurs]. Therefore, we shall proclaim the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s> first.'

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ tv idam abhyācaṣṭa-
children.translated_text: He clearly declared:

children.text:
kavayo ye bhuvi khyātās ta evākavayo matāḥ |
  sukham āyāsyatīty evaṃ suduḥkhaṃ varṇayanty amī ||JGc_1,13.1|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Those poets who are renowned on earth are considered non-poets;
for these ones describe the most terrible suffering [simply] as "happiness will come!"' ||13.1|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: iti tūṣṇīkām āsajya punar āha sma: athavā-
children.translated_text: Having attached [himself to] silence, he spoke again: 'Or rather:'

children.text:
sukhaṃ vā vīryaṃ vā tad iha paramaṃ yat pratimukhaṃ
  pratīpaṃ nirjityānavaratam atulyaṃ vijayate |
  kaviś ca śreyān sa sphurati khalu yas tad-vidhatayā
  sadā tat tad gāyann api na paritas tṛpyatitarām ||JGc_1,13.2|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'That happiness or valor is supreme here which, conquering the opposing [force] head-on,
triumphs unceasingly and incomparably;
and that poet is the greater one who shines by fashioning it thus,
always singing of this and that, yet never becoming fully satiated!' ||13.2|| [śikhariṇī]

children.text: ataḥ kāliya-niryāpana-phalaṃ tad idaṃ vṛttam āpātataḥ suduḥsaham apy āyatyāṃ pratyāpta-bahula-sukha-sahacaratayā varṇanam evāsmābhir ākarṇanīyam eva ca yuṣmābhir iti yācitvā sa-kampam uvāca-
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, this event whose fruit is the expulsion of <s>Kāliya</s> — though at first glance most unbearable — is to be narrated by us and listened to by you, because of its companionship with abundant happiness obtained in the sequel.' Having thus entreated, he spoke with a trembling [voice]:

children.text: tad evam arjunīṣu paryāg eva cirāya cāryamāṇāsu pari kāliyālaya-jalāśayāśayam eva calituṃ khalu śrī-balarāmaḥ samanujñāṃ kalayāñcakre, śrī-vrajeśvaryāḥ śikṣita-caryānugamāt | śrī-balāvarajasya tu tasya cirata evāvirataṃ tad didṛkṣā na kṣīṇāsīt | [6] bahalena kutūhalena, janmata eva durjana-tejasām asahanatāyām avikalena tejasvitā-balena ca |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, while the cows were being tended in the area of the <s>Arjuna</s> trees for a long time as before, the glorious <s>Balarāma</s> made an agreement to move toward the pool that was the abode of <s>Kāliya</s>, following the conduct trained by the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s>. But the desire of the glorious younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) to see that [pool] had long been unceasing and undiminished. [6] With abundant curiosity, and with unimpaired power of valor born of an intolerance, from birth itself, for the might of the wicked.'

children.text:
tad evaṃ sthite sadāvad eva kadāpi kṛṣṇāgra-janmanaḥ śravaṇākhyaṃ māsikaṃ
janmarkṣam atithivat prathitiṃ vraja-sadasi samāsasāda | tadā ca saṅkarṣaṇaḥ sa khalu harṣaṇa-maṅgala-snapanādy-āsaṅgataḥ sva-gṛha eva saṅgata āsīt | [8] tadā ca kāsāñcanābhinavānāṃ gavām atipratyāsanna-prasavānām avaśyam eva svāvanīyatayā vināpi taṃ vanīm anugata-sakhaḥ śrīdāma-sakhaḥ prasthitavān | kintu sambhojana-samaya-samayane samayaṃ vidhāya tadā ca labdhe vipralabdher avasare tad-itaraṃ prati yaḥ kāla-kūṭa-tulyaḥ kāla-kūṭas tan-maya-kālindīya-kāliya-hrada-haritam eva tvaritaṃ hari-sudhā-vāridhir avajagāhe |
children.translated_text: This being so, once, as always, the monthly birth-<s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation) called <s>Śravaṇa</s> of the one born before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) arrived as a guest, as it were, in the assembly of <s>Vraja</s>. And then <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), being engaged in the joyous auspicious bathing and other [ceremonies], remained at home. [8] And then, since some newly acquired cows on the verge of calving necessarily needed his own tending, even without him (<s>Balarāma</s>), <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, friend of <s>Śrīdāmā</s>, accompanied by his friends, set out for the forest. However, having fixed a time for the mealtime rendezvous, and when the opportunity for mischief was obtained, he — the ocean of nectar of <s>Hari</s> — swiftly plunged into the green waters of the pool of <s>Kāliya</s> on the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), which were equal to the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) and filled with <s>Kālakūṭa</s>.

children.text: tatra gavām agresarā ye gopa-kumāra-varās, teṣu cānāśitaṅgavīna-navīna-vana-vibhāgāvakalana-kalita-bahala-kutūhala-jāta-rabhasataḥ kiñcid vilambam ālambamāneṣu nidāgha-drāghīyas tṛṣṇā-vyākulam agrima-gokulaṃ kāliya-viṣākulaṃ kṛṣṇā-jalaṃ pibati sma | pāna-mātrāc ca vicetanatayā nipapāta, kṣaṇatas te cāgre-sarās tad-avaloka-śoka-dharā deha-jihāsayā sahasā svayam api dhayantaḥ patanti sma | [10] iyaṃ punar yogamāyāyā evānapāyā gatiḥ, yā khalu khalānām utkalanāyāsambhavam api sambhāvayati |
children.translated_text: There, the foremost cowherd youths who led the cows — while they were slightly delayed due to the abundant curiosity arising from their assessment of the allotment of the fresh, unexplored forest sections with uneaten fresh grass — the leading group of <s>Gokula</s> [cows], tormented by thirst prolonged by the summer heat, drank the water of the <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) polluted by <s>Kāliya's</s> poison. And from merely drinking, they fell unconscious; and in a moment, those leading [boys], bearing the grief of seeing that, themselves too, wishing to abandon their bodies, drinking [the water] in haste, fell. [10] This, however, was indeed the unfailing course of <s>Yogamāyā</s>, who brings about even the impossible for the purpose of uprooting the wicked.

children.text: atha muhūrta-pūrtāv āgato' yaṃ toyada-śyāmala-mūrtir mūrtān eva tān paśyann anyādṛśa-śyāmalatām ājagāma, vilalāpa ca-
children.translated_text: Then, arriving at the completion of a <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), this one of cloud-dark form, seeing them in their embodied [but lifeless] state, arrived at a different kind of darkness (<s>śyāmalatā</s>), and lamented:

children.text:
yā gāvaḥ khalu devatā vrajasadām asmākam uccaistarāṃ
  ye bālāś ca sadaiva jīva-tulitās te' mī vipannāḥ puraḥ |
  hā hanta svayam asmi tat-sahacaraḥ kiṃ bhrātaraṃ mātaraṃ
  tātaṃ sarva-janaṃ ca vacmi mama dhik cāpalyataḥ sāhasam ||JGc_1,13.3|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
'Those cows who are indeed the supreme deities of us <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers,
and those boys who are always deemed equal to life itself — they have perished before me!
Alas, alas! I myself am their companion! What shall I say to brother, mother,
father, and all people? Shame on my reckless impulsiveness!' ||13.3|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: tataś ca vipratīsāra-sārānusārādruta-vidrutatara-cetasaḥ śrī-vraja-kula-candramasaḥ kramaśaḥ sarveṣāṃ mukham abhidatta-dṛśaḥ stimitī-kṛta-nijādharā netrāmbhu-dhārā nipetuḥ, yā evāṅkurī-kṛta-vasudhāḥ sudhāyamānā yathā-kramaṃ sarvaṃ cetayāmāsuḥ | kintu mura-śatruḥ puraḥ puraḥ-stha-gamanāveśād apuraḥ-stha-deśāśritānāṃ cetanāṃ tadā na ciceta, cirād eva tv acetīt |
children.translated_text: Then, as the mind of the moon of the <s>Vraja</s> clan became swifter and ever more swiftly melted, following the essence of deep remorse, he, directing his gaze gradually at each one's face, with his own lips made motionless, shed streams of tears from his eyes. These very [tears], having sprouted upon the earth, becoming nectar-like, gradually revived all of them. But the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), from his impetus of moving forward and forward, did not at that time notice the consciousness of those not stationed before him; only after a long while did he perceive it.

children.text: te ca cetitāḥ sarve cirāya vicāra-pracāraṃ nānucaranti sma, yasmād ātmānam agha-nāma-dhara-viṣadhara-viṣama-viṣa-mohād rakṣitavantam agha-dviṣam eva tatra tatra bhramantam anubhūya, bhūyaḥ sa eva cetanā-mūlam iti niścitavantaḥ |
children.translated_text: And all of them, having been revived, for a long time did not follow the course of deliberation, because, having experienced that the enemy of sin (<s>Agha-dviṣ</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who bore the name 'enemy of <s>Agha</s>,' had saved them from the terrible poison-delusion of the venomous serpent named <s>Agha</s>, and wandering here and there, they determined: 'He alone is the root of consciousness!'

children.text:
kṛṣṇas tu tān vilulitaveśān labdhopaveśān dṛṣṭvā yugapad eva sarvān kṛṣṭvā pṛthak pṛthag evāśliṣṭavān | [15] tad uktam eva yad asya khalv autpattika evāyam upapattim atītavān guṇaḥ, yad-bhāva-bhāvanaḥ syāt tatrānurūpa-rūpāvirbhāvanam asau yaugapadyam upasadya, bahutrāpi sadya evāpadyate iti |
[16] tatra bālair milanaṃ, yathā,
  dṛṣṭir bāṣpam itā tanuḥ stimitatām antarmatir līnatām
  itthaṃ saṅgati-sādhane tu nikhile' bhīkṣṇaṃ gate vyarthatām |
  kiṃ saukhyaṃ kim asaukhyam etad iti ca sphūrtiṃ vināvasthitau
  kañcit ko' pi na kiñcid ujjhitum abhūc chakti-prayuktaś ciram ||JGc_1,13.4|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seeing them with their garments disheveled and having found their seats, drew all of them at once and embraced each one individually. [15] It was indeed stated that this is his innately natural quality that has surpassed [all] demonstration: that he who would evoke a particular <s>bhāva</s> (sentiment), in that [context] manifests a form befitting it, and by simultaneously attaining [multiple forms], even among many, he accomplishes [this] at once.
[16] There, the meeting with the boys, as follows:
Their gazes had gone to tears, their bodies to stillness, their inner minds to absorption;
thus, when every means of achieving union had repeatedly gone to futility,
remaining in a state without awareness of 'is this happiness or unhappiness?' —
no one was able to abandon anyone for even a moment, bound by [the Lord's] power! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: gobhir yathā-
children.translated_text: With the cows, as follows:

children.text:
gāvo huṅkṛti-ghoṣaṇā valayitāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ lihantyaś cirāt
  tad-bāhu-dvaya-veṣṭanena vilasat-kaṇṭhyaḥ samutkaṇṭhitāḥ |
  yatnāt tyājita-tad-grahāś ca paśupaiḥ kṣiptāś ca tasthuś ciram
  tās tad-vaktra-sudhākara-dyuti-sudhā-pītāvatṛptekṣaṇāḥ ||JGc_1,13.5|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
The cows, surrounded and lowing with bellowing sounds, licking <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> for a long time,
their necks gleaming by the encirclement of his two arms, were filled with longing;
forcibly released from their grasp by the cowherds and pushed away, they stood for a long time,
their eyes unsatiated, drinking the nectar of the moonlight-radiance of his face! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: tad evaṃ sati tasya bhāva-viśeṣodbhavaḥ samudbhāvyate | pūrvam evāyaṃ śrī-yuta-kṛṣṇaḥ pārāvāra-bhaviṣṇu-sthāsnu-cariṣṇu-duḥkha-dāna-dhṛṣṇoḥ kṛṣṇādhiṣṇyasya kāliyasya nirākariṣṇu-tṛṣṇo' pi, tat-patnībhyo' patrapiṣṇutayā cirāya tūṣṇīṃ babhūva | samprati tu go-gopāla-kāla-dharmāpāta-jātāsahiṣṇutayā vardhiṣṇu-krodhaḥ suṣṭhu jātaḥ |
children.translated_text: This being so, the arising of a special sentiment in him is now shown. Previously, this glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though desirous of subduing <s>Kāliya</s> — whose abode was dark, who was bold in giving suffering to all that was to be, to be established, and to be in motion across the ocean — had remained silent for a long time, out of bashfulness before <s>Kāliya's</s> wives. But now, by the intolerance born of the onset of the law of death upon the cows and cowherds, his wrath grew mighty and well-formed.

children.text: tataś ca sāvahittham ittham uvāca-aho, vayasyāḥ! paśyatha atrodaka-stambha-vidyā-kṛtāvakāśa-prakāśamāna-hradinī-hrada-sthita-sva-sadane kāliyākhya-manda-dandaśūkas tiṣṭhati | tena ca duṣṭa-niṣṭhyūtayā sarva evākharva-viṣa-jvālayā jvalitāḥ paryag-deśā dṛśyante | upary apy utpātitāḥ patatriṇaś cātra patitā ity ātma-netrābhyāṃ pratīyatām, yebhyas tu prāṇā jagat-prāṇāśana-bhayataḥ sadya eva vipratipadyeva svayam utpatantaḥ kadāpi na nyavartanta | so' yaṃ punar garutmat-kṛtāmṛta-seka eka eva kāla-kuṭa-jvālayāpi kṛtālambaḥ kadambaḥ sulalita-dalāditayā lālasīti | tasmād asyopariga-koṭara-piṭhare sphuṭaṃ tad anavadyam amṛtam adyāpi vidyata iti prasahyāham āruhya paśyāni | bhavantas tu gāḥ kiñcid dūracaratayā cārayantaś carantu |
children.translated_text: Then he spoke with careful attention thus: 'Ah, friends! Look — in the pool of this river, where a space has been made manifest by the art of water-petrification, in his own abode situated there, dwells a sluggish serpent named <s>Kāliya</s>. By his wicked spitting, all the surrounding regions are seen ablaze with immense, undiminished poison-flames. Even the birds flying above have fallen here, struck down — let this be perceived with your own eyes! As for those whose life-breaths, out of fear of the world-breath-devourer, abruptly departing of their own accord and flying upward, never returned. But this one <s>kadamba</s> tree alone, sprinkled with the nectar produced by <s>Garuḍa</s>, though supported even by the flame of <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison, is flourishing with tender leaves and such. Therefore, in the hollow-vessel atop this tree, that faultless nectar clearly still exists; so I shall forcefully climb up and see! And you, graze the cows by leading them to graze a little farther away!'

children.text: tad etad vadan vigata-kadanaḥ kañja-vadanaḥ kadambam adhiruhya parikaraṃ samūhya, svayaṃ kiraṇa-gaṇāmṛta-ghanāghanaḥ sānnidhya-mātra-nirmita-sādharmye tasmin kāliya-harmye nirmala-jala-krīḍā-kutukāya papāta-
children.translated_text: Having said this, he of the lotus-face, free of distress, climbed the <s>kadamba</s> tree and, gathering his waistband, himself a dense cloud of nectar composed of ray-clusters — plunging for the sport of playing in the pure water upon whose mere proximity the semblance of identity [with the tree] was created — he leaped into that <s>Kāliya</s>-palace, the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>)!

children.text: yatra ca tatra sarpa-hrada-gata-jalaṃ dhanuḥ-śatam udasarpat | tac ca śrī-vrajarāja-tapaḥ-pratāpa-phalasya saṅkhyātīta-balasya tasya na citram ity eva mantavyam, yena hi paugaṇḍatayā nātipracaṇḍam api tad eva tad-vapuś caṇḍāṃśu-koṭivad atīvoddaṇḍatayā tatra kuṇḍalīnāṃ bhāti sma | tataś ca tasyāmara-vāraṇa vāraṇa-vikrama-kramatayā ghūrṇad-bhujāpūrṇa-vār-ghoṣaṇa-saṅgharṣaṇayā gharṣitas tad-utkarṣāsahana-samājaḥ sahasā tanūnapān-mahasāhi-rājaḥ svīya-līlāntarīpāntaḥ svayaṃ krīḍā-harṣataḥ smitaṃ varṣantaṃ pītāṃśuka-vidyudbharaṃ kara-caraṇādhara-rohitākaraṃ vanamālā-śacīpati-cāpa-dharaṃ sulalita-nīla-ghana-varaṃ tam evāsasāda |
children.translated_text: And there, the water of the serpent-pool rose up a hundred bow-lengths! And that should be understood as not at all wondrous, for he was the fruit of the glory of the austerities of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, possessed of incalculable strength — for even though, being in the <s>paugaṇḍa</s> age, that very body of his was not excessively fierce, like tens of millions of suns it blazed with supreme loftiness among those coiled ones there! Then, by his striding with the vigor of a celestial elephant's step, the grinding produced by the churning of the water filling his arms with roaring sound — ground down, the assembly unable to bear his superiority — the great serpent-king, son of <s>Tanūnapāt</s> (<s>Agni</s>), himself sporting within his own play-island, showering a smile from the delight of play, bearing a yellow garment like lightning, a mine of redness in his hands, feet, and lips, wearing the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest garland) [like] the bow of <s>Indra</s>'s wife, that supreme beautiful dark cloud — he himself approached him.

children.text: samprati tu kṛta-yava-kṣāra-sāra-sandha-gandhakendhana-vahnīyamānam etam ātmanā cachāda nanāda ca | kevala-bali-mānitāmayāsahiṣṇutayā dhṛṣṇag asau nāga-jiṣṇur ārto' pi na nivartate sma |
children.translated_text: Now, being inflamed like a fire fueled with barley-alkite, resinous sandalwood, and sulfur, he covered him with his own [coils] and roared. Solely through the intolerance of being honored by mere offerings, that vanquisher of serpents, though afflicted, boldly did not retreat.

children.text:
atha kāliyasya varuṇa-pāśapāśīyamānābhogāśaya-nīyamānāśī-rāśībhyāṃ yāhaṅkṛtis tasyāś cūrṇī-kṛti-kautukāya yogamāyā-maya-kaṅkaṭa-saṅghaṭitāṅgatāṅgatas tṛṇāvarta-vartana-samudvartanaḥ sa muhūrtaṃ tathaiva vartate sma, yatra hi tasya sad-ahitasya bhoginaḥ śatam ekātirekābhogā markaṭikā-jālavad vighaṭita-śaktayaḥ santi sma | āśiṣaś ca tūla-varti-tulāṃ kalayāmāsuḥ |
[24] kintu yadā kadambād asau kadamba-mālī kāliyālaya-kālindī-śambaram apaptat tadātitapta-hṛdayatayā hāhā-kāra-kṛta-mithaḥ-kreṅkāraḥ sa khinnaḥ sakhi-vāraḥ skhalac-caraṇa-cāraḥ sahasā tasminn eva sasāra | [25] gāvaś ca śāva-sahitāḥ sahitās tam evānudrāvakatām avāpuḥ |
children.translated_text:
Then, as <s>Kāliya's</s> hoods — their coils being led by [his] binding like the nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s> — and the mass of fangs were brought to bear with pride, for the sport of pulverizing that pride, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], his limbs clad in armor made of <s>Yogamāyā</s>, [performing] the rotation of the <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>-like whirling, remained thus for a moment — where indeed a hundred of that evil serpent's hoods, each exceeding the next in [their] coiling expanse, had their powers dismantled like a net of puppet-strings. And his fangs attained the weight of cotton-wicks.
[24] But when that wearer of the <s>kadamba</s> garland fell from the <s>kadamba</s> tree into the <s>Kālindī</s> which was <s>Kāliya's</s> abode, the host of friends, their hearts extremely scorched, making mutual 'hāhā' cries mingled with wailing, distressed, stumbling in their steps, suddenly rushed toward that very [pool]. [25] And the cows too, together with their young, unitedly attained the state of running toward him.

children.text: tataś ca sveṣu viśveṣu tam eva hradaṃ sāvega-gadaṃ prāviśatsu pratidiśaṃ gāvaś ca praviśantīty evaṃ dṛṣṭvā parama-kaṣṭaṃ spṛṣṭvānupāyāḥ paśupāḥ naṣṭa-prāyā bhraṣṭa-kāyā, yamunāyāḥ prahvā iva kahvāsura-jaṭharād iva tat-pratyāgaty-āśayā paraṃ prāṇanti sma | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then, as all his own people entered that very pool with anxious agitation, and seeing the cows also entering, the cowherds — having touched the utmost extremity of distress, resourceless, nearly destroyed, their bodies fallen — bowed as if to the <s>Yamunā</s>, as if from the belly of a whale-demon, breathing only in the hope of his return from there. And there:

children.text:
kiṃ jñaptiḥ svapanaṃ suṣuptir athavā mūrcchā mṛtir jīvanaṃ
  bhāty evaṃ nahi niścikāya nikhilaḥ so' yaṃ sakhīnāṃ gaṇaḥ |
  usrāṇāṃ tatir asra-vṛṣṭi-kalitaiḥ sā ca pravāhaiḥ punas
  tarhy eṣāṃ hṛdayaṃ hradaṃ ca tam atha kṣveḍair ivāpūpurat ||JGc_1,13.6|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
'Is it waking, sleep, deep-sleep, or else fainting, death, or life?' —
Thus this entire group of friends could not determine at all;
and the row of cows, with streams mingled with tear-showers —
then they filled that pool and their hearts, as if with [poison's] hissing! // [sragdharā]

children.text: teṣu ca bahir īdṛg-avastheṣu tathāntar anavastheṣu na ko' pi prakopi tad-vṛttaṃ vraje vṛttaṃ kuryād iti vicārya diviṣad-varya-vrajena muhur utpāta-vrātaṃ pratyāpayya tam anusañcāryate sma |
children.translated_text: While they were in such a state externally and internally unsettled, [<s>Balarāma</s>], reflecting that no one in such agitation should report what had happened to <s>Vraja</s>, was being guided along by the foremost host of celestials who repeatedly dispelled the shower of portents.

children.text: tatra vraja-prajā-vacanaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: The words of the people of <s>Vraja</s> there, as follows:

children.text:
divi bhuvi khe cotpātāḥ katham iva tat-kālam udbhūtāḥ |
  āṃ naḥ sarveṣāṃ yaḥ prāṇeṣv adhi tat-kṛte ta ime ||JGc_1,13.7|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'How have portents arisen at this very time, in heaven, on earth, and in the sky?
Ah — they are on account of him who is over and above the life-breaths of all of us!' // [upagīti]

children.text: iti vyagrī-bhūya samagrāḥ prajāḥ sa-grāmaṇyas taṃ vrajāgra-gaṇya-samājaṃ kṛṣṇāgra-janma-janmarkṣa-mahasi sambhojanāya janāyatanatām āptavatyaḥ, kiṃ bahunā, vraja-mahī-pati-patnī ca vraja-mahilābhir apatrapām apahāya tatrājighāya | sandideśa dūra-deśataḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, becoming agitated like tigresses, all the people together with the village headmen — having come to that assembly foremost in <s>Vraja</s>, which had gathered for the celebratory feast of the birthday great-festival of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> first birth-constellation — in short, the wife of the king of <s>Vraja</s> too, abandoning all shame before the <s>Vraja</s>-women, hastened there. She sent word from afar:

children.text:
durnimittam udabhūd balaṃ vinā
  hā yayau viṣa-diśaṃ balānujaḥ |
  hanta pūrṇa-samayaḥ sa nāyayau
  goṣṭha-rāṭ katham ihāsti nirvṛtaḥ? ||JGc_1,13.8|| [svāgatā] iti |
children.translated_text:
'An evil omen arose when <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) was absent —
alas, the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> has gone toward the poison-direction!
Alas, the appointed time has passed and he has not returned —
how can the king of the cow-settlement be at peace here?' // [svāgatā]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  dehaṃ gehaṃ tat tad arthaṃ ca sarvaṃ
  dhik-kurvantas tyakta-tat-parva-bhogāḥ |
  te gacchantaḥ kāliyānaccha-kacchaṃ
  vāta-vrāta-kṣipta-cittā ivāsthuḥ ||JGc_1,13.9|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Cursing body, home, and every possession,
having abandoned the enjoyment of that festival,
they, going toward the murky bank of <s>Kāliya</s>,
stood as if their minds were scattered by hosts of wind!' // [śālinī]

children.text: bhrātṛ-prabhāva-jñānārāmaḥ śrī-rāmas tu teṣāṃ śaṅkāyām aniśām ayann api na tadānīṃ tad-bhāvam avāpa, kintu rirakṣiṣām eva | anyathā hy anyathāpattir eva syād iti samucita eva bhāvaḥ svayam eva yogamāyayācitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Rāma</s>, the garden of knowledge of his brother's power, though he accompanied them in their apprehension continuously, did not then attain that [same] state, but rather [aimed] only to protect them. For otherwise, there would be only a different outcome — and the appropriate sentiment was itself solicited by <s>Yogamāyā</s>.

children.text:
atha sva-manasy evaṃ sa viviveca, vayam idaṃ muhur unnīya niyamata eva jānīmaḥ, yat khalu tasya khala-vaṃśadavahuta-vahasya nirasyamānatā na kenāpy akenāpi kartuṃ śakyate | tathāpy ete kevala-sneha-bala-dehā vidyut-pātāyamāna-durnimitta-labdha-jīvana-sandehā nija-jīvana-mūlaṃ pīta-dukūlaṃ prati gamanāya durmadehā vartante | tasmād araṇyāraṇyaṅgaja-dahana-sandahana-sahanatāmanda-samuddiṣṭa-hima-drava-sandrava-samutkaṭatā-galat-kaṭa-vāraṇa-durgaṇa-gaṇavad āpātatas tu mama vāraṇam api na maṃsyate | yat khalv eteṣāṃ tad-viśleṣātiśaya-śaṅkitā-duḥkham anu mayy api duḥkhaṃ duḥkhanana-mūlaṃ jātam asti, tad api na vyañjanāya prāñjalatām arhati, prajvalita-jvalana-vanam anu jvalanāntara-santānanavat | tasmāt
kevala-maṅgala-vyaṅga-vyaṅga-saṅgami-sad-iṅgita-viśeṣa-saṅgitayā ta ete sambhāvita-tad-bhavyā bhāvanīyā, na tu nirākariṣṇutayā | āvayor āvayo hy eka-prāṇatāṃ khalv ete manyante iti |
children.translated_text: Then he deliberated thus within his own mind: 'We, having repeatedly elevated and regulated this matter, know this well — that the irremovability of that one, who has a lineage like a forest-fire burning consumed oblations, cannot be accomplished by anyone whatsoever. Nevertheless, these people, whose bodies are composed solely of the strength of love, whose lives are in doubt due to lightning-fall-like evil portents, are resolved to go toward the one who is the root of their lives, clad in a yellow garment, foolish [with love]. Therefore, my restraint of them will not even be considered at first appearance — like an elephant herd with streaming rut, ungovernable, against which [even] the endurance of the melting of slow Himalayan ice, the fire-burning of a forest fire [is unavailing]. Indeed the suffering that has arisen in me too, following their apprehension of extreme separation from him, is a root of torment, and that too does not deserve clarity of expression — like a fire within a fire amidst a blazing forest-fire. Therefore, these people should be consoled with special auspicious gestures and tokens of purely auspicious import — with the sentiment of esteeming his future [triumph] — and not with dismissive [words]. For these people consider us two to have but one life-breath.'

children.text: atha sa evaṃ vivicya sahasā jahāsa | tad anu kiñcil-labdhāśvāsatayā calantaś ca te-
children.translated_text: Then, having thus deliberated, he suddenly laughed. And following that, they, having gained a little reassurance, moved forward —

children.text:
duḥkhāghrāta-prādhvatā-manda-netrāḥ
  kṛṣṇāṅghri-śrī-lakṣma-labdhāvalokāḥ |
  vartmany asmin picchile' py aśrubhis te
  rāma-prāpta-nyasta-hastā viceluḥ ||JGc_1,13.10|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
With eyes made sluggish, their swiftness dulled by the scent of grief,
having gained sight of the auspicious mark of the beauty of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> feet [on the path],
on this slippery road [made so] by their tears, they,
placing their hands upon <s>Rāma</s> [for support], tottered! // [śālinī]

children.text:
yathā yathā vidadhur atīva śīghratāṃ
  tathā tathāpy adadhur alaṃ vilambitām |
  kathaṃ kathañcana bata taṃ hradaṃ gatā
  daśāṃ tu kāṃ samadhur amī na vedmi tām ||JGc_1,13.11|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
The more they tried to move with utmost speed,
the more they achieved only delay;
having somehow, alas, reached that pool,
what state they attained — I do not know! // [rucirā]

children.text:
tatra tu-
  dṛṣṭvā kāliya-bhoga-saṅgha-valitaṃ gopālakaṃ gopakā
  nandādyā bata gopikāś ca vidalac-cittā yaśodā-mukhāḥ |
  hā śuṣkāṅga-daśāṃ mahā-malinatām apy ūhur itthaṃ yathā
  teṣām āntara-vahninaiṣi bahir apy udyātum ity ūhyate ||JGc_1,13.12|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And there:
Seeing the cowherd-protector wrapped in the mass of <s>Kāliya's</s> coils, the cowherds,
<s>Nanda</s> and others — alas! — and the cowherd-women led by <s>Yaśodā</s>, their hearts splitting —
alas, they attained a state of withered limbs and extreme defilement, such that
it is surmised: their inner fire was attempting to burst forth externally! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
mānuṣān buddhi-rāhityāt paśūn iva nirīkṣya te |
  paśūṃś ca krandanān mānuṣān iva kleśam aiyaruḥ ||JGc_1,13.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Seeing the humans, bereft of intelligence, like animals, and
the animals, by their lamentations, like humans — they attained [equal] distress! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  teṣāṃ sadā snehamayātmanāṃ tadā
  trāsāt tu śuṣkī-bhavatāṃ himād iva |
  mithaḥ-samīkṣā-bhavatāpasaṅgamād
  bhūyo babhūva dravatā raver iva ||JGc_1,13.14|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
And then:
Of those whose nature was always composed of love, then,
drying up from fear as if from frost,
by the non-contact that arose from mutual gazing,
the melting increased further, as if from the sun's [heat]! // [upajāti]

children.text:
snehāt pravāhāvali-tulyatāṃ yatāṃ
  vrajaukasāṃ drāg viśatāṃ viṣa-hradam |
  bālo' py athāveśa-valad-balo balo
  drutaṃ mahā-setu-daśāṃ sasāda saḥ ||JGc_1,13.15|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
As the stream-like flow of the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers, swept by love,
swiftly entering the poison-pool —
even the boy <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), though young, with strength surging through possession,
quickly assumed the state of a great dam! // [upajāti]

children.text: uvāca ca-
children.translated_text: And he spoke:

children.text:
prītiḥ kiṃ nv anuje na me? vraja-pate tāta vrajādhīśvari
  śrī-rohiṇy api mātar, asya tu sadā tattvaṃ paraṃ vedmy aham |
  satyaṃ vaḥ pada-paṅkajāśraya-rucāṃ kuryām amuṣya kvacin
  naikasminn api mūrdhaje kṣati-lavo bhāvī yathā garga-gīḥ ||JGc_1,13.16|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'Is there no affection in me for my younger brother? O king of <s>Vraja</s>, dear father! O queen of <s>Vraja</s>!
O glorious <s>Rohiṇī</s>, mother too! But I always know his supreme truth!
Truly, by the beauty of those who take shelter at your lotus feet, I would ensure
that not even a single hair of his shall ever suffer the slightest harm — as <s>Garga's</s> words [foretold]!' // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: tad evaṃ praśastena sva-hastena śrī-rāmeṇa hasta-vāraṇe kṛte-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the restraining hand was placed by the glorious <s>Rāma</s> with his praiseworthy hand —

children.text:
viṣa-hradāntād vinivartitāś ca te
  pratīyur evādhi tad-ātmanaḥ sthitim |
  yat kāla-kūṭa-jvalanāntaraṅgataṃ
  svaṃ menire vīkṣya tad-antare harim ||JGc_1,13.17|| [upajāti 12]

kāliya-hradam ite baka-śatrau
  gokulasya rudataḥ pratiśabdāt |
  rodasī ca rudatī sva-niruktiṃ
  bāḍham ajñapayatāṃ rudasijbhyām ||JGc_1,13.18|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: 'When the enemy of <s>Baka</s> went to <s>Kāliya's</s> pool, | from the echo of <s>Gokula's</s> weeping, | heaven and earth too, weeping, clearly proclaimed | their own etymology from the root "rud" (to weep)!' || (JGc 1,13.18) [svāgatā]

children.text:
gopyo mithaḥ kaṇṭha-vilagna-kaṇṭhās
tā rorudāmāsur alaṃ vilapya |
  smṛtiṃ nayat pūtanikādi-nāśaṃ
yan mātṛ-santvāya muhur babhūva ||JGc_1,13.19|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: 'The <s>gopīs</s>, their throats clasped to one another's throats, | wept profusely, lamenting much; | they recalled the destruction of <s>Pūtanā</s> and others, | which repeatedly served to console the mother.' || (JGc 1,13.19) [indravajrā]

children.text:
evaṃ sva-goṣṭham ahiveṣṭa-vivikṣu vīkṣya
  sastrī-kumāram atiduḥkhitam ātma-hetoḥ |
  kṛṣṇaḥ saroṣa-vitatāṅgatayā tad aṅgaṃ
  chindan ślathaṃ vidadhad āśu balād udasthāt ||JGc_1,13.20|| [vasantatilaka]
children.translated_text: 'Thus, seeing his own cow-settlement — with its women and children — exceedingly distressed on his account, as if embraced by the serpent, | <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with body fiercely extended in anger, severing those coils, | loosening them, swiftly rose up by force!' || (JGc 1,13.20) [vasantatilakā]

children.text: tad evaṃ kṛṣṇasyotthānam eva kāliyasya vyutthānaṃ jātam iti sarvo' pi jaharṣa | yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, the very rising of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> became the overthrow of <s>Kāliya</s> — and everyone rejoiced. As follows:

children.text:
tadā mudā kalakala-garjitair jitaṃ
  vrajaukasāṃ śiśu-savayo-jarā-juṣām |
  divaukasāṃ kusumaja-vṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-yug-
  jaya-dhvani-dhvani-yuta-tūrya-laṅghibhiḥ ||JGc_1,13.21|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: 'Then, with joyful tumultuous roars, the dwellers of <s>Vraja</s> — young, middle-aged, and old — | prevailed, [their sounds] joined with the victory-cries of the celestials, | accompanied by showers of flowers and the beating of instruments!' || (JGc 1,13.21) [rucirā]

children.text: tataś ca samuttejita-tat-tejobhir udvejita-cittaḥ kuṇṭhatāvaguṇṭhitotkaṇṭhatayā dūrata evotkaṇṭhatayātiṣṭhan mūḍha-dhīr asau gūḍha-pāt prarūḍha-krodhaḥ svabodha-rodhatas taṃ pratidrogdhum udyataḥ sann, uddhata-buddhis thūtkāra-phutkāra-dṛṣṭi-vāra-kṛta-kūṭaṃ kālakūṭaṃ prakaṭī-kurvan girikūṭāyamānaḥ kartavya-vihvalatayā jihvā-dvaya-samudayena muhuḥ kṣveḍa-bāḍava-pakvaṃ sṛkvaṇī-dvaya-samudaya-lehanād dvijihva-lelihānādy-āhvayo' smīty uṭṭaṅkanena ghaṭayitu-kāmaḥ sarvato dṛṣṭa-vapur babhūva |
children.translated_text: Then that one [<s>Kāliya</s>], his mind agitated by the stirred-up radiance [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], standing far off with eagerness veiled by shame, his intellect bewildered, his deep-rooted anger swelling from the obstruction of his own understanding — ready to strike back against him — with arrogant mind, making manifest the deadly poison (<s>kālakūṭa</s>), fashioned into a peak of fraud through hissing, spitting, and volleys of glances, appearing mountain-like, with the rising of his two tongues churning repeatedly the submarine-fire-cooked hissing-sounds by licking both corners of his mouth, wishing to establish [his supremacy] by the stamp 'I am the one called the licking forked-tongue!' — he became visible on all sides in his full body.

children.text: tataś cākhaṇḍāhi-tuṇḍika-vidyā-paṇḍitavad uccaṇḍatayā sakaṇṭha-tuṇḍāvaguṇṭhanāya sa-darpam abhitaḥ sarpati sarpāśana-vāhane, sarpo' yam api śirobhiḥ kṛta-parisarpaḥ sarpavad evāpasarpann upasarpaṃś ca jihmagavad eva jihmaṃ gacchaṃś ca parito babhrāma śaśrāma ca |
children.translated_text: Then, as if an expert snake-charmer dealing with a whole serpent, with fierce audacity rushing to envelop his (<s>Kāliya's</s>) throat and snout, he — mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, the serpent-devourer — moved proudly. And that serpent too, crawling with his heads, slithering like a snake, retreating and advancing, moving crookedly like an oblique animal, wandered about on all sides and became exhausted.

children.text: tad evam ahīnam ahinaṃ prati sāṃyugīnatārato' pi cirato labdha-cchidratayābhidravann eva tadīya-samagra-grīvāgra-gaṇya-mūla-nālam eva balānujanmā balād avajagrāha nijagrāha ca |
children.translated_text: Thus, charging at that vile serpent [who was] inferior [in strength], having found an opening through persistence, the one born alongside strength (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) forcefully seized and restrained the very root-stem of the foremost neck-array of that serpent.

children.text:
tataś ca vivaśāṅga-saṅghe tasminn uraṅgame tu,
  udyad-ratna-citeṣu puṣṭa-niṭila-prastheṣu raṅga-śriyā
  śasteṣu sphuṭa-nṛtya-kṛtya-kalanā-lobhena śobhekṣaṇaḥ |
  dyo-vidyotana-vādya-gīta-kalayā saṃhāya sāhāyakaṃ
  śrī-kṛṣṇas tad upary udapluta mudām uccair udāra-cchaviḥ ||JGc_1,13.22|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
Then, when that serpent lay with limbs rendered helpless:
'Upon those jewel-studded, well-fed, broad hoods — which by the beauty of their arena | were commended and inviting for the undertaking of conspicuous dance — | the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of splendid beauty, summoning the assistance | of heavenly illumination, instrumental music, and song, leaped high upon them with great joy!' || (JGc 1,13.22) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  punar vrajaḥ sphuṭa-sukha-vismayārava-
  plava-śriyāspṛśad amara-vrajaṃ divi |
  asau ca taṃ bhuvi bata yatra cobhayoḥ
  pratidhvani-dhvani-vibhidā na tarkitā ||JGc_1,13.23|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Again, <s>Vraja</s>, with the splendor of its cascade of joyful, wondrous clamor, | touched the host of celestials in heaven; | and they [touched] it on earth — indeed, where between the two | the distinction of echo and sound was not discerned!' || (JGc 1,13.23) [rucirā]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  śaśvad garvada-parva-śarva-ḍamaru-svar-vādya-sarvādyatāṃ
  vindan kuṇḍali-daṇḍanāya rabhasād uddaṇḍa-sat-tāṇḍavaḥ |
  ārād ūrdhvitam ūrdhvitaṃ bhujaga-rāḍ-mūrdhānam unmardayan
  krodhād rodha-kutuhalād dharir ihānarte nanarta sphuṭam ||JGc_1,13.24|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
atha-
  jayaj-jaya-jayāravāḥ kusuma-vṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-prathāḥ
  sphurat-pulaka-pālayaḥ prathita-śarma-gharmāśravaḥ |
  bhujaṅga-śirasī-śitus tad-anukṛtya-nṛtyaṃ surā
  bhavāmbuja-bhavādayaḥ pramada-garjam ārjan muhuḥ ||JGc_1,13.25|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Finding a supreme precedence in all the music — the heavenly instruments including the <s>ḍamaru</s> of <s>Śarva</s> (Śiva), which always bestows pride at festivals — | with a violent, magnificent <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance for the punishment of the hooded one, | pressing down again and again from afar the upraised heads of the serpent-king, | <s>Hari</s> here danced — clearly danced — out of anger, out of the curiosity of restraint!' || (JGc 1,13.24) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
Then:
'Victorious victory-cries, displays of flower-showers, | shining horripilation, famous streams of joy-sweat — | imitating his dance on the serpent's hoods, the gods — | <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born, and others — repeatedly produced roars of delight!' || (JGc 1,13.25) [pṛthvī]

children.text:
sarpasyānana-jāla-kūṭa-ghaṭanād utthānam ātmāyuṣā,
  nirmañchyāgra-nakhasya tasya naṭanaṃ tan-mūrdhni cātyadbhutam |
  dṛṣṭvā śrī-vraja-rāja-tat-praṇayinī-mukhyā vraja-prāṇino
  netraṃ gātram api praphullam abhajan manye jagad-vyāptaye ||JGc_1,13.26|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the rising from the array of that serpent's mouth-cluster by his own life-force, | and his wondrous dance on those hoods, [performed] with the tips of his nails scraped [against them], | the chief consorts of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> and all the life-beings of <s>Vraja</s> | bloomed in their eyes and bodies — I believe, for pervading the world!' || (JGc 1,13.26) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
mūrdha-śreṇyāṃ tasya śūnye ca kṛṣṇe
  nṛtyaṃ kurvāṇe tu citraṃ tadāsīt |
  tena krodhān mastakaṃ yady udastaṃ
  tatrānena prāpitā tāla-lattā ||JGc_1,13.27|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was dancing on the row of hoods and an empty one [appeared], | a wonder occurred: | if a head was raised out of anger by him [<s>Kāliya</s>], | upon that one, he [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] delivered a rhythmic beat!' || (JGc 1,13.27) [śālinī]

children.text:
mukhai rudiram udvaman garalam udgirann akṣibhiḥ
  skhalan-maṇika-mastaka-sthita-tad-aṅghri-cihna-vraṇaḥ |
  ślathāṅgakatayājahad anuja-saṅghajid-raṅgatāṃ
  vyālokyata nijāṅganāvalibhir eṣa kālīyakaḥ ||JGc_1,13.28|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text: 'Vomiting blood from his mouths, spewing poison from his eyes, | with falling jewels and wounds from the imprint of those feet on his heads, | with limbs gone slack, he abandoned his contest with the younger brother's conqueror — | this <s>Kāliya</s> was beheld by his own row of wives.' || (JGc 1,13.28) [pṛthvī]

children.text: tataś cāsāv upaskīrṇa-vikīrṇa-mūrtyā sva-pauruṣāpūrtyānanya-gatitāsphūrtyā tat-kāraṇa-kakāraṇā-nivāraṇāya taṃ nārāyaṇam eva matvā śaraṇam amanyata |
children.translated_text: Then that one, his body scattered and shattered, through the incompleteness of his own prowess and the flashing of having no other refuge, considering that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone as his shelter for averting the cause of his calamity, accepted [Him] as his refuge.

children.text: tad-aṅganānāṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And of his wives:

children.text:
na tāvad ārdratvam abhūd amūṣāṃ
  bahirmukhatvaṃ yad abodhy amuṣya |
  dṛṣṭe tu bhakty-aṅkura-janmani sphuṭaṃ
  kṛṣṇaṃ gatiṃ jagmur amūs tad-artham ||JGc_1,13.29|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text: 'Those [wives] had no tenderness [toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] so long | as his (<s>Kāliya's</s>) hostility was perceived; | but when the sprout of devotion was clearly seen, | they went to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as their refuge, for his sake.' || (JGc 1,13.29) [upajāti]

children.text:
kāścit kumārān atyartha-bālān kāścana tāś tadā |
  kāścid aṇḍāni puratas tasya nyasya vyanaṃsiṣuḥ ||JGc_1,13.30|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Some [placed before Him] their very young children, some their eggs, | placing them in front of Him, and bowed down.' || (JGc 1,13.30) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
hasati ca bhakta-sāntvana-tṛṣṇe kṛṣṇe, tās tu bahudhā stava-budhā mṛdākulāḥ pṛdāku-patnyaḥ sakāku vijñāpayāmāsa | tatra saṅkṣepa-nikṣepaś cāyam-
  asty eṣa sphurada-matiḥ sadarpa-sarpas
  tvaṃ viṣvag-vid asi tathā kṛpāmburāśiḥ |
  asmāsu tvad-anugatāsv amuṣya patnī-
  bhāvaś ced ajani yathā-yathaṃ vidhehi ||JGc_1,13.31|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text:
And when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who thirsts for consoling his devotees, laughed, those serpent-wives — well-versed in hymns, distressed with gentleness, trembling — petitioned him. Here is the summary of their deposit:
'This serpent indeed is of manifest intelligence and possessed of pride; | You are the all-knowing one and an ocean of compassion; | toward us who follow You, if his status as husband | has arisen, then dispose [of the matter] as is fitting!' || (JGc 1,13.31) [praharṣiṇī]

children.text:
daṇḍaṃ te vidadhatu ye sva-saṅga-mātrād
  duṣṭatvaṃ praśamayituṃ na śaknuvanti |
  tvat-sparśāj jhaṭiti hrado' pi so' yam aujjhat
  kṣveḍatvaṃ balavad atīha naḥ samakṣam ||JGc_1,13.32|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text: 'Let those who cannot pacify wickedness by mere contact alone | punish him [instead]; | by Your touch, even this very pool has suddenly abandoned | its venomous nature, powerfully, before our very eyes!' || (JGc 1,13.32) [praharṣiṇī]

children.text:
mūrkhatvaṃ na idam anugrahe' pi yasmāt
  tvat-spṛṣṭe sphuṭam iha bhāti daṇḍa-buddhiḥ |
  daṇḍaś ced amum aparair adaṇḍayiṣyas
  taṃ kartuṃ katham adadhāḥ padāravindam? ||JGc_1,13.33|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text: 'This is not stupidity on our part, since even in [what appears as] grace, | the perception of punishment is clearly evident here; | if the punishment — which no others could inflict upon him — | were not [Your purpose], then why would You have placed Your lotus-foot [upon his hood]?' || (JGc 1,13.33) [praharṣiṇī]

children.text:
sat-puṇyair iha khalu kais tvad-aṅghri-padma-
  sparśo' yaṃ parivalate bhujaṅga-rāje |
  duṣpāpair api bata kair amuṣya dehas
  tad-bhāvaṃ druta-mṛti-lambhāya vetti ||JGc_1,13.34|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text: 'By what good merits indeed does this serpent-king | receive the touch of Your lotus-feet here? | And by what terrible sins, alas, does his body | know that [touch] only as a means to swift death?' || (JGc 1,13.34) [praharṣiṇī]

children.text:
tasmāt-
  śīrṣa-cchedyasya yaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śīrṣṇi kāliya-bhoginaḥ |
  anvagṛhṇāt pada-nyāsāc cihna-śreṇyā gatiḥ sa naḥ ||JGc_1,13.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Therefore:
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who would deserve to have his head severed, [instead] on the hood of the serpent <s>Kāliya</s> | graciously imprinted rows of marks by His foot-steps — He is our refuge!' || (JGc 1,13.35) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha hīne tasmin ahīne sadayaṃ tad-anumoda-mānaḥ krodhaṃ vinayamānaḥ kṛta-yaśodā-yaśo-dānaḥ svāṅghri-saṅghaṭṭana-truṭitāt kāliya-niṭilād avatīrya nātiprakaṭita-vīryas tasyāvag-vaktratayā sthitasyāgre kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ karuṇā-vyagrekṣaṇatayāvatasthe | atha vanamālī kālindīya-hradam iva kāliya-hradaṃ dāyati sma |
children.translated_text: Then, when that vile serpent [became] submissive, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], compassionately approving him, withdrawing his anger, having bestowed the fame worthy of <s>Yaśodā</s> (glory), descending from <s>Kāliya's</s> forehead — which had been cracked by the impact of His own feet — without excessively displaying his heroism, He stood before that one who remained with downturned face for a few moments with a look of compassionate intensity. Then the wearer of the forest-garland dried out <s>Kāliya's</s> pool, just as he had the <s>Kālindī's</s> pool.

children.text: tadā so' pi līyamāna-doṣatayā tadīya-roṣaṃ proṣitam akarot, valitāñjali-karo darvīkaro vijñāpayāmāsa ca-
children.translated_text: Then that one too, his guilt dissolving, made His anger depart. With folded palms, the hooded one petitioned:

children.text:
yadyapi vṛjina-gāmino mama vṛjinam eva svabhāvas tathāpi tu,
  guṇo vā doṣo vā bhavati mayi yaḥ kṛṣṇa sa bhavad-
  vaśasthāyī nityaṃ mama tu kṛti-sādhyaṃ kim aparam? |
  tvad-aṅghri-dvandvasyāśrayaṇam iti cet tac ca śirasi
  tvayā me vinyastaṃ mama tu kṛti-sādhyaṃ kim aparam? ||JGc_1,13.36|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'Although I am one whose nature is sin itself, being of sinful course, nevertheless:
"Whatever quality or fault exists in me, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, it is | forever under Your control — so what else can be accomplished by my effort? | The taking refuge at the pair of Your feet — even that | has been placed by You upon my head — so what else can be accomplished by my effort?" || (JGc 1,13.36) [śikharinī]'

children.text: tasmāt kām api diśaṃ svayaṃ eva mām ādiśa |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, command me Yourself to whatever direction [You wish].'

children.text: atha sa ca sadeśa-rūpam idam ādideśa, ahipate, tyakta-daurjanyatayā dhanyasyāpi tava yasmād ahitā svayaṃ jagad-ahitā, tasmāt-
children.translated_text: And He gave this command in the form of an instruction: 'O lord of serpents, since even your allies, having abandoned cruelty, are blessed — yet are self-destructive to the world — therefore:

children.text: nātra stheyaṃ tvayā sarpa samudraṃ yāhi mā ciram |
children.translated_text: "You must not stay here, O serpent! Go to the ocean without delay!

children.text: tvaṃ jñāty-apatya-dārāḍhyo go-nṛbhir bhujyate nadī ||[BhP 10.16.61]
children.translated_text: You, rich in kinsmen, offspring, and wives — let the river be enjoyed by cows and men!" || [BhP 10.16.61]

children.text:
dvīpaṃ ramaṇakaṃ hitvā hradam etam upāśritaḥ |
  yad-bhayāt sa suparṇas tvāṃ nādyān mat-pāda-lāñchitam ||[BhP 10.16 |64]
children.translated_text: "Having left <s>Ramaṇaka</s> island and taken refuge in this pool — | out of fear of <s>Garuḍa</s>, he will not [harm] you now, bearing the marks of My feet." || [BhP 10.16.64]

children.text:
rephaṃ visṛṣṭaṃ nirmāyād avasāne padāntagam |
  iti śāsana-vijñānāṃ matam eva mataṃ mama ||JGc_1,13.37|| [anuṣṭubh]
  adhunā kāliya yasmān mat-pada-kṛta-lakṣaṇas tvam asi |
  tad amutra ca sambhavitā mat-pada-kṛta-lakṣaṇaḥ sa bhavān ||JGc_1,13.38|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'The letter "re" released from artifice, at the end placed at a word's foot — | this is my view, which is the very view of those who know the teaching.' || (JGc 1,13.37) [anuṣṭubh]
'Now, O <s>Kāliya</s>, since you bear the marks made by My feet, | there too you shall be one honored as bearing the marks made by My feet.' || (JGc 1,13.38) [upagīti]

children.text: atha daṇḍavad eva patitaḥ kuṇḍali-patis tena nakhara-sudhākarākara-kara-sarasiruhaṃ śirasi nidhāya sudhā-sikta-tanutayā nīrug niramāyi |
children.translated_text: Then the lord of hooded ones, having fallen prostrate like a staff, having placed upon his head the lotus-hand of that one — a mine of nectar-moon-nails — having been sprinkled with nectar [and thus] his body [made] free from disease, he was healed.

children.text: etad-anantara-līlā taṃ pūjayāmāsa [BhP 10.16.65] ity ādikaṃ śrī-śuka-vacanam anūdya, mahattvaṃ ca ity ādinā viśadyate |
children.translated_text: The subsequent pastime — 'worshipped Him with joy' [BhP 10.16.65] and so forth, following the words of the glorious <s>Śuka</s> — is elaborated by 'and the greatness' and so forth:

children.text: taṃ pūjayāmāsa mudā nāgaḥ patnyaś ca sādaram |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Nāga</s> and his wives, with respect, worshipped Him with joy,

children.text: divyāmbara-sraṅ-maṇibhiḥ parārdhyair api bhūṣaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: with divine garments, garlands, and jewels, with most precious ornaments too,

children.text: divya-gandhānulepaiś ca mahatyotpala-mālayā ||
children.translated_text: with divine fragrant unguents, and with a great garland of blue lotuses.'

children.text: pūjayitvā jagannāthaṃ prasādya garuḍa-dhvajam |
children.translated_text: 'Having worshipped the Lord of the world, having propitiated the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>,

children.text: tataḥ prīto' bhyanujñātaḥ parikramyābhivandya tam ||
children.translated_text: then, pleased and permitted, having circumambulated and saluted Him,

children.text: sakalatra-suhṛt-putro dvīpam abdher jagāma ha |
children.translated_text: together with wives, friends, and sons, he went to the island in the ocean.'

children.text: tadaiva sāmṛta-jalā yamunā nirviṣābhavat ||[BhP 10.16.65-68]
children.translated_text: 'At that very moment, the <s>Yamunā</s> became nectarean-watered, free from poison.' || [BhP 10.16.65-68]

children.text:
kṛṣṇaṃ hradād viniṣkrāntaṃ divya-srag-gandha-vāsasam |
  mahā-maṇi-gaṇākīrṇaṃ jāmbūnada-pariṣkṛtam |
upalabhyotthitāḥ sarve labdha-prāṇā ivāsavaḥ ||[BhP 10.17.13-4] iti |
children.translated_text: all rose up, as if having regained their life-breaths!' || [BhP 10.17.13-14]
'Seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> emerged from the pool, wearing divine garlands, fragrances, and garments, | adorned with clusters of great gems, ornamented with gold —

children.text:
mahattvaṃ ca parārdhyatvaṃ cātra divyatvam ucyate |
  divyatvaṃ teṣu kṛṣṇasyāpy aṅge dedīpyamānatā ||JGc_1,13.39|| [anuṣṭubh]
  ato' syāmūni nityāni sthitāny aruṇajā-hrade |
  teṣu kaustubha-nāmā tu maṇiḥ kṛṣṇe virājate |
  nakṣatreṣu sadā pūrṇa-candravat pūrva-parvate ||JGc_1,13.40|| [anuṣṭubh]
  jagannāthaṃ ca yat prāha tathā taṃ garuḍa-dhvajam |
  tatrāścaryaṃ na cācaryaṃ dvārakāyāṃ hi viśrutam ||JGc_1,13.41|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kādraveyasya devābha-nānā-śakti-vidhāriṇaḥ |
  vartmāsya sura-vartma syād iti yuktyāvagamyate |
  anyat tu jīva-pīḍāya tat kathaṃ kṛṣṇa-saṃmatam? ||JGc_1,13.42|| [anuṣṭubh]
  vāri-līlā-parāmarśaḥ sparśaś cāgharipor yadā |
  tadaiṣāmṛta-tulyāsīd yamunety avagamyate ||JGc_1,13.43|| [anuṣṭubh]
  kṛṣṇasyāklinna-veśatvaṃ kāliyenopavāhataḥ |
  akasmād darśanaṃ yat tan nāgāli-parivāritaḥ |
  tasmāt kṛṣṇaṃ hradād ity ādy uktaṃ yuktaṃ prakāśate ||JGc_1,13.44|| iti | [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Greatness and supreme preciousness — here, divinity is spoken of; and divinity in them is the blazing radiance upon <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> own body.' // [anuṣṭubh]
'Therefore, these [jewels] are eternally situated in the lake born of <s>Aruṇā</s>; among them, the gem named <s>Kaustubha</s> shines upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — like the ever-full moon upon the eastern mountain, among the stars.' // [anuṣṭubh]
'And that which designates him as Lord of the Universe and as the one bearing the <s>Garuḍa</s> banner — therein is no wonder, for no wonder is needed — it is well-known in <s>Dvārakā</s>.' // [anuṣṭubh]
'The path of the son of <s>Kadrū</s> (<s>Kāliya</s>), who bears manifold god-like powers, would be the path of the gods — this is understood through reason. But any other [path] would be for the torment of living beings — how could that be sanctioned by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?' // [anuṣṭubh]
'When the touch and caress of the water-sport of the enemy of <s>Agha</s> [occurred], then this [river] became equal to nectar for them — thus it is understood that she is the <s>Yamunā</s>.' // [anuṣṭubh]
'That <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> garments were unwet, that he was borne upon <s>Kāliya</s>, that he suddenly appeared surrounded by a multitude of serpents — therefore, the statement "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> from the lake" and so forth appears fitting.' // [anuṣṭubh] — thus.

children.text:
tan-nirvaṛnane viśeṣas tu varṇyate,
  kolāhalas tvaritatā vivaśāṅga-caryā
  kampaḥ skhalad-vacanatā sravad-asratā ca |
  vīkṣyādi-tṛpti-parihānir iti vrajasthāḥ
  saukhye' pi duḥkham agaman pratilabhya kṛṣṇam ||JGc_1,13.45|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
The special description of their reception is given:
Clamor, haste, involuntary movements of limbs, trembling, faltering speech, flowing tears, and the loss of the initial satisfaction of gazing — thus the residents of <s>Vraja</s>, even in happiness, experienced suffering upon recovering <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
āgato' yam iti kevalaṃ mudā
  sphūrti-pūrtir abhavad vrajaukasām |
  hanta yena na vapur na vā manaḥ
  kiñcid añcitum avāpa śaktatām ||JGc_1,13.46|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: Simply the joy that 'He has come!' — the fullness of its manifestation occurred among the people of <s>Vraja</s>; alas, by which neither body nor mind could manage to move even slightly! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  stambhaḥ sandhiṣu bandhanaṃ pulakitāsāndra-vraṇābha-sthitir
  bāṣpaḥ srasta-vilokanaḥ svara-bhidā kaṇṭhāntara-stambhinī |
  kampaḥ pātavad-anta-danta-valayaḥ svedas tanu-drāvaṇaḥ
  syād evaṃ kṛta-vīkṣaṇaṃ sva-suhṛdāṃ vyagrī-babhūva prabhuḥ ||JGc_1,13.47|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And then:
Paralysis at the joints, binding of the body, a state resembling thick wounds of bristling [hair], tears with drooping gaze, a breaking of voice that choked the throat's interior, trembling with a row of teeth chattering as if about to fall, perspiration that dissolved the body — such a sight of their own dear ones the Lord made, and he became absorbed [in them]! // [śārdūla]

children.text: atha prathamata eva prathamataḥ sthitāḥ samāna-vayasaḥ savayasas tasmāt tam uttīrṇaṃ nirvarṇya vistīrṇa-tad-varṇāmṛta-bhṛta-nayanatayā sthitāḥ kramatas tad-aṅga-saṅga-raṅga-bhūmitām itās tad-āliṅgana-riṅgat-sukha-taraṅgatāṃ gatā na tāvat pratisvam ayam aham asmīti tasmin nyavediṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, first of all, the age-mates standing foremost, perceiving him emerged from that [lake], standing with eyes brimming with the nectar of his expansive description, gradually reaching the ground of the joy of bodily contact with him, attaining the surging wave of happiness from embracing him — they did not for a while announce to him their individual identity, saying 'I am this one.'

children.text: yadvad etāṃs tadvad eva śrīman-nanda-janmā krama-bhajana-sammānanayā jananīṃ janakaṃ suhṛj-janatām api janitānandān janayāmāsa, yatas tata eva te sarve stabdha-dehā labdha-sukha-dehā babhūvuḥ | [53] aho, yadi satya-vacasas te nāvadiṣyaṃs tadā tad idaṃ vā kaḥ pratīyāt? yat khalu gāvaś ca mṛgāś ca tad-āgamanaṃ mṛgayamāṇā vraja-jane cābhedam āyayuḥ, yac ca nagā api tad-duḥkhataḥ śuṣka-carāḥ samprati puṣkala-sukhās tat-kāla-kalita-pallavādibhiḥ praphullā babhūvur iti | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Just as with these, so too the one born of the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, through the honor of sequential reverence, generated delight in his mother, father, and the community of dear ones as well — for from that very [contact], all of them became rigid of body yet attained bodies of happiness. [53] Ah, if those truth-speakers had not reported, then who would have believed this? — that the cows and the deer, seeking his arrival, came together without distinction among the people of <s>Vraja</s>; and that even the trees, dry-moving from grief at his [absence], now abundantly happy, became fully blossomed with newly-sprouted leaves and the like manifesting at that very moment. And there:

children.text:
suhṛl-lokā ye ye sura-ripu-jitā yarhi militās
  tadā satyaṃ sarve samayur abhitaḥ prītim atulām |
  yadā tu śrīmātā sapadi militā prema-vivaśā
  tad āstāṃ tad-vārtā, sakala-janatāgād drava-daśām ||JGc_1,13.48|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: Whatever groups of dear ones, conquered by the enemies of the gods, met [him] — then truly all attained incomparable joy on all sides; but when the glorious mother suddenly met [him], overwhelmed by love — let that account be set aside! — the entire community went into a state of melting! // [śikharinī]

children.text: atha rāmaṃ svīya-prabhāva-bhāvanārāmatāyām apy antar vraja-jana-duḥkhataḥ śuṣkaṃ, tādṛśatāyām api bahir lambhita-gambhīratā-bhṛd-upālambha-sambhavad-vikāśa-hāsaṃ hasann eva namaskurvann, ātmany āliṅganaṃ lambhayaṃś ca ciraṃ tad-utsaṅga-saṅgī babhūva |
children.translated_text: Then, bowing to <s>Rāma</s> — who, though inwardly dry from the suffering of the <s>Vraja</s>-folk despite being in the garden of contemplating his own power, yet outwardly bore a gravity-laden reproach and a smile of budding laughter [saying] 'even so!' — he remained long in his lap, embracing him and receiving his embrace, laughing all the while.

children.text:
atha tatra janānāṃ vimarśaḥ,
  harer eṣā prāptir yadi bhavati nidrāvakalitā
  tadā śoko' py eṣa svayam ayati tatraiva tulanām |
  asau jāgrad-bhūtā sphurati yadi vā tarhi nitarām
  abhīṣṭaṃ sampannaṃ katham api na śarma-pratihatiḥ ||JGc_1,13.49|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Then the people's reflection there:
'If this attainment of <s>Hari</s> is comprehended through sleep, then this grief too by itself reaches the same level of comparison; if it manifests as a waking reality — then indeed the desired has been perfectly fulfilled, and in no way is there an obstruction of happiness!' // [śikharinī]

children.text: atha sarvata eva nidhyānāya naṣṭa-nidhy-āptivat kṛṣṇaṃ madhye nidhāya paritaś carita-niveśeṣu paridhi-veśeṣu kharvita-vrīḍeṣu vyoma-cāriṇāṃ locana-krīḍeṣu sarveṣu strī-puṃsānāṃ kharveṣu prathama-prathita-bhāvi-bhavikā brahma-vidaḥ sampraty api taṃ praty āśiṣāṃ kṛta-dānā vraja-patiṃ praty upālambhamānāḥ pratyāyayāmāsuḥ | yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, for contemplation from all sides, placing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the middle — as if obtaining a lost treasure — among all who had entered the circumference of their assembled dwellings, all with loosened modesty, in the playground of the eyes of the sky-wanderers, among those crowds of diminished [stature] of men and women, the learned ones in the science of destiny who had first proclaimed the future — they now too, having offered blessings toward him, reproaching the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, won them over. As follows:

children.text:
śrī-nanda-rāja tanayas tava sarva-śatru-
  mardīty abhāsi muhur apy alam asmakābhiḥ |
  premṇā tathāpi nikhilaṃ bata hantum aicchaḥ
  puṇyena kevalam asau drutam ājagāma ||JGc_1,13.50|| [vasantatilakā] iti |
children.translated_text: 'O king <s>Nanda</s>, you were told by us again and again: "Your son is the crusher of all enemies!" Even so, you wished, alas, to destroy everything through love — only by merit has he quickly returned!' // [vasantatilakā] — thus.

children.text: tad evaṃ śokena harṣeṇa kālam ajānati vraja-loke rajanir ajanīti tatraiva kṣut-tṛṣṇāti-krami-kṛṣṇātikrama-khedena kṛśatāṃ gatāḥ pratyūṣaṃ yāvad ūṣuḥ | tatra ca sarvām eva śarvarīṃ vrajorvīśa-patnī sapatna-śaṅkayā sutam aṅkata eva niveśayantī paramāveśena muhur api tan-mukha-nirīkṣaṇa-sukha-sakṣaṇāpi tad-vṛtta-smaraṇena tasmād vilakṣaṇā prabhātam āsasāda | hanta hanta kṣudvantaṃ tam api gavāṃ dugdham api dugdhaṃ vidhāya na pāyayāmāsa, satyaṃ sarvam atratyaṃ viṣa-sakalaṅkam iti śaṅkayā |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the people of <s>Vraja</s>, not knowing the passage of time through grief and joy, remained until dawn — having grown thin from the suffering of the transgression of hunger, thirst, and excess that transgressed <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> [absence] — as the night did not pass [for them]. And there, the entire night, the queen of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, out of the suspicion of a rival, kept her son on her very lap, and though with supreme absorption she repeatedly had moments of happiness gazing at his face, she reached the dawn perturbed by the remembrance of that event. Alas, alas! Though he was hungry, she had the cows' milk milked but did not give it to him to drink — out of the suspicion that everything here was tainted with poison.

children.text: rātrau punar anyad api caritraṃ dhanyaṃ jātam | yadā kāliyasya kālindī-jalān niṣkalanam, tat-kālata eva gūḍha-puruṣa-mukhāt paruṣatayā kalitavāṃs tadā sa durjana-vataṃsaḥ kaṃsaś cintā-santata-svāntayā nirīha ivāsīt | [59] cintā yathā, hanta, hanta! santatam asmākam eva vīrās tasmād unmantham āgacchantaḥ santīti duṣkīrti-vahni-mukha-piśāci-mūrtir atīva hasantī hasantīva madīyān jvalayantī tribhuvanam ayantī ca narīnarti | [60] haṃho balīyān api kāliyaḥ sapadi vilīyamāna-balatāṃ valate sma | tasya tad idaṃ nirvāsanaṃ nirvāsanam eva ca manyāmahe, yato vayam api nirvāsanatāṃ gatāḥ | tasmād adhunā tathā vidheyaṃ, yathāsmadīyānāṃ nāpacāras tasya cāpakāraḥ syāt iti |
children.translated_text: During the night, another blessed event had also occurred. When <s>Kāliya's</s> departure from the waters of <s>Kālindī</s> took place, that very instant, through the mouth of a spy, learning of it harshly — that crest-jewel of the wicked, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, became as if inert, with his mind pervaded by continuous anxiety. [59] The anxiety was thus: 'Alas, alas! Constantly, only our own heroes keep getting churned up by him! — the fiend-like figure of the fire-mouth of bad-fame, laughing as if laughing, burning my people, and also roaming the three worlds, dances!' [60] 'Aho! Even the mighty <s>Kāliya</s> suddenly went into a state of dissolving strength. We consider his banishment as our own banishment indeed, for we too have reached the state of being expelled. Therefore, now it must be arranged so that there is no offense toward our people and yet harm to him.'

children.text: tadānīm eva cānyataḥ sa vraja-rājātmaja-vraja-vāsināṃ taraṇijā-tīra eva vāsam ākarṇayann abhyarṇa-gatān ājñāpayāmāsa, bhavantas tatra praviśantaḥ samantataḥ pravalatayā jvalanaṃ prajvalanam ācarantaḥ svayam antardhānam ācarantu |
children.translated_text: And at that very time, from another source, hearing that the prince of <s>Vraja</s> and the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers were residing on the very bank of <s>Yamunā</s>, he commanded those who had come near: 'You, entering there, setting blazing fire on all sides with full force, conceal yourselves!'

children.text: tataś ca teṣu tathā-kṛta-cariteṣu vipolati tu davānale śīghraṃ palāyiteṣu teṣu ca sarva eva vraja-bhavanāḥ sneha-vṛtta-labdha-sambhāvanāḥ sāgrajaṃ vraja-rāja-tanūjam evāvrajya vijñāpayāmāsuḥ-
children.translated_text:
Then, when those had so acted — when the forest fire spread and those [agents] had quickly fled — all the people of <s>Vraja</s>, who had gained esteem through their bond of affection, went to the prince of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> together with his elder brother, and informed him:
'We fear neither death nor the flood of hardship, but only the cruelty of the absence of seeing the moon-rays of your face!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
śaṅkāmahe na mṛtyoś ca na ca kṛcchra-pravāhataḥ |
  kintu tvan-mukha-candrāṃśu-darśanābhāva-vaiśasāt ||JGc_1,13.51|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text:
tataś ca-
  hareḥ phutkāra-mātreṇa nirvavau dava-dīpakaḥ |
  utprekṣante tu munayas tasya tat-pāna-kartṛtām ||JGc_1,13.52|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'By <s>Hari's</s> mere blowing, the forest fire was extinguished. But the sages conjecture that it was he who drank it!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evam ahitena ya upāhita upāhitas tasminn apavāhite sarva eva trāṇa-prāṇāḥ prabhāte ca prabhāte, tat-prabhāvata eva yathāvasthitaṃ vrajaṃ vraja-vāsinaḥ sānandaṃ tam anv avindanta | kintu tasminn eva madhuratā-kalile kālindī-hrada-salile saṅkarṣaṇena kṛta-kṛṣṇākarṣaṇena viharatā sakhibhir, akhilaṃ saha-dhavalā-vrajaṃ vrajam api samāharatā yadā bahalaṃ kutūhalaṃ jātam, tadā tena gṛhāya gamanam anujñātam |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the danger that had been set up by the enemy was averted, all — whose lives were saved — at dawn after dawn, by his very power, found <s>Vraja</s> exactly as it had been, and the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers joyfully found him. But in those very waters of the <s>Kālindī</s> lake, sweet with sweetness, when <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), who attracted <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sported with his friends, gathering the entire herd of white cows together with the settlement of <s>Vraja</s> itself — when great curiosity had arisen, then he gave permission to go home.

children.text: tathā ca gamanaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: And the manner of going was as follows:

children.text:
vādyair nṛtyaiḥ pragītaiḥ śruti-śiva-paṭhanair divya-bhauma-prasūna-
  pravṛṭ-kalpābhivarṣair jaya-jaya-ninadaiḥ śarma-kolāhalaiś ca |
  kṛṣṇaṃ madhye vidhāya prakaṭatara-mahānanda-nirvrīḍa-bhāvān
  nṛtyantas te vraja-sthā vrajam abhiviviśuḥ khaṃ yathā jyotiroghāḥ ||JGc_1,13.53|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: With music, dances, sung praises, auspicious Vedic recitations, showers almost like an epoch of celestial and earthly flowers, victory-cries of 'Victory! Victory!', and clamor of happiness — placing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the middle, with conspicuously great, unashamed joy, those residents of <s>Vraja</s>, dancing, entered <s>Vraja</s> — as hosts of luminaries [enter] the sky! // [sragdharā]

children.text: tad-anantaraṃ ca dhavalāḥ parataś cālayitvā tat-pūrva-kāla-pālakāsadbhāve' pi śrīmatāṃ tatra-bhavatām eṣāṃ prabhāveṇa tatrodapātra-mātraṃ na vikalpam āgād iti svalpa-paribhavāyāpy akalpamāne samasta-vraje yātayāmam api yātayāmatāṃ nāgataṃ tad-ghṛta-pakva-pracurānnam iti sadyastanam iva rāma-parvaṇi pūrvāhnetanaṃ gṛhāntaḥ-saṅgṛhīta-jemana-sāmagrī-samudayaṃ sarva eva tāv agrajānujāv agrato vidhāyāvyagraṃ samyag rasayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: And after that, having moved the white [cows] onward, and despite the absence of former-time guardians of that [area], by the power of these glorious ones — not even a water-vessel's worth of doubt arose there. And in the entire <s>Vraja</s> settlement, where not even slight disrespect could be imagined, though the time had already passed, the meal-time did not become stale — the food, cooked abundantly with ghee, was like freshly made, as if at the festival of <s>Rāma</s>. The collection of dining provisions gathered within the houses from the morning — all of them, placing those two, elder and younger brothers, at the front, savored it completely and without anxiety.

children.text: tad evam udghaṭita-gīḥ-kaṇṭhaḥ sa madhukaṇṭhaḥ samāpayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Thus, with throat cleared for speech, that <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> concluded:

children.text:
īdṛśas tanayo jātas tava vraja-narādhipa |
  kaṃsādīn damayāmāsa kāliya-damanena yaḥ ||JGc_1,13.54|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Such a son has been born to you, O king of <s>Vraja</s>, who subdued <s>Kaṃsa</s> and others by the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s>!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ, tarīyamāṇena hariṇā varīyasā vraja-parīvāreṇa saritāv ivātarīṣātāṃ te āpadāv iti sukhada-vṛtte sabhyānāṃ tal-līlā-samādher abhyavakarṣaṇāya stavanāmṛta-varṣaṇāya ca sāñjali-sthitayos tayoś cirād bahir avahita-tad-upasevāḥ pūrvavad eva sa-vraja-devāḥ sarve svaṃ svaṃ kāryam āseduḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when <s>Hari</s>, the supreme one, together with the retinue of <s>Vraja</s>, had crossed over those two calamities as if crossing two rivers — and when all the assembly-members, for the withdrawal from the meditation of his pastimes and for the showering of the nectar of praise, had long stood in their joyful routine, having devoted themselves externally to the service of those two who stood with joined palms — accompanied by the deities of <s>Vraja</s>, as before, all proceeded to their own respective duties.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
kāliya-dava-caṇḍatā-daṇḍanaṃ nāma
trayodaśa-pūraṇam
 ||13||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the Śrī Śrī <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Thirteenth Chapter named 'The Chastisement of the Ferocity of <s>Kāliya</s> and the Forest-Fire'
||13||

children.text: śrī-śrī-gopījana-vallabhāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to Śrī Śrī <s>Gopījana-vallabha</s> (the Beloved of the <s>Gopīs</s>)!

children.text: atha kaiśora-līlā
children.translated_text: Now the Adolescent Pastimes (<s>Kaiśora-līlā</s>).

children.text: atha caturdaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Fourteenth Chapter.

children.text: gadarbhāsura-mardanam
children.translated_text: The Crushing of <s>Gadarbhāsura</s> (the Donkey-Demon).

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
children.translated_text: O Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, together with <s>Sanātana</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>!

children.text: gopāla raghunāthāpta-vraja-vallabha pāhi mām ||JGc_1,14.1||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gopāla</s>, obtained by <s>Raghunātha</s>, O Beloved of <s>Vraja</s>, protect me! // [1.14.1]

children.text: tad evaṃ goloka-vilāse śrī-gopāla-pālyamāna-gopālānāṃ nitya-lokaḥ śrī-golokaḥ kathitaḥ | tatra ca śrī-goparāja-sabhāyām apūrva-vīkṣita-kavi-kṣitipati-kumāra-sukumāra-kumāra-yugalāvakalanam udbhāvitam |[2] tad-anantaram api bālya-vilāse tad-yugalena kṛṣṇa-bālya-carita-varṇanaṃ kāliya-dalana-līlāvasānam ācaritam | samprati tu tat prathitaṃ kaiśoracaritam ākhyāyate | [3] tad yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the play of <s>Goloka</s>, the eternal world of the cowherds tended by Śrī <s>Gopāla</s> has been described as Śrī <s>Goloka</s>. And there, in the assembly of the king of the cowherds, the apprehension of the supremely tender pair of boy-princes — the poet-king's sons, seen for the first time — was brought forth. [2] Subsequently too, in the play of childhood, the depiction of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> childhood exploits performed by that pair was enacted up to the concluding pastime of the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s>. Now, however, the well-known adolescent exploits (<s>kaiśora-carita</s>) are narrated. [3] As follows —

children.text: atha dināntare ca pūrvavad eva vraja-naradeva-sabhāntare tayor ekataraḥ samutkaṇṭhatayā snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ svagatam idam uvāca-[4] atha kaiśoraṃ varṇanīyam | kintu rahasya-rasa-hāri-prasabhāyāṃ sabhāyām asyāṃ yathā lajjā na sajjā syāt tathā yujyate | [5] yadi ca jātu nija-mādhurī-bubhukṣita-kukṣim-bhariṇā hariṇā svaka-sukhāvaham iti rahas tad anuyujyevahi, tadā tad ucitam eva tad-upacitam ācariṣyāvaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, as before, in the assembly of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, one of those two (<s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>), with great longing, said within himself: [4] "Now the <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence) is to be described. But in this assembly — which is forcefully captivating with the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) of the confidential — it is proper that modesty should not become entangled."
