[5] "And if ever <s>Hari</s> — who fills the belly of his own hunger for sweetness — should privately enjoin [the narration] as bringing his own happiness, then we two shall perform what is fitting and has been accumulated."

children.text: atha spaṣṭaṃ tu vyācaṣṭa-tataś ca spaṣṭaṃ kṛta-gamāyāṃ ṣaṣṭha-samāyāṃ samullasita-sammati-maye janma-tithi-samaye harṣa-samṛddhi-prada-varṣa-vṛddhi-parvaṇi sarva-niḥśreyasam āvistarāṃ vistārayataḥ samastaṃ vinistārayatas tasya śrīmad-vrajarāja-sutasya viśveṣām eva manaś coraṃ kaiśoram udayāñcakre | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Then he clearly declared: "And so, when the clearly arrived sixth year, at the birthday <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) that had blossomed with the fullness of delight, at the festival of the growth of years that bestows the abundance of joy — [<s>kaiśora</s>] arose, spreading forth all supreme welfare widely, setting everything free — for the glorious son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, the stealer of everyone's minds, adolescence dawned." As follows:

children.text:
rājyaṃ samyag upetya kṛṣṇa-vapuṣi trailokya-lakṣmī-maye
  krīḍābhir laghu nirgamayya samayān audārya-paryākulam |
  pātrāya svayam āgatāya guṇitāvāsāya sad-vedine
  kaiśorāya nijaṃ pradāya viṣayaṃ paugaṇḍam antardadhe ||JGc_1,14.2|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
Having duly attained sovereignty over <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> body — which is the abode of the splendor of the three worlds —
swiftly ushering out the ages through sports, overflowing with magnanimity,
to <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence) — a worthy recipient, who had come of his own accord, an abode of virtues, a knower of truth —
having given his own domain, <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (pre-adolescence) disappeared! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.2, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  dṛṣṭi-prasāda-kṛta-sāmabhir aṃśudānaiḥ
  śaśvan manoharaṇa-nirmita-buddhi-bhedaiḥ |
  arthāntarābhiviniveśaja-bhāva-daṇḍaiḥ
  kaiśorakaṃ vaśayati sma hareḥ samastam ||JGc_1,14.3|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
And then:
By rays of glances that created concord through their grace,
by constantly producing bewilderment fashioned of mind-stealing,
by rods of sentiment born of immersion in various meanings —
<s>Hari's</s> adolescence brought everything under its sway! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.3, <s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text:
tatra ca,
  mukhe pūrtiḥ kāntir nayana-yugale dairghyam aruṇa-
  prabhā hṛdy ucchrāyaḥ pratatir api madhye tu kṛśatā |
  itīdaṃ saundaryaṃ yad-avadhi manāg apy adhijage
  jagan-netra-śreṇī tad-avadhi harau tena cakṛṣe ||JGc_1,14.4|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
And there:
In the face, fullness; in the pair of eyes, length and reddish radiance;
in the chest, loftiness; breadth too; and in the middle, slenderness —
this beauty, to the extent that it was attained even slightly,
to that extent, the row of the world's eyes was drawn to <s>Hari</s> by it! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.4, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: tad itthaṃ taj-jyeṣṭhaś ca nirdiṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, in this way, his elder brother too was described.

children.text: tadā ca tāla-phala-pākāvasare varṣā-prasare kadācin nikhila-sukha-vardhanasya govardhanasya girer āgneyyāṃ hariti hari-rāmādayaḥ sāmodā gāś cārayantaḥ santi sma | [9] tataś ca pūrvānubhava-sampātātītaṃ pūrva-vātānītam atidūrataḥ sajātīya-pūra-dharaṃ paktrima-tāla-phala-jāla-saurabhya-bharam upalabhya, pūrvata eva tat-kīrti-vivartita-cittā vraja-vartiṣu vittās te sarvaṃ-sahāyāḥ spṛhaṇīyāḥ sarva eva tayoḥ sahāyā hṛdi spṛhayāmbabhūvuḥ- rāma-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ valitā vayam itaś calitā rāsa-bhāsura-rāja-bhavanaṃ tāla-vanaṃ tat-pāla-gaṇam api tathā-vidhaṃ nibhālayituṃ nūtana-kutukāḥ sma | tataḥ sva-bubhukṣā-sukṣāmatā-lakṣya-vinodād imau vinudāma iti |
children.translated_text: At that time, at the season of ripening palm-fruits, during a shower of rain, once, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rāma</s> and the others were joyfully tending cows in the southeastern quarter of <s>Govardhana</s>, which augments all happiness. [9] Then, having perceived from a great distance — surpassing the range of previous experience and borne on the preceding wind — the mass of fragrance of the baked palm-fruits, with their kindred flood — those all-helping, desirable ones, all the companions of those two, their minds already turned by that fame, became eager in their hearts: "Led by <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, we have set forth from here — we are curious for a fresh visit to that palm forest, which is brilliant with sports, a royal abode — and also to behold its guardian-host of that kind. Then, let us prod these two with the pretext of our own hunger for sport!"

children.text: te ca śrīdāma-subala-stokakṛṣṇa-śavalā bala-kṛṣṇayoḥ sama-balā labdha-marmāṇaḥ sadharmāṇa ity ataeva śaśvad akhilatayā sakhitayā virājante | yayor eva samaṃ vīryam ity ādikam īryate iti | tataḥ satatam eva kramate tat-parākrame teṣāṃ buddhi-krama ity akṛta-śaṅkāśeṣeṇa praṇaya-viśeṣeṇa jighatsā-miṣeṇa ca tad-arthaṃ bhrātṛ-balaṃ balabhadraṃ prārthayāmāsuḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Among them, <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Subala</s>, <s>Stokakṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Śavala</s> — who were equal in strength to <s>Bala</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who had grasped the innermost secrets, and who shared the same <s>dharma</s> — for that very reason always shone with complete friendship. Of them it is declared: "Whose valor was equal [to theirs]" and so forth. Therefore, their intellectual calculation always followed the course of those two's valor. So with complete confidence, with special affection, and with the pretext of hunger, they entreated brother <s>Balabhadra</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) for that purpose, as follows:

children.text:
tālānāṃ vanam atra paktrima-phalaṃ nirhāri pūraṃ yataḥ
  saurabhyaṃ bata dūram eti tad idaṃ bhogaṃ vinā niṣphalam |
  śrūyante hi kharā narāśana-karās tasyādhipā ity adaḥ
  śrī-rāmāyata-dor-yugārpaya tathā śrī-kṛṣṇa duṣṭāpaha ||JGc_1,14.5|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[11] āyata-dor-yuga ity anena ca dhvanitam idam-
children.translated_text:
"Here is a forest of palms, from which baked, ripe, full fruits
exude fragrance — alas, from a distance, it is fruitless without enjoyment!
We hear that asses who eat men are its overlords, and so —
O glorious <s>Rāma</s>, extend your long pair of arms! O glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, remover of the wicked!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.5, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
[11] And by "of long pair of arms" this is also implied:

children.text:
mahābāhutayā rāma tarkyase tvaṃ ca vikramī |
  na tathā lakṣyathāḥ kvāpi lakṣaṇīyas tu samprati ||JGc_1,14.6|| [anuṣṭubh] iti |
children.translated_text:
"By your great-armedness, O <s>Rāma</s>, you are surmised to be valorous;
but you are not so perceived anywhere — yet now you should be recognized!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.6, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: śrī-rāmas tu sa-smitam uvāca-bho bhavanto lobhavanto bhavanto' py asmattaḥ prati pratīyadhve, yato mugdhāḥ! niyuddhābhimukhair bhrū-bhaṅga-sūcita-śauṭīrya-sukhaiḥ prabhavadbhir bhavadbhiḥ kadācid āvām api parābhavam āsādyāvahe | tat katham āvām eva yācyāvahe ?
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Rāma</s> said with a smile: "O you covetous ones! Even you should be recognized by us, since you are foolish! By you — whose prowess, signaled by eyebrow-furrows, is capable of confrontation and delight — sometimes even we two might be brought to defeat. Then how is it that we two alone are being importuned?"

children.text: te ca procuḥ-sarvato' py atiguṇavantau bhavantau khalv asmākaṃ sārau rāja-kumārau | rāja-nīti-rītiś caivam eva yad rāja-kulam eva vriyate puraskriyate ca | mṛgayāyāṃ mṛga-tāḍanavan na punar anyena svayam agra-gaṇyena bhūyate | yadi tat kulaṃ parama-vīryākulaṃ bhavati, tadā tu kim uta? tatra cāgrajatayā bhavataḥ sadāpāgryato nāgryāyate | tasmād yady asmad-icchā-pūraṇāya bhavator icchā saṅgacchate, tadā nānyad anumanyatām |
children.translated_text: And they said: "Even though you two are endowed with all surpassing virtues, you are indeed our essence — the two royal princes! And it is indeed the custom of royal polity that the royal family alone is chosen and placed foremost. In hunting, it is as in the striking of deer — one does not, however, put forward someone else who is himself the foremost. If that family is overwhelmed with supreme valor, then what more need be said? And therein, by your seniority, you always are at the very forefront, without rival. Therefore, if your desire accords with the fulfillment of our desire, then let nothing else be contemplated!"

children.text: tad evaṃ saha-prahasite śubhrāṃśu-site kṛṣṇāgraje svayam agrato vraje siṃha-nādam ādadānā dāmodarādayaḥ sāmodaṃ tad-anuplavāḥ plavamānatayā tad-vanāya tad-avasthā eva pratasthire | gās tu sva-sthāna eva sthāpayāmāsuḥ | prasthāya ca rāmam,
children.translated_text: Thus, when the elder brother of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, white as the bright moon, had smiled in assent, <s>Dāmodara</s> and the others, placing themselves before him, taking a lion's roar, joyfully leaped forth as his followers, and in that very state they set out for that forest. But the cows they stationed in their own place. And having set out, [they addressed] <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text:
sopālambham ivāvadaṃs tam anu tad bāhū ca mitrāṇi yat
  tena drāk sa ca serṣyā-cittam iva tāṃ gatvā tu tālāvalim |
  sarvām eva bhujāyugena yugapad vikṣipya saṅghaṭṭayan
  vibhraṣṭāni mithaḥ phalāni vidadhe ghṛṣṭāni digdantivat ||JGc_1,14.7|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
They spoke to him as if with reproach, and then, following that, to those arms and to the friends;
by which, swiftly and as if with a jealous mind, having gone to that row of palms,
shaking all of them at once with both arms simultaneously, striking them together,
he made the fruits, mutually crushed, fall — like being ground by the tusks of elephants of the quarters! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.7, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
taj jñātvāsra-parāsabhāś ca paritaḥ sākrandam abhyāyayur
  yān dṛṣṭvā paśupāḥ sa-mādhava-balāḥ śaśvadd hasantaḥ sthitāḥ |
  hāsāveśa-vaśāt kṛtānavahitiṃ pratyak padābhyāṃ balaṃ
  vajrābhyām iva dhenukas tam anudat tac caiṣa nābudhyata ||JGc_1,14.8|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
Knowing that, the tear-bold asses, braying all around, approached in alarm;
seeing whom, the cowherds, together with <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), stood constantly laughing!
From the excess of the transport of laughter, as their vigilance was lost, with both hind feet,
<s>Dhenuka</s> kicked <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) like thunderbolts — but he did not even notice! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.8, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
na jñātavān api yataḥ sa tu taṃ prahāraṃ
  tenātiroṣa-bhara-nāsti-viveka-caryaḥ |
  bhūyaḥ parāk-sthiti vinardya vikīrṇa-lattas
  tenātha vatsaka ivāraci dhenukākhyaḥ ||JGc_1,14.9|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
Since he indeed did not even notice that blow,
therefore, that one, with the conduct of one devoid of discernment through excess of anger,
turning back and braying, with flailing hooves,
was then made like a calf by the one named <s>Dhenuka</s> (the ass-demon)! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.9, <s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: atha brahmāṇḍam api khaṇḍayituṃ pracaṇḍatā-maṇḍitāc caṇḍa-caṇḍīśa-śūlād apy uddaṇḍa-prahāreṇa bala-bhuja-daṇḍena tāla-maṇḍala-maṇḍaleśvara-śirasi cakrīvac-chakrārir vicakare | tena ca tāla-parāvara-parasparāsu yaḥ khalu nihita āvega-saṃskāraḥ pralaya-jāta-durvāra-prabhañjanākāraḥ, sa tu hindolayaṃs tat tad uparigam ardham ardham agni-yantra-prakṣiptam iva vikṣiptaṃ vidhāya prāyaḥ sarvam evākharva-tāla-kharva-mayaṃ tad vanaṃ nimeṣa-mātreṇa vitroṭayāmāsa | yatra svayaṃ tu bhavantu tṛṇa-rājāḥ khalv ime, tathāpi tṛṇāny eva iti balabhadraś cintayāmāsa ca |
children.translated_text: Then, with a blow from the rod of <s>Bala's</s> arm — more formidable than even the fierce trident of <s>Caṇḍa-Caṇḍīśa</s> (Śiva), which is adorned with the ferocity capable of shattering the cosmic egg — he whirled <s>Dhenuka</s> around like a discus-bearer (<s>Cakrin</s>) upon the head of the lord of the circle of palm trees, the enemy of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). And from that, the momentum-imprint deposited among the palm trees upon each other — resembling an irresistible cataclysmic storm — swaying them, causing each successive upper half to fly up as if shot from a fire-device, nearly destroyed the entire forest of sturdy palm-stumps in the blink of an eye. Where <s>Balabhadra</s> himself reflected: "Let these be kings of grasses (<s>tṛṇa-rājas</s>) indeed — still, they are but grass!"

children.text: atha tad-anugatā deva-vispardhinaḥ pare' py asvaratayā gardabhā gardantaḥ pratighāt pratighātam ācarantaḥ sahasā ruddhādhvānaḥ saha yudhvānaḥ paryāgatās tṛṇavan-matāḥ paramānandārāma-rāma-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ hasadbhyāṃ vilasadbhyām evākhava iva dhṛtāsava eva tucchīkṛtya gṛhīta-puccha-caraṇās teṣāṃ tāla-bhakṣaṇa-saukaryārtham ivādhimadhyām adhyavasthita-tṛṇa-kṣmāpaty-upari kṣipram eva parikṣiptāḥ kṣapita-jīvitāḥ kṣiti-nipatitāḥ saha nistala-tāla-phalaiḥ ketava iva rāhubhir dināni kānicit kaṃsa-pakṣīyān abhīṣayanta |
children.translated_text: Then, the other asses who followed him — bellowing like demons rivaling the gods, incapable of proper sound — braying, delivering counter-blow after counter-blow, suddenly having their paths blocked, fighting together, arriving — considered as mere grass by the supremely blissful <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who were laughing and shining — were seized like sport-pieces, seized by tail and hoof, and as if for the convenience of eating the palm-fruits, were swiftly hurled upon the high ground of the tree-king (palm-tree) that stood between the lower and middle regions, their lives extinguished, having fallen to the ground along with stalkless palm-fruits — like false luminaries [eclipsed] by <s>Rāhu</s>s — they frightened <s>Kaṃsa's</s> partisans for some days.

children.text:
rāsabhān śamayituḥ kiyad bhavet
  pauruṣaṃ tad iti nāvamanyatām |
  yad diviṣṭha-paṭalī tadāpi tau
  vādya-gīta-kusumair asevata ||JGc_1,14.10|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
"How great would be the valor of subduing mere asses?" —
let this not be disrespected;
for even then, the host of celestials
served those two with music, song, and flowers! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.10, <s>svāgatā</s>]

children.text: atha hāsa-sahitam upajahāsa ca, sā maghavat-pradhānā dhenukam aghajid-abhiprāyam abhiprayatī | yathā,
children.translated_text: Then, the divine host led by <s>Maghavat</s> (<s>Indra</s>) laughed with laughter, contemplating <s>Dhenuka</s> and the intention of <s>Aghajit</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the conqueror of <s>Agha</s>). As follows:

children.text:
aghāsuraḥ kāliya-kadru-janmāpy
  asoḍha vīryaṃ yadi nāsmadīyam |
  putrī-pramardin, bata gardabha tvaṃ
  kartuṃ kathaṃ dhārṣṭyam iyaj jagantha? ||JGc_1,14.11|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
"<s>Aghāsura</s>, born of <s>Kāliya</s> and <s>Kadru</s>,
could not bear our valor;
O donkey, you destroyer of your own children — alas!
how did you dare to commit this boldness?" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.11, <s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: atha sadyaḥ pitṛ-vana-vilāsa-tāla-vana-vāsa-rāsabha-śava-spṛṣṭāni tāni tālāni na tu taiḥ parāmṛṣṭāni, na ca tadīya-tṛṇāni gāvas tarṇāvitāḥ, kintu tad-visṛṣṭāni tāni kecid itara eva mānavā gāvaś ca vigata-sādhvasādhvatayā ciraṃ sādhv āsvāditavantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, the palms in the palm forest — the playground of the fathers — that had been touched by the donkey-carcasses were immediately not handled by them, nor did the cows with their young calves eat the grasses of that [area]; but those [palms] thus abandoned — certain other humans and cows, with their apprehension having departed due to the long journey, duly relished them well for a long time.

children.text:
tad evaṃ nṛ-jagdhaṃ taṃ sa-gaṇaṃ krodha-dagdha-sūkṣma-deha-paryantam ācarya śrīmān kṛṣṇas tu sāgrajaḥ saha-sakhi-vrajaḥ puraskṛta-dhenur vādita-veṇur vrajan vrajam ājagāma | yathā,
  kamala-dala-viśāla-lola-netraḥ
  sakhi-jana-gīta-pavitra-citra-kīrtiḥ
  saha-balam aviśad vrajaṃ sa-veṇuṃ
  kvaṇita-kalaṃ kalayan vrajeśa-sūnuḥ ||JGc_1,14.12|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
Thus, having dispatched him of compact-build along with his host — down to the destruction of [even] his anger-burned subtle body — the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with his elder brother, accompanied by the company of friends, placing the cows before him, playing the flute, proceeded to <s>Vraja</s> and arrived. As follows:
With broad, wide, restless, lotus-petal eyes,
with fame pure and wondrous, sung by his companion-folk,
accompanied by <s>Bala</s>, bearing a flute with sweetly resonating sound,
the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> entered <s>Vraja</s>! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.14.12, <s>puṣpitāgrā</s>]

children.text:
taṃ gorajaś churita-kuntala-baddha-mālya-
  sambaddha-piñcham amalekṣaṇa-cāru-hāsam |
  ānandita-veṇum anugeḍita-puṇya-kīrtiṃ
  gopyaḥ sa-tṛṣṇa-nayanāḥ paritaḥ samīyuḥ ||12a|| [vasantatilakā][*4]
[*4] Compare BhP 10.15.42, which is found in this verse' s place in some editions.
children.translated_text:
Him — his curly locks sprinkled with cow-dust, his garland adorned
with a fastened peacock-feather, with pure eyes and a charming smile,
his flute delighted, his auspicious fame resounded —
the <s>gopīs</s>, with longing eyes, surrounded on all sides! // [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: tad etat paryantam udantaṃ samudantaḥ kathayitvā tatra ca kṛṣṇa-manaś-corīṇāṃ nava-kiśorīṇāṃ tan-mukha-vidhu-darśana-śāta-jāta-bhrū-bhaṅga-taraṅga-saṅgatānurāga-sāgara-garimāṇam anusmṛtya vismṛta-sarvendriya-kṛtyaḥ sa-bāṣpa-kaṇṭhaḥ snigdhakaṇṭhas tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ muhūrta-dvayaṃ mūrta-bhāvam evāsasāda | [21] śrīmad-vrajarājādayas tu tad-abhiprāya-jānānāḥ sadayatayā tadīya-sāntva-vidhaye sāvadhānā nānā-vidha-vidhānam ācarantaḥ sarva eva cintāturā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Having narrated the tale up to this point, and then, recalling the weight of the ocean of love — generated by the wave-like play of eyebrow-arching arising from the sight of the face-moon of that one — in the hearts of the new young maidens who stole <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mind, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, having forgotten the function of all his senses, his throat choked with tears, attained in that assembly a state of embodied emotion for two <s>muhūrtas</s>. [21] The glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> and the others, knowing his intention, with compassion, attentive to the means of consoling him, performing various kinds of arrangements, all became anxious.

children.text: tat-tad-vidhānasya cākiñcit-karatāyām aviratāyāṃ madhukaṇṭha eva tān sphurad-utkaṇṭhaḥ sāntvitān vidhāya bhrātuḥ sarvendriya-kuṇṭhatā-śāntaye tadānīntana-vraja-rājñī-santata-tal-lālana-saṅgānam ātatāna | yathā-
children.translated_text: When the inefficacy of each of those arrangements continued unabated, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> alone — his longing manifest — having consoled them, in order to relieve the numbness of all his brother's senses, extended the [description of the] constant maternal caressing by the then queen of <s>Vraja</s>. As follows:

children.text: hariṇā halinā saha ripu-dalinā |
children.translated_text: Of <s>Hari</s>, along with <s>Halin</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), the crusher of foes —

children.text: rajanī-mukham anu jananī-lālanam iti kalitaṃ jita-kalinā ||dhru||
children.translated_text: The motherly caressing at nightfall — thus it is known — by the conqueror of <s>Kali</s>! // [refrain]

children.text: nirmañchana-nīrājana-mārjana-vadanālokana-racanam |
children.translated_text: The arrangement of wiping, lustration (<s>nīrājana</s>), cleaning, face-gazing;

children.text: mardana-majjana-saṃvastraṇataḥ paścāt puṇḍraka-sacanam ||
children.translated_text: After massage, bathing, and dressing — then the application of auspicious marks (<s>puṇḍraka</s>);

children.text: rasa-caya-yojana-bhojana-pūraṇa-surabhita-nīrāsvadanam |
children.translated_text: The combining of flavors, the filling of the meal, the tasting of fragrant water;

children.text: aguru-drava-yutir atha tāmbūla-svadanaṃ sukha-saṃvadanam ||
children.translated_text: Then the application of liquid <s>aguru</s> (agarwood), and the savoring of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), and pleasant conversation;

children.text:
sukṛti-janaṃ prati śayyā-saṃskṛti-samanujñām anuśayanam |
  priya-sakha-saṅgatim anu sevy-anugatim anu ca mudām aticayanam ||JGc_1,14.13|| iti | [7 x 4]
children.translated_text:
For the virtuous ones, lying down follows the permission of the bed-sacrament;
following the company of dear friends, following the attendance of servants, there is an overflowing of joys! ||14.13|| Thus. [7 x 4]

children.text: tad evam atiparicaritam | hari-carita-varṇanaṃ madhura-rāga-nīrandhraṃ karṇa-randhraṃ praviśad eva taṃ mūrcchām ṛcchantam api jāgarayāmāsa, nāma-dheyam iva nidrā-labdha-cid-rāhityam |
children.translated_text: Thus was he exceedingly attended. The description of <s>Hari's</s> deeds, entering the ear-aperture impenetrably dense with sweet melody, awakened him even as he was attaining a swoon — like his very name dispelling the absence of consciousness obtained in sleep.

children.text: atha svasthāvasthatayā kuṇṭhatā-rahitas tādṛśa-guṇa-mahitaḥ snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sa-bāṣpa-kaṇṭham uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, free from hesitation by his state of composure, honored by such virtues, spoke with a tear-choked throat:

children.text:
so' yaṃ gopāla-bhūpāla tanayas tava nirdayaḥ |
  mugdhaṃ ca mad-vidhaṃ mugdhaṃ karoti svaira-līlayā ||JGc_1,14.14|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'This son of yours, O king of the cowherd-realm, is merciless!
And he makes innocent ones like me bewildered by his spontaneous pastimes!' ||14.14|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ vṛtte nivṛtte sarvatra ca vraja-jane gṛha-vartmānuvṛtte nityavad eva vraja-mahendra-tanūjas tau sūta-rāja-tanūjau saṅgata eva nināya | nītvā ca tayor ātmanā tṛtīyaḥ san prasaṅgataḥ pracchannatayā papraccha-kathayataṃ, katham etāvān kasmān mūrcchāveśaḥ kleśa iva parāmṛṣṭaḥ? iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the event had occurred and concluded, and when all the <s>Vraja</s>-folk had followed the path homeward, as always, the son of the great <s>Indra</s> of <s>Vraja</s> escorted those two sons of the bard-king together. And having led them, being himself the third with them, he asked casually and privately: 'Tell me, how and why was such an intense swoon-seizure experienced as if it were suffering?'

children.text: ubhau tu sa-gadgadaṃ jagadatuḥ-kiṃ brūvahe, bhavanta iva sarvam anubhavanti iti |
children.translated_text: Both said with faltering voices: 'What shall we say? [We] experience everything just as you do!'

children.text: kṛṣṇaś ca sa-tṛṣṇam uvāca-jānīma eva kevalaṃ na, kintu tadānīṃ svayam api nitarām ācarāmas, tathāpi tad varṇanam ākarṇayitum icchāmaḥ | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with longing: 'We know indeed, and not merely that — at that time we ourselves also performed [those deeds] most intensely. Yet still, we wish to hear that description. For indeed:'

children.text:
svayam api yat puru racitaṃ tad yadi hṛdayaṃ tadā sadā śrāvyam |
  kāvyaṃ nija-sacitaṃ yat tad idaṃ yuvakāṃ parasparaṃ śṛṇuthaḥ ||JGc_1,14.15|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
'That which one has oneself abundantly composed, if it is dear to the heart, then it is always worth hearing;
what poetry is one's own composition — that, O youths, you hear from each other!' ||14.15|| [gīti]

children.text: tasmāt prathamaṃ tāvat preyasī-gaṇādhikāyā rādhikāyā bimboṣṭhī-goṣṭhī-madhyam adhyāsya vyasyatām eṣā paṭīyasī rasa-paripāṭī |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, first then, having taken a seat in the midst of the assembly of <s>bimboṣṭhī</s> (ruby-lipped) maidens, presided over by <s>Rādhikā</s> who surpasses all the beloved ones — let this most excellent succession of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) be unfolded!'

children.text: ubhau sa-bāṣpatayā parasparaṃ nirūpayantāv ūcatuḥ-
children.translated_text: Both, gazing at each other tearfully, said:

children.text:
yad antar yasya sarvaṃ tat tasya jānāty abhīpsitaḥ |
  sa eva ced vasaty antas taṃ tu jānīta kaḥ paraḥ ||JGc_1,14.16|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'He who is desired knows everything that is within anyone;
but if he himself dwells within — who else can know him?' ||14.16|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: kṛṣṇaś ca sānandam uvāca-tad adya naktam evānavadyā seyaṃ vidyā nivedyatām iti bāhu-yugaṃ gṛhītvā sakhi-goṣṭhīm anu tāv amū nītvā bahala-kutūhala-veṣṭitena ceṣṭitena yāvad virocana-nimlocanāvasaraṃ vāsaraṃ gamayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said joyfully: 'Then tonight itself, let this blameless art be presented!' Taking them by both arms, he led them to the assembly of friends, and with conduct enveloped in abundant curiosity, he passed the day until the time of the sun's setting.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
gardabhāsura-mardanaṃ nāma
caturdaśaṃ pūraṇam
 ||14||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Fourteenth Chapter, named
'The Crushing of the Donkey-Demon (<s>Gardabhāsura</s>).'
||14||

children.text: atha pañcadaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Fifteenth Chapter.

children.text: apūrvānurāga-caryā-jāgaryā
children.translated_text: The Awakening to Unprecedented Love.

children.text: atha goloka-yuva-rājaḥ sakhibhiḥ saha rājamānaḥ, sāyaṃ pratyavasāya, mātur ājñām ādāya, valita-prabhāyāṃ gopa-rāja-sabhāyāṃ prati-rajanī-janita-sarvāyata-parvākṛtābhiprāye prahara-prāye gurūn anujñāpya, tad anyān prasthāpya, mahāntaḥ-puraṃ prāpya, prasū-nideśam avāpya, subala-madhu-maṅgalādibhir antaraṅga-saṅgibhiḥ saṅgataḥ sūtāṅga-jātābhyāṃ ca tābhyām anugataḥ prāg-varṇita-gokula-kamala-patra-sthitaṃ parama-sukha-satratayā pramitaṃ śrī-rādhārāma-dhāma jagāma |
children.translated_text: Then the prince of <s>Goloka</s>, resplendent with his friends, having concluded the evening, having taken his mother's leave, when the assembly of the king of the cowherds had acquired its glow — with the intention that was fully formed for the festival occurring on each night in its entirety — having obtained permission from his elders at the approximate completion of the first watch of night, having dispatched the others, having reached the great inner quarters, having received his mother's instructions, accompanied by his intimate companions <s>Subala</s>, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, and others, and followed by those two sons of bard lineage, he went to the abode of the glorious <s>Rādhā-rāma</s> — situated upon the previously described lotus-petal of <s>Gokula</s>, designated as the site of supreme blissful sacrifice.

children.text:
akasmād āgate ca tasmin sasmita-krīḍā-narma-juṣām amūṣāṃ sambhrama-bhrama-vismaya-smaya-trapā-patrapādarādara-harṣa-tarṣādayas te bhāvā yugapad eva samutpannāś citrīyamāṇatāṃ citrāyamāṇatām apy āceruḥ | atra ca,
  akasmād āyāntaṃ harim anubhavantī kila hriyā
  daśām akṣṇor nānā-drutam apidadhe sā nata-mukhī |
  mudā smerā bhugnā vikasitavatī kuñcitavatī
  sa-bāṣpā stabdhābhābhavad iti samaṃ yā na ghaṭate ||JGc_1,15.1|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
And when he arrived unexpectedly, among those maidens who delighted in smiling, playful, jesting sport, the sentiments of flurry, confusion, wonder, delight, modesty, bashfulness, reverence, eagerness, and the like arose all at once and assumed a state of being both painted and being painted. And here:
When she experienced <s>Hari</s> arriving unexpectedly, out of shyness,
she covered the state of her eyes in various rapid ways, her face lowered;
smiling with joy, bent and yet blossoming, contracted and yet expanding,
tearful and yet motionless — she became [all these] simultaneously, in a way that does not cohere! ||15.1|| [mandākrāntā]

children.text: atha praguṇa-guṇālaṅkṛtā kiṅkarī-tatir vitasti-daghna-rāṅkavās taraṇena tam ativistīrṇaṃ maṇi-kīrṇam alindam āstīrṇaṃ cakre | āstīrṇasya ca tasya pratīcī-pracita-sulalita-tulikāyāṃ prācī-mukhatayā svayaṃ niviśamānaḥ śubhratārāma-cāmarādi-karābhiḥ kiṅkarībhiḥ sevyamānaḥ śrī-rādhāyā bahir api virājamāna-prāṇaḥ pāṇinā tām ādāya sva-rasa-milita-tadīya-rasa-veṇī-samāplavana-jīvanānāṃ śreṇī-kṛtānām eṇīdṛśāṃ gaṇāgra-deśa-gatatayā vāma-deśe niveśayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then a row of maidservants, adorned with excellent qualities, wearing carpets a span-length thick, spread out that very spacious jewel-strewn terrace. And on the western side of that spread-out [terrace], on a most delicately beautiful cushion, seating himself facing eastward, attended by maidservants bearing white <s>tāla</s>-palm fans, <s>cāmara</s> whisks, and the like — he whose vital breath shone forth externally even in <s>Rādhā</s> — taking her by the hand, placed her at the foremost position of the rows of doe-eyed maidens, life-giving streams of the confluence of her own <s>rasa</s> merged with his <s>rasa</s>, on his left side.

children.text: dakṣiṇatas tu kevala-tadīya-nava-taruṇimāvatāra-samucita-sevā-prakāra-kāmanārāma-prathama-vayasaḥ subalādi-savayasaḥ | [5] yat-paṅkti-dvayāntima-sīma-madhya-gatau tan-mithunābhimukhatābhiratau tādṛśa-praṇaya-sukumārau sūta-kumārau tasthatuḥ, yayo rāga-tālādi-sāhāyakāḥ sakhāya eva kecana sacante sma |
children.translated_text: And to the right, solely those age-mates of the first youth — <s>Subala</s> and others — suited to the mode of service appropriate to the descent of her ever-new youthfulness. [5] At the midpoint of the final boundary of those two rows, stationed facing that couple with devoted affection — those two bard-youths, tender as that same love — stood; and certain friends who assisted them with <s>rāga</s> (melody), <s>tāla</s> (rhythm), and the like were present.

children.text: yau khalu dvayor api tayoḥ savayasām āvalyor ardha-maṇisara-vallyor ivāgrima-sīma-madhyam adhikṛtya mithaḥ śobhā-vinimaya-śīlatayā nīla-pītatā-viveka-vyatireka-maya-mahā-nāyakāyamānaṃ sarvatra prathita-dṛṣṭi-prasādam api mithaḥ samarpita-netra-tribhāga-rāgaṃ tan-mithunam avalokayantau dvi-tra-kṣaṇaṃ citravad ivāsthiṣātām |
children.translated_text: Those two indeed, gazing at that couple — seated at the foremost midpoint of both rows of age-mates like the front-ends of two half-necklaces — [the couple] whose nature was to exchange beauty mutually, who despite being manifestly the great hero whose grace of vision was famous everywhere in the distinction of blue and yellow, had their three-part gaze of mutual affection directed toward each other — those two [bards] remained for two or three moments as if they were paintings.

children.text: tataś ca prahasya nava-ghana-śyāmenādi-śyamānatayā sāvadhānatāṃ dadhānāv ānandād ubhāv eva saṃhitāñjali-karau nāndī-karau babhūvatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, laughing, as the dark-cloud-hued one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) caused them to assume attentiveness through his primordial gentleness, both of them, from joy, with hands joined in <s>añjali</s>, became performers of the <s>Nāndī</s> (benedictory invocation).

children.text: tatra vastu-nirdeśaḥ-
children.translated_text: There, the indication of the subject matter:

children.text:
imau gaurī-śyāmau manasi viparītau bahir api
  sphurat tat-tad-vastrāv iti budha-janair niścitam idam |
  sa ko' py accha-premā vilasad-ubhaya-sphūrtikatayā
  dadhan mūrti-bhāvaṃ pṛthag apṛthag apy āvirudabhūt ||JGc_1,15.2|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'These two — fair and dark — are reversed within the mind and externally too,
shining with their respective garments — thus is it determined by the wise.
That certain pure, transparent love, by the flashing manifestation of both,
assuming embodied form, became manifest both separately and inseparably!' ||15.2|| [śikhariṇī]

children.text:
atha namaskriyā,
  śrīr āsāṃ na tulāṃ bibharti nitarām ity uddhavaḥ kīrtayan
  yāsām aṅghri-rajo nanāma hariṇā yaḥ svena tulyo mataḥ |
  tāsāṃ tat-priyatā-sudhākara-tanuṃ viṣvak cakorāyite-
  nānenānugatāṃ samasta-mahitāṃ vandāvahe rādhikām ||JGc_1,15.3|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitā]
children.translated_text:
Then, the salutation:
'The beauty (<s>Śrī</s>) of these [<s>gopīs</s>] does not bear comparison at all' — thus <s>Uddhava</s> proclaimed,
and he, whom <s>Hari</s> himself considered equal to himself, bowed to the foot-dust of those [<s>gopīs</s>];
among those [<s>gopīs</s>], we salute <s>Rādhikā</s> — the moon-body of his belovedness,
followed by [all others], honored by all — as the entire universe becomes a <s>cakora</s> bird [gazing at her]! ||15.3|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
athāśīḥ,
  premā yo' sau rādhikā-kṛṣṇa-yugmaṃ
  svānandena plāvayitvā sakhīś ca |
  śaśvad viśvaṃ plāvayan suprasiddhaḥ
  so' yaṃ buddhiṃ naḥ samiddhāṃ karotu ||JGc_1,15.4|| [śāliṇī]
children.translated_text:
Then, the benediction:
'May that love which, having flooded the couple of <s>Rādhikā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
with its own bliss, and their friends too,
constantly flooding the universe, is supremely renowned —
may it make our intellects fully kindled!' ||15.4|| [śālinī]

children.text: iti parasparaṃ sa-vailakṣya-smitam īkṣitvā sthitayos tayoḥ snigdhakaṇṭha eva sotkaṇṭham uvāca-
children.translated_text: Thus, having exchanged glances with an embarrassed smile, while those two (<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) stood [still], <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> himself spoke with eager longing:

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇa-janmādi-mādhuryavad eva śrī-rādhikāyās tat-tan-mādhurī varṇanīyeti nirṇaye' py ativistīrṇatā-saṅkocanāya kiñcid eva sūcayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Now, just as the sweetness of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> birth and other [episodes], so too the various aspects of sweetness of the glorious <s>Rādhikā</s> ought to be described. Yet, for the contraction of excessive expansiveness, we shall indicate only a little.'

children.text:
tatra śrīmad--bhāgavate khalv etad udbhāvitam-
  tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarva-samṛddhimān |
  harer nivāsātma-guṇai ramā-krīḍam abhūn nṛpa ||iti|| [BhP 10.5.18]
tac caivaṃ viśadayanti-
children.translated_text: And they elucidate this as follows:

children.text:
janmārabhya harer vraja-sthalam abhūd viśva-rddhi-yuktaṃ punar
  lakṣmīṇāṃ ramaṇāspadaṃ ca tad-adhiṣṭhānād viśiṣyājani |
  rādhā yāsu lalāsa pūrṇa-śaśabhṛn-mūrtīva tārāsu sā
  kāntiḥ kintv iha citra-bhāva-valitā yā kṛṣṇa-pakṣādhikā ||JGc_1,15.5|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'From the birth of <s>Hari</s>, the land of <s>Vraja</s> became endowed with universal prosperity; moreover,
it became the resort of <s>Lakṣmīs</s> — and from his presiding there, it was especially born;
among those [<s>Lakṣmīs</s>], <s>Rādhā</s>, who delighted them, like the full moon among stars —
that radiance, however, enfolded in wondrous sentiments, was greater on <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> side!' ||15.5|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: bṛhad-gautamīye' py eṣā sarvato labdha-viśeṣā prastūyate-
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bṛhad-gautamīya</s> too, she is celebrated as distinguished above all:

children.text:
devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā |
  sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ sammohinī parā ||iti |
children.translated_text:
'The Goddess is declared to be <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-formed — <s>Rādhikā</s> is the supreme deity;
she is the embodiment of all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, all radiance, the supreme enchantress.'

children.text: alaṃ-lakṣmīṇām etad-ādīnāṃ lakṣmīṇāṃ janma ca śrīmat-parjanyam ārabhya dhanyatayā labhyasya puruṣa-trayasya paramātula-stotrāṇāṃ mātula-gotrāṇāṃ ye khalv āmuṣyāyaṇa-kulatā-nirbandhinaḥ sambandhinas tebhya eveti māgadhānām anusandhānaṃ sa-yatnī-bhūya yajña-patnīs tyaktavatas tasya tathāvyakta-maryādatānyathā na paryāptatām āpadyate |
children.translated_text: The birth of these <s>Lakṣmīs</s> — these and other such <s>Lakṣmīs</s> — beginning from the glorious <s>Parjanya</s>, and through the blessed attainment of the triad of men whose praises by the supremely venerable maternal uncle and whose maternal clan names are bound to the <s>āmuṣyāyaṇa</s> (distinguished lineage) ancestry — is indeed from those very [sources]. The investigation by the <s>Māgadhas</s> (genealogists) — having become diligent, by the one who rejected the wives of the sacrificers — does not otherwise attain completeness without [noting] his thus-undisclosed boundaries.

children.text: tad evaṃ sthiteṣu ca śrī-rādhikāyās tu sarvato' py āḍhya-kulīnāś chrīmad-vṛṣabhānutayā labdha-khyātikān mahā-gopa-payonidher janma sammatam |
children.translated_text: This being the case, the birth of the glorious <s>Rādhikā</s>, from the great cowherd-ocean who had gained renown through the glorious <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, of wealthy and noble family from every side, is acknowledged.

children.text: atra copagāyanti-
children.translated_text: And here they sing:

children.text:
satyaṃ bahu-suta-ratnā- karatāṃ na prāpa gopa-dugdhābdhiḥ |
  kintv amṛta-dyuti-rādhā- lakṣmī-jananād agāt pūrtim ||JGc_1,15.6|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
'Indeed, the cowherd milk-ocean did not attain the status of being rich in many son-jewels;
but from the birth of the <s>Lakṣmī</s> named <s>Rādhā</s>, of nectar-like radiance, it attained completeness!' ||15.6|| [āryā]

children.text: sā khalu śrī-kṛṣṇa-janma-varṣānantara-varṣe sarva-sukha-satre rādhā-nāmni nakṣatre jāteti rādhābhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: She was indeed born in the year following the year of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> birth, during the great sacrifice of all happiness, under the constellation called <s>Rādhā</s> (Viśākhā) — hence she is called <s>Rādhā</s>.

children.text: janmānantaraṃ tasyāḥ san-mādhurī ceyaṃ kṛtāvalokena lokena kīdṛg iti pṛcchataḥ prati nirūpitā-
children.translated_text: The excellence of her sweetness after birth was assessed by the people who had come to behold [her], in response to those who asked 'What is she like?' — as follows:

children.text:
navendur mūrtir vā kanaka-kamalaṃ vaktram athavā
  cakorau netre vā visarad-amṛtaṃ dṛṣṭir athavā |
  apītthaṃ rādhāyāṃ yadi jita-tulāyāṃ na valate
  vikalpaḥ kiṃ tarhi prasajatitarāṃ tat-tad-upamā ||JGc_1,15.7|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'Is her form a new moon? Or is her face a golden lotus?
Are her eyes <s>cakora</s> birds? Or is her gaze flowing nectar?
Even if [comparisons] thus applied to <s>Rādhā</s> — who has defeated all scales of comparison —
do not hold, what then? All the more do those respective similes proliferate!' ||15.7|| [śikhariṇī]

children.text: āstāṃ tāvad asau vraja-lakṣmīṇāṃ parama-lakṣmīr akhilāś ca tās tathā varṇyante | yathā-
children.translated_text: Let that be — she is the supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the <s>Lakṣmīs</s> of <s>Vraja</s>, and all those [<s>Lakṣmīs</s>] are likewise described. As follows:

children.text:
harim anu vindati śaśval lakṣmīr iti yā tu sarvataḥ khyātā |
  tām api kila gopāyituṃ gopī-saṃjñā jayanti tā lakṣmyaḥ ||JGc_1,15.8|| [āryā*]
children.translated_text:
'That <s>Lakṣmī</s> who is celebrated everywhere as she who always follows <s>Hari</s> —
even her, those <s>Lakṣmīs</s> called <s>Gopīs</s> (cowherd-women) surpass in concealing (protecting) her!' ||15.8|| [āryā]

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text:
kṛṣṇānurūpam apy āsāṃ vayo-vṛddhiḥ samṛddhyate |
  yathā candramasaḥ puṣṭis tathā tasya rucām api ||JGc_1,15.9|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'The growth of age of these [<s>gopīs</s>] too flourishes in proportion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
just as [there is] the waxing of the moon, so too [there is the growth] of his radiances!' ||15.9|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tatra kaumāra-madhyam adhyāsīnāyāṃ śrī-rādhikāyāṃ tadānītanānāṃ keṣāñcin nārī-janānām utprekṣā yathā-paśya paśya,
  aruṇita-laghu-śāṭī-khaṇḍa-kamrādharāṅgī
  śravaṇa-galava-randhra-prota-susparśa-sūtrā |
  rajasi nija-sakhībhiḥ krīḍayā lola-netrā
  madhuri-purati-bīja-śrī-nibhā bhāti rādhā ||JGc_1,15.10|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
There, when the glorious <s>Rādhikā</s> was in the midst of her childhood, the fancy of certain women of that time was as follows — 'Look, look!'
'With reddened small garment-fragment, with lovely reddish-hued limbs,
with a pleasant-to-touch string threaded through the holes of ear and throat,
with darting eyes playing with her own girlfriends in the dust —
<s>Rādhā</s> shines like the seed-beauty of the city of <s>Madhura</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>)!' ||15.10|| [mālinī]

children.text: tad evam īdṛg-vayasi paryavasite tadādīnāṃ tāsāṃ saundarya-sārasya pracāraḥ sarvata eva prasarpan mātara-pitarādibhir nāpasarpayitum īśāñcakre cintayāmāse ca, na jānīmahe, durjanaḥ kaṃsaḥ kiṃ samprati sampratipatsyate iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, when such an age had been completed, the spreading of the essence of beauty of those [<s>gopīs</s>] from that time onward, pervading everywhere, could not be turned away even by mothers, fathers, and others. And they reflected: 'We do not know what the wicked <s>Kaṃsa</s> will now contrive!'

children.text: atha pratyaham eva pratyekam antaḥ paraspara-militāḥ santaś ca te sarve vicāritavantaḥ, sāmpratam eva pātrasātkartum etāḥ sāmprataṃ | tatrāpy āsāṃ śrīman-nanda-nandanād avaras tu na varatām arhati | avara eva hi sarvaḥ | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Then, every day, each of them, having met one another privately within, all deliberated: 'Right now these [maidens] must be made worthy vessels [for marriage] right now!' And in that regard, none inferior to the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s> deserved the status of bridegroom for them. For indeed, every [other suitor] was inferior. As follows:

children.text:
kanyā dhanyatamā ramām api jitāṃ kurvanty amūr nandajaḥ
  svasmād ūnadaśāṃ ramā-ramaṇam apy āsādayan dṛśyate |
  tasmāt tulyatayā sa eva varatām arhaty amūṣāṃ tadapy
  āstāṃ dhāma-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇā hi nas tatkṛte ||JGc_1,15.11|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
These most blessed girls make even <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) appear conquered; and the son of <s>Nanda</s>
is seen to bring even the consort of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) to a state lesser than himself;
therefore, by equality, he alone deserves to be the bridegroom for these girls — yet even that aside,
for he is our home, friend, beloved, self, son, and life-breath! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: atha, yadyapy adhunā yajña-sūtram alabdhavatas tasya na vivāhāvasaraḥ sambhavati, tathāpi sajjana-samājñām ācārya bhāṣā-bandhaś ca sandhātavya iti |
children.translated_text: Now, although the occasion for his marriage cannot arise since he has not yet received the sacred thread (<s>yajña-sūtra</s>), nevertheless, the verbal agreement should be arranged in accordance with the custom of the good community.

children.text: tad etad vicārya sthitānāṃ teṣāṃ niścayāvadhāraṇa-pūrvakaṃ tan nivāraṇaṃ prati pūrvavad eva vasudeva-mantraṇayā yantrita-vicāra-vargatayāpi gargaḥ sarva-darśitayā tad idaṃ parāmamarśa-
children.translated_text: Thus, when those who had been deliberating stood firm, for the purpose of preventing that [marriage plan], <s>Garga</s>, whose group of deliberations was controlled as before by <s>Vasudeva's</s> counsel, with his all-seeing vision, reflected upon this:

children.text: tal-līlā-kramaḥ khalv ayaṃ duratyayatayā mayāsugamas tal-līlā-śakti-prayutānām asmākaṃ ca tatra pratyag-vadācaraṇe' pi nāradavan na pratyavāyas, tathāpi tathā prathanīyam yathā tāsāṃ na pratyavāyaḥ syād, āyatyām iṣṭāpattiḥ syād, akhilāyatyāṃ pūrna-tad-āpattiś ca syāt iti |
children.translated_text: 'This sequence of his pastimes is indeed difficult to surpass and hard for me to follow; and for us who are endowed with the power of his pastimes, even in acting contrary [to convention], there is no transgression — as with <s>Nārada</s>. Nevertheless, things should be arranged in such a way that there would be no transgression for these [girls], that the desired outcome would come about in the future, and that in the complete future, the full attainment of that [outcome] would come to be.'

children.text: tad evaṃ vimṛśan sa kila vilambam anavalambamānaḥ śrī-vrajam ājagāma | āgamya ca nijam uṭaja-taṭaṃ sa-dhyānam adhyāsīnāṃ paurṇamāsīṃ prati jagāma | gatvā ca sarvam evedaṃ nivedya punar nivedayāmāsa, mayedaṃ tāvat kartavyam, bhavatyā tu tāsāṃ yathānyatra patyādi-vyavahāraḥ satyāya na kalpate, kintu loka-pratyāyana-mātrāya tathā vyavahartavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Thus deliberating, not holding to delay, he came to the glorious <s>Vraja</s>. Having arrived, he went to <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, who was seated meditatively at her own hermitage-bank. Going [there] and reporting everything, he further stated: 'This much is to be done by me; but by your ladyship, [it should be arranged] so that the transaction of husband and such for those [girls] elsewhere does not become real, but should be conducted merely for worldly appearances.'

children.text: tad evaṃ tāṃ sambhāṣya śrīmad-vrajarāja-sambhāṣaṇaṃ nirvāhya, bāhyāvaraṇa-vāsinām āvāseṣu babhrāma | te ca tam āgatam akasmān niśāmya śāmyac-cintā-tamasaḥ sva-sva-manoratha-labdhaye lubdha-manasaḥ praṇāmādibhiḥ paripūjya kuśalam anuyujya pracchannatayā tam evārthaṃ papracchuḥ, idaṃ tāvac chaṅkitaṃ; tatra kiṃ kartavyam? iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, having conversed with her and carried out the conversation with the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, he wandered to the dwellings of those living in the outer enclosure. And they, suddenly hearing of his arrival, their darkness of anxiety abating, their minds eager to obtain their respective heart's desires, having honored him with obeisances and the like, inquiring about his well-being, secretly asked him about that very matter: 'This much is our apprehension — what is to be done about it?'

children.text: sa tūvāca-vayam idaṃ sarvam apūrvaṃ pūrvam api jānīmahe | idaṃ ca bhavadbhiḥ sambaddhyam adhyavasitam, kintv ekā śaṅkā śaṅkur iva maṅkṣu hṛdi parivartate | yadā bhavad-aṅga-jātāṅganānāṃ vraja-rājāṅgaja-vara-kumāreṇa saha saṅgamaḥ syāt, tadā nātivilamabataḥ sarvasyāpi vrajasya tadīya-cira-vipralambha-lambhanaṃ bhavitā, kim utāmūṣām? kiṃ ca, prauḍhatām ūḍhavatīnāṃ tu sahaja-tad-anurāga-svābhāvyenādarśane' py udbhavat-tat-sphūrtīnāṃ na ko' pi tasmād vinivartanaṃ kartuṃ samarthaḥ syād ity api kadarthanāntaraṃ bhaviṣyati | tasmān nanda-kulāvataṃsāt kaṃsāc ca vañcayituṃ cañcalam evānyebhyaḥ sampradātavyā navyāḥ kanyakāḥ |
children.translated_text: He said: 'We already know all of this unprecedented [situation]. And this has been aptly resolved by you. But one apprehension revolves in the heart swiftly like a spike. When the union of the young women born of your families with the excellent young prince born of the king of <s>Vraja</s> should come to be, then before long, for all of <s>Vraja</s> too, the attainment of prolonged separation from him will follow — how much more so for those girls! Moreover, when those who have attained maturity, by the naturalness of their innate love for him, experience spontaneous manifestations [of that love] even without seeing [him], no one would be capable of turning them back from that — and this will be yet another vexation. Therefore, to deceive the ornament of <s>Nanda's</s> family and <s>Kaṃsa</s> alike, the new girls should be quickly given away to others!'

children.text: tad evam ādiśya prasthite yadu-purohite tat-kṛtopadeśopajātādaro nija-nija-kanyā-gopana-paro gopa-nikaro' pi tāsāṃ sampradānāya sampradānam anveṣṭuṃ suṣṭhu cintām avāpa, kintu santatam asya sā lālasā tu nālasā jātā |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>Yadu</s> family-priest (<s>Garga</s>) had departed after giving these instructions, the group of cowherds, having developed respect born of his instructions and being devoted to the concealment of their respective daughters, also attained much anxiety in seeking recipients for their bestowal — but their longing for him (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) remained continually undiminished.

children.text: tad evam etāsāṃ sva-tanayena pariṇayanaṃ prati vrajapati-jampatī ca pūrvam atīva tīvra-spṛhā-gṛhīta-cittāv āstām | viśeṣatas tu rādhāyā mādhurya-viśeṣāvadhāraṇataḥ | kintu gargeṇa tadvad eva nirastāv ity astamita-prayatnāv abhūtām |
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding the marriage of their own son with these [girls], the royal couple of <s>Vraja</s> had previously been seized by extremely intense desire in their hearts — especially due to the recognition of <s>Rādhā's</s> special sweetness. But having been similarly rejected by <s>Garga</s>, they became ones whose efforts had set [like the sun].

children.text: anutāpas tu tayor nāpajagāma, tad-bhrātṛ-paryāyāś ca tad ekānugati-maryādayā paryākulās tāsāṃ kanyānām sva-putrāya nyāsam anyāyaṃ manyamānās tataḥ parāṅ-mukhā babhūvuḥ | kiṃ bahunā? sarva eva kevala-snehatas tatra kṛṣṇa-varatāyām eva jātehatāṃ saṃhitavantaḥ samadṛśyanta | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Yet their remorse did not depart. And those who were in the position of brothers [to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], agitated by the standard of exclusive allegiance to him, considering the entrusting of those girls to their own sons as an impropriety, turned away from that. In short, everyone, solely out of affection, was seen to have invested their very lives in the prospect of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> being the bridegroom there. For:

children.text:
yogyena yogyasya tu nitya-saṅgamaḥ
  kasmai na roceta bhṛśaṃ sa-cetase |
  ratnena hemnaḥ śaradā saro' mbhasaḥ
  sitākhya-pakṣeṇa yathā sudhā-ruceḥ ||JGc_1,15.12|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
The eternal union of the worthy with the worthy —
who among the intelligent would not greatly relish that?
As of a jewel with gold, of autumn with lake-waters,
as of the bright fortnight with the moon! // [upajāti]

children.text: varatā-sambhāvanā-viṣayāṇāṃ pitṛ-vargaś ca tādṛg apy anargala-karṇe-japa-labdha-saṃsarga-garga-vacana-sargata eva bhinna-cittatām āpa | [34] putrān apy atikramya tatra sthitānāṃ kṛṣṇa eva hi sukhasatrāyate |
children.translated_text: And the father-group of those who were the subjects of the prospect of his being bridegroom, even though [determined] thus, attained a divided mind solely from the utterances of <s>Garga</s>, acquired through the unstoppable whispering-in-the-ear contact. [34] Surpassing even [concern for] their own sons, for those who stood there, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone was the source of the sacrificial feast of happiness.

children.text: tad evaṃ jñāta-rahasyo' pi nirṇīta-nīti-praṇītaye rahasi vraja-rājam upavrajya sa ca tat-pitṛ-vargaḥ pratisvam eva tam artham arthayāmāsa, [36] āmuṣyakulikā kalitā dhanyāḥ khalu tāḥ kanyāḥ kṛṣṇanyāsata eva sa-nyāyatām arhanti | sa yadi bhavadbhiḥ svayam aṅgīkriyate, tadā bhaṅgībhiḥ prasaṅgam aṅgīkriyatām asmābhir iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, though knowing the secret, for the purpose of carrying out the determined policy, the father-group, approaching the king of <s>Vraja</s> privately, each entreated him regarding that very matter: [36] 'Those girls of such distinguished lineage — those blessed maidens — surely deserve to be properly entrusted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone. If he is accepted by your honors of your own accord, then let the occasion be accepted by us through indirect means.'

children.text: vrajarājas tu tad ākarṇyam ākarṇya sa-niśvāsam idaṃ vivarṇatayā varṇitavān, asmābhiḥ sva-putrāya sarvathā na te sambandhāḥ sandhātavyāḥ, kintu yūyam apīdaṃ vidāṃkurute | yat khalu yuṣmākam apatyāni yuṣmākam ivāsmākaṃ sneha-sātatya-vahāni samudvāhayitavyāni ca, tasmād asmābhir eva tatra tatra satrā-kurvadbhiḥ prayatanīyam |
children.translated_text: But the king of <s>Vraja</s>, hearing that and sighing, spoke with a pallid expression: 'By us, the marriage-connections with our own son should by no means be arranged by them. But you too should know this: that your children, who sustain the continuity of affection like our own, are also to be married by us. Therefore, we ourselves, making the sacrificial arrangements here and there, should make the effort.'

children.text: tad evaṃ sthagita-samullāse nikhile ca vrajāvāse vrajapaty-anumaty-anusāratas tāsāṃ pitaras tad-vitaram ācarituṃ ruciṃ vināpi bahir udyamam ācaritavantaḥ | [39] tat kumāryas tv atibālya-caryā-paryākulatayā na kiñcid api cid-amatratāṃ ninyire |
children.translated_text: Thus, when all delight in the entire <s>Vraja</s>-settlement was suppressed, following the permission of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, the fathers of those [girls], even without relish, conducted the external effort to carry out that different [arrangement]. [39] But the young maidens, being engrossed in the activities of extreme childhood, did not bring any awareness whatsoever to that matter.

children.text: atha yā kācid vṛndāvana-gahvarataḥ sākṣāt kila yogamāyāyā vyājatas tāpasyās tatra cāhvayataḥ paurṇamāsyāḥ samabhyarṇaṃ ahar-divaṃ prāyaḥ kimapi mantrāyituṃ āgantrī dṛśyate; yā ca mānuṣy api devīyamāneti vā devy api mānuṣīyamāṇeti vā lakṣayituṃ na śakyate kintu sad-ānukūlatayā tad-vana-pālitāsiṣā-dhayiṣita-kṛṣṇa-līlatā rādhādiṣu ca parama-sneha-latā yasyām anumīyate, sā vṛndāriketi nijākhyāṃ prakhyāpayanty api jana-vṛndena lāghavād vṛndeti svenaiva nāmnā samāmnāyate | sā ca samprati sarva-śocyatā-maya-tad-vārtā-śravaṇād atīvārtā tad-abhyāsam evābhyajagāma |
children.translated_text: Now, there was one who, from the depths of the <s>Vṛndāvana</s> forest, directly — under the pretext of <s>Yogamāyā</s> herself — as an ascetic woman, summoned by <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> there, was seen coming almost daily for some kind of consultation; and who could not be determined as either 'a human woman becoming divine' or 'a divine woman becoming human,' but in whom, by her excellent benevolence, the quality of being a guardian of that forest, a nurturer of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> pastimes through blessings, and a creeper of supreme affection toward <s>Rādhā</s> and the others was inferred — she, though proclaiming her own name as <s>Vṛndārikā</s>, was conventionally called <s>Vṛndā</s> by the people, by abbreviation of her own name. And she now, having heard the tidings full of all-pitifulness, extremely distressed, came to the very vicinity [of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>].

children.text: abhyāgatām atha tāṃ japārtham āsīnāpi, paurṇamāsī tūrṇam upavrajya namaskurvatīṃ pariṣvajya śubhāśiṣā ca saṃyujya svacchamanāḥ papracchuḥ, kathyatāṃ katham asamayam idaṃ tava samāgamanam? iti |
children.translated_text: Then, though <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> was seated for her recitation, upon her approach she swiftly went to meet her, embraced the bowing one, and, joining her with auspicious blessings, asked with a clear mind: 'Tell me — how is this untimely arrival of yours?'

children.text: vṛndāha-bhagavati, param āpadāṃ padam ekam utpannam asti, kathaṃ tava niścintatā dṛśyate?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'O Venerable One, a singular abode of calamities has arisen — how is it that your serenity is apparent?'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-kiṃ tāvac cintā-kāraṇaṃ tat-padam?
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'What is that abode which is the cause for such worry?'

children.text:
vṛndāha-hanta, yāḥ khalu nityatayā kṛṣṇasya preyasya iti śrūyante, tāsām apy anya-sambandhaḥ sanirbandha iva dṛśyate |
[45] paurṇamāsī uvāca-katham ivāyaṃ parāmṛśyate?
children.translated_text:
<s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Alas! Those who are always heard of as the beloveds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — even their connection with others appears to be insistently [proceeding]!'
[45] <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'How is this being considered?'

children.text: vṛndāha-tasyānubandhaś cakṣuṣā spṛśyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'The process of that [arrangement] is being touched by the eye [i.e., visibly perceived].'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-na bhaviṣyati tāsām anyenānyena saṃyoga-sambandhaḥ, yato mayā hi māyayā parā nirmāya nirmāsyate tatra pratibandhaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'There shall be no connection of union with any other for those [girls], because by me, through <s>Māyā</s>, having fashioned a supreme [illusion], the obstruction shall be created there.'

children.text: vṛndāha-atha tathāpi lokataḥ kalaṅkaḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'But even so, stigma from the world is to be apprehended.'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-na syād api tasyāpi sthitiḥ, yato munayaḥ punar idaṃ gāsyanti-
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'There shall be no permanence even of that, because the sages will hereafter sing this:

children.text:
nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya
mohitās tasya māyayā |
  manyamānāḥ sva-pārśva-sthān
svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ ||[BhP 10.33.39] iti |
children.translated_text: the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers!' // [BhP 10.33.39]

'They did not censure <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
being deluded by his <s>Māyā</s>,
considering their own wives to be standing beside them —

children.text: ataeva putrotpatty-abhāvāt pāyayantyaḥ śiśūn payaḥ ity atra śiśūn ity eva payaḥ ity eva ca vakṣyanti, na tu sutān stanam iti | etad apekṣayaiva kvacit putratva-vyapadeśaś ca śrī-kṛṣṇa-parihāsa-nirdeśaś ca saṅgaṃsyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, due to the absence of offspring, when it is said 'they nourished children with milk' — there 'children' will be stated, and 'milk' will be stated, but not 'sons' and 'breast.' In consideration of this very fact, the designation of sonship and the jesting indication of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> will be accommodated in certain places.

children.text: vṛndāha-yady evaṃ tarhy anyena tāsāṃ pāṇipīḍanaṃ punar atīva pīḍanam | yatra prāyaścittāntaram api na cintayanti tantra-vidaḥ, tat kathaṃ sāmprataṃ sva-vratam upekṣase?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'If so, then the hand-grasping (marriage) of those [girls] by another is extremely painful! Where the knowers of <s>tantra</s> do not even consider another atonement — how then do you now disregard your own vow?'

children.text: paurṇamāsī sasmitam uvāca-bhāviny, etad api na bhāvi, tvayā tu ramyānanatayā gamyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said with a smile: 'O blessed one, this too shall not come to be — but you should go with a delighted face!'

children.text: vṛndā sānandaṃ padāravindayoḥ patantī sānumodaṃ ruroda | sā tu tāṃ niravahittham utthāpya sāntvayitvā gahanāya prasthāpayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, falling at her lotus feet with joy, wept with delight. And she (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), raising her up without concealment and consoling her, dispatched her toward the forest depths.

children.text: atha vṛndāpi tathā viśvasatī niśvasatī ca vitrāsa-rahitā dvitrāho-rātrān gamayāmāsa | dināntare tu tāsām udvāha-nirvāham ākarṇya vivarṇa-vadanā paurṇamāsy-abhyarṇaṃ punar api tūrṇam upasthānā mṛtaka-pratīkā tasthau |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> too, thus trusting yet sighing, without fear, passed two or three days and nights. But on another day, hearing of the completion of their marriages, her face turning pale, she again swiftly stood before <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, appearing like an image of death.

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-kim iva vṛttaṃ vṛttam yasmād bhavaty udvṛtta-cittā dṛśyate?
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'What has happened, what has happened, that you appear with an agitated mind?'

children.text: vṛndāha-mama mukhataḥ kācid apy uktir na vyaktībhavati, kim iva vaktavyam?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Not even a single utterance becomes articulate from my mouth — what is to be said?'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-paṅkajākṣi, na kācid api śaṅkā manasi śaṅkanīyā |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'O lotus-eyed one, no apprehension whatsoever should be apprehended in the mind!'

children.text: vṛndā sa-rūkṣa-hāsam āha-bhagavati, katham iva?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said with a harsh laugh: 'O Venerable One, how so?'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-yad adyāpy asiddha-nirvāha eva tāsāṃ vivāhaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'Because even today, the marriage of those [girls] remains unfulfilled in its completion!'

children.text: vṛndāha-vicakṣaṇe, tam etaṃ cākṣuṣam eva vidhāya sarve' py ācakṣate |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'O discerning one, having made it visible to the eye, everyone declares it so!'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-samprati tā bālikāḥ kutra?
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'Where are those young girls now?'

children.text: vṛndāha-tad idam api śrutam, yad atibālakatayāvagatāḥ pitṛ-geha eva tā nidhāya te gatā iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'This too has been heard — that being understood as extremely young, they have been kept in their fathers' houses, and those [grooms] have departed.'

children.text: paurṇamāsī sa-praṇaya-roṣam uvāca-atha kathaṃ mat-kathanaṃ na pratyeṣi yat kiṃvadantīm eva muhur vadantī vartase?
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said with affectionate anger: 'Then why do you not believe my words, since you continue repeatedly speaking only rumor?'

children.text: vṛndā sānandam uvāca-bhagavati, tad etad ṛtam anṛtam eva bhavatu, kintu mayā nāyaṃ sandhir anusandhīyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said joyfully: 'O Venerable One, let this be true or untrue, but this connection is not being traced by me [i.e., I cannot comprehend it].'

children.text: paurṇamāsī sahāsam uvāca-na lokenātathyaṃ kathyate, na ca grathyate sma tāsām udvāha-bandhah |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said with a laugh: 'The world has not spoken untruth, nor was the marriage-bond of those [girls] tied!'

children.text: vṛndāha-nedaṃ ca budhye |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Even this I do not understand.'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-yuktam evedam, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'This is fitting, because:

children.text:
tvayy api līlā-śaktyām, avasara-nāmnī bhaved vibhoḥ śaktiḥ |
  tvām api yā bhramayantī, tasmiṃs tasmin pravartayati ||JGc_1,15.13|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
Even in you, who are a <s>līlā-śakti</s> (pastime-potency), there would be the Lord's potency
named 'Occasion' (<s>Avasara</s>);
which, bewildering even you, sets things in motion
in this and that [affair]! // [udgīti]

children.text: vṛndā sa-kāku prāha-tarhi svayam evedaṃ rahasyaṃ prakāśyatām?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> spoke imploringly: 'Then let this secret be revealed by you yourself!'

children.text: paurṇamāsī kṣaṇaṃ hasitvā nīcair uvāca-yugapad eva, devi, sarveṣu tādṛg-duḥsvapna eva kevalaṃ jāgara-kalpatayā mayā kalpitaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, having laughed for a moment, spoke softly: 'Simultaneously, O goddess, in all [cases], it was merely such a bad dream, made to appear as wakefulness by me!'

children.text: vṛndā viśvasya niśvasya ca punar uvāca-tathāpi tāsāṃ tathā khyātir api na yuktā |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, trusting and yet sighing, spoke again: 'Even so, such a reputation for those [girls] is not fitting!'

children.text:
paurṇamāsī uvāca-sāpi na bhaviṣyati, yato munaya eva punaḥ punar idaṃ gāsyanti, tatra tapanyāṃ tāḥ pṛcchatīḥ prati durvāsāḥ, sa vo hi svāmī [Gtu 2.27] iti; rāsaprasaṅge ca bhagavān bādarāyaṇiḥ, kṛṣṇavadhvaḥ [BhP 10.33.7] iti; uddhava-sandeśe svayaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa eva ca, ballavyo me madātmikāḥ [BhP 10.46 |3] iti | tad idaṃ gacchoddhava vrajaṃ saumya pitror naḥ prītim āvaha iti vallabhābhimānitām ātmani vyajya śrī-kṛṣṇasya vacanaṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ mama brāhmaṇīty ādivat | tathā, mām eva dayitaṃ preṣṭham ātmānaṃ manasā gatāḥ [BhP 10.46 |4] iti pracuraṃ pracuratārdha-padyena ca tābhir api bahir-dṛṣṭyā paraṃ tatra kvacid upapatitvaṃ pratīyate, śaśvad antar-dṛṣṭyā tu patitvam evānubhūyata iti sūcyate, yathā ca, api bata
madhu-puryāṃ ārya-putro' dhunāste? iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'That [doubt] too will not arise, for the sages themselves will sing this again and again. There, in the <s>Tapanī</s> [Upaniṣad], <s>Durvāsas</s> says to those [gopīs] who asked: "He indeed is your Lord" [Gtu 2.27]; and in the context of the <s>rāsa</s> [dance], the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva) [says]: "the wives of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" [BhP 10.33.7]; and in the message to <s>Uddhava</s>, the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself [says]: "the cowherd women who are absorbed in Me" [BhP 10.46.3]. Thus, the statement "Go, O <s>Uddhava</s>, to <s>Vraja</s>, O gentle one, and bring pleasure to Our parents" — by using the word of one's own beloved — reveals the beloved-status claimed by the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in Himself, like the statement of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like: "my <s>brāhmaṇī</s>." Similarly, "They have gone to Me alone, the beloved, the dearest, the Self, with their minds" [BhP 10.46.4] — and by the copious [use of] half-verses [indicating] copiousness — by them too, though externally the status of paramour (<s>upapatitva</s>) may sometimes appear to be encountered, it is indicated that through the internal vision, it is always the status of husband (<s>patitva</s>) alone that is experienced. As [they say]: "Does the noble one's son now dwell in <s>Madhupurī</s>?"

children.text: athāgame ca mantra-draṣṭāro gopī-padānantaraṃ janety asyānte vallabheti | [72] tad idaṃ tridhā niruktam apy āgamasya rahasya-rītitayā kramāt pūrva-pūrva-pakṣasya tūttara-pakṣatvaṃ vyañjitam | yathā gautamīya-tantre,
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Āgama</s> (tantric scripture), the seers of <s>mantras</s>, after the word <s>gopī</s>, [state] <s>jana</s> (people), and at the end of that, <s>vallabha</s> (beloved lord). [72] This, though etymologized in three ways, reveals — through the esoteric method of the <s>Āgama</s> — that each prior interpretation gradually becomes the subsequent, better interpretation. As in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>:

children.text: gopīti prakṛtiṃ vidyāj janas tattva-samūhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: "'<s>Gopī</s>' one should know as <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature); '<s>jana</s>' is the aggregate of principles (<s>tattvas</s>);

children.text: anayor āśrayo vyāptyā kāraṇatvena ceśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: of these two, the support, by pervading them and being their cause, is the Lord;

children.text: sāndrānandaṃ paraṃ jyotir vallabhatvena kathyate ||
children.translated_text: He is called '<s>Vallabha</s>' (beloved) as the supreme light of concentrated bliss."

children.text: athavā gopī prakṛtir janas tad-aṃśa-maṇḍalam |
children.translated_text: "Or, '<s>gopī</s>' is <s>Prakṛti</s> (the essential energy), '<s>jana</s>' is the circle of her portions;

children.text: anayor vallabhaḥ proktaḥ svāmī kṛṣṇākhya īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the '<s>Vallabha</s>' of these two is declared to be the Lord named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>."

children.text: kārya-kāraṇayor īśaḥ śrutibhis tena gīyate ||
children.translated_text: "The Lord of cause and effect is sung of by the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) for that reason."

children.text:
aneka-janma-siddhānāṃ gopīnāṃ patir eva vā |
nanda-nandana ity uktas trailokyānanda-vardhanaḥ ||iti |
children.translated_text: "Or, He who is the husband of the <s>gopīs</s> perfected through many births — | He is called '<s>Nanda-nandana</s>' (Joy of <s>Nanda</s>), the increaser of the three worlds' bliss."

children.text: atra prathamā prakṛtiḥ pradhānam, dvitīyā svarūpa-śaktiḥ | tattvāni mahad-ādīni aṃśāḥ,
children.translated_text: Here, the first '<s>Prakṛti</s>' means the primordial matter (<s>pradhāna</s>); the second means the essential energy (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>). The principles (<s>tattvas</s>) are the <s>mahat</s> and so forth; the portions (<s>aṃśas</s>) are:

children.text: jñāna-śakti-balaiśvarya-vīrya-tejāṃsy aśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: "Knowledge, power, strength, sovereignty, valor, and splendor — in their entirety

children.text: bhagavac-chabda-vācyāni vinā heyair guṇādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are denoted by the word '<s>Bhagavat</s>' (the Lord), excluding the inferior qualities and the like."

children.text: iti viṣṇu-purāṇoktāḥ [ViP 6.5.79] | aneka-janma-siddhānāṃ iti, bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna [Gītā 4.5] iti śrī-bhagavad-gītā-vadanāditvam eva bodhayati, patir eva iti kadācid upapatitva-vyavahāras tu māyika evety arthaḥ | vā-śabdas tv asyaivottara-pakṣatā-bodhanāya |
children.translated_text: — as stated in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> [ViP 6.5.79]. 'Perfected through many births' indicates [the teaching] from the <s>Śrī Bhagavad Gītā</s>: 'Many births of Mine have passed, and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>' [Gītā 4.5] — it teaches that very statement of the Lord and the like. 'Husband indeed' — meaning that any occasional usage of the paramour relationship (<s>upapatitva</s>) is merely illusory. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) serves to indicate this [third interpretation] as the superior alternative.

children.text: ataevāprakaṭa-līlāyāṃ prakaṭam eva brahma-saṃhitā tathānusaṃhitavatī yatra brahmā prāha-
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in the unmanifest pastime (<s>aprakaṭa-līlā</s>), the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> manifestly corroborates this, where <s>Brahmā</s> declares:

children.text:
ānanda-cin-maya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhis
  tābhir ya eva nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ |
  goloka eva nivasaty akhilātma-bhūto
  govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||iti||[5.48] |
children.translated_text: "With those who are pervaded by the essence of bliss-consciousness-form, | with those very ones who are his own portions in his own essential form — | in <s>Goloka</s> alone does He dwell, the Self of all — | that primeval Person, <s>Govinda</s>, I worship!" || [5.48]

children.text: atra kalātvān nija-rūpatve svataḥ-siddhe' pi nija-rūpatayeti punar upādānam, na tu prakaṭa-līlā-madhyavat parakīyābhāsatayopalakṣitābhis tābhir ity artha-jñāpanārtham |
children.translated_text: Here, though the status of 'own essential form' (<s>nija-rūpatā</s>) is self-established from their being portions (<s>kalās</s>), the repetition 'in his own essential form' (<s>nija-rūpatayā</s>) is not — as in the manifest pastime — to convey the meaning 'with those who are characterized by the appearance of belonging to another' (<s>parakīyābhāsa</s>).

children.text: tathā ca tatraiva śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ ity atra yuktiṃ ca darśitavān | śrī-parama-puruṣayor aupapatyaṃ nāstīti | kāśī-khaṇḍe ca dharma-rājaḥ, gopī-pate yadu-pate vasudeva-sūno iti | saṅgīta-śāstre ca, gopī-patir ananto' pi vaṃśa-dhvani-vaśaṃ gataḥ iti | bhaviṣyat-kāvyeṣu śrī-gīta-govinde patyur manaḥ kīlitam iti |
children.translated_text: And there itself, in the [verse] 'The beloved consorts of <s>Śrī</s>, the supreme Person is the beloved' — [<s>Brahmā</s>] has shown the reasoning: there is no paramour-status (<s>aupapatya</s>) between <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) and the Supreme Person. And in the <s>Kāśī-khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Dharmarāja</s> [says]: 'O lord of the <s>gopīs</s>, lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, son of <s>Vasudeva</s>!' And in the treatise on music (<s>Saṅgīta-śāstra</s>): 'The lord of the <s>gopīs</s>, though infinite, has come under the sway of the flute's sound.' And in the future literary works, in the <s>Śrī Gīta-govinda</s>: 'the mind of the husband is transfixed.'

children.text: etad abhiprāyeṇaiva lakṣya-bhedenoktam-
children.translated_text: With this very intention, it was stated with a difference of focus:

children.text:
tvām aprāpya mayi svayaṃ-vara-parāṃ kṣīroda-tīrodare
  śaṅke sundari kāla-kūṭam apiban mūḍho mṛḍānīpatiḥ |
  itthaṃ pūrva-kathābhir anya-manaso vikṣipya vakṣo' ñcalaṃ
  rādhāyāḥ stana-korakopari milan-netro hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||iti |
children.translated_text: '"Not having obtained You, O beautiful one, who chose her own beloved, on the shore of the Milk-ocean, | I suspect that the foolish lord of <s>Mṛḍānī</s> (Śiva) drank the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison!" | Thus, distracting <s>Rādhā's</s> mind with tales of the past, lifting her bodice, | <s>Hari</s>, his eyes meeting the buds of <s>Rādhā's</s> breasts, may He protect you!'

children.text: anyatra ca, gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamalayor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ iti | bhagavac-chaṅkarācārya-kṛte yamunā-stotre ca, vidhehi tasya rādhikā-dhavāṅghri-paṅkaje ratim iti |
children.translated_text: And elsewhere: 'I am the servant of the servants of the servants of the lotus-feet of the lord of the <s>gopīs</s>.' And in the hymn to the <s>Yamunā</s> composed by the glorious <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>: 'Grant me devotion to the lotus-feet of the beloved of <s>Rādhikā</s>!'

children.text: lalita-mādhave śrī-rādhikādīnāṃ tathā-varṇanaṃ tu sphuṭam eva nirvarṇitam | ujjvala-nīlamaṇau sākṣāt-kathanayā kumārikāṇāṃ sākṣād anya-sambandhābhāva-prathanayā ca parāsām api yad eva samṛddhimad-ākhya-sambhoge lalita-mādhavānusāreṇa sphuṭam aṅgīkṛtam asti |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>, the description of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> and the others is clearly delineated. In the <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>, by direct assertion of the unmarried maidens' direct absence of any other relationship, it is clearly accepted — following the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> — that even for others, the fully prosperous conjugal love (<s>sambhoga</s>) is designated as such.

children.text:
bhāvārtha-dīpikāyāṃ ca, ṛṣabhasya jaguḥ kṛtyāni [BhP 10.33.21] ity atra ṛṣabhasya patyuḥ iti kṛṣṇavadhvaḥ iti svayam uktam idam eva patitvaṃ śrī-parīkṣit-praśnottare paty-antarābhyupagama-vādenaiva hi bahir-aṅgānām bodhāya paramātmatayā śrī-bādarāyaṇinā bodhitam: gopīnāṃ tat-patīnāṃ ca sarveṣām api ca dehinām | yo' ntaś carati so' dhyakṣaḥ eṣa krīḍana-deha-bhāk ||[BhP 10.33.35] ity atrānataraṅgān prati tv ayam arthaḥ: gopīnāṃ kāścid vyūḍhāḥ kāścid avyūḍhā iti dvidhātra loka-mātra-prasiddhānāṃ vastutas tu nitya-siddhānāṃ sarvataḥ śreyasīnāṃ tat-preyasīnām anyāsām api nānā-bhāva-samṛddhānāṃ kumārītaruṇī-vṛddhānāṃ, tathā yathā-sambhavaṃ tāsāṃ patīnāṃ tad-upalakṣitatayā kumāra-tatīnāṃ,
kiṃ bahunā? sarveṣām api tad-eka-jīvānāṃ vraja-jīvānāṃ yāni tat-tad-upacitatācita-tadīya-krīḍā-sādhana-dehāni, tad-āsaktaḥ sann antaḥ-śabdābhihite mahite jagan-netrād antar-hite sadābhave sva-vaibhave yaś carati krīḍati | sa eṣa evādhyakṣaḥ kadācij jagat-pratyakṣaḥ san krīḍati | tasmān nija-preyasībhiḥ samam anādita eva mithunateti kathanād aupapatyam asya nopapatty-arham, kintu parama-vyomādhipa-lakṣmī-nārāyaṇavad dāmpatyam eva tad-arhaṃ bhavatīti |
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Bhāvārtha-dīpikā</s> commentary, on 'they sang the deeds of the Bull' [BhP 10.33.21] — 'of the Bull, the husband' — this very husband-status, stated by [the word] 'wives of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' [BhP 10.33.7], was taught by the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva) in the reply to <s>Śrī Parīkṣit's</s> question, through the doctrine of acceptance of another husband (<s>paty-antarābhyupagama</s>), for the instruction of the externally-oriented, through the <s>Paramātman</s> doctrine: 'He who moves within the <s>gopīs</s>, their husbands, and all embodied beings — He is the Overseer, He has assumed a body for sport' [BhP 10.33.35]. For those of deeper [understanding], however, the meaning is this: the <s>gopīs</s> are of two kinds — some married (<s>vyūḍhā</s>), some unmarried (<s>avyūḍhā</s>) — thus known only in worldly convention, but in reality they are eternally perfect, supreme in all respects, His beloveds; and of the others too, endowed with a variety of <s>bhāvas</s>, whether maidens, young women, or elderly; and likewise, as occasion permits, of their husbands — who are indicated by [association with] them — and of the groups of boys;
in short, of all the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers whose sole life is He — whatever bodies are fashioned and unfashioned as instruments for His various sports — He, being attached to them, in the inner [realm] — denoted by the word 'within' — in the exalted, hidden-from-the-world's-eye eternal self-glory, He moves, He plays. He, this very Overseer, sometimes becoming visible to the world, plays. Therefore, from the statement that He consorts from beginningless time with His own beloveds, paramour-status is not appropriate for Him; rather, just like the Lord <s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s>, the ruler of the supreme abode — it is conjugal status alone that is appropriate.'

children.text: tad idaṃ, jayati jananivāsaḥ [BhP 10.90.48] ity ādau vraja-pura-vanitānāṃ vardhayan kāma-devam iti pura-vanitābhiḥ saha tāsāṃ saha-pāṭhād draṣṭavyam | śrīmān uddhavas tu, etāḥ paraṃ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvaḥ [BhP 10.47.58] ity ādāv āsām anugatiṃ mumukṣu-mukta-mad-vidha-bhaktā api vāñchanti ity uktvā kṛṣṇe paramātmani vṛndāvana-carya imāḥ kva, tad-īdṛśa-bhāva-vyabhicāra-dṛṣṭās tv anye kveti vadan kṛṣṇe paramātmani hy eṣa rūḍha-bhāva iti pratyakṣato darśayann āsu māhātmya-viśeṣaṃ darśayati, nāyaṃ śriyo' ṅge [BhP 10.47.60] ity ādau śrī-prabhṛtibhyaḥ punar api viśeṣayati ca |'
children.translated_text: This should be understood from [the verse] 'Victorious is the dwelling of beings' [BhP 10.90.48] and so forth, where the joint reading of them together with the 'women of <s>Vraja</s>-town, increasing the god of love' shows [their identity]. The glorious <s>Uddhava</s>, however, in 'These cowherd women are the highest of embodied beings on earth' [BhP 10.47.58] and so forth — having said that 'even those seeking liberation, the liberated, and devotees like me desire to follow them,' and then asking 'Where are these [gopīs] who experience such <s>bhāva</s> toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the <s>Paramātman</s> wandering in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, and where are others in whom such deviation of <s>bhāva</s> is observed?' — thus directly showing that toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the <s>Paramātman</s>, the deep-rooted emotion of these [gopīs] is established, he demonstrates their special greatness; in 'This is not [the grace] of <s>Śrī</s> at His side' [BhP 10.47.60] and so forth, he further distinguishes them from <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) and others.'

children.text: atha sānandāpi vṛndā punaḥ papraccha-katham īdṛśī prakriyā nātipriyā, nānyathā kriyate sma bhavatyā? bhavatyāḥ khalu nāśakyaṃ tarkyate |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s>, though delighted, asked again: 'How is it that this arrangement was not more pleasing [to you], and was not made otherwise by your honor? For nothing is inconceivable for your honor.'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-rasa-viśeṣa-sampādayitrī līlāvaśyakatāvasara-vaicitrīyaṃ sītāyā rāvaṇa-gṛha-gativan nāsmābhir apy anyathā kartuṃ śakyate | rasa-viśeṣaś caivam eva saṅgacchate | bhrama-janitatvād aślīlatā-viśliṣṭe para-sambandhasyābhāsa-mātre dṛṣṭe sati tāsāṃ para-nivāraṇa-kuṇṭhitānām utkaṇṭhā-vardhanataḥ sphurad-akharva-sukha-gatyāṃ sarvāyatyāṃ viśrānta-bhrama-nitānta-sthiratā-nirata-kānta-prāptitas tasyātīva dīptatā-prāptir iti | tathā ca bhaviṣyat-kāvyeṣu śrīmad-ujjvala-nīlamaṇau pramāṇī-kṛtaṃ prācāṃ matam | tatra mūlaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'The variety of occasion necessitated by the pastime, which generates the special <s>rasa</s>, — like <s>Sītā's</s> going to <s>Rāvaṇa's</s> house — cannot be made otherwise even by us. And the special <s>rasa</s> is achieved precisely thus: when, in the mere semblance of another's relationship — which is separated from impropriety because it is born of illusion — the eagerness of those [gopīs] who are thwarted by others' prevention grows, there arises, in the entire future, a most radiantly manifest, immense happiness, and from the attainment of the beloved — who is devoted with the most steady, confusion-free constancy — that [rasa] obtains its supreme brilliance. And thus, in the future literary works, in the glorious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>, the view of the ancients is validated. The root-text there is as follows:

children.text: laghutvam atra yat proktaṃ tat tu prākṛtanāyake |
na kṛṣṇe rasaniryāsasvādārtham avatāriṇi ||[1.21] iti |
children.translated_text: not for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the descender [of the divine], who savors the extracted essence of <s>rasa</s>." || [1.21]
"The lightness that is said [to apply] here is for an ordinary hero,
