children.text:
pramāṇaṃ yathā,
  neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhir paroḍhā
  tad gokulāmbujadṛśāṃ kulam antarena |
  āśāṃsayā rasavidher avatāritānāṃ
kaṃsāriṇā rasikamaṇḍalaśekhareṇa ||[5.3] iti |
children.translated_text: by the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the crest-jewel of the circle of connoisseurs." || [5.3]

The authority is as follows:
"The married-woman role that poets do not desire in the principal <s>rasa</s> — | that, except for the lotus-eyed women of <s>Gokula</s>, | [applies to those] who were descended [to earth] with the hope of the procedure of <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: atra rasotkarṣasya tarṣata eva kaṃsāriṇāvatāritānām iti tāsāṃ nityaṃ tan-nija-preyasītayā vihāras, tad-avatāra-samaya eva tu rasa-maya-mahotkarṣāya māyayā paroḍha-vyavahāra ity ato na doṣaḥ, pratyuta parama-guṇa eveti bhāvaḥ | iha cāvatāritānām iti devī-caratāṃ sādhāraṇa-lakṣmī-caratāṃ ca na pracārayati, nāyaṃ śriyo' ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ svar-yoṣitāṃ nalina-gandha-rucāṃ kuto' nyāḥ? [BhP 10.47.60] ity anena virodhāt | tenaivānyatamatānyathā-kāritayā tadīya-parama-lakṣmītvam eva tāsāṃ lakṣyata iti |
children.translated_text: Here, because the excellence of <s>rasa</s> is the very object of longing — since they were 'descended by the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>' — their play as His own eternal beloveds is permanent; it is only at the time of His descent (<s>avatāra</s>) that the convention of being married-to-another is effected through <s>Māyā</s>, for the supreme exaltation of <s>rasa</s> — therefore there is no fault; rather, it is the supreme virtue — this is the purport. And here, 'descended' does not promote [the idea of] their being mere goddesses or ordinary <s>Lakṣmī</s>-like beings, because of the contradiction with 'This is not [the grace] of <s>Śrī</s> at His side, nor of the celestial women of lotus-fragrance and beauty — whence then of others?' [BhP 10.47.60]. By that very [verse], since some other status is overridden, their supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s>-hood alone is indicated.

children.text: tad evaṃ ca nirūpya punar apy āha sma-tādṛśaṃ parama-rahasyam ākāśāya ca na prakāśanīyam | kintu-
children.translated_text: Thus having determined this, she again said: 'Such a supreme secret should not be disclosed even to the sky. But:

children.text:
rādhādīnāṃ kevalānāṃ kevalo nanda-nandanaḥ |
  varaḥ syāt kevalaṃ tasmāt ke balāt kuryur anyathā? ||JGc_1,15.14|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'For <s>Rādhā</s> and the others alone, the sole <s>Nanda-nandana</s> alone | shall be the bridegroom — therefore, who could forcibly make it otherwise?' || (JGc 1,15.14) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
yataḥ,
  vraja-lakṣmī-janatāyā harir iha ramaṇaḥ paraṃ na paraḥ |
  katham atha cakora-jāter vṛttiś candrād bhaved anyaḥ? ||JGc_1,15.15|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
For:
'For the people of <s>Vraja's</s> <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Hari</s> here is the supreme lover, not another. | How indeed could the livelihood of the <s>cakora</s>-bird species come from anything other than the moon?' || (JGc 1,15.15) [upagīti]

children.text: atha vṛndā tu, bhavatu yāthākathācaṃ | yad idam ācitam, tad ācitam eva | kintv āyatyāṃ sarva-sukha-samutthāpanaṃ bhavad-abhyutthānam eva gaty-antarāya bhavitā iti prārthya namaskṛtya ca calitā |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> [said]: 'So be it, however it may be. What has been arranged has been arranged. But in the future, your rising up — which will generate all happiness — will alone be the path without obstruction.' — thus praying and saluting, she departed.

children.text: paurṇamāsī tu prāha-
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> then said:

children.text:
avacam avocam uvāca ca, vacmi hi vaktāsmi vakṣyāmi |
  ucyāsam idaṃ vacyāṃ vacāni no ced avakṣyaṃ na ||JGc_1,15.16|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'I said, I spoke, and I have said; I speak indeed, I shall speak, I will speak; | I would say this, let me say, let me utter — if not, I would not have spoken!' || (JGc 1,15.16) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tad evaṃ tāsāṃ khelā-mātra-vilāsinīnāṃ sva-vāsinīnāṃ mātara-pitarādibhir antaḥ-puryām asūryampaśyatayā dhūtākarṇana-kṛṣṇa-varṇanatayā ca paritaḥ parītaṃ vāritānām api dīpyamāna-kaiśora-sāmīpya-samiddhaḥ sva-bhāva-siddhaḥ kṛṣṇa-bhāvaḥ svayam udbhūtavān vāridā-gamana-samayaṃ samayā kāsāñcid vallī-jātīnāṃ pallava iva | yataḥ-
  hṛdayam anaṅgas tāsām aviśad vayasaḥ kramād eva |
  śyāmāṅgaḥ sa tu sāṅgaṃ viveśa sahasā tataḥ pūrvam ||JGc_1,15.17|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Thus, for those [gopīs] who sported only in play, dwelling in their own homes — though they were warded off on all sides by mothers, fathers, and others in the inner quarters as those who should not see the sun [i.e., kept in strict seclusion], and whose hearing was shielded from any description of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-feeling, innately established, kindled by the proximity of his radiant adolescence, arose of its own accord — like a tendril's sprout at the arrival of the rainy season — for some among them. For:
'<s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid) entered their hearts in due course of age; | but that dark-limbed one entered whole and entire — suddenly, even before that!' || (JGc 1,15.17) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: dṛṣṭāntayanti cedam-
children.translated_text: And they illustrate this:

children.text:
āsīd āsu hareḥ sphūrtir darśana-śravaṇe vinā |
  yathāntaḥpura-ruddhāsu kanyāsu madanodgamaḥ ||JGc_1,15.18|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The awareness of <s>Hari</s> arose in them without seeing or hearing — | just as in maidens confined in the inner quarters, the surge of love [arises on its own]!' || (JGc 1,15.18) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: ataevoktam-
children.translated_text: Therefore it is said:

children.text:
navya-yauvanataḥ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇe tāsāṃ tu yā ratiḥ |
  tasyāṃ nātiśayoktiḥ sā sva-bhāvoktis tu manyatām ||JGc_1,15.19|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> that existed in them even before new youth — | let the statement about that not be considered hyperbole, but a statement of natural fact!' || (JGc 1,15.19) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tadā ca, yadā prasaṅga-saṅgatyā kṛṣṇeti varṇa-dvayaṃ karṇābhyarṇam āpadyate, vaṃśī-vādyaṃ vā, tadā tam eva paśyantya iva hṛṣyantyaḥ punar apy apaśyantyas tāpam āpnuvanti sma, kintu kañcit prati na kiñcit prakāśayām āsuḥ | cetasi tu bhāvayām babhūvuḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: And then, whenever by the conjunction of context the two syllables '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' reached the vicinity of their ears, or the flute-music — then, as if seeing him, they would rejoice; but again, not seeing him, they experienced anguish. Yet they did not reveal anything to anyone. But in their hearts, they contemplated as follows:

children.text:
yaḥ kṛṣṇa-nāmākṣara-mādhurī-jharair
  āsvādyate veṇu-kalī-rasair api |
  sa eva ekāmbuda-rocir eṣa me
  kaḥ svāntam uccaiḥ kurute puru-vyathām? ||JGc_1,15.20|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: 'He who is savored through the cascading sweetness of the syllables of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> name and through the flavors of the flute's melodies — that very one, of the luster of a single cloud — who is he that makes my heart intensely, greatly distressed?' // [upajāti]

children.text: tatra ca śrī-rādhāyā bhāvanā, yathā-
children.translated_text: And there, the contemplation of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, as follows:

children.text:
yāte kṛṣṇeti śabde śruti-patham amṛtād apy atisvāda-yukte,
  vaṃśī-vādye ca śaśvan manasi sapadi yaḥ sphūrtim āpnoti so' yam |
  ājanmābhyāsa-hīno' py atisuparicita-prāya eveti bhāti
  prāpti-vyāvṛttitas tu prasabham acirato neṣyati prāṇavargam ||JGc_1,15.21|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: When the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' reaches the path of hearing — more delectable even than nectar — and when the flute-music [is heard], whoever constantly manifests in the mind — this one, though without any practice from birth, appears as if supremely familiar; but through the obstruction of attainment, he will forcefully carry away my life-breaths before long! // [sragdharā]

children.text: punaś ca samprati svayam eva parasparam ivāha-rādhe, kim udagraṃ vyagracittāsi? rādhike, tad etan nāvadadhāsi ced avadhānaṃ vidhehi |
children.translated_text: And again, now she speaks to herself as if to another: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>, why are you so agitated and distracted of mind? O <s>Rādhikā</s>, if you do not heed this, then pay attention!'

children.text:
śravyāṇāṃ svāda-sāraṃ śrutir anumanute yat tu yad vā sudhābdher
  manthāl labdhaṃ, rasajñā sukha-hṛdija-sukhaṃ citta-vṛttir yad eva |
  kiṃ tat kṛṣṇeti varṇa-dvayam ayam athavā kṛṣṇa-varṇa-dyutīnām
  ājīvyaḥ ko' pi śaśvat sphurati nava-yuvety ūhayā mohitāsmi ||JGc_1,15.22|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: 'The quintessence of savor among all things heard — the ear approves of it; or that which was obtained from the churning of the nectar-ocean — the mind, a connoisseur of <s>rasa</s>, [recognizes it as] the happiness born of happiness in the heart. What is that? Is it the two syllables "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>"? Or rather, among the radiances of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> dark luster, some ever-fresh youth flashes forth as the sustainer of life — by this conjecture I am enchanted!' // [sragdharā]

children.text: evaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇasya ca tadīya-pracariṣṇu-tat-tad-guṇa-bhaviṣṇu-tṛṣṇasya bhāva-ramyatā gamyatām-
children.translated_text: Thus, let the delightful state of feeling of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself be understood — he who thirsted with the ever-spreading longing for each of their respective qualities:

children.text:
nāmni śrotraṃ sadana-saraṇau netram āmoda-pūre
  ghrāṇaṃ pṛṣṭhe vapur api guṇe sūktam āsāṃ madīyam |
  māṃ projjhyāsīd drutam iti hariḥ svīya-doṣaṃ vicārāt
  pratyākhyāya sphuṭam anusaraṃ tatra citrāyate sma ||JGc_1,15.23|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'My ear [goes] to their name, my eye to the path of their dwelling, my nose to the abundance of their fragrance, my body to their back, my eloquence to their virtues — having abandoned me, it went swiftly!' — thus <s>Hari</s>, having through reflection rejected the notion of any fault of his own, manifestly followed after [them] there — and it was wondrous! // [mandākrāntā]

children.text:
rādhāṛkṣe kvacana gaṇake nāntikād varṇyamāne
  dṛṣṭvā rādhāṃ ghaṭayati jane sañjanaṃ svasya dūrāt |
  rādhā-gehān mṛdula-pavane vāti nāsmāri tat tat
  kṛṣṇenāsmin punar alam asau sasmare saiva rādhā ||JGc_1,15.24|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: When somewhere an astrologer was describing the constellation '<s>Rādhā</s>' (Viśākhā) in the vicinity — seeing <s>Rādhā</s>, he from afar brought about people's recognition of himself by connecting it with her. When a gentle breeze blew from <s>Rādhā's</s> house — this and that was not remembered by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; but then again, that very <s>Rādhā</s> was intensely remembered by him! // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tad evam apūrva-kṛṣṇa-darśana-parvaṇy ajāta-pūrve yadā tu kāliya-dandaśūka-sandalanam āsīt tadā vidhvasta-nirodhā rādhādayo' pi vrajavāsi-sādhāraṇatayā tatra gacchanti sma | [92] etad artham eva kāliya-damanārthe tāvān vilambārambha-sambhāras tena lambhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, at the unprecedented festival of the first sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — when the subduing of the venomous serpent <s>Kāliya</s> took place — then <s>Rādhā</s> and the others too, having broken through their restraints, went there together with all the other <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers. [92] For this very purpose, such an elaborate delay and preparation for the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s> was arranged by him.

children.text: tad evaṃ tatra gatavatīnām api bālyām okataḥ śokataś ca na lokatas tāsāṃ bhāvaḥ svasya viśeṣaṃ bhāvayāmāsa, kintu premātiśaya-mātram | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Thus, even though those who had gone there — because of their young age, because of confusion, and because of the public [setting] — their feeling did not manifest its special quality before him, but only the excess of love. For thus:

children.text:
yadā dūre nṛtyaṃ phaṇi-śirasi cakre muraripus
  tadā tābhiḥ sākṣād araci sa itīdaṃ nahi mṛṣā |
  tathāpy āsāṃ bālyād bahujana-samājād api śucā-
  vṛter bhāvo naiva sva-rasa-mayatām aṇv api yayau ||JGc_1,15.25|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: When the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) performed the dance on the hood of the serpent far away, then they directly praised him — 'This one!' — and this was not false. Even so, because of their youth, because of the large public assembly, and because of the course of grief — their feeling did not attain even an atom of its own essential nature. // [śikharinī]

children.text:
yadā kālīyasya hrada-valayataḥ so' yam uditas
  tadā rādhā-mukhyāḥ prathama-kalanād eva patitāḥ |
  bahir-jñānaṃ nāsīd yadapi tadapi sphūrti-valitā
  na mūrcchāṃ nāmūrcchāṃ yayur ahaha rātrindivam anu ||JGc_1,15.26|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: When that one arose from the circle of <s>Kāliya's</s> pool, then <s>Rādhā</s> and the chief [<s>gopīs</s>] fell [unconscious] from the very first perception! There was no external awareness — yet even that [state], pervaded by manifestation, was neither fainting nor not-fainting — alas, throughout day and night! // [śikharinī]

children.text:
yadyapi kṛṣṇas tāsāṃ kalanād antar-vikāramāsannaḥ |
  tadapi ca samayāntarajāṃ cakāra gambhīratāṃ śaraṇam ||JGc_1,15.27|| [āryā]
children.translated_text: Although <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was near the inner agitation [caused] by their perception, even so he took refuge in the gravity of the intervening occasion. // [āryā]

children.text: tataś ca, prabhāte tāḥ śakaṭa-samārohitatayā vrajam ānītāḥ katham api svasthatāṃ yātāḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, at dawn, they — having been placed upon carts — were brought to <s>Vraja</s> and somehow restored to composure, as follows:

children.text:
muhur bandhu-stome tad-upacaraṇād utthita-matau
  jana-dvārā tāsāṃ harir api vimūrcchāṃ kalitavān |
  atha vyagrībhūyāmṛtam iva muralyā mṛdu-kalaṃ
  jagau tāś ca prāpur bahir-avahitiṃ satvaratayā ||JGc_1,15.28|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: When the awareness of their group of relatives arose repeatedly through their ministrations, <s>Hari</s> too, through the medium of people, effected their recovery from the swoon. Then, becoming earnest, he played on his flute a softly melodious [tune], like nectar — and they attained external consciousness with great swiftness. // [śikharinī]

children.text: kintu tasya vaṃśī-śaṃsana-mādhuryam eva tāsv abhiṣajyad avabudhya tad-avadhi tāsāṃ pratibandhāya bandhavas tenātinirbandhaṃ yayur iti kadācic cirato darśanam api tasya tāsu paryavasyati sma |
children.translated_text: But perceiving that it was the sweetness of the flute's proclamation itself that acted as medicine upon them — from that time onward, their kinsmen undertook to restrain them with extreme insistence. Thus, sometimes even a sight of him after a long time would come to an end for them.

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇasya ṣaṣṭhe varṣe gate tāsāṃ ca tataḥ kiñcid ūnatayā mate samārabdha-prapañcād bhāvād akṣīṇānāṃ nava-kaiśora-lakṣmīṇāṃ mud-añcanaṃ tasya ca tāsāṃ ca tathā jātaṃ yathā parasparaṃ spardhayeva sañcayam añcad āsīt |
children.translated_text: Then, when Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> sixth year had passed, and theirs was considered slightly less than that — the joy-raising of those whose undiminished new adolescent beauty had commenced the elaboration of feeling from the undecaying [source], both his and theirs, had become such that it was as if advancing with mutual rivalry in accumulation.

children.text: tatra tasya śrī-kṛṣṇasya, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows:

children.text:
vaktraṃ pūrṇa-kapola-kānti-valitaṃ keśā bhṛśa-śyāmalā
  netre lola-viśāla-pāṭala-taṭe vakṣaḥ sphūrad-vistṛti |
  bāhu-dvandvam akharva-puṣṭa-ghaṭanaṃ madhyaḥ kṛśas tat-paraḥ
  sphītas tadvad urū pṛthū bhavitum udyātau sma tasmin hareḥ ||JGc_1,15.29|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: His face, adorned with the beauty of full cheeks; his hair, intensely dark; his eyes, with tremulous, wide, reddish edges; his chest, manifesting expansive breadth; his pair of arms, of full, robust structure; his waist, slender thereafter; his thighs, broad and ample, preparing to become thick — all these were in that <s>Hari</s>! // [śārdūla]

children.text: tatra ca kasyacin marmajña-janasya narma-vacanam-
children.translated_text: And there, the jest of a certain person who understood the inner meaning:

children.text:
tanau śyāmā lakṣmīr abhajad ayam antar-hṛdi punaḥ
  sadā gaurīr itthaṃ kapaṭam abhipaśyan muraripoḥ |
  sphuran-netra-dvandvaṃ bhajad aruṇatām īṣad abhito
  muhuḥ karṇābhyarṇaṃ vrajati kila kiñcit kathayitum ||JGc_1,15.30|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'The dark beauty settled upon his body, but within his heart [settled] the golden one (<s>Rādhā</s>), always' — perceiving this deception of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>, his flashing pair of eyes assumed a slight reddishness and constantly drew near his ears, as if to say something! // [śikharinī]

children.text: atha tāsāṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: And of those [<s>gopīs</s>], as follows:

children.text:
kaṭākṣe kṛṣṇābhā sphuṭam adharayo rāga-garimā
  kapola-dvandvāntaḥ śucir urasi cārūnnati-ruciḥ |
  amī ceto-dharmā bahir ahaha yady evam uditā
  bhavet kiṃvā tarhi vraja-mṛgadṛśāṃ gopana-padam ||JGc_1,15.31|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: In the sidelong glances, a dark-<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-like luster; clearly, in the lips, the gravity of passion; within the pair of cheeks, purity; on the breast, the charm of beautiful elevation — alas, if these states of the heart have thus appeared outwardly, what then would be the concealment of the doe-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>? // [śikharinī]

children.text: tatra śrī-rādhāṃ prati kasyāścid uktiḥ-
children.translated_text: There, someone's words to Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>:

children.text:
bhadrā padmā dhaniṣṭhā śivi-paśupa-sutā pālikā śyāmalā sā
  candrāvaly apy abhīkṣṇaṃ vayasi nija-nija-śrī-samutkarṣi dṛṣṭā |
  śrī-rādhe tvaṃ punaḥ svaṃ jita-kanaka-guṇaṃ dyotam udyotayantī
  tad divyaṃ śyāmadhāma prathayasi paritaḥ kena vā tan na vedmi ||JGc_1,15.32|| śārdūla]
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Śivi</s> the cowherd, <s>Pālikā</s>, <s>Śyāmalā</s>, and <s>Candrāvalī</s> — each constantly appears with her own surpassing beauty in youth. But O Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, you — illuminating your own luster that conquers gold, displaying that divine dark abode (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) on every side — by whom [is this done]? I do not know!' // [śārdūla]

children.text: tatrānyasyā vacanam-
children.translated_text: There, the words of another:

children.text:
vilasati kṛṣṇa-navābdaḥ sphuṭam adhi hṛdayaṃ praviśya rādhāyāḥ |
  na bhavati tad yadi katham iva pulakaiḥ saha locane sravataḥ ||JGc_1,15.33|| [āryā] iti |
children.translated_text: 'The fresh cloud of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> manifestly shines, having entered the heart of <s>Rādhā</s>; if it were not so, how would her eyes overflow together with bristling [of hair]?' // [āryā] — thus.

children.text: tat-prabhṛti tāsāṃ bhāvanā ceyam-
children.translated_text: From that time onward, their contemplation was this:

children.text:
tad eva yamunāraṇyaṃ ta eva ca tamālakāḥ |
  tad eva cittam asmākaṃ sāmprataṃ kim ivānyathā? ||JGc_1,15.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'It is the same <s>Yamunā</s> forest, and the same <s>tamāla</s> trees; our mind is the same — what now could be different?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  śārada-prathama-śubhra-pañcamī
  bhāvi-rātri-nikarābja-saprabham |
  subhruvāṃ mukham uroja-yugmam apy
  āyata pratidinaṃ mahodayam ||JGc_1,15.35|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
And then:
The first bright fifth day of autumn — with the splendor of lotuses in the nights to come — the faces of the beautiful-browed ones, and their pair of breasts too, daily grew in great excellence. // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
yadā rādhā tāsu prathama-vayasākīrṇa-kiraṇā
  tadā tāḥ sarvāś ca pratihata-samajñāḥ samabhavan |
  paraṃ nānā-puṣpāvaliṣu latikāsu prathamataḥ
  praphullantī khyātiṃ sadasi suravallī valayate ||JGc_1,15.36|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: When <s>Rādhā</s> among them, with rays of first-youth beauty spreading, [shone forth], then all of them became as if their cognition was obstructed; but among diverse clusters of flowers and vines, the <s>Suravallī</s> (celestial vine), blossoming first, alone encircles fame in the assembly! // [śikharinī]

children.text: tatra ceyaṃ kiṃvadantī vadantī-babhūva-
children.translated_text: And there, this rumor arose, saying:

children.text:
indur mandati khañjarīṭa-taruṇaḥ khañjann ivālokyate
  dūnaṃ bhāti tila-prasūnam aruṇād bimbaṃ guṇāl lambate |
  svarṇa-śrī-jayi-varṇa-jāla-vilasad-vallī na līnāyate
  rādhāyā madhurimṇi yad vidhuratām āpnoti tan-mādhurī ||JGc_1,15.37|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'The moon grows dim; the young <s>wagtail</s> appears as if limping; the sesame-flower looks afflicted; the <s>bimba</s> fruit hangs down in quality; the vine shining with a network of colors that conquers gold does not diminish — whatever in <s>Rādhā's</s> sweetness attains agitation, that is because of her own charm!' // [śārdūla]

children.text: tad evaṃ labdha-dara-sphore kaiśore tāsāṃ sa eva kṛṣṇa-premā tṛṣṇā-viśeṣam āsāditavān | [105] vratati-tatīnāṃ kṛta-vratatitve labdha-sattve svāśrayaṃ pratyabhimukha-prasāras tad-valayana-lālasam iva | tatra tāsāṃ bhāvanā, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, when adolescence had obtained its slight initial blossoming, that very love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in them attained a special thirst. [105] When the rows of creeper-like women had obtained firmness through their accomplished vows, the expansion toward their own refuge [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] was as if eager for his encirclement. There, their contemplation was as follows:

children.text:
janmany etad aho kim atra bhavitā yat tasya vakṣaḥ-sthalaṃ
  vistīrṇātula-nīla-ratna-masṛṇaṃ spṛśyeta mad-vakṣasā |
  tāmbūlaṃ bata carvitaṃ ca mukhataḥ kṛṣyeta kiṃ man-mukhe-
  naivaṃ keyam aho mamādya vimatir dharma-dhrug abhyāgatā ||JGc_1,15.38|| [śārdūla]
[106] atha premāpi parama-varimāṇamāsasāda, yathā-
children.translated_text:
'In this birth — ah, what will come of it? — would my breast touch that broad, incomparably smooth, blue-jeweled expanse of his chest? Would his chewed <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) be drawn from his mouth to mine? — No, no! Ah, what is this dissonant thought of mine that has now arrived like a transgressor of <s>dharma</s>?' // [śārdūla]
[106] And then, the love too reached supreme magnitude, as follows:

children.text:
pūrvaṃ yat parito harer anubhavāt kaiśoram atyudgataṃ
  tat tāsu sphuritaṃ tam eva vidadhal līlābhir uccaiḥ sthitam |
  apy ākarṇanadarśanādirahitās tā devatāviṣṭavac
  ceṣṭante sma yataḥ śaśāka nahi yad boddhuṃ janaś cāṇv api ||JGc_1,15.39|| [śārdūla]
tatra tu-
children.translated_text:
That adolescence which had previously arisen intensely from the experience of <s>Hari</s> on all sides — it manifested in those [<s>gopīs</s>], producing that very thing through the pastimes, [and they] stood exalted. Even without hearing or seeing [him], they behaved as if possessed by a deity — because [their love] had a nature that people could not understand even slightly. // [śārdūla]
And there:

children.text:
śūnyaṃ paśyati bāṣpa-pūram aniśaṃ momucyate kampate
  svidyaty udgata-kaṇṭakatvam ayate stambhaṃ punaḥ prārcchati |
  glāniṃ gacchati vācitāpi vacanaṃ nābhāṣate seti tāṃ
  paśyantī suhṛdāṃ tatir muhur aho rādhām aśocan muhuḥ ||JGc_1,15.40|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: She gazes at emptiness, she constantly sheds torrents of tears, she trembles, she perspires, she attains bristling of hair, she obtains paralysis again, she falls into languor, even when spoken to she does not speak — seeing this <s>Rādhā</s>, the array of her friends, alas, repeatedly and repeatedly grieved! // [śārdūla]

children.text: tasyā bhāvanā ceyam-
children.translated_text: And her contemplation was this:

children.text:
rūpeṇāmṛta-sindhuḥ kīrtibhir amṛta-dyutir yad api |
  tad api harir mama hṛdayaṃ vidahati hā dhig vidhir vāmaḥ ||JGc_1,15.41|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text: 'Though he is an ocean of nectar in form, though he is the luster of nectar in his fame — even so, <s>Hari</s> burns my heart! Ah, shame upon perverse fate!' // [upagīti]

children.text:
tasya ca pūrvaṃ hṛdayam aliptaṃ
  bhāvaḥ kaḥ punar alipta me sahasā? |
  smarad api yasya tu viṣayān
  svayam atha cittaṃ svato' pi jihreti ||JGc_1,15.42|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text: 'His heart was formerly unattached — what feeling then suddenly attached itself to me? Even while remembering his objects [of sense], my mind by itself feels ashamed even of itself!' // [udgīti]

children.text: punaś ca kāliya-damanam anv anubhūtaṃ tāsāṃ bhāvaṃ vibhāvayann āha-
children.translated_text: And again, contemplating the feeling of those [<s>gopīs</s>] experienced after the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s>, he (<s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>) said:

children.text:
pitā me sādhūnāṃ kula-tilakatā-viśruta-gatis
  tathā mātā sādhvī-samudaya-vivekāgrima-lipiḥ |
  kathaṃ rādhādīnāṃ para-mṛgadṛśāṃ bhāvam abhito
  bhajaty antaḥ kiṃvā mama mṛdulatā māṃ klamayati ||JGc_1,15.43|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'My father is renowned as the crest-jewel of the virtuous lineage; likewise my mother is the foremost inscription of the assembly of chaste women. How then does this love for <s>Rādhā</s> and other doe-eyed women pervade my inner being? Or rather, is it my own tenderness that exhausts me?' // [śikharinī]

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text:
hanta jñānaṃ mama vilulitaṃ kvāpi na syāt parantu
  premārdraṃ tad bhavati sutarāṃ tāsu tu preyasīṣu |
  yasmāt tāsu sphurati na dhiyā premamayyā parā tvaṃ
  nāpi khyātiṃ bahir anugayā tāṃ parākartum īśe ||JGc_1,15.44|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'Alas! My knowledge has been undone — nowhere would it be so! But that [knowledge] becomes exceedingly tender with love precisely in those beloveds. Since in those [women], through love-filled wisdom, no higher [reality] than you manifests — nor can you banish by outward fame that [love] which follows [you]!' // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tac-ceṣṭā ca, yathā-
children.translated_text: And his behavior was as follows:

children.text:
maunārhe pratibhāṣate sma vacanaucitye munitvaṃ dadhe
  śocyatve hasati sma hāsa-kathane rūkṣatvam evādade |
  prastāve vraja-subhruvāṃ sakhi-janair nirmīyamāṇe harer
  yadyapy evam athāpi-varṇa-vikṛter vyatyastir ālakṣyate ||JGc_1,15.45|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitā]
children.translated_text: Where silence was fitting, he would speak; where speech was fitting, he maintained silence; in what was pitiable, he laughed; when laughter was called for, he assumed harshness. When the topic of the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s> was being fashioned by his friends — although <s>Hari</s> [acted] thus, even so, a contrary transformation of complexion was observed! // [śārdūla]

children.text: tāsāṃ vivāha-śravaṇe tu-
children.translated_text: But when they heard of their marriages —

children.text:
bahiḥ surasatāṃ vyañjann api tarhi balānujaḥ |
  antas tu virasaḥ praikṣi marmajñaiḥ pakva-pīluvat ||JGc_1,15.46|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Though outwardly manifesting the appearance of juiciness, the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) at that time
was inwardly perceived as tasteless by those who knew the vital points — like a ripe <s>pīlu</s> fruit! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.46, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite tāsāṃ janyaṃ-manya-janena nija-nija-vadhūnāṃ nayanāya yācyamānaṃ tat-pitṛ-kulaṃ tāsu na tad-vācyam akārṣīt, kevalaṃ tu karṇe karṇe mitha eva varṇayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Things being thus, the natal families of those [girls], being entreated by those people who considered themselves their well-wishers, for the purpose of leading away their respective brides, did not make that matter a subject of speech to them, but only described it in whispers, ear to ear, among themselves.

children.text: tāsu gargādi-hita-vargād api kramād adhigata-kṛṣṇaika-tṛṣṇāsu prāṇa-paryanta-saṅkṣayāśaṅkayā tam udvāham api na sahasā na ca sākṣād udbhāvayāmāsa, kim uta tādṛg-avasthānāṃ prasthāpanam?
children.translated_text: Among those [girls] who had gradually, through the group of well-wishers headed by <s>Garga</s>, acquired an exclusive thirst for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone, out of apprehension of the waning of their very life-breaths, he (<s>Garga</s>) did not suddenly or directly bring up even that marriage — how much less the sending away of those in such a state!

children.text: atha yathā durvahaś ca vivāha-niśamana-saṅklamaḥ prathama-labhya-bālyam ārabhya pūrva-pūrva-krama-labdha-visaratayā paramparayāvadhārita iti krama-viṣayatayā viṣa-bhakṣaṇavad abhyāsavyāsata eva soḍhas tathedam api bāḍhaṃ soḍhavyam iti tathaiva śrāvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, just as the unbearable agony of hearing about the marriage was gradually established through progressive stages from the first-attained childhood onward, step by step, and thus endured through habituation like the eating of poison — so too [was it conveyed that] this must assuredly be endured — and thus he made them hear it.

children.text: tās tu tad-vārtā-mātrataḥ paramārtā jātāḥ | yatra ca kaṣṭam bhoḥ kaṣṭam, jīvanam api niṣṭhīvanam āpayituṃ vyavasitim āyātāḥ | [115] tathā hi prathamaṃ tāvat pratyekaṃ pūrvāhnataḥ pūrvam eva gṛhād ātmānaṃ nihnuvānāḥ sambhṛta-gambhīra-nīram ucchalat-taraṅga-saṅgha-nihrāda-vilīyamāna-karṇaṃ kāla-varṇaṃ kāliya-hradam eva nirvyatireka-vivekam antareṇa bhāvāntareṇa bhāvayām babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: But they, from the mere tidings of it, became supremely afflicted. And there — O the suffering! O the suffering! — they arrived at a resolve to make even life itself something to be spat out! [115] For indeed, at first, each one, concealing herself from her home even before the forenoon, contemplated the <s>Kāliya</s> pool — dark in color, with deep accumulated water, with the roaring sound of surging wave-masses dissolving in the ears — without any distinction of discernment, with a different kind of intention.

children.text: atha tāḥ samastā evābalāḥ kevalatayā gatā api samastā babhūvuḥ | parasparam aparicita-prāyatayā nicāyanti sma | papracchuś ca-kā bhavatyaḥ? iti | [117] pracite ca paricaye tatrāvrajana-prayojanam apy anvayuñjata |
children.translated_text: Then, all those helpless women, having gone individually, found themselves assembled. They kept looking at one another as if mostly unacquainted. And they asked: "Who are you?" [117] And when recognized and identified, they also inquired about the purpose of coming there.

children.text: tataś ca samāna-vāsanāvāsita-mānasa-vyasana-śaṃsaka-daśana-vasanādi-ruci-vilokana-valita-mithaḥ-snehād āliṅgita-kaṇṭhā mukta-kaṇṭham utkaṇṭhayā sphuṭam eva rurudur, vividuś ca parasparaṃ hṛdayam |
children.translated_text: Then, their minds perfumed by identical longings, proclaiming their shared affliction through the luster of their bitten lips and garments and other [signs], looking at each other and bound by mutual affection — embracing one another's necks, they wept aloud with full throat out of intense longing, and came to know each other's hearts.

children.text: tad evaṃ kulāṅganānām api tāsāṃ svayam eva niṣkulākṛta-manasām utkṛṣṭa-guṇatayākṛṣṭa-sarva-nayanā śrī-rādhā tu svata eva madhyam ādhāratām āpannātikaṣṭataḥ prakaṭam eva nija-niścayam āviścakāra, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, even among those well-born women whose minds had on their own become free of family [attachments], the glorious <s>Rādhā</s> — whose excellent virtues drew all eyes — herself naturally having attained the position of the central support, made her own resolve clearly manifest from the midst of extreme anguish, as follows:

children.text:
yady etad-vapur anya-sātkṛtam abhūt pitrādibhis tarhy adaḥ
  preta-grastam ivāpi jīvad adhikaṃ dhik-kāra-yogyaṃ bhavet |
  dhik cātmānam aho yad eṣa sahate' py etasya saṅgāpadaṃ
  tat-tīrthāya balād balānujakṛte kartavyam asyārpaṇam ||JGc_1,15.47|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
"If this body has been made the property of another by fathers and such, then
it would be like one seized by a ghost — though living, yet even more worthy of 'shame!'
And shame upon myself, alas, that it should endure even the calamity of contact with him!
Therefore, for the sake of the <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred bathing), it must be forcibly offered
for the sake of the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.47, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: vistaram atra cālaṃ kṛtvā, yataḥ śreyāṃsi bahu-vighnāni iti nīti-nighnatayā nātivilambanam ālambanīyam ity utthāya tābhiḥ saha mitho baddha-pāṇitayā pānīya-samīpaṃ prasthāya yamunāṃ praty añjaliṃ valayantī sāśru-gadgadam ardhodgata-varṇam udgadati sma-
children.translated_text: "And enough of elaboration here, for 'meritorious undertakings have many obstacles' — by this maxim's cutting force, no excessive delay should be clung to!" — and so, rising, with them together, hands clasped in one another's, proceeding toward the water, facing the <s>Yamunā</s>, folding her palms in supplication, she uttered with tears and stammering, in half-risen syllables:

children.text:
goṣṭha-kṣmāpati-dampatī śvaśuratāṃ rāmānujaḥ svāmitāṃ
  vṛndāraṇyam idaṃ sadāpi bhajatām ārāmatāṃ naḥ pari |
  yāḥ snehād vyatibaddha-hastam abhitaḥ kālindi magnā bhavat-
  pānīyāntar amūr bhajantu sakhitāṃ tvām āśritās tad vayam ||JGc_1,15.48|| [śārdūla]
atha sahāyāntarāṇy api tābhis tad antarāptāni yathā |
children.translated_text: Then the other supplementary means too were obtained by them within that [river].

children.text: tad evam amūm anu punar amūr asādhāraṇa-bādhānām ādhāratayā prāṇa-dhāraṇāyāṃ tu dhuta-kāraṇā hradam agādha-jalaṃ valamānāḥ prati prathitākāśa-vāṇī pratyāvartayituṃ pratyāśāṃ vardhayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Thus, as they were approaching the pool of fathomless water — being the foundation of unprecedented afflictions, their motivation for holding onto life having been shaken — a celestial voice (<s>ākāśa-vāṇī</s>), proclaimed from the sky, caused hope to grow in turning them back:

children.text:
ahaha gopa-sutāḥ saha-sāhasaṃ
  na sahasā kurutāpuru-buddhayaḥ |
  śṛṇuta vaḥ pratikūla-kusaṅgatir
  na bhavitā na bhaven na bhaviṣyati ||JGc_1,15.49|| [drutavilambitā]
children.translated_text:
"Ahaha, O daughters of cowherds! Do not rashly commit this rash deed,
O ones of immature intelligence!
Hear this: an adverse misfortune
for you has not happened, is not happening, and shall not happen!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.49, <s>drutavilambita</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ-
children.translated_text: Thus:

children.text:
virahāvagraha-kliṣṭā gopī-bhūmi-sarojinīḥ |
  kṛtvā gīḥ-sudhayā siktā devābdās tri-divaṃ yayuḥ ||JGc_1,15.50|| [anuṣṭubh}
children.translated_text:
The <s>gopī</s>-earth-lotuses, tormented by the frost of the grip of separation,
having been sprinkled with the nectar of that divine speech,
the divine clouds ascended to the third heaven! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.50, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tataś ca vismaya-phulla-vilocanatayā vyativilokamānāsu tāsu sūrajā-pūrataḥ kāpy adūrataḥ sametya śrī-rādhām upetya sarvāś cāhūya svayaṃ vibhūya tat-tad-gātraṃ gṛhītvā pātraṃ mocayitum īhitvā tīraṃ pratīrayāmāsa | [125] sā hi phullendīvara-sundarī svayam eva kālindī | tayā ca tīram ānītāsu tāsu vṛndayā kathita-tat-tad-vṛtta-vṛndayā madhumaṅgalena ca vāñchita-tad-vṛtta-maṅgalena sahitā parama-hitā mahitā pūrṇimā ca tūrṇam evāgatā |
children.translated_text: Then, as they looked at each other with eyes blossoming with wonder, someone from the fullness of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), coming from not far away, approaching the glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and summoning all the others, herself manifesting [in person], grasping their respective limbs, desiring to release [them from] their vessel [of death], urged them toward the shore. [125] For she was the beautiful one of blooming blue lotuses — the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) herself! And by her, when they had been brought to the shore, together with <s>Vṛndā</s> — who narrated the various occurrences [to them] — and with <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — who desired the auspicious [outcome] of those events — <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) too, supremely devoted and honored, arrived swiftly.

children.text: tataḥ pratisvaṃ taru-mātrāvalambana-gātratayā niścetanavat kṛta-ketanā vraja-niketanāṅganāḥ sāliṅgana-sambodhana-pūrvaṃ gīrvāṇa-varṇita-vāṇīvad eva vadamānā tatrānuvadamānābhyāṃ vṛndā-kālindībhyāṃ sārdhaṃ bodhayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, to the <s>Vraja</s>-settlement women — who had taken refuge by merely leaning their bodies against trees, rendered nearly unconscious — she (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), preceded by embracing and addressing [them], speaking like divine speech composed by the gods, with <s>Vṛndā</s> and <s>Kālindī</s> echoing her words there, awakened them.

children.text: bodhayitvā ca punar bhaṇati sma, parama-masṛṇa-matīnāṃ bhavatīnāṃ katham etāvatī karkaśatā jātā? | [128] vastutas tu-
children.translated_text: And having awakened them, she spoke again: "How has such harshness arisen in you, who are of supremely tender disposition?" [128] "But in truth:"

children.text:
candro na hata-kalaṅkaḥ kvacid api na kalaṅki vaktraṃ vaḥ |
  candro muhur api naśyati naśyati nahi varṣma yuṣmadīyaṃ tu ||JGc_1,15.51|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
"The moon is never freed from its blemish, but your faces are nowhere blemished;
the moon repeatedly perishes, but your bodies never perish!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.51, <s>upagīti</s>]

children.text: kiṃ ca, tisṛbhir apy asmābhir aparokṣaṃ parokṣam api tathā sāhāyyaṃ kāryam, yathā kṛṣṇa-mātra-pati-gatīnāṃ bhavatīnāṃ nānabhīpsita-puruṣa-śayyā-yogaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: "Moreover, by all three of us too, the same assistance must be rendered — openly and covertly — so that for you, whose sole husband-destination is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone, there would be no consummation of the bed with an undesired man."

children.text: athavā tad-viṣayakasya bhāva-mātrasya sa eṣa prabhāvaḥ, kim uta bhavad-vidhānāṃ mahā-bhāvasya? yaṃ khalu gopa-varga-nṛpatiṃ prati gargaḥ pratijñātavān |
children.translated_text: "Or rather, such is the power of mere <s>bhāva</s> (sentiment) regarding him — how much more of <s>mahā-bhāva</s> (supreme ecstatic love) in ones such as you! Which indeed <s>Garga</s> had promised to the king of the cowherd community:"

children.text: ya etasmin mahā-bhāge prītiṃ kurvanti mānavāḥ |
nārayo bhibhavanty etān viṣṇu-pakṣān ivāsurāḥ ||[BhP 10.8.18] iti |
children.translated_text: "Calamities do not overpower them, who are of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> party, as <s>Asuras</s> [cannot overpower the gods]!" // [BhP 10.8.18]
"Those people who cultivate love for this greatly fortunate one —"

children.text: tasmāt parama-śubhavatyaḥ svayaṃ bhavatyaḥ punar atra cintāṃ na kurvantu, kintu guru-vaśaṃvadatayā vadamānāḥ śam āsīdantu iti |
children.translated_text: "Therefore, O supremely auspicious ones, you yourselves should not worry about this any further, but rather, speaking as ones obedient to your elders, be at peace!"

children.text:
evaṃ tasyāṃ sāntvayantyāṃ tamālasy-
  ādhaḥ sthātrī hema-gātrī-tatiḥ sā |
  nyañcad-vaktrā bāṣpa-netrā tadīyāṃ
  patra-śreṇīṃ mārjayanty eva tasthau ||JGc_1,15.52|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
As she was thus consoling, beneath the <s>tamāla</s> tree,
that assemblage of golden-limbed ones,
with downcast faces and tear-filled eyes,
stood as if wiping its row of leaves! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.52, <s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ sānuvrajanam ātmānaḥ parirabhya tāḥ kṛta-prasthitīr upalabhya tad-upadeśaṃ viśrabhya sadyaḥ samudyantīṃ kṛṣṇāvaloka-tṛṣṇāṃ pratilabhya hasta-graha-grahila-mahilābhiḥ sāhacaryam ācarya pracchanna-vartmanā niṣpratyūha-nigūha-mānāṅgaṃ nija-nijāṅgana-samīpa-vanaṃ śrī-rādhādayaḥ samājagmuḥ | tad-dinataś ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, embracing themselves along with their companions in departure, and understanding those [girls] to have set out, trusting that instruction, immediately regaining the thirst for the sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> that was suddenly arising, accompanied by the women who grasped [their] hands to hold them, through a concealed path, hiding their unobstructed bodies — the glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and the others came to the forest near their respective homes. And from that day onward:

children.text:
viśākhā-lalitā-mukhyāḥ śrī-rādhā-sakhyam aiyaruḥ |
  padmā-śaivyādayaś candrāvaler ity ādi gamyatām ||JGc_1,15.53|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
<s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Lalitā</s> and the other chief ones attained the friendship of the glorious <s>Rādhā</s>;
<s>Padmā</s>, <s>Śaivyā</s> and the others [attained the friendship] of <s>Candrāvalī</s> — and so on, let it be understood! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.53, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tad etad-avadhikā muhur adhikā sahāyatāyāḥ sahāyatā tāsu kṛṣṇa-tṛṣṇā-niratāsu nāścaryā | [134] yataḥ sādhāraṇasyāpi-
children.translated_text: Thus, the ever-increasing assistance of helpers toward them — who were devoted to the thirst for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — up to this point, is no wonder. [134] For even in ordinary [cases]:

children.text:
sāhāyakaṃ suvidhir icchati yasya kartuṃ
  tasyānukūla-nicitiṃ yugapac cinoti |
  nānā-graharkṣa-śakunāmara-mānavās tad-
  rājyādi-labdhi-samaye hy udayanti bhavyāḥ ||JGc_1,15.54|| [vasanta] iti |
children.translated_text:
"When Providence desires to render assistance to someone,
it simultaneously gathers favorable accumulations;
the various planets, constellations, birds, celestials, and humans —
at the time of obtaining a kingdom and the like, the auspicious ones rise!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.54, <s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: prastūyamānaṃ ca śrūyatām | atha madhumaṅgalaṃ saṅginaṃ vidhāya pūrṇa-manāḥ pūrṇimā vṛndayā saha sahasā hari-samīpam āsasāda | [136] bhānu-tanūjānubhāvita-bhāvi-bhāva-viśeṣa-śleṣā samīpataḥ svāgamanam apahnutavatī | pathi punar idaṃ pracchannaṃ papraccha-vṛnde, vrajendra-nandanasya prema kim āsu vartate?
children.translated_text: Now let what is being narrated be heard. Then <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), making <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> her companion, with a fulfilled mind, together with <s>Vṛndā</s>, swiftly reached the proximity of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). [136] Concealing the fact of her own arrival from nearby, she, who had become imbued with the forthcoming special sentiment brought about by the influence of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), secretly asked this: "<s>Vṛndā</s>, does the love of the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> exist toward those [girls]?"

children.text: vṛndāha-atha kiṃ? kintu nigūḍham |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: "And how could it not? But it is concealed."

children.text: yamunāha-etāsāṃ tu spaṣṭam adya dṛṣṭam |
children.translated_text: <s>Yamunā</s> said: "But for those [girls], it was plainly seen today."

children.text: vṛndāha-tac ca daśama-daśā-vaśād eva |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: "That too is merely due to the influence of the tenth state (full maturity of love)."

children.text: yamunāha-tarhi kiṃ pārasparikaṃ tat parasparaṃ na jānate?
children.translated_text: <s>Yamunā</s> said: "Then is that mutual [love] unknown to each other?"

children.text: vṛndāha-yadapi tathā nigūḍham, tathāpi vikriyāṃ vinā prema kathaṃ dhriyatām? satyāṃ ca vikriyāgatyāṃ parasparaṃ durapahnava eva nava-navānurāgaḥ katham āvrīyatām? yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: "Even though it is thus concealed, how can love be sustained without transformation? And when transformation inevitably comes, how can the ever-new mutual love — which is hard to conceal — be veiled? For:"

children.text:
tamālā vakṣoja-prabha-ghusṛṇa-mudrā-nivalitā
  nakhāṅka-śreṇībhiḥ śavalita-dalāś campaka-latāḥ |
  sarojāni śyāmāny uta kanaka-varṇāny adharaja-
  dravyāṇy evaṃ vanyāpy ubhaya-ratim atra prathayati ||JGc_1,15.55|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"The <s>tamāla</s> trees are marked with saffron-colored imprints of breast-radiance,
the <s>campaka</s> vines have their leaves streaked with rows of nail-marks;
the lotuses are dark, and the golden-colored [signs] of lip-born
substances — thus even the forest reveals the mutual delight of both!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.55, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ sampṛcchya pracchannāyāṃ yamunāyāṃ vṛndā-madhumaṅgala-pūrṇa-pārśvā pūrṇimā harer abhyarṇam ājagāma | āgamya ca virahatāpa-nirvāpaṇāya kvacid ekānte nitānta-kānta-candrakānta-śilā-madhyam adhyāsīnaṃ parama-dhyānavantaṃ tam antar-manasaṃ santaṃ nidhyātavatī | tasmāt pracchannā cedaṃ sa-gadgadam ākalitavatī-
children.translated_text: Thus, having inquired, when <s>Yamunā</s> had concealed herself, <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), flanked by <s>Vṛndā</s>, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, and <s>Pūrṇā</s>, came near to <s>Hari</s>. And having come, for the purpose of quenching the fever of separation, she meditated upon him — that inner-minded, supremely contemplative one — who sat alone upon an exceedingly beautiful moonstone slab in some secluded spot. From her concealment, she perceived with a choked voice:

children.text:
doṣākaraḥ sa doṣā-
kara eva na cātra sandehaḥ |
  kamalaṃ khalv api kamalaṃ
rādhā-vadanaṃ tu śarmaṇāṃ sadanam ||JGc_1,15.56|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
"The moon is indeed a maker of faults —
a maker of faults, and there is no doubt about this!
A lotus is indeed just a lotus;
but the face of <s>Rādhā</s> is the abode of all blessings!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.56, <s>udgīti</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ muhur moham ūhamānā śanair upasṛtya tad ādṛtya tāḥ kṛta-kṛtyaṃ-manyā sāsram āśīḥ-sahasreṇedaṃ śrāvitavatī-
children.translated_text: Thus, repeatedly surmising his infatuation, having slowly approached and honored him, those [women] — who considered themselves fulfilled — with tears, made him hear this through a thousand blessings:

children.text:
vidyate durlabhaṃ kiṃ te vinte tad yad bhavān api |
  avaśya-vaśyatāṃ yasya paśya labdhās tu mad-vidhāḥ ||JGc_1,15.57|| [anuṣṭubh}
children.translated_text:
"What rare thing exists that you do not obtain — [you] who obtain that very thing?
See — ones such as I have been brought to a state of inevitable subjection to you!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.15.57, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu prema-puṣitena ghuṣitena tena vākyena spaṣṭam api teṣām api nija-bhāvam astariṣṭa | saj-jātānāṃ lajjā kevalaṃ balāya sajjatīti |
children.translated_text: But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by that speech — which was nourished by and proclaimed love — did not conceal his own sentiment toward them, even though it was manifest. The modesty of the well-born merely girds itself for strength.

children.text: atha kamala-locane sādara-dara-saṅkoca-locana-nikocatayā kṛta-rocane sā sa-prarocanam avocata-
children.translated_text: Then, when the lotus-eyed one had become favorably inclined, with the contraction of eyes that was [a sign of] respectful slight bashfulness, she (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) spoke with encouragement:

children.text: ayaṃ madhumaṅgala-nāmā svayaṃ sva-saṅgama-maṅgala-saṅghena saṅgamanīyaḥ iti tat-pāṇī samānīya hari-pāṇī prati samarpaṇīyatayā praṇītavatī |
children.translated_text: "This one named <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> is himself worthy of being met through the auspicious assembly of his own companionship" — thus bringing his hands and presenting them toward <s>Hari's</s> hands with the quality of being an offering.

children.text: harir api, sva-vihāra-sukha-sāra-samupahāra evāyam iti tam anusandhāya prema-bandhāya sphurad-iṅgitam āliṅgitavān | [148] so' pi taṃ kila vilakṣaṇam āślikṣad yatra cāśliṣan mithaḥ pulaka-kulam |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> too, understanding him as "this is indeed an offering of the essence of the happiness of one's own sport," and tracing him back to the bond of love, embraced him with a manifest gesture. [148] And he too reportedly embraced that extraordinary one, where, in their mutual embracing, there arose a host of horripilation.

children.text: tad evam upatiṣṭhamānatayā dvayor apy eka-niṣṭhatāyāṃ jātāyāṃ punar vṛndāvana-candramā vṛndāṃ nirvarṇya pūrṇimāṃ prati varṇayāmāsa, keyaṃ bhavatīm anuvartamānā vartate?
children.translated_text: Thus, when exclusive devotion had arisen in both through this attendance, the moon of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), examining <s>Vṛndā</s>, described [her] to <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>): "Who is this one who stands following you?"

children.text:
paurṇamāsī sa-smitam uvāca-kim iyaṃ na paricīyate bhavatā?
[151] śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-nūnaṃ yan-nāmnā vanam idaṃ dhāmnā samāmnātam asti, saiveyam anumeyā |
children.translated_text:
<s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said with a smile: 'Is this one not recognized by you?'
[151] The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Surely she by whose name this forest is famously designated by its name — she is to be inferred as this one.'

children.text: pūrṇimā tu smita-pūrṇa-vadanaṃ tām avādīt, nādyāvadhikam asya vidyamānā babhūvitha?
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), addressing her whose face was full of smiles, said: 'Were you not already in his presence until today?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa sa-smitam uvāca-aparicitā na svayaṃ milanāya samucitāyate |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'One who is unacquainted is not suitable for meeting on her own.'

children.text: pūrṇimātha vṛndām ūce-bhavatu cetaḥ paraṃ bhavatī sacetaḥ sarvadāsya dāsyam ivācarantī cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> then said to <s>Vṛndā</s>: 'Let your mind be at ease! You, possessing consciousness, will always serve him as though performing servitude.'

children.text: atha sāśru-vṛndāṃ vṛndāṃ praṇamantīm eva ramā-ramaṇas tu vanamālayā puraskurvan vana-mālayā puraścakāreti gamayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Vṛndā</s>, with tear-filled eyes, was bowing, the consort of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), honoring her with a forest-garland, indicated: 'He has placed her at the forefront with a garland of the forest' — and thus she was sent forth.

children.text: tad anu ca vyañjita-nija-sukhāsañjanayā pūrṇimā-vṛndayoḥ vācā rañjanayā cirād virājamānaḥ punar gatayos tayor labdha-mahā-sahāyatā-mahasā bṛṃhita-manā mahāmanāḥ sa tu puruṣa-siṃhaḥ saha gacchatas tad eva madhumaṅgalataḥ kāliya-hrada-saṅgataṃ preyasī-prasaṅgaṃ śravasi saṅgamayan sakhi-saṅghaṃ saṅghati sma | sa tu prasaṅgaḥ saṅgamyate-
children.translated_text: Then, after those two (<s>Pūrṇimā</s> and <s>Vṛndā</s>) had departed, their words having revealed his own innate bliss and being delightful — he, having shone for a long while, with his mind nourished by the grandeur of having gained their great assistance, that great-minded lion among men, converging with the group of friends who walked alongside, received from <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> himself the account connected with the beloveds at the <s>Kāliya</s> pool, pouring it into his ears. And that account is narrated:

children.text:
kasmād āgān munīśā phaṇi-hrada-valayāt tatra kiṃ rādhikādyā
  hetau kasmiṅs tad etan mama tu kathayato rudhyate hanta kaṇṭhaḥ |
  hā dhik kiṃ kiṃ vidhātā kuśalitam akarod eva kiṃ yāvad evaṃ
  sidhyed itthaṃ sa tena vyatikathitayā vyaśvasīn nyaśvasīc ca ||JGc_1,15.58|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
'Why did you come from the rim of the serpent's pool, O lord of sages? Were <s>Rādhikā</s> and the others there?
For what reason? — Tell this to me, but alas, my throat is being choked!
Ah, shame! What has the Creator wrought well? Indeed, how much longer — thus' —
by that narration exchanged with him, he both trusted and sighed! // [sragdharā]

children.text: punaś ca śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-bhagavatyāḥ purataḥ kim api tābhir uktam?
children.translated_text: And the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again said: 'Did they say anything before the Venerable One?'

children.text: madumaṅgala uvāca-nahi nahi, kintu sā sumukhī-tatir adhomukhī-bhavantī santīvra-locana-jala-skhalanataḥ stanaṃ siñcantī tamālam api taṃ mlāpayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'No, no! But that row of beautiful-faced ones, becoming downcast, from the intense flowing of tears from their eyes, wetting their breasts, made even that <s>tamāla</s> tree wilt.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-atha tāsāṃ manoratha-pathaḥ kim avagataḥ?
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, was the path of their heart's desire understood?'

children.text: madumaṅgala uvāca-atha kiṃ |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'Indeed!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-katham iva?
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'In what manner?'

children.text: madumaṅgala uvāca-tābhir muhur api bhavataḥ savarṇasya tamālasyāvalocana-racanena |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'By their repeated gazing at the <s>tamāla</s> tree of your same complexion.'

children.text: śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca-viśeṣeṇa cet kathyatām |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'If there is more, let it be told.'

children.text: madumaṅgala uvāca-kālindī-vacanena ca, yatas tāṃ praviśantīnāṃ tāsām imāṃ kākum ākulī-bhavantī paścād asmāsu sānukṛtavatī | yathā-goṣṭha-kṣmā-pati-dampatī [GCP 15.120] ity ādi |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'And by the speech of <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), because the river, having become agitated afterwards when they entered it, reproduced to us their plaintive cry. As follows — "The royal couple of the cowherd-earth" [GCP 15.120] — and so forth.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa sa-gadgadam uvāca-āgaccha gacchāva tāvat sakhi-saṅgham iti |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a choked voice: 'Come, friend, let us go then to the company of friends!'

children.text: atha madhukaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭhaṃ papraccha-tatas tāsāṃ kā matir jātā?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> asked with longing: 'And then, what resolve arose in those [gopīs]?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca vraja-sundarīṇām unmanastayā dharma-trastatayā ca mahatī manaḥ-kathā jātā | yathā-[168] nanu yady evam unmanastā-grastā dharma-rakṣaṇārtham akṣamāsi, tarhi pratyāsanna eva dharma-tyāgaḥ? tatrāha-
children.translated_text:
<s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, among the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>, by their state of being love-maddened and yet frightened by <s>dharma</s>, a great inner discourse arose. As follows:
[168] Now, if you are thus seized by love-madness and unable to preserve <s>dharma</s>, then is not the abandonment of <s>dharma</s> imminent? To that, she says:

children.text: dharmas tyājyaḥ katham atitarāṃ loka-yugmābhinandī?
children.translated_text: 'How can <s>dharma</s> be abandoned — that which is cherished by both worlds?'

children.text: tarhi loka eva tyājyāḥ? tatrāha-
children.translated_text: Then should the worlds themselves be abandoned? To that, she says:

children.text: lokas tyājyaḥ katham atitula-prārthitārthasya dhārī? |
children.translated_text: 'How can the world be abandoned — the sustainer of incomparably desired ends?'

children.text: nanu tarhi tena cārthena kim? tatrāha-
children.translated_text: But then, what use is that goal? To that, she says:

children.text: arthas tyājyaḥ katham ayam atha prāṇa-rakṣādhikārī?
children.translated_text: 'How can one's goals be abandoned — they are the authority for protecting life?'

children.text: nanv etāvati saṅkaṭe prāna-tyāga eva trāṇadaḥ? tatrāha-
children.translated_text: But in such a predicament, is not the abandonment of life itself the deliverer? To that, she says:

children.text: prāṇas tyājyaḥ katham iva na sā lālasā māṃ jahāti ||JGc_1,15.59|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'How can life be abandoned — when that longing will not leave me!' // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ śūnyam iva sthitvā pratisvaṃ punaḥ svagatam ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: Standing as if blank for a moment, each then said to herself:

children.text:
hanta tāta-jananī-kulaṃ kulaṃ
  cānyad ākṣipatu māṃ yathā tathā |
  kṛṣṇa-rāga-rucirā matiḥ kathaṃ
  jātu yātu rucim anyabhāvitām ||JGc_1,15.60|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
'Let father, mother, family, and the other clan
reproach me however they will!
How can a mind beautified by passion for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
ever turn to relish another sentiment?' // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: punaś cintāyām api sodvegam ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: And in further anxiety, they spoke with agitation:

children.text:
nidrā mama sukhadālir yā tasya sphūrti-vismṛtī datte |
  tām api cintā kravyād-vṛddhā śaśvad balād grasate ||JGc_1,15.61|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
'That sleep, my friend, which is a vine of happiness and which gives
forgetfulness of his appearance —
even that is constantly devoured by force
by the aged she-wolf of worry!' // [āryā]

children.text: tasya ca tathā vacanam, yathā-
children.translated_text: And his words likewise, as follows:

children.text:
re re citta, praṇaya-mayatāpāratantryaṃ kim eṣi
  tvaṃ tatrāpi vyasani yadi vā dharmatas tat prayāhi |
  haṃho kiṃvā para-gṛha-juṣāṃ bhāvinīnāṃ ca bhāve
  lagnaṃ magnaṃ bhavasi bahudhā projjhya tat-tad-vicāram ||JGc_1,15.62|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
'O mind! Do you not go toward the complete dependence that is the nature of love?
Or if you do, O troubled one, then go there by the path of dharma!
Or rather — why, in the sentiment of women who belong to another's house,
having deeply sunk, do you become submerged in many ways, abandoning all discrimination?' // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tad evam abhidhyābhramābhidhyānataḥ kathaṃ katham api kṣapiteṣu teṣu dineṣu vraja-vāsināṃ sambhrameṇa jāta-vyutkrame dhenuka-vadha-vikrameḍita-vāsare preyasā saha camūru-dṛśām amūṣāṃ parasparam atiramyaṃ samyag-darśanam āsīt | tatra tu-
children.translated_text: Thus, when those days had somehow been spent through the meditation of longing and bewilderment, on the day adorned by the valorous play of the slaying of <s>Dhenuka</s> — amid the commotion of the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers — there was a supremely beautiful, proper first meeting of those doe-eyed ones with their beloved. And there:

children.text:
tāsāṃ nitya-preyasīnāṃ murārer
  janmany asmin vismṛtātma-sthitīnām |
  śobhā tasya smārayantīva tattvaṃ
  dharmatrāsaṃ drāṅ muhur lumpati sma ||JGc_1,15.63|| [śālinī]
[176] tathā ca varṇitaṃ śrī-bādarāyaṇinā-
children.translated_text:
Of those who were his eternal beloveds, the enemy of <s>Mura</s>'s,
who in this birth had forgotten their own true nature —
his beauty, as if reminding them of the truth,
quickly and repeatedly robbed them of their fear of <s>dharma</s>! // [śālinī]
[176] And this was described by the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>):

children.text:
pītvā mukunda-mukha-sāragham akṣi-bhṛṅgais
  tāpaṃ juhur virahajaṃ vraja-yoṣito' hni |
  tat-sātkṛtiṃ samadhigamya viveśa goṣṭhaṃ
  savrīḍa-hāsa-vinayaṃ yad apāṅga-mokṣam ||[BhP 10.15.43] iti | [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
Having drunk the nectar of <s>Mukunda's</s> face with the bee-eyes,
the young women of <s>Vraja</s> offered their anguish born of separation into the fire during the day;
and having attained his gracious acknowledgment — the release of his sidelong glance
accompanied by bashful smile and modesty — he entered the cow-settlement! // [BhP 10.15.43, vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tathā hi-
  pītaṃ harer vadanam abja-rasaṃ prasahyāpy
  āsāṃ dṛśā racita-bhṛṅga-cakora-bhaṅgi |
  tenāpi satkṛtim amanyata sa praśastām
  ājīvyatāṃ gatavatīṣu tad āsu yuktam ||JGc_1,15.64|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
And furthermore:
Though the lotus-nectar of <s>Hari's</s> face was forcibly drunk
by these women's gazes fashioned in the manner of bees and <s>cakora</s> birds,
even he considered their gracious acknowledgment praiseworthy —
since they had attained the state of being his livelihood, that was fitting for them! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tasminn apāṅga-śara-mokṣam amūr akurvan
  vrīḍā-smitāñci-nayanair anuninyire ca |
  tenāpi sat-kṛtim amanyata sa-praśastām
  ājīvi loka-caritaṃ kila tādṛg eva ||JGc_1,15.65|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
These [gopīs] discharged the arrows of sidelong glances upon him,
and with eyes curved by bashful smiles, they followed him;
even he considered their gracious acknowledgment praiseworthy —
for worldly conduct is indeed just such! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ lakṣyaṃ vidhāyāmūr abhyāsthan netra-patriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Making <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the target, these [gopīs] practiced the archery of their eyes!

children.text: tac ca bhaktir itīvāhuḥ śarābhyāsa upāsanam ||JGc_1,15.66||
children.translated_text: And that, they say, is <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) — for the practice of archery is indeed worship! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tadā ca, tās tan-mukha-sudhā-ruci-rucipā-nānā-pūrṇa-rucayo' pi valatas tat-kula-pālikābhir nilayam eva nītāś cakora-vadhva iva pañjara-madhyam | tad anu ca-
children.translated_text: Then, those [gopīs], though their desires were fully filled with the taste of the nectar-beauty of his face and other [features], were led home by the female guardians of their families, like <s>cakora</s>-hen brides into a cage. And then:

children.text:
āyātāḥ pratibimbatāṃ yadapi tāś citta-hrade śrī-hareś
  citraṃ tatra tathāpi bimba-padavīṃ sthityā vikarṣe' py ayuḥ |
  yatra prasphuṭa-tārakā iva tadā sarvā babhuḥ sarvataḥ
  śrī-rādhā punar antarindu-valaya-dyota-śriyā didyute ||JGc_1,15.67|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitā]
children.translated_text:
Though those [gopīs] had arrived at the state of being reflections in the heart-pool of the glorious <s>Hari</s>,
wonderfully, even so, they attained the standing of the original image, even while drawn away by steadfastness;
where all of them then became like clearly visible stars everywhere,
but the glorious <s>Rādhā</s> shone with the splendor of the inner moon's halo! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
tatra ca-
  pūrvaṃ tāsāṃ vyavasitir abhūd evam īṣat kadācit
  kṛṣṇaṃ paśyanty upaśamam asau lapsyate citta-vṛttiḥ |
  dṛṣṭe dṛṣṭe punar atha muhus tatra cinteyam āsīt
  kiṃ bhūyaś ca kvacid ahaha tad-vaktra-lakṣmīṃ pibāmaḥ ||JGc_1,15.68|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
And there:
Formerly, their resolve had been thus: 'Once, even slightly,
if this mind sees <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, it will attain peace.'
But having seen and seen again, this thought arose repeatedly:
'Ah, when, somewhere again, shall we drink the beauty of his face?' // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tatra ca sakhīṣv api gopana-prakriyeyam-
children.translated_text: And there, even before their friends, this concealment-practice [was maintained]:

children.text:
nahi para-puruṣe vāñchā mama sakhī kācit kathañcid apy asti |
  prakṛtiḥ seyaṃ yad asita-vastuni dṛṣṭe bhavet kampaḥ ||JGc_1,15.69|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
'No desire of mine for another man, O friend, exists in any way whatsoever!
It is simply my nature that when a dark object is seen, there is a trembling!' // [āryā]

children.text:
tatra tu,
  rādhā bādhā-pratihata-tanuḥ sarvadā dhāraṇābhiś
  citte śāntīr api nidadhatī vyākulāsīd atīva |
  hā hā tasyāḥ priya-savayaso py āśu tad-bhāva-bhāvāt
  tām evāpuḥ kaṭutara-daśāṃ hanta ke' mūm avantu ||JGc_1,15.70|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
And there:
<s>Rādhā</s>, her body struck by the affliction [of love], always maintaining composure through fortitude,
placing even peace within her mind, was yet exceedingly agitated;
alas, alas — even her dear age-mates, swiftly from the sentiment of that very state,
attained the same most bitter condition — ah, who shall protect them? // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tad eva para-cchandatā-mandatāyām api-
children.translated_text: And even in the sluggishness of dependence on another's will:

children.text:
saṅkalpaḥ kvacanānvajīgamad itaḥ sākṣāt-kṛtiṃ śrī-hareḥ
  svapnaḥ kutra ca locanaṃ kva ca viyogārtau ca rādhādiṣu |
  yair etaiḥ sudhayā latāsv iva tayā tāsv indu-bimbair javād
  ullāsāvali-lambhanāt taruṇimārambho' pi sambhāvitaḥ ||JGc_1,15.71|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitā]
children.translated_text:
Somewhere, intention pursued the direct vision of the glorious <s>Hari</s>;
somewhere a dream; somewhere the eye; somewhere in the anguish of separation — for <s>Rādhā</s> and the others,
by these [means], like nectar upon creepers, like full moons upon them, swiftly —
from the attainment of series upon series of ecstasy, even the onset of adolescence was thereby fostered! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ samāpana-digdham āha-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke the conclusion-anointing words:

children.text:
sa eṣa rādhike sarva-durlabhas tava vallabhaḥ |
  tvad-arthaṃ pīḍayāpy ārto dināni krīḍayānayat ||JGc_1,15.72|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'He, this very one, O <s>Rādhikā</s>, your beloved, most difficult to attain by all,
for your sake, though afflicted, spent his days in play even through torment!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tad evaṃ sūtāṅga-prabhava-śiśu-yugme kathayati
  sphurat-premāveśāt pratipada-vivikter nighaṭanāt |
  kathā kiṃ nāṭyaṃ kiṃ kim uta nija-līleti vividhaṃ
  samajyāsau sārdhaṃ sphuraṇam ajitenāpy anuyayau ||JGc_1,15.73|| [śikhariṇī]
[181] atha kathāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ cirād eva ca dhīratāyāṃ pravṛttāyāṃ yathāsvaṃ sūta-suta-dvayāya vitīrṇa-sarvehitāḥ sarve śayanāya sadanaṃ viviśuḥ |
children.translated_text:
Thus, as the pair of bard-sons narrated, from the surging impulse of overflowing love,
from the dissolution of distinctness at every step,
'Is this a tale? Is this a drama? Or is this their own pastime?' — thus in various ways
this narrative shone forth together with the manifestation of the unconquered one himself! // [śikhariṇī]
[181] Then, when the tale had concluded and composure had been gradually restored, all, having bestowed all desired [gifts] upon the pair of bard-sons, entered their homes for rest.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anv
apūrvānurāga-caryā-jāgaryā nāma
pañcadaśaṃ pūraṇam |
 ||15||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Fifteenth Chapter, named
'The Vigilance of Unprecedented Love.'
||15||

children.text: atha ṣoḍaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Sixteenth Chapter.

children.text: pralamba-dava-saṃvarta-nivartanaṃ
children.translated_text: The Cessation of <s>Pralamba</s>, the Forest Fire, and the Deluge.

children.text: atha prabhāte sabhātejasā prabhāte parama-prabhāvavatāṃ gomatāṃ prabhāv upaviṣṭe kṛṣṇa-viśiṣṭe tasmin sadasi pūrvavan madhukaṇṭhaś ca kathāyāṃ yathāvad upakramate sma--snigdhakaṇṭha! madupakaṇṭhatayā rāma-vikramāntaram ākarṇyatām, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, when the morning had dawned with the splendor of the assembly, when the supreme majestic ones, the cows, were seated in the luminous morning, in that assembly distinguished by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as before, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> duly commenced the tale: 'O <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>! Being near like bees, hear the exploits of <s>Rāma's</s> valor! As follows:

children.text:
evaṃ gocāraṇa-miṣa-mayaṃ krīḍati bhrātṛ-yugme
  vṛndāraṇyaṃ tapa-ṛtur agāt prāṇināṃ nātirucyaḥ |
  dhatte yad drāk sa ca madhu-guṇaṃ tac ca nāścarya-caryaṃ
  tad-yugmaṃ yad vasati satataṃ tatra nityānurāgi ||JGc_1,16.1|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
As the pair of brothers played under the pretext of cow-grazing,
the summer season came to <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — not very pleasing to living beings;
but that it quickly assumed the quality of the honey [season] — that is no wonder,
for that pair, eternally enamored, constantly dwelt there! // [mandākrāntā]

children.text:
nirjhara-svana-vaśāmbudāgama-
  bhrānti-jhilli-kulam āpa mūkatām |
  aṅghripāś ca jhara-śīkara-plutāḥ
  puṣpitāḥ param amī madhuṃ dadhuḥ ||JGc_1,16.2|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
The cricket-swarms that had arrived through the delusion caused by the sound of waterfalls
[mistaken for] the arrival of clouds, attained silence;
and the trees, drenched by the spray of cascades,
blooming — these indeed gave honey! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
vanasya cchāyābhir jaḍita-jala-vṛnde vikasataḥ
  śucāv apy abjādeḥ pavana-vitatir mādhava iva |
  tad evārdraṃ kṛtvā kusumitam akārṣīd avirataṃ
  mitho yogyānāṃ yad vyativahati maitrī-sukha-śatam ||JGc_1,16.3|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
By the shade of the forest, even in summer, when the lotus and other [flowers]
blooming amid the stilled water-masses, the spread of the wind, like <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Spring</s>) —
by that very [wind], having moistened and made [them] blossom continuously,
it accomplishes hundreds of the happiness of friendship among those suited to one another! // [śikhariṇī]

children.text:
tatrāsīn nara-jātīnāṃ grīṣme' pi ṛtu-rāṇ-matiḥ |
  pika-bhramara-mukhyānāṃ tiraścāṃ tarhi kā kathā? ||JGc_1,16.4|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
There, for the human race, even in summer, the perception was that of the king of seasons (<s>Spring</s>);
how much more so, then, for the cuckoos, bees, and other animals? // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
mādhavas tu yadā mitraiḥ praviśan veṇunā jagau |
tadā dvi-guṇito reje mādhavas tatra so' paraḥ ||JGc_1,16.5|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
But when <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), entering with friends, sang with the flute,
then that other <s>Mādhava</s> (the Spring season) there shone doubly! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
te gṛhe maṇibhir apy alaṅkṛtāś
  cāru-kānti-vidhaye yad udbhavaiḥ |
puṣpa-pallava-mukhair alaṅkriyāṃ
  śaśvad ādiṣata tasya kiṃ bruve ||JGc_1,16.6|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
Those [boys] who at home were adorned even with jewels,
for the purpose of beautiful radiance, with natural [ornaments] —
flowers, sprouts, and such — always desired adornment
from him; what more shall I say? // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: atha śrīdāma-pradhānatayā sudāma-vasudāmādiṣu sabhāsadvad gojāla-sambhālanāya nātidūrataḥ pṛthag upaviśatsu lasatsu balānuja-bala-subalārjunādayas tatrāgatya nṛtya-raṅgājīvi-bhaṅgitayā saṅgatya śubhāśiṣā viśeṣitavantaḥ | taiś ca kutratyā vicitra-nartaka-prāyāḥ prayātā bhavantaḥ? iti pṛṣṭā hṛṣṭātmānaḥ sphuṭam uddiṣṭavantaḥ-bhoḥ parama-dānaśūrāḥ ! dūrād āgatā vayam yataḥ prathamaṃ tāvad bhavat-kīrti-nartita-manaskā jātāḥ, tataś ca śarīreṇāpi bhavad-agre nartitum icchāvaḥ | kutrāpi cirāya vartituṃ na samarthāḥ | śrotrayor iva netrayor api sukhaṃ bibhrataḥ samprati vartāmahe |
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Śrīdāmā</s> and others such as <s>Sudāmā</s> and <s>Vasudāmā</s>, sitting like assembly-members, tended the cow-herds separately at no great distance, the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), together with <s>Bala</s>, <s>Subala</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and others, having arrived there, came together in the manner of stage-performer dance-artists and blessed them with auspicious salutations. And when asked by them, 'From where have you come, O wondrous dancer-like ones?' — they, with delighted hearts, declared openly: 'O supremely generous ones! We have come from afar, because first of all, we became ones whose minds were set dancing by your fame, and then we wish to dance before you with our bodies as well! We are unable to remain anywhere for long. As we bear happiness for the ears, so now for the eyes too, we present ourselves!'

children.text: tatra śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ svān uvāca-aho, pratyekam evāsmākaṃ labdha-varṇāv imau karṇāv eva puru-gurū abhūtām yābhyām eṣāṃ mahāśayānāṃ guṇānubhavam āsādyāmahe sma | kiyad vā manaḥ sampraśaṃsayā mānayāmaḥ, yena tatraiva sāmodaṃ prodasāhayiṣmahi? caraṇābhyāṃ paritaḥ kiṃ nācaritam, yābhyāṃ manoratha-patham alambhayiṣmahi? locana-yugalāya rocanaṃ kim anyad vitarāmaḥ, yena gurūpadiṣṭaṃ tan-miṣṭam anubhāvyāmahe? nāsādvayāt kiṃ nāsādayāma, yenānenāmodena sāmodīkriyāmahe? tvacaḥ kiṃ vacaḥ kathayāmaḥ, yayā tam idam adaḥ-sambandhi-gandhavāham avagāhyāmahe? ātmani tu subhaga-nāma-dheyaṃ bhāga-dheyaṃ kiyad ādheyatāṃ vindeta, yasya tat-tat-phala-valayenāntar bahir apy āvriyāmahe?
children.translated_text: There, the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to his own [friends]: 'Ah, these two ears of each of us have become exceedingly honored, by which we attain the experience of the virtues of these great-souled ones! How much shall we honor the mind with praise, by which we may joyfully assist them? What has not been traversed by the two feet, by which we shall bring them the path of [our] heart's desires? What other delight shall we offer to the pair of eyes, by which we may experience the sweetness instructed by the guru? What have we not attained from the pair of nostrils, by which we are made joyful with this fragrance? What words shall we say of the skin, by which we immerse ourselves in this wind-bearer that is connected with this and that? And upon the self, how much room would the fortune named "blessed" find, whose interior and exterior we are surrounded by with the garland of this and that fruit?'

children.text: aho ! astu tāvan nāmnaiva śriyaṃ dātur asya mahārājasya virājamānatā, pāriṣadānām apy amīṣāṃ mahīmānam upaniṣado' pi varṇayituṃ na śaknuvanti, yenātmānam api vismārya nṛtyam anuvartyāmahe | kim asaṅkīrṇam asmāsu na vitīrṇam amībhir mahā-mahima-caraṇaiḥ, yat khalv atīta-lokena nijālokena nirnimeṣatayā suparvāṇaḥ kriyāmahe? katiśaḥ svayaṃ na pratipālitā vayaṃ, yan nija-cchāyām āpāyya paryāpyāmahe? katarad vā manaḥ-santoṣaṇaṃ poṣaṇaṃ na vihitaṃ yan nija-dṛṣṭi-sudhā-vṛṣṭibhir abhitarpyāmahe | paśyata paśyata, netra-gati-vicitratām amīṣām, yayā khalu nṛtyam upādiśadbhir āmībhir anugṛhyāmahe | tasmān nṛtya-caryā-paricaryā-paryutsukā vayaṃ tad-artham eva yogyam avasaraṃ mṛgyanto vartāmahe |
children.translated_text: 'Ah! Let this suffice — although this great king's resplendence [serves] to bestow prosperity by name alone, even the <s>Upaniṣads</s> are unable to describe the greatness of these attendants of his; by whom, having caused us to forget even ourselves, we follow their dance! What unmixed [gift] has not been bestowed upon us by these feet of great glory, by which, through their transcendent, unblinking radiance, we are made into celestials? How many times have we ourselves been protected by them, by whose own shade we are satisfied and fulfilled? What nourishment for the mind's satisfaction has not been provided, by whose nectarean showers of glances we are made content? Behold, behold the variety of their eye-movements, by which indeed we are being graced by these [dancers] who are instructing us in dance! Therefore, we who are eagerly devoted to the service of dance-practice, are seeking a suitable occasion precisely for that purpose!'

children.text: sabhāsada ūcuḥ, bho bhoḥ suśīla-vāsanāḥ! kuśīlavā iva stuvānā yadi sarva-parvaṇi vartakā nartakāḥ stha, tarhi bhavadbhiḥ samarhitā nija-kalā-kalāpāḥ kalpyantām, viśeṣād anena śyāma-dhāma-nikāma-rāma-rāma-vigraheṇa | yaḥ khalu citrāṅgo na tu citrāṅgaḥ, candrakī na tu candrakī, pītāṃśuko na tu pītāṃśukaḥ, śyāma-ghano na tu śyāma-ghanaḥ, vaṃśa-pravīṇādharo na tu vaṃśa-pravīṇādharaḥ, guṇa-rūpī na tu guṇa-rūpī, vidyādharo na tu vidyādhara iti vaicitrībhir netrāṇi vicitrayati |
children.translated_text: The assembly-members said: 'O you who are perfumed with good character! If you are performers who praise at every festive occasion, then let your assembled artistic repertoires be arranged — especially by this dark-lustered, supremely delightful, beautiful-<s>Rāma</s>-like form. For he is indeed "<s>Citrāṅga</s>" (of variegated limbs) but not [the king] <s>Citrāṅga</s>; "<s>Candrakī</s>" (moon-like) but not a peacock; "<s>Pītāṃśuka</s>" (yellow-garmented) but not the sun; "<s>Śyāma-ghana</s>" (dark cloud) but not an [actual] dark cloud; "<s>Vaṃśa-pravīṇādhara</s>" (skilled-lipped on the flute) but not [merely] a player; "<s>Guṇa-rūpī</s>" (embodiment of virtues) but not [merely] a quality-form; "<s>Vidyādhara</s>" (knowledge-bearer) but not a [celestial] <s>Vidyādhara</s>" — thus, with such variegations, he astonishes the eyes!'

children.text:
tataś ca,
  arjuna-subalādibhir upagāne
  pāṇi-śṛṅga-dala-tāla-nidhāne |
  nṛtyantaṃ taṃ vraja-śiśu-sabhyāḥ
  praśaśaṃsur ye śruti-nuti-labhyāḥ ||JGc_1,16.7|| [pādākulaka]
children.translated_text:
And then:
While <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Subala</s>, and others provided accompaniment in song,
with clapping, horns, leaf-cymbals, and rhythmic beats,
the assembly-members of <s>Vraja's</s> boys praised
him who was dancing — he who is attainable only by the laudation of the <s>Vedas</s>! ||16.7|| [pādākulaka]

children.text:
śrī-kānte' py atha niṣkrānte viveśāveśato balaḥ |
  tad-ālokaḥ sabhya-lokaḥ ślokayāmāsa tad dvayam ||JGc_1,16.8|| [anuṣṭubh]
  yady etayor varṇa-bhedaḥ syān naiva śyāma-gaurayoḥ |
  tadā na paricīyetām etāvaṅga-guṇādibhiḥ ||JGc_1,16.9|| iti | [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And when the glorious beloved [of <s>Lakṣmī</s>] had exited, <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) entered with inspiration;
the assembly-world that beheld them composed a verse about that pair: ||16.8|| [anuṣṭubh]
'If there were no color-difference between these two — the dark and the fair —
then they could not be distinguished by their limbs, qualities, and the like!' ||16.9|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
aṅga-hāre taḍil-līlām aṅge meghendutāṃ kramāt |
  vyañjaṃ vyañjaṃ viviśatuḥ saṅgi-gātṛ-kulācale ||JGc_1,16.10|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Manifesting step by step the sport of lightning in their limb-movements, and cloud-moon quality in their bodies,
they entered the mountain-range of the assembled singers' clan! ||16.10|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha sabhāsadaḥ sva-sva-hṛdaya-vihāri maṇimaya-hāri hārādikaṃ dadatas te tu pratyācakhyuḥ-na vayaṃ dravya-vanīyakā nartaka-nāyakāḥ, kintu niyuddha-yācanakā eva, śubhavanto bhavanto malla-tallajā iti varṇanāṃ karṇayoḥ sañcitya niścitya ca samantād vicitya sarvordhvaṃ bhavatāṃ bhavatāṃ samitiṃ samāgatāḥ | atas tad evāsmadīyāya toṣāya poṣāya ca dīyatām, na tu moṣāya nīyatām |
children.translated_text: Then, when the assembly-members offered their gem-studded necklaces and other jeweled ornaments that dwelt in their own hearts, those two declined them: 'We are not commodity-seeking dance-leaders, but rather wrestling-challengers! Having stored in our ears, fixed upon, and searched out from all sides the description that you, O blessed ones, are scions of wrestlers, we have come here to your assembly surpassing all. Therefore, let that alone be given for our satisfaction and nourishment, and let it not be carried away as plunder!'

children.text: tad evam avadhārayadbhir eva hasadbhis taiḥ sabhāsadbhir upasarpadbhiḥ saha sahajātau kṛta-śātau tatra-bhavantau tadārabdhavantau | yatra-
children.translated_text: Thus, even as those laughing assembly-members were understanding [the situation] and approaching, those two, of natural birth and sharp-witted, commenced [the wrestling] then and there with those present. Wherein:

children.text: bhrāmaṇair laṅghanaiḥ kṣepair āsphoṭana-vikarṣaṇaiḥ | [BhP 10.18.12]
children.translated_text: With whirling, leaping, hurling, clapping, and dragging — [BhP 10.18.12]

children.text: uraḥpeṣam ivāmībhir nyayudhyetāṃ balājitau ||JGc_1,16.11|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: those two, unconquered by strength, wrestled as if in chest-crushing combat with those [boys]! ||16.11|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś cānavadyayā vidyayā toṣiteṣu teṣu nikhila-guṇi-jana-garva-nivartakeṣu kṛṣṇādi-nartakeṣu sarva-durāsada-śrīdāmādi-sabhāsadaḥ svaka-sarva-kalā-veditā niveditācaraṇāya nṛtya-vidyām udbhāvayāmāsuḥ |
