children.translated_text: Then, when those dancers led by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — who dispel the pride of all men of talent — had delighted them with their faultless art, the assembly-members led by the wholly unconquerable <s>Śrīdāmā</s> brought forth their dance-art, presenting the knowledge of all their own arts for evaluation.

children.text: yatrānanda-kandalitatayā svayam api labdha-tṛṣṇāḥ kṛṣṇādayas tadīya-śikṣā-parīkṣaṇāya sudurgama-tālādi-dharās tat-parikarā eva babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Wherein, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the others, having themselves become eager from the sprouting of delight, became their very accompanists, bearing the extremely difficult rhythmic patterns and the like, for the purpose of testing their instruction.

children.text: ataevoktam ṛṣiṇā-
children.translated_text: Hence it was said by the sage:

children.text: ||JGc_1,16.12|| MISSING!
children.translated_text: ||16.12|| MISSING!

children.text: kvacin nṛtyatsu cānyeṣu gāyakau vādakau svayam |
śaśaṃsatur mahārāja sādhu sādhv iti vādinau ||[BhP 10.18.13] iti |
children.translated_text: and they said, O great king, "Bravo! Bravo!" — being speakers [of praise]!' [BhP 10.18.13]
'Sometimes, when others danced, those two themselves became the singers and instrumentalists;

children.text: atha goṣu gocaratām atītāsu tataś calitavantas te-
children.translated_text: Then, when the cows had gone beyond the grazing range, they all moved on from there:

children.text:
bilvaiḥ kumbhaiḥ kara-sthāmalaka-samudayais tāḍayanto mithas te
  hāsaṃ hāsaṃ mṛgehāvikira-bhaṇitibhir dardurādi-plutādyaiḥ |
  asparśi-sparśanārthaṃ nayana-parivṛter mocanaiḥ kṛṣṇa-rājya-
  syandolī-siṃha-pīṭhādy-adhikṛtija-sukhair ninyire yāma-vargam ||JGc_1,16.13||[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
tatra ca-
  nṛpatir ajani kṛṣṇaḥ stokakṛṣṇaḥ pradhānaṃ
  subala-saciva-rāmasyāpi tadvan nṛpatvam |
  ubhaya-bala-patī śrīdāma-bhadrāv itīdaṃ
  vidha-vividhatayā tau rāṣṭra-lakṣmīm akārṣṭām ||JGc_1,16.14|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
Striking each other with <s>bilva</s> fruits, gourds, and handfuls of <s>āmalaka</s> (emblic) fruits,
laughing and laughing, with calls imitating deer, bees, and scatter-talk, leaping with frogs and the like,
for touching in the game of non-touching, with releases of revolving glances, in <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> kingdom —
with the joys of those appointed to swings, lion-thrones, and the like — they passed the watches of the day! ||16.13|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
And there:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> became king and <s>Stokakṛṣṇa</s> the chief minister;
<s>Rāma</s> too likewise attained kingship with <s>Subala</s> as minister;
<s>Śrīdāmā</s> and <s>Bhadra</s> became the army-chiefs of both sides — thus,
with this and that variety, those two fashioned the royal fortune! ||16.14|| [mālinī]

children.text:
kvacit sthānaṃ kvacid yānaṃ kvāpy arthe sandhi-vigrahau |
  parājaya-jayau kvāpi krīḍāyām anucakratuḥ ||JGc_1,16.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Sometimes stationing, sometimes marching, sometimes making alliances and wars in matters of state,
sometimes defeat and victory — in play, those two conducted all!' ||16.15|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: evaṃ tau loka-siddhābhiḥ krīḍābhiś ceratur vane |
children.translated_text: 'Thus those two, with sports well-known to the world, roamed about in the forest,

children.text: nady-adri-droṇi-kuñjeṣu kānaneṣu saraḥsu ca ||[BhP 10.18.16]
children.translated_text: in rivers, mountains, valleys, groves, forests, and lakes.' [BhP 10.18.16]

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite dina-katipaye ca prasthite kadācid ahar-mukha eva pūrva-pūrva-pūrvadeva-nirvāpaṇa-bhṛta-nibhṛta-cintā-kṛta-mati-bhraṃśasya kaṃsasya svayam abhyāsaṃ pralamba-nāmā deva-dhrug abhyājagāma | abhyāgamya ca praṇamya vyaktam eva tam anuyuktavān-deva, tava keyaṃ paridevanā balavad āvartamānā dṛśyate?
children.translated_text: This being the situation, when a few days had passed, once, at the very break of day, <s>Pralamba</s> by name — an enemy of the gods — of his own accord came near <s>Kaṃsa</s>, whose intellect had been shattered by the concentrated anxious thoughts borne of the repeated extinguishing of each prior demon. Having approached and bowed, he openly asked him: 'My lord, what is this lamentation of yours that is seen swirling with great force?'

children.text: kaṃsa uvāca-na jānāsi? mamānvag-bhūya sthitaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ kiṃ vāvaśiṣṭam?
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s> said: 'Do you not know? What distinguished [resource] remains after following in my wake?'

children.text: pralamba uvāca-bhavatu, mām api yāmam ekaṃ vyāpāraya | kaṃsas tu tuṣṇīm-bhūya dūyamāna-vadanaḥ kṣaṇam āsīt |
children.translated_text: <s>Pralamba</s> said: 'So be it — employ me too for one watch!' And <s>Kaṃsa</s>, falling silent, remained for a moment with a pained expression.

children.text: pralamba uvāca-deva, katham iva |
children.translated_text: <s>Pralamba</s> said: 'My lord, how so?'

children.text: kaṃsaḥ sa-vairasyaṃ vihasya tasya tatra pataṅgatāṃ vibhāvayann uvāca-tvam apy atamasi prajvalaj-jvalana-vartmani vartanīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s>, laughing with disgust and contemplating his moth-like [fate of flying into fire] there, said: 'You too must tread upon the path of a blazing fire in the darkness!'

children.text: pralambaḥ sa-krodham uvāca-aho, sarvaṅkaṣa-jvālasya kālasya mahimā himācalam api jvalayati, yadāśritāṃs taḍāgāṃś ca tāḍayati |
children.translated_text: <s>Pralamba</s> said angrily: 'Ah, the glory of all-consuming, blazing Time sets even the <s>Himālaya</s> ablaze, and strikes even the reservoirs it shelters!'

children.text: kaṃsa uvāca-bhavatu yathā bhavad-icchā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s> said: 'So be it — as you wish!'

children.text: iti niśamya tam ānamya tad-avamānitaś ca tadaiva daiva-sandānitatayā kṛtāvilambaḥ pralambas tādṛśa-krīḍā-pareṣu śrī-kṛṣṇa-vareṣu bāla-nikareṣu prāpta-dūra-bhūr vicāritavān-
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard this, bowing to him, and being slighted by him, <s>Pralamba</s> — bound by divine fate, having made no delay — in the midst of those boys devoted to such play, the excellent followers of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having reached the distant ground, reflected:

children.text:
tāv imau sukumārau ca sarva-mārau kumārau yau |
  sahasā rahasā yena yena kaṃsād agaṃsātām ||JGc_1,16.16|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'These two tender boys, who are destroyers of all,
were secretly and suddenly taken away from <s>Kaṃsa</s> by someone.' ||16.16|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: sarvo' py asau sarva-cālena kālena ghaṭita-kaṭhinatābhyām ābhyāṃ carvita-garvaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, tad adya samasta-vāsara-visṛmara-vihāra-visaraja-viśvāsa-prapañcanayā vañcayan bandhuvad eva skandha-dvaye hasta-dvaya-kṛta-bandhaṃ dvayam api prakṣipya kṣipram eva bhojarāja-parisaraṃ parisamupahariṣyāmi iti |
children.translated_text: 'All of this [<s>Kaṃsa</s>] has had his pride ground down by Time, which drives everything, through these two who are hardened [in battle]. So today, by the strategy of trust-deception through the entire day's relaxed, carefree, sport-scattered intimacy, deceiving like a kinsman, throwing both of them — bound by the binding of two hands upon two shoulders — I shall quickly carry them to the vicinity of the <s>Bhoja</s> king (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) and present [them].'

children.text: atha sa tu kalkī valkīkṛta-kaccaratādi-pracchanna-sparśa-veśatayā pūrvaṃ goṣṭham āgatya parito dṛṣṭiṃ vitatya veśma-sthita-gopa-bāla-viśeṣa-veṣaṃ samūhya tam eva ca vyūhya miśrī-bhavituṃ śiśrīṣan hasann eva tatra praviṣṭaḥ paridṛṣṭaś ca kṛṣṇena |
children.translated_text: Then he — that deceitful one — having concealed his appearance through a covering disguise of rags and the like whose touch was hidden, first came to the cow-settlement, cast his gaze all around, assembled a special cowherd-boy costume from the garments of a boy dwelling in a house, and arranging it and desiring to mingle, entered laughing — and was observed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tac-chalam evāsvaccha-svacchalāyāvalambya-bhadra, kathaṃ vilambam ālambathās, tathāpi bhadraṃ dudyūṣā-samaya eva samayitas tvam asi iti vihasya tad-anukṛta-gopa-bāla-sambandha-viśeṣa-sambandhaṃ parihasya ca bahu-paritoṣitena tena saha sahacaratvaṃ balasya bala-nirjayārtham eva kalayāñcakre | ūce ca-adyārabhya, sabhya, mama parama-suhṛd bhavān eva | tvām aham akṣi-gatatayā sthāpayiṣyāmi | śrīdāmā rāmam evānvetu, sa kila hy antar-vardhana-spardhaḥ spardhana-gaṇam evārhati iti |
children.translated_text: And seeing him, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, adopting as his own stratagem the very deception of that impure one with its transparency [visible to him] — 'O good fellow, why do you resort to delay? Even so, it is well — you have arrived at the very time of the desire to play' — thus laughing, and having jested about the particular affiliation of that cowherd-boy identity he had assumed, with great satisfaction, arranged companionship with him for the purpose of defeating <s>Bala's</s> (<s>Balarāma's</s>) strength. And he said: 'From today, O good sir, you alone are my supreme friend! I shall place you in the position of my own eyes. Let <s>Śrīdāmā</s> attend <s>Rāma</s> alone — for he is indeed a rival in the contest of concealment and deserves only the band of contestants!'

children.text: sa tu kratubhuk-śatrus tatra nirvismayam eva kusmayam ānatayā tathā sthitaḥ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And that enemy of the sacrifice-enjoyers (gods), without any wonder, stood there with a false smile and bow, because:

children.text:
viśvacikīr api sa vidhiḥ pipaṭhīr yasmād bhavet tasmin |
  ko vā caturaṃ-manyaḥ prathayatu nija-cāturīṃ kṛṣṇe ||JGc_1,16.17|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'Even he who would undo the cosmic order, before whom [even the learned] would become bewildered —
who, thinking himself clever, would display his cleverness before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?' ||16.17|| [upagīti]

children.text: athārbhaka-samudayaṃ vibhāga-dvayam ayaṃ vidhāya taṃ ca pralambaṃ sva-bala-parivṛḍhatayā dṛḍhaṃ nidhāya tatra ca sa-matsaram iva bala-pralambau śrīdāmātmānau mithaḥ pratisaṅghaṭṭinau saṅghaṭayya parān api sajūḥ-kurvāṇatayā tathā praghaṭayā parājitānāṃ ca śatāya parikrītānām api vāhakatvaṃ prakaṭayya saṅgarāya kṛta-saṅgaraḥ sa mādhavo vividha-krīḍā-niviḍamanā babhūva | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, dividing the group of boys into two sections, and firmly placing <s>Pralamba</s> within his own army's strength, and pairing <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and <s>Pralamba</s>, and <s>Śrīdāmā</s> and himself as opponents striking against each other — as if with rivalry — and making the others join together likewise, and announcing that the defeated [team's members] would be carried on the backs of the victors as their purchased price for a hundred — having made a compact for battle — that <s>Mādhava</s> became absorbed in mind in manifold dense play. And then:

children.text:
avrīḍa-krīḍatāyāṃ jayavad itarayor vāhayanto vahantas
  tasmin vāhānukartṝṃs turaga-tulanayā hāsayanto hasantaḥ |
  maryādā-nirṇaye tu prathita-kali-kulaṃ vādayanto vadantaḥ
prāpur bhāṇḍīram ete vanavana-bhuvi gāś cālayantaś calantaḥ ||JGc_1,16.18||[sragdharā]
[24] tad evaṃ kutūhale tu prabale balaṃ pralamba-skandhārūḍhaṃ sandhātuṃ jita-bhujaga-bhujaḥ śrī-balānujaḥ parābhavam agaṇayan durbalam adurbalam avicitya svīkṛtaṃ svagaṇam eva parābhāvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text:
In shameless play, making the other two carry them as if in victory, and being carried themselves; making those who imitated mounts laugh by comparing them to horses, and laughing themselves; in determining the rules, creating disputes like a famous family of quarrels, arguing and speaking — these [boys], driving the cows and moving, reached the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> [tree] in the forest-land! // [sragdharā]
[24] Thus, even in the tumult of the encounter with <s>Pralamba</s>, the younger brother of Śrī <s>Bala</s> — the conqueror of the serpent-armed one — not reckoning the defeat, without examining whether the weak ones were truly weak, caused the defeat of his own team itself that had been accepted [by Pralamba].

children.text: tasyāpātatas tu vahanāyamānānāṃ mano-glāniḥ syād iti svam api tathā cakāra, tataś ca-
children.translated_text: But at his first approach, lest the minds of those being carried should become dejected, he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) did the same himself. And then:

children.text:
ūhe kṛṣṇaḥ śrīdāmānaṃ daityaḥ sa śrī-rāmākhyānam |
  anyo' py anyaṃ śūraṃ-manyaḥ sarvaḥ proce dhanyo dhanyaḥ ||JGc_1,16.19||[vidyunmālā]
  pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kautuke yena dṛṣṭaḥ
  saumyaḥ paścād rāmakarṣe tu bhīṣmaḥ
  ity evāyaṃ sa pralambas tu paryaṅ-
  maryādātaḥ paryagāt taṃ pragṛhya ||JGc_1,16.20|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> carried <s>Śrīdāman</s>; the demon carried the one named Śrī <s>Rāma</s>; each other one too, thinking himself heroic, said to each: 'Blessed! Blessed!' // [vidyunmālā]
At first, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was seen by him with curiosity, he appeared gentle; but afterward, in bearing <s>Rāma</s>, he appeared terrible. Thus this <s>Pralamba</s>, transgressing the boundary of the game's rules, went far away, having seized him! // [śālinī]

children.text:
rāmaḥ krīḍāviṣṭatāśliṣṭa-bodhas
  taṃ nājñāsīd dṛṣṭa-mātraṃ ca kṛṣṇaḥ |
  pūrvaḥ prāyeṇārjutā-bhitta-cittaḥ
  paścād-bhāvī cāturī-sandhurīṇaḥ ||JGc_1,16.21|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, with his awareness closely bound by absorption in play, did not recognize him at first glance, but <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> did. The former was mostly of a mind broken by simplicity; the latter was to become the commander-in-chief of cleverness! // [śālinī]

children.text: atha tathāpi giri-nivaha-nibha-vahala-sāratā-vaha-durvaha-svabhāvatā-bhāvita-saṅkarṣaṇa-vapuḥ-karṣaṇa-jāta-dharṣaṇa-vaśān niviḍa-pīḍitatayā vrīḍita-cittatayā ca sa punaḥ punar īḍitaṃ-manyaḥ svam akharvaṃ pūrva-siddhaṃ pūrvadeva-vapur āvirbhāvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, even so, because of the strain arising from the dragging of the body of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> — who was endowed with a nature heavy and hard to carry, dense with solidity like a mass of mountains — being pressed tightly and his mind embarrassed, that one — thinking himself praised — revealed again and again his own immense, previously established former-divine body.

children.text:
yarhi rāmam avahad danoḥ sutaḥ
  śubhra-dhāma-vapuṣaṃ tamaḥ-prabhaḥ |
  indu-hāri tama ity amuṃ tadā
  divya-loka-nikaras tv amanyata ||JGc_1,16.22|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: When the son of <s>Danu</s> (<s>Pralamba</s>), of the luster of darkness, carried <s>Rāma</s> of bright, radiant body — then the host of the divine world considered him darkness that steals the moon! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
tasmin kiñcit trāsam āpannavān sa
  jyeṣṭhaḥ paśyan drāk kaniṣṭhasya vaktram |
  tad bhrāmyad-bhrū-līlayā labdha-dṛṣṭir
  duṣṭaṃ muṣṭyā tāḍayat suṣṭhu mūrdhni ||JGc_1,16.23|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: In that [situation], the elder brother, having become somewhat frightened, looking quickly at the face of his younger brother — and having obtained the sight of his playful, moving eyebrow-gesture — struck the wicked one excellently on the head with his fist! // [śālinī]

children.text:
tataḥ prahata-mastakaṃ rudhira-rūṣitaṃ tad vapuḥ
  patat tulitam ujjahat pratihari drutaṃ pupluve |
  yathāñjana-mahī-dharaṃ dalitam akta-rakta-dravaṃ
  tyajan dravati vajrakaḥ sapadi vajra-pāṇiṃ prati ||JGc_1,16.24|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text: Then that body, with head struck, blood-stained, falling, discarding equivalence, flew back swiftly toward <s>Hari</s>; just as the collyrium-mountain (<s>Añjana</s>), split and dripping red liquid, when abandoned, runs swiftly — the thunderbolt toward the wielder of the thunderbolt (<s>Indra</s>)! // [pṛthvī]

children.text:
pralamba-patanaṃ dūre pralambāryāptir antike |
  ubhe te yugapad dṛṣṭe jajñāte smita-vismitī ||JGc_1,16.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
  bāṣpa-śliṣṭatayā tasminn āśliṣṭau bhrātarau mithaḥ |
  yā vāśliṣyārdratāṃ yātā bandhutā bahir antaram ||JGc_1,16.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
The fall of <s>Pralamba</s> far away and the attainment of <s>Pralamba's</s> enemy (<s>Rāma</s>) nearby — both were seen simultaneously, and smiles and wonder were born! // [anuṣṭubh]
Moist with tears, the two brothers embraced each other there; the kinship that had been embraced — the tenderness it attained, both within and without! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
mahā-ravaṃ kṛtavati ca pralambake
  tadā drutaṃ mṛtavati ca dyavi sthitāḥ |
  sunirvṛtā vavṛṣur alaṃ kulaṃ
  vyatarkayann upahasitiṃ harer api ||JGc_1,16.27|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text: When <s>Pralamba</s> had made a great roar and then swiftly died, those stationed in heaven, supremely satisfied, showered abundantly; the entire clan conjectured it as the mockery of <s>Hari</s> himself! // [rucirā]

children.text:
vāhaka-śirasi praharaṇam atrādiṣṭaṃ sadā vihṛtau |
  maryādātikrāntā pralamba bhavatā tathā tu nāsmābhiḥ ||JGc_1,16.28|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text: 'Striking the carrier on the head is always prescribed in this game. O <s>Pralamba</s>, you transgressed the boundary — but not we!' // [udgīti]

children.text: tad evaṃ pralambālambhana-sambhrame' py anudbhrānta-cittās te śṛṅginī-vittāḥ kuṇapatām itasya pramītasya tasya pitṛ-vana-veśaṃ pradeśa-leśaṃ parityajya yojana-vyajya-vistāra-praśasta-bhāṇḍīra-tala-maṇḍalam evādhiṣṭhāya vihāra-niṣṭhāḥ krīḍāpaṇasya spṛhayāyyā jayāyyā gṛhayāyyās tṛṇalobhāviṣṭa-tayā vṛkṣa-ṣaṇḍād viprakṛṣṭām api yamunācchānaccha-muñjāṭavīṃ praviṣṭānām andhī-bhūtānāṃ pāda-bandhanānām anveṣaṇād viśleṣam ājagmuḥ | tataḥ katham apy avadhānataḥ pranaṣṭa-cittatayā spaṣṭa-kaṣṭa-cittā raṃhasā saṅghaśaḥ sabhayaṃ hvayante sma | [28] nūnaṃ deśādhipati-nideśataḥ sadeśam āgatā eva kecit krūrā gā dūragā vidadhur iti ca dhyāyanti sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, even in the tumult of the encounter with <s>Pralamba</s>, those horn-trumpet-bearing ones, their minds unperturbed, abandoning only a small piece of the cremation-ground area of that slain one, and establishing themselves in the circle of the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> tree — which was laudable in its extent of a <s>yojana</s> — they remained devoted to sport. But through the eagerness for the market-games of play — the victorious, house-worthy [games] — from the desire for grass, the cows had entered even the distant dense <s>muñja</s>-grass thicket beyond the <s>Yamunā</s>, becoming blinded and their feet entangled, and [the boys] experienced separation from them through their search. Then, somehow, through attentiveness, with minds bewildered and hearts clearly distressed, they called out hastily, en masse, with fear. [28] Indeed, they thought: 'Surely some cruel ones, sent by the regional lord's command, have made the cows go far away from their proper place.'

children.text: tataś ca gavāṃ khurādi-cihnair ahnāya tāsām adhvānaṃ labdhvā samastā eva tā harir ahvāsta, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, by the hoof-marks and other signs of the cows, having found their path within the day, <s>Hari</s> called all of them together, as follows:

children.text:
kṛṣṇe taṭāgram adhiruhya suvarṇa-varṇa-
  valgūttarīyam anughūrṇya vitīrṇahutau |
  gāvaḥ pratisvam abhinedur udīrṇa-tāpā
  garjat-taḍid-ghana-ghanāghana-tṛṣṇayeva ||JGc_1,16.29|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having climbed to the edge of the bank, waving his gold-colored fine upper garment — threw it open wide, the cows, each one lowing, greatly agitated, [responded] as if with the thirst of a roaring, lightning-filled, dense-dark-cloud! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text: tad evaṃ yadālambhi cāstambhi ca naicikīnicayas tadānīm eva ca dṛṣṭa-nirvilamba-pralamba-pralaya-carāḥ kaṃsa-carā labdhāvasarā muñjāṭavīm udbhaṭa-ceṣṭatayā veṣṭayitvā nirnivāraṇa-kṛpīṭa-kāraṇa-vṛṣṭiṃ jhaṭiti tādṛśa-duṣṭa-vauṣaṭ-kārāspada-tad-vilakṣaṇa-tejasi tasmin pratipakṣatā-kalpanayā nisṛṣṭavantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, at the very time when the cow-herd was found and arrested, just then <s>Kaṃsa's</s> agents — who had seen the swift destruction of <s>Pralamba</s> — finding an opportunity, having encircled the <s>muñja</s>-thicket with violent action, suddenly released an unstoppable fire of no good cause upon that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] of extraordinary radiance — imagining hostility toward him — as an oblation of their wicked 'vaṣaṭ' cry.

children.text: yā khalu jvāla-kalayāpi sarvaṃ roṣād oṣāmāsa kalpam iti prajvalati mahā-jvalane paṭa-paṭāyamānāyāṃ ca mahā-muñjāṭavyāṃ bhītatayāsta-vyasta-cālās te gopālāḥ sakhi-valayārāmatayā kalita-keli-jālāv iha rāma-gopālāv eva bhūri-dūrataḥ śaraṇatayā samupājagmuḥ | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Indeed, when the great fire blazed — which, even with a mere spark of flame, angrily scorched everything for an entire <s>kalpa</s> (eon) — and when the great <s>muñja</s>-thicket was crackling with 'paṭa-paṭa' sounds, those cowherd boys, terrified, running about in confused agitation, approached <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) here — who were entwined in the garland of play with their circle of friends in the grove-delight — as a refuge from a very great distance. And there:

children.text:
dāvāgniṃ dṛṣṭvā te yadapi harir akṣāparatayā
  samīyur vaiyagryaṃ tadapi nija-rakṣām avṛṇuta |
  prasaktis tasyetthaṃ kila bhavati sā ced uyate
  tadā śaktiś cāsya prabhavati yathecchaṃ muhur iti ||JGc_1,16.30|| [śikhariṇī]
yathā-
children.translated_text: As follows:

children.text: kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-vīrya he rāmāmita-vikrama |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O one of great might! O <s>Rāma</s> of immeasurable prowess!

children.text: dāvāgninā dahyamānān prapannāṃs trātum arhathaḥ ||[BhP 10.19.9] ityādi
children.translated_text: You are worthy of saving us who are surrendered, being burned by the forest fire!' // [BhP 10.19.9] — and so forth.

When they saw the forest fire, even though they came to <s>Hari</s> with the foremost urgency, their agitation still chose his own protection. His attachment thus — if it is spoken of — then his power too prevails according to his wish, again and again! // [śikharinī]

children.text: tad evaṃ dūrāgatānāṃ kārpaṇya-paṇya-bhaṇita-śravaṇam ārabhya tasmād abhyāsa-gatānām api bhayam upalabhya śrīmān kṛṣṇas tv idaṃ sasaṃrambhaṃ bhāvayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Thus, beginning from hearing the pitiable, merchandise-like words of those who had come from afar, perceiving even the fear of those who had come nearby — the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> contemplated this with agitation:

children.text:
ātmano' py alam amī mama priyā
  hā davaṃ prati davaṃ samiyrati |
  gīrṇam eva karavāṇy amuṃ tataḥ
  ko yamaḥ ka iha vā bhaved haraḥ ||JGc_1,16.31|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'These dear ones of mine, dearer even than myself — alas, they run swiftly toward the forest fire! Then let me simply swallow it — what is <s>Yama</s> (Death) here, or who would be <s>Hara</s> (Śiva)?' // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: kintu mayā vaiśvānara-nigaraṇaṃ na soḍhuṃ parivṛḍhā bhaveyur ete iti vicintya provāca-mā bhaiṣṭa netra-puṭaṃ tv anudghaṭitaṃ ghaṭayata iti |
children.translated_text: But thinking: 'These might not endure my swallowing of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire), and would be confounded' — he said: 'Fear not! But close your eyelids!'

children.text: nimīlad-vilocaneṣu ca teṣu tad-āveśa-vaśayā kṛta-praveśayā yogamāyayā tat-kāla-kalpita-mahā-jaladhara-kalpāpara-śarīras tatratyenānalpenānanena tam aduḥkhata eva sarvaṃ vibhrakṣantaṃ bhakṣitavān |
children.translated_text: And when they had closed their eyes, through <s>Yogamāyā</s> — who, by his will, had made an entrance — with another body fashioned at that moment as a great rain-cloud, and with a vast, immense mouth situated right there, he swallowed all of that [fire] which was consuming everything without distress.

children.text: tathā tad-icchayā sudhā-culukāyamānam ity eke | tayaivaṃ cānyad api cakāra | yad uktaṃ-
children.translated_text: And thus, some say, by his will it was transformed into a draught of nectar. And she (<s>Yogamāyā</s>) did something else too. As it is stated:

children.text:
tataś ca te' kṣīṇy unmīlya punar bhāṇḍīram āpitāḥ |
  niśāmya vismitā āsann ātmānaṃ gāś ca mocitāḥ ||iti | [BhP 10.19.13]
children.translated_text: 'Then they, opening their eyes, were brought back to the <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> [tree]; perceiving [this], they were astonished — [finding] themselves and the cows liberated!' // [BhP 10.19.13]

children.text:
atha dhenu-tatiṃ vinivartya harir
  bala-yuktatayā muralīṃ kalayan |
  sahacāri-gaṇa-prathitātma-yaśā
  vrajam āgatavān ahani glapite ||JGc_1,16.32|| [toṭaka]
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, having turned back the herds of cows, playing the <s>muralī</s> (flute) with the force of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), his own fame celebrated by the circle of companions, arrived at <s>Vraja</s> when the day had waned. // [toṭaka]

children.text:
gavāṃ dhūlir nādaḥ khura-ghaṭita-ghaṭṭa-dhvani-ghaṭā
  hares tāsāṃ hūtiḥ śravaṇa-gaṇa-bhid-veṇu-raṇitam |
  amībhis te kṛṣṭās taratamatayā gokula-janā
  na pṛṣṭhyaṃ nāgrīyaṃ na samam avidur na svam api ||JGc_1,16.33|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: The dust of the cows, their lowing, the cluster of clattering sounds from hoof-impacts, <s>Hari's</s> calling of them, the flute-sound that splits the faculty of hearing — by these, the people of <s>Gokula</s> were drawn with varying degrees; they knew neither what was behind nor what was ahead, neither what was level nor even their own selves! // [śikharinī]

children.text:
yadyapi bahu-saṅghaṭṭana-dhūli-dhvāntaṃ ca sarvatra |
  tadapi harer mukha-candraḥ pratijanam ānanditaṃ cakre ||JGc_1,16.34|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text: Even though everywhere there was the darkness of dust from the massed collision — even so, the moon-face of <s>Hari</s> delighted each person! // [upagīti]

children.text: atha pūrvavan mātara-pitarādi-racita-sukha-vitarau bhrātarau nija-nilayaṃ praviviśatuḥ | [37] sakhāyaś ca pralamba-davānala-kathā-prathanayā sarvaṃ vismāyayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, as before, the two brothers — who spread happiness created by their parents and others — entered their own home. [37] And the companions, through the narration of the tales of <s>Pralamba</s> and the forest fire, astonished everyone.

children.text: tad etat procya samāpanam āha sma-
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he (<s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>) recited the conclusion:

children.text:
īdṛśas tava gopendra putraḥ puṇya-kṛta-stavaḥ |
  premārdraḥ suhṛdāṃ yas tu dāvāgnim api pītavān ||JGc_1,16.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Such is your son, O lord of the cowherds, praised by the meritorious — he who, tender with love for his friends, drank even the forest fire!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
pralamba-dava-saṃvarta-nivartanaṃ nāma
ṣoḍaśaṃ pūraṇam
 ||16||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the Śrī Śrī <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Sixteenth Chapter named 'The Removal of the Catastrophe of <s>Pralamba</s> and the Forest Fire'
||16||

children.text: atha saptadaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Seventeenth Chapter.

children.text: veṇu-śikṣā-cchalena preyasī-bhikṣā
children.translated_text: Soliciting the Beloveds under the Pretext of Flute-Instruction.

children.text: atha pūrvavad vilakṣaṇāyāṃ kṣaṇadā-sabhāyāṃ samutkaṇṭhaḥ sa madhukaṇṭhaḥ kathayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then, as before, in the distinguished evening assembly, that <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, full of longing, narrated:

children.text: pūrva-pūrvānusāreṇa dhenuka-vadhānantara-vyavahāreṇa preyasīnāṃ pratyaham eva vardhamānāḥ kamala-kalikāvad utkalikā madhusūdanasya bahir īhitair durūhāṃ spṛhāṃ bṛṃhayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: 'In accordance with the previous [narrative] sequence, following the events after the slaying of <s>Dhenuka</s>, the daily increasing longings of the beloveds — like lotus buds — nourished their desire, difficult to fathom, through the outward deeds of <s>Madhusūdana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).'

children.text: tatrāpi sarvādhikāyāḥ śrī-rādhikāyās tu nitarāṃ, tatra tūpalakṣaṇatayā śrī-rādhā-mādhavayor varṇyate-
children.translated_text: And among them, of Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s>, who excels all — especially; there, as representative, [the love] of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> is described:

children.text:
prasaṅgecchā vīkṣā-spṛhitam anuṣaṅgābhilaṣitaṃ
  pṛthag loka-dveṣaḥ pratisamayam udvega-kalanā |
  ime bhāvā yugme yugapad uditās tat-krama-vaśād
  aho dūra-sthityor api dayitayor eka-rucitā ||JGc_1,17.1|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: The desire for contact, the wish for a glance, the longing for companionship, aversion to the public, agitation at every moment — these feelings arose simultaneously in both, and consequently, ah, even when standing far apart, the two beloveds had a single inclination! // [śikharinī]

children.text:
ādarśāv iva tau svacchau sadābhimukhatāṃ gatau |
  rādhā-mādhavayor bhāvau mitho bhāvān upeyatuḥ ||JGc_1,17.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Like two mirrors, those two, being clear and always facing each other — the feelings of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> attained each other's feelings! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
bhūyo bhūyo dṛśyate yarhi mūrcchā
  rādhāyāṃ vā śrīharau vā rahas tu |
  anyo' nyasya sphūrtir evāpti-tulyā
  kalyāṇāya prāyaśaḥ kalpate sma ||JGc_1,17.3|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: When fainting was seen again and again, whether in <s>Rādhā</s> or in Śrī <s>Hari</s> — in secret, it was the very manifestation of the other that was equal to attainment, and mostly it served their welfare! // [śālinī]

children.text: tad evaṃ tābhis tasyātidurlabhasya spṛhātiśaya-vāhitayā nātihitāyāṃ śarady ativāhitāyāṃ mārgaśīrṣas tu tāsāṃ patiṃ-manya-gṛha-gamanāya mārga-śīrṣatām avāpa |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the autumn — which was not very favorable through the excess of their longing for him, the supremely difficult to attain — had been passed through by those [<s>gopīs</s>], the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> (November-December) attained the headship of the path for their going to the houses of those [husbands] whom they considered their masters.

children.text: yatra ca kanyānāṃ mātara-pitareṣu tad-dānāya pūrvam eva svayam anabhirucitī-kṛta-murajid-itareṣu, svapna-doṣād evānyatrāvagata-tad-vitareṣu, tata eva duḥkhitatayānabhinandita-tat-sambandhi-nikareṣu, samprati tāsām atiduḥkha-śuṣkatā-dṛṣṭyā bhīti-pareṣu, tata eva tat-prasthāpanāyāṃ sthagitāntareṣu loka-dharma-vigāna-labdha-dareṣu ca, ghūrṇita-cittā pūrṇimā tad idaṃ nirdideśa-
children.translated_text: Where, regarding the parents who had previously themselves rejected suitors other than the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) for the giving of their daughters in marriage — having learned of such others only through the fault of dreams — and therefore being unhappy and not welcoming the company of those marriage-relatives — now, seeing the excessive withered unhappiness of their daughters and being consumed by fear, and hence inwardly blocked regarding sending them off — having gained anxiety through consideration of worldly <s>dharma</s> — the full-moon goddess (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), with agitated mind, gave this instruction:

children.text: bhavantas tāvat taṭasthī-bhavantas tiṣṭhantu, vayam evāmūr anunīya tat-tad-gṛham upanīya tat-tat-prakriyāṃ kriyā-viṣayī-kariṣyāmaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: 'Let your honors for now remain neutral bystanders! We ourselves, having appeased these [girls], shall lead them to their respective houses and make each respective procedure the object of action.'

children.text: atha janyaṃ-manyāṃs teṣām anādaram avadhāya manyuṃ manyamānān svayam eva sā devatādi-mānyā sāmnā sammānya yathā sva-manīṣitam evāṅgīkārayāñ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving the disrespect of those who considered [the suitors] worthy of the wedding, and thinking them wrathful — that one, worthy of worship by deities and others, herself personally honoring them with conciliation, made them accept exactly her own intention.

children.text: kanyās tu tā dhanyā varaṃ-manyālayāntaḥ-prayāṇaṃ tatra ca labdha-tad-añcala-nyāsa-nijāñcalatādy-anyāyam asammanyamānā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: But those blessed maidens did not accept the journey into the house of those considered worthy husbands, and the injustice there of the deposit of the hem [of the garment] — [the marriage ceremony] — they did not regard as proper.

children.text: atha tāḥ sā śapatha-prathanayā tad-ālayeṣv asambhavam apīṣṭa-lambhanam aniṣṭa-vipralambhanaṃ ca viśrambhaviṣayaṃ vidhāya duḥsaha-nānādhyavasāyād viṣkambhya gamana-karmaṇi lambhyamānāḥ pathi tu svamāyayā gopayantī tatra tat-sadṛg-anyāś cāropayantī tat tan nirvāhayāmāsa | paścād eva ca tās tatra vāsayāmāsa | tās tu tatra ca parama-trastā babhūvuḥ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then she (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), by the declaration of an oath, having arranged in their [husbands'] homes both the impossible attainment of the desired and the [avoidance of] unwanted deception as a matter of trust, and having motivated them — who were being engaged in the act of going despite their various unbearable resolutions — on the path she concealed [them] through her own <s>māyā</s>, and substituting other women resembling them there, she managed those respective situations. And afterwards, she settled those [gopīs] there [in their in-laws' homes]. But they became supremely frightened there as well, for:

children.text:
yāsāṃ deho' py eṣa bandī-gṛhābhaḥ
  kṛṣṇālābhād gopikānāṃ babhūva |
  tāsāṃ gehaṃ paitṛkaṃ śarmaṇe kiṃ
  yady evaṃ dhik śvāśuraṃ vahnir eva ||JGc_1,17.4|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: 'For those <s>gopīs</s> whose very body had become like a prison | due to not obtaining <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, | what happiness could their father's house bring? | If so, then curse the father-in-law's house — it is fire itself!' || (JGc 1,17.4) [śālinī]

children.text:
apy anukūlaṃ yāsāṃ pratikūlaṃ syād vidūrage kṛṣṇe |
  tāsāṃ pratikūlaṃ tu sphuṭam evāsīt kukūla-talpābham ||JGc_1,17.5|| [gīti]
children.translated_text: 'Even what is favorable for them would become unfavorable when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is far away; | and what was unfavorable was clearly like a bed of burning chaff!' || (JGc 1,17.5) [gīti]

children.text: tathāpi paurṇamāsī tās tat-tad-geha-madhyam adhyāsīnā vidhāya yadā calitum udyatāsīt tadāmūḥ punar vica-pracām āptā niśca-pracā-kṛte tad idam ādiṣṭavatī, yadā bhavatībhiḥ sva-maryādā-lopas tarkyate, tadā prapalāyya sthīyatām | samādhānaṃ punaḥ kayācid vidyayāsmābhir eva vidhātavyam, sahasā palāyana-dhāma ca tatra tatra vidhātavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, when <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, having settled them within those respective houses, was about to depart, they — having obtained anxiety without finding certitude — she instructed this for the sake of [their] certitude: 'Whenever your honors apprehend a breach of your own boundaries [of propriety], then flee and take your stand. Restoration shall again be arranged by us through some skill, and a refuge for sudden flight should be prepared in various places.'

children.text: tad evaṃ rāja-kārāgṛhād vairi-kārāgṛha iva pitṛ-gṛhāt tatra gatvā vasantīṣu,
children.translated_text: Thus, as they went from the king's prison to an enemy's prison, as it were — from the father's house to there — and dwelt [there]:

children.text:
yāvān ajani nirodhas tāvaty utkāpi saṃvavṛdhe |
  kṛṣṇa-premavatīṣu śvāsānila-līnatāṃ yātā ||JGc_1,17.6|| [upagīti]
  yadyapi manasi samiddhā hari-pariripsā tathāpi tābhiḥ sā |
  āvriyate sma vicārais tatir iva vahneḥ sad-indhana-prakaraiḥ ||JGc_1,17.7|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
'As much as the restraint grew, so much did the longing increase even more | in those who possessed love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — [that longing] had merged into the movement of their breaths!' || (JGc 1,17.6) [upagīti]
'Although the desire to embrace <s>Hari</s> was kindled in their minds, nevertheless | it was being covered by deliberations — like fire by heaps of good fuel!' || (JGc 1,17.7) [gīti]

children.text: tac ca śrī-rādhā-pradhānatayā varṇyate, yathā-
children.translated_text: And this is described principally through <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>, as follows:

children.text:
pīyūṣa-cchavi-dhāri-hāri-kiraṇaḥ sarvatra śaśvaj-jaḍī-
  bhāva-prāpti-guṇaḥ sadārdra-hṛdayaḥ sad-bhrū-cakorī-gatiḥ |
  so' yaṃ hanta mayā kathaṃ harir aho tat-prāṇayā tyajyatāṃ
  dharmo gacchati kintv adharma-padavīṃ ruddhvā ca māna-kṣayām ||JGc_1,17.8|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[13] śrī-kṛṣṇasya ca bhāvanā, yathā-
children.translated_text:
'He whose nectar-hued, enchanting rays are everywhere, whose quality is to bring | perpetual stupefaction at every moment, whose heart is ever moist, | who is the refuge of the good <s>cakora</s>-eyebrowed ones — | alas, how shall I, <s>Hari</s>, forsake him? Yet by my very life-breath, | let duty be abandoned — but it goes toward the path of unrighteousness, blocking the dissolution of pride!' || (JGc 1,17.8) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[13] And the feeling of the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows:

children.text:
mad-eka-ceto mat-prāṇā rādhānya-vaśatāṃ gatā |
  yāṃ smaran mama hā cetaś cetanām āvariṣyati ||JGc_1,17.9|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s>, whose sole mind is fixed on Me, whose very life-breath is Mine, has gone under another's control! | Alas, remembering her, my consciousness will become clouded!' || (JGc 1,17.9) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  rādhāṃ tathā smaran kṛṣṇaḥ snigdhaṃ rāgi vilocanam |
  kiyanty ahāni mārṣṭi sma hanta hāridra-vāsasā ||JGc_1,17.10|| [anuṣṭubh]
[14] milanāyāti-vaiyagryaṃ ca-
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Thus remembering <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with tender, impassioned eyes, | wiped [his tears] with a yellow cloth for how many days — alas!' || (JGc 1,17.10) [anuṣṭubh]
[14] And the intense eagerness for union:

children.text:
dharmātikrami cittaṃ katham adhimitraṃ ca tat prakāśate? |
  iti harir upacita-yuktir yuyoja dūtyāya kevalāṃ dṛṣṭim ||JGc_1,17.11|| [gīti]
children.translated_text: '"How can the mind that transgresses duty, and the excessive friendliness, be revealed?" | Thus <s>Hari</s>, having accumulated reasoning, employed his glance alone as a messenger!' || (JGc 1,17.11) [gīti]

children.text: idam eva vakṣyate tābhiḥ-
children.translated_text: This very thing will be said by them [the gopīs]:

children.text:
śarad-udāśaye sādhu-jāta-sat-
  sarasijodara-śrī-muṣā dṛśā |
  surata-nātha te' śulka-dāsikā
varada nighnato neha kiṃ vadhaḥ? ||[BhP 10.31.2] iti |
children.translated_text: O bestower of boons — for one who slays, is there no [guilt of] slaying here?' || [BhP 10.31.2]

children.text:
yataḥ-
  kṛṣṇasyānyatra dṛk-prāntaḥ sadbhiḥ śāstra-phalaṃ smṛtam |
  hanta tāsu punaḥ so' yam ebhiḥ śastra-phalaṃ matam ||JGc_1,17.12|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
For:
'The sidelong glance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [directed] elsewhere is considered by the good to be the fruit of scripture; | alas, but when that same [glance falls] upon those [gopīs], by these [others] it is deemed the fruit of a weapon!' || (JGc 1,17.12) [anuṣṭubh]
'With a glance that steals the beauty of the interior of a well-born, fine | lotus in the clear autumn lake, | O Lord of love, we are Your unpurchased maidservants,

children.text:
tataś ca-
  rātrindivaṃ vasati cetasi hanta bhāva-
  jvālā harer uta tadīya-ramā-gaṇānām |
  sandhyā-dvaye vyativiloka-sukhājya-siktā
  sāgni-dvijālaya ivāgnitatiḥ samiddhā ||JGc_1,17.13|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Night and day, the flame of the emotion for <s>Hari</s> and for His beloved <s>Ramā</s>-host | dwells in the heart, alas — anointed at the two twilights | with the ghee of the happiness of beholding in worldly encounters — | like the fire-row in a house of fire and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, it blazes ever more!' || (JGc 1,17.13) [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tatra ca-
  goṣṭhād vanaṃ praviśato vanataś ca goṣṭhaṃ
  lokena lokana-kṛte saha mādhavendoḥ |
  sambhūya saṅgatavatīṣu ca tat-priyāsu
  rādhā jayaty uḍuṣu paurṇima-rādhikeva ||JGc_1,17.14|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
And there:
'As the moon of <s>Mādhava</s> enters the forest from the cow-settlement and [returns] from the forest to the cow-settlement, | [seen] by the people for the purpose of beholding, when His beloveds come together and join [to see Him] — | among the stars, <s>Rādhā</s> is victorious, like the full-moon <s>Rādhikā</s> (the asterism)!' || (JGc 1,17.14) [vasantatilakā]

children.text: tatra ca pragetana-vana-prasthāne-
children.translated_text: And there, at the early-morning departure to the forest:

children.text:
mithyāhāsān akuruta hariḥ spṛṣṭa-pārśvastha-hastaṃ
  vīkṣāṃ vakra-praṇaya-valitām ardham ardhaṃ vitene |
  āśleṣādyaṃ viharaṇa-gaṇaṃ mitra-vargeṣu cakre
  dūre gatvāpy ahaha muralī-saṃvidaḥ saṃvyadhatta ||JGc_1,17.15|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: '<s>Hari</s> made false laughter, touching the hand of one standing beside him; | extended a crooked, love-laden glance, half and half; | performed the first embracing and other sport-acts among the friend-groups; | and even having gone far, alas, he arranged the signals of the flute!' || (JGc 1,17.15) [mandākrāntā]

children.text:
idam eva ca tābhir vakṣyate,
  prahasitaṃ priya prema-vīkṣitaṃ
  viharaṇaṃ ca te dhyāna-maṅgalam |
  rahasi saṃvido yā hṛdi-spṛśaḥ
children.translated_text:
And this very thing will be said by them [the gopīs]:
'Your laughter, O beloved, Your love-laden glance, | Your play, and Your auspicious meditation — | the private conversations that touch the heart —

children.text: kuhaka no manaḥ kṣobhayanti hi ||[BhP 10.31.10] iti |
children.translated_text: O deceiver, they agitate our minds indeed!' || [BhP 10.31.10]

children.text: atha sāyantanāgamane tu-
children.translated_text: Now, at the evening return:

children.text:
yadā vā goṣṭhaṃ sampraviśati tadā ca bhramarakair
  vṛtaṃ vaktrāmbhojaṃ dhana-khura-parāgair valayitam |
  amūṣāṃ netrāliṣv abhimukhatayā darśayati tan-
  milat-pāśaṃ yantraṃ madana-racitaṃ bandhum iva tān ||JGc_1,17.16|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'Or, when He enters the cow-settlement, then His lotus-face, | surrounded by bees, encircled by the dust of the cows' hooves — | He shows it face-to-face to the rows of their eyes — | as a device fashioned by <s>Madana</s> (Cupid), with meeting nooses, as if binding them!' || (JGc 1,17.16) [śikharinī]

children.text: evam eva ca tābhir vakṣyate-
children.translated_text: And thus this very thing will be said by them:

children.text:
dina-parikṣaye nīla-kuntalair
  vana-ruhānanaṃ bibhrad āvṛtam |
  dhana-rajasvalaṃ darśayan muhur
manasi naḥ smaraṃ vīra yacchasi ||[BhP 10.31.12] iti |
children.translated_text: You grant Love in our minds, O hero!' || [BhP 10.31.12]

children.text: evam aharahar api parasparaṃ spardhayeva vardhamānatayā tāsām utkalikāḥ kalita-madhu-mādhavādhikalā-vyākulatākulatāṃ kalayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, day after day, their surging longings — growing as if in mutual competition — reached the state of agitation, troubled by the excessive portion of the spring's (<s>madhu-mādhava</s>) honeyed [season].
'At the close of day, bearing Your face | — that of a forest-born [lotus], covered with dark locks, | displaying [the radiance of] dust-enriched wealth — again and again

children.text:
yathā varṇitaṃ pralamba-vadha-vāsara-sambandhi-sandhyām anusandhāya,
  gopīnāṃ paramānanda āsīd govinda-darśane |
children.translated_text:
As was described, tracing the twilight connected with the day of the slaying of <s>Pralamba</s>:
'The <s>gopīs</s> had supreme bliss in seeing <s>Govinda</s>;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ yuga-śatam iva yāsāṃ yena vinābhavat ||[BhP 10.19.16] iti |
children.translated_text: a single moment without whom was like a hundred <s>yugas</s> for them.' || [BhP 10.19.16]

children.text:
asya cābhidheyam idam,
  tāsāṃ kṛṣṇāvaloke pramada-samuditir na svarūpeṇa vaktuṃ
  śakyā kintu sva-kārya-sphuraṇa-padatayā kiñcid uddeśam āptā |
  tad-viśleṣe yathāsāṃ yuga-śataka-daśāṃ yāti kālaḥ kalākhyas
  tadvat tasyānuṣaṅge yuga-śatam api tad bhāti śaśvat kalābham ||JGc_1,17.17|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
And the meaning of this is:
'The ecstatic delight of those [gopīs] in beholding <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> cannot be described in its own nature, | but has been indicated somewhat through the shining of its effect; | just as in separation from Him, even a moment called <s>kalā</s> reaches the state of a hundred <s>yugas</s> for them, | so too in His company, even a hundred <s>yugas</s> always appears like a mere <s>kalā</s>!' || (JGc 1,17.17) [sragdharā]

children.text:
kalāpi yadi viśleṣe yugānāṃ śatatāṃ gatā |
  rātrindivīya-saṅkhyāyāṃ tadā śaṅkāmahe vayam ||JGc_1,17.18|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'If in separation even a <s>kalā</s> reaches the state of a hundred <s>yugas</s>, | then we suspect [what happens] in the calculation of day and night!' || (JGc 1,17.18) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: evaṃ sāyam-prātikāvalokana-valataḥ katham api nidāghe' pi kṣapite mayūrān madayitnūnāṃ gadayitnūnāṃ ca stanayitnūnāṃ samāgamaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, from the leverage of the evening and morning beholdings, even though the summer had somehow been endured, the arrival of the peacock-delighters, the thunder-bearing ones (rain-clouds), occurred. As follows:

children.text:
akuṇṭhām utkaṇṭhāṃ niravadhi vitarkyāli-vitatir
  yadā tāsām agre hari-paricitaṃ vṛttam aruṇat |
  tadā varṣā jātās taḍid-anugatāmbhoda-valitāḥ
  pratīpābhāḥ kṛṣṇa-sphuraṇam adhikaṃ hā vidadhire ||JGc_1,17.19|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'When the rows of bee-swarms, whose unblunted longing was limitless, | before those [gopīs] painted the scene familiar to <s>Hari</s>, | then the rains came — rolling with clouds accompanied by lightning — | whose appearances, alas, produced even greater the flashing of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' || (JGc 1,17.19) [śikharinī]

children.text:
nūnaṃ nidāghena vibhūya jajñe
santaptir āsāṃ hari-rāginīnām |
  varṣāsu śāmyed iti saṅginīnāṃ
nirṇītir āsīd viparīta-rītiḥ ||JGc_1,17.20|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: 'Surely, the torment of these women enamored of <s>Hari</s> | — having been generated by the summer heat — would be cooled in the rains — | such was the conclusion of their companions; but the course was the reverse!' || (JGc 1,17.20) [indravajrā]

children.text:
varṣā dvitīyā dadhire' kṣi-nīrair
  antaḥ sphurat-kṛṣṇa-ghanābhir ābhiḥ |
  itthaṃ nininduḥ kila te ruvantaḥ
  svājīvya-varṣānugatāḥ plavādyāḥ ||JGc_1,17.21|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: 'A second rainy season was borne by these women through the tears in their eyes, | in whom the dark cloud of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> flashed within; | thus, those frogs and the like who croaked, following the rains — | their livelihood — were reproached by them!' || (JGc 1,17.21) [indravajrā]

children.text:
kalāpām āsur etāsu kalāpāś ca kalāpināṃ |
  smarārdha-candra-bāṇābhā yatraike bhānti conmukhāḥ ||JGc_1,17.22|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The arts (<s>kalās</s>) among these [gopīs] became the plumage (<s>kalāpas</s>) of peacocks; | of which some, resembling Cupid's half-moon arrows, | shone radiantly, facing forward.' || (JGc 1,17.22) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
varṣāḥ śītalatākarair nija-guṇair āsāṃ manaḥ-śāntatām
  ānetuṃ kila yad yad atra vidadhuḥ sarvaṃ ca tat pratyuta |
  dveṣaṃ tā bata menire yad anu ca prāṇālibhiḥ śaṅkitaṃ
  hanta dviṣṭa-suhṛd-daśeyam uditā hā hā vidheḥ kā gatiḥ? ||JGc_1,17.23|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'Whatever the rains did with their cooling qualities | to bring peace to the minds of these [gopīs] — all of it instead | they considered to be hostility! And thereafter, their companions suspected | that alas, the condition of a hostile friend has arisen — ah, ah, what is fate's course?' || (JGc 1,17.23) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: tatra ca gṛha-nigṛhītānāṃ tāsāṃ manaḥ-kathā, yathā-
children.translated_text: And there, the inner narrative of those who were confined in the house, as follows:

children.text:
kharjarādi-phalaiḥ sukanda-valitair mitraiḥ samaṃ prāvṛṣi
  prāñcad-vṛṣṭija-vāri-vāriṇi taru-kroḍe' śana-krīḍanam |
  nīra-prānta-śilāsu tāsu dadhi-yug-bhipsādi sambhojanaṃ
  dūrād dhenv-anuhūtir apy aghajitā naś cittam ulluñcati ||JGc_1,17.24|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'Eating dates and other fruits with sweet stalks, together with friends, in the rainy season, | in the hollow of a tree that shelters from the descending rain-water, | feasting with food including yogurt on those rocks by the water's edge — | even the calling of cows from afar by the slayer of <s>Agha</s> tears at our hearts!' || (JGc 1,17.24) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
yatra ca,
  ghanāgama-ghanāgame viramitājitonmīlane
  samasta-jana-śarmadāḥ sapadi khañjarīṭekṣaṇāḥ |
  amūḥ śuci-ruci-śriyā sva-hṛdi kṛṣṇa-bhāvaṃ gatā
  hari-vraja-nava-priyās tamasi līnatām āgatāḥ ||JGc_1,17.25|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
And there:
'At the dense arrival of the dense clouds, when the opening of the unconquered one [the sun] had ceased, | those <s>khañjarīṭa</s>-eyed ones (wagtail-eyed gopīs), who bestow happiness on all people, | suddenly having entered the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-state in their hearts through the splendor of pure radiant beauty — | those new beloveds of <s>Hari's</s> <s>Vraja</s> — merged into the darkness.' || (JGc 1,17.25) [pṛthvī]

children.text: atra tāsāṃ trāsa-vacanam-
children.translated_text: Here, their words of fear:

children.text:
iraṃmada-radās te' mī nīradā api sarvadā |
  carvanti kṣauṇi-pṛṣṭha-sthān garjanti kila garvataḥ ||JGc_1,17.26|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text: 'Those clouds with teeth of <s>Iraṃmada</s> (Indra's elephant), always | devour those standing on the earth's surface and roar with pride!' || (JGc 1,17.26) [udgīti]

children.text: aho, citrīyate seyaṃ prema-gati-vaicitrī yatas tādṛśi ca tad-vṛtte kadācid ānukūlya-spṛśīva śrī-rādhā-stutīnām ādhāratā dṛśyate | [27] yathā tasyās tat paśyantyā bhāvaneyam-
children.translated_text: Ah, this variety of the course of love is wonderful, for in such circumstances and such behavior, sometimes even <s>Śrī Rādhā's</s> praises appear to be touched by favorableness. [27] As follows, her contemplation while seeing that [rainy season]:

children.text:
ayi taḍit tvam asau kva nu kiṃ tapaḥ
  kiyad aho kṛtavaty asi tad vada |
  yad imam ambu-dharaṃ hari-vakṣasas
  tulitam āli gatā ramase sadā ||JGc_1,17.27|| [drutavilambitā]
children.translated_text: 'O lightning! You — where, pray, have you been? What austerity, | and how much of it, have you performed — tell me! | That you, having reached this rain-cloud, comparable to <s>Hari's</s> chest, | O friend, always sport with delight!' || (JGc 1,17.27) [drutavilambitā]

children.text: yatra ca pramādataḥ sā kiñcana procyāpi sakhyām api saṅkocād anyathā prakhāpayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: And where, having inadvertently said something [revealing], she covered it up differently even before her friend, out of shyness:

children.text:
ahaha paśyata: kṛṣṇa-ghanāghanaṃ
  prasajatī capalā khalu khelati |
  smarasi kiṃ nu hareḥ smara-kautukaṃ?
  nahi nahīdam ṛtor guṇa-varṇanam! ||JGc_1,17.28|| iti | [drutavilambita?]
children.translated_text: 'Ahaha, look: the fickle one (<s>capalā</s> = lightning) indeed plays, | clinging to the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-dark dense cloud! | Do you remember the love-play of <s>Hari</s>? | No, no — this is [merely] a description of the season's qualities!' || (JGc 1,17.28) [drutavilambitā]

children.text:
kadācic ca-
  meghāgama-samaye' sminn adhigata-haritā dṛśāṃ sampat |
  haraye spṛhayasi rādhe nahi nahi śādvala-vibhūtaye dviṣati ||JGc_1,17.29|| iti | [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
And sometimes:
'In this time of cloud-arrival, the greenness attained is the wealth of the eyes — | do you long for <s>Hari</s>, O <s>Rādhā</s>? No, no — [you long] for the verdant splendor, you hater [of it]!' || (JGc 1,17.29) [udgīti]

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇasya dig-darśanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Now, an indication from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa's</s> side, as follows:

children.text:
śikhaṇḍināṃ yā kala-nṛtya-mādhurī
  śikhaṇḍa-cūḍasya sadātiśarmadā |
  na sānusandhānam itā tad astu yan
  mūrdhnaḥ śikhaṇḍaṃ ca jagāma vismṛtim ||JGc_1,17.30|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: 'The sweetness of the beautiful dance of the peacocks — | always supremely delightful for the crest-crested one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — | it did not reach him with [its usual] resonance; so be it — | even the peacock-feather on his head fell into forgetfulness!' || (JGc 1,17.30) [upajāti]

children.text: tad evaṃ suṣṭhu cāpaṣṭhutām anuṣṭhāya gatāyāṃ prāvṛṣi śarad api, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the rainy season had passed, having performed well the practice of restless longing, even the autumn [came]:

children.text:
āgamiṣyati śarad bhuvi dyavi
  svacchatāṃ vidadhatīti cintitam |
  hanta tābhir udaye tadīyake
  svaṃ dadhe dvi-guṇa-bhāvanāvilam ||JGc_1,17.31|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: '"Autumn will come and create clarity on earth and in the sky" — | thus they had thought; | but alas, at its rise, | their own [clarity] was rendered doubly turbid with emotion!' || (JGc 1,17.31) [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
sa-taḍid-vārida-vṛndaṃ nirīkṣya pūrvaṃ yad eva yā taptā |
  tad apaśyanty api seyaṃ samprati rādhā bhṛśaṃ dūnā ||JGc_1,17.32|| [āryā]
children.translated_text: 'Having previously seen the cloud-cluster with lightning and been scorched, | she — even now, this <s>Rādhā</s>, not seeing it — is exceedingly distressed!' || (JGc 1,17.32) [āryā]

children.text: tatra ca rādhā-kṛṣṇayor nakha-lipi-valayita-kisalaya-dala-dvaya-gataṃ padya-dvayaṃ vāyunā parasparaṃ nītam | tad, yathā-
children.translated_text: And there, a pair of verses inscribed by nail-writing on a pair of tender leaf-sprouts by <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was carried to each other by the wind. They were as follows:

children.text:
taḍitaḥ puṇya-śālinyaḥ sadā yā ghana-jīvanāḥ |
  tena sārdham adṛśyanta, nādṛśyanta ca taṃ vinā ||JGc_1,17.33|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Those lightning-flashes who are rich in merit and whose life is always the cloud — | they were seen together with him, and were not seen without him!' || (JGc 1,17.33) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
āvṛtim ajahād indur vilasati haṃsaś ca nīla-kañjaṃ ca |
  vṛndāvanam anu hā dhig daivaṃ tat tan na dṛśyate tasyāḥ ||JGc_1,17.34|| iti|| [gīti]
  rādhā-kṛṣṇāv ittham anyo' nyam āptaṃ
  daivāt patraṃ śaśvad āśliṣya sāśru |
  antaḥ-śūnya-svarṇa-bimbāntar uptaṃ
  madhye hāraṃ nāyakaṃ nirmimāte ||JGc_1,17.35|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
The moon abandoned its covering, and the swan and the blue lotus shine forth;
in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — alas, curse the fate — these things of hers are not seen! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.34, <s>gīti</s>]
<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, thus each having received a letter destined for the other,
constantly embracing it with tears,
fashion as if a leading necklace planted within
a golden image that is inwardly hollow! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.35, <s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: atra sakhīnām api svinnatā, yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, the distress of the <s>sakhīs</s> (female friends) too, as follows:

children.text:
jalaṃ kumudam ambujaṃ vidhu-ruciś ca yasyāṃ śarady
  aho vikasad-ātmatām agamad āśu tasyām api |
  mano nayanam ānanaṃ daśana-kāntir āsāṃ punaḥ
  sadā malinatām agād iti kim ālibhiḥ sahyatām? ||JGc_1,17.36|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
In autumn, the water, the night-lotus, the day-lotus, and the moonlight —
alas, in that [season] too, they quickly attained the state of blossoming;
but the mind, the eyes, the face, and the luster of the teeth of these [<s>gopīs</s>]
always attained a state of pallor — so how could this be endured by their friends? // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.36, <s>pṛthvī</s>]

children.text: atra ca varṇitaṃ labdha-varṇair api,
children.translated_text: And here, even those who had attained eloquence described it:

children.text: āśliṣya sama-śītoṣṇaṃ prasūna-vana-mārutam |
children.translated_text: "Embracing the forest breeze, equally cool and warm, laden with flowers,"

children.text: janās tāpaṃ juhur gopyo na kṛṣṇa-hṛta-cetasaḥ ||[BhP 10.20.45]
children.translated_text: "people bore away their fever — but the <s>gopīs</s>, whose minds were stolen by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, [could not]!" // [BhP 10.20.45]

children.text:
yataḥ-
  saundaryaṃ tan-nīlimāsau dyutiḥ sā
  lāvaṇyaṃ tat te ca līlā-vilāsāḥ |
  pīyūṣa-śrīṇy aṅga-saṅge priyāṇāṃ
  viśleṣe tāny eva hālāhalāni ||JGc_1,17.37|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
For:
That beauty, that dark luster, that radiance,
that charm, and those playful graces —
are nectars for the beloved in bodily union,
but in separation, those very things are <s>hālāhala</s> poisons! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.37, <s>śālinī</s>]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  harer gandhavahān sarve jagat-prāṇatayā viduḥ |
  tad-viyogena tu kṣāmā rāmās tān āśugākhyayā ||JGc_1,17.38|| [anuṣṭubh]
tad evaṃ yadyapy utkaṇṭhāyāḥ parama-kāṣṭhā jātā, tathāpi kācid api kāñcit prati na prakāśayāmāsa | adharmeṇāpi taṃ bhajāni, iti yathā tās tathā kṛṣṇo' pi tatra tā nirvidyā nirvidya khidyate sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, although the uttermost limit of longing had arisen, none among them revealed it to any other. "Even through <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), I shall worship him" — just as they [felt thus], so <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too, despairing again and again about them, suffered.

children.text: kṛṣṇas tūpayāntaram apaśyan netra-vikṣepa-vetra-vikṣepa-vitrastānām api tāsāṃ vaśyatām ayātānām āvaśyaka-tad-bhāvanāya vaṃśī-śaṃsana-viśeṣam abhyasyati sma | [36] yathaiva vakṣyate tatra tatra tad evālakṣya tābhiḥ veṇu-vādya urudhā nija-śikṣāḥ iti | [BhP 10.35.14]
children.translated_text: But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seeing no other means, and though those [<s>gopīs</s>] — frightened even by the casting of his glance like the strike of a switch — had not come under his sway, practiced a special proclamation through the flute for the purpose of the necessary cultivation of that sentiment [in them]. [36] As it will be stated here and there: "The flute-playing was, in many ways, his own training for them." [BhP 10.35.14]

children.text: atha prathamatas tan-manā nijāgra-janmanā yugalī-bhūya muralī-kalīm āvartayati sma | [38] tatra tu yadā samuddīpita-bhāvāntare vanāntare go-cāraṇe sarva-manaso' py agocarān sahacarān vismāpayann atikānta-guṇa-vrajena nijāgrajena saha svayam aharahaḥ saharṣa utkarṣaṃ pravīṇayan veṇu-śikṣām īkṣayām āsa,|| [39] tadā tāsāṃ tad-rūpa-sphūrtir atīva pūrtim āyātā |
children.translated_text: First, becoming one-minded with his first-born (elder brother, <s>Balarāma</s>), paired together, he would practice the art of the <s>muralī</s> (flute). [38] And there, when the sentiment had been kindled within, as he beheld the flute-practice day after day in the forest during cow-herding — astonishing even his companions who were beyond the reach of everyone's mind, together with his own elder brother by that supremely charming company of virtues, himself joyfully refining the excellence — [39] then the eruption of his form [in the minds] of those [<s>gopīs</s>] attained exceedingly great fullness.

children.text: sā ca yathāvad eva, yatas tasya bhāva-vaibhavasya svabhāva evāyam, yad dūrataś ca sva-viṣayaṃ viṣayīkaroti | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: And that [vision] was exactly as it should be, for this is the very nature of his sentimental glory — that from afar too, it makes its own subject the object [of vision]. As follows:

children.text:
anumāna-gatā tāsām arthāpattiḥ pratīyate |
  yataḥ kṛṣṇasya dayitās tā eva nyāya-paṇḍitāḥ ||JGc_1,17.39|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
The inference-derived <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) of those [<s>gopīs</s>] is understood,
for <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> beloveds are themselves experts in logic! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.39, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tatra yāḥ punar atīva snigdhatā-digdha-hṛdayās tad duḥkhataḥ śuṣkatām avāpur na tu punaḥ svaka-duḥkhaṃ puṣkalaṃ menire |
children.translated_text: Among them, those whose hearts were exceedingly smeared with tenderness attained dryness from his suffering, but did not consider their own suffering to be substantial.

children.text: yathā rādhāyā viśākhā lalitā paryāyānurādhā ca, candrāvalyāḥ śaivyā padmā cety-ādayaḥ | tāsu tu tāḥ sva-mātra-niṣṭhatāṃ niṣṭaṅkya svayam eva sa-sauhārdaṃ nija-hārdam āvedayāñcakruḥ | tathāpi tatra prathamaṃ rāma-sahitatā-pihitam eva taṃ lupta-varṇa-padaṃ varṇayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: For example, for <s>Rādhā</s>: <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, and <s>Anurādhā</s> in turn; for <s>Candrāvalī</s>: <s>Śaivyā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, and others. Among those [friends], having certified the exclusive devotion of their own [beloveds], they themselves, with goodwill, made their own heartfelt feelings known. Yet even so, they at first described him in veiled terms, concealed by the accompaniment of <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tatra gītaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: The song there, as follows:

children.text:
rāmo rāmānuja iti yugalam |
kṛta-naṭa-veṣatayā paṭu rājati gāyati sakhi-gaṇa-yugalam | [dhruva]
sarasa-rasālaja-pallava-tallaja-pallavitāmala-śīrṣam |
children.translated_text: With their spotless heads decorated by sprouts budding from the juicy mango-tree sprouts,

children.text: nava-yauvana-vana-bījāṅkuram iva dhāvayad-atanu-cikīrṣam ||b||
children.translated_text: As if making a seed-sprout of the forest of new youth run, with expanding desires! //

<s>Rāma</s> and the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> — the pair!
Having assumed the costume of dancers, brilliantly they reign and sing — the pair of friend-groups! // [refrain]

children.text: vāñchita-piñchāvali-parilāñchita-maṇi-nicayāñcita-keśam |
children.translated_text: With hair adorned by rows of desired peacock-feathers set with clusters of gems,

children.text: dadhad iva hari-dhanur-anugata-tārā-vali-valitāmbuda-leśam ||c||
children.translated_text: As if bearing a fragment of cloud encircled by a row of stars following the rainbow of <s>Hari</s>! //

children.text: valayita-nava-dalad-utpala-karṇika-karṇa-yugādbhuta-śobham |
children.translated_text: With wondrous beauty of the pair of ears [adorned] with ear-ornaments of freshly blossoming blue lotuses,

children.text: latikā kāsāv iti vismayakṛti madhukṛti vinihita-lobham ||d||
children.translated_text: "What creepers are these?" — causing wonder, with greed deposited in the work of the honeybee! //

children.text: hasta-kamalam abhi kamala-vighūrṇana-ramaṇa-kalā-ramaṇīyam |
children.translated_text: Upon the lotus-hand, the art of the charming whirling of a lotus — delightful,

children.text: madhupa-gaṇaṃ prati madhu-kaṇa-varṣaṇam akṛta yataḥ kamanīyam ||e||
children.translated_text: Having showered drops of honey toward the swarm of bees, rendered lovely thereby! //

children.text: mālāmālā-parimala-bali-bali-vapur ali-valita-sadeśam |
children.translated_text: With body perfumed by the offerings of fragrance of garland upon garland, surrounded by bees,

children.text: ali-jhaṅkṛti-nuti-kolāhala-vaha-bahula-kutūhala-veśam ||f||
children.translated_text: With a costume bearing abundant curiosity, carrying the clamor of the bees' buzzing praise! //

children.text:
sitam asitaṃ vapur asitaṃ pītaṃ vasanaṃ yasya ca gītam |
tad idaṃ yadi gokulam anu gokulam ayati tadāgham atītam ||g|| ||JGc_1,17.40|| | iti |
children.translated_text:
One fair, one dark — the body of the dark one — yellow the garment, and whose song
is this: if it comes to <s>Gokula</s> following <s>Gokula</s>, then sin is surpassed! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.40]

children.text:
api tu tasya gokula-sadeśa-pradeśa-praveśa eva sarveṣām abhiniveśa-hetuḥ, yataḥ-
  cakṣur-bhājāṃ phalam idam aho yad vrajasya praveśe
  gobhiḥ sākaṃ sakhi-valayitaṃ dṛśyate bhrātṛ-yugmam |
  yugme tasmin laghur iha mukhāmbhojam asmin muralyā
  dīptiḥ kiñcin nigamana-kalāśāli netraṃ ca tatra ||JGc_1,17.41|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
Moreover, the very entry of that one into the region near <s>Gokula</s> is the cause of everyone's absorption, for:
"This is the fruit of the eyes — ah! — that at the entrance to <s>Vraja</s>,
together with the cows, encircled by friends, the pair of brothers is seen;
of that pair, the younger one here — his lotus-face, his flute's radiance,
somewhat possessed of the art of downward-gazing — and there, his eye!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.41, <s>mandākrāntā</s>]

children.text: atra caiva dhvanitam-
children.translated_text: And here this too is suggested:

children.text:
dhāmāgatasya samaye sakhi-dhenu-saṅgi
  saṅgāyato viharato harataś ca tasya |
  kiñcid vimṛgyad iva cañcalatāñci-tāraṃ
  hārāṇi-netram anu vidhyati mānasaṃ naḥ ||JGc_1,17.42|| [vasantatilakā]
tasmāt-
  sā kila kulajā kulajā nayane tasyāḥ paraṃ nayane |
  veṇu-vinodī madanaḥ sa bhavati yasyāḥ svayaṃ madanaḥ ||JGc_1,17.43|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
"At the time of his arrival home, accompanied by friends and cows,
singing, sporting, and stealing [hearts] —
his eye, somewhat restlessly searching, with a flickering pupil,
the necklace-like — [that eye] pierces our minds!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.42, <s>vasantatilakā</s>]
Therefore:
"She indeed is well-born, well-born is the eye of that one, supremely the eye;
he who sports with the flute is <s>Madana</s> (Cupid) — she for whom he himself becomes <s>Madana</s>!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.43, <s>upagīti</s>]

children.text: tad evam aghadamanena tāsāṃ krama-paramparātaḥ parasparaṃ sva-viṣayābhilāṣa-vyañjanā-sañjanaṃ kiñcil lajjā-paryayam ācarya tādṛśa-ramya-sva-vidyā-bala-tāratamya-viduratayā vidūrato' pi tam avadhārya para-parataḥ parārdhyaṃ samardhyamānāṃ punar veṇu-śikṣāṃ vilakṣaṇī-kurvatā saṅkarṣaṇaḥ kevalaṃ lakṣyāya kalpayāñcakre | yatra hi sarvam eva yugapan mugdhatā-digdhaṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: Thus, by the conqueror of <s>Agha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), through the successive sequence among those [<s>gopīs</s>], the mutual manifestation of desire regarding himself — having somewhat involved the alternation of modesty, and by the gradation of mastery of such charming personal knowledge — even from afar, having ascertained him, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), making the flute-training increasingly extraordinary beyond the others' [perception], merely directed [it] as a target. Where indeed everything was simultaneously anointed with enchantment.

children.text: yatra śrī-vraja-devībhir api nija-bhāva-vyaktiṃ śaṅkamānābhiḥ saṅkarṣaṇaṃ lakṣyaṃ vidhāya tad varṇayāmāse, yathā-
children.translated_text: Where, even the glorious queens of <s>Vraja</s>, apprehending the manifestation of their own sentiments, made <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> the [ostensible] target and described it, as follows:

children.text:
veṇoḥ śikṣām atha racayator dhenu-rakṣādi-lakṣyān
  nānāraṇyaṃ prati viharator bibhrator yaṣṭi-rajjū |
  stambhaṃ lole calanam acale kurvator atyapūrvaṃ
  bhrātror āsīd bata tanu-bhṛtāṃ dharmato vaiparītyam ||JGc_1,17.44|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
"When the two brothers — with cow-guarding and such as their purpose —
practice the flute-art, roaming through forest after forest, bearing staffs and ropes,
causing stillness in the restless and movement in the motionless, performing the supremely unprecedented —
alas! For embodied beings, there arose a reversal of <s>dharma</s> (natural law)!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.44, <s>mandākrāntā</s>]

children.text: atra caivaṃ dhvanitam-
children.translated_text: And here, this too is suggested:

children.text:
nūnam evaṃ vidadhatoḥ sarveṣāṃ dharma-paryayam |
  kṛṣṇo' mūlam asau cāsmad-dharmam unmūlayiṣyati ||JGc_1,17.45|| [anuṣṭubh]
[49] tad evaṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ saṅgāne yugapad eva sarveṣāṃ mohanam ūhamānenānujena vicāritam-[50] hanta tāsām eva mohanākarṣaṇe suṣṭhu mamābhīṣṭe, tatrāpi rādhābhidhāyāḥ | tasmāt pṛthag bhavan pṛthag eva yathā jīvānāṃ jātir yathā-yuktaṃ tayor dvayam ekaṃ vā vahati, kramaśo vyaktir api, tathā śikṣārthaṃ prayatiṣye | tac ca tat-tan-mātrātiśayitābhīpsita-svarādi-marma-samudbhāvanayā sambhaviṣyati iti |
children.translated_text:
"Surely, those two who thus create a reversal of <s>dharma</s> for all —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [is] the root, and that one (<s>Balarāma</s>) shall uproot our <s>dharma</s>!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.45, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
[49] Thus, the younger brother, contemplating the simultaneous enchantment of all through the pair of brothers' companionship, reflected: [50] "Ah! The enchanting attraction of those very ones is my true desire — and therein, especially of the one named <s>Rādhā</s>. Therefore, existing separately, and separately, just as the birth of living beings fittingly bears two or one of a pair, so too the manifestation [of love] gradually — for this I shall endeavor through the flute-training. And that will come to pass through the evocation of the innermost secrets of desired tones and the like, surpassed only by the excellence of each [beloved]."

children.text: tad evaṃ vicārayatā tena parīkṣā-paryālocanārtham uttaram uttarāṃ vaśyatām atītatarāṇy avarāṇi sattvāni kramaśaḥ sva-vaśatām ānītāni, tathāpi tat-preyasībhiś citta-kṣobha-mātraṃ tu lebha eva |
children.translated_text: Thus, as he who was reflecting carried out an examination for the purpose of deliberation, the higher and higher degrees of subjugation brought the lower beings gradually under his sway — and yet even from those beloved ones of his, he received at least a tremor of the heart.

children.text: tatra yathā prathamato gāḥ prati tad-gānam avakarṇitam, tathā varṇitam, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, as his song toward the cows was first heard, so it was described, as follows:

children.text:
harer vaktraṃ veṇu-dhvani-miṣatayā varṣati sudhāṃ
  pibaty etāṃ gavyā yad anu rasanā-karṇa-yugalam |
  ahāsīt prastabdhā nija-viṣayam anyā tu rasanā
  kim etat kiṃ naitad bhavati kim ivaitat kim iti vā ||JGc_1,17.46|| [śikhariṇī]
atrāpi dhvanitam idam-
children.translated_text: Here too this is suggested:

children.text:
gavām asmākaṃ ca śravaṇam anu veṇoḥ samadaśā
  yadapy eṣā jātā tadapi kila bhedo vilasati |
  amūs tad-vaktenduṃ sapadi kalayanti pratipadaṃ
  vayaṃ naitad vidmaḥ kva bhavati yuge tasya kalanam ||JGc_1,17.47|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"Though our hearing and the cows' hearing of the flute attained an equal condition,
even so, a difference shines forth;
they immediately perceive, step by step, the face-moon of that one,
but we do not know this — where in the age does his [moon] wax?" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.47, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: athāpare-dyuś cāparāṃ śikṣām adhikṛtya vanyāny api sattvāni samāhṛtya mohitāni, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, having applied another lesson and gathered even the forest creatures, they were enchanted, as follows:

children.text:
vaṃśaḥ so' yaṃ tu vītaṃsaḥ kaṃsa-śatror itīyate |
  tena śaṃsanato yānti vidhvaṃsaṃ mṛga-pakṣiṇaḥ ||JGc_1,17.48|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
"This flute is indeed the shoulder-ornament of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — thus it is known;
through its proclamation, the deer and birds go to destruction!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.48, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tad api tābhir udbhāvitam, yathā-
children.translated_text: That too was expressed by those [<s>gopīs</s>], as follows:

children.text:
vṛndāraṇyaṃ prathayati bhuvaḥ kīrtim atra svayaṃ hi
  śrīmān kṛṣṇo viharati padāmbhoja-lakṣmīṃ vitanvan |
  veṇor vādye naṭana-ghaṭanaṃ barhiṇaḥ sabhya-bhāvaṃ
  vanyāḥ sarve yayur iti sadā raṅgatāṃ yaj jagāma ||JGc_1,17.49|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
"<s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (Vṛndāvana) spreads the fame of the earth, for here indeed
the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself sports, extending the splendor of his lotus-feet;
the peacocks' dance-enactment at the sound of the flute, the civil behavior [of all creatures],
all the forest-dwellers attaining [audience] — thus what went [there] always became a theater!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.49, <s>mandākrāntā</s>]

children.text: atra cedaṃ dhvanitam-
children.translated_text: And here this is suggested:

children.text:
vṛndāraṇyasya puṇyaṃ vrajitum iha na naḥ śaktir astīti cāstāṃ
yad barhyādyāś ca bhānti pratipada-sukṛta-prodayād asmad-arhyāḥ |
gṛhyāṇāṃ gṛhyakāḥ smaḥ sphuṭam iha tad alaṃ gṛhyakebhyaś ca garhyās
te tasya svairam īkṣāṃ vidadhati na tad-ābhāsam aṇv apy ayāma ||JGc_1,17.50||[sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
"We have no power to go to the sacred ground of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> — and let that be;
that the peacocks and others shine there, at every step worthy of us by the arising of their merit —
we are the domestics of the house-dwellers, clearly, and therefore contemptible compared to even the domestic ones —
they gaze at him freely, but we do not attain even a semblance of that!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.50, <s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text: atha dināntare' pi tebhyo vicchidya hariṇyas tathā kṛtāḥ | tac ca pūrvavat tābhir varṇitam-
children.translated_text: Then, on another day, the does too were similarly captivated. And that too was described by those [<s>gopīs</s>] as before:

children.text:
āścaryaṃ sakhi kṛṣṇasāra-dayitā-vṛndaṃ milad-bhartṛkaṃ
  jātyā mūḍham api vyatītya bhavatīr apy evam īhāṃ dadhe |
  śrutvā veṇu-kalaṃ hariṃ prati gatis tad-rūpataś citratā
  tasyāpy arcanam ullasat-praṇayatas tatrāpi netrāñcalaiḥ ||JGc_1,17.51|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
"Wondrous, O friend! The herd of <s>kṛṣṇasāra</s> (black-antelope) does, meeting their mates,
though dull by birth, surpassed even you and made such an effort!
Hearing the sweet flute, they went toward <s>Hari</s>; from his form, wonder;
from that, his worship, from overflowing love, therein with the corners of their eyes!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.51, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: dhvanitam apīdam-
children.translated_text: This too is suggested:

children.text:
vayaṃ jātyā nāryaḥ puru-guṇavatām ādṛtatamās
  tathā bhartāras tat-praṇaya-naya-siddha-vraja-bhuvaḥ |
  hariṇyo nedṛśyas tadapi patibhis taṃ yayur aho
  dhig asmān duṣpuṇyā dadhima nahi tāsām api tulām ||JGc_1,17.52|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"We are women by birth, most honored among those of great virtue,
and likewise our husbands, [men of] the <s>Vraja</s>-land perfected in the way of love;
the does are not like this, yet with their mates they went to him — ah!
Shame on us, the un-meritorious! We do not even equal them!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.52, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: dināntare tu viśiṣya vihaṅgamās tathā-bhāvaṃ gamitāḥ, tatra ca tābhir abhihitaṃ,
children.translated_text: On another day, the birds especially were brought to such a state. And regarding them, those [<s>gopīs</s>] said:

children.text:
asmin vane tu vihagā munayaḥ pradiṣṭāḥ
  kṛṣṇas tu tad-gurur iti pratataṃ pratīmaḥ |
  naivānyathā tad amunā kimapi pragītaṃ
  mauna-vratena śṛṇuyuḥ parito niviṣṭāḥ ||JGc_1,17.53|| [vasantatilakā]
atra tu sa-nirvedaṃ dhvanitam-
children.translated_text: Here too, with self-reproach, this is suggested:

children.text:
yasmād asau munis te ca munayaḥ sarvataḥ sthitāḥ |
  tasmāt kāñcit spṛhām atra nāñcitāṃ kartum arhatha ||JGc_1,17.54|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
"Since he is the sage and they are sages, stationed everywhere,
therefore you should not form even the slightest desire here!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.17.54, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: atha dināntare devyo' pi tathā kṛtāḥ, tatra tābhir varṇanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, on another day, the goddesses (river-goddesses) too were similarly affected. And their description by those [<s>gopīs</s>], as follows:

children.text:
veṇūdgāna-guṇena tasya paritaḥ kṛṣṭe vimānotkare
  devyo rūpa-vilāsa-mohana-kalām āsādya mohaṃ gatāḥ |
  yatredaṃ na viduḥ kim etad abhitaḥ pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ vīkṣitaṃ
  veti srastam abhūt kacādi kim u vā naivety api prāyaśaḥ ||JGc_1,17.55|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
By the quality of his flute-song, as the multitudes of aerial chariots were drawn from all sides,
the goddesses, having attained the art of enchantment through the charm of his beauty and grace, swooned;
wherein they did not know 'what is this? Was this previously heard or seen from all around?' —
their hair-braids and such became loosened, or rather, they mostly did not even know [that much]! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: atra ca dhvanitam-
children.translated_text: And here, the implied meaning:

children.text:
hanta devyo' pi yatraitām avasthām āpur añjasā |
  tadīya-vraja-bhū-bālā varākyas tatra kā vayam? ||JGc_1,17.56|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Alas, when even the goddesses directly attained such a state,
what wretched ones are we, mere young girls of his <s>Vraja</s>-earth?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ cetanāṃs tathā vitatha-cetanān vidhāyācetanān api cetanān ivācaritum ārabhate sma | acala-maryādayā paryāptāḥ sphuṭam amūr ākraṣṭum acetanatām atikramyāpi duḥśakā iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, having rendered the conscious beings falsely unconscious, he began to make even the unconscious [inanimate things] act as if conscious. For these, being sufficient by the boundary of immovability, are clearly difficult to attract even by transcending their unconsciousness!

children.text: tatra nadī-caritaṃ tābhir evaṃ vicāritam-
children.translated_text: There, the conduct of the river was thus contemplated by them:

children.text:
dvīpinyaḥ śravaṇena veṇu-raṇiteḥ stambhaṃ gatāḥ sabhramāḥ
  phullat-pūratayā sphurad-ghana-rasā haṃsādi-gīḥ-śiñjitāḥ |
  unmaryāda-daśām itā muraripuṃ dūre' bhisṛtyāgatā
  bhaṅgālola-bhujaiḥ saroja-valayas tasyāṅghri-yugmaṃ dadhuḥ ||JGc_1,17.57|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
The river-women, having heard the sound of the flute, attained a stunned state with bewilderment;
with swelling fullness, with dense <s>rasa</s> manifesting, jingling with the songs of swans and such,
having transgressed their proper bounds, having run far to meet the enemy of <s>Mura</s>,
with arms trembling in their waves, they offered lotus-garlands at his pair of feet! // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: atra cedaṃ dhvanitam-
children.translated_text: And here, this was the implied meaning:

children.text:
nadyaḥ sindhu-pati-vratā hari hari pratyakta-maryādikās
  taṃ vidrutya milanti ced ahaha kā dīnās tadānīṃ vayam? |
  kintu svairam amūr udūḍha-sukṛtā nāsmāsu tat-tulyatā
  svalpāpīti nivṛttir eva sukhato yuktāthavā duḥkhataḥ ||JGc_1,17.58|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
'The rivers, devoted to the ocean as their lord, O <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! — having transgressed their very boundaries,
if they run to meet him — alas, what wretched ones are we then?
But these, being of freely earned merit, are not equal to us —
even a little withdrawal from that would be proper, whether from happiness or from sorrow!' // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: dināntare cāmbhoda-varṇanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: And on another day, the description of the cloud, as follows:

children.text:
murārer ambhodaḥ suhṛd iti na vā kevala-rucā
  svasādṛśyāt kintu vyatikṛta-hitatvād api sadā |
  asau mallāreṇa prabalayati taṃ veṇu-januṣā
  sa cāyaṃ chāyābhiḥ praśamayati tāpaṃ tad-upari ||JGc_1,17.59|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
The cloud is <s>Murāri's</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) friend — not merely by its similar complexion,
but because of its perpetual reciprocal beneficence;
he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) invigorates it with the <s>mallāra</s> (rainy-season) <s>rāga</s> produced by the flute,
and it, in turn, cools his heat above with its shadows! // [śikhariṇī]

children.text: atra ca dhvaniḥ-
