children.translated_text: And here the implied meaning:

children.text:
haṃho paśya jaḍo' pi vārida-cayaḥ sarvopari sthāyy api
  cchāyābhiḥ svarasaiś ca taṃ paricaraty antaścara-premataḥ |
  kaṣṭaṃ suṣṭhu vayaṃ tad-eka-śaraṇa-prāṇa-sthitiṃ-manyatā-
  gaṇyās tasya vinā tu sevanam amūr jīvāma dhig jīvitam ||JGc_1,17.60|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
'Alas! Behold — even the insentient mass of clouds, though dwelling above all,
serves him with shade and natural juices, from the love dwelling within!
What a pity! We, who are to be counted among those who consider life itself to depend solely on him as refuge,
without serving him, we live — shame upon such a life!' // [sragdharā]

children.text: aho, śilāmayy api śailajātiḥ sukham evaṃ bhajate, yathā-
children.translated_text: Ah, even the mountain race, though made of stone, enjoys happiness thus, as follows:

children.text:
śrīmān govardhanādriḥ sphuṭam ayam abhitaḥ śrī-harer dāsa-varyaḥ
  kṛṣṇe rameṇa yasmāt tam anu muralikā-vādanāyādhirūḍhe |
  labdhair yaḥ sāttvikābhaiś caraṇa-sarasija-sparśajair aṅkurādyaiḥ
  sarvāṅgīna-dravair apy anuga-sakhi-dhanaṃ sevate taṃ cirāya ||JGc_1,17.61|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
This glorious <s>Govardhana</s> mountain is clearly the foremost servant of the glorious <s>Hari</s> on all sides;
because, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, accompanied by <s>Rāma</s>, has ascended it for flute-playing,
with the <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s> (ecstatic symptoms) — horripilation and such — born from the touch of his lotus-feet,
and with the all-pervading meltings, it serves him as a follower, friend, and treasure for a long time! // [sragdharā]

children.text:
āstāṃ govardhanādreḥ pulaka-mukha-daśā śrūyatām anyad etat
citraṃ cen na pratītir bhavati kila girau dṛśyatāṃ cāparatra |
yaḥ snigdhatvaṃ samantād dadhad iha muralī-gānataś cikvaṇākhyām
āgād yatrāsti sākṣi pratipadam uditaṃ kṛṣṇa-mukhyāṅghri-cihnam ||JGc_1,17.62||[sragdharā]
[69] atra cedaṃ dhvanitam-
children.translated_text:
Let the horripilation-like state of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain stand — listen to yet another matter:
If belief does not arise about the mountain, let it be seen elsewhere;
for he who, maintaining oiliness everywhere, from the flute-song attained the name '<s>cikvaṇa</s>' (melodious) —
there stands as witness the footprint of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and others, imprinted at every step! // [sragdharā]
[69] And here, the implied meaning:

children.text:
mahatāṃ padavīm āptuṃ vāñchā yadyapi dhṛṣṭatā
  tathāpy anugatis teṣāṃ bhāti ced asti dṛṣṭatā ||JGc_1,17.63|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Though the desire to attain the path of the great ones is indeed boldness,
nevertheless, following them, if it shines forth — there is [true] vision!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ tāsām atasmiṃs tad-bhāvanāṃ bhāvayann unmāda-daśā-vaśatāṃ parikalayya vihvala-hṛdayaḥ sadayatayā sa madhukaṇṭhaḥ kṣaṇaṃ gadgada-kaṇṭhaḥ saṃvastrita-mukhaḥ samasta-manyu-nyasta-nijāsukhaḥ puru ruroda, anūditavāṃś ca śrī-rādhā-nibaddham abaddhaṃ padyam ekam-
children.translated_text: Thus, contemplating their attribution of his sentiment [even] to things that were not [appropriate objects], perceiving that they had attained the state of being under the sway of the condition of love-madness, that <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, his heart distressed with compassion, his throat choked with emotion for a moment, his face covered over, all grief and his own discomfort set aside — wept greatly, and then recited one verse composed about the glorious <s>Rādhā</s>, unbounded [in its feeling]:

children.text:
veṇoḥ puṇyam atīva hanta yad asāv astrī ca tasyādharaṃ
gopīnāṃ svam api hriyaṃ pariharan śaśvat pibann ardati |
tṛptyā chardi-nibhād amuṣya raṇitān nadyo' pi phullanty amūr
yad-vaṃśyā naga-jātayo' pi madhubhir bāṣpaṃ madād bibhrati ||JGc_1,17.64|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'How supremely blessed indeed is the flute — alas! — that it, though not a woman, ardently drinks
his lip, perpetually sipping away the very modesty of the <s>gopīs</s>!
From the disgust arising from its satiety, these rivers too bloom from its music;
and those of its lineage — the tree-species — bear tears with honey from their joy!' // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: dhvanitaṃ cedaṃ-
children.translated_text: And the implied meaning of this:

children.text:
yāce' haṃ vaṃśa-dehaṃ na tu kulaja-vadhū-deham ādye hi kṛṣṇas
tṛṣṇag-bhāvena sajjan bahu-ruci viharan durlabhaḥ syāt paratra |
vaṃśī-bhāve cid-aṃśa-praśamana-vaśatā-vismṛtātmā yadi syāt
tena jñāyeya seyaṃ mama viraha-dutā dārutām āgateti ||JGc_1,17.65|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
'I pray for the body of a bamboo, not the body of a well-born wife; for in the first, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
with a thirsty disposition, would sport with much relish and be unattainable elsewhere;
if in the state of being a flute, by the subduing of the conscious portion, I were to become self-forgetful —
then through that I would be known: "This messenger of my separation has come to [a state of] woodenness!"' // [sragdharā]

children.text: tataś cetasi cedaṃ vicāritaṃ-
children.translated_text: Then, this was contemplated in the mind:

children.text:
gaṇḍaṃ cumbasi kuṇḍala-stham akari tvaṃ tasya vaṃsi tvam apy
āsyaṃ prekṣi tathāṅgam aṅgam asakṛn māle tvam āliṅgasi |
tad yuktaṃ yad atīta-sarva-vidhikā yūyaṃ, vayaṃ tu sphuṭaṃ
hā tat-tad-vidhi-bhāg-vicāra-hatakenābhīpsitād vañcitāḥ ||JGc_1,17.66|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'You, O flute, kiss his cheek where the earring rests; you are made his [instrument];
you, O garland, behold his face and embrace each limb repeatedly!
So it is fitting that you have transcended all rules — but we, clearly,
alas, by reflection on the claims of this and that rule, are cheated of our desire!' // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
aho sumanaso muktā vajrāṇy api harer uraḥ |
na tyajanti vayaṃ tatra kā vā smara-vaśāḥ striyaḥ? ||JGc_1,17.67|| [anuṣṭubh]
  cen na saṅgam aparasya vidhatte
  śyāma eṣa na tu tarhi dunomi |
  aṅkapālayati hā gata-śaṅkaḥ
  saṅginaḥ katham idaṃ kalayāmi ||JGc_1,17.68|| iti | [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
'Ah, the flowers are released, even the diamonds do not abandon <s>Hari's</s> chest!
What then are we — women under the sway of <s>Kāma</s> (desire)?' // [anuṣṭubh]
'If this dark one does not arrange union with another,
then I do not torment [him];
but alas, he fearlessly fondles [another] in his lap —
how can I, being his companion, reckon this?' // [svāgatā]

children.text: tad etat-paryantam antara-sparśi-rāga-parīte tasya veṇu-gīte ko' pi sambhramaḥ sarvam eva vrajaṃ nighnaṃ kurvan vighnam ācarati sma | [74] sa tu prātaḥ prastoṣyate | ity añjaliṃ baddhvā punar uvāca-
children.translated_text: Thus, up to this point, in his flute-song pervaded by the inner touch of <s>rāga</s>, a certain agitation, striking all of <s>Vraja</s>, was causing obstruction. [74] But that shall be narrated in the morning. And joining his palms, he again said:

children.text:
asya tvadīya-kāntasya rādhe jānāti ko' pi na |
  prayāsābhyantara-sthāyi-tvan-nimitta-prayāsatām ||JGc_1,17.69|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Of this beloved of yours, O <s>Rādhā</s>, no one knows
the exertion for your sake that dwells within the interior of his exertions!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ kathāyāṃ samāpta-prathāyāṃ sarve yathā sva-svāvāsam āsannāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the tale had reached the completion of its fame, all went to their respective abodes.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
veṇu-śikṣā-miṣa-preyasī-bhikṣā nāma
saptadaśaṃ pūraṇam
 ||17||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Seventeenth Chapter, named
'The Solicitation of the Beloveds under the Pretext of Flute-Instruction.'
||17||

children.text: atha aṣṭadaśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Eighteenth Chapter.

children.text:
gotrabhid-garva-khaṇḍana-
govardhana-gotra-māna-vardhanam
children.translated_text:
The Shattering of the Pride of <s>Gotrabhid</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and
the Augmentation of the Honor of <s>Govardhana</s> Mountain.

children.text:
atha prabhāte sadasi vrajeśitur
  mahā-prabhāveṣu vibhāta-paṅktiṣu |
  ānarccha sāmodam udaśru-kaṇṭhatāṃ
  sa snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ kathayāmbabhūva ca ||JGc_1,18.1|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
Then, in the morning, in the assembly of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>,
when the rows of supremely majestic [cows] were manifest,
with joyful but tear-choked throat,
that <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> offered worship and began to narrate: // [upajāti]

children.text: atha tasminn āśvināvaśeṣe labdha-viśeṣe yajña-yogya-veśe vrajād bahiḥ pradeśe sarva eva parvaṇā sāndrānanda-vrajā iva sa-prajāḥ vrajendrādayaḥ sambhrāntāśaya-prāyatayā carantaḥ surendra-yāga-yogam ācarantaḥ sthānādi-sañceṣkriyamāṇān ādiśantaḥ sva-sva-vasatiṃ vihāya vasatiṃ bahir vasanti sma |
children.translated_text: Then, in that remainder of the month of <s>Āśvina</s>, having attained special distinction, in a region fit for sacrifice, outside <s>Vraja</s>, all of them — led by the king of <s>Vraja</s>, dense hosts of bliss like <s>Vraja</s> itself, together with their children — going about with the prevailing intent of earnest preparation, performing the arrangement for the sacrifice to <s>Indra</s>, directing the preparation of sites and the like, abandoning their own dwellings — were dwelling outside.

children.text: tadā ca kadācid ekasyāṃ sandhyāyāṃ gocāraṇa-bhū-bhāgataḥ samāgataḥ saṅkarṣaṇa-sahacāritayā labdha-harṣaḥ sa-kutuka-tṛṣṇaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇas tadīya-caritam ālocitavān | tatraiva ca prabhūta-kutukākuta-sambhūtatayā vasati sma |
children.translated_text: Then, once, at one twilight, having arrived from the cow-grazing area, the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who had gained delight through companionship with <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), thirsty with curiosity, observed their activities. And right there, he was dwelling, through the arising of abundant and intense curiosity.

children.text: tad api ca yad api pūrva-pūrva-saṃvatsareṣu dṛṣṭam ity apūrva-dṛṣṭaṃ na bhavati, tathāpi samprati prauḍhatāprakāśataḥ śatamanyuṃ prati manyuṃ janayan janakādiṣu praṇaya-kopaṃ jñāpayann ajñānata iva jijñāsāñcakre | yadyapi śataparva-pāṇir evaṃ garvāyate, ete gopālana-kārakāḥ ke varākāḥ? nikhila-loka-lokapāla-pālakasya mama dakṣa-mukhyāḥ prajāpatayaḥ svīya-manvantara-pati-prabhṛtayaḥ pṛthivī-patayaḥ kamalajanma-janma-pradhānā munīśānā yajamānā virājantetarām iti, tathāpy ete mat-pitṛ-puraḥ-sarās tatra bhaktim atiriktīkurvanti iti |
children.translated_text: And although this had been seen in previous years — and thus was not something seen for the first time — nevertheless, now, from the manifestation of maturity, generating anger toward <s>Śatamanya</s> (<s>Indra</s>, 'the hundred-sacrificed one'), making his love-born displeasure known to his father and others, as if from ignorance, he began to inquire. 'Although this hundred-thunderbolt-handed one (<s>Indra</s>) is thus puffed with pride, who are these wretched cow-tenders? Of me, the protector of the protectors of all the worlds' people, my chief progenitors are <s>Dakṣa</s> and the other <s>Prajāpatis</s>, along with the <s>Manu</s>-period rulers and other earth-kings, and sacrificers who are lords of sages prominent through <s>Brahmā's</s> creation — these shine superbly! Yet these [cowherds], with my father at the fore, devote excessive devotion there!'

children.text: atha spaṣṭīkṛta-gaurava-sauṣṭhavam antaḥ-kaṣṭa-parāmṛṣṭaṃ pṛṣṭavān-
children.translated_text: Then, having made the weight of his dignity clear, he asked, touching upon the inner hardship:

children.text:
kathyatāṃ vaḥ pitaḥ ko' yaṃ sambhramaḥ samupāgataḥ? |
  yajñārtho yadi devaḥ kaḥ? pramāṇaṃ kiṃ, phalaṃ ca kim? ||JGc_1,18.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Tell me, O father, what is this commotion that has arrived?
If it is for a sacrifice, to which deity? What is the authority? And what is the fruit?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: vrajeśvare tu jñāna-pūrvaka-praśna-vijñānatas tad-abhiprāyaṃ prāyaḥ pratipadya sadyaḥ prativacanam adattavati, punar lālyatocita-bālyato dīnatā-dhīnam ivovāca-
children.translated_text: But when the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, from his understanding of the question as one asked with prior knowledge, mostly perceiving its intention, did not immediately give a reply, he spoke again with the humility befitting a child to be fondled, as if dependent in his helplessness:

children.text:
yathā vidhātuṃ bhavatāṃ tathā śrotuṃ ca naḥ spṛhā |
  ubhayeṣāṃ yatas tatra viśeṣāśrayatā-sthitiḥ ||JGc_1,18.3|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Just as you have the desire to perform, so we have the desire to hear;
for in both cases, there rests the position of special dependence!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha, kim asmābhir vyaktaṃ vaktavyaṃ gotrabhit-satraṃ prati, kiṃ vāyaṃ vatsaḥ pratipatsyete iti vicikitsati tāta-pāde tad eva kiñcid atiriktaṃ vyaktam iva kartum icchati sma | [7] yathā ca, tāta, sarvatra nipuṇānāṃ vaijñānikānāṃ bhavatāṃ putrā vayaṃ na tāvad gocārakatā-mātra-paryavasita-paryālocanāḥ, kintu kiñcit kiñcij jñāna-nītiṃ dharma-rītim api pratipadyāmahe iti vyañjanayā mañju vadati sma-
children.translated_text: Then, while the father was deliberating, 'Should we explain clearly about the <s>Indra</s>-sacrifice, or will this child himself understand?' — he wished to make that very [point] somewhat more explicit. [7] As follows: 'Father, we, sons of you who are experts and scientists in all matters, are not [to be regarded as having] deliberation limited merely to cow-grazing; rather, we comprehend bit by bit the policy of knowledge and the course of <s>dharma</s> as well' — thus, with suggestive charm, he spoke sweetly:

children.text:
sarva-kṣetra-prājña ekaḥ parātmā
  tasmin jīvāḥ santi naivātibhinnāḥ |
  etad-vijñāḥ sādhavo vidvad-ijyās
  tasmād eṣāṃ gopanaṃ naiva yuktam ||JGc_1,18.4|| [śālinī]

yogināṃ matam etac cen nītir apy avadhāryatām |
  udāsīno' rivad varjyaḥ suhṛd ātmaiva sammataḥ ||JGc_1,18.5|| yady eṣa panthā dharmasya so' pi nāsty avicārataḥ |
  tatra yad viduṣaḥ siddhir bhaven nāviduṣaḥ kvacit ||JGc_1,18.6|| dharmo vaidika eveṣṭau laukikaḥ kvāpi dṛśyate |
  bhavadbhiḥ kas tayor eṣa viśeṣatvena sammataḥ? ||JGc_1,18.7|| [anuṣṭubh]

tad evaṃ sva-sutasya suparva-pati-māna-carvaṇāyāvirbhavantaṃ sarva-mata-jñatā-garvam akharvam ālocayann, apūrvatayā bhāvanāṃ kurvāṇas tena ca nija-pakṣasyāpekṣaṇīyatāṃ lakṣayann, idaṃ vraja-patir upakṣiptavān-
children.translated_text: Thus, contemplating the undiminished pride of his own son's complete knowledge of all doctrines, which was manifesting for the purpose of crushing the honor of the lord of the gods — reflecting upon its unprecedented nature, and observing that his own position deserved consideration — the lord of <s>Vraja</s> proposed:

children.text:
dharmo' yaṃ laukikas tāta yadyapi syād athāpy asau |
  yuktatvād api cāmnāyād āmnāyaja iveṣyate ||JGc_1,18.8|| ya indro devatātra syāt parjanyaḥ sa tu sarvavit |
  tasyārcanaṃ kulāyātam asmākaṃ ketanaṃ matam ||JGc_1,18.9|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'This <s>dharma</s>, dear child, even if it be worldly,
nevertheless, because of its propriety and because it comes from tradition,
is to be regarded as if born of scripture. // [anuṣṭubh]
The deity here is <s>Indra</s>, and he is <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god), the all-knowing one;
his worship, inherited through our lineage, is our established banner!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: kṛṣṇas tad etat karma karma-pradhānatayā varṇyamānaṃ tad uttaram ākarṇya vāsava-hrāsa-vāsanayā karma-kāṇḍa-paṇḍitaṃ-manyānāṃ matam anusṛtya devatā-khaṇḍanam āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, hearing that further reply describing this <s>karma</s> (ritual action) as the principal thing, with the desire to diminish <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), following the doctrine of those who consider themselves scholars of the <s>karma-kāṇḍa</s> (ritual portion), began his refutation of the deity:

children.text:
svataḥ karma-vaśād evādātuṃ karmānusāriṇaḥ |
  īśaś ced asti karmānugāmy asau kā nu devatā ||JGc_1,18.10|| sarvaṃ tad bhasmani hutaṃ para-tantre yad arpaṇam |
  gārhapatye hutaṃ tat tu yad ātmātmīya-poṣaṇam ||JGc_1,18.11|| tasmād ābhīra-vaiśyatvād aghnyāsevā tu naḥ kṛtiḥ |
  devatā yadi manyeta mantavyā sā tad-āśrayā ||JGc_1,18.12|| [anuṣṭubh]
atha śatamanyor api parjanyatayā tad-āśrayatvam āśaṅkya sāṅkhya-saṅkhyāvatāṃ matāt pratyācacakṣe-
children.translated_text: Then, apprehending that even <s>Śatamanya</s> (<s>Indra</s>), being <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god), could be the shelter [of cows], he refuted this from the view of those versed in <s>Sāṅkhya</s> enumeration:

children.text:
rajo-bhūr yavasādy-arthas tasmān nendro gavāśrayaḥ |
  kintu govardhanākhyāna-kṣauṇī-bhṛd yaḥ sa eva saḥ ||JGc_1,18.13|| nijājīvyatayā gāvaḥ kulāgatyā ca bhū-surāḥ |
  āśrayatve samakṣatvaṃ yānty ete na divaukasaḥ ||JGc_1,18.14|| [anuṣṭubh]

tatra matāntaraṃ vitaṇḍā-paṇḍitānāṃ matena khaṇḍayati-
  āptavāg anumānaṃ ca pratyakṣād eva gamyate |
  tasmāt pratyakṣam eva syāt pramāṇaṃ sarva-mardakam ||JGc_1,18.15|| tasmād gavāṃ brāhmaṇānām adreś cārabhyatām mahaḥ |
  aindrair nirmīyatāṃ seyaṃ tri-karmī haviṣāṃ kulaiḥ ||JGc_1,18.16|| homo yadi vidhātavyo vahnim uddiśya hūyatām |
  āśrayaḥ sa hi sarveṣāṃ pratyakṣaś cānubhūyate ||JGc_1,18.17|| atha viprāḥ prīṇanīyā dattvā dhenūḥ sadakṣiṇāḥ |
  svabhāva eṣa bhavatāṃ vidhi-kiṅkaratā nahi ||JGc_1,18.18|| [anuṣṭubh]

annaṃ dattvā brāhmaṇādiśvapākānt-
  ebhyaḥ śvabhyo' py atra gobhyas tṛṇāni |
  kṣauṇī-bhartre dīyatām annakūṭo
  yasmād eṣo' py anna-kūṭābhidhaḥ syāt ||JGc_1,18.19|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Having given food to all — from <s>brāhmaṇas</s> down to <s>caṇḍālas</s> and dogs —
and grass for the cows here,
let a mountain of food (<s>anna-kūṭa</s>) be offered to the bearer of the earth,
since this [festival] too would bear the name "<s>Anna-kūṭa</s>" (food-mountain)!' ||18.19|| [śālinī]

children.text: tad evaṃ śvapāka-śva-paryantebhyaḥ pradātavyaṃ, na tu pākaśāsanāyety abhipretya sarvān nirvacanekṛtya pratyekaṃ pravartayan prāha-
children.translated_text: Thus, intending that [food] should be given to all including <s>caṇḍālas</s> and dogs, but not to <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>), having rendered everyone speechless, setting each one in motion individually, he said:

children.text:
bhuktvā vastrālepa-veśān gṛhītvā
  vipraṃ vahniṃ gāṃ parikrāmatādrim |
  nātrāpy aṅghri-krāmitāvaśyakatvaṃ
  svacchandatvād yānam apy atra diṣṭam ||JGc_1,18.20|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Having eaten, having donned garments, sandalwood paste, and finery,
let the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the fire, and the cow circumambulate the mountain!
Even here there is no compulsory need for foot-traversal;
from the freedom [of this worship], even conveyance by vehicle is ordained here!' ||18.20|| [śālinī]

children.text:
ye vā kratubhujo' py atra janās te syur janāv iha |
  suparvāṇaḥ sumanaso nirjarāś ca surā iva ||JGc_1,18.21|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'And those who are enjoyers of sacrifice among the people here would become people in this world —
celestials, with auspicious minds, undecaying, and like gods!' ||18.21|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
  āḍhyaṅ-karaṇī subhagaṅ-karaṇī tadvat priyaṅ-karaṇī |
  śrī-govardhana-pūjā-nāmnī vidyā parisphurati ||JGc_1,18.22|| [upagīti]
  govardhana-giri-yajñāvajñā tu gotrabhit-pūjā |
  andhaṅ-karaṇī palitaṅ-karaṇī nagnaṅ-karaṇy api ca ||JGc_1,18.23|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'The worship named <s>Śrī Govardhana-pūjā</s> is an art that shines forth
as one that enriches, beautifies, and endears!' ||18.22|| [upagīti]
'But the sacrifice to <s>Gotra-bhid</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — the worship of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain being scorned —
is an art that blinds, grays, and strips bare!' ||18.23|| [upagīti]

children.text: tad evam agrajamukhaṃ nirīkṣya mṛdu hasitvā punaḥ sādaram āha sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, looking at his elder brother's face and smiling gently, he spoke again with respect:

children.text:
ity etan me bāla-bhāvena buddhaṃ
  go-viprādi-prepsitaṃ mad-dhitaṃ ca |
  yuṣmabhyaṃ ced rocate tarhi śīghraṃ
  kāryaṃ vighnaḥ syād vibhinna-praveśe ||JGc_1,18.24|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'This was understood by me through childish insight —
what is desired by cows, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and the like, and what is beneficial to me;
if it pleases you, then quickly
let it be done — an obstacle would arise if the onset is fragmented!' ||18.24|| [śālinī]

children.text:
sarvaṃ yan-mānasaṃ vācikaṃ vā
  yuṣmadṛgbhiḥ sādhyate kāyikaṃ vā |
  nityaṃ tat tad dṛśyate man-nimittaṃ
  tasmād etan mad-dhitatvād vidheyam ||JGc_1,18.25|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Whatever mental, verbal, or
physical [act] is accomplished by you all —
that is always seen to be on my account;
therefore this should be done as it is beneficial to me!' ||18.25|| [śālinī]

children.text:
anunmattaḥ svataḥ sarvaṃ vetti svīyaṃ hitaṃ pitaḥ |
  no ced vetti na ca brūte brūte ced vetti niścitam ||JGc_1,18.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'One who is not deluded naturally knows his own benefit, O father!
If he does not know, he does not speak; but if he speaks, he surely knows!' ||18.26|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad etad vipralambha-lambhanam apy akliṣṭa-varṇana-viśiṣṭam ākarṇya tan-mukhaṃ ca nirvarṇya, tad eva savarṇair asavarṇair apy adhi parvam āgataiḥ sarvakair nirṇinye | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Having heard this — which was a charming deception, yet distinguished by effortless description — and having gazed upon his face, it was affirmed as a festive occasion by all — those of the same class and of different classes alike — who had arrived. For indeed:

children.text:
preṣṭhaḥ kiñcid yad bravīti pratītiṃ
  sarveṣāṃ tad yāti nūnaṃ ruciṃ ca |
  tac ced aṇv apy arhitaṃ tarhi kiṃ vā
  vācyaṃ tasmāt te' py amanyanta tadd hi ||JGc_1,18.27|| [śālinī]
[15] tad etad avadhārya madhukaṇṭhas tv amukta-kaṇṭhaṃ parāmṛśati sma, ced apy ativedaḥ suvicāratā-naśvaraḥ so' yam anīśvara-vādaḥ kṛta-vakra-bhāva-cakra-śakra-parābhava-kautuka-tātparya-mātra-pātratayā tena prayuktaḥ, kintu na pravṛtti-virodhi-pātratayā; tathāpi tatra mitratāticitratayā labdha-nigama-visrabdha-sarva-puruṣārtha-sārtha-śiromaṇi-rūpa-svarūpeṣu teṣu vraja-bhūpeṣu nāyuktaḥ | īśvara-jñāna-gurubhir api tad-bhāvam eva pari sarvopari-purutā-parāmarśāt | yathoktam-
children.translated_text:
'Whatever the beloved one says even slightly gains the conviction
and the favor of all people;
if even a trifle spoken by him is to be honored, then what more is to be said?
Therefore they too considered that [proposal] to be fitting!' ||18.27|| [śālinī]
[15] Having ascertained this, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, however, reflected with unfettered throat: 'Even though this argument of denying the Lord (<s>anīśvara-vāda</s>) — extremely knowing yet destructible by proper reasoning — was employed by him solely as a vessel for the purpose of the curiosity of humbling the crooked <s>Indra</s> through the wheel of feigned disposition, and not as a vessel for opposing [true] conduct; nevertheless, it was not inappropriate for those lords of <s>Vraja</s> who, in their essential nature, were the crest-jewel of the caravan of all human aims, established through the confidence of revealed scripture, and marked by the wonderful quality of friendship — even for those who are weighty in the knowledge of the Lord, the contemplation of the supreme manhood around that very [loving] sentiment [was paramount].' As it was said:

children.text: aho bhāgyam aho bhāgyaṃ nanda-gopa-vrajaukasām |
yan-mitraṃ paramānandaṃ pūrṇa-brahma sanātanam ||[BhP 10.14.32] ityādi |
children.translated_text: Whose friend is the Supreme Bliss, the Complete Eternal <s>Brahman</s>!' [BhP 10.14.32] And so forth.
'Oh, the fortune! Oh, the fortune of <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd and the residents of <s>Vraja</s>!

children.text: tataḥ kautuka-cāritayāpi tena yad vicāritam iva sampadyate, tad api pāramārthya-varyatayā paryavasyatīty evam aho parama-maho-vara-kara-svabhāva-dhāraḥ so' yaṃ vraja-dharā-pati-vaṃśa-janmā śaśadharaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then, even that which was deliberated by him through the course of mere curiosity comes to fruition — and that too culminates as the highest truth — thus: 'Ah, this bearer of the nature of bestowing the supreme great festival is indeed the moon born of the dynasty of the lord of the cow-earth!'

children.text: atha spaṣṭaṃ cācaṣṭa-tatas tataḥ?
children.translated_text: Then he clearly declared: 'Then what next?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca dīpāvalīnāmānam amāvāsyām anu dīpāvali-bali-kautukaṃ pratipadya pratipat-prātas tu viśrambhataḥ paramāśrayatām āśrayamāṇair amībhir yathā tena vihitaṃ tathā vihitam |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, on the new-moon day named <s>Dīpāvalī</s>, after observing the festival of lamps and offering of <s>Bali</s>, on the morning of the first day (<s>pratipad</s>), with confidence, taking him as their supreme shelter, they carried out what he had ordained just as he had ordained it.'

children.text:
tatra ca mukhya-kalpa-kalpanāya vicitra-citra-vitāna-patākādibhiḥ sarva-sukha-saṃvardhanasya śrī-govardhanasya kūṭa-maṇḍalaṃ maṇḍayitvā, yathāvidhi nirbandha-sādhita-sādhu-gandha-bandhura-pādyādi-prāgrya-sāmagrībhir abhisabhājya, tam abhi prājya-caraṇācalavad ājya-prāghāra-nirjharāś citra-varṇa-vyañjana-vyañjita-dhātu-rañjanāḥ, dugdha-taṭinī-saṅkaṭitā dadhi-taḍāga-saṅghaṭitāḥ sampannam anna-kūṭāḥ saṅghaṭṭayya nikaṭād upaḍhaukayāmāsire | yeṣāṃ prāg-bhāvenāpūpikaṃ śāṣkulikam ityādi bhūyiṣṭha-niṣṭhāna-kūṭa-nāmnā sthānāny api ciram āmnātāni |
  nānā-vādyaṃ loka-kolāhalāḍhyaṃ
  svargaṃ bāḍhaṃ vyānaśe tatra satre |
  yat tad deva-kṣmāpater āśvineyau
  nirṇinyāte karṇa-śūle nidānam ||JGc_1,18.28|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
For the arrangement of the principal creation, having adorned the summit-circle of <s>Śrī Govardhana</s> — the augmenter of all happiness — with varied and wondrous canopies, banners, and the like, and having worshipped him duly with the finest materials — fragrant <s>pādya</s> (foot-wash) and other foremost offerings achieved through persistent devotion — they brought near from close by, and presented before him, food-mountains (<s>anna-kūṭas</s>) with streams of ghee cascading like waterfalls from a mountain of rich offerings, embellished with seasonings of varied colors revealing mineral-like hues, hemmed in by rivers of milk, joined with lakes of yogurt — prosperous and complete. Even the sites of these [offerings] — such as <s>āpūpika</s> (cake-place), <s>śāṣkulika</s> (pastry-place), and the like — have long been remembered by the name 'food-mountain summit.'
Various musical instruments, enriched with the uproar of the populace,
truly vanquished heaven at that sacrificial session;
for that reason, the twin <s>Āśvineyas</s> (celestial physicians) of the king of gods and earth
were determined as the cause of earache! ||18.28|| [śālinī]

children.text:
sṛṣṭeṣv adrer anna-kūṭeṣv analpaḥ
  kṛṣṇākāraḥ kaścid āvirbabhūva |
  alpīyastvaṃ kevalaṃ bheda-buddher
  yasmāt kṛṣṇe kāraṇatvaṃ jagāma ||JGc_1,18.29|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
When the food-mountains were created for the mountain, a certain not-small
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-form appeared!
Only the smallness belongs to the intellect of distinction [between <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the mountain],
since causality resided in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [himself]! ||18.29|| [śālinī]

children.text: taṃ ca prathamaṃ vasundharādhara-śilā-sandhitaḥ samedhamāna-sphurad-utsedhaṃ prekṣākāriṇaḥ samutprekṣāmāsuḥ-
children.translated_text: And him they first perceived — arising from the rock-joints of the earth-bearer mountain, blazing forth with surging prominence — the spectators conjectured:

children.text:
pīta-śyāmā kiṃ prabhā? kiṃ taḍitvān?
  kiṃ vā dhātu-dyoti-bhūbhṛd vibhāti? |
  suṣṭhūttiṣṭhan kiṃ svid etad bakījin-
  mūrti-vyūhaḥ sphūrtim atrātanoti? ||JGc_1,18.30|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Is it a yellow-dark radiance? Is it a lightning-bearer?
Or does a mountain gleam with the luster of minerals?
Or is it some army-formation of the slayer of <s>Bakī's</s> [son]
that manifests its flash here, standing up mightily?' ||18.30|| [śālinī]

children.text:
kāya-prāyata-bhājitāñjana-girir vastrāṇi sandhyābhrajid
  vistāra-dyutimanti veṣamaṇayaḥ sūryādi-jetṛ-prabhāḥ |
  uttaṃsā vara-puṣpa-bhāra-balavac-chākhā-sahasrāṇy aho
  yasya kṣmādhara-deva eṣa kurute netrāṇi citrāṇi naḥ ||JGc_1,18.31|| [śārdūla]
tataḥ sa tu caturānana-cāturī-cālana-caturaḥ kṛṣṇa-nāmnā madhuraḥ sa-praśrayaṃ papraccha-bhagavan, ko bhavān? iti |
children.translated_text: Then he — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that sweet one, skilled in setting in motion the artfulness of the four-faced (<s>Brahmā</s>) — asked with humility: 'O Blessed One, who are you?'

children.text: devas tu nirghoṣa-nibha-ghargharita-svareṇābhra-bhramaṃ prathayann, arthena tu tam anyathayan vacaḥ pracārayām āsa, pūrvitākharvavat-parvan! parvataḥ so' yam aham asmi iti |
children.translated_text: The god, with a voice like thundering rumbling in a cloud-like roar, spread the semblance of cloud-wandering, but by his meaning he bewildered him, uttering the word — in the manner of the preceding undiminished [usage] — 'Festival! The Mountain! I am he!'

children.text: tad etad avadhārya devāry-amitraḥ śrīdāmādi-mitraḥ sva-bhujau prasārya visphūryamāṇa-kolāhalānargalaṃ gopa-vargaṃ nivārya, namaskāryaḥ khalv asau yasmāt karuṇā-vyagratā-jāgran-mahā-vigraha-samagra-vigraha-prakāśa-grahilatayā pratyakṣa-pratyayam eva sa eva devaḥ pratyavaruddhavān iti sarvān praty akharvāṃ vācam uvāca |
children.translated_text: Having ascertained this, the friend of <s>Śrīdāmā</s> and others, the friend of the enemies of the gods (<s>asuras</s>), stretching out his arms, restraining the cowherd host whose raging uproar was unbridled, spoke a full-throated utterance to all: 'He is indeed to be saluted, because through the seizure of the manifestation of his complete great form — awakened by the intensity of compassion — that very god has obstructed direct perception as his evidence!' And he spoke a complete word to all.

children.text: uktvā cākhaṇḍa-daṇḍavan-natiṃ kurvati sahasa-smita-pūrvaje tasmin vismita-manasaḥ sarva eva prati parvataṃ tathākurvata | kṛtvā ca śraddhayā baddhāñjaliṣu tadāvaliṣu sarva-sukha-vardhanaḥ sa govardhanaḥ punar uvāca-
children.translated_text: Having spoken, as that one whose elder brother [was smiling] first with a hundred smiles performed an unbroken, staff-like prostration — all, with astonished minds, likewise prostrated before the mountain. And when they, with faith, stood with joined palms in those rows, <s>Govardhana</s> — the augmenter of all happiness — spoke again:

children.text:
nānya-devavad asmākaṃ
bhedaṃ yuṣmad vicakṣmahe |
  tat paśyata bhaved dattaṃ
pratyakṣaṃ bhuṅkṣmahe vayam ||JGc_1,18.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'We do not perceive any distinction
from other deities between us and you!
Therefore behold — what is given,
we consume directly!' ||18.32|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad etad uktvā ca-
children.translated_text: Having said this:

children.text:
annāny āḍhaka-koṭi-taṇḍula-kṛtāny ādāya tad-vyañjanāny
  apy eṣa pratikūṭam eka-kavala-prāptānnam ādat tathā |
  madhyaṃ madhyam anuprakṛṣya tu yathā nīraṃ piban palvalān
  kuṇḍāny āśu sarāṃsi kiṃ ca sarito ninye kṣayaṃ sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,18.33|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Taking the foods made from millions of <s>āḍhaka</s>-measures of rice, and the condiments too,
he consumed a full mouthful of food per mountain-heap;
drawing the water from the middle of middle [pools], drinking —
he quickly emptied the ponds, tanks, lakes, and rivers everywhere! ||18.33|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
yadā grāsāya sa karaṃ prasārayati cāgrataḥ |
  tadā sarve dravanti sma sarvataś caṭakā iva ||JGc_1,18.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
  madhye-kṛtya vyañjanāny anna-kūṭaṃ
  grāsaṃ grāsaṃ pāṇinā dakṣiṇena |
  tarjanyāsāv uddiśan vāmayā taṃ
  śakraṃ lolat-prānta-gatyā jahāsa ||JGc_1,18.35|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Whenever he extends his hand forward for a morsel,
then all flee in every direction like sparrows! ||18.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
Placing the condiments in the center of the food-mountain,
morsel by morsel with his right hand,
pointing with this forefinger and [then] with the left [hand] at him (<s>Indra</s>),
he laughed with a quivering sideways glance! ||18.35|| [śālinī]

children.text:
doṣṇas tasyāśv atiparimiti-grāsa-hetoḥ prasāre
  cākuñce ca sthagita-haritaḥ prāpta-tat-tad-gatīnām |
  akṣṇām āsīd vraja-kula-bhuvāṃ citra-vṛnde' pi citraṃ
  yat kvāpy ekaṃ na kila gaṇitaṃ siktham ekaṃ sthitaṃ na ||JGc_1,18.36|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
From the extension of his arm — due to the swiftness of the immensely-proportioned morsels —
and from its contraction, the horizon was obscured;
for the <s>Vraja</s>-dwelling people's eyes, even amid that variegated spectacle, the wonder was
that not even a single morsel was counted anywhere, nor did a single crumb remain! ||18.36|| [mandākrāntā]

children.text:
atarītṛṇyata grāsān bhūbhṛd-bhūbhṛd yathā yathā |
  acalīklpyatāpy uccair māṃsalāya tathā tathā ||JGc_1,18.37|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
As the earth-bearer consumed morsel after morsel like a mountain,
he simultaneously grew taller and taller, becoming ever more fleshy! ||18.37|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tatra ca-
  bālā bhītiṃ yauvanonmatta-cittā
  hāsaṃ vṛddhāś citram arhās tu bhaktim |
  yātā ye ye teṣu sarveṣu devaḥ
  śuddhāṃ tuṣṭiṃ kautukitvād babhāja ||JGc_1,18.38|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
And there:
Children attained fear, youths maddened with excitement attained laughter,
the aged attained wonder, and the worthy ones attained devotion;
whatever each and every one among all those people [felt],
the god, out of his curiosity, shared in their pure satisfaction! ||18.38|| [śālinī]

children.text:
dūrād dūrāt pūram ādāya vārāṃ
  vaktraṃ śaśvat kṣālayann adridevaḥ |
  ṣṭhīvann uccaiḥ pṛṣṭha-deśe samantād
  vṛṣṭiṃ kurvan śampa-sṛṣṭiṃ cakāra ||JGc_1,18.39|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Drawing floods of water from far, far away,
constantly washing his mouth, the mountain-god,
spitting loudly behind him on all sides,
created rain and produced lightning! ||18.39|| [śālinī]

children.text:
gaṇḍūṣāṇām antare vaṃśa-daṇḍair
  dantāntargāny anna-piṇḍāni kuñcan |
  udyan-mūrtis tatra śailādhidevaḥ
  pūrtiṃ kurvan prāṇa-bhājāṃ sasarja ||JGc_1,18.40|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
Between mouthfuls, with bamboo-staves,
picking out food-lumps lodged between his teeth,
the mountain-god, rising in form, performing
fulfillment there, created life for all beings! ||18.40|| [śālinī]

children.text:
tāmbūlānāṃ vīṭikāḥ koṭi-kharvaṃ
  kūṭī-kurvaṃś carvayan garva-phullaḥ |
  prānta-cchāyā-maṇḍalaś caṇḍa-raśmiḥ
  prātar yadvat tadvad āsyaṃ cakāra ||JGc_1,18.41|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: Chewing ten-billion rolls of betel, making them into heaps, swelling with pride — like the fierce-rayed sun whose radiance-circle is at the edges, just so in the morning he made his face! // [śālinī]

children.text:
jātaṃ nīrājanasya kṣaṇam anu nikhilā moham āpur yad etat
  tasmin drāghīyasi syāt katham iti vividhād dhvasta-cittā vicārāt |
  kṛṣṇas tv alpaṃ vihasya pratividhim akarot kalpitād yantra-bhedād
  yasmin dīpāḥ sahasraṃ talam upari ca te cālyamānā virejuḥ ||JGc_1,18.42|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: When the moment of the <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration with lamps) arrived, all fell into a swoon — 'How could this occur during that extended [ceremony]?' — their minds dismayed by various considerations. But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, laughing slightly, made a remedy through a contrived mechanism, in which a thousand lamps, placed one above another, were moved about and shone brilliantly! // [śārdūla]

children.text: atha sarvam icchan anvicchan pratīcchann api girir ayam aho giriṃ karotīti nidhyāya, mūrdhani baddhāñjalitayā sarvasminn apy ūrdhvaṃ sthitavati, sarvato' pi varān varān viracayyātarkitam antarhite parama-hite tasminn, akhaṇḍa-daṇḍavat-praṇāma-pūrvam atra dvitra-kṣaṇaṃ citram iva sarva evāsīt |
children.translated_text: Then, while he (<s>Govardhana</s> in <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> form) — wanting everything, seeking everything, and accepting everything — was meditating 'Oh, this mountain indeed makes mountains [of offerings]!' — when all, with palms joined at their foreheads, stood above him [in reverence], and he — having bestowed the best of boons upon everyone — unexpectedly disappeared, being supremely beneficent, everyone stood for two or three moments like a picture, having first offered full prostrations like unbroken staffs.

children.text: avahite ca bahir-arthe śrī-harir asau sarvān parvata-parvāgatān praty uvāca-
children.translated_text: And when external awareness had been regained, Śrī <s>Hari</s> addressed all those who had come to the festival of the mountain:

children.text:
aho kalayatācalaḥ karuṇayātma-rūpaṃ mahad
  vahat-prakaṭatāṃ bhajann akhilam eva bhuṅkte sma saḥ |
  anādara-kṛtāmayaṃ dalayiteti sambhāvyate
  purandara-bali-grahād atibalī tathā tarkyate ||JGc_1,18.43|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'Ah, behold! The mountain, out of compassion, assuming his own great form, manifesting himself openly, consumed everything! It is believed that he will crush the disease of disrespect; from seizing the offerings [meant for] <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), he is conjectured to be exceedingly powerful!' // [śikharinī]

children.text: tataś ca sarvo' pi visrabdhaḥ parama-prema-bhājana-go-sabhājanam ārabdhavān | yat khalu-
children.translated_text: Then everyone, trusting, commenced the honoring of the cows — the vessels of supreme love. For indeed:

children.text:
gobhir gopā mithaḥ syuḥ pratipada-dayitās tatra nanda-vrajasthās
  tatra śrī-nanda-rājaḥ svayam ayam upamā tatra tatrāsya putraḥ |
  yady evaṃ tarhi govardhana-mahasi tad-abhyarcane te gavādyāḥ
  kiṃ varṇyāḥ kintu nirvarṇanam anu paramaṃ jñeya-bhāvaṃ prayānti ||JGc_1,18.44|| [sragdharā]
tathā ca,
  labdhārcāś cāru-veśaiḥ śavalita-vapuṣaḥ prāpta-bhogāvalīkā
  vatsaiḥ pṛktāḥ pramodaṃ pṛthutaram abhajan dhenavaḥ satyam eva |
  kintu śrī-kṛṣṇa-dṛṣṭi-pramada-valayitā yarhi tarhy eva no cet
kecid yadvad bhajante madhura-vidhurataḥ saṃskṛtaṃ ṣāḍavādi ||JGc_1,18.45||[sragdharā]
[29] tad-dṛṣṭi-puṣṭīkṛtās tu-
children.translated_text:
Cowherds and cows are mutually dear at every step — among them, those dwelling in the settlement of <s>Nanda</s> [are the dearest]; among them, the king <s>Nanda</s> himself is the standard of comparison; and among them, there is his son. If this be so, then in the great festival of <s>Govardhana</s>, in that worship — the cows and others who are worshipped — what can be described? Rather, through close examination, they attain the supreme state of the knowable! // [sragdharā]
And also:
Having received worship, beautifully attired, their bodies variegated, having obtained rows of offerings, united with their calves — the cows truly experienced the greatest joy! But when encircled by the delight of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> gaze — then indeed! Otherwise, some [would] worship as if the sacred food and other offerings were savored with sweet longing. // [sragdharā]
[29] And those nourished by his gaze:

children.text:
svarṇa-nirmita-viṣāṇa-surūpā
  rūpya-saṃvṛta-khurā dhṛta-hārāḥ |
  kiṅkiṇi-prakara-jhaṅkṛti-yuktā
  naicikī-nicitayo rucim āñcan ||JGc_1,18.46|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: With gold-fashioned horns, beautifully formed, with silver-covered hooves, wearing garlands, endowed with the tinkling sounds of hosts of little bells — the clusters of cows attained splendor! // [svāgatā]

children.text: tatra gopāḥ śrī-gopālādi-gopāla-satkṛti-camatkṛtim adhigamya, vidhim anugamya, citrakāṅga-nibha-citrātiramya-vastrāvṛtāṅgatayā tarṇakam ākramya, kautukato gāḥ sambhramya, taj-jāta-hāsa-kolāhalād viramya, grāsa-viśrāṇanena tā viśramya, parikramya, praṇamya, cācaryaṃ vāryam ācarya, vitāna-vitānenāgniṃ paricarya, pradakṣiṇāvartatayā vartamānaṃ ca taṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ viracayya, bhūṣaṇa-nivaha-mahitānāṃ purohitādīnāṃ pūjanam api pūrayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: There, the cowherds — having attained the wonder of the excellent worship by Śrī <s>Gopāla</s> and other cowherds, following the ritual procedure, their limbs wrapped in garments of wondrous beauty resembling <s>Citrakāṅga</s> (the spotted-limbed deer), mounting young bulls, rushing the cows with curiosity, resting from the uproar of laughter thus produced, giving the cows fodder to refresh them, circumambulating, bowing, performing the fire-ritual with wonder and respect, tending the fire with an awning-spread, and circumambulating him who was going clockwise — they also completed the worship of the <s>purohitas</s> and others who were honored with heaps of ornaments.

children.text: tatra śrī-gopāla-pūjā, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the worship of Śrī <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), as follows:

children.text:
snānīyāṃśuka-citrakādi-surabhi-srak-kuṇḍalādyaṃ yadā-
  ścaryaṃ tatra muhuś ca toṣa-rahitās tat-tat-parīvartataḥ |
  tad govardhana-pūjanāṅga-paśupābhyarcānu kṛṣṇārcane
  tātāmbādi-tadīya-bāndhava-janā nāntaṃ cirād aiyaruḥ ||JGc_1,18.47|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: When bathing-cloths, painted designs, fragrant garlands, earrings and the like — wondrous, and yet repeatedly they had no satisfaction, exchanging this and that — in the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which was a part of the <s>Govardhana</s> worship together with the cowherd worship, the father, mother, and other relatives of his did not reach an end even after a long time! // [śārdūla]

children.text:
yathā kṛṣṇas tathā rāmo rāmo yadvat tathā sa ca |
  vrajeśayor nātra bhedas tan-mitreṣv api tad-dṛśoḥ ||JGc_1,18.48|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: As <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, so <s>Rāma</s>; and as <s>Rāma</s>, so he — for the two lords of <s>Vraja</s>, there was no distinction herein, nor in their friends' view of them. // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: go-sambhramaṇaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: The rushing of the cows, as follows:

children.text:
yadā mudā yāti hariḥ parokṣatāṃ
  gavāṃ, tadā tā nija-vatsa-kṛṣṭitaḥ |
  vyagrībhavanti sma yadā samakṣatāṃ
  yāty eṣa yānti sma tadā tad-ātmatām ||JGc_1,18.49|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: When <s>Hari</s> went joyfully out of the cows' sight, then they, drawn by their own calves, became agitated; but when he came into their sight, then they attained the state of his very self! // [upajāti]

children.text: hāsa-kolāhalo, yathā-
children.translated_text: The uproar of laughter, as follows:

children.text:
ākṛṣṭe vatsa-vṛnde kila-kilita-ravair mātaro rambhamāṇā
  dantair ākarṣakāṃs tān vyathayitum abhito dhāvanārtā yadā syuḥ |
  hāsaṃ kolāhalāḍhyaṃ kalayati nikhile tarhi kṛṣṇānanābjaṃ
  jīyād udbhāsa-hāsa-drava-madhu parito mādanaṃ yad vavarṣa ||JGc_1,18.50|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: When the herd of calves was pulled, the mothers, bellowing with 'kila-kila' sounds, began [charging]; and when they ran about distressed on all sides to torment the pullers with their teeth — when all made laughter rich with uproar, then the lotus-face of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — victorious! — which rained all around the maddening liquid honey of bursting, flowing laughter! // [śārdūla]

children.text: go-grāsa-viśrāṇanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: The distribution of fodder to the cows, as follows:

children.text:
gopā ūcuḥ kṛṣṇa go-grāsam etaṃ
  hastāmbhoja-spṛṣṭam īṣat kuruṣva |
  tat saugandhya-prāpta-sandhānam enaṃ
  gāvaḥ suṣṭhu prītitaḥ svādayante ||JGc_1,18.51|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: The cowherds said: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, touch this cow-fodder just slightly with your lotus-hand! By the fragrance thus obtained and joined, the cows will savor it most excellently with love!' // [śālinī]

children.text: go-viśramaṇaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: The resting of the cows, as follows:

children.text:
govardhanācala-mahasy ayutādi-yūtha
  go-rodhanāya paśupā nahi tatra śekuḥ |
  phutkāra-keli-kalayā muralī murārer
  āsīd alaṃ yad asakau guṇa-koṭi-kalpā ||JGc_1,18.52|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: In the great festival of <s>Govardhana</s>, for the restraining of the cow-herds numbering in groups of ten thousand and more, the cowherds were unable [to manage]; but the flute of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), through the play of its blowing, was alone sufficient — being equivalent to ten million virtues! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text: go-parikramaṇas tu śrī-kṛṣṇenettham ādiṣṭam-
children.translated_text: Regarding the circumambulation of the cows, Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> instructed thus:

children.text:
na bhavati bata bahulānām atibahulānāṃ parikramaḥ sadyaḥ |
  ity ekasyā vyakteḥ kriyatāṃ yasmād aśeṣagā jātiḥ ||JGc_1,18.53|| [gīti]
  tatra pradakṣiṇī-kāryam ekaṃ vṛddhaṃ gavaurasam |
  mūlārādhanataḥ sarvārādhanaṃ vibudhair matam ||JGc_1,18.54|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'It is not possible to immediately circumambulate the exceedingly numerous, most abundant [cows]! Therefore, let it be done for a single individual, since the universal class pervades each!' // [gīti]
'There, one old bull of tawny color should be circumambulated — through the worship of the root, the worship of all is considered [accomplished] by the wise.' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: goṣu praṇāmātmikā bhaktis tu teṣāṃ varṇanāya nābhyarṇatām anveti, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: But the devotion in the form of bowing to the cows — that approaches no nearness to description, because:

children.text:
bhaktaḥ svabhāvāt kila gopa-lokaḥ
  śrī-nanda-lokas tu tato' pi goṣu |
  asyātha govardhana-yajña-yoge
  yogeśa-durgā-namanākhya-bhaktiḥ ||JGc_1,18.55|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: The cowherd folk are by nature devoted; the world of Śrī <s>Nanda</s> is even more so toward cows. And now, at the conjunction of the <s>Govardhana</s> sacrifice, the devotion named 'the bowing of the lord of <s>yoga</s> and <s>Durgā</s>' [was manifest]! // [indravajrā]

children.text: ācārya-varaṇa-lakṣaṇam api vilakṣaṇam eva tatra | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: The distinctive feature of selecting the ritual priest (<s>ācārya</s>) was also extraordinary there. For:

children.text:
svayam āvriyatācāryas tatra nādyavad arthitaḥ |
  yatra suṣṭhu sitaṃ yaṣṭuś cittaṃ tatraiva tasya ca ||JGc_1,18.56|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: The <s>ācārya</s> was chosen by himself there — he was not entreated as before; for where the mind of the sacrificer was purely inclined, there was his [the <s>ācārya's</s>] mind as well! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: home ca-
children.translated_text: And in the fire-offering:

children.text:
govardhana-mahā-yajñe hutabhug-vyājatas tadā |
  hareḥ pratāpa evendhāñcakre śakra-pratāpanaḥ ||JGc_1,18.57|| yadāgnir dakṣiṇāvarto yajñe jajñe tadā janaḥ |
  sarvaś ca dakṣiṇāvarta-parīvartam avartata ||JGc_1,18.58|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
In the great sacrifice of <s>Govardhana</s>, through the pretext of the sacrificial fire, it was the very splendor of <s>Hari</s> that the tormentor of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) kindled! // [anuṣṭubh]
When the fire turned clockwise in the sacrifice, then all the people too revolved in a clockwise turn! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
kṛte satre vastraṃ tilakam atha carcām avayava-
  prakārālaṅkāraṃ sakalam idam apy uttamatamam |
  dvijebhyaḥ prāyacchal laṣita-laṣitaṃ śaśvad anugān
  mudāvādīd yasmin dada dada damātraṃ vrajapatiḥ ||JGc_1,18.59|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: After the ritual, garments, <s>tilaka</s>, unguent, limb-by-limb adornments — all of the very finest — to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he gave, desired again and desired again, constantly; to his followers, the lord of <s>Vraja</s> joyfully said: 'Give, give — give abundantly!' // [śikharinī]

children.text:
divya-dātavya-sambhāre vraja-rājena yojite |
  parīkṣakās tatra paraṃ tat-parīkṣakatāṃ yayuḥ ||JGc_1,18.60|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: When the collection of divine gifts was arranged by the king of <s>Vraja</s>, even the inspectors there went beyond [the capacity of] their inspecting! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: yad anu sarve' pi prāṇinaḥ prīṇate sma | tathā hi vandi-jana-vandanam,
children.translated_text: After which, all living beings were delighted. Thus the praise of the panegyrists:

children.text:
arthena goduhān nandād arthena ca sadārthinām |
  vadānyaś ca vadānyaś ca vadānyaḥ ko bhaved ataḥ? ||JGc_1,18.61|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Through the wealth of <s>Nanda</s>, [who is like] a cow-milker for the always-needy with riches — generous, and again generous, and again generous — who then could be [more] generous?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: kintv ayam atrātiśayaḥ-
children.translated_text: But this was the surpassing wonder here:

children.text:
annāt pūrtir abhūd galāvadhi nṛṇāṃ govardhanādrer makhe
  sarva-prāṇa-bhṛtāṃ tathāpi hṛdayaṃ nāpūri tatrāṇv api |
  yasmin snigdham abhūd aśeṣa-diviṣad-vṛndaṃ yadapy atra bhoḥ
  paśyāścaryam athāpi hanta gatavān saṅkrandanaḥ śuṣkatām ||JGc_1,18.62|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: Food filled people up to the throat in the sacrifice of Mount <s>Govardhana</s>; yet the hearts of all living beings were not filled even slightly! In which [festival] all the hosts of heaven became tender [with love] — and yet, behold the wonder! — even so, <s>Saṅkrandana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) went dry [with anger]! // [śārdūla]

children.text: atha tad evaṃ vipratrākṛta-satrādikaḥ purohita-hita-sahitaḥ śrī-vraja-yuva-rāja-mahitaḥ sa khalu vijñānāṃ samājaḥ puraskṛta-vraja-rājas tad-yajñāvaśiṣṭaṃ param aviśiṣṭam annam upabhujya, veśa-viśeṣaṃ saṃyujya, gīta-nibaddhaṃ sa-śraddhatayā hari-caritaṃ prati rasan hasan, viśvasan, lasan, parito govardhanaṃ paricakrāma |
children.translated_text: Then, that assembly of the wise — who had conducted the sacrifice with the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, accompanied by the beneficent <s>purohita</s>, honored by the glorious young prince of <s>Vraja</s>, placing the king of <s>Vraja</s> at the fore — having consumed the excellent remainder of that sacrifice, donning special attire, savoring with faith the song-accompanied narrative of <s>Hari's</s> deeds, laughing, trusting, glowing, circumambulated <s>Govardhana</s> all around.

children.text: yathā ca prathā śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe [5.10.45]-
children.translated_text: As the custom [is described] in the Śrī <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> [5.10.45]:

children.text: dvijāṃś ca bhojayāmāsuḥ śataśo' tha sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And they fed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> by the hundreds and by the thousands.'

children.text: gāvaḥ śailaṃ tataś cakrur arcitās tāḥ pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: 'Then the cows, having been worshipped, circumambulated the mountain.'

children.text:
tatra pūrvāparībhāvo, yathā--
  dhenavo hari-balādayo dvijāḥ
  svāminaḥ parijanā guru-striyaḥ |
  nūtna-yauvata-śatāni dāsikāḥ
  śreṇi-mukhya-janatāś ca cakramuḥ ||JGc_1,18.63|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
The order of precedence there, as follows:
The cows, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) and the others, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the masters, the retinue, the wives of the elders, hundreds of young maidens, the maidservants, and the communities headed by guild-chiefs — [all] circumambulated! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
ākraṣṭuṃ pratidiśam atra netra-mīnān
  vādyādi-prakaṭana-dhīvarā naṭādyāḥ |
  kṛṣṇasya prathita-guṇāli-gīta-jālaṃ
  tanvānāḥ punar iha dhīvaratvam āpuḥ ||JGc_1,18.64|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text: To draw the fish-like eyes in every direction, the dancers and others — fishermen of display through music and the like — weaving the net of songs proclaiming <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> renowned virtues, here again attained the state of fishermen! // [praharṣiṇī]

children.text: tatra gopāṅganānāṃ gānaṃ ca, yathā-- yatra praśnamayam ardham ekasyās taduttaram ayaṃ tu bahūnām-
children.translated_text: And the song of the cowherd women, as follows — where the first half is the question of one, and the second half is the answer of the many:

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? araci śakra-padam abhayaṃ yena |
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who made the station of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) fearless!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? pūtanikā sā nihatā yena ||
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him by whom the she-demon <s>Pūtanā</s> was slain!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? tṛṇāvarta-tanu-dalanaṃ yena |
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who crushed the body of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? yamalārjuna-tarum udakali yena ||
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who uprooted the twin <s>Arjuna</s> trees!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? vatsa-bakāsura-hananaṃ yena |
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who slew <s>Vatsa</s> and <s>Bakāsura</s>!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? vyomāghāsura-maraṇaṃ yena ||
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who caused the death of <s>Vyoma</s> and <s>Aghāsura</s>!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? kāliya-damanaṃ kalitaṃ yena |
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who accomplished the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s>!'

children.text: giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? khara-pralambaka-śamanaṃ yena ||
children.translated_text: 'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who pacified the fierce <s>Pralamba</s>!'

children.text:
giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? dava-yugmaṃ paripītaṃ yena |
  giri-pūjeyaṃ vihitaṃ kena? trasyati kaṃsaḥ satataṃ yena ||iti|| [||JGc_1,18.65||]
[mātrāsamaka x15]
kintu-
  tadaiva guṇināṃ guṇā vividha-kautukāny apy aho,
  mano-haraṇam āvahan vraja-nivāsināṃ sarvataḥ |
  yadāgharipu-vaṃśikākala-tuṣāra-kānti-tviṣā
  jaḍīkṛta-śarīratā bhavati taṃ tu kālaṃ vinā [||JGc_1,18.66||] [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him who drank both forest fires!'
'By whom was this mountain-worship ordained?' 'By him of whom <s>Kaṃsa</s> constantly trembles!' // [mātrāsamaka]
But:
Then indeed the virtues of the virtuous and diverse curiosities too — ah, captivating the minds of all the residents of <s>Vraja</s> on every side — except for that time when, by the frost-like radiance of the sweet melody of the flute of the enemy of <s>Agha</s>, a rigidity of the body came upon [them all]! // [śikharinī]

children.text:
agre kāñcana-ratna-śṛṅga-valitā dhenv-ādikāḥ sarvatas
  tāsāṃ gopa-tatīr vidhāya sakhibhiḥ sārdhaṃ hariḥ sāgrajaḥ |
  dīvyad-divya-suvarṇa-varṇa-vasanād udgacchad-aṅga-prabhaḥ
  kanyā-kuṅkuma-yuk-karāṅka-vilasat-pṛṣṭhaḥ sphurad-veṣavān ||JGc_1,18.67|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: In front, cows adorned with golden, jeweled horns and the like on all sides — having arranged the cowherd rows behind them, <s>Hari</s>, together with his companions and elder brother, his bodily radiance rising from the shining divine golden-colored garment, with his back gleaming from the saffron-marks of the hands of the maidens — appeared in resplendent attire! // [śārdūla]

children.text:
sad-gandhāruṇa-cūrṇa-rocana-tanur yaṣṭiṃ nabhasy utkṣipan
  gṛhṇaṃś ca pratikūla-gāmi-dhavalā vidrutya saṅkocayan |
  hāsaṃ krīḍanakaṃ mithaḥ karayutiṃ saṃvāditāṃ vāditāṃ
  kurvan vādita-valgu-veṇu-paritaś cakrāma govardhanam ||JGc_1,18.68|| [śārdūla]
[yugmakam]
  yadā harir yatra gatiṃ vilāsataś
  cakāra mandaṃ laghu vā yadṛcchayā |
  tadā dṛśaḥ sarva-janasya tāṃ daśāṃ
  tatrāyayuḥ sūtra-niyantritā iva ||JGc_1,18.69|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
His body anointed with fragrant reddish powder and <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), tossing his staff into the sky, seizing and swiftly curbing the contrarily-moving white [cows], laughing, playing, clasping hands together, conversing, playing music — with the charmingly-played flute resounding all around, he circumambulated <s>Govardhana</s>! // [śārdūla]
[a pair of verses:]
Wherever <s>Hari</s> directed his gait, slowly or swiftly, of his own accord — then the eyes of all people went to that state, to that place, as if drawn by a thread! // [upajāti]

children.text: tad evaṃ bahula-kutūhalataś cālaṃ cālam amī gopa-grāmaṇyas tad eva ramyaṃ yajña-dhāma samāgamya paramānandād vāṇinī-prabhṛti-kṛta-nṛtya-vādya-gīta-grāmiṇīṃ yāminīṃ viśrāmyanti sma | prātaś ca dvitīyāyām ahimakara-kanyāyā mahima-śravaṇataḥ praṇatatayā tasyāṃ snānam ācarya nikāyyam evāgacchanti sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, with abundant curiosity, these cowherd chieftains, returning to that very delightful sacrificial ground, spent the night in supreme bliss with the village-festivity of dancing, music, and singing led by the <s>Vāṇinī</s> troupe and others. And in the morning, on the second day, having bathed with reverence in her [the river-goddess] upon hearing the glory of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), they returned punctually.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca bhrātṛ-dvitīyāyāṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ praśastena bhaginī-hastena bhoktavyam iti parama-dhanyābhir upanandādi-kanyābhir mitho milantībhir nimantritau praṇaya-yantritau tatra sa-tṛṣṇau ca rāma-kṛṣṇau sahacara-nikareṇa saha bhojana-kareṇa saha maham arocayatām |
children.translated_text: And on that <s>Bhrātṛ-dvitīyā</s> (Brother's Second day), since one should eat from the praiseworthy hand of a sister — the supremely blessed daughters of <s>Upananda</s> and others, coming together and inviting them affectionately, constrained by love and longing, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with the group of companions and the dining troupe, graced the feast.

children.text: tad evaṃ vṛtte vṛtte, kṛṣṇasya samunnaddhatā-bandhayā kuhanayā mad-yajña-pratyūhanam idam ity ūhamānaḥ śakras tu vakra-bhāva-cakratayā cukrodha | [49] kṛṣṇena tasya yā gūḍhāpi khaṭvārūḍhatā tarkitā, sā katham anyathā samparkitayā varteteti vyaktīkartum iva matsaratas tat-sahita-viśva-mahita-śrīman-nandādi-nindā-pūrvakaṃ saṃvartaka-meghān vraja-vighātāya pravartayāmāsa | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, as things progressed, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), conjecturing 'This is an obstruction to my sacrifice!' — through the binding of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> swelling deception — became wrathful through the wheel of his crooked disposition. [49] The secret reclining-on-the-bed [state] of <s>Indra</s> — surmised by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> even though concealed — in order to make manifest how else it might unfold through [actual] contact, as if out of jealousy, preceded by criticism of the glorious <s>Nanda</s> and others — who, together with the world, were honored by him — he set the <s>Saṃvartaka</s> destruction-clouds in motion for the devastation of <s>Vraja</s>. And then:

children.text:
kauveryāṃ pūrvam āsīt kim api hima-marut kālimā meghaleśaḥ
  śampā-nirghoṣa-vīpsā-spṛg iti paśu-kule goṣṭham evāśu nīte |
  gopādyā durnimitta-prakara-kalanayā kṛṣṇam āvṛtya vṛttās
  tan-nirdeśāt tam ādriṃ sapadi parigatās tasthur ūrdhvaṃ nirīkṣya ||JGc_1,18.70||[sragdharā]
[50] nirdeśā, yathā--
  indro yadi mahā-vṛṣṭiṃ naṣṭa-sṛṣṭiṃ taniṣyati |
  tad-aṅgīkāri-girirāṭ kṛpāṃ sāṅgīkariṣyati ||JGc_1,18.71|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'First there was on the <s>Kauverī</s> [horizon] some frost-wind, blackness, a patch of cloud, | a touch of lightning, thunder, and hail-like sprinkles — and when the cattle were quickly driven to the cow-settlement, | the cowherds and others, discerning a mass of bad omens, surrounding <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, turned to him; | and at his direction, they swiftly went to that mountain and stood looking upward.' || (JGc 1,18.70) [sragdharā]
[50] The direction was as follows:
'If <s>Indra</s> will stretch out a great rain that destroys creation, | the mountain-king who accepts that [challenge] will show compassion!' || (JGc 1,18.71) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: upatyakām upetya, taṃ vighnaṃ nighnaṃ kartum ādrim upaghnaṃ kṛtvā kṛtādhiṣṭhāne tu goṣṭhe goṣṭhendra-tanaye ca samayaṃ pratipālayati-
children.translated_text: Having reached the foothill and making the mountain nearby to render that obstruction obstructed, when the cow-settlement and the son of the cowherd-chief had been placed in readiness and he was awaiting the moment:

children.text:
ghaḍad-ghaḍad iti dhvana-daghana-ghaṭābhisaṅghaṭṭanaiḥ
  kaṭhora-kuṭha-kuṭṭakaiḥ kuṭila-vāyubhiḥ kuṇṭhite |
  prakoṣṭha-kuṭa-kuṭṭimā-vaṭa-taṭādi-maty ujjhite
  jane prakaṭam āṭa sā prathita-dhṛṣṭi-vṛṣṭi-prathā ||JGc_1,18.72|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text: 'With crashings of 'ghaḍ-ghaḍ' from the collisions of dense cloud-clusters, | with harsh hailstone-poundings, with crooked winds causing suffocation, | when the people, abandoning their yard-shelters, courtyard-platforms, banyan-edges and the like, | that renowned display of fierce downpour marched forth openly!' || (JGc 1,18.72) [pṛthvī]

children.text:
dhārāḥ śakra-dhanur vimukta-śaratāṃ tanvanti varṣopalā
  vajratvaṃ bata vajra-pāta-nicayāḥ sūrya-prapāta-bhramam |
  itthaṃ duḥkhitayā hariṃ gatim ite goṣṭhe sa govardhanaṃ
  haste' dhatta yathā na kena ca tadā śaktaṃ darāpy ūhitum ||JGc_1,18.73|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'The rain-streams render <s>Indra's</s> bow (the rainbow) as discharged arrows; the hailstones | acquire the nature of thunderbolts; alas, the cascading thunderbolts produce the illusion of falling suns! | Thus, when the distressed [people] had gone to <s>Hari</s> as their refuge in the cow-settlement, he raised <s>Govardhana</s> | in his hand — in a way that no one then could even slightly conceive!' || (JGc 1,18.73) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: tad evaṃ meghaṅkare purandare niviḍīṣa-varṣādinā bhayaṅkare cārtiṅkare ca jāte kṣemaṅkaraḥ sa murāriḥ purā hy evaṃ parāmamarśa-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the cloud-maker (<s>Indra</s>) had become terrifying with fierce hail-showers and the like, and had become a cause of suffering, that beneficent slayer of <s>Mura</s> had previously thus reflected:

children.text:
indraḥ svairābhimānī mayi mad-anugate cāvamānī tataś ca
  svāntān medūra-mānī tad amum anu mayā māna-bhaṅga-prasaktaḥ |
  goṣṭhaṃ mad-gaty-aśeṣaṃ mama mad-anugatasyāpi mud-bhṛd-viśeṣaṃ
  mac-citte sāvaśeṣaṃ tad idam atha mayā prāṇa-sāmyena dhāryam ||JGc_1,18.74|| iti |
[sragdharā]
  samajani halinā na harer giri-dhṛti-sambhrama-vaśena saṃvādaḥ |
  tad api paraspara-hārdā- jñānaṃ tasminn ajījanat tam iva ||JGc_1,18.75|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
'<s>Indra</s>, of willful pride, is contemptuous of me and my followers; and therefore, | thinking himself mighty from within — by me, the destruction of his pride must be pursued! | The cow-settlement, entirely dependent on me, and even of my follower (<s>Govardhana</s>), especially joy-bearing — | is still remaining in my heart — this therefore must be upheld by me as [dear as] my own life-breath!' || (JGc 1,18.74) [sragdharā]
'There was no dialogue between the Plough-bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>) and <s>Hari</s> arising from the agitation of mountain-lifting; | yet their mutual heart-knowledge generated that [understanding] in him as if [there had been one].' || (JGc 1,18.75) [gīti]

children.text: taṃ nagam unnayamānaś cāsau romāñcataḥ sūci-nicaya-nicita-sarvāvayavān iva nicāyann, amūla-bhīru-māthurābhīra-jāti-jātīya-gambhīra-madhura-svara-vikasvara-dūra-bhū-vibhūti-hūtibhir ūrjita-garjitādi-garvaṃ sarvaṃ kharvaṃ vidhāya priyaṅkaratayā vyaktam uktavān-
children.translated_text: And he, raising that mountain, as if surveying all his limbs studded with clusters of needles from horripilation, and with deep, sweet, resonant, far-reaching calls of glory — in the manner of the <s>Ābhīra</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>) cowherd clan, bold and fearless — rendering insignificant all the proud thunderings and the like, he clearly spoke as one doing a pleasing service:

children.text:
yatra khalu muhur api he-śabdaḥ plutatāpluta evāsīt | tathā hi-amba he, mā vilambasva | tāta he, atraiva yūyam āyāta | ārya he, sarvān ādāyāgaccha iti prabhṛti |
[55] tad evaṃ balarāmeṇa balenāntikam ānīteṣu teṣu punar ūcivān-
children.translated_text:
Wherein, indeed, the exclamatory syllable 'he!' was both prolonged and unprolonged again and again. For thus: 'Ho, mother! Do not delay!' 'Ho, father! Come right here!' 'Ho, elder brother! Come bringing everyone!' — and so forth.
[55] Thus, when those had been brought near by <s>Balarāma</s> with strength, he spoke again:

children.text:
pitar na kuru sambhramaṃ janani nārtim āvartaya,
  praśāmya suhṛdāṃ tate mama tu ko' pi nātra śramaḥ |
  yato giri-varaḥ svayaṃ karuṇayā kare māmake
  samutpatana-līlayā sa varivarti tūla-prabhaḥ ||JGc_1,18.76|| [pṛthvī]
kiṃ ca,
  bhūbhṛd-garte' py atra niśreṇi-yukte
  sthānaṃ paśyann asmi pātāla-kalpam |
  vistīrṇo' bhūd adrir ity antar-ambhaḥ-
  saṅgātīte no nipatyādi cātra ||JGc_1,18.77|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Father, do not be agitated! Mother, do not turn to distress! | Be calm, O company of friends — for me there is no exertion here at all! | For the excellent mountain, of its own compassion, upon my hand, | with the sport of leaping up, revolves — light as cotton!' || (JGc 1,18.76) [pṛthvī]
Moreover:
'Even in the mountain's cavity here, fitted with stairways, | I see a space resembling the netherworld! | The mountain has expanded — so inner water | need not fall upon us here either, having gone beyond the pooling!' || (JGc 1,18.77) [śālinī]

children.text:
punaś ca teṣāṃ bhāvāntaraṃ vibhāvya sva-kartṛka-dhāraṇam apy ardham aṅgīkṛtya bhaṇati sma-
  mātar mantraṇayā mā māṃ nivartayata sattamāḥ |
  udasto yena tad-dhastād dhvastaḥ syād girirāṭ katham? ||JGc_1,18.78|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And again, perceiving their altered state of mind and half-accepting even his own role as bearer, he said:
'Mother, do not turn me back with counsel, O best ones! | How could the mountain-king, upheld by whose hand, | fall — if cast down by that [same] hand?' || (JGc 1,18.78) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
  mā vilambadhvam atyarthaṃ yuṣmad-duḥkhena kampratām |
  mayi gacchaty adripatiḥ patitā viśata drutam ||JGc_1,18.79|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'Do not delay excessively — the mountain-lord | trembles from your suffering! | If I depart, it would fall — enter quickly!' || (JGc 1,18.79) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
atha paśupa-janas tadīya-hārdād
  drutam aviśan nikhilas tadādri-garte |
  nahi śaraṇatayā kadācid enaṃ
  sa bhajati kintu tad-eka-tarṣi-buddhyā ||JGc_1,18.80|| [puṣpitāgrā]
tataś ca-
  suvinyasta-niḥśreṇi-labdha-praveśaṃ
  maṇi-śreṇi-vidyotamāna-pradeśam |
  gṛhasyeva ratnāṅga-bhitti-prakāraṃ
  tad-ūrdhvaṃ ca tat-tūlya-śobhā-pracāram ||JGc_1,18.81|| [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
children.translated_text:
Then all the cowherd folk, from their heartfelt trust in him, | swiftly entered the mountain's cavity; | not indeed as a shelter did he embrace it, | but with the sole understanding of one thirsting for it alone. || (JGc 1,18.80) [puṣpitāgrā]
And then:
'With well-placed stairways providing entrance, | with areas illuminated by rows of gems, | with walls like the gem-embedded ramparts of a house, | and above, a display of equal splendor,' || (JGc 1,18.81) [bhujaṅgaprayātā]

children.text:
sukha-sparśa-maṇy-ācita-kṣauṇi-bhāgaṃ
  samastāvakāśārha-sandhā-vibhāgam |
  yathāpekṣa-vibhrājita-svaccha-nīraṃ
  sukhākāri-dharmāñci-nīcaiḥ samīram ||JGc_1,18.82|| [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
children.translated_text: 'With ground-area studded with pleasant-to-touch gems, | with divisions of partitions fit for all necessary spaces, | with clear water shining as needed, | and with a gentle, comfort-creating, low breeze,' || (JGc 1,18.82) [bhujaṅgaprayātā]

children.text:
kare svasya vāme tu vāme vasantaṃ
  giriṃ līlayāspṛśya santaṃ hasantam |
  tadīyāntar-udyan-mahā-kuṭṭima-sthaṃ
  hariṃ hāri-rūpādibhiḥ prāg-avastham ||JGc_1,18.83|| [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
children.translated_text: 'On his own left hand, on the left side, the mountain resting — | touching it playfully, laughing peacefully — | standing within, on the great elevated platform inside, | <s>Hari</s>, with his enchanting form and other attributes, as before,' || (JGc 1,18.83) [bhujaṅgaprayātā]

children.text:
dadhad-veṇum ānamra-hasta-pradhānaṃ
  kadācin mudā sakhyur aṃse dadhānam |
  dadarśa praharṣaṃ satarṣaṃ sabhītiṃ
  vrajāvāsi-loko yayau cātirītim ||JGc_1,18.84|| [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
children.translated_text: 'Holding the flute, with his chief hand lowered, | sometimes joyfully resting [it] on a friend's shoulder — | the people dwelling in <s>Vraja</s> beheld him with delight, longing, and fear, | and were transported beyond all measure!' || (JGc 1,18.84) [bhujaṅgaprayātā]

children.text:
govardhanādris tatrāsīd ratna-citraṃ mahā-gṛham |
  harir yatra harid-ratna-stambhatārambhi-vibhramaḥ ||JGc_1,18.85|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: '<s>Govardhana</s> mountain was there a great mansion adorned with gems, | where <s>Hari</s> was the graceful one, beginning from the emerald-gem pillars!' || (JGc 1,18.85) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
api ca-
  vilasati maṇi-daṇḍa-śrīr mukundasya bāhus
  tad-upari parito' pi cchatra-tulyo girīndraḥ |
  pratidiśam iha muktā-dāmavad vāri-dhārā
  vraja-sadana-janānāṃ pratyutābhūd vibhūtiḥ ||JGc_1,18.86|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'The splendor of the gem-studded staff — <s>Mukunda's</s> arm — shines forth; | above, all around, the mountain-chief, like an umbrella; | in every direction here, the streams of water [fell] like pearl-garlands; | for the people of the <s>Vraja</s> settlement, it became instead their prosperity!' || (JGc 1,18.86) [mālinī]

children.text: tataś ca sahasā rohiṇī-sahitā vrajeśa-gṛhiṇī taṃ pārśvayor gṛhītavatī | tad idaṃ varṇibhir nirvarṇya varṇyate sma, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then suddenly, <s>Rohiṇī</s> together with the queen of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> seized him on both sides. This was observed and described by the bards, as follows:

children.text:
mātṛbhyāṃ pārśva-yugme dhṛta-tanur asakṛn mṛjyamānānanābjaḥ
  pitrādy-ātmīya-vargaiḥ sa-pulakam abhito vīkṣito' tarkya-karmā |
  so' yaṃ smerābja-netraṃ kalita-taṭa-kalā-hastakaḥ savya-hasta-
  nyasta-kṣauṇī-bhṛd uccair jaya-jaya-ninadānvīḍitaḥ krīḍatīva ||JGc_1,18.87|| [sragdharā]
  govardhana-dharasyāgre vilāsān vyañjato balaḥ |
  kṛtsnān utsāhayaty eṣa nāṭye vā naṭa-nāyakaḥ ||JGc_1,18.88|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Held in body at both sides by the two mothers, his lotus-face repeatedly wiped, | gazed at all around with horripilation by his father and other kinsmen — he of inconceivable deeds — | he, with smiling lotus-eyes, a hand playing at the slope-edge, | the earth-bearer placed on his left hand held high — hailed with cries of "Victory! Victory!" — plays as it were!' || (JGc 1,18.87) [sragdharā]
'Before the bearer of <s>Govardhana</s>, <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), displaying graces, | inspires everyone — like a hero-protagonist in a dance-drama!' || (JGc 1,18.88) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ sati-
children.translated_text: Thus, this being so:

children.text:
mahā-vṛṣṭir garjaḥ khara-hima-pavanaḥ sphūrjathur dhvāntam abdas
  tathā vajrīty evaṃvidha-vividha-gati-kleśa-hetur bahir yaḥ |
  tam antar nirvarṣaṃ madhura-nigaditaṃ cāru-vāyuḥ pragītaṃ
  marīciś citraśrīr ajitagiribhṛd ity āptaśarma vyakārīt ||JGc_1,18.89|| [śobhā]
children.translated_text: 'The great rain, the thunder, the harsh frost-wind, the lightning, the darkness, the clouds, | and <s>Indra</s> himself — all these various sources of distress [were] outside; | but inside — rainless, sweetly spoken, beautiful breezes, singing, | radiance, variegated beauty — the unconquered mountain-bearer made all comfort!' || (JGc 1,18.89) [śobhā]

children.text:
nṛtya-stotra-pragītāny aticaṭula-naṭādy-arthināṃ dāna-caryā
  varyāṇāṃ svasti-pāṭhaḥ śruti-samaya-vidāṃ krīḍitaṃ bālakānām |
  garvāt kharvākhilānām iti sakalam abhūd yasya tu prema-jātaṃ
  sa śrī-govardhanādri-pravara-dhara-karaḥ kaṃ na toṣaṃ pupoṣa? ||JGc_1,18.90||[sragdharā]
  gurau namrā tulye smita-yug anupālye dhṛta-jalā
  kvacil līlālolā maghavati tu vakrā bata satī |
  dhṛtādrer dṛṣṭis tat tad anu guṇam arthaṃ vidadhatī
  kriyām anyāṃ tasya svam anu punar-uktām akuruta ||JGc_1,18.91|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'Dances, hymns, and songs; gift-giving for the performers eager for acrobatics and such; | benedictory recitations by those versed in Vedic tradition; play of children — | all of this arose from love for him whose pride rendered all others insignificant — | that bearer of the supreme earth-bearing <s>Govardhana</s> mountain — whom did he not nourish with delight?' || (JGc 1,18.90) [sragdharā]
'Bowed toward elders, smiling toward equals, tear-eyed toward dependents, | sometimes playfully sportive, but toward <s>Indra</s> — indeed crooked — a virtuous woman; | the glance of the mountain-bearer, producing effect appropriate to each quality, | made his other action seem like a repetition of his own [nature]!' || (JGc 1,18.91) [śikharinī]

children.text:
giridhara-vadanendo raśmi-pīyūṣa-dhārāṃ
  pibad iha paśu-jātaṃ sapta-rātrin-divāni |
  kṣudham api sa-tṛṣaṃ tan nāyayau tarhi tasya
  praṇayi-jana-gaṇānāṃ kiṃ bruve na bruve kim? ||JGc_1,18.92|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text: 'Drinking the stream of nectar-rays from the moon-face of the mountain-bearer, | the cattle-kind here, for seven nights and days, | did not feel hunger or thirst at all — then, | of his beloved people, what shall I say and what shall I not say?' || (JGc 1,18.92) [mālinī]

children.text:
śrī-mukhena janatā sudhā-rasair
  asya bhūdhara-dharasya pūryate |
  evam apy avayatī tadā prasūs
  tan muhur bahu-rasair apūrayat ||JGc_1,18.93|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'The people are filled with nectar-essences from the glorious face | of this bearer of the earth-bearer; | even so, his mother, not content, | repeatedly filled him with many juices then!' || (JGc 1,18.93) [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
saptāhar-niśa-nirmitā giribhṛtā ye ye vilāsās tadā
  tān kalpair api saptabhiḥ kathayitā śeṣo' pi nāśeṣataḥ |
  evaṃ ced vacanair amūṃs tri-caturaiḥ sac-cāturī-varjitais
  tūrṇaṃ varṇitavān kaviḥ svayam asau durbhūya dodūyate ||JGc_1,18.94|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'The sports that were fashioned during the seven days and nights of mountain-bearing — | even <s>Śeṣa</s> (the cosmic serpent) with seven cosmic cycles could not narrate them fully! | If so, then the poet himself, having described them quickly | with three or four words devoid of genuine skill, becomes wretched and tormented!' || (JGc 1,18.94) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: tad evam atra prastāve labdhāvasthāne, tatra śakras tu duṣṭa-kramam anuṣṭhitavān-
children.translated_text: Thus, in this very context, when the situation was established, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) then carried out his wicked course:

children.text:
prathamaṃ tāvat prathamānena vātena vātena te pralayaṃ gatā iti sandihya, tadaiva tad-daivata-śatam eva tatra prabhūta-dūtatayā prasthāpitavān | tat tu tasmād atisatvaram āgatvaratayā tad abhīṣṭaṃ pratyācaṣṭa | tataś ca balārātir balāt pravartita-prasāreṇa jalāsāreṇa tad-vilāpanaṃ pratītya ca satyatā-pratipattaye jalada-devān eva tad-vārtāyāṃ vartayāmāsa | vartitāś ca te tad-vīkṣitena pathā pratyāgatya yathā-pūrvaṃ tat pratyāśā-padaṃ pratyākhyāya sthitavantaḥ | tataś ca paramam apūrvaṃ matvā, manasy atīva dhūrvaṇaṃ gatvā, ghanāghana-bṛṃhaṇaḥ sa ghanāghanaḥ sva-vāhanaṃ ghanāghanaṃ krodhād aṅkuśena maṅkṣu jaghāna | hatvā ca kiñcid agrato gatvā satvaram airāvatīya-vahnim ahni cāpahnuta-netra-vīryaṃ vikīrya dūtyāya tad-devatām avatārayāmāsa
| sā ca tato nivṛtya pravṛtty-antaraṃ nivedayāmāsa-deva, paramāścarya-caryeyam avadhāryatām, yat khalu sa eva bali-bhojana-valita-balaḥ sann acalaḥ samyag utpatann ivāvalokyate |
children.translated_text:
At first, suspecting that they had been destroyed by the wind-accompanied destructive wind, he (<s>Indra</s>) at that very moment dispatched a hundred of those very deities there as an abundant delegation. But that [group], having returned from there with extreme haste, reported back that his desire [had not been fulfilled]. Then, the enemy of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Indra</s>), perceiving the dissolution of [the effect of] the forcefully deployed water-torrents, and for the purpose of ascertaining [their] truthfulness, deployed the cloud-gods themselves to report on the situation. And they, dispatched and returning by the path he had indicated, rejecting the grounds for hope as before, stood firm. Then, considering this supremely unprecedented, his mind having gone to extreme distraction, that thunderer, augmenter of dense clouds — that dense cloud [himself] — in rage, immediately struck his mount, the dense cloud (<s>Airāvata</s>), with his goad. Having struck, going a little forward, swiftly deploying the <s>Airāvatī</s>-fire (<s>Airāvata's</s> lightning) whose eye-power had been concealed during the day, he dispatched that divinity itself as his emissary.
And she, returning from there, reported a different development: 'My lord, let this most wondrous conduct be considered — for that very one, strengthened by the sacrificial feast-offering, appears to be correctly rising up as if the immovable [mountain] itself!'

children.text: indra uvāca-dṛśyatāṃ kīdṛśam anantaram antaraṃ jātam? labdha-śokaś ca vraja-lokaḥ kutra vā sa-putraḥ prayātaḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> said: 'Let it be seen — what kind of gap has appeared next? And where has the grief-stricken <s>Vraja</s>-populace gone together with their children?'

children.text: atha sarve yathājñāpayantīti vidrutya punaḥ saṅgatya saṃhatya pratyabhāṣanta-sarvadaiva sarva-daivata-mānya! śatamanyo! manyāmahe te sarve śata-parva-sagarbha-vidyud-vahninā pralīnatām eva nītāḥ, yad bahir na hi vilokyante |
children.translated_text: Then all of them, saying 'As you command!' — ran, reassembled, gathered together, and reported: 'O one always honored by all deities! O <s>Śatamanya</s> (hundred-wrathful one)! We believe they have all been dissolved into nothingness by the fire of lightning contained in the hundred-jointed [thunderbolt] and the womb of clouds, for they are not seen outside!'

children.text: indra sa-harṣam uvāca-āyuṣmadbhir yuṣmābhir punar api nirūpyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> said joyfully: 'O long-lived ones, let it be verified by you once more!'

children.text: atha tathā punaḥ saṅgatya gaty-antaraṃ prathayāmāsuḥ-divīśvara, nādyāpi te naśvaratāṃ prāptāḥ, pratyuta pātālatala iva giri-garta-tale praviśya tad diśantīvānanda-kolāhalaṃ kurvantaḥ pratīyante | acalaś ca svayaṃ balānuja-hasta-nyasta-prāya-grāva-nikāya-maya-kāyatayā pratīyate |
children.translated_text: Then, having thus assembled again, they announced a different development: 'O Lord of Heaven, even now they have not attained destruction; rather, having entered as if into the nether world, into the gorge of the mountain's cavity, they appear to be giving [forth sounds] and making a joyful clamor! And the mountain itself appears to have a body composed of masses of stones mostly placed by the hand of <s>Bala's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)!'

children.text: indra uvāca-lakṣayāmi | mayā pūrvaṃ chinna-pakṣatir apy asau punaḥ kiṃ sa-pakṣaḥ sampannaḥ, yata eva garvavān sa parvataḥ sarvatas teṣām akṣayāya pakṣapātam ācacāra? bhavatu nāma, tam enaṃ punar nihrādi-hrādinī-vahni-prahāreṇa saṃhāre yojayāmi, yena tadīya-tale valamānatayā labdhāvalepās te' pi tūrṇam eva cūrṇatām āsādayanti iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> said: 'I observe!
