Was that [mountain], whose wings I had previously clipped, again endowed with wings, since that proud mountain showed partiality toward them on all sides for their indestructibility? So be it — I shall again subject him to destruction by the blows of the thundering <s>Hrādinī</s>-fire, whereby those who have taken shelter at his base, having gained arrogance through their reliance, will also quickly be pulverized!'

children.text: tathā ca, tad-vajreṇa biddhaṃ vidhāya praṇidhāna-dvārā tad anyathā praṇidhāya, manasi kopa-prakopam ādhāya, muhur api tad eva sandhāya, vyarthatā-kadarthita-puruṣārthaḥ punar nūtana-dūta-gaṇaṃ prahāpayann āha sma-are, nirūpyatāṃ tirobhūya, bhūyaḥ kiṃ tatra citram iva vartate, yenāśaner api pracāraḥ sva-vyavahārād vyabhicāraṃ sañcacāra |
children.translated_text: And so, having made that thunderbolt pierce [the mountain] by the gateway of concentrated meditation, disposing of that [effort] otherwise by further meditation, placing fury upon fury within his mind, aiming again and again — his purpose made worthless by the frustration of his aim — again dispatching a fresh group of emissaries, he said: 'You! Go incognito and investigate — what strange wonder is occurring there, that even the course of the thunderbolt has deviated from its normal operation!'

children.text: athāmī ca tathāgatya sva-pratyakṣaṃ pratyāyāmāsuḥ-sutrāman, na tatra kutracid api dvi-trāṇy api patrāṇi srastāni dṛśyante, na ca kācit pipīḍikāpi pīḍitā | tad evaṃ yady uparitanaṃ vṛttaṃ parito vṛttaṃ, tadā vilasita-raṅga-taraṅgāṇām antaraṅgānāṃ vārtā tu dūre vartatām |
children.translated_text: Then those ones, having gone there, reported their own direct perception: 'O <s>Sutrāman</s> (<s>Indra</s>)! Not even two or three leaves are seen fallen anywhere there, nor is even a single ant harmed! Thus, if the events on the upper side have occurred all around, then let the news of the inner ones — those of the play-arena's wave-crest — remain far away!'

children.text:
atha taṃ nikhiloccaṃ śiloccayaṃ prati pratihata-nija-ṭaṅkatayā sa-śaṅkaḥ sa vajrapāṇir vismaya-lajjā-bhayāni sajjaṃś ciram eva tuṣṇīmbhūṣṇutayā cintayāmāsa-
āṃ, kṛṣṇākāram anu viṣṇur eva tatrāvirbhaviṣṇutām āsasāda | kathaṃ vā sa ca parāt parājiṣṇutām āsīdatu, yaḥ khalv ahāryam api hāryatām āsādayāmāsa |
children.translated_text:
Then, toward that supremely lofty rock-mass, his own axe-blade having been repelled, that thunderbolt-handed one, apprehensive, harboring wonder, shame, and fear, contemplated in prolonged silence:
'Ah — following the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself who has attained manifestation there! Or how can he who has made even the irremovable become removable be defeated by a superior [force]?'

children.text:
atha tadānīm eva mūḍhaḥ, saṃjñayā śaṅkhacūḍaḥ, kaṃsa-sapakṣaḥ kaścid yakṣaḥ pratikṛṣṭam atitayātihṛṣṭaḥ saṅgamya praṇamya ca provāca-mahendradeva, drumila-dānava-nandana-mahīndra-sadanād bhavat-padāravindaṃ vindamānaḥ so' yam asmi | sa hi parama-hita-sahitatayā dundubhi-sandoha-nirghoṣaṃ pratidiśaṃ joṣayitvā bhavantaṃ prati prīti-pariṇāmaṃ praṇāmaṃ nirdideśa sandideśa ca | tad idaṃ bhavadbhir yad etad anuṣṭhitam, tena parama-tuṣṭim āpannā vayam | yataḥ kṣudratama-nirmita-garva-kirmīrita-mahad-atikramaḥ samastasya ca duḥsahaḥ sampadyate | balād utpatana-līla-pipīlikāvad amūdṛśāṃ tad-diṣṭataḥ prāpta-diṣṭāntatā ca dṛṣṭā | kiṃ ca, kiyad vābhīra-jātīnāṃ yajamānatayā bhavat-prayojanaṃ
janitā? vayam eva hi nānā-yajñān anujñāpya bhavatsu santarpaṇam arpayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, at that very time, a certain <s>Yakṣa</s> — foolish, named <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> by designation, an ally of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — having arrived completely delighted at the reproach [inflicted upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], met and bowed, and said: 'O Great Lord <s>Indra</s>, I am he who comes finding your lotus feet from the palace of <s>Drumila</s>, the <s>Dānava</s>-descendant earth-king. He, with the utmost benevolence, having caused the rumbling of drum-masses to resound in every direction, directed and sent his respectful salutation as a transformation of affection toward you. And by this that has been performed by your lordship, we have attained supreme satisfaction. For the transgression of a great one — provoked by pride fabricated by the most insignificant — is intolerable to all. The ant-like sport of forcefully rising up by such [insignificant ones], struck by his command, has been observed as having reached its destined conclusion. Moreover, how much purpose has been generated by your lordship from the status of <s>Ābhīra</s>-folk as sacrificers? We ourselves shall authorize various sacrifices and render offerings to you!'

children.text:
atha tad etad avadhārya sa deva-kula-nirdhāryaś camatkāram āsasāda, [71] yatraivaṃ cintām āpa-aho, śakrāśana-vyasanatayā mama buddhir na sadā śuddhim avaruṇaddhi, yato mitrāmitratā vaiparītyaṃ parītya rīty-atikramam āpannavān asmi | tad etac ca, gotrabhid iti sva-nāma-sphurad-upaśruti-phalam iva mama pratibhāti | kiṃ ca,
  garviṇaḥ suṣṭhu me yuktāpy eṣābhibhava-bhāvanā |
  ātta-garvo' bhibhūtaḥ syād iti paryāyatā yataḥ ||JGc_1,18.95|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then, having ascertained this, that one worthy of being determined by the divine family was seized by astonishment. [71] And there, he thus attained anxiety: 'Ah, through my vice of being addicted to the food of <s>Indra</s>-offerings, my intellect does not always maintain purity, since I have transgressed the boundary of propriety by inverting the distinction between friend and foe. And this seems to me like the fruit of the reverberating secondary meaning of my own name <s>Gotrabhid</s> (splitter of mountains / destroyer of lineage)! Moreover:
Even this properly befitting thought of mine — of overpowering the proud one —
when the proud one is overpowered, he himself becomes overpowered — for such is the cycle!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: prakāśas tu sva-dāsān uvāca-bhavatu, nivartantāṃ saṃvarta-vartanā megha-vārtāḥ | avarajanmāyam iti vrajarāja-tanūjaṃ prati titikṣā-bhāja eva vayaṃ śikṣā-mātra-pātratām āsāditavantaḥ, na tu katham apy anyathā-bhāva-bhāvana-vyathām iti |
children.translated_text: Openly, he said to his own servants: 'Enough — let the <s>Saṃvartaka</s>-operation of the destructive cloud-tidings cease! We, regarding this son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> as one of lower birth, have been brought to only the level of receiving a lesson in forbearance, and in no way to the state of contemplating any altered disposition [toward him].'

children.text: atha yakṣam apy ādidesa, nijaṃ rājānam idaṃ sandiśa-[74] muhuḥ kopito' pi so' pi bhavāṃs tasmād bhayam iva bhāvayan vartata ity avadhārayata eva mamādhikaḥ krodhas tatra vardhate sma | yadi tad api tathyaṃ syāt tadā vayaṃ yāthātathyam eva prathayiṣyāmaḥ: śatamanyoḥ sahasrākṣasya śatakoṭi-hastasya mamāpi kaḥ khalu khalatayānabhīpsitaṃ kurvīta? api ca-
children.translated_text: Then he instructed the <s>Yakṣa</s> as well: 'Convey this message to your own king: [74] "He should understand that even he, who continues to cultivate something like fear toward him (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) despite being provoked by me repeatedly — my greater wrath was growing there. If even that were true, then we shall proclaim the truth as it is: who indeed, among those of wicked intent, would do what is undesired by me — <s>Śatamanya</s>, the thousand-eyed one, the one with a hundred billion hands? Moreover:'

children.text:
tvaṃ puṇya-janasevya-śrīr devānāṃ priyatāṃ gataḥ |
  so' py agre tvad-vidhānāṃ syād bhojānāṃ gopa-dārakaḥ ||JGc_1,18.96|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'You are one served by the glory of the <s>Puṇyajanas</s> (<s>Yakṣas</s>), and have attained the affection of the gods;
but he too, that cowherd-boy of the <s>Bhojas</s>, would be [nothing] before ones like you!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad etad anubhūya kupūyaḥ khalv asau dūyamāna-hṛdayatayā yakṣaḥ pratasthe, svena cānītaṃ sandeśaṃ pravāhe mūtritam ivātasthe |
children.translated_text: Then, having experienced this, that wretched <s>Yakṣa</s> departed with a burning heart, and the message he had brought stood [neglected] as if urinated upon in a stream.

children.text: tad evam apadhvastaṃ-manyaḥ śatamanyuś ca śata-manyutayā vimāna-gatiṃ prati vimāna-gatim āsādya sadyaḥ sānuśayaṃ saṃśayānatayā śayānatayā ca nijāntar-nilayam ayāñcakre | śābdikāṣṭakam anu viśiṣṭatayā ralayor vyatyayam ivāvetya, nirayam eva ca taṃ manyate sma | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Śatamanya</s> (<s>Indra</s>), his pride shattered and with a hundred resentments, having attained a disposition of disregard toward the celestial-chariot path itself, immediately, with remorse and with a state of indecision and recumbence, retired to his own inner chamber. Understanding, as if from the group of eight [grammatical rules] regarding the interchange of 'r' and 'l' specifically, he considered his abode to be hell (<s>niraya</s>) itself. For indeed:

children.text:
vikṣeptuṃ vrajam aicchad eṣa pavanair vikṣepam āpa svayaṃ
  varṣair dharṣayituṃ ca dharṣam agamad bāḍhaṃ viḍaujā hṛdi |
  vajrais tāḍayituṃ tathāpa śirasi sve vajra-tāḍyātmatāṃ
  sādhūtpāta-karatvam arjati viparyastā gatir yujyate ||JGc_1,18.97|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
tad evaṃ geha-guhām avagāhamāne kauśike-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the descendant of <s>Kuśika</s> (<s>Indra</s>) had entered the cave of his dwelling:

children.text:
atha dyavi divākaraḥ prakaṭa-bhāvam āṭa drutaṃ
  diśaḥ sphuraṇam āgaman dharaṇir āpa vartma-prathām |
  tadā ca nayana-śravaś-caraṇa-saṃhatiḥ prāṇinām
  idaṃ nija-nijāśraya-trayam anu svavṛttiṃ yayau ||JGc_1,18.98|| [pṛthvī]

niryāte megha-jāte harir atha paśupānākhyad uccair amuṣmān
  niryāta prātta-gṛhyā dara ca dara-matiṃ mā kurudhvaṃ tvaradhvam |
  yasmin gāmbhīrya-bhāji sphuṭa-vacasi ghanāḥ pūrvam apy asya kāntyā
  bhūbhṛd-bhūtyā ca dhūtāḥ punar ahaha yayur garja-garvād vidhūtim ||JGc_1,18.99|| [sragdharā]
[78] atha tadāmreḍita-preritatayā vādita-bahula-kāhalādi-halahalāyamāna-kolāhalam ācarya haridāsa-varya-giri-hṛdayāyamāna-kuharāt tat-purata eva nirvrajan sa-go-samaja-vrajajana-samājaḥ sa-yaśaḥ-sneha-prasara-deha iva tasya virarāja |
children.translated_text:
When the cloud-host had departed, <s>Hari</s> then called out loudly to the cowherds:
'Come out from that [mountain], having taken your household goods — and do not be the least afraid, hasten!' —
at his grave and clear-sounding words, the clouds, which had previously been driven away
by his radiance and the mountain's glory, again — alas — from their thundering pride, went to dissolution! // [sragdharā]
[78] Then, by his repeated urgings, sounding horns and other instruments in a great reverberating clamor, the assembly of <s>Vraja</s>-people together with their cows emerged right before him from the cavern — the heart of that foremost servant of <s>Hari</s>, the mountain — and shone like a body of fame and affection flowing from him.

children.text:
gāvas tāvat purastād giri-vara-vivarāc cālyamānāḥ samantād
  ārād apy antarantar giridhara-vadanaṃ draṣṭum āsan nivṛttaḥ |
  yāsāṃ niryāpaṇāyāṃ muhur api tad alaṃ lokamānaḥ sa lokaḥ
  stabdhī-bhāvaṃ prapannaḥ, para-vaśa-daśayā tatra vaiyagryam āpa ||JGc_1,18.100||[sragdharā]
[79] atha katham api nirgiri-vara-vivaraḥ sarvaḥ parasparam anuyānaṃ parīkṣya nirnimeṣatayā śrī-kṛṣṇa-niṣkramaṇaṃ pratīkṣya kṣaṇatas tad api nirīkṣya jīva iva jīvana-nibhaṃ tam āsīdan punar atīva mudam avāpa | yataḥ-
children.translated_text:
First, the cows, being driven out from the cavern of the best mountain on all sides,
even from afar, were turning back again and again to see the face of the Mountain-Lifter;
and when they were being driven out repeatedly, that populace, watching them,
attained a state of stupefaction, and by the helpless condition, attained perplexity there! // [sragdharā]
[79] Then, when all had somehow exited the cavern of the best mountain, examining one another's sequential passage and with unblinking eyes awaiting the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> emergence — observing that too in a moment — they approached him like life itself approaching the life-breath-like one, and again attained extreme joy. For:

children.text:
svabhāvaḥ saundaryaṃ guṇa-garima-bhūmā mṛdulatā-
  khila-vyāpi-premā giri-dhṛtir api svāvana-kṛte |
  kramād ete dharmāḥ praṇayam anu sāndrīkṛti-parā
  yadīyāḥ so' bhyāgān nijadṛśi gires tasya talataḥ ||JGc_1,18.101|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
His natural beauty, the magnitude of his virtues' weight, his tenderness,
his all-pervading love devoid of barrenness, and even his lifting of the mountain — for the sake of his own [people's] protection;
gradually, these qualities of his, intent on intensification following upon affection,
belonging to him who came before their very eyes from the base of that mountain! // [śikhariṇī]

children.text:
kintu-
  yadvad utthāpitas tadvat kṛṣṇenādriḥ sa ropitaḥ |
  dṛṣṭaś ca sarva-lokena prakāras tu na lakṣitaḥ ||JGc_1,18.102|| [anuṣṭubh]

darśanād anantaraṃ tu,
  atiśayitam avega-prema-dhārā-nimagnā
  vivaśa-paśupa-lokā gotra-gartān milantam |
  harim abhi parirambhādy-ātma-yogyaṃ dadhānā
  dadhur anu nija-lābhaṃ vyutkramaṃ ca kramaṃ ca ||JGc_1,18.103|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
Immediately after seeing him:
Drowned in the streams of love exceeding all excess, without any haste,
the cowherd-folk, helpless, meeting him who was meeting the mountain-gorges,
performing embraces and the like befitting themselves toward <s>Hari</s>,
they maintained their own gain, and both transgression and order! // [mālinī]

children.text:
gopyas tatra tu mānya-bhāva-valitā dadhy-akṣatādi-sphurad
  bhavya-dravya-sabhājitaṃ viracayāmāsur jita-svarpatim |
  yadyapy evam athāpi mūrdhni ca karaṃ dhṛtvā tam āśīśiṣan
  saṃvitte tad idaṃ sa eva ya idaṃ hṛdy anvabhūt karhy api ||JGc_1,18.104|| [śārdūla]
śrī-vrajeśvarādīnāṃ milanaṃ tu śrīman-muni-varyeṇaivaṃ varṇyate sma, yatra cedaṃ suṣṭhutaram anuṣṭup-chandasā svalpa-vadyam api padyam amṛta-sambhṛta-kumbhavad akṣaya-rasaṃ prasūte-
children.translated_text: The meeting of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s> and others was described by the glorious eminent sage (<s>Śukadeva</s>) thus, where this most excellent verse in the <s>anuṣṭubh</s> meter — though small in utterance — produces inexhaustible <s>rasa</s>, like a pot filled with nectar:

children.text: yaśodā rohiṇī nando rāmaś ca balināṃ varaḥ |
kṛṣṇam āliṅgya yuyujur āśiṣaḥ sneha-kātarāḥ ||[BhP 10.25.30] iti |
children.translated_text: embracing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bestowed blessings, overwhelmed by affection!' // [BhP 10.25.30]
'<s>Yaśodā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, and <s>Rāma</s>, the best of the powerful,

children.text: tathā hi, ahaha, nava-navanīta-nīti-sukumārā kumāra-tanur iyam akharva-parvata-bhārataḥ kīdṛg abhavad bhavati bhaviṣyati ca iti sneha-maya-sandeha-rīti-bhītimantas te, tad etat kleśa-kulam asmad-vapur āveśaṃ sandeśatayā prayāsyati ity abhiprayanta iva, tam āśliṣyantas tatrāpy aviśvāsā iva, viśeṣād aśeṣāśiṣaḥ prayuñjānā, nija-vaṃśaṃ yaśasvatādi-yuktaṃ kurvāṇā iva, te tat-tan-nāmnā samāmnātāś ciraṃ bāṣpa-niṣpatti-bhitta-netra-vṛttayaḥ saṃvṛttāḥ |
children.translated_text: For indeed — 'Ah, ah! This boy's body, tender as the custom of fresh butter — how did it become, how does it become, and how will it become [capable of bearing] the weight of this immense mountain?' — thus, possessed of fear born of the ways of love-filled doubt, they, as if intending 'This mass of suffering will travel as a message into our body,' embracing him and yet even in that seemingly untrusting, especially bestowing complete blessings, as if making their own lineage endowed with glory and such — they, celebrated by their respective names, for a long time became ones whose eye-movements were shattered by the production of tears.

children.text: tatra yadyapi yaugapadyatas tūrṇam eva caturṇāṃ milanaṃ samapadyata, tathāpi prema-tāratamyam anukramya kṛṣṇāvadhāna-kramaḥ kramate sma yasmāt tasmād eva tathā śrī-śuka-devaḥ pracakrame yaśodety-ādinā |
children.translated_text: There, although the meeting of the four [parents] occurred simultaneously and swiftly, nevertheless, the sequence of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> attention followed the gradation of love's hierarchy; therefore the glorious <s>Śukadeva</s> himself proceeded thus, with '<s>Yaśodā</s>' and so forth [first].

children.text: yatra jñāna-kriyā-śaktibhyāṃ balaṃ valamānasyāpi baladevasya tādṛśī sneha-kātaratā niratā, tatra kimutāparasya | sa khalv apara eveti | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: When even <s>Baladeva</s>, who was empowered by the powers of knowledge and action, was thus immersed in such tender solicitude of love — then what of the other one? He was indeed the other [younger] one. And there:

children.text:
mātā sāśru mamārja vaktram abhitas tātaḥ śikhām aspṛśad
  dvāv apy aṅgakulaṃ nibhālya paritaḥ papracchatuḥ śantamam |
  mitrādyāḥ samavāhayann avayavān evaṃ vrajasthāḥ pare
  pretyekānvitam eva sevanam adhuḥ prāṇā hi sarvasya saḥ ||JGc_1,18.105|| [śārdūla]

atrāparāpi kautuka-paramparāvadhāryatām | [86] gate ca kaṃsa-pakṣe yakṣe yadā sa khalu vṛddhaśravā vṛddhaśravastvam evātmānaṃ pratimanyate sma, tadā sāvahittham idam utthāpitavān-bho madīya-gaṇāḥ, samavadhīyatām | sa khalu dānavārir vārita-mad-udyamatayā vipakṣavad ācarann api vairi-śamanatayā mayā sahāyatayā niścitas tat-parīkṣārtham eva ca tathā vibhīṣita ity abhinandanīya eva bhavadbhiḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Here, let a further succession of wonders be noted. [86] When the <s>Yakṣa</s> on <s>Kaṃsa's</s> side had departed, and when that one of ancient fame (<s>Indra</s>) began to regard himself as <s>Vṛddhaśravas</s> (of aged fame), he raised this [point] with attention: 'O my attendants, listen! This enemy of the <s>dānavas</s> (demons), though acting like an opponent by thwarting my effort, is determined by me as an ally for the purpose of subduing enemies — and he frightened [us] thus only to test [us]. Therefore, he is indeed to be applauded by you!'

children.text: tataś ca sa-vraja-vrajarāja-nandana-niṣkramādy-anantaram-
children.translated_text: Then, immediately after the departure of the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> along with <s>Vraja</s>:

children.text:
divi deva-gaṇāḥ sādhyāḥ siddha-gandharva-cāraṇāḥ |
  tuṣṭuvur mumucus tuṣṭāḥ puṣpa-varṣāṇi sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,18.106|| śaṅkha-dundubhayo nedur divi devādi-vāditāḥ |
  jagur gandharva-patayo yeṣāṃ tumburur āditaḥ ||JGc_1,18.107|| [BhP 10.25.31-32]
children.translated_text:
'In heaven, the hosts of gods, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>
praised him and joyfully showered flowers everywhere!' ||18.106||
'Conches and kettledrums sounded in heaven, played by gods and others;
the lords of <s>Gandharvas</s> sang, with <s>Tumburu</s> leading them!' ||18.107|| [BhP 10.25.31-32]

children.text:
tadā divi bhuvi sthitair vividha-vādya-gītādibhiḥ
  kṛta-stavatayā calan-mudita-gopa-vṛndair vṛtaḥ |
  diviṣṭha-mahilā-jayi-prakaṭa-gīta-gopī-tati-
  sphurat-parama-sampadaṃ vrajam agād vrajeśātmajaḥ ||JGc_1,18.108|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
Then, with various musical instruments and songs performed by those stationed in heaven and on earth,
and with worship offered, surrounded by the joyfully moving cowherd multitudes,
with the radiant rows of <s>gopīs</s> singing — conquering the celestial women — in prominent song,
the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> went to <s>Vraja</s>, displaying supreme prosperity! ||18.108|| [pṛthvī]

children.text:
gartaṃ praviṣṭāḥ śakaṭādi-dadhya-
  kṣatāntimārtha-pracitā yathā te |
  tathā nivāsaṃ punar āptavantaḥ
  kiñcic ca nājñāsiṣur artha-nāśam ||JGc_1,18.109|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text:
Those who had entered the mountain's cavities, amassed with their carts and yogurt,
and provisions of every last kind —
they obtained their dwellings again just as before,
and knew not even the slightest loss of possessions! ||18.109|| [upajāti]

children.text: giri-gartān niṣkramaṇe yathoktaṃ śrī-bādarāyaṇinā gopyaś ca sa-sneham apūjayan mudā dadhy-akṣatādibhiḥ [BhP 10.25.29] iti |
children.translated_text: Regarding the exit from the mountain-cavities, as stated by the glorious <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (Śukadeva): 'And the <s>gopīs</s> lovingly worshipped him with joy, with yogurt, unbroken rice, and the like' [BhP 10.25.29].

children.text:
gopa-rāja tava sūnur īdṛśaḥ
  śailam apy adhṛtaḥ yaḥ svakān avan |
  yaś ca śakram api ghātam antarāpy
  uddhūtaṃ vyadhita dūra-deśataḥ ||JGc_1,18.110|| [indravajrā]
children.translated_text:
'O king of cowherds, such is your son,
who held up even a mountain while protecting his own people!
And who cast even <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), though striking from within,
shaking [him] off to a distant land!' ||18.110|| [indravajrā]

children.text:
dhṛtvā girim asau naikadhuratām āgataḥ param |
  bhavatāṃ jagatāṃ cāgād api sarva-dhurīṇatām ||JGc_1,18.111|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Having held up the mountain, he attained not merely one burden's capacity;
but he attained the bearing of all burdens — of you and of the worlds!' ||18.111|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ kathā-prathana-pūrvakaṃ pūrvavan nija-nija-prayojanāya kṛta-vrajanāyāṃ janatāyām anukṛṣṇaṃ raveḥ samastam astaṃ yāvat kṛta-vihārau sūta-kumārau punar api rajanī-sabhāyāṃ sabhājitau nanditājitau babhūvatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, preceded by the exposition of the tale, when the people had departed for their respective purposes as before, until the sun had fully set — those two bard-youths, having sported following <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, were once again honored and delighted in the evening assembly.

children.text: tatra prathamataḥ parama-śreyasīṃ tat-preyasīṃ prati snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: There, first, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke to the most beloved one among the beloveds:

children.text:
svalpāpi līlā bhavadīyatāṃ gatā
  vistāram āyāti tathā bakīripoḥ |
  rādhe vivektuṃ nahi śakyate yathā
  prathīyasī kā bata kā tanīyasī? ||JGc_1,18.112|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
'Even a small pastime, having become yours, O enemy of <s>Bakī</s>,
expands to such an extent, O <s>Rādhā</s>,
that it cannot be distinguished — which, alas, is the greater
and which the lesser?' ||18.112|| [upajāti]

children.text: tām apy asmākaṃ grantha-lāghavāya saṅkocayatāṃ kaviṣu lāghavam eva paryavasyati | tathāpy akuṇṭha-buddhyā svayam eva sā bahudhā budhyatām | ity uktvā bhrātaram āha sma, ārya kathakācārya bhūyaḥ śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: 'To condense even that [pastime] for the brevity of our text results in lightness [i.e., inadequacy] among poets. Nevertheless, with unblunted intellect, let it be understood by you yourself in its manifold [dimensions].' Having said this, he spoke to his brother: 'O elder brother, teacher of narrators, let more be heard!'

children.text:
paraṃ girer eva satraṃ hariṇā na prakāśitam |
  kintu śrī-rādhikādīnām ānanendu-rucer api ||JGc_1,18.113|| yadā tu makha-sambhāraḥ kṛṣṇena vipulīkṛtaḥ |
  tadālaṅkāra-sambhāras tābhir apy urarīkṛtaḥ ||JGc_1,18.114|| yadā dīpālir ajvāli śikharaṃ śikharaṃ prati |
  sa cāmūś ca mithas tarhi vyadṛśyantāvṛta-sthalāt ||JGc_1,18.115|| yadā pravartitas tasmin bakahantrā girer mahaḥ |
  prāvarti ca tadā tābhis tad-didṛkṣā-mahā-mahaḥ ||JGc_1,18.116|| yadā samuditā jātā mahilā bhūmi-bhṛn makhe |
  tadā tā muditā jātā hari-darśana-niściteḥ ||JGc_1,18.117|| kṛṣṇe saṃlāpam ācerur yadā vividha-subhruvaḥ |
  tadārha-bodha-sadṛśaṃ dṛśaṃ tāś ca nyayūyujan ||JGc_1,18.118|| yadādrir janatā-dṛṣṭiṃ kṛṣṭavān prakaṭī-bhavan |
  āśādhāma yayuḥ svairaṃ tadāsām akṣi-pakṣiṇaḥ ||JGc_1,18.119|| yadā go-pūjanaṃ kartum ārabdhaṃ sarvakais tadā |
  tābhiḥ pratisva-dhenv-arcā-praśnāspadam akāri saḥ ||JGc_1,18.120|| yadā gopāla-pūjāyā maho vyaktam abhūd bahiḥ |
  tadā mano-mahas tāsāṃ vaktre vaktre vyalokyata ||JGc_1,18.121|| gopa-pṛṣṭhaṃ yadā dṛṣṭaṃ kanyāpāṇyaṅkitaṃ puru |
  tadāsāṃ pāṇayaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ spraṣṭum utkaṇṭhitāṃ gatāḥ ||JGc_1,18.122|| homa-kāle yadā kṛṣṇaḥ prāviśad brahma-saṃsadi |
  hutaṃ bata tadā tābhir mānasaṃ virahānale ||JGc_1,18.123|| gireḥ parikrame yarhi vyavadhānaṃ yayau hariḥ |
  tadā tāṃ vyavadhām eva girīyanti sma tat-priyāḥ ||JGc_1,18.124|| yaṣṭiṃ yarhy utkṣipan gṛhṇan kṛṣṇaś cakrāma tarhi tām |
  dṛṣṭvā dūrād añjanāsrair bhānujā bhānujāyate ||JGc_1,18.125|| yadā yadā mitho rūpaṃ draṣṭum āsīd asambhavaḥ |
  gavānudrava-lakṣyeṇa sa tāsāṃ madhyam adravat ||JGc_1,18.126|| dhenv-anudravaṇa-vyājāt spṛśan vavrāja yāṃ hariḥ |
  cillī-vallī-tāḍyamānas tayā sa stambham īyivān ||JGc_1,18.127|| yadā rādhām anu spṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭir asya gatā tadā |
  ayaṃ sarvaṃ visasmāra kintu sasmāra tan-mukham ||JGc_1,18.128|| yadā rātrāv abhūd vāsaḥ sarveṣām eka-dhāmani |
  tac-chabda-mātra-tāt-paryāḥ śrutitāṃ tarhi tāḥ yayuḥ ||JGc_1,18.129|| kṛṣṇāyās tu yadā kṛṣṇaś cikrīḍa srotasi svayam |
  tadāmodiny amūs tasminn akrīḍann atidūrataḥ ||JGc_1,18.130|| bhaginīnāṃ gṛhe yarhi bhoktum abhyāyayau hariḥ |
  sakhya-lakṣyāt tadā tāsāṃ sarvās tatrāpy amūr gatāḥ ||JGc_1,18.131|| yathā-pūrvaṃ yadā sarve pratisvaṃ vāsam avrajan |
  tadā kārā-gṛhe hanta menire tāḥ punar gatim ||JGc_1,18.132|| yadā saṃvarta-meghās te prāvartanta tadā tu tāḥ |
  akāmayanta kṛṣṇāya sva-svaccha-trāyamāṇatām ||JGc_1,18.133|| yadā suhṛdbhiś chatrādyair lālitaṃ tam alokayan |
  svāṅga-bhetrīm amūr vṛṣṭiṃ tadā saudhīm amaṃsata ||JGc_1,18.134|| vichinna-prakharāsāra-cchatre tatreha dīvyati |
  kṛṣṇe svairaṃ gatā dṛṣṭiṃ menire vṛṣṭim āmṛtīm ||JGc_1,18.135|| abhi kṛṣṇaṃ yadā sarvaḥ śaila-garte' nvavartata |
  gṛha-prāpta-nidhīnāṃ vā tadā tāsāṃ sthitir matā ||JGc_1,18.136|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'The great sacrifice of the mountain alone was not revealed by <s>Hari</s>;
but also that of the glorious <s>Rādhikā</s> and others — of moon-like luster!' ||18.113||
'When the sacrificial materials were amply provided by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
then the ornamental materials were undertaken by them [the <s>gopīs</s>] too!' ||18.114||
'When the row of lamps blazed from peak to peak,
then he and they saw each other from their respective concealed positions!' ||18.115||
'When the great festival of the mountain was set in motion by the slayer of <s>Baka</s>,
then too was set in motion by them the great festival of the desire to see him!' ||18.116||
'When the women became exultant at the mountain-sacrifice,
then those [<s>gopīs</s>] became delighted, certain of seeing <s>Hari</s>!' ||18.117||
'When various fair-browed ones engaged in conversation with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
then those [<s>gopīs</s>] too cast glances befitting their awakened understanding!' ||18.118||
'When the mountain, manifesting itself, drew the gaze of the multitude,
then the eye-birds of those [<s>gopīs</s>] went freely to the abode of their hopes!' ||18.119||
'When the worship of the cows was commenced by all,
then he was made by them [the <s>gopīs</s>] the subject of questions regarding the worship of their own respective cows!' ||18.120||
'When the great festival of <s>Gopāla</s>-worship became outwardly manifest,
then the mental festival of those [<s>gopīs</s>] was seen upon each face!' ||18.121||
'When the backs of the cowherds were seen abundantly marked by the hands of the maidens,
then the hands of those [<s>gopīs</s>] went to a state of longing to touch <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' ||18.122||
'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, at the time of the fire-offering, entered the assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
then alas, those [<s>gopīs</s>] offered their mental [oblation] into the fire of separation!' ||18.123||
'When <s>Hari</s> went behind the mountain during the circumambulation,
then those beloveds of his called that very obstruction a "mountain"!' ||18.124||
'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> walked about, lifting and taking up his staff,
seeing him from afar — the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) shone with collyrium-tears!' ||18.125||
'Whenever it was impossible for them to see each other's form,
under the pretext of running after the cows, he ran into their midst!' ||18.126||
'Under the pretext of running after a cow, <s>Hari</s>, touching her [<s>Rādhā</s>], walked on;
being struck by her sidelong glance-creeper, he became motionless!' ||18.127||
'When his gaze went toward touching <s>Rādhā</s>,
then he forgot everything else, but remembered only her face!' ||18.128||
'When at night there was lodging of all in one dwelling,
then those [<s>gopīs</s>], intent only upon his sound, attained the state of [all]-hearing!' ||18.129||
'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself played in the current of the <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),
then those joyful ones played not in that [stream] but at a great distance!' ||18.130||
'When <s>Hari</s> came to eat at the houses of his sisters,
then all of those [<s>gopīs</s>] too went there, under the pretext of friendship!' ||18.131||
'When, as before, all went to their own lodgings,
then those [<s>gopīs</s>] considered that return to be a return to prison!' ||18.132||
'When the dissolution-clouds poured forth,
then those [<s>gopīs</s>] desired their own transparent [presence] to serve as <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> protector!' ||18.133||
'When they saw him fondled by friends with umbrellas and such,
then those [<s>gopīs</s>] considered the rain that pierced their limbs to be celestial!' ||18.134||
'When the umbrella's shelter from the fierce, cutting downpour was removed, and
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> played there freely — those who freely directed their gaze [at him]
considered the rain to be nectarean!' ||18.135||
'When everyone assembled in the mountain-cavity around <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
then the state of those [<s>gopīs</s>] was considered to be like having found a treasure at home!' ||18.136|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
nimeṣa-rahitās tadā pratinimeṣam āsedire
  harer mukha-sudhā-rasaṃ rasanayā dṛg-ākārayā |
  aho rajani-saptakaṃ vraja-cakora-netrāḥ kiyat
  kutaḥ sukṛtam udgataṃ na iti vismṛtīr avrajan ||JGc_1,18.137|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
Without blinking, at every moment, they attained
the nectar-taste of <s>Hari's</s> face, with their tongues in the form of their eyes;
ah! For seven nights, how much merit must have arisen
for these <s>Vraja</s> <s>cakora</s>-eyed ones — they went into forgetfulness [wondering]! ||18.137|| [pṛthvī]

children.text:
rādhā tatra sukhātisīma-dṛśayā yuktāpi muktāvalī
  svacche netra-jale tad-īkṣaṇa-bhave koṣṇatvam itthaṃ gatā |
  hā dhig daiva sadaiva nāsti tava ko' py uccair viveko yataḥ
  kāntasyāniśa-darśitasya ca cirād adriḥ kare dṛśyate ||JGc_1,18.138|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
<s>Rādhā</s> there, though joined with a gaze at the extreme limit of happiness, [like] a free pearl-string,
in the clear water of her eyes — born from seeing him — thus attained a tepid [teary] state;
'Alas, fie on fate! There is never any high discernment in you! For
though the beloved is continuously visible, a mountain is seen in the hand for a long time!' ||18.138|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
yadā giri-varaṃ dadhe muraharas tadā locanaṃ
  nijārthita-vinākṛtām api diśaṃ sa ninye muhuḥ |
  kadācid iha cet prathāṃ bhajati rādhikāyā mukhaṃ
  tadā phala-mayaṃ mama śramatamaḥ prasajjed iti ||JGc_1,18.139|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
When the slayer of <s>Mura</s> held up the best of mountains, then his eye
repeatedly directed itself even toward the direction deprived of his desire;
'If perchance the face of <s>Rādhikā</s> should become famous here,
then my utmost darkness of toil would bear fruit!' — thus [he thought]. ||18.139|| [pṛthvī]

children.text:
ayaṃ girivaraṃ dadhe karuṇayeti kāruṇyavān
  samastam abhitarkyate tad iha citta-dhairyaṃ bhaja |
  nirantarita-locana-prabhava-vṛṣṭi-bhītībhavad-
  vapuś ca tava rakṣitety akṛta bhāvam eṣā tadā ||JGc_1,18.140|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
'This one holds up the best of mountains out of compassion' — thus the compassionate
[friend] surmised everything — 'therefore, let your mind adopt firmness here!
And your body, which was becoming fearful from the unceasing rain of eye-born showers,
has been protected!' — such was the sentiment she (<s>Lalitā</s>) then conveyed. ||18.140|| [pṛthvī]

children.text:
girer gartān niṣkrāma-vacanam ākarṇya dayitā
  murāres taṃ prāṇa-pratimam apahāyāpi nirayuḥ |
  sa evaṃ taṃ bhāvaṃ bata visṛjatītthaṃ sa tu paraṃ
  tad āsāṃ viśliṣṭer bharam asahamāno niragamat ||JGc_1,18.141|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Hearing the word to exit from the mountain-cavities, the beloved ones
of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, abandoning that life-like [one], departed;
but he — thus releasing that sentiment, alas — then
unable to bear the burden of their separation, himself came out! ||18.141|| [śikhariṇī]

children.text:
kiṃ girer vivarato bahir gataḥ
  kiṃ sa vā sva-hṛdayād iti sphuṭam |
  nātiboddhum aśakan hari-priyās
  tarhi yarhi niragād asau priyaḥ ||JGc_1,18.142|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
'Did he come out from the mountain's interior,
or from his own heart?' — this clearly
the beloveds of <s>Hari</s> were unable to fully comprehend,
at that time when that beloved one came out! ||18.142|| [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
yad dṛgambu vavṛṣuḥ stana-bhūbhṛd
  bhūri-bhūmi-valayeṣu mṛgākṣyaḥ |
  uddhṛta-prathita-bhūbhṛti tasmiṃs
  tat kim apy akathayan nija-hārdam ||JGc_1,18.143|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
The tears that the doe-eyed ones rained
upon the extensive grounds of the breast-mountains —
when that renowned mountain was lifted up by him,
those [tears] somehow expressed their innermost heart! ||18.143|| [svāgatā]

children.text: atha samāpanam āha-
children.translated_text: Then he spoke the conclusion:

children.text:
rādhe parito yāsīd govardhana-dhāriṇas tadā karuṇā |
  sāsrān nayana-prāntāt prāntāt tvayy eva sā suviśrāntā ||JGc_1,18.144|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, the compassion of the holder of <s>Govardhana</s>
was on all sides;
but from the tear-filled corner of each eye,
that [compassion] came to rest solely in you!' ||18.144|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad etad api kathana-śeṣaṃ samāpya pūrvavad eva sūta-sutayor gatayoḥ sarve' pi yathāsvaṃ prasthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, having completed even this remainder of the narration, just as before, when the bard-sons had departed, all set out for their own [dwellings].

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
gotrabhid-garva-khaṇḍana-
govardhana-gotra-māna-vardhanam
nāmāṣṭādaśaṃ pūraṇam
||18 ||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Eighteenth Chapter, named
'The Shattering of <s>Gotra-bhid's</s> (<s>Indra's</s>) Pride —
the Augmentation of the Honor of <s>Govardhana's</s> Lineage.'
||18||

children.text: athaikonaviṃśapūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Nineteenth Chapter.

children.text:
jambha-bhedi-surendratā-stambhana-
nagendra-dhara-gavendratālambhanam
children.translated_text:
The Blocking of the Supreme <s>Indra</s>-ship of the Smasher of <s>Jambha</s> —
the Attainment of the Mountain-bearer, the Lord of Elephants (<s>Airāvata</s>).

children.text: atha prabhāte sabhā-tejasā vibhātayoḥ sūta-jātayor madhukaṇṭha-nāmā kathayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then, at dawn, when the assembly was illuminated by the splendor of the assembly-hall, the one of the bard-pair named <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> narrated:

children.text: tad evaṃ tādṛk-sampadi pratipadi govardhana-samardhanaṃ siddham | tṛtīyām ārabhya navamy-avadhikaṃ ramyaṃ tad-dhāraṇam addhāvadhāryatām |
children.translated_text: "Thus, in such prosperity, at every step, the enrichment of <s>Govardhana</s> was accomplished. From the third [day] up to the limit of the ninth, let that delightful holding [of the mountain] be truly understood!"

children.text: atha tādṛśa-daśā-ramyāyāṃ daśamyāṃ śrī-vraja-rāja-samājam anu nimantraṇayā prāmāṇi-kamāṇikya-vraja-janāḥ sukha-yojanaṃ bhojanaṃ saṃyujya mukha-vāsanaṃ mukha-vāsam upajyujya vārtāṃ vartayāmāsuḥ | [4] yatra kṣitidhara-dhāraṇa-nidhyānān nirdhārayantaḥ pūtanāvadhādikam etad avadhikam asambhāvitaṃ sambhāvitaṃ cāviśeṣatayā tat-karma-viśeṣatayā gaṇayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: "Then, on the tenth day — beautiful in the condition of such a state — following the invitation to the assembly of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, the authoritative jewel-like <s>Vraja</s> folk, having partaken of a delicious feast, and having enjoyed mouth-freshening and mouth-fragrance, conversed. [4] Where, meditating upon the sustaining of the earth-bearer [mountain], they equally reckoned the unprecedented and the expected — from the slaying of <s>Pūtanā</s> onward up to this point — with regard to the extraordinary nature of those feats."

children.text: punaś caivam āhuḥ-
children.translated_text: "And they further said:"

children.text:
vāvahiḥ parvataṃ bālaḥ sāsahir na tu cācaliḥ |
  bahir eva yathā vṛṣṭiḥ pāpatir na tad-antare ||JGc_1,19.1|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
"The child bore the mountain — he did not waver, and it did not shake;
the rain was only outside — it did not fall within!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.1, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
tad evaṃ parama-prabhāvatā tāvad vismaya-jananī jananītim atikrāmati | tasyām api satyāmatyāsakti-maya-sneha-caya-svabhāvatā mādṛśām anyādṛśām api tasmin niścitā vismitim ātanoti | [7] tasya ca mādṛkṣu visadṛkṣu ca yāsau lakṣyate, sā tu parama-vilakṣaṇatayātīva vailakṣyaṃ lakṣayati | kiṃ ca-
  pratyekaṃ sve tanūje pravalayati janaḥ svairam evānurāgaṃ
  sarveṣāṃ nas tadīye sa katham atha kathaṃ śakyate nāpi moktuṃ |
  sarveṣv apy asya so' yaṃ sphurati sahabhavas tādṛg eva vrajeśa
  smāraṃ smāraṃ tad etat na katham api manāg uktiyuktī vrajāmaḥ ||JGc_1,19.2|| [sragdharā]
[8] tad evaṃ pravaṇatayā śravaṇataḥ śrīmān nandaḥ prajātānandaḥ praṇaya-mayatayā sammata-samayatayā ca garga-siddhānta-vargam evānugadya niravadya-sauhṛdyatas teṣām amandehodbhava-sandehodyamaṃ saṃyamanam anaiṣīt, śrūyatāṃ me vaco gopo vyetu śaṅkā ca vo' rbhake [BhP 10.26.15] ity ādinā | ante coktavān-
children.translated_text:
"Thus, his supreme power, insofar as it surpasses the capacity of his mother, is a source of wonder. And even in that being true, the nature of the heap of affection — full of attachment devoid of obstruction — that ones such as us and others of different kinds [feel] toward him, causes amazement. [7] And that which is perceived in him toward ones like us and unlike us — that, by its supremely extraordinary nature, produces exceedingly great embarrassment. Moreover:"
Each person freely intensifies attachment toward one's own child;
for all of us toward his — how is that? And how is it that it cannot even be released?
In all [toward him], this same co-natal [feeling] shines forth identically, O lord of <s>Vraja</s> —
remembering and remembering this, we cannot at all arrive at even a slight verbal propriety! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.2, <s>sragdharā</s>]
[8] "Thus, when the glorious <s>Nanda</s>, delighted by such devoted hearing, out of the nature of love and the consensus of the occasion, merely echoed the doctrinal conclusions of <s>Garga</s>, and through faultless friendship brought about the restraint of their effort arising from doubt born of embodiment — with 'Hear my words, O cowherds! Let your apprehension about the child depart!' [BhP 10.26.15] and so forth — at the end, he said:"

children.text:
yad-avadhi mām upadiśya
prāsthita gargas tad-avadhi jānāmi |
  śiśur ayam adbhuta-caryāṃ
valayati nārāyaṇī yayā śaktyā ||JGc_1,19.3|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
"From the time <s>Garga</s>, having instructed me, departed,
from that time I know:
this child performs wondrous deeds —
the power by which he does so is that of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.3, <s>gīti</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ śrīman-nanda-rāja-vākyatas tad-avakalanānanda-bhājas taṃ yadā samasta-janāḥ samasta-janānandana-tan-nandana-vārtayā nandayantaḥ santi sma, tadā nija-vṛndair vṛndārakaiś ca vandyamānatayā nandyamānatayā nandyamānatayā ca vṛndāvana-candraḥ sahasā saha-rāmaḥ samājagāma |
children.translated_text: "Thus, when all the people — enjoying the bliss of comprehending through the words of the glorious king <s>Nanda</s>, delighting one another with tidings of his son, <s>Nandana</s>, the delight of all people — were in that state, the moon of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, together with <s>Rāma</s>, suddenly arrived, being praised and celebrated and honored by his own hosts and by the celestials."

children.text: samājaś cāyaṃ samam eva taṃ pariveṣa iva paritaś chādayāmāsa, cakora-vāra iva tat-kāntim āsvādayāmāsa, vārāṃ nidhir iva cātmānam ullolatayā sampādayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: "And this assembly simultaneously enshrouded him like a halo, tasted his radiance like a flock of <s>cakora</s> birds, and made itself agitated like a reservoir of waters!"

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite sarvasminn api svasthatayā cāvasthite kṣaṇa-katipaye ca prasthite sarva eva te sāmājikāḥ pratisvam amanendirād ātma-mandirād ānīta-prīta-sitāsita-praśasta-vastra-saṅkaraṃ sad-alaṅkaraṇādikaṃ taṃ ca tad-bhrātaraṃ tat-pitaraṃ ca pṛthak pṛthag alaṅkāraṃ svīkārayāñcakruḥ |
children.translated_text: "Thus, when everything was well-established and composed, and a few moments had passed, all those assembly-members, from their own lustrous residences, brought with love excellent white and dark fine garments and beautiful ornaments, and had him and his brother and his father separately accept the adornments."

children.text: yathaivaṃ bahir ebhir ācaritaṃ, tathāntaḥ-pure sa-rāma-mātṛkāṃ giridharasya mātaram abhi caiṣāṃ mahilābhir viracitam iti nirviśeṣam eva tad ubhayatra parvāsīt |
children.translated_text: "Just as this was done outwardly by these [men], so too within the inner apartments, the women performed the same toward the mother of the mountain-bearer, accompanied by <s>Rāma's</s> mother — it was a festival identically in both places."

children.text: atha sura-pure sureśasya vṛttam anuvṛtyatām | [14] ito gatvā dainyaṃ matvā skhalad-ojā viḍaujāḥ kṣayaṃ gacchann apy asau kṣayam ṛcchann iva sthitavān na tu śacīm acīkamata, na ca nirjara-sadasi nirjagāma |
children.translated_text: "Now let the events of <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the celestials, in the celestial city be traced. [14] Having gone from here, having realized his abasement, his vigor faltering, <s>Indra</s>, though reaching the point of decline, remained as if dwelling in decline; but he did not face <s>Śacī</s>, nor did he come forth into the assembly of the immortals."

children.text: tad evaṃ varṇyamānam avakarṇya vācaspatir vāstoṣpatim anurahasaṃ bhartsayāmāsa, yataḥ sa khalu vibudhānām api vibudhaḥ | [16] bhartsanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: "Having heard this being described, <s>Vācaspati</s> (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) rebuked <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (<s>Indra</s>, lord of the abode) privately, since he was indeed the wise one among the wise. [16] The rebuke, as follows:"

children.text:
yasmād abhajasi viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇo tasmād anedhitāse tvam |
  na vinā candraṃ vindati jīvana-vṛttiṃ vanaspatiḥ ko' pi ||JGc_1,19.4|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
"Because you did not worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O <s>Jiṣṇu</s> (<s>Indra</s>), therefore you have not prospered;
without the moon, no tree whatsoever finds the means of life!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.4, <s>gīti</s>]

children.text: athavā sahasradṛśam apy aho bhavādṛśam abhibhūya bhṛśī-bhavantī tādṛśī madāndhatā nāsadṛśī, yataḥ sureśo' si | kintv amṛtapatā tava kathaṃ mrtapatā jātā? yatas tyakta-prāṇa-prāyaṇa-kāya-prāyataḥ pramādaḥ so' yam āpatitaḥ |
children.translated_text: "Or rather, such blindness of pride — overpowering even the thousand-eyed one like yourself — is not unbecoming, since you are the lord of the gods! But how has the lord of nectar come to have the state of a lord of the dead? For this calamity has befallen from a body that is practically in the state of one who has abandoned life-breath!"

children.text:
tathā ca smarati-
  apasnāta iva snāto' py alam aspṛśya eva saḥ |
  mṛtakaṃ vapur āsajjan yaḥ sadbhyo bhaya-dāyakaḥ ||JGc_1,19.5|| [anuṣṭubh]
kiṃ ca-vṛṣāhvaya, tava cedam atyavicārata eva | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: "Moreover — O <s>Vṛṣāhvaya</s> (one called "Bull", i.e., <s>Indra</s>), this action of yours is sheer thoughtlessness. As follows:"

children.text:
yad-ālambāj janaḥ prāṇaṃ yasmād rakṣitum icchati |
  vaiparītyaṃ tayoḥ kurvann anunmatto na kathyate ||JGc_1,19.6|| [anuṣṭubh]
[20] indra uvāca-avicāritam evācaritam idaṃ mayā, bhavadbhiś ca sāmprataṃ sāmpratam upadiśyatām |
children.translated_text:
"That from whose support people wish to protect their life-breath,
and that for whose sake — one who reverses the relation of those two,
is not called anything but a madman!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.6, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
[20] <s>Indra</s> said: "This was done by me without deliberation; and now let it be instructed by your honors what is presently appropriate."

children.text: vācaspatir uvāca-śatamanyo, tādṛśa-visadṛśatāyāṃ śatadhṛtir eva dhṛtim āsādayitā, tasmāt tad-anusaraṇam eva śaraṇam |
children.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) said: "O <s>Śatamanyu</s> (hundred-wrathed one)! In such a state of incongruity, <s>Śatadhṛti</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>, of hundred resolves) alone will grant composure; therefore, recourse to him alone is the refuge."

children.text: tad evaṃ jambhabhedī sakhedī-bhavann avadhāya dhātāram eva gatvā saṅkocam amatvā svāparādham avadhārayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: "Thus, the slayer of <s>Jambha</s> (<s>Indra</s>), becoming afflicted, having resolved [upon this course] and having gone to <s>Dhātā</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) without contracting [from shame], confessed his own offense."

children.text: sa tūvāca-hanta, vibudhādhipenāpy abudhena bhavatā bhavatā duḥsādha-rādhaḥ so' yaṃ mahān evāparādhaḥ kṛtaḥ, yaṃ khalu sādhavaḥ sakṛd apy avadhārayantas tvām avadhīrayantaḥ sāvadhānāḥ śrotram apidadhate | tathāpi sṛṣṭi-vidhitsā-durvidhinā vidhinā mayā tad idam upadiśyate | pūrvaṃ tan-mahima-jijñāsayā dhārṣṭyam anuṣṭhitam astīti tan-mātra-kilbiṣa-viṣama-viṣama-viṣaha-mānena mayā durmāṇa-mayāgādha-bhavad-aparādha-kṣamāpaṇāya kṣamatā na labhyate |
children.translated_text: "He (<s>Brahmā</s>) said: "Alas! Even by you, the lord of the wise, who are [supposed to be] wise, a great offense has been committed — an offense that is difficult to remedy! Which indeed the righteous, even merely hearing of it, would disregard you and attentively close their ears. Nevertheless, by me — the creator, whose creative intention is an unfortunate fate — this is instructed: Formerly, the boldness committed out of curiosity about his greatness — by that alone, through the measure of that singular guilt, with endurance that is hard and yet hard — I do not find the capacity for the absolution of your fathomless offense.""

children.text: kintu-
children.translated_text: "But:"

children.text: gavāṃ kaṇḍūyanaṃ kuryād go-grāsaṃ go-pradakṣiṇām |
children.translated_text: "One should scratch the cows, give them fodder, and circumambulate them;"

children.text: nityaṃ goṣu prasannāsu gopālo' pi prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: "When the cows are pleased, even <s>Gopāla</s> (the cow-protector) is pleased!"

children.text: iti gautamādi-sammatyā gojātiṣu prīti-rīti-parītasya tasya kṣamāpaṇāya kātaras tvaṃ taj-jāti-mātaraṃ surabhīm eva bhajasva, na ced asurataḥ surabhī-saṅgatir bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: "By the consensus of <s>Gautama</s> and others, in order to seek forgiveness from him who is devoted to the cows with the manners of affection for the cow-species, you, trembling, should worship <s>Surabhī</s> (the divine cow) herself, who is the mother of that species — otherwise your association with <s>Surabhī</s> will come from the <s>Asura</s>-side (i.e., will be hostile)."

children.text: atha sunāsīras tv asurabhītaḥ surabhī-lokam āsādya sadyas tad avadya-carita-pracārād vimanasam api tāṃ mātuḥ svasāraṃ muhuḥ prasādya vedhasaḥ savidham evānināya |
children.translated_text: "Then <s>Sunāsīra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), without fear, having reached the realm of <s>Surabhī</s>, and having repeatedly propitiated her — who was displeased by the proclamation of his disgraceful conduct — even though she was the sister of his mother, he brought her to the vicinity of the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>)."

children.text: tataś ca vidhātedam abhidadhe-ayi, surabhi, surapati-bhī-sāntvanārtham asurāntakasyāntikaṃ gaccha | gatvā ca tvam asya nūnam evam eva labdha-duścyavana-nāmnaḥ parikilbiṣa-kīrtana-bhiyā kila kavi-pariṣad-upekṣaṇīya-tan-nāma-dheyasya kṛṣṇataś cyavanaṃ vicyāvaya | tac ca sva-sampad-upakaṇṭha-kuṇṭhī-kṛtāpara-vaikuṇṭha-loka-goloka-mahendratā-martya-loke' py asya vyaktībhavatād iti tad-abhiṣeka-sevātirekataḥ sambhāvitā iti |
children.translated_text: "Then <s>Brahmā</s> declared this: "O <s>Surabhī</s>, for the purpose of consoling the fear of the lord of the gods, go to the presence of the destroyer of the <s>Asuras</s>. And having gone, cause the fall from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of this one who has surely thus earned the name <s>Duścyavana</s> (hard to fall from) — through the fear of proclaiming his guilt, which makes his very name worthy of being ignored by the assembly of poets. And may this [consecration] manifest — even in the mortal world — his sovereignty, which, by the proximity of its own wealth, has humbled even the other <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>-world and <s>Goloka</s> — through the excess of the service of his consecration!""

children.text:
atha hari-vāsara-divase surabhiḥ sura-rājam anu vṛndāvana-bhūpari-bhuvar-loka-bhāgam āgamya tad-avasaraṃ pratīkṣāmāsa | tatra ca dūrataḥ sura-patiṃ surabhir abhihitavatī-
nāsau meghaḥ paśya govardhanādrir
  nāyaṃ navyas tasya bhāgaḥ sa kṛṣṇaḥ |
  neyaṃ vidyul-lola-pītāṃśuka-śrīr
  naitan mandaṃ garjitaṃ narmavārtā ||JGc_1,19.7|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
"Then, on the day sacred to <s>Hari</s> (Thursday), <s>Surabhī</s>, following the king of the gods, arrived at the region above <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — the domain of the aerial world — and waited for the [right] occasion. And there, from afar, <s>Surabhī</s> said to the lord of the gods:"
"That is not a cloud — look! — that is the mountain <s>Govardhana</s>!
This is not a new portion of it — he is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!
This is not lightning — it is the splendor of the flickering yellow garment!
This is not soft thunder — it is intimate speech!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.7, <s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: paśya paśya, samyag utpatiṣṇuḥ pataga-jiṣṇur viṣṇu-vāhanaḥ so' yam asmad apy upari-bhāgam ārūḍhaḥ san vidyud-gūḍha-vārida-vāra iva yasya cchāyām icchan kila yatra cchāyāṃ prasārayati | [29] so' yaṃ tu-
children.translated_text: "Look, look! The one eager to fly upward, the conqueror of <s>Pataga</s> (the sun), the vehicle of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that <s>Garuḍa</s> — has ascended even above our level, and as if concealed behind the lightning-hidden clouds, spreads his shadow wherever he wishes to shade. [29] And this one:"

children.text:
śrī-govardhana-śaila-ratna-dṛśadi prakṣipta-śubhrāstare
  vāmoru-sthita-kañja-cāru-caraṇe savyaṃ karaṃ dakṣiṇe |
  nyasyann anyam apūrva-rūpa-muralī-nāle manāg atra naḥ
  smereṇākṣi-taṭena sandadhad aho manye kṛpāṃ varṣati ||JGc_1,19.8|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
"Upon the jewel-slab of the glorious <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, on a spread of white cloth,
with his lovely lotus-foot placed on his left thigh, his left hand on the right [knee],
placing the other [hand] upon the stem of the incomparably beautiful flute — slightly here,
with a smiling corner of his eye, bestowing — ah, I think he rains compassion upon us!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.8, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
atra cāyam asman-milanam aṅgīkurvann eva saṅginaḥ prasaṅgāntarāya prasthāpitavān | baladevaś ca nādya vanam āgatavān iti cāsthīyate | tasmād atisvacchatara-cetasam amuṃ bhavāṃs tāvan nibhṛtatayā nibhṛtam avyagratayā cābhyagraṃ gatvā daṇḍavan natvā prasādayitum arhati | yataḥ,
  svayam aparādhyati kurute prabhum abhi tan-mārjane sahāyaṃ yaḥ |
  tasyedaṃ para-śakter darśanam atha naiva dainyasya ||JGc_1,19.9|| [āryā]
  yasmin svayam aparādhī namati rahas taṃ sahāya-nirviṇṇaḥ |
  kṛpayati sā jana-mātraṃ dainyāvasthā mahājanaṃ kim uta? ||JGc_1,19.10|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
"And here, this one, while indeed accepting our meeting, has dispatched his companions to other business. And it is established that <s>Baladeva</s> has not come to the forest today. Therefore, you should approach this one — whose heart is exceedingly pure — first, privately, quietly, without agitation, going forward, prostrating like a staff, and propitiating him. For:"
"He who offends and then makes the lord his helper in wiping it clean —
this is a display of another's power, and not at all of humility!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.9, <s>āryā</s>]
"When one who has personally offended, deprived of helpers,
bows down in secret — the pitiable condition of mere common folk is compassioned;
how much more that of a great personage?" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.10, <s>gīti</s>]

children.text: tataś ca paścād eva viśeṣa-nivedanāyām aham āyāsyāmi |
children.translated_text: "And then, afterwards, I shall come for the special presentation."

children.text: atha pāka-śāsanas tad-anuśāsanam urarīkṛtya pracchannatayā muralī-dhara-samīpam āgatya pratyagraṃ caraṇa-khara-daṇḍayor daṇḍavat papāta |
children.translated_text: "Then <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>), having accepted that instruction, came secretly to the vicinity of the flute-bearer and prostrated like a freshly [fallen] staff at his feet and toenails."

children.text:
indro nanāma ca yathāṅghri-nakhā murārer
  agryām amuṣya mukuṭe maṇitām avāpuḥ |
  cakranda cātha sa yathāmbaka-kairavāmbu-
  mādhvīka-vidrava-vidhau vidhutām agacchan ||JGc_1,19.11|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
<s>Indra</s> bowed, and the foremost toenails of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)
attained the status of jewels in his crown;
and then he wept, such that his eye-<s>kairava</s> (night-lotus) waters —
in the process of intoxicating dissolution — became agitated! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.11, <s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: atha krandati saṅkrandane paṅkaja-locanaḥ saṅkocitaḥ kirīṭāgram agra-hastena sāgraham udastam ācarann uvāca-[34] bhagavann, evam ayuktaṃ mā kārṣīr, ārṣīṇāṃ vāṇīnāṃ tvam eka evātirekataḥ parāyaṇam asi |
children.translated_text: "Then, as the vanquisher [of demons] wept, the lotus-eyed one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), embarrassed, placed his foremost fingertip eagerly and upward upon the tip of his crown, and said: [34] "Blessed one, do not do anything so improper! You alone are supremely the ultimate refuge of the <s>ṛṣis\</s>' utterances!""

children.text: vajrapāṇis tu mūrdhni prasajjitāñjali-pāṇitayā salajjaṃ svayaṃ svavajra-hata iva maunam evāsasajja | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: "But the thunderbolt-wielder, with palms joined upon his crown, bashfully maintained silence as if struck by his own thunderbolt. For:"

children.text:
parasya kāyaṃ badhnāti tejasā vacasā manaḥ |
  śaktaḥ śaktaś ca so' yaṃ yas tasya bhaktaḥ kathaṃ na kaḥ? ||JGc_1,19.12|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
"He who binds another's body with his splendor, speech with his words, and mind [with his mind],
is powerful, supremely powerful — who would not be his devotee?" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.19.12, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ tasya tejasā kṛpayā ca suparvādhipasya vividhā gatir jātā, yathā-
children.translated_text: "Thus, by his splendor and compassion, the lord of the celestials attained various states, as follows:"

children.text:
anyatra candrati hariḥ śakre tarhi sma sūryati |
  śakro' pi sūryaty anyasmin khadyotati harau sma saḥ ||JGc_1,19.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
  yadā maunaṃ sasajjāsau tadā mūka ivābhavat |
  yadā tu stotum ārabdhas tadāgād vāvadūkatām ||JGc_1,19.14|| [anuṣṭubh]
  yathāmūṃ stutavān indras tathā vaktuṃ na śakyate |
  śrī-vrajendra yataḥ so' yaṃ tvattaḥ saṅkucati sphuṭam ||JGc_1,19.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Elsewhere <s>Hari</s> shines like the moon, but compared to <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), he is like the sun; <s>Śakra</s> too is like the sun elsewhere, but in the presence of <s>Hari</s>, he was like a firefly! // [anuṣṭubh]
When he (<s>Indra</s>) prepared himself for silence, he became as if mute; but when he began to praise, he attained extreme verbosity! // [anuṣṭubh]
The manner in which <s>Indra</s> praised him cannot be expressed — O glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, for he clearly shrank before you! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: avamānam anālocya kavamānaḥ sa punar evam añjasā tad upasañjahāra-
children.translated_text: Not regarding the humiliation and yet swallowing it, he straightforwardly concluded with this:

children.text: mayedaṃ bhagavan goṣṭha-nāśāyāsāra-vāyubhiḥ |
ceṣṭitaṃ vihate yajñe māninā tīvra-manyunā ||[BhP 10.27.12] iti |
children.translated_text: when the sacrifice was disrupted — by a proud one, with fierce anger.' // [BhP 10.27.12] — thus.
'O Lord, this was done by me for the destruction of the cow-settlement, with torrential rains and winds,

children.text: ayaṃ ca prahasya provāca-
children.translated_text: And he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), laughing, said:

children.text: mayā te' kāri maghavan makha-bhaṅgo' nugṛhṇatā | [BhP 10.27.28]
children.translated_text: 'The disruption of your sacrifice was done by me, O <s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>), out of grace toward you!' // [BhP 10.27.28]

children.text:
yan mat-pitrādi-sac-chreṣṭhān nātikrāmer mama smaran ||JGc_1,19.16|| [anuṣṭubh]
  suraś ced viṣayābhoga-garvād roceta vāsava |
  tadā vipraś ca śobheta śauṣkalaṃ-manyatā-madāt ||JGc_1,19.17|| [anuṣṭubh]
  aham unmūlayiṣyāmi śakra tvad-vairi-pakṣagān |
  kathaṃ man manyase bhītiṃ nītim eva pravartaya ||JGc_1,19.18|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'So that, remembering me, you would not transgress my father and other excellent saintly persons!' // [anuṣṭubh]
'If a god should desire [merely] the pride of sensual enjoyment, O <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), then a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> too would shine with the intoxication of thinking himself ascetic!' // [anuṣṭubh]
'I shall uproot those of your enemy's faction, O <s>Śakra</s>! How can you consider me a source of fear? Simply practice proper policy!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha dūrataḥ surabhir abhītam iva tam abhīkṣya, huṅkārataḥ sva-santāna-santānam ākārya, kārya-viduṣī sa-tṛṣṇa-nayanā kṛṣṇam abhijagāma | [40] kṛṣṇaś ca svajāti-rītikāvasthitita evāvanamantīm iva tām imāṃ sahasā sahasām asasambhramam añjali-sañjita-karaḥ sañjagāda-mātā kathaṃ samāyātā?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Surabhi</s> (the divine cow), seeing him from afar as if fearless, summoning her own progeny from the 'huṅ' sound, knowing the task at hand, with thirsty eyes — approached <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. [40] And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, standing in the custom of his own species (as a cowherd), with hands joined reverently in a <s>añjali</s>, addressed her — who was as if bowing — this thousand-fold mother, without haste, without alarm: 'Mother, how have you come?'

children.text: tataś cāśiṣaḥ siṣāsantī tāḥ sambhramād anudbhāvya surabhy uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Surabhi</s>, desiring to offer blessings, without expressing them due to agitation, said:

children.text:
ete mad-anvayā dhanyā gotvaṃ tvāṃ sevituṃ gatāḥ |
  ahaṃ tu nedṛk-puṇyā yad gocaratvaṃ ca nāgatā ||JGc_1,19.19|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'These descendants of mine are blessed — they have attained the status of cow in order to serve you! But I am not as meritorious as that, since I have not attained the status of being in your range!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
athavā-
  daitya-ghātī bhavān nityaṃ sarva-lokaika-pālakaḥ |
  vayaṃ ca loka-madhye smas tvan-nāthāḥ svata eva tat ||JGc_1,19.20|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Or rather:
'You are eternally the slayer of demons, the sole protector of all worlds; and we are among those worlds — thus we are naturally under your lordship!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tatas tad idaṃ kiñcit prārthaye-
children.translated_text: And then, I request this:

children.text:
go-sūktaṃ bhāṣate gāvaḥ padaṃ sarva-suparvaṇām |
  tad brahmādau suparvatvam avan vinda gavendratām ||JGc_1,19.21|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tavedaṃ kiyad aiśvaryaṃ yad brahmāvadhi-pālanaṃ |
  vaikuṇṭha-kuṇṭhatā-kāri yasya goloka-vaibhavam ||JGc_1,19.22|| [anuṣṭubh]
  sarvasya pālakāt kvāpi khaṇḍa-pālanam iṣyate |
  jagat-prakāśakād bhānor nija-dhāma-prakāśavat ||JGc_1,19.23|| [anuṣṭubh]
  nāsmākaṃ kevalam idaṃ mataṃ kintu vidher api |
  yad bhaved asya cendrasya durbuddheḥ śuddhi-bhāvanam ||JGc_1,19.24|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tvat-kṛpāyāḥ paraṃ sthānaṃ vayam ity eṣa vāsavaḥ |
  āśiśriye yad asmāṃs tad dvāra-mātrāya kalpate ||JGc_1,19.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
  yasmān mṛgyati tām eva mad-vidhād bhavataḥ kṛpām |
  kūpād iva rasāntaḥ-sthāṃ tarṣī ghana-rasa-sthitim ||JGc_1,19.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
  tad eva deva paśyendraḥ paśyaṃs tava pada-dvayam |
  sūcayaty abhiṣekaṃ te netra-dhārā-sahasrataḥ ||JGc_1,19.27|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'The Vedic hymn declares: "Cows are the station of all the gods." Therefore, by protecting the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, attain the lordship of cows!' // [anuṣṭubh]
'How slight is this sovereignty of yours — that of protecting up to <s>Brahmā</s>! Yours is the majesty of <s>Goloka</s>, which puts even <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> to shame!' // [anuṣṭubh]
'From the protector of all, a particular protection is desired somewhere — just as from the sun that illuminates the world, the illumination of its own abode [is desired]!' // [anuṣṭubh]
'This is not our view alone, but also that of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) — that this might also be the means of purification for this foolish <s>Indra</s>.' // [anuṣṭubh]
'We are the supreme station of your grace — and this <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) has sought refuge in us; for him, that serves only as a gateway.' // [anuṣṭubh]
'Since one like me seeks from you that very grace — like a thirsty one [seeking] the state of deep rain-water stationed within a well!' // [anuṣṭubh]
'Therefore, O Lord, look — <s>Indra</s>, gazing at your two feet, indicates your consecration through thousand-fold streams of tears from his eyes!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha tatra sacita-saṅkocanena vilocanena gocaritānumateḥ śrī-gokula-pateḥ prasādam āsādayantī surarṣi-sura-mātṛ-surapati-suratatibhir upasura-prabhṛtibhiś ca sākaṃ surabhī sarabhasam asura-mardanaṃ puraskartuṃ puraḥ-saratām avāpa |
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained the favor of the lord of Śrī <s>Gokula</s> — who was following the custom of the cows — through her glance gathered with contraction, <s>Surabhi</s>, together with the divine sage, the mother of the gods, the king of the gods, the hosts of gods, and the demi-gods and others — hastened to come forward to place the crusher of the demons foremost.

children.text: te hi druhiṇena tāv anu samanujñātā drutam eva vidrutya nihnutya ca rājīva-locanaṃ rājīyantaḥ paritaḥ sthitā babhūvuḥ, yatra rudra-druhiṇāv api teṣām agresaratām avāpatuḥ |
children.translated_text: For they, having been permitted by <s>Brahmā</s> to follow those two, ran swiftly, concealed themselves, and stood around the lotus-eyed one, serving him — where even <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> attained the foremost position among them.

children.text: tataś ca surabhir abhihitavatī-śrīmad-vrajendra-kula-candra! bhavad-bhavadīya-svīya-caraṇānām anucaraṇatas tāvad atratyāni tīrthāni sārthakāny eva jātāni | dhenavaś ca yuṣmad-vihita-dugdha-dhayanād dhanyatām adhuḥ | [46] tataś ca svarga-sthita-tīrtha-varasya gaṅgā-nirjharasya tathātmīyasyāpy ūdho-bharasya tvad-ārādhanayā vyarthatāvadhāya payaḥ samāhartuṃ bhavantaṃ vidhim arthayāmahe | athavā, yathādiśyate tathāvaśyaṃ prathayāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Surabhi</s> spoke: 'O moon of the dynasty of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>! By the service of your feet, and those of your devotees and your own people, all the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred sites) here have indeed become fruitful. And the cows, through the drinking of milk offered by your honors, have attained blessedness. [46] Therefore, perceiving the futility of the excellent celestial <s>tīrtha</s> of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> waterfall situated in heaven, and also of our own udder's burden, for your worship — we entreat your honor to gather the milk. Or rather, whatever is commanded, we shall certainly enact.'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-smitam uvāca-yatheṣṭham anuṣṭhīyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'Let it be done as you wish.'

children.text: athābhravāhana-bhrū-bhramaṇataḥ sa-sambhramam abhra-mātaṅgaḥ svaḥ-saṅgata-gaṅgātaḥ samuddaṇḍita-śuṇḍā-daṇḍenāmbhaḥ-sambhṛtān nidhi-kumbhān nirvilambam eva muhur api lambhayāmāsa | surabhir api surabhi-payasā sura-pati-sarasīm upagiriṃ vibharāñcakāra | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, from the furrowing of the brow of the cloud-rider (<s>Indra</s>), with great haste, the cloud-elephant (<s>Airāvata</s>), with his upraised trunk, from the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>, repeatedly and without delay provided water-filled treasury-pots. And <s>Surabhi</s> too, with her fragrant milk, adorned the pool at the base of the mountain as a celestial lake. And then:

children.text:
vādya-spṛg-gīta-nṛtyair upasura-sadasāṃ stotra-mantrair ṛṣīṇāṃ
  harṣāndolātikolāhala-jaya-ninadair brahma-rudrādikānām |
  utsarpad-bhaktir indraḥ saha harid-adhipais tad-gaṇaiś cābhyaṣiñcat
  kṛṣṇaṃ yenaiva sarve' py ahaha sukha-sudhāsikta-rūpā babhūvuḥ ||JGc_1,19.28|| [sragdharā]
  aditir mātṛ-kṛtyāni svasṛ-kṛtyāni pārvatī |
  garutmān bhṛtya-kṛtyāni cāhṛtyātra mudaṃ yayau ||JGc_1,19.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
With music, garlands, songs, and dances by the assemblies of demi-gods; with hymns and <s>mantras</s> of the sages; with the resounding, swaying, tumultuous victory-cries of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others — <s>Indra</s>, with surging devotion, together with the lord of the <s>dik</s>-elephants and their hosts, consecrated <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — by which indeed all became as if sprinkled with the nectar of happiness! // [sragdharā]
<s>Aditi</s> performed the duties of a mother, <s>Pārvatī</s> the duties of a sister, <s>Garutmān</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) the duties of a servant — and having carried [these offerings] here, they attained joy! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ yadā nirṇiktatayā devagaṇas tam asikta, tadā-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the host of gods had consecrated him in a purified manner:

children.text:
kīrtir yātā digantaṃ parimala-valanāpy abhramīd bhūmi-golaṃ
  maṅgalya-dhvāna-dhārā dig-anuga-kariṇāṃ prāviśat karṇa-gartam |
  itthaṃ sarvatra harṣa-prasara-bhara-vara-prāvṛṣā prāṇi-jāteḥ
  śāte jāte' pi kaṃsaḥ saraṭa-paṭala-rāṭ-ceṣṭayā veṣṭyate sma ||JGc_1,19.30|| [sragdharā]
[50] tad evaṃ sa vrajendra-nandanaḥ sarva-dig-gatān yadā digye, tadā tu---
children.translated_text:
Fame went to the ends of the directions; fragrance too roamed over the globe of the earth; the streams of auspicious sounds entered the ear-cavities of the directional elephants. Thus, everywhere, through the excellent monsoon of the spreading flood of joy for all living beings — even though coolness had arisen — <s>Kaṃsa</s> was enveloped by the behavior of a chameleon-horde-king [i.e., cold-blooded with dread]! // [sragdharā]
[50] Thus, when the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> was consecrated by all the directions:

children.text:
yāvad viṣṇupadaṃ vibhāti parama-vyomādi tāvaty api
  śrī-goloka-padaṃ praśastim ayate lakṣmī-parārdhāspadam |
  tatrāpīndratayā vibhāsi nitarāṃ govinda-nāmnā yathā
  tena tvaṃ jagad aṅga tadvad avatād ity ucire te samam ||JGc_1,19.31|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'As far as the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s> shines — the supreme sky and beyond — that far too the station of Śrī <s>Goloka</s> attains praise, being the abode of the supreme half of <s>Lakṣmī</s>. And there, through the name <s>Govinda</s>, you shine forth especially as <s>Indra</s> (king); therefore, just as that, may you protect the world, O dear one!' — thus they spoke in unison. // [śārdūla]

children.text:
ākāśa-kusumaiḥ sārdham ākāśa-vacanaṃ tadā |
  govinda iti yad vittaṃ tataḥ kim iva sādbhutam? ||JGc_1,19.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Along with flowers from the sky, a celestial voice at that time [declared] '<s>Govinda</s>' — what is known from that, is that indeed astonishing? // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
indraś chatraṃ vivasvān bahu-vidha-madhurālaṅkṛtīnāṃ kadambaṃ
  brahmā līlābjam īśaḥ svaracita-muralīṃ mādhavāya vyatānīt |
  anyaṃ ca svasvam arthaṃ tridaśa-pati-tatir yat punaḥ sarvam eṣāṃ
  pūrvaṃ cāpūrvam āsīd abhavad atha tad-aṅgāvṛtījyāsu pūjyam ||JGc_1,19.33|| [sragdharā]
[51] tad evaṃ sthite-
children.translated_text:
<s>Indra</s> [offered] a parasol, <s>Vivasvān</s> (the Sun) a host of diverse, sweetly adorned items, <s>Brahmā</s> a play-lotus, <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva) a self-fashioned flute — to <s>Mādhava</s> they presented. And each host of the thirty [gods] offered their own respective gift; yet all these were both previously existing and unprecedented — and then became worshipable in the services that adorned his limbs! // [sragdharā]
[51] Thus, when this had been established:

children.text:
rājad-rājāsanam upari-gacchatra-citraṃ suramya-
  bhrāmyad-vālavya-jana-yugalaṃ prasphurad-divya-veśam |
  kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sura-parivṛtaṃ stabdha-netrāṇi dūrāc
  citrāṇīva kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ tatra mitrāṇi tasthuḥ ||JGc_1,19.34|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: The shining royal throne, the resplendent parasol above, the charming pair of <s>cāmara</s>-bearing attendants whirling about, the manifestly divine attire — seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> surrounded by the gods, his friends, with motionless eyes, stood for a few moments at a distance, like pictures! // [mandākrāntā]

children.text: tataś ca kṛpayā snapita-nayanāravindena govindena kṛtam ānandanam anu phullatayā pūrvataḥ puruṣu mahendrādi-deva-guruṣu chatrādikaṃ taruṣu sandhāya, nija-hita-nibandhāya tat-pada-dvandvam eva vandaṃ vandam amanda-bāṣpa-nisyandaṃ nijām avajñāspadatāṃ vijñāpya tam anujñāpya dūraṃ vindamāneṣu labdha-vigata-nindamāneṣu vṛndārakeṣu, sakhi-sandohaḥ śandoham anuvindan mandaṃ mandam āsasāda | āsādya ca-
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Govinda</s>, with his lotus-eyes bathed in compassion, had created delight — and when, blooming [with joy], the gods had fastened the parasol and other [gifts] upon the trees before [them], among the venerable great ones like <s>Mahendra</s>, and for his own welfare bowing to his pair of feet, shedding copious tears again and again, having informed him of their own unworthiness, having taken his leave — when the hosts of the immortals had gone far and obtained freedom from reproach, the circle of friends, discovering a flood of joy, slowly, slowly approached. And having approached:

children.text:
adrākṣīd amahīd avocad alagīd ājighrad apy acyutaṃ
  chatrādyaṃ ca cacāya mitrapaṭalī papraccha bhūyaś ca tam |
  so' pi vyājam ihācacāra bahudhā sā na pratīyāya taṃ
  kintu prītibharaṃ mithaḥ pravalayaṃ hāsas tad āvardhata ||JGc_1,19.35|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: They saw, they touched, they spoke to, they clung to, they smelled <s>Acyuta</s>; and the circle of friends wondered at the parasol and other [things], and asked him again and again. He too practiced many pretexts here, and they did not believe him — but the flood of mutual affection, spreading widely — that laughter only increased! // [śārdūla]

children.text:
tataś ca-
  iha sthitaiḥ pṛthag aparais tu bhūṣaṇair
  vibhuḥ parasparam api tām abhūṣayat |
  amī tadā sa-kanaka-daṇḍa-cāmaraiḥ
  paricchedaiḥ svayam api taṃ siṣevire ||JGc_1,19.36|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
And then:
The Lord adorned them mutually with other ornaments separate from those stationed here; and those [friends] then, with gold-handled <s>cāmaras</s> and other accoutrements, attended him themselves! // [rucirā]

children.text: tasminn atha rājany ati sakhi-vṛnde-
children.translated_text: Then, in that king's [presence], with that extensive circle of friends:

children.text:
dṛṣṭvā devatatir vidūrataratas taṃ sevyamānaṃ suhṛd-
  vargais tad-guṇa-rūpa-śīla-tulitaiḥ sva-pratta-tat-tac-chriyā |
  tān svajñāna-vilāsa-sañcita-phalaṃ mene tathā tām api
  sva-premārjita-karma-sampadam amaṃstānyan na mānyaṃ tataḥ ||JGc_1,19.37|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: Seeing from a very great distance the host of gods being served by groups of friends — matched in virtues, beauty, and character, adorned with the splendor of their respective [gifts] — the gods considered them the fruit accumulated by the sport of their own knowledge; and that [friendship] too they considered the wealth of merit earned by their own love — and nothing else was deemed worthy of respect beyond that. // [śārdūla]

children.text: tad evam ārabdhe' pi gamane stabdhe sati satīpati-prabhṛtayas tasminn abhiṣeka-prabhavaṃ prabhāvāntaraṃ paśyantaḥ parasparaṃ sādbhūtam idam udbhāvayāmāsuḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, even though the departure had commenced and then stopped, <s>Satīpati</s> (Śiva) and others, perceiving in him a different power arising from the consecration, produced this with mutual wonder, as follows:

children.text:
kṛṣṇārcāraci daivataiḥ sukham ayur lokāś ca gāvas tathā
  pṛthvīṃ dugdha-bhṛtāṃ vyadhur bahu-vidhān nadyo rasān susruvuḥ |
  vṛkṣā madhv adhur uddadhuś ca girayo ratnāni nirvairatāṃ
  jīvāḥ prāpur aho mahaty apacitiḥ puṣyaty akartṝn api ||JGc_1,19.38|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was worshipped by the gods — longevity, happiness, and worlds, and likewise cows, yielded milk to the earth in many forms; rivers flowed with juices; trees yielded honey; mountains produced gems; living beings attained freedom from enmity — ah, great reverence nourishes even those who did not perform [the worship]!' // [śārdūla]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
  indraḥ krūra-caritram ācaritavān yat tena cintāgame
  cittaṃ kampam iyarti ced giri kathaṃ cittena tad vyajyatām |
  kṛṣṇas tatra ca yāṃ kṛpāṃ bata tayā cittaṃ dravī-bhūtatām
  āyāti svayam eva ced giri kathaṃ cittena sā vyajyatām? ||JGc_1,19.39|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'When one thinks of <s>Indra's</s> cruel deeds and anxiety comes — if the mind trembles, then, O mountain, how can the mind express that? And the grace that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> showed there — if the mind by that becomes liquefied by itself — then, O mountain, how can the mind express that?' // [śārdūla]

children.text: atha caramācalaṃ cucumbiṣati bhānu-bimbe vilambaḥ saṃvṛtta ity avilambam eva go-nikuramba-saṃvalanayā sakhibhiḥ samaṃ vrajaṃ vrajan vraja-rāja-janmā san-mānayadbhir nirjara-vrajair upary atula-puṣpa-varṣair upacarya vrajadbhir anuvavraje, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, when the sun-orb was about to kiss the western mountain, perceiving that delay had occurred — without delay, tending the hosts of cows, together with his friends, the one born of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, proceeding toward <s>Vraja</s>, was attended above by the hosts of immortals with incomparable flower-showers, honoring him as he went; and he was followed by them, as follows:

children.text:
divyātapatra-sita-cāmara-śasta-hastaiḥ
  saṃsevyamāna-savidhaḥ sakhibhiḥ pragītaḥ |
  puṣpa-vrajena vividhair vibudhaiś ca siktaḥ
  śrī-pṛkta-kāntir ajitaḥ sadanaṃ sasāda ||JGc_1,19.40|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: Attended on all sides by friends bearing divine parasol and white <s>cāmaras</s> with auspicious handles, praised [by them], showered by the gods with diverse flowers — the unconquered one, his beauty joined with Śrī (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), reached his home! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
niśamitam akaron niśāmitaṃ ca
  dyujani-vibhūṣaṇa-bhūṣaṇāṅgam etam |
  vraja-nṛpati-mukha-vrajaḥ samantād
  ajani ca sāttvika-rājirāji-mūrtiḥ ||JGc_1,19.41|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text: The host [of people] headed by the king of <s>Vraja</s> beheld and honored him — whose limbs were adorned with ornaments fit for celestial beings — from all sides; and they became embodiments of rows and rows of <s>sāttvika</s>-ecstasies! // [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text: yat tu niśamya ramyacetā rāmaḥ sānukrośaṃ krośamātram upavrajya nijāvarajavijayaṃ paśyan sukha-vaśyamanās tam āliṅgya mūrdhānam āśiṅghya kṣaṇa-katipayam upaviśya, vacana-cāturībhis tat-prasaṅgaṃ saṅgatavān | tataś ca nijānujena pūrvam eva svakṛte nirdiśya rakṣitair divyeṣv api divyatā-lakṣitair analpair ākalpaiḥ so' yam agrajaḥ sva-kareṇa virājayāmāsa | tataś ca svānujaṃ guru-janānām agratas tādṛśatayā prayātuṃ saṅkocam arocayan so' yam agrajaḥ śanaiḥ sanair anaiṣīt |
children.translated_text: But <s>Rāma</s>, hearing this with a charmed heart, having approached compassionately to within a <s>krośa</s> (about two miles), beholding the victory of his own younger brother, with a mind controlled by happiness, embraced him, kissed his head, and sat down for a few moments, joining in that affair through the elegance of his words. And then, that elder brother adorned him with his own hand with the not-few divine ornaments — which were marked by divinity — that had been previously set aside and guarded by his younger brother for his sake. And then, that elder brother — not relishing the shyness of his younger brother proceeding before the elders in such a state — slowly, slowly led him.

children.text: atha tasmin dine tu go-sandoha-doha-nibandhanaṃ tad-anubandhi-janān sandhāya svayaṃ tu tat-tad-udantānusandhānāya dhenu-sannidhāna eva sānandaṃ nanda-rājaḥ sannidhāya, vandamānaṃ sa-rāma-sakhi-vṛndaṃ govindaṃ purastād vidhāya samam eva bandhubhiḥ samam āsanam āsajjann āsāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Now, on that day, the king <s>Nanda</s>, having arranged the people connected with the cow-milking and its related tasks, himself joyfully settled nearby the cows for the investigation of those various tidings, and placing before him <s>Govinda</s> who was saluting — together with <s>Rāma</s> and his friend-group — together with his kinsmen, he settled on his equal seat and sat.

children.text: tatra cānantaram ācaritāgatibhiḥ samyag urīkṛta-śrī-rāmānujānumatibhiḥ sūnṛta-vādibhiḥ śrīdāmādibhiḥ sa-samājāya vraja-rājāya divyac-chatrādy-arcāmatrādiṣu samarpiteṣu santarpiteṣu ca sarveṣu tad apracchannam eva sa papraccha-kathyatāṃ tathyaṃ kim idaṃ vṛttaṃ vṛttam? iti |
children.translated_text: There, subsequently, when <s>Śrīdāmā</s> and others — speakers of pleasant truth, who had properly accepted the assent of the younger brother of <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, and whose conduct was impeccable — had presented the divine umbrella and other worship-objects to the king of <s>Vraja</s> along with the assembly, and when all had been gratified, he asked them quite openly: 'Tell the truth — what event has transpired?'

children.text: śrīdāmā prāha-vayam api go-saṅkalanāya kalita-bhūri-dūratayā ciraṃ viramya sthitā na samyag avagamyaṃ tad ācarāma, kintu sāmagrīyam eva nija-samyag-rītim āvedayati iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdāmā</s> said: 'We too, having paused for a long time due to our having gone a great distance for cow-gathering, did not properly comprehend what transpired; but the collective evidence itself reports its own proper course.'

children.text: tato namratāṃ vindati śrī-govinde parasparam avadhāya sādhu, śrīdāman, sādhv idam uktam ity abhidhāya sarva evānarvācīna-gopāś citra-pratikṛtaya iva dvitra-kṣaṇaṃ nirnimeṣatām avāpuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, when the glorious <s>Govinda</s> assumed humility, all having observed one another and [said] 'Well done, O <s>Śrīdāmā</s>, this is well spoken!' — all the cowherds of no mean standing became motionless like painted images for two or three moments, attaining the state of not blinking.

children.text: madhumaṅgalas tūccaiḥ sahāsam āha sma-śrīman vrajarāja ! śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: But <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said loudly with laughter: 'O glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>! Hear!
