children.text:
gaur ekā giram ātanod atha pumān anyaḥ sahasrekṣaṇo'
  naṃsīt ko' pi karī sitaḥ svar-udakāny āhṛtya śaśvad dadau |
  kaucit pañca-caturmukhāṅga-valitau stotra-prathāṃ cakratus
  te cānye ca mahāmahena siṣicur gopeśa putraṃ tava ||JGc_1,19.42|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: 'A certain cow uttered a cry; then a certain thousand-eyed being (<s>Indra</s>) | bowed; a certain white elephant brought heavenly waters and gave them constantly; | a certain pair of four-and-five-faced beings (<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>), adorned with limbs, performed the spread of hymns; | and those and others, O chief of cowherds, consecrated your son with a great festival!' || (JGc 1,19.42) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: atha svayaṃ cātra sarvataś citraṃ māṅgalikaṃ karma nirmātuṃ yuktam iti vicārya citrāyamāne kṛṣṇa-prāṇe sasamāje vrajarāje viṣṇu-pada-cariṣṇu-vāṇīyam āvirbabhūva-
children.translated_text: Then, considering that it was fitting to create an auspicious ceremony from every side by themselves too, when the king of <s>Vraja</s> — whose very life was <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — became wonderstruck in the assembly, this voice worthy of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> abode appeared:

children.text:
yathābhyaṣiñcāma vayaṃ vrajeśitaḥ
  saṃsajya govindatayā sutaṃ tava |
  samaṃ samastaiḥ kṛta-maṅgalaṃ tathā
  taṃ yauvarājyena javād virājaya ||JGc_1,19.43|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text: 'Just as we consecrated your son, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>, | establishing him as <s>Govinda</s> — | so too, having performed the auspicious rites together with all, | quickly install him in the crown-princehood!' || (JGc 1,19.43) [upajāti]

children.text: atha tad etad amṛta-varṣa-dharṣitā vraja-varṣīyāṃsaḥ parasparaṃ vicārya kārya-māṇa-maṅgalya-tauryatrika-vādanāpaurvāparyataḥ svasti-vācanādikam ācārya-dvārā samācārya, pratisvam api vividha-vidhāna-dāna-pūrvakaṃ parva pūrayitvā pūra-rājatayā taṃ sabhājayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, the senior <s>Vraja</s>-folk, emboldened by that shower of nectar, having deliberated with one another, having had the benedictory recitations and the like performed through the officiating priests — from the beginning to end of the instrumental music made for the auspicious occasion — and having fulfilled the festival with various ritual gifts for each [attendee], they honored him as the prince-regent.

children.text:
āgamyātha śataṃ śataṃ vraja-mahendrāṇī-pradhānāṅganāḥ
  pratyekaṃ maṇi-dīpa-santati-karā maṅgala-kolāhalāḥ |
  nīrājyābhisabhājya ratna-nikarair nirmañchya gehaṃ prati
  snehaṃ mūrtam ivātiyatna-valitā govindam āninyire ||JGc_1,19.44|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: 'Then, coming a hundred and a hundred, the women led by the queen of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, | each bearing rows of gem-lamps, clamorous with auspicious sounds, | having performed the lamp-waving ceremony and honored him, having swept [the path] with clusters of gems, toward the house | they brought <s>Govinda</s> — as if love embodied — with supreme effort!' || (JGc 1,19.44) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
īdṛśas te vrajādhīśa sutaḥ sūta-mukhotsavaḥ |
  yo gavendratayā gāṃ ca gāṃ ca gāṃ ca sukhākarot ||JGc_1,19.45|| [anuṣṭubh]
  subhagambhaviṣṇu jātaṃ jagad api kṛṣṇābhiṣekataḥ paścāt |
  andhambhāvukam āsīd bhāvuka-śūnyaṃ kulaṃ tu danujānām ||JGc_1,19.46|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
'Such, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>, is your son, the festival of the bard's mouth, | who, as the king of cows, made the cows happy, and the earth happy, and speech happy!' || (JGc 1,19.45) [anuṣṭubh]
'Having become auspicious after <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> consecration, the world too | became fortunate; but the clan of demons became blind and devoid of fortune.' || (JGc 1,19.46) [gīti]

children.text: tad evaṃ divā-kathāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ naktam api sā pūrvavad vṛttā | yathā madhukaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the day-narrative had transpired, the night[-narrative] too transpired as before. As <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text:
bhaved analpaṃ kutrāpi svalpaṃ kutrāpi poṣakam |
  yathānna-vyañjanaṃ loke yathā rasa-rasāyanam ||JGc_1,19.47|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'What is abundant somewhere may be slight elsewhere, yet both are nourishing — | just as food and condiments in the world, just as the essence and the elixir of flavor.' || (JGc 1,19.47) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tasmāt saṅkṣiptam apy etad vistaravad eva mantavyam | [66] tathā hi-tasmin mahasi nīrandhraṃ purandhrībhiḥ samam āsām api samāganaṃ vṛttaṃ, yatropakaṇṭha-gatānām apy amūṣāṃ vastrāvaguṇṭhitāni netrāṇy atīvotkaṇṭhitāni jātāni |
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though told in brief, it should be considered as if told in full detail. [66] For thus: at that great festival, without interruption, the meeting of these [gopīs] too occurred together with the women, wherein the eyes of those who had come nearby — though veiled with garments — became exceedingly longing.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca tasya vivāha-samatāvahe mahā-mahe manasīdam asīmam ābhir vibhāvitam-
children.translated_text: And at that great festival, which equaled a wedding, this boundless [thought] was contemplated by them in their minds:

children.text:
keyaṃ jagaty ahaha rājati gopa-kanyā
  dhanyā yayā tu karapīḍanam asya gantā? |
  hā yogyatām api vidhāya vidhiḥ samastām
  astaṃ nināya bata nas tam amūṃ dhig astu ||JGc_1,19.48|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: 'Who is this cowherd-maiden, ahaha, who reigns in the world, | blessed — by whom the hand-pressing [wedding] of this one shall be attained? | Alas, fate, having created all [our] fitness too, | has cast it down — curse [that maiden]!' || (JGc 1,19.48) [vasantatilakā]

children.text: bhavatu, tad api kintv idam atīvānyāyyam-
children.translated_text: So be it; but this is exceedingly unjust:

children.text:
kulīnā rūpiṇyaḥ parama-guṇa-śīlāḥ praṇayitā-
  bhṛd-utkaṇṭhākaṇṭhāgata-tulita-jīvā bata vayam |
  na tāvad vaṃśī tat-tad-anuguṇatām añcati jaḍā
  tathāpy eṣā hā dhik kalita-hari-saṅgā na tu vayam ||JGc_1,19.49|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'We are well-born, beautiful, endowed with the highest qualities and character, | bearing the longing of love, our life-breath barely reaching the throat! | That flute, wooden [thing], does not even attain the fitness for his various [lips] — | and yet, alas, curse it! — it has obtained the association of <s>Hari</s>, but not we!' || (JGc 1,19.49) [śikharinī]

children.text: kevaleyaṃ varākī kevala-mukha-cūṣaṇa-sukhā, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: This wretched thing is merely a pitiable mouth-sucker, for:

children.text:
āliṅgya kaṇṭham urasi pratipadya kāntiṃ
  māle kaṭaṃ prakaṭam eva sadā dadhāsi |
  na śrī-harir na bhavatī tu vā jano' yaṃ
  saṅkoca-leśam ayate tvam ato' si dhanyā ||JGc_1,19.50|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: 'Embracing his neck, obtaining radiance upon his chest, | O garland, you clearly always bear the fragrance! | Yet neither <s>Śrī Hari</s> nor you — nor these people — | feel the slightest embarrassment; therefore you are blessed!' || (JGc 1,19.50) [vasantatilakā]

children.text: tad evaṃ manasi vadantīṣu-
children.translated_text: Thus, as they spoke within their minds:

children.text:
pūrṇāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ vidhi-vaśatayā kācid āñcīn murārer
  ardhaṃ kācid vraja-jana-gatā kācid asyās tribhāgam |
  kācit kiñcin na ca tad akhilaṃ tulyatām eva dadhre
  sarvāsāṃ yan manasi caklpe hanta tāpāya tadvat ||JGc_1,19.51|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'By fate's compulsion, one [gopī] caught a full glance of <s>Murāri</s>, | some [caught] half, some who had gone among the <s>Vraja</s>-folk [caught] a third part, | some [caught] a little — yet all of this was held equally alike; | for whatever was fashioned in the minds of all of them — alas — became a cause of torment in the same way!' || (JGc 1,19.51) [mandākrāntā]

children.text: atha tasyām eva niśāyāṃ candraśālikāyāṃ kṛta-śayanena kañja-nayanena tāsām aparāhnetanāpāṅga-sāṅga-śara-nikara-saṅga-labdha-bhaṅge hṛdi samutthita-vyathatayā jāta-niśītha-jāgaratāyām aviratāyāṃ tāsu nijānirvṛtiṃ vivṛtīkartuṃ tām iva ca tartuṃ purahara-kṛta-vitara-nava-muralīkalaḥ khuralībhiḥ kalayāmāse |
children.translated_text: Then, on that very night, when the lotus-eyed one had made his bed in the moonlit pavilion — when the wound arising in his heart from the volleys of the embodied sidelong-glance-arrows of those [gopīs] received during the afternoon had produced a midnight wakefulness that was unceasing in them — in order to reveal his own restlessness and also to cross beyond it, [he played] a novel flute-melody created by the destroyer of <s>Pura</s> (Śiva), and performed it with [expert] fingering:

children.text:
tadā kedāra-rāgas tu prāpa kedāratāṃ niśi |
  gopībhir vāsanā-bījam uptaṃ yatrāṅkurāyitam ||JGc_1,19.52|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Kedāra</s> rāga attained the quality of a plowed field at night, | in which the seed of longing was sown by the <s>gopīs</s> and sprouted!' || (JGc 1,19.52) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tatra ca-
  tūkāraḥ khalu māthureṣu paritas tvaṅkāra-bhāṣā matā
  so' yaṃ vaiṇava-gānataḥ pratipadaṃ prāyaḥ parāmṛśyate |
  pratyekaṃ yugapat priyāṃ niśamayan kṛṣṇo yadā taṃ jagau
  matvā svaṃ prati tat pratisvam api tāḥ sarvā vimūrcchāṃ yayuḥ ||JGc_1,19.53|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And there:
'The syllable "tū" among the <s>Mathurā</s> folk is everywhere understood as the word for "you" (<s>tvaṃ</s>); | this very [syllable], through the flute-song, is encountered at almost every step [of the melody]; | when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> sang it, hearing each beloved simultaneously — | each one, thinking it addressed to herself, all of them swooned!' || (JGc 1,19.53) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
  ānuṣaṅgikatayāpi sagānād
  āsv adhād yad avidus tad amūś ca |
  uddideśa puru yāṃ bata sā tu
  svaṃ ca samprati viveda na rādhā ||JGc_1,19.54|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'Even incidentally, whatever he placed in those [gopīs] through song — | they did not know it, nor did those [others]; | but she to whom he especially directed it — | even that <s>Rādhā</s> did not know herself at that moment!' || (JGc 1,19.54) [svāgatā]

children.text: tad evam alpa-samayam ayam api kalpa-cayam ayam iva kalpayitvā kathakaḥ samāpayan kathanaṃ ślathayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Thus, even this brief time the narrator fashioned as if it were a cosmic cycle, and loosening the conclusion, he brought the tale to a close:

children.text:
so' yaṃ te ramaṇo rādhe labdhaḥ kṛcchreṇa yas tvayā |
  tvad-vinā-bhāvataḥ saukhyaṃ yaś ca kutrāpi nāptavān ||JGc_1,19.55|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'He, this very one, is your beloved, O <s>Rādhā</s>, whom you have obtained with difficulty; | who, without you, has not obtained happiness anywhere!' || (JGc 1,19.55) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ saṅkṣepenāpi kathite prathite muhūrta-dvayaṃ muhūrtavad eva tāś ca te ca tuṣṇīmbhāvam āseduḥ, punaś ca yathāyatham āvāsaṃ samāseduḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, even though told in brief, it became renowned; for two <s>muhūrtas</s> (about 96 minutes), [passing] as if a single <s>muhūrta</s>, both they [the gopīs] and those [narrators] attained silence, and then all returned to their respective dwellings as before.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
jambha-bhedi-surendratā-stambhana-nagendra-dhara-
gavendratālambhanaṃ nāma
ekonaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
 ||19||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Nineteenth Chapter, named
'The Blocking of the Supreme <s>Indra</s>-ship of the Smasher of <s>Jambha</s> —
the Attainment of the Mountain-bearer, the Lord of Elephants (<s>Airāvata</s>).'
||19||

children.text: atha viṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Twentieth Chapter.

children.text: varuṇa-lokāloka-camatkāra-tiraskāraka-golokāvalokanam
children.translated_text: The Vision of <s>Goloka</s>, Which Puts to Shame the Wonder of the World of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text:
atha prabhāta-kathāyāṃ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tad evam ekādaśī-kathā kathitā | tāṃ ca tithim aśithilitayā prathita-manorathāṃ pratītya nityavad eva vraja-devaḥ samyag ullāsam upovāsa | [2] kintu pāraṇa-kāraṇam avaśīrṇam eva dvādaśīm avaśiṣṭām avadhāya bahv-avaśiṣṭāyām api rajanyāṃ viśiṣṭa-vidhi-balataḥ snānādi-kalanāya kalindīṃ praviṣṭavān | praviśya ca yathā-yatham atrasnuḥ sasnau | snātvā cāntar eva vāriṇaḥ śrī-nārāyaṇam ekāyanatayā sāgama-niṣṭham upatiṣṭhamānaḥ suṣṭhu dhyātum ārabdhavān | tatra cāyaṃ janmata eva tan-mayatayā san-matir āsīt | tādṛśa-nandana-lābhānandatas tu tatrāpy atiśayaṃ vindati sma | tataś ca tad-vidha-dhyānāvadhānataḥ samādhim anavadhim āpannavantaṃ taṃ sarvataḥ pracarantaḥ
pracetasaś carāḥ sahasā samāsadya sadyaḥ svīya-svāmi-nivāsaṃ praty eva pravāsayāmāsuḥ | eṣa nivāsa-viśeṣaś ca tasya jala-stambha-vidyālambhitāra-bhavān svata eva bhāsvān bhāsvat-kanyā-hrada-stha-vivarasyādhaḥ-pradeśe sadeśa eva rasā-vivara-deśe niveśam āsīdati | na ca kṛṣṇa-prabhāvatā vidita-mahitānubhāvasya tasya tathānayanaṃ nayavatāṃ na sambhāvanīyam | sa hi nirantaram idaṃ cintayati-yad asya mad-bhāgya-jātataḥ sañjātasya sutasya yathottara-prathamāna-mānatayā parama-prema-harṣadam utkarṣaṃ śaśvad eva paśyāma iti | tatas tad evāsakṛd eva yogam āpayituṃ tal-līlāyām upayoga-māyātāyā yogamāyāyā eva samayās ta ete pūtanā-gamanādivat | [3] atha tathāveśinam eva vrajeśānaṃ yadā pāśinaḥ puratas tad-ādeśābhiniveśinas te sañcāritavantas,
tadā tad-ākārata eva taṃ nirdhārayan punaś ca nārāyaṇa-dhāraṇāvantam avadhārayann ayam atidarādarābhyāṃ kṛta-divya-vastrādi-praśastitayā varaśayyām evādhiśāyayāmāsa | [4] svayaṃ ca pitṛ-haraṇāsahiṣṇu-kṛṣṇāgamanam anantaram eva manvānaḥ sudūra-dṛṣṭi-hetuṃ pūr-dvāram adhitiṣṭhann ūrdhvam eva tiṣṭhati sma | [5] athātratyaṃ vṛttam anuvṛttyatām | [6] yadā khalu kṛṣṇasya tātaḥ kṛṣṇā-pāthasi tan-nāthavattā-mātra-dhanānāṃ janānām adṛśyatām avāpa, tadā diśi diśi kāndiśīkās te jalam avagāhya tad-aprāptitas tad-bāhyaṃ pradeśam āgatāḥ | āgamya ca vikrośanta eva vrajam abhigacchantaḥ, kṛṣṇa-rāmāgraṇyas tān vraja-grāmaṇyaḥ kalitāsukhān svābhimukhān eva lebhire | [7] tatra ca vṛtte śruta-mātre
parama-duḥkha-pātre sarvataḥ kṛta-mano-virāmau kṛṣṇa-rāmau vikramya sarvam atikramya, paramotkaṇṭhita-matyā jhaṭiti-gatyā pṛthivīm api ghaṭṭayantau, tam eva ghaṭṭam āṭatuḥ | tatra ca kṛṣṇaḥ samagra-vyagram agrajam āliṅgan riṅgad-asram evedam aśrāvayat-bhrātar, mātaram akātaratayābhirakṣya sarva eva rakṣaṇīyāḥ, yāvad ahaṃ pitaram ānīya sukha-vitaraṃ karavāṇi | mātary atrāgatāyāṃ tu na kathañcid api paryāptiṃ paryāpayituṃ śakṣyāmīti | [8] tad evaṃ kṛta-saṃvāda-mātraḥ pitaram ānetuṃ nirmita-yātraḥ saṃhanana-bṛṃhita-siṃha-lajjaḥ saṃhita-parikara-sajjaḥ pātāla-vivara-dvāra-pātraṃ sarit-pātram anu mamajja | [9] anantaraṃ ca, vrajeśvarī-pradhānāḥ sarva eva tatra caraṇa-mātram ādadhānā rāmam ekam avadhānāḥ
kṛṣṇam anusandadhānāḥ papracchuḥ-kva nu yātas tavānujātaḥ? iti | [10] sa tu tāṃ vrajendrasudṛśaṃ visadṛśadṛśaṃ parāmṛśann uvāca-mātar, na kātaratām āyāhi | sa tu sampraty eva janakam ādāya svajanasukhaṃ janayi-ṣyati iti | [11] atha svamātaram uvāca-hanta, tvam api kathaṃ māṃ hantāsi? mayi viśvāsataḥ śvāsamātraviśiṣṭām etāṃ pāhi | [12] tataś ca sarva evānarvāñcaḥ kāliyadamanaprakramatas tadvacanam aklamapramam eva manvānās tāṃ viśramayāmāsuḥ | kintu,
children.translated_text: Then, in the morning narration, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Thus, the tale of <s>Ekādaśī</s> has been told. And having observed that sacred day — whose fame spread through unwavering heart's desires — the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, as always, duly fasted with complete delight. [2] But having ascertained that the <s>Dvādaśī</s> remaining as the cause for the breaking of the fast had declined, even though much of the night still remained, from the force of the special ritual rule, he entered the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) for the performance of bathing and the like. Having entered, he bathed fearlessly as was proper. And having bathed, remaining within the very water, he began to meditate intently, worshipping the glorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as the sole object with firm scriptural devotion. And there, from birth itself, by his absorption in him, his mind had been well-established. But from the bliss of having obtained such a son, he found even greater exaltation in that [meditation]. Then, as he attained a limitless state of <s>samādhi</s> through the concentration of such meditation, the agents of <s>Pracetas</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>), roaming about everywhere, suddenly came upon him and immediately transported him to the very abode of their own master. And this particular dwelling [of Varuṇa], through the art of water-petrification gained [by Varuṇa] from the Lord's self-luminous realm, was itself naturally luminous, situated in the region below the cavern of the pool of the <s>Bhāsvatī</s>'s (<s>Sun's</s>) daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>), in a proper place within the nether-world cavity. Nor is it improbable that ones of such propriety would thus carry away one whose great power was well-known through <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> majesty. For he (<s>Varuṇa</s>) constantly contemplated thus: 'May I always behold the increasing glory of this son of mine [<s>Nanda's</s>], born through the fortune of my [previous merits], with supremely love-delighting exaltation growing progressively!' Therefore, these are precisely the occasions of <s>Yogamāyā</s> — whose application serves to unite [<s>Nanda</s>] with that [vision] repeatedly within his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] pastimes — just like <s>Pūtanā's</s> arrival and such. [3] Then, when the servants of the Noose-bearer brought the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — who was in that very state of trance — before him, he (<s>Varuṇa</s>), by his very appearance, recognized him, and further ascertained him as one bearing the meditation of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; he, with extreme and mild respect, having honored him with divine garments and the like, laid him upon a fine bed. [4] And he himself, reckoning that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, unable to bear the abduction of his father, would arrive immediately thereafter, stood upright at the entrance gate, looking far ahead, maintaining a far-sighted lookout. [5] Now let the events on this side be followed. [6] When the father of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> vanished from sight for those people — whose sole wealth was his lordship — in the dark waters of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), then, in every direction, those bewildered ones, having plunged into the water and not finding him, came out to the bank outside. Coming out and crying aloud, approaching <s>Vraja</s>, those village headmen of <s>Vraja</s> led by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> met them coming toward them in a state of distress. [7] And there, upon merely hearing the event — a vessel of supreme sorrow — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, ceasing all mental [activity], leaping forth and transcending everything, with supremely longing minds, with a sudden pace that struck the very earth, rushed to that very bank. And there, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, embracing his agitated elder brother, with crawling tears, conveyed this: 'Brother, protect Mother without timidity, and everyone else too, while I bring Father back and create happiness abundantly! But if Mother comes here, I shall be unable to make her settle down in any way!' [8] Thus, having merely exchanged words, prepared for the journey to bring his father, with a musculature that put a lion to shame, with his entourage girded — he plunged into the river-vessel, the gateway to the nether-world cavity. [9] Immediately thereafter, all of them — led by the queen of <s>Vraja</s> — arriving there with barely a footstep's [delay], attentive to <s>Rāma</s> alone, searching for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, they asked: 'Where has your younger brother gone?' [10] And he, regarding that queen of <s>Vraja</s> with an incomparably beautiful gaze, touching upon [the matter], said: 'Mother, do not succumb to anxiety! He is, at this very moment, about to bring Father and create the happiness of his own people!' [11] Then he said to his own mother: 'Alas, how will you also kill me? Trusting in me, protect her who is distinguished only by breath beyond mere breath!' [12] And then, all the elders, considering his words — from the precedent of the valor of the <s>Kāliya</s>-subduing — to be effortless and authoritative, made her rest. But:

children.text:
kiṃ svapnaḥ kim u jāgaraḥ? kim athavā mūrcchā kim unmāditā?
vety etat paricetum āpur asakṛd-buddhiṃ na tasmin janāḥ | kintūtkaṇṭhitatāvaguṇṭhita-hṛdāṃ teṣām abhūd vāg iyaṃ
hā hā śrī-vrajarāja hā bata hahā śrī-kṛṣṇa kutrāsi bhoḥ? ||JGc_1,20.1|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'Is this a dream or wakefulness? Or else a swoon, or a state of madness?' —
Thus those people were repeatedly unable to find certainty of understanding in that [situation];
but the speech of those whose hearts were shrouded by longing was this:
'Alas, alas, O glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>! Alas, ah! O glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, where are you?' // [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
janī-catuṣṭaya-dhṛtā pluṣṭa-cittā vrajeśvarī |
śvāsāstitā-tarka-pātraṃ hā hā mātraṃ jagāda sā ||JGc_1,20.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
[13] atha tuṅgācala-jala-cita-suraṅgā-praveśataḥ pracetaḥ-sadana-gatasya tasya vraja-lakṣmī-dayitasya caritam anupacaritam avadhāryatām |
 [14] yada tu te yādasāmpati-bhavanaṃ javataḥ śrī-vraja-rājam abhājayaṃs tadā sa ca tatra sacate sma | yathā ca,
children.translated_text:
The queen of <s>Vraja</s>, held by four women, her mind scorched,
whose breath alone was the object of inference —
only uttered 'Alas! Alas!' and nothing more! // [anuṣṭubh]
[13] Now let the unserved conduct of the lord of <s>Vraja's</s> splendor — who had entered the abode of <s>Pracetas</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>) through the water-filled tunnel of the lofty mountain — be duly attended to.
[14] When those [servants] of the lord of aquatic creatures caused the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> to be present swiftly in their master's palace, he (<s>Varuṇa</s>) was also attending upon him there. And as follows:

children.text:
snigdha-śyāma-rucy api krud-aruṇa-dyotād adṛśyaṃ vapur
dhvānta-dhvāṃsy api tīvratā-śavalanād dṛg-rodhanaṃ dṛg-dvayam |
kaumalyādi-guṇāpi roṣa-rabhasād ugrā tathā tasya gīḥ
kalpāntābhra-taḍid-dhvani-bhrama-dharān vismāpayante sma tān ||JGc_1,20.3||[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[15] tataś ca-bilaṃ valamānaḥ sa khalu jambukaḥ kva nu vartate? iti jalpa-kalanayā tasminn avajñā-vardhanasya śrīman-nanda-kula-samardhanasya bhṛśam ardidhiṣati dṛśam ardidiṣati ca tejasi bahula-kolāhala-pravāham avalambamānaḥ sva-gala-valayita-celatayā kṣmāmelita-bhālaḥ sarva-jala-pālaḥ śaṅkita-kaliḥ kalitāñjalir vidūra-bhū-gata evākhaṇḍa-daṇḍavat praṇanāma | [16] tasya cedṛśāt kharva-garvatāvalokanāt sarva eva tan-nāthās tathā prathāñcakruḥ | [17] tataś ca taruṇāruṇa-kamala-locanaḥ sarva-rocanaḥ karuṇayā puraḥ-saratām āsādya sadyas taṃ varuṇaṃ papraccha-te tu kutra parama-dharmācaraṇā madīya-pitṛ-caraṇāḥ? iti | [18] varuṇas tu galita-dhairya-sañjanaḥ sāñjalitayā sāntvaṃ vaco vyānañja-puruṣottama! yatra khalu tatra-bhavāṃs, tatra
param asāv asamaḥ parama-mahān sambhavati, nānyatra | kintu teṣām eṣāṃ kiṅkarāṇāṃ kiṃ karavāṇi śāsanam ātmanaś ceti tad anuśāsanam āśāse |
 [19] kṛṣṇaḥ sa-śānta-svāntam āha-varākāṇām eṣāṃ daṇḍaḥ kevalaṃ daṇḍayituṃ pauruṣaṃ khaṇḍayati | avilamba-sparśam eva tu darśayatāt tāta-caraṇa-sarojātam | [20] atha yathādiśanti dīrṇa-dīnādīnavās tatra-bhavantaḥ iti | [21] vāri-rājaḥ śrī-vraja-rāja-virājamāna-sadana-paryantaṃ panthānaṃ tac-caraṇa-mūlataḥ parama-dukūlānukūlaṃ cakāra, tatra nināya ca gopa-kula-nāyaka-kula-nāyakam | uvāca ca-govinda nīyatām eṣa pitā te pitṛ-vatsala [BhP 10.28.9] iti | [22] idam ahaṃ jānāmy eva, tat katham anyathā carāmi? kathaṃ vā parād asya parābhavaḥ syāt? iti bhāvaḥ | [23] tad evaṃ varuṇasya pāśād yad bhaya-pātrāyamāṇatvam, tasmād api sva-prabhāveṇa mocakasya tasya-

upalabhya ca saurabhyam alabhyasya sutasya saḥ |
abhyāyayau bahir-vṛttiṃ sabhyānāṃ vismayaṃ vahan ||JGc_1,20.4|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And he (<s>Nanda</s>), perceiving the fragrance of his unobtainable son,
returned to external consciousness, bearing the wonder of the assembly-members! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
unmīlayāmāsa vilocane sa
śrīman mukhaṃ tasya ca sandadarśa |
sandarśanād eva babhūva sāsraḥ
svapnāyitaṃ cāsravṛter amaṃsta ||JGc_1,20.5|| [indravajrā]
[24] kṛṣṇas tu tac-caraṇa-yugala-tala-sparśa-pūrvakaṃ tam āliṅgan unnamitavān-tāta, so' ham āgato' smi, ity adhigatavāṃś ca | 25] tatra dvayor api samagra-vyagratām āgacchator atha haris tu paritaḥ parīta-para-parīvāra-parīhāsa-śaṅkayā saṅkucita-cittas tatra cātmani ca bāṣpādi-vikāra-vyatiriktākāratām āsādayituṃ vyājahāra-tāta, paritaḥ samavadhīyatām | [26] atha vraja-sūtrāmā paritaḥ samīkṣya ca kutrāvām āgatau? iti sa-vailakṣyaṃ putrānanam īkṣate sma | [27] sa covāca-tāta, mā tanyatām anyathā-bhāvaḥ | yathāvrajanam eva sva-vrajaṃ vrajiṣyāvaḥ | tataḥ purataś caraṇa-kamalam avadhīyamānam ādhīyatām | [28] tatra tu tathā kurvati vyākulatākula-kāku-pūrvaṃ varuṇa uvāca-

kṛpālus tvam aho kṛṣṇa dvayor ekataraṃ kuru |
daṇḍaṃ vātha prasādaṃ vā nāparādhaṃ tu śeṣaya ||JGc_1,20.6|| [anuṣṭubh]
[29] tad evaṃ kṛta-yātratayā sthitayor api kṣaṇa-mātram avasthitayos tayor mahopacārāṃś caraṇāgrataḥ samarpitān ācaran praṇāmam ācacāra, cacāla ca sa tābhyāṃ saha yāvad-vivarābhyāsam | āgamya ca tad-abhyāsaṃ tad-vartma-bhāga-sthita-nīraṃ vibhāgam āgamayya tābhyāṃ saha vrajaṃ prati prahita-jana-prahita-mahitālaṅkṛti-mukha-paribarha-sambhṛti-muhūrta-sukha-pūrtitaḥ kṛta-kṛtyaṃ-manyatayā nṛtyann iva nivavṛte |
children.translated_text:
'You are compassionate, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — ah! — do one of two things:
either punishment or grace — but do not leave the offense remaining!' // [anuṣṭubh]
[29] Thus, even as those two stood still for but a moment while their departure had been arranged, he (<s>Varuṇa</s>), presenting great offerings at their feet, performed prostration, and accompanied them both up to the vicinity of the [exit] cavern. Having arrived at that vicinity, having parted the water that stood in the path of that passage, he, together with them both, [proceeded] toward <s>Vraja</s>, furnished with the arrangement of honorific adornments and personal accessories dispatched by the people sent ahead — filled with momentary happiness in the completion of his duty, considering himself as one who had accomplished his purpose — returned dancing as it were.

children.text:
tadā tīra-sthānā vraja-jani-janāḥ prāṇa-rahita-
prabhās tad-vartmekṣā-sthita-śithila-jīva-sthiti-daśāḥ |
pitā-putrau vārāmpati-cara-yutau nirvyathatayā
gatau dṛṣṭvā bhūyo' py ahaha sukha-tandrīm abhiyayuḥ ||JGc_1,20.7|| [śikhariṇī]
[30] kevalas tu baladevas tāv abhijagāma, praṇanāma ca vraja-rājam | datta-sukha-samāje vraja-rāje tu, tam upagūhya vismṛta-bāhyatayā kiñcana cāsamūhya kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ viramati | punaś ca rāme punaḥ punar namati, rāmānujaḥ sahasā sahasā parikramya parama-ramya-nija-sparśāmṛta-sparśanataḥ prathamaṃ mātaram eva kātaraḥ punar jīva-lokam ālokayāmāsa, kramaśas tv anyam anyam api |
children.translated_text:
Then the <s>Vraja</s>-born people standing on the bank, their radiance devoid of life-breath,
in a state of loosened life-condition, fixed upon watching for his path —
seeing the father and son, accompanied by a servant of the lord of waters, arriving without distress,
again — alas! — they attained the languor of happiness! // [śikhariṇī]
[30] <s>Baladeva</s> alone, however, went to meet those two and prostrated before the king of <s>Vraja</s>. And when the king of <s>Vraja</s>, having granted the assembly of happiness, embraced him, forgetting everything external, gathering something together, he rested for a few moments. And again, as <s>Rāma</s> bowed again and again, <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), suddenly and swiftly circumambulating, through the touch of the supremely delightful nectar of his own touch, first of all, anxiously, restored his mother to the world of the living, and gradually the others too.

children.text:
samāgate pitari harer ubhāv amū
milanty api vraja-janatāmilan mithaḥ |
tadā na sā paribubudhe paraṃ paraṃ
parantu tāv akhilam avait parāparam ||JGc_1,20.8|| [rucirā]
children.translated_text:
When the father of <s>Hari</s> arrived, both of these two,
though meeting, met with the <s>Vraja</s>-people together;
then she (<s>Yaśodā</s>) did not comprehend the supreme from the supreme —
but those two comprehended everything, both higher and lower! // [rucirā]

children.text:
hambā-rāvair jana-kalakalaiḥ svargataḥ puṣpa-pātair
vādyair nṛtyaiḥ stava-rava-śatair utthite' nyo' nya-marde |
śrīmān rāmaḥ paśu-samudayaṃ vārayan loka-vṛndaṃ
ślakṣṇālāpair api samucita-sthāna-niṣṭhaṃ cakāra ||JGc_1,20.9|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
With the lowing of cows, the clamor of people, the rain of flowers from heaven,
with music, dances, hundreds of praise-sounds, when mutual jostling arose —
the glorious <s>Rāma</s>, restraining the multitude of cattle and the host of people,
made them settle in their proper places, even with gentle words! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.9, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
tatra ca-
svayaṃ dattvā śubhrāsanam iha mahā-gopa-pataye
yathā-yogyaṃ cānyān vidadhad upaviṣṭān atha balaḥ |
upānta-prakrānta-sthitim anujam āpṛcchya paritaḥ
kathām etāṃ śṛṇvan paśupa-kulam aśrāvayad api ||JGc_1,20.10|| [śikhariṇī]
 [31] tatrātha datta-svātantryatayā viprān āmantrya paramānnādibhiḥ santarpya tad-abhīpsitāni vīpsayā samarpya, dvādaśyatikrama-bhiyā tat-pravaṇa-dhiyā vratam idam acchidra-pratham astv iti prārthya, gīrbhis tad-āśīrbhis tatra sāmarthyaṃ samartha-kṛtārthaṃ-manyās te dhanyā bahula-kutūhalataḥ sarva eva vrajam āvrajanti sma | [32] yatra vrajādhyakṣaḥ svayam adhvānaṃ vrajan, madhye-suta-dvayam abhrājiṣṭa | [33] atha kathakas tām etāṃ kathāṃ samāpayan śrī-vrajeśvaraṃ praty āha-
children.translated_text:
And there:
Having himself given a white seat here to the great lord of cowherds,
and duly arranging the others seated, <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>),
having asked leave of his younger brother who stood at the periphery,
himself listening to this tale, also made the cowherd clan hear it. // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.10, <s>śikharinī</s>]
[31] There, having invited the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with full freedom, having satisfied them with <s>paramānna</s> (sweet rice-pudding) and the like, having eagerly offered them their desired [gifts], and having prayed — with minds inclined toward the <s>Dvādaśī</s> (twelfth-day observance) — out of fear of transgressing it, "May this vow remain unbroken and foremost!" — blessed by the benedictions of their sacred words, those blessed ones, considering their goals fulfilled, with abundant curiosity, all proceeded toward <s>Vraja</s>. [32] Where the superintendent of <s>Vraja</s>, himself walking the road, shone with his pair of sons in the middle. [33] Then the narrator, concluding this tale, said to the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>:

children.text:
pāśi-pāśena sambandhas tvayy āsīn neti kā kathā |
tad-bhayenāpi nāsīt tvat-putrasyāsya prabhāvataḥ ||JGc_1,20.11||tad uktaṃ varuṇenāsya karuṇāṃ vīrya-bhīruṇā |
govinda nīyatām eṣa pitā te pitṛ-vatsalaḥ ||JGc_1,20.12|| iti | [anuṣṭubh]
[34] atha dināntare kṛṣṇam antareṇa sabhāntare niviṣṭā gopa-kula-śiṣṭā vraja-patiṃ prati tatratyaṃ citraṃ papracchuḥ | [35] sa ca loka-pālasya tasya taṃ mahodayam aihika-lokānām āloka-pathātītam astokaṃ ślokayāmāsa | tatra ca-mitrāṇi, citraṃ śrūyatām iti tad-vāsināṃ kṛṣṇe bhaktim atiriktāṃ varṇayāmāsa | [36] tad-varṇanāntaraṃ tu nija-nijam antaram anu vismitānāṃ tasminn īśvaratālambhaka-sambhāvanayā sarveṣām eva seyaṃ bhāvanā-yadi cānaśvara-pratipatti-vaśād ayam īśvaras, tathāpy autpattika-sneha-sampatti-viṣayāśrayatā-maya-nirāmaya-sukha-dāyīti tu sadā mukhya-vyatīta-sarva-tarṣaṃ samutkarṣaṃ draṣṭuṃ suṣṭhu muhur ullasaty eva naś ceto-vṛttiḥ | tac ca kim anena nirbādhaṃ sādhayiṣyate? iti | [37] eṣa cāśeṣāṇām eṣāṃ
svāpara-paryāya-jñātitayā svābhedena vijñāyamānānām etad abhijñāya, kāruṇya-jāta-yantraṇayā śīghratā-paratantratayā cintitavān- [38] aho, ete ca te te mama parama-svajanā, mayi pāramaiśvaryaṃ paryālocya sarvato' py asambhavaṃ mad-vaibhavam anubhavitum icchanti, kintu nānubhavanti yata eva loka-pāla-vaibhava-mātraṃ camatkāra-pātraṃ kurvanti | tādṛśaṃ tad vaibhavaṃ punar eṣāṃ svagati-mayam eva | tat tu tan-mayam api yan nānubhavanti, tat khalv avidyā-kāma-karma-nirmitoccāvaca-gatimati jagati viracitam avatāram anu sarva-sādhāraṇaṃ-manyatayā buddhi-bādhāta eva | sā caiṣām,
children.translated_text:
"The lord of <s>Pāśin</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>, bearer of the noose) — was there a relationship through his noose with you? — that is no question!
There was no fear of that, either, because of the prowess of this your son!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.11]
"Thus spoke <s>Varuṇa</s> — with compassion and awe of his valor:
"O <s>Govinda</s>, let this father of yours be led back — he who is devoted to his father!"" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.12, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
[34] Then, on the following day, the distinguished members of the cowherd clan, seated in the assembly without <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, asked the lord of <s>Vraja</s> about the wonders that had occurred there. [35] And he praised at length the great glory of that world-protector (<s>Varuṇa</s>) — surpassing the perceptual path of this-worldly folk. And there: "Friends, hear the wonder!" — thus he described the exceptional devotion of those dwellers toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. [36] Then, after that description, as all were inwardly amazed, this thought arose in all of them through the attribution of lordship to him — "Even if this one is the Lord by virtue of his imperishable nature, nevertheless, the bestowal of unfailing, healthy happiness — consisting of the shelter of inherent affection's wealth — always supremely flourishes in our mental disposition, seeing the eminence that surpasses all thirst, beyond the principal [considerations]. And will this be accomplished by him without obstruction?" [37] And he, who was known without distinction through the identity of those who knew themselves as his alternating kinsmen — understanding this, impelled by the compulsion born of compassion and subject to the urgency of swiftness, reflected: [38] "Ah! These various people are my supreme kinsmen, and contemplating supreme lordship in me, they desire to experience my glory — impossible from every perspective — yet they do not experience it, since they marvel at the mere glory of a world-protector. Such glory, however, is itself inherent in their own nature. But that they do not experience it even though it is identical with them — this is indeed because of the general belief that in a world fashioned of higher and lower states, created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>karma</s> (action), an incarnation that has descended is to be considered common — it is an obstruction of the intellect. And that [obstruction] in them is:"

children.text: iti nandādayo gopāḥ kṛṣṇa-rāma-kathāṃ mudā |
children.translated_text: "Thus <s>Nanda</s> and the other cowherds, joyfully"

children.text: kurvanto ramamāṇāś ca nāvindan bhava-vedanām ||[BhP 10.11.58]
children.translated_text: "narrating the tales of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, sporting, did not perceive the suffering of [material] existence!" // [BhP 10.11.58]

children.text:
kṛṣṇe' rpitātma-suhṛd-artha-kalatra-kāmāḥ [BhP 10.16.10] iti | kṛṣṇe kamala-patrākṣe sannyastākhila-rādhasaḥ [BhP 10.65.6] iti |
[39] tathā ca-
children.translated_text:
"They who had offered their selves, friends, wealth, wives, and desires to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" [BhP 10.16.10]; "They who had surrendered all prosperity to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lotus-petal-eyed one" [BhP 10.65.6].
[39] And accordingly:

children.text: eṣāṃ ghoṣa-nivāsinām uta bhavān kiṃ devarāteti naś
children.translated_text: "Of these dwellers of <s>Ghoṣa</s> (the cowherd settlement), or indeed, O <s>Devarāta</s>, is you —"

children.text: ceto viśva-phalāt phalaṃ tvad-aparaṃ kutrāpy ayan muhyati |
children.translated_text: "our mind is confused about where there might be a fruit other than you, from the fruit of the universe;"

children.text: sad-veṣād iva pūtanāpi sa-kulā tvām eva devāpitā
children.translated_text: "even <s>Pūtanā</s>, though in the guise of virtue, with her clan, attained you, O Lord of the gods —"

children.text: yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tvat-kṛte ||[10.14.35]
children.translated_text: "for whose abode, wealth, friends, beloveds, self, children, and life-breaths exist for your sake!" // [BhP 10.14.35]

children.text:
ity ādibhiḥ pramita-sarvopari-mad-vaśīkāri-prema-mahimnāṃ yadyapi nāvidyādi-mayī, tathāpy eṣām anya-sādhāraṇaṃ-manyatām asahamāno' haṃ madīya-prema-sandoha-maya-mohābhilāṣa-lālanā-jālataḥ sañjāyamānām apy etāṃ tan-mayīm eva manye | [40] vastutas tu tādṛśa-premarṇenānādi-kalpata evānyebhyaḥ prattānavakāśām uttamarṇatāṃ gatānām apy eṣāṃ mayy arpita-sarvārthānāṃ gatir eva mama gatis, tad-anugatam eva ca mama paramaṃ vaibhavam, na punar ataḥ param api paraṃ sambhavati | [41] tad evaṃ jalāvitur vaibhavād api pitur mama yaś camatkāraḥ, sa tu māṃ duḥkhākaroti | tasmād eteṣāṃ yathā mayi premāveśas tathā naiteṣu mameti tad-anusandhānavatā mayā tad etad eṣām eva vaibhavam eteṣām eva śubhānudhyāna-maya-yogamāyānubhavataḥ
sāmpratam enān anubhāvayāni iti | [42] tad etad vicintanānantaraṃ dinānantare punar ādi-varāha-purāṇa-vācaka-yācaka-vipra-dvārā-pura-dvārāsthānī-sthitika-vicitra-pitrādy-ābhīra-vīra-pariṣadaṃ prati-kārtika-varti-pūrṇimā-snānam akrūrābhīṣṭa-prade brahma-hrade tūrṇam eva pūrṇa-tat-phalatāṃ sādhayati ity avadhārayan, sāratayā dhārayaṃs tat-prātaḥ sarvāṃs tān dāyādādīn ādāya satrā tatrāgatavān | [43] āgatya ca sarveṇa saha tatra nimajjya, tam utsṛjya, tīram āsajya, prakṛtitaḥ paratayā sac-cid-ānanda-ghanaṃ parama-svarūpa-rūpa-rasa-gandha-sparśa-śabdatayātmārāmāṇām apy alabhya-ghanaṃ gopānāṃ sva-niketam etaṃ golokam āvaraka-śaktim apākṛtya vyaktīkṛtavān |
 [44] tiraskariṇīṃ nirākṛtya vicitraṃ divya-citram iva yaṃ khalv asya narākṛti-para-brahmaṇaḥ sva-lokatayā brahmaṇo loka ity ācakṣate | [45] yatra kila sveṣām eva madhyam adhyāsitaṃ nija-kula-tilaka-kṛṣṇākāratayā paricitaṃ kṛta-janmādi-gokula-līlā-stuti-śruti-sākṣikatayātiniścitaṃ tam etaṃ sa-lokam ālokayan vraja-lokaḥ sarva-śokaṃ vyatītya, vismayānanda-sandohataḥ pratikṣaṇam eva sukha-saṃroham avāpa | [46] tad evaṃ vyajya rajyan-manasas tān vraja-lokān golokataḥ sa daiteyārir daiteyapīḍanādi-krīḍāṃ pūrayituṃ punar vyavadhāpitavāṃś ca | [47] atha kathakaḥ samāpanam āha-
children.translated_text:
"Thus, by these and such [verses], though those whose love-grandeur conquering even me from the supreme height above all is well-established — though not made of <s>avidyā</s> and the like — nevertheless, I, unable to bear their belief of commonality with others, consider this [avidyā] — though arising from the web of the desire for the bewilderment born of the flood of my own love — as identical with it. [40] But in truth, by the debt of such love, having from the beginningless cycle attained the status of creditors — with no room [for others] to advance before them — the course of these [devotees] who have surrendered all purposes to me is indeed my own course; and my supreme glory follows theirs — and nothing beyond this can possibly exist. [41] Thus, the wonder that arose in my father from the glory of the lord of waters — that causes me distress. Therefore, just as their love-absorption is in me, so is mine in them — and by me, who traces this, this very glory of theirs, from the experience of their own auspicious meditation composed of <s>Yogamāyā</s>,
I shall now cause them to experience it." [42] Thus, after this reflection, on the following day — through the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> intermediary who was the petitioner-reciter of the <s>Ādi Varāha Purāṇa</s>, and was stationed at the city gate — determining that the full-moon bathing in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, at the <s>Brahma-hrada</s> (Brahmā's pool) — which grants the desires of <s>Akrūra</s> — would swiftly accomplish the complete fruition of that [goal], and holding fast to its essence, early that morning, taking all his kinsmen and others, he came there in a body. [43] And having come, having bathed there together with all, having left them, having reached the shore, from his natural transcendence — the dense <s>sac-cid-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), the form of his supreme essential nature with its inherent taste, scent, touch, and sound — being an unattainable treasure even for those who are <s>ātmārāmas</s> (self-delighting) — he, removing the concealing potency from this <s>Goloka</s>, the cowherds' own abode, made it manifest.
[44] Having removed the curtain of concealment, he made visible what was wondrous, like a divine painting — which they indeed call the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, being the own world of this supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form. [45] Where, beholding this [<s>Goloka</s>] together with its world — recognized as seated in their very midst, in the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>tilaka</s>-ornament of their own clan, and thoroughly ascertained by the testimony of the <s>śruti</s> hymns praising the sports of birth and so forth performed in <s>Gokula</s> — the <s>Vraja</s>-folk, having surpassed all grief, through the flood of astonished bliss, at every moment attained the growth of happiness. [46] Thus, having made the <s>Vraja</s>-folk — whose hearts were delighted — perceive [<s>Goloka</s>], the enemy of the <s>Daityas</s>, in order to fulfill his sport of tormenting the <s>Daityas</s>, again veiled it. [47] Then the narrator spoke the conclusion:

children.text:
īdṛg vrajeśa putras te jita-lokeśa-lokakaḥ |
yas tvāṃ ca tava lokaṃ ca lokam etam alokayat ||JGc_1,20.13|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
"Such a son is yours, O lord of <s>Vraja</s> — the conqueror of the lord of worlds and his worlds;
he who revealed to you and your world this very world!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.13, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
adhi goloke gopāḥ svayam adhi gopeṣu golokaḥ |
iti kalayan vanamālī yas taṃ vyānañja taṃ naumi ||JGc_1,20.14|| [upagīti]||
children.translated_text:
"The cowherds rest upon <s>Goloka</s>, and <s>Goloka</s> rests upon the cowherds" —
thus perceiving, the wearer of the forest-garland (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — who revealed this — I praise him! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.14, <s>upagīti</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ prātaḥ-kathāyāṃ prayātāyāṃ vibhāvarī-kathā vibhāti sma | yathā snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the morning tale had concluded, the evening tale shone forth. As <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text:
yadā yātaḥ pitrā saha varuṇa-lokaṃ harir asau
tadā rādhādīnāṃ sthitir iha mṛṣā kā prathayitā |
jaḍānāṃ jāḍyaṃ syād asukha-sukha-buddhis tu sudhiyāṃ
na śūnyasya prāptiṃ bhajati paritaḥ kāpi ca daśā ||JGc_1,20.15|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"When <s>Hari</s> had gone to <s>Varuṇa's</s> world with his father,
then the state of <s>Rādhā</s> and others here — what falsity shall be proclaimed?
For the dull, there would be dullness; but the perception of unhappiness-as-happiness belongs to the wise;
no state at all attains the attainment of emptiness!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.15, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text:
yadāyāsīt kṛṣṇaḥ kila varuṇa-lokaṃ pitṛ-kṛte
tadā śrī-rādhāyāḥ śvasitam amunā sārdham agamat |
yadāyāsīt tasmād ayam atha tadā tatra sahasā
samāgād ity eṣā param iha kavīnāṃ sukavitā ||JGc_1,20.16|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> went to <s>Varuṇa's</s> world for his father's sake,
then the breath of the glorious <s>Rādhā</s> departed along with him;
when he returned from there, then suddenly
hers too arrived" — this, they say, is the finest poetry of the poets! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.16, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
āyāte tu vraja-pati-sute pāśi-lokāt tadā kāpy
ekā rādhām anu tam anu ca snigdha-bhāvā vidagdhā |
autsukyaṃ tad dvayam anu niśi śrāvayantī dvi-niṣṭhaṃ
ceto-vṛtter mukham iva tayor añjasā jāyate sma ||JGc_1,20.17|| [śārdūla]
[49] tatra śrī-rādhā-niṣṭham, tad yathā-
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
When the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> returned from the world of <s>Pāśin</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>), a certain
one — tender-hearted, witty — following <s>Rādhā</s> and then following him,
making both of them hear the eagerness that was twofold in devotion,
became as if the very face of the mental activity of those two! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.17, <s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
[49] There, that which was devoted to the glorious <s>Rādhā</s>, as follows:

children.text:
yadi māṃ nayasi vidhātar
lokāntaram antarā sevām |
naya māṃ tan-mukha-suṣamā-
sa-sukhāṃ virahān na duḥkhitāṃ tasya ||JGc_1,20.18|| [udgīti]
[50] śrī-kṛṣṇa-niṣṭhaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text:
"If you, O Creator, take me to another world
without the opportunity of his service,
then take me together with the happiness of the beauty of his face,
not distressed by separation from him!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.18, <s>udgīti</s>]
[50] That which was devoted to the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows:

children.text:
ānītāḥ pitṛ-caraṇā vāruṇa-lokāt prananditā lokāḥ |
hā rādhā mama śokād bādhā-gīrṇā na jīrṇāsti ||JGc_1,20.19|| [āryā]
 [51] atra kākvā jīrṇāsty eveti sambhāvyate | [52] tad evaṃ sā tasyāṃ tasminn api rahasi nivedya viśeṣataḥ śrīkṛṣṇam apy upālabdhavatī, yathā-
children.translated_text:
"My father's feet have been brought from <s>Varuṇa's</s> world; the people are delighted!
Alas, <s>Rādhā</s> — my grief and its impediment, swallowed up, is not digested!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.19, <s>āryā</s>]
[51] Here, by the tone of sarcasm, it is to be understood as: "it is indeed digested!" [52] Thus, she, having communicated to <s>Rādhā</s> and to him privately and especially, also reproached the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows:

children.text:
rāgaṃ vināsti hṛdayaṃ mādhava tava rocate ca tat tubhyam |
iti niyataṃ kanakāṅgī pāṇḍū-bhavati sphuṭaṃ rādhā ||JGc_1,20.20|| [āryā]
[53] tataś ca tasya sneha-vaśād deha-dravī-bhāvaṃ vyavasya punaḥ prahasya provāca-
children.translated_text:
"Without passion, your heart exists, O <s>Mādhava</s>, and that pleases you!"
Thus, inevitably, the golden-limbed <s>Rādhā</s> visibly turns pale! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.20, <s>āryā</s>]
[53] Then, having concluded from the tenderness of love that his body was melting, she laughed again and said:

children.text:
bhavān guṇī mādhava rādhikāpi sā
yenātidūrād api suṣṭhu kṛṣyate |
rādhāpi bāḍhaṃ sarasā nijālayād apy
evam ārdrīkriyate yayā bhavān ||JGc_1,20.21|| [upajāti 12]
[54] madhukaṇṭha uvāca-keyaṃ vṛddhā? yatas tatra nānya-janasya praveśaḥ sambhavatīti pūrvaṃ nirṇītam | [55] snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sahāsam āha-paurṇamāsy eva nānā-veśena tatra praveśatīti | [56] atha tadārabhya-
children.translated_text:
"You are virtuous, O <s>Mādhava</s>, and that <s>Rādhikā</s> too is such
that she is well drawn even from a great distance;
and <s>Rādhā</s> too is truly full of <s>rasa</s> — from her own abode,
thus you are made moist by her!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.21, <s>upajāti</s>]
[54] <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: "Who is this elderly woman? For it was previously established that no other person can enter there." [55] <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said with laughter: "It is <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> herself who enters there in various guises!" [56] Then, from that time onward:

children.text:
niśīthaṃ niśīthaṃ tadāsau prakarṣād
agāsīn muralyeti tathyaṃ mṛṣā na |
amūs tu pratīyuḥ sphuṭaṃ marma-bhedī
sa vā kaḥ śarair yaś chinatty āśu sarvam ||JGc_1,20.22|| [bhujaṅgaprayātā]
children.translated_text:
"Deeper and deeper into the night, from that time, that [flute-sound]
came forth intensely — 'it is the <s>muralī</s> (flute)' — this is truth, not falsehood!
But these [<s>gopīs</s>] perceived it clearly: 'It is a piercer of the vital points!'
Or who is that one, who with arrows swiftly cuts through everything?" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.22, <s>bhujaṅgaprayātā</s>]

children.text:
niveśe saṃveśe mathi pathi jane pāthasi vane
harir yady apy udyan pratiharitam eva sphuritavān |
sphuṭaṃ draṣṭuṃ spraṣṭuṃ tadapi tad-alabdher vidhurajād
dadhe rādhā-bādhā tad-anadhigamād apy adhikatām ||JGc_1,20.23|| [śikhariṇī]||
children.translated_text:
In the house, in the bed, on the path, among people, in water, in the forest —
though <s>Hari</s>, rising, manifested as if reflected everywhere,
clearly, to see, to touch — yet from the non-attainment of that, from the agitation [of the mind-moon],
<s>Rādhā's</s> affliction grew even greater than [the affliction from] the non-attainment of him! // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.23, <s>śikharinī</s>]

children.text: atha samāpanam-
children.translated_text: Then the conclusion:

children.text:
īdṛśas te patiḥ śyāme yat-kāntes tvaṃ parā gatiḥ |
atrābhilāṣaḥ śobhā vā kāntir ity adhigamyatām ||JGc_1,20.24|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
"Such is your husband, O dark one, for whose beauty you are the supreme destination!
Whether the desire here is beauty or radiance — let that be understood!" // [<s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.20.24, <s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
varuṇalokāloka-camatkāra-tiraskāraka-golokāvalokanaṃ nāma
viṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||20||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Twentieth Chapter, named
"The Wonder-Eclipsing Vision of <s>Goloka</s> —
Surpassing the Spectacle of <s>Varuṇa's</s> World."
||20||

children.text: athaikaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the Twenty-first Chapter.

children.text: kumārī-vastra-haraṇa-sukumārī-samasta-karṣaṇam
children.translated_text:
The Stealing of the Maidens' Garments —
the Drawing of All Tender Ones.

children.text: tadānīṃ punaḥ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> again spoke:

children.text: atha garga-kṛta-vraja-varga-bheda-maya-samayataḥ paścād udbhūtāḥ kāścid anyāś ca dhanyāḥ prabhūtā nānā-kula-prasūtā yā vraja-kumārikāḥ svabhāvataḥ kṛṣṇa-bhāvānusārikās tāsāṃ kaumāra-pāram ārabhya vāsanā varṇanīyā yathā,
children.translated_text: "Now, after the time determined by <s>Garga</s> for the division of the <s>Vraja</s> community, those other blessed, abundant maidens of <s>Vraja</s> — born from various clans — who naturally followed the sentiments of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, their yearnings from the end of childhood onward are to be described, as follows:"

children.text:
kumārīṇāṃ tāsāṃ aghajiti patiḥ syād iti rucir
yadā jātā tarhi pratipadam upāyākṛta-dhiyām |
vidhu-śrīṇāṃ śaśvad bata bahula-pakṣa-sthiti-juṣāṃ
tamaskṛd-viśvasminn ahaha kṛśatā nityam ajani ||JGc_1,21.1|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
'When the maidens' desire arose that the enemy of <s>Agha</s> should be their husband,
then, for those whose intellects were fashioned into devices of strategy at every step,
for those who always dwelt in the state of the full [bright] fortnight — possessing moon-like splendor —
alas, a thinness [of the moon, i.e., the dark fortnight of longing] was forever born, creating darkness in the entire world!' ||21.1|| [śikhariṇī]

children.text: tataś ca tad-artham anurahasaṃ nānā-devatām arthayamānā vyartham iva bhramanti sma |
children.translated_text: Then, for that purpose, they wandered about in secret, propitiating various deities — seemingly in vain.

children.text: prārthanā ceyaṃ-
children.translated_text: And this was their prayer:

children.text:
vrajeśitroḥ sadma vāsaḥ paraṃ śvasuratānayoḥ |
kṛṣṇa eva patir bhūyān mama janmani janmani ||JGc_1,21.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Let the home of the lord and queen of <s>Vraja</s> be the supreme abode — of the in-laws and the son;
may <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone be my husband, in birth after birth!' ||21.2|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś ca kadācit kālindīm anu parasparaṃ vindamānā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then once, along the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), they chanced to find one another.

children.text: yuktaṃ ca tat, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And that was fitting, because:

children.text:
ekaṃ padam uddeśyaṃ
bhavati samantād bahūnāṃ cet |
vividha-bhuvām api teṣāṃ
milanaṃ ghaṭate yathā sa-tīrthānām ||JGc_1,21.3|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
'When one single destination is the aim
of many from various places,
then even their meeting comes about —
as with those [who go] to the same sacred ford (<s>tīrtha</s>)!' ||21.3|| [udgīti]

children.text: militānāṃ tāsāṃ parasparaṃ hārdam api jātam | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: When they had met, heartfelt affection also arose among them mutually. For indeed:

children.text:
diśi diśi jātāḥ snigdhā vyatimilitāḥ suṣṭhu bibhrati sneham |
medura-mudira-samūhe muhur api yasmāt tathā dṛṣṭam ||JGc_1,21.4|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
'Those born in various quarters, who are affectionate, when they meet closely, bear love well;
for even in a mass of dense, wet clouds, this is repeatedly seen!' ||21.4|| [āryā]

children.text: tatra jāte cāsauhārde hārdam api parasparaṃ vyaktam | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And when that friendship had arisen, their innermost feelings too became mutually manifest. Because:

children.text:
hnutam apy ekāśrayiṇāṃ
hṛdayaṃ vyaktiṃ mitho yāti |
tat tu vyatimilitaṃ ced
vada tarhi syāt pidhānaṃ kim? ||JGc_1,21.5|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'Even if concealed, the hearts of those who share a single refuge
become mutually manifest;
but if they have met each other,
then tell — what concealment could there be?' ||21.5|| [upagīti]

children.text:
tataś ca parasparaṃ hṛd-bāṣpam udgīrṇavatīnāṃ dṛg-bāṣpam api vikīrṇavatīnāṃ tāsāṃ daśānta-daśāvaśāṅgatayā sambhāvyamānānām anukṣaṇaṃ sukhā-kāṅkṣiṇī pārikāṅkṣiṇī-veśa-viśeṣaṃ vindamānā tatra vṛndā gatā |
[10] sā hy evaṃ purā cintitavatī-rāga eva khalv āsāṃ vrajanāgarasya tasya samāgamāya vāgagocaraśaktibhāg avasīyate |
children.translated_text:
Then, as they poured forth the tears of the heart to one another, and also scattered the tears of the eyes, and as they were being perceived as assuming the state at the edge of the final state [of desperation] — <s>Vṛndā</s>, who moment by moment was assuming the special guise of an attendant seeking their happiness, came there.
[10] For she had previously reflected thus: 'Love alone is determined to be the possessor of a power beyond the reach of speech for the union of these [maidens] with that gallant of <s>Vraja</s>.'

children.text: rāgaś ca loka-rīti-maya-praṇayata eva jāgarūkatayā garīyān varīvartīti devatāntarārādhanam eva sādhayitavyam, na tu tad-ārādhanam iti |
children.translated_text: 'And love, being indeed superior through its wakefulness surpassing even love born of worldly convention, revolves [supremely] — therefore the worship of another deity must be accomplished, not the worship of that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself].'

children.text: athāgamya ca tat-kṛtābhivādana-sva-kṛtābhivadana-vidhau labdha-vidhau sābhidadhāti sma-[13] aham atraiva vane vasantī bhavatīnāṃ bhāvavatīnām avasthāḥ paśyantī dayā-vidīrṇa-hṛdayā samāyātāsmi | tad iyaṃ mama siddhā vidyā sva-karṇānubiddhā vidhīyatām | nātiprayāsa-bhāvitatā ca bhavatīnāṃ bhavitā, kintu māsa-mātram atra śramābhāsaḥ | [14] sā khalu mantra-mayī yogamāyā mayā dayāvatī sādhitāstīti |
children.translated_text: And having arrived, when the ritual of their salutations to her and her address to them was duly accomplished, she declared: [13] 'I, dwelling in this very forest, seeing the states of you, possessors of deep emotion, have come with a heart split by compassion. Therefore, let this perfected art of mine, pierced into my own ears [by tradition], be applied! And the effort required of you will not be too great — merely a semblance of exertion for one month. [14] That <s>Yogamāyā</s>, consisting of <s>mantras</s>, has been mastered by me through her compassion.'

children.text: tad evaṃ tāsāṃ karṇa-vivaram anu mantra-varṇān nidhivan nidhāya tad-vidhim api sa-vidhim abhidhāya mudāntar-hitavatī sāntarhitavatī | tataś ca tās tad-upadeśa-lagnāḥ parama-sukha-magnā babhūvuḥ | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, having deposited the syllables of the <s>mantra</s> into the aperture of their ears, like treasures, and having expounded its ritual procedure with proper method, she joyfully became hidden and disappeared. And then they, devoted to her instruction, became immersed in supreme happiness. Because:

children.text:
nityaṃ tāvad analpa-rāga-mahimā sarvaṃ sahāyīyati
prāpnoty eṣa tu yogya-kalpam atha ced dhatte sad-ullāsitām |
tasmiṃs tādṛg abhūd guruḥ svayam asau śaktiḥ parā vaiṣṇavī
pūjyā mantra-varaś ca vāñchita-dharas tāsām itaḥ kiṃ sukham? ||JGc_1,21.6|| [śārdūla]

ataevāmūr viśramya mārgaśīrṣīya-śirṣāyāmāṇatā-labhya-pratipadam ārabhya saṃgatya vratam ārabdhavatyaḥ | yatrāruṇa-kṛtāruṇa-guṇa-prasaram avasaram anu parasparaṃ gṛha-visarataḥ samākāraṇāparā vyatibaddha-karā yamunā-gamana-tat-parā gāna-parāyaṇā babhūvuḥ; yatra paraspara-parīhāsa-prāyatayā nijābhiprāyaṃ vyañjayāmāsuḥ | yathā-
children.translated_text: Therefore, these [maidens], having rested, beginning from each first day [of the month] that was approaching the summit of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, having assembled together, commenced their vow. Wherein, following the occasion that spread the quality of dawn-redness upon redness, they — summoning one another from their respective homes, hands interlocked, devoted to going to the <s>Yamunā</s>, absorbed in singing — expressed their own intention through mutual teasing. As follows:

children.text: tvām upayantā sakhi vanamālī |
children.translated_text: 'The forest-garlanded one (<s>Vanamālī</s>) shall marry you, O friend!

children.text: sakala-śubhākara-vara-guṇa-śālī ||dhru||
children.translated_text: He of all auspicious, excellent, virtuous qualities! ||refrain||

children.text:
yatra vraja-patir ita-rucir ucitām
vārtāṃ cālayitā sukha-sacitām ||a||
children.translated_text:
Where the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, of pleasing beauty,
will set in motion the fitting, joy-filled tidings!

children.text: śrutvā tat tava mātara-pitarau
children.translated_text: Hearing that, your mother and father

children.text: sukham ayitārau kṛta-dhana-vitarau |
children.translated_text: will attain happiness, having dispensed their wealth!

children.text: harir api mudam iha hṛdi gopayitā
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> too will conceal his delight here in his heart —

children.text: sakhibhir narmaṇi yaḥ kopayitā ||b||
children.translated_text: he who is provoked to anger by friends in jest!

children.text: gaṇaka-nidiṣṭa-tare sudināhe
children.translated_text: On the most auspicious day determined by the astrologer,

children.text: veśaṃ dhāsyati sa nijavivāhe |
children.translated_text: he will assume his wedding attire!

children.text: nīla-rucī-cita-gaura-dukūlam
children.translated_text: A fair silk cloth studded with blue splendor —

children.text: ghana-capalābhirucām iva mūlam ||c||
children.translated_text: like the very root of the radiance of lightning in a cloud!

children.text: antara-vasanaga-kañcuka-pītaṃ
children.translated_text: An inner garment-bodice of yellow,

children.text: citra-pracchada-ruci-parivītam |
children.translated_text: enveloped by the luster of a variegated coverlet!

children.text: mukuṭa-kirīṭa-tirīṭa-virājam
children.translated_text: Resplendent with crown, diadem, and tiara,

children.text: alakāvali-maṇi-citraka-bhājam ||d||
children.translated_text: adorned with rows of jeweled locks of hair!

children.text: kuṇḍala-maṇḍita-gaṇḍa-vibhāgam
children.translated_text: With cheek-portions adorned by earrings,

children.text: tāmbūla-cchavi-jid-adhara-surāgam |
children.translated_text: with a lower lip whose deep color conquers that of betel-leaves!

children.text: adharāvṛtaye kara-dhṛta-celam
children.translated_text: With a cloth held in hand covering the lower lip,

children.text: graiveyakam anukṛta-maṇi-melam ||e||
children.translated_text: a necklace imitating an assemblage of jewels!

children.text: sāṅgada-kaṅkaṇa-mudrika-hastam
children.translated_text: With hands bearing armlets, bracelets, and rings,

children.text: āvāpaka-dhṛti-valayita-śastam |
children.translated_text: beautifully praised by the firmness of the finger-rings!

children.text: hāravalita-hṛdi dhṛta-maṇi-rājam
children.translated_text: With a jeweled pendant adorning the heart encircled by garlands,

children.text: vanamālādika-mālya-samājam ||f||
children.translated_text: an assembly of garlands beginning with the forest-garland (<s>vanamālā</s>)!

children.text: maṇimaya-śṛṅkhala-lasad-avalagnam
children.translated_text: With jeweled anklet-chains gleaming and dangling,

children.text: caraṇa-vibhūṣaṇa-gaṇa-ruci-magnam |
children.translated_text: immersed in the luster of hosts of foot-ornaments!

children.text: veṣe cāsminn etad apūrvam
children.translated_text: And in this attire, this is unprecedented —

children.text: yat tu na dṛṣṭaṃ kvacana ca pūrvam ||g||
children.translated_text: that which was never before seen anywhere!

children.text: aṅgaṃ bhūṣaṇam api kila sarvam
children.translated_text: His very limbs are indeed all ornaments,

children.text: sarvābharaṇaṃ svayam iti garvam |
children.translated_text: and every ornament is itself [merely] a boast!

children.text: atha maṇi-śakaṭādhiṣṭhitam etam
children.translated_text: Then, mounted upon a jeweled cart,

children.text: kalayiṣyanti suhṛdbhir upetam ||h||
children.translated_text: they will behold him, accompanied by friends!

children.text: taṃ janyānāṃ śakaṭa-parītam
children.translated_text: Him, surrounded by the carts of the wedding-party,

children.text: kusumair varṣiṣyanti sagītam |
children.translated_text: they will shower with flowers, with songs!

children.text: śakaṭa-dhvani-yuta-vādya-śatena
children.translated_text: By the hundred musical instruments joined with the cart-sounds,

children.text: mudam āpsyati sa svayam api tena ||i||
children.translated_text: he himself too will attain delight thereby!

children.text: tad-dhvani-kalanāt tava sakhi cittam
children.translated_text: From the perception of those sounds, your heart, O friend,

children.text: dhṛtam api yatnād bhavitā bhittam |
children.translated_text: though held firm with effort, will be split!

children.text: sa yadā gantā dvāra-sadeśam
children.translated_text: When he comes to the vicinity of the doorway,

children.text: sakhi visṛjeḥ sukha-mūrcchā-veśam ||j||
children.translated_text: O friend, you will release the swoon of joy!

children.text: tam upavrajitā sā tava goṣṭhī strī
children.translated_text: That community of women will approach you,

children.text: tatir api gāsyati bimboṣṭhī |
children.translated_text: the row of ruby-lipped ones will sing too!

children.text: upayānaṃ tad-vādya-vitānam
children.translated_text: That canopy of musical instruments for the wedding procession,

children.text: gāli-prāyaṃ tad api ca gānam ||k||
children.translated_text: and that song too — [will be] mostly teasing!

children.text: sārātrika-nirmañchana-dṛṣṭiṃ
children.translated_text: Those performing the <s>ārātrika</s> (lamp-waving) and the <s>nīrājana</s> (lustration) with their gaze

children.text: kartāras te sa-kusuma-vṛṣṭim |
children.translated_text: will create a shower of flowers upon you!

children.text: maṇḍapa-varam upanīte śyāme
children.translated_text: When the dark one (<s>Śyāma</s>) is brought to the fine wedding pavilion,

children.text: sukha-sammardo bhavitā rāme ||l||
children.translated_text: there will be a joyful press of the delightful <s>Rāma</s>!

children.text: gopendrādika-gaṇa-pūjām anu
children.translated_text: After the worship of <s>Gopendra</s> (<s>Nanda</s>) and the assembly,

children.text: narma-kutūhalam udayed varatanu |
children.translated_text: a playful curiosity will arise, O beautiful-bodied one!

children.text: pūrvaṃ vidhim api kṛtvā sadvidhi
children.translated_text: Having first performed the proper rites duly,

children.text: āneṣyanti tvām iha sahanidhi ||m||
children.translated_text: they will bring you here with your treasure!

children.text: varapuratas tvāṃ śithilitagātrīm
children.translated_text: Before the bridegroom, you — with limbs gone slack —

children.text: sthāpayitāraḥ priyaratipātrīm |
children.translated_text: they will station, O vessel of beloved delight!

children.text: tātas tava karam atha dadhad abalam
children.translated_text: Then your father, placing your delicate hand,

children.text: grāhayitā varakaram anu sajalam ||n||
children.translated_text: will make [you] grasp the bridegroom's hand, with tears!

children.text:
tatra ca bhavatī sumukhi sukhena
kim bhaviteti jñātā kena? |
kiṃ bahunā, tava karasaṃyamanam
kṛtam iva paśyāmy amunā kamanam ||o|| ||JGc_1,21.7|| | iti | [mātrāsamakā]
children.translated_text:
And there, O fair-faced one, what your happiness will be —
who could know that?
What more [need I say]? I seem to see your hand-grasping
already accomplished by him, your beloved!' ||21.7|| [mātrāsamakā]

children.text: tad evaṃ yamunāṃ prāpya drutam eva gānaṃ samāpya velāyāṃ bālya-cāpalyena kalye projjhita-celā eva mithaḥ kṛta-melā velāyāṃ nimajjanti sma | nimajjya ca-kauṣeyatayā kṣālanāṃ vināpi na pariheyam iti tad eva celaṃ paridhāya sevyāyā devyāḥ saikatām arcām arcitāṃ vidhāya mantram anusandhāya dhāma samāyānti sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, having reached the <s>Yamunā</s>, swiftly completing the song, at the bank, with the fickleness of childhood, having cast off their garments and meeting together, they plunged in. And having plunged, [reflecting] 'Since [the garments are] silk, even without washing they should not be abandoned,' they put on those very garments and, having fashioned and worshipped a sand image of the goddess to be served, and having recited the <s>mantra</s>, they returned home.

children.text: tad evaṃ tāvan māsaṃ yāvad vidhāya tat-pūraka-dinaṃ vratasyāpi pūrakaṃ jātam iti paramānanda-pūraṇataḥ sūrajā-pūram anu dūranirjanatā-jāta-nirvrīḍatayā kṣaṇam akrīḍan |
children.translated_text: Thus, having performed [the vow] for a full month, the day of its completion arrived — the completion of the vow too was accomplished — and from the fullness of supreme bliss, along the banks of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), from the shamelessness born of the remoteness and solitude, they played for a moment.

children.text: tad evaṃ pūrva-pūrvaṃ jānan vraja-rāja-nandanas tuṣṭa-manāḥ kumāra-catuṣṭayam anuvidhaṃ vidhāya tatra prasthāya guptam upta-cittatayā tāḥ paśyati sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing everything from before, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, with a delighted mind, having arranged four boys as an entourage, having proceeded there, watched them with concealed, implanted attention.

children.text: ye khalu dāma-sudāma-vasudāma-kiṅkiṇi-saṃjñās tasya prajñāhaṅkāra-citta-manasāṃ bahiḥ-prakāśatayā labdha-samajñās tantra-vijñātṛbhir vijñāyante, ta ete hi kumārā jāta-catuḥ-pañca-varṣāḥ paraspara-savayaskatā-dhṛta-harṣāḥ kṛṣṇād anudinam āsādita-prema-varṣāś calanārambhata eva-kutra yāmaḥ? iti pṛcchanta eva gacchantaḥ kṛta-tat-saṅgam āgacchanti sma | tad evaṃ-
children.translated_text: Those who bore the names <s>Dāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, <s>Vasudāma</s>, and <s>Kiṅkiṇi</s> — known by the knowers of the <s>tantras</s> as external manifestations of his wisdom, ego, mind, and inner sense — these boys, having reached the age of four or five years, bearing delight in their mutual age-fellowship, receiving showers of love daily from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, from the very beginning of walking — always asking 'Where shall we go?' and going — came along, having joined his company. Thus:

children.text:
saṅge vidhāya caturaś caturaḥ kumārān
āgamya tatra kara-vārita-tat-prahāsaḥ |
namrībhavann alam alakṣitatāṃ prapadya
sadyas tad-aṃśuka-cayaṃ sa harir jahāra ||JGc_1,21.8|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
Having arranged the four clever boys in his company,
having arrived there, his laughter checked by his hand,
bowing down and attaining complete concealment,
that <s>Hari</s> instantly stole the pile of their garments! ||21.8|| [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
hṛtvā sa satvara-kadamba-nagādhiroha-
pūrvaṃ sa-ḍimbha-nikaraḥ sphuṭam ujjahāsa |
śrutvā prahāsam atha gopa-kumārikāṇāṃ
vargaḥ samaṃ sabhayam ūrdhvita-dṛṣṭir āsīt ||JGc_1,21.9|| [vasanta]
children.translated_text:
Having stolen them, with a prior swift ascent of a <s>kadamba</s> tree,
together with the group of children, he openly burst into laughter;
then, hearing the laughter, the troop of cowherd maidens
became simultaneously fearful and upward-gazing! ||21.9|| [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
gambhīra-svara-saṅgataṃ tad-itarānudbhāvya-bhavya-śriyaṃ
hāsaṃ taṃ paricitya bālya-valitās tāḥ prekṣya cānyo' nyataḥ |
vastrāṇy apy anabhīkṣya tatra vidhṛtāny uccaṃ tu vakṣaḥ-sthalaṃ
kṛtvā nīcam udakta-vaktram udake nyak-cakrire padminīḥ ||JGc_1,21.10|| [śārdūla-vikrīḍitam]
children.translated_text:
Recognizing that laughter — joined with a deep voice, of auspicious beauty not producible by any other —
and seeing each other, enfolded in childhood [modesty],
and not seeing their garments held up there, but [seeing] the high chest-level [of the tree],
they lowered their upturned faces and in the water sank down like lotuses! ||21.10|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
atalina-nalina-vanānāṃ bhramam iha cakrur mukhāni tāsāṃ na |
hemante tad-ayogāt kintu nyak-kāram evātra ||JGc_1,21.11|| [āryā]

tataś ca,
kṣaṇam adhi jala-madhyaṃ tasthur ānamra-netrāḥ
punar udayati śīte' drākṣur etāḥ kadambam |
api harir adhiśākhaṃ gupta-mūrtiḥ purāsīt
punar avṛtim ayāsīc cātma-lakṣāya tābhiḥ ||JGc_1,21.12|| [mālinī]

tāsāṃ jalastha-vapuṣāṃ vadaneṣu kṛṣṇa-
syārūḍha-nīpaka-taroḥ sahasā dṛg-antaḥ |
padmeṣu padmapa-kalām adadhād amuṣmin
yāsāṃ ca nīrabhṛti cātakarītim āpa ||JGc_1,21.13|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
Upon the faces of those [maidens] standing in the water, the tip of the eye
of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who had suddenly climbed the <s>nīpa</s> tree,
imparted upon those lotuses the art of a bee;
and their [eyes] upon that cloud-bearer assumed the nature of <s>cātaka</s> birds! ||21.13|| [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tataś ca-
uccakair jahasur bālāś cukruśus tatra bālikāḥ |
ūcuś cedaṃ tu vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vrajādṛtyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||JGc_1,21.14|| [anu]
atha kṛṣṇena muhur api śikṣitā bālāḥ procuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the boys, having been repeatedly instructed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, spoke.

children.text: tatra prathamaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the first [response], as follows:

children.text:
kṛtyaṃ vā kim akṛtyaṃ vā na vidmo vayam aṇv api |
śikṣārthaṃ kintu vaḥ prāptā vīkṣyājñāsiṣma tat punaḥ ||JGc_1,21.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
[23] atha sarvāḥ salajjaṃ parasparam īkṣitvā punar ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text:
'What is proper or what is improper — we do not know even the slightest!
But we came for the purpose of instruction from you — having looked, we learned that again!' ||21.15|| [anuṣṭubh]
[23] Then all of them, looking at each other bashfully, spoke again:

children.text:
yaḥ kaścic chikṣakas tasmād bhavadbhiḥ suṣṭhu śikṣitam |
abhyasyatha vraje tac ca sva-guror māna-vṛddhaye ||JGc_1,21.16|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Whatever instructor there is, from him you have been well instructed!
Practice that in <s>Vraja</s> too, for the increase of honor of your own guru!' ||21.16|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: punas tac-chikṣitā ḍimbhāḥ procuḥ-
children.translated_text: Again, the children, instructed by him, said:

children.text:
kimartho' yam upālambhas tan na vidmas tu kiñcana |
bhavatyo jala-cāriṇyo vayaṃ vṛkṣāgra-gāminaḥ ||JGc_1,21.17|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
'What is the purpose of this reproach? We know nothing whatsoever!
You are water-goers, and we are tree-top-goers!' ||21.17|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tā ūcuḥ-
vikrāntir luṇṭhatāṃ yogyā yad vaḥ śākhāgragāmitā |
dīnatā luṇṭhitānāṃ syād yan naḥ salilagāhitā ||JGc_1,21.18|| [anu]
atha śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ svayam eva sa-kopa-vismayam iva vakti sma-kiṃ luṇṭhitaṃ bhavatīnām?
children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself spoke, as if with angry astonishment: 'What have you been robbed of?'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-aho bata! katham asmākam asaṅkhyatayā duḥsaṃvaram ambaraṃ saṃvaraṇam āpadyate?
children.translated_text: They said: 'Alas! How can our garments, being innumerable and hence hard to conceal, come to be concealed?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-bhavatīnām ambarāvaraṇatā vidyata eva, tad ambaraṃ vā katham apahāreṇa saṃvalanam avalambatām?
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'You indeed possess sky-garmentedness (nakedness), so how does a garment (<s>ambara</s>) come to be a covering through theft?'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: They said:

children.text:
ambaram apy ambaratām āsādayituṃ tavāsti sāmarthyam |
iha dāmodara cauryaṃ kiyad iva śauryaṃ samarpayatu? ||JGc_1,21.19|| [āryā]
children.translated_text: 'Even the sky you have the power to make sky-less! O <s>Dāmodara</s>, how much is this thievery? Let your valor manifest!' // [āryā]

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaḥ sa-smayam āha sma-na nagnā etāḥ pāthasi magnāḥ | tad idaṃ tu mayā parihasitam eva | dṛṣṭaṃ bhavadbhir duṣṭhu-prakṛtīnām ākṛti-mātra-suṣṭhutā-yutānām āsām anuṣṭhitam; yan madīyāny eva śastāni vastrāṇi vihārataḥ samasta-vyastatayā yatra tatra visrastāni | tāny etā daridrāṇāṃ kanyāḥ sphuṭam anyāyatayā paricitya ca vicitya paridadhānā, mādṛśas tu dṛśaḥ sakāśād gopanaṃ kāmayamānā bāḍhaṃ jalam evāvagāḍhāḥ | yāni khalv atisvacchānāṃ tigma-cchavi-kanyā-jalānām antar apracchannāny eva lakṣyante, yāny eva cāsāṃ jala-magna-pratyaṅga-lagnāni svarṇa-savarṇa-varṇāni varṇā iva nirvarṇyante | tasmāt plavanta eva bhavantaḥ pratyekam etāḥ kara-gṛhīta-karāḥ samānayantām |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'These girls are not naked — they are immersed in water! This was merely my jest. You have seen what has been done by these ones — whose nature is wicked though their appearance alone is pretty; for they have scattered my own fine garments here and there, everywhere, in the course of play, in various states of disarray. These poor-girls clearly picked those up as if by right, and recognizing them and selecting them, put them on; but desiring to conceal [this] from eyes such as mine, they have plunged deep into the water. Those [garments] which indeed are visible uncovered inside the crystal-clear waters filled with girls of blazing beauty — those very ones clinging to each submerged limb are perceived as golden-colored stripes! Therefore, you yourselves, swimming, should bring each one here by the hand!'

children.text: tad etad avadhārya tīra-paryantam avatīrya sambhrama-pratīkṣitālpa-kālān kṛṣṇājñā-pālān bālān amūḥ pratyūcuḥ-[32] kathaṃ stambham avalambadhve? niḥśaṅkam eva saṅkrāmata |
children.translated_text: Having understood this, having descended to the water's edge — those [girls] addressed the boys who had been guarding <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> commands, awaiting the agitation for a brief moment: [32] 'Why do you cling to the pillar? Cross over without apprehension!'

children.text: sakhīḥ prati ca prāvocan-atraivānīya pānīya-vāsa-sukhaṃ luṇṭhākān etān ākuṇṭham āsādayata |
children.translated_text: And they said to their friends: 'Bring [them] here — reach these robbers unhesitatingly, who [enjoy] the pleasure of water-dwelling!'

children.text: atha tān prati ca-
children.translated_text: And to those [boys]:

children.text:
āhara-vasanām āhara- vanitāṃ yasmāt kriyāṃ sadādhīdhve |
kātyāyanī-prasādāt tam api vikarṣāma toyāntaḥ ||JGc_1,21.20|| [āryā]
children.translated_text: 'Fetch the garments! Fetch the woman!' — since you always devise such actions, by the grace of <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, we shall drag him too into the water! // [āryā]

children.text: atha tad etac chrutavanta eva drutavantaḥ skhalanta iva nīpa-tarv-antam āsadya sadyas tam eva tarum āruruhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those very ones, having heard this, ran and stumbled, as it were, reaching the base of the <s>kadamba</s> tree and at once climbing up that very tree.

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu sa-hāsaṃ spaṣṭam idam abhyacaṣṭe-aho, śubhaṃyūyamānānām āsām ahaṃyutā bhavatīnāṃ bhavatu, paśyāmas tatra-bhavatīṣu devatā-prabhāvam | yāvad eva tad etam udavāsam urīkṛtya bhavatyas tiṣṭhanti, tāvad vayam api dhṛta-niṣṭhās taror upariṣṭād eva nabho-vāsam urarīkṛtya tiṣṭhāma |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, laughing, declared this plainly: 'Oh, let those of you who call yourselves well-mannered have their arrogance! Let us see the power of the deity in your ladies! As long as your ladies stand accepting this water-dwelling, so long shall we too, maintaining our resolve, accept sky-dwelling from atop the tree!'

children.text: atha tatra tad-uttaram urarī-kurvatyaḥ sarvāḥ saśleṣam ātma-hṛd-gatam udgamayāmāsuḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, accepting that [challenge] in turn, all of them, with heartfelt affection, brought forth from within their hearts:

children.text:
na nādeya-bhayaṃ tasya tarau yasya bhavet sthitiḥ |
pātra-sātkṛta-gātrāṇāṃ pṛcchyā nādeyatā punaḥ ||JGc_1,21.21|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'There is no cause for fear from the river for one whose abode is on a tree; but for those whose limbs are made into vessels [by the water] — is the question of unworthiness even relevant?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś ca tan-mukha-tuṣāra-karatas tuṣāra-kara-taraṅga-nikarataś ca kampamānāḥ sa-narmānukampam amūr ayam uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, trembling from the frost-ray-like beams of his moon-face and from the swarms of frost-moon waves, he spoke to them with playful compassion:

children.text: aho, hima-śratha-ślathāṅga-sandhayaḥ parama-durbalāḥ ! sarvābhir evārvāg āgamyatām |
children.translated_text: 'Oh, your joints loosened and melting from the cold — supremely weak! Let all of you come toward this side!'

children.text: tās tu bhrū-bhaṅga-saṅgatam ūcuḥ-punaḥ kim artham āgamayitum arthayase?
children.translated_text: But they spoke with furrowed brows: 'For what purpose again do you ask us to come?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-vanadevatayā hṛtaṃ mayā tu prasahya tasyāḥ samāhṛtaṃ vāsaḥ samāsādyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'The garments were stolen by the forest-deity; I forcibly recovered them from her. Come and obtain your clothing!'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-kim ataḥ śeṣam anveṣāmaḥ?
children.translated_text: They said: 'What more remains for us to seek?'

children.text: tad etad uktvāntar-vāriṇa eva prasārita-karāḥ kiñcid abhyānañcuḥ | kṛṣṇas tu sāṅguli-vyaṅgam uvāca-aye śata-patra-patra-netrāḥ ! savidhe' trāgamyatām |
children.translated_text: Having said this, they from within the water itself extended their hands and advanced a little. But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with a finger-gesture of humor, said: 'O hundred-petaled-lotus-eyed ones! Come nearby, right here!'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-tavaitad ehīhaṃ karma katham iva?
children.translated_text: They said: 'How could this be your doing — this "Come here" business?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-mama dṛṣṭir visṛṣṭiś ca viśiṣṭatām āpnoti' iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'My gaze and my giving both attain excellence thereby.'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-tarhi kim arhitaṃ bhavet?
children.translated_text: They said: 'Then what would be the appropriate [action]?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-grahaṇātivṛttir vastra-parivṛttiś ca na syāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'There should be no excess in taking, nor exchange of garments!'

children.text: tāś ca parasparam ūcuḥ-aho mugdhāḥ! vañcayitum eveyaṃ prapañcanā |
children.translated_text: And they said among themselves: 'Oh naive ones! This is merely a stratagem to deceive!'

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu tāḥ sandarśya jihvāṃ sandaśya babhāṣe-satyam evedaṃ bravīmi, nāsatyam |
children.translated_text: But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, showing them his tongue and biting it, declared: 'I speak the very truth, not falsehood!'
