children.text: tāḥ punaḥ pratyūham ūhamānā vyatyūcuḥ-aho, mūḍha-buddhayaḥ ! suvyaktāntar-nigūḍha-hāsaḥ parīhāsa evāyam asya |
children.translated_text: Still imagining obstacles, they said in turn: 'Oh, foolish-minded ones! This is clearly his mockery — with laughter well-concealed within!'

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu gūḍham api smitam agūḍha | samūḍha-priya-vadyatayāpy avādīt-hanta, nahi nahi, yasmād vrata-kṛśatayā bhṛśa-dayā-viṣayā eva yūyam, na tu dūyamānatām arhatha |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, did not conceal even his hidden smile. With the eloquence of one speaking lovingly, he said: 'Come now, no, no! For you, emaciated by your vow, are indeed objects of intense compassion — you do not deserve to be tormented!'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: They said:

children.text:
spṛhayāluś cānya-vastraṃ gṛhayāluś ca yaḥ sa tu |
śītaluṣu dayāluś ced āścaryātiśayālutā ||JGc_1,21.22|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'One who covets another's garments and one who seizes them — if such a one is compassionate toward those who are cold — that is a superfluity of wonderment!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: bhavatu | visrabdhaṃ vadata, kadā satyaṃ vaktum ārabdhaṃ tatra-bhavadbhiḥ?
children.translated_text: So be it. Speak candidly — when did your honors begin to speak the truth?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-kadāpi nānṛtaṃ vacasi kṛtavān asmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Never have I uttered falsehood in speech!'

children.text: tā ūcuḥ-kaḥ kathayati?
children.translated_text: They said: 'Who says so?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa sa-hāsam uvāca-aho, kūṭakūṭaṃ ghaṭayamānāḥ! yady anyathā manyadhve, parama-dharma-parān etān eva sametān pṛcchata?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a laugh: 'Oh, you who fashion fraud upon fraud! If you think otherwise, ask these very assembled ones, supremely devoted to <s>dharma</s>!'

children.text: tā sahāsam ūcuḥ-satyam ete bhavataḥ prāpta-marmāṇaḥ sa-dharmāṇaś ca dṛśyante |
children.translated_text: They said with a laugh: 'Indeed, these appear to be ones who have grasped your inner meaning and share your principles!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta, muṣṭi-sambadhya-madhyamāḥ, pratītim atītha cet pratyakṣata eva lakṣyatām | sarvābhir evāgamya na vā sarvān atirekayā kayācid ekayāpi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Come now, you middle-fisted ones! If you have gone beyond trust, then let it be observed directly! By all of you coming — or without all, even by a single one surpassing the others!'

children.text:
tataś ca-
tasya tat kṣvelitaṃ śrutvā
bālāḥ prema-pariplutāḥ |
vrīḍitāḥ prekṣya cānyo' nyaṃ
jāta-hāsā na niryayuḥ ||JGc_1,21.23|| [BhP 10.22.12] iti |
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Having heard his jesting, the girls, flooded with love, modestly glancing at one another — though laughter had arisen — did not come out.' // [BhP 10.22.12] — thus.

children.text:
tīre gantuṃ lajjā sthātuṃ
nīre ca śītam ity ubhayam |
samajani jāḍyaṃ yugapat tad
imās tatraiva kiñcid abruvata ||JGc_1,21.24|| [anu]
children.translated_text: Shame to go to the bank, cold to stay in the water — both! Simultaneously a numbness was born; then, right there, they spoke a little: // [anu]

children.text:
vraja-nṛpa-kula-ratna tvaṃ vraja-prīti-śālī
vraja-jana-mahanīyaś cāsi yācāmahe tat |
vayam atitara-śīta-vyagratā-grasta-cittā
vitara vitara vāsaś cānayaṃ mā ca kārṣīḥ ||JGc_1,21.25|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text: 'O jewel of the dynasty of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, you who are rich in love for <s>Vraja</s>, you who are venerable to the people of <s>Vraja</s> — we beseech you! We are minds seized by the affliction of excessive cold — give, give the garments, and do not commit this injustice!' // [mālinī]

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-mamānayaṃ ko vā nayana-viṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ? pratyuta sat-kula-prabhavatīnāṃ bhavatīnāṃ vana-devatāhṛta-vastrāṇāṃ sāhāyyam eva kāryam iti tathā mayārabdham asti | na tu bhavatīnāṃ cela-cela-pracaye mādṛśām abhilāṣa-melaḥ sambhavati | tasmād asmat-paritoṣa-poṣaṇāya yadi kiñcid api dattha, tadā tan-madād eva devatā-virodham apy anurodha-viṣayī-kurmaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'What injustice of mine has been made visible to your eyes? On the contrary, I must render assistance to women of your good families whose garments were stolen by the forest-deity — and thus I have begun. But in your garment-collection there is no mingling of desire from the likes of me. Therefore, for the nourishment of our satisfaction, if you give even a little, then from that intoxication alone we shall take upon ourselves even the opposition of the deity!'

children.text: atha tad etad evam avadhāritavatyaḥ kātyāyanī-vratavatyas tad etan manasi vicāritavyaḥ-hanta, yad asmābhir manasi rañjitaṃ, tad evāyaṃ vyañjitaṃ kartuṃ prayatate | tasmād asmākam ayam eva samayaḥ | kintu kim api lakṣyam evātra lakṣyam, tad api svata eva labdham yat pṛthu-śīta-bhītatādikam atra prakaṭam eva ghaṭate |
children.translated_text: Then, having thus ascertained, the women devoted to the <s>Kātyāyanī</s> vow deliberated in their minds: 'Ah, what we have colored in our minds — this very thing he strives to make manifest! Therefore, this is indeed our opportunity. But indeed, the very object is discernible here — and that too has been obtained spontaneously, for the fear of intense cold and such is manifestly present here.'

children.text: atha taṃ prāhuḥ-hā, hā, drutam anena haimanena pavanena śīta-parītatayā jīvana-viparītatāṃ vayam āyātāḥ, tasmān marma-bhedakaṃ narma vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ, kintu vastram eva sevaya | yad vā vāñchasi, tat tu lāñchanam aṅgīkṛtyāpi kariṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then they said to him: 'Alas, alas! By this wintry wind, we have been so encompassed by cold that we have reached the reverse of living! Therefore, do not make sport that pierces the heart in vain — but serve us with garments! Or whatever you desire — even accepting that stigma, we shall do it!'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-smitam uvāca-hanta, yadi madiṣṭaṃ dāsyatha, tarhi dāsyam eva svīkuruta |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'Well then, if you will give what I desire, then accept servitude itself!'

children.text: atha tāś cintayāmāsuḥ-hanta, sahasā marma-sparśe karmaṭhatām eva labdhavān asau | bhavatu, vayam api narmāśritya tad eva śarmāṅgī-kurmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then they pondered: 'Ah, he has suddenly achieved his skill in touching the vital point! So be it — we too, taking refuge in jest, shall accept that very happiness!'

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ ca procuḥ-śyāmsundara te dāsyaḥ [BhP 10.22.15]
children.translated_text: And they said plainly: 'O dark-beautiful one, [we are] your servants!' [BhP 10.22.15]

children.text: kṛṣṇaś ca sa-smitam āha sma-tatra ca yan mamoditam, tad anumoditaṃ purataḥ kuruta |
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'And therein, put into effect what I have declared — the approved!'

children.text: atha tāḥ parasparam ālocana-pūrvaṃ nikocita-locanam ūcuḥ-bhavatu, karavāma tavoditam iti |
children.translated_text: Then they, after mutual consultation, with shyly contracted eyes, said: 'So be it — we shall do as you have declared.'

children.text: tad evam api kṛṣṇe sa-tṛṣṇe' pi tuṣṇīm eva sthite punar ūcuḥ-dehi vāsāṃsi dharmajña iti |
children.translated_text: Even so, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — though full of desire — stood silently, they said again: 'Give the garments, O knower of <s>dharma</s>!'

children.text: atra cānyathā nijāṅgīkāra-sabhaṅgī-bhāvād dharma eva marma-bādhāyāṃ nātmānaṃ saṃvarmayed iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: And here the meaning is: since otherwise the breaking of her own acceptance would result, <s>dharma</s> itself [demands that] in the affliction of the vital point, one should not conceal oneself.

children.text: tathāpi tathā sthite tasmin kautuka-nigūḍha-smite punar ūcuḥ-no ced rājñe bruvāmahe' iti |
children.translated_text: Even so, when he stood thus — with curiosity-concealed smile — they said again: 'If not, we shall tell the king!'

children.text: atra ca bhaya-nirmuktam imaṃ tad-yukta-mātram ācaritum uktam idaṃ na tu vastutaḥ |
children.translated_text: And here, freed from fear, this was spoken merely to practice what was fitting — not in actuality.

children.text: tad eṣa vyāja-padena rāja-padena yaṃ viśeṣam abudhyate, tam eva budhyatāṃ nāma nikāmam ity abhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: And by the pretextual word 'king,' whatever special [meaning] he understood — let that indeed be understood as desired to the utmost — such was the intent.

children.text: kṛṣṇaś ca tad-upayuktam uktavān-aho, kadā dāsyo bhaviṣyatha? kadā vā mayoditaṃ kariṣyatha? tat tu nopalabhāmahe | yadi vettham satyam eva, tadā gaty-antaram antarā, jalād utthāya sarva-sampad utthāya smitena sametam eva sameta, na tu sūkṣmayāpi rukṣatayā | na cen, mithyā-saṅkalpa-jalpānāṃ tata evādharma-marma-kalpānāṃ sāhāyyam asmābhiḥ kathaṃ vā prathanīyam?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Ah, you whose middle fingers are clenched together! When will you become servants? When will you do what I have declared? We do not perceive that! If this is truly so, then without any alternative, having risen from the water, having risen to all prosperity, come forth with a smile itself — not with even the subtlest harshness! Otherwise, how shall we promote assistance for those whose false-resolve-utterances result in the essence of <s>adharma</s>?'

children.text: tathāpi tāsām anutthānam uṭṭaṅkya kaṭhinatā-ghaṭitam ācaṣṭe-na vayaṃ vṛthā kṛtāśānāṃ kanyā-pāśānāṃ vaḥ sambandham anurundhmahe | kintu-
children.translated_text: Even so, hearing their non-rising, he declared what was fashioned from hardness: 'We do not indulge the relationship with you maidens who are ropes of vain desires! But —'

children.text:
idaṃ ca me dayālutvam eva budhyadhvam añjasā |
no cen nāhaṃ pradāsye kiṃ kruddho rājā kariṣyati? ||JGc_1,21.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Understand this straightforwardly as my very compassion! Otherwise, I shall not give [the garments] — what will an angry king do?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atra ca rāja-padaṃ vyājāya vyājahāra | tataś ca maunaṃ pratilabhya tāsāṃ bhayam upalabhya, tena karuṇa-sabhya-śiromaṇinā pratyayam ācarya, kathañcit pratyaye cācarite śītārtatā-nirvarti-vārtatām āhartuṃ vrīḍā-niviḍa-jaḍa-vapuṣo' pi jaḍād utterur iti vārtayanti | tad yadi tathā syāt tadā vastutas tu tat-kāraṇam idam astu-
children.translated_text: And here too, the word 'king' he spoke as a pretext. And then, having perceived their silence and their fear, that crown-jewel of the compassionate assembly, having demonstrated trustworthiness — and when trustworthiness had somehow been demonstrated — they report that even those whose bodies were rigid with dense modesty, numb — they rose from the cold-afflicted waters to bring the news of relief from cold-distress. If it were truly thus, then the real cause would be this:

children.text: ||JGc_1,21.27|| MISSING!
children.translated_text: ||JGc_1,21.27|| MISSING!

children.text:
prārthyaṃ cet phalati tadā bhajema
dehaṃ no cen no' ti samayasya yaiva sīmā |
tāsāṃ sā yadi viphalā kva tarhi lajjā
nirvastrā gati-vidhaye himaṃ tu lakṣyam ||JGc_1,21.28|| [praharṣiṇī]
children.translated_text: If the prayer bears fruit, then we would cherish the body; if not, then this is the very limit of the vow. If that [prayer] of theirs is fruitless, where then is shame? Unclothed, the cold itself is the aim for the course of action! // [praharṣiṇī]

children.text: tad evaṃ kathañcid udakād uktāś ca tā na vyaktāvayavā jātāḥ | kintu-
children.translated_text: Thus, having somehow been told to come out of the water, they did not become clearly visible in their limbs. But —

children.text:
hasta-pallava-kṛtāgra-vastrikāḥ
keśa-vistṛti-dhṛtāparāmbarāḥ |
ādi-niṣṭhita-kaniṣṭha-dārikāḥ
kubjikāvad amilan kumārikāḥ ||JGc_1,21.29|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: With the tips of hand-sprouts covering the front garment-area, with the spreading of hair serving as the other garment, the maidens — from the eldest-established to the youngest girls — met [him] hunched like little hunchback women! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: tataś ca-paśya kṛṣṇa, paśya sarvatas trastā etā loptrāṇi vastrāṇi pāthasy eva srastāni vidhāyāgatā iti saṃlapya prabala-hāsaṃ valgati bāla-varge, haris tv idaṃ bhāvitavān atīva dayām ayāmāsa | yathā-
children.translated_text: And then — 'Look, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, look! These frightened ones from all sides, having left their coverings as garments in the water itself, have come!' — as the group of boys chattered thus with boisterous laughter, <s>Hari</s> however contemplated this and felt intense compassion. As follows:

children.text:
śaśadhara-tanvā tulanām āhata-lakṣaṇatayā yayur yad api |
tad api ca tāṃ sahasāmūr āhata-lakṣaṇatayā jigyuḥ ||29|| [āryā]
children.translated_text: Although they attained comparison with the moon-bodied ones by the characteristic of being struck [with beauty], even so, these ones surpassed them — by the characteristic of being stricken [with modesty]! // [āryā]

children.text:
etāḥ sat-kula-sambhavā varam aho vāñchanti dehavyayam
na vrīḍākṣayam evam apy atha daśām etāṃ gatā mat-puraḥ |
bījaṃ cātra parantu mad-vimukhatāśaṅkā tataḥ kuṇṭhatām
utkaṇṭhā kiratī viloṭhayati mām āsāṃ nijāśarmaṇi ||JGc_1,21.30|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'These women of noble birth — ah, they would rather wish for the destruction of the body | than for the destruction of modesty — and yet they have come to this state before me! | The seed here, however, is the apprehension of my aversion — therefore their shame, | though scattering longing, rolls me about in [concern for] their own suffering!' || (JGc 1,21.30) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: tathāpy āsāṃ suṣṭhu tan-niṣṭhāṃ niṣṭaṅkayituṃ paṅka-darśinaṃ mano-ratha-sparśinaṃ parihāsam apy atīva spaṣṭayituṃ cittam idam utkaṇṭhate | yadā gatā api saṅkocāvagāhataḥ parasparam āhata-prakāśāvayavā eva tiṣṭhanti iti |
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, his heart yearns to firmly establish their devotion to him, and to make exceedingly clear even the jest — which shows mud [the coarse surface] yet touches the chariot of desire. For even when they have gone [into the water], they remain with their bodies of appearance mutually struck [hidden] out of the immersion of shyness.

children.text: prakāśayann uvāca-are re, capalāḥ, kathaṃ bhavanto hasanti? etāḥ khalu nagnikā eva kathaṃ nagnikā-bhāve doṣam arhanti?iti |
children.translated_text: Making it explicit, he said: 'Hey, hey, playful ones! Why do you laugh? These are indeed naked — how can naked ones be faulted for nakedness?'

children.text: atha punar vastra-kadambaṃ kadamba-skandha-sandhi-viśeṣe sa-pratyāhāraṃ tat-pratyakṣa-saṃvalitatayā sandhāya prema-bandhāya sa-smitaṃ tāḥ praty evam āha sma-[80] dāsyāṅgīkāra-kāraṇāt pradāsyāmy eva tāny etāni vastrāṇi | kintu pūrvam aśakya-nirṇayaḥ, samprati tu nirvarṇya nirṇītaḥ, so' yaṃ sad-guruto yajata-namatāṃ prāptavatīnāṃ bhavatīnāṃ durnayaḥ sapadi māṃ vivarṇayan vartate | tad etad avadhāryatāṃ bhavatībhiḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, placing the bundle of garments again at a particular juncture of the <s>kadamba</s> tree-trunk, arranged with withdrawal yet within their direct sight — for the binding of love — he said with a smile to those very [gopīs]: [80] 'Because of accepting servitude, I shall indeed give back these garments. But previously the determination was impossible to make; now, having examined, it is determined — this misconduct of your honors, who have obtained the status of worshippers bowing to the true guru, immediately discolors me. Let your honors consider this:

children.text:
śambaraṃ praviviśe bimbādharaṃ
yat tad eva jaladevahelanam |
chidram āvaritum atra tadvrate
śīrṣabhākkarayugaṃ sa namyatām ||JGc_1,21.31|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'The <s>bimba</s>-[red] lower lip entered the reflection (<s>śambara</s>) [of the water], | and that itself is an affront to the water-deity! | To cover the opening in this vow, | let the pair of hands upon the head be bowed!' || (JGc 1,21.31) [rathoddhatā]

children.text: tās tu tatra sāpatrapa-cittāś ca parama-bhīti-bhittās tathākāryatayāvadhārya paśyata ke' pi śabdāyante iti bālānāṃ dṛṣṭīḥ pratārya patir eva devatā iti vicārya sa-parihāsa-vilāsa-vyājatas tam eva namaścakruḥ-svāmin, namas tubhyam iti |
children.translated_text: And those [gopīs], though with shame-struck minds and shattered by supreme fear, having determined that this must be done, deceiving the gazes of the boys [by saying] 'Look, someone is making a sound over there!' — and deliberating 'the husband alone is the deity' — under the pretext of sportive play, they bowed to him alone: 'Lord, obeisance to you!'

children.text: tataś ca kṛṣṇaḥ sa-kautuka-tṛṣṇayā tāsāṃ prati pratīkaṃ sandṛśya, snigdhatāṃ vidagdhatām api parāmṛśya, labdha-prasāda-melaḥ khelā-valitaṃ celāni yathāsvam arpayāmāsa | yatra ca-dṛṣṭi-patha-sevanād eva bhavatīnāṃ puṣṭi-dīrghatādikaṃ mama muṣṭi-gataṃ jātaṃ, katham anyathā samarpaṇaṃ kuryām? ity evaṃ tuṣṭiṃ dadānaḥ sva-vicakṣaṇatāṃ lakṣayāmāsa | kintu-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with curiosity-thirsty eyes, gazing at each of them one by one, touching upon their tenderness and also perceiving their cleverness, having obtained the meeting of grace, bestowed the garments upon each one with playful gestures. And there: 'From the mere service of your gaze-path, your nourishment, stature, and the like have come into my grasp — how could I surrender them otherwise?' — thus, generating satisfaction, he indicated his own discernment. But:

children.text:
prātikūlya-vacanaṃ ca sauhṛdād
ānukūlyam abhigamya śarmadam |
paśya vastra-haraṇādinā hariḥ
pratyuta pramadayām babhūva tāḥ ||JGc_1,21.32|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'The unfavorable words, having approached the favorable | that arises from affection and is happiness-giving — | behold: through the garment-stealing and the like, <s>Hari</s> | actually delighted those women!' || (JGc 1,21.32) [rathoddhatā]

children.text: tataś ca vṛkṣād avatīrṇavati tasmin,
children.translated_text: Then, when he had descended from the tree:

children.text:
lajjā-saṃvaraṇārtham asaṃvara-madhur bālā bhṛśaṃ lajjitās
tarhi svāṅga-vṛtiṃ dadhur muhur aho vyaktāntaraṅgārati |
kṛṣṇād alpa-vivṛtta-vaktra-kamalās tasthur dṛgantaḥ punas
tatrāgād vraja-subhruvām ahaha bhoḥ kāmasya vāmā gatiḥ ||JGc_1,21.33|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'The young women, deeply embarrassed, wishing to veil their shame, yet with irrepressible sweetness, | then repeatedly placed the covering of their own limbs — ah, manifestly revealing their inner passion! | With lotus-faces slightly turned away from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, they stood; but their side-glances went | back there again — alas, for the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s>, ahaha, the crooked course of love!' || (JGc 1,21.33) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: ||JGc_1,21.34|| MISSING!
children.translated_text: || (JGc 1,21.34) || [text missing]

children.text:
tataś ca-
bhṛṅga-śreṇya ivāmbhojaṃ rasa-pūrṇaṃ kumārikāḥ |
bhartṛ-kāmās tadā kṛṣṇaṃ varītuṃ paritaḥ sthitāḥ ||JGc_1,21.35|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Like rows of bees around a nectar-filled lotus, | the maidens, desiring a husband, | stood around <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> at that time, ready to choose!' || (JGc 1,21.35) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha teṣu cākarāleṣu bāleṣu-cala cala kiṃvā karaṇīyam atra? iti kara-dvayaṃ vasanādi-parikara-cayaṃ cākṛṣya hṛṣyatsu vitaraṇīyaṃ varam ambara-hāritāhārī hariḥ svam anusaṃhitavān | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, when those mischievous boys [were saying] 'Move, move! What is to be done here?' — pulling with both hands the collection of garments and accessories, rejoicing at what was to be distributed — the best <s>Hari</s>, thief of sky-garments, recollected himself. And then:

children.text:
tāsāṃ vijñāya gopālaḥ sva-kara-sparśa-kāmyayā |
dhṛta-vratānāṃ saṅkalpaṃ kalpayāmāsa siddhidam ||JGc_1,21.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: '<s>Gopāla</s>, knowing the intention of those vow-observing maidens — | their desire for the touch of his own hand — | arranged the fulfillment of their wish!' || (JGc 1,21.36) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
yathā-
svasyārthaḥ sa tu yad vibhāti parataḥ svīyaṃ samārādhanaṃ
mayy āviṣṭa-manās tv anādaram athācaryātra mā bādhayati |
tatrādye svayam asmi śaśvad upamā yūyaṃ dvitīye tataḥ
saṃkalpo nirupadhir eṣa bhavatīṣv evātisatyo mataḥ ||JGc_1,21.37|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
As follows:
'"The purpose of oneself that shines from another [direction] — one's own worship [directed] | toward Me — with mind absorbed in Me, yet showing disregard for the teacher — let it not cause distress here! | In the first [purpose], I myself am always the comparison; you are [the standard] in the second — | therefore, the intention in your honors is considered to be without deceit and supremely true!" || (JGc 1,21.37) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
sarpir-bhṛṣṭam āguḍa-kvathitatām āptāś ca dhānā yathā
vasyante svayam eva bījavad amūs tanvanti nānya-spṛhām |
man-mātra-spṛhiṇāṃ madīya-bhajanaṃ no tadvad anya-spṛhaṃ
kintu syād rasanīyarūpam iti ced yuṣmākam āstāṃ kathā ||JGc_1,21.38|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'Just as parched grains, fried in ghee and boiled in jaggery, | are subdued by themselves, like seeds, and do not produce desire for another; | so too, the worship of Me by those who desire Me alone does not produce desire for another — | but if it would become worthy of being savored — then let the tale of your honors remain [as it is]!' || (JGc 1,21.38) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: tad evam ākarṇinīr vara-varṇinī sadya eva gāndharva-parva sampadyatām ity abhiprāyatayā sāpatrapa-nayanāḥ svīkṛta-maya-samayam apekṣamāṇāḥ prati samardhakatayā samardhakatāṃ gacchan punar accham uvāca, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, making those excellent women [understand] that the <s>Gāndharva</s> festival [i.e., a love-marriage] should be accomplished right now — with modesty-filled eyes, awaiting the fulfillment of the appointed time accepted by him — he, moving toward conferring ability upon their ability, spoke again clearly, as follows:

children.text:
mithaḥ svīkāraḥ syāt pariṇaya-vidhis tat-parikāraḥ
pare te te dharmāḥ sa punar udabodhi svayam iha |
ato yūyaṃ siddhā vraja-gamanam evādya kuruta
kṣapāyāṃ kasyāñcit kila milanam apy āśu bhavitā ||JGc_1,21.39|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'Mutual acceptance constitutes the marriage rite; the rest is its paraphernalia; | those various other formalities — those have been understood here on their own. | Therefore, you are [already] perfected — just go to <s>Vraja</s> today; | on some night indeed, the meeting too shall swiftly come to pass!' || (JGc 1,21.39) [śikharinī]

children.text: tad evaṃ tābhyaḥ pratiśrutavati tasminn adhikam eva tāsām āveśo jātaḥ | yathāha śrī-śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, when he had given his promise to them, their intensity of absorption increased even more. As the glorious <s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: ity ādiṣṭā bhagavatā labdha-kāmāḥ kumārikāḥ |
dhyāyatyas tat-padāmbhojaṃ kṛcchrān nirviviśur vrajam ||[BhP 10.22.28] iti |
children.translated_text: meditating on His lotus-feet, with difficulty returned to <s>Vraja</s>.' || [BhP 10.22.28]
'Thus instructed by the Lord, the maidens, their desire fulfilled,

children.text:
tathā hi-
akṣibhyāṃ vaktra-bimbād bhuja-yuga-rucibhāṅ madhya-bhāgān nitambād
ūrubhyāṃ jānu-yugmāt pada-sarasi-ruha-dvandvam āpur murāreḥ |
vrīḍā-namrāḥ sva-dṛgbhyām ahaha mṛga-dṛśas tad-viyuktau tu tat tat paścād
dṛṣṭaṃ padaṃ tu pratipadam udabhūd antare lagnam āsām ||JGc_1,21.40|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
For thus:
'From His face-disc through their eyes, from the beauty of His arm-pair, from the middle portion, from the hips, | from the thighs, from the knee-pair, they received the pair of lotus-feet of <s>Murāri</s>; | bowed with modesty, the doe-eyed ones, through their own eyes — alas — in the separation from Him, | each step they had seen thereafter became lodged between [their steps]!' || (JGc 1,21.40) [sragdharā]

children.text:
dve cittavāsasī nītvā kumārīṇāṃ paraṃ dade |
na pūrvaṃ tu nirākāraṃ gopanīyam atīva saḥ ||JGc_1,21.41|| [anuṣṭubh]
yat tarhy antima-ghasra-pūryam api tā devy-arcanaṃ san-madād
vismṛtya vrajam eva jagmur abhavaṃs tenaiva pūrṇa-kriyāḥ |
premṇā yasya tu tac ca tac ca laṣitaṃ tasyātha sākṣāt-phalaṃ
kṛṣṇāṅgī-kṛti-śarma ced vavalire kiṃ śiṣṭam iṣṭaṃ param? ||JGc_1,21.42|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'Having taken the two garments-of-the-mind of the maidens, he gave the outer [garments] back; | but the former — formless, supremely concealed — he [kept] first!' || (JGc 1,21.41) [anuṣṭubh]
'When, indeed, even though the final-day completion [of the vow] was still due, those [maidens], out of excellent intoxication, | forgot the goddess-worship and went straight to <s>Vraja</s> — they became complete in their rites by that very [act]; | if by love for Him both this and that became desired, and its direct fruit | is the happiness of acceptance by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — they rolled [in bliss] — what more supreme thing remains desired?' || (JGc 1,21.42) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-māsikam iṣṭam anu miṣṭaṃ miṣṭaṃ bhuktavatī devī katham iṣṭa-dānārtham āgamanaṃ muktavatī?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'After the month-long desired [vow], when they had eaten the sweet and sweet [food], how did the goddess, having come for the purpose of granting the desired boon, depart having released [them]?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text:
rāga eva kila siddhi-kṛd āsāṃ
nāsmad arcanam iti pratipadya |
nāgamad vara-vidhāv iha durgā
kintu rāga-viṣayaḥ svayam eva ||JGc_1,21.43|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: '"Passion alone is the cause of perfection for them, | not our worship" — having understood this, | <s>Durgā</s> did not come here for the excellent rite, | but the object of passion [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] came himself!' || (JGc 1,21.43) [svāgatā]

children.text:
madhukaṇṭha uvāca-nūnam etāś ca gargeṇaiva govindād apetāḥ kṛtāḥ |
[90] snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-kṛtāḥ, kintu na sākṣāt |
children.translated_text:
<s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Surely these [maidens] were separated from <s>Govinda</s> by <s>Garga</s> himself?'
[90] <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Separated, but not directly.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-katham iva?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'How so?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-yadyapi sādhvī-śiromaṇi-ramaṇīnāṃ rādhādīnāṃ dīnāyamānānām ālocana-saṅkocatas tasya punar vrajāgamanam anu mano na jātaṃ, tathāpi tad-anusandhānaṃ vinā vrata-bandhādi-dvayaṃ na sandhātavyam iti śrī-vraja-pati-jampatyoḥ kṛta-nibandhatayā, rādhādīnāṃ vadhūnām ābhād utpanna-manaskāra-pratibandhatayā ca tāḥ parasparayā parākṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Although <s>Garga's</s> mind did not incline toward coming to <s>Vraja</s> again, out of his reluctance to see those jewel-crest women — <s>Rādhā</s> and the others — becoming pitiable, nevertheless, since without his involvement the dual bond of the vow and [marriage-]arrangement could not be fashioned, and because of the mental obstruction that arose in the brides <s>Rādhā</s> and others from these very ones — [the maidens] were separated from one another by mutual [arrangement], at the insistence of the royal couple of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tarhi tāḥ kumārikāḥ katham āsan?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then how were those maidens [situated]?'

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-bahiḥ kaumāreṇa rahas tu śrī-hari-pariṇītatā-vyavahāreṇa |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Outwardly in maidenhood; but in secret, through the practice of being married to <s>Śrī Hari</s>.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-satyaṃ, bālyam eva khalu pūrvāsāṃ bodhasya virodhaṃ kurvāṇam āsīd iti viparīta-rītir jātā | katham iva jñānottarāṇām āsāṃ sā bhavet? iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'True — indeed, it was childhood that created the obstruction to the earlier [gopīs'] understanding, and thus the opposite course arose. How could the same apply to these [maidens] who have subsequent knowledge?'

children.text: tad etat kathāṃ prathayitvā kathakaḥ śrī-rādhāṃ bodhayati sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, having spread this tale, the narrator awakened <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>:

children.text:
evaṃ balānujātena yad vilambāvalambanam |
tad balaṃ balavaj jātaṃ tava saṃvalanaṃ vinā ||JGc_1,21.44|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Thus, the delay that was sustained by the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> — | that has now become a powerful strength — | without your meeting!' || (JGc 1,21.44) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: yata eva pūrvaṃ stabdhā veṇu-śikṣā ena punar ārabdhā | yatra kathā-viśeṣa-prathanaṃ padya-dvayaṃ sāmprata-līlā-mayam api, śaradu-dāśaye sādhujāta [BhP 10.31.2] ityādivat tāsāṃ vacasā rasāvahaṃ syād iti tad-dvārā śrī-parīkṣic-chikṣā-guruṇā nikṣiptaṃ, tad yathā-
children.translated_text: For indeed, the flute-practice that was first suspended was resumed again. Where the two special story-spreading verses, though belonging to the present pastime, would be conveyed with relish through the words of those [gopīs] — like 'In the clear autumn lake, well-born' [BhP 10.31.2] and so forth — deposited by the glorious teacher of <s>Parīkṣit</s> through that channel. They are as follows:

children.text: yarhy ambujākṣa tava pāda-talaṃ ramāyā
children.translated_text: 'O lotus-eyed one, when Your sole-surface — | that of <s>Ramā's</s> (Lakṣmī's) [Lord] —

children.text: datta-kṣaṇaṃ kvacid araṇya-jana-priyasya |
children.translated_text: giving [us] a moment, O lover of the forest-folk,

children.text: asprākṣma tat-prabhṛti nānya-samakṣam añjaḥ
children.translated_text: we touched — from that time onward, directly before others

children.text: sthātuṃ tvayābhiramitā bata pārayāmaḥ ||[BhP 10.29.36]
children.translated_text: to stand, we — delighted by You — alas, are unable!' || [BhP 10.29.36]

children.text: iti tāsāṃ rāsa-rajany-ārambhe dainya-saṃvedanaṃ nivedanam |
children.translated_text: — thus, their pitiful expression of humility at the beginning of the <s>rāsa</s>-night.

children.text: pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāya-padābja-rāga-
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Pulinda</s> women, fulfilled, with the red pigment of the lotus-feet of the greatly-praised one —

children.text: śrī-kuṅkumena dayitā-stana-maṇḍitena |
children.translated_text: the <s>Śrī</s>-<s>kuṅkuma</s> that had adorned the breasts of His beloveds —

children.text: tad-darśana-smara-rujas tṛṇa-rūṣitena
children.translated_text: afflicted by love-sickness at the sight of that, with grass they wiped away

children.text: limpantya ānana-kuceṣu juhus tad-ādhim ||[BhP 10.21.17]
children.translated_text: [that kuṅkuma], anointing it on their faces and breasts — they offered that suffering [as oblation]!' || [BhP 10.21.17]

children.text: iti pūrva-varṇita-veṇu-varṇana-mayam |
children.translated_text: — this is part of the previously described flute-description (<s>veṇu-varṇana</s>).

children.text: tad idaṃ sparśa-dvitayaṃ kānta-yogaja-bhoga-viśeṣam ayaṃ na syāt, rāsa-rajanyāṃ vakṣyamāṇa-kṛṣṇa-pratyākhyānāyukteḥ | rāsārambha eva bhagavān api rantuṃ manaś cakre [BhP 10.29.1] ity ukteś ca |
children.translated_text: This pair of touches [mentioned in the two verses] would not be a special enjoyment born of union with the beloved — because of the unfitness of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> forthcoming rejection described in the <s>rāsa</s>-night. [This is confirmed by] the statement that 'at the very beginning of the <s>rāsa</s>, the Lord too set his mind to sport' [BhP 10.29.1].

children.text: tad evaṃ tvayābhiramitā [BhP 10.29.36] ity asya tu tat-sparśānantaraṃ tvayā sarvato-bhāvena prayukta-raty-ākhya-bhāvā ity evārthaḥ saṅgacchate |
children.translated_text: Thus, the meaning of 'delighted by You' [BhP 10.29.36] fits as follows: 'after that touch, the emotion called love (<s>rati</s>), employed by You in every way' — this is the meaning that agrees.

children.text: tasmād athedaṃ vivriyate | tad evaṃ dīrgha-rātratayā mandatā-pātraṃ hemantārdhena sārdhaṃ śiśiraṃ niśi niśi vaṃśī-śaṃsitam abhyasyati tasmin vasanta āyātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is now explained. Thus, the winter half — a vessel of tardiness due to the length of the nights — together with the cold season, as he practiced night after night the flute-praised [melody] — spring arrived.

children.text: sa ca sārvatrika-cārv-anubhavo' pi vṛndāvane vṛndārakatām avindata, yathā-
children.translated_text: And that [spring], though universally experienced as beautiful, attained the status of the chief of the heavenly beings (<s>Vṛndāraka</s>) in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, as follows:

children.text:
vasantati nidāgho' pi vasantasyātra kiṃ bruve |
vasantaṃ yatra govindaṃ sarva-santaḥ sadā viduḥ ||JGc_1,21.45|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'Even summer becomes spring-like here — what then shall I say of spring? | For all the good ones always know <s>Govinda</s> dwelling here as spring!' || (JGc 1,21.45) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tathāpi hemanta-śiśirāv api tāpad-āpad-āyatanatayā yasya yāsāṃ ca pratibhāsate sma | tathā ca tāsāṃ kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇa-preyasīnāṃ pratyekaṃ bhāvanā,
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, even winter and the cold season appeared as the abode of torment and calamity for him and for those [gopīs]. And thus, the contemplation of each of those <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-beloveds:

children.text:
samāgantā yarhi prathamam ṛtu-rājaḥ sakhi tadā
ṛtūnām anyāyaṃ bata kathayitāsmīti laṣitam |
tad āstām eṣa prāk para-bhṛta-śilīvaktra-tatibhir
vitarjann evāsmān akṛta-vṛjinā dhik praviśati ||JGc_1,21.46|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: '"When the king of seasons shall first arrive, O friend, then | I shall proclaim the injustice of the other seasons!" — thus was the desire. | But let that be — this one [spring], even before [arriving], with its rows of cuckoo and <s>śilīvaktra</s> birds nourished by others, | threatening us even now — curse it! — enters without having committed any offense!' || (JGc 1,21.46) [śikharinī]

children.text:
dvirepho barbaraḥ proktaḥ para-puṣṭaś ca ceṭakaḥ |
tau cāgraṇyau madhor dṛṣṭau yāpyatā kāpy ataḥ kim u? ||JGc_1,21.47|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The bee (<s>dvirepha</s>) is called a barbarian; the cuckoo (<s>para-puṣṭa</s>) is a servant [raised by another]; | and these two are seen as the foremost of spring — | what wretchedness is then [to be expected]?' || (JGc 1,21.47) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
prasūna-nikarāḥ smitaṃ sarasijāni netra-prathāṃ
pikāḥ parama-pañcamaṃ madhu-lihāṃ ganāś cumbanam |
harer nigamayanti cet kva nu kutaḥ kathaṃ vā gatir
bhaved ahaha naḥ samaṃ sapadi mādhavīyair vṛtam ||JGc_1,21.48|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'If the clusters of flowers convey His smile, the lotuses the expanse of His eyes, | the cuckoos His supreme fifth-note, and the swarms of bees His kisses — | then where, whence, or how would there be a course of escape | for us — alas — when [we are] suddenly surrounded by the retinue of <s>Mādhava</s> (spring/Kṛṣṇa)?' || (JGc 1,21.48) [pṛthvī]

children.text:
ṛturājaḥ praṇāyyo' yaṃ nyāyyam atra na vidyati |
prapalāyya kva vā yāmaḥ śyāmaṃ naḥ sa tu karṣati ||JGc_1,21.49|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'This king of seasons is to be bowed to — but what is fitting here does not exist!
Where would we flee? But that dark one (<s>Śyāma</s>) draws us!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
dhūmāḥ ṣaṭ-caraṇā visarpi-kharatā-sparśā mṛdu-sparśanāj
jvālāḥ kiṃśuka-sañcayā diśi vidiśy aṅgāra-sārāḥ pikāḥ |
bhasmāny atra parāga-puṣpa-paṭalāny agnir madhuś chadmanā
hā hā kṛṣṇa-ghanaṃ vinā kathaya ko nistāra-vistārakaḥ? ||JGc_1,21.50|| [śārdūla]
atra śrī-kṛṣṇasyāpi bhāvaneyaṃ-
children.translated_text: Here, the sentiment to be understood as belonging to the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself:

children.text:
yadi na bhavati gopa-sundarīṇām
ayam atha melayiteti sampratītiḥ |
kusuma-śara-śara-praṇetur asya
sphuṭam anayatvam ṛtoḥ sahate ko vā? ||JGc_1,21.51|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
'If for the beautiful women of the cow-settlement
there is no such certainty that "this one will unite them" —
then who can bear the lawlessness of this season
that is the creation of the <s>Kusuma-śara</s> (flower-arrowed <s>Kāmadeva</s>)?' // [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text: rādhā-mādhavayoś ca yathā-
children.translated_text: And regarding <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, as follows:

children.text:
rādhā rādhā-padaṃ māsi mādhave vidhutāṃ vidhuḥ |
priyā-saṅga-kṛte labdhuṃ paurṇamāsīm avaikṣata ||JGc_1,21.52|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
<s>Rādhā</s>, in the month of <s>Mādhava</s> (spring/Vaiśākha), dispossessed of the position '<s>Rādhā</s>' (prosperity),
looked toward <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> (the full-moon day / the ascetic woman)
for the purpose of gaining the company of her beloved, the Moon! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: punaḥ sarvāsām udvego yathā-
children.translated_text: And the agitation of all [the gopīs], as follows:

children.text:
dvijānāṃ kākalī tatra viyoge yāga-sammite |
ajani vrajatanvīnāṃ dhāyyevāgni-samindhanī ||JGc_1,21.53|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
The warbling of the birds there, in a separation reckoned as a sacrifice,
became for the slender women of <s>Vraja</s> like a nurse kindling the fire! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atra vṛndayā śikṣitaḥ śukaḥ kaścic chrī-kṛṣṇa-purataḥ prajajalpa-
children.translated_text: There, a certain parrot, trained by <s>Vṛndā</s>, prattled before the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text:
sahante śaśino jvālāṃ vāyoḥ kṣveḍaṃ pibanti ca |
rādhādayo mahābādhā vaiyagryād vrajanāyaka ||JGc_1,21.54|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
'They endure the flames of the moon and drink the hissing of the wind!
<s>Rādhā</s> and the others suffer great affliction — from their distraction, O leader of <s>Vraja</s>!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atra ca kasyām api campakalatāyāṃ śrī-rādhayā sva-hastena likhitaṃ padyam idaṃ vṛndā śrī-govindaṃ darśayāmāsa, yathā-
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Vṛndā</s> showed <s>Govinda</s> a verse written by the glorious <s>Rādhā's</s> own hand upon a certain <s>campaka</s> creeper, as follows:

children.text:
vṛndāvane tamālas tvam ahaṃ campakavallikā |
agayor nau mithaḥ saṅgo vṛndayaiva na cānyathā ||JGc_1,21.55|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
'In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, you are the <s>tamāla</s> tree, and I am the <s>campaka</s> vine;
our mutual union, of the movable and the immovable, is through <s>Vṛndā</s> alone and by no other means!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tac ca dṛṣṭvā muhur api nayanābhyāṃ spṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam idam acintayat-[110] hanta, bhadrāṃ padmāṃ nityam āgacchann api bhadrāṃ padmām adyāpi nāgacchann asmi | śyāmalābhā-madhuratām añcann api śyāmalābhilāṣa-vidhuratām añcann asmi | nakhara-vijita-candrāvalīkatām āpnuvann api candrāvalīṃ prati labdha-tṛṣṇatām āpnuvann asmi |
children.translated_text:
And seeing that, touching it again and again with his eyes, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> thought with longing:
[110] 'Alas, though always approaching <s>Bhadrā</s> and <s>Padmā</s> (the auspicious lotus), I have not even today reached the auspicious lotus [<s>Rādhā</s>]! Though attaining the sweetness of <s>Śyāmalā's</s> beauty, I attain the agitation of longing for <s>Śyāmalā</s>! Though winning the conquest-of-<s>Candrāvalī</s>-ness through my nails [surpassing the moon's lustre], I find myself gaining thirst toward <s>Candrāvalī</s> [herself]!'

children.text: hanta hanta, yadyapy evam evam, tathāpi krama-prāpta-sulalita-viśākhānvita-rādhatāṃ āvrajann apy alabdha-sulalita-viśākhānvita-rādhatāṃ yadāvrajāmi, tad idaṃ mām atiduḥkhākaroti | tasyā rādhāyā eva nūnam iyaṃ vidagdhatā-nidagdha-buddheḥ paṭīyasī paripāṭī iti |
children.translated_text: 'Alas, alas! Even though it is thus and thus — nevertheless, even when I approach the gracefully obtained state of <s>Rādhā</s>-ness accompanied by <s>Sulalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>, when I [actually] arrive without having obtained the state of being with <s>Rādhā</s> accompanied by <s>Sulalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s> — that causes me extreme sorrow! This indeed must be the superior stratagem of <s>Rādhā</s> herself — she of an intellect scorched by cleverness!'

children.text: atha mādhava-pūrṇimām āsājya, sarvato virajya ca, pūrṇa-śikṣā-vilakṣaṇaṃ-manyamanā mādhavaḥ kiñcana durgamaṃ gahanam avagāhamānaḥ parama-muralī-dhamana-līlayā dhairyam ūnayann, amūḥ pradhūyanati sma; muhuḥ pradharṣayann ākarṣati sma ca, sādhāraṇatayā rādhāpi samāgamiṣyatīti |
children.translated_text: Then, having reached the full-moon of the month of <s>Mādhava</s> (Vaiśākha), and having become completely detached from everything, <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), considering himself distinguished by complete instruction, penetrating a certain impassable forest-depth, by the pastime of supreme flute-playing, diminishing [their] fortitude, blew them forth; repeatedly provoking and drawing them — [thinking] 'By the general [summons], <s>Rādhā</s> too will come.'

children.text: rādhā tu tatra dvitra-praharaṃ citravad evāsīn na punar ākṛṣṭatām avaliṣṭa pūrvam anyeṣām ākarṣaṇe tā iva |
children.translated_text: But <s>Rādhā</s>, for two or three watches there, remained like a painting — she did not fall into being drawn as the others had been drawn before by the attraction of the rest.

children.text: atha śrī-vanamāli-śāli vṛndāvanam indranīla-kāntibhir valitam iva dṛśā, yamunā-jala-paramāṇubhiḥ paricitam iva tvacā, mṛgamada-parāgaiḥ sa-rāgam iva nasā vicārya, tābhir viveśa | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, having surveyed <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — adorned with [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] the wearer of the forest garland — as if enveloped by indigo-blue lustres with the eyes, as if anointed with the atoms of <s>Yamunā</s> water upon the skin, discerning the musk-pollen with the nose as if passionate — those [gopīs] entered. And then:

children.text:
ekā dvitrāś catasro yuta-viyutatayā pañcaṣāḥ sapta cāṣṭau
paṅktis tad-vṛddhi-saṅkhyā-miti-rahitatamās tatra yātāḥ samantāt |
yasmād vyaktiḥ prapannā kalita-muralikāt karṣaṇī nāma vidyā
tac-chrī-vaktraṃ nirīkṣya pratihata-matayaḥ śarmalīnā babhūvuḥ ||JGc_1,21.56||[sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
One, two or three, four, in groups joined and separated, five or six, seven and eight,
rows innumerable by the count of that increasing number went there from all sides;
for the particular enchantment named 'Attraction,' emanating from the flute-bearing one, attained manifestation —
seeing the beauty of his face, their minds arrested, they became absorbed in bliss! // [sragdharā]

children.text: tataḥ sa-maryādāś ca tāḥ sahasā hareḥ samaryādaṃ sajjamānā lajjayā tatrāvahitthām apy avalambamānās tasya caraṇa-spṛṣṭi-prathamakaṃ dṛṣṭi-patham adhitiṣṭhanti sma | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And those modest ones, suddenly being received by <s>Hari</s> with proper honor, though also resorting to concealment through bashfulness, first stood in the path of his glance with the touch of his feet. And there:

children.text:
yadyapi murahara-purataḥ kiñcana na vyañjitaṃ tābhiḥ |
tad api vilakṣaṇam evāprathayad amūṣāṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ bhāvam ||JGc_1,21.57|| [udgīti]
children.translated_text:
Although nothing was expressed by them before the slayer of <s>Mura</s>,
nevertheless, their extraordinary [behavior] itself
revealed their extraordinary sentiment! // [udgīti]

children.text: tad evaṃ sa ca samātmane tiṣṭhamānā goṣṭha-ramaṇīr nirīkṣya kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ tal-lakṣmī-niṣṭha-manā āsīt |
children.translated_text: Thus, he too, beholding the cowherd women standing in a state of composure, remained for a few moments with his mind absorbed in their beauty.

children.text: paścāt tu rādhikā-sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ vinā nirjanāraṇyam api saṅgatās tā bhaṅgī-viśeṣād anaṅgī-kurvaṃś cārvaṅgīr āyatyām aṅgīkāra-kāraṇāvadhāraṇāñci kiñcid vyañjanayā rañjayann iva kañja-nayanaḥ punar akṛta-spṛhāya ca gṛhāya prahāpayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Afterwards, without the co-presence of <s>Rādhikā</s>, though they had come together even in the uninhabited forest, making as if to render them bodiless through a special stratagem — those beautiful-limbed ones — the lotus-eyed one, as if delighting them through suggestive speech with the determination of the cause for acceptance in the future, again sent them back to their homes — homes for which they had no desire.

children.text: tatra bhaṅgī-viśeṣo yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the special stratagem was as follows:

children.text:
mayā svabhāvān muralī nināditā
tasmād bhavatyaḥ kila saṅgatā iha |
ataḥ parīyur bata cet pare janāḥ
śaṅke tataḥ suṣṭhv iti nātra tiṣṭhata ||JGc_1,21.58|| [upajāti 12] iti |
rañjanā yathā-
children.translated_text: The delighting, as follows:

children.text:
vrajata bata nivṛtya drāg-vrajaṃ nāpratītaṃ
kuruta mayi na kiṃ vaḥ prītim apy asmi vedmi |
ahaha yadi na vedmi prāṇa-sakhyas tadā sā
bhavad-abhimata-siddhiṃ svena śīghraṃ dadhīta ||JGc_1,21.59|| [mālinī] iti |
children.translated_text:
'Go, return quickly to <s>Vraja</s>! Do not create distrust in me!
Do I not also have love for you? I know!
Ah — but if I do not know, O life's companions, then she
who is dear [to you] will swiftly accomplish the fulfillment of your desire by herself!' // [mālinī]

children.text: yatra tu tāsāṃ-
children.translated_text: Where, however, in their case:

children.text:
nātṛpat karuṇā-dṛṣṭir nātrāpsīt prāpitā śrutiḥ |
nātārpsīt prārcchitā nāsā nātarpīd arpitaṃ manaḥ ||JGc_1,21.60|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
Their compassion-seeking glance was not satiated; their hearing, though delivered [words], did not obtain [satisfaction];
their nose, though it sought [fragrance], was not gratified; their mind, though offered, was not contented! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ gītaṃ, yarhy ambujākṣa [BhP 10.29.36] ityādi |
children.translated_text: Thus was sung, 'O lotus-eyed one' [BhP 10.29.36] and so forth.

children.text: rādhāyāṃ tu tatra yāma-dvayaṃ cetanā-virāmataḥ prāpta-bādhāyāṃ bandhu-samavāye ca nivṛtta-sarvopāye, tūrṇam eva tad-abhyarṇaṃ pūrṇimā vṛndayā saha vindamānā babhūva | vindamānā ca kaṣṭa-bhāg atispaṣṭam ācaṣṭa-
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rādhā</s>, afflicted there for two watches by the cessation of consciousness, and when the assembly of her kinswomen had exhausted all remedies — <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) together with <s>Vṛndā</s> swiftly came to her vicinity. Coming near and herself sharing in the distress, she spoke very clearly:

children.text: yadi mad-uṭaja-kuṭajam etām ekākinīṃ yāma-mātrāyāmam avasaraṃ vāsayatha, tadā mayā nātivirāmayā pratikartavyam iti |
children.translated_text: 'If you house this solitary one at my hermitage of <s>kuṭaja</s> flowers for the duration of merely one watch, then I, who shall know no rest, will attend to the remedy.'

children.text: tataś ca sarva-sammatyā katham api jātayā tasyās tatra saṅgatyā sphurad-atyāveśa-maṅgalā madhumaṅgalena śārṅgiṇam ānāyitavatī | ānāyya cāsanādinā sabhājya smita-sphurad-upālambhaṃ sambhāṣate sma-bhavatu, bhavatā yat kṛtaṃ tat kṛtam eva | samprati tatra sampratipattiṃ vidhehi |
children.translated_text: Then, by the somehow-obtained consent of all, by the meeting with her there, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, radiant with auspicious possession, had the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) brought by <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>. Having brought him and honored him with a seat and the like, she conversed with a rebuke sparkling with smiles: 'So be it — what has been done by you has been done! Now provide the remedy there!'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-mandākṣamam uvāca-hanta, kīdṛśaṃ katham iva?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with slow indulgence: 'Alas — what kind and how?'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-ārtānām asmākaṃ bahu-vārtā na vārtatvāya vartate, kintu nija-mūrti-sparśatas tasyā mūrtim apasāraya |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'The many tidings of us who are afflicted do not serve the purpose of news — but by the touch of your own form, remove the formlessness from hers!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-kā sā?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Who is she?'

children.text: madhumaṅgalaḥ sa-praṇaya-roṣam uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said with affectionate anger:

children.text:
antare vasati yasya cañcalā
jñāyate na jaladena tena cet |
vyaktim īṣad api tarhi saṅgatā
gopyate kim iti sā muhur muhuḥ? ||JGc_1,21.61|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
'If the restless one who dwells within his heart
is not recognized by that cloud [of his],
then if she who has arrived even slightly in union,
why is she concealed again and again?' // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: paurṇamāsī tu smitvā tasya mukhaṃ paśyantī kṛṣṇa-mukhaṃ paśyati sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, however, having smiled, while looking at his (<s>Madhumaṅgala's</s>) face, was looking at <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> face.

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-sa eṣa vātulatayā taralaḥ kāmaṃ jalpatu nāma, yad asabhyānām abhyākhyānam eva ca labhyam | bhavatīnām ājñā tu nāvajñātuṃ śakyate, kintu yuktam eva niyujyatām |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'This one, being fickle by nature, let him prattle as he wishes — for what is obtainable from the declarations of the uncouth! But the command of your ladyships cannot be disregarded — only, let what is fitting be enjoined!'

children.text: vṛndāha-gokula-kula-pālaka sarva-gokula-kula-vilakṣaṇā lakṣmī-lakṣaṇā sā bhavat-sparśa-parāmarśata eva bahir darśaṃ prāpnoti cet, kā tava hāniḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'O protector of the <s>Gokula</s> clan! She who is distinguished from all the <s>Gokula</s> clan, bearing the marks of <s>Lakṣmī</s> — if by the mere consideration of your touch she would attain an external manifestation, what is your loss?'

children.text: hanta, hanta-
children.translated_text: 'Alas, alas!'

children.text:
kṛṣṇa ced bata rādhāyām udāsīno bhavān api |
udāssva, kim ahaṃ tatra kaṭhora-hṛdayā bruve? ||JGc_1,21.62|| [anu]
[133] kṣaṇaṃ vibhāvya punar uvāca-
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! If you are indifferent toward <s>Rādhā</s>,
then be indifferent! What shall I, hard-hearted one, say in that matter?' // [anuṣṭubh]
[133] After reflecting for a moment, she spoke again:

children.text:
sātiśrīr bhavatātyāji śrīvakṣā na bhavāṃs tayā |
vayaṃ tu saralā yugme yugmaṃ roddhuṃ na śaknumaḥ ||JGc_1,21.63|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'She of surpassing beauty was not abandoned by you, O <s>Śrī</s>-chested one, nor you by her!
But we who are simple cannot hold back the pair in this pair!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: kṛṣṇas tuṣṇīṃ sthitavān |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> remained silent.

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-vraja-jana-vraja-jīvana! vācaṃ-yamatām ācaran katham iva giraṃ mama na saṅgirase?
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: 'O life of the <s>Vraja</s>-people's life! Practicing the restraint of speech — how is it that you do not swallow my words?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-adharma evātra marma-bhedī bhavatīti |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'In this matter, it is <s>adharma</s> itself that pierces the very core!'

children.text: paurṇamāsī uvāca-adharmaḥ khalu mayā svīkṛta eva, dharmas tu tava vardhatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> said: '<s>Adharma</s> has indeed been accepted by me; but may <s>dharma</s> increase for you!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-sparśanaṃ vinānyad anumanyatām |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Let something other than touch be approved!'

children.text: vṛndāha-darśanaṃ tāvat kriyatām | tan-mātreṇa siddha-yātre sati parama-guṇa-pātre bhavati katham anyad atha prārthayitāsmahe?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Let a mere glance be given first! If, by that alone, the journey of [your] purpose is accomplished — then, O supreme vessel of virtues — how would we then entreat for anything further?'

children.text: atha-
children.translated_text: Then:

children.text: dehendriya-mano-buddhi prāṇādīnāṃ priyaṃ priye |
children.translated_text: 'Of the body, senses, mind, intellect, life-breaths, and the like, O beloved,

children.text: tvad-anādara-bhājo me jātaṃ sarvam anādṛtam ||
children.translated_text: all that was dear to me has become disregarded by your disregard!' //

children.text: iti rādhāṃ prati cetasi cintayantaṃ kṛṣṇam antaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam api bahis tūṣṇīkatām eva puṣṇantaṃ, madhumaṅgalaḥ kara-sarasije gṛhītvā kuṭaja-kuñja-gṛham eva nītavān | nītvā ca tat-paryanta-bhuvi vṛndāṃ rakṣitvā bāhyam avagāhya, pūrṇimāṃ saṃvāhya tasminn ante-gurutayā tatrakīyaṃ vṛttaṃ citravad īkṣitavān |
children.translated_text: Thus, as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, thinking this in his heart toward <s>Rādhā</s>, though inwardly thirsty, outwardly nourished only silence, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, taking him by the lotus-hand, led him to the very bower-house of <s>kuṭaja</s> bushes. Having led him, posting <s>Vṛndā</s> on the ground at its border, going outside himself, escorting <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, and regarding himself as the outsider with gravity — he watched the events within there as if they were a painting.

children.text: tatra śrī-vṛndā-vacanaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the words of the glorious <s>Vṛndā</s>, as follows:

children.text:
indur indu-bhramaṃ yāti darpaṇaḥ pratibimbatām |
mohaṃ padmālayā yatra kṛṣṇa tan-mukham īkṣyatām ||JGc_1,21.64|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'The moon attains the delusion of being the moon; the mirror, the state of reflection;
the lotus-dwelling <s>Lakṣmī</s> attains bewilderment — where that face of hers [is], O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, behold it!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś ca samāvṛtājasra-pulakāsratayā sa ca tad āluloke, yathā cādyāpi sakhyo gāyanti-
children.translated_text: And then, he too beheld that [face], covered with continuous horripilation and tears, as even now the friends sing:

children.text: tāṃ rahasi gatāṃ kisalaya-śayana-śayānām |
children.translated_text: 'Her — gone there in secret, reclining on a bed of tender leaves,

children.text: harir ālokata nija-muralī-kalakalayā citrita-bhānām ||dhruva||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> beheld — she who was painted by the melodious sound of his own flute!' // [refrain]

children.text: yā nija-vadanāmṛta-rucinā tan-mukha-ratnam ajasram |
children.translated_text: 'She whose face-jewel, by the nectar-luster of his own face,

children.text: bahalam asisravad iha yad bhātaṃ pratipada-sampatad asram ||b||
children.translated_text: was abundantly streaming — what shone here was a tear falling at every step!' //

children.text: yasyā hṛdayaṃ svāntaram anu tat kāyaṃ bhaja dava-kalitam |
children.translated_text: 'She whose heart, following its own interior, consider — her body, seized by a forest-fire;

children.text: bahir api taṃ pratibimba-vyājād vyānañjātmani valitam ||c||
children.translated_text: and externally too, under the pretext of a reflection, it manifested itself enveloped upon him!' //

children.text: yasyāṃ doṣa-trayam iti matibhiḥ prattaṃ kuṅkuma-rāgam |
children.translated_text: 'In whom the triple fault [of redness in eyes, cheeks, and lips] was considered by the discerning as <s>kuṅkuma</s>-color;

children.text: mene muraripur atha sākṣād iva yātaṃ hṛd-gata-rāgam ||d||
children.translated_text: the enemy of <s>Mura</s> then regarded it as if the passion dwelling in the heart had come forth directly!' //

children.text: yāṃ paśyan sa tu sāttvika-bhāvaṃ dadhad api citta-vikāram |
children.translated_text: 'Beholding whom, he, though bearing <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s> (ecstatic symptoms), also [bore] mental agitation,

children.text: bheje yatra pratikṛti-kṛd api pratikṛtir iti ca vicāram ||e||
children.translated_text: adopted the reflection there: "Is she who creates a replica also a replica?"' //

children.text: sa yayā pratikṛtitābhramam āgād evaṃ bhāvana-śālī |
children.translated_text: 'He, by whom the delusion of her being a replica arose — thus, being one who possessed the workshop of sentiments,

children.text: bhāva-parīkṣaṇa-kṛn me kṛtako' py etām indraka-jālī ||f||
children.translated_text: the examiner of sentiments — even this illusionist was my net-of-<s>Indra</s> (a supreme trickster)!' //

children.text: tad api ca yatra spṛhayann atha yām enāṃ mene rādhām |
children.translated_text: 'Yet even there, he, desiring her and considering this one to be <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: vṛndā yācñāṃ pratyācaṣṭa ca dadhad api duḥkhād bādhām ||g||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> declined his request, yet bearing affliction from sorrow!' //

children.text:
sa punar yasyā hetoḥ śocan vyājita-vṛndā-vananam |
vidadhe yadd hṛdi nija-pada-pallavam abhito jīvana-jananam ||h|| ||JGc_1,21.65|| | iti |
children.translated_text:
'He again, grieving for her sake, fashioned a pretense of [wandering in] <s>Vṛndā's</s> forest,
and placed within his heart the tender shoots of his own feet, as the generator of life everywhere!' //

children.text:
kramas tu yathā, tatra tasya ca durnivāraṃ vikāraṃ niśāmya kāmyamānam artham eva vṛndā prārthayāmāsa-śrī-vraja-yuvarāja ! parama-premavatī khalv asau, yataḥ-
hanta kṛṣṇa tava yauvana-sthitau
bhoga-tarṣam anumāya tan-mayam |
duḥkham ātmani vikṛṣya santataṃ
svīya-śarma vijahāv iyaṃ ramā ||JGc_1,21.66|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
The sequence, however, was as follows: therein, perceiving his irresistible agitation and the very object desired, <s>Vṛndā</s> entreated — 'O prince of glorious <s>Vraja</s>! She is indeed one of supreme love, for:
'Alas, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! In the state of your youth, | estimating the thirst for enjoyment to be fully absorbed in that, | continuously drawing suffering upon herself, | this beautiful one has abandoned her own happiness!' || (JGc 1,21.66)

children.text: tad etad avadhāya bhavān apy etad-arthaṃ veṇu-vādanādikaṃ kurvann evāste, tasmād avadhānaṃ sandhāya samādhīyatām |
children.translated_text: Therefore, taking note of this, your honor too remains engaged in flute-playing and the like for this very purpose — so fix your attention and apply yourself!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ sa-gadgadam uvāca-kiṃ kartavyam?
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a choked voice: 'What is to be done?'

children.text:
vṛndāha-hastam eva hṛdi vinyastaṃ kuru |
[147] śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-tad etad atyanucitam |
children.translated_text:
<s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Simply place your hand upon her heart!'
[147] Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'But that is most improper!'

children.text: vṛndāha-tarhi caraṇam eva tathācara |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Then at least place your foot [upon her heart] — do that!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇas tuṣṇīṃ tasthau |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> stood silent.

children.text: vṛndā pādayoḥ patantī-hanta, mā vilambam avalambasva iti kāku-vyākulā tayor ekaṃ balad iva tasyā hṛdi saṃvalayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, falling at his feet — 'Alas! Do not cling to delay!' — distraught with entreaty, forcibly as it were, pressed one of his [lotus feet] against her (<s>Rādhā's</s>) heart.

children.text: kṛṣṇaś ca kampa-sampadā padāravindaṃ sandadhad eva vaivaśya-vaśyatāṃ vindati sma |
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, placing his lotus-foot [there] with a wealth of trembling, found himself overcome by helplessness.

children.text: tataś ca sañjīvanī-pallava-vinyāsavat tal-lava-sparśata eva cakṣuḥ-puṭa-yugam udghaṭayya tayā sa eva dṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, just as by the application of the <s>Sañjīvanī</s> sprout, from the mere touch of that fraction [of contact], she opened the pair of her eye-lids and beheld him — that very one.

children.text: tadaiva ca-
children.translated_text: And at that very moment:

children.text:
subhruvo muraripoś ca dṛg-dvayaṃ
bimba-dambham aviśat parasparam |
śobhayā vyativilobhataḥ sphuṭaṃ
tāv amuṣya parivṛttim aicchatām ||JGc_1,21.67|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'The pair of eyes of the beautiful-browed one and of the foe of <s>Mura</s> | entered each other's reflection-image; | manifestly enchanting each other with their beauty, | those two clearly desired the return of that [mutual gaze]!' || (JGc 1,21.67)

children.text: tadaiva sa cātrakīyāpatrapātaḥ śirasi vasanāvaraṇaḥ sahasā nirgamya pūrṇimāṃ praṇamya ca calita evāsīt | kintu skhalann iva calan, karmaṇā narmaṇā ca madhumaṅgala-dattāvalambaḥ sakhi-kulaṃ saṃvalate sma |
children.translated_text: At that very moment, he — shamefaced with the embarrassment pertaining to her, covering his head with a garment — suddenly went out, and having bowed to <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, had already set off. But stumbling as if while walking, supported by <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> who offered assistance through jest and sport, he rejoined the company of friends.

children.text: sā ca svapnam iva paśyantī vaivaśyata eva samuttiṣṭhantī, nirakṣara-sūkṣma-rodanaṃ cānutiṣṭhantī yadā vṛndayā sādaraṃ kṛtasāntvā, tadā darasāntvā pūrṇimāṃ natvā vṛndayā saha suhṛttamekṣita-tad-āgame tasminn aparāhnetame vrajaṃ gatvā, katham api samaya-katipayān gamayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And she, seeing as if in a dream, rising from helplessness itself, and softly weeping without syllables — when she was respectfully consoled by <s>Vṛndā</s>, then, slightly consoled, having bowed to <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, together with <s>Vṛndā</s>, observed by her dearest friends as she departed — in that late afternoon, having gone to <s>Vraja</s>, she somehow passed a few hours.

children.text: tad ārabhya tu sa khalu parasparaṃ sparśo' yaṃ sparśāyaiva paraṃ sañcakpe,
children.translated_text: From that point onward, that mutual touch was indeed considered by her solely for the purpose of further touch,

children.text:
yataḥ sakṛt tādṛśaṃ sukham upalabhya kṣaṇāt tad-viyuktayā tayā katham iva prathamānaṃ duḥkhaṃ stabhyatām? tat tu sukhaṃ sva-saṃvedyam eva, na tu nivedyam | tathā hi-
tayor yāvasthāsīd vyatimilana-śarma prasajati kaviḥ
ko vā tāṃ syāt kavayitum iha svalpakam api |
yayoḥ kāśmīraṃ tat patitam api pārasparikam apy
aho paulindīnām api tad iva śaśvad vyatanuta ||JGc_1,21.68|| [śikhariṇī]
[158] tad evaṃ yadā hareḥ padāravindaṃ vindamānāni kuṅkuma-paṅkāni kṛta-tad-aṅkāni pulindī-jātālaṅkāratayā jātāni, tadānīm anyāsāṃ dhanyānāṃ pūrvavad pūrvānubhava-racana-pūrvakaṃ vacanam idam, pūrṇāḥ pulindyaḥ ityādi | [BhP 10.21.17]
children.translated_text:
because, having experienced such happiness even once, how could the foremost suffering be restrained by her when separated from that even for a moment? That happiness, however, is to be experienced only by oneself, not to be reported. Thus:
'Whatever state of bliss arose from their mutual meeting — what poet | could be capable of composing even a small portion of it here? | That <s>Kāśmīra</s> (saffron) which had fallen from their mutual [contact] — | alas! — perpetually extended even to the <s>Pulindī</s> women as if it were [their own treasure]!' || (JGc 1,21.68)
[158] Thus, when the saffron-pastes that had found the lotus-foot of <s>Hari</s>, marked with his insignia, had become the ornaments of the <s>Pulindī</s> women — at that time, of those other blessed ones, with the composition of prior experience as before, came this utterance: 'The <s>Pulindī</s> women are fulfilled' and so on [BhP 10.21.17].

children.text: atra cedaṃ vyañjitam-
children.translated_text: Herein is suggested the following:

children.text:
āstāṃ sā dayitā yadīya-kuca-yuk śrī-kuṅkumaṃ tat-padaṃ
prāptaṃ tat-tṛṇam apy aho vijayatāṃ sākṣāt tu tat-saṅgi yat |
asmattas tu pulinda-jāti-sudṛśāṃ bhāgyaṃ ca dūre sthitaṃ
yās tat prāpya nijāṅga-lepana-sukhād āsedire pūrṇatām ||JGc_1,21.69|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'Let that beloved one be set aside — from whose bosom the glorious <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) reached his foot, | and even the grass that directly touched that [foot] — ah! — let it triumph! | But from us, even the fortune of the fine-eyed women of the <s>Pulinda</s> tribe stands far away — | they who, having obtained that [saffron], attained fulfillment from the happiness of smearing it on their own limbs!' || (JGc 1,21.69)

children.text: atha kathakaḥ samāpanam āha sma-
children.translated_text: Then the narrator spoke the conclusion:

children.text:
sa īdṛk-praṇayī labdhas tvayā rādhe purā tu yaḥ |
nānā-manorathaṃ cakre rathavad bhavad-āptaye ||JGc_1,21.70|| [anu]
children.translated_text:
'Such a lover was obtained by you, O <s>Rādhā</s>, formerly — he who | fashioned manifold desires like a chariot for the attainment of you!' || (JGc 1,21.70)

Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the twenty-first <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Stealing of the Maidens' Garments — the Attraction of All Tender Ones'
|| 21 ||

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
kumārī-vastra-haraṇa-sukumārī-samasta-karṣaṇaṃ nāma
ekaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||21||
atha dvāviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the twenty-second <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter):

children.text: yajña-bhāryā-sad-upacaryā-paryāptiḥ
children.translated_text: The Sufficiency of the Virtuous Service of the Wives of the <s>Yajña</s>-[performers]

children.text: atha prabhāta-kathāyāṃ prabhāta-prathāyāṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ sphurad-utkaṇṭhas tal-līlāntaraṃ śaṃsan śaṃsad-upalabdhaṃ kartum ārabdhavān |
children.translated_text: Then, in the morning narrative, in the manner of the morning, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, trembling with eagerness, narrating another sport of his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>], began to make manifest what was perceived through praise.

children.text: tatra śrī-daśama-skandha-prabandha-saṅgamana-maṅgalācaraṇa-pūrvakaṃ tat-kathanam, yathā-
children.translated_text: Therein, with the auspicious invocation of the connection to the composition of the glorious Tenth <s>Skandha</s>, the narration was as follows:

children.text: gatvā kāmyakam adri-dhātu-rucimuk kurvan vrajaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having gone to the <s>Kāmyaka</s> [forest], making <s>Vraja</s> to the south beautiful with the luster of mountain minerals,

children.text: gharmartau dhavalānikhavraśatatṛḍ-nirjiṣṇu-kṛṣṇāṃ vrajan |
children.translated_text: traversing [the land] — dark as hundreds of glistening white quartz [rocks] conquering the thirst of heat —

children.text: vṛkṣān suṣṭhu pathi stuvan dhavalayā pītāṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ piban
children.translated_text: praising the trees excellently along the path, and drinking the white, yellow, and dark [waters],

children.text: kṣud-vyājād adhiyajña-patni-karuṇā-kārī hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||JGc_1,22.1||
children.translated_text: under the pretext of hunger, <s>Hari</s> — the bestower of compassion upon the wives of the sacrificial lord — protect you!' || (JGc 1,22.1)

children.text:
tathā hi-
atha gopaiḥ parivṛto yaśodānanda-nandanaḥ |
vṛndāvanād gato dūraṃ cārayan gāḥ sahāgrajaḥ ||JGc_1,22.2||nidāghārkātape tigme cchāyābhiḥ svābhirātmanaḥ |
ātapatrāyitān vīkṣya drumān mitrāṇy abhāṣata ||JGc_1,22.3|| [BhP 10.22.29-30]
children.translated_text:
Thus:
'Then the son of <s>Yaśodā</s> and <s>Nanda</s>, surrounded by cowherds, | together with his elder brother, went far from <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, grazing the cows.' || (JGc 1,22.2)
'In the fierce heat of the summer sun, seeing trees | that had become umbrellas through their own shadows, | he spoke to [them as] friends.' || (JGc 1,22.3) [BhP 10.22.29-30]

children.text: tatra ca megha-nirghoṣa-nibha-gambhīratā-sambhṛta-madhura-svarata eva harṣam utkarṣayan mitra-mukhyān pratyekaṃ racitābhimukhyāṃś cakāra | yathā-
children.translated_text: And there, raising delight with his sweet voice endowed with a depth resembling the rumble of a cloud, he made each of the chief friends face him individually. As follows:

children.text: he stoka-kṛṣṇa he aṃśo śrīdāman subalārjuna |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Stokakṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Aṃśu</s>! <s>Śrīdāman</s>! <s>Subala</s>! <s>Arjuna</s>!

children.text: viśāla rṣabha tejasvin devaprastha varūthapa ||[BhP 10.22.31]
children.translated_text: <s>Viśāla</s>! <s>Ṛṣabha</s>! O radiant one! <s>Devaprastha</s>! <s>Varūthapa</s>!' || [BhP 10.22.31]

children.text: tata eva ca tān amṛta-kṛtābhiṣekān iva kṛtvā sa-kautukam uvāca-māṃ sukhayantu evābhimukhatas ete taravo virājante, tasmād bhavadbhir vilokya pṛthak pṛthag upaślokyantām |
children.translated_text: And from that point, having anointed them as if with an ablution of nectar, he said with curiosity: 'These trees that stand facing me bring me happiness — therefore, having beheld them, let them be praised in verse by you, each one separately!'

children.text: sarve vihasya procuḥ-bhavān evāsmāsu vismāyakatayā kavi-maṇḍalākhaṇḍala-gaṇḍa-maṇḍanam asti | tasmād ātmanaiva varṇayatu |
children.translated_text: All laughed and said: 'Your honor alone is among us the ornament of the cheeks of the lord of the circle of poets, [producing] amazement! Therefore, describe them yourself!'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-smitam uvāca-śrūyatāṃ nāma-
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'Listen then!

children.text: etenāṅgata eva kintu guṇato' py addhā mahānto matā
children.translated_text: 'By their limbs alone these are indeed [great]; but truly by their qualities too they are considered great,

children.text: yat tāpādi-nivāraṇaiḥ sva-vapuṣo jīvānavantaḥ sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: because through the removal of heat and other [sufferings], they stand in their own bodies as infinite [givers of] life.

children.text: eṣām eva ca janma yat tu phalavad dṛśyeta tac cettham apy
children.translated_text: And that their birth should appear fruitful — even that should be considered thus:

children.text: ūhadhvaṃ yad aśeṣa-jīvanatayā rājanty amī sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,22.4||
children.translated_text: that they reign everywhere through [their nature of] giving life to all!' || (JGc 1,22.4)

children.text: kiṃ ca-
phalaiḥ puṣpaiś chāyā-cchadana-samid-ādyaiś ca taravaḥ
children.translated_text: 'With fruits, flowers, shade, covering leaves, firewood, and so on, the trees

children.text: svabhāvād viśveṣām upakṛti-vidhā dhanya-tanavaḥ |
children.translated_text: are by nature disposed to beneficence toward all — they of blessed bodies!

children.text: narāḥ karhy apy eke vidhi-vaśatayā tat-kṛti-kṛtas
children.translated_text: Human beings, at some time or other, perform such deeds by the force of destiny;

children.text: tato bhaktāḥ pūrve sukṛtam anu bhāktāḥ kila pare ||JGc_1,22.5||
children.translated_text: therefore, the former are devoted [by nature], while the latter are distributed [by merit] — so it is said!' || (JGc 1,22.5)
Moreover:

children.text: atra vṛndāvana-vāstavyatā punar eṣāṃ stavyatām apy atikrāmati iti gūḍham abhimatam |
children.translated_text: Herein, the hidden meaning is that their residence in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> also transcends even praiseworthiness.

children.text: sarve sa-smitam ūcuḥ-kavi-cakra-cakravartinā bhavatā na kiṃ vā supraśastaṅkaraṃ bhavitā, tato yad eva yojayiṣyate, tad eva vijeṣyate | tathā hi-
children.translated_text:
All said with a smile: 'By your honor — the emperor of the circle of poets — what could fail to be praised most excellently? Therefore, whatever you compose shall triumph. Thus:
'Where you, skilled in the art of verbal composition, have attained the status of the best of speakers,

children.text: vāco-yukti-paṭur yatra tvaṃ vadāvadatāṃ gataḥ |
vācaspatiś ca tatra syān na vācaḥ-patir aṇv api ||JGc_1,22.6||
children.translated_text: there <s>Vācaspati</s> (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) himself would be not even the slightest lord of speech!' || (JGc 1,22.6)

children.text: kṛṣṇo' pi sa-smitam uvāca-bhavatu, kadācid etad apy anubhaviṣyatha iti nānā-sukha-vitarakara-puruha-bhūruhāṇāṃ vanyayā mihira-kanyā-tīram udanyayā mudā jagāma | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too said with a smile: 'So be it — at some time you too shall experience this!' — and with the delight of the wilderness of trees bestowing manifold happiness, he joyfully went to the bank of the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) with the desire for water. And there:

children.text: vyajjann aṅghripa-śaṃsana-svavacanaṃ yajñāṅganānugrahaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Manifesting his own words of praise of trees as the grace upon the wives of the sacrificers,

children.text: cātmīyāgami bhojya-vartma sa yadā santyajya kṛṣṇāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: and his own approaching path of food-to-be-eaten — when he, abandoning the dark [<s>Yamunā</s>], went [further] —

children.text: tarhi svacchatarā himāḥ śubha-karāḥ svādūr apaḥ pītavān
children.translated_text: then, purer cool [waters], auspicious [in nature], sweet — the waters he drank;

children.text: aghnyānāṃ nikaras tataḥ svayam apur gopālakās tan-mukhāḥ ||JGc_1,22.7||
children.translated_text: and from those, the herds of inviolable cows themselves drank, and the cowherds [drank] facing him!' || (JGc 1,22.7)

children.text: tataś ca vidūraṃ samujjhitātalina-phalinatara-taru-vrajasya vraja-rājñī-prahita-mādhyāhnika-bhojya-sampatti-viyojyatā-bhāg-upasattikasya kṛṣṇasya tat-tṛṣṇatāṃ vitarkya tad-bhāva-bhāvitatayā svayam apy atīva tat-tṛṣṇā-bhājaḥ stokakṛṣṇādayas tad-abhāva-bhāvanā api praṇaya-maya-paryutsukatayā vyañjita-tat-kṛta-bhojana-vartma-vañcanāḥ karāñcala-cālana-pūrvakaṃ tad-yācñām akurvata-
children.translated_text: Then, from afar — in a grove of trees more fruitful and free of palms — being the portion of one who was separated from the midday meal-provisions dispatched by the queen of <s>Vraja</s> — surmising <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> hunger, being themselves most desirous of that [food] through identification with his state, <s>Stokakṛṣṇa</s> and the others — even while contemplating the absence of that [food] — with the eagerness born of affection, revealing the deception of the path of food prepared by him, with the preliminary waving of their fingertips, made their entreaty:

children.text: rāma rāma mahā-bāho kṛṣṇa duṣṭa-nibarhaṇa |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rāma</s>! O <s>Rāma</s>! O mighty-armed one! O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, destroyer of the wicked!

children.text: ito' vidūre su-mahad vanaṃ tālāli-saṅkulam ||[BhP 10.23.1]
children.translated_text: Not far from here is a very great forest, dense with rows of <s>tāla</s> trees!' || [BhP 10.23.1]

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu sa-smitam uvāca-atrāloka-pathāśoka-vanikāyām anaśanīya-prasavāyām aśanāyantas te bhavantaḥ kutra vā psātavyaṃ lapsyante ?
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'In this grief-free grove within the range of sight here, where the fruits are not to be eaten — you who are hungry, where indeed will you find something to eat?'

children.text: ārtiś ced varivarti, tarhi nikaṭām api kuṭilayā sūratanayā-ghaṭanayā dūrāyamāṇām itas tu dakṣiṇāhi yā śūrasena-purī, tām uttareṇa niravajñaṃ yajña-śālā-mālām ālokayanta evānena samyag upatiṣṭhamānena pathā pratiṣṭhadhvam | gatvā ca tān kārmān karmaṭhācāryatamasya mama ca nāmnā yācadhvam | kintu bhikṣākāṇāṃ titikṣā-mātram ucitam iti śikṣā manasi kāryā |
children.translated_text: 'If distress does indeed persist, then — being made distant even though nearby by the winding course of the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) — to the south from here, the city of <s>Śūrasena</s> [<s>Mathurā</s>] — passing to the north of it, looking respectfully at the row of sacrificial halls — proceed on this well-attended path! And having gone, ask those sacrificers — most diligent practitioners — in my name! But the instruction to be kept in mind is that for mendicants, mere forbearance is fitting.'

children.text: atha te' pi ke' pi saṃvalitāś calitāḥ | svayam ayaṃ tu tadīya-gatyāgati-dṛṣṭy-artham upanadaṃ mahā-kuṭṭimam adhitaṣṭhau | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then some of them, having assembled, set out. And he himself, for the purpose of observing their coming and going, stood upon a great elevated platform. And then:

children.text: saurabhyaṃ dhūma-dhārā yajur-anupaṭhanaṃ śubhra-śālā dvijānāṃ
children.translated_text: 'The fragrance, the streams of smoke, the recitation of the <s>Yajur</s> [Veda], the gleaming sacrificial halls, the <s>brāhmaṇas'</s>

children.text: gatyāgatyādi-ceṣṭāḥ śubha-yuta-hutabhug-vedi-bhāg-ṛtvijaś ca |
children.translated_text: activities of going and coming, the fire-pit with auspicious oblation-fire, the portion of the priests —

children.text: gatvā natvāpy abhīkṣṇaṃ puṭita-karatayā nādare' py asthur ete
children.translated_text: having gone and bowed repeatedly, with cupped hands, yet receiving no regard, they stood there,

children.text: yasmād brahmaṇya-deva-svatulita-suhṛdaḥ kintv idaṃ māṃ dunoti ||JGc_1,22.8||
children.translated_text: because [the brāhmaṇas were] friends of equal rank to the god of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — but this pains me!' || (JGc 1,22.8)

children.text: tataś ca tān prakṛti-śleṣeṇa kenāpy ākṛti-viśleṣeṇa veṣeṇa ca gopān jñātvā vipratā-garva-parvatam ārūḍhās te tu vyūḍha-bahula-sthala-dṛṣṭayas tiṣṭhanti sma | tathāpi sakhāyas te kṛṣṇasya bubhukṣā-sukṣāmatāṃ sākṣād ivānubhūya dūyamāna-manasaḥ svayam eva nivedayāmāsuḥ | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, recognizing them as cowherds by some natural intimacy despite their unfamiliar appearance and attire — those [<s>brāhmaṇas</s>], having ascended the mountain of pride in their <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-status, with their vision fixed upon the thick level ground [i.e., worldly ritual], stood [unmoved]. Nevertheless, those friends, as if directly experiencing <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> sharp pangs of hunger, with aching hearts, reported of their own accord. Because:

children.text: huṃ phaṭ śrauṣaḍ-vauṣaḍ ity evam ādyāḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Huṃ</s>! <s>Phaṭ</s>! <s>Śrauṣaṭ</s>! <s>Vauṣaṭ</s>! — such and similar

children.text: śabdāḥ yasmin na kvacit kṛṣṇa-mukhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: sounds, in which nowhere is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the chief —

children.text: tasmiṃs teṣāṃ kiṃ ruciḥ syāt parantu
children.translated_text: in that [setting], what delight could there be for them? And yet,

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇārthaṃ kiṃ na te mānayanti ||JGc_1,22.9||
children.translated_text: for the sake of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, why do they not honor [them]?' || (JGc 1,22.9)

children.text:
atha nivedanaṃ cedam--bho bho bhūmi-devāḥ ! kiñcid evāvadhānaṃ vidhīyatām | rāma-rāmānujau khalu parama-prabhāva-yujau śrutavadbhir bhavadbhir avadhāritāv eva staḥ | tau cātra bhavad-vidhānāṃ sannidhānam eva dhenu-sevanānurodhād āgatavantau | kintv adya sadya evānavadya-krīḍā-maya-śūratā-kautuka-puratas tata itaḥ saṅgatyāsannāpi pratyāsannāpi śrī-gopādhibhū-sadana-bhūr vidūrāyamāṇāsmākaṃ bhāti sma | gṛha-lokena ca na tathālocayāmbabhūvimahe | tata eva sākṣāl-lakṣmī-pati-gṛhāyamāṇa-gṛhād bhojana-saṃyojanaṃ vinā krīḍā-yudhi ca kṣudhitāv abhūtām | tataś ca kula-paramparā-prāpta-vyavahāraṃ paryāyatayā pitṛ-paryāyatayā bhavatsu saṅkocam aparyālocamānau pitṛ-bhavanād iva bhavadīya-savanād annaṃ yācitam akurvātām
iti |
children.translated_text: Now this was the petition: 'O, O earth-gods (<s>brāhmaṇas</s>)! Kindly grant but a moment's attention! <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) are indeed endowed with supreme power — this has been ascertained by your learned selves. And these two have come here, to the very vicinity of your honors, following the needs of cow-tending. But today, due to the excitement of blameless sport and martial play coming to the fore, though the estate of the glorious king of the cowherds (<s>Nanda</s>) was nearby, even close at hand, it appeared to us as exceedingly distant — coming from here and there in our wanderings.
