And we did not think to look toward the household folk. Therefore, from the house that has come to resemble the very abode of <s>Lakṣmī's</s> lord, without the arrangement of a meal, and in the play-battle too, these two became hungry. And so, regarding the customary practice received through the lineage of generations, in the succession of fathers' succession, they had you — toward whom they felt no hesitation — request food from your sacrificial session, as if from a father's house.' Thus.

children.text: atha tathāpi manasy abhakti-rasikatā-vaśikatayā tad asat-kṛtya tuṣṇīm-bhuṣṇuṣu teṣv antar-vāṇiṃ-manyeṣu tādṛg-adhanyeṣu punar amī manasi mīmāṃsayāmāsuḥ-[17] nūnam asmān ete mūḍhān matvā gūḍhānubhāsaṇā babhūvus tasmād gaty-antara-racana-niṣiddha-bhāvāya siddhāntataś cāmīṣāṃ suṣṭhu mauna-biddhāntastāṃ kurma iti | [18] atha spaṣṭaṃ punar ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, even so, when those [<s>brāhmaṇas</s>], whose minds were enslaved by the disposition of non-devotion, disregarded that [request] and remained intent on silence — considering the inner voice [of ego], being such unfortunate ones — these [boys] deliberated within their minds: [17] 'Surely these [<s>brāhmaṇas</s>] considered us fools and made their response in concealment; therefore, to make an alternative course of action impossible, let us also establish well within them the inner state of silence-doctrine!' [18] Then they spoke openly:

children.text:
dīkṣādy-agnīṣoma-paśvaṅga-homa-
prāntaṃ vijñair yājñikānnaṃ na bhojyam |
sautrāmaṇyāṃ sarvadā neti viprās
tābhyām anyatrāsti tad grāhyam eva ||JGc_1,22.10|| iti |
tatra-bhavad-bhavad-anuṣṭhāna-dṛṣṭita evāsmābhis tad-avasaraḥ sphuṭaṃ niṣṭaṅkita iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therein the sense is: 'We have clearly discerned the occasion from the very observation of your honors' own performance.'

children.text: tad evaṃ bhikṣā-niṣṭhānām iva tasminn upatiṣṭhamānānām api śāstrārthaṃ nayamānānāṃ tad avadhārya te vāryācāryā manasi paryālocayāmāsuḥ-hanta ! brāhmaṇā evāsmākam etān brahma-vicāram api viśiṣṭatayā lobhād anuśiṣṭavantaḥ santi | yena tatrāpi kṛta-mukhatayā mukharatām āpannāḥ | bhavatu, tathāpy ete paramebhyayopalabhyamānāḥ kiñcid dāna-rūpam avadānaṃ vinā pratyutādānāya param atrāgatāḥ | aho ! kali-praveśa-deśasya deśa-rūpam idam |
children.translated_text: Thus, when even those who stood there as if devoted to begging were citing the meaning of <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), having ascertained that, those hostile teachers deliberated within their minds: 'Alas! These very <s>brāhmaṇas</s> [boys] have instructed us in the inquiry of <s>Brahman</s> too, with superior distinction — out of greed! By which, having gained facility in that too, they have attained loquacity. So be it — yet these ones, being perceived by the supreme [Lord], have come here not for some gift-like offering, but rather for receiving! Ah! This is the very form of the region where <s>Kali</s>-[yuga] enters!'

children.text: kiṃ ca, kecic ca vipaścitas tayor īśvaratām āropayanti | tarhi bata garhitaṃ kṣudhādikaṃ katham etāvarhataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Moreover, some wise ones attribute lordship to those two. Then alas, how can they be worthy of such contemptible things as hunger and the like?

children.text: tad etad vibhāvya durbhāva-bhāvatayā tathā sthiteṣu bahu-pacanatāyām api mitampaceṣu dvirjātatāyām api yathā-jāteṣu yājñika-kitavatāṃ yāteṣu teṣu yācñāyāṃ vadanānatā-kadanataḥ parasparam īkṣitvā mandaṃ mandaṃ mandākṣa-mandatayā śrī-govindam eva te vindate sma |
children.translated_text: Then, having discerned this, when those of evil disposition remained thus — though abundant in their cooking, yet miserly; though twice-born, yet as if merely born [once] — when those who had attained the state of sacrificial charlatanry were thus, the [boys], from the degradation of the downcast faces in begging, having looked at each other, slowly, with the sluggishness of drooping eyes, returned to the glorious <s>Govinda</s> alone.

children.text: govindaś ca tāṃs tathāvidhān netra-pathān vidhāya manohatān vijñāya ca hasati sma-ehi manyāmahe, yājñikebhyaḥ sva-labhyam abhyādadidhve yathā vṛkṣebhyaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: And <s>Govinda</s>, having observed them in such a state upon the path of his vision, and understanding their dejection, laughed and said: 'Come, we think you obtained from the ritualists what is obtainable by you — just as from trees!'

children.text: te' pi sa-smitam ūcuḥ-tat tu bhavanta eva jānanti, vayam api yat-preraṇa-samīraṇa-vikīrṇa-manaso jātāḥ |
children.translated_text: They too said with a smile: 'That indeed your lordship knows; we too have become ones whose minds were scattered by the impulsion of your urging!'

children.text: kṛṣṇas tv antar yajña-patnīnāṃ svāvaloka-prayatnānāṃ sañjānaṃs tatra cāvaśya-lābhaṃ pratijānānaḥ prahasya provāca-ā evaṃ manyadhve tarhi bhadram | mayā tu patriṇām eṣāṃ satriṇāṃ ca teṣāṃ tāratamyāvadhāraṇārtham eva tatra-bhavantaḥ prasthāpitāḥ | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, inwardly perceiving the efforts of the sacrifice-wives to behold him, and knowing that gain would certainly be obtained from them, laughed and said: 'Ah, you think thus — then well and good! I dispatched your honors there precisely to ascertain the relative hierarchy between those [husbands] endowed with foliage [i.e., the ritualists] and those performers of sacrifice. And thus:

children.text: amānināṃ yathā dharmaḥ sthitas tadvan na māninām |
children.translated_text: As <s>dharma</s> is established for the humble,

children.text: adyāpi cen na pratītha drāk tat-patnīḥ pratīta ca ||JGc_1,22.11||
children.translated_text:
so it is not for the proud;
if even now you do not trust [them], swiftly trust their wives instead! ||22.11||

children.text: bhavanti ca bhavanta iva yajña-patnī-janā mat-prema-mātra-sayatna-dhanāḥ | ye khalu dhṛta-mada-nava-loka-dharmaṃ dvyaha-tarṣaṃ jalaṃ pibanti, try-ahātyāsaṃ dvitra-grāsaṃ bhuñjate |
children.translated_text: And the sacrifice-wife folk are, like your good selves, ones whose only striving wealth is love for me. They indeed drink water of two-day thirst, observing the newly-adopted worldly <s>dharma</s> with intoxicated pride, and eat but two or three morsels over three days.'

children.text: sarve sa-vailakṣyam ācakṣata-hanta satyam evedam |
children.translated_text: All said with embarrassment: 'Alas, this is indeed true!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-bāḍham |
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Certainly!'

children.text: sarve sāścaryam ūcuḥ-tarhi kutukam idaṃ vidāṅkarvāma |
children.translated_text: All said with wonder: 'Then let us perform this curious [experiment]!'

children.text: iti kṛṣṇodyam anu sodyamatayā tatra tan-nimeṣata eva jigamiṣatsu teṣu sa-praṇayavatsu kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇam uvāca-annaṃ ca tatra śrīmad-āryādi-sahita-mad-artham arthayadhvam |
children.translated_text: Thus, with enthusiasm following <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> initiative, when those affectionate ones wished to depart there at that very instant, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with longing: 'And request food there on behalf of me, along with the honored elder [<s>Balarāma</s>] and others.'

children.text: atha punar atīva kautuka-dravataḥ parasparam atītya dravanaḥ patnī-śālāyāṃ dvija-patnīr vilokayāmāsus tābhir vilokayāmāsire ca, kṛṣṇāt prati ca iti ca niśckyire |
children.translated_text: Then, exceedingly melting with curiosity, overtaking one another in their running, they beheld the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-wives in the wives' quarters, and were beheld by them; and they ascertained that these were from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and so forth.

children.text: vilokanāt pūrva-kramas tu yathā-
children.translated_text: The sequence prior to the beholding was as follows:

children.text: sā kāpi dhvani-mādhurī-svara-kalā-rāga-valla-valgutā
children.translated_text: That certain sweetness of voice-sound, the beauty of the melodic art of <s>rāga</s>,

children.text: varṇa-nyāsa-śubhaṃyutā kavi-jana-stavyārtha-citra-prathā |
children.translated_text: the auspiciousness of the arrangement of syllables, the wondrous renown of meanings praised by poets,

children.text: kaṃsārer guṇa-rūpa-keli-kalanā bāṣpādibhiḥ sārdratā
children.translated_text: the portrayal of the qualities, beauty, and sport of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — the moistness through tears and such —

children.text: yajña-strī-kalitā kramād iha sakhīn ārdrān akārṣīn muhuḥ ||JGc_1,22.12||
children.translated_text: performed by the sacrifice-wives, gradually made the companions moist again and again! ||22.12||

children.text: tataś ca tāḥ-
children.translated_text: And then they [the wives]:

children.text: gavādhva-sambandha-nibandha-vastravān
children.translated_text: Seeing ones bearing garments bound with the fastening-band of the cow-path,

children.text: praśasta-vetrān muralī-puraskṛtān |
children.translated_text: carrying excellent staffs, with flutes held before them,

children.text: piñchāvataṃsān avataṃsa-sundarān
children.translated_text: adorned with peacock-feather crests, beautiful with ear-ornaments —

children.text: vilokya kṛṣṇāgam apy amaṃsata ||JGc_1,22.13||
children.translated_text: they deemed that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself had come! ||22.13||

children.text: tataś ca yat kṛṣṇa-samāgamaṃ te
children.translated_text: And then, when those best among the wise, bowing down,

children.text: vyajijñapan vijña-varāḥ praṇamya |
children.translated_text: announced the meeting with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: tās tad dviruktāyitam apy apūrvaṃ
children.translated_text: they — considering that even-though-repeated [news] as unprecedented

children.text: pūrvaṃ ca matvā na viduḥ sma kṛtyam ||JGc_1,22.14||
children.translated_text: and as if for the first time — knew not what to do! ||22.14||

children.text: yasyājasra-didṛkṣayā vidalita-prāyāḥ sadāmūḥ sthitās
children.translated_text: They who had always stood nearly shattered by the constant desire to see him —

children.text: tasya prāṇa-suhṛd-varāḥ svayam amī tat-preraṇād āgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: his dearest life-friends themselves have come, sent by him!

children.text: tat-samprāptim avādiṣuḥ punar adaḥ prārthyaṃ ca kiñcit tad apy
children.translated_text: They announced his arrival and moreover requested something —

children.text: annaṃ tatra kathaṃ kathaṃ kathaya tāḥ prāpsyanti dhairya-sthitim ||JGc_1,22.15||
children.translated_text: and that too was food! — how, how, tell me, could they maintain composure? ||22.15||

children.text: tataś ca-
yogyam atra kim ayogyam ity amū-
children.translated_text: 'What is fitting here and what is unfitting?' — in the disclosure

children.text: neyabhojya-vivṛtāv anirṇayāḥ |
children.translated_text: of what was to be given to them, they had no deliberation;

children.text: tat-tadīyam akhilaṃ ca bhājanaṃ
children.translated_text: all the vessels belonging to them and to their husbands

children.text: kṣipram ādadata vipra-subhruvaḥ ||JGc_1,22.16||
children.translated_text: the fair-browed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-wives swiftly took up! ||22.16||
And then:

children.text: atha puraskṛta-gopa-sutāyutā
children.translated_text: Then, placing the cowherd boys at the front,

children.text: vividha-bhojana-bhājana-mastakāḥ |
children.translated_text: with heads [bearing] various food-vessels,

children.text: pratipada-kramaṇaṃ kiyad agrataḥ
children.translated_text: at every step, 'How much further ahead

children.text: sa iti tarṣi-giraḥ paricakramuḥ ||JGc_1,22.17||
children.translated_text: is he?' — thus, with thirsty words, they stepped along! ||22.17||

children.text: āmodaḥ kānti-pūraḥ sukhadadapadatā garjad ūrjasvi-bhāṣā
children.translated_text: A fragrance, a flood of radiance, a joy-giving tread, a thundering mighty speech,

children.text: vidyud vidyud-ghana-śrīḥ smita-vadana-vidhu-dyota-lakṣmī-pracāraḥ |
children.translated_text: a lightning, the splendor of a lightning-cloud, the glory of a smiling moon-face's radiance,

children.text: āyāntv ity ukti-hasta-prathana-madhurimā yat-kramād āvirāsīt
children.translated_text: the sweetness of the gesture 'Come!' — extended by his hand — that which appeared gradually

children.text: kaṃsārātes tad āsāṃ pratipadam udabhūd bāḍham ākarṣaṇāya ||JGc_1,22.18||
children.translated_text: from the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — that, at each step, became indeed a force of attraction for them! ||22.18||

children.text: yāmune samam aśoka-kānane
children.translated_text: On the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in an <s>aśoka</s>-grove,

children.text: gopakaiḥ sa viharan mudānvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: he, sporting with the cowherd boys, filled with joy,

children.text: aikṣi bhūsura-vadhūbhir īkṣyatāṃ
children.translated_text: was seen by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-wives — and they deemed

children.text: dhyānam eva gatam ity amāni ca ||JGc_1,22.19||
children.translated_text: that their meditation itself had come [to life]! ||22.19||

children.text: yatra bhūsura-bhāryās taṃ sura-bhāvya-padaṃ yayuḥ |
children.translated_text: Where the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-wives went to him whose feet are worthy of worship by the gods —

children.text: aśoka-kānanaṃ tat tu babhūvāśoka-kānanam ||JGc_1,22.20||
children.translated_text: that <s>aśoka</s>-grove truly became a 'sorrowless' (<s>aśoka</s>) grove! ||22.20||

children.text: tataś ca tāḥ sapulaka-pulakatayā tam avalokayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: And then they, with the thrill of horripilation upon horripilation, beheld him.

children.text: tathā hi lokānāṃ gītam-
children.translated_text: As the people sang thus:

children.text:
kṛṣṇam apaśyan pīta-dukūlam |
bibhratam arcitatamam arcir nava-ghana-capalāruci-mūlam ||dhruvam||a||
children.translated_text:
They saw <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wearing a yellow silk garment,
bearing the most worshipped radiance — the root of the flickering splendor of a fresh cloud! ||refrain||a||

children.text: śirasi śikhaṇḍāvalim urasi srajam api dadhataṃ giri-dhātum |
children.translated_text: Bearing upon his head a row of peacock-feathers, upon his chest a garland, and also mineral pigment —

children.text: indradhanur yuga-madhya-madhuratara-sandhyāṃ dhurvam atiyātum ||b||
children.translated_text: as if a rainbow had come to surpass the sweeter-than-sweet twilight between the two <s>yugas</s>! ||b||

children.text: udayad-aruṇa-dara-kiraṇaṃ tama iva viracita-ciratara-śobham |
children.translated_text: Like the faint rays of the rising dawn, [his hair] like darkness fashioned into long-lasting beauty,

children.text: nava-kisalaya-dala-valitaṃ kaca-kulam anu kalitākhila-lobham ||c||
children.translated_text: the mass of hair, curled with fresh tender leaves, producing covetousness in all who perceived it! ||c||

children.text: bhālopari-milad-alaka-tatiṃ śruti-kumudam udañci kapolam |
children.translated_text: With rows of curls meeting upon the forehead, with cheeks [like] lilies risen above the ears,

children.text: smita-mukham upamita-lakṣaṇa-tārā-yuga-dhara-śaśadara-golam ||d||
children.translated_text: a smiling face likened to a globe of the crescent moon bearing a pair of characteristic stars! ||d||

children.text: kṛta-naṭa-veṣa-viśeṣa-vilakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇa-kṣaṇam upacita-rūpam |
children.translated_text: Having assumed a dancer's costume of distinctive, extraordinary characteristics — his beauty enhanced at every moment,

children.text: kartum ivāmṛta-vṛṣṭim uditam iha kañcana jaladhara-bhūpam ||e||
children.translated_text: as if some cloud-king had risen here to create a shower of nectar! ||e||

children.text:
citraṃ tatra ca mitra-skandhārpita-bandhāvara-hastam |
nirmala-kamala-vidhūnana-dakṣiṇa-dakṣiṇa-kara-ruci-śastam ||f||JGc_1,22.21|| iti |
children.translated_text:
Wondrous there too — his hand placed upon a friend's shoulder, covering the other hand,
praised by the beauty of the skillful right hand fanning an immaculate lotus! ||f|| ||22.21|| Thus.

children.text: śrutvā śaśvat sphuṭam ahaha yaṃ draṣṭum āśā nibaddhā
children.translated_text: He whom they had always heard of clearly — alas! — for whom the hope to see was bound,

children.text: sa drāg aikṣi svayam iti gatas tat-kṛtas tāpa-vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: he was swiftly seen by them in person — thus the entire mass of affliction caused by him was destroyed;

children.text: yaḥ kaścid vā vyavahitatayā tasya leśas tu śiṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: and whatever trace remained due to some obstruction,

children.text: so' py āveśān milana-tulitāt tāsu na sphūrtim āpa ||JGc_1,22.22||
children.translated_text: that too, from the intensity, being equaled by the meeting, did not attain manifestation in them! ||22.22||

children.text: atha bhojana-bhājanāni śirastaḥ-kṛtya sthitāsu tāsu sakala-bhāva-vicaksaṇaḥ smitāvaloka-lakṣaṇa-svamukha-mādhurya-dhuryaḥ suvicārya yasya kṛte prayasyanti sma, tās tad etad avadhārya tāsāṃ vāñchitaṃ kiñcid añcayan vañcayaṃś ca kāñcana-vasanaḥ kāñcana vācam uvāca-svāgataṃ vo mahābhāgāḥ [BhP 10.23.25] iti prāyaś cāyamm asyābhiprāyaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, when they stood with food-vessels placed upon their heads, he — discerner of all sentiments, endowed with the excellence of his own face's sweetness characterized by a smiling glance — having duly considered on whose account they had set forth, having ascertained this, slightly fulfilling yet also playfully denying their desire, that golden-garmented one spoke a certain word: 'Welcome to you, O greatly fortunate ones!' [BhP 10.23.25]. And the general purport of this was as follows:

children.text:
aho bata mahābhāgā yuṣmākaṃ bhūri-bhāratā |
jātā saṅkocayaty asmān pṛcchadhve svāgataṃ tataḥ ||JGc_1,22.23|| iti |
tad evam ehi-svāgatāṃ kriyām ācarya tat-pratyuttara-saṅkathane tāsāṃ saṅkocaṃ vicārya punar uvāca āsyatām iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, having performed the rite of 'Come! — Welcome!' and having considered their bashfulness in the exchange of reply and conversation, he spoke again: 'Be seated!'

children.text: asya cāyam abhiprāyaḥ-
children.translated_text: And the purport of this was:

children.text:
svāgata-pṛcchādikam api
viśrama-kāryaṃ vilambitaṃ tanute |
tasmāt tat-paripāṭīm
ajahāṃ bhavatībhir āsyatām eva ||JGc_1,22.24|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'Even the asking of welcome and the like
prolongs the business of rest;
therefore, I abandoned that sequence —
be seated, O noble ladies!' ||22.24|| Thus.

children.text: tataś ca praṇaya-praṇeyatayā vikhyātaḥ so' yam āsām asaṅkocāya svayaṃ bhāram avatārayann eva samupaviśann eva ca tāḥ sadeśa eva samupaveśayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And then, he — renowned for being guided by love — himself lowering the burden [from their heads], and himself sitting down, seated them right there in the same place, to put them at ease.

children.text: punar uvāca ca-karavāma kiṃ iti |
children.translated_text: And he spoke again: 'What shall we do?' Thus.

children.text: atra cedaṃ nivedanam iva vibhāvitavān-
children.translated_text: And herein he indicated, as if a petition:

children.text: asmān yam upakartuṃ vāñchati
children.translated_text: 'He who wishes to render us service —

children.text: tad-ṛte sa tu saṅkucann āste |
children.translated_text: without that [service], he sits abashed;

children.text: iti saṅkucitātmānaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: thus, being themselves abashed,

children.text: anujānantu tat tu bhū-devyaḥ ||JGc_1,22.25||
children.translated_text: let the earth-goddesses (<s>brāhmaṇa</s>-wives) themselves give permission for that!' ||22.25||

children.text: atha tāsām ātma-darśana-mātra-vāñchā-vimarśana-pūrvam uvāca-yan no didṛkṣayā prāptā upapannam idaṃ hi vaḥ [BhP 10.23.25] iti |
children.translated_text: Then, having first considered their desire for nothing more than the sight of himself, he said: 'That you have come out of desire to see us — this is fitting for you!' [BhP 10.23.25].

children.text: atra cāyam arthaḥ-
children.translated_text: And herein the meaning is:

children.text: asmad-darśana-mātraṃ yad vo' bhīṣṭaṃ tad eva yuktaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: 'That your desire is merely to see us — that is indeed fitting;

children.text: tatra hi hetur yūyaṃ tādṛśa-suṣṭhu-svabhāvāḥ stha ||JGc_1,22.26||
children.translated_text: for the reason thereof is that you are of such an excellent nature!' ||22.26||

children.text: atha tasya svabhāvasya suṣṭhu-bhāvatvaṃ vibhāvayan punar uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, elucidating the excellence of that nature, he spoke again:

children.text: mad-viṣayā vaḥ prītiḥ kauśalyād eva nānyataḥ sacate |
children.translated_text: 'Your love directed toward me succeeds only through skill, not from any other [cause];

children.text: yan mayi kuśalāḥ sarve vīkṣyante prīti-kartāraḥ ||JGc_1,22.27||
children.translated_text: for in me, all who are skilled are seen as makers of love!' ||22.27||

children.text: tatra kuśalānāṃ kaimutyaṃ pratyāyann uvāca-
children.translated_text: Therein, establishing the <s>kaimutya</s> (a fortiori) of the skilled, he said:

children.text: paśyāmy aham iha sarvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'I see here everything —

children.text: mat-premāṃśād aśeṣaga-prītim |
children.translated_text: from a portion of love for me, [arises] love for all;

children.text: nirupadhi yan mayi jantuḥ
children.translated_text: for unconditionally, a being loves me,

children.text: prīṇāty anyatra sopādhi ||JGc_1,22.28||
children.translated_text: whereas elsewhere, [love is] conditional!' ||22.28||

children.text: tad evaṃ sādhāraṇatāvadhāraṇaṃ tathā sannidhāna-sthiti-vidhānam upasīdat pratyācakṣāṇaḥ prāha sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, when he who was pronouncing the ascertainment of universality and the arrangement of remaining in [his] proximity repudiated [their departure], he spoke:

children.text:
sarvatra tu mat-sphūrtir na bhavati bata sarvadeti pūrtir naḥ |
bhavatīr anu sā nityā yaiva ca mat-sannidhāna-rūpaiva ||JGc_1,22.29||tasmāt pati-suta-valitaṃ nilayaṃ tvarayā prayāta tā yūyam |
mama ca tataḥ sukham uccaiḥ sāmañjasyaṃ hi sarvato vaśmi ||JGc_1,22.30||
children.translated_text: and My happiness will thereby be great, for I desire fitness in all respects! ||22.30||

But My manifestation does not occur everywhere — alas, our fulfillment is not constant! That [fulfillment] toward you is eternal, and is indeed of the very nature of My presence. ||22.29|| Therefore, go quickly to your homes, accompanied by husbands and sons,

children.text: tad evaṃ vrajadeva-kumārataḥ śrutaṃ sukumāram apīdaṃ vacanam āpāta-sampāta-hīnatayā duḥsaha-racanaṃ manyamānāḥ prativacanam āceruḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, having heard from the prince of <s>Vraja</s> this speech — tender yet, by its lack of abruptness or rudeness, deemed to be of unbearable composition — they fashioned a reply:

children.text: etat-prakāram api nārhasi vaktum īśa
children.translated_text: You should not speak even in this manner, O Lord!

children.text: prāhur bhavān iva bhavān iti tat prasīda |
children.translated_text: They have said "You are like the Lord" — and so indeed You are; therefore be gracious!

children.text: satyaṃ kuruṣva karavāma kim evam aṅgī-
children.translated_text: Make it true — what shall we do? Thus accept

children.text: kāraṃ nijāṅghri-parivāra-daśāṃ diśasva ||JGc_1,22.31||
children.translated_text: the state of attendants at Your own feet — grant it to us! ||22.31||

children.text: vihāya suhṛdaḥ parān vraja-nareśa-geheśvarī-
children.translated_text: Having abandoned other friends, we have taken refuge at the lotus feet

children.text: padāmbujam upāśritāḥ paricarema taṃ tvā sadā |
children.translated_text: of the queen of the king of <s>Vraja</s> — may we serve you always!

children.text: imāṃ vacana-cāturīṃ bata turīya-pūrtiṃ gatām
children.translated_text: This verbal cleverness, alas, having reached the fourth fulfillment —

children.text: urīkuru puru-śravaḥ śravaṇa-maṅgala śrīpate ||JGc_1,22.32||
children.translated_text: accept it, O <s>Puru-śravas</s>, O auspiciousness of the ears, O Lord of <s>Śrī</s>! ||22.32||

children.text: atha vikacamāna-kamala-samāna-locanaḥ saṅkocam anayaṃ cālocamānaḥ savainayam uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, he whose eyes resembled blossoming lotuses, considering their reticence, spoke with modesty:

children.text:
yathā vo bāndhavā nābhyasūyeran na ca majjanāḥ |
sureśāś cānumoderaṃs tathā kuruta nānyathā ||JGc_1,22.33||yuṣmākaṃ vipra-bhāryāṇāṃ paricaryārtham āhṛtiḥ |
kenāpi nānumodyeta pratīkṣya samayas tataḥ ||JGc_1,22.34||
children.translated_text: would not be approved by anyone; therefore, await the [proper] occasion." ||22.34||

"Act so that your kinsmen would not resent [this], nor would your people disapprove, and the lords of the gods would approve — do thus and not otherwise. ||22.33|| The requisitioning of you, wives of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, for the purpose of service

children.text: tad evaṃ locana-tṛṣṇāspadāya ca kṛṣṇāya tāś cira-sthiratāṃ pratyarocamānās tasya saṅkocam ālocamānās tatra nātivilambamānās tad-ājñām ālambamānāḥ patrāmatrādiṣu bhojyaṃ saṃyojya nija-kupya-pātrāṇy ādadamānās tena sādaraṃ visarjamānāḥ sakhibhir anuvrajyamānā muhuḥ parāvṛtya tam eva vilokamānā bhṛśaṃ saṃvardhi-kṛcchraṃ kalayamānāḥ kathaṃ katham api gṛha-gatiṃ prati sacamānāḥ sva-vaṃśa-prathamānāṃ yaśaḥ-prathāṃ prathayamānā veśmāntaḥ praviśanti sma | kintu-
children.translated_text: Then, those [wives], finding delight in prolonged stay before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — the abode of the eyes' thirst — yet perceiving his reticence, not tarrying there excessively, following his command, having placed food in vessels and platters and taking their own precious utensils, being respectfully dismissed by him, accompanied by [his] companions, turning back repeatedly to gaze at him alone, experiencing greatly augmented distress, somehow proceeding toward their homes, spreading the fame — the foremost of their lineages — they entered within their dwellings. But—

children.text: yāṃ yām āśām ahaha vanitās tā dvijānām apaśyann
children.translated_text: Whatever, whatever hope those women of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, alas, perceived,

children.text: āśā-pūrtiṃ pratipada asāv ācarat tāsu śīghram |
children.translated_text: he swiftly fulfilled that hope at every step!

children.text: sā hi śyāmaṃ kanaka-vasanaṃ vīkṣitākāram āsāṃ
children.translated_text: For that [hope], placing again and again in their sight the dark one (<s>Śyāma</s>) clad in golden garments, of the form [they had] beheld,

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ dṛśi vidadhatī citra-bhāvaṃ cakāra ||JGc_1,22.35||
children.translated_text: produced a marvelous state [in them]! ||22.35||

children.text: evaṃ cireṇa gṛhaṃ gṛhītavatīṣu tu tāsu-
children.translated_text: Thus, when those [wives] had at length reached home:

children.text: anna-pātrāṇi pātrāṇi ratnānāṃ vīkṣya sakṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Seeing the food-vessels [transformed into] vessels of jewels,

children.text: gṛhāṇi ca gṛhādhīśā na hīśāmāsur ūhitum ||JGc_1,22.36||
children.translated_text: the lords of the households were unable to fathom [it]! ||22.36||

children.text: anantaraṃ tu-
children.translated_text: Then next:

children.text: bālya-krīḍā-kṛīta-phalenānena maṇi-pūritān |
children.translated_text: Seeing their own homes filled with jewels

children.text: sva-gṛhān vīkṣya te viprāḥ sva-patnī-matim anvayuḥ ||JGc_1,22.37||
children.translated_text: by the fruits won through childhood play, those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> followed the counsel of their wives! ||22.37||

children.text: ūcire ca-
children.translated_text: And they said:

children.text: tasmai viśva-janīnāya yās tad-bhogīnam āharan |
children.translated_text: Those [wives] who brought [offerings] to him who is the benefactor of all the world, to him the enjoyer —

children.text: tā evāsann ātmanīnā dīnās tu bata mādṛśāḥ ||JGc_1,22.38||
children.translated_text: they alone were devoted to the Self; wretched indeed are those like us! ||22.38||

children.text: mā jīvan yasya kṛṣṇāya kramate cakṣur ādi na |
children.translated_text: Let him not live whose eye and so forth does not hasten toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: mriyamāṇaś ca mā yasya tasmai tan na pravartate ||JGc_1,22.39||
children.translated_text: and dying, let him not [live] for whom that [devotion] does not arise! ||22.39||

children.text: sa kiñjīvaḥ sa kubrahmaḥ suparva-hatakaś ca saḥ |
children.translated_text: He is barely alive, he is a degraded <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and he is one struck down by the gods,

children.text: rājīva-nayanaṃ yas tu nājīvanatayā bhajet ||JGc_1,22.40||
children.translated_text: who does not worship the lotus-eyed one as the very life! ||22.40||

children.text: atha kṛṣṇāya tṛṣṇāṃ te dadhur vṛṣṇi-pura-dvijāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the city of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> conceived a longing for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: kintu dhṛṣṇak kaṃsa-bhiyā nājagmuḥ kṛṣṇam īkṣitum ||JGc_1,22.41||
children.translated_text: but, out of fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, they did not boldly go to see <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! ||22.41||

children.text: ekena kenacit pūrvaṃ bhāryāmāryātigam iva |
children.translated_text: It is heard that one of them had earlier forbidden his wife, as if [she were going] beyond bounds,

children.text: nivārya vāryatālabdhā vāryatāyām iti śrutam ||JGc_1,22.42||
children.translated_text: and she, having been prevented, [died and] was not obtained even through preventive [efforts] — thus it was heard. ||22.42||

children.text: tataś ca teṣām ucitam eva, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And that was fitting for them, since:

children.text: kṣaṇād uccaiḥ kṣaṇān nīcair gati-bhājāṃ kanīyasām |
children.translated_text: Of those of lesser [resolve], whose course goes now high, now low,

children.text: reṇūnām iva kārmāṇāṃ viṣamā rītir īkṣyate ||JGc_1,22.43||
children.translated_text: an uneven conduct is observed, like that of dust-particles driven by <s>karma</s>! ||22.43||

children.text: pūrvī kṛṣṇasya sevāyām iṣṭī vā tatra yaḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: He who always has a prior inclination toward the service of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: adhītī vā bhāgavate bhakta-pūrvī sa taṃ bhajet ||JGc_1,22.44||
children.translated_text: or a prior devotion to the <s>Bhāgavata</s> — such a devotee-first one would worship Him! ||22.44||

children.text: tatra ca tair bhojya-madhurādibhir upayojyamānaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ madhumaṅgala uvāca-suṣṭhu miṣṭam idaṃ pākimatāpannam anna-jātaṃ yācita kam apy amṛtāyate | nedṛśam āpam ity akam amṛtaṃ vā | yat khalu bhūmi-skhalitaṃ sarajasaṃ kaṇam apy abhyavahartum īhāmahe | tasmād asmākam eva parṇaśālābhyarṇe tāḥ kuṭīr vidhāya tiṣṭhantu, tat-kṛta-madhura-paripāka-pāka-śāka-sūpa-pūpa-pūṭīs tu savayaso vayam eva yuṣmabhyam uṣṇāḥ koṣṇā eva samarpayiṣyāmaḥ | tatrāpy āha prāgraharatayā prāgrahara eva bhaviṣyāmīti sthite ko vāyaṃ doṣaḥ | kintu roṣa-bhiyā na vaktuṃ śaktāḥ sma |
children.translated_text: And there, being served with the sweet food-offerings and other [delicacies] by them, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said to Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: "Excellent! This cooked food, the product of skilled cooking, is delicious — any food obtained by begging becomes like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar)! I did not find such [food] — or was it <s>amṛta</s> itself? For we are eager to eat even a grain fallen on the ground, mixed with dust! Therefore, let them stay, having built huts near our leaf-pavilion; and we ourselves, of the same age, shall deliver to you their sweet preparations — dishes, vegetables, soups, cakes, and sweets — hot, or at least warm! Moreover, I declare that I shall be the chief taster by right of first serving — what fault is there in this arrangement? But out of fear of [your] anger, we were unable to speak."

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-ādyūna nūnam unmadiṣṇutayāpatra-piṣṇutām apy aticariṣṇur jāto' si |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "Today, surely, through your tendency to madness, you have gone beyond even shamelessness!"

children.text: atha sarve' pi hasantaḥ procuḥ-priya-vayasya ! yady apy asau parānnatārocanam āpannas tarhi sa eṣa eva tundaparimṛja iva vipra-sundarīṇāṃ tāsām upāsanāṃ ghaṭayamānas tad-bāṭa-taṭagam uṭajam adhitiṣṭhan sambhavad āśitambhavān miṣṭam iṣṭa-vighasa-bhojanān nijam iṣṭaṃ racayatu |
children.translated_text: Then all, laughing, said: "Dear friend! Even if he has developed a fondness for food cooked by others, then let this very lip-licker, arranging the service of those beautiful <s>brāhmaṇa</s> ladies, residing in a hut by that road-bank, being a probable eater, fashion his desired enjoyment of the relished remnants of the beloved [food]!"

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-sādhūktaṃ vyaktam idaṃ bhagavatī-viditaṃ vidhāsyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: "Well spoken! Evidently, we shall arrange this as known to the divine lady (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>)."

children.text: madhumaṅgalas tu sa-krodham ivovāca-yuvarāja ! gardhanatayā kukṣim-bharayas te eta eva muhur aśanāyāṃ smarayantaḥ sarvatra ca ghasmarā eva bhaṇyante, bhikṣāyām akṣāma-samudyamatayā sarvānnīnāś ca lakṣyante, na tu vayam |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, however, said as if with anger: "O prince! Those belly-fillers of yours, out of gluttony, constantly remind [us] of hunger and are everywhere called voracious; and in begging, by their unflagging eagerness, they are perceived as all-devouring — but not I!"

children.text: sarve' py ūcuḥ-vāvadūka ! vipratayā bhavān eva yāyajūkatāyāṃ jañjapūkatām āsīdan purobhāśānāṃ dandaśūkas tad-āsvādāya jāgarūkatām āsādayati | asmābhis tu bhavaj-jāter dvijāteḥ parīkṣaivācaritā iti |
children.translated_text: All said: "O chatterbox! You yourself, being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, approaching the state of chanting in sacrificial prattling, as a biter of the fore-offerings, attain wakefulness for tasting them! By us, however, only a test of your twice-born nature has been conducted!"

children.text: tad evaṃ hasatsu sakhi-sabhāsatsu svayam āśitambhavenodana-sambhāreṇa bhuktvā suhitaḥ sarva-hitaḥ śrāvita-veṇur dhenuḥ prāpya tat-tat-kathā-kautukatas tad-artham anugavam āsādita-dṛṣṭi-vrajaṃ śrīmad-vrajam avāpya nija-viraha-dahanaṃ nirvāpya svaka-rūpāmṛtenāpyāyayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Thus, while the assembly of friends laughed, having himself eaten with a eater's fulfillment from the store of rice, being well-fed, the benefactor of all, having sounded his flute and gathered the cows, through curiosity about various stories, having brought the gaze of each cow following [him] to glorious <s>Vraja</s>, he extinguished the fire of separation from himself and refreshed [all] with the nectar of his own form.

children.text: sakhāyas tu yājñikeṣu jagmivāṃso jakṣivāṃsaś ca vayam iti saṅkocena na kañcid apy ūcivāṃsaś ca |
children.translated_text: And the friends, having gone to the sacrificers and having eaten, out of embarrassment did not tell anyone.

children.text: atha kathakaḥ kathā-samāpanam āha sma-
children.translated_text: Then the narrator spoke the conclusion of the story:

children.text: ||JGc_1,22.45|| MISSING!
children.translated_text: ||22.45|| MISSING!

children.text: so' yaṃ śrī-gokulādhīśa kulādhīśas tavoditaḥ |
children.translated_text: This very lord of glorious <s>Gokula</s>, the head of the clan, has been described by you;

children.text: ākarṣaṇād guṇā yasya sarvān anuguṇān vyadhuḥ ||JGc_1,22.46||
children.translated_text: whose qualities, by their attraction, made everything favorable! ||22.46||

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anv
yajña-bhāryā-sad-upacaryā-paryāptir nāma
dvāviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||22||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the twenty-second <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
"The Fulfillment of the Worthy Service of the Wives of the Sacrificers"
||22||

children.text: atha trayoviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the twenty-third <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter)

children.text:
prathama-saṅga-raṅgaja-
vākovākya-bhaṅgī-saṅgītam
children.translated_text:
A composition of dialogue-patterns
born from the delight of the first meeting

children.text: atha rāsārambhe nija-śapatha-sambhedaṃ vedayaṃṣtadīdaṃ yācanam ācinomi |
children.translated_text: Now, at the commencement of the <s>rāsa</s> [dance], I compose this petition of his, revealing the violation of his own oath:

children.text:
nije kāvye sarvaṃ rasa-valanam astiti likhatā
mayā dhārstyāt spaṣṭī-kṛta-mati-rahasyaṃ tu yadīha |
tad etad govinda-vraja-vijana-kāntānucaraṇaṃ
dadhadbhir yogyasya śravasi param arpyaṃ na sadasi ||JGc_1,23.1|| iti | [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
"By me, who writes that in my own poem all is a turning of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment),
if, out of boldness, the secret of my mind has been made manifest here,
then let this — the pursuit of <s>Govinda</s> with the beloved in the solitude of <s>Vraja</s> —
be offered by those who hold [it] worthy, only to the ear, not in public assembly." ||23.1|| [<s>śikhariṇī</s>]

children.text: atha rātri-kathāyām grathyamāna-prathāyāṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ snigdhakaṇṭhaṃ snigdhakaṇṭham apy ālambamānaḥ sambabhāṣe, yatra prathamamīdaṃ prāñjali vyañjayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then, in the night-tale being woven with renown, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, embracing <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, conversed, wherein first he expressed this with folded hands:

children.text:
rāsa-kelir ajaniṣṭa jāgaraṃ
sa sphuṭaṃ bhavatu tat-kathā tathā |
kāraṇaṃ bhavati yasya yad-vidhaṃ
tasya tad-vidhatayā matā sthitiḥ ||JGc_1,23.2|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
"The <s>rāsa-keli</s> (dance-sport) arose as a night-vigil;
let the tale thereof be equally vivid!
Whatever is the nature of a cause,
the state of its [effect] is deemed to be of that very nature!" ||23.2|| [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text: tad etad ākarṇya sānandaṃ nirvarṇya ca sarve' pi procuḥ-yukti-yuktam eva cedam uktam, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this and examining it with delight, all said: "This is indeed well-reasoned, since:

children.text:
paramā yā rasa-dhārā
sā yadi madhye viyuktim āyāti |
pūrvāpara-saṃvalanā-
bhāvān naiva svarūpam āyāti ||JGc_1,23.3|| [gīti]
tasmād yatheccham avicchedam evedaṃ prastūyatām |
children.translated_text: Therefore, let this be presented as desired, without interruption!

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text:
mukhaṃ śaśimukhī-gaṇa-pracura-moha-saṃrohaṇaṃ
dṛśor yugam amūdṛśāṃ mṛga-dṛśāṃ ghūrṇanam |
tanuḥ sutanu-maṇḍalī-dhṛti-vikhaṇḍanī śrī-hares
tadājani yadā janiṃ mṛgayate sma rāsotsavaḥ ||JGc_1,23.4|| [pṛthvī]

mukhaṃ vidhu-vimohanaṃ nayanam abja-dṛg-lobhanaṃ
rucir ghana-rucī-hita-prathama-saṅga-raṅga-pradā |
ramā-ramaṇa-rāmaṇīyaka-vibhūṣi-rāmāvales
tadājani yadā janiṃ mṛgayate sma rāsotsavaḥ ||JGc_1,23.5|| [pṛthvī]

atha pūrva-krameṇa pūrṇimāśrame pūrṇāḥ pulindyaḥ [BhP 10.21.17] ity ādié vṛtte nirvṛtte satya-pūrnaṃ-manyatayā rādhikā-mātra-karṣāya haris tarṣaṃ dhṛtavān-katham aho, nibhṛtamīdaṃ sambhṛtaṃ syāt?iti |
children.translated_text: Then, in the previous order, at the hermitage of <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (Full Moon), when the episode beginning with "the <s>Pulinda</s> women were fulfilled" [BhP 10.21.17] had transpired and concluded, <s>Hari</s>, considering [his vow] to be fulfilled in truth, conceived a longing specifically to attract <s>Rādhikā</s> — "How, alas, might this concealed [love] be brought to fruition?" — thus.

children.text: tatra kācit tat-kuṅkuma-lipta-carī vana-carī śrī-rādhām anu karuṇayā taruṇāruṇa-kamala-locanam uvāca-
children.translated_text: There, a certain forest-dwelling woman, smeared with his <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), said to Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, out of compassion, with fresh-dawn-lotus eyes:

children.text:
tava muralīm iva nitarāṃ viṣama-śaraḥ sa vijito bhavatā |
ahaha na jāne katham iva śuṣkāṃ biddhāṃ ca tām kurute ||JGc_1,23.6|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
"Like your flute, exceedingly, the sharp-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) has been conquered by him;
alas, I do not know how he makes her dry and pierced!" ||23.6|| [<s>upagīti</s>]

children.text:
tadā ca vana-gīrvāṇibhir ākāśa-vāṇīyam udbhāvitā-
śuṣkā tapta-śalākayā ca parito biddhā suvaṃśodbhavā
seyaṃ te muralī priyeti niyataṃ vijñātavān manmathaḥ|
tāṃ śuṣyad-vapuṣaṃ vidhāya kulajāṃ bāṇair nijaiḥ pañcabhir
biddhāṅgīṃ vidadhāti hā bakaripo tvat-prītaye samprati ||JGc_1,23.7|| [śārdūla-vikrīḍītam]
children.translated_text:
And then, by the divine forest-voices, this celestial voice was produced:
"Dried by a heated iron rod and everywhere pierced — born of fine bamboo —
this flute of yours is dear [to you] — so has <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) surely understood!
Making that well-born woman's body dry, pierced in her limbs
by his own five arrows — alas, O enemy of <s>Baka</s>, he fashions [her] now for your pleasure!" ||23.7|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
tarhy eva cādhīratayā bhraman vanamālī kvacana tamāle kuṅkumālekham imam ālokayāmāsa-
ānaṅgārcir bhinnā tvad-atiśubhagāṅgāvṛta-manā
muralyāṃ rāga-śrī-parimala-kulaṃ sambhṛtavatī |
sadā śyāmāṃ kāntiṃ diśī vidiśi cābhāvayamato
mayāptaṃ kṛṣṇatvaṃ tad api na hi kṛṣṇa tvam abhitaḥ ||JGc_1,23.8|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Just then, wandering restlessly, the garland-wearer (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) beheld on a certain <s>tamāla</s> tree this <s>kuṅkuma</s>-inscription:
"The flame of <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Love), shattered, its mind concealed by your exceedingly beautiful limbs,
has gathered into the flute the fragrance of the lineage of the beauty of passion.
Everywhere and in every direction, always envisioning a dark (<s>śyāmā</s>) luster —
I have thereby attained blackness (<s>kṛṣṇatva</s>); yet not even that, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, [makes me] you!" ||23.8|| [<s>śikhariṇī</s>]

children.text: tad etan niśamana-pūrvakān niśāmanān muraśamanena tad idaṃ vicāritam-hanta hanta ! rādhāyā eveyam asādhāraṇa-vāg-arthavatī lipiḥ | seyaṃ sambhavet | evam api kula-janmatayā tayā manmatha-vikāram ācchādayantyā sthīyate | tasmān nikhilāvṛti-dhvaṃsanaṃ vaṃśī-śaṃsanaṃ paraṃ mama śaraṇam iti |
children.translated_text: Then, having perceived that [inscription], during the nights, the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) reflected thus: "Alas, alas! This is indeed the writing of <s>Rādhā</s> alone — possessed of extraordinary verbal meaning! It could be hers. Even so, being of noble birth, she remains concealing the transformations of love. Therefore, the proclamation of the flute, which destroys all concealment, is my supreme refuge!"

children.text: tad evaṃ rādhā-sudhā-durbhikṣāditas titikṣām abhajan sa punar veṇu-śikṣā-bhikṣam eva kevalāṃ sevate sma, yatra varṣā api tarṣākaratayā vyatīyuḥ, samṛddha-gardhanatayā śarad apy ardhaṃ vardhate sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, enduring the famine of <s>Rādhā</s>'s nectar, he again pursued solely the instruction of flute-playing as his alms, wherein even the rains passed by as [mere] agents of thirst, and autumn, with its abundance of fullness, also grew to [only] half [its potential].

children.text: tatrāha, rahaḥ-śikṣā tu yathā-
children.translated_text: There he said, "But the secret instruction [shall be] as follows—"

children.text:
yarhy ākarṣa-vidhiṃ harir muralikā-śikṣāsu tasyāh kramāc
cakre tarhi gatāś cirāt para-para-kṣobhās ta ete tayā |
kampo ghūrṇanam āsanād vicalanaṃ dvitra-kramā vāstuto
niṣkrāntir vana-vartma-vartanam upavrajyā ca dūrādhvani ||JGc_1,23.9|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: When <s>Hari</s> systematically performed the method of attraction in the teachings of the flute, then those successive layers of agitation that had long been [building] in her were produced by it: trembling, swooning, rising from her seat, stumbling a step or two, actually going out, traversing the forest-path, and approaching from a great distance. // [śārdūla]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
rādhākarṣa-kṛte kṛtā muralikā-śikṣātha yā yā tadā
sā sā tena sadāśayā valayitāpy āsīd alaṃ niṣkalā |
tām etāṃ nata-kandharaḥ sa-pulakaṃ vande' ham uccaiḥ sadā
yā kṛṣṇasya manorathāvalim aho pūrṇam akārsīn muhuḥ ||JGc_1,23.10|| [śārdūla-vikrīḍītam]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
The flute-teaching that was devised for the attraction of <s>Rādhā</s> — each and every one of those [melodies], though encircled by that ever-well-intentioned [<s>Rādhā</s>], was perfectly whole and unblemished. I bow always and loudly to that [flute], with lowered head and <s>pulaka</s> (horripilation), which fulfilled again and again the entire train of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> desires! // [śārdūla-vikrīḍītam]

children.text: tathā hi, tad evaṃ prāvṛṣi veṇu-śikṣā-parīkṣā-tṛṣṇag asau kṛṣṇaḥ samayaṃ pratīkṣamāṇaḥ śaral-lakṣmīm āgatāṃ lakṣitavān | lakṣayann eva ca vicāritavān-
children.translated_text: For thus it was: that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, thirsting for the trial of the flute-teaching during the rainy season, while awaiting the [right] moment, perceived the beauty of autumn (<s>śarad</s>) as having arrived. And even as he perceived it, he reflected:

children.text: iyaṃ khalu svabhāvataḥ svacchā mal-līlā-paricchadatāṃ yadi gacchati, tadā pramadāvalim ṛcchāmaḥ | kintu, samaya-mayatayā sarvavaśya-kāriṇam api bhāvaṃ vaśyaṃ kurvatīm enāṃ paśyāmi, yathā mām api rādhā |
children.translated_text: 'This [autumn], which is naturally clear, if it attains the status of being an accessory of my <s>līlā</s> (divine play), then we shall reach the company of the young women. However, I see that this [season], by its very nature of being governed by time, makes even the disposition that commands everything become subservient — just as <s>Rādhā</s> [does] to me.'

children.text:
tato yady asyāṃ api vaśyatām vyasyan bhāvāntara-bhāvitatvaṃ bhāvayituṃ prabhavāmi, tad-ārādhāyām api tad-ādhānāya nirbādhatāṃ gatavān asmīty avadadhāmi |
[15] tad evaṃ vicārayann agrecaraṃ maṅgalaṃ vilocayann uvāca-āho ! śvo-vasīyasam evādhyavasīyate | yataḥ-
khañjana-khelā-rañjita-kañja-nayanaṃ nayan vidhiḥ sa mama |
rādhā-mañjula-netra-sphurad-ānanam āsu sañjayitā ||JGc_1,23.11|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'Therefore, if I am able to infuse in this [season] too an alternate emotional state by casting subservience upon it, then I affirm that I have attained unobstructedness for establishing that [state] in the worship of her (<s>Rādhā</s>) as well.'
[15] Thus reflecting, perceiving a favorable omen ahead, he said: 'Ah! It is determined that [this will happen] on the very morrow! For —
The Creator, who brings before [me] eyes beautified by the play of <s>khañjana</s> birds (wagtails), will swiftly unite [me] with the face radiant with the lovely eyes of <s>Rādhā</s>!' // [upagīti]

children.text: tad etacchubha ṣakunamanubhavatā, yāvat paurṇamāsaṃṃā sameva sarvata eva veṇudhareṇa ve nusvanacaryāsañcāryate sma | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, experiencing this auspicious omen, until the full-moon day itself, the flute-bearer (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) caused the practice of flute-music to pervade everywhere from all sides. And then —

children.text:
vaṃśī-kalād udayataḥ śaradi prabhāvān
mallībhir apy atula-phulla-daśāṃ gatābhiḥ |
rātrīr nibhālya muhur ullasitāh sa ṛāma-
bhrātā ratiṃ rati-kṛte' kṛta vallavībhiḥ ||JGc_1,23.12|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: In autumn, from the power arising from the flute's melody, the nights — even by the <s>mallī</s> (jasmine) blossoms that had attained an incomparable state of full bloom — having been gazed upon again and again with delight, he, the brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), produced desire for the sake of desire among the cowherd women! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tataś ca tūrṇam eva pūrṇa-candrā bahu-tithī tithir atithir iva tasya prasannatāṃ vidhātum āsannavatī | tatra cājñāyāhni vana-vihāra-śālī vana-mālī dhenūr ādāya vrajāgamanaṃ vidhāya sāyaṃ pratyavasāya nija-candra-śālikālindaṃ vindamānaḥ sphuṭam āditye' staṅgatya sthite sa-tārā-samudayaṃ taṃ sāndra-candrikaṃ candram udayantaṃ paśyaṃs tad-vaśya-bhāva-viśeṣa-śleṣatas tad idaṃ cintayāmāsa-
jāguḍa-piṇḍa-sapiṇḍaṃ kiṃ vidhu-bimbaṃ tad etad unnamati |
kiṃ vā roṣāruṇa-ruci mukham idam udbhāti kāmasya? ||JGc_1,23.13|| [āryā]
children.translated_text:
And then, very swiftly, the full-moon <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), over many days, arrived like an unexpected guest to produce his delight. There, on the day known [to him], the garland-wearing one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the enjoyer of forest-pastimes, having taken the cows and having returned to <s>Vraja</s>, having rested in the evening, finding his own moon-like pavilion-terrace — when clearly the sun had set and stood [below the horizon] — seeing that moon rising with its dense moonlight and host of stars, by the special adhesion of the subservient state toward it, he pondered thus:
'Is this moon-disc that rises up a kinsman of a ball of raw sugar? Or is this the face of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) shining forth, reddened with the glow of anger?' // [āryā]

children.text:
punaś ca,
kuṅkuma-rasa-saṅkulam iva kiṃ vidhu-bimbaṃ puraḥ sphurati |
athavā rādhā-mukham idam udayati yamunā-vanāt purataḥ ? ||JGc_1,23.14|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
And again:
'Is it a moon-disc, as if saturated with saffron-liquid, that shines forth before [me]? Or is this the face of <s>Rādhā</s> rising from the forest of the <s>Yamunā</s> before [me]?' // [upagīti]

children.text: tatra yadi vidhu-bimbam evedaṃ, tadā tad idaṃ vibhāvyate-
children.translated_text: There, if this is indeed a moon-disc, then this is what is to be perceived:

children.text:
pūrṇa-candro' yam aindrīṃ haritam anugataḥ preyasīṃ dūradeśād
asyāvaktraṃ vilimpan ghusṛṇa-śavaliteneva śaśvat kareṇa |
tad-vyājān mām amūdṛk-kṛtim upadiśatīvādya sadyaḥ kiśoraṃ
śubhrātmā yas tadīyaṃ bhavati viracanaṃ sarvato-bhadram eva ||JGc_1,23.15|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'This full moon, having followed his beloved, the green <s>Aindrī</s> (direction of the east), from a far country, anointing her face as it were with a perpetually saffron-dappled hand — through that pretext, he seems to instruct me, a youth, to act precisely thus! He, the bright-souled one — his arrangement is auspicious in every way!' // [śārdūla]

children.text: kiṃ cāyam idam apy upadiśann iva sambhāvyate-
children.translated_text: Moreover, this [moon] appears to be instructing this as well:

children.text:
vidhur ahaṃ haritaḥ pratidik-pati-
praṇayiṇi ramayan jana-śarmadaḥ |
tvam iha kiṃ nu vidho sthagitāyase
para-ramā-ramaṇaṃ prati samprati? ||JGc_1,23.16|| [drutavilambita]
children.translated_text: 'I, the moon, having gladdened every quarter and its directional lord's beloved, am the bestower of the people's happiness. Why then do you, O moon, conceal yourself now before the lover of another's beauty (<s>Śrī</s>)?' // [drutavilambita]

children.text: tad evaṃ sarvathaiva daivānukūlyataś candra-candrikā-sāndrita śubhaṃ tasya kakubham eva gantuṃ śantur asmi, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Thus, in every way, by divine favor, in that direction made dense with moon and moonlight, I am prepared to go, for —'

children.text:
nikhilam eva vanaṃ vidhunāmunā
diśi diśi pratirañjitam īkṣyate |
mad-anukūlam idaṃ śakunaṃ bhaved
iti gatir mama tatra śubhāvahā ||JGc_1,23.17|| [drutavilambita]
children.translated_text: 'The entire forest is seen illuminated by this moon in every direction. May this be an auspicious omen for me — thus my going there is auspicious!' // [drutavilambita]

children.text: atha yadi kāmābhidhānasya kopa-dhāmānanam idam, tadā viṣama-bāṇasya tasyānuyānam eva bhaya-nirvāṇaṃ viśrāṇayati | yadi ca tasyā eva kānti-sadanaṃ vanam idaṃ vidyate, tadā tu sutarām eva tad-diśaṃ praviśatas tan mama śarma-marma praviśatiti | kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: 'Now, if this is the anger-laden face of the one called <s>Kāma</s> (Love), then following that crooked-arrowed one yields only the cessation of fear. And if this forest is the abode of her radiance, then all the more — for one entering that direction, the essence of happiness enters me!' Moreover —

children.text:
rayāṇe vartate cittaṃṇrtyaty akṣīca dakṣiṇam |
tasmād vṛttaṃ caṇrtyaṃ ca kānt abhirbhavitāmama ||JGc_1,23.18|| [anuṣṭubh]
[22] tad etad uṭṭaṅkya niṣṭaṅkya ca praṇaya-paṇa-santuṣṭaṃ dāmādi-kumāra-catuṣṭayaṃ saṅgataḥ prasajya, tad-dvārā nidrā-vyājād anyān dvāra-pālakatayā tatraiva saṃvalayya, nibhṛta-kṛta-pratīhārataś caraṇa-vihāratas tām eva haritaṃ harir muralī-dhara-karatayānusaran dina-kara-tanayā-tīram anvatīrṇavān | āvatīrya ca vicāritavān-
children.translated_text:
'My heart is in a state of eagerness, and my right eye dances — therefore, both what has occurred and what will dance [forth] will be from the beloved!' // [anuṣṭubh]
[22] Thus, having resolved and confirmed this, having joined the four youths — <s>Dāma</s> and others — who were content with the wager of love, having through them lulled the others to sleep under the pretext of slumber and posted them as doorkeepers right there, having cautiously dismissed the attendants, he, <s>Hari</s>, through the excursion of his feet, following the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), descended to her bank — with flute in hand. And having descended, he reflected:

children.text:
na kruddha-kāmānanam etad asti
prayāti yac chubra-daśām udañcat |
viyogi-rādhāsyam idaṃ ca na syād
yataḥ kalaṅkādi bhaved vibhedi ||JGc_1,23.19|| [upajāti 11]
children.translated_text: 'This is not the angry face of <s>Kāma</s>, since it is attaining a bright state as it rises. And this could not be the face of <s>Rādhā</s> in separation, since it would be marked by blemishes and the like!' // [upajāti]

children.text: tataś ca mrga-lāñchana evāyam iti niścitya punar vicāritavān-
children.translated_text: Then, having ascertained that this was indeed the hare-marked one (the moon), he reflected again:

children.text:
śārvaraṃ ṣarvarīśānaḥ saṃhartuṃ siṃhatāṃ gataḥ |
pūrva-parvatam ārohan sarvaṃ parvati parvaṇa ||JGc_1,23.20|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The lord of the night has assumed the form of a lion to destroy the darkness — ascending the eastern mountain, he makes everything a festival on the full-moon day!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
kintu,
candramā rādhikā-vaktram anukurvan virājate |
tadākāram idaṃ cetaḥ kathaṃ mama vidūyate? ||JGc_1,23.21|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
However:
'The moon shines forth imitating the face of <s>Rādhikā</s> — [seeing] its form, how is this heart of mine distressed?' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: punar vibhāvya candraṃ prati prāha sma-
children.translated_text: Perceiving again, he addressed the moon:

children.text:
anupama-rucir asmi sarva-lokeṣv
iti bhagavann amṛta-dyute na dṛpya |
na tu bhavad-upamā daśāpi tasyāś
caraṇa-nakhā vilasanti rādhikāyāh ||JGc_1,23.22|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text: 'O blessed one of nectarine radiance, do not be proud [thinking] "I am of incomparable beauty in all the worlds!" Not even the toenails of that <s>Rādhikā</s> in their splendor bear comparison to you!' // [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text:
tad evaṃ vicintya samucita-sthānaṃ vicitya dūrataś caturāṃś caturaḥ kumāran vartmani vartamānatayā vidhāya, svayam upasaritam uccatara-catvaram ātmanā rūḍhaṃ sandhāya, vraja-diśam avadhāya, veṇuṃ mukhe nidhāya, vādayiṣyamānaś cintayāmāsa-prathamaṃ rādhā-
gamanam eva sādhayāmaḥ | tām vinā phalasya ca viphalatām kalayāmi | tad-āgamana-kamanīyatayā tu ramaṇīnāṃ anyāsām apy āgatir mama manasi ramaṇīyatām āyāmam ānayati | kintu tad eva bhavyaṃ kathaṃ bhavyam ity eva pratipattavyam | ām ām, bāṇa-vidyā-pravīṇenaiva vaiṇavikena mayā tathā yoktavyam, yathā tena saivāviṣṭākṛṣṭā ca bhavati nāparā iti |
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, having sought out a suitable place, having stationed the four clever youths — <s>Dāma</s> and others — at a distance along the path as [if they were merely] present there, having himself ascended a rather elevated platform that he had come upon, having fixed his gaze toward the direction of <s>Vraja</s>, having placed the flute to his mouth, about to play, he pondered: 'First, let us accomplish the coming of <s>Rādhā</s> alone. Without her, I perceive the fruitlessness of the fruit. And the loveliness of her arrival makes the coming of the other beautiful women also lovely in my mind. But how exactly should this desirable thing be brought about? Yes, yes — I, the flautist expert in arrow-like skill, must employ it such that she alone is possessed and attracted, and no other!'

children.text:
tad evaṃ sampradhāryāvadhārya ca tena, veṇum evaṃ vādayiṣyāmīti yadā vicāryate sma, tadā ca tābhiḥ sāndra-candrika-candramasaḥ sandṛṣṭ-vaśatayā sāndṛṣṭikam idaṃ parāmṛṣṭam-
hanta ! sa khalv ayam oṣadhīśo' py ādhi-vyādhita-janān asmān adya sadyaḥ pratiritsed eva, na tu cikitset iti |
children.translated_text:
Thus, having deliberated and resolved, when he was contemplating 'I shall play the flute thus' — at that time, those [<s>gopīs</s>], having perceived the moon with its dense moonlight under its sway, reflected on this pertaining to the visible:
'Alas! This lord of herbs (the moon) will surely today immediately torment us, afflicted ones, rather than cure us!'

children.text:
tataś ca tat-kṣaṇaṃ kiñcid vilakṣaṇaṃ śaśa-lakṣmāṇam ālakṣya vṛndā cedaṃ cintitavatī-
hanta hanta !
tāsāṃ kṛṣṇa-viyogāgni-bāṣpair viṣvag-viniḥśrtaiḥ |
ādarśa iva paśyāndhaś candramā mandatāṃ gatah ||JGc_1,23.23|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And then, at that very moment, <s>Vṛndā</s>, observing the somewhat unusual hare-marked one (moon), pondered thus:
'Alas, alas!
The moon, blinded by the tears flowing forth in all directions from those [<s>gopīs</s>] due to the fire of separation from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, has attained dimness — as if [it were] a mirror!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha camūru-dṛśām amūṣāṃ muhur api saṃmukhatayā vaśīkṛtim ivāpannaḥ śaśī svadiśi tadā madād unnatena kṛṣṇasya gabhasti-śatena tasya sphūrtiṃ samānināyeti |
children.translated_text: Now, the moon — as if having been brought under the sway of those broad-thighed, bright-eyed ones through their repeated facing of it — was then brought to resplendence by the hundred rays of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which rose proudly in his direction, through their brilliance.

children.text: tad-avalokanāya vyākulatākulāyamanāsu tāsu-
children.translated_text: As those [<s>gopīs</s>] became agitated with anxiety to behold it —

children.text:
śāradena śaśinā hariṃ prati
prasthitiḥ samam ayoji subhruvām |
pratyayoji kila tena sā tadā
maṅkṣu tasya muralī-kalena tu ||JGc_1,23.24|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: The setting forth of the beautiful-browed ones toward <s>Hari</s> was joined together with the autumnal moon; but that [setting forth] was then swiftly conjoined by the melody of his flute! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: yatas tadaiva ca-
children.translated_text: For at that very moment —

children.text:
anurāgeṇa rāgeṇa varṇa-bhāgena mādhurīḥ |
kalayantaṃ kalaṃ veṇoḥ kalayāmāsa keśavaḥ ||JGc_1,23.25|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> began to produce the sweet melody of the flute, creating charms through <s>anurāga</s> (deep attachment), <s>rāga</s> (musical mode), and the share of syllables! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tatrānurāgo yathā,
sāśru-kaṇṭha-nayanaṃ sakaṇṭakaṃ
kampa-sampad-ayanaṃ sa-mādhavaḥ |
rādhikā-virahajādhibādhitaḥ
śravya-veṇu-kalabhavyam ājagau ||JGc_1,23.26|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
The <s>anurāga</s> (deep attachment) therein, as follows:
Afflicted by the pain born of separation from <s>Rādhikā</s>, he, with <s>Mādhava</s> (the spring-air/himself), with eyes and throat full of tears, with horripilation, with a wealth of trembling, sang a worthy melody upon the audible flute! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: rāgo yathā-
children.translated_text: The <s>rāga</s> (musical mode), as follows:

children.text:
rāgam īdṛśam asāv acīkpat
prāpa rāgaīva yaḥ priyā-hṛdi |
yaḥ sphuṭaṃ na rasitaḥ purā bhuvi
kvāpi nāmṛtavad aṅga-viśrutaḥ ||JGc_1,23.27|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: He produced such a <s>rāga</s> as entered the heart of his beloved like passion itself — one that had never before been heard clearly anywhere on earth, nor renowned anywhere as being like nectar! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text: tat-praṇāda-maya-varṇa-vibhāgo, yathā-
children.translated_text: The distribution of syllables within that sound, as follows:

children.text:
ayi sudhāṃśu-sudhā-mukhi rādhike
madhura-bhāva-dhurā madhu-mādhavi |
mayi sadā dayite dayite ciraṃ
tava guṇair hṛdayaṃ mama dīryati ||JGc_1,23.28|| [drutavilambita]
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhikā</s>, whose face is like the nectar of the moon's nectar! O sweet-natured one, foremost in sweetness, honey-like spring-beauty! O eternally beloved one, beloved for long — my heart is being torn apart by your virtues!' // [drutavilambita]

children.text: atha bāṇaīva veṇu-nāde pravīṇaḥ svayamaṣav anena tasyāh siddhāṃ biddhatām avabudhya sudhy-agraṇīr anyāś ca tan-nyāyam ājuhāva | [35] tatra varṇa-vibhāgas tv evam-
children.translated_text: Then, he himself — expert in the flute's sound like an arrow — having perceived by this [melody] the accomplished piercing of her (<s>Rādhā</s>), the foremost among the wise, he invoked the others as well by that same method. [35] The distribution of syllables there was thus:

children.text:
ahaha gopa-sutā mama gīḥ-sitā
dharatha hanta manoratha-durdharāḥ |
iti bhavāmi bhavaj-jita-lajjitas
tad-udayaṃ sudayaṃ kuruta priyāh ||JGc_1,23.29|| [drutavilambita]
children.translated_text: 'Aha, O daughters of cowherds! My speech is exhausted! Bear these desires that are unbearable to the mind! Thus I become embarrassed, conquered by you — therefore, O beloveds, make your rising a compassionate one!' // [drutavilambita]

children.text: atha yadā pīta-vasanena gītam evam udgītam, tadā tāsam eva karṇābhyarṇatām āgataṃ tatra ca yathāyatham abhirucitam eva cittī-kṛtaṃ rāgādikam avadhārya nivārtyatātikrama-niratāsthiratāh pratasthire | tatra ca kṛṣṇābhimukhatām evātasthire, nānyat kim api | tathā hi,
children.translated_text: Now, when the yellow-garmented one had thus sung this song, and it had come near to their ears, and the <s>rāga</s> and other [elements] had been perceived there, each as befitting — then, having resolved [their] unsteadinesses and excesses, they set forth. And there, they oriented themselves solely toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and nothing else. For thus:

children.text:
yā yatra karmaṇi gatās tad-anusthitiṃ tā
vismṛtya tasya muralī-śruti-divya-netrāh |
dṛśya-prabhaṃ tam abhivavrajur aśru-nīra-
srotasvatī-mayatayā nija-jīvaneśam ||JGc_1,23.30|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: Those who had gone to whatever task wherever — forgetting the continuation of that [task], their eyes made divine by the hearing of his flute, with streams of tears as their rivers — they approached him, the resplendent one, their lord of life! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tadā ca-
gokula-kumudākṣīṇāṃ
kumudvatīnāṃ tadā tathā kumudām |
akuruta kumad-ādhīśaḥ
sa tadā śatadhā parām sumudām ||JGc_1,23.31|| [āryā]
tadā ca-
śuśrūṣantyaḥ patīn kāścin niruddhāh prasthitiṃ prati |
kṛṣṇaṃ tatraiva tāh prapur ity evaṃ muni-jalptam ||JGc_1,23.32|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And then:
The moon-lord produced a hundredfold supreme joy for the lotus-eyed women of <s>Gokula</s>, who were like <s>kumudvatīs</s> (night-lotus ponds)! // [āryā]
And then:
'Some, while attending their husbands, were prevented from setting forth; those [<s>gopīs</s>] attained <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> right there' — thus spoke the sage. // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: ātra ca ṣnigdhakaṇṭhenāntaś cintitam, tā etāh khalu pādmottarakhaṇḍa-dṛṣṭa-daṇḍakāraṇya-gata-muni-varyatayā sādhaka-caryas tadānim api lakṣmī-varyāṇāṃ rādhikādi-nitya-tad-bhāryāṇāṃ sva-kāmyaṃ sukāmyaṃ sāmyam anavāptā yathā tad avāpya śrī-kṛṣṇam avāptās tathā varṇyam iti sthite-
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> reflected within: 'These [<s>gopīs</s>] who are seen in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> as having been the foremost sages dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> forest — they were practitioners at that time too; but having not attained the easily desirable equality with the foremost among <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, the eternal wives such as <s>Rādhikā</s>, they then obtained [it] and thereby attained Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — this is how it is to be narrated.' Given this:

children.text: tam eva paramātmānaṃ jāra-buddhyāpi saṅgatāh|
jahur guṇa-mayaṃ dehaṃ sadyaḥ prakṣīṇa-bandhanāh ||[BhP 10.29.11]
children.translated_text: they abandoned the body made of <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities) and were immediately freed from bondage.' || [BhP 10.29.11]
'Those who consorted with that very <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self), even with the notion of a paramour (<s>jāra-buddhi</s>) —

children.text: ity eva pratipattaye kalpate |
children.translated_text: — this alone is fit for the understanding [of the matter].

children.text: uktaṃ ca pādmottara-khaṇḍa [272.167] eva-
children.translated_text: And it is stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, Uttara-khaṇḍa [272.167] itself:

children.text:
te sarve strītvam āpannāh samudbhūtāś ca gokule |
hariṃ samprāpya kāmena tato muktā bhavārṇavāt ||iti |
[39] kintu, nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇaya [BhP 10.33.37] ity ukta-diśā tadīyās tu na tad ūhitum īśāmāsur iti jñeyam | yac ca jighāmsayāpi haraye stanaṃ dattvāpi sad-gatim [BhP 10.6.35] ity asya sadṛśena tam eva paramātmānaṃ jāra-buddhyāpi ity ādinā sādhanasya nikarṣa-rūpam aper abhidheyaṃ phalasya tu sarvottama-rūpatvaṃ pratipadyate |
children.translated_text:
'All of them, having attained womanhood, were born in <s>Gokula</s>; | having attained <s>Hari</s> through desire (<s>kāma</s>), they were then liberated from the ocean of worldly existence.' ||
[39] However, in the direction indicated by 'they did not bear ill-will toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' [BhP 10.33.37], it should be understood that his [devotees] could not even conceive of that. And just as by the parallel of 'even by giving the breast to <s>Hari</s> with the intention of killing, [<s>Pūtanā</s>] attained the supreme destination' [BhP 10.6.35], so too by 'those who consorted with that very <s>Paramātmā</s>, even with the notion of a paramour' and so forth — the lowest form of the <s>sādhana</s> (spiritual practice) is being expressed, while the fruit is established as being of the most supreme form.

children.text:
tac ca yuktaṃ, yataḥ-
tāsāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ parātmā na tu paraiti na prāpnuyāj jāratāṃ tat
prānte prāptaḥ patitvaṃ dadad ucita-matiṃ jāram atyāpi vittaḥ|
yadvad bakyāṃ jighāṃsāv api samucitam atyarpaṇāl lālya-bhāvaṃ
lebhe dhātrī-nibhāyāṃ sthiratamam iha yad yuktitas tat phalaṃ hi ||JGc_1,23.33|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
And this is fitting, because:
'For them, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>Paramātmā</s> — he does not go away, nor could he attain paramour-hood; | in the end, having attained husband-hood, bestowing proper understanding, he is known even beyond a paramour; | just as in the case of <s>Bakī</s> (<s>Pūtanā</s>), even through the intention of killing, through the offering of the supremely appropriate, he obtained | the cherished status [of a child] with one resembling a wet-nurse — the most stable [relationship]: here, what is fitting — that indeed is the fruit!' || (JGc 1,23.33) [sragdharā]

children.text: tathāpi-
children.translated_text: Nevertheless —

children.text: uktaṃ purastād etat te caidyaḥ siddhiṃ yathāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This was told to you before: how <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) attained perfection —

children.text: dviṣann api hṛṣīkeśaṃ kim utādhokṣaja-priyāh ||[BhP 10.29.13]
children.translated_text: though hating <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> — what then of those dear to the Transcendent Lord (<s>Adhokṣaja</s>)?' || [BhP 10.29.13]

children.text: ity anusārātā premāmṣena tu tāsāṃ mahad eva vailakṣaṇyam anugatam |
children.translated_text: — following this, through the portion of <s>prema</s> (divine love), a great distinction indeed attaches to them.

children.text: ṇa ca nitya-kāntāsv api prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ jāra-buddhir dṛśyata iti tasyāh ślāghaiva vācyā | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And since even in the case of the eternal consorts (<s>nitya-kāntās</s>), the paramour-notion (<s>jāra-buddhi</s>) is not seen in the manifest <s>līlā</s>, its praise alone is to be declared. Because:

children.text:
yā nityā eva kāntā danuja-kula-ripo rādhikādyā na tāsām
ślāghāṃ sā jāratā-dhī-saciva-janir iyāt kintu rāgaḥ sa nityaḥ |
tāṃ bhittvā vighna-kartrīṃ druta-muditavatā tena taṃ nitya-kāntaṃ
prāpus tā nāparāsām iva vapur aparaṃ sa pratīkṣeta tāsām ||JGc_1,23.34|| [sragdharā] iti |
children.translated_text: 'Those who are the eternal consorts — <s>Rādhikā</s> and the others — of the enemy of the demon-clan, | their praise would not arise from the companion-birth of paramour-notion; rather, that love (<s>rāga</s>) is eternal. | Having broken through that [notion] which creates obstacles, joyfully and swiftly, through Him, that eternal beloved — | they attained Him; nor did He, as with the others, await another form of theirs.' || (JGc 1,23.34) [sragdharā] — thus.

children.text: tad etad vicintya sphuṭaṃ proce, tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Having contemplated this, he clearly proclaimed — then, from that point onward:

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-abhiṣrtavatīnāṃ viśeṣo yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — the special [description] of those who had come forth [to meet <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]:

children.text:
śrute murali-kākale nija-nijāhvaya-prāpake
samaṃ vraja-nata-bhruvaḥ sapadi phulla-dehā babhuḥ |
anaṅgam api vardhitaṃ vihitavān aho yas tadā
kathaṃ na kila vardhayen nija-kalā-balenāṅganāh ? ||JGc_1,23.35|| [pṛthvī]
[45] kiṃ ca,
children.translated_text:
'When the tender warbling of the flute was heard, conveying each one's own name, | the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s> simultaneously became blossomed in body. | He who had augmented even <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god) — ah! — at that time, | how could he not cause the women to flourish by the power of his own art?' || (JGc 1,23.35) [pṛthvī]
[45] Moreover,

children.text: satvara-prasāravattva-sattva-dhāma-hāyinī
children.translated_text: Possessing the essence of swiftly-spreading vitality, diminishing the abode of [all other] vitality,

children.text: sarva-gurv-ahārya-kūṭa-vāraṇatiyāyinī |
children.translated_text: surpassing the insurmountable barriers of all elders,

children.text: nātham ekam anv aneka-dāra-sampad-arpiṇī
children.translated_text: offering the wealth of manifold wifehood to the one Lord alone,

children.text: ogha-mogham anv ananta-bhakta-loka-tarpiṇī ||a||
children.translated_text: vainly following the current yet satisfying the infinite host of devotees; ||a||

children.text: lola-keśa-śaivalāñci-karṇa-pūra-cakriṇī
children.translated_text: bearing the wheels of ear-ornaments amid loose hair like water-weeds,

children.text: puṣpa-jāta-niṣprapāta-śubhra-pheṇa-cakriṇī |
children.translated_text: bearing the wheels of bright foam from cascading masses of flowers,

children.text: ucchalan-navīna-mīna-netra-nīra-gātriṇī
children.translated_text: having limbs [streaming] with the water of eyes [like] darting fresh fish,

children.text: agrimādhva-mātra-pātra-sammukhānuyātriṇī ||b||
children.translated_text: following directly in the path of the foremost course alone; ||b||

children.text: manda-cāla-bāhu-nāla-pāṇi-padma-sālinī
children.translated_text: possessing lotus-hands with arm-stalks gently swaying,

children.text: accha-bāla-kacchapāṅga-vatsa-janma-jālinī |
children.translated_text: having the net of offspring [like] clear young turtles [on their] flanks,

children.text: jūti-dhūti-kṛt-kuṭīra-tīra-dhīra-gāminī
children.translated_text: moving steadily along the banks, creating shelters with their movement and splendor,

children.text: ūru-bhūruhāli-pāta-samprapāta-kāminī ||c||
children.translated_text: lovers who cascade and descend [like] rows of great trees along the thighs; ||c||

children.text: kāñci-kāñci-kaṅkaṇādi-śiñjad-ambha-sañjinī
children.translated_text: producing the jingling of waters [like] girdles, girdle-bells, bangles and the like,

children.text: prāyaśas tu haṃsa-saṅgha-śṣabditānurañjinī |
children.translated_text: mostly harmonizing with the sounds of flocks of swans,

children.text: tūrṇa-tūrṇa-ghūrṇanādi-saṅkulāṅga-nartinī
children.translated_text: dancers whose limbs are crowded with swift, swift whirlings and the like,

children.text: pūrṇa-pūrṇa-bhāva-gūrṇa-jāḍya-jāta-vartinī ||d||
children.translated_text: abiding in the stupor born of being overwhelmed with full, full emotion; ||d||

children.text: veśa-vastra-sanniveśa-cañcalatva-bhaṅginī
children.translated_text: having the fickleness of dress and garments in their attire,

children.text: tat-tad-artha-vaiparītya-kāri-vega-saṅginī |
children.translated_text: accompanied by the velocity that produces the reversal of each and every purpose,

children.text: yan-nimittam ātma-sarva-saṅga-bhaṅga-bhāvinī
children.translated_text: on whose account the breaking of all one's own attachments comes to be,

children.text: yatra sarva-nāma-rūpa-vismrtiś ca bhāvinī ||e||
children.translated_text: and in whom the forgetting of all name and form comes to be; ||e||

children.text:
śyāma-dhāma-suṣṭhu-rāmam etam atra sad-dhavam
sindhu-tulyam uttaraṅgad-aṅgam āśu mādhavam |
pūrva-pūrva-bhinnayātir uttarāpta-saṅgatiḥ
āpagāli-sammitāpa seyam āli-saṃhatiḥ ||f|| ||JGc_1,23.36|| [tūṇaka]
children.translated_text: 'Toward the dark-hued abode [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], supremely delightful, this <s>Mādhava</s> — | ocean-like, with limbs surging with waves — swiftly [they flowed]; | each previous [gopī] arriving by a different route obtained union at the further end — | this company of friends was like a series of rivers, O friend!' || (f) || (JGc 1,23.36) [tūṇaka]

children.text: tās tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And they, there —

children.text:
śubhaṃyu-vana-mañjule savitṛjā-rucā saṅkule
prasūna-gaṇa-rājite bhramara-kokila-bhrājite |
sugandha-marud-añcite kumuda-bandhu śobhācite
samasta-guṇa-niścite nidhitayā ciraṃ sañcite ||JGc_1,23.37|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text: 'In the beautiful <s>Śubhaṃyu</s> forest, crowded with the radiance of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), | adorned with clusters of flowers, resplendent with bees and cuckoos, | perfumed by fragrant breezes, beautified by the friend of the <s>kumuda</s> (the moon), | endowed with all qualities, long treasured as if stored up —' || (JGc 1,23.37) [pṛthvī]

children.text:
sthale maṇija-catvaraṃ samadhiruhya taṃ satvaraṃ
vicitra-muralī-kalaṃ viracayantam udyat-kalam |
ghanāghana-ghana-śriyaṃ taḍīd-abhīṣu-vastra-priyaṃ
maṇi-dyuti-vikasvaraṃ dadṛśur aṅgi divya-smaram ||JGc_1,23.38|| [pṛthvī]
(yugmakam)
children.translated_text:
'On a platform, having swiftly ascended the gem-paved terrace, | [they saw] him creating the variegated melody of the flute, with rising musical measures, | possessing the beauty of dense dark clouds, dear to the garment of lightning-rays, | radiant with the luster of gems — they beheld the embodiment of divine <s>Smara</s> (Love).' || (JGc 1,23.38) [pṛthvī]
(a pair of verses)

children.text:
nirmāya kṛṣṇam abhitaḥ sthitim atra gaurī-
paṅktis tadā tam avalambitum utka-cittā |
madhye tamālam upalabhya suvarṇa-varṇa-
vallī-tatir vilasatīti kila vyaloki ||JGc_1,23.39|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: 'Having fashioned themselves around <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, standing on all sides, the row of fair-complexioned women (<s>Gaurīs</s>), | with eager hearts, yearning to cling to him — | perceiving a <s>tamāla</s> tree in their midst, of golden-hued | creeper-clusters twining about — thus indeed it appeared!' || (JGc 1,23.39) [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
atha-
vaṃśī-dūtikayā nimantrya kalitāh saurabhya-dhārā-sakhī
saṅghaiḥ sādrti bhūri dūra-saraṇer ānāyitāh subhruvaḥ |
prāptāh svāntikam ātma-rocir amṛtāny apy āśitāh preyasā
ṭrptiṃ naiva yayur na vā viramitaṃ tad-dāna-karmāmunā ||JGc_1,23.40|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Then:
'Invited by the flute-messenger, assembled — the companies of fragrance-stream-friends | brought the beautiful-browed ones with great respect from the distant path; | having arrived near him and been fed the nectar of his own radiance by the beloved — | they did not reach satisfaction, nor did he cease his act of giving!' || (JGc 1,23.40) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
pratyuta-
navyāh kalādharāh śubhrā bhrāji-nakṣatra-mālikāh |
arāla-locanāh kṛṣṇa-cakoraṃ ṭrsṇa-jaṃ vyadhuḥ ||JGc_1,23.41|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
On the contrary:
'The fresh crescent moons — bright, with shining garlands of stars — | with curved eyes — created thirst-born | desire [like] <s>cakora</s> birds for the dark [moon] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' || (JGc 1,23.41) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha kṛṣṇas tatra sa-tṛṣṇam acintayat-aho ! nava-tāruṇyasya puṇya-sampada etā, vara-lāvaṇyasya mat-kretavya-navya-paṇya-śreṇyas trilokī-lakṣmyāś cūḍāmaṇayaḥ, sphuran-manmathasya jīvanauṣadhayaḥ kumudāyamāna-madīya-locanayor navīnāś candra-kalāh sahāvatīrya ruciṃ vitīrya virājante |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> there thought with longing: 'Ah! These are the blessed treasures of fresh youth, the rows of new merchandise of supreme beauty purchased by me, the crest-jewels of the splendor of the three worlds, the life-giving herbs of blazing <s>Manmatha</s> (the Love-god), and the fresh lunar digits of my <s>kumuda</s>-blossoming eyes — they have descended together, bestowed their charm, and shine forth!'

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite-
children.translated_text: This being so —

children.text:
kṛṣṇāpāṅga-śaraḥ sāṅgaṃ bhittvāpāṅga-śaraṃ mama |
manorathinam udbhettuṃ kila prāviśad antaram ||JGc_1,23.42|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The side-glance arrow of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having pierced the side-glance arrow of mine | along with its body, entered within | in order to burst forth the chariot of desire!' || (JGc 1,23.42) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: iti tāh pratyekaṃ pratyetavyaṃ cakruḥ |
children.translated_text: — thus each of them was made to realize [his attention].

children.text: vastutas tu hares tāsu sarvāsu latāsv iva dvitra-lava-sevana-pūrvakam apūrvatayābhraman-netra-bhramara-yugalaṃ kamalinyām iva rādhāyām nirbādhām sthitim ātasthe |
children.translated_text: But in truth, <s>Hari's</s> pair of roaming eye-bees, wandering with unprecedented novelty among all those [gopīs] like creepers — with a preliminary service of two or three portions — settled in unobstructed repose upon <s>Rādhā</s>, as upon a lotus.

children.text: āsthitavatīti ca tatredaṃ sa tu vicārayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: And that he had so settled — here he reflected on this:

children.text:
śobhāyāh śubhadā śobhā ramāyāh paramā ramā |
seyaṃ mal-locanasyāpi rādhikā-cāru-locanam ||JGc_1,23.43|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'The beauty of beauty, the auspicious bestower of splendor; | the supreme delight (<s>Ramā</s>) of delight (<s>Ramā</s>) — | this is the lovely eye of <s>Rādhikā</s> for my own eye too!' || (JGc 1,23.43) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ sati sā ca tadīya-tādṛśa-dṛśaḥ sparṣataḥ kampa-sampad-unmīlana-rasa-prasara-vaśatayā kṣobhaṃ labhamānāpi taṃ prati prahita-lobhāṃ śobhām uvāha |
children.translated_text: This being so, she too — from the touch of his such gaze — though becoming agitated through the power of the stream of <s>rasa</s> produced by the unfolding of the treasure of trembling, displayed a beauty charged with longing directed toward him.

children.text: ātra ca praśnottara-mayaṃ padyam:
children.translated_text: And here is a verse in question-and-answer form:

children.text:
smerayoḥ prati vidhūdyad-asrayo
rādhikā-nayanayos tulāṃvada |
śāradaṃ vikaca-mecakotpalaṃ
yan maranda-jhara-moci tat kim u? ||JGc_1,23.44|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: 'Tell the comparison for <s>Rādhikā's</s> eyes — | smiling, yet with tears streaming forth in response! | Is it the autumnal, fully-bloomed dark <s>utpala</s> lotus | that releases a flow of nectar? Is that it?' || (JGc 1,23.44) [rathoddhatā]
