children.text: tad evaṃ sthite tāḥ puraḥ-sthitā yadyapy anavadya-saṃvanana-pravīṇa-veṇu-vidyā-maditā lajjām ujjahati sma, tathāpy avitathābhijātyatayā namratā-kamrā muni-vratam evānuvavṛtire |
children.translated_text: This being so, those [gopīs] standing before him — though intoxicated by the supremely skilled, blameless, caressing flute-art — were abandoning their shyness; yet, by the truth of their noble birth, graceful in modesty, they continued to observe the vow of a sage.

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇas tu yadā viśīṣṭa-lalanā-madhyam adhyāvasann evam adyotiṣṭha, tadā
tāsāṃ parama-durlabha-parimala-mātrāṇām api vaiṇava-madhura-gīta-madhu-maditatayā svayam eva kṛtābhiyātrāṇām āgatiṃ dṛśoḥ pathi nirmāya, sa-narma-smitas tad-vidhām buddhim upadhayā labdha-śuddhim avadhārayann iva tan-mukhād unmukhānurāga-jāgarūka-vāg-amṛtam āsvādayitum, tāsu ca samutsukatām āsādayituṃ, nijāntika-sthiti-yācñā-garbheṇa sphurad-upekṣā-sandarbheṇa vacasā tāh kṣobhayāmāsa | yathā-
children.translated_text: But when <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, dwelling amidst those distinguished women, shone forth in this way, then — fashioning at the path of his eyes the arrival of those who, intoxicated by the honey of the sweet flute-song, had come of their own accord even though they were of supremely rare fragrance — with a playful smile, as though ascertaining through a pretext their purified understanding, and in order to savor the nectar of speech flowing with awakened love from their mouths, and also to generate eagerness in them — he agitated them with words whose core was a request for them to stay near him, yet whose surface bore an elaborate structure of apparent indifference. As follows:

children.text:
mahābhāgā yuṣman-milanam abhavan naḥ śubha-kṛte
tataḥ pṛcchāmy atrāgamanam idam avyāhatam iti |
tad etāvat-kleśād abhigamanataḥ saṅkucita-dhīḥ
sa bhūyaḥ sampṛcche bhavad-abhimataṃ kiṃ nu karavai? ||JGc_1,23.45|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: 'O greatly blessed ones! Your meeting with us has been for our auspiciousness; | therefore I ask: this unobstructed arrival of yours — [what is its purpose]? | My mind, contracted from your having come through such exertion, | asks again: what is your desire? What shall I do?' || (JGc 1,23.45) [śikharinī]

children.text: tad evam atrādara-jñāpanayā jñātvāpy ajñāna-vijñāpanayā ca sveṣūpekṣāpekṣayor ekataratayā tad-abhiprāyaṃ prāyaśo boddhum asamarthāsu tāsu tata evānabhivyakta-kiñcid-arthāsu punaḥ sa-narma ca tathā vācaṃ prāha-
children.translated_text: Thus, when through the indication of his regard, though knowing, he expressed as if unknowing — and through one or the other of [apparent] indifference or expectation toward them — they, being mostly unable to comprehend his intention, remaining there with their meaning unexpressed — he again spoke playfully in this manner:

children.text:
pṛcchato' pi purato mama bhavyaṃ
maunam eva kurutha pratigīr yat |
tad-bhavad-vraja-gṛhe gṛha-bhājāṃ
kiṃ nirāmayam atha pratibhāti? ||JGc_1,23.46|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text: 'Though I ask directly before you, O noble ones, | you maintain only silence — no counter-song! | Well then — in your households in <s>Vraja</s>, | is all well with the household members?' || (JGc 1,23.46) [svāgatā]

children.text: tataś ca mithaḥ sa-smita-nirīkṣitāsu tāsu punar uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, as they exchanged smiling glances with one another, he spoke again:

children.text: tad idaṃ durabhiprāyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'This intention of yours is difficult to fathom —

children.text: boddhuṃ bahvadīyam asmi na samarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am unable to comprehend that which belongs to you all;

children.text: svayam iha yūyaṃ tasmāt
children.translated_text: therefore, here, you yourselves,

children.text: kathayata saṅkocam uddhūya ||JGc_1,23.47||
children.translated_text: speak — casting off your reserve!' || (JGc 1,23.47)

children.text: punar atīva saṅkacatīr nirīkṣya yojanāviśeṣa-śleṣamayatayāpi tathā prathayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Again, observing them exceedingly contracted [with shyness], he proclaimed [the matter] in a manner interwoven with a special ambiguity of interpretation (<s>śleṣa</s>):

children.text: atha na bhavati kāryaṃ brūtha tan neti buddhaṃ
children.translated_text: 'If there is no business [for you here], then say so — that is understood;

children.text: vrajam anu cala-cittā yāta nādhvaṃ mayātra |
children.translated_text: go back to <s>Vraja</s>, O unsteady-minded ones — do not [stay] here with me on the road!

children.text: vanam idam aitghoraṃ rātrir atrātighorā
children.translated_text: This forest is exceedingly terrible, the night here is exceedingly terrible,

children.text: svayam atiśayi-ghora-prāṇi-vṛndaiḥ parītāḥ ||JGc_1,23.48||
children.translated_text: and you are surrounded by exceedingly terrible throngs of creatures!' || (JGc 1,23.48)

children.text: atra nādhvam iti na yāteti vā yojanā | punas tad eva śleṣayituṃ sopāna-viśeṣaṃ cakāra-na cedṛśī svairatā bhavādṛśīnāṃ sadṛśī bhavati yataḥ mātāpitara-pramukhāḥ sahajāḥ patayaś ca vaḥ santi iti |
children.translated_text: Here, 'do not [stay] on the road' is to be construed alternatively as 'do not go.' Again, to employ the same ambiguity, he fashioned a particular step [of argument]: 'Such willfulness is not becoming of those like your honors, for your mothers, fathers, and other principal [relatives], natural kinsmen, and husbands exist' — thus.

children.text: punaḥ sa-hāsam āha sma-śrūyante' pi tanūjāḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Again, with a laugh he said: 'Children too, I hear!' — thus.

children.text:
atra kathakaś cintayāmāsa-vṛndā-paurṇamāsī-saṃvāda-gata-siddhāntānusāri-dhiyā-
siṣeva ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ
sarvāḥ śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ [BhP 10.33.25]
ity anena pratipannasya tatrakīya-rasasyālambana-vairūpyād vairasyāpannatā-bhiyā ca tad idaṃ parihasitam eveti vidvan-matatayā vyaktīkariṣyāmi iti |
children.translated_text:
Here the narrator reflected — with an understanding following the established doctrine contained in the conversation of <s>Vṛndā</s> and <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>:
'He who served the erotic sentiment (<s>saurata</s>) confined within himself, | and all the autumn-poetry-narrative-<s>rasa</s>-abodes —' [BhP 10.33.25]
— by this, because of the deformity of the foundational element (<s>ālambana</s>) of the <s>rasa</s> established therein, and out of the fear of repugnance arising — 'this was spoken only in jest' — 'I shall make this clear as the view of the learned' — thus [he resolved].

children.text: atha tad eva spaṣṭam ācaṣṭa-[61] tad evaṃ tābhiḥ saha rantuṃ kṛta-vaṃśī-dhvaniḥ sa tu sarasānāṃ śiromaṇir yadyapḸ tāsām utpattita eva sva-mātra-sātkṛta-pati-bhāvānām anyatra patir iti pratītir loka-saṃvadana-vaśaṃvadatā-mātra-mayī kevala-sva-saṅgama-kāmanā-vrataś cāparāṅga-saṅgama-rūpa-virūpatā-nirjayīti viśadam arthaṃ tāsu svīya-kāntā-bhāva-samutpatty-anyathānupapattyā sambhāvitavān |
children.translated_text: Then he expressed that very [view] plainly: [61] Thus, having sounded his flute to sport with them, he — the crest-jewel of the amorous — although from the very birth of those [gopīs] their sense of husband-hood was exclusively absorbed in him alone, and the notion of 'husband' directed elsewhere was merely a conformity to worldly convention — and [although] his vow was the desire for union with himself alone, and the victory over the deformity of union with another's limb [was his aim] — he clearly established this meaning among them through the impossibility of any other explanation for the arising of the consort-sentiment (<s>kāntā-bhāva</s>) toward himself.

children.text: yadyapi ca tāsām ajāta-putrāṇām api devaraṃ-manya-putrādiṣu putratā-vyavahāraḥ kevalaṃ sannihita-bālaka-viṣayaka-vatsalatā-svabhāvākāras tat-sambandhābhimānas tu bahir evācāra ity āpta-vacanān nirdhāritavāṃs tathāpi tat-tad-ullekhana-karmaṇā narma-mātram ācaritavān | tad ācarya ca tad-bandhūnām andhāyamānānām api tad-anveṣaṇa-nirbandhād bhayaṃ vicārya sāmarṣam iva vivakṣitam uvāca-katham iha tat-tad-bhayaṃ kurutha iti | atra ca ṣaṣṭhī pañcamī vā samasyate |
children.translated_text: And although those [gopīs], even though they had no sons of their own, maintained the convention of calling brother-in-law's sons and such as 'sons' — this was merely an outward expression of the maternal affection natural toward children present nearby, while the identification of relationship was only an external custom — thus he ascertained from the words of the learned. Nevertheless, by the act of mentioning these [relationships], he performed only a jest. And having performed that jest, considering the fear arising from the insistence of their kinsmen — who were becoming blind [with rage] — in searching for them, he spoke as if with indignation: 'Why do you create such fears here?' And here, the sixth or fifth case-ending is to be construed.

children.text:
kiṃ cātra khaṇḍam akhaṇḍaṃ ca padyaṃ yathāyatham anūḍhā ūḍhābhāsāś ca tā dṛṣṭvācaṣṭeti gamyate | tatrānūḍhāḥ prati sahajā ity antam | ūḍhābhāsāḥ pratiśrūyante' pi tanūjā ity antam | akhaṇḍaṃ tu sarvāḥ pratīti jñeyam |
[64] punaś cārtha-dhvani-saṃvalanayā cittam āndolayāmāsa-
children.translated_text:
Moreover, here the verse is partly fragmented and partly whole, and it is understood as: 'seeing them — both unmarried and those having the appearance of being married — he spoke.' Therein, to the unmarried ones, [he spoke] ending with 'natural.' To those having the appearance of being married, [he spoke] ending with 'sons are heard of.' But the unfragmented [portion] is to be understood as [addressed] to all.
[64] And again, agitating their minds with the blending of implied meaning:

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ yad-vanam aty apūrva-kusumair divyartunā pūjitaṃ
children.translated_text: 'It has been seen that this forest, honored by an extraordinary divine season, with most wondrous flowers,

children.text: dyotaiś carcitam indunā yamunayā cātmānilair nartitam |
children.translated_text: illuminated and anointed by the moon, danced by the <s>Yamunā</s> and the breezes —

children.text: sāmagrīyam udeti deva-nicitāsmākaṃ vihāra-krame
children.translated_text: this assemblage of materials arises in the course of our sport, arranged by the gods;

children.text: tasmād etad abhāvatas tu va iha stavyā na vāstavyatā ||JGc_1,23.49||
children.translated_text: therefore, from its absence, your dwelling here is not to be praised!' ||23.49||

children.text: kintu-
diṣṭenāpte tatra gatvā sva-goṣṭhe
children.translated_text: 'Having obtained by fortune, going there to your own cow-settlement,

children.text: kaṣṭenāpi svīya-dharmaṃ kurudhvam |
children.translated_text: even with difficulty, perform your own <s>dharma</s>!

children.text: patyur bhaktir bāla-vatsādi-pālya-
children.translated_text: Devotion to one's husband, and the care of children, calves, and other dependents

children.text: vyaktīnāṃ yaḥ pālanādiś ca diṣṭaḥ ||JGc_1,23.50||
children.translated_text: to be nurtured — that has been ordained!' ||23.50||
But —

children.text: tataḥ kaṣṭa-sādhyaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ bādhyamānaṃ vidhāyātrāvikala-sarva-dharma-phale mama sukha-vihāra-sthale praviśata | [66] anyathā punar udyad-vidhu-vanam idaṃ bhavatīnāṃ vidhuvanāya sampatsyata iti yācñā-pakṣābhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having established that <s>dharma</s> — achievable only with difficulty — as something being overridden, [he said:] 'Enter here, the arena of my blissful sport, where all <s>dharma</s>-fruits are fully intact.' [66] Otherwise, [the sense is:] 'this forest of the rising moon will become a cause of torment (<s>vidhuvana</s>) for you' — this being the purport of the entreaty-alternative.

children.text: punaḥ sa vimarśam iva provāca-
children.translated_text: Again, he spoke as if with deliberation:

children.text: aham ahaha na budhye smeti pūrvaṃ pralāpaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Alas, I made a prattle earlier, "I do not understand!"

children.text: cakara tad iha yūyaṃ tad vicārya kṣamadhvam |
children.translated_text: Having done that, here now, you — considering it — forgive me!

children.text: rati-visara-vilāsair yantraṇād āgatā yas
children.translated_text: You who have come, compelled by the sportive play of love's outpourings —

children.text: tad-ucitam akhilaṃ yat snigdhatā mayy upaiti ||JGc_1,23.51||
children.translated_text: it is fitting that all the affection toward me arises [thus]!' ||23.51||

children.text: tad api na yadvad virahe prītis tadvan na sānnidhye
bhavati tato gṛha-yānaṃ bhavatīnām aucitīṃ cinute ||JGc_1,23.52||
children.translated_text: therefore, your going home is what propriety demands!' ||23.52||
'Yet, just as there is no delight in separation, so too there is none in proximity —

children.text: atra ca prīti-viṣayād dūre sthitir na yukteti virodhi-lakṣaṇayā yācñāpakṣaḥ saṅgamyate | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And here, through the indicative figure of contradiction — that standing far from the object of love is not proper — the entreaty-alternative is arrived at. And then:

children.text: pūrvaṃ yac cirataḥ spṛhāvalanayā saṃkptam āsīt punar
children.translated_text: 'What had previously, through the prolonged impulse of longing, been contracted,

children.text: vaṃśyākāraṇayā balād upacitaṃ tad bhagnam uccair yataḥ |
children.translated_text: was then forcibly augmented by the instrumentality of the flute, and that has been shattered utterly;

children.text: tac chrutvā dayitād vyalīka-vacanaṃ bāḍhaṃ na niścikyire
children.translated_text: hearing that dissembling speech from their beloved, they could not determine at all

children.text: kiṃ na smaḥ kim u vā sma ity aḸ tadā gopāla-vāma-bhruvaḥ ||JGc_1,23.53||
children.translated_text: whether "we exist" or "we do not exist" — thus then [were] those beautiful-browed wives of the cowherds!' ||23.53||

children.text: tad āsāṃ niścalāṅgīnāṃ kāñcīnām api rājayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even the rows of their girdle-bells, of those whose limbs were motionless,

children.text: samaṃ samantataḥ kleśāt tūṣṇīkām eva saṅgatāḥ ||JGc_1,23.54||
children.translated_text: together on all sides, from anguish, arrived at silence alone!' ||23.54||

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text: bāṣpa-vyājād āsāṃ priya-kṛta-parihṛti-samūḍha-santāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Under the pretext of tears, the clusters of their heart-lotuses,

children.text: manye hṛdayāmbhoruha-nivahaḥ svarasān muhuś ca susrāva ||JGc_1,23.55||
children.translated_text: I believe, whose anguish was born of the beloved's rejection, streamed forth their essences repeatedly!' ||23.55||

children.text: atra caivaṃ vicārayāmāsuḥ-
children.translated_text: And here, they deliberated thus:

children.text: prāṇāṃs tyajāma dayitasya pade luṭhāma
children.translated_text: 'Shall we abandon our life-breaths? Shall we roll at the beloved's feet?

children.text: kupyāma tatra vinivṛtya gṛhaṃ vrajāma |
children.translated_text: Shall we rage? Shall we turn back and go home?

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ viśāma ca na vā kaṭhināyamānam
children.translated_text: Shall we enter the dark <s>Yamunā</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>)? Or shall we not? — becoming hardened,

children.text: etaṃ svabhālam abhihatya nicāyayāma ||JGc_1,23.56||
children.translated_text: shall we strike our own foreheads and declare our resolve?' ||23.56||

children.text: tatra tu-
children.translated_text: But there:

children.text: śiraḥ-pīḍā bāṣpa-vyathita-galatā hṛd-gata-mahā-
children.translated_text: 'Headache, a choking throat distressed by tears, a great

children.text: prakampaḥ pratyaṅga-skhalanam iti nānā-vikṛtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: trembling within the heart, stumbling of every limb — such various distortions

children.text: priye rūkṣe jātā dalayitum amūr āvavṛtire
children.translated_text: arose when the beloved became harsh, and began to shatter them;

children.text: paraṃ tad-vaktrāntaḥ-prasadanam agāt pālayitṛtām ||JGc_1,23.57||
children.translated_text: but the gracious expression within his face assumed the role of protector!' ||23.57||

children.text: masī-valita-dṛg-jala-srava-tamobhir ārād uraḥ-
children.translated_text: 'With the darkness of tear-streams rolling from their ink-smeared eyes, from afar

children.text: sthalaṃ valita-kuṅkuma-praciti-sandhyam āvṛṇvatīḥ |
children.translated_text: covering the chest-area twilight-hued with smeared <s>kuṅkuma</s> deposits,

children.text: avāṅ-mukha-vidhur vadhūḥ sapadi paurṇamāsī-śaśi-
children.translated_text: that <s>Hari</s>, as the full-moon (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) gleaming in the night, with downturned face,

children.text: sphuran niśi ca tāmasīr iva cacāya tasmin hariḥ ||JGc_1,23.58||
children.translated_text: regarded those women as if they were dark shadows of the night!' ||23.58||

children.text: tataś ca kiñcid amarṣe sati-
children.translated_text: And then, when some anger arose:

children.text: śvāsa-dīrṇa-madhurādhara-śriyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Their beauty of sweet lips torn by sighs,

children.text: komalāṅghria-dala-kīrṇa-bhūmayaḥ |
children.translated_text: the ground strewn with [petals from] their tender lotus-feet —

children.text: hanta kāntam api taṃ nata-bhruvo
children.translated_text: alas! Those bowed-browed women pierced even that beloved one

children.text: vivyadhur nayana-sāyakāsribhiḥ ||JGc_1,23.59||
children.translated_text: with the bloodied arrows of their glances!' ||23.59||

children.text: tad evaṃ kṣobhe sati dāḍimād antaḥ-sakta-rakta-bījānām iva nijānāṃ bhāvānāṃ hṛdayān niṣkulākṛtiḥ svayam eva jātā, tathāpi vaidagdhī-digdhatayā priya-gīrvad eva sandigdham ūcuḥ | yad adyāpi gāyanti-
children.translated_text: Thus, when such agitation arose, the outward expression of their inner feelings, whose red essence was embedded within the heart — as red seeds within a pomegranate — emerged of its own accord. Nevertheless, because they were coated with amorous cleverness (<s>vaidagdhī</s>), they spoke in an ambiguous manner, like the speech of the gods. And even now they sing:

children.text: iyam iva mā kuru punar ativādam |
children.translated_text: 'Do not make such excessive speech again!

children.text: bhakta-janān bhaja muhur itarāṃs tyaja
children.translated_text: Serve your devotees repeatedly, abandon others,

children.text: vibhur iva rahita-vivādam ||dhruvam||
children.translated_text: like a lord, free from dispute!' ||[refrain]||

children.text: pati-putrādika-bhajanam ihādhikam iti yaṃ vadasi vicāram |
children.translated_text: 'The consideration you speak of — that serving husband, sons, and such is superior here —

children.text: sa tvayy eva hi tiṣṭhatu na tu bahir iti vimṛśāmaḥ sāram ||JGc_1,23.60||
children.translated_text: let that remain in you yourself; but we consider the essence to be not outside [of you]!' ||23.60||

children.text: anayor artha-śleṣo' yam ubhayam eva pakṣaṃ viśeṣayati |
children.translated_text: The double meaning (<s>artha-śleṣa</s>) of these two [verses] distinguishes both alternatives.

children.text: atha dhava-suta-mukha-gaṇatas tava sukham asti satāṃ hṛdi yātam |
children.translated_text: 'If you have happiness from the assemblage of husband, sons, and other faces,

children.text: tad api ca na hi bhavad-anusaraṇaṃ bhavad-icchati yuvatī-jātam ||JGc_1,23.61||
children.translated_text: then even so, the race of young women does not desire following you — it does desire following you!' ||23.61||

children.text: atra sandigdha-kāku-padaṃ nahīti padaṃ tad-icchā-nirdhāraṇe, yad vā niṣedhe-
children.translated_text: Here, the word 'nahi' is of ambiguous intonation (<s>kāku</s>) — for ascertaining that desire, or alternatively, for denial:

children.text: svām āśām anuvardhaya vara-tanu-tatir iha labhatāṃ śātam |
children.translated_text: 'Increase our hope, O one of excellent form — let this body attain its nourishment!

children.text: satatānaśvara-vara varadeśvara na vitanu vitanūtpātam ||JGc_1,23.62||
children.translated_text: O eternally imperishable, excellent, lord of boon-givers — do not produce bodily catastrophe!' ||23.62||

children.text: atrānuvardhayeti samedhane chedane vā-
children.translated_text: Here, 'increase' means either 'make grow' or 'cut off' —

children.text: gṛha-karmāṇy anucittaṃ sukha-tanu bhavatā nahy apinaddham |
children.translated_text: 'Household duties have not been bound upon us by you, O source of happiness —

children.text: caraṇau pracalata iha na ca valataḥ pratigamanaṃ kila baddham ||JGc_1,23.63||
children.translated_text: our feet move here but do not turn back — the return is indeed blocked!' ||23.63||

children.text: atra sukha-tanv iti bhavatety asya cittam ity asya vā viśeṣaṇam | apinaddham iti bandhanābhāve bandhane vā na ceti pūrva-nahi-vat | kileti niścaye' nṛte vā |
children.translated_text: Here, 'source of happiness' is either an adjective of 'you' or of 'mind.' 'Not bound' means either absence of binding or binding itself. 'Not' is like the previous 'nahi.' 'Indeed' means either certainty or falsehood.

children.text: svabhava-tāpa-bharam amṛta-dharādhara-rasa-jharataḥ svata eva |
children.translated_text: 'The burden of the heat of love's fire — from the nectar-bearing cloud raining of itself —

children.text: nāśaya yadi na hi mādṛśam api sa hi saṅkramitā sakhideva ||JGc_1,23.64||
children.translated_text: destroy it! For if not, even one like me — that [fire] is indeed a transmitter, O friend-god!' ||23.64||

children.text: atra svabhaveti kāme svajāte vā | mādṛśam ity asmat-sadṛśe vā jane' smad-arthe vā |
children.translated_text: Here, 'of love' means either 'of desire' or 'of one's own nature.' 'One like me' means either 'a person similar to us' or 'for our sake.'

children.text:
lakṣmī-sukha-dadam api bhavataḥ padam ahaha pulindī-bhavyam |
spṛṣṭaṃ yad-avadhi dṛṣṭaṃ tad-avadhi sarvaṃ jagad-apasavyam ||JGc_1,23.65||atrāpasavyaṃ pratikūlam ity ubhaya-pakṣe' pi samañjasam | ākṣepa-pakṣe punlindī-bhavyam iti nīca-gāmitvaṃ vyajyate-
children.translated_text:
'Your foot, though giving happiness even to <s>Lakṣmī</s> — alas! — is worthy of the <s>Pulinda</s> women!
Since it was touched, since it was seen — from that moment, the entire world has become adverse!' ||23.65||
Here, 'adverse' (<s>apasavya</s>) is fitting in both alternatives as 'contrary.' In the reproach-alternative, 'worthy of <s>Pulinda</s> women' suggests low-going inclination:

children.text:
lakṣīr vrajam anu tulasī-vanam anu bhavad-udaya-sphurad-udayā |
dṛśyata iti tava pada-dhūlyāplavam icchaty api pati-hṛdayā ||JGc_1,23.66||yasyā vīkṣaṇam api valita-kṣaṇa-pārṣada-vṛnda-nidhānam |
tadvad vayam api hṛdi vāñchām api nahyāmaḥ savitānam ||JGc_1,23.67||
children.translated_text: likewise, we too bind even the desire in our hearts, with a canopy!' ||23.67||

'The glories, following <s>Vraja</s>, following the <s>Tulasī</s> grove, have their arising radiant from your arising!
They are seen — thus your foot-dust's flooding is desired even by one whose heart belongs to her husband!' ||23.66||
'She whose mere glance is a treasury of the attendant-host of turning moments —

children.text: atrāpi-śabdaḥ samuccaye pūrvavat kākvā niṣedhe vā |
children.translated_text: Here too, the word 'even' is either for aggregation as before, or by intonation (<s>kāku</s>) for denial.

children.text: tattvaṃ sukṛpaya kṛta-vṛjinātyaya tava yāś caraṇe raktāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O truth! With supreme compassion, you who have removed sin — those who are devoted to your feet,

children.text: tā bhavataḥ smita-vīkṣaṇa-vismita-cittāḥ kuru nija-bhaktāḥ ||JGc_1,23.68||
children.translated_text: their minds astonished by your smile and glance — make them your own devotees!' ||23.68||

children.text: idam ubhayatra ca yogyam |
children.translated_text: This is fitting in both [alternatives].

children.text: alakāvṛta-mukha kuṇḍala-dhṛta-sukha hasita-vibhūṣita-netra |
children.translated_text: 'O one whose face is veiled by curls, who bears the joy of earrings, whose eyes are adorned with smiles,

children.text: dattābhaya-bhuja-vakṣaḥ-śrī-yuja dāsyo vayam api te' tra ||JGc_1,23.69||
children.translated_text: who is united with the beauty of fear-dispelling arms and chest — we too are your maidservants here!' ||23.69||

children.text: atra cāpiḥ pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: Here too, 'even' is as before.

children.text: tava muralī-kalam api ca rūpa-balam anubhūyābhavad eva |
children.translated_text: 'Having experienced even the melodious power of your flute and the power of your beauty — indeed!

children.text: druma-kulam api pulakāṅkura-saṅkulam iha kā nārī deva ||JGc_1,23.70||
children.translated_text: Even the tree-families are bristling with horripilation — what woman then, O Lord?' ||23.70||

children.text: atra keti kaumutye niṣedhe vā-
children.translated_text: Here, 'what' is either in the sense of 'every' or of denial —

children.text: vyaktaṃ vraja-bhaya-hara-līlā-caya devas tvam asi sa ko' pi |
children.translated_text: 'Clearly, O one of sport-sequences that remove the fear of <s>Vraja</s>, you are that certain god!

children.text: tan no nija-karam api śirasi ca dhara dāsīnāṃ bhramato' pi ||JGc_1,23.71||
children.translated_text: Therefore, place even your own hand upon the heads of us, your maidservants, even though we wander!' ||23.71||

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite-
children.translated_text: Thus, things being so:

children.text: tathā vilāpa-tāpena na tāsāṃ vivyathe hariḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> was not distressed by the burning of their lament

children.text: yathā rādhā preṅkhita-bhrū-dhanur iṅkhi-dṛg-āśugaiḥ ||JGc_1,23.72||
children.translated_text: as much as [he was] by <s>Rādhā</s>'s swaying-brow-bow and its trembling-glance-arrows! ||23.72||

children.text: atha vyathita-mānasaḥ prathita-bhāva-kāruṇyataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, his mind distressed, from the compassion of his manifest sentiment,

children.text: prahasya muditānanaḥ svaka-rahasyam ullāsayan |
children.translated_text: laughing, with a joyful face, revealing his own secret,

children.text: pratisvam anayat priyā druta-matiḥ sva-pārśvaṃ balī
children.translated_text: the mighty one, with swift resolve, drew each beloved to his own side —

children.text: balād api balānujo valayati sma līlāṃ prati ||JGc_1,23.73||
children.translated_text: the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) powerfully enclosed [them] in his sport! ||23.73||

children.text:
āmṛśann aṅgulīḥ pāṇiṃ prakoṣṭhaṃ bāhum apy atha |
tāsāṃ hari-karas tṛptiṃ nāgāndhanam ivādhanaḥ ||JGc_1,23.74||yad api ca rādhā tāsu svam abhijugopāyutādi-saṅkhyāsu |
tad api ca hariṇā spaṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭā tārāsu candralekheva ||JGc_1,23.75||rādhā yarhi svakara-spṛṣṭā jātā murārāteḥ |
ativismitaye jajñe tarhi ca sā tatra candralekheva ||JGc_1,23.76||
children.translated_text: then she appeared there, causing supreme wonder, like a crescent moon! ||23.76||

Touching their fingers, then their hands, then their forearms, then their arms —
<s>Hari's</s> hand did not attain satisfaction with them, like an elephant not sated with perfume! ||23.74||
And although <s>Rādhā</s> concealed herself among those [gopīs] numbering ten thousand and more,
nevertheless, she was clearly seen by <s>Hari</s>, like a crescent moon among the stars! ||23.75||
When <s>Rādhā</s> was touched by the hand of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>,

children.text: gopyaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ tatra kṛṣṇaś ca rādhām
children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s> [embraced] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> there, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [embraced] <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: āśliṣoccair āvrajan narma-śarma |
children.translated_text: embracing loudly, approaching the joy of amorous play —

children.text: bhāva-śreṇyaḥ sthāyi-bhāvaṃ svabhāvo
children.translated_text: the series of sentiments [approached] the permanent mood, by their own nature,

children.text: yadvat puṇyād vāsanāṃ pūrva-labdhām ||JGc_1,23.77||
children.translated_text: just as merit [approaches] the previously obtained impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>)! ||23.77||

children.text: tatra kāścid bhūrur iva nibhālya vana-mālyaḥ parīhāsataḥ parasparam ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: There, some, beholding the forest garland [on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] as if [beholding] the earth, said to one another in jest:

children.text: jalade vilasati vidyud bibhyati hṛdayāni bhīrūṇām |
children.translated_text: 'In the rain-cloud, lightning flashes — the hearts of the timid tremble!

children.text: kiṃ parihasasi sakhi tvaṃ kiṃ na hi paśyasi puraś citram ||JGc_1,23.78||
children.translated_text: Why do you jest, O friend? Do you not see the wonder before [you]?' ||23.78||

children.text: ātmārāmā apy aho yasya gandhād
children.translated_text: 'He whose fragrance alone — alas! — even though those who delight in the Self,

children.text: brahmānandaṃ bāḍham āccādayanti |
children.translated_text: thoroughly overshadows the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: pūrṇānandaḥ sa svayaṃ hanta tābhiḥ
children.translated_text: He, full bliss himself — alas! — with those [gopīs]

children.text: svānandāya krīḍanāya prayete ||JGc_1,23.79||
children.translated_text: proceeds for his own bliss, for sport!' ||23.79||

children.text: atha samāpanam-
children.translated_text: Now, the conclusion:

children.text: īdṛg apyayi rādhe yas tāsāṃ mukha-nirīkṣakaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>! He who was thus the beholder of their faces

children.text: tvad-utkarṣa-rasāyāsīd iva tāsu parīkṣakaḥ ||JGc_1,23.80||
children.translated_text: became, as it were, through the <s>rasa</s> of your supremacy, an examiner among them!' ||23.80||

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
prathama-saṅga-raṅgaja-vāko-vākya-bhaṅgī-saṅgītaṃ nāma
trayoviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
 ||23||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the twenty-third <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
"A Composition of Dialogue-Patterns Born from the Delight of the First Meeting"
||23||

children.text: atha caturviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the twenty-fourth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter)

children.text: śrī-rādhā-saubhāgya-śravaṇa-subhāgyaṃ nāma
children.translated_text: Named "The Good Fortune of Hearing about Śrī <s>Rādhā's</s> Supreme Good Fortune"

children.text: tataḥ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text: atha saṅkṣepeṇa varṇitaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Now, it was narrated in brief, as follows:

children.text:
tābhiḥ sametābhir udāraceṣṭitaḥ
priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir acyutaḥ |
udāra-hāsa-dvija-kunda-dīdhitir
vyorocataiṇāṅka ivoḍubhir vṛtaḥ ||[BhP 10.29.43] iti |
children.translated_text: shone like the moon surrounded by stars!' ||[BhP 10.29.43]||

'With those [gopīs] assembled, of noble conduct,
their faces blossoming from the beloved's glance — <s>Acyuta</s>,
with the radiance of jasmine-white teeth in his noble laughter,

children.text: tatra prathama-caraṇaḥ śloka-sātkriyayālaṅkriyayā paricaryate-
children.translated_text: There, the first quarter [of the verse] is attended to with the service of verse-embellishment:

children.text:
kāntasya tābhiḥ sva-karaṃ spṛśan karaḥ
sarpan paraṃ cāvayavaṃ vitarkitaḥ |
kīrṇaś ca tasyāntaram antaraṃ bhajan[*5]
dṛṣṭaḥ punas taj jitakāśitāṃ gataḥ ||JGc_1,24.1|| [indravaṃśā]
[*5] vrajan (gha)
children.translated_text:
'The hand of the beloved, touching his own hand with theirs,
creeping further, was considered [to have reached] another limb;
and it, scattered, seeking the inner space within —
was seen again and attained the state of having conquered radiance!' ||24.1|| [<s>indravaṃśā</s>]

children.text: atha dvitīya-caraṇaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, the second quarter:

children.text:
priyaṃ niyutaśo' py amūr na hi vilokamānāḥ samaṃ
nimeṣam upasedire yad iyam eva divyā sthitiḥ |
priyeṇa nijam arpitaṃ yad avaloka-śuddhāmṛtaṃ
samaṃ bubhujire pṛthak tad adhikaṃ tu kiṃ varṇyatām? ||JGc_1,24.2|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
'These [gopīs], though beholding their beloved ten-thousand-fold, did not equally
approach even a blink — for this itself is the divine state!
The nectar of pure glances offered by the beloved to his own —
they enjoyed together and separately; but what more of the surpassing [experience] — let it be described?' ||24.2|| [<s>pṛthvī</s>]

children.text: atha siṃhāvaloka-nyāyād dvitīya-tṛtīya-caraṇau ca, yathā-
children.translated_text: Now, by the principle of the lion's backward glance, the second and third quarters also, as follows:

children.text:
yathā dṛśāṃ diśi diśi tā dadhur muhus
tathā haris tad-abhimukhaṃ dadhe dṛśam |
yadānvabhūd arahita-cāturakṣyatā
tadāhasīt sphuṭam asakṛt kṛta-kramam ||JGc_1,24.3|| [rucirā*]
children.translated_text:
As they placed their gazes in every direction, again and again,
so <s>Hari</s> directed his gaze toward them;
when an unchecked state of playful glancing occurred,
he laughed openly, and repeatedly, in measured sequence! ||24.3|| [<s>rucirā</s>]

children.text:
tadvad uttarārdhaṃ ca-
kavibhiḥ kṛṣṇe śaśitā tāsu ca nakṣatratā kavitā |
kintu smita-mukha-dīvyad-vilasita-vṛndair amī varitāḥ ||JGc_1,24.4|| [anuṣṭubh]

tataś ca nānā-narma-karmaṭhatayā haṭhavattayā ca kṛṣṇena kiṃcid asaṃkoce viracite, prāyaśaḥ sarvāvayave cāvalocite, nicolādi-viparyaye ca paricite sāsraṃ bahu vihasya tad iha sarvam eva yathāvat paryācitam ācere |
children.translated_text: Then, through various playful mischief, done with persistence, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had contrived some shamelessness, and had observed nearly every limb, and had become acquainted with the reversal of garments and such, they, laughing greatly with tears, properly observed all of that here as well.

children.text: tad evam ācārya sasukham udaṅ-mukha-gati-caryayā yamunā-tīra-vana-śreṇīṃ śobhayann eṇīdṛśas tāḥ sva-kāntibhir ācakarṣa, [9] yatra labdha-harṣaś candramasam api nija-dakṣiṇataḥ samākarṣann iva saṅgitayāṅgīcakāra | [10] tad anu ca sarvābhir arvācīna-yauvanābhis tam ekam anusarantībhir ata eva parasparaṃ saṅgam apariharantībhir, ata eva sahasānupalabdhānurahasa-kaṇikābhir, ata eva tan-milana-viśeṣāya kalita-purūtkalikābhiḥ saha, sa haris tādṛśatām eva parāmṛśati sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, having conducted [themselves] happily, adorning the row of forests along the <s>Yamunā</s> bank with their northward movement, those doe-eyed ones he attracted with his own radiances. [9] There, having gained delight, as if drawing the moon itself to his right, he accepted [it] with song. [10] And then, with all of them — of fresh youth — following him alone, and therefore not avoiding contact with one another, and therefore suddenly finding no fragment of privacy, and therefore having fashioned great eagerness for a special meeting with him — with them, that <s>Hari</s> contemplated this very condition:

children.text: athānyathānupapattyā saṅgānasukham evāvalambamānaḥ kevalaṃ cañcac-cañcarīka-lulita-lalita-sukumāra-kusumāñcitaṃ vanam evāyaṃ sarva-guṇa-śālī vanamālī cañcati sma | kintu,
children.translated_text: Then, since the impossibility of otherwise [proceeding] made him embrace only the un-pleasure of [collective] association, this garland-wearer, possessed of all virtues, merely wandered through the forest adorned with delicate, tender flowers stirred by buzzing bees. But—

children.text:
saṅgānaṃ tad idaṃ paraspara-guṇa-grāmānubhūtiḥ svataḥ
śarmāpy atra manorathāntara-kṛteḥ śaśvad babhūvāspadam |
yatrāliṅgana-cumbanādi-vidhaye tāsāṃ harer apy adaḥ
saukhyaṃ lakṣyam abhūt parāvṛti-vidhāṃ cāveśitā nirmame ||JGc_1,24.5|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
This collective association — the mutual experience of each other's host of qualities —
independently became a ground even for happiness, [yet also] perpetually for other desires;
wherein, for the performance of embracing, kissing, and such, for those [gopīs] and for <s>Hari</s> too,
that bliss was the aim — and he devised methods of turning away [from the group]! ||24.5|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: tad etad varṇitaṃ yathā śrī-bādarāyaṇinā-
children.translated_text: This has been described by Śrī <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (<s>Śuka</s>) as follows:

children.text: upagīyamāna udgāyan vanitā-śata-yūthapaḥ |
mālāṃ bibhrad vaijayantīṃ vyacaran maṇḍayan vanam ||[BhP 10.29.44] iti |
children.translated_text: wearing the <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland, he wandered about, adorning the forest. ||[BhP 10.29.44]||
Being sung to, [and himself] singing, the leader of hundreds of women,

children.text: gāne viśeṣaś ca śrī-parāśareṇa-
children.translated_text: And the special detail about the singing, by Śrī <s>Parāśara</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ śarac-candramasaṃ kaumudīṃ kumudākaram |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> sang of the autumn moon, the moonlight, and the bed of night-lotuses;

children.text: jagau gopī-janas tv ekaṃ kṛṣṇa-nāma punaḥ punaḥ ||[ViP 5.13.52]
children.translated_text: but the company of <s>gopīs</s> [sang] only the one name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, again and again! ||[ViP 5.13.52]||

children.text: vidhur ayam āgatavān śaradaṃ prati samprati |
children.translated_text: "This moon has come now toward the autumn;

children.text: itavān vidhur atha nahi bhavatīḥ prati |
children.translated_text: the moon has gone, but not toward you!

children.text: mādhava jaya gokula-vīra jaya jaya kṛṣṇa hare ||a||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, victory! O hero of <s>Gokula</s>, victory! Victory, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Hari</s>!" ||a||

children.text: kumudākara-calanaṃ na bhaved iti seyaṃ |
children.translated_text: "That the bed of night-lotuses should not be disturbed — this is why

children.text: kaumudikāgād idam unneyam |
children.translated_text: the moonlight has come here — this should be inferred!

children.text: keśava jaya hārda-śarīra jaya jaya kṛṣṇa hare ||b||
children.translated_text: O <s>Keśava</s>, victory! O embodiment of the heart, victory! Victory, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Hari</s>!" ||b||

children.text: kusuma-vanī madhupair iyam añcati kāntim |
children.translated_text: "This flower-garden shimmers with bees in beauty;

children.text: mama bhavatīṣu prathayatu kāntim |
children.translated_text: may it spread beauty among you!

children.text: śyāmala jaya hārda-samīra jaya jaya kṛṣṇa hare ||c||
children.translated_text: O dark one (<s>Śyāmala</s>), victory! O breeze of the heart, victory! Victory, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Hari</s>!" ||c||

children.text:
puṣpita-kuñja-caye vṛndācita-śobhā |
bhavad-anugataye kila kṛta-lobhā |
mohana jaya saṃvidi dhīra jaya jaya kṛṣṇa hare ||JGc_1,24.6|| [daśāvatārastotra]
children.translated_text:
"In the cluster of flowering bowers, the beauty adorned by <s>Vṛndā</s> (the forest) —
it has indeed become covetous for following you!
O enchanter (<s>Mohana</s>), victory! O one steadfast in awareness, victory! Victory, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Hari</s>!" ||24.6|| [<s>daśāvatārastotra</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ gāyate priyāya pratigṛṇatīṣu tāsu nava-yuvatīṣu punaḥ śrī-śuka-vacanāti-rahasyaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, as those young maidens sang responsively to their beloved, [there follows] the deeply secret statement of Śrī <s>Śuka</s>, as follows:

children.text: nadyāḥ pulinam āviśya gopībhir hima-vālukam |
children.translated_text: Having entered the sandy bank of the river, with the <s>gopīs</s>, [a bank] of cool sand,

children.text: juṣṭaṃ[*6] tat-taralānandi-kumudāmoda-vāyunā ||
children.translated_text: delightful with the fragrance-bearing breeze of night-lotuses, whose shimmering brought joy—
Variant: "reme" (sported), <s>Vallabha</s>, <s>Gītā</s> press

children.text: reme, vallabha, gītā press

bāhu-prasāra-parirambha-karālakoru-
nīvī-stanālabhana-narma-nakhāgra-pātaiḥ |
kṣvelyāvaloka-hasitair vraja-sundarīṇām
uttambhayan rati-patiṃ ramayāñcakāra ||[BhP 10.29.45-6] iti |
children.translated_text:
through amorous glances, laughter — of the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>,
arousing the lord of love (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), he sported [with them]! ||[BhP 10.29.45-46]||

through arm-extensions for embracing, through [touches of] hands, locks of hair, thighs,
waist-knots, and breasts, through playful nail-tip scratches,

children.text: tad etad, yathā-tad evaṃ bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ jāta-prasare' py alabdhāvasare sa-tṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇa-sahita-mahita-mahilāvisare' bhilaṣita-vilasitāya viralatā na jātā |
children.translated_text: That is to say — thus, wandering and wandering, though the spread [of desire] had arisen, yet no opportunity being found, in the venerable assembly of women accompanied by the longing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, no scarcity arose for the desired sport.

children.text: ajātāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ kṛṣṇayā taraṅga-kara-nikara-citam aharahar avakalitaṃ pulina-viśeṣam eva tad-ucitaṃ prabalam avakalayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And when that [scarcity] had not arisen, he powerfully discerned that particular sandy bank — daily noted by <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) through the multitude of her wave-like hand-gestures — as suitable for that [sport].

children.text: balānujanmā yaḥ khalu hima-bālukeva bālukā yasmiṃs tādṛśa iti parama-śubhra-śubhra-guṇatayā vibhrājate sma |
children.translated_text: He who was born after <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), [at a place] where the sand was like cool sand — it shone with the quality of supreme whiteness and purity.

children.text: yatraiva ca tādṛśa-sarva-guṇa-pūrṇa-pūrṇimā-nija-dvija-rāja-virājamāna-suṣamāsuṣama-pratisaṅkrama-para-bhāga-jāgarūka-mahā-mahasā sahasā nayanāni nābhyudaya-dayanāni bhavanti sma |
children.translated_text: And there, the splendor of the full moon of that very <s>pūrṇimā</s> (full moon night) — full of all such qualities — resplendent with the beauty of its own prince of the twice-born (the moon), with the great brilliance that was alert to the far shore of the most exquisite transition — suddenly, the eyes became [sources of] not-just-rise-but-compassion.

children.text: yatraiva ca tūlikāvad anukūlikā bālukā vastra-mātram āstaraṇam apekṣate sma; yatraiva ca kalinda-tanayā svayaṃ valita-sakhīnayā saugandhika-sugandha-gandhavāha-vahanādinā sevāṃ vahati sma |
children.translated_text: And there, the sand, favorable like a pillow, required only a garment as a bed-covering; and there, the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) herself, with the gait of an attendant friend, performed service through carrying fragrant breezes of sweet-scented <s>saugandhika</s> lotuses and such.

children.text: tatra cātra śrī-keśavaḥ praveśam anubhūya pratipreyasy api yugmībhūya bāhu-prasārādi-līlāṃ śīlayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And there, Śrī <s>Keśava</s>, having entered, with each beloved pairing up, practiced the sport of arm-extension and the like.

children.text: sā ceyaṃ paramarahasyeti rahasy eva kiñcid vyasyate |
children.translated_text: And this, being supremely secret, is disclosed only a little, in secrecy.

children.text: yathā mithas tat tan mithunam-
children.translated_text: As each couple mutually [interacted]:

children.text:
bāhu-prasāram akarot parirambhaṇāya
bāhū tu tat-karaṇatāṃ ciram īyatur na |
yo yasya naiti vaśatāṃ sa kathaṃ nu tasya
prāpnotu sādhakatama-sthitim añjasaiva? ||JGc_1,24.7|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
He extended his arms for embracing,
but the arms did not long attain the state of performing that!
What does not come under one's control — how can it
achieve the most effective state straightforwardly? ||24.7|| [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text:
kṛtaṃ ca parirambhanaṃ na parihartum īśāv amū
babhūvatur aghāri-tat-priya-vadhū-janāv ātmanā |
kathañcid api vīrudhā bhavati cet taroḥ saṃgamas
tayoḥ katham apṛktatā svayam anīhayor jāyatām? ||JGc_1,24.8|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
The embrace was made — these two, the foe of sin (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and that dear bride, were unable
to release [it] of their own accord.
If even a creeper's union with a tree occurs somehow,
how could the separation of those two, themselves unwilling, come about? ||24.8|| [<s>pṛthvī</s>]

children.text:
sakhīnām apy āsyā-rahita-samaye yat praṇayinoḥ
parīrambhārambhāt prabala-sukha-mūrcchā samajani |
tayos tāṃ vicchetuṃ param ahaha nānā-vilasita-
pratīkṣā supteva svayam atha jajāgāra paritaḥ ||JGc_1,24.9|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
Even in the absence of the friends' faces, when from the beginning of the lovers' embrace
a powerful swoon of bliss arose —
to sever it from them, alas, the anticipation of various sports,
as if asleep, then awoke all around! ||24.9|| [<s>śikhariṇī</s>]

children.text:
tataś ca-
rahasi saṅkucatī punar apy asau
nija-kareṇa harer akirat karam |
vyathitatām iva tāṃ tu vivṛṇvatīṃ
tad anumṛṣṭi-miṣād ayam aspṛśat ||JGc_1,24.10|| [drutavilambitā]
children.translated_text:
Then:
She, shrinking again in private,
scattered his hand with her own hand;
but as she revealed, as it were, her pain,
he touched her under the pretext of wiping [her tears]! ||24.10|| [<s>drutavilambitā</s>]

children.text:
vadanaṃ tava vṛṇvate bata
bhramarā nānugatāsti kācana |
iti lālayati sma sa cchalād
alakānāṃ tatim apy amūm anu ||JGc_1,24.11|| [viyoginī]
children.translated_text:
"Bees are covering your face — alas,
there is no one following [to shoo them away]!"
Thus, under a pretext, he caressed
that row of her hair-locks! ||24.11|| [<s>viyoginī</s>]

children.text:
uru-sparśe niraste' pi nīvīm aspṛkṣad acyutaḥ |
niḥśaṅkayācakānāṃ hi tathācaritam īkṣyate ||JGc_1,24.12|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Even when the touch of thighs was repelled, <s>Acyuta</s> touched her waist-knot;
for such is the observed conduct of those who beg without apprehension! ||24.12|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
kalayati saṃvastrayati
saṃhastayate sma tasya yā rāmā |
praṇayī sa haris tasyāḥ
spṛśati ca colīṃ vitūstanavyājāt ||JGc_1,24.13|| [gīti]
children.translated_text:
She who was fashioning the garments, arranging them,
and adjusting the hands of that one — his beloved —
that loving <s>Hari</s>, her [lover],
touched her bodice too, under the pretext of loosening! ||24.13|| [<s>gīti</s>]

children.text:
vakṣas te kim api nirīkṣyate praphullaṃ
sparśaṃ cāṇv api sahate calākṣi yan na |
tasmān man-nakha-nakharañjanī-spṛg eva
syān nīruk tad iti harir jahāsa cātra ||JGc_1,24.14|| [praharṣiṇī][*7]
[*7] This verse does not appear in ca, gha.
children.translated_text:
"Your chest appears somehow in full bloom,
yet it cannot bear even the slightest touch, O restless-eyed one!
Therefore, only the touch of my nail — a [healing] lac-dye —
would be painless for it!" — thus <s>Hari</s> laughed here! ||24.14|| [<s>praharṣiṇī</s>]
[This verse does not appear in manuscripts ca, gha.]

children.text:
madhusūdanatāṃ mukhāmbuje
haritāṃ hṛd-bhava-kumbhi-kumbhayoḥ |
gatavān bata nandajaḥ kathaṃ
rati-nātha-prabhavāya nārhati ||JGc_1,24.15|| [viyoginī]
children.translated_text:
How can the son of <s>Nanda</s>, who has attained
the state of a bee-slayer (<s>Madhusūdana</s>) upon the lotus-face,
and greenness upon the pot-like frontal globes of the elephant of heart-born [Love],
not be conducive to the arising of the lord of love (<s>Rati-nātha</s>)? ||24.15|| [<s>viyoginī</s>]

children.text:
atha yat kathanīyatocitaṃ
kathitaṃ tat prathitaṃ ca kiñcana |
yad athākathitaṃ dvi-karmakaṃ
smṛti-rītyā tad avehi pāṇineḥ ||JGc_1,24.16|| [viyoginī]
ity evaṃ sthite-
children.translated_text: Thus, in this situation:

children.text:
gopyas tāḥ pratipadya sarva-viṣaya-śreyāṃsam ātma-priyaṃ
svādhīnaṃ sapadi pratisvam asakṛt tatrātigarvaṃ dadhuḥ |
lokaś ced bahu-rāja-rāṣṭra-vasatir jaṅganti bhaṅgaṃ tadā
tasyāntar-hitatā hiteti kila so' py antardadhe mādhavaḥ ||JGc_1,24.17|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Those <s>gopīs</s>, having obtained the beloved of the self, superior to all [worldly] objects,
under their own power, at once, each individually, assumed excessive pride there.
If a realm with many kings and territories begins to crumble,
then its hidden-ness is beneficial — and so that <s>Mādhava</s> too disappeared! ||24.17|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: tena ca vicāritaṃ khalv idaṃ-ahaha, mama paramam uddeśyam eva vismṛta-deśyam abhūt, yataḥ sarvābhir eva nirviśeṣaṃ ramamāṇe mayi ramā-śiromaṇīyamānā rādhāpi sādhāraṇatāṃ gatā |
children.translated_text: And he reflected thus: "Alas, my supreme objective itself has become forgotten-territory, since, as I sported with all of them equally, <s>Rādhā</s> too — who is the crest-jewel of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — has become [merely] ordinary!

children.text: kiṃ ca, sva-manoratha-prathanāyāṃ rādhāyāḥ prathamā prathamānā-gamanatā samprati pratipannā, tasmān mahā-maha eva mama hitāya mahīyate | sa ca śāradatā-viśāradatāyām asyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ rāsa-rasa eva tūrṇaṃ pūrṇatām arhati | eṣa tu sarvāsām aikamatya-pratipatty-anusārata eva sāratām prasārayati | aikyamataṃ ca pratyekaṃ sābhimānāntarāsu parāsu kiñcin mad-udāsīnatā-paraṃ dāsī-kartum āsīdati | tasmād aśeṣa-guṇādhikāṃ rādhikām ādāya tirodhāya sthāsyāmi iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, for the fulfillment of her own desire, <s>Rādhā</s>'s primacy — the state of being foremost — has now been established; therefore, the great festival itself magnifies my welfare. And that [festival], in the expertise of the autumnal season, on this full-moon night, deserves to be quickly brought to fullness as the <s>rāsa-rasa</s> (the aesthetic essence of the circular dance). But this [rāsa] extends its essence only in accordance with the unanimous agreement of all. And unanimous agreement, among the others who individually harbor pride within, nearly succeeds in rendering [them] servants through a certain indifference from me. Therefore, taking <s>Rādhikā</s>, who surpasses all in every quality, I shall disappear and remain [with her alone]!"

children.text: tad etad vibhāvya bhāvyam arthaṃ sādhayan, mādhavas tatra tatrālasa-kara-caraṇādi-kriyāṃ priyāṃ priyāṃ praty uvāca-nūnaṃ vañcita-kāñcī-dhvanitayā kayācid apy atra sthīyata iti nāsthīyate | tac ca mama bhavad-ekānucāri-vihāritayā vicāritīkriyate | tasmād atyāyāsavatyā bhavatyā sthīyatām | mayā tu samayā mṛgayamāṇatāṃ nirmāya nātisamaya-virāmam āgamanīyam |
children.translated_text: Having thus envisioned the purpose to be achieved, <s>Mādhava</s>, accomplishing it, said to each beloved with languid movements of hands, feet, and such: "Surely, since the jingling of someone's girdle-bells has been silenced, it is not possible for anyone to remain here. And that is pondered by me through my sporting, which follows you alone. Therefore, you, being excessively fatigued, must stay here; but I, having fashioned the state of searching [for her], shall return before long."

children.text: tad etad abhidhāya, tatas tataḥ sarvataś cāntardhāya rādhayā saha sahasā jagāma |
children.translated_text: Having said this, disappearing from everywhere and in every direction, he swiftly departed with <s>Rādhā</s>.

children.text:
atha samaya-katipaya-vyatyayam asahamānā sā sā ca tatas tata utthāya prasthāya ca tam anvicchantīti bhramaṇāt kramaśaḥ eka-dvāditayā paramparaṃ militāḥ | militāś ca tāḥ paramparam apratītitaḥ śapathaṃ prathamānāḥ kṛṣṇa-patham evānveṣayāmāsuḥ | kintu-
anveṣṭuṃ kṛṣṇam iṣṭaṃ nikaṭam abhigataṃ cintayitvā pradūnāḥ
kartuṃ tan naiva śekuḥ param ahaha gatāḥ klāntim etā nipetuḥ |
sthitvā tadvac cirāya sphuraṇa-mayam amuṃ prāpya sarvāḥ samantān
matvānyo' nyaṃ tam eva pratihata-matayaś cakrur āliṅganādi ||JGc_1,24.18|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
Then, unable to endure the passing of even a few moments, each and every one, rising from here and there, setting forth, and seeking him — from their wandering, gradually, in ones and twos, they met one another in succession. And having met, distrusting each other in turn, taking oaths, they searched only for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s path. But—
Seeking the beloved <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having reflected that he had come near, [they were] greatly distressed;
they were unable to do so — alas, having reached exhaustion, they fell!
Having remained thus for long, attaining a flash [of awareness], all of them, from every side,
deeming one another to be him, with bewildered minds, performed embraces and such! ||24.18|| [<s>sragdharā</s>]

children.text:
tataś ca-
yās tu tṛṣṇākulatayā kṛṣṇa-bhāva-vaśaṃ gatāḥ |
kṛṣṇāyante sma tā eva sarva-pālakatām itāḥ ||JGc_1,24.19|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Then:
Those who, out of agitation born of longing, had come under the sway of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>bhāva</s> (absorption in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) —
they themselves, having attained the state of protecting all, enacted <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! ||24.19|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: atha kathañcid anusaṃhita-bahirarthāḥ samayaṃ gamayitum asamarthāḥ pūrvābhyāsa-vaśān nija-rakṣāyā vaśān nikhila-sukhada-śīlāṃ bālyādi-katal-līlāṃ gātum ārabdhās tad-āveśa-parirabdhā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having somehow regained awareness of external things, unable to pass the time, from the force of prior practice, [and] from the power of their own protection, they began to sing the auspicious deeds of the one who gives happiness to all — the sports from childhood onward — and became embraced by absorption in him.

children.text: tatra ca kṛṣṇam anvicchantyas tata ito gacchantyas taru-vallī-pallīm api muhur api pṛcchanti sma, unmāda-vṛtter anuvṛtteḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: And there, while searching for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, going here and there, they repeatedly asked even the trees, creepers, and villages — because of the continuation of their mad state — as follows:

children.text:
līlā gāyaṃs tat-tad-āveśa-vaśyas
tat-tad-bhāvaṃ prāpa gopī-nikāyaḥ |
citraṃ kṛṣṇāveśitām āpa yā yā
gaurāṅgī sā kṛṣṇa-varṇā pratītā ||JGc_1,24.20|| [śālinī]
adyāpi smṛtam uttapaty ahaha mac-cittaṃ yad etā muhuḥ
pṛcchanti sma hariṃ viyoga-vidhurā hā hā tarūn apy aho |
āstāṃ tan mama hṛdy aruntudam idaṃ gītābhir etat-kṛte
ghorād bhītibhir unmadiṣṇu-hṛdayā ghorānukāraṃ dadhuḥ ||JGc_1,24.21|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
Singing his pastimes, overcome by various states of absorption,
the host of <s>gopīs</s> attained each corresponding emotion;
wondrous — whichever fair-limbed one was possessed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s presence,
she was perceived as having become dark-complexioned (<s>kṛṣṇa-varṇā</s>)! ||24.20|| [śālinī]
Even now, the memory scorches my heart — alas! — that they
repeatedly asked about <s>Hari</s>, distraught with separation — ah, ah! — even of the trees!
Let that be — this is what lacerates my heart: through their songs on his account,
with hearts maddened by fear of the terrible, they produced imitations of the terrible! ||24.21|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: tadīdṛśalīlāveśaḥ paraparagacchapṛcchābhiniveśataḥ kramaśaḥ pracita-niṣkramīkṛtim avāpa, yat pṛcchābhiniveśaś caivam apagacchati sma, yathā-
children.translated_text: This absorption in his pastimes, through the intensity of questioning each one they encountered, gradually attained a state of accumulated departure, as the intensity of questioning also subsided thus:

children.text:
kāṃścit vikāsi-kusumair upahāsa-bhāvān
kāṃścin natāgra-valanair vimukhī-kṛtāsyān |
kāṃścin madāli-virutai rūṣitokti-yuktān
matvā tarūṃs tad anuyoga-rasād viremuḥ ||JGc_1,24.22|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
Regarding some [trees] with blossoming flowers as expressing mockery,
some with drooping, bent tips as having turned their faces away,
some with the cries of intoxicated bees as uttering harsh words —
thus perceiving the trees, they desisted from the relish of interrogation! ||24.22|| [vasantatilakā]

children.text: tataś ca kṣitim eva praśna-lakṣitī-kṛtavatyaḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: And then they made the earth itself the target of their inquiry, as follows:

children.text:
aho kim akaros tapaḥ kiyad ihorvi yac chrī-hareḥ
pada-spṛg anu vindase pulaka-rūpa-nānāṅkurān |
trivikramaja-vikramāt kim iva tat tvayā sambhṛtaṃ
varāha-parirambhataḥ kim athavā kvacit kintu na ||JGc_1,24.23|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
'O earth! What austerity did you perform, and how much, that from the touch of the glorious <s>Hari's</s> feet
you obtain sprouts in the form of horripilation?
Was that [merit] accumulated by you from the stride of <s>Trivikrama</s> (<s>Vāmana</s>),
or perhaps from the embrace of <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar) — or somewhere else — but surely yes!' ||24.23|| [pṛthvī]

children.text:
pṛthvī kṣamā ca nāmnā tvaṃ tat-padāṅkam udaṅkitā |
tasmāt tvām eva taṃ praṣṭuṃ tā vayaṃ gatim āgatāḥ ||JGc_1,24.24|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'O earth, you are by name <s>Kṣamā</s> (forbearance), and you are marked with the imprint of his feet;
therefore, to ask about him, we have come to you as our [last] recourse!' ||24.24|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ sarvāsu tarv-ādikaṃ pṛcchantīṣu tata itaś ca gacchantīṣu tadīyaṃ saurabhyaṃ parirabhya, jagat-prāṇeṣu sannidhānaṃ prati praṇīta-prayāṇeṣu, tad-vaidagdhī-digdha-snigdha-hṛdayā rādhā-sakhī-samudayā hariṇīṃ prati kṛta-praṇayāḥ sānumodatayā hāri vyāharanti sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, when all of them were questioning the trees and such, and were going hither and thither, having embraced his fragrance — when the world's life-breaths had set forth toward his proximity — <s>Rādhā's</s> company of friends, their hearts tender and anointed by his charm, having affectionately addressed a doe, spoke delightfully with approbation:

children.text: apy eṇapatny upagataḥ priyayeha gātrais
children.translated_text: 'O doe-wife, has <s>Acyuta</s> come here,

children.text: tanvan dṛśāṃ sakhi sunirvṛtim acyuto vaḥ |
children.translated_text: with his beloved, gladdening your eyes with his limbs, O friend?

children.text: kāntāṅga-saṅga-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ
children.translated_text: The fragrance of the <s>kunda</s>-garland of the lord of the clan wafts here —

children.text: kunda-srajaḥ kula-pater iha vāti gandhaḥ ||[BhP 10.30.11] [vasantatilaka]
children.translated_text: the garland colored by the <s>kuṅkuma</s> of the breast through the bodily embrace of his beloved!' ||[BhP 10.30.11] [vasantatilakā]

children.text: bāhuṃ priyāṃsa upadhāya gṛhīta-padmo
children.translated_text: 'Having placed his arm upon the shoulder of his beloved, holding a lotus,

children.text: rāmānujas tulasikāli-kulair madāndhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), followed by swarms of bees

children.text: anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṃ
children.translated_text: intoxicated by the <s>tulasī</s> — do the trees here

children.text: kiṃ vābhinandati caran praṇayāvalokaiḥ? ||[BhP 10.30.12] [vasantatilaka]
children.translated_text: return his loving glances with a bow, as he walks?' ||[BhP 10.30.12] [vasantatilakā]

children.text: atra khalu eṇeti patnīti sakhīti pada-trayeṇa-he praśasta-netre ! mādṛśa-mānuṣī-sadṛśa-vicāra-saṃcarita-vṛndāvana-kṣetre ! tat-tad-asmadīya-sukha-prakhyeṇa sukhena labdha-mad-vidha-sakhye ! iti vyajya sukha-rajya-māna-hṛdayāḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: Here indeed, by the three words '<s>eṇa</s>' (doe), '<s>patnī</s>' (wife), and '<s>sakhī</s>' (friend), [they imply]: 'O one of excellent eyes! [You,] in the field of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, where contemplation like ours — like that of human women — courses! Having attained friendship like mine through a happiness resembling our own such-and-such happiness!' — thus, with hearts thrilling with the joy of happiness, they spoke:

children.text:
priyayā samam acyutaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ śliṣṭatayā tasyāḥ sakāśād aviśliṣṭaḥ sann adasīya-śobhā-kṛtāsaṅgair aṅgair yuṣmākaṃ tādṛśāṃ dṛśāṃ kevala-sva-darśanajānandād apy atiśayitam ānandam utkarṣayan kiṃ yuṣmat-samīpam āpa? tatra tan-mithuna-ślāghā-garbha-vacanena hetuṃ racayanti kānta iti | gokula-rāja-kula-tilakasya yā kunda-mālā, tasyāḥ kutrāpy alabhya-saurabhyam iha tad-bhāra-milaj-java-bhaṅga-nibha-vāyu-saṅgataḥ prasarati | kīdṛśyāḥ? mālāyāḥ kāntā-parama-puṇyena parama-sarva-sādguṇyena tasyāpi lālasasya yā paramāspada-rūpā, tasyā aṅga-saṅge kuca-kuṅkuma-paṅka-kula-saṅkulāyāḥ | ataḥ santata-paricaya-viśeṣeṇa tat-saurabhya-viśeṣaṃ parirabhya sphuṭam ābhis tathā samupalabhyata ity arthaḥ
|
children.translated_text: '<s>Acyuta</s>, glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, being inseparable from her — embraced by his beloved — did he come near you, with limbs creating an enchantment produced by her beauty, heightening a delight surpassing even the joy born of merely seeing himself alone, for the eyes of such ones as you?' There, through the statement containing the praise of that couple, they fashion the reason. 'The <s>kunda</s>-garland of the ornament of the royal clan of <s>Gokula</s> — its fragrance, unobtainable elsewhere, spreads here from the contact of the wind resembling the breaking of the rush of the weight of that [garland]. Of what sort? Of the garland that, through the bodily embrace of the beloved — the supreme abode of his desire, by virtue of the supreme excellence of all good qualities, which is the supreme merit of the beloved — is crowded with the mass of breast-<s>kuṅkuma</s> paste.' Thus, through the special intimacy of continuous familiarity, they clearly perceived that special fragrance — this is the meaning.

children.text: atha tāṃ tad-darśana-jātena harṣeṇa samprati tad-viyoga-jātena tarṣeṇa sthagita-vacanām āśaṅkya, tena ca tayoḥ saṅgamam eva niṣṭaṅkya, paramānandatas tadīya-vilāsa-viśeṣaṃ vandamānās, tatra pallavādi-bhara-namrāṇāṃ kamrāṇāṃ purūṇāṃ tarūṇām api tadīya-sauvidallādi-bhṛtya-viśeṣa-bhāvena tad-vandanam utprekṣya, priyayā saha vihāra-ratena tena teṣām abhinandanaṃ sandihānās, tayos tādṛśa-vilāsāveśātiśayam āha-bāhum iti |
children.translated_text: Now, suspecting that she [<s>Rādhā</s>] was silenced by the joy born of seeing his [footprints], and now also by the thirst born of separation from him, and thereby confirming the union of those two, worshipping with supreme joy the special grace of his sport — and there, imagining the bowing of the beautiful, abundant trees, bent with the weight of blossoms and such, to be their obeisance in the special capacity of his attendants — doubting whether he who delighted in sport with his beloved acknowledged them with loving glances — they spoke of the extraordinary intensity of the amorous absorption of those two: [the verse beginning with] '<s>bāhum</s>' ('arm').

children.text: atha tasyām udāsīnā vadanti sma-
children.translated_text: Now, those who were indifferent toward her [<s>Rādhā</s>] said:

children.text:
latā imāḥ pṛcchata yā na lokitāḥ
purā taru-śliṣṭatayāpi puṣpitāḥ |
sampraty amūḥ sparśa-vaśād bakī-ripoḥ
puṣpānvitās tan-nakha-citram atra hi ||JGc_1,24.25|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
'Ask these creepers, who were not previously seen
even in the embrace of a tree to have blossomed;
but now, from the touch of the enemy of <s>Bakī</s> (<s>Pūtanā</s>),
they bear flowers — therein the wonder is of his nails!' ||24.25|| [upajāti]

children.text: atha tasmāl labdhavismaye, punar akasmād akhilaśubhapadyāni tadīya-padanalinayor amalināni padāni dadhānā, vasudhā sudhām iva sudhāmāvaliṃ tāsām anyāsām api tadapratītispṛśi dṛśi kirati sma, yāni prekṣya cāmūbhir utprekṣyate sma-
children.translated_text: Then, from the wonder obtained from that, again, suddenly, the earth, bearing upon the immaculate feet of his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] foot-lotuses the immaculate footprints — [those prints] possessing all auspicious marks — scattered, as if nectar-like, a succession of nectar-streams, touching even the incredulous gaze of those other [<s>gopīs</s>]. Seeing these, they imagined thus:

children.text:
iyaṃ kṣitir muni-caritā tad-uttaraṃ
dade na hīty avamṛśatī punar dade |
dhvajāmbhjādy-upavalitāṅghri-lāñchana-
pradarśanād iva likhatī tad-āgamam ||JGc_1,24.26|| [rucirā*] ||
children.translated_text:
'This earth, marked by the conduct of sages, gave no [direct] answer to that [question],
yet reconsidering, she gave [one] again —
by displaying the foot-marks adorned with flag, lotus, and other signs,
as if inscribing his arrival!' ||24.26|| [rucirā]

children.text: kiyad-dūre tu tābhis tat-padāntarāṇy eva padāntarāṇi pratipannāni | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: At some distance, they perceived among his footprints other footprints. As follows:

children.text:
tad anu tasya padaṃ padam antarā
padam anīdṛśam ādadṛśe param |
anatam alpam amadhya-kṛśaṃ dhvajādy-
upacitiṃ viparītadiśi śritam ||JGc_1,24.27|| [drutavilambitā*]
children.translated_text:
'Then, among his footprints, step by step,
another footprint — unlike his — was seen:
unbent, small, not slender in the middle, bearing
the marks of flag and such in the opposite direction!' ||24.27|| [drutavilambitā]

children.text: tatra cedam anumīyate sma-
children.translated_text: And therein this was inferred:

children.text:
mṛgākṣyā lakṣyaṃ syād iha caraṇa-cihnaṃ hari-pada-
prasaktaṃ vaiśiṣṭyād api tu nahi pūrvatra kim api |
sphuṭaṃ tasmāt kāñcidd hṛdi vidadhad atrārpayad asau
prasiddhā stenānāṃ jagati hi hatāṅka-praśamitā ||JGc_1,24.28|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'The footprint that would be the target of the doe-eyed one here, attached to <s>Hari's</s> footprint —
from its distinctive quality, nothing like it [appears] anywhere before;
clearly, therefore, he placed some [woman] in his heart and set her down here —
famous [is the way] that in this world, the concealment of thieves is dispelled by the obliteration of marks!' ||24.28|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
asavya-savyau yūnor yat
padāṅkau vyatimardinau |
tat tarkyate mithaḥ spaṣṭam
aṃsa-nyasta-prakoṣṭhatā ||JGc_1,24.29|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'That the left and right footprints of the young pair
are mutually overlapping —
from that, it is clearly inferred
that [they walked with] forearms placed upon each other's shoulders!' ||24.29|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad evaṃ sādhāraṇīnāṃ varṇanam ākarṇya rādhā-sakhyaḥ punar ālapanti sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard the description by the ordinary [<s>gopīs</s>], <s>Rādhā's</s> friends spoke again:

children.text:
paraspara-karagra-sphurad-amanda-khelāspadaṃ
pramatta-kari-dampati-sthiti tayos tu yūnor yugam |
yad atra vijane vane vigata-śṛṅkhalaṃ līlayā
vidhāsyati paraṃ mahas tad atisuṣṭhu puṣṇāti naḥ ||JGc_1,24.30|| [pṛthvī]
children.translated_text:
'The pair of those two youths, like a pair of intoxicated elephants,
with play at the tips of each other's hands — radiant, unhurried —
whatever supreme splendor they shall create in this solitary forest,
free of all restraint, in sport — that nourishes us exceedingly well!' ||24.30|| [pṛthvī]

children.text: atha tatra suhṛdāṃ vacanam-
children.translated_text: Now, the words of the friends [from BhP]:

children.text: anayārādhito nūnaṃ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ |
yan no vihāya govindaḥ prīto yām anayad rahaḥ ||[BhP 10.30.28] iti |
children.translated_text: since, leaving us behind, <s>Govinda</s>, pleased, led her away in seclusion!' ||[BhP 10.30.28] Thus.
'Surely this one has been worshipped by her — the glorious Lord <s>Hari</s>, the Supreme Controller —

children.text: ayam arthaḥ: nūnam anayā param anayayā ko' py anaśvara-śaktir aṅgīkṛta-bhakta-bhaktir īśvara eva nirbādhitam ārādhitaḥ, na tu devatā-mātram | sa ca sakala-harit-pati-patiḥ śrī-harir eva, na ca haraḥ sṛṣṭi-karaś ca | haritāyām api sarvāvatāra-vistāravān svayaṃ bhagavān iti sambhāvitī-bhavati na cānyas tad-aṃśatayāpi labdha-praśaṃsaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is the meaning: 'Surely by her — by the supreme [lady] — some imperishable power, who has accepted the devotion of devotees, the Lord himself has been worshipped without obstruction — not a mere deity. And he is the lord of all lords of the directions — glorious <s>Hari</s> himself — and not <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) nor the creator (<s>Brahmā</s>). Even within the <s>Hari</s>-nature, the venerable one who possesses the expanse of all <s>avatāras</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself — it is fitting [to surmise thus] — and not another who has gained praise as merely a portion of him.'

children.text: tādṛśa-camatkāra-kāraṇam apy avatārayanti, yan naḥ iti | yāṃ khalu guṇa-rūpa-mahasā sahasā nikhila-hṛdayaṃ vindamānaḥ śrī-govindaḥ svayam ayaṃ nināya, na tu na iva na nināya | tat-paripāṭī ca praty-urasaṃ vidhāya prīti-rīti-parītatayā kṛtā, na tu tad-viparītatayā | prītir api smara-mahaḥ-pravaha-rahaḥ-saṃhatatayā, na tu sāmānyatā-mānyatayā | rahaḥ-saṃhananam api śarma-sampad-aṃhati-bṛṃhita-guṇa-baṃhitatayā, na tu tad-asaṃhitatayā | tac ca sarva-guṇa-vismāyikānām apy asmākaṃ tyāga-jāgarūka-samayata eva, na tu tad-vinimayata iti svayaṃ yan gacchann eva nināya iti |
children.translated_text: They also unpack the reason for such wonder — [the verse beginning with] '<s>yan naḥ</s>.' 'The glorious <s>Govinda</s> himself, who suddenly, by the greatness of his qualities, beauty, and majesty, wins every heart — he himself led [her] away; truly he led her, not that he did not lead her. And the manner thereof was accomplished by creating [a place] against each breast, with the course of affection surrounding [her] — not in the opposite manner. And the affection was with the intimacy of the privacy in the flow of Love's splendor — not with the ordinariness of [mere] respectability. And the intimate privacy was expanded with the greatness of qualities, amplified by the abundance of bliss-wealth — not without that coherence. And all of this was at the very moment of awakened [love's] departure from even us who are wonder-struck by all [his] qualities — not in exchange for that.' Thus, 'he himself, even as he was departing, led [her] away.'

children.text: tad evam eva manyāmahe-yā khalu dhanyā rādhābhidhā vidhātrā niḥsādhāraṇa-nāma-guṇa-rūpatayā nirmitā, saiva daiva-kṛtānukulyā bhavitum arhati | tatra yadyapi tādṛśa-bhagavad-ārādhana-sādhanatayā tan-nāma-nirvacanaṃ sacita-racanaṃ bhaved, athāpi phala-sambandha-nirbandha eva śreyān iti rādhayati govindaṃ, govindena vā rādhyata iti niruktir eva yukti-matīti mati-gamyam iti |
children.translated_text: Thus indeed we understand: 'She who is called <s>Rādhā</s>, the blessed one, fashioned by the Creator with a name, qualities, and form that are extraordinary — she alone is fit to be one who has the favor of fate.' Therein, although the etymology of her name as a means of worshipping (<s>ārādhana</s>) such a Lord would be a well-fashioned derivation, nevertheless, the interpretation connected with the result [of worship] is preferable — [namely] '<s>Rādhā</s> [is she who] gratifies <s>Govinda</s>' or '[she who] is gratified by <s>Govinda</s>' — this etymology alone is endowed with reason — thus it is to be understood by the mind.'

children.text: atha punas tasyām udāsīnāḥ procuḥ-
children.translated_text: Then again, those indifferent toward her said:

children.text:
ayi kalayata ete reṇavo' py atra dhanyā
yad ajita-pada-padma-sparśa-bhājaḥ sphuranti |
dhruvam agham apahartuṃ brahma-bhargābdhi-kanyā
dadhati śirasi yāṃs tad-darśa-bhāgyaṃ stavāma ||JGc_1,24.31|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
'Behold, these dust-particles too are blessed here,
for they gleam as recipients of the touch of the unconquered one's foot-lotus!
Surely, to remove sin, the daughter of the ocean of the radiance of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>)
bears them upon her head — let us praise that fortune of seeing [his feet]!' ||24.31|| [mālinī]

children.text: atha kācit tasyāṃ pratispardhinī vardhamāna-matsarāgnir dhūma-śikhāyamānaṃ vacanam ujjagāra-
children.translated_text: Then a certain one, a rival toward her [<s>Rādhā</s>], with the fire of jealousy increasing, uttered a speech that smoked [with envy]:

children.text:
bhavati sukhadam asmin śrī-harer aṅghri-cihnaṃ
yadi na sajati tasyā hanta durnīti-matyāḥ |
kalayata bata dhārṣṭyaṃ suṣṭhu bhāvatka-bhogyaṃ
tad-adhara-madhu juṣṭaṃ kurvatī sā nililye ||JGc_1,24.32|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
'If the footprint of glorious <s>Hari</s> on this [earth] is a source of joy,
then it does not adhere to her — alas! — that one of wicked-minded conduct!
Behold her audacity — thoroughly fit for your lordships' enjoyment —
having savored the honey of his lips, she has hidden away!' ||24.32|| [mālinī]

children.text: atha tasyāḥ sakhyaḥ punar ūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: Then her [<s>Rādhā's</s>] friends said again:

children.text:
katham ahaha padāni tāni tasyāḥ
subhagatarāṅka-padāni na sphuranti |
api hṛdi dadhad eva tāṃ nininye
sakhi dayitāṃ dayitaḥ sujāta-gātrīm ||JGc_1,24.33|| [puṣpitāgrā]
children.translated_text:
'How is it that her footprints — alas! —
marked with most auspicious signs, do not appear [anymore]?
Surely, holding her in his very heart, the beloved led away
his beloved, the one of lovely limbs, O friend!' ||24.33|| [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text: atha punaḥ pratispardhinīnāṃ vacanam-
children.translated_text: Then again, the words of the rivals:

children.text:
paśyotsaṅga-kṛtāṅganā-valayinaḥ kāmāturasyāsakṛt
tad-vastrādika-saṃvṛti-prathanayā vyagrasya lakṣmāṇy ataḥ |
nimna-vyasta-padāni mālya-ghusṛṇāstīrṇāni gharmāmbhasā
bhūyaḥ siktatamāni velli-talatā-kṣepānta-vartmāni ca ||JGc_1,24.34|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'Behold the signs of the passion-afflicted one who repeatedly
placed the woman in his lap — being occupied with
the spreading of the covering of her garments and such:
footprints sunken, strewn with garlands and saffron,
wet with perspiration,
and paths [ending] with the tossing of trailing creeper-like [garments]!' ||24.34|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text: tasyāḥ sakhīnāṃ vacanam-
children.translated_text: The words of her [<s>Rādhā's</s>] friends:

children.text:
nyag-jānu-dvaya-lakṣaṇasya purataḥ sūkṣmaṃ padāṅka-dvayaṃ
vaimukhyena dhṛtaṃ vyanakti sudṛśas tasyās tad-ūrvoḥ sthitim | iti |
children.translated_text:
'Before the [footprint] characterized by a pair of lowered knees,
a subtle pair of footprints held in the opposite direction
reveals the lovely-eyed one's posture upon his thighs.' Thus.

children.text: atha spardhinīnām-
children.translated_text: Then [the words] of the rivals:

children.text:
tasmin garbhaka-mālya-khaṇḍa-patanād uddaṇḍam ālakṣyate
kāminyāḥ kila kāmukena racitā keśasya veśakriyā ||JGc_1,24.35|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
'At that spot, from the falling of fragments of the inner garland,
it is conspicuously seen that by the lover
the arrangement of the beloved woman's hair was performed!' ||24.35|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
atrāpraguṇatābaddhā mithaḥ paddhati-paddhatiḥ |
rādhā-mādhavayoḥ krīḍāṃ nirvrīḍāṃ vedayaty asau ||JGc_1,24.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'Here, the trails of footprints bound together in an irregular manner
of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> reveal
their play — unabashed!' ||24.36|| [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha tāḥ sanijavṛndayā vṛndayā pariṣkṛtasya latāmandiravṛndasya dvāraṃ tayoḥ praveśadvāraṃ vivikṣanti sma |
children.translated_text: Then they, along with their own company led by <s>Vṛndā</s>, wished to enter the door — the entrance of the pair — of the decorated bower-pavilion of creepers.

children.text: tatra tayā samadhutayā madhuraṃ puṣpavṛndaṃ tathā praveśadeśe niveśitam, yathā tallolubha-śubhaṃyumadhukaranikarā eva dauvārikā iva nivārakā jātāḥ | [54] te hi praveśārambhata eva dhṛtasaṃrambhāḥ praviśatām abhimukhaṃ dhāvantaḥ svakaśilīmukhatām arthāntareṇāpi prathayanti sma | [55] atha kathañcana ślathatāṃ cirataḥ prathayamāneṣu teṣu kramaśaḥ sarvās tarvādipallavavellanapūrvakam āviddhapaddhatitayā praviśya param apūrvaṃ tad dhāma niśāmayāmāsuḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, she (<s>Rādhā</s>), being sweetly disposed, placed a sweet cluster of flowers at the entrance in such a way that the swarms of bees, beautiful and covetous of it, became like doorkeepers and guardians. [54] For they, having seized their vehemence from the very beginning of entry, rushing toward those who were entering, proclaimed their own arrow-like nature by yet another meaning. [55] Then, when those [bees] gradually became slack after a long time, all [the gopīs], one by one, waving the creeper-shoots and other foliage, entered in a winding manner and beheld that supremely unprecedented abode, as follows:

children.text:
pika-prathita-pañcamaṃ bhramara-pūrṇa-mandra-svaraṃ
maruc-calita-pallava-prakaṭa-vādyam udyat-prabham |
bhujaṅga-ripu-nartana-jñapita-cañcalāvāri-bhṛd-
vibhā-valita-tad-dvayātula-sabhāsad-aṅgīkṛtam ||JGc_1,24.37|| [pṛthvī]
 vicitra-kusumaiś cita-sthalam analpa-talpākulaṃ
bahu-vyajana-cāmaraṃ surabhi-vīṭikā-sampuṭam |
sa-candra-vara-candanāguru-gurūru-pātrānvitaṃ
latā-gṛha-rahaḥ-puraṃ dhvanayati sma tāḥ praty adaḥ ||JGc_1,24.38|| [pṛthvī]
(yugmakam)
ayaṃ kusuma-saṃcayaś caraṇa-pāta-jāta-ślathas
tad etad api talpakaṃ vighaṭitāṅga-bhaṅgī-sthiti |
idaṃ vyajana-cāmaraṃ galita-yantrajāndolanaṃ
tathā surabhi-vīṭikādy api vibhukta-muktī-kṛtam ||JGc_1,24.39|| [pṛthvī] tataḥ kim iva pṛcchatha sva-vadaveta mām ujjhitaṃ
paraṃ drutam itaḥ paraṃ vrajata tatra taṃ prāpnuta |
amī pika-mukhā mama sphuṭam upeyur utpitsutāṃ svayaṃ
bhavati duḥkhite bhavati kasya vāṅgīkṛtiḥ? ||JGc_1,24.40|| [pṛthvī] (yugmakam)
children.translated_text:
Resounding with the fifth note proclaimed by cuckoos, full of the deep hum of bees, with instruments manifested by the wind-stirred foliage, radiant with rising light, adorned with a pair of incomparable court-seats made of the splendor enveloped by the dancing of <s>Garuḍa</s> (the serpent's enemy) revealing the trembling of cloud-bearing [waters] — // [pṛthvī]
Strewn with various flowers upon the ground, abundant with many couches, with numerous fans and <s>cāmaras</s>, with fragrant betel-leaf caskets, furnished with excellent large vessels of fine camphor, sandalwood, and <s>aguru</s> (aloe) — that secret bower-city resounded toward them thus! // [pṛthvī]
(a pair:)
'This heap of flowers, loosened by the fall of feet; this couch too, with its postures of limbs disturbed; this fan and <s>cāmara</s>, its mechanism of swinging fallen slack; and the fragrant betel and other [items] too, consumed and discarded — // [pṛthvī]
Then what are you asking of me? He has abandoned me, his own dear one! But swiftly go from here, onward — and there, find him! These cuckoos and other [birds] of mine have clearly attained the desire to fly away — when the master is distressed, whose is the acceptance [of remaining]?' // [pṛthvī] (a pair)

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
idaṃ mṛga-madāvṛtaṃ ghusṛṇa-bindu-mandokṣitaṃ
kṣitaṃ śayanakaṃ tataḥ sa-parivṛtti-lakṣmāpy adaḥ |
paraspara-viparyaya-prathiti-śāli yad bāndhavaṃ
kulaṃ katham amuṣya na sphuratu pāribhāvī daśā ||JGc_1,24.41|| [pṛthvī]
[56] atha tayor vṛttam anuvṛttyatām | [57] yadā tu nikuñja-pura-dvāri praveśa-kṛtāveśānāṃ tāsāṃ kolāhala-vikalatāvakalitā, tadā sambhrama-valitena rādhā-lalitena tena tataḥ pracalana-kalanāya tasyāḥ svasya ca cela-sambhālanādikam ārabdham, na tu labdham | kintu-
children.translated_text:
Moreover:
'This couch, smeared with musk, lightly sprinkled with drops of saffron, is pressed down — and that [other spot] bears the mark of turning over. The two [places], showing the imprint of mutual interchange, are kindred — how could the humiliating state of that [faithless] one's family not become evident?' // [pṛthvī]
[56] Now, let their affair be followed. [57] When the commotion and agitation of those [gopīs] entering eagerly at the door of the bower-city was perceived, then by the flustered <s>Rādhā</s> and the graceful one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), an effort was begun to arrange their garments and prepare for departure from there — but it was not achieved. Rather —

children.text:
utkarṇatā-samavakarṇana-vastra-veṣā-
dhānāni yā vivaśatā nijagāra tāṃ ca |
tūrṇir yadā nigirati sma tadā murārir
labdha-kṣaṇaḥ praṇayinī-valitaṃ nililye ||JGc_1,24.42|| [vasantatilakā] ||
children.translated_text: The straining of ears, the perception of sounds, the arranging of garment and attire — and the helplessness that she (<s>Rādhā</s>) swallowed — when haste consumed [it all], then the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, having found the moment, hid along with his beloved! // [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
athāgrima-kathā-prathanāya parāmṛśyate |
