 [59] na caivam api tāsāṃ tasya ca kāmukatā-sāmānyaṃ manyatām | tan-nikāma-katā-nivāraṇasya karaṇasya kāraṇaṃ svarūpaṃ tāvan nirūpyate-
children.translated_text:
Now, for the presentation of the subsequent narrative, it is recalled.
[59] Nor should the commonality of lustfulness between those [gopīs] and him be imagined thus. The essential nature of the cause for the prevention of their excessive desire is now ascertained:

children.text:
preta-prāya-śarīrāḥ sarve te kāmukāḥ kalitāḥ |
kṛṣṇaḥ sāndrānandas tasya ca rādhā-mukhāḥ śobhāḥ ||JGc_1,24.43|| [upagīti] ||
children.translated_text: All those lustful beings are recognized as having corpse-like bodies; <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is dense bliss, and those headed by <s>Rādhā</s> are his splendors! // [upagīti]

children.text: yathoktam-
children.translated_text: As stated:

children.text: tvakśmaśru-roma-nakha-keśa-pinaddham antar
children.translated_text: 'Inwardly covered with skin, hair, body-hair, nails, and head-hair,

children.text: māṃsāsthi-rakta-kṛmi-viṭ-kapha-pitta-vātam |
children.translated_text: filled with flesh, bone, blood, worms, excrement, phlegm, bile, and wind —

children.text: jīvac-chavaṃ bhajati kāntam ativimūḍhā
children.translated_text: an exceedingly deluded woman courts a living corpse as her beloved,

children.text: yā te padābja-makarandam ajighratī strī ||[BhP 10.60.45]
children.translated_text: she who does not smell the honey of your lotus feet!' // [BhP 10.60.45]

children.text: kṛṣi bhūr-vācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛti-vācakaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The word <s>kṛṣ</s> denotes the earth (existence), and the syllable <s>ṇa</s> denotes supreme bliss;

children.text: tayor aikyaṃ paraṃ brahma kṛṣṇa ity abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: their unity is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text: narākṛti paraṃ brahma |
children.translated_text: 'The supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form.'

children.text: tvayy eva nitya-sukha-bodha-tanāv anante | [BhP 10.14.22],
children.translated_text: 'In you alone, the embodiment of eternal bliss and consciousness, who are infinite —' [BhP 10.14.22],

children.text: tābhir vidhūta-śokābhir bhagavān acyuto vṛtaḥ |
vyārocatādhikaṃ tāta puruṣaḥ śaktibhir yathā ||[BhP 10.32.10] iti ca |
children.translated_text: shone forth exceedingly, O dear one, like the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) with his <s>Śaktis</s> (divine powers)!' // [BhP 10.32.10] — thus.

children.text: bhāvaś ca na kāmatāṃ bhāvayate, kintu tan-nibha-prema-viśeṣatām eva, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And the emotional state does not engender lustfulness, but rather a special type of <s>prema</s> (divine love) resembling it, because:
'<s>Bhagavān Acyuta</s>, surrounded by those women freed from sorrow,

children.text:
utkaṇṭhā prāpti-yogaḥ pratipada-milanāśleṣa-cumbādi-keliḥ
śrī-gopī-kṛṣṇayor apy avara-taruṇayor apy amī tulya-rūpāḥ |
kintu prācor mithaḥ syur nirupādhi-hitatāmātra-śarma-pradhānās
te' rvācor ātma-tṛpti-pravalana-paratāmātra-kptāḥ prathante ||JGc_1,24.44|| [sragdharā]
[62] yathaiva svayam eva tās tat-prema-devatā vadiṣyanti-
children.translated_text:
Longing, the union of attainment, the play of embrace and kiss at every step — these appear similar in form for the younger <s>gopīs</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as well as for the younger [worldly couples]. But in the former pair, they are predominantly characterized by unconditional benevolence and pure happiness alone; in the latter pair, they are known to be characterized by the predominance of self-gratification alone! // [sragdharā]
[62] Just as those <s>gopīs</s> themselves, the deities of that <s>prema</s>, will declare:

children.text: yat te sujāta-caraṇāmbu-ruhaṃ staneṣu
bhītāḥ śanaiḥ priya dadhīmahi karkaśeṣu | [BhP 10.31.19] ity ādinā |
children.translated_text: fearfully, gently, we would place [them], O beloved, though they are rough!' // [BhP 10.31.19] — and so forth.

children.text: tasmāl lakṣaṇaviśeṣāt tatpremaviśeṣa evāsau kāmaveśāyata iti kāmatayo-pacaryate na tu vastutas tattayā smaryate | atas tatkeliśrutiphalaśrutir api tathā viśrutiḥ-
children.translated_text: Therefore, by this distinguishing characteristic, that special <s>prema</s> alone has assumed the semblance of <s>kāma</s> (desire) — hence it is figuratively spoken of as desire, but in reality it is not remembered as being of that nature. Thus, the hearing of the fruit of hearing about their play is also such a proclamation:
'Your well-born lotus feet — upon our breasts,

children.text:
vikrīḍitaṃ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ
śraddhānvito' nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ |
bhaktiṃ parāṃ bhagavati parilabhya kāmaṃ
hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ ||[BhP 10.33.39] iti |
children.translated_text: having attained supreme <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) for <s>Bhagavān</s>, he, the steadfast one, swiftly dispels desire — the disease of the heart!' // [BhP 10.33.39] — thus.

children.text: tāsām eṣa ca bhāva-viśeṣataḥ khalu sarveṣām api mahatāṃ mahattarāṇāṃ mahattamānām apy anveṣaṇa-padavīm anavacchinnatayā navīkaroti | yathā ca prathayiṣyate śrīmad-uddhavena-
children.translated_text: And their particular emotional state indeed renews the path of seeking of all the great, the greater, and the greatest, in an unbroken manner. As will be proclaimed by the illustrious <s>Uddhava</s>:

children.text: etāḥ paraṃ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo
children.translated_text: 'These cowherd women, the highest among embodied beings on earth,

children.text: govinda evam akhilātmani rūḍha-bhāvāḥ |
children.translated_text: in <s>Govinda</s>, the soul of all, had established their love.

children.text: vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṃ ca kiṃ brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathā-rasasya ||[BhP 10.47.58]
children.translated_text: What sages and we, who fear worldly existence, desire — of what use are births as <s>Brahmā</s> for [tasting] the nectar of the stories of the infinite one?' // [BhP 10.47.58]
'Whoever with faith hears or narrates this play of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the women of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: ataeva tādṛśa-tat-prema-tṛṣṇaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaś ca tena svasya vaśatām urīkariṣyati-
children.translated_text: Therefore, Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who thirsts for such <s>prema</s> of theirs, will himself acknowledge his own subservience to it:

children.text: na pāraye' haṃ niravadya-saṃyujāṃ
sva-sādhu-kṛtyaṃ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ | [BhP 10.32.22] ity ādinā |
children.translated_text: your own good deeds, even in a lifetime of the gods!' // [BhP 10.32.22] — and so forth.
'I am unable [to repay] the faultless union —

children.text: tad evaṃ sati tāsu sarva evānye' pi guṇāḥ svata evānuguṇā bhavanti-
children.translated_text: This being so, in those [gopīs], all other virtues too naturally become harmonious:

children.text: yasyāsti bhaktir bhagavaty akiñcanā
sarvair guṇais tatra samāsate surāḥ | [BhP 5.18.12] itivat |
children.translated_text: all virtues and gods reside in such a one!' // [BhP 5.18.12] — in this manner.

children.text: tataś caivaṃ varṇyate-
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is described thus:
'One who has unalloyed <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) for <s>Bhagavān</s> —

children.text: yad-amita-rasa-śāstre vyañji vaidagdhya-vṛndaṃ
children.translated_text: 'In his treatise of immeasurable <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), the multitude of cleverness that is suggested —

children.text: tad-aṇum api na vettuṃ kalpate kāmi-lokaḥ |
children.translated_text: even an atom of it the world of lovers is not capable of knowing.

children.text: tad akhilam api yasya prema-sindhau na kiñcin
children.translated_text: All that too, in the ocean of his <s>prema</s>, is nothing —

children.text: mithunam ajita-gopī-rūpam etad vibhāti ||[*8] [mālinī]
children.translated_text: this couple in the form of the unconquered <s>gopī</s> shines forth!' // [mālinī]

children.text:
tad evaṃ sati ca sarvāsu tāsu śrī-rādhā punar asādhāraṇatāṃ dhārayati | yathoktaṃ, anayārādhito nūnam ity ādinā | [69] tad evam ākalite nirgalite phalitam avakalitaṃ kriyate |
[*8] This verse is marked as a quote in Puri Das' edition, but I have no evidence that it is indeed so.
children.translated_text: And this being so, among all those [gopīs], Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> again holds an extraordinary position. As stated: 'By her alone was he worshipped (<s>ārādhita</s>)' [BhP 10.30.28] — and so forth. [69] Thus having been ascertained, the manifested fruit is now presented.

children.text:
evaṃ rādhā-prema-dhāmā yayā'sāv
ātmārāmo' py āpta-kāmo' py adabhram |
reme yasmāt kāmināṃ kāminīnāṃ
nyakkāro' bhūd ātmanaiveti manye ||JGc_1,24.45|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Rādhā</s>, the abode of <s>prema</s>, by whom he — though self-delighted (<s>ātmārāma</s>) and though self-fulfilled (<s>āptakāma</s>) — sported abundantly; because of which there arose the surpassing of all lovers and beloveds — by his own self alone, I believe! // [śālinī]

children.text: ātmārāmatā hy atra paramānanda-rūpatayā āpta-kāmatā ca parama-lakṣmī-lakṣaṇa-gopī-lakṣa-vallabhatā-vilakṣaṇatayā, [71] adabhratā ca tāḥ parityajyāpi tasyām akhaṇḍitatāyā vyajyamānatayeti prasajyate | [72] tatra ca sati-
children.translated_text: The quality of being <s>ātmārāma</s> (self-delighted) here is by virtue of his nature as the form of supreme bliss; the quality of being <s>āptakāma</s> (self-fulfilled) is by virtue of the extraordinariness of being the beloved of the <s>gopīs</s> marked by supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s>; [71] and the abundantness is manifested by the fact that even having abandoned those [others], his unbroken [devotion] to her (<s>Rādhā</s>) is evident. [72] And this being so:

children.text:
anyo' nyānugatiṃ yadapy anusṛtau premṇaḥ pravāhau tayo
rādhā-mādhavayos tadapy anupadaṃ kauṭilyam āsīdataḥ |
yo gāmbhīryam apāṃ javaṃ ca dadhate pūraḥ sa hi prekṣyate
sāvarta-pracayas tataḥ parataraḥ sāralya-kaivalyavān ||JGc_1,24.46|| [śārdūla] [73] yathoktam-
children.translated_text:
Although the two currents of <s>prema</s> between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> followed mutual succession, even so, at every step, crookedness was setting in. For the flood that holds both depth and velocity of waters is indeed seen, and the whirlpool-mass beyond that possesses sincerity alone! // [śārdūla]
[73] As stated:

children.text: aher iva gatiḥ premṇaḥ svabhāva-kuṭilo bhavet | ato hetor ahetoś ca yūnor māna udañcati ||[UN 15.102] ||
children.translated_text: 'The course of <s>prema</s>, like a serpent's, is by nature crooked; therefore, with cause and without cause, pride (<s>māna</s>) rises between the young couple.' // [UN 15.102]

children.text:
tad evaṃ sthite tan-maya-vilāsa-viśeṣo varṇyate-
dara-mukulita-netrā tiryag-ālambi-kaṇṭhī
śithilita-bhuja-yugmā stabdha-sakthīyam āsīt |
tad api ca madhu-hantrā jānatā svaṃ kṛtārthaṃ
muhur api hasitā kiṃ bhrū-kuṭiṃ nāpi kuryāt? ||JGc_1,24.47|| [mālinī] ||
children.translated_text:
This being so, the special pastime imbued with her is now described:
With slightly closed eyes, her neck drooping sideways, her pair of arms relaxed, her thighs motionless — she sat thus. Even so, having been laughed at again and again by the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, who knew himself to be fulfilled — would she not form a frown? // [mālinī]

children.text: tad evaṃ vṛtte vṛtte netari cānunetari mānvat tasyāḥ kiñcid ahaṃ-māna-sparśo' pi sadarśo babhūva | yathā ca tayā pūrvaṃ nātyūhāpoha-sāmarthyam āsīd ity adhunā khalv idaṃ bhāvitam-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the affair had transpired, and the leader (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) was both leading and conciliating, a touch of self-pride akin to <s>māna</s> (love-pride) also became visible in her. And as she had previously lacked the ability to reason through such deliberations, now indeed she conceived this:

children.text:
etāvantaṃ diṣṭam ajñāsiṣaṃ na
preyaḥ-saṅgāt kintv idānīṃ tad ūhe |
preyān sarvāḥ projjhya mām eva ramyāṃ
saṅgamyāntaḥ-kānanaṃ yan nināya ||JGc_1,24.48|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text: 'I did not know this much of destiny before, due to the company of the beloved; but now I infer it — that the beloved, having abandoned all [the others], has brought me alone, the beautiful one, into the interior of the forest!' // [śālinī]

children.text: tataś cāgrima-gamanāya vyagreṇa nāthena prārthitāpi sā lālityena kiñcid ālasyam api vyañjayāmāsa, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, when the Lord, eager for going further ahead, entreated her, she, through her gracefulness, also displayed a slight languor, as follows:

children.text:
tvad-gātra-spṛṣṭatā-mātra-
ślathāṅga-gatitāṃ gatām |
spandāya cātimandāṃ māṃ
yatra tatra svayaṃ naya ||JGc_1,24.49|| [anuṣṭubh] ||
children.translated_text: 'My limbs have become slack merely from the touch of your body — I have reached a state of sluggishness; and for movement, I am too languid — carry me yourself wherever [you wish]!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tad anu ca tad-udāsīnatādhīna-bhāva-samūham ūhamānaḥ praṇayavān api praṇaya-mānavān idaṃ sopalambha-parīhāsa-lambham uvāca-kathaṃ bhavatyā muhyate? mama skandha eva sa-nirbandham āruhyatām iti | [78] tadā ca tajjayā serṣyālajjayādhaḥsajjadānanam asyāḥ paśyann, antarhitavān api sakautukam antarhitavān | sahasāntarhite ca tasmin vismitā vismitā ca sā vidhurahitā kumudinīva vidhuritā babhūva | tatra kila sānulāpaṃ vilalāpa ca-
children.translated_text: Then, inferring the assemblage of emotional states dependent on her aloofness, though full of love, the one possessed of love-pride (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) spoke this with playful reproach: 'Why are you deluded? Simply climb upon my shoulder with determination!' [78] And then, seeing her face lowered shyly with jealous embarrassment at his victory, though he disappeared, he disappeared with curiosity. And when he suddenly disappeared, she, astonished and again astonished, became agitated like a night-lotus without the moon. There, she lamented with sobs:

children.text:
hā nātha ha ramaṇa hā priyatātikānta
hā hā kva gacchasi mahābhuja hā kva vāsi? |
dāsyāṃ sadā kṛpaṇatājuṣi nanv amuṣyām
ātmopakaṇṭham api sūcaya jīviteśa ||JGc_1,24.50|| [vasantatilakā]
 [79] atrāstu tāvat tava rūpa-nirūpaṇaṃ tvan-nikaṭa-bhūmim ivodhaghaṭanayāpi dhīratāṃ dhārayāmīti dhvanitam |
[80] tataś ca, yadyapy evam api catura-śiromaṇinā tena vicāritam asti sma, yathā-yady etasyāś ca mayā parityāgaḥ parityaktābhiḥ samprati pratīyate, mayā pṛthag enayā ca saṅgamyate, tadā parasparam āsattyāṃ satyāṃ mahā-rāsa-mahaḥ sampadyate iti, tathāpi sneha-vaśān mūrcchantīṃ tām āgacchati tasminn accha-hṛdaye mṛgayamāṇā mṛgalocanā drutam āgacchanti sma |
children.translated_text:
'Alas, O Lord! O lover! O dearest, most beloved one! Alas, alas, where do you go, O great-armed one? Where do you dwell? To this servant, always steeped in wretchedness — reveal yourself, even [if just to be] near, O lord of my life!' // [vasantatilakā]
[79] Here, 'let there be the contemplation of your form' — through the effort of producing even the ground near you — 'I shall maintain my steadfastness' — this is the implication.
[80] Then, although that crown-jewel of the clever had already reflected thus — 'If her abandonment by me is perceived by the abandoned ones as well, [and] if she is met by me separately, then in the presence of mutual proximity, the great <s>rāsa</s> festival will be accomplished' — even so, out of the compulsion of affection, she, the doe-eyed one, swooning, searching for him in that clear-hearted one who was approaching, came swiftly.

children.text: tataś ca sambhramataḥ pracchannatāṃ gacchati śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ-
children.translated_text: And then, as Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was frantically going into concealment —

children.text:
eṣā campaka-mālikātra patitā kiṃ candralekhāthavā
kāntīnām adhidevatā bhavati vā vṛndāvana-śrīr uta? |
hā kaṣṭaṃ nahi ceṣṭate kim iyam ity udvigna-dhī-vṛttayas
tām āvavrur amūś camūru-nayanā bhṛṅgī-nibhāḥ padminīm ||JGc_1,24.51|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'Is this a garland of <s>campaka</s> flowers fallen here? Or a crescent of the moon? Or is it the presiding deity of radiances? Or the beauty of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>? Alas, how terrible — it does not stir! What is this?' — their minds agitated with anxious thoughts, those broad-eyed ones, bee-like, surrounded that lotus-woman (<s>Rādhā</s>)! // [śārdūla]

children.text:
tatrānyās tu sakhī-nibhāḥ samabhavaṃs tasyāṃ dravan-mānasāḥ
prāṇa-prāṇa-samāḥ sa-māna-manasaḥ sakhyaś citaṃ tatyajuḥ |
yasmin nāsty avalambanaṃ kila kim apy asmin vidhiḥ sad-vidhis
tādṛkṣeṣu vilakṣaṇeṣu valayaty anyac ca dhanyaṃ bahu ||JGc_1,24.52|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text: 'The others then became like companions to her, with melting hearts toward her, | equal to her very life-breath, with minds full of respect — [yet] the friends abandoned composure. | Where there is truly no support at all, what can fate — even good fate — do? | In such extraordinary [circumstances], much else that is blessed revolves [around them].' || (JGc 1,24.52) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
kṛṣṇa-prasaṅga-parivāsitam aṅganānām
aṅgaṃ yadā tu nasi saṅgatim aṅgati sma |
sāraṅga-laṅgima-dṛśaḥ param aṅga-saṅghāś
cācetiṣuḥ savayaso' pi tadāṅga-tulyāḥ ||JGc_1,24.53|| [vasantatilakā]
  [82] tadā tu-
kāśmīrārdraṃ kvāpi sindūra-liptaṃ
kvāpi cchinnaṃ kvāpi bhinnaṃ kva cāpi |
antaḥ-pītācchādanaṃ tan-nicolaṃ
paśyan saṅghaḥ saṅginīnāṃ nananda ||JGc_1,24.54|| [śālinī]
children.translated_text:
'When the bodies of the women, perfumed by contact with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, | came into the proximity of their noses, | the doe-eyed ones — ah! — and the other groups of women | became conscious of their own equals, like friends of the same age.' || (JGc 1,24.53) [vasantatilakā]
[82] And then:
'Somewhere moist with saffron, somewhere smeared with vermilion, | somewhere torn, somewhere split, and somewhere else — | the inner yellow garment, that blouse of hers — | seeing it, the company of her companions rejoiced!' || (JGc 1,24.54) [śālinī]

children.text:
svayam api yadapi tadā sā
hari-parimala-bhāg athāpi tāsāṃ tu |
āgantuka-subahūnāṃ
gātrāt tad-bhāg uvāha vailakṣyam ||JGc_1,24.55|| [āryā]
[83] tad evaṃ sarvā eva hṛdya-sauhṛdya-visrabdhās tām ātmaikadhyam āgatāṃ madhyam adhyāsya tayā saha paraspara-parīrambha-baddhāḥ sudustara-duḥkha-naddhāḥ puru ruruduḥ |
children.translated_text:
'Although she herself at that time | was a partaker of <s>Hari's</s> fragrance, nevertheless, | from the bodies of those many newcomers, | she bore embarrassment at being a sharer of that [fragrance].' || (JGc 1,24.55) [āryā]
[83] Thus, all of them, trusting in heartfelt friendship, placing her — who had come to be one with their very selves — in their midst, bound to her through mutual embrace, bound by supremely difficult-to-overcome grief, they wept profusely.

children.text:
sudustaraṃ ruditvā ca tām amūs tu papracchuḥ-asmākaṃ khalu na duḥkhaṃ pañcabhiḥ saheti kalpenānalpam api duḥkhaṃ kalpatvāya nākalpata kalpam | tatas tan nātipraṣṭavyaṃ bhavatīty ananya-gatyā bhavatyās tu tat tyāgaḥ katham iti kathyatām, kathaṃ vā vikalatā-hetuḥ kevalatā jātā, tad api ca |
 [85] sā punar anutāpa-vipad-uttaram uttaram uvāca-
children.translated_text:
And having wept with great difficulty [to overcome], they asked her: 'For us, the grief together with the five [senses] — though not slight — did not manage to become manageable even by the imagination of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age). Therefore that need not be asked of you; but being without any other recourse, how did you come to abandon him? Let that be told — and how did the state of being alone, the cause of distress, come about? And further:'
[85] She in turn spoke, overwhelmed by the calamity of remorse:

children.text:
kutaḥ kathaṃ kutra ca tena nītā
cakāra kiṃ vāham idaṃ na jāne |
anena hīnā tu vicārayāmi
svīyaṃ tu daurātmyam anartha-hetuḥ ||JGc_1,24.56|| [upajāti 11]
[86] tataś ca dhairya-paryayataḥ punaḥ krandanam anuvindamānā khinnatā-nati-bhinna-sakhīkābhiḥ kābhiścit kṛta-sāntvanā mārjitānanā veśa-niveśa-kṛta-mānanā sā samam unnamayāmāse |
children.translated_text:
'Whence, how, and where I was taken by him, | or what I did — this I do not know. | But being separated from him, I reflect: | my own wickedness alone is the cause of this misfortune!' || (JGc 1,24.56) [upajāti]
[86] Then, as she obtained weeping again through the fluctuation of fortitude — consoled by some friends who were bent low with distress, her face wiped, her appearance restored with honor — she was gradually lifted up together [with them].

children.text: tayā ca samam unnayanam āyāmase-samprati ca kutra sa pratilabhyate? iti | [88] sā covāca-nātidūram akrūra-cetāḥ sa tu kutukitayā vilasati, na tu kitavatayā-
children.translated_text: And as she was being lifted up together [with them], they endeavored [to ask]: 'Where can he be found now?' [88] And she said: 'Not far away — he whose heart is gentle (<s>akrūra</s>) plays out of curiosity, not out of deceit' —

children.text:
yataḥ gokula-rāja-kumāraḥ
śuci-rati-gambhīra-dhīr hrīmān |
tad api ca maryādāṃ naḥ
svīkārāyātyajat karuṇaḥ ||JGc_1,24.57|| iti [upagīti]
children.translated_text: 'Because the prince of <s>Gokula</s> | is pure in love, profound in wisdom, and modest; | yet even so, for our sake, he did not abandon | propriety — [such is] his compassion!' || (JGc 1,24.57) [upagīti] — thus.

children.text:
tasmāt tadīya-caraṇa-carita-vartmānucaraṇam eva naḥ śreyaḥ | tad etad vacanaṃ racayamānā vana-pracayaṃ puṣpāvacaya-parā iva vicinvanti sma | tato dhvajādi-padāni pada-padma-cihnāni kramatas tāvad amūr anvakrāman yāvat tāni spaṣṭāni dṛṣṭāni | paratas tu parivīrun-mahīruha-niviḍatam āraṇya-dharaṇy-andha-tama-praviṣṭāni dṛṣṭvā nyavartanta, na ca tatrāvartanta |
 [90] tatra cedaṃ vicārayāmāsuḥ-nūnam asmajjayā lajjayā sajjann asāv iha sahasā na sākṣād-bhavitum adhyavasyati, tasmāt tad abodha-nidhāya-bhūr iyaṃ dūrataḥ pariharaṇīyā parihṛtya ca sā pulina-dharaṇir evānusaraṇīyā |
children.translated_text:
'Therefore, following the path traversed by his feet is indeed our best course.' Uttering these words, they searched through the forest-thickets as if intent on gathering flowers. Then they followed step by step the footprints marked with the flag and other [auspicious signs] of his lotus-feet, so long as those were clearly visible. But beyond that, seeing those [footprints] entered into the pitch-darkness of the densest forest-ground overgrown with thick trees, they turned back — and did not linger there.
[90] There they reflected thus: 'Surely, clinging to the shyness [arising] from our victory over him, he does not resolve to appear directly here before us suddenly; therefore this ground — the repository of non-recognition — should be avoided from afar, and having avoided it, that sandy riverbank alone should be followed.'

children.text: yatrāham atrāsmi-tatra-bhavatyas tu kutratyatām itā ity apadeśād apatrapām apanayann ayam aparokṣatāṃ prapanīpadyate |
children.translated_text: 'Where I am — there you have gone to the state of being elsewhere' — by this pretext, removing the shame [of his absence], he would come into direct presence.

children.text: tad etad vicārya samācārya ca paryanveṣaṇās tam uddiśya diśyaṃ diśyaṃ vanaṃ praviśya, svayam anvicchantam iva saṃcarantaṃ dainya-sainya-mayam atigāna-vitānam ācaranti sma iti |
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated and conducted themselves accordingly, they, searching for him, entering forest after forest in each direction, and as if finding him himself searching [for them], they performed a vast canopy of song pervaded by the army of pathos — thus it is said.

children.text:
tad evaṃ teṣāṃ sabhāsadāṃ kathā-samādher avadhāya kathakaḥ samāpanam āha-
īdṛg eṣa varaḥ kṛṣṇas tava vṛndāvaneśvari |
tvāṃ vinā tu paraḥ-koṭīr api nāṅgīcakāra yaḥ ||JGc_1,24.58|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Thus, having drawn from the absorption in the narrative of those assembly-members, the narrator spoke the conclusion:
'Such is this excellent <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — your [beloved], O queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! | He who did not accept even crores of others without you!' || (JGc 1,24.58) [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
śrī-rādhā-saubhāgya-śravaṇa-subhāgyaṃ nāma
caturviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||24 ||
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the <s>Śrī Śrī Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Twenty-fourth Chapter, named
'The Good Fortune of Hearing of <s>Śrī Rādhā's</s> Blessed Supremacy.'
||24||

children.text:
(25)
atha pañcaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text:
(25)
Now the Twenty-fifth Chapter.

children.text: vipralambhana-stambhana-śrī-kṛṣṇa-lambhanam
children.translated_text: The Attainment of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> through the Paralysis of Separation.

children.text: atha madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tac ca gānam avadhīyatām | yathā-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'And let that song be attended to. As follows:' —

children.text: vrajavidho daśāsmākam īkṣyatām
vrajavidho daśāsmākam īkṣyatām ||JGc_1,25.1||
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Vraja</s>, behold our condition!' || (JGc 1,25.1)
'O Lord of <s>Vraja</s>, behold our condition!

children.text: jayati te' dhikaṃ janmanā vrajaḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Vraja</s> is supremely glorious through Your birth;

children.text: śrayata indirāpy asya bhūrajaḥ |
children.translated_text: even <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) takes refuge in its dust;

children.text: tad api hā'jahā nas tvam atra bho
children.translated_text: yet — alas, alas! — You have abandoned us here, O Lord!

children.text: vayam imaḥ kathaṃ vānyatāṃ prabho ||JGc_1,25.2||
children.translated_text: How shall we go elsewhere, O master?' || (JGc 1,25.2)

children.text: parama-jāti-bhāg uttamaṃ svataḥ
children.translated_text: 'The autumn-born lotus — supremely noble by birth,

children.text: śaradijaṃ ca yat paṅkajaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: of the highest class by its own nature —

children.text: dala-kulāvṛteḥ kānti-devatāṃ
children.translated_text: with its covering of petals, the deity of beauty —

children.text: harasi yad dṛśā śaśvad eva tām ||JGc_1,25.3||
children.translated_text: that You perpetually steal with Your glance!' || (JGc 1,25.3)

children.text: katham aho vayaṃ svacchatām itā
children.translated_text: 'Ah, how can we, having attained transparency,

children.text: bhavitum īśmahe tad-bahiḥ-sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: possibly remain standing outside of that?

children.text: api kila tvayā yācñayā sitāḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, summoned by You through [Your] entreaty,

children.text: svayam amūr vareṇāpi sanditāḥ ||JGc_1,25.4||
children.translated_text: they [the lotuses/we] have been given over by choice itself!' || (JGc 1,25.4)

children.text: iti gatās tava preṣyatāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having thus come into Your servitude —

children.text: kim u tayā dṛśā haṃsi tās tu naḥ? |
children.translated_text: do You now mock us with that glance?

children.text: yad iha śastrataḥ kevalaṃ vadhaḥ
children.translated_text: For here, through a weapon, there is merely killing —

children.text: sphurati nākṣitas tan-mataṃ tv adhaḥ ||JGc_1,25.5||
children.translated_text: but what is not destroyed [by the glance] — that intent is worse!' || (JGc 1,25.5)

children.text: bahu-vidhād bhayād yat tvayāvitaṃ
children.translated_text: 'That which was protected by You from manifold dangers —

children.text: sakala-gokulaṃ kānanānvitam |
children.translated_text: all of <s>Gokula</s>, together with the forest —

children.text: tad api manmahe svāvanaṃ yatas
children.translated_text: yet even so, we think [it was] Your own [self-]protection, since

children.text: tvad-anurāgataḥ so' pi kiṃ hataḥ? ||JGc_1,25.6||
children.translated_text: from love for You — has even that [protection] been slain?' || (JGc 1,25.6)

children.text: kṛpaṇa-pālaka śrī-vrajeśvarī-
children.translated_text: 'O protector of the wretched! The wisdom

children.text: tanuja yogya-dhīr asti naśvarī |
children.translated_text: of the son of the queen of <s>Vraja</s> is fit, yet perishable;

children.text: iti tavātmaval lipti-riktatā
children.translated_text: thus Your self-like detachment

children.text: paraga-pīḍayā bhāti tiktatā ||JGc_1,25.7||
children.translated_text: shines as bitterness through the affliction of estrangement!' || (JGc 1,25.7)

children.text: tvam asi nānyavat ko' pi kopanaḥ
children.translated_text: 'You are not wrathful like others —

children.text: sphurasi yat prabho viśva-gopanaḥ |
children.translated_text: for You shine forth, O Lord, as the protector of the universe!

children.text: tad iha padmajābhyarthitaḥ sva-bhūḥ
children.translated_text: Here, entreated by <s>Brahmā</s>, You — the Self-born —

children.text: parama-sātvatād anvayād abhūḥ ||JGc_1,25.8||
children.translated_text: appeared from the supreme <s>Sātvata</s> lineage!' || (JGc 1,25.8)

children.text: iti taveśituḥ suṣṭhu yaḥ karaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, that hand of Yours, the Lord's —

children.text: prathita-saṃsṛter bhīti-bhīkaraḥ |
children.translated_text: terrifying to the terror of the notorious cycle of rebirth —

children.text: śirasi naḥ kuru śrī-kara-grahaṃ
children.translated_text: place it upon our heads as an auspicious hand-grasp;

children.text: tam iha nānyathā bhāvayāgraham ||JGc_1,25.9||
children.translated_text: do not consider it otherwise — [it is] a shelter!' || (JGc 1,25.9)

children.text: vrajaga-bhī-hṛtau vīra yoṣitāṃ
children.translated_text: 'O hero, You who steal the fear of the women of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: śamayasi smitenaiva roṣitām |
children.translated_text: You who pacify their anger with a mere smile —

children.text: tad iha nānyathā daṇḍanaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: do not inflict punishment otherwise here,

children.text: prakaṭayānana-śrī-mahaḥ puru ||JGc_1,25.10||
children.translated_text: but reveal abundantly the splendor of Your face!' || (JGc 1,25.10)

children.text: yad api te padaṃ śrī-niketanam
children.translated_text: 'Although Your feet are the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),

children.text: vṛjinajin mahā-puṇya-ketanam |
children.translated_text: O conqueror of sin, the banner of great merit —

children.text: tad api go-gaṇasyānuvartanaṃ
children.translated_text: yet there is also the tending of the cows,

children.text: viṣa-bhṛtaḥ śiro-varti-nartanam ||JGc_1,25.11||
children.translated_text: and the dancing upon the head of the venomous one (<s>Kāliya</s>)!' || (JGc 1,25.11)

children.text: yad adhi tat tad apy ātta-duḥsthiti
children.translated_text: 'Upon whichever [feet] that distress too

children.text: svayam abhūt tataḥ śāntatākṣitiḥ |
children.translated_text: itself arose — from that, the ground of peace [was established];

children.text: ahaha tan manāg nas tu vakṣasi
children.translated_text: ahaha, will You not protect us even a little

children.text: sva-viraha-jvale kiṃ na rakṣasi? ||JGc_1,25.12||
children.translated_text: upon Your chest, from the fire of separation from You?' || (JGc 1,25.12)

children.text: madhura-līlayā karṇa-ramyayā
children.translated_text: 'With sweet <s>līlā</s> (play), delightful to the ears,

children.text: viśada-vākyayā vyakta-gamyayā |
children.translated_text: with lucid words, clearly accessible,

children.text: mukha-sugandhitāsātmyayā cirāt
children.translated_text: with the incomparable fragrance of Your mouth —

children.text: tṛṣam itā vayaṃ hanta te girā ||JGc_1,25.13||
children.translated_text: we have long thirsted, alas, for Your speech!' || (JGc 1,25.13)

children.text: tava kathāmṛtaṃ tapta-jīvanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The nectar of Your stories is the life of the afflicted,

children.text: kavibhir īḍitaṃ kalmaṣārdanam |
children.translated_text: praised by poets, destroyer of impurities;

children.text: pravitaranti ye teṣu durjanāḥ
children.translated_text: those who distribute it — toward them the wicked

children.text: sapadi naḥ kṛte jñapta-varjanāḥ ||JGc_1,25.14||
children.translated_text: are immediately made known [as fit] for our avoidance!' || (JGc 1,25.14)

children.text: prahasitaṃ tava preṅkhi-locanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Your laughter, Your swinging glances,

children.text: viharaṇa-kramād bhāva-rocanam |
children.translated_text: Your playful movements, beauteous in character,

children.text: muralikā-rutaṃ sarva-śocanaṃ
children.translated_text: the sound of the flute — causing all to lament —

children.text: vipinatas tu naḥ prāṇa-mocanam ||JGc_1,25.15||
children.translated_text: and from the forest, releasing our very life-breaths!' || (JGc 1,25.15)

children.text: calasi yarhi vā dhenu-cāraṇe
children.translated_text: 'When You go for cow-herding,

children.text: dalati dhīs tu nas tatra kāraṇe |
children.translated_text: our minds are split on that account;

children.text: śila-tṛṇāṅkurair yāva-sannatā
children.translated_text: the pain from pebbles, grass-shoots, and the like — bent down —

children.text: kila bhavat-padoḥ sāsmakān gatā ||JGc_1,25.16||
children.translated_text: of Your feet, has come to be ours as well!' || (JGc 1,25.16)

children.text: ahaha jājvalaty antarāṇi naḥ
children.translated_text: 'Ahaha! Our inner beings are ablaze!

children.text: smara nijān janān dīna-māninaḥ |
children.translated_text: Remember Your own people who consider themselves wretched!

children.text: caraṇa-paṅkajaṃ hṛdy amūdṛśāṃ
children.translated_text: The lotus of Your feet — in the hearts of such ones as us,

children.text: ramaṇa he tvayā dhīyatāṃ bhṛśam ||JGc_1,25.17||
children.translated_text: O lover — let it be firmly placed by You!' || (JGc 1,25.17)

children.text: ahaha yarhi yāsy ahni kānanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Ahaha! When You go to the forest by day,

children.text: kuṭila-kuntalaṃ śrīmad-ānanam |
children.translated_text: Your curly-locked, glorious face —

children.text: muhur apaśyatāṃ tarhi sa kṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: for those who cannot see it, that moment

children.text: sphurati sarvadā kalpa-lakṣaṇaḥ ||JGc_1,25.18||
children.translated_text: always appears to have the measure of a cosmic age!' || (JGc 1,25.18)

children.text:
kim iha tac ca vā vācyatāṃ vrajen
nimir apīha yac chapyate vraje? |
katham aho vayaṃ tās tu gopikā
na hi bhavāma vā tatra kopikāḥ? ||JGc_1,25.19||vitata-gītikā-jāla-sanditāḥ
svaka-janān atikramya cārditāḥ |
children.translated_text: having transgressed our own kinsmen, [are now] tormented;

children.text: karam itā mahāraṇya-bhṛd diśi
children.translated_text: having come to the direction of this great forest-bearing [region] —

children.text: cchalamayaḥ striyaḥ kas tyajen niśi? ||JGc_1,25.20||
children.translated_text: what deceitful man would abandon women at night?' || (JGc 1,25.20)

'What more is there to say, or what could be expressed? | Even a blink here in <s>Vraja</s> is suppressed! | How then could we — those <s>gopīs</s> — | possibly not be angry there?' || (JGc 1,25.19) —
'We who have been bound by the net of Your expansive song,

children.text: prahasitaṃ priya prema-vīkṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Your laughter, O beloved, Your loving glances,

children.text: vihasitādikaṃ valgu-lakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Your smiling and such — of beautiful character —

children.text: bṛhad uraḥ śriyo dhāma vīkṣyate
children.translated_text: Your broad chest, the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — is beheld;

children.text: nija-vimūḍhatāsmābhir īkṣyate ||JGc_1,25.21||
children.translated_text: [yet] our own bewilderment is [all that] is perceived by us!' || (JGc 1,25.21)

children.text: dina-laye' laka-dhvāntam ekataḥ
children.translated_text: 'At the close of day, on one side the darkness of [Your] curls,

children.text: prasṛta-gorajaḥ sandhyam anyataḥ |
children.translated_text: on the other, the twilight of the spreading cow-dust —

children.text: mukhatayā mataṃ yāminīśvaraṃ
children.translated_text: by way of Your face, presenting what is regarded as the lord of the night (the moon),

children.text: darśayan muhur yacchasi smaram ||JGc_1,25.22||
children.translated_text: You repeatedly bestow the Love-god (<s>Smara</s>)!' || (JGc 1,25.22)

children.text: sva-rati-vṛddhito' nanya-kāṅkṣiṇī
children.translated_text: 'Desiring none other, augmented by love for You —

children.text: bhavati vaṃśikā yatra sākṣiṇī |
children.translated_text: where the flute is the witness —

children.text: tam adhara-dravaṃ śoka-nāśanaṃ
children.translated_text: that nectar-flow of the lower lip, the destroyer of sorrow —

children.text: vitara vīra bhoḥ prāṇadāśanam ||JGc_1,25.23||
children.translated_text: bestow it, O hero, as nourishment for our life-breaths!' || (JGc 1,25.23)

children.text: iti tu yat tvayā kāma-kalpanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'That romantic imagining that You [create] —

children.text: kila kalābalāt tac ca kalpanam |
children.translated_text: through the power of art, that is [mere] fancy;

children.text: vayam anārataṃ sneha-bhāvanāḥ
children.translated_text: we who are constantly disposed to affection —

children.text: katham ayāmahe jātu kāmanāḥ? ||JGc_1,25.24||
children.translated_text: how could we possibly become desiring [mere fancy]?' || (JGc 1,25.24)

children.text:
prakaṭatā tu te goṣṭha-vāsināṃ
vṛjina-nāśinī prāṇa-bhāsinām |
vitara naḥ sakṛt tvat-spṛhā-yujāṃ
yad iha sūdanaṃ snigdha-hṛd-rujām ||JGc_1,25.25|| [rājahaṃsī]
children.translated_text: 'Your manifestation to the dwellers of the cow-settlement — | destroyer of sin, illuminator of their life-breaths — | bestow upon us, who are joined with longing for You, | that which would heal the ailments of [our] tender hearts!' || (JGc 1,25.25) [rājahaṃsī]

children.text: tad etad udgāya tad apy etad ity āhuḥ-yat te sujāta-caraṇāmburuhaṃ [BhP 10.31.19] ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Having sung that, they also recited this — namely, 'Your well-born lotus-feet —' [BhP 10.31.19] and so forth.

children.text: atra cedaṃ gadyam-yat kila kamalataḥ komalatā-yugalaṃ tava caraṇa-yugalaṃ stanāv anu snehataḥ saṃhananāyehamānāś ca vayaṃ tāv atikarkaśāv iti tarkataś ca stambhamānāḥ, śanair eva tayos tad dadhīmahīti vāñchāmaḥ | tad aho, kaṭhina-manastayā duraṭām aṭavīm anughaṭayati tvayi kūrpādibhis tat kiṃ na vyathate? kintu vyathata eva, yatas tad-bhāvanā-juṣāṃ bhavad-ekāyuṣām asmākaṃ manasi tan maṅkṣu saṅkrāmati | tasmāt tad aṭanam evāsmākaṃ hṛt-pīḍā, tal-lālanam eva tac-chamanam iti tal-lālanam eva dehīti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here is this prose [commentary]: 'That pair of Your feet — more tender than the lotus — we, desiring to clasp them upon our breasts out of affection, yet hesitating from the thought that they are exceedingly rough [for those tender feet], gently wish: "let us just hold them." Ah then, when You, with hard-hearted resolve, traverse the difficult forest path, do those [feet] not suffer pain from stones and the like? Indeed they do suffer, for that [pain], felt in the imagination of us whose sole life is You, instantly transmits itself to our hearts. Therefore, that walking itself is our heart's torment, and the soothing of those [feet] alone is its remedy — so the meaning is: "give us that soothing [of Your feet]."'

children.text: tad evaṃ sati-
children.translated_text: This being so —

children.text:
gīter āsīd vipariṇamanaṃ tarhi tāsāṃ vilāpas
tasyāpy uccai ruditam iti yan nādbhutaṃ tat tu tāsu |
kṛṣṇaṃ draṣṭuṃ prabhavati balād yasya tṛṣṇātidhṛṣṇak
tasyānyasyāpy ahaha śatadhā dṛśyate tat tad atra ||JGc_1,25.26|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: 'The song of those [gopīs] then transformed into lamentation, | and that [lamentation] further into loud weeping — this is not surprising in them; | for the thirst that audaciously overpowers [them] to behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — | ahaha — that and other [emotions] are seen here a hundredfold!' || (JGc 1,25.26) [mandākrāntā]

children.text: atha tathā masṛṇam asṛṇikam aśru nudatīṣu rudatīṣu sudatīṣu, tad-anuṣaṅgata eva tamasaḥ saṅgataḥ kramaśas tan niśamayan niśāmayan mura-śamanaḥ svaka-nayana-salila-kalilatayā nayana-lakṣeṇāpy alakṣitaḥ sahasā mahasāvṛtaḥ sarvāsāṃ madhyam adhyāsitavān, ambarāvṛtatayā sva-prathām āvṛtavāṃś ca |
children.translated_text: Then, as those beautiful-teethed women shed soft, warm tears, weeping — by the very continuity of that [weeping], gradually observing the darkness's approach, the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, his own eyes blurred with tears, invisible even to the perception of [their] eyes, suddenly enveloped by splendor, took his seat in the midst of all of them, concealing his own glory by being covered in [dark] garments.

children.text: ekā tu tatra tasya manāg āgamanādhigama-kamana-nayanāpi pūrvavad idam apūrva-sphuraṇa-puraskṛtam iti kevalaṃ kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇety alaṃ kala-kalatayā kalaṃ kalayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And one [gopī] there, though her eyes were just beginning to apprehend the faint sign of his arrival, as before — prefaced by an unprecedented flash [of recognition] — merely intoned 'Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa!' in a beautiful, melodious murmur.

children.text: ākarṇita-tad-varṇa-karṇāś ca vara-varṇinyas tan-nirṇāyaka-svābhyarṇa-tan-nirvarṇanās tūrṇam eva pūrṇatām avāpuḥ |
children.translated_text: And the excellent women, whose ears had drunk in the description of his qualities, through the examination of their own proximity to its determinant, swiftly attained fullness!

children.text: mahāghana-ghanāghana-ghana-saṅgamān nidāgha-drāghīyastayātihrasva-doghā hradinya iva | ubhayatra hi gata-prāya-jīvanatābhiprāyam āgatā |
children.translated_text: Like river-ponds whose yielding has been rendered extremely short by the prolonged summer heat, from the encounter with the dense, massive rain-clouds. For in both cases, the purport of having arrived with life nearly departed [is the meaning].

children.text:
tan-nirvarṇanaṃ ca, yathā-
āvis tāsu babhūva narma tad iti vyañjan viyujyāpi sa
smeraḥ saṅkucad anantaraṃ svam adhiyan pītāmbara-prāvṛtaḥ |
kartuṃ sad vinayaṃ srag-aṃśu-yugalaṃ hasta-dvayenāmṛśan
sragvī manmatha-manmatha-sthitir atiśrīṇām gatiḥ śrīpatiḥ ||JGc_1,25.27|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And the examination [of his appearance], as follows:
That playful charm then became manifest among them — expressing it, even while separating [from them],
he was smiling; then, contracting, immediately covering himself, clad in his yellow garment,
in order to perform proper modesty, touching with both hands the two ends of his garland —
the garlanded one, whose state was that of the enchanter of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) — the destination of supreme beauties — <s>Śrīpati</s> (the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>)! ||25.27|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
tataś ca-
priyas tyāga-vrīḍād vidadhad iva tāṭasthyam abhitaḥ
sa tābhiḥ kāntābhis tvaritataram āsādi paritaḥ |
samudraḥ saṅkocaṃ samaya-kalitaṃ ced valayate
tadā nadyaḥ sadyaś capala-gatitāṃ sannidadhati ||JGc_1,25.28|| [śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text:
And then:
The beloved, as if maintaining neutrality on all sides from the shame of [having caused their] abandonment,
was surrounded on all sides by those beloved women with the greatest haste;
just as when the ocean contracts at the appointed time,
then the rivers immediately manifest their swiftly flowing course [toward him]! ||25.28|| [<s>śikhariṇī</s>]

children.text: tatrāhaṃ-prathamikayā samupetāsu tāsu prathamataḥ śrī-parāśareṇa kathitā kācit, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, among those who had arrived with the priority of 'I first,' first the one described by the glorious <s>Parāśara</s> (<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>), a certain one, as follows:

children.text:
kācid ālokya govindam
āyāntaṃ atiharṣitā |
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti kṛṣṇeti
prāha nānyad udairayat ||JGc_1,25.29|| [ViP 5.13.43] iyaṃ bhadrā-nāmnī |
children.translated_text:
A certain one, seeing <s>Govinda</s>
coming, exceedingly overjoyed,
said '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!'
and uttered nothing else! ||25.29|| [ViP 5.13.43] This is the one named <s>Bhadrā</s>.

children.text: atha śrī-bādarāyaṇinā varṇitā varṇyate-
children.translated_text: Now, the one described by the glorious son of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>) is presented:

children.text:
kācit karaṃ murārāter
ācacāra nijāñjalau |
nava-pallava-pātrāntar
yathā kamala-tallajam ||JGc_1,25.30|| [anuṣṭubh] eṣā candrāvalī |
children.translated_text:
A certain one placed the hand of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>
in her own joined palms,
as if [placing] a lotus-stalk
within a vessel of fresh leaves! ||25.30|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>] This is <s>Candrāvalī</s>.
Likewise,
a certain one placed his lotus-foot
upon her breasts under a pretext,
as if performing the worship of <s>Śiva</s>,
having obtained the fulfillment of her desire! ||25.31|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>] This is <s>Padmā</s>.
Likewise,
a certain slender one received with joined palms
his chewed betel-remnant;
when she did that, she acted
as if she were the vessel of his passion! ||25.32|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>] This is <s>Śaivyā</s>.

children.text:
tathā,
kācit tad-aṅghri-kamalaṃ
vyājato kucayor dadhe |
labdha-vāñchita-niṣpattiḥ
kurvatīva śivārcanam ||JGc_1,25.31|| [anuṣṭubh] eṣā padmā |
tathā,
kācid añjalināgṛhṇāt
tanvī tāmbula-carvitam |
yadā tadīya-rāgasya
pātrīvācarati sma sā ||JGc_1,25.32|| [anuṣṭubh] iyaṃ śaivyā |
children.translated_text: This is not a duplicate segment.

children.text:
tathā,
kācid dadhāra tad-bāhuṃ
aṃse candana-rūṣitam |
yā dehataḥ snehataś ca
vyānañja sva-samarthatām ||JGc_1,25.33|| [anuṣṭubh] seyaṃ śyāmalā vāmataḥ |
tathā,
apagamita-nimeṣā yā tu tasyāsyam abjaṃ
nayana-yugam alīndra-dvandvam uccair apīpyat |
avakalitam akārṣīd rūpakaṃ tat tad eṣā
rasa-rasana-vibhūter jigyatus te tu yad yat ||JGc_1,25.34|| [mālinī] asau lalitā |
children.translated_text:
Likewise,
a certain one bore his arm upon her shoulder,
smeared with sandalwood,
she who, by body and by affection,
manifested her own capability! ||25.33|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>] This is <s>Śyāmalā</s>, on the left side.
Likewise,
she who, with unblinking eyes, drank deeply
his lotus-face with the pair of her eyes — twin bee-kings —
perceiving, she fashioned that very figure of speech — this is she,
through whom the glory of the <s>rasa</s> of aesthetic relish conquered whatever it conquered! ||25.34|| [<s>mālinī</s>] That is <s>Lalitā</s>.

children.text:
tathā,
tasmin kāpy avaloka-mātra-balaval lajjā-prasajjan-manā
mīlan-netratayā vicitra-pulakā citrāyamāṇā sthitā |
tām antar-valita-priyāṃ prati mamāścaryaṃ viyoga-sthiter
madhye yogam ihāpi bhogam itavaty eṣeti yā cintyate ||JGc_1,25.35|| [śārdūla]
eṣā khalu viśākhā |
children.translated_text:
Likewise,
a certain one, her mind overwhelmed by modesty powerful from mere sight of him,
with closing eyes and variegated horripilation, stood there in a wondrous state;
regarding her — that beloved one turned inward — my wonder is this:
that in the midst of the state of separation, she attained here also the enjoyment of union —
thus she who is contemplated is this one! ||25.35|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
This indeed is <s>Viśākhā</s>.

children.text:
tathā,
premā kopaṃ prasavati vṛthāpy astram atrāsti netraṃ
tac ca sthānād acalam api sad vidhyad udbhāti dūram |
vedhaś cāsau vraṇam api vinā śrīhareḥ kleśadaḥ syād
evaṃ yasyāḥ kim api caritaṃ tām imāṃ varṇayet kaḥ? ||JGc_1,25.36|| [mandākrāntā]
asau tu śrī-rādhā, tā etāḥ sammukhataḥ |

tathā,
kṛṣṇa-meghāgamollāsa-
pallavad-vadana-śriyaḥ |
sarvāś ca labdha-parvāṇaḥ
sadyaḥ siddhāḥ punar navāḥ ||JGc_1,25.37|| [anuṣṭubh] etāḥ sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text:
Likewise,
all [the <s>gopīs</s>], their face-beauty blossoming with joy at the arrival of the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-cloud,
having obtained their festive occasion, at once accomplished, and yet ever new! ||25.37|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>] These were on all sides.

children.text:
atiparimiti-śobhā-bhājanaṃ kṛṣṇa-rūpaṃ
nayad anupama-kāntiṃ yauvataṃ tad vireje |
idam upamiti-śūnyaṃ yat tu kāvyaṃ samāptaṃ
sa iha na mama doṣas tadd hi tattvaṃ tathaiva ||JGc_1,25.38|| [mālinī]
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> form, the vessel of beauty surpassing all measure,
and the womanhood bearing incomparable radiance — together they shone;
this which is devoid of simile — that the poem is concluded —
that is not my fault here, for truth itself is exactly thus! ||25.38|| [<s>mālinī</s>]

children.text: tad evaṃ tāsāṃ tasya ca parasparaṃ parama-madana-mada-prada-vadana-nayana-nilaya-līlayā candra-cakora-śīlatā latāvad utphullatāṃ gatā |
children.translated_text: Thus, by the mutual play dwelling in the supremely love-maddening faces and eyes of those [<s>gopīs</s>] and of him — their moon-and-<s>cakora</s>-bird nature blossomed forth like a vine.

children.text: tathā ca kṣaṇa-katipaye labdha-kṣaṇa-pracaye tāḥ sādaram ādāya, jala-jāta-jāta-samīraṇa-samīra-saraṇi-taraṇijā-taralatara-taraṅga-raṅga-nibha-nīra-sanīḍa-tīra-sarasaika-saikata-pulināntaraṃ nirvrīḍaṃ krīḍann eva vṛndāvana-devaḥ sevayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And then, in a few moments, having gained an accumulation of moments, taking them with affection, the lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, playing without shame, resorted to the sandy expanse of a single pleasant sandbank on the shore near the nest of waters — resembling the sport of waves, exceedingly tremulous, of the <s>Yamunā</s>, born of the wind-breeze born from the lotus-born [breezes].

children.text: tad eva khalu praśasta-bhaṅga-saṅgha-lakṣeṇa hasta-lakṣeṇa parama-dhanyayā svayam eva ravi-deva-kanyayā kañja-kiñjalka-piñja-latā-mañjula-gandha-gandhavāha-parirabdha-komala-sitābhra-śubhra-bālukābhir atiniścita-citta-yācitam, tatra ca śārada-sudhākara-kara-nikara-sudhā-liptatayā dūrato' pi tamastoma-śamanaṃ, jala-sthala-kusuma-samudayāmodā-moda-madita-mukhara-madhukara-madhurī-kṛtam urīkṛtavān |
children.translated_text: That [sandbank] indeed, by the supremely fortunate daughter of the sun-god (<s>Yamunā</s>) herself — with her exceedingly fine sandy stretches, lovely with creepers fragrant as lotus-pollen, embraced by breezes carrying fragrance, soft as white clouds, bright and white — was offered as earnestly entreated by the mind. And there, being smeared from afar with the nectar of the rays of the autumnal moon, [the place] was a dispeller of the mass of darkness even from a distance, and was made melodious by the buzzing of bees intoxicated by the collective fragrance of water and land flowers — [all this] he accepted.

children.text: urīkṛte ca tasmin paramādeye nādeye puline, smita-vilasita-netraḥ sva-nāmnā sita-śata-patra-netraḥ sarvāsām arvācīna-vayasāṃ savayasāṃ sva-hasta-vinyasta-praśasta-kuṅkuma-grasta-nava-stana-vastra-vistṛtī-kṛta-svastikāsanas tatra stotra-bhaṅgī-saṅgīta-kalā-raṅga-bhūmitām avāpa sa tāpa-nodanaḥ | yathā,
children.translated_text: And when that supremely desirable sandbank by the river had been accepted, the remover of sorrow — with eyes playful with smiles, bearing the name 'white-hundred-petalled-eyed' by his own name — having placed with his own hand on the fresh breast-cloths of all the young women of his own age, the excellent <s>kuṅkuma</s> paste, with their garments spread out in the cross-legged posture, attained the status of a stage-ground for the art of song-compositions in the form of hymns. As follows:

children.text:
ūrdhvaṃ glaur ātapatraṃ talam anu pulinaṃ hīra-cūrṇācitāṅgaṃ
śrīmat-pīṭhaṃ samantāt kusuma-vana-śataṃ toraṇānīva yasya |
taṃ divya-svarṇa-varṇa-vraja-kulaja-ramā-rāji-vibhrāji-dehaṃ
sneha-śrī-kāmya-gehaṃ hari-maṇi-ruciraṃ prāṇa-nāthaṃ smarāmi ||JGc_1,25.39||[sragdharā]

tataś ca vṛndāvana-sevikābhir vṛndā-pradhāna-kānana-devikābhiḥ parama-prayatna-pālya-mālya-divya-gandha-sandha-candra-candana-madhura-madhu-madānukūla-tāmbūlādyaṃ dadānābhir, muhūrtārdhaṃ vardhamāna-parihāsa-vilāsaṃ preyasī-sahitaḥ preyān mahita-mahattayā śuśubhe |
children.translated_text: And then, by the servitor-women of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — the forest-goddesses headed by <s>Vṛndā</s> — who were offering divine garlands tended with supreme care, blended fragrant pastes of moon-sandalwood, sweet honey-wine suitable for intoxication, betel and the like — for half a <s>muhūrta</s>, the beloved one, accompanied by his beloveds, with play of increasing jest, shone in honored greatness.

children.text: śobhamānaś ca nigūḍha-mānābhir amūbhir vraja-camūru-dṛgbhiḥ saṃvādam akpta |
children.translated_text: And while shining, he held a conversation with those large-thighed women of <s>Vraja</s>, who bore concealed pride.

children.text: tataś ca tāsāṃ vṛthā-parityāga-doṣa-labdha-poṣa-roṣa-mayābhiprāyakatayā jātaṃ citta-śoṣaṃ moṣaṃ nayantīnāṃ toṣa-prāyaṃ vyañjayantīnām anunaya-garbha-nānā-vinoda-sandarbha-vārtāṃ vartayati tasmin,
children.translated_text: Then, as they were leading their mental anguish — born of the nourishment of the fault of their vain abandonment — to oblivion, while manifesting a predominantly pleased [demeanor], when he was conducting a variety of conciliatory and amusing exchanges pregnant with soothing intent,

children.text:
kācit karaṃ caraṇam asya parā tathorum
anyāvalagnam aparā mṛdu mardayantī |
antar nigūḍha-kupitā bahir accha-bhāvā
bhrū-locana-prasṛmara-smitam abhyuvāca ||JGc_1,25.40|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text:
a certain one [grasped] his hand, another likewise his thigh,
another, leaning close, softly massaging [him],
inwardly concealing anger, outwardly showing transparent emotion,
spoke with a smile spreading through her brow, eyes, and expression! ||25.40|| [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: kecid evaṃ ca varṇayanti-
children.translated_text: And some describe it thus:

children.text:
nayana-valanaiś cillī-cālair nigūḍha-mṛdu-smitair
lalita-lapitair antar-bhaṅgair bahir valitārjavaiḥ |
catura-manasas tasmin kṛṣṇaṃ priyaṃ vaśa-vartinaṃ
praṇaya-nayataḥ prāhuḥ pṛkta-prahelikam aṅganāḥ ||JGc_1,25.41|| [hariṇī]
children.translated_text:
With rolling glances, with the play of eyelashes, with concealed gentle smiles,
with graceful murmurs, with inner obliquity and outer directness —
those clever-minded women, governing that beloved <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bringing him under their sway,
spoke to him in loving discourse interlaced with riddles! ||25.41|| [<s>hariṇī</s>]

children.text: ayi catura-pura-purandara! prahelikā-kalikām ekāṃ vikāśaya | yathā,
children.translated_text: O clever lord of the city! Open one bud of a riddle. As follows:

children.text:
bhajanti bhajataḥ kecin nānye' nyān eva kecana |
ubhayāṃś cāpare ke' pi nobhayān agatīn pare ||JGc_1,25.42|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Some serve those who serve [them]; some others [serve] only others;
still others [serve] both; and others [serve] neither — the shelterless ones!' ||25.42|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇas tu citte tad avabudhyābhidhatte sma-
children.translated_text: But Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having understood that in his mind, declared:

children.text:
arthajñāḥ kṛta-hantāro dhārmikā dharma-gāthinaḥ |
vimūḍha-pūrṇa-muktāś ca dayāvantaś ca te kramāt ||JGc_1,25.43|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'Those who know meaning, doers of deeds, righteous ones, speakers of <s>dharma</s>,
and those who are deluded, fulfilled, liberated, and compassionate — [they are] respectively [in that order]!' ||25.43|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tac chrutvā ca parasparam asaraṇa-cillibhir amūbhiś cillī-vallī-vellanenedaṃ jñāpitam-
children.translated_text: And hearing that, those [<s>gopīs</s>], with the flickering of their desperate eyebrow-creeper-waving, communicated this to one another:

children.text:
cāturībhir iha nas tu karṣato
dharma-dhāma diśataḥ samujjhataḥ |
nirdayaṃ punar amuṣya śiṣyate
yena nāsmad-atiduḥkham īkṣyate ||JGc_1,25.44|| [rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text:
'He who attracts us here with his cleverness,
who bestows the abode of <s>dharma</s> and abandons [us] completely —
of this merciless one, what remains
is that by which our extreme sorrow is not perceived!' ||25.44|| [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]

children.text: atra cāturībhiḥ iti tasyānarthajñatā, dharma-dhāma diśataḥ ity adhārmikatā, tad-ubhayābhyāṃ tad-ubhaya-rahitatā, punaḥ cāturībhiḥ iti vimūḍhatā, tābhir nas tu karṣataḥ iti pūrṇatā muktatā ca | tatra svakṛtānuddeśena kṛta-hantṛtā ca niṣiddhā | tyāge cāsmad-duḥkha-vīkṣaṇābhāvena nirdayatā tu śeṣiteti śliṣyati |
children.translated_text: And here: 'with cleverness' indicates his lack of understanding of true meaning; 'bestowing the abode of <s>dharma</s>' indicates his unrighteousness; by both of those, his freedom from both [defects is indicated]; again, 'with cleverness' indicates his delusion; 'attracting us by those means' indicates his fullness and liberation. Therein, the killing of deeds done for one's own purpose is also negated. And in [the case of] abandonment, mercilessness is what remains, since our sorrow is not perceived [by him] — thus the <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) works.

children.text: sa tu tad evam avabudhya sva-śuddhy-avagamanāya punar uvāca-
children.translated_text: But he, having understood that thus, in order to make them understand his own purity, spoke again:

children.text: nāhaṃ teṣāṃ sadṛg api tu māṃ lubdham ūhadhvam ṛddhau
children.translated_text: 'I am not even equal to those [reciprocators] — but consider me as one desirous of prosperity!

children.text: premṇas tāṃ tad-viṣaya-virahaṃ hanta kṛtvāpi vaśmi |
children.translated_text: Even having created separation from that object of love — alas! — I endure, through love!

children.text: yuṣmān vācyaṃ kim iha mayakā māyitāvat-pratīter
children.translated_text: What here should be said to you? Of a magician, [one expects] the perception of magic!

children.text: etad yan me vyasanam asakṛn māṃ ca duḥkhākaroti ||JGc_1,25.45||
children.translated_text: This which is my calamity — it causes me suffering repeatedly!' ||25.45||

children.text:
yūyaṃ hitvā nikhilam aniśaṃ kāmayadhve paraṃ māṃ
mat-kāmyās tu prayuta-niyutaṃ prema-bhedena santi |
tasmān na pratyupakṛti-kalāleśa-kalpaṃ vidhātuṃ
śaknomīti prathayata nijaiḥ sad-guṇair eva tuṣṭim ||JGc_1,25.46|| [mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text:
'You, having abandoned everything, constantly desire me alone;
but those desired by me, through the differentiation of love, exist in millions and tens of millions!
Therefore, I am unable to fashion even a fraction of a particle of reciprocation —
so manifest your satisfaction through your own good qualities!' ||25.46|| [<s>mandākrāntā</s>]

children.text: tad evam anavadyaṃ kṛṣṇa-vadyam avadhārya-
children.translated_text: Thus, having grasped this faultless speech of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text:
manojñatvena na paraṃ surūpatvam ihānvabhūt |
budhatvenāpi kṛṣṇasya sa-tṛṣṇo' yaṃ priyā-gaṇaḥ ||JGc_1,25.47|| [anuṣṭubh] ||
children.translated_text:
Not merely his handsomeness was experienced here as charming,
but also his wisdom — this beloved-host of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> remained thirsting! ||25.47|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: tatra gīrvāṇīnām ākāśataḥ parihāsavāṇīyam-
children.translated_text: There, the jesting voice of the divine women (<s>Apsarases</s>) from the sky:

children.text:
rucim anu kuṭilākṣīṇāṃ stutim anu jihmaṃ bruvāṇānām |
mādhava gopa-vadhūnāṃ guṇataḥ kasmān mudaṃ tanuṣe ||JGc_1,25.48|| [upagīti]
children.translated_text:
'Following the inclination of the sidelong-glancing ones, following the praise of the crookedly speaking ones —
O <s>Mādhava</s>, why do you delight in the qualities of the cowherd women?' ||25.48|| [<s>upagīti</s>]

children.text:
sa eko jayatān māna-mātaṅgo vraja-subhruvām |
hariṇā nirjitasyāpi yasya vīryād bibhīyate ||JGc_1,25.49|| [anuṣṭubh] ||
children.translated_text:
'Let that one elephant of pride of the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s> be victorious!
Even though conquered by <s>Hari</s>, from its valor, [he] is afraid!' ||25.49|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: atha samāpanam-
children.translated_text: Now, the conclusion:

children.text:
vaidagdhī-digdha-buddhīddhaḥ so' yaṃ rādhe sakhā tava |
alambhūṣṇuṃ tatra mene yas tvāṃ tuṣṇīṃ sthitām api ||JGc_1,25.50|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, this companion of yours, his intellect ablaze, anointed with amorous cleverness (<s>vaidagdhī</s>),
considered even you, who stood silent, as unobtainable!' ||25.50|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
vipralambhana-stambhana-śrī-kṛṣṇa-lambhanam nāma
pañcaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||25||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the twenty-fifth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
"The Winning of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> through the Arrest of Separation"
||25||

children.text: atha ṣaḍviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the twenty-sixth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter)

children.text: rāsa-vilāsa-prasāraṇam
children.translated_text: "The Expansion of the Sport of the <s>Rāsa</s> [Dance]"

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text:
suvacanam aghaśatroḥ śṛṇvatī śreṇir āsāṃ virahajanitaduḥkhaṃ pūrvasiddhaṃ vyadhāvīt | param iha na tad eva vyādhunot kintu śaṅkā- ntaram api yad amaṃsta spaṣṭam āyattam etam ||JGc_1,26.1|| [mālinī]
 [2] tad evam amūr utphullavadanakañjasadana-mañjunayanakhañjarīṭāḥ sa punar mañjulam ābhāṣate sma-
 yuṣmatkṛte sma sucirān manasāsmi dūya- mānena yūyam api tastha madartham eva | tasyātha durlabhatamasya manorathasya prāptāv ihānurahasaṃ maham ācarāma ||JGc_1,26.2|| [vasantatilakā]
 [3] sa ca rāsarūpa eva nirūpyate | tathā hi-
children.translated_text:
The host of those [<s>gopīs</s>], hearing the excellent speech of the enemy of <s>Agha</s>, chased away the sorrow born of separation, previously established;
but here it did not merely shake off that [sorrow], but also another [fear] — the apprehension
that she clearly considered him as dependent [on her]! ||26.1|| [<s>mālinī</s>]
[2] Thus, those whose eyes were like <s>khañjarīṭa</s> birds dwelling in the abode of their blossoming lotus-faces — to them again he spoke charmingly:
'For your sake, I have long been anguished in mind;
and you too have remained for my sake alone!
Of that most unattainable desire,
now that attainment [has come], let us here celebrate the festival in secret!' ||26.2|| [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]
[3] And that [festival] is to be determined as the <s>Rāsa</s> [dance] itself. For thus:

children.text:
dīpaḥ śāradabhūripūritaśaśī yatrāsti vṛndāvanaṃ raṅgaḥ śrīvrajanāyikāḥ svayam imā yūyaṃ kalākovidāḥ | taṃ cemaṃ samayaṃ sametya muditaḥ so' haṃ hariḥ kiṃ paraṃ kartāsmi kṣaṇam antarā tam api kiṃ rāsaṃ vinā bhoḥ priyāḥ ||JGc_1,26.3|| [śārdūla]
 [4] iti kṣīṇatamā vrajajaladhisambhavākṣīṇacandramāḥ sarvā api tāś cakorākṣīr aṣaḍakṣīṇayugapad liṅganādinā sukhalakṣalakṣitīkṛtya, balavad ādṛtya, rāsanṛtya-vidhaye nirjambālam astambajālam abandhuraṃ bandhuraṃ kamalabandhujāpulinam āvṛtya, parasparakarasaṃvalanayā valayākārāś cakāra |
children.translated_text:
"The lamp is the autumn's abundantly full moon; the stage is <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;
the leading actresses of glorious <s>Vraja</s> are yourselves, skilled in the arts!
Having met this occasion, I, that <s>Hari</s>, am delighted — what more
shall I do even for a moment without the <s>rāsa</s> [dance], O beloveds?" ||26.3|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
[4] Thus, the most diminished [moon] — the unwaning moon born of the ocean of <s>Vraja</s> — simultaneously embracing all those <s>cakorī</s>-eyed ones with a six-fold embrace and the like, making them marked with a hundred-fold happiness, honoring them greatly, for the purpose of the <s>rāsa</s> dance, he formed them into a circle — encompassing a mire-free, pillar-less, not-uneven yet beautiful lotus-companion sandbank — by the joining of their mutual hands.

children.text:
kṛte ca valaye-
 kṛṣṇāyāḥ pulinaṃ gatena ramaṇenāpūri kāmas tadā tenāmuṣya manas tathā pratipadaṃ tena dvayaṃ cakṣuṣoḥ | tenāṅgasphuradaṅganāsamudayas tenātha pūrvaṃ paraṃ sarvaṃ parva ca tad bruve kim aparaṃ nādyāpi viśrāmyati ||JGc_1,26.4|| [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]||

tad evaṃ sva-kalita-caye valaye vanamālī śobhānicayam upalabhamānaś cintayāmāsa-
upari yathojjvalam indor valayaṃ pulinaṃ tathā bhuvi ca | kintu kalaṅkas tasmin nirmala-ramaṇī-kulāny atra ||JGc_1,26.5|| [upagīti]
 [7] tad aho ! cāmīkara-maṇisarākāro' yaṃ ramaṇīya-ramaṇī-valayaḥ prati-yugma-madhyaṃ yadi mahāmara-katāyamāna-nāyaka-sambadhyamānatām ābadhnāti, tadā hṛdyatām āpadyate |
children.translated_text:
Thus, the garland-wearer, perceiving a treasure of splendor in the circle he himself had fashioned, reflected:
"Above, the circle of the moon is as brilliant as the sandbank below on the earth;
but in that [moon] there is a blemish, while here [there are] families of spotless beauties!" ||26.5|| [<s>upagīti</s>]
[7] "Ah! This circle of beautiful women, resembling a necklace of gold and jewels — if, at the center of each pair, it binds the union of the hero acting as a great immortal, then it attains charm!"

children.text:
tac ca tathāveśena mat-praveśena paraṃ sidhyatīti nidhāya sthitaḥ sann, akasmād yathā-manorathākāram evāvasthitavān, yathā svayam api katham iti tu na tat-prathanam avāpa | tataś ca-
 hari-hariṇākṣī-valitaṃ pulinaṃ tad valgu bhāti sma | sva-pratibimbenādād
yad vidhu-bimbāya sārūpyam ||JGc_1,26.6|| [upagīti]
 suhṛd indoḥ pulinaṃ tat- pulinasyābhūn nata-bhruvāṃ pracayaḥ | tat-pracayasya ca valanaṃ śrīyuta-gopāla-mūrtīnām ||JGc_1,26.7|| [āryā]
yatra ca,
paraspara-karāvali-grathita-maṇḍalī-maṇḍanīr anusvam abalā milann ubhayatas tadā mādhavaḥ | tadīya-bhujapāśyayā kalita-mṛṣṭa-pṛṣṭhas tathā tad-aṃsa-nihitātma-dor abhavad eṣa rāsodyame ||JGc_1,26.8|| [pṛthvī]
 gaurī-kṛṣṇau gaurī-kṛṣṇāv itthaṃ lakṣe lakṣe yugme | vṛttākāre vaṃśī-śaṃśī rādhā-saṅgī tasthau madhye ||JGc_1,26.9|| [vidyunmālā]
 rāsaṃ prārabhata svayaṃ harir asau kaiśorakaṃ mānayann ity evaṃ sa parāśaro' pi bhagavān prāvocad uccair yataḥ | tasmād gopa-vadhūbhir eva saphalaṃ taj-jātam itthaṃ tu me haṃho paśyata vacmi vā kim aparaṃ romṇāṃ ca jātaṃ mahaḥ ||JGc_1,26.10||[śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
 sa vividha-vanitā-vṛndair yadapi bahu-preyasī tadā jajñe | tadapi ca rādhā jñaptir manye tasyāparāḥ kṛtayaḥ ||JGc_1,26.11|| [āryā]
tad evam-
 anaṅgam aṅgena nijena sāṅgaṃ
kṛtvādhi-raṅga-kṣiti saṅgamayya | aṅgīcakārāṅga tam aṅga-hārair
navyāṅganā-saṅgama-maṅgalāya ||JGc_1,26.12|| [upajāti 11]
kalita-kanaka-bhāsaḥ smera-netrā vidhūti-
kṣubhita-valaya-vīthī-śiñjita-vyakta-tālāḥ | vividha-gati-vihārānaṅga-sārāṅga-hārā hari-hari-maṇi-mūrtīr antarā tā virejuḥ ||JGc_1,26.13|| [mālinī]
 tataś ca-
navīna-vinata-bhruvāṃ nija-navīna-kānta-cchavī- juṣāṃ naṭana-cāturī-kula-dhurīṇa-līlā-yujām | calad-valaya-śṛṅkhalāvalita-nūpurāṇāṃ dhvanir naṭādhva-nidhi-tālatāṃ dhvanayati sma yāvad divam ||JGc_1,26.14|| [pṛthvī]
rāse śiñjita-tāla-jālam udabhūt tadvad yathā khecarān apy ākṛkṣad aho vidūratarataḥ kṛtveva pūrva-sthitān | dyo-yānābhidha-mañca-sañcaya-gatā vādyaṃ ca gītaṃ ca ye sabhyatvaṃ ca samaṃ madād vidadhataḥ svaṃ nātra niścikyire ||JGc_1,26.15||[śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
 [9] tatra devīnāṃ sañjalpaḥ-paśya, paśya-
 hariṇā gānam āsādi gānena ramaṇī-kulam | ramaṇībhir atho gānaṃ gānena sa hariḥ punaḥ ||JGc_1,26.16|| [anuṣṭubh] pulinaṃ vilasat-kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sāliṅganāṅganaṃ kalaya | āṅganam abhinava-gītaṃ gītaṃ saṅgīta-saṅgi-saṅgītam ||JGc_1,26_17|| [gīti]
[10] tatra svayam ārambhe lāsya-sambheda eva jātaḥ | [11] tad yathābhinayaṃ yathā-
 aṅga-hāra-calad-aṅga-hāriṣu svāntahāri vilasadvihāriṣu | lāsya-kāriṣu ca lāsyam ācaran bhrū-naṭī-ghaṭita-netrā nartakāḥ ||JGc_1,26.18|| [rathoddhatā]
 [12] tauryatrika-śaurya-varāṇāṃ khecarāṇāṃ vādye tūdbhūte tāṇḍava-maṇḍalaṃ ca sābhinayam, yathā-
 udyad-dundubhi-maḍḍu-ḍiṇḍima-ḍamar-vādye mṛdaṅgaṃ gate vādye dyo-pada-vidya-vedya-nadane sadyo' tha vidyotite | te tarhy udbhaṭa-nāṭya-nīti-ghaṭanā-saṅghaṭṭa-niṣkuṇṭhatā- sūtkaṇṭhāḥ pada-pāṇi-kaṇṭha-kaṭi-sammoṭāli-koṭiṃ dadhuḥ ||JGc_1,26.19|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And having resolved that this could be accomplished supremely by his entering [between each pair] through [yogic] absorption, standing thus, suddenly, just as the form of his desire had been, so he stood — yet even he himself did not comprehend the 'how' of its manifestation. Then:
The sandbank encircled by <s>Hari</s> and the doe-eyed ones shone beautifully;
by its own reflection, it gave
to the orb of the moon a likeness! ||26.6|| [<s>upagīti</s>]
The sandbank was the friend of the moon;
of that sandbank, the assembly of women with arched brows [was the ornament];
and of that assembly, the encirclement
was [formed] of the glorious <s>Gopāla</s> forms! ||26.7|| [<s>āryā</s>]
And there:
The women who adorned the circle strung by the lines of each other's hands —
with each woman, <s>Mādhava</s> was present on both sides;
by the noose of their arms he was clasped upon his polished back, and likewise
his own arm was placed upon their shoulders — in the commencement of the <s>rāsa</s>! ||26.8|| [<s>pṛthvī</s>]
A fair one and a dark one, a fair one and a dark one — thus in each pair, in each hundred;
in the circular formation, the announcer of the flute, accompanied by <s>Rādhā</s>, stood in the center! ||26.9|| [<s>vidyunmālā</s>]
<s>Hari</s> himself commenced the <s>rāsa</s>, honoring [his] adolescence —
thus indeed the blessed <s>Parāśara</s> too spoke aloud, since:
"Therefore, it was accomplished fruitfully by the cowherd wives alone" — thus indeed I say:
what more? Behold — even the hairs [of my body] have produced a radiance! ||26.10|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
Even though, with the multifarious hosts of women, many beloveds then arose,
yet <s>Rādhā</s> was the [true] awareness — I consider the others [mere] manifestations! ||26.11|| [<s>āryā</s>]
Thus:
Having made <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Love) complete with his own body,
upon the stage-ground, having united [all] —
he accepted him (<s>Anaṅga</s>) with bodily gestures,
for the auspiciousness of the union with the new women! ||26.12|| [<s>upajāti</s>]
Possessing golden radiance, with smiling eyes, with bangles
on their trembling rows of wrists producing the rhythmic jingling of the beat,
with diverse gaits, playful — bearing Love's <s>sāraṅga</s> (deer-like) gestures —
between the jewel-like forms of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hari</s>, they shone! ||26.13|| [<s>mālinī</s>]
Then:
The sound of the bangles, chains, and anklets of those women
with freshly arched brows, adorned with their own fresh beloved's radiance,
skilled in the art of dance, joined in sport —
resounded the beat of the treasury of the dancer's path, up to heaven! ||26.14|| [<s>pṛthvī</s>]
In the <s>rāsa</s>, the network of jingling beats arose — such that it drew
even the sky-dwellers, ah! — as if making even those previously stationed far away;
those who, having ascended the platforms called celestial chariots, performed music, song,
and connoisseurship alike with exhilaration — did not consider their own [arts] here! ||26.15|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
[9] There, the conversation of the goddesses — 'Look, look!'
By <s>Hari</s>, singing was attained; by the singing, the host of beautiful women;
by the beautiful women, again the song; by the song, that <s>Hari</s> again! ||26.16|| [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]
Behold the sandbank shining with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with embracing women;
the courtyard with novel song — song joined with concerted music! ||26.17|| [<s>gīti</s>]
[10] There, at the very beginning, a <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance) fusion itself was produced. [11] And the acting, as follows:
Among those charming with swaying body-gestures, delightful in their radiant sport,
among those performing <s>lāsya</s>, he too performed <s>lāsya</s> —
the dancer with eyes framed by the acting of his brows! ||26.18|| [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]
[12] When the celestial beings — supreme in the heroism of the triple performing art — produced their music, the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance) circle arose with acting, as follows:
When the music of resounding <s>dundubhi</s>, <s>maḍḍu</s>, <s>ḍiṇḍima</s>, and <s>ḍamaru</s> drums proceeded,
when the <s>mṛdaṅga</s> music, the heavenly footwork-knowledge-audible dance, suddenly blazed forth,
then, with the shamelessness of the clash of bold dramatic conventions,
with eager throats, they produced myriads of beats of feet, hands, throat, and hip! ||26.19|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text:
tatra ca śastra-praśastānām iva teṣāṃ kṛta-hastakānāṃ punar lakṣyād acyava eva lakṣitaḥ | tathā hi-
 hitvā hitvāpy atra hastāli-bandhaṃ tālālambā hastakāni pradarśya | gaurī-śyāmā lāghavāt pūrṇamānā rāsollāse tadvad āsan punaś ca ||JGc_1,26.20|| [śālinī]
puṣpa-vṛndam apatan muhur muhuḥ kṛṣṇa-gaura-tanu-maṇḍalīm anu | vṛṣṭir ūrdhvam adharatra nīra-bhṛd vidyud-ālir iti yatra citratā ||JGc_1,26.21|| [rathoddhatā]
 [14] atra devā devyaś ca bhavya-bhāva-bhavān navya-paribhavāt kamalākṣaṃ sākṣād iva sambodhayantas tathā yoga-māyāyā yogataḥ paraṃ sva-sva-yogyam antaḥ samadhigamya ramyam idaṃ vādya-kolāhalāvṛtam ujjaguḥ |
children.translated_text:
And there, like those skilled in arms (<s>śastra</s>), their expert hand-gestures (<s>hastaka</s>) were observed as unfailing from the target. Thus:
Even though releasing the hand-chain here again and again, displaying hand-gestures sustained by the beat,
the fair and dark ones, from their lightness, maintaining their fullness,
were in the delight of the <s>rāsa</s> just as before, and again! ||26.20|| [<s>śālinī</s>]
Showers of flowers fell again and again upon the circle of dark and fair bodies;
rain above, the cloud-bearer below,
a row of lightning — such was the wonder there! ||26.21|| [<s>rathoddhatā</s>]
[14] Here, the gods and goddesses, from the auspicious emotion born of sublime feeling, from unprecedented astonishment, addressing the lotus-eyed one as if directly, and likewise, through the power of <s>Yogamāyā</s>, each having internally grasped what was fitting for themselves, they sang this delightful [song], enveloped in the tumult of music:

children.text:
tad etad ekīkṛtyānugīyate-
 jaya jaya sad-guṇa-sāra | jagati viśiṣṭaṃ kalayitum iṣṭaṃ gokula-lasad-avatāra ||a||dhruvam||kamala-bhaveśvara-vaikuṇṭheśvara-patnī-cintita-seva | rājasi rāse valita-vilāse nija-ramaṇībhir deva ||b|| naṭavat-parikara nikhila-kalādhara racita-paraspara-moda | āliṅgana-mukha-vitata-mahā-sukha vallava-vadhu-hṛta-toda ||c|| vyativīkṣaṇa-kṛta-sāttvika-parivṛta-maṇḍalam anu bahu-mūrte | vraja-taruṇī-gaṇa-racita-nayana-paṇa-sacita-vaśīkṛti-pūrte ||d|| caraṇa-kañja-dhṛti-kara-pallava-kṛti-cillī-valita-vihārān | madhya-bhaṅga-tati-maṇi-kuṇḍala-gati-pulaka-sveda-vikārān ||e|| kalayati bhavatā ghana-sāmyavatā taḍid iva sarvā lalanā | api vaḥ parimiti-taratamatām iti seyaṃ jñapayati tulanā ||f|| sumadhura-kaṇṭhe nṛtyotkaṇṭhe tava rati-mātra-prīte | tvat-sparśāmṛta-mada-caya-saṃvṛta-citte
bhāva-krīte ||g||
children.translated_text:
This is sung together as one:
"Victory, victory, O essence of true virtues! To behold the extraordinary in the world
is the desire — O radiant <s>avatāra</s> of <s>Gokula</s>!" ||a|| Refrain ||
"Served in the meditation of the consorts of the Lord born of the lotus (<s>Brahmā</s>), the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> —
you shine in the <s>rāsa</s>, in circling sport, with your own beautiful women, O Lord!" ||b||
"With an entourage like dancers, bearing all arts, creating mutual delight —
with the great happiness spread through embraces and faces, the remover of the cowherd wives' pain!" ||c||
"With mutual glances creating <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary emotional) [responses], around the circle, O one of many forms —
the bet of the eyes fashioned by the host of young women of <s>Vraja</s>, filled with the accomplishment of subjugation!" ||d||
"With the holding of lotus-feet, with the sprout-like gesture of hands, with the play of the movement of brows,
with the bending of the waist, the motion of jeweled earrings, the transformations of horripilation and perspiration!" ||e||
"By you, who possess the semblance of a cloud, all women [shine] like lightning;
and this comparison announces the gradation of your proportions!" ||f||
"O one of sweet throat, eager for dance, delighted by love alone —
whose hearts are enveloped by the accumulation of the intoxication of the nectar of your touch,
purchased by emotion!" ||g||

children.text: yuvatī-jāte gītaja-śātenāvṛta-viśva-prabhave | yas tvaṃ rājasi tat-sukha-bhāg asi nama etasmai prabhave ||h|| yā saha bhavatā vismayam avatā svara-jātīr atiśuddham | gāyati seyaṃ nikhilair geyaṃ kalayati nija-guṇa-ruddham ||i|| tata utkarṣaṃ valayita-harṣaṃ valayati yeyaṃ gāne | sā śrī-rādhā valitārādhā bhavatā kalitā māne ||j|| yeyaṃ rāse śramaja-vilāse vigalan-mallī-valayā | sā bhavad-aṃse lasad-avataṃse dharati karaṃ vara-kalayā ||k|| yā cāṃsaṃ pari bhuja-parighaṃ paricumbati tava sa-vinodam | hṛṣyati seyaṃ tan na gaṇeyaṃ yad roma ca sāmodam ||l||
children.translated_text:
"O one born among young women, surrounded by the hundreds born of song, whose universal power [is manifest] —
you who shine thus are the partaker of that happiness — homage to this Lord!" ||h||
"She who, with you who descend into wonder, sings the modes of melody in supreme purity —
she renders what is to be sung by all, restraining [it] by her own virtues!" ||i||
"Then, she who encircles the exaltation joined with delight in song —
she is Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, whose worship is encircled, held by you in honor!" ||j||
"She who, in the <s>rāsa</s>, in the sport born of fatigue, with her <s>mallī</s>-flower bracelet slipping —
she places her hand upon your shoulder, adorned with an ear-ornament, with a beautiful gesture!" ||k||
"And she who, around your shoulder, with the bar of her arm, kisses playfully —
she thrills — let me not count what [thrilling] arises even in the hair, with delight!" ||l||

children.text: cala-kuṇḍala-dhara gaṇḍa-mukura-vara samiṣa-sparśa-vidhāne | tāmbūla-drava-parivartād dravam ayase cumbana-dāne ||m|| eṣā nartana-kīrtana-vartana-śiñjita-jāta-sutālā | tava rāmānuja karam atulāmbujam iṣam ādhādd hṛdi bālā ||n||
children.translated_text:
"O bearer of trembling earrings, O one whose cheeks are excellent mirrors, in the act of mutual touching —
from the exchange of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) juice, you melt in the giving of kisses!" ||m||
"This young girl, having produced the proper rhythm of dancing, singing, and turning with jingling [ornaments],
O younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), placed your incomparable lotus[-like hand] as her treasure in her heart!" ||n||

children.text:
atha rāsa-krama-parivalita-śrama-vanitālambita-deha | parito-bhramaṇaka-gaṇa-viśramaṇaka samudita-parama-sneha ||o|| kavi-kṛta-niścaya-śubhra-yaśaś-caya-mālā-samudaya-hārin | jayajayajayajaya jayajayajayajaya jayajaya rāsa-vihārin ||p|| ||JGc_1,26.22|| | iti | [8 x 8 x 12]
 [16] rājasi rāse valita-vilāse ity uktaṃ rūpam evaṃ nirūpayanti-
 rūpaṃ yan nijanityasaubhagaśiroratnaṃ narākṛty asāv ānīyātra yadīyaśaktivibhavasyāgryāṃ sthitiṃ praikṣayat | citraṃ vismayate yataḥ svayam api svāśeṣasaṃveditā tasmin bhūṣaṇabhūṣaṇe' py adhur amūḥ śobhāṃ svayā śobhayā ||JGc_1,26.23||[śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[17] tad uktam, yan martya-līlaupāyikam [BhP 3.2.12] ity ādi, tatrātiśuśubhe [BhP 10.33.6] ity ādi ca |
 [18] tad evaṃ sati śrī-rādhikāyāṃ tu kaimutyam eva stutyaṃ jātam | [19] yuvatī-jāta ity ādāv evaṃ varṇayanti-
children.translated_text:
"Now, in the <s>rāsa</s>'s progression, with the fatigue of circling, leaning upon the women's bodies,
with the resting of the circling host, there arose supreme affection!" ||o||
"O one whose fame — a garland of pure radiance, established by poets —
is captivating in its assemblage:
victory, victory, victory, victory! Victory, victory, victory, victory! Victory, victory, O sportsman of the <s>rāsa</s>!" ||p|| ||26.22|| [8 × 8 × 12]
[16] 'You shine in the <s>rāsa</s>, in circling sport' — thus describing this form, they say:
The form that is the eternal crest-jewel of one's own beauty, which in a human guise
he brought here and displayed the foremost state of the splendor of his power —
wonderful, for even he himself, the knower of his own entirety, marvels!
Upon that [form] which is the ornament of ornaments, these [<s>gopīs</s>] too conferred splendor by their own splendor! ||26.23|| [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]
