[17] Thus it is said: 'That which is befitting the human <s>līlā</s>' [BhP 3.2.12] and so forth, and 'therein he was supremely resplendent' [BhP 10.33.6] and so forth.
[18] This being so, regarding Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s>, the praise that arose was indeed a fortiori. [19] Beginning with 'O one born among young women' and so forth, they describe thus:

children.text:
tāsāṃ vraja-kiśorīṇāṃ nityam aprasavātmanām | guṇaiḥ sa-prasavaiḥ pūrṇaṃ viśvam apy anvayair iva ||JGc_1,26.24|| [anuṣṭubh]
[20] yā saha bhavatā ity ādāv upaślokayanti ca-
 śarva-brahma-sureśa-mukhya-diviṣad-vṛndāni yad-gānataḥ śaśvan moham ayus tam eva dayitaṃ kṛtvānugaṃ yā jagau | sārdhaṃ tena parāś camat-kṛti-parās tāṃ nirmimāṇām api vyarthīkṛtya vivikta-rāga-valanāṃ vandāmahe rādhikām ||JGc_1,26.25|| [śārdūla]
 [21] tām evoddiśya cala-kuṇḍala ity ādāv ca kavayanti-
 tad-adhara-rasam ācāntaṃ prāg akṛta dvir yad eṣa tad yuktam | dvija-saṃskṛta-tāmbūlaṃ katham adyād anyathā tasyāḥ ||JGc_1,26.26|| [āryā]
kiṃ ca-
kṛṣṇaḥ snehasya mūlaṃ kila lasati vapū-rūpam ity evam asmiṃs tādṛg nanda-vrajāntar-jana-sadasi sadaivānu-bhūti-pracāraḥ |
so' yaṃ yāsām amaṃsta praṇaya-maya-ṛṇāny ātmani preyasīnāṃ tāsām apy ūrdhvam ūrdhva-prathita-nidhi-maṇiṃ rādhikām eva naumi ||JGc_1,26.27|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text:
Of those maidens of <s>Vraja</s>, who are eternally without [physical] birth,
the entire world is filled by their qualities — which are [themselves] productive —
as if by their lineages! ||26.24|| [anuṣṭubh]
[20] And in the verse beginning with 'she who with you,' they also compose:
'The hosts of divine beings headed by <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Sureśa</s> (<s>Indra</s>) —
who always became bewildered by his singing — she sang, having made that very beloved her follower;
along with him, the others too — intent upon wonder — even fashioning her [imitation],
yet rendered futile [by comparison] — we worship <s>Rādhikā</s>, of solitary, vibrant passion!' ||26.25|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[21] And composing [a verse] directed at her [<s>Rādhā</s>] in the one beginning with 'trembling earring':
'That he had previously drunk the nectar of her lip and did not do so a second time — that is fitting;
how could he eat the betel already sanctified by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> twice — hers [being already sacred]?' ||26.26|| [āryā]
Moreover:
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed the root of love, shining forth in bodily form — thus,
such is the constant experience-practice within the assembly of the people of <s>Nanda's</s> <s>Vraja</s>;
he who considered the love-filled debts of the beloveds to himself —
even beyond them, I praise <s>Rādhikā</s> alone, the jewel of the treasury famed above all!' ||26.27|| [sragdharā]

children.text:
rādhā sva-kāntaṃ vaśitaṃ vidhāya niḥśeṣam ākrīḍati tena sārdham | nāhaṃ tathetīva śivā śivāntas- tanau nilīnārdha-tanu-cchalena ||JGc_1,26.28|| [upajāti 11]
 athavā-
ardhenārdhena tanvā vyatimilanavato rudrayor eṣa bhāvaḥ kāvya-jñais tarkyate yaḥ sa punar iha mayā manyatāṃ bhaṇyamānaḥ |
premṇā yau pūrṇa-rūpau trijagati viditau rādhikā-mādhavākhyau pūrṇāṅgatvaṃ tayor apy ati-tad-asamayor nāv apīty aucitī na ||JGc_1,26.29|| [sragdharā]
[22] tad evaṃ sati-
 vādye gīte ca divye pramada-śithilite bhūṣaṇānām alīnām apy āsīd dhvāna-vargaḥ pratinidhi-samaye tasya tasyāpi tatra | khede jāte tathāgāt prabala-naṭa-kalā lāsyatāṃ yena keśa- karṇottaṃsāvataṃsa-pramukha-vara-sabhā tadvad ullāsyate sma ||JGc_1,26.30||[sragdharā]
evaṃ pariṣvaṅga-karābhimarśa- snigdhekṣaṇoddāma-vilāsa-hāsān | samaṃ priyābhir vyatikṛtya nṛtyan vyāñjīd asau sa-pratibimba-bimbam ||JGc_1,26.31|| [upajāti 11]
 tataś ca-
mālāḥ keśāli-veśān kuca-yugala-paṭīr maṇḍanāny anya-vāsāṃsy apy etā naiva śekuḥ kalayitum asakṛd rāsa-parvāvasāne | dhyāte yatrāpi sampraty api muni-vitatir vismaraty eva sarvam citraṃ tat-preyasīnāṃ tad iha bhavati kiṃ tādṛśe tat-prasaṅge ||JGc_1,26.32||[sragdharā]
taṃ dṛṣṭvāpy atha rāsam ambara-gatā rāmāś ca kāmārditā mohaṃ prāpur, adaś ca tāvad abhito' py āstāṃ paraṃ śrūyatām | candrādyair upalakṣitaṃ nabhasi yad bambhramyate sarvadā jyotiś-cakram idaṃ ca vismaya-karī caskambha yan mādhurī ||JGc_1,26.33||[śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
 [23] tad evaṃ līlā-lubdhāsu paramāveśataḥ sa-priyāsu tāsu vilubhita-kriyāsu rāsa-vilāsaḥ samupararāma | [24] uparamati ca tasmiṃs, tat-tad-ananusandhāna-sandhim anu tāni mithunāni yathāvat kuñjāya kuñjāya pṛthak pṛthag antardadhire | antardhāya ca, tat tan mithunaṃ paraspara-parikara-pariṣkāra-parāyaṇatām āsasāda | [25] tatra ca pratyekaṃ teṣām āliṅganādi-sacivaṃ vacanādi-racanam evāsīt | yathā-
children.translated_text:
'<s>Rādhā</s>, having brought her beloved under her sway, sports completely with him;
"I cannot do likewise" — thus [felt] <s>Śivā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), concealed within half the body of <s>Śiva</s>,
under the pretext of being half his body!' ||26.28|| [upajāti]
Or alternatively:
'This sentiment of the two <s>Rudras</s> (<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s>), whose halves merge body with body —
which is conjectured by the knowers of poetry — let that, being spoken by me here, be considered;
those two known in the three worlds as <s>Rādhikā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, full in form,
even for them, who are supremely unequal [to comparison], full-bodiedness does not fit us [<s>Śiva-Pārvatī</s>] — thus [the comparison] is not fitting.' ||26.29|| [sragdharā]
[22] Thus being so:
'In the divine music and song, when the ornaments loosened by delight,
even the humming of the bees became a chorus as a substitute [accompaniment];
when weariness arose, then came the powerful art of dance, by which the assemblies
of hair-decorations, ear-ornaments, and crest-jewels were likewise enlivened!' ||26.30|| [sragdharā]
'Thus, exchanging embraces, hand-caresses,
affectionate glances, and exuberant playful laughter
with the beloveds equally, dancing,
he displayed a reflected image with its reflection!' ||26.31|| [upajāti]
And then:
'Garlands, hair-arrangements, the cloths of the pair of breasts, ornaments, other garments —
these they were unable to restore even once at the conclusion of the <s>rāsa</s> festival;
even when merely contemplated now, the assembly of sages forgets everything —
wondrous! Then what would happen to his beloveds in such a situation with him?' ||26.32|| [sragdharā]
'Seeing that <s>rāsa</s> [dance], the celestial women in the sky, too, afflicted by desire,
became bewildered — and let all that be set aside, hear further:
the wheel of luminaries that always revolves in the sky, observed by the moon and others —
even that was brought to a halt by his sweetness, creating wonder!' ||26.33|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[23] Thus, when those [<s>gopīs</s>], greedy for the sport, through supreme absorption, together with their beloveds, had their activities confounded, the <s>rāsa</s> sport came to a rest. [24] And when it rested, following the juncture of the non-pursuit of each [previous activity], those couples separately disappeared into bower after bower, each pair. And having disappeared, each couple attained the state of devotion to adorning each other's paraphernalia. [25] And there, for each of them, there was the composition of words and such, accompanied by embraces and the like. As follows:

children.text:
hanta mām antarā kāntam antar āptaṃ tamas tvayā | iti bruvantaṃ śliṣyantaṃ taṃ sāsiñcan nijāśrubhiḥ ||JGc_1,26.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
 tataś ca-
hanta klamaḥ samajani sphuṭa-mad-vihārād asyā navīna-taru-pallava-komalāyāḥ | jñātaś ca hanta na maye' ti pṛthak sa tāsāṃ sāśrur mamārja muhur ānana-gharma-bindūn ||JGc_1,26.35|| [vasantatilakā]
 bāṣpe mṛjye harir bāṣpaṃ svede svedaṃ tadā dadhe | gopāla-kula-subhrūṇāṃ śrame rāsa-vilāsaje ||JGc_1,26.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
 [26] tatra bahula-sāmagrī-vāhinīnāṃ vṛndā-sakhī-vāhinīnāṃ kṛta-praśna-vṛndāyāṃ vṛndāyāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-varṇanam, yathā-
children.translated_text:
'Alas! Between me and the beloved, you have placed darkness!' —
thus saying, while embracing him,
they sprinkled him with their own tears! ||26.34|| [anuṣṭubh]
And then:
'Alas, weariness has arisen from my manifest sport
for this one, tender as the sprout of a new tree;
and alas, I did not perceive it!' — thus, separately, to each of them,
he tearfully wiped the beads of perspiration from their faces, again and again! ||26.35|| [vasantatilakā]
When tears were wiped, <s>Hari</s> [wiped] tears; when there was perspiration, he held [wiped] perspiration —
of the fair-browed women of the cowherd clan,
during the fatigue born of the <s>rāsa</s> sport! ||26.36|| [anuṣṭubh]
[26] There, when <s>Vṛndā</s> questioned the troops of <s>Vṛndā's</s> companion-armies, bearers of abundant supplies, the description of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [was given], as follows:

children.text:
sāsrālokanam añcalānila-kṛtir vaktrālakādy-unmṛjā- gaṇḍāntaḥ-paricumbanaṃ paṭa-yugādhānaṃ tanū-carcaṇam | tāmbūlārpaṇam atyapūrva-madhurālāpaḥ stava-prakriyā seyaṃ rāsa-pariśrama-praśamanī kāntāsu kṛṣṇa-kriyā ||JGc_1,26.37|| [śārdūla]
 [27] atha kāntā-varṇanaṃ, yathā-
vakra-smera-vilokanaṃ nava-dalaiḥ saṃvījanaṃ mārdavād aṅgānām abhimardanaṃ vighaṭita-srag-vastra-saṃyojanam |
samyaṅ marmaga-narma-śarma-racanaṃ tāmbūla-candrārpaṇaṃ seyaṃ rāsa-pariśrama-praśamanī kṛṣṇe priyāṇāṃ kriyā ||JGc_1,26.38|| [śārdūla]
[28] tataḥ svayam āgatya pratyakṣīkṛtya cānyathā manyamānāyāṃ tasyāṃ sa-smitaṃ punar amūr ūcuḥ-
dṛṣṭaṃ devi mitho hari-vraja-vadhū-dvandva-vrajenāmunā svīkṛtya pramadāt prayatna-vidhinā nepathyam aṅge dhṛtaṃ | etad yatra sakhi kṣaṇād apagataṃ kiṃ brūmahe tad varaṃ gīrṇaṃ sad-bhavatān mṛṣā na tu rahas tad vyaktim āpadyatām ||JGc_1,26.39||[śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
 [29] atha vṛndā sa-smitaṃ cetasi cintayāmāsa-satyam āhur imā, yat punaḥ punaḥ śramāpanodanaṃ sarvendriyāmodanaṃ śubha-veśaṃ gāna-vinoda-viśeṣam ārabhamāṇāni tānīmāni mithunāni mṛśyante |
children.translated_text:
'Tearful gazing, creating a breeze with the hem of the garment, wiping the face-curls and such,
kissing the inner cheek, adjusting the pair of garments, massaging the body,
offering betel, exceedingly unprecedented sweet conversation, the process of praise —
this is the activity of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> toward the beloveds, soothing the fatigue of the <s>rāsa</s>!' ||26.37|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[27] And the description of the beloveds, as follows:
'A crooked, smiling glance, fanning with fresh leaves out of tenderness,
massaging the limbs, fastening the disheveled garlands and garments,
properly creating the playful delight of tender wit, offering betel and sandalwood —
this is the activity of the beloveds toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, soothing the fatigue of the <s>rāsa</s>!' ||26.38|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[28] Then, having herself come and witnessed directly — when she [<s>Rādhā</s>] was thinking otherwise — they said to her with a smile:
'O goddess, we have seen it: each pair of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Vraja</s>-bride, mutually,
with delight and effort, having assumed and worn each other's costumes upon their bodies!
And this, O friend, which departed in an instant — what more shall we say? —
that excellence was consumed; it was not false — rather, let that privacy attain manifestation [in our telling]!' ||26.39|| [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
[29] Then <s>Vṛndā</s> reflected with a smile in her heart: 'They speak truly, for again and again, the removal of fatigue, the delighting of all senses, the beautiful costumes, the special sport of song and entertainment — these couples [engaged in all this] are indeed perceived.'

children.text:
atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ samāpanam āha sma-
 rādhe tvad-vallabhaḥ so' yaṃ sarveṣām api durlabhaḥ | varītuṃ tvām antaraṅgām anyā gopīr vṛtīyati ||JGc_1,26.40|| [anuṣṭubh]
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
rāsa-vilāsa-prasāraṇaṃ nāma
ṣaḍ-viṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||26 ||
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke the conclusion:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, this beloved of yours, difficult to attain for all,
chooses the other <s>gopīs</s> in order to select you as the innermost one!' ||26.40|| [anuṣṭubh]
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the twenty-sixth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Expansion of the <s>Rāsa</s> Sport.'
||26||

children.text:
(27)
atha saptaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
rāsa-prapañca-pañca-pūraṇī-pūraṇam
children.translated_text:
(27)
Now, the twenty-seventh <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter):
'The Fulfillment of the Five Chapters of the <s>Rāsa</s> Elaboration.'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text:
atha vilasita-kheda-sveda-kulyāyamānāḥ saha hari-vara-gauryaḥ sūrya-putrīṃ samīyuḥ |
yad amita-śatam etāḥ sā bhajantī sravantī sarabha-sarasa-pūrtiṃ tat-kṣaṇād eva bheje ||JGc_1,27.1|| [mālinī]
atikramya sva-maryādāṃ śyāmaḥ śyāmāś ca māṃ yayuḥ | itīva yamunā śyāmā drāg atikrāmati sma tām ||JGc_1,27.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
 [2] athāṅga-rucā ghana-capalā ghanāyamānā, vācā ca cāṭaka-bhaṇita-stanitāyamānā ghanāgama-lakṣmīr iva lakṣmī-lakṣmī-patīnāṃ sabhā sā mihirajā-pravāhe nabhasi hasta-grāham avagāhamānā bhāsate sma |
 mithaḥ prahasita-prathā-kala-kalaḥ samākarṣaṇaṃ muhuḥ stimita-gātratā pṛthula-vepathu-prakramaḥ | tad etad atha yat sthitaṃ bata jalāvagāhāt purā tad evam anumīyate samudiyāya tasya cchaviḥ ||JGc_1,27.3|| [pṛthvī] yadā jalaṃ na hi viviśur nata-bhruvas tadāmunā prasiṣicire samaṃ tathā | amuṃ yathā laghu-gatim atra menire vibhūbhavann udaka-bhṛd añcatīti tāḥ ||JGc_1,27_4|| [vasantatilakā] jalād evaṃ siṣecāmur ghanaṃ ghana-rasa-pradaḥ | viviśur jalam evāmūr yathāsāra-śarārditāḥ ||JGc_1,27_5|| [anuṣṭubh] tadāvalagna-daghnaṃ vārmagnāś capala-locanāḥ | kṛṣṇasāra-vadhū-rūpāḥ purastād gatim adviṣan ||JGc_1,27_6|| [anuṣṭubh] yadā tāsāṃ netra-pratiphalana-miśrā jhaṣa-gaṇā muhur naivāgacchan pariciti-vidhānaṃ katham api | tadā spardhābaddhā
iva mṛdulaṃ kṣaṇagaṃ bhṛśam amī spṛśanto bhīrūṇāṃ murahara-dṛśoḥ kautukam adhuḥ ||JGc_1,27_7|| [śikhariṇī] haṃsā gatīś cakra-khagāḥ payodharān
mīnā dṛśaḥ sārasanāni sārasāḥ | tāsām upetyāpagatā yatas tadā teṣāṃ tu sāmrājyam apūri sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,27.8|| [indravaṃśā] mukha-vṛndaṃ khalu tāsāṃ
kamalāny abhibhūya babhrāje | taj-jātiṣu tad-adhikatā
vidhutā vā kiṃ nidānam asti sma? ||JGc_1,27.9|| [udgīti] ||
children.translated_text:
'Then, the fair ones of the supreme <s>Hari</s>, becoming streams of perspiration from the fatigue of sport,
approached the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>);
since these innumerable hundreds [of <s>gopīs</s>] came to her, that flowing one,
she instantly attained an overflowing, passionate, abundant fullness!' ||27.1|| [mālinī]
'The dark one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and the dark ones (<s>gopīs</s>) have come to me, transgressing their own boundaries!' —
thus, as if the dark-hued <s>Yamunā</s> swiftly overflowed her banks! ||27.2|| [anuṣṭubh]
[2] Then, the assembly of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī's</s> lord, with bodily luster flickering like cloud-lightning, with speech thundering like the chatter of <s>cātaka</s> birds, appeared like the splendor of the arrival of the rainy season — plunging into the stream of the Sun's daughter (<s>Yamunā</s>) in the sky, bathing hand-in-hand.
'The spreading of mutual, playful laughter's fame; the repeated mutual pulling;
the motionlessness of limbs; the onset of great trembling —
all this which existed before the plunge into the water —
is thus inferred: his beauty arose!' ||27.3|| [pṛthvī]
'When the curved-browed ones had not yet entered the water,
he sprinkled them all together;
and they deemed him as one moving swiftly here,
thinking: "A water-bearer (cloud) is rising!"' ||27.4|| [vasantatilakā]
'Just as they sprinkled him from the water, the cloud-like one, giver of cloud-[rain's] delight,
they entered the water — as if struck by arrows of rain-showers!' ||27.5|| [anuṣṭubh]
'Then, clinging to him, submerged in waist-deep water, the restless-eyed ones,
in the form of <s>kṛṣṇasāra</s>-doe wives, did not disdain moving forward!' ||27.6|| [anuṣṭubh]
'When the shoals of fish, mixed with the reflections of their eyes,
could by no means achieve familiarity [with them],
then, as if bound by rivalry, softly, fleetingly, intensely,
these [fish], touching [their bodies], created delight in the eyes of the timid ones and of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>!' ||27.7|| [śikhariṇī]
'The swans [came for] their gaits; the <s>cakra</s>-birds for their breasts;
the fish for their eyes; the <s>sārasa</s> cranes for the crane-like ones [themselves] —
having approached them and then departed, [the birds lost their supremacy],
for [the <s>gopīs</s>'] sovereignty filled everything on all sides!' ||27.8|| [indravaṃśā]
'The cluster of their faces indeed
outshone the lotuses;
was the superiority of the lotuses among their own kind
dispelled [by the <s>gopīs</s>] — or what was the cause?' ||27.9|| [udgīti]

children.text:
tataś ca locana-nikocaṃ hasantīṣu tāsu svayaṃ tena nāgara-candreṇa pravartitā vyātyukṣī, yathā-
 meghaṃ vidyud vidyutaṃ cātra meghaḥ siñcaty uccair megha-tulye pravāhe | citraṃ citraṃ citram etat kim etat nāṭyaṃ paśyety ūcire vyoma-rāmāḥ ||JGc_1,27.10|| [śālinī] tataś cākaṇṭha-nirmagnā mahilāḥ kamalānanāḥ | madhusūdana-saṃsaktāḥ kamalinya iva sthitāḥ ||JGc_1,27_11|| [anuṣṭubh] gaṇe gaurāṅgīnāṃ harir acita-dharṣāt paribhavaṃ gate tatra svarṇāmbuja-ghana-vanī nihnutim adāt | viparyāso yarhy asphurad iha ca nīlāmbujavanī tadā tasyāpahnuty-ucita-citi-kṛte' bhūd anupamam ||JGc_1,27_12|| [śikhariṇī] ambuja-gandhi tathāmbuja-
rūpaṃ madhu-yug yathāmbujaṃ tad iva | tāsāṃ tasya ca vadanaṃ kiṃ jala-kelāv adād bhramaṃ na mithaḥ ||JGc_1,27.13|| [gīti] kathañcid api yā labdhā hariṇāmbhoja-kānane | kim api vyañjayāmāsa tasyā hāhā-kṛtiṃ param ||JGc_1,27_14|| [anuṣṭubh] smita-vilasita-nīlāmbhojam āsīdad ekā mukham anu hari-vaktra-sphūrti-sandigdha-cittā | iha ca vara-maranda-svādam āsādya sadyaṃ samaruci-yuvatībhyaḥ śaṅkinī svaṃ jugopa ||JGc_1,27_15|| [mālinī] durlabhaṃ yad ajani svayaṅgrahā- liṅganaṃ tad iha jātam añjasā | yarhi magnam anayā gabhīra-vār ujjahāra harir apy amūm atha ||JGc_1,27_16|| [rathoddhatā] drutam atha vara-rāmā vāri vakṣoja-daghnaṃ yugapad ayi bhavatyaḥ prāṇa-nāthaṃ vijetum | sthagita-kṛti-karābhyām icchavaḥ sektum uccaiḥ katham atha bata jigyur jigyire vā kathaṃ
na ||JGc_1,27_17|| [mālinī] padminyā mukha-padmaṃ
mudritam api sa madhusūdanaḥ pibati | iti miṣa-kalayā sudṛśaś
chalita-dṛśas tadvad ācarat kṛṣṇaḥ ||JGc_1,27.18|| [gīti] hariṇā hṛdaye tāsāṃ vitīrṇā nakhara-vraṇāḥ | adbhutaṃ sahasā śliṣṭā madaneṣu-kṛta-vraṇāḥ ||JGc_1,27_19|| [anuṣṭubh] aupajānuka-bhujas tu yadāsau pārśvatīya-mukhatīyatayāsīt | aupakarṇika-dṛśāṃ sa tad āsām aupanīvika-karo' py ajaniṣṭa ||JGc_1,27_20|| [svāgatā] yadā rādhā vāri-kelau sakhīnāṃ purato gatā | vināpi sekaṃ sa tadā jaḍatām abhajat priyaḥ ||JGc_1,27_21|| [anuṣṭubh] rādhā-puraḥ-saratayā jala-keli-yuddhe kṛṣṇaṃ cakāra jaḍam udyamam antarāpi | naitad viveda vanitā-nicitir mithas tu svīyām ajijñapad asau jita-kāśitāṃ ca ||JGc_1,27_22|| [vasantatilakā]
 alaka-valayi-netraṃ kañja-netreṇa kīrṇaṃ
svam anu madhupa-tīkṣṇaṃ kañjam unnīya tasyām | sabhayam apagatāyāṃ tatra senādhipāyāṃ sa tu tad-anuga-sainyaṃ prāviśac cāviśac ca ||JGc_1,27.23|| [mālinī]
tataś ca-
nīra-keli-bhṛta-rāga-cakṣuṣām aṭṭa-hāsa-nibha-hāsa-rociṣām | māra-yuddha-lasad-uddhata-śriyāṃ raudravad vyajani so' py asau rasaḥ ||JGc_1,27.24|| [rathoddhatā] tataḥ krīḍā-yuddhaṃ dadhad agha-ripur nīra-vihṛti- prathāyām ekākī vraja-yuvati-koṭībhir abhitaḥ | tathā kṛtvā tīraṃ prasabham itavān samprati yathā purā kātyāyanyā bhajana-kṛti-kanyāsv akuruta ||JGc_1,27_25|| [śikhariṇī]
tataś ca-
 marāla-kūjitā nīra-vasanā nīra-jānanāḥ | cañcad-bhramarakā nīrajānāṃ nālya iva sthitāḥ ||JGc_1,27.26|| [anuṣṭubh]
atha hā hā hāsa-śabdāḥ pravṛttā nīra-tīrayoḥ | eke cātaka-gīs-tulyāḥ pare' lpa-stanita-prabhāḥ ||JGc_1,27.27|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
And then, while those [gopīs] were laughing at the closing of their eyes, the urbane moon (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) himself initiated a water-splashing game, as follows:
The cloud [sprinkles] the lightning, and the lightning here sprinkles the cloud, in a flood resembling a cloud! 'Wonderful, wonderful! What a marvel this is! See this drama!' — exclaimed the celestial women. // [śālinī]
Then, the lotus-faced women, immersed up to their necks, attached to <s>Madhusūdana</s>, stood like lotus plants! // [anuṣṭubh]
When <s>Hari</s> was submerged among the group of fair-limbed women, that group of golden lotuses gave concealment to his dark complexion; but when the reversal appeared, the group of blue lotuses — for the concealment of that [golden group] — became incomparable! // [śikharinī]
The faces of those [gopīs] and his — lotus-fragrant, lotus-formed, honey-conjoined, like lotuses — did they not create mutual bewilderment in the water-sport? // [gīti]
One who was somehow obtained by <s>Hari</s> in the lotus-garden — she manifested some supreme exclamation of 'Ah!' toward him! // [anuṣṭubh]
One woman, her mind doubtful of the manifestation of <s>Hari's</s> face, approached the smiling blue lotus [before her]; and having attained the taste of its excellent honey there, becoming suspicious of the women of equal beauty, she guarded her own [prize]! // [mālinī]
What was difficult [to obtain] — the self-grasped embrace — here came about effortlessly, when <s>Hari</s> lifted her who was submerged in deep water! // [rathoddhatā]
Swiftly then, O excellent women, [wishing] to simultaneously conquer the lord of your lives in water reaching to your breasts — with hands concealing your actions, you wished to splash him abundantly! Ah, but how then did you conquer? Or rather, how could you not be conquered? // [mālinī]
The bee (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) drinks the face-lotus of the lotus-woman even when it is closed — and those beautiful-eyed ones, with the pretext of dissimulating gazes, acted likewise! // [gīti]
The nail-wounds bestowed by <s>Hari</s> upon their hearts — wonder of wonders — once embraced, [merged with] the wounds made by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s>! // [anuṣṭubh]
When he, whose arms reached to his knees, was near to the faces of those at his sides, then for those with eyes reaching to their ears, his hand also reached to their waists! // [svāgatā]
When <s>Rādhā</s> went ahead of her companions in the water-sport, then the beloved, even without being splashed, became stunned! // [anuṣṭubh]
Because <s>Rādhā</s> went ahead in the water-sport battle, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was rendered motionless, even in the midst of effort. But the assemblage of women did not perceive this; rather, they mutually desired to investigate their own [victories] and the appearance of being conquered. // [vasantatilakā]
Lifting toward her a [blue] lotus as sharp as a bee — [reflecting] a lotus-eye encircled by curls — when she, the commander, retreated in fear, he entered the army following her, and was himself entered [by love]! // [mālinī]
And then:
For those whose eyes bore the passion of water-sport, whose laughter had the radiance of thunderous mirth, whose beauty flashed with the exuberance of Love's battle — that <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic savor) arose as if it were the <s>raudra</s> (terrible)! // [rathoddhatā]
Then the enemy of <s>Agha</s>, maintaining the play-battle in the course of water-sport, alone against tens of millions of young women of <s>Vraja</s> on all sides, having thus forcibly reached the bank, acted now just as he had formerly done with the maidens performing the worship of <s>Kātyāyanī</s>! // [śikharinī]
And then:
With the cooing of swans, water as their garments, water as their ornaments, with hovering bees — they stood like stalks of water-born lotuses! // [anuṣṭubh]
Then cries of 'Ah! Ah!' and sounds of laughter arose on both banks of the water — some resembling the songs of <s>cātaka</s> birds, others having the power of soft thunder! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
tataś ca bahudhā parihasya vinoda-viśeṣaṇāya sakhyātireka-vivekāya ca dvābhyāṃ dvābhyām ekam ekam aṃśukaṃ dattavān, haris tāḥ sarvā vastraikaika-veṣṭita-dvi-dvi-kāya-yaṣṭīr utthitā nirīkṣya pratimukhaṃ parīkṣya ca bahu jahāsa | hasitvā ca tāsām uttam uttamaṃ vāsas tathā dhārayantīnāṃ cañcalatā-sambhṛtaṃ tiryag añcalatā-saṃvṛtaṃ sambhavad aruṇa-guṇaṃ, madhye madhye stambha-nipuṇaṃ kvacana kvacana cākasmika-smita-lambhanaṃ vināpi dṛg-ambhaḥ kranditena vilokita-dambhaṃ vilocana-saṃrambhaṃ lambhaṃ lambhaṃ trilokī-mohane cikīrṣita-tadīya-ruci-dohane kusumāsāra-kāriṇī vimāna-cāriṇī-saṃhatiḥ praśasta-vastrālaṅkāra-mālyādīnāṃ puṭīḥ peṭakāś ca tat-purataḥ śanaiḥ pātanam anaiṣīt |
 [5] kṛṣṇas tu tāḥ sarva-stutāḥ samunna-vastrāḥ paśyann ati-samunnatānanda-vaśyaḥ svayam anurajya samupayujya vibhajya ca tāni vastrādīni prattavān |
 [6] tatra prathamataḥ svalpenaiva tena tena vicchittir jātā, yathā-
children.translated_text:
Then, having teased [them] in many ways, for the sake of special amusement and for discerning the excess of friendship, he gave one garment to every two [gopīs]. <s>Hari</s>, seeing all of them risen, their pairs of bodies wrapped in a single garment each, examining [them] face to face, laughed abundantly. And having laughed — [beholding] their restlessness while wearing each garment most excellently, their sideways-tucking of the border-edges, their becoming endowed with reddish qualities, their skill at becoming motionless in the intervals, their obtaining of an unexpected smile somewhere or other, their eye-tears of weeping without deception and the vehemence of their glances — receiving and receiving all this, an assembly of celestial women, who were like flower-showers in [their power of] enchanting the three worlds, and who travelled in aerial chariots, gently caused boxes and caskets of excellent garments, ornaments, garlands, and the like to fall before them.
[5] But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seeing all those praised ones with uplifted garments, overwhelmed by supremely exalted bliss, himself delighting and partaking, divided and bestowed those garments and other [gifts].
[6] There, at first, even with those slight [adornments], an elegance was born, as follows:

children.text: majjanena tanu-rocir ācitaṃ sūkṣma-śubhra-vasanaṃ sata-cchavi | citrakaṃ dyuti-vicitram ity adaḥ prāyaveśam arucan hari-priyāḥ ||JGc_1,27.28|| [rathoddhatā] ||
children.translated_text: Their bodily luster adorned by the immersion, the fine white garment with a hundredfold radiance, like a marvelous painting resplendent with brilliance — thus they, <s>Hari's</s> beloveds, attained an almost [complete] beauty! // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
bahubhir bhūṣaṇais tu tatra tatra mithune parama-śobhā netra-lobhāya jāyate sma | tathā hi-
 yadā yadā nūtana-veśa-yauvanaṃ tathāvidhābhiḥ samam īkṣate harim | matvā tadā navya-vadhū-varān amūn divyo janaḥ puṣpa-kulāni varṣati ||JGc_1,27.29|| [upajāti 12]
children.translated_text:
But with many ornaments, the supreme beauty of each couple here and there was born as a feast for the eyes. For thus:
Whenever those [gopīs] of such a kind beheld <s>Hari</s>, adorned with the freshness of new attire and youthful beauty, the celestial folk, deeming them new brides and grooms, showered clusters of flowers! // [upajāti]

children.text: atha vana-vihārāya hariṇākṣīṇāṃ tatir evam ādi-vyājaṃ vyājahāra-
children.translated_text: Then, a group of doe-eyed ones expressed this sort of pretext for the forest-pastime:

children.text: anaṅgo nāma senānīḥ kṛṣṇa kas tava vidyate | hanta darśaya taṃ nityaṃ sakhīyaṃ māṃ bravīti yam ||JGc_1,27.30|| [anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, what commander-in-chief named <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god) do you have? Come, show him — the one who always calls me a companion!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇas tu gūḍha-smitam ūcivān tatra śrī-rādhāṃ prati, yathā-
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, however, spoke to Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> there with a hidden smile, as follows:

children.text: rādhe, maiṣīr draṣṭum anaṅgam | tasya tu paśya gaṇaṃ kṛta-sat-kṛta-sukṛta-sulambhita-saṅgam ||dhruvam||
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, do not desire to see <s>Anaṅga</s>! Rather, behold his retinue — well-honored, meritorious, easily attained in company! //refrain//
The row of tree-and-creeper couples, a settlement welcoming you as a guest, beckons with wind-stirred new-leaf hands, claiming you as its own! //a//
She again scatters flowers on the path to prepare a carpet-like course for you; and the family of cuckoos too produces sweet melodies in succession, calling for you, O excellent one! //b//
And the bees produce the sound of war-drums with their buzzing, joyfully; and hundreds of peacocks too perform their dance all around, led by the leader! //c//
This lord of the night spreads his own lamp-like radiance all around; and this path too has spread itself wide, desirous of the dust of your feet!' //d//

children.text: taru-vallī-tati-dampati-pallī bhavatīm atithīyantī | ākārayati calan-nava-pallava-pāṇibhir ātmīyantī ||a|| sā punar iha kusumāni kirati pathi racayitum āstara-caryām | kokila-kulam api tava hūtiṃ kila kalam anu kalayati varyām ||b|| bhrūṅkāreṇa ca bherī-śabdaṃ bhramarā vidadhati sa-sukham | śikhi-śatam api bata tanute nartanam abhitaś cālī-pramukham ||c|| nija-ruci-dīpaṃ paritaḥ prathayati so' yaṃ rajanī-svāmī | eṣa ca panthāḥ svaṃ vistṛtavāṃs tvat-pada-rajasāṃ kāmī ||d|| ||JGc_1,27.31|| | iti |
children.translated_text: This said.

children.text:
atha savitṛ-sutāyā dhanya-vanyā-pradeśe viracita-bahu-veśe tā virejuḥ sa-kāntam | tam anu paraparasmin vāsare kāryam anyad vilasitam anukāntaṃ sūcayāmāsa kāntaḥ ||JGc_1,27.32|| [mālinī] atha bhramara-dampati-vraja-janaḥ pratisvaṃ nijā- layād anugatiṃ dadhad bhavika-gītavad gītavān | aho kim iva so' pi taṃ nija-ramā-yutaṃ tad-vana- prabhuṃ pramitavān anuvrajati tatra sarvatra ca ||JGc_1,27_33|| [pṛthvī]
 [10] atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ papraccha-
 rātrīḥ kiñcin mātra-śeṣatvam āgād bambhramyante smāpi tasmin sapatnyaḥ | krīḍā-tṛṣṇā dhṛṣṇag evāṅga jātā hā kiṃ cakre tatra kṛṣṇāṅganābhiḥ? ||JGc_1,27.34|| [śālinī]
[11] tatra madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca tad-vanasya nirvarṇana-pūrvakaṃ varṇanaṃ vidhāya, keli-kalāpe vidhīyamāne-
 anyo' nyaṃ nihnutānveṣaṇa-kṛti-vihṛtiṃ preyasībhir murārir yāṃ cakre sā rahas tan-mithuna-mithunatā-kāraṇaṃ jāyate sma | yatrānviṣyānuyātā vividha-gati-vapuḥ-sphūrtinā tena yā yā kuñjāntas taṃ gṛhītvā pṛthag apara-dṛśāṃ dūratāṃ sāñcati sma ||JGc_1,27.35|| [sragd] kathañcana dadarśa yā kvacid apīha kṛṣṇānvitāṃ vadhūṃ rahasi kām api svayam idaṃ-vidhā kācana | pratītim agaman na hi sphuṭam amūṃ tamālānvitāṃ sphuṭat-puraṭa-yūthikāṃ sapadi manyamānā hṛdi ||JGc_1,27_36|| [pṛthvī] śiñjitaṃ vihaga-kākalī-kulair gānam anya-bhṛta-sambhṛta-svaraiḥ | rūpam apy atha tamāla-campaka- śreṇibhir muhur avāri tādṛśām ||JGc_1,27_37|| [rathoddhatā] yatra santamasam asti santataṃ tad vanaṃ na para-durgamaṃ param | kuñja-madhya-lasad-oṣadhī-śriyā
tatra tatra mithuna-rddhi-vardhi ca ||JGc_1,27_38|| [rathoddhatā] atha rahasi girāṃ vilāsa-kamraṃ calad-amalāṅga-vikāsi-romaharṣam | smara-valayi-kalā-spṛhātilolaṃ didivur alaṃ yugalāni tatra tatra ||JGc_1,27_39|| [puṣpitāgrā]
 [12] atha krama-vaśād adbhuta-bhayānaka-raudra-bībhatsa-vatsala-karuṇa-vīra-hāsya-śānta-śṛṅgāra-rasāḥ śṛṅgārānukūlatayā yathāyogaṃ rasayitum āsāditāḥ | [13] yathā-
children.translated_text:
Then, in a blessed forest-region by the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), adorned with many costumes, they shone forth with their beloved. Thereafter, on the next successive day, the beloved one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) intimated another charming pastime to be performed. // [mālinī]
Then, the community of bee-couples, following each from their own abode, sang as if singing festive songs. Ah, how indeed did he too, accompanied by his own <s>Ramā</s> (beloved), measure that lord of the forest — and follow him everywhere there! // [pṛthvī]
[10] Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> asked:
'The nights have come to a point where only a little remains — are those co-wives still wandering about in that [forest]? The thirst for play has indeed arisen boldly, O friend! Alas, what did <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> do there with those women?' // [śālinī]
[11] There <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'And then, having first described and then narrated that forest, when the array of sports was being enacted:
The game of mutual hiding, seeking, and playing that the slayer of <s>Mura</s> played with his beloveds — that became the cause of coupling, pair by pair, in secret. Whatever [<s>gopī</s>] followed [him] who was sought with various gaits, bodily manifestations, and expressions — having seized him inside a bower, far from the sight of the others, she made [him her own]! // [sragdharā]
One who somehow saw somewhere a maiden accompanied by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in secret — some such one, of this kind — did not clearly recognize her as being accompanied by a <s>tamāla</s> tree, thinking in her heart that she was a golden <s>yūthikā</s> (jasmine) suddenly appearing! // [pṛthvī]
The tinkling sounds with the rows of bird-cries, the songs with voices supplied by other [creatures], and the forms too — by rows of <s>tamāla</s> and <s>campaka</s> trees — were repeatedly blocked for such ones! // [rathoddhatā]
Where there was constant dense darkness, that forest was not merely difficult for others [to traverse]; by the splendor of the luminous herbs shining in the midst of the bowers, the prosperity of each couple there was enhanced! // [rathoddhatā]
Then, in secret — the delightful play of words, the horripilation blossoming on their stirring, pure limbs, the extreme eagerness craving the arts of Love's circle — the couples shone forth abundantly, here and there! // [puṣpitāgrā]
[12] Then, by the force of sequence, the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) — <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terror), <s>raudra</s> (fury), <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgust), <s>vātsalya</s> (parental love), <s>karuṇa</s> (compassion), <s>vīra</s> (heroism), <s>hāsya</s> (humor), <s>śānta</s> (peace), and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (love) — were made to be savored as befitting, in a manner favorable to <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. [13] As follows:

children.text:
sa eṣa keśavaḥ preyasībhiḥ saha vilalāsa |
 bhramaram iha nibhālya dattacumbaṃ vratatiṣu kīram apīha dāḍimīṣu | punar api ramaṇo manojavaśya- sthitiramaṇāya babhūva vallavīṣu ||JGc_1,27.40|| [puṣpitāgrā] alir iha vadanopadaṃśam āsīn madhurasapānakaraḥ sarojinīnām | yad ajitaramaṇītatir nirīkṣya sphuṭam abhajan madanaṃ vidūrato' pi ||JGc_1,27_41|| [puṣpitāgrā] ||
children.translated_text:
This <s>Keśava</s> sported with his beloveds.
'Observing the bee here giving a kiss to the creeper-rows, and the parrot here to the pomegranate-trees — | the lover, for the sake of delighting the mind-born [Love-god] subdued within, | again became [engaged] among the cowherd-women!' || (JGc 1,27.40) [puṣpitāgrā]
'The bee here was the biting of the lip-surface, the hand drinking the sweet nectar of the lotus-women; | seeing which, the host of <s>Ajita's</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) beautiful women | clearly worshipped <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god) even from afar!' || (JGc 1,27.41) [puṣpitāgrā]

children.text: tac ca tac ca na varṇayitum ātmaśaktiṃ nirvarṇaye, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: But I cannot discern my own capacity to describe this and that, because:

children.text: tāṃ jyautsnīṃ tac ca vṛndā-vipinam api ca tat kuñja-vṛndaṃ tathā tāḥ śayyā dve dve ca te te hari-hariṇa-dṛśau tāś ca sa-prema-līlāḥ | paśyat paśyan mano me sapadi viṣayitām ujjhad atrānumuhyat paśyad drāg yāti tat-tad-viṣaya-valayatāṃ hanta paśyāni kena? ||JGc_1,27.42|| [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: 'That moonlit night, and that forest of <s>Vṛndā</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>), and those clusters of bowers, and those | beds — pair by pair — and those <s>Hari</s>-and-doe-eyed couples, and those love-filled sports — | my mind, seeing [them], immediately abandoning objecthood, swooned here upon beholding; | and when it sees [again], it swiftly goes into the compass of each and every object — alas, with what shall I see?' || (JGc 1,27.42) [sragdharā]

children.text:
tad etad iha sāmānyatayā varṇitam, viśeṣataḥ punar evam-
 anyā varṇāḥ santi yatra sphuren na śrīrādhāyāḥ kāpi saubhāgyalakṣmīḥ | tasyāḥ sphūrtau varṇanāyāṃ na śakyā sāpy evaṃ ced anyavārtā tu dūre ||JGc_1,27.43|| [śālinī] ||
children.translated_text:
This has been described here in general terms; but in particular, thus:
'Where other descriptions exist that might shine — no blessed fortune of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> [appears]; | when her [glory] does shine forth, description is incapable — | and if even that [is so], then the account of others is far [beyond reach]!' || (JGc 1,27.43) [śālinī]

children.text:
tataś ca parasparaṃ para-parāgamanātaṅkayā maṅkṣu saṅkucita-līlā-vilāsāḥ sa-viśleṣaṃ veṣaṃ saṃśleṣa-valitaṃ vidhāya vallī-gṛha-pallīnāṃ bahir-varti-sanniveśa-veṣaṃ sthalī-viśeṣaṃ kramataḥ krāmanti sma, yatra kṛṣṇasyāpy aikadhyam udbudhyate sma | [18] tathā ca taṃ krāntvā ca dāruṇatā-padāruṇatā-prakāśa-sānnidhyaṃ nidhyāyanti sma | tataḥ-
 pūrvasyāṃ diśi kācanāruṇa-ruci-cchāyāvṛṇoc candrikāṃ candro' py āśu tadā patann iva karair ālambatāstācalam | itthaṃ kairaviṇī-kulaṃ kila dara-glāniṃ yayāv ity amūs tad-rāsāṅkita-rātri-śānti-vibudhā mamluś ca kṛṣṇa-priyāḥ ||JGc_1,27.44|| [śārdūla]
[19] tatra khecara-strīṇāṃ vacanam
children.translated_text:
Then, their sport-and-play suddenly contracted by the mutual apprehension of the approach of dawn, having arranged their dress and appearance interwoven with the embrace of [impending] separation, they gradually traversed to a particular open ground outside the bower-village enclosures, where <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> singularity of being also awakened.
[18] And having traversed that, they contemplated the proximity of the dawn — a harsh, terrible [moment of] redness. Then:
'In the eastern direction, a certain reddish glow began to cover the moonlight; | the moon too then, as if falling, quickly grasped the western mountain with its rays; | thus the night-lotus (<s>kairaviṇī</s>) family became slightly wilted — and those | beloved ones of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, learned in the cessation of the <s>rāsa</s>-marked night, swooned!' || (JGc 1,27.44) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[19] There, the words of the celestial women:

children.text:
nīca-bhāva-valayī balād vrajann ūrdhvatāṃ nipatatīti niścitam | paśya gopa-sumukhī-mukhātigaḥ puṣkarāt skhalitavān asau vidhuḥ ||JGc_1,27.45|| [rathoddhatā]
 kiṃ ca-
ahriyata kuvalaya-mālā-
līlā gopāṅganāpāṅgaiḥ | iti kila dūnita-bandhuḥ
kuvalaya-bandhuḥ papāta hā sindhum ||JGc_1,27.46|| [upagīti]
 [20] śrī-vraja-devīnām api-
children.translated_text:
'One who proceeds forcefully in the course of low states, | while ascending, certainly falls — behold! | The moon, passing beyond the faces of the cowherd beauties, | has slipped from the lotus [of the sky]!' || (JGc 1,27.45) [rathoddhatā]
Moreover:
'The sport of the blue-lotus garland | was stolen by the side-glances of the cowherd women; | thus — with its friend (<s>bandhu</s>) afflicted — | alas, the friend of the blue-lotus (the moon) fell into the ocean!' || (JGc 1,27.46) [upagīti]
[20] And [the words] of the queens of <s>Śrī Vraja</s> too:

children.text:
tārāṇāṃ vṛndam āmṛdnann asmākam api sarvataḥ |
ayam ākramate' nūrur vyoma cākramati drutam ||JGc_1,27.47|| [anuṣṭubh]
 [21] tataś ca tāsāṃ tathā-bhāvaṃ vibhāvya bhavya-svabhāvaḥ sa śrīmān navya-kiśoratā-navya-sad-bhāvaḥ pratisvam āliṅgitānāṃ darśita-praṇaya-sampad-iṅgitānāṃ vaktra-kamalaṃ sravad-asraṃ mamārja |
 [22] sāntvayann eva cedaṃ sāntvam uvāca-
children.translated_text:
'The host of stars, crushing [them] on all sides | and [crushing] us as well — | this broad-rayed one (the dawn) advances | and swiftly conquers the sky!' || (JGc 1,27.47) [anuṣṭubh]
[21] Then, having perceived such a state in them, the one of blessed nature — that glorious lord, of freshly-youthful, freshly-good disposition — wiped the lotus-faces streaming with tears of those who had been individually embraced and shown the wealth of affection's gestures.
[22] And while consoling, he spoke this consolation:

children.text:
acchinnaṃ samayaṃ vahāmi bhujayor antaḥ sakhi tvām iti pratyāśā yadi sidhyatīha tad api svāntaṃ na me tṛpyati | siddhau tatra tu vighna-jātam atulaṃ bandhvādi-sambhālanaṃ tasmād geha-gater avaśya-valane mā mlānir āsādyatām ||JGc_1,27.48|| [śārdūla]
[23] iti pūrvavad eva pratyekaṃ hastena vyatiṣajya sajyamāna-vihāratayā vraja-vartmānuvartate sma |
children.translated_text:
'"I bear you perpetually within my arms, O friend" — | if this promise be fulfilled here, even then my heart is not satisfied! | But there is an incomparable obstacle to its fulfillment — the duty of attending to kinsmen and the like; | therefore, at the inevitable turning of the homeward path, let no dejection be attained!' || (JGc 1,27.48) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[23] Thus, as before, entwining each one individually by the hand, with the play being set in motion, he followed the path toward <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: yadyapi vanitā-vaśatām antar yātas tathāpy asau kṛṣṇaḥ | bhajati snigdhān anyān sat-puruṣāṇām iyaṃ śailī ||JGc_1,27.49|| [āryā] ||
children.translated_text: 'Although <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had inwardly entered into the power of the women, | nevertheless, he cherishes other beloved ones — | this is the manner of virtuous persons!' || (JGc 1,27.49) [āryā]

children.text:
atha labdha-paraspara-vicchedeṣu ca tat-tat-pallī-vartma-bhedeṣu prāyeṇa prāpta-gaṇa-saṅgama-troṭatām adhika-koṭatayā bhāvinī-samudayaḥ svayaṃ na bhāvayitum īśāmbabhūva |
 [25] krameṇa cātyanta-raṅga-tat-tad-aṅganā-gaṇe gaṇeyatayāvaśiṣṭe tena saha nija-nijopavanāntar-varti-gehāṅgaṇa-vartma-bhedam āsādya, kṣaṇaṃ gamanād virarāma reme ca | tatra ca-
 gāḍhopagūḍha-ciratāṃ paṭu-cumbitaṃ tad- viśrambha-bhāg-abhihitaṃ bahu-mānitaṃ ca | tāsāṃ gatau racayatā vraja-rāja-putre- ṇākāri kiṃ na kim ito gaṇanāṃ na vedmi ||JGc_1,27.50|| [vasantatilaka]
 [26] tataś ca tāḥ sa-gadgadaṃ jagaduḥ-
children.translated_text:
Then, when they had obtained mutual separation at the branching of the paths to their respective villages, the community of women, on account of the rupture of the group-meeting [becoming] exceedingly intense, was itself unable to imagine [the pain].
[25] And gradually, when only a countable group of the most intimately passionate women of each category remained with him, having reached the branching of the path to their own respective garden-enclosure homes, he paused from walking for a moment and delighted [in their company]. And there:
'The prince of <s>Vraja</s>, in fashioning their departure — | a long, tight embrace, a skillful kiss, | confidential words spoken in trust, great honor — | what did he not do? I do not know the count of it all!' || (JGc 1,27.50) [vasantatilakā]
[26] Then they spoke with faltering voices:

children.text: sambhāvitaṃ na valate sma yad asmakābhis tvat-prāptir atra bhaviteti tayā ca jātam | vijñāpanaṃ tu na idaṃ śṛṇu kṛṣṇa tasmin aṅgīkṛtaṃ pariharanti na jātu santaḥ ||JGc_1,27.51|| [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: 'What we did not dare to hope — | that the attainment of You would occur here — that has happened. | But this is not a petition — hear, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: | what has been accepted [by You], the virtuous never abandon!' || (JGc 1,27.51) [vasantatilakā]

children.text:
tataś ca-
mitho mithunam uttaraṃ viraham ūhamānaṃ mithaḥ
patan-nayana-vāribhiḥ samabhiṣiktam āśliṣyata |
tad evam akhilaṃ vapur niyatam ārdram āsīd bahis
tad asya hṛdayaṃ punar vyajani tādṛg antar bahiḥ ||JGc_1,27.52|| [pṛthvi]
 [27] tataś ca, saha-kāntaḥ kāntā-samudayaḥ śakunta-kula-kala-kolāhalāt prātar iti -kalita-camatkāraḥ kampa-sampat-sampatad-asram ajasra-bhāvanā-nidānaṃ kathañcid eva viśleṣam iyeṣa |
 [28] tathā viśliṣya ca-
 tiryak paśyan muhur api mithas tatra tatrāpi sāsrī- bhāvād vyasraṃ mithunam atha tat kṛṣṇa-rādhādi nāma | gehaṃ gacchad yad iha gamanāyāśakan tan na citraṃ dhanyānāṃ syād ucitam akhilaṃ yat prayatnaṃ vināpi ||JGc_1,27.53|| [mandā]
ajani bahu-vyathatāntar bahu-dayitānāṃ viyogatas tasya | sarvāvaraka-rug-antaram iva jajñe sā tu rādhikā-viyutiḥ ||JGc_1,27.54|| [gīti]
 jyautsnīṃ śāradikāṃ vihṛtya vividhaṃ tasmin balād āgataṃ vīkṣya brāhma-muhūrtam ullala-dhiyaś channādhva-mūrti-kriyāḥ | tat-tat-keli-kalā-vilāsa-valita-svāntāḥ sva-kānta-priyāḥ sāntas tarṣam anantar īṣad udita-śrānti vrajaṃ prāviśan ||JGc_1,27.55|| [śārdūla]
children.translated_text:
And then:
'Each couple, weighing the subsequent separation from each other, | drenched by falling tears, embraced one another. | Thus all bodies were certainly moist externally — | and his heart too became just so, within and without!' || (JGc 1,27.52) [pṛthvī]
[27] Then, the beloved — together with the host of beloveds — startled by the dawn [announced by] the tumultuous warbling of flocks of birds, and with tears cascading from the treasure of trembling — born of the endless dwelling [of thought] — somehow or other submitted to separation.
[28] And having separated:
'Glancing sideways repeatedly at each other, here and there, with tearful | disposition, tearfully — that couple, called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-and-<s>Rādhā</s> and others — | going home — that they were unable to walk — that is not surprising; | for the blessed, everything appropriate happens even without effort!' || (JGc 1,27.53) [mandākrāntā]
'From the separation from him, great anguish arose within many beloveds; | but the separation from <s>Rādhikā</s> — that became | like an all-encompassing inner illness!' || (JGc 1,27.54) [gīti]
'Having sported variously on the autumnal moonlit night, when the <s>brāhma-muhūrta</s> arrived by force, | seeing it, with surging minds, their forms and actions concealed on the path — | with hearts entwined by the arts and graces of each and every amorous play — | the beloved women of their beloved, with inner thirst and slight weariness, | entered <s>Vraja</s>!' || (JGc 1,27.55) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]

children.text:
sa eṣa rāsotsava-viśeṣaś ca nivṛtta iti bahir eva vṛttaṃ nāntaḥ, yataḥ-
 rāsotsavaṃ kila samāpya gṛhādi-kṛtya- vyagrāś ca tan-mayatayā vraja-vāma-netrāḥ | nānā-vilāsa-maya-nartana-gīta-vādyaṃ sākṣād iva vyadadhatātra ca tat tad eva ||JGc_1,27.56|| [vasantatilakā]
 netā yeṣu tu rāsa-keliṣu bhavet kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ nāyikāḥ śrī-jaitra-vraja-subhruvo, rasa-kathās tatraiva nirlāñchanāḥ | tat-tad-varṇanam eva kāvya-vibudhāḥ kārtsnyena kuryuḥ paraṃ kintu śrī-śuka-sammataṃ na yad idaṃ pūryeta taiḥ sarvakaiḥ ||JGc_1,27.57|| [śārdūla]
[30] snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-hanta, catvāras te kumārakāḥ kva gatāḥ? |
 [31] madhukaṇṭha uvāca-pūrvam ārūḍha-mahā-taravaḥ paścān nija-prabhoḥ sva-gṛha-vartmānuvartanam avadhāya, dūra-cariṣṇutayā tūṣṇīm evānuvartiṣṇutām avāpuḥ iti |
[32] tad evaṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ prathitam api rāsa-līlā-varṇanaṃ triyāmāniyamataḥ saṃkṣipya tadīya-samādher vikṣipyamāṇatā-sañjanāya sāñjalir vyañjayāmāsa-
 sa īdṛg vallabho labdhas tvayā śrīmati rādhike | yaṃ bheje rāsa-rabhasāt trilokī nāyikā-nibhā ||JGc_1,27.58|| [anuṣṭubh]
 [33] atha kañja-netraḥ kṛtāñjalitayā pratīkṣitānujñā-sārau sūta-kumārau svāntikam āhūya bhūyaḥ paricaskāra nijānām aṅgānām aṅganānām api pariṣkāra-dravyeṇa |
 [34] yad anu dāna-parvaṇā sarva eva bhāsamānaḥ sabhā-sajjanaḥ pratyekam eka-vyaktir api kriyā-lāghavād bahu-vidha-nibhāṃ vyaktim avāpa |
[35] tato brāhma-muhūrte muhūrta-viśramāya sarva eva sva-sva-dhāma jagāma |
  iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
rāsa-prapañca-pañca-pūraṇī-pūraṇam nāma
saptaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||27 ||
children.translated_text:
This special <s>rāsa</s> festival was thus concluded — outwardly; but not inwardly, because:
'Having concluded the <s>rāsa</s> festival, the lotus-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>, though busy with household duties, | through their absorption in him, | performed exactly that very dance, song, and instrumental music of manifold play — as if directly [in his presence]!' || (JGc 1,27.56) [vasantatilakā]
'In those <s>rāsa</s> sports where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself would be the leader, the beautiful-browed women of victorious <s>Vraja</s> the heroines, | and the tales of <s>rasa</s> therein are blemishless — | those very descriptions, the learned poets of <s>kāvya</s> should compose in their entirety — | but that which is approved by <s>Śrī Śuka</s> — even all of them together could not fulfill it!' || (JGc 1,27.57) [śārdūlavikrīḍitam]
[30] <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Alas, where have those four boys gone?'
[31] <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Having first climbed great trees, then observing their master's homeward path, through their nature of far-roaming, they silently attained the state of following [him].'
[32] Thus <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, condensing the well-known description of the <s>rāsa-līlā</s> out of the constraint of the three watches of the night, in order to generate the disruption of her [<s>Rādhā's</s>] absorption, made a gesture with folded hands:
'Such is the beloved obtained by you, O glorious <s>Rādhikā</s>! | He whom the three worlds, resembling heroines, worshipped in the fervor of the <s>rāsa</s>!' || (JGc 1,27.58) [anuṣṭubh]
[33] Then the lotus-eyed one, through the gesture of folded hands, having summoned the two bard-princes — whose permission had been awaited — near him, adorned them again with the adornment-materials of his own limbs and of the women's limbs.
[34] Whereupon, by the festival of gift-giving, the entire resplendent assembly — each individual being even one single person — through the lightness of action attained a manifold manifestation.
[35] Then, at the <s>brāhma-muhūrta</s>, for a moment's rest, all went to their respective abodes.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the Twenty-seventh Chapter, named
'The Fulfillment of the Five Chapters of the <s>Rāsa</s> Elaboration.'
||27||

children.text: athāṣṭaviṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the Twenty-eighth Chapter.

children.text: ambikā-vana-gamana-saṃvidhānaṃ
children.translated_text: The Arrangement of the Journey to the <s>Ambikā</s> Forest.

children.text: atha pratyahavat prabhāta-bhāsamānāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ svāvasara-jāta-prasaraḥ snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭham āha sma- madhukaṇṭha śrūyatām anantaraṃ hari-caritam |
children.translated_text: Then, in the assembly shining like the morning as on every day, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, having found an occasion for his own arising eagerness, spoke with longing: 'O <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, hear the subsequent deeds of <s>Hari</s>!'

children.text: tataḥ sarvānanda-varṣe harer navame varṣe parutnād apy adhikatayā yatnād aiṣamastye sāmastyena kṛta-vistāre giri-yajña-sāre nirvṛtte māsa-katipaye ca vṛtte vilakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇā śiva-kṣaṇadātipracuraṃ jana-samājam ājahāra | kintu prāyaśo yaśodhanādikām anayā sāmānādhikaraṇyād ambikāraṇyāya samam ambikā-pati-pūjanārthaṃ janā varṣaṃ varṣaṃ prati saharṣaṃ gacchanti | yacchanti ca vividhāni dhanāni kimuta tasyāṃ yogaviśeṣād asamāyāṃ samāyām | yatra kutūhalāvakalanādi-līlā-kallolinī-kallola-lola-śrī-gopāla-cālita-cittā gopālāḥ | kiṃ bahunā, gopāla-kṣiti-pāla-caraṇāś ca tad-yātrā-spṛhā-pātratām avāpuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, in the year of universal bliss — <s>Hari's</s> ninth year — with greater effort than even the previous [year], in the present year, when the essence of the mountain-sacrifice (<s>Govardhana-pūjā</s>) had been accomplished with full comprehensiveness, and some months had passed, the auspicious night of extraordinary characteristics abundantly gathered a great assembly of people. Moreover, generally, to <s>Yaśodhanā</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>) and the like, to the <s>Ambikā</s>-forest — on account of the shared grammatical correlation [of the name] — people went year after year with joy, for the worship of <s>Ambikā's</s> lord (<s>Śiva</s>). And they bestowed various riches — how much more so in that extraordinary year, with its special conjunction! Where the cowherds, their minds stirred by the waves of the playful river of pastimes — curiosity-perception and such — of the glorious <s>Gopāla</s>! In short, even the feet of the cowherd king attained the state of being a vessel of desire for that pilgrimage.

children.text: saṃcerire ca te cireṇa mahārambha-sambhāra-bhāra-hāra-viśaṅkaṭa-vāra-niḥsāraṇayā | tatra janair nānā-sāmagrīr agarhya-vahyānaḍuhaś cānāṃsi vāhayantaḥ kolāhala-kutūhalam anvabhuvaṃś ca |
children.translated_text: And they set forth, after a long time, through the formidable process of assembling, carrying, and dispatching the burdens of great preparations. There, the people, making blameless oxen draw carts bearing various provisions, experienced the tumult and curiosity.

children.text:
yatra putrānurāga-parimala-nirmala-pātrī vraja-dharitrī kṣiti-pālayitrī nānā-gopa-kalatrāṇāṃ sukha-satrāyamāṇatayā taiḥ saha satra-yātrāṃ cakāra | kiṃ bahunā, go-gokula-pālana-kṛte kṛtehānupanandābhinandādīn ṛte sarva eva parva-pūrvaṃ calanti sma | yatra lālya-bhāvataḥ saṃnanda-nandanāv agrajam anuvrajataḥ sma lālaka-bhāvāt taj-janmānam anu ca |
 [5] tatra viśeṣatas tu-
children.translated_text:
Where the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, protector of the earth, a pure vessel of the fragrance of filial love, undertook the pilgrimage-procession together with the wives of various cowherds, as if making it a festive hall of happiness. In short, for the sake of protecting the cows and cowherds, except for <s>Upānanda</s>, <s>Abhinanda</s>, and others assigned for that purpose, all set forth on the eve of the festival. Where the two sons of <s>Nanda</s> — out of the state of being cherished — followed the elder one [<s>Nanda</s>], from the state of the cherishing [parents] following their offspring.
[5] There, especially:

children.text:
mukha-kamala-virājan-nāṭya-dṛk-khañjarītā
stana-kanakaja-kumbha-bhrāji-patrāvalīkā | caraṇa-sarasijāṇāṃ haṃsaka-svāna-ramyā
vraja-nija-mahilālī tatra bhavyaṃ babhāra ||JGc_1,28.1||
children.translated_text: the assembly of <s>Vraja's</s> own women bore a splendid [appearance] there! ||28.1||

With <s>khañjarīṭa</s>-bird-like dancing eyes shining on the lotus of the face,
with leaf-garland patterns gleaming on the golden-pot-like breasts, with the charming swan-like sounds of the lotus-feet —

children.text:
tataś ca-
na paraṃ cākṣuṣam āsīt tad-vraja-jana-calanaṃ vidūrataḥ kintu | śakaṭa-ghaṭāṭananād vādād apy andha-vedyaṃ ca ||JGc_1,28.2||surāṇāṃ nṝṇāṃ ca pratipada-bahūbhāva-mayatāṃ
sa-vādyair gītādyaiḥ saha kusuma-varṣair jaya-ravaiḥ | mukundālokāya prathita-pathikālī-śavalanaiḥ
samantāt saṅghaṭṭair abhiyayur amī āmbika-vanam ||JGc_1,28.3||tatra ca-
bhrātrā satrā haris tatrāruhya kambali-vāhyakam | vicitra-mitra-gantrīṇāṃ vṛtaṃ pṛtanayāyayau ||JGc_1,28.4||kadācid unnataṃ tatra śakaṭaṃ ghaṭayan pṛthak | abhīṣṭaṃ draṣṭum utkaṇṭhī sa sma suṣṭhu pratiṣṭhate ||JGc_1,28.5|| sakhi-bala-balavān vihāra-caryāṃ
pathi vidadhat-kutukaṃ ca lokamānaḥ | muhur upacaritaḥ svayaṃ jananyā
bakaripur āmbika-kānanaṃ viveśa ||JGc_1,28.6|| tatra ca-
jaṅghālās te lakṣaśo loka-saṅghās
tīrthaṃ yātāḥ kṛṣṇam āpuś ca daivāt | tṛṣṇā-dīnāḥ pāthasas tat-prayātāḥ
saudhīṃ yadvad vṛṣṭim ante labhante ||JGc_1,28.7|| [6] tasminn idam adbhutam udbhūtam abhūt-
children.translated_text:
And then:
'That procession of the <s>Vraja</s> people was not merely visible from afar, but
from the rattling of the carts, it was perceptible even by the blind!' ||28.2||
'With musical instruments, songs and such, together with showers of flowers and cries of victory,
with the crowds of pilgrims adorning the renowned roadside at every step —
for the sight of <s>Mukunda</s> — with jostling on all sides,
they approached the <s>Ambikā</s>-forest!' ||28.3||
And there:
'<s>Hari</s>, with his brother, as part of the procession, mounting a blanket-covered cart,
surrounded by a retinue of various clever friends, went like an army!' ||28.4||
'Sometimes, setting up a high cart separately there,
eager to see what he desired, he stood forth excellently!' ||28.5||
'Mighty with the strength of his companion friends, performing playful pastimes
along the road, and observing curiosities — constantly served by his own mother —
the enemy of <s>Baka</s> entered the <s>Ambikā</s>-forest!' ||28.6||
And there:
'Those people in their hundreds of thousands, walking on foot, pilgrims to the sacred ford,
found <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> by divine fortune; wretched with thirst, having gone for water,
like those who at last obtain an ambrosia-like rainfall!' ||28.7||
[6] In that [place], this marvel arose:

children.text:
utphulla-netra-kamalaṃ pulaka-prasāra-
śaivālam aśru-milad-ūrmi-jana-pravāhaḥ | ākramya setum adhigamya suramya-kṛṣṇa-
śobhā-mahāmbudhim agāj jalatām apīha ||JGc_1,28.8|| [7] tataś cābhikhyā-mātrataḥ kṛta-sarva-vaśībhāvasya tasya tad-āsecanaka-rūpa-nirūpaṇāt paśya paśyety evāsmin paśyati loke kathaṃcit kṛta-nivāraṇe ca tasmin kolāhala-kāraṇe vraja-vāsi-janaḥ sarva eva yathāyatham āvāsam āsasāda |
 [8] āsādya ca purohita-hita-sahitatayā kṛta-snāna-dāna-vyāpāre śrī-vrajarāja-virājamāna-samāja-vāre kutukatas tairthika-sārtha-darśanārthaṃ snātānuliptatā-dīptaḥ sakhi-rāmārāma-ramaṇaḥ kamana-kamala-locanas tatra tatra bhramaṇa-kramam ācacāra | yatra nānā-deśa-janānāṃ veśa-niveśa-nirveśa-saṃveśa-bhāṣābhiniveśa-kriyā-viniveśa-viśeṣān anubhūya bahula-kutūhalam ākalayāṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text:
'With eyes like fully bloomed lotuses, with horripilation spreading like water-moss,
with waves of tears-mingled people flowing — having crossed the bridge
and reached the supremely beautiful ocean of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> splendor —
it attained the state of water even here!' ||28.8||
[7] Then, when all had been brought under his sway merely by his appearance, and when that overflowing beauty was being perceived — with cries of 'Look! Look!' — and when somehow a restraint was imposed upon that tumultuous crowd looking on, all the <s>Vraja</s>-dwelling people duly reached their respective lodgings.
[8] And having reached [there], having performed the activities of bathing and giving, accompanied by the family priest — in the splendid assembly presided over by the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> — out of curiosity, for the purpose of seeing the assemblage of pilgrims, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], bathed and anointed, radiant, the companion and delight of his friend <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), the enchanting lotus-eyed one, undertook a course of wandering here and there. Where, having experienced the special features of the costumes, settlements, transactions, residences, linguistic practices, and distinctive ritual customs of people of various lands, he apprehended an abundance of curiosity.

children.text:
yatra ca kṛṣṇaṃ paśya rāmaṃ paśya śrīdāmānaṃ paśyety amī paśyantaḥ kolāhalaṃ baṃhayām āsuḥ |
 [10] yatra ca tadīya-vṛndāni govindīya-sundaratā-maranda-vinisyandam amandaṃ nayana-rasanayā rasayanti | mohātiśayavanti vihita-hita-sarvasvātma-nivedanaṃ sāsra-namra-kamra-vadanaṃ sadana-sadanād asīdanti ca saṃjitāñjalitayā tasthuḥ |
 [11] śrī-kṛṣṇas tu tad aṅgīkṛtyāpi śīla-vṛttyā tadīya-snehaṃ sāṅgīkurvan madīyā eva bhavad-bhavadīyārthā mat-pratyarpaṇataḥ pratisvaṃ yathā-niṣṭham avatiṣṭhantām iti santoṣayan kramaśo nijāśramam evāśramam ājagāma |
 [12] āgamya ca sāyantanam aśanaṃ saṃgatya mātur mānasam ānandena vitatya praśasta-vastra-mālālaṃkāra-sāraṃ parikṛtya sakhibhir ātmānaṃ parivṛtya sarva-bhāgavata-śiva-pradasya bhāgavata-paramparā-parama-guroḥ śivasya varivasyāyāṃ śiva-rātri-yātribhiḥ pitrādibhir ekāgratayā sva-maṅgala-kṛte kṛta-jāgaraṃ svīya-parakīya-rājakīya-janakīya-bahala-kolāhala-prakāraṃ śivāgāram anu nānā-vidyā-vismāyakatayā vidyamānān saṃpaśyati sma |
children.translated_text:
Where, those crying 'Look at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Look at <s>Rāma</s>! Look at <s>Śrīdāma</s>!' — thus looking, they intensified the tumult.
[10] Where their groups, with the tongue of their eyes, abundantly savored the nectar of the beauty of <s>Govinda</s>'s handsomeness flowing copiously. Being overwhelmed with bewilderment, having offered their entire being — their all — as a gift, with tear-stained, bowed, beautiful faces, they poured forth from dwelling after dwelling and stood with palms joined.
[11] But glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, even while accepting that, through his gracious conduct reciprocating their affection, saying 'My own purposes and your purposes, through my returning [love], may each stand as determined by your respective devotion' — thus satisfying [them], gradually came to his own camp, [finding it to be] a [true] hermitage.
[12] And having arrived, having partaken of the evening meal together, having expanded his mother's mind with joy, having adorned himself with excellent garments, garlands, and ornaments, having surrounded himself with friends, and for the sake of his own auspiciousness, worshipping <s>Śiva</s> — the supreme guru in the succession of the supremely <s>Bhāgavata</s> lineage, who bestows what is auspicious upon all devotees — he beheld with wonder, throughout the <s>Śiva</s>-night vigil, the pilgrims keeping watch along with his father and others with single-pointed attention, and the extensive tumult of his own people, strangers, royal folk, and common folk, and the various forms of knowledge and marvel present at the temple of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text:
sarve vrajajanās tatra kalpa-vṛkṣa-samā babhuḥ | adhideva ivādīpyad dhanyaḥ parjanya-nandanaḥ ||JGc_1,28.9|| [13] prabhāte ca prabhāte vadānyatā-pracārāhṛta-viprādīnām agaṇeya-gaṇāya guṇa-guṇitānnādi-dānataḥ saṃmānataś ca vitānita-yaśasi śrī-vrajarāja-sadasi teṣu tat-tīrtha-yātri-śateṣu ca cira-paricita-caravat parama-prīti-sphītībhāvana-nītitaḥ katham api prasthāpiteṣu tasyām amāvasyāyāṃ tāsminn eva vraja-vasatibhiḥ saha pitṛbhyāṃ lālitaḥ sa harir vāsateyīm uvāsa |
 [14] tataḥ sā ca rātrir yātrika-jana-prācurya-pūryamāṇā nāsīd iti kolāhalāpagamena hyastana-jāgara-klamena ca suptiḥ sarvataś ca nirbharam evāvirbhavati sma |
children.translated_text:
All the <s>Vraja</s> people there became like wish-fulfilling trees;
the blessed son of <s>Parjanya</s> (<s>Nanda</s>) blazed like the presiding deity! ||28.9||
[13] And at dawn, when the innumerable groups of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, brought by the practice of generosity, had been honored with gifts of food multiplied by excellent qualities, and bestowed with respect — when the fame of the glorious king of <s>Vraja's</s> assembly was spread wide like a canopy — when those hundreds of pilgrims to the sacred ford, like familiar travellers of long acquaintance, had been dispatched through the conduct of supreme expanding affection, with great difficulty — on that new-moon night, <s>Hari</s>, cherished by his parents together with the other <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers, spent the night there.
[14] And that night, since the fullness due to the abundance of pilgrim folk was no more — through the departure of the tumult and the weariness from the previous night's vigil — sleep fully manifested on all sides.

children.text: yatra danujāmitras tu vrīḍātaḥ krīḍātaś ca kiṃcid dūragataḥ sakhi-jana-janita-sukhaṃ nidrāyate sma |
children.translated_text: There, the enemy of the demons (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), out of modesty and out of playfulness having gone somewhat far away, was sleeping in the happiness generated by his circle of friends.

children.text:
atha tasyāṃ niśi diśi diśy api darśita-tamasi rahita-dantagaraḥ kaścij jarada-jagaraḥ sarpaḥ sarpan vrajarāja-caraṇa-rājīvaṃ nijagāra |
[17] tena ca vīryavattayā nigīryamāṇe caraṇe śaraṇecchur vraja-dharaṇīśaḥ santata-kṛṣṇa-sphūrti-pūrti-pracita-cittatayā jāgrad eva kṛṣṇam uddiśya cukrośa | yathā-
children.translated_text:
Now, in that night, when darkness was displayed in every direction, bereft of fangs — some aged, lethargic serpent, slithering, swallowed the lotus-like foot of the king of <s>Vraja</s>.
[17] And when the foot was being swallowed by that powerful one, the lord of <s>Vraja's</s> earth, desiring refuge, his mind ever filled with the fullness of the awareness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, while still awake, cried out toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. As follows:

children.text:
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa bata kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa he
tāta mām ajagaro graseta kim | ity asau smaraṇatas tanūjanes
tasya moha-maya-bhāvam ayayau ||JGc_1,28.10|| [18] atha tat-pārśva-vartinaḥ śūra-cakra-vartinaś candra-hāsam ādāya samutthitāś candramasaṃ grasamānaṃ rāhum iva bāhu-śālinas taṃ paśyantaḥ pravyathitā vyarthī-bhūta-tat-prahāra-prayāsās tad-upāyāntaram apaśyantaś ca vyagratā-kvathitāḥ śarārubhir jvalad-agrodagra-dārubhir jaghnuḥ |
 [19] tathāpy atyajati tatrājagare prathama-śabdād eva jāgrad-vrajarāja-tanūjaḥ sura-gaja-rāja iva dhāvaṃs tarhy evājagāma |
children.translated_text:
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Alas, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O son!
Will the python devour me?'
Thus, from the remembrance of his offspring,
he went into a bewilderment-filled state. ||28.10||
[18] Then, the valiant warriors at his side, champions like the <s>cakravartins</s>, having taken up their moon-bladed swords and risen, seeing [the python] — like <s>Rāhu</s> swallowing the moon — mighty-armed, distressed, their efforts to strike proving futile, seeing no alternative means, agitated and boiling with anxiety, struck [it] with burning, fiercely blazing torches.
[19] Nevertheless, when the python did not release [the foot] — the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, awakened by the very first sound, like the king of celestial elephants, came running at that very moment.

children.text:
āgacchataś ca tasya sa dīrghatara-dīrgha-pṛṣṭhaḥ puccham anu vāṭa-ghaṭita-nyāyena caraṇa-pallava-spṛṣṭatāṃ prāpa |

[22] tat-kara-pallava-spṛṣṭa-caraṇāḥ śrī-vraja-rāja-caraṇāś ca yathāvad virājamānatām āpuḥ |
[23] tataḥ sāścaryaṃ kṛtāvalokeṣu sarva-lokeṣu sudarśana-nāma-dharaḥ sa tu vidyādhara-caraḥ punar-labdha-svarūpa-varas taṃ praśaṃsan sva-śāpa-vṛttāntaṃ śaṃsaṃs tadīyāṃ kṣamām āśaṃsaṃs tad-anujñātaḥ svādhiṣṭhānam eva pratiṣṭhate sma |
 [24] ye pūrvaṃ tatrāpatrapām apahāya śrī-vraja-patipatnī-prabhṛtayaḥ kula-strī-janāḥ kim utānye saṃsṛjyamānatayānusṛtya kṛtya-mūḍhatām anubabhūvuḥ |
 [25] samprati tu te yathāyathaṃ mithaḥ samupagūḍhāh kevala-mūḍha-rodanā babhūvuḥ |
 yathā tātaṃ kṛṣṇaś ca rāmaś ca kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ ca mātaraḥ | mātṝś cānyāstathānyo' nyam anye śiśliṣur unmadāḥ ||JGc_1,28.11|| [26] tad evaṃ kṛta-kṣapaṇāyāṃ kṣapāyāṃ tat-kṣaṇam eva tūrṇa-gamana-manasaḥ samam anaḥ-samūham ārohayantaś cira-gantavyaṃ panthānam antikam ivātikrāntavantaḥ prāptavantaś ca nija-vrajam |
 [27] yatropanandādayaḥ sa-nandanaṃ sahaja-mātraṃ śrīman-nanda-rājam anavadya-vādya-gīta-parīta-veda-ghoṣānugata-sarva-ghoṣā yathāyathaṃ saṃsajya nīrājya ca vrajopavanam āvāsya snapanādibhir upāsya ca tatraiva nija-gṛha-janaṃ prāpayya pākaṃ samāpayya ca sarvān eva sambhojya sukhena saṃyojya ca vartma-vārtāṃ saṃpṛcchya harṣa-dharṣādikaṃ samṛcchya ca sva-sva-vasatim anu vasatīṃ vāsayām āsuḥ |
 [28] atha samāpanam āha-
 īdṛśas te vrajādhīśa putraś citrayaśāḥ śaśī | yad-aṅghri-nakhara-jyotsnā tamaḥ sarvam anīnaśat ||JGc_1,28.12||
children.translated_text:
And as he approached, the [python], exceedingly long-backed, following [him] from the tail end, by the logic of a fence-encirclement, attained the touch of his foot-bud.
[21] And this one, touched by him, having released his [<s>Nanda's</s>] foot, of its own accord, unexpectedly rising from the serpent-form, assumed through an intermediary another body — the form of a <s>Vidyādhara</s>.
[22] And the feet of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, touched by the tender hand of his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] hand-bud, were duly restored to their radiant state.
[23] Then, when all people looked on with wonder, that <s>Vidyādhara</s> named <s>Sudarśana</s>, having regained his original form as a boon, praising him [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], narrating the story of his own curse, invoking his forgiveness, and having been given leave by him, returned to his own abode.
[24] Those who previously — setting aside embarrassment — the wife of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s> foremost, and the clan-women, let alone others, following [him] with intermingled [concern], experienced a bewilderment of not knowing what to do.
[25] But now, they, having mutually embraced as appropriate, became merely bewildered weepers.
As follows: 'The father [embraced] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>; the mothers [embraced] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>;
the mothers and other women likewise [embraced] each other;
and others — intoxicated — embraced one another!' ||28.11||
[26] Thus, when the night had been made to pass, at that very moment, with minds intent on swift departure, they mounted the assemblage of carts, traversed the long road as if it were short, and reached their own <s>Vraja</s>.
[27] Where <s>Upānanda</s> and others, joining the glorious king <s>Nanda</s> together with his sons and his mere-born [family], accompanied by irreproachable music, song, and Vedic chanting followed by the sounds of the entire cowherd settlement — duly meeting and performing the lamp-waving ceremony, settling them in the <s>Vraja</s> garden, serving them with baths and such, then delivering their household members there, completing the cooking, feasting all, happily uniting [them], and inquiring about the news of the journey, encountering joy, thrill, and such — they settled [everyone] into their respective dwellings for rest.
[28] Then he spoke the conclusion:
'Such, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>, is your son — of marvelous fame, [radiant as] the moon!
By the moonlight of whose toenails, all darkness was destroyed!' ||28.12||

'She places <s>tamāla</s> trees near <s>Vraja</s>
and luminous herbs in the far regions of <s>Vraja</s>' — thus and so forth. There, in that tryst, <s>Vṛndā</s>, together with <s>Vṛndā's</s> [attendants], performed service to <s>Hari</s>. ||29.2||
And then:
He illuminated the forests, he attracted the beloveds here;
through those <s>rāsa</s>-extended, hastening nights, these [gopīs] kept vigil! ||29.3||
The beautiful-thighed one obtained [her beloved] again and again — then <s>Hari</s>
held those sports in his heart like necklaces, one by one! ||29.4||
[3] Once, by the conduct of a thief, he came to their houses. There, the direction [was thus]:
With the help of <s>Lalitā</s>, assuming the guise of <s>Viśākhā</s>,
and when reversed, reversely — <s>Hari</s> entered in the darkness the house of <s>Rādhā</s>! ||29.5||
[4] There, in the pitch darkness, words spoken under the pretext of addressing a friend to the one whose coyness was desired:

children.text:
susakhīyati te subhrūr asau gopa-matallikā | śape tubhyaṃ lapeyaṃ ca svayaṃ sakhyam urīkuru ||JGc_1,29.6|| [5] tatra kathaṃcid api tad-āgamane vṛddhābhiḥ kiṃcid ivāvagate kuñjāneva sva-līlayā kañja-locanas tābhiḥ samaṃ rañjayati |
 [6] tatra tat-preyasyā vṛddhābhivañcanā-cañcutā, yathā-
yas tvāṃ rātriṣu vṛddhe mām api devo vibhīṣayate | sa tu mantribhir utkalito goṣṭhāt kuñjān vimardayati ||JGc_1,29.7||[7] tasmād atrānyathā māvagās tatra ca māgā iti dhvanitam |
children.translated_text:
'That beautiful-browed cowherd girl befriends you warmly!
I swear to you and beseech — accept her friendship yourself!' ||29.6||
[5] There, when his arrival was somehow slightly detected by the elder women, the lotus-eyed one, by his own playfulness, delighted with them only in the bowers.
[6] There, the cleverness of his beloved in deceiving the elder women, as follows:
'He who frightens you, O old one, and me too during the nights, O god —
he, having been incited by his counselors, crushes the bowers from the cattle-settlement!' ||29.7||
[7] Therefore, the suggestion is: 'Do not understand otherwise here, and do not come there!'

children.translated_text:
Now, the [words of the] friend:
'Truly, O old woman! On the excellent cheek of my friend, the mark of a <s>makara</s>-shaped earring —
not drawn by me out of curiosity, nor by the lying rival-wife!' ||29.8||
[9] Here, by the figure of contradiction through 'my being her friend' and 'that one being a rival wife,' the suggestion is that 'it was indeed drawn by me.' [10] But by the poet, who follows that [suggestion], its falseness [is implied].
[11] Now, right in <s>Vraja</s> itself, due to the removal of obstacles, the <s>proṣita-bhartṛkā</s> (one whose husband is away) is described. [12] There, the contemplation of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'You see <s>Rādhā</s>, you speak, you touch, and within yourself you embrace her;
within yourself, you enjoy the reciprocal actions initiated by her and rejoice!
Yet you do not consider this as trust — if even so you have gone to another state,
then tell me — O you! — longing for union with her, will your happiness be achieved?' ||29.9||
[12] The words of the friend to Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text:
bhūṣaṇam agni-prāyaṃ bhūṣaṇa-nibham agnim apy asau rādhā | tvad-virahe yā kalayati sā katham anyaiḥ samādheyā ||JGc_1,29.10|| tasyāḥ prāṇā bhavān sā ca bhavat-prāṇā iti sphuṭam | etad-vācā laghūkartuṃ prāṇantīṃ māṃ tu dhik prabho ||JGc_1,29_11||[13] athotkaṇṭhitā | tatra ca taṃ prati sakhī-vacanam-
 tām eva prerayaty uccair utkaṇṭhā tvāṃ tu naiti sā | iti tasyām asau kṛṣṇa vitṛṣṇā-śarma nāñcati ||JGc_1,29.12||
children.translated_text:
'Ornaments like fire, and fire resembling ornaments — this <s>Rādhā</s>,
who endures [both] in your separation — how can she be comforted by others?' ||29.10||
'Her life-breath is you, and she is your life-breath — that is clear;
shame on me, O lord, who would diminish this with mere words, while she barely breathes!' ||29.11||
[13] Now, the <s>utkaṇṭhitā</s> (the one in eager longing). And there, the words of the friend to him:
'Longing drives her forth loudly, but she does not come to you;
thus, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she does not attain in that [state] the peace of desirelessness!' ||29.12||

and of power devoid of all defects!
How then would you superimpose upon her

Now, the <s>abhisārikā</s> (the one setting out to meet her lover). There, the mocking words of a certain one to her:
'Where do you go at twilight, O restless-eyed one, with single-minded eagerness for the foremost?
Even there, bearing in your mind some foremost spot —
that [rival] does not perceive your course — yet seeing a <s>tamāla</s> tree again and again,

'You have ascended the western mountain, [which is] set with the gem of the sky;
I suspect that you go to the vicinity of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to perform your own task!' ||29.16||

children.translated_text:
There, the setting-out, as follows:
'And others too set out, possessed by emotion — on bright nights, in disguises
made bright-white, covering their true selves — this word is true!
But those cowherd-women of highest rank, from the memory of contact with the beloved's body,
becoming joyful, enveloped in the luster of their smiles, rendered those [disguises] futile!' ||29.17||
'The co-extensionality of radiance and darkness was secretly contrived;
but even so, it created in the darkness the illusion of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> for the women of <s>Vraja</s>!' ||29.18||
'From the very beginning, the heart trembles; from setting forth, the pair of feet
becomes paralyzed — ah! — as the mind closes, the beloved is blocked in the body!
Of those bowed-browed cowherd-women, in the act of setting out, the supreme cause

children.text: daivaṃ yan nayate tad-antikam amūs taṃ vā balāt karṣati ||JGc_1,29.19||
children.translated_text: is destiny, which either leads them to his vicinity or forcibly draws him [to them]!' ||29.19||

tatrādṛṣṭe bhavati samaya-kṣepa-leśākṣamā sā | cakre cakrāṅkita-kara mahā-kampa-sampad-vihastā
children.translated_text:
Sometimes, a certain one persuades another to go to <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> proximity even during the day, under a pretext, as follows:
'O friend, look — all around, a flock of peacocks
is dancing, free from the ways of fear!
Surely, playfully approaching the object [of their dance],
a new rain-cloud of excellence appears!' ||29.20||
[18] Here, the solitude and the presence of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the midst are suggested. Now, the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (one adorned and waiting):
'She gathers flowers, choosing; she arranges a bed — this woman of <s>Vraja</s> —
[with items] that do not clearly exist even in the three worlds, ah, nor even in the avenues of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>!
Thus, the adorned-and-waiting one shines, accompanied only by her shadow;
but her companion, who had arranged the rendezvous, knows nothing at all, as it were!' ||29.21||
There, the words of the friend to him, when she was distressed by eager longing:
'Having prepared the bed, contemplating your arrival all around —
when you are not seen there, she is unable to endure even the slightest delay!
She, with the excellence of great trembling rendering her hands unsteady, O one whose hand bears the disc-mark —

children.text: śasta-kalpaṃ kṛtam api ca tat kalpayantī viśīrṇam ||JGc_1,29.22||
children.translated_text: even what she had prepared as fitting, she, [now] rearranging, makes it fall apart!' ||29.22||
