 mānini vacmi tvām aham iha suhṛdāṃ tava śṛṇotu vṛndaṃ ca | sahajā yā nija-vṛttir govinde svayam upāsva tām eva ||JGc_1,29.25|| [23] tatra kaṭhorāyamānāṃ prati ca-
children.translated_text:
Now, the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the one with a faithless lover). And there, the words of the friend to him:
'You would make some [woman] a <s>khaṇḍitā</s> through the contact of your nails and other bodily marks;
but she whom you made thus without that [excuse] — therein lies your great artistry!' ||29.24||
[22] The words of the messenger to the <s>khaṇḍitā</s>, being the composition of a friend's reproach to her:
'O proud one, I speak to you here — let the company of your friends hear too!
The innate nature that is your own conduct toward <s>Govinda</s> — cultivate that very thing yourself!' ||29.25||
[23] And to her who was becoming hardened:

children.text: mānāgni-maya-dṛg-vāṇaṃ muñca tvaṃ kiṃ nu garvasi | rādhe kṛṣṇaś ca dṛk-paryak-parjanyāstraṃ vimokṣyati ||JGc_1,29.26||
children.translated_text:
'Release the arrow of your gaze, which is made of the fire of pride — why do you boast?
O <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too will release the weapon of the rain-cloud of his all-encompassing glance!' ||29.26||

children.text:
atha sambhramād āgatasya nakharādi-sparśāt kṣatāyamāna-raktimnā samaktasya kāntasya vacanaṃ tasyāḥ prativacanaṃ ca |
dayite dayita kathaṃ tvaṃ malina-mukhī dhig na vetsi hā kim idam | nakha-radana-kṣatam ūhet tvayi supte supti-rākṣasī cakre ||JGc_1,29.27||[25] atha tasyāḥ sakhyā saṃvādaḥ-
 jalade vilasati vidyud bibhyati hṛdayāṇi bhīrūṇām | hasasi hariṃ kimu mugdhe na hi hṛdi citraṃ stuve' ham etasya ||JGc_1,29.28||[26] atha tasyāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ prati-
children.translated_text:
Now, the speech of the beloved who arrived in haste and was being wounded by the touch of nails and such, and her reply:
'O beloved, O beloved, why are you dark-faced? Shame! Alas, do you not know what this is?
She would say it is a nail-and-teeth wound — but while you slept, the she-demon of sleep did this!' ||29.27||
[25] Now, the dialogue with her friend:
'In the rain-cloud, lightning flashes — the hearts of the timid tremble!
Why do you laugh, O innocent one? I do not [laugh] — I praise this wonder in my heart!' ||29.28||
[26] Now, her [words] to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text:
āvṛṇutāmaruṇāṃśur nakha-pada-sindūra-cihnāni | añjanam api kṛṣṇābhaṃ tat tu tavauṣṭhaḥ sphuṭaṃ kurute ||JGc_1,29.29|| pūrvāṃ haritam ākramya niṣkrāman kṛṣṇa-nīradaḥ | nihnute śaśabhṛl-lekhāṃ harid-antara-lajjayā ||JGc_1,29_30|| strī-bhāvam ākalayituṃ kamaṭhānukāraṃ
gacchan-mahādri-talam āśritavān bhavān yat | tac cājitasya na tavānucitaṃ yatas tvaṃ
svāṃ devatāṃ ramayituṃ sudhayodyato' si ||JGc_1,29.31|| māmapi hitvā krīḍasi tāmapi hitveti nānṛtaṃ vacanam | ekaṃ tatra jahāteranyadrūpaṃ dadhāter hi ||JGc_1,29_32|| nīrasā sarasā veti viviktir nātikāminām | paśya vaṃśyā mukhaṃ nāyaṃ pibann ujjhati mādhavaḥ ||JGc_1,29_33||[27] tatra śrī-kṛṣṇasya vacanam-
 rādhe vapuṣā tanvī komala-hṛdayātisūkṣmādhīr asi ca | mānaḥ katham etāvān māti tvayi tat tu pṛcchāmi ||JGc_1,29.34|| mukham abjaṃ tava rasanā pallava-patrī kathaṃ vacaḥ krūram | āṃ jñātaṃ kila yasmāt tan-mūlaṃ bhāti hṛd-vajram ||JGc_1,29_35||[28] bhavatu ca-
 yathā me rocate māno na prasādas tathā tava | yatra svādhīnatā-vyaktiṃ kuruṣe tāḍanena ca ||JGc_1,29.36|| ardito' pi ruṣā rādhe līlābjenāsmi nārditaḥ | hanta mat-kaṇṭakair etat tvad-aṅghri-suhṛd ardyate ||JGc_1,29_37||[29] tad evam upavadamāne tasmin punas tasyā vacanam-
children.translated_text:
'Let the dawn-glow conceal the marks of nail-prints and vermilion!
Even the black collyrium — for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-hued [stains] — but your lip clearly reveals [them]!' ||29.29||
'Covering the former green [love-mark], the dark <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-cloud departing
conceals the crescent-moon streak — from the shame of [revealing] the green within!' ||29.30||
'To assume the female state, you assumed the form of a tortoise
and took shelter beneath the great mountain — O unconquered one, that was not unfitting for you, since
you are prepared to delight your own deity with nectar!' ||29.31||
'"Having abandoned even me, you sport; having abandoned her too" — that is no false word!
For there, one [form] is being left while another form is being assumed!' ||29.32||
'Juiceless or juicy — such discrimination does not belong to the excessively passionate!
Behold, this <s>Mādhava</s>, drinking the face of the flute, does not abandon it!' ||29.33||
[27] There, the speech of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, you are slender of body, tender of heart, of exceedingly subtle intellect!
How then is such great pride contained in you? — that I ask!' ||29.34||
'Your face is a lotus, your tongue a tender leaf-plate — how then [can it produce] harsh words?
Ah, I understand — since at its root shines the diamond of your heart!' ||29.35||
[28] So be it:
'Your pride pleases me as your grace does not,
wherein you manifest the display of self-governance — even with a strike!' ||29.36||
'Though struck by your anger, O <s>Rādhā</s>, I am not struck by the play-lotus!
Alas — by my thorns, your foot, the friend [of the lotus], is wounded!' ||29.37||
[29] Thus, as he was speaking coaxingly, her words again:

children.text:
nirvṛty-ambudhi-kumbhajaḥ sthiti-mahā-meghāvalī-mārutaḥ
prāṇānāṃ pavanāśanas tanuvanī-naidāgha-dāvānalaḥ | so' yaṃ te viraho yayā bata mayā soḍhastayā vā kathaṃ
soḍhuṃ hanta na śakyate nava-navaḥ padmāpate durnayaḥ ||JGc_1,29.38|| [30] evaṃ rudatīṃ sakhīm ālakṣya sakhī taṃ prāha-
 anurāgavatī sandhyā svaccho' yaṃ vāsarastataḥ | sthāne tayā tasya saṅgo na rātryā malinātmanā ||JGc_1,29.39||[31] tvayi tu tad-etad-viparītaṃ pratīyate tato na svacchateti vyañjanā | tataḥ sā māninī punas tām āha-
 dīpa-jvālā mama hṛdi gatā sneham uddhūya vakre
cakre yena pratihati-mitā taṃ kathaṃ nindasi tvam | nirdvandvāhaṃ sapadi bhavitāsmy eva so' py eṣa nānā-
gopī-saṅghāt pramadam ayitā hanta kiṃ kasya duḥkham ||JGc_1,29.40|| [32] atha tasya tad-bāṣpāpasāraṇāya vyāja-racanaṃ vacanam-
 mīnād api tan-muktā-
phalam udbhavatīti ratna-śāstrārtham | paśyann iva mama hastas
tava mukham abhiyāti mānini prasabham ||JGc_1,29.41|| [33] tataś ca sā vimukhī-bhavantī manasīdaṃ vadantī kalahāntaritā-bhāvam āsasāda |
 aiṣīstvaṃ yadi mānasa mānenāmuṃ vaśīkartum | vaśage' py asmin kṛṣṇe tyajasi na kiṃ taṃ vṛthā-bhūtam ||JGc_1,29.42||[34] tadā ca sakhī tam uvāca-
 yā tava hṛdaya-vidāraṃ nakharair akaron murārāte | tāṃ manuṣe priya-dayitāṃ jvalati tu tasmād dṛg asmākam ||JGc_1,29.43|| yā khalu mānam amānaṃ dadhire tvan-māna-jīvanā dayitā | ghaṭate gopī-vallabha tasyāḥ sphuṭam asugamaḥ sugamaḥ ||JGc_1,29_44||[35] iti sakhīṣu parāṅ-mukhīṣu bahu taṭasthatāṃ ghaṭayan dūra-deśīya-deśam aṭati sma yadāsau, tadā tu-
 rādhāyā dṛṣṭa-mānāyāḥ sṛṣṭa-romāñca-sañcayāḥ | vaiṇava-dhvani-jātīyā jīyāsuḥ kīcaka-svanāḥ ||JGc_1,29.45|| [36] tad avagamya vāmāyā vacanam-
 na vadasi paruṣaṃ ruṣaṃ na dhatse
manasi ca tatra kathaṃ kṛtāparādhe | hari hari satataṃ vimānitāhaṃ
tvayi bata śarma kadāpi nāparādhe ||JGc_1,29.46||[37] tatra tasyā manaḥ-kathā-
children.translated_text:
Born from the ocean of bliss, the wind of the great cloud-mass of steadfastness, the devouring wind of the vital breaths, the summer forest-fire of the body-forest — this separation of yours, endured somehow by me, but how can it be endured by her? Alas, O lord of <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), your ever-renewed treachery cannot be borne! // [śārdūla]
[30] Thus, seeing her friend weeping, the companion (<s>sakhī</s>) said to him:
'The twilight is full of passion; this day is clear — therefore it is fitting that his company be with her, not with the night, which is of impure nature!' // [anuṣṭubh]
[31] 'But in your case, the opposite of that is perceived — therefore the suggestion is that there is no clarity.' Then that proud one (<s>māninī</s>) again said to her:
'The flame of the lamp, having entered my heart and dispelled affection, has made my face the object of its counter-measure — how can you blame it? I shall instantly become free from all conflict; and he too, from his association with hosts of various <s>gopīs</s>, will produce no delight — alas, whose is the sorrow?' // [mālinī]
[32] Then, his words devised as a pretext to wipe away her tears:
'Even from a fish, the fruit of a pearl arises — such is the meaning of the science of gems! As if perceiving this, my hand approaches your face forcibly, O proud one!' // [āryā]
[33] And then she, turning away, saying this in her mind, attained the state of <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (one separated by a quarrel):
'If you wished, O mind, to bring him under control through pride — [even] when this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is already under control, why do you not abandon that [pride] which has become futile?' // [āryā]
[34] Then the companion (<s>sakhī</s>) said to him:
'She whose nails tore your heart, O enemy of <s>Mura</s> — her, the dear beloved, you still desire! Therefore our eyes burn!' // [āryā]
'She who indeed placed pride as non-pride, the beloved who lives by your pride — O beloved of the <s>gopīs</s>, for her clearly the difficult path becomes easy!' // [āryā]
[35] Thus, when the companions had turned away, greatly maintaining their neutrality, when he was wandering to a distant place, then:
'For <s>Rādhā</s>, whose pride was visible, clusters of horripilation were created — let the sounds of the bamboo-grove, of the flute-sound type, be victorious!' // [anuṣṭubh]
[36] Having perceived that, the words of the contrary one:
'You do not speak harshly, you do not hold anger in your mind — yet how [can this be] toward the one who has committed offenses? O <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! I am constantly dishonored — yet in you, alas, happiness never commits an offense!' // [puṣpitāgrā]
[37] There, her inner thought:

children.text:
mānaṃ kurviti vakti sā priya-sakhī mānaṃ na vedmi sphuṭaṃ
kauṭilyena yadi prasidhyati sa tat kauṭilyam evātra kim | hā tasya smita-kañja-cāru-nayanaṃ śyāmasya man-mānasaṃ
draṣṭuṃ vāñchati hanta kaṣṭam aparāṃ sphūrtiṃ kathaṃ gacchatu ||JGc_1,29.47|| āgas-kṛte' pi tasmai rajyati hṛdayaṃ khalaṃ tad etan me | tyaktuṃ tad api na śakyaṃ katham iva sa hariḥ parityājyaḥ ||JGc_1,29_48||tataś ca-
balān mānaṃ śikṣayantīr api tatra sakhī-tatīḥ | rādhayā sārdham ākarṣan jīyād veṇu-kala-svanaḥ ||JGc_1,29.49||[38] tasyā mukham avakalayya tat-tad-upamā-jātiyatayā saṃśayya sthitavantaṃ kāntaṃ prati sakhī-vacanam-
 tasminn api vidhu-buddhiṃ kartuṃ mā kṛṣṇa sāhasaṃ kārṣīḥ | sarvaṃ jetṛ tad etad bhrū-dhanur anu netra-vāṇam utkṣipati ||JGc_1,29.50||tataś ca-
children.translated_text:
'My dear companion says "she is manifesting pride" — I do not clearly know pride; if it is established through crookedness, then what is merely crookedness here? Alas, my mind desires to see the <s>śyāma</s> (dark) one's face, beautiful with its smiling lotus-eyes — how terrible! — how can it proceed to any other manifestation?' // [śārdūla]
'Even toward the offender, my wicked heart is attracted — this [heart] of mine! Even that cannot be abandoned — how then could that <s>Hari</s> be abandoned?' // [āryā]
And then:
'Let the sweet sound of the flute be victorious, which dragged even the rows of companions who were forcibly teaching pride, along with <s>Rādhā</s>!' // [anuṣṭubh]
[38] Having perceived her face and having stood in doubt due to the various categories of comparison, the companion's words to the beloved:
'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, do not venture to form the notion of "moon" regarding that [face]! That [face], which conquers everything, is casting an eye-arrow following the bow of the brow!' // [āryā]
And then:

children.text:
bhramarīvāmbujāraṇyaṃ śapharīva jalāśayam | kṛṣṇaṃ labdhvā pūrvameva dṛṣṭā sābhūnna tūttaram ||JGc_1,29.51||atha svādhīnabhartṛkā |
 nityaṃ yā yācitāpi priyatama-hariṇā necchati sparśa-mātraṃ
vācā seyaṃ muhus taṃ nidiśati rasanām apy aho saṃvarītum | tan manye nūnam asyāvayava-samuditir divya-sīdhu-prakāraḥ
saṅgād apy aṅga yasya prabhavati muhur unmāda-lakṣmīr amūdṛk ||JGc_1,29.52|| tatra ca vakti rūpaṃ yadā kṛṣṇas tadā sā rādhikādhikam | śṛṇoti naiva tat tasya paśyantī rūpam adbhutam ||JGc_1,29.53|| [39] etad-anantaraṃ sakhīnāṃ nibhṛtālāpaḥ-
 api līlāyitam anayā campakalatayā tamālādhaḥ | prāgalbhyāt punar etāṃ tad upari ramaṇa-spṛhāṃ vedmi ||JGc_1,29.54|| [40] atha śrīmat-parama-rūpa-gurūpadeśa-maya-svapna-kalitaṃ prātastana-lalita-rāga-saṃvalitaṃ lalitā-gītam-
 jāgaraṇād atha kuñja-vare | vīkṣita-bhāskara-ruci-nikare ||kāntā-nidrā-bhaṅga-kare | api saṅkalita-sva-parikare ||mama dhīr majjati kaṃsa-hare | mauli-śikhopari-piñcha-dhare ||[dhruvam]
children.translated_text:
'Like a bee-woman [finding] a lotus-garden, like a fish [finding] a lake — having obtained <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she was seen earlier, but not afterward!' // [anuṣṭubh]
Now, the <s>svādhīnabhartṛkā</s> (one whose husband is under her control):
'She who, though entreated constantly by the most beloved <s>Hari</s>, does not desire even the slightest touch — she, with her speech, repeatedly directs him to restrain even his tongue! Ah! I think her assembled limbs are surely a variety of divine liquor, from the mere contact with which such a manifestation of the splendor of intoxication repeatedly arises!' // [mālinī]
And there, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> describes her form, then that <s>Rādhikā</s> does not even hear it — exceedingly [absorbed in] beholding his wondrous form! // [anuṣṭubh]
[39] After this, the whispered conversation of the companions:
'Has this <s>campaka</s>-creeper indeed performed a pastime beneath the <s>tamāla</s>? Rather, due to her boldness, I know she has a desire for the lover [to come] atop her!' // [āryā]
[40] Now, the song of <s>Lalitā</s>, composed of a dream containing the instruction of the supremely beautiful preceptor, joined with a charming morning <s>rāga</s> (melody):
'Waking from the excellent bower, beholding the multitude of the sun's radiance, — breaking the sleep of the beloved — and yet gathering my own retinue — my mind is immersed, O slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, O wearer of the peacock-feather upon the crest of your head!' //refrain//

children.text: muhur ullāsita-yuvati-kare | samamanyā bahir anaya-care ||ghana-gahanādhvani gamana-pare | tatra ca bahu kṛta-sukha-vitare ||āśāstambhita-viraha-gare | dhāmni sanātana-śarma-hare ||iti|| ||JGc_1,29.55||
children.translated_text: '[In him] whose hand repeatedly delights the young women, who otherwise wanders outside in wrong conduct, who is devoted to traversing the dense forest-paths, and who there distributes happiness abundantly — who has propped up the pillar of hope against separation, in the abode that carries away eternal happiness — thus!' // [end of song]

children.text: dināntare sakhī-saubhāgyam-
children.translated_text: On another day, the good fortune of the companions:

children.text: kiṃcid vilokya kuñje sakhyāḥ prāgalbhyam ekāntāt |
children.translated_text: 'Having glimpsed a little of a companion's boldness privately in the bower,

children.text: smerā karam anu muralīṃ prāgād barhāvaliṃ śirasi ||JGc_1,29.56||
children.translated_text: smiling, she took the flute in hand and placed the peacock-feather garland upon her head!' // [āryā]

children.text:
tāṃ prati śrī-rādhā kim apīdam ācārya provāca-
śete mañju-nikuñja-talpam anu sa preyān iti preyasi
tvāṃ veṇuṃ kila hartum asya kutukāt prāhaiṣam asmi drutam | taṃ tu tvaṃ parihṛtya cāgatavatī śrānteva ca prekṣyase
children.translated_text:
To her, Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> spoke something as if to an <s>ācārya</s> (teacher):
'That dearest beloved is sleeping upon the lovely bower-couch' — O beloved,
'I sent this message to you: out of curiosity, I have come swiftly to steal his flute!
But you, having abandoned him, have also come — and you appear as if fatigued!'

children.text: tad-vartmāny adurī-cakartha rabhasā yan mādṛśāṃ durgamam ||JGc_1,29.57||
children.translated_text: 'You have quickly traversed that path which is impassable for the likes of me!' // [śārdūla]

children.text:
tad evaṃ tāsāṃ tasya ca prāvṛṣija-kṛṣivad daiva-vaśata eva vaśe vaśaṃvade tad-anantaraṃ vasanta-pañcamīm anu vasanta-rāgaṃ janayan gopāla-janībhir militvā śrīmān gopālaḥ khalu khelati sma | [44] tathā hi-tasyāṃ pañcamyām utkaṇṭhita-ṣaṭ-pada-khaṇḍita-tuṇḍa-mudrākula-mukula-maṇḍalatayā prathamam unmīliteṣu keṣucit puṇḍrakeṣu śrīman-mādhava-rādhādīnām abādham āgamanam asambhāvya bhṛśam unmanāyamānāyāṃ vṛndāyāṃ sumanāyamānā kācid āli-pālir āgamya tām ullāsitavatī-[45] sakhi vṛnde ! katham iva mandatāṃ vindase ? āgamya ramyam idam avagamyatām |
 [46] vṛndāha--kīdṛśam ?
[47] sā prāha-yādṛśaṃ bhavad-abhirucitam |
 [48] vṛndāha-kathyatāṃ tathyam |
 [48] sā prāha-kācid ālī mādhavī-maṇḍalam anu mādhavaṃ mādhava-prakāśa-darśanataḥ samujjṛmbhita-rādhā-vipralambha-bādhaṃ nibhālya tām ullolayāmāsa | ullolya ca saṅgataś calantī sakhībhir idaṃ vasanta-rāgeṇa gāyantī vallabham api lambhayāmāsa |
 [49] gānaṃ yathā-
 kṛṣṇa-vanaṃ sakhi bhāti saraṅgam | bhavatīm iva laghu netum adhīśaṃ | sevita-madhura-sa-saṅgham ||[dhruvam]
jāgaram itam iva mādhavikāśatam anukṛta-jṛmbhā-bhaṅgam | cumbati madhupa-gaṇe kṛta-bhaṅgi smārayati priya-saṅgam ||sarasa-rasālaja-mukula-kulaṃ paripulakayad iva samam aṅgam | ākāritam iva tava kurute pika-kalam anukalayad anaṅgam ||tvāṃ celā-kali-candana-marutā vāsayatānulavaṅgam | karṣati madhuripu-madhu-parvodita-vīṇā-veṇu-mṛdaṅgam ||nītāyāṃ tvayi mādhavi mādhava-mādhava-gāna-taraṅgam | kirati parāga-cayaṃ locanam iva naṭayati cāru-kuraṅgam ||iti sā labdhvā vallabham aniśaṃ manasā valitāsaṅgam | jayati nirupama-rūpiṇi madhye yamunā-mānasa-gaṅgam ||JGc_1,29.58||[51] atra ca padyam ekaṃ gadyate-
 vana-ruci-ruciraḥ śrīmān
madana-vinodāya nunna-gopīkaḥ | abhitaḥ surabhita-deśaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus, for those [<s>gopīs</s>] and for him, as if by the force of destiny like the monsoon-cultivation of farmers, afterward, generating the spring-<s>rāga</s> (melody of spring) following the <s>vasanta-pañcamī</s> (spring fifth-day), the glorious <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), having met with the cowherd women, indeed sported. [44] For thus: On that fifth-day, when some first shoots — whose bud-clusters were disturbed by the breaking open of their seal by the longing, sharp-mouthed bees — had blossomed, and when, upon the unanticipated arrival of the glorious <s>Mādhava</s> and <s>Rādhā</s> and others, <s>Vṛndā</s> was becoming exceedingly agitated — a certain row of companions, becoming well-disposed, came and delighted her:
[45] 'O friend <s>Vṛndā</s>! How can you experience dullness? Come — perceive this delight!'
[46] <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Of what kind?'
[47] She said: 'Of the kind that suits your taste!'
[48] <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Tell [me] the truth!'
[48] She said: 'A certain companion, seeing <s>Mādhava</s> near the <s>mādhavī</s>-bower, by the sight of the <s>mādhava</s> (spring)-like radiance, having perceived the pain of <s>Rādhā's</s> separation fully stirred up, agitated her. And having agitated her, walking together with her companions, singing in the spring-<s>rāga</s>, she caused even the beloved to be obtained.'
[49] The song, as follows:
'O companion, the forest of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> shines with deer! As if to lead you lightly to its lord, it serves a sweet companionship!' //refrain//
'The <s>mādhavikā</s> creeper, as if aroused from awakening, imitating the breaking of a yawn — when kissed by swarms of bees making their way — recalls the company of the beloved!' //a//
'The cluster of luscious mango-buds, as if causing horripilation simultaneously upon the body — as if beckoning to you — the cuckoo, producing its sweet melody, makes one perceive <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love)!' //b//
'The spring-breeze, fragrant with <s>celā</s>-grove sandalwood, making you dwell as if in a clove-garden — draws [you] with the <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, and <s>mṛdaṅga</s> born of the spring festival of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>!' //c//
'When you, O <s>Mādhavī</s> (spring-woman), have been brought, the wave of the spring-song of <s>Mādhava</s> in spring — scatters heaps of pollen, makes the eye dance, and makes charming deer dance!' //d//
'Thus, she, having obtained the beloved — constant, with a mind entwined in attachment — is victorious, O one of incomparable beauty, in the midst of the <s>Yamunā</s>, the <s>Mānasa</s>-lake, and the <s>Gaṅgā</s>!' //e//
[51] Here too, one verse is rendered in prose:
'Handsome with the forest's beauty, the glorious one, impelled by <s>Madana</s> (Love) for the sake of amusement, among impelled cowherd women, with fragrant surroundings on all sides —

children.translated_text: Thus, having heard this, she (<s>Vṛndā</s>), finding herself present there, showed [them] again in this manner:

 [53] atha tāvatīṃ gatim apy asahamānāḥ sahamānā guravaḥ kuravam ācarya paryavasthayā tāsāṃ svatantratām āvārya sarvato nirodham udbodhayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text:
'<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Hari</s> too — [behold] the horripilation-producing spring! She sings, following her own impetus, blossoming!' //refrain//
'He who instructs in every direction — the cuckoo following the fifth note, prolonging it — the one who drinks the honey of the spring-<s>vāsantī</s> creeper in secret — she [<s>Rādhā</s>] declares the bee as following along in song!' //a//
'He who delights, following the song's nectar — she savors the created [melody], with the lips approaching — the fragrance borne by the sandalwood-breeze of <s>Malaya</s>, staggering — she composes [verse about] the wind joining [them]!' //b//
'The instruments, filling the directions with stringed sound — she dances with the restless edge of my glance following them — she scatters powder, following the full [moon], endlessly — together with the playful women, endlessly!' //c//
'The drops of perspiration, following the shining — he bears the mass of pollen, with an unending luster!' //d// — thus.
[53] Then, the elders, unable to tolerate even that much freedom, having performed the <s>kurava</s> (the protective ceremony), through their authority, having curtailed the independence of those [<s>gopīs</s>], aroused restraint on all sides.

rādhā-gīr-bhaṅgi-mātrāt paricitim akarod astu tat kāmya-vastu ||JGc_1,29.72|| [58] tad evaṃ śrī-rādhayā tad-viraha-cintā-saṃbādhayāpi gata-tad-bādhayā kvacid anyathānyathā ca rajany antare punaḥ punar anya-bahu-vidha-veśaṃ keśavaṃ niśāmya bhaṇitam, yathā-
children.translated_text:
Where indeed the group of female guardians observed them from all sides — whereby <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> subjection to them arose of its own accord. Thus, in this state of distress, and everywhere when distress prevailed:
'She who looks at the path, who handles the flute, who sends a messenger and so forth, | who employs every other stratagem — that beloved, formerly together with his beloved! | When the mature restrictions and bonds of elders and the like [were in force], | attraction arose only as futility — whereby the vital points of those two were pierced!' || (JGc 1,29.61)
[55] And there, the inner thoughts of both, as follows:
'That the gaze of this beloved one was not formerly [directed at me] — that was supreme happiness; | I think — alas — that it has now occurred, and that is [his/her] suffering. | The possessiveness that has gradually arisen between him/her and oneself — that now | wishes to crush both — what shall I do here? What shall he/she do?' || (JGc 1,29.62)
'Only tonight, and only this much — I saw that beloved person, and he/she saw me too; | yet not even this much — alas — the ever-new Love-god touched [us] here swiftly! | If this appears as merely a dream, then even so I do not consider it the protection of my own life-breath; | or if it be the waking state — even then, no — ahaha! O beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, where indeed are you?' || (JGc 1,29.63)
'Between [them and] the dark-limbed one, the body, friends — all of them — | like a network of fire, bear the anguish of inner mental cleavage.' || (JGc 1,29.64) — thus.
'When those husbands thus became wrathful and the brides wept, | then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with longing, devised a pilgrimage as a pretext.' || (JGc 1,29.65)
'When that pilgrimage was devised with those [women] devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, | then the kingdom of [their] mind's desire was both abundantly realized and unrealized.' || (JGc 1,29.66)
'When <s>Govinda</s> set forth, finding a tall cart, | then the severance from their kinsman was perceived by those bird-eyed ones.' || (JGc 1,29.67)
'Night after night, wherever they stayed, there certainly | those [gopīs] attained union with him, as the moon [visits] the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s> (the lunar mansions).' || (JGc 1,29.68)
Accordingly:
'With those women of his own [circle] who were nearby — setting out for trysts, with blazing passion, | having dressed for the journey, with their rising and joyful play — | and with some who had been deceived, and some who were exceedingly pervasive, and some whose | couples had been displaced — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> enjoyed manifold play of his own on that path!' || (JGc 1,29.69)
'When the people of <s>Gokula</s> had gone on pilgrimage, then <s>Hari</s> fashioned | the guise of women whose livelihood was [reading] qualities — for the sake of proximity-happiness with those [gopīs].' || (JGc 1,29.70)
[56] There, the guise of a woman versed in astrology, <s>mantra</s>s, <s>yoga</s>, and <s>tantra</s>, as follows:
'O omniscient one! What is the happiness-giving abode in the three worlds? — <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> cow-settlement. What is the livelihood therein? — The singing of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. What is the incomparably auspicious attainment? — The desire for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. | What is to be enjoyed? — <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> form. What is the fruition here? — The attainment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, on all sides.' | Thus, to <s>Rādhikā</s>, this making of counter-replies — may <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> imposture protect us!' || (JGc 1,29.71)
[57] The guise of a messenger-woman, as follows:
'Whose maidservant are you? Whose is this [one] you follow? What qualities [does she have]? Equal to him? | What proof would there be of that? — Come to this secluded house, behold all my limbs!' | Thus, with a smile, the meaning spread across every direction — she who was appointed by him — | <s>Rādhā</s>, from the mere turn of her speech, recognized [him] — let that be the object of desire!' || (JGc 1,29.72)
[58] Thus, <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>, though crowded by the anxiety of separation from him, yet freed from that distress — somewhere in one way and somewhere in another — again and again during the night, having perceived <s>Keśava</s> in his many varied disguises, she spoke, as follows:

tad-aguru-sattvaṃ tasyā gṛhṇāmi gandha-jīvinyāḥ | tad-avadhi guravo mayi sakhi kṛṣṇam akṛṣṇaṃ ca bruvate ||JGc_1,29_81||[59] atha śrīvatsa-lakṣaṇasyāpy etad-upalakṣaṇaṃ bahu-racanaṃ vacanaṃ lakṣaṇīyam, yathā-

children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> attained the position of the pericarp [i.e., the central place] — this is our conviction!' || (JGc 1,29.88)

'This dark-limbed physician-woman has been obtained to cure the burning of my heart; | she touches the pulse of my hand, O friend — but curse it, why does she touch another limb?' || (JGc 1,29.73)
'This dark flute-player woman, | dwelling nearby, has appeared at midnight; | this ground of friendship is small — | so let my bed contract!' || (JGc 1,29.74)
'Let this dark figure be an incomparable poetess, learned in that very art! | How she knows our secrets — I do not know that!' || (JGc 1,29.75)
'This dark painter-woman reveals a wondrous picture in seclusion — | O friend, in which she has painted someone like me, accompanied by a man resembling herself!' || (JGc 1,29.76)
'In private I tell you this, O friend — nowhere else, anywhere: | this dark betel-offering woman knows the <s>mohana</s> (enchantment) <s>mantra</s>!' || (JGc 1,29.77)
'This figure of a garland-maker-woman spreads out garlands; | why does she suffuse the flowers with the fragrance of that dark-formed one?' || (JGc 1,29.78)
'This dark fruit-selling woman spreads various fruits here; | does she accept only the <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple)? — she looks at us!' || (JGc 1,29.79)
'This dark one is no virtuous woman — [she is] one who produces wealth from the exchange of necklaces; | though unacquainted, she herself wishes to place a jewel-string [on me]!' || (JGc 1,29.80)
'Ever since | I grasp the <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) substance from that fragrance-living woman, | from that time onward, O friend, the elders speak of me as dark and not-dark!' || (JGc 1,29.81)
[59] And of the one bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark too, this abundantly composed speech marked [with meaning] is to be noted, as follows:
'I am a woman skilled in sewing, and also a doer of the beholding of others' crafts; | I am a loving person — behold, O cowherd girl, the blouse in your own heart!' || (JGc 1,29.82)
'I am a dyer-woman here, named <s>Śyāmā</s> (dark one), of fame pervading the world; | she who wears my cloth — the dyeing of even her heart-lotus blossoms!' || (JGc 1,29.83)
'You wish to sell openly: mirrors, bows, coral, and pearls; | but secretly, a pair of caskets — I, O woman of <s>Vraja</s>, ask to buy them!' || (JGc 1,29.84)
'I am a slender-bodied woman skilled in massage, desiring to serve you; | the happiness born from a portion of my touch, O beautiful one, surpasses even <s>Brahman</s>-bliss!' || (JGc 1,29.85)
[60] And in that context:
'Having approached <s>Keśava</s> in the guise | of a bangle-making woman, certain ones | performed deeds both righteous and otherwise — | which we shall not enact in this assembly!' || (JGc 1,29.86)
'Having arranged that journey to the <s>Ambikā</s> forest, | marked by the dark-fortnight phase — | if that was commanded by the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, | then much that was sweet and desired was spread!' || (JGc 1,29.87)
[61] This being so:
'The beloveds of <s>Vraja</s>, becoming like rows of bees | born from the heart-lotus of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, | manifestly went step by step into the innermost position — | if this is so, we do not say to your honors with doubt —

Now, the conclusion:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, the one who ends the curse of <s>Sudarśana</s> — that beautiful <s>Sudarśana</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]! | He, the exceedingly beloved, blows upon you — | he is this slayer of <s>Baka</s>, the exceedingly beloved one!' || (JGc 1,29.89)

children.translated_text: Now, the Thirtieth Chapter.

children.text: nirvrīḍa-horikā-vikrīḍanaṃ
children.translated_text: The Shameless <s>Horikā</s> (Holī) Sport.

children.text: atha madhukaṇṭhaḥ prabhātakathāṃ kramataḥ prakramate sma-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> proceeded step by step with the morning-narrative:

children.text: ambikā-vana-gatir babhūva sā keli-karmaṇi hareḥ samardhanī |
children.translated_text: 'The journey to the <s>Ambikā</s> forest became | the furthering of <s>Hari's</s> sport-activity;

children.text: āgatāvapi tadā punar vraje horikā-pramada-parva-paddhatiḥ ||JGc_1,30.1||
children.translated_text: and even after returning then to <s>Vraja</s>, | the festive course of the joyful <s>Horikā</s> (Holī) festival [continued]!' || (JGc 1,30.1)

children.text: tatra ca parvaṇi sarva eva strī-puṃsa-janaḥ pramatta-gaṇa iva gāyan nṛtyan yudhyan kriḍatīti madhya-deśataḥ samudācāraḥ pracarati bhaviṣyottara-purāṇa-prāmāṇyasya purāṇānāṃ mānyatayā |
children.translated_text: And at that festival, all people — men and women alike — as if an intoxicated multitude, singing, dancing, fighting, and playing — this custom prevails from the central region (<s>Madhyadeśa</s>), by the authority of the <s>Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa</s>, through the respectability of the <s>Purāṇas</s>.

children.text: atha tatra yadā pūrṇa-guṇa-phālguna-pūrṇimā-niśāyāṃ kutuka-tṛṣṇak kṛṣṇaś ca rāmaś ca ḍhuṇḍhā-paraparyāya-horikā-gṛha-gṛhyāyāṃ bhuvi ramate sma | tadākasmād uttarasmād āgataḥ kaścid yadyapi guhyakādhipa-saṃgrāhyas tathāpi guhyaka-garhyatayā kaṃsa-śubhāśaṃsanas tatra krīḍantīr vraja-yuvatīḥ prati durdṛṣṭiṃ vidhāya tad-ākṛṣṭiṃ cintitavān |
children.translated_text: Now, when on the full-moon night of <s>Phālguna</s> — replete with all virtues — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, with curiosity and eagerness, were sporting on the earth where the <s>Horikā</s> (also called <s>Ḍhuṇḍhā</s>) is received in the home — suddenly, from the north, a certain one arrived who, though fit to be received by the chief of the <s>Guhyakas</s> (<s>Yakṣas</s>), was nonetheless blameworthy as a <s>Guhyaka</s> — a well-wisher of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — casting an evil gaze upon the young women of <s>Vraja</s> who were playing there, he contemplated abducting them.

children.text: cintayann eva ca sahasā tatra praviṣṭaḥ sa khalu durdhyānāviṣṭas tasmād akasmād aṅganānāṃ gaṇam udajavaj javataḥ kālayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And even as he was contemplating, having suddenly entered there — that one, possessed by wicked meditation — from that [entry], he immediately swept away the group of women and proceeded to carry them off swiftly.

children.text: atha sāgrajaḥ so' yaṃ gadāgrajastamasabhyasvabhāvamupalabhya pūrvaṃ tatparvarasikavaihāsikaveśaviśeṣaṃ dadhṛṣaṃ manvānaḥ sthagita ivāsīt | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Now he — together with his elder brother, the elder brother of the mace — upon perceiving the inherently dark nature of that [demon], at first considering the special costume of that festive-occasion's jesting entertainer to be bold [i.e., part of the fun], was as if stunned. And then —

children.text: pratihari-gati-ceṣṭā śaṅkhacūḍena ruddhā
children.translated_text: The efforts of those moving to counter [him] were blocked by <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>;

children.text: dṛg api rutir api drāk kṛṣṇa-rāmeti tāsām |
children.translated_text: their sight and their cries of '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! <s>Rāma</s>!' were [blocked] too —

children.text: yad ayam atula-vega-drohi-rūpāti-śabdaiḥ
children.translated_text: for this one, with sounds of form [and speed] hostile to incomparable velocity,

children.text: pratipadam anuvartī vṛtti-lopaṃ cakāra ||JGc_1,30.2||
children.translated_text: at every step as he followed, caused the cessation of [their] activity!' || (JGc 1,30.2)

children.text: atha tatra śrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyam-
children.translated_text: Now, the words of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> there:

children.text: pratyayantyo' py atijava-bharād asya ghorān nivṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: 'They [the women] who are turning back are forced to retreat by his terrible speed;

children.text: paśyantyo nāv api dhig amutas trāsa-vidhvasta-netrāḥ |
children.translated_text: they who look at us both — curse [that demon]! — their eyes are shattered by terror;

children.text: krośantyo' pi pratirutikṛtānena nīruddha-śabdāḥ
children.translated_text: they who cry out — their sound is obstructed by the counter-echo he creates;

children.text: bhrātas tarhy apy ahaha kim amū rakṣituṃ na dravāva ||JGc_1,30.3||
children.translated_text: O brother, even so — ahaha! — shall we not both rush to protect them?' || (JGc 1,30.3)

children.text: tad evaṃ niścinvānau taṃ bhīṣaṇārambhatayā stambhayituṃ vicinvānau sahasā śāla-dvayaṃ sahasā troṭayantau punas tad-viṭapādikam api pramoṭayantau sudṛḍha-bhujāgra-jāgrat-tad-yugalatayā prabalatayā ca tāv anudadruvatuḥ | tad anu vidrava-vaśād anye' pi saṃvidrate sma | tadā ca-
children.translated_text: Thus, as the two were resolving, and searching for [a way] to immobilize him through the fearfulness of the undertaking — suddenly uprooting two <s>śāla</s> trees, and further breaking off their branches and the like — with those two [trees] held awake [upraised] at the tips of their firmly-strong arms, and with great might, those two chased after him. Thereupon, by the force of his flight, others too scattered. And then:

children.text: itthaṃ na tarkitaṃ laukair anayoḥ śāla-hastayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Thus it was not imagined by the people — of these two with <s>śāla</s>-trees in hand —

children.text: śālau kiṃ laghutāṃ yātau vigrahau gurutām uta ||JGc_1,30.4||
children.translated_text: did the <s>śāla</s>-trees become light, or did their bodies become heavy?' || (JGc 1,30.4)

children.text: tataś ca-
agre śubhraṃ rauhiṇeyaṃ vidhāya
children.translated_text: 'Placing the bright son of <s>Rohiṇī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) in front,

children.text: śrī-govindaḥ pradravac chaṅkhacūḍam |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Govinda</s> chased <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>;

children.text: kīrti-stoma-prāyatāṃ tasya tanvann
children.translated_text: creating something almost like a mass of fame for him [the demon],

children.text: eṣa prāyas taṃ purastāt karoti ||JGc_1,30.5||
children.translated_text: he generally placed him [<s>Balarāma</s>] before [himself]!' || (JGc 1,30.5)
And then:

children.text: vilokya sa-balaṃ hariṃ parama-vikramaṃ sa-kramaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Seeing <s>Hari</s> together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), of supreme valor, advancing step by step,

children.text: visṛjya vanitā-janaṃ tvaritam adravad guhyakaḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Guhyaka</s>, releasing the group of women, fled swiftly;

children.text: balasya kila kālatām amata mṛtyutāṃ yad dharer
children.translated_text: he deemed <s>Bala</s> to be Death, and <s>Hari</s> to be Death's death —

children.text: mṛgaṃ tad ucitaṃ yataḥ sa sa jagāma tat tat kṛtim ||JGc_1,30.6||
children.translated_text: it was fitting that the beast fled, for he adopted that very course of action!' || (JGc 1,30.6)

children.text: tena visṛṣṭāyāṃ cāvalāvalāvayaṃ balābhidhas tat-saṃvalanāya tatra sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the women had been released by him, the one named <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) — the protector of the weak — remained there for their consolation.

children.text: atha śrīmān danuja-gajasiṃhas tad-anujas tu sa-vikramaṃ vikramamāṇaḥ prahasya sphuṭam auttarāhvasya ca tasya dākṣiṇātyaṃ palāyanam avetya dūretyaṃ taṃ pratyavajñayā taru-yaṣṭiṃ hastād vibhraṣṭāṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious one — a lion against the elephants of the demon-clan — his younger brother, advancing step by step with valor, having laughed aloud and clearly called out to that northerner, and perceiving his southward flight, contemptuously caused the tree-staff to drop from that [demon's] hand from afar.

children.text: vidrutya labdha-sanīḍaṃ punar asau vikrīḍana-catura-cittas tata itas taṃ vidrāvya ceṣṭitena veveṣṭi sma | nṛsiṃha iva hiraṇyakaśipuṃ ripuṃ sa-nigraham eva jagrāha ca |
children.translated_text: Having fled and found his lair, that one — clever-minded in sport — from here and there, chasing him about with his feints, enveloped [him]. Like <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> [seizing] <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, he seized the enemy with full restraint.

children.text: tatas taṃ hasta-rodhaṃ gṛhṇann ahnāya maṇi-gṛhītaye sphurann urasilaḥ kara-sarasijena tac-chirasi kakkhaṭī-bhāva-vighaṭita-tad-adhīci-muny-asthijena gṛhīta-saṃgrāha-sāraṃ prahāram ājahāra uttarasminn anehasi mṛta-deha-pratīkādānam anuttaram itīva bhraṃśayāmāsa ca tasya tam uttaṃsam |
children.translated_text: Then, seizing that hand-obstruction, the one with the gleaming gem upon his chest — for the purpose of seizing the jewel — without delay, with his lotus-hand, upon that one's head, delivered a blow of concentrated force by means of [a weapon] resembling a tortoise-shell, which had shattered the bone of its hardness-state — and as if giving in return for the unsurpassed dead body, he dislodged that crest-ornament from him.

children.text: sa punar ātatāyī durmāyī maṇim anu prāṇān api vyaktam eva tyaktavān | tad-dhana-mātra-jīvana-yātraḥ khalv asau | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And that aggressor, that evil-magician, having lost the jewel, clearly abandoned even his life-breaths as well — for he was one whose life-journey subsisted on that wealth alone. And then:

children.text: jīvo ratnaṃ veti bhedākṣamaṃ taj-
children.translated_text: 'Life or gem?' — that which is indivisible in its distinction, that

children.text: jyotir-mātraṃ vastu yakṣād gṛhītvā |
children.translated_text: mere luminous substance, having been seized from the <s>Yakṣa</s>,

children.text: paśyantīnāṃ yoṣitāṃ kaṃsa-vairī
children.translated_text: while the women looked on, the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>

children.text: ninye kāmaṃ rāma-sāyujyam eva ||JGc_1,30.7||
children.translated_text: indeed led [him] to the state of union with <s>Rāma</s> (death/Balarāma)! ||30.7||

children.text: taṃ cābhipannaṃ mukhaṃ vyādāya vinnapātaṃ panna-maṇiṃ vyāpannaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrī-kṛṣṇābhiprāyam abhiprayadbhir diviṣadbhir upahasitam, yathā-
children.translated_text: And seeing him who had fallen face-down, his mouth gaping open, his gem having fallen, thoroughly destroyed — the celestial beings, who comprehended Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> intention, mocked him, as follows:

children.text: strī-ratnaṃ puru parakīyam ādithas tvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'You seized another's jewel-woman in abundance;

children.text: svaṃ cūḍāmaṇim api hārayāṃ cakartha |
children.translated_text: your own crest-jewel too, you caused to be taken away!

children.text: atyākṣīr bata nija-jīvanaṃ ca dhik tvāṃ
children.translated_text: You even threw away your very life — shame on you!

children.text: vyādāḥ kiṃ mukham atha vaktram atra yakṣa ||JGc_1,30.8||
children.translated_text: Did you open your mouth or your face here, O <s>Yakṣa</s>?' ||30.8||

children.text: tad evaṃ karṇa-rasanayā rasyamānam ācarya rahasyaṃ vihasya ca snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ punaḥ sa-bāṣpa-kaṇṭham uvāca-
children.translated_text: Thus, having enacted that secret drama, relished by the tongue of the ears, and having laughed, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke again with a tear-choked throat:

children.text: tat-kṣobhaṇaṃ tad dravaṇaṃ tathā tad-
children.translated_text: 'That agitation of his, that melting, and likewise that

children.text: vikrīḍanaṃ tad-dhananaṃ sva-śatroḥ |
children.translated_text: sporting, that slaying of his own enemy —

children.text: tad-rakta-rajyan-maṇi-pāṇi-rocir
children.translated_text: that luster of his hand, reddened by the blood-stained gem,

children.text: mayy adya sadyaḥ prabham asya bhāti ||JGc_1,30.9||
children.translated_text: shines upon me today, immediately, as his radiance!' ||30.9||

children.text: punar madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tad evaṃ dalita-cūḍe śaṅkhacūḍe niṣpīḍite krīḍite ca vrīḍitena nivṛtte kolāhala-paramparātaḥ kātaratā-virata-prakṛtayaḥ sarva eva vrajorvīpati-prabhṛtayaḥ samāgatya vismitya ca tādṛśa-duṣṭa-naṣṭībhāvataḥ punar bhaya-sandehenāspṛṣṭāḥ spaṣṭānanda-sandoha-dohās tat-parva-krīḍāṃ nirvrīḍā iva vivavruḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: Thus, when <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa's</s> crest had been crushed, when the sport had been squeezed out and concluded, when [he had] returned, shame-faced, from the succession of tumults — all, beginning with the king of <s>Vraja's</s> earth, their dispositions now freed from the cessation of fearfulness, having assembled and marveled at the destruction of such a villain, untouched again by any doubt of fear, being vessels of manifest congregations of bliss, shamelessly as it were, resumed the festive sport.

children.text: vivṛtya ca śāstra-vipratipatti-viprayojayitṛ-viprebhyaḥ sūta-sarvānanda-guṇa-prabhūta-sūta-māgadha-vandibhyaś ca paramāvadānāni dānāni bahūni cakruḥ | tābhyaś ca śasta-vastrādīni prasthāpayāmāsuḥ | svasthāyamānāḥ samājagmuś ca kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇāgrajau puraskṛtya nijaṃ vrajam iti |
children.translated_text: And having resumed, they bestowed many and supreme gifts upon the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who removed the contradictions of scriptural disputes, and upon the bards, <s>sūtas</s>, <s>māgadhas</s>, and <s>vandins</s> — who were abundant in the quality of universal delight. And they dispatched praised garments and such to those [women]. And becoming calm, they returned together to their own <s>Vraja</s>, placing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> elder brother at the fore.

children.text: evaṃ vicitra-vikrīḍaḥ putras te goṣṭha-nāyaka |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, your son, of marvelous sports, O leader of the cattle-settlement —

children.text: taṃ krodha-vahnau ḍhuṇḍhāgre yakṣor abhraṃ jahāva yaḥ ||JGc_1,30.10||
children.translated_text: he who cast that <s>Yakṣa</s> into the fire of wrath before <s>Ḍhuṇḍha</s> like a cloud!' ||30.10||

children.text: athātra rātri-kathāyāṃ madhukaṇṭhas tāṃ horikā-kathām eva viśeṣataḥ sevayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Now, in the night-tale, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> attended especially to that <s>Holikā</s> (Holī) narrative.

children.text: śiva-kṣapāyām atha yāpitāyāṃ
children.translated_text: When the auspicious night (<s>Śivarātrī</s>) had been passed,

children.text: valgūtsavā phālguna-pūrṇimāgāt |
children.translated_text: the full-moon of the month of <s>Phālguna</s> arrived, beautiful with festivities!

children.text: pakṣa-dvayasyāsya yathaiva kāntiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the splendor of both halves (fortnights) of this [month],

children.text: parva-dvayasyāsya ca tadvad asti ||JGc_1,30.11||
children.translated_text: so too is [the splendor] of both festivals of this [month]! ||30.11||

children.text: hime gate hima-rucir ujjvalaṃ babhāv
children.translated_text: When the frost had departed, the frost-rayed one (moon) shone brilliantly;

children.text: aphalguni sva-mahasi phalgu-parva ca |
children.translated_text: the <s>Phālguna</s> festival too [shone] in its own glory, not insignificantly!

children.text: na vābhavan katham atha tatra gopikā
children.translated_text: And how could the <s>gopikās</s> not be present there —

children.text: madotkarād api paribhūta-gopikā ||JGc_1,30.12||
children.translated_text: those who, even from the excess of their intoxication, surpassed [all other] <s>gopikās</s>? ||30.12||

children.text: atha balakṣa-pakṣa-sapakṣakair avaprakara-śobhākara-karani-kara-karambitāṃ sva-manoratha-prathanāvalambitāṃ kṣapam anvīkṣya sarvās tat-parvānarvācīna-samudācāra-garvān mudā bahir āvirbhavanti sma, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, having beheld the night — supported by the partisans of the bright fortnight, adorned with the radiance of the plantain-trunk-hands of the elephant's trunk, interlaced with the spreading of their own fancied desires — all [the <s>gopīs</s>], with pride not inferior to the customs of that festival, joyfully emerged outward, as follows:

children.text: muhur agaṇita-gauravāḥ samantāt
children.translated_text: 'Repeatedly disregarding all propriety, on all sides,

children.text: praṇaya-madāt paridhāya divya-veśam |
children.translated_text: having donned divine costumes from the intoxication of love,

children.text: api bata janatāsu horikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: even among the people, in the Holī festival,

children.text: harim abhisasrur aho vrajasya nāryaḥ ||JGc_1,30.13||
children.translated_text: the women of <s>Vraja</s> — ah! — set out toward <s>Hari</s>!' ||30.13||

children.text: tad evaṃ sadma-sadmanāṃ sakhī-padma-varūthinībhiḥ saha yūtha-nātha-kavaca-sthiti-racana-kañculikādi-vastraiḥ surabhi-kaṣāya-mocana-yantra-prabhṛti-śastrair bahula-kāhalādi-vāditra-vicitra-kutūhalaiḥ sa-keli-gāli-rīti-maya-gīti-kolāhalaiḥ sārvatrika-tat-pārvaṇa-rītyā nirlajjatayā sajjatayā ca vraja-pura-dvāra-puraḥ-sthita-horikāyatanāgrīya-samagrāyata-prāṅgaṇa-vihāra-saṅgara-raṅga-bhuvi saṃgatā babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, those household women, together with their lotus-armies of companions, with armor-jackets and covering garments as the equipment of the herd-lord's protection, with weapons such as fragrant saffron-releasing syringes and the like, with various musical instruments — especially kettledrums — creating diverse curiosities, with the tumult of playful abusive sport-songs — in accordance with the universal custom of that festival, with shamelessness and readiness, assembled at the courtyard-ground — the vast, extended forecourt of the Holī-arena standing before the gate of the town of <s>Vraja</s> — for the battle-sport of play.

children.text: yāḥ khalu bala-balānujayor yathāsvaṃ pṛthak pṛthag anurāga-dharaṇād vibhāgam āgatās tat-tan-niṣṭha-dṛṣṭitayā tiṣṭhanti sma |
children.translated_text: Those [women] who, from bearing affection for <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) and <s>Bala's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) respectively and separately, had arrived at a division, stood with their gaze fixed each on their respective [chosen one].

children.text: tatra tābhir īryamāṇaṃ vardhita-śauṭīrya-parimāṇaṃ kala-kalam ākalayya jayyatāmayyas tā iti bhāvanāṃ paryavasāya-sāhāyyāya sakhi-ghaṭayā kaṭakaṃ saṅghaṭayya tadvad eva sajjatayā bala-balānujāv api valgu valgantau tatraiva gacchataḥ sma |
children.translated_text: There, perceiving the beautiful clamor being produced by those [women] — of augmented measure of boldness — and having concluded with the thought 'they are to be conquered!' — assembling a battalion with the company of friends for the assistance of that conclusion, with equal readiness, <s>Bala</s> and <s>Bala's</s> younger brother too, prancing handsomely, went to that very [arena].

children.text: gatau cānavadya-vādya-ghoṣeṇa ghoṣaṃ vadhirayantau pratisenām avadhīrayāmāsatuḥ | yena samuddīpita-mānāḥ pratisenāyamānāś ca tās tathā vādyataḥ saṃmukhatām āsādya paritas tān api sarvān aticitrayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: And having gone, deafening the settlement with the sound of irreproachable musical instruments, the two treated the opposing army with contempt. Whereby those [women], their pride inflamed and forming a counter-army, upon reaching the front of that musical assembly, astonished even all of them on all sides.

children.text: yatra pratispardhayā vardhamānayos tayor yūtha-varūthinī-pramāṇayor ekatra mādhavaḥ paratra tu rādhā rājāyate sma | jāyate sma ca tena janānām ativismayaḥ | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Where, as the two rival armies grew with competition, in one [army] <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and in the other <s>Rādhā</s> reigned as sovereign. And among the people, supreme wonder arose thereby. For thus:

children.text: yadvac chubhratara-prakīrṇaka-maṇi-cchatrādikaṃ śrī-harer
children.translated_text: 'Just as the parasol adorned with bright, scattered gems and such belonged to Śrī <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: āsīt tadvad amūbhir aprathi tadā śrī-rādhikāyām api |
children.translated_text: so too, just the same, was it displayed for Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> by those [women]!

children.text: kiṃ cābhyāṃ na parasparaṃ nayanayoḥ prāntaś ca sehe
children.translated_text: Moreover, neither of them endured the edge of each other's eyes' corner,

children.text: yathā jetṛtvaṃ kva nu jeyatā ca bhavitā kutreti nātrohitam ||JGc_1,30.14||
children.translated_text: [wondering] where would be the victoriousness and where the defeat — that was not ventured here!' ||30.14||

children.text: tad evaṃ parasparam utsāhamānatām asahamānatām apy adhikṛtya kṛta-kṛtyatā-samāhārayor manoharaṇāyābhihāra-vihārayos tayor anīkinī-sahitayoḥ sarva-mahitayoḥ samañjasatām iva saṃjayantī vrajarāja-savayaḥ-purohita-śvaśurāvaraja-dāratayā gantavya-pakṣaṃ narma-śarmaṇā rañjayantī kācid ardha-vṛddhā tat-prema-samṛddhā madhyastha-padavīm adhyāsya pragalbhatayā gatyā vātyāyamānā rādhā-varga-madhyāt tat-pratipakṣasya kṣmādhavaṃ śrīman-mādhavaṃ saṃnihitavatī | saṃnidhāya ca yathā-yathaṃ prathamāna-smitatayā kṛte' bhivādane' bhivadane ca teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ śṛṇvatām abravīt-
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding those two — who could not endure each other's mutual enthusiasm, and yet whose mutual captivation-sport constituted the accomplishment of their purpose — the two accompanied by their armies, honored by all: a certain half-elderly woman, enriched by their love, occupying the position of mediator, proceeding with boldness in her gait, blowing as a gale, as it were — she being the wife of the family-priest who was of the same age as the king of <s>Vraja</s>, his father-in-law's younger brother's wife — gladdening the party that was to be approached with the happiness of jest, having emerged from the midst of <s>Rādhā's</s> group, presented herself before the lord of the earth, the glorious <s>Mādhava</s>, to the opposing side. And having presented herself, with properly commenced smiling, having performed salutation and address as was appropriate, while all of them listened, she said:

children.text: ahaṃ kila prajñā prājñā ca mahā-dharādhīśa-gaṇa-kṛtārādhāyā śrī-rādhāyā dūta-karmaṇi prabhūtatām āsannāsmi | tad etad avadhāryatām-
children.translated_text: 'I, named <s>Prajñā</s> — the wise one — have attained eminence in the office of messenger for Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, who is worshipped by hosts of great earth-lords! So let this be heeded!'

children.text:
ity ukta-mātrām etāṃ madhumaṅgalaḥ sahāsam āha sma-kim uktam avadhāryatām iti |
[27] tac chrutvā sarvasmin prahasati sovāca-vadhiro' yaṃ bhavatāṃ sabhāsad iti |
children.translated_text:
Having barely said this, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> laughingly said to her: 'What did you say — "let it be heeded"?'
[27] Hearing that, while everyone laughed, she said: 'This fellow of yours is deaf!'

children.text:
madhumaṅgala uvāca-yuktaṃ tavedaṃ nirargalatvam | yatas tasyā dharādhiśāyā vaśā bhavatī kasya vānyasya vaśā bhaviṣyati |
[29] śrī-kṛṣṇas tu sa-gāmbhīryam uvāca-nikāmam eva nivedyatām |
children.translated_text:
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'This unbridled conduct befits you! For since you are under the sway of that mistress of the earth, who else would be under anyone else's sway?'
[29] But Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with gravity: 'Let the message be duly delivered!'

children.text: dūtī tu tayā śiṣṭācāra-pratipālayitryā viśiṣṭam idam ādiṣṭam ity ardhokte viṣṇu viṣṇv ity uktvā provāca-śacī-jayi-tadīya-saciva-varābhir idam ādiṣṭam | sarvatra prasṛmara-samajñām asmadīya-rājñīm avajñāya dūrataś ca kim uta pūrataś chatrādika-dhāraṇaṃ bhavatām asādhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: The messenger, however — being an observer of good conduct — having been commissioned by her with a distinguished [instruction], began with the half-utterance 'This distinguished [message] has been commanded —' and then exclaiming '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>!' said: 'This has been commanded by the chief advisors — who surpass even <s>Śacī</s> (Indra's wife): "The bearing of parasols and such by your people is extraordinary — disregarding our queen, whose fame spreads everywhere, [even] from a distance, let alone from the front!"'

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaḥ sabhābhiḥ saha hasitvā provāca-satyaṃ tad-ādeśatas tad-abhiniveśaṃ tyajāmaḥ | kintu yuddhaṃ vinā rājñāṃ veda-buddhaṃ syād iti yuddhāya saṃnaddhayā bhavatyā bhāvyam ity eva vaktavyam |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having laughed together with the assembly, said: 'Truly, by her command we abandon that insistence! But since the giving up of royalty by kings without battle would be scripture-sanctioned — you must convey that she should be girded for battle!'

children.text: atra madhumaṅgalaḥ saṃmukhaṃ gatas tad idam āha sma-deva tad idam eva samākarṇyatām | jātitaḥ strī cāstrī yo janastasmin vāmatārāme nāmamātreṇa rāmāspadamāgate nārjavacaryayā kāryamaryate | tasmādārjavavarjanādūrjasvinaste vayam evadūtyāya sthāpanīyāḥ prasthāpanīyāśca | asmāsu cāham evaprahāpaṇīyaḥ | yataḥ kovido' smi |
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, coming forward, said this: 'Lord, let this alone be heard! She who by birth is a woman, and he who is not a woman — in that arena whose name alone makes it an abode of women (<s>Rāmā</s>) — the business is not to be conducted with straight-forward behavior! Therefore, we ourselves — through the abandonment of straight-forwardness, being energetic — are to be installed and dispatched as messengers! And among us, I alone am indispensable — for I am an expert!'

children.text: dūtī sahāsamāha sma-lālāṭika bhavān yadi kovidas tarhy anyaḥ ko' vidaḥ |
children.translated_text: The messenger said with laughter: 'O forehead-marked one! If you are an expert, then who else is not an expert?'

children.text: madhumaṅgalaḥ sotprāsam uvāca-jalpāki kalayāmi bhavatī tasyāḥ sabhāyā vindur asti | tathāpi trayītanor mamāgrataḥ sthitir api tava na sthiratāṃ labheta |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said with mockery: 'O chatterbox, I perceive that you are a drop from that assembly of hers! Even so, standing before me — one whose body is the triple <s>Veda</s> — even your standing would not attain stability!'

children.text: dūtī sāvajñam uvāca-viśāradāyā mama purataḥ śāradas tvaṃ kiyad vā vaditāsi | tasmān nīvākavalitam ākalaya |
children.translated_text: The messenger said with disdain: 'Before me, who am accomplished, O autumnal one — how much will you speak? Therefore, swallow [your words] covered with spittle!'

children.text: madhumaṅgalaḥ sa-roṣaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇam avalocya vakti sma-para-vaktavyā khalv iyaṃ vaktavyā bhavatīti nāsmākaṃ vaktavyā bhavitum arhati | kintu seyaṃ tāvad atra nirudhyatām yāvad ahaṃ tad vṛttam avabudhya sudhy-agraṇīr bhavantam avaruṇadhmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, looking at Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with anger, declared: 'This one is indeed to be spoken to by others as "you are to be spoken to" — and should not be one to be spoken to by us! But for now, let her be detained here while I investigate that affair and block you, O foremost of the wise!'

children.text: dūtī sa-hāsam uvāca-nūnaṃ bhavatāṃ dūtaḥ so' yam agrata eva vyagratām avāpa | yan māmatra ruddhann eva tatra jigamiṣati | tasmān na mādṛg iva niḥśaṅkaṃ so' yam iti bhavatāṃ kalaṅkāya paraṃ pratipatsyate | yuktam eva ca tat-tad-āvayoḥ | svāmi-guṇā hi parijanam anuyanti |
children.translated_text: The messenger said with laughter: 'Surely, your messenger here has already attained agitation right at the outset! For he who, while detaining me here, wishes to go there — therefore he will not be as fearless as someone like me, and will only lead to your disgrace! And that is indeed fitting for both of us respectively — for the qualities of the master indeed follow the attendant!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-bhāmini svāmi-guṇatvaṃ punaḥ prakārāntareṇa mantavyam | sā khalu vāmā vayaṃ tu dakṣiṇā iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'O spirited one! The quality of being the master's [reflection] should rather be understood in another sense — she indeed is crooked (<s>vāmā</s>), but we are courteous (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>)!'

children.text: dūty uvāca-yūyaṃ khalv apasavyā iti satyam eva yataḥ sveṣāṃ dakṣiṇatāvācitve' pi pratikūlatāṃ na jahītha |
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'You are indeed "left-handed" (<s>apasavya</s>, adverse) — that is certainly true, since even in proclaiming your own courteousness, you do not abandon contrariness!'

children.text: madhumaṅgalas tu tad aśṛṇvann iva provāca-mahārāja vāmātvam eva khalu tāsāṃ balāya kalpate yasmād abalāḥ |
children.translated_text: But <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, as if not hearing that, said: 'Great king! Their crookedness (<s>vāmatva</s>) indeed serves for their strength, since they are "weak" (<s>abalā</s>, lit. without strength)!'

children.text: dūty uvāca-doṣa-jñāḥ khalu bhavantaḥ katham iva guṇānusandhānaṃ kurvantu |
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'You are indeed knowers of faults — how would you undertake the investigation of virtues?'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca-doṣaika-dṛk purobhāgīty evaṃ yac-chābdikair matam tasmāt tvam eva purataḥ sudhībhis tābhir āhitā |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'A fault-seer is a forward-marcher — this is the view of the grammarians! Therefore, it is you who have been placed in front by those wise ones of yours!'

children.text: dūty uvāca-asaṅkhyāvatāṃ bhavatāṃ purataḥ katham eka-saṅkhyāvatī pratyuttaraṃ dadyām | bhavāṃs tu tatrānubandha eva | tathāpi sarve śṛṇvantu | tāsām abalātvaṃ khalu virodhi-lakṣaṇayā yataḥ śastra-śarīratvam eva dṛśyate | tad etac ca tan-mukhyām upalakṣya lakṣyatām |
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Before me, who am innumerable, how would one of a single number give a counter-reply? But you are merely an appendage there. Nevertheless, let all listen! Their weakness (<s>abalatva</s>) is indeed, by the figure of contradiction, [to be understood as] — for their body is of the nature of weapons! And this should be discerned by looking at their chief:

children.text: keśāḥ pāśāś cala-nayana-yugaṃ vāṇa-yugmaṃ namad-bhrūś
children.translated_text: 'Her hair is a noose; her pair of restless eyes, a pair of arrows; her bowing brow,

children.text: cāpaḥ karṇāvari-paridadhatau nāsikā divya-śastrī |
children.translated_text: a bow; her pair of ears, bestowing a covering, her nose a divine weapon;

children.text: dantā vajrāṇy apara-tad-aparaṃ tarkyam evaṃ tad etac-
children.translated_text: her teeth are thunderbolts; and the rest beyond that is to be inferred likewise — thus,

children.text: chastrai rādhā svayam udayati ko vā balīyān ato' nyaḥ ||JGc_1,30.15||
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> herself rises forth armed with weapons — who else is mightier than she?' ||30.15||

children.text: atra ko vā balīyān ato' nya iti kṛṣṇam eva kaṭākṣeṇa paśyantī prāha sma- [45] evaṃ vivadamānayor anayoḥ kṛṣṇas tu tayā prastutaṃ tasyāḥ saundaryam avadhārya kṣaṇaṃ dhīratāṃ saṃdhārya provāca-dūti jātita eva pratīpadarśiny asi | kiṃ bruve | kintu madīya-dūta-nirmitā rāja-nītir iyaṃ na tu bhītiḥ |
children.translated_text:
Therein, 'Who or what other is mightier?' — thus, glancing sidelong at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone, she spoke.
[45] While these two were thus disputing, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having ascertained the beauty that she had set forth, composing his steadiness for a moment, said: 'O messenger-woman, from birth itself you are one who sees things contrarily! What shall I say? But this is a royal policy fashioned by my ambassador — not fear!'

children.text: tato bhavatī tāvad atra sthitim anubhavatu | mama dūtas tatra gacchatu | tataḥ saṃcārakāṇām ācāreṇa samācāreṇa sācāre labdha-pracāre yathāyatham ācaritavyam |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let your ladyship experience the situation here for now. Let my ambassador go there. Then, according to the custom of emissaries, with proper protocol, once access has been gained through proper conduct, what is appropriate shall be done.'

children.text: punar madhumaṅgalaṃ praty uvāca-bhadraṃ svayam eva tatra gamyatām iti |
children.translated_text: And again he said to <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: 'My good fellow, go there yourself!'

children.text: dūty uvāca-
children.translated_text: The messenger-woman said:

children.text: nyāye yuktau pramāṇe ca sthito madhyastha ucyate |
children.translated_text: 'One who stands in justice, propriety, and evidence is called impartial;

children.text: paraṃ madhye sthito yaḥ syāt sa madhya-sthāvaraḥ smṛtaḥ ||JGc_1,30.16||
children.translated_text: but one who merely stands in the middle — he is remembered as a middle-standing-plant!' ||30.16||

children.text: so' yaṃ punaś cheka eva | tataḥ śikṣām api nārhatīti svairam eva gacchatu |
children.translated_text: 'And this one is again merely clever! Therefore, he does not even deserve instruction — let him go freely!'

children.text: madhumaṅgalas tu viśastā khalv iyaṃ kathaṃ śastaṃ vadatu nāmeti nivedya yathādiśanti mahārāja-mahāśayā iti prasthitavān | prasthāya ca tāsāṃ sthānam āsīdann āśī-rāśibhiḥ prasādam āsādayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: But <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, having reported 'This one is indeed a slayer — how can she speak what is praiseworthy?' — set forth saying 'As the great king and great-souled ones command!' And having set forth and arrived at their place, he obtained their gracious reception with heaps of blessings.

children.text: sarvāś ca namaskṛtya sa-smitaṃ kṛtyaṃ pṛcchanti sma |
children.translated_text: And all, having bowed, smilingly inquired about his business.

children.text: madhumaṅgalas tu bhavatīnām etan-nṛtya-darśanam eva kṛtyam iti procya pratyuvāca-kiṃ ca bhavatīnāṃ dūtī tatra gatā vartate brūte ca | asmākaṃ rājñī sārvabhaumaṃ bhavantaṃ militum icchatīti | tad avadhārya vismayād asmākaṃ rājñā cājñāpitam | sā khalu parānugatā jātāstīti śrūyate | tasmād etan na śraddadhyāma | ataḥ svasya svasā kācid asmāsu kasmaicana vivahanāya dīyatām | tadā tasyāḥ śvovasīyasāya syād iti |
children.translated_text: But <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, having said 'To see this very dance of your ladyships is my business,' replied: 'Moreover, your ladyships' messenger-woman has gone there and is speaking: "Our queen wishes to meet your sovereign lord." Having ascertained that, our king too commanded with wonder: "It is heard that she has become one who follows others. Therefore, we do not believe this. Hence, let her own sister — whoever she may be among us — be given in marriage to someone. Then that would secure her [the queen's] future."'

children.text: sarvāḥ sa-bhrū-vijṛmbham āhuḥ sma-vācāṭa-tāpāṭavamaya-dhūrtatāyā mūrtir evāyaṃ sphuṭam anyathākāraṃ vadann asmān vañcayitum evānañcitavān asti | sa kadācid evaṃ na kadvadāyate | sā punar asmākaṃ saṃcārikā nemāṃ kucaratām ācaret | kintu baddheti saṃbadhyate |
children.translated_text: All said, with a furrowing of brows: 'This one is clearly the very embodiment of the roguery of the fire-forest of chattering-heat — speaking otherwise, he has come only to deceive us! He would never speak so baselessly! Moreover, she is our emissary — let her not practice bad conduct. Rather, she is detained!'

children.text: viśākhovāca-yathākāraṃ tathākāraṃ vā vadatu | so' yaṃ kathaṃkāraṃ yūyam idaṃ vicārayatha | yato viprasyāsya kṛtaṃ khalu viprakṛtam eva bhaṇyate | katham iva prakṛtaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> said: 'Let him speak as he will, truly or otherwise. Why do you all deliberate how? For whatever this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has done is declared to be nothing but mischief! How could it be proper?'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca-ko vātra mama lābhaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'What gain is there for me in this?'

children.text: viśākhovāca-aye bhadra vipra labdhamapi tathaivānusandheyam |
children.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> said: 'Ah, good <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — what is gained [by you] should be investigated in precisely that way!'

children.text: tad evaṃ pratyādiṣṭas tu madhumaṅgala uvāca-sarva-klamatha-mathanānāṃ śamatha-damatha-satpatha-prathana-parāṇām atha kathaṃ na bhavaty asmākam evāyaṃ doṣaḥ | yat khalu sandhy-anusandhānam etābhis tu yuddham evānubaddham asti |
children.translated_text: Thus rebuffed, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'For those who are devoted to treading the good path of quelling and subduing, the churners of all weariness — how then is this our fault? For surely, it is these [women] who have always bound a war to the diplomacy of the twilight-junction!'

children.text: atha śrī-rādhikābhidadhāti sma-kiṃ balaḥ saṃvalate bhavadīyaḥ sa rājā | yasmād etāvad garvāyase |
children.translated_text: Then glorious <s>Rādhikā</s> said: 'Is your king capable of holding his own? Since you boast to such an extent!'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said:

children.text: uccāṭanaṃ guṇa-gaṇa-prathanād vikṛṣṭir
children.translated_text: 'Bewilderment through the spreading of [his] host of virtues; attraction

children.text: vaṃśī-kalād vikalanaṃ vara-rūpa-vṛndāt |
children.translated_text: through the art of the flute; distraction through the assemblage of excellent beauty;

children.text: stambho vilāsa-valayād vaśatā ca vāṇī
children.translated_text: paralysis through the circle of [his] graces; and subjugation through the sweetness

children.text: mādhuryataḥ sumukhi yasya balī tataḥ kaḥ ||JGc_1,30.17||
children.translated_text: of [his] speech — O fair-faced one, who then is mightier than he?' ||30.17||

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: drāghiṣṭa-kṣepiṣṭha-preṣṭha-variṣṭha-sthaviṣṭha-baṃhiṣṭhāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The tallest, the swiftest, the dearest, the greatest, the mightiest, the strongest —

children.text: asman-nṛpateḥ purataḥ sarve garveṇa ricyante ||JGc_1,30.18||
children.translated_text: all are surpassed in pride before our king!' ||30.18||

children.text: api ca-
children.translated_text: And further:

children.text: vṛndiṣṭha-kṣodiṣṭha-jyeṣṭha-gariṣṭha-hrasiṣṭha-sādhiṣṭhāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The most clustered, the tiniest, the eldest, the heaviest, the shortest, the most accomplished —

children.text: asman-nṛpater agre viparītābhā-parītāḥ syuḥ ||JGc_1,30.19||
children.translated_text: before our king, [all] would be surrounded by opposite splendors!' ||30.19||

children.text: atha śrī-rādhā tu tad-avadhāraṇād antaḥ-prema-bādhāṃ katham api samādhāya lalitā-mukham īkṣitavatī | lalitā tu sa-vipralāpam ālalāpa-
children.translated_text: Then glorious <s>Rādhā</s>, having somehow composed the agitation of inner love arising from ascertaining that, gazed upon <s>Lalitā's</s> face. And <s>Lalitā</s>, with teasing babble, prattled:

children.text: sa veṇur mūka-vadhiro yatrāgād vāvadūkatām |
children.translated_text: 'That flute, which is mute and deaf — where it attained garrulity,

children.text: tatrāyaṃ kiṃ na vāgmī syād brahma-vaṃśa-samudbhavaḥ ||JGc_1,30.20||
children.translated_text: how then would this one, born of <s>Brahmā's</s> lineage, not be eloquent?' ||30.20||

children.text: kintu yathāsmākaṃ dūtī niruddhā tathā tam etam api nirudhya yuddhāya saṃnahyāmaḥ | anantaraṃ tu parama-pracaṇḍāḥ sva-pitṛ-purohita-paugaṇḍāḥ samādiśyantām | te ca strī-veśam evāsya balāt kurvantu | kṛte ca tad-veśe śrī-vrajarāja-purohita-bhāgineyaḥ so' yaṃ na cārbhakas tatra gacchann asmadīya-saṃdeśa-varṇāṃs tat-karṇābhyarṇān karotu | asmākam anyā kanyā na vidyate | kintu siṃhala-dvīpād dīpābhā padminīyam ekā jita-sarvātirekā nītāsti | sā tu svayaṃ rājñā pariṇīyatām |
children.translated_text: 'But just as our messenger-woman was detained, let us likewise detain this one too and gird ourselves for battle! Next, let the supremely fierce boys — the young <s>paugaṇḍa</s> apprentices of her own father's family priest — be dispatched! And let them forcibly put women's attire upon him! And once that costume is donned, let this nephew of the glorious king of <s>Vraja's</s> family priest — this one who is no child — going there, bring to the vicinity of their ears our message in these words: "We do not have another maiden. But from the island of <s>Siṃhala</s> (Śrī Laṅkā), a <s>Padminī</s>-[type woman] of radiance like a lamp, surpassing all — she has been brought! Let the king himself marry her."'

children.text: tatra padminī-prāyeṇa duṣkula-sadmajeti nāvajñātavyā |
children.translated_text: 'Therein, the <s>Padminī</s>-type should not be looked down upon as being from a low household, because:

children.text:
viṣād apy amṛtaṃ grāhyam
amedhyād api kāñcanam |
nīcād apy uttamāṃ vidyāṃ
strī-ratnaṃ duṣkulād api ||[GarP 1.110] iti hi smaryate |
children.translated_text:
even from the lowly, the highest knowledge;
a jewel-woman even from a bad family!' ||[Garuḍa Purāṇa 1.110] — thus it is remembered.

'Even from poison, nectar is to be taken;
even from filth, gold;

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca-nanu bhavatyaś ca padminyas tarhi tā eva kathaṃ kule nānarhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'But you ladies are <s>Padminīs</s> too — then how are they not worthy within [their] family?'

children.text: lalitā sa-roṣam uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> said angrily:

children.text: āvṛtā jagati padminī yayā padmayā jitavatī sadāpi tām |
children.translated_text: 'She by whom the <s>Padminī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is enveloped in the world, and who has always conquered her —

children.text: rādhikādir api padminītayā bhaṇyatāṃ tatir aho mṛgī-dṛśām ||JGc_1,30.21||
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> and others too, as <s>Padminīs</s> — ah, let the assembly of doe-eyed ones be proclaimed!' ||30.21||

children.text: atha śrī-rādhikā hasitvā cillī-cālanayā lasitvā ca sva-pitṛ-purohita-bālakānāṃ pañcāśataṃ tad-veśāyādiśya rāja-purohita-svasrīyeṇa ca tathā saṃdiśya yuddha-kautukāyābhiniviśya tasya strī-veśasya purataḥ sthitiṃ nidiśya cāmūbhiś camūru-cakṣuś-camūbhir abhikrantavatī yuddhābhimukhatayā ca sthitavatī kṛṣṇaṃ ca manasyāhitavatī | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then glorious <s>Rādhikā</s>, having laughed and having shone with the fluttering of her eyelashes, directed fifty boys — apprentices of her own father's family priest — for his [<s>Madhumaṅgala's</s>] costume-change, and having instructed the king's priest's nephew [to deliver] the message accordingly, and having devoted herself to the curiosity of battle, and having directed the positioning of his women's costume before [her], with her army-of-thigh and army-of-eyes she advanced, stationed herself facing battle, and held <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in her mind. And there:

children.text: abībhaṣad ayaṃ horīm ababhāṣad iyaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: 'He challenged the <s>Holī</s>-war; she too proclaimed likewise;

children.text: adīdipad asau bhāvam asau ca tam adīdipat ||JGc_1,30.22||
children.translated_text: he kindled that emotion; and she too kindled it in return!' ||30.22||

children.text: tataś ca rājāyamāna-gokula-yuvarājas taṃ nikāra-prakāraṃ baṭu-mukhataḥ kaṭu-nibhaṃ karṇa-puṭam ānīya tāṃ dūtīṃ sva-pakṣa-rakṣitābhiḥ kābhiścit pragalbhatā-lakṣitābhis tādṛśa-strībhiḥ puruṣa-veśāṃ vidhāya tena baṭunā saṃdideśa | tasyāḥ kanyāyāḥ so' yam evadhanyo vara iti |
children.translated_text: Then, the shining prince of <s>Gokula</s>, having brought to his ear — through the mouth of the boy [disguised messenger] — that offensive stratagem, sharp as bitterness, having some bold women of his own faction disguise that messenger-woman in men's attire, sent the message through that boy: 'Of that maiden, this very same [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] is the blessed bridegroom!'

children.text: saṃdiśya ca tām api madhumaṅgalavat puraḥ praḥīyābhiṣeṇayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And having dispatched her thus — just like <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — he sent her forth at the front with laughter and as a vanguard.

children.text: tad evaṃ mithaḥ kṛte niyate netroḥ kābhiścid anyābhiḥ kutuka-kṛte taṭasthatayā tatra saṅghaṭamānābhiḥ prakaṭa-haṭhatayā dvayos tat-tad-veśa-viśeṣiṇoḥ kṛta-sandhe paṭāñcala-bandhe jāte cobhayataś ca nānā-hāsa-prabandhe śrī-rādhā-pakṣa-lakṣitābhir mṛgākṣībhir idam ākhyāyi |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the mutual assignment was made, and when some other women, drawn by curiosity and standing as spectators from a neutral position, assembled there with open boldness, and when a curtain-screen was tied between the two parties, each distinguished by their respective costumes — and when bursts of various laughter arose on both sides — the doe-eyed ones aligned with glorious <s>Rādhā's</s> party declared this:

children.text: varṣīyasānena vareṇāsmat-padminīyaṃ dharṣitā | tasmād yuddhārtham udyamaḥ saṃbadhyatām |
children.translated_text: 'Our <s>Padminī</s> has been violated by this older suitor! Therefore, let the effort for battle be bound!'

children.text: tataḥ saṃbaddheṣu śuṣirādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ yuddha-vādyārtham ānaddheṣu |
children.translated_text: Then, when [war-preparations] were bound, and the battle-drums were beaten together with wind-instruments and such:

children.text: narmāṅga-gālir udaka-kṣipa-yantra-yuktir
children.translated_text: 'Witty insults as the limb of jest, the device of water-squirting machines,

children.text: daṇḍī-prapātana-nivartana-keli-rītiḥ |
children.translated_text: the play-custom of staff-striking, felling, and reversing,

children.text: kāntākṛti-vyati-kṛta-grahaṇaṃ sakhīnāṃ
children.translated_text: the seizing [of opponents] cross-dressed in beloved's forms,

children.text: sāhāyakaṃ yudhi babhau hari-horikāyāḥ ||JGc_1,30.23||
children.translated_text: and the aid of companions — shone in the <s>Holī</s>-battle of <s>Hari</s>!' ||30.23||

children.text: cirataś ca kṛṣṇa-keli-kalāvakalana-kevalatayā vikalita-sva-sva-keli-kalaha-pralāpeṣu rāma-śrīdāma-sudāmādi-kalāpeṣu tal-līlā-tṛṣṇak-kṛṣṇa eva sva-preyasībhiḥ saha sahasāhava-nibhaṃ viharati sma |
children.translated_text: And after a long time, when <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, and the other groups were confounded — their play-quarrel-chatter dissolved solely through absorption in perceiving <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> play-art — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, thirsting for that sport, sported suddenly with his beloveds in what resembled a real battle.

children.text: prathamaṃ tāvad asāv amūś ca parasparaṃ snigdhā vyatiṣajya vyatibiddhā babhūvuḥ, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: First, he and they, being affectionate toward each other, became mutually intertwined and pierced, because:

children.text: bhrū-kārmukā netra-bāṇā ye teṣāṃ māra-saṃyati |
children.translated_text: 'In the battle of <s>Kāma</s>, those whose bows are brows and whose arrows are eyes —

children.text: aṅgāstrāṇāṃ hanta kiṃ syād aparāddha-pṛṣatkatā ||JGc_1,30.24||
children.translated_text: alas, what then would be the body-armor against the weapons of limbs?' ||30.24||

children.text: atha punar daṇḍādaṇḍidaṇḍanapūrvakaṃ bāhābāhavibahalamevāyaṃ harirāhavamuvāha | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Then again, preceded by staff-to-staff and stick-to-stick striking, this <s>Hari</s> waged a battle that was exceedingly arm-to-arm. As follows:

children.text: dorāndolanam aṅgulī-parimalaṃ keśa-grahaṃ veśanut
children.translated_text: 'The swinging of arms, the fragrance of fingers, the seizing of hair, the disarranging of costume,

children.text: pāṇyoś cañcalatāṃ tathā para-paraṃ vācyāṃ vicārāt param |
children.translated_text: the restlessness of hands, then the mutual utterance of reproachable words from deliberation onward —

children.text: kurvaṃs tat-para-dāra-sainyam aviśat kṛṣṇas tathā svaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: performing [all this], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> entered the army of the other-wives in such a way

children.text: kutrāgād iti veda na sma janatā sāpy astu nāpi svayam ||JGc_1,30.25||
children.translated_text: that neither the people nor he himself knew where he had gone!' ||30.25||

children.text: tataś ca kramaśaḥ para-parātikrama-pūrvakam apūrvotsāha-vṛtayoḥ sakhībhir āvṛtayor asādhāraṇa-krīḍā-raṇa-javayo rādhā-mādhavayor eva vyatiṣaṅgaḥ prasaṅga-māyātaḥ | tatra ca | yathā-yathaṃ tat-kautukāvakalanataḥ sva-sva-vyāpāraṃ parityajya rajyamāna-citratayā citrāyamāṇā vara-varṇinyaḥ sauvarṇa-varṇākāratayā vṛṇvānā mithas tad varṇayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, gradually, preceded by mutual transgression upon transgression, with unprecedented exertions of enthusiasm, the two — <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> — surrounded by companions — of extraordinary battle-play speed — came into contact through the <s>māyā</s> of the occasion. And there, in proportion to the perception of curiosity therein, abandoning their own respective activities and being fascinated by the picturesque quality of enchantment, the excellent, fair-complexioned women, as if assuming the form and appearance of golden color, described it to one another.

children.text: tatha hi gītam-
children.translated_text: As follows, the song:

children.text: paśya paśya sakhi horīyuddham |
children.translated_text: 'Behold, behold, O friend, the <s>Holī</s>-battle

children.text: rādhā-mādhava-kṛtam anurahasaṃ suciraṃ bhavad-anuruddham ||dhru||
children.translated_text: performed by <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> — semi-secretly, long-restrained by you!' ||refrain||

children.text: daṇḍādaṇḍi-gate parikhaṇḍita-taratamato vyatirodham |
children.translated_text: 'When they advanced to staff-on-staff, having shattered the gradation of hierarchy — [there was] mutual opposition;

children.text: vyatiṣañjanam iha bhāti taḍid-ghana-ruci-jaya-lasad-udbodham ||
children.translated_text: the mutual entanglement here shines with the splendor of lightning-and-cloud beauty, blazing victoriously!' ||

children.text: mastaka-vastra-skhalanārambhāt pihite tan-mukha-yugale |
children.translated_text: 'When, from the onset of the cloth slipping from the head, both their faces were covered —
