children.text: bhramara-varāyitam ekenāsminn anyasmin bahu kamale ||
children.translated_text: by one, a bee-like buzzing [arose], while in the other, abundant lotus-like [blushing]!' ||

children.text: bhuja-bhujagena harer bahudhāraci hṛdi tasyāḥ phaṇa-līlā |
children.translated_text: 'The arm-serpent of <s>Hari</s>, manifoldly creating its hood-play upon her heart —

children.text: cakravāka-yuga-gīrṇir avākali yatra muhuḥ kṛti-śīlā ||
children.translated_text: the swallowing of the pair of <s>cakravāka</s>-birds [her breasts] — was repeatedly performed with practiced skill!' ||

children.text: api punar asminn avakalayata kila niravaniruha-tati-deśam |
children.translated_text: 'And again, behold in this [scene] the region devoid of trees and vegetation —

children.text: abhinava-kanaka-latā-parivalayita-taruṇa-tamāla-kuleśam ||
children.translated_text: a fresh golden creeper encircling the lord of young <s>tamāla</s> trees!' ||

children.text: taṃ yuvatī-kula-sāhāyaka-kṛta-bala-rādhā-vaśa-balinam |
children.translated_text: 'Him — made mighty by the assembled strength of the young-women's party of <s>Rādhā</s> —

children.text: racayati nayati ca nija-viṣaye diśi rabhasarasād api valinam ||
children.translated_text: she fashions [as captive], leads to her own domain, with the vehemence of her essence, even him the mighty one!' ||

children.text: nītaṃ taṃ nava-pīta-paṭaṃ mṛga-nābhi-jalair abhiṣiktam |
children.translated_text: 'That one — [now] led [away], wearing a fresh yellow garment, anointed with musk-water —

children.text: tanute sutanū-tatir iha vitanu-pramada-madād atiriktam ||
children.translated_text: the array of slender-bodied ones creates here [a spectacle] excessive even beyond the limitless joy of Love!' ||

children.text: seyaṃ rādhā svayam iha muralīṃ yad bata harati sa-yatnam |
children.translated_text: 'That this <s>Rādhā</s> herself here steals his flute with effort —

children.text: na tad adbhutam iva yad aharad asya prathamaṃ hṛn-maṇi-ratnam ||
children.translated_text: that is not so wondrous, since she first stole the jewel-gem of his heart!' ||

children.text: atha rāmādiḥ sakhi-janatā taṃ paśyantī viniruddham |
children.translated_text: 'Then, <s>Rāma</s> and the company of friends, seeing him captured,

children.text: sandhim adhitsata visṛjantī tāḥ prati dūtaṃ guṇa-śuddham ||
children.translated_text: sought a truce, dispatching a messenger of pure qualities toward them!' ||

children.text: rāmaḥ sa yadā phālguna-parvaṇi deyaṃ mene dātum |
children.translated_text: 'When that <s>Rāma</s>, at the <s>Phālguna</s>-festival, considered giving what was to be given,

children.text: pratibhuvam ādāyātha tadā harir ābhir amanyata rātum ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Hari</s>, having accepted a surety, was deemed [fit] to be released by them!' ||

children.text:
jāte sandhāv akhilenāpi ca śaṃsati divye loke |
nija-nija-kāntā-moha-virohaṇa-gītiḥ sa sa viluloke ||iti|| ||JGc_1,30.26||
children.translated_text:
'When the truce was made, and all in the divine world proclaimed it —
each one, composing a song of enchanting union with his own beloved, beheld [the spectacle]!' || Thus. ||30.26||

children.text: evaṃ sthite parasparaṃ carcarikā-racana-nicāyane vismāyake jāte samāja-dvaye ca mithaḥ kiṃcid dūraṃ yāte kasmād apy akasmān mūḍha-dhīḥ śaṅkhacūḍaḥ samāgataḥ | sa tu vigīta evety alam ati-tad-vistareṇa |
children.translated_text: Thus, when a wondrous state arose in the mutual exchange of the <s>carcarikā</s> (color-powder) play, and the two parties had gone somewhat far from each other — from some unknown [direction], suddenly, the dull-witted <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> arrived. But he was already ill-famed — so enough with excessive detail about him.

children.text: atha samāpanam-
children.translated_text: Now, the conclusion:

children.text: śaṅkhacūḍaṃ nihatavān yan maṇiṃ dattavān api |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> was slain, and the jewel was given [to <s>Balarāma</s>] as well;

children.text: rādhe kāntas tavāyaṃ tat kṛtavāṃs tvat-kṛte dvayam ||JGc_1,30.27||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rādhā</s>, this beloved of yours did both those deeds for your sake!' ||30.27||

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
nirvrīḍa-horikā-vikrīḍanaṃ nāma
triṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||30||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the thirtieth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Shameless <s>Holī</s>-Sport.'
||30||

children.text: athaikatriṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the thirty-first <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter),

children.text: nānā-rāga-vicitra-caritra-citram
children.translated_text: 'The Marvel of Diverse-Colored (<s>rāga</s>) Conduct.'

children.text:
atha snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ prabhāta-kathāṃ prathayāmāsa-[2] tad evaṃ pratikṣaṇam eva parama-prema-lakṣaṇa-līlāṃ phullad-ullāsataḥ sa gokula-bandhur daśamaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvalate sma |
 [3] sa tu nṛśaṃsaḥ kaṃsaḥ kramaśaḥ sarveṣu nirmita-nija-garveṣu tarhi nistarhiteṣu vaira-śuddhiṃ prati pratigata-buddhiḥ sarvataḥ śreṣṭhatayā rakṣitāvariṣṭa-keśināv āhūya saṃrabha-māṇatayā sabhayatayā cābhihitavān | mayāvajñayā nātiyogyā eva tatra viniyogyāḥ kṛtāḥ | sa tu dāraka iti buddhyā | kintu sphuṭam asau sarveṣāṃ dāraka eva jātaḥ | tataḥ kausīdya-khidyamānatayā bhavantāv anuyujyete | kim iha yujyata iti |
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> began the morning narrative:
[2] Thus, moment by moment, that friend of <s>Gokula</s>, with the divine play characterized by supreme <s>prema</s> blossoming with delight, was completing his tenth year.
[3] But that cruel <s>Kaṃsa</s>, when all those in whom he had fashioned his own pride had been successively dispatched, his mind turning toward the purification of enmity, summoned the two — <s>Ariṣṭa</s> and <s>Keśī</s> — who were the best of all, reserved [for this purpose]. With a mixture of fury and fear, he said: 'Through my neglect, those who were not even very capable were assigned there. That was with the notion "he is [merely] a boy." But clearly, he has become the destroyer of all! Therefore, you two are being employed, since you are afflicted by [my] reproach of laziness. What is appropriate here?'

children.text:
tāv ūcatuḥ-deva tad etad eva pratīkṣya sthiratayābhīkṣṇaṃ vartāvahe | sāmprataṃ tu sāmpratam ājñāpyatām | athavā kim ājñāpanayā | vināpi tāṃ viniyuktā eva yukta-sevakatayā vayam ity utthāya sābhyutthāna-praṇāmaṃ prasthitayos tayoḥ kaṃsaḥ śaśaṃsa |
[5] ariṣṭas tāvat pratiṣṭhatām | iṣṭāpatti-vipattitas tu keśī ca tat-prativeśa-veśī bhavitā | tad etad avadhāya tau ca gṛham āgatya sātatyata eva tad-artham ājagṛhatuḥ |
children.translated_text:
Those two said: 'Lord, awaiting precisely this, we have been standing firm with steadfastness constantly. Now, let it be commanded at once! Or rather, what need is there for a command? Even without it, we are already deployed as fit servants!' — thus, rising with a respectful bow, as the two set forth, <s>Kaṃsa</s> instructed:
[5] 'Let <s>Ariṣṭa</s> first establish himself. And <s>Keśī</s>, from the fortune and misfortune of the desired goal, shall assume the guise of a neighbor to that [place]. Having understood this, those two, returning home, continuously prepared themselves for that purpose.'

children.text: atha kadācil lohitāyamāne sāyaṃ mārtaṇḍa-raśmi-maṇḍale nāmnāriṣṭaḥ sarva-diviṣa-dariṣṭaḥ sarvatra ca raṃhasā jaṅghanyamānaḥ sarvāṃś cāghnā jeghnīyamānaḥ śrīmantaṃ goṣṭha-dvārāntam ājagāma |
children.translated_text: Then, on a certain evening when the disc of the sun's rays was becoming reddish, the one named <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, evil-destined among all celestials, rushing with speed in all directions, striking all with his horns — arrived at the entrance of the glorious cow-settlement.

children.text:
yadā hi citrāyuta-pūrṇa-candrāṃ pūrṇimām anu turṇita-cetāḥ sva-sukha-vardhana-govardhana-vilokana-kāmanayā śrī-rāma-kaniṣṭhaḥ kiṃcid dūraṃ praviṣṭa āsīt | tataś ca-
 bhū-kampa-kramaṇān mahīdhra-calanaṃ tasyāgater vāri-bhṛd-
vikṣobhaṃ nadanān niśācara-varaṃ vaikṛtyabhāg-ākṛteḥ | tad-rūpādri-viniścayaṃ kakudi vār-mug-vṛnda-saṅghaṭṭanād unnīya vrajaga-prajā diśi diśi drāk kāndiśīkyaṃ gatāḥ ||JGc_1,31.1|| kiṃcit kiṃcin mūtraṇād āpagānāṃ
gūtha-tyāgād gaṇḍa-śailāvalīnām | sṛṣṭiṃ kartā paśyatāriṣṭa-nāmā
devāriṣṭaḥ parvatātmā pratītaḥ ||JGc_1,31.2|| vṛṣa-dambhī sa-saṃrambhaṃ rambhaṇaṃ yad-vyadhād asau | tenāsīd vyakta-sandarbhaḥ svayaṃ go-garbha-pātinā ||JGc_1,31_3|| vapraṃ yadāpaskirate sma śṛṅgā-
dibhir vikurvāṇatā vṛṣaḥ saḥ | tadākhilaṃ gokulam āśu mṛdbhiḥ
pracchannam āsīd vana-maṇḍalaṃ ca ||JGc_1,31.4|| yatra tatra khuram ādadhāti
sa kṣmāpi tatra valate vidīrṇatām | netra-tulya-vilataḥ samucchritaṃ
vāri rodana-nibhaṃ bibharti ca ||JGc_1,31.5|| [9] tatra lokānāṃ vacanaṃ-
children.translated_text:
When indeed, following a full-moon night replete with tens of thousands of wonders, with eager mind, desiring to see happiness-enhancing <s>Govardhana</s>, the younger brother of Śrī <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) had gone somewhat far. And then:
From the earthquakes of his tread, the mountain appeared to move; from his bellowing, a disturbance of clouds; from the distortion of his form, he [appeared as] a supreme night-stalker (demon). Ascertaining it to be a mountain in that form from the collision of his hump with hosts of birds — the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> swiftly fled in every direction in panic! // [śārdūla]
By his slight urinating, [he created] streams; by his dropping of dung, rows of boulder-hills — the one named <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, evil-destined, a mountain-bodied one, was perceived as the creator of a [new] creation! // [śālinī]
The bull-disguised one, with fury, produced such a bellowing that thereby the arrangement became evident — of one who himself causes the miscarriage of cows' offspring! // [anuṣṭubh]
When that bull tore up the rampart with his horns and other acts of violence, then all of <s>Gokula</s> was swiftly covered with earth, and the forest-circle too! // [upajāti]
Wherever he placed his hoof, there the earth too cracked apart; and from the eye-like crevices, raised-up water, resembling weeping, was borne forth! // [rathoddhatā]
[9] There, the words of the people:

children.text:
jātu mātu girireṣa samantād- uccalann api tathāvidha-mūrteḥ | kiṃ tu śṛṅga-talagaṃ ravi-yugmaṃ
hā vyasismayata gokula-lokam ||JGc_1,31.6|| iti |
 [10] evam udghnatā gavām udghnān nighnatā ca sarvaṃ vastu prastubhyatā cāriṣṭena kṛtād ākruṣṭāt kaṣṭam anuspṛṣṭavantas te goṣṭha-niṣṭhā go-nara-prakṛṣṭāḥ kṛṣṇāya muhur vikṛṣṭavantaḥ |
 [11] sūrataḥ sa tu dūratas teṣām avagata-vikrośana-leśa-mātraṃ kutrāpy akṛta-yātra iva saṃmukhata evāvatasthe | avasthāya ca mā bhaiṣṭety abhayam uddiṣṭaṃ vidhāya krodhāviṣṭas tam ariṣṭam ājuhāva balīvarda-krodha-vardhana-narda-viśeṣeṇa | tad idaṃ tu taṃ prati samprati sukarārdanas tvam asīti jñāpanāya |
children.translated_text:
'No matter what — even if this mountain-bodied one were to leap up on all sides — but the pair of suns upon the tips of his horns — alas! — they astonished the people of <s>Gokula</s>!' // [svāgatā] — thus.
[10] Thus, when <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, butting the cows with his horns and striking everything with his hooves and trampling it, had created distress — those superior cow-folk and men of the settlement, loyal to the settlement, cried out repeatedly to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
[11] But he, from a distance, having perceived merely a trace of their outcry, as if having gone nowhere, stood facing them directly. And having stood, having declared 'Fear not!' and bestowing fearlessness, he, filled with anger, challenged that <s>Ariṣṭa</s> with a special bellowing that enhanced the anger of a bull. And this was indeed to inform him: 'You are now the one to be crushed by the wild boar (<s>sukarārdana</s>)!'

children.text:
atha covāca, yathā-
sapālaiḥ paśubhir manda trāsitaiḥ kim asattama | mayi śāstari duṣṭānāṃ tvad-vidhānāṃ durātmanām ||[BhP 10.36.7] iti |
 punaś ca-
 piṇḍīśūra vidūraḥ san krūratāṃ tvaṃ kim ṛcchasi | sāmudra-pūra iva māṃ kumbha-jātaṃ prapūrayeti ||JGc_1,31.7||[13] tad idaṃ ca tasya gāṃ-manyasya jighāṃsayā lokānāṃ gotva-bhramāpagamanayā coktavān iti gamyate | kiṃ ca-
 āsphoṭanaṃ kṛtam anena tadā yad asmād- āsphoṭanaṃ samabhavad danuja-śrutīnām | ko' yaṃ cakāra sa tu yad vṛsabhas tad
uccaiḥ kopaṃ ca varṣa-śiśuvan nahi jāhasīti ||JGc_1,31.8|| kṛṣṇaḥ sakhyuḥ skandha-deśe sva-bāhuṃ
nikṣipyāsāv uddhasann eva tasthau | yena krodhaṃ vardhayāmāsa tasya
preyo-vargāṇāṃ ca sandeha-sargam ||JGc_1,31.9|| vṛṣas tv asau raja iva puccha-mārjanī- paribhramair ghana-gaṇa-lakṣam utkṣipan | kṣitiṃ kṣatām atha khura-vajra-vijvalat- khanitrakair vidadhad agād dhariṃ prati ||JGc_1,31_10|| sa vajrati sma na param āśu vidravaṃ
prati dviṣat-pratirutatī-vratāṃ prati | na kevalaṃ harir iha hā samāyayau
sakhāpi yaḥ parikṛta-tad-bhujāṃsakaḥ ||JGc_1,31.11||[14] tādṛśatayā spaṣṭam aviprakṛṣṭe ca tasmin śrīmān kṛṣṇas tu śṛṅga-dvayam evābhijagrāha, yathā-
 śṛṅge ye pūrvatāṃ nīte jayāya vṛṣa-rakṣasā | sva-sandānāya te sṛṣṭe kṛṣṇa-doṣṇor vaśaṃ gate ||JGc_1,31.12||
children.translated_text:
And he spoke, as follows:
'O dull one, what [use is] frightening the cattle and their keepers, O most wicked one? In my presence, the chastiser of the wicked, the likes of you, the evil-souled!' // [BhP 10.36.7] — thus.
And again:
'O champion of the arena, O you who are fierce from afar — why do you assume cruelty? Like an ocean-flood [trying to fill] the jar-born one (<s>Agastya</s>), you try to fill me!' // [anuṣṭubh]
[13] And this was said, it is understood, for the purpose of killing that cow-impersonator and for the removal of the people's delusion of cow-identity. Moreover:
When he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) clapped his hands, from that came a clapping of the ears of the demons! 'Who is this that did [that]?' — that bull then greatly increased his anger, like a child of the rains, and did not laugh! // [śārdūla]
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, placing his arm upon the shoulder of his friend, stood there laughing heartily — by which he increased that one's anger and also created a discharge of doubt among his circle of dear ones! // [śālinī]
But that bull, hurling dust with his tail-sweeps like fan-strokes, kicking up the ground marked like a cloud-mass, digging the scarred earth with the sparking diamond-hooves like shovels, charged toward <s>Hari</s>! // [vaṃśastha]
He (<s>Ariṣṭa</s>) rushed not merely for swift flight, but toward the vow of hostile counter-challenge. Not only did <s>Hari</s> come here — but also his friend, whose shoulder had been used as an armrest! // [upajāti]
[14] In such a manner, when he (<s>Ariṣṭa</s>) was clearly not far off, the glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> seized precisely his two horns, as follows:
The horns which were brought forward by the bull-demon for the purpose of victory — those were sent forth for his own binding, having come under the control of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> arms! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
bāhu-pāśa-sita-tīvra-śṛṅgakaḥ
sa sphuṭaṃ pratimukhaṃ sarann api | pratyag aṣṭādaśa ca kramān balād dity-apatya-ripuṇāpayāpitaḥ ||JGc_1,31.13|| ayam uddhutas tad iha nāsti bhāratā
na phalaṃ vinodana-kalā-vinodataḥ | iti mādhavaḥ sphuṭam ariṣṭam utkṣipan
nati-rīḍhayā bata vivṛttim āṭiṭat ||JGc_1,31.14|| vyavartata hari-kṣiptaḥ paraṃ nokṣāsuraḥ kṣitau | hāsāveśa-vaśe kṣiptaḥ svarge' pi svargiṇāṃ gaṇaḥ ||JGc_1,31_15|| papāta pucchaṃ bhuvi śṛṅgayor balāc
chṛṅge tu pucchasya nipetatur bhuvi | pṛṣṭhāṅghri caivaṃ vṛṣa-rakṣasas tadā
yuktaṃ tad asmin viparīta-kāriṇi ||JGc_1,31.16|| tajjā lajjāpy utthitā tasya so' pi
pratyuttasthāv abhyayuṅktāpi bhūyaḥ | kṛṣṇas tv enaṃ pātayan vāma-śṛṅge- ṇotkṛttenāmuṣya vaktraṃ cukuṭṭa ||JGc_1,31.17||[14] śṛṅgotpāṭaṇaṃ ghaṭayaṃs tv idam ācaṣṭa-
 abhadrasyāpi bhavato bhadrākṛti-vidha-sariṇaḥ | viṣāṇa-muṇḍanād bhadrākṛtir eva praśasyate ||JGc_1,31.18|| athārdra-vasanaṃ yathā parinipīḍayan jīvanaṃ
vikarṣati janas tathā tam akarod ariṣṭaṃ hariḥ | malāni ca yadākirac chamala-mūtra-raktādikāny
asyau parama-śuddhatām api jagāma kaivalyataḥ ||JGc_1,31.19|| layaṃ paramam āgatas tad api yat padaṃ nairṛtaṃ
yayāvayam iti smṛtaṃ munibhir etad uccai ruṣā | prasūnam atha yan mudā vavṛṣur āditeyās tad apy
amitra-vilayād bhaved ucitam īdṛśāt kiṃ punaḥ ||JGc_1,31.20||
children.translated_text: from such a destruction of an enemy, this would be fitting — what more [need be said]? // [śikhariṇī]

With horns rendered acutely white by the noose of his arms, he, even while clearly retreating face-forward, was forcibly driven back eighteen paces by the enemy of <s>Diti's</s> offspring! // [rathoddhatā]
'This one has been uprooted — so there is no point here, O <s>Bhāratā</s> (friend) — the fruit from the sport of entertaining art is not [obtained]!' — thus the <s>Mādhava</s>, clearly tossing <s>Ariṣṭa</s> up, struck him with the humiliation of a bow! // [upajāti]
The <s>ukṣa</s>-demon (<s>Ariṣṭa</s>), flung by <s>Hari</s>, did not indeed [merely land] on the earth; the host of heaven-dwellers too was flung into the grip of laughter! // [anuṣṭubh]
His tail fell on the ground, but his two horns, by force, fell on [the area of] the tail upon the ground; likewise, his hind-legs [fell where] the forelegs [had been] — of that bull-demon, then — this was fitting for that doer of the contrary! // [upajāti]
The shame born of that [defeat] also arose in him; he too rose again and attacked yet again. But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bringing him down, with the left horn torn out, struck his face! // [śālinī]
[14] And accomplishing the uprooting of the horn, he declared this:
'Even for you, the inauspicious one, who have the guise of an auspicious-formed bull — through the shearing of your horns, the auspicious-formed appearance itself is to be commended!' // [anuṣṭubh]
Then, just as a person wrings out a wet garment and extracts the water, so <s>Hari</s> dealt with <s>Ariṣṭa</s>. And when he [<s>Ariṣṭa</s>] discharged filth, foul urine, blood, and the like, even he attained the supreme purity of ultimate liberation! // [śikhariṇī]
That he attained supreme dissolution and yet went to the demonic realm — this is recorded by the sages loudly, in anger. But that the sons of <s>Aditi</s> (gods) then rained flowers in joy —

children.text:
atra ca śrī-gokula-prāṇābhiprāyam abhiprayadbhis tad eva cānuvadadbhir diviṣadbhir upahasitam-
 vatsaṃ laghuṃ daityatayāvagacchan
jaghāna bāle' py aham ukṣa daitya | prauḍhaḥ kathaṃ tvām atibhīṣma-varṣma- praṣṭhaṃ na jānāni na ghātayānīti ||JGc_1,31.21||
children.translated_text:
And here, the celestials, perceiving the intent of the life-breath of glorious <s>Gokula</s> and echoing it, mocked [<s>Ariṣṭa</s>] thus:
'The calf, being slight as a demon, was slain even when he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) was a child — O bull-demon, I did so! Now that he is mature, how would I not know and not slay you, of exceedingly fearsome form, who stand behind [others]?' // [upajāti]

children.text:
atra gokula-janasya gokula-jīvanasya ca bhāvam āviśann eva śrī-śukadevas tad idaṃ vadati sma-
 evaṃ kukudminaṃ hatvā
stūyamānaṃ svajātibhiḥ | viveśa goṣṭhaṃ sabalo
children.translated_text:
Here, Śrī <s>Śukadeva</s>, entering the emotional state of the people of <s>Gokula</s> and of the life of <s>Gokula</s>, declared this:
'Thus, having slain the humped one (<s>Ariṣṭa</s>), praised by his own people,
he entered the cow-settlement together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Rāma</s>),

children.text: gopīnāṃ nayanotsavaḥ ||[BhP 10.36.15] iti |
children.translated_text: the festival of the eyes of the <s>gopīs</s>!' // [BhP 10.36.15] — thus.

children.text:
āyāte vrajam acyute ripu-jaya-svasti-praśastīḍite
sarve' py unmadatāṃ gatā bahu-vidhaṃ saṃvādam unnirmamuḥ | kiṃ tu drāk pitarāv amuṣya vadanaṃ tad vīkṣyamāṇāv amū
svair bāṣpāmbubhir āplutaṃ mamṛjatur vikruśya mūkāv iva ||JGc_1,31.22|| [17] atha samāpanam-
 ayaṃ sa stava-bhāk sūnus tava gopa-narādhipa | pūṣitās tridaśā yena mūṣitās tridaśārayaḥ ||JGc_1,31.23||
children.translated_text:
When <s>Acyuta</s> arrived at <s>Vraja</s>, praised with auspicious victory-benedictions over the enemy, all attained a state of intoxication and produced manifold conversation! But swiftly, his two parents, gazing at that face of his, awash with the tears of their own eyes, wiped it — crying out as if mute! // [śārdūla]
[17] Then, the conclusion:
'This is that son of yours who receives praise, O cowherd chief! By whom the gods were nourished and the enemies of the gods were plundered!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha rātri-kathāyām api snigdhakaṇṭha evābhidadhe-[19] evaṃ horikā-prānta-kānta-krīḍāntarānusāreṇābhira-vīra-sarasijākṣīṇām akṣīṇānaṅgānāṃ vṛtta-kṛṣṇa-saṅgānāṃ bahudhā nivṛttaṃ rātri-vṛttaṃ svayam eva sakhībhir anusandhīyatām |
children.translated_text:
Now, in the night-tale as well, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> himself declared:
[19] 'Thus, following the sequence of the sports at the border of the <s>Holī</s>-festival with the beloved, the nighttime conduct of the cowherd-hero's lotus-eyed women — whose <s>Anaṅga</s> (desire) was undiminished and whose company with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was fully established — was itself investigated by the companions in many ways.'

children.text:
vāsarāvasaraś cāyaṃ mad-ukti-nidigdha-dig-darśanataḥ parāmarśam ānīyatām | yathā cāha śrī-parāśaraḥ-
 sa tathā saha gopībhī rarāma madhusūdanaḥ | yathābda-koṭi-pratimaḥ kṣaṇas tena vinābhavat ||[ViP 5.13.57]
 yathā ca śrī-śukaḥ-
 gopyaḥ kṛṣṇe vanaṃ yāte tam anudruta-cetasaḥ | kṛṣṇa-līlāḥ pragāyantyo ninyur duḥkhena vāsarān ||[BhP 10.35.1] iti |
children.translated_text:
'And this daytime occasion, through the direction indicated by my utterance, should be brought to consideration. As said by the glorious <s>Parāśara</s>:
"Thus, <s>Madhusūdana</s> sported with the <s>gopīs</s> in such a manner that a moment without him became equivalent to ten million years!" // [ViP 5.13.57]
And as said by the glorious <s>Śuka</s>:
"The <s>gopīs</s>, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> went to the forest, their minds racing after him, singing of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> pastimes, passed the days with difficulty!" // [BhP 10.35.1] — thus.'

children.text: tathā hi-yadā khalv aharahaḥ kṣayam āsādya vādya-gīta-nṛtyaṃ vivṛtya sahacara-saṅginībhiḥ śṛṅgiṇībhiḥ saha sa harir vraja-jana-sneha-dhanaḥ sva-veśma praviśati tadā vigata-parimāṇā vimānānucāriṇaḥ sarva eva samam upary-upari-cariṇaḥ saha gaṇena kaṇehatya spaṣṭaṃ draṣṭum icchantas tad-abhāva-labdha-kadanāḥ sadanānta-paryantam āyānti | kṛta-veśma-praveśe tu tasmin vismaya-sthagitatayā sa-lālasatayā ca tatra tatra citrāyamāṇā rātriṃ gamayanti sma |
children.translated_text: For thus: When, day after day, at the end [of each day], having expanded music, song, and dance, together with the horned ones (cows) accompanied by his female companions, that <s>Hari</s>, rich in affection for the people of <s>Vraja</s>, entered his own dwelling — then the measureless ones, the followers of aerial chariots, all the sky-coursers together with their hosts, with the sound of buzzing, clearly desiring to behold, having attained distress from the inability [to see], came as far as the boundary of the dwelling. And when he had made his entry into the dwelling, through the concealment of astonishment and through eagerness, becoming various pictures here and there, they passed the night.

children.text:
śaraṇāntarāt punar yāvan niḥsarati sa eṣa śaraṇāgatāyāgatānusaraṇaḥ | tad evaṃ yadā niḥsarati niḥsṛtya ca gopa-gogaṇa-sañcaraṇāya veṇuṃ raṇayati | tadātanaṃ caritaṃ gocaratām aticarad api nija-bhāva-prabhāva-sampadā cakṣuṣīva racitaṃ vidhāya śrīmad-ābhīra-bhīrubhir abhigītam, yathā-
avadhāraya sakhi tava sakhi-vṛttam | virahi-janānāṃ janayati hṛdayam vidayatayā bata kṛttam |
[dhruvam idaṃ paraparatrāpi |]
vāma-bhujākṛta-vāma-kapolakam ullala-cilli-bhāsam | sukumārāṅguli-vilasitam ujjvala-veṇu-mukhaṃ mṛdu-hāsam ||rāga-kalā-kulitākhila-bhūcara-gāna-kalair anuviddham | vyomaga-yāna-janījana-mohanam anugamitākhila-siddham ||JGc_1,31.24|| [24] tataś ca muhur api tāvan mātre tāsāṃ gāna-pātre sati vana-vrajayor madhyam adhyāsya harṣaṃ tarṣaṃ ca dhāsyan vaṃśaṃ śaṃsayati sma | [25] tatra ca tābhir gītaṃ, yathā-
citraṃ lakṣmī-rekhāsau hṛdi capalā na bhavati capalā | maṇim ambara-maṇim anu tārāvalir api sā rājāti taralā ||yasya sa cāyaṃ veṇu-kalāmṛta-varṣī kalayati gavyām | sa-tṛṇaka-daśanām unnata-karṇāmatrām arthiṣu bhavyām ||JGc_1,31.25||[25] tataścātuccha-piccha-guluccha-puṣpa-guccha-dhātu-cchavibhir malla-paricchadaṃ gacchati sma śrī-gopikānāṃ pracchanna-ramaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text:
And whenever he emerges again from within the shelter, he follows the one who has come seeking refuge. Thus, when he emerges and, having emerged, sounds the flute for the movement of the cowherd-and-cow assembly — then that daily conduct, though surpassing [ordinary] perception, was made as if fashioned for the eyes by the wealth of the power of his own emotional state, and was sung by the awe-inspired, glorious cowherd women, as follows:
'Attend, O friend, to the conduct of your companion! Alas, it renders the hearts of those separated as if cut, through its piercing!
[This refrain applies hereafter too.]
With the left cheek resting on the crook of the left arm, with the shining of the fluttering brow-play, with the sport of delicate fingers, with the radiant flute at his mouth and a gentle smile — ||pervaded by the musical measures of melody-art, confounding all earth-dwelling song-birds, enchanting the people of the sky-vehicles, followed by all the <s>Siddhas</s>! ||31.24||
[24] Then, again and again, as long as there was a recipient-vessel for their songs in the mother, he — seated between the forest and <s>Vraja</s> — bestowing both delight and longing, proclaimed the flute. [25] And there, their song, as follows:
'Wonderful — that line of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) upon the heart is fickle, yet it does not become fickle! Following the jewel, the sky-jewel, even the row of stars shines, trembling! ||He, that one, raining the nectar of the flute's art, fashions the cowherd-settlement — the cows with grass-blades between their teeth, with ears upraised, with mouths like vessels, auspicious toward supplicants! ||31.25||
[26] Thereupon, that concealed lover of the glorious <s>gopīs</s> assumed the wrestling-costume, [adorned] with the splendors of abundant peacock-feathers, flower-clusters, and mineral pigments.

children.text:
taṃ gatvā ca satvara-prathama-payaḥ-pāyanāya gaṅgā-yamunādi-nāmnā gāḥ su-vikasvara-sarasijaṃ saraḥ prati kramād veṇu-gānataḥ samākārayati tasmin vraja-ramānāthe buddha-nijākāraṇa iva ruddha-pravāha-prasaratayāsthiratām utkalikām apy anusarati | vidūra-cara-sarid-visare ca punar āsāṃ gītaṃ, yathā-
candraka-dhātu-dala-stavakādika-kṛta-mallottama-veśam | ākārayati sa gāḥ sarid-ālī labhate tatra viśeṣam ||kamita-bhaṅga-bhujā kila tat-pada-raja āśuga-tati-nītam | laghu sukṛtāsmād dṛg iva spṛhayati vidatī svam anabhinītam ||JGc_1,31.26||[28] atha tadā tadāhūti-kṛtām ānanda-vibhūtim ārabhya tac-caritam upalabhya kadācid vraja-dharitrīśitrī-sadasi gatabhiḥ kābhiścana tābhir utkaṇṭhayā suṣṭhu pratuṣṭuṣamāṇābhir api nija-bhāvaṃ pidhāya bhāvāntara-sādhāraṇyaṃ vidhāya tad idaṃ varṇanaṃ tan-nirvarṇanam ivāsīt |
[29] tatra gānāntaraṃ, yathā-
 ādi-puruṣa iva vaibhava-śālī | anucara-varṇita-vīrya-samunnatir ayam udayati vanamālī ||dhru|| sa gavākāraṇa-muralī-kalam anu tanute yatra vanaṃ ca | tad-rūpāntaryāmi-sphuraṇaja-bhāvān kalayati pañca ||puṣpa-hasita-madhu-baṣpa-navāṅkura-pulaka-tatīr anuyātam | ejan-namad api śākhā-tatibhir yat kila kalayati śātam ||JGc_1,31.27||[30] tad evam aniṅgānām apīṅgānām iva śaśvad iṅga-vyaṅgaṃ vihitavān |
children.translated_text:
Having gone there, for the quick first feeding of milk, he summoned the cows by the flute-song toward the lake — named after <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and others — [whose surface was adorned] with blossoming lotuses. In that lord of the <s>Vraja</s> beauties, who had awakened his own true form, as if the flow had become arrested in its current, even the eagerness followed an unsteadiness. And at the distant course of the river-expanse, their song again, as follows:
'[Behold] him in the supreme wrestler's attire made of peacock-crest-feathers, mineral-leaf-clusters, and such — he summons the cows, and the river-line attains a special [beauty] there! ||The river, whose arms are waves, longing for the touch of his foot-dust carried swiftly — light [in her steps], her fortune greater than ours, with her eye desiring [him], she does not perceive her own [inferior] acting! ||31.26||
[28] Then, beginning from the blessed wealth of those summons, perceiving his daily conduct, at some time, in the assembly of the queen of <s>Vraja</s> and her companions, some [<s>gopīs</s>], with longing, though indeed praising excellently, concealing their own feelings and fashioning a commonality through another mood, described [him] — that description was as if a direct observation. [29] There, another song, as follows:
'Like the primal being (<s>Ādi-puruṣa</s>), resplendent with glory, with his valor proclaimed by his attendants, this garland-wearer (<s>Vanamālī</s>) arises! ||Refrain|| When he fashions the cowherding along with the sweet sound of the summoning flute — the forest experiences five [emotional responses] born of the flashing of his inner-dwelling form: ||the rows of flower-laughter, honey-tears, new-sprout-horripilation that follow [him] — even the shaking, bowing branches fashioned, as it were, a greeting! ||31.27||
[30] Thus, even upon the immovable things, he continually wrought the gestures of moving beings.

children.text: atha samāsanne vinodenāhnāyavan madhyāhne kvacin mahā-sarasi sarasija-saurabha-sarasena ghana-rasena snāna-līlām abhiniviśya kevala-tilaka-vanamālā-valita-veśa-bhaṅgi-saṅgitā-pūrvakam apūrve tasminn ekānte kusumita-vanānte kānte mahā-śaila-prānte pallava-lasad-urutara-taru-tala-vilasita-śilāyām upaviśya virājannusrāvāra-cāraṃ prati bhūri-dūrī-bhāvam iteṣu mitreṣu nija-saurabha-rabhasa-samudita-madhura-madhu-kara-nikara-gāna-kṛtāvadhānas tad-dhūṅkāra-kāraṇa-svara-sāram anu kutuka-kṛtānusandhānas tad-anusāri-veṇu-cāri-raṇitena suracita-sārasādi-rasādhānaḥ so' yaṃ ramate sma |
children.translated_text: Then, near midday, when an entertaining noontime arrived — somewhere, at a great lake, having engaged in a bathing-sport rich with the essence of the abundant fragrance of lotuses — adorned only with <s>tilaka</s> markings and a forest garland, preceded by the composition of dress-style and song — in that unprecedented solitude, at the edge of the flowering forest, at the charming border of the great mountain, seated upon a stone slab beneath the shade of a tree gleaming with broad sprouts — when his friends had gone far away for the grazing of the herds of cows and cowherds — attentive to the song of the sweet-buzzing host of bees stirred by the fragrance of his own [garland], and out of curiosity applying his investigation to the essence of the melody that was the cause of their humming, and through the sounding of the flute following that [melody], having established a foundation of the <s>rasa</s> of <s>sārasa</s> (crane) birds and such — he sported.

children.text:
tac ca, yathā-
ramya-tilaka-nava-tulasī-dala-bhava-vana-mālātivikāsī | nija-saurabha-vaśa-madhupa-gītam anugāyati veṇu-vilāsī ||atha sārasa-yuta-haṃsāyuta-tatir alam anugamya parītā | parito nyaviśata tām āviśatī rutim iha yā hari-gītā ||JGc_1,31.28||[33] tataś ca tatas tataḥ samāgate sāgraje samagre sakhi-varge tadānīntana-barhi-prabarha-barhādi-nānā-vanya-nepathya-prathyamāna-śobha-lobhanīya-rūpa-varīyastayā praśasta-srajīyastayā ca vistṛta-śātasya tasya gocāraṇa-caritaṃ pracāraṇīyam |
children.translated_text:
And that, as follows:
The one who sports with the flute, radiant with the overflowing beauty of fresh <s>tilaka</s>, new <s>tulasī</s> leaves, and the forest garland — sings along with the bee-song controlled by his own fragrance! ||Then, the flock of <s>sārasa</s> cranes joined with swans, having fully followed, surrounded [him]; and all around settled [those who] entered that melody — that song of <s>Hari</s>! ||31.28||
[33] Then, when the entire company of friends, together with the elder brother, had reassembled from here and there — his splendor being most covetable, made famous by the various sylvan costumes of peacock-plumage, bark, and such of the present [time] — his cow-herding conduct, with his composure widely spread, is worth proclaiming.

children.text: tathā hi-kvacid api kṣiti-bhṛti vṛkṣa-śūnya-kṣiti-gata-puṇya-tṛṇaṃ dhenuṣu carantīṣu vahnīyamāna-mādhyāhnika-lalāṭaṃ-tapa-tapana-tāpāpanodāya veṇuṃ vāditavān | yatra balāhakās tat-pratimalla-nibha-mallāra-rāga-balād āhṛtās teṣāṃ śītalatā-valanāya babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus — somewhere, upon a treeless hillside, when the blessed grass was on the ground and the cows were grazing, he played the flute to dispel the burning midday heat of the blazing sun upon their foreheads. There, clouds, drawn by the force of the <s>Mallāra</s> <s>rāga</s> (rain-melody) resembling his rival-combatant, came into being for cooling them.

children.text: yac ca vādyam udbhavat-puru-guru-garima-giri-droṇīḥ pratidhavan yat tat paramparayā ca sarvam api tatha raṇayat-trilokī-lokam api tat-kautukālokanāyākarṣati sma |
children.translated_text: And the music that arose — reverberating through the great, weighty, massive mountain valleys — and that which, by succession, caused all three worlds to resound — drew the people of the <s>triloki</s> (three worlds) too, for the spectacle of that curiosity.

children.text:
tatha ca sati tat tad anubhūya bhūyaś ca tābhir idaṃ tasyām eva sabhāyāṃ varṇitam-
 dhṛta-vana-mālya-vataṃsa-lasad-vana-veśa-tatir bala-saṅgī | giri-taṭam anu gocāraṇa-kāraṇa-veṇu-vinodana-raṅgī ||viśvaṃ bhramayati karṣati varṣati mudam api ghana-gaṇa-hārī | sāndra-cchāyām anu śītala-tanur anu sakhi-sukha-saṃcārī ||kusumaṃ varṣan nija-ruci-vitaraṇa-sauhṛdam enam upāste | ambu-dharaḥ sphuṭam upagantā na ca kiṃ tu chatram ivāste ||JGc_1,31.29||[37] tataś ca tatrātighane ghana-cchāye vihāraṃ vicchāyati sma |
children.translated_text:
Thus, having experienced each of these [marvels], they [the <s>gopīs</s>] described them again in that very assembly:
'With the company of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), in the attire of a supreme wrestler made of peacock-crest-feathers, mineral-pigments, and leaf-clusters — he entertains with the flute along the mountain slopes for cow-herding! ||He whirls the world, attracts it, rains delight, stealer of cloud-hosts — in dense shade, his body cool, a companion conveying happiness to friends! ||The rain-cloud, showering flowers, attending him out of the friendship of bestowing its own luster — clearly a visitor, yet it stays not [in rivalry], but stands like an umbrella! ||31.29||
[37] Then, in that exceedingly dense cloud-shade, he embellished the pastime.

children.text:
tad etac ca vrajarāja-jāyā-samājam anu sādhāraṇa-sampradhāraṇatayā tābhir varṇitam, yathā-
 sva-sutaṃ kalayata keli-kalā-budham ātmopakrama-veṇum | vidhi-śiva-mohana-vividha-sva-ramaya-rāga-nivartita-dhenum ||JGc_1,31.30|| iti |
 [39] tad-anantaraṃ ca prāyaśaḥ kāścid vraja-devīr vrajād ahni cāpahnuty vyājaṃ vyajya vā tad-āgamana-vartmani tad-anuvartanāya vartamānās taṃ paśyantīḥ punar apaśyantīr iva dūrāt pariharantīr itthaṃ kāścid dūtikāḥ parihasanti-
 madāndhe rājate piñchī na sapiñchī puras tava | veṇu-dhvānī jagat-prāṇaḥ sa jagat-prāṇa eṣa neti ||JGc_1,31.31||[40] śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ ca chalena vijñāpayanti, yathā-
 jyotsnāṃ tanoti lalitāṃ dadhate vicitrāṃ
śākhāṃ dadhāti nikhilaṃ jayatīti-bhāṅgyā | candrāvalīṃ ca lalitāṃ ca viśākhikāṃ ca
rādhāṃ ca tāḥ sakhi-sadasy api sūcayanti ||JGc_1,31.32||[41] tatra kāścid deva-pūjā-vvyājena duṣprāpa-puṣpādikam avacinvānā bahala-kalaha-mūlatāṃ prayānti |
children.translated_text:
And this was described by them in the assembly of the queen of <s>Vraja</s> and her companions, as a general reflection, as follows:
'Behold your own son — wise in the arts of sport, with his own flute taken up — who diverts the cows through the various <s>rāgas</s> of his own amusement, enchanting <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śiva</s>! ||31.30||
[39] Thereafter, some [<s>gopīs</s>], for the most part, concealing their identities by pretext or openly feigning [innocence], stationed on the path of his arrival from <s>Vraja</s> during the day, following him — seeing him yet pretending not to see him, avoiding [him] from afar — some messengers teased them thus:
'O one blinded by passion — the peacock-feather shines, not the one with the peacock-feather, before you! The flute-sound is the life of the world — he is not the life of the world!' ||31.31||
[40] And they informed Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> under a pretext, as follows:
'She spreads moonlight, she holds a wonderful branch, she makes all victorious' — by the device of [describing] <s>Candrāvalī</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and <s>Rādhā</s>, they indicated [them] even in the assembly of companions! ||31.32||
[41] There, some, under the pretext of divine worship, while gathering hard-to-obtain flowers and such, became the cause of abundant quarrel.

children.text: kāścit tu navya-bhavya-gavyādikaṃ tad-artham evānayanti tathāpi nātmanā tasminn arpayanti | tata eva kṛtrima-dāna-catvara-deśam apadeśam avarudhya vartma vinirudhya pṛcchantaṃ taṃ prati kraya-vikrayika-rītyānyathā khyāpayanti | divyād api divyam etad vijñāya yajña-patnīr anu kṛta-yatnāsu krayikatām āśrayamāṇāsu yajña-bhuk-pati-vratāsu satyākṛti-kṛtinīvāka-parīpākam ākalayya kṛtsnaṃ vasnaṃ ca saṃkalayya vikretavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Some brought fresh, fine dairy products and the like expressly for his sake, yet did not offer [them] personally to him. Instead, having blocked the road by occupying the pretext of a contrived toll-gate area, to him who was inquiring, they proclaimed otherwise, in the manner of buying and selling. Understanding this to be more divine than even the divine, following the example of the sacrificers' wives, for those who were resorting to the state of purchasers, devotees who were faithful to the sacrifice-enjoyer — having perceived the full ripening of the deed of the truly-formed doers, and having reckoned the entire price — [they declared:] 'This must be sold!'

children.text:
tatra puṣpāvacaye praṇayinā saha vākovākyam, yathā-
 kā yūyaṃ vana-devatāḥ kurutha kiṃ puṣpāṇi saṃcinmahe
kiṃ nirmāsyatha devatārcanam ato yūyaṃ kathaṃ devatāḥ | tac ca krīḍanam eva naḥ sphuṭam abhūd asmābhir īdṛg-vidhair
aikātmyaṃ va iti prasahya viharan hārī hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||JGc_1,31.33||[44] kadācic ca-
 kā yūyaṃ vana-devatāḥ kurutha kiṃ puṣpāṇi gṛhṇīmahe
rājyaṃ nas tridaśair vihāpitam idaṃ devyo vanasyātra kāḥ | asmaj-jātibhir arpitaṃ yadi tadāpy asmākam uccaiḥ sthitiḥ
syād evaṃ sa-vivādam aṅgaja-raṇaḥ kṛṣṇasya tābhir babhau ||JGc_1,31.34|| [45] kadācic ca kasyāścid dūtyā saha kṛṣṇasya vākovākyam-
children.translated_text:
There, the dialogue with the beloved during the flower-gathering, as follows:
'Who are you?' 'Forest goddesses.' 'What do you do?' 'We gather flowers.'
'What will you make?' 'Deity-worship.' 'Then how are you goddesses?'
'But that is clearly our play!' 'With such ones as us,
is there oneness or not?' — thus, forcibly sporting, may that captivating <s>Hari</s> protect you! ||31.33||
[44] And on another occasion:
'Who are you?' 'Forest goddesses.' 'What do you do?' 'We pick flowers.'
'The kingdom over the celestials has been relinquished by us — and here, what goddesses of the forest?'
'It was offered by those of our own kind — even so, our position is supreme!' —
Thus, with dispute, the battle of Love between <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and them shone forth! ||31.34||
[45] And on another occasion, the dialogue of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with a certain messenger:

children.text:
iyaṃ kā strī strītvaṃ bhavati katham īṣat-padam idaṃ
kim asthāne siddhaṃ tava vacanam asthānakam idam | na kākor udbhūtaṃ bhavati tad aho kākūr iha kā
tad evaṃ dūtī-vāg jayati hariṇākṣyā harim anu ||JGc_1,31.35|| [46] atha gavya-vikraya-vyājataḥ krīḍā-vivādo, yatha-
 kā yūyaṃ kila gavya-vikrayikikā lakṣmīm atītya sthitiṃ
prāptānāṃ na tad asti sambhava-padaṃ yuṣmākam āsāṃ kvacit | mūlyaṃ tām atipatya tasya viditaṃ tasmān na tad-dūṣaṇaṃ
dānaṃ tarhi mamāpi tadvadam idaṃ dattātha ghaṭṭeśituḥ ||JGc_1,31.36|| [47] atha sakhīn prati śrī-kṛṣṇasyādeśaḥ-
 gṛhṇīdhvaṃ pūrvam āsāṃ phalam atula-balād ghaṭṭa-caryā-vighaṭṭaṃ
kartrīṇāṃ tasya cāste vitanuta parito rodanaṃ bodhanaṃ ca | budhyeran yady amūr na sphuṭataram aṭavīkārayā dhārayiṣyāmy
etāḥ kiṃ vā hariṣye svayam atha pihitāḥ samyag anviṣya nīvīḥ ||JGc_1,31.37||[48] tad evam uditvā muditvā ca tat tad ācaritavati tasmin kathaṃcid gṛham āgatya gaty-antareṇa sakhīṣu tat-prakhyāpayantībhir idam api gītam-
 taṃ śṛṇu sad-vidha-mohana-karaṇam | dhvaja-vajrāṅkuśa-lapa-dārpaṇa-bhūruha-punar-aṅkuraṇam ||dhruvam|| gajagati viharati gāyati nṛtyati vādayate ca sa vaṃśam | asmat-paddhatim āvṛṇute' pi ca nāthati ghaṭṭagam aṃśam ||JGc_1,31.38||[49] tad evaṃ naukayā ramaṇam apy avagamanīyam |
children.translated_text:
'Who is this woman?' 'Womanhood is what [she has] become — how?' 'Just this much [I'll say]!'
'What? Is your speech settled in the wrong place?' 'This [speech of yours] is out of place!'
'Is it not born from <s>kākū</s> (intonation)?' 'Well then, what is this <s>kākū</s> here?' —
Thus, the speech of the messenger following the doe-eyed one conquers <s>Hari</s>! ||31.35||
[46] Now, the play-quarrel under the pretext of dairy-product selling, as follows:
'Who are you?' 'Indeed, dairy-product sellers!' 'Of those who have surpassed even <s>Lakṣmī</s> in their state,
there is no place of origin for you anywhere!' 'The price, surpassing her, is well-known for that —
therefore that is no fault!' 'Then a gift to me too — tell me that!' 'You have given [us] the toll-keeper's [toll]!' ||31.36||
[47] Now, Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> command to his friends:
'Seize their fruits first, by incomparable force — a smashing of the toll-gate conduct!
And of those women who did that, spread weeping and awakening all around!
If they do not understand more clearly, I shall hold them in forest-captivity!
Or else I shall steal them myself — then, having properly concealed [them], search out their waist-knots!' ||31.37||
[48] Thus, having spoken and rejoiced, when he had enacted each of those [pastimes], [the <s>gopīs</s>], having somehow come home and by another path proclaiming it to their companions, also sang this:
'Hear about him — the cause of six kinds of enchantment — the one with the marks of flag, thunderbolt, goad, hook, mirror, and tree newly sprouting [on his feet]! ||Refrain|| With an elephant's gait he sports, sings, dances, and plays his flute — he blocks our path and commands the toll-station portion! ||31.38||
[49] Thus, even the pastime with the boat is to be understood.

children.text:
yadā hi kvacid amūś camūru-dṛśas tadīya-saundarya-sārāvalokana-kutuki-dṛśaḥ samūha-vyūham ācarya vihāra-caryayā tam upasadya ca parihāsataḥ parataś caraṇa-caryām ācaranti | tadā caturānana-vimohanaḥ sa ca khalu sahacara-sahasra-visrambha-mahakaraḥ sahacaratayā sarvataḥ parvata-nirjharānekī-bhāvenāvarjya sphuṭam arjyamāna-sukhatayā madhye tāsāṃ vāmatā-yujāṃ mohanāya kūla-mud-rujāṃ durdhyāna-kāraṇāṃ durnivāraṇāṃ sarid-varāṃ pravartayati | pravartya ca puruṣa-dvayadvayasīyam iti vyavasīya-mānatayā tasyāṃ nāvyatayā bhāvyāyāṃ bahula-palāśa-dala-mayīṃ mahā-taraṇiṃ saraṇim anu sakhibhir akhila-maṇiḥ praṇīya karṇa-dhārāyamāṇas tābhir ātara-vitara-vistārādi-kātarābhiḥ praṇaya-maya-nayatayā praṇīta-kalahaṃ bahula-vilāsaṃ
niculitālaṅkāra-kalanāya kalayati |
[50] tad api gītaṃ, yathā-
 saritaṃ nāvaṃ racayati ca drutamasmākaṃ pathi tasyām | ārohayate pārayituṃ naḥ spṛśati miṣādapi yasyām ||JGc_1,31.39|| [50] tābhir evātra ślokitaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text:
When indeed, somewhere, those army-thighed, doe-eyed women — whose eyes were curious to behold the essence of his beauty — having arranged themselves in a group-formation and approaching him through the course of play, jestingly performed the attendance of his feet from the farther side — then he, the bewilderer of the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, accompanied by a thousand companions with the intimacy of great trust, with his quality of companionship, having drawn them from all sides like mountain-torrents becoming manifold, and with happiness being clearly earned — set in motion among those women who were joined with coyness, that excellent river which was enchanting, which broke the embankments, which was the cause of difficult meditation, and which was impossible to restrain. And having set it in motion, deeming it to be 'for every two persons' — in that [river] which was to be regarded as navigable — he fashioned a great vessel made of abundant <s>palāśa</s> leaves, and, piloted along the course [of the stream] by his friends, the jewel of all, he — while being steered — with those women who were anxious about the crossing, the ferrying, the breadth, and the like — through the conduct of love-filled governance, creating a lovingly-fashioned quarrel and abundant play, arranged the art of ornament-adjusting beneath the clothing.
[50] And that too was sung, as follows:
'He creates the river, and swiftly fashions a boat on our path within it; | he makes us board it to ferry [us] across — and in it, touches [us] even under a pretext!' || (JGc 1,31.39)
[50] And this was versified by those very [gopīs], as follows:

children.text: ārohāya vidhāya saṃstaramilatparyakstavaṃ tadvacaḥ- sāhāyyaṃ viracayya naḥ sakhi nadīmadhyaṃ yadā jagmivān | vṛṇvan durvitaraṃ tadātarapaṇaṃ viṣkabhya naukāṃ na kāṃ cakre vakrakalākalāpakalanāṃ cakrāṅkapāṇiḥ sa tu ||JGc_1,31.40||[53] tad evaṃ sākṣāt-kṛta-manoratha-tatiḥ samabhīpsita-gṛha-gatiḥ sakhibhiś carita-jalpaḥ punaḥ snānādi-racitākalpas tatraiva ca kutracana taṭinī-taṭe kadāpi yamunā-nikaṭe payaḥ-pāyanāya saṃkaṭitāṃ go-ghaṭāṃ ghaṭayan kramaśaś ca gaṇanayā gaṇaśaḥ prakaṭayaṃs tan-manana-caritārthatayā jagau |
children.translated_text:
'Having arranged a couch-bed that meets the requirements for boarding, making his speech | an aid, O friend, when he had gone to the middle of the river — | concealing the difficult-to-cross ferry, blocking the boat — what crooked art-cluster-arrangement | did that disc-marked-handed one not perform?' || (JGc 1,31.40)
[53] Thus, with his train of desires fulfilled, proceeding toward the desired home-path, having chatted with his friends, again adorned with the arrangement of bathing and the like — right there, somewhere on a riverbank, at some time near the <s>Yamunā</s>, assembling the herd of cows crowded together for the purpose of milk-watering, and gradually displaying them group by group with counting — he sang, having fulfilled the purpose of contemplating them.

children.text:
tac ca tābhir anupaṭhitaṃ, yathā-
maṇi-mālā-kṛta-go-gaṇa-gaṇanā-pūraṇam anu sānandam | praṇayitarāṃsaga-bhujam udgāna-hṛta-hariṇīkam amandam ||kṛṣṇaṃ kalayata mohana-mantragam eṇīm eṇī-nayanām | na yadi tadā katham ubhaya-vyaktiṃ vīkṣe tad apṛthag-ayanām ||JGc_1,31.41|| iti |
[55] tataś cetas tataḥ sakhibhir akhilaiḥ praṇītānītāmanda-makaranda-sundara-kunda-dāmabhir mukundaḥ kṛtālaṅkṛtir yathā nijahāra | śreṇīkṛta-go-samāhṛtir yathā cāsasāra | tathā varṇitam | kintu tad-vilambataḥ kātarya-paryākulāyāḥ śrī-vrajeśvaryāḥ sabhāgatatayā svabhāva-gopanayā | tathā hi-
 āgatam iva harim aciram | kalayata suhṛdāṃ dayayā yad asau nagam api dadhre suciram ||dhruvam|| kunda-srag-avita-kautuka-veśaṃ go-gopair viharantam | mṛdu-mṛdu-marud-anuvījitam anu lavam akhila-manāṃsi harantam ||sura-vandibhir abhivanditam avahita-tat-kṛta-nartana-vādyam | muni-samudaya-nuti-guṇitaṃ guṇitā-nipuṇaṃ jagad abhivādyam ||atha go-dhana-gaṇam anu samam anugais tad-varṇita-garimāṇam | śrama-kāntibhir api sukha-kāriṇam ita-veṇu-kalā-varimāṇam ||khura-reṇu-pluta-mālya-mano-haram īṣad-ghūrṇita-nayanam | etaṃ paśyata nija-jana-mānadam īpsita-gavyānayanam ||kuṇḍala-lakṣmī-bhṛta-pāṇḍu-dyuti-gaṇḍaṃ gaja-pati-khelam | kṣaṇadā-pativat pramuditam uditaṃ prāgadhi-sandhyā-velam ||JGc_1,31.42|| iti |
 [56] atha vaiṣṇavaṃ vārāham api purāṇam anusṛtya gaty-antaraṃ pratyāyayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text:
And that was recited along by those [gopīs], as follows:
'After completing the counting of the cow-herds, [done] by a jewel-rosary, joyfully — | with the arm of the more-affectionate-companion upon his shoulder, with the fawn-group enchanted by his singing, with great vigor —' || 'Behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who has entered the enchantment-<s>mantra</s>! [Behold] the doe-eyed one with doe-eyes! | If not, then how do I see that dual manifestation as having an undivided course?' || (JGc 1,31.41) — thus.
[55] Then, from there, by all the friends, <s>Mukunda</s> — adorned with beautiful <s>kunda</s>-flower garlands, rich in abundant nectar, arranged and brought — was thus bedecked, and as he pleased, he departed. And as the cow-herd-gathering was arranged in rows — thus it was described. But from the anxiety born of his delay, to the greatly agitated queen of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>, [the description came] in an assembly-appearance, by the nature of her disposition:
'That <s>Hari</s> has arrived, it seems, just now — | behold, by the compassion of his dear ones, he sustained even the mountain for a long time!' || [refrain] || 'Behold him in the costume of curiosity, adorned with <s>kunda</s>-garland — playing with cows and cowherds! | Gently, gently fanned by the breeze, stealing all minds even for a moment!' || 'Worshipped by the celestial bards, attentive to the dance and music arranged by them! | Praised by the multitude of sages, skilled among the skilled, to be honored by the world!' || 'Then, together with the cow-herds, with his greatness described by his attendants! | Producing happiness even through his weariness-beauties, with the measured art of the flute departed!' || 'Enchanting in appearance, bearing a garland of cow-hoof dust — with slightly rolling eyes! | Behold this one who gives honor to his own people, bringing the desired cow-products!' || 'Bearing the radiance of a pale glow from the <s>kuṇḍala</s>-jewel beauty upon his cheek, sporting like the lord of elephants! | Delighted like the lord of the night (moon), having risen at the pre-twilight hour!' || (JGc 1,31.42) — thus.
[56] Now, following even the <s>Vaiṣṇava Vārāha Purāṇa</s>, we shall present an alternative course:

children.text:
evaṃ samayana-samayānavalokataḥ samayākaraṇāya tad-varṇanāvagāha-rocanāsu karṇajāha-vilocanāsu cetasi racita-tadīya-śocanaḥ śrī-kamala-locanaḥ samāgamya yathā-yatham avitatha-ramya-sukha-dhārayā sarvaṃ sukhākurvann api tāsāṃ viraha-dahana-jvālā-viśeṣāvaśeṣa-santapta-bhaṅgurāpāṅga-pātra-sapatra-kṛtas tad apasāraṇāya muralī-kalī-kalayā go-dhanālaya-govardhanācalayor antarāle tā evānanya-gatitayā saṃkalayya nirvṛtiṃ parikalayya ca vasanta-santata-rāsāya yukti-mukti-viṣayāṃ saṃvalayya tāsām āśāsānānām āśāṃ dadamānaḥ sva-vrajataḥ pragarjad-ariṣṭa-kṛtāriṣṭa-kaṣṭataḥ prakaṭam ākruṣṭaṃ śrutavān | śruta-mātre ca tatra nija-nija-vartmanā tābhiḥ saha sahasā vrajam āvavrāja | tad-anantaraṃ tu vṛttaṃ pūrvam
eva vṛttam asti | tatremāṃ gāthāṃ prathayanti-
 gatasya rāsa-vikrīḍām āgatasya vṛṣāsuram | devair na dṛṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇasya sambhramaḥ kim uta śramaḥ ||JGc_1,31.43|| [58] yadā khalu riṣṭaḥ so' yam ariṣṭas tadāpi tad-ariṇā hariṇā nijāviṣṭatā nāpakṛṣtā | vīryasya bahu-vikīryamāṇatām avāptāsya paryāpta-viṣayatāṃ so' yam anāsīdan diti-sūnur āsīditi |
[59] anapakṛṣṭāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ saraṅga-bhūtāgas tat-saṅgamataḥ sāgaska iva pārṣṇi-prahārāl lambhita-vidaratayā vibhāgam āgamitaḥ | ya eva vibhāgas tīrthatāṃ samarthayan nikhila-puruṣārthaṃ pratyavyarthatām āsasāda |
children.translated_text:
Thus, the lotus-eyed <s>Śrī Hari</s>, observing at every moment the season and its time, for the sake of making the time [propitious] — upon those ear-born, eye-possessing [women] whose hearts were engaged in the delight of immersing in the description of him, whose hearts were fashioned with lamentation for him — having arrived as was fitting, though making everything happy with the stream of truly delightful joy, and being made leaf-companioned (<s>sapatra</s>) by the sidelong-glance vessels of those [women] remaining scorched by the residual flames of the fire of separation — for the purpose of dispelling that [sorrow], through the art-melody of the flute, having assembled those very [gopīs] — who had no other refuge — between the cow-settlement and <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, and having fashioned their bliss and arranged the means of skill and liberation for the spring-continuous <s>rāsa</s>, granting the hope of those who were hoping — he, from his own <s>Vraja</s>, heard clearly the ominous cry produced by the calamity wrought by <s>Ariṣṭa</s>. And at the mere hearing, together with those [gopīs], by their own respective paths, he swiftly returned to <s>Vraja</s>. What happened thereafter has already been narrated before. Here they proclaim this verse:
'Of him who went to the <s>rāsa</s> sport and [then] arrived at the bull-demon (<s>Vṛṣāsura</s>) — | neither haste nor fatigue of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was seen by the gods — what then [to say of mere mortals]?' || (JGc 1,31.43)
[58] When indeed this <s>Ariṣṭa</s> was destroyed (<s>riṣṭa</s>), even then <s>Hari</s>, the enemy of that [demon], did not withdraw his own absorption [in play]. Though the valor was being widely scattered, that son of <s>Diti</s> did not approach [any closer to] the sphere of adequacy — [this is because] he was a son of <s>Diti</s> indeed.
[59] And when that [absorption] had not been withdrawn, the one whose body had become a field of sin, by the contact with him — as if guilty — received his division through the blow of a hoof-strike, having obtained the splitting [of the earth]. That very division, authenticating its <s>tīrtha</s>-hood (sacred pilgrimage status), attained the unfailingness of [conferring] all the goals of human life.

children.text:
yatra ca śrī-harir iyaṃ svayam akhilaiḥ sakhibhir majjan sajjanānām ācāraṃ pracārayāmāsa | pātālān mahā-tīrtham idaṃ samutthitam itītthaṃ vyajya nimajjya samunmajjya bahu visarjya ca sarva-vraja-janatayā janita-śarmā gīti-ripu-vijaya-karmā vrajam evāvavrāja |
 [61] āvrajya ca śrī-vraja-rājādīn praṇaya-vinayābhyāṃ susabhājya viśramaṇa-vyājataḥ śayyā-gṛham āsajya saṅketita-veṇu-saṃkvaṇitena paramānurāga-sāgaraḥ sarvataḥ śreyasīr amūḥ preyasīḥ pūrva-kṛta-vraja-vraja-bāhya-vibhāga-mayyāṃ mahyāṃ saṃkalayya kenāpy avayajyatayā punar api rāsāyāsāditavān | tatra ca-
 rādhayāsvāditā yāsīn mādhurī mādhavādhare | saivānubhūtā muralī-kalī-khuralikām anu ||JGc_1,31.44||tatraiva ca-
abhisāre calacelā vraja-tanvīnāṃ tatī ruruce | api kiṃ vijaya-patākā dadhire' naṅgasya saṅgatiḥ ||JGc_1,31.45||
children.translated_text:
And there, <s>Śrī Hari</s> himself, bathing with all his friends, propagated the conduct of the virtuous. 'This great <s>tīrtha</s> has arisen from the netherworld!' — having thus proclaimed, plunging in, emerging, and lavishly performing [ablutions] — generating happiness for all the people of <s>Vraja</s>, and with the deeds of the song of victory over the enemy — he returned to <s>Vraja</s> itself.
[61] And having returned, having honored the king of <s>Śrī Vraja</s> and others with the affection and modesty befitting [them], under the pretext of rest, having reached the bed-chamber, and with the flute-signal of the arranged rendezvous — the supreme ocean of passion, assembling all those beloved ones who were his supreme beloveds from every direction — who had no other refuge — on the great earth that consisted of the division between the outer environs of <s>Vraja</s> and [the region] beyond <s>Vraja</s> as previously arranged, and having fashioned their bliss, and with some means of inexplicable release — he brought them again to the <s>rāsa</s>. And there:
'The sweetness that was savored by <s>Rādhā</s> on <s>Mādhava's</s> lip — | that very [sweetness] was experienced following the art-melody of the flute!' || (JGc 1,31.44)
And there too:
'The restless-hemmed row of slender-bodied <s>Vraja</s>-women setting out for the tryst shone forth; | were they the victory-banners of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Love-god) | that they bore as his entourage?' || (JGc 1,31.45)

children.text: yatra ca pathi prathama-labdha-nirgamayā parama-ramayā nikhila-kalitārādhayā rādhayā samam ekāntataḥ kāntasya narma mahadeva śarma pupoṣa |
children.translated_text: And on the path, where his supreme delight (<s>Ramā</s>), first-obtained in departure, the one worshipped by all — <s>Rādhā</s> — was with him, the jest of the beloved in their solitude fostered great happiness indeed.

children.text: yadā hi cintā-santāpa-tānta-svāntā sā kāntā tādṛśa-vipattim uttīrṇaṃ taṃ kāntaṃ rahaḥ saṃhitavatī tadā lajjā-maryādām apy asajjantī pariṣvajya vyajyamāna-stambha-mukha-sāttvika-sambhavā ciraṃ vicāra-rahitatām ācarati sma |
children.translated_text: When indeed she — that beloved whose inner heart was worn out by the anguish of anxiety — had encountered in private that beloved who had crossed beyond such calamity, then, abandoning even the boundary of modesty, embracing him — she who was endowed with the <s>sāttvika</s>-manifestations arising from the <s>stambha</s> (paralysis) on her face — for a long time enacted the state of being devoid of deliberation.

children.text:
sa ca tathaiva tām anucarati sma |
 [65] tataś ca sakhībhiḥ kathaṃcana sāntvitayoḥ kāntayoḥ kāntas tu sva-nirmitaṃ tat-kuṇḍaṃ tāsāṃ dṛṣṭi-kirmīritaṃ nirmimāṇaḥ sanarma kāntāṃ vyājahāra |
 [66] paśya paśya mama kamalākaro' yaṃ sāgara iva girirājam āsajya kamalodbhavaṃ bhāvayitā | sudhākara ivaika-deśa-sthityāpi nija-rucibhiḥ kumuda-vanaṃ vikāsayitā | dambholi-pāṇir iva sa-dambholitayā vilāsī | ambhoja-janir iva bhuvana-visarjanena prabhāsī | tripura-jiṣṇur iva saha-sāgara-māna-śamanaḥ | śrīmān viṣṇur iva paramahaṃsa-cakrāśrayatā-kamanaḥ | śrī-rāma iva rohiṇī-sukha-saṃcārī | kiṃ bahunā, śrī-rāmānuja iva ca śiṣṭa-kaṣṭa-prada-pāpāriṣṭa-hārī | tad etan mayā khalu kṛta-sukṛta-prasaraṃ sara idam aciraṃ viracayya caritārthatā labdhā | bhavatyā tu nedṛśa-naipuṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ kṛtam iti guṇy-anuguṇatā katham āpsyate ?
 [67] atha tasyāḥ savayasas tv idaṃ parihasanti sma-[68] na vayaṃ vṛṣaghnatā-nighnatayā vighnam āptāḥ | yena prāyaścittata iva lokasya prāyaścittam ārādhayāmaḥ |
[69] kṛṣṇaḥ sahāsam āha sma-na khalv asau vṛṣaḥ | kiṃ tu vṛṣa-virodhī vṛṣatā-miṣavān asuraḥ | tasmāt tat-pakṣapātitayā bhavatīnām eva vṛṣaghnatā paryavasyatīti bhavatīnām eva niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtir viṣayatām arhati |
children.translated_text:
And he too followed her in exactly the same way.
[65] Then, when the two beloveds had been somehow consoled by the friends, the beloved one, fashioning before their eyes that lake created by himself — while playfully addressing the beloved, said:
[66] 'Look, look! This lotus-lake of mine — like an ocean, having attached itself to the king of mountains — will nurture the lotus-born! Like the nectar-bearing moon, even from a single locale, it will cause the <s>kumuda</s>-forest to blossom through its own rays! Like the wielder of the thunderbolt (<s>Indra</s>), it will sport with the splendor of its own thunderbolt! Like the lotus-born one (<s>Brahmā</s>), it will shine by the projection of worlds! Like the conqueror of the three cities (<s>Śiva</s>), it will quell pride together with the ocean! Like the glorious <s>Viṣṇu</s>, it will delight in the resort of the <s>paramahaṃsa</s>-circle! Like <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, it will convey happiness to <s>Rohiṇī</s>! In short — like the younger brother of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself), it will remove the calamity-giving evil afflicting the good! Thus, this lake, fashioned by the spread of my own merit, has been quickly created, and fulfillment has been obtained by me. But has your honor performed such meritorious skillfulness?'
[67] Then, her companions mocked [him] thus: [68] 'We have not incurred the sin of bull-slaying! For which reason, as if an atonement for the world, we should worship an atonement!'
[69] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a laugh: 'Indeed, that was no [real] bull! Rather, it was a demon with the disguise of a bull, opposed to <s>dharma</s> (<s>vṛṣa</s>). Therefore, by partiality toward him, the bull-slaying devolves upon your honors yourselves — and so it is your honors' own atonement that merits being made the subject!'

children.text:
tatra ca prajākṛtaṃ rājanīti rājanīti-nyāyena bhavadīya-rājāyamānāyām asyām eva sā jāyamānā syād ity asāv eva tatra pradhānatayāvadhīyate |
 [71] sakhya ūcuḥ-bhavatu, tathāpi yathā-katham api bhavat-prasaṅgata eva saṅgataḥ khalv ayaṃ doṣa iti tan-moṣa-kṛte bhavat-kṛtam evānukartavyam |
children.translated_text:
And there, by the maxim 'what the subjects do is [attributed to] the king,' since it would arise in her who reigns supreme over your honors — that very [atonement] is established, and she alone is principally to be attended to.
[71] The friends said: 'Be it so; nevertheless, this fault is connected only through your involvement — therefore, for its removal, what you yourself have done must be followed [by us].'

children.text: yā khalu bhavan-maṅgalataḥ sarasī-bhūtāyāḥ savayasaḥ sarasī bhavitā sā punar amara-taraṅginīva kṛṣṇāṅga-rāga-vilāsinī | amṛta-nidhi-priyāvalir iva bahula-tārāṅgatā-bhāsinī | sūtrāma-gṛha-netrīvopendra-deva-ratāmodātirekiṇī | sāvitrī-mukha-vicitra-śrutir iva nālīkinī | umā-mūrtir iva giri-rājād udbhava-dhātrī | māmūrtir iva hari-hṛdi vilāsa-pātrī | rāma-śaktir iva gāmbhīryataḥ pralambamāna-mada-majjanī | kiṃ bahunā, rādheva rādhāntika-pūrṇa-vidhor vaśatā-sajjanīti |
children.translated_text: 'And the lake of your companion, which will come into being from your auspiciousness, will be like the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> — sporting with the hue of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> body! Like the garland of the beloved of the nectar-ocean (the moon) — shining with the abundant star-like wave-motions! Like the cord of <s>Indra's</s> domestic guide — exceeding the delight of devotion to the <s>Upendra</s>-deity! Like the hearing adorned by the face of <s>Sāvitrī</s> — a lotus-pond! Like the form of <s>Umā</s> — a mother born from the king of mountains! Like the form of <s>Māyā</s> — a vessel of sport in <s>Hari's</s> heart! Like the power of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — submerging the intoxication of depth-plumbing! In short — like <s>Rādhā</s> herself — the producer of the subjection of the full moon near <s>Rādhā</s>!'

Then <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, with longing, gently lifting <s>Rādhā's</s> chin with his hand, spoke this with a charming smile:
'If that face [of hers] is [called] the moon, and the art of her smile its radiance — then gloryless | are they, a sham — and if those are the stars, curse [them], and if those eyes [are compared to] <s>cakora</s> birds — enough! | Thus, the words of contempt toward her own retinue from all people — | hearing them as extolling your excellence, O <s>Rādhā</s>, [my heart] repeatedly withers in the heart!' || (JGc 1,31.46)
[74] Then, having moved forward and by stages, having met with all the women of every path — the travelers of all roads — whose every limb was trembling — and with all of them together, on a moon-banished-darkness night, together with the mountain, following the mountain-king, in a forest shining with the king of seasons (spring) — he brought forth a <s>rāsa</s> of even greater play than all [previous ones], spread in every direction.

This <s>rāsa</s>-festival too, as follows:
'When the <s>rāsa</s> took place formerly following autumn, then
it had, from its very commencement, celestial musical accompaniment and the like;
but when others composed [rāsas] subsequently, then — the conqueror of all —
he fashioned that [<s>rāsa</s>], worthy of the great concert, with <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>, and others!' ||31.51||

on the lovely <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, he stood, eager for the <s>rasa</s> of the <s>rāsa</s>!' ||31.56||

children.text: atha tad-vasanta-rāsa-vilāsa-rajanyāḥ prātar eva sakhībhir agaṇyābhiḥ kṛtārādhayā tadīya-sāhāyaka-saṃbādhayā śrī-rādhayā sva-kara-kamala-kalite lalite sarva-sukhaṃ valayitum ullale tasmin pallale tayoḥ kāntayor alam eva sukha-parimalaḥ samullalāsa | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Then, on the very morning after that spring <s>rāsa</s> sport-night, when Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, attended by innumerable companions, supported by the throng of her attendants, had been duly worshipped — at that pool (<s>kuṇḍa</s>), grasped by the lotus-hands of <s>Lalitā</s>, swelling to encompass all happiness for the two beautiful lovers, the fragrance of supreme happiness abundantly blossomed. For thus:

children.text: kadācit kuṇḍasyāmbhasi viharate karhy api bahiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Sometimes he sports in the waters of the <s>kuṇḍa</s>, sometimes outside,

children.text: kadāpy antaḥ-kuñje kvacana-samaye rāsa-valaye |
children.translated_text: sometimes in an inner bower, sometimes in the <s>rāsa</s> circle —

children.text: samaṃ rādhā-devyā harir akhila-sakhyāli-sukhadaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, together with <s>Rādhā</s> the goddess, giving happiness to all the companions' companies —

children.text: purā tat tan nityaṃ smarayati mano naḥ svam abhitaḥ ||JGc_1,31.57||
children.translated_text: my mind constantly recalls each of those [pastimes] of old, on all sides!' ||31.57||

sarva-gopīṣu saivaikā viṣṇor atyanta-vallabhā ||iti |
punaḥ smṛtim abhinīya samāpanaṃ padyaṃ nijagāda-
children.translated_text: Again, having drawn forth the remembrance, he proclaimed the concluding verse:

children.text:
anyo' nyaṃ milana-spṛhā-milanam apy asyāhatir dānavād yasmāt tad-dhitarātta-narma-milanaṃ kuṇḍa-dvayasya kriyā |
sarvāsām adhi madhyam ujjvalatayā rāsāntarāla-sthitiḥ śrī-rādhā-jitayor mano mama manāg adyāpi naivojjhati ||JGc_1,31.58||[85] iti vaivaśya-pāravaśyam āsīdan sīdann iva mūrccham ṛcchan snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sarvān eva ca tat-tad-bhava-bhavanān bhāvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text:
'The mutual meeting-desire-and-meeting, and also the blow from the demon against that —
the playful meeting obtained from the benefit of that [demon's attack], and the creation of the pair of <s>kuṇḍas</s>;
the position within the innermost <s>rāsa</s> circle, with supremely radiant intensity, amidst all —
the mind of Śrī <s>Rādhā's</s> conquered pair does not even slightly abandon me even now!' ||31.58||
[85] Thus, attaining the state of being helplessly overwhelmed, sinking as if swooning, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> caused all indeed to dwell in the abodes of those respective emotional states.

children.text:
tac ca yuktaṃ, yathā-
atipūrvaṃ yad apūrvaṃ nija-matir
durlabham atīva hṛdyaṃ ca | vṛttaṃ tat pratinavatāṃ prayāti
bhūyo' nubhūyamānaṃ ca ||JGc_1,31.59||[87] tad etad varṇayitvā snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ samāpanam āha sma-
 rādhe tvad-vallabhaḥ satyaṃ sarvair api sudurlabhaḥ | sulabho' py adhunā yo' yaṃ bhavatyā manyate' nyathā ||JGc_1,31.60||[88] atha kathaṃcid api jāta-sāntvane tan-manasāṃ tv aneka-vikāre pāre manoratha-patham akhila-śobhā-śubha-pathya-nepathya-sāratanya-māna-dānatas tau sūta-kumārāv ārādhayāmāsur āśu rādhā-ramaṇa-prabhṛtayaḥ kṛta-sādhāraṇātikrama-prakṛtayaḥ sadaḥ-sadaḥ-sadayatayā śubhāśīrbhir abhyudayam āsādayāmāsuś ca | tataś ca pūrva-pūrvavad eva sarve svadhāma samāsannāḥ svapnataś ca tat-tad-anubhavantaś carita-jāgarā iva vāsarādim āsāditavantaḥ |
children.translated_text:
And that was fitting, as follows:
'That which was supremely ancient, unprecedented, found by one's own mind,
most difficult to attain and exceedingly heart-delighting —
that event, attaining ever-renewed freshness,
even when re-experienced, proceeds further [in intensity]!' ||31.59||
[87] Having described this, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke the conclusion:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>, your beloved — truly difficult to attain for all —
though easily attained even now by you, is considered otherwise [by you]!' ||31.60||
[88] Then, when their minds had been somehow pacified yet remained in manifold agitation, those [narrators] — <s>Rādhā's</s> beloved's devotees and the like, whose natures had transcended ordinary propriety — beyond the path of desire, through the bestowal of supreme honor, the all-beautifying auspicious theatrical costume — quickly gratified those two sons of the bard (<s>sūta</s>). And the assembly members, with benevolent blessings, attained prosperity. Then, just as before, all reached their own homes and, experiencing those [events] even in sleep, as if with wakefulness that had already been lived, arrived at the beginning of the [next] day.

Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the thirty-first <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Marvel of Diverse-Colored Conduct'
||31||

children.text:
atha dvātriṃśaṃ pūraṇam
 keśi-dhvaṃsana-śaṃsanaṃ
 [1] atha punaḥ prātaḥ-kathāṃ yathāvat prathayiṣyāmaḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text:
Now, the thirty-second <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter)
'The Proclamation of the Destruction of <s>Keśī</s>'
[1] Now, we shall duly set forth the morning narrative again, as follows:

children.text: madhukaṇṭhaḥ prathamataḥ kaṇṭha-ravam akṛtvā manasi nirṇiktam idaṃ viviktavān-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, first, without making a throat-sound, disclosed this thought, purified within his mind:

children.text: etad-anantaraṃ yadyapi ye khalv asmāsu bālyād eva stuhi-kṛṣṇatāṃ gatās teṣāṃ bhagaval-līlā-sukha-varṣi-devarṣi-vara-caraṇānāṃ kaṃsaṃ prati śaṃsanaṃ śaṃsanīyatām āsannam |
children.translated_text: 'Immediately after this, although for those among us who from childhood onward have attained the state of " praising <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" — for those blessed feet of the chief of divine sages who rain the bliss of the Lord's pastimes — the reporting to <s>Kaṃsa</s> is approaching as something to be proclaimed.'

children.text:
tathāpi bhagaval-līlādhikṛtim anuvartamānānāṃ sarvadopākurvāṇānāṃ na tūdākurvāṇānāṃ teṣāṃ tatraucitīm apy anaucitīṃ citī-kurvanty avipaścita iti tathaivaiṣāṃ parama-vipaścitām api vraja-vāsināṃ viniścita-nija-prema-jātīya-lasad-advitīya-sukha-prakarṣāṇāṃ nātiharṣāya syād iti cānirṇeya-vaktra-nāmnā tad-āmnātavyam iti | [5] atha sāpalāpaṃ spaṣṭam abhyācaṣṭa-
 [6] śrī-hariṇāriṣṭe vidviṣṭe kliṣṭena ca kaṃsena varṣaṃ yāvan na kaścit prasthāpitaḥ | keśī ca gacchan punaḥ sva-veśma praveśitaḥ | vṛthā vairaṃ mā kṛthā iti | [7] atha mukhya-māgha-kṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ kaścid diviṣṭhaḥ sārvadika-jñāna-mahiṣṭhas taṃ prati pratikūla eva sann anukūla iva śrī-vasudevasya rahasyaṃ vṛttam anuvṛttaṃ cakāra yena khalu rāma-kṛṣṇāv api vasudeva-sutatayodāya-sātām | [8] tataś ca tat-kṛta-pratirodhād dhantum aśakyatayā vasudeva-devakyau punar maṅkṣu loha-śṛṅkhalayā kārāgāre kruddhena satā satāṃ viruddhena tena niruddhe |
[9] nirudhya cārva-matinārva-dānavaḥ samāhūya bhūyaś ca niyuktaḥ | niyukta-mātraś cāyaṃ vrajāya kṛta-yātraḥ prātar eva tatrāyātaḥ | vrajaś cāriṣṭa-vadhād adhastān nandiśvara-girim ārabhya para-parastāt kṛta-vāsa iti dūrata eva taṃ labdhavān | [10] yatra ca sa prakharatara-khara-khura-ghṛṣṭi-cchinna-kṣoṇi-pṛṣṭhatayā goṣṭham āgacchan saṭāghaṭāmudasya nabhasy abhibhramayan bhreṣa-vaśād adabhra-bhayādabhra-pracchannatayā tat-tad-vṛtta-māṣa-cchatāṃ vimāna-paricchadānāṃ vimānān ucchādayāmāsa pūrva-pūrvamānān iva | yata eva nirjarāś ca te sphūrjad-ūrjasvalatā-varjanataḥ sa-jarā iva jātāḥ | [11] tataś ca jaṅghālagatilaṅghitāṅghripaḥ sa punarakharvagarvataḥ sarvameva dhunvannarvadānavaḥ siṃhasaṃhatiriva ghargharitanirghoṣamātatāna
|
[12] ātate ca nirghoṣe samyag-argalita-mahārgalāvarga-durghaṭṭa-vikaṭa-kaṇṭaka-kavāṭa-durghaṭa-nirgama-maty-udagra-durgāyamāṇa-gariṣṭha-goṣṭha-viśaṅkaṭa-kuṭha-śākhāvṛti-saṅghaṃ saṅghaśaḥ samullaṅghitavatyaḥ sāsnāvatyaḥ pluta-gatyā sodbhramaṃ sapady aṭavīṃ praty eva ca drutaṃ paridrutavatyaḥ | [13] tad agaṇayann eva goṣṭhasyopaśalyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ paritaś ca ghoṭamānaḥ sa deva-dviḍ-ghoṭakas tu tamariṣṭa-moṭakam eva dhorita-rīti-gaty-anviṣṭavān | [14] atha gavāṃ dravācchokāviṣṭāḥ praṣṭhagoṣṭhapativiśiṣṭāḥ sarva eva gomino lokā nijānyokāṃsi jhagiti samujjhantastadabhimukhameva paramunmukhatayā cakrumuḥ |
children.translated_text:
'Nevertheless, those who are constantly following the domain of the Lord's pastimes and are always sub-serving [them] rather than creating [their own agenda] — the undiscerning ones deem even their propriety as impropriety! And thus, for these supremely discerning <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers too — who are resplendent in the unmatched happiness of their own determined love of the purest kind — it would not lead to excessive delight' — thus, by the one named <s>Anirṇeya-vaktra</s> (Indeterminate-face), it is to be narrated accordingly.
[5] Then, with lamentation, he spoke plainly:
[6] 'When <s>Ariṣṭa</s> had been hated and destroyed by Śrī <s>Hari</s>, for an entire year, no one was dispatched by the afflicted <s>Kaṃsa</s>. And <s>Keśī</s>, while departing, was again made to enter his own home: "Do not wage enmity in vain!" [7] Then, on the dark <s>Ekādaśī</s> of the chief <s>Māgha</s> month, a certain celestial being — supremely knowledgeable of universal matters — though actually opposed to him [<s>Kaṃsa</s>], as if favorably [disposed], performed the secret past and continuing report of the glorious <s>Vasudeva</s>, whereby indeed <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> were proclaimed as sons of <s>Vasudeva</s>. [8] And then, from the obstruction created by him, unable to kill [them], <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s> were again immediately imprisoned in iron chains by that enraged one, the opposer of the righteous.
[9] And having imprisoned [them], the evil-minded demon summoned the one of beautiful intellect [<s>Keśī</s>] and again assigned [him]. And this one, barely assigned, having prepared his journey to <s>Vraja</s>, arrived there the very next morning. And <s>Vraja</s>, [which] from the slaying of <s>Ariṣṭa</s> onward had made its abode extending from beneath <s>Nandiśvara</s> hill to the farthest beyond — thus he found it from a distance. [10] Where, by the sharply scraping, harsh, hard hooves, the back of the earth being severed as he came to the settlement, shaking the manes with their clumps, whirling [things] into the sky, from the force of his snorting, with immense fearfulness and immense concealment, he scattered the awnings and canopy-accessories of the dwellings — knocking them about like prior dignities. Whereby even the immortals, from the abandonment of their manifest vehement strength, became as if aged. [11] And then, he of the swift-legged galloping gait, from his immense, undwarfed pride, shaking everything — that non-dwarf demon — stretched out a thundering roar like a host of lions.
[12] And when that roar was stretched out — the cows, with their massive, firmly bolted, great-barred, formidable, thorny, gate-shuttered, hard-to-exit, greatly fortified cow-pen, whose fearsome thorny branch-fence enclosures were leapt over en masse by the groups of dewlapped ones (cows), [who] with bounding gait, bewildered, swiftly ran straight toward the wilderness! [13] Disregarding even that, having entered the outskirts of the settlement and bellowing all around — that demon-horse sought out that very <s>Ariṣṭa</s>-crusher through the course of a guided gait. [14] Then, all the cattle-owning people, grief-stricken from the stampede of the cows, foremost among whom was the chief of the cattle-settlement, each suddenly abandoning their respective dwellings, rushing face-forward toward that very one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] with supreme eagerness, cried out.

yugapad aririṣatīva cikariṣatīva jigariṣatīva ca tasmiṃs tad-asahamānaḥ sahasā siṃha-nādaṃ bṛṃhayan siṃha-saṃhananaḥ sa ca kṛṣṇas taṃ dhṛṣṇajam abhisāgraham abhigraham eva jagrāha | samagra eva vrajaś ca vyagratayā tad-anugatim iti sthite sa tu tat paśyann utteritākhyayā gatyā tam eva roṣāda-mandam abhyavacaskanda, yatra-
 vyoma so' yam atiyan nirāplavat

kārṣṇo bāhur nirgataḥ prāghuṇābhaḥ | gehaṃ tac ca svāminaṃ taṃ vinābhūt

children.translated_text:
Having surpassed even all of them, going forward with proper impetuosity, performing the deeds of a mighty warrior, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), surpassing even <s>Rāma</s>, was marveled at for his confrontational valor. [16] Then the leaders of the <s>Vraja</s> people, having become utterly agitated, discouraging him as he advanced, declared this:
'This horse has a body-hair array [hard as] thunderbolts, is a conqueror of <s>Vajrī</s> (<s>Indra</s>), his path forsaken by the gods who flee from the roar of his own sound! You are comparable to a fresh <s>tāpiñcha</s> (dark tamāla) tree of shadow-like luminance — therefore, do not go swiftly before him, before his very face!' // [śikharinī]
[17] Thus, when this extreme danger was imminent, there was this dispute between mother and son:
'Son, where do you go?' 'I perceive a horse, mother — this one is indeed of exceedingly wicked resolve!' 'What will he do to us?' 'That one has lost his own sweet disposition — go home! Am I unconscious?' // [vasantatilakā]
[18] And then she, her boldness generated from agitation, addressed even the lord of the settlement with tears:
'By me, out of childishness, never have strong words been directed at you, O master of the house; but today, I wish to make [something] manifest — hear this! Why do you not, together with all [men], seize the child at once? And why do the others too not come against the horse, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>?' // [śikharinī]
[19] But the younger brother of Śrī <s>Rāma</s>, who had rendered even <s>Diti's</s> sons like <s>Diti</s> (i.e., destroyed them) — though disrespected from the start — having heard this being described, laughing, having reassured his mother, the bestower of happiness that is the foundation of the entire world's trust, having observed that one (<s>Keśī</s>) for a moment with a penetrating glance, challenged him to come near. [20] And he (<s>Keśī</s>), summoned by the enemy of <s>Pūtanā</s>, though inwardly overcome by his radiance, considering himself valiant, undaunted by him, at first, for the gradual deployment of his own prowess, striding with a slowness following a retrograde course, cleared for him the ground as far as the <s>Yamunā</s>. But reckoning that his own attack from a distance would be more impressive, having cleared the ground and having fixed upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with determination, the horse of the gods' enemy, roaring like a rhinoceros out of pride, menaced the enemy faction. [21] And then, as if wishing to kill, to scatter, and to swallow all at once — unable to tolerate him — that lion-bodied <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, suddenly amplifying his lion-roar, seized that bold one and grappled him. And as the entire <s>Vraja</s> followed him in agitation — he, seeing that, with the gait called 'the surpassing,' swiftly leaped upon that very one, where:
That one soared into the sky, submerging [in the air]; he split open his mouth as if to drink it. Thus, when he struck with both legs — <s>Hari</s> countered even that! // [rathoddhatā]
And then:
Lifting up his swiftly thrashing legs and massive tail — huge and not insignificant — like a cluster of bristling body-hair, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] hurled him, like a ball of mud, at a spot marked at the distance of a hundred bows, like the crash of ocean-waves! // [vasantatilakā]
He (<s>Keśī</s>), having regained consciousness, rose again, and then, gaping his mouth wide, rushed at <s>Hari</s> with speed. And he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), laughing, gave his right arm into that mouth — like [giving it] to a great frog, like [feeding] a serpent! // [upajāti]
And <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> arm, like a divine serpent, clearly swelled in the cavity of his (<s>Keśī's</s>) throat, from the <s>vīra-rasa</s> (heroic sentiment). And the teeth of that one fell then from the radiance of the blazing flame of great poison, as if struck! // [upajāti]
The teeth fell, along with the senses which were also shaken, and the body attained trembling. Here, old age, having arisen at that time, was clearly waiting for death! // [upajāti]
