When his (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) arm blocked his (<s>Keśī's</s>) throat, then all his limbs went to a state of being torn apart. From the grief of that alone, further, those [limbs] everywhere became refuges [of that grief]. // [upajāti]
Seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> arm-staff entering <s>Keśī's</s> throat — deeming it the devourer of the world's life-breath — his (<s>Keśī's</s>) vital airs fled! // [anuṣṭubh]
'This one door named the throat is blocked for my exit — I shall make those [other doors] many!' — thus, did that company of his vital airs search for openings on all sides and then depart? // [śālinī]
When his life-breath departed from the body-house, <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> arm emerged like a guest. And that house, without its master, became piece by piece — indeed, destroyed by fate! // [upajāti]
When the arm was withdrawn from <s>Keśī's</s> throat-cavity, it attained its own natural state — like a divine arrow at the time of withdrawal! // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text:
ante muktaṃ tena gūtham ity uktaṃ yuktam iṣyate | tādṛśāṃ mukti-kṛt-kṛṣṇa-kṛpā yā sātiyuktikā ||JGc_1,32.14|| dvidhākṛtaṃ keśi-dehaṃ varṇayanti dvidhākṛtam | jarāsandha-nibhaṃ kecit kecit karkaṭikā-nibham ||JGc_1,32_15||[22] tad evam aśva-daiteye vapuṣā labdha-dvaite svarūpeṇa tu labdhādvaite pramanasāṃ vikīrṇa-sumanasāṃ sumanasāṃ kṛṣṇābhiprāyam abhiprayatām uktir yathā-
 āsyaṃ vyādāḥ sapadi nikhilaṃ mad-vapus tvaṃ
garītuṃ tatrāhaṃ tat parikalayituṃ tad-gale bāhum ādhām | tenaivāsīr yadi vigalita-prāṇakas tarhi tāvad
garvinn arvann ahaha sahasā sāhasaṃ kiṃ nv akārṣīḥ ||JGc_1,32.16|| iti |
children.translated_text:
That at the end he released excrement — this statement that 'it is fitting' is to be accepted. For the grace of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who grants liberation to such ones, is supremely well-reasoned! // [anuṣṭubh]
The body of <s>Keśī</s>, cut in two, is described in two ways — some say it was like <s>Jarāsandha</s>, others say it was like a crab! // [anuṣṭubh]
[22] Thus, when the horse-demon had obtained duality in body but non-duality in essential nature, the utterance perceiving the intent of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> by the delighted, flower-scattering gods was as follows:
'You opened your mouth to swallow my entire body at once — and I placed my arm in your throat to ascertain that! If by that alone you became one whose life-breath departed — then, O proud horse, alas! Why did you suddenly commit such rashness?' // [śārdūla] — thus.

children.text:
atha vrajaḥ kala-kala-śabdam abdavat
sṛjan muhur harim acalaṃ mudāvṛṇot | sa vṛṣṭivat pramadajam asram asravaj
jhara-prabhaṃ sa ca tad asūta bhūtale ||JGc_1,32.17|| [23] atha sarve sa-tṛṣṇā madhyam adhyāsita-kṛṣṇāḥ prematāratamya-ramyatayā yathāsvam antar-antar-labdhāntarās tad-anta-vyantaritatve' pi tad-anantaraṃ-manyās te dhanyās tad-aparam apy āliṅganatas tam eva manvānā vikāra-vṛndam avindata |
 [23] tataś ca kṣaṇa-katipayāt pratigata-bahir-matitayā saha-kṛṣṇāḥ kṛṣṇāghaṭṭam aṭitvā sasnuḥ | yat khalv adyāpi keśi-tīrthatayā tīrtha-varyāḥ paryavayanti | yasya ca bhāsvat-putryāḥ pratiloma-gatiṃ prati kiṃcin nikaṭata eva kuṭha-kūṭa-ghaṭita-taṭa-ghaṭṭāntaram adhiṣṭhāya tat-pariśrama-śamanāya viśaśramuḥ | dvitīya-ghaṭṭaś cāyaṃ cenaghaṭṭa iti vṛddhaiś cīra-ghaṭṭa iti cādhunikair udghaṭyate | ceneti viśrama-sukhasya hi māthura-bhāṣā | [25] atha viśramya ca kaṃsa-bhraṃśana-śaṃsanam idaṃ keśi-dhvaṃsanam iti ramya-sukhaṃ samyag avagamya dvi-guṇa-phullam ullasantas taṃ tanyamāna-kīrti-nartita-mukhair vandi-mukhair vanditam antar-vindamānaṃ śrī-govindam āvṛṇvantaḥ śrīmantaṃ vraja-devam anu vrajantas te vraja-janāḥ
prathamaṃ go-vrajam ayojayan |
hī-hī-jāte go-duhāṃ tatra jāte
kārṣṇaṃ tat tu prasphuṭaṃ paryacāyi | āsārāṇāṃ nardite yadvad uccair
ambhodasya snigdha-gambhīra-śabdaḥ ||JGc_1,32.18|| [26] atha śakraṃ jitavantas te vraja-yuvarājādi-gomantaḥ pratisvaṃ go-vṛndam anvitavantaḥ paraṃ vraja-rājādaya eva vrajam āvrajitavantaḥ |
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Vraja</s>, producing the sound of tumultuous rejoicing like a cloud, repeatedly enveloped the immovable <s>Hari</s> with joy. He rained the tears born of delight, waterfall-like — and that [downpour] produced [more joy] on the ground! // [drutavilambita]
[23] Then all, thirsty, having <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> seated in their midst, through the loveliness of the gradation of <s>prema</s>, having respectively found an interval in their inner-innermost [hearts] — though interrupted by that [outer commotion] — deeming themselves blessed and regarding what came thereafter as the very embrace — they experienced a multitude of emotional transformations.
[23] Then, after a few moments, having recovered their outward composure, together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having walked to the <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) landing, they bathed. Which indeed even today is honored by pilgrims as the foremost of sacred fords under the name '<s>Keśī-tīrtha</s>.' And at the place of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), somewhat near the upstream course, stationed at a landing constructed with a hewn stone bank, they rested for the relief of that exertion. And this second landing is disclosed by the ancients as '<s>Cena-ghaṭṭa</s>' and by the moderns as '<s>Cīra-ghaṭṭa</s>.' For '<s>cena</s>' is the <s>Māthura</s>-dialect word for the happiness of rest.
[25] Then, having rested, and having fully understood this destruction of <s>Keśī</s> as the proclamation of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> downfall — a delightful happiness — their joy doubly blossoming, they — encircling the glorious <s>Govinda</s>, who was being internally discovered, praised by panegyrists with faces dancing with the spreading of his fame — following the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, those <s>Vraja</s>-people
first set the herds of cows in motion.
When the cow-milking commenced among the milkers there, the dark <s>Kārṣṇa</s> (i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> essence) was clearly perceived [flowing forth]; just as when the rumbling of rain-showers sounded loudly, the cloud's deep, tender sound [was heard]! // [śālinī]
[26] Then those who had conquered <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — the young princes of <s>Vraja</s> and the leading cowherds — each following their own herd, returned; and the king of <s>Vraja</s> and his court alone entered <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: kaṃsas tu keśi-dhvaṃsanam api śṛṇvan vyagra-manā vigra iva gṛhān na niḥsasāra | [28] atha samāpanam |
children.translated_text: But <s>Kaṃsa</s>, hearing of the destruction of <s>Keśī</s> as well, agitated in mind, did not emerge from his house as if paralyzed. [28] Now, the conclusion.

children.text: so' yaṃ tava vrajādhīśa sutaḥ sūtamanorathaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This is that son of yours, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>, the fulfiller of his parents' desires!

children.text: keśinaṃ cātra yaścakre yamasya prativeśinam ||
children.translated_text: He who made <s>Keśī</s> here a neighbor of <s>Yama</s> (Death)!'

children.text: iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu keśi-dhvaṃsana-śaṃsanaṃ nāma dvātriṃśaṃ pūraṇam ||32||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the thirty-second <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Proclamation of the Destruction of <s>Keśī</s>.'
||32||

children.text: atha trayastriṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the thirty-third <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter),

children.text: sarva-manoratha-pūraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The Fulfillment of All Desires.'

children.text: atha niśīthinī-kathāyāṃ kuṇṭhaḥ samutkaṇṭhaś ca madhukaṇṭhaḥ sa-gadgadaṃ jagāda-[2] tad evaṃ rāmānujasya ramaṇinām apy amūṣāṃ dinaṃ dinam apy anuparamaṇaṃ ramaṇam atīva jīvana-samatām avāpa | [3] yatra samutkaṇṭhaāpy akuṇṭhā jātā | yataḥ-
children.translated_text:
Now, in the midnight narrative, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, bewildered and yet eager, spoke with a choked voice:
[2] 'Thus, the daily, unceasing sport of the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) with those charming women — day after day — attained the very equivalence of life itself. [3] Where even the longing became unchecked. For:'

children.text: yadapi paraspara-milanaṃ hari-gopīnāṃ cirān na vicchinnam |
children.translated_text: 'Even though the mutual meeting of <s>Hari</s> and the <s>gopīs</s> was long unbroken,

children.text: tadapi na tṛṣṇā śāntā svāpnika-pāne yathā pipāsūnām ||JGc_1,33.1||
children.translated_text: even so, the thirst was not quenched — like the thirst of those who drink in a dream!' // [āryā]

children.text: tatra tu ramaṇaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the sport, as follows:

children.text: anyo' nyaṃ rahasi prayāti milati śliṣyaty alaṃ cumbati
children.translated_text: 'Mutually, in secret, he approaches, meets, embraces closely, and kisses;

children.text: krīḍaty ullasati bravīti nidiśaty udbhūṣayaty anvaham |
children.translated_text: he plays, delights, speaks, instructs, and adorns [them] — day after day!

children.text: gopī-kṛṣṇa-yugaṃ muhur bahuvidhaṃ kintu svayaṃ nohate
children.translated_text: The <s>gopī</s>-<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> couple, in many diverse ways — yet of its own accord does not think:

children.text: śaśvat kiṃ nu karomi kiṃ nv akaravaṃ kurvīya kiṃ vety api ||JGc_1,33.2||
children.translated_text: 'What indeed am I doing? What have I done? What should I do?' — even this!' // [śārdūla]

children.text: utkaṇṭhāyāṃ tu tad eva padyaṃ bahu-vidham ity anantaram evaṃ paṭhanīyam-
children.translated_text: In longing, however, that very verse should be read thus after 'in many diverse ways':

children.text: gopī-kṛṣṇa-yugaṃ muhur bahu-vidhaṃ kintv etad evohate
tac caitanb na hi jāgarastham api tu svapnādi-citta-bhramaḥ ||2b||
children.translated_text: yet that is not even of the waking state, but the bewilderment of dream-and-such consciousness!' // [śārdūla, second half]
'The <s>gopī</s>-<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> couple, repeatedly in many diverse ways, of its own accord thinks only this —

children.text: kiṃ bahunā tad-anubhave ca tāsāṃ bhāvaneyam-
children.translated_text: In short, in the experience of him, their feeling was this:

children.text: utpattir akṣṇor abhito na sat-phalā
children.translated_text: 'The birth of the eyes on both sides is not fruitful

children.text: yābhyāṃ na tasyadbhuta-rūpam īkṣitam |
children.translated_text: by which his wondrous form was not beheld!

children.text: hā karṇayor apy alam arthadā na sā
children.translated_text: Alas, even the birth of the ears is not sufficiently meaningful

children.text: yābhyāṃ śrutaṃ naiva hareḥ subhāṣitam ||JGc_1,33.3||
children.translated_text: by which <s>Hari's</s> beautiful words were never heard!' // [upajāti]

children.text:
hā cakṣur-ādīni hareḥ samāgame
yady āgamiṣyan śravaṇādi karma ca |
tad āvrajiṣyan viṣayīṇi nāpy amūny
aṣūyayā dhig vyatidūyamānatām ||JGc_1,33.4|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'Alas, the eyes and other [senses], in the encounter with <s>Hari</s> — if they would come, and the functions of hearing and the like too — if they would arrive — then these sense-objects would not suffer — shame! — the state of being excessively tormented, out of jealousy!' // [upajāti] — thus.

children.text: kadācic ca-
children.translated_text: And on a certain occasion:

children.text:
sāṅgāliṅgana-laṅgime' ṅga-valayā-saṅge' pi śārṅgī tadā
gopīnāṃ sphurati sma dūra-gatayā premāpagā-pūrataḥ |
yasmād utkalikā-kalāpa-valanā-vṛttiṃ bahir lumpatī
svapnābhāṃ diśatī śatīm api dṛśi sphūrtiṃ muhur lumpati ||JGc_1,33.5||[8] śrī-rādhāyāṃ tu sutarām anirvacanīyam eva sarvaṃ tat-prathamatayā mithas tan-mithunasyāpi | tathā hi-
children.translated_text:
Even when the body of the bow-bearing one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) was entwined with the full embrace and the limb-encirclement of the <s>gopīs</s>, the river of <s>prema</s> appeared in its fullness as if from a distance. For the wave-play of longing — the surging pattern, sweeping away externally — even while giving a dream-like vision, even while producing a hundred manifestations in the eye, repeatedly swept them away! // [śārdūla]
[8] And in Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, all this was all the more indescribable, by virtue of her primacy, for that couple too, mutually. For thus:

children.text: rādhā'jānād asaṅge danuja-vijayinaḥ saṅgam ārād asaṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> knew not separation from the conqueror of demons — [she knew] meeting from afar as if non-meeting;

children.text: saṅge caivaṃ samantād gṛha-samaya-sukha-svapna-śītādikāni |
children.translated_text: and in meeting too, the joys of home, time, sleep, cold, and such on all sides [were perceived as obstacles].

children.text: etasyā vṛttir eṣājani sapadi yadānyad vicitraṃ tadāsīt
children.translated_text: Such was the conduct of this one that arose at once; and when something wonderful [occurred],

children.text: kāntākānta-svabhāvo' py ahaha yad anayor vaiparītyāya jajñe ||JGc_1,33.6||
children.translated_text: the nature of the beloved and the non-beloved — alas — that of both of them turned to its opposite! // [śārdūla]

children.text: tad evam atibhūmitām ite bhāva-bhūmani tena ca sarvābhyarṇatām iva jāte vṛtta-jāte sva-sva-vadhū-nirodhāya niyukta-pura-janī-janeṣu ca guruṣu tad-uṭṭaṅkanataḥ kṛṣṇas tu tṛṣṇā-lajjābhyāṃ sajjan-manāḥ sva-mānasam anv evaṃ bhāvayāmāsa-[10] hanta kim idam antarā jātam ? kaulīnaṃ khalu kaulīnaṃ janaṃ kau līnam iva karotīti man-manaḥ kañcana vicāram ācāraṃ ca na sañcarati | lokaś ca śokaṃ prayāsyatīti nija-vargyam anu duḥkhaṃ pāṇi-sargyaṃ svayam evākaravam | tatḥ kiṃ karavāṇi ?
children.translated_text:
Thus, when the ground of emotion had reached the state of extreme abundance, and when the event had brought [him] as if to nearness with all [the gopīs], and when the elders, appointed as guardians for the confinement of their respective brides, were pressing forward in that — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, his mind stirred by both longing and shame, reflected within his own mind as follows:
[10] 'Alas! What has come about in the meanwhile? Family honor indeed makes a person of good family as if dissolved in a trough! My mind does not proceed toward any [proper] deliberation or conduct. And the people will go to grief — thus, for my own party, the painful surrendering of hands [in marriage] I myself brought about. What then shall I do?'

children.text: punaḥ sa-praṇidhānam idaṃ vivinakti sma-nedam anācāram iva pratibhāti | bhāti hi mama cittam anena | na tu mlāniṃ yāti |
children.translated_text: Again, he discerned this with careful attention: 'This does not appear to be misconduct. For my mind shines through this — it does not go to withering.'

children.text: punar api ca parāmamarśa-tāḥ punar mama parāṅganā evānubhūyante, na tu parāṅganāḥ | tasmād bhaved atra viśeṣaḥ sandarbha-viśeṣaḥ | yam eva khalv aham iva loko' py ayam anirṇīya nūnaṃ garga-durvarṇanayāsmad-apayānaṃ nirṇīya ca śīrṇībhavan śaṅkayā saṅka-sukatām urīcakre yena cāmūr api nūnaṃ svaṃ dhik-kurvanti | yathā-
children.translated_text: And again he reflected: 'Those [women] are again experienced by me as my own wives, not as others' wives. Therefore, there must be a distinction here — a distinction of [theological] composition (<s>sandarbha</s>). The very one whom even this world, like myself, has not determined — surely through <s>Garga's</s> obscure description, having determined our departure and crumbling with apprehension, it accepted a contraction into distress — by which even these [gopīs] surely condemn themselves.' As follows:

children.text:
vraje jāter jātā vraja-jana-samāna-prakṛtitā
tataḥ kṛṣṇe premā tam anu sahasā taṃ prati gatiḥ |
tatas tatrāsaṅgas tam anu viparītaṃ kim api tat
tato vyaktaṃ tac ca praṇaya sakhi dhik kiṃ nu karavai ||JGc_1,33.7|| iti |

atha taṃ parāṅganā-pārāṅgana-vicāra-garbhaṃ sandarbhaṃ punar asmin nija-nijābhilaṣita-kallola-lola-mat-prema-kallolinī-vallabhe mad-aṅga-saṅgata-marul-lavenāpi velati vallavāvalaye na samyag anusandhātuṃ sandhāṃ labhamahe |
children.translated_text: Now, regarding that composition pregnant with the deliberation about others' wives and the shore of others' [propriety] — again, in this cowherd community, whose beloved is the river of my love, tossing with waves of their respective desires — even by a mere breeze-fragment of contact with my body, [it] overflows — we do not find an opportunity to properly investigate [this].

children.text: kiṃ ca yadi ca vāstavatayā na vidyate doṣas tathāpi tat-kathāpi prathayati mama saṅkocam iti vrajād vyavadhātum ivāvadadhāti me citta-vṛttiḥ | [15] tad etad vyavadhānam eva cāyatām āyati-śuddhiṃ vidhāsyati | [16] ṛṇa-vraṇa-kalaṅkānāṃ kāle lopo bhaviṣyatīti nyāyena mama samyag-anusandhānena teṣām lokānāṃ paścāt-tāpam anu sad-upadeśa-grahaṇena ca |
children.translated_text: Moreover, even if in reality there is no fault, still, even the telling of it expands my reticence — thus my mental disposition determines to create, as it were, a separation from <s>Vraja</s>. [15] And let this very separation become the means of purifying the future. [16] By the maxim 'Of debts, wounds, and blemishes, there will be disappearance in time' — through my proper investigation and through those people's acceptance of good instruction following their repentance.

children.text: atha tad etad vibhāvya punaḥ sodvegaṃ vibhāvayāmbabhūva-
children.translated_text: Then, having envisioned this, he again reflected with agitation:

children.text: hā goṣṭhaṃ vipinaṃ paśūn vraja-janaṃ dāsān sakhīn preyasīs
children.translated_text: 'Alas! The cow-settlement, the forest, the cattle, the people of <s>Vraja</s>, the servants, the companions, the beloveds,

children.text: tātaṃ mātaram apy aho katham amūṃ hāsyāmi rādhām api |
children.translated_text: the father, the mother too — ah! — how shall I abandon this <s>Rādhā</s> as well!

children.text: māṃ yāny aṅga vinā kṣaṇaṃ katham api prāpsyanti nātma-sthitiṃ
children.translated_text: Those who without me cannot attain their own state of being even for a moment —

children.text: yāny antar-jvalana-prabhāni vidadhat prāpsyāmi dāha-prathām ||JGc_1,33.8||
children.translated_text: those whom, placing within the fire of inner burning, I shall attain the spread of conflagration!' ||33.8||

children.text: punar vibhāvyātmānam uddiśyāha-
children.translated_text: Again, having reflected and addressing himself, he said:

children.text: antaḥpurīyasi vaneṣu sakhīyasi tvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'You hold the inner quarters as the forests, the companions as your own;

children.text: vanyān mṛgān nija-tanūyasi gopa-rāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: you make your own body [one with] the wild deer, [and you hold] the cowherd women [as yourself]!

children.text: dṛṣṭaś cakora-nayanābhir amūbhir indu-
children.translated_text: Seen by these <s>cakora</s>-eyed ones, [you are their] moon —

children.text: darśaṃ kathaṃ vahasi kṛṣṇa paratra tṛṣṇām ||JGc_1,33.9||
children.translated_text: how then do you bear the longing for elsewhere, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?' ||33.9||

children.text: punaḥ preyasīr anusandhāya-
children.translated_text: Again, reflecting upon the beloveds:

children.text: yasminn āropitā hārās tāsāṃ hanta mayā hṛdi |
children.translated_text: 'The garlands that were placed upon their hearts by me, alas —

children.text: sāmrājyaṃ hā kariṣyanti tasminn apy asra-bindavaḥ ||JGc_1,33.10||
children.translated_text: even upon those, teardrops will exercise sovereignty!' ||33.10||

children.text: tatra ca śrī-rādhām anusandhāya hanta hanteti procya punar āha-
children.translated_text: And there, reflecting upon Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, having exclaimed 'Alas! Alas!' he said again:

children.text: hā candra-drava-yuta-candanena siktā
children.translated_text: 'Alas! The body-creeper of <s>Rādhā</s>, sprinkled with affection

children.text: rādhāyāṃ tanu-latikā mayā sahārdam |
children.translated_text: by me with sandalwood mixed with moon-extract —

children.text: saiṣā mad-virahaja-locanodagāhā
children.translated_text: this very [creeper], from the emergence of tears born of my separation,

children.text: mlāsyantī pratapati sampratīha māṃ ca ||JGc_1,33.11||
children.translated_text: will wilt — and [even so] she scorches me now!' ||33.11||

children.text: yā pūrvam upalabdhāsīn nava-candra-kalopamā |
children.translated_text: 'She who was formerly perceived as resembling the digit of the new moon —

children.text: vahneḥ śikheva sā jātā rādhā dandagdhi hṛn mama ||JGc_1,33.12||
children.translated_text: that <s>Rādhā</s> has become like a flame of fire — she burns my heart!' ||33.12||

children.text: rādhā prema-prādhvam atrāgato' haṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s>! By the path of love I have come here —

children.text: hā prādhvaḥ śyāmāśu so' haṃ kathaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: alas, that path, O dark one (<s>Śyāmā</s>)! — how am I that [same person]?

children.text: tasmāt prādhvaṃ kṛtya dhī-vṛttayo' sminn
children.translated_text: Therefore, having made the faculties of the mind travel upon this very path,

children.text: eva prādhvaṃ kutracin nāparatra ||JGc_1,33.13||
children.translated_text: let [them travel] on this path alone, nowhere else!' ||33.13||

children.text: iti kṣaṇaṃ bāṣpāyamāṇekṣaṇatayā tūṣṇīm āsīt | punaś ca tathā tathā bhāvana-vrāte jāte-hanta hanta katham aham aho klībamānaḥ punaḥ śoka-prapañcam añcāmi yataḥ samprati bhiduraṃ cittaṃ na vidūratāṃ vindeta iti vicintayati sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, for a moment, with tearful eyes, he remained silent. And again, when such a multitude of reflections had arisen — 'Alas, alas! How am I, becoming enfeebled, again extending this expanse of sorrow! Since at present, a heart that is breakable would not find remoteness [from grief]' — thus he pondered.

children.text: tad evaṃ sāvadhānaṃ sahasā rahas tad vimuñcan sahacara-sahacāritām āpannaḥ, kintu nātiprasannatayā etad anantaram udantas tu prātar eva prathayiṣyāmi iti sa-gadgadaṃ gaditvā snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sa-madhukaṇṭhaḥ sva-vāsasā vadanaṃ vasānaḥ sa-śabdaṃ rudann alabdha-tad-avasānaś ciram āsīt | cirata eva tu tasmād viramya śrī-rādhā-mādhavādīn api sva-sādhāraṇān adhigamya tad idam avādīt-
children.translated_text: Thus, carefully and suddenly releasing that [grief] in private, having attained the companionship of his companions — but not with full composure — having said with a faltering voice 'The remaining account I shall announce in the morning itself' — <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, together with <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, covering his face with his own garment, weeping audibly, having not attained the cessation of that [grief], remained thus for a long time. And only after a long time, having ceased from that, having again encountered Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, and others as common to himself, he spoke this:

children.text:
sukyākurvanta evādhvaṃ tad idaṃ sukham ātmanaḥ |
kathāgataṃ tu tad duḥkhaṃ kathakānena bādhatām ||JGc_1,33.14|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'They simply made the journey well — that is their own happiness;
but that sorrow which has entered the story — let that trouble the narrator [alone]!' ||33.14||

children.text: tad evaṃ tayoḥ sadanam āsannayoḥ śrī-rādhā-mādhavādayaś ca punaḥ svapna-labdham iva tad duḥkhaṃ sukha-paryavasānam upalabdhaṃ vidhāya yathāsvam āvāsam āsādayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when both of them [narrators] had nearly reached home, Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, and the others too, having reckoned that sorrow — obtained as if in a dream — to be one that culminates in happiness, each reached their respective dwellings.

children.text: atha prātaḥkathāyāṃ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tad evaṃ kaṃsa-gṛhyānanyānanyāya-bhājo nigṛhyārvaveśi-keśi-vadhāt pūrvam ahar-mukhe cālita-cakṣur-aravindaḥ śrīmān govindaś cetasi cintitavān-prāyaḥ sarva eva hiṃsitāḥ kaṃsa-pakṣīyāḥ keśī cādya śvo vā patiṣyati | kevalaṃ kuvalayāpīḍaḥ karī varīvarti |
children.translated_text: Then, in the morning narrative, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Thus, at dawn, before the slaying of <s>Keśī</s>, with stirred lotus-eyes, having seized those who belong to <s>Kaṃsa's</s> grasp — with no other recourse — the glorious <s>Govinda</s> reflected in his mind: "Almost all of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> partisans have been destroyed. <s>Keśī</s> too will fall today or tomorrow. Only the elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> remains.'

children.text: anye labdhāntare tat-pradhānatāsv avyapekṣatayā na tatra mama gantavyam asti | yataḥ pitṛ-mukhāvṛtakaḥ khalv aham, na tu svatantra-mantraḥ | kintu yogyaṃ vyājantaraṃ mṛgyate | bhavatu, yathāprāptaṃ tat samāptavyam | tad alaṃ tac-cintanam anena |
children.translated_text: 'Others, having found opportunity and not [being] dependent on their primacy, need not concern me to go there. For I am [bound by] the covering of my father's [authority], not one of independent counsel. But a suitable alternative pretext must be sought. So be it — whatever comes, that must be completed. Therefore, enough of pondering this!'

children.text: tad etad vicārya ca-hanta hanta tatra prayāne ca jāte na jāne kiyān kārya-paryāyāvarodhaḥ syāt iti | kathaṃ vrajaṃ vinā samayaṃ gamayiṣyāmi iti | [28] punaḥ sāsraṃ cintayāñcakāra-
children.translated_text: And having deliberated thus: 'Alas, alas! When the departure does take place, I do not know how great an obstruction of the sequence of duties there will be!' — 'How shall I pass the time without <s>Vraja</s>?' — thus. [28] Again, he reflected with tears:

children.text: vinā māṃ tātaḥ prāg na pibati jalaṃ sā ca jananī
children.translated_text: 'Without me, the father first does not drink water, and that mother

children.text: vinā mām ucchvāsān visṛjati batāsūn iva muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: without me, alas, repeatedly releases sighs as if [releasing] her life-breaths!

children.text: yathā tau hā tadvad vrajam anugatā viśva-janatā
children.translated_text: Just as those two — ah! — so too the entire people following <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: tad āstāṃ tiryañco' py ahaha hṛdi śalyaṃ vidadhati ||JGc_1,33.15||
children.translated_text: let that be — even the animals, alas, create a thorn in my heart!' ||33.15||

children.text: tad idaṃ cāgrajam api vedayitum utsahe | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'And this I am eager to convey even to my elder brother. Since:'

children.text: duḥkhāyate pumān kaścit kaścid vā yaḥ sukhāyate |
children.translated_text: 'Some person causes sorrow, some causes happiness;

children.text: pūrvasmin na dayālutvaṃ parasmiṃs tu dayālutā ||JGc_1,33.16||
children.translated_text: toward the former, [there should be] no compassion; toward the latter, [there should be] compassion!' ||33.16||

children.text: tad evaṃ prātar vicāram ācārya tadaiva daivata āpatitaṃ keśinaṃ ca mṛtyuṃ prāpayya gocāraṇāya caraṇa-caryayā vanaṃ sañcarantaṃ śrīkāntaṃ kvacid ekanta-gatayā harṣitaḥ śrīmān devarṣiḥ sapadi sākṣād āsedivān | sa cāsannam āgaccantam accha-paricchadaṃ śrī-nāradaṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: Thus, having performed the morning deliberation, and at that very moment having dispatched to death the divinely-arrived <s>Keśī</s>, while he was walking to the forest for cow-herding with the course of his feet — somewhere, in a solitary place, the glorious <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), delighted, suddenly appeared before that radiant beloved of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). And he beheld Śrī <s>Nārada</s> approaching — [wearing] bright garments.

children.text:
dṛṣṭvā ca gīrdevatā-deham ivākṣara-rūpatāṃ dharantaṃ
gaṅgā-pravāham iva viṣṇupadād avatarantam,
kailāsam iva vaiṣṇava-lakṣa-śiva-mūrtiṃ,
nija-yaśaḥ-stomam iva vividha-gāna-kṛta-karṇa-pūrtim,
kṣīra-nīra-nidhi-m ivāntarvāsita-nārāyaṇaādi-nāmānam,
amanda-kalā-sāndra-candramasam ivāntaraṅgatayā dhṛta-kṛṣṇa-dhāmānam,
śārada-nīrada-samudāyam iva śarma-netrāpy adhārā varṣantam,
bhakti-viśeṣāsakti-vyakta-nija-bhakta-prahāsam iva kṛta-harṣantaṃ parāmamarśa |
children.translated_text:
And having seen [him] — bearing the form of imperishability as if [he were] the body of the goddess of speech (<s>Sarasvatī</s>),
descending from the foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s> like the stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
like <s>Kailāsa</s> in the form of <s>Śiva</s> marked with <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [signs],
like the mass of his own fame, with manifold singing filling the ears,
like the milk-ocean with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and other names dwelling within,
like the moon of abundant arts, internally bearing the abode of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as an intimate,
like an assemblage of autumnal clouds raining joy to the eyes even without rain,
like the laughter of his own devotees, made manifest through the intensity of special devotion, creating delight — [thus] he reflected.

children.text:
sa ca tam evaṃ dadarśa-sadācaraṇa-suṣṭhutāyāṃ sādhu-padmavat,
sadāśeṣa-sukhada-pada-pṛṣṭhatāyāṃ kṛta-tad-vidha-tanu-śrī-kamaṭhavat,
jaṅghāla-sat0kaṭaka-śobhitāyāṃ vijaya-dhvajavat,
sahajānūru-nāma-śastatāyāṃ garutmata-stambhavat,
kākudmatavitatatāyāṃ nija-vraja-taṭavat,
śubha-śobhāvalagna-prahlādakatāyāṃ narasiṃhavat,
bhuvana-kamala-ramaṇīya-nābhitāyāṃ sarovaravat, nārāyaṇavad vā,
vara-guṇa-rasanāpītāmbaratāyāṃ navya-ravy-aṃśuvat,
santatam udara-śvasana-calatāyāṃ pippala-dalavat,
hṛdayaṅgama-svarṇa-rekhā-śrī-kaṭāyāṃ nīlamaṇi-nikaṣa-paṭṭavat,
sad-guṇa-ratnālaya-hṛdayatāyāṃ ratnākaravat,
maryādā-paryāpaṇa-bhujatāyāṃ jiṣṇu-ratnārgalavat,
aṅgadādi-labdha-praveṣṭatāyāṃ kauśalyā-garbha-maṅgalavat,
rocamāna-mudrākaratāyāṃ kalpa-vallī-pallavavat,
samutkaṇṭha-svara-rūpatāyāṃ pāñcajanyavat,
dvijatārādhirāja-dāsyatāyāṃ dvija-rājavat,
nāsayā śuka-mukha-sakti-jetṛ-śobhitāyāṃ svayam eva yadvat,
nija-satya-vrata-bhakta-rocana-vilocanatāyāṃ navīna-divya-mīnavat,
candraka-śobha-keśa-nirmāṇatāyāṃ sanīradāgama-samaya-nīradavat,
makarāṅkālaṅkṛta-śravaṇatāyāṃ makaradhvajavat,
sarvadā sarvatrāmṛta-varṣi-śiti-mūrti-kṛta-pūrtitāyāṃ punar amṛta-raśmivat,
rohiṇī-yaśodā-nanda-nandanatāyāṃ rauhiṇeyavat,
narasiṃhatā-saṃhita-saṃhananatāyāṃ pnuar narasiṃhavat,
muhur apūrva-māna-rūpatāyāṃ punar mīna-mahīnavat,
paṭiṣṭhatā-vighaṭita-bali-gariṣṭha-bhāvatāyāṃ vāmana-devavat,
utpatha-vṛṣalāñchita-vṛṣa-nindakatāyāṃ jina-nandanavat,
payorāśi-nimajjad-uddhara-gotra-samuddharaṇa-dhūryatāyāṃ punaḥ śrī-kamaṭhavat,
dharaṇī-dhara-hāri-vihāritāyāṃ vārāhāvatāravat,
kṛtavīrya-jāta-durjana-kṣatra-kṣapaṇatāyāṃ bhārgava-rāmavat,
bhāvi-kālayavana-saṃyamanatāyāṃ viṣṇuyaśas-tanayavat,
lakṣmaṇa-carita-racita-pracura-sukhatāyāṃ punaḥ śrī-rāmacandravad iti |
tad evam aikarūpya-śleṣeṇa śabda-śleṣeṇa ca mithaś cintita-sad-upamānayor anayoḥ śrī-devarṣir amuṃ śrī-harṣi-śrī-nidhānaṃ veda-pārāyaṇataḥ stūyamānaṃ vidhāya vīkāśaṃ nivedayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Thus, through the <s>śleṣa</s> (double-meaning) of essential identity and the <s>śleṣa</s> of words, when those two had mutually conceived apt comparisons — the glorious <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), having caused him — the repository of the joy of the blessed one — who was being praised through the recitation of the <s>Vedas</s>, to be radiant, submitted his message:

children.text:
śamitaḥ śamito yena dānavo' sau sadānavaḥ |
sa paro' paratāṃ yātaḥ sodayo' nudayo bhavān ||JGc_1,33.17||avilambena ye ḍimbe hasatāhasata tvayā |
te sarve pūtanāpūrvāḥ pūnāḥ pūtāś ca sarvataḥ ||JGc_1,33.18||guṇair aguṇatāṃ yātas tvam asau nandanandana |
bibharṣi vasudhāṃ citraṃ sthitvāpi vasudhopari ||JGc_1,33.19||śaśadhara-mūrtiḥ śuklā gaṅgā-viśadā sarasvatī śyenī |
kīrtis tava tu bakāntaka śubhrā sarvaṃ karoti śubhrābham ||JGc_1,33.20||tvat-kīrtyā śvetitaḥ kaṃso' py etat kṛṣṇa mṛṣoditam |
tat-sparśas tasya nāsty eva kintu tad-bhīti-vaikṛtam ||JGc_1,33.21||
children.translated_text: there is no touch of that [fame] upon him at all — rather, it is the discoloration born of fear of it!' ||33.21||

'He by whom that demon, always demonic, was pacified and destroyed —
he, the supreme one, has gone to non-supremacy; you, of noble dawning, are he!' ||33.17||
'Those whom you slew without delay in childhood, laughing —
all of them, beginning with <s>Pūtanā</s>, were purified and made pure on all sides!' ||33.18||
'By your qualities, you have attained the state of being quality-less, O son of <s>Nanda</s>;
wondrous — you bear the earth, even while standing upon the earth!' ||33.19||
'The moon-bodied, bright [<s>Gaṅgā</s>], limpid like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s> of hawk-like [speed] —
but your fame, O slayer of <s>Baka</s>, being resplendent, makes everything shine resplendently!' ||33.20||
'Even <s>Kaṃsa</s> has been whitened by your fame — but this, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is falsely spoken;

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite tu kiñcin mama nivedanam asti, tathā hi-
children.translated_text: 'That being so, I have something to submit — as follows:

children.text:
premā vaśayati sarvaṃ khalv iti na mṛṣā prasiddhir udbhāti |
kṛṣṇa tvam api sa yasmān na bhajasi pūrvāparānusandhānam ||JGc_1,33.22||tasmād vimana-sama-dhiyaṃs tvām aham āgacchamācchannam |
tāṃ smārayitum avaśyaṃ yā sambhavitā bhaval-līlā ||JGc_1,33.23||loke' smiṃs tava bhaktā bahavaḥ kramaśaś ca te pālyāḥ |
tasmād avaśyam udiyuḥ paurvāparyeṇa tā līlāḥ ||JGc_1,33.24||
children.translated_text: therefore, those pastimes must necessarily arise in due sequence!' ||33.24||

'Love subjugates everything — this is indeed no false renown!
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, you too are he [who is subjugated], since you do not attend to the investigation of what comes before and after!' ||33.22||
'Therefore, approaching you secretly, with mind like an aerial vehicle,
I [have come] necessarily to remind you of that which is your destined pastime!' ||33.23||
'In this world, your devotees are many, and they are to be protected in succession;

children.text: keśinaṃ ditijam aśva-veśinaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The horse-disguised demon <s>Keśī</s> —

children.text: yo jaghāna sa bhavān athābhavān |
children.translated_text: he who slew [him] is you — then you became [as one who is] not;

children.text: tān vidhātum aparān satāṃ parān
children.translated_text: to accomplish those other [deeds], being the supreme ones for the righteous,

children.text: uccakaiḥ prabhavitākhilāvitā ||JGc_1,33.25||
children.translated_text: you will arise mightily, O protector of all!' ||33.25||

children.text:
tathā hi-
keli-mātreṇa te daityā yad-bhidelimatāṃ gatāḥ |
pacelimas tena tāpāt kaṃsaḥ pradhvaṃsam eṣyati ||JGc_1,33.26||krūraḥ sa netuṃ sadyas tvām akrūras tu prahāsyati |
tvaṃ ca mātrādikaṃ hitvā yātrāṃ taṃ hantum āpsyasi ||JGc_1,33.27||
children.translated_text: and you, leaving mother and others, will obtain the journey to slay him!' ||33.27||

As follows:
'Since those demons were defeated by mere sport —
by that very heat, <s>Kaṃsa</s> will come to destruction!' ||33.26||
'That cruel one [<s>Akrūra</s>], in order to take you quickly — being <s>Akrūra</s> (not-cruel), will smile;

children.text: atha sa-vaivarṇyaṃ nirvarṇya tathāvasthitavati tasmin bhāvāntaram ṛṣir udbhāvayann uvāca-tataś ca sujana-roṣṭāraṃ kaṃsaṃ kroṣṭāram iva roṣitāsi, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then, observing the change of complexion in him who stood thus affected, the sage, producing a different sentiment, said: 'And then, you will anger <s>Kaṃsa</s>, that howling one who enrages good people, like a jackal — because:

children.text: kūpa-maṇḍūkavat kaṃsaḥ kaṇḍūtiṃ khaṇḍayan nijām |
children.translated_text: 'Like a frog in a well, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, scratching his own itch,

children.text: tvat-karkaśa-bhujābhogi-saṅgharṣaṃ labdhum icchati ||JGc_1,33.28||
children.translated_text: desires to obtain the friction of your hard, serpentine arms!' ||33.28||

children.text: yaṃ khalu mātari-puruṣaṃ puruṣottarmas tvam iha jīva-grāhaṃ grhīṣyasi | samūla-ghātaṃ haniṣyasy akṛta-kāraṃ kariṣyasi, kara-grāhaṃ gṛhṇaṃś ca viśrānti-paryantam aśrānti-vikramatayā virkakṣyasi |
children.translated_text: You will seize him — that <s>Mātari-puruṣa</s> (son of the man who strikes) — O <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person) — alive! You will slay him with root-and-all destruction! You will render him actionless! And seizing him by the hand, you will exhibit him with unflagging valor to the very end of rest!

children.text: harṣadbhiḥ pāṇi-karṣaṃ niṣkarṣaṃs tama anekapam |
children.translated_text: 'Dragging with joy that many-armed darkness (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) out by the hand,

children.text: drakṣyase puṇḍarīkākṣa tvaṃ vyaktaṃ haritāṃ gataḥ ||JGc_1,33.29||
children.translated_text: you shall be seen, O lotus-eyed one — you will clearly have gone among the divine ones!' ||33.29||

children.text: tatra saṅkṣepārtha-nikṣepaś cāyam-
children.translated_text: And here is the deposit of the summary meaning:

children.text: akrūraṃ dvāra-mātraṃ vidadhad atha bhavān vṛṣṇi-dhiṣṇyāni gatvā
children.translated_text: 'Making <s>Akrūra</s> merely a doorway, you, having gone to the abode of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,

children.text: bhuṅktvā traiyakṣa-cāpaṃ sapadi kuvalayāpīḍakaṃ pīḍayitvā |
children.translated_text: having consumed the bow of the three-eyed one (<s>Śiva</s>), instantly having crushed <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>,

children.text: mallān hatvā paraśvo danuja-jani-tanuṃ kaṃsakaṃ dhvaṃsayitvā
children.translated_text: having slain the wrestlers, and on the following day having destroyed the demon-born body of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: rājyaṃ dattvograsenaṃ prati nija-janakau mocayiṣyaty avaśyam ||JGc_1,33.30||
children.translated_text: having given the kingdom to <s>Ugrasena</s>, you will certainly liberate your own parents!' ||33.30||

children.text: atra paurāḥ paurāṇikīm iva gāthāṃ gātāraḥ-
children.translated_text: Here, the city-dwellers — as if singing an ancient ballad — [will say]:

children.text: unmīlan nīla-śubhrāruṇa-kamala-jitī khañjana-dhvaṃsi-līlā-
children.translated_text: 'The blooming blue-bright-red-lotus-conquering, <s>khañjarīṭa</s>-destroying playful

children.text: cāñcalye siṃha-saṅgha-pramathana-madatā-vyañjinī yasya netre |
children.translated_text: flickering, lion-pack-crushing, manifesting-intoxication-of-his-two-eyes —

children.text: ceṣṭā durduṣṭa-vṛnda-praśama-paṭu-kalā-kalpinī majjayantī
children.translated_text: whose activity — skilled art for quelling the wicked — submerging

children.text: pīyūṣe sajjanālīr nava-vayasi varā śyāmalaḥ kaḥ sameti ||JGc_1,33.31||
children.translated_text: the hosts of the good in nectar — in fresh youth, excellent: who is this dark one that comes?' ||33.31||

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svagatam uvāca-ugrasenāya rājyaṃ dāsyāmīti yuktam eva khalūktam | yato mama vrajāgamanam eva ramaṇīyam | [40] prakāśaṃ cāha sma-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to himself: 'That I shall give the kingdom to <s>Ugrasena</s> — that is indeed aptly spoken! For my return to <s>Vraja</s> alone is delightful.'
[40] And he spoke aloud: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-
children.translated_text: The sage said:

children.text: grāmyāḥ paurā nṛpālāḥ sadasi nabhasi tu svarga-saṅgīta-vijñā
children.translated_text: 'The rustic ones, the city-folk, the kings in the assembly, and in the sky, the experts in celestial music —

children.text: devā devādi-nāthā vidhi-śiva-vidhijās te vayaṃ ca stuvānāḥ |
children.translated_text: the gods, the lords of gods and of others, the sons of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and <s>Śiva</s>, and we — all praising!

children.text: rakta-tyag-danti-danta-cchavir avikara-bhāgaṃsakau lūna-mallau
children.translated_text: The luster of the passionate-red-elephant-tooth hue, with blemish-free shoulder-portions, the slain wrestlers —

children.text: drakṣyāmo bhrātarau vāṃ kavalita-balavat kaṃsakaṃ tvām apīha ||JGc_1,33.32||
children.translated_text: we shall behold the two brothers — you, who has swallowed the mighty <s>Kaṃsa</s>, here too!' ||33.32||

children.text: tatra malla-sabhā-gatānām idaṃ kolāhala-kutūhalaṃ bhavitā-
children.translated_text: There, the curiosity-tumult of those who have entered the wrestling-arena shall be:

children.text: kim idaṃ śyāmalaṃ rūpaṃ madhuraṃ raudram eva vā |
children.translated_text: 'What is this dark form — is it sweet or indeed terrible?

children.text: strī cāstrī ca na yad divyaṃ vastram astraṃ yathāyatham ||JGc_1,33.33||
children.translated_text: Is it a woman or not a woman? Is it divine — or a garment or a weapon, as appropriate?' ||33.33||

children.text: pāpa-kaṃse cāpavargam ite-
children.translated_text: And when the sinful <s>Kaṃsa</s> has gone to his release:

children.text: vadhārhasyāpi kaṃsasya strīṇāṃ dṛg-vāri-bindavaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who deserved death, the teardrops of the women

children.text: dharaṇyāṃ nipatiṣyanti drāvayiṣyanti hṛt tava ||JGc_1,33.34||
children.translated_text: will fall upon the earth and will melt your heart!' ||33.34||

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta tau mama nija-janakāv iti bhavatā kāv uktau ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Alas! Who are these two whom you have called my own parents?'

children.text: ṛṣiḥ sa-hāsam uvāca-
children.translated_text: The sage said with a smile:

children.text: prāg ayaṃ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Previously, this son of yours was born somewhere of <s>Vasudeva</s>;

children.text: vāsudeva iti śrīmān abhijñāḥ sampracakṣate ||[BhP 10.8.14]
children.translated_text: the knowledgeable call him the glorious <s>Vāsudeva</s>!' ||[BhP 10.8.14]

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sāścarya-smitam uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with an astonished smile: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-vasudevādayas tu naṣṭaṃ cintāmaṇim iva spaṣṭaṃ vindamānās tvāṃ hātuṃ na hi sahiṣyante | [48] tava ca tad-anurodhāya yadūnām itas tataḥ palāyana-samavāya-dūnānām avarodhāya ca niścita-cittasya katicid vāsarāṇi bhaviṣyanti | [49] tvad-anuṣaṅgatas tatra saṅgatā tad-apekṣitī-kṛtya vraja-kṣiti-pati-prabhṛti-vraja-janatāpi śākaṭa-vāṭa-paṭa-nivāsam asatsyati |
children.translated_text:
The sage said: '<s>Vasudeva</s> and the others, finding you clearly like a lost wish-fulfilling jewel, will not endure to let you go.
[48] And for you, for their sake, [there shall be] the prevention of the <s>Yadus</s>, afflicted by flight hither and thither — for your determined mind, some days shall pass.
[49] Following your association, the people of <s>Vraja</s> too — the lord of <s>Vraja's</s> earth foremost, and all the <s>Vraja</s> folk — having been made a matter of concern, shall dwell in a camp of cart-and-tent enclosures.'

children.text: tathāpi cirataḥ kaṃsa-prathita-vyathatayā prāpta-vitathatāyāyadu-rāja-rājadhānyāḥ sphurad-ugrasenenāpy ugrasenena duḥsamādhānaṃ samādhānam | svayaṃ bahu-praṇidhānata eva syād iti kṣaṇam api kṣaṇam alabhamāś cirāyamāṇe nija-vraja-prayāṇe vicārya rāmeṇa sama aikacarya-caryayā svajana-vraje vraje virājamānaṃ vrajeśam upavrajya svasya vrajāgamanam avaśya-kāryatayā nirdhārya vrajam eva vrājiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, after a long time, when the anguish made famous by <s>Kaṃsa</s> has attained its cessation, and when the settlement of the capital of the <s>Yadu</s> king — gleaming with <s>Ugrasena</s> himself, the fierce <s>Ugrasena</s> — [has reached a state of] difficult-to-achieve equilibrium; through your own extensive deliberations, you — not obtaining even a moment's rest, while the departure to your own <s>Vraja</s> was being prolonged — having reflected, together with <s>Rāma</s>, through the practice of solitary conduct, approaching the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, resplendent among his own <s>Vraja</s> people, and having determined your return to <s>Vraja</s> as an absolute necessity, you shall indeed return to <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta ! te kiṃ tyajanta eva mām āvrājiṣyanti ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Alas! Will they not abandon me and return [without me]?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-
children.translated_text: The sage said:

children.text: nandādayas tava paraṃ mahatāgraheṇa
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s> and the others, with supreme insistence,

children.text: prāpsyanti goṣṭham atha tad-vapuṣātmanā na |
children.translated_text: shall reach their cow-settlement — but not in that bodily form of his;

children.text: dṛśyaṃ bhaved vapur iti sphuṭam asya tasmin
children.translated_text: the body would indeed be visible, clearly, in that [<s>Vraja</s>] —

children.text: saṅkocitā samucitā na tu tadvad ātmā ||JGc_1,33.35||
children.translated_text: that [body] is appropriately contracted, but the Self is not likewise [contractable]!' ||33.35||

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta kim ahaṃ vakṣyāmi ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Alas! What shall I say?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tatrabhavatā tad idaṃ saṅgīrṇaṃ gīrṇam ācariṣyate-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'By your honor, this which has been assimilated and absorbed shall be enacted:

children.text: yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān |
jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham ||[BhP 10.45.23] iti |
children.translated_text: your kinsmen — we shall come to see them, having established the happiness of friends!' ||[BhP 10.45.23] — thus.
'Go, all of you, to <s>Vraja</s>, O father! And we, the ones grieved by the affection of

children.text:
tad idam eva bhavad-āśvāsanaṃ teṣāṃ viśvāsya śaśvāyamānatām ācariṣyati |
[56] kṛṣṇa uvāca-kadāham āgamiṣyāmi ?
children.translated_text:
This very assurance of yours will effect an everlasting faith in them.'
[56] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'When shall I return?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-yadā suhṛdāṃ hṛdayaṅgamaṃ sukham utpatsyate |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'When the heart-penetrating happiness of [your] friends shall arise.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tac ca kadā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'And when will that be?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-teṣāṃ sukhasyotpattaye tu dūraṃ vyāptum unmukhaṃ bhavitā |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'For the arising of their happiness, [your activity] shall become directed toward pervading far.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-aho bata ! viyatīva kiyatī vyāptis tatra ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Ah alas! Like the sky — how vast will that pervasion be?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tat-tat-kārya-jālataḥ kāla-kṣepaaṃ kṣepayaty api bhavati yāvat kaṃsa-pakṣa-lakṣa-vidhvaṃsanaṃ, yāvad-bhavat-putrādi-vicitra-sampad-gaṇaś ca sampatsyate |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'From the net of various necessary tasks, [the delay] shall extend the passage of time, until the destruction of the host of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> faction has been accomplished, and until the multitude of your sons and other marvelous possessions shall come to fruition.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-aho mahātman! mahad vyasanaṃ khalu mayi nyasanam āyāsyati | yatho dīrghasūtratā mama bandhanāya nirbandham āpatsyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Ah, great soul! A great calamity indeed — the placement [of burdens] upon me — will come to pass! For this procrastination will forcibly bind me!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-mā tāpam āpadyatha, bhavataḥ svabhāva evāyam, yat kadācid antraṅgāṇāṃ parivāra-saṅghānāṃ sukha-bhaṅgaṃ svāṅgānām iva viṣahya bahiraṅgāṇāṃ duḥkha-bhaṅgaṃ karomi |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Do not fall into sorrow! This is indeed your very nature — that "Sometimes, enduring the disruption of the happiness of my intimate retinues as if [it were the disruption] of my own limbs, I accomplish the destruction of the suffering of those who are external."'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-bhavatu, bhāvi-kathā prathyatām | tatra madīya-durvṛttatām ayaṃ vraja-duḥkha-vṛttaṃ tāvad āstām, pura-vṛttaṃ purastād anuvartyatām, yenāham uparaktas tatra niṣpratibhatāṃ vyaktam āpsyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'So be it. Let the future narrative be set forth! As for my misconduct there — let the account of <s>Vraja's</s> suffering remain aside for now. Let the city-narrative be continued forward, by which I, being engaged there, shall clearly attain unrivaledness.'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-sāmprataṃ tava gāyatra-vratam eva sa-gargeṇa vasudevādi-yadu-vargeṇa prathayiṣyate | yatra ca vrajataḥ karṇī-rathārohiṇī rohiṇī ca tatra neṣyate, na tu vraja-janaḥ kaścit | kṣātra-vidhāna-pātratayā tan-nirmāṇe tasya nirmāṇa-duḥkhaṃ duḥkhanana-mūlaṃ bhavitā iti |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'At present, your <s>Gāyatrī</s>-initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) ceremony shall be publicized by the <s>Yadu</s> clan of <s>Vasudeva</s> and others, together with <s>Garga</s>. And there, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, who rides in the ear-chariot, shall be taken there, but no person from <s>Vraja</s> [shall go]. Since he [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] is worthy of the <s>kṣatriya</s>-rite procedure, the sorrow of the construction of that [ritual] shall become the root of the sorrow of the destruction [i.e., departure].'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svagatam idam adhigatavān-hanta prasaṅgatas tad-duḥkham evāsaṅgaṃ labhate | man-mātṛ-saṅginī hi sā rohiṇī kathaṃ tad-bhaṅginī bhaviṣyati iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> inwardly perceived this: 'Alas! Incidentally, that very sorrow obtains spontaneously! For that <s>Rohiṇī</s>, being the companion of my mother — how will she become the one who breaks [the connection] with her?'

children.text: tataḥ kathāntaraṃ pṛcchāma iti spaṣṭaṃ papraccha-tatas tad-vratācārānantaraṃ kintarām ācariṣyāmi ?
children.translated_text: Then, [saying] 'Let us ask about another matter,' he asked plainly: 'Then, after the conduct of that initiation-rite, what further shall I do?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tataḥ sāndīpani-sandīpita-vidyā-sabhām avantīm āsādyānavadya-vidyā-samudāyāya bhrātarau yuvām akātarau sa-brahmacāritayā gaurava-saṅkulatayā gauravaṃ kulam eṣyatha | yatra sakṛn-nigada-mātreṇa sarvāṃ vidyām adhīyantau dhārayantau ca sarvataś camatkāram arpayiṣyathaḥ | yatredaṃ sakhedam upaślokayan mahāṃl loka-saṅghaḥ parasparaṃ savismayam ālokayiṣyati | yathā-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then, having reached <s>Avantī</s> (Ujjain) — the assembly illuminated by <s>Sāndīpani's</s> learning — you two brothers, undaunted, with the conduct of <s>brahmacārins</s>, with the weight of veneration, shall bring honor to the lineage. Where, merely by a single utterance, learning and retaining all knowledge, you two shall bestow wonder everywhere. And there, reciting this [verse] with sorrow, a great assembly of people shall look at one another with wonder. As follows:

children.text: aṅgaṃ pallava-komalaṃ prabhavanaṃ lakṣmī-parārdhāśritaṃ
children.translated_text: 'His limbs tender as sprouts, his dwelling the half-summit of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,

children.text: sevyatvaṃ sama-sevakāyuta-mano-rājyābham udbhrājate |
children.translated_text: his worthiness of service shining like the mind-kingdom of equal attendants in myriads —

children.text: yasya śrī-ramaṇasya so' pi nitarāṃ vāgīśvarī-lobhano' py
children.translated_text: he who is the beloved of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — even he, exceedingly captivating to <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of speech) —

children.text: ācāryāṇy upadiṣṭa-kāṣṭha-ghaṭanaṃ śarma-śriyā nirmame ||JGc_1,33.36||
children.translated_text: fashioned, with the bliss of happiness, the fuel-chopping instructed by teachers!' ||33.36||

children.text: tad evaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭhi-mātraikr aho-rātraiḥ sarvāsv api kalāsvadhītinā bhavatā guru-patnī-bhikṣita-pañca-jana-bhakṣita-tat-putrānayana-maya-dakṣiṇā-nivedane cedaṃ lokā vyativedayiṣyante | yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, when you — having mastered all the arts in sixty-four day-and-nights — shall offer the <s>guru-dakṣiṇā</s> (teacher's fee) consisting of bringing back the son of the guru's wife, who had been devoured by <s>Pañcajana</s> — the people shall proclaim this. As follows:

children.text: vastv asti yat tad gurave pradīyatām
children.translated_text: 'An object exists — let it be given to the guru;

children.text: adurlabhaṃ ced athavā sudurlabham |
children.translated_text: if not hard to obtain, or even exceedingly hard to obtain —

children.text: naṣṭaṃ vapur yad gurujasya tad vapuṣ-
children.translated_text: the lost body of the guru's son — that body,

children.text: mantaṃ yamāt paśyatam ānināya saḥ ||JGc_1,33.37||
children.translated_text: enveloped [in death] — behold! — he brought it back from <s>Yama</s>!' ||33.37||

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text: yamād api samānetā gurv-apatyaṃ tvayā yadā |
children.translated_text: 'When the guru's child was brought back by you even from <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: vivaderan mukhe tarhi miryeran narayo hṛdi ||JGc_1,33.38||
children.translated_text: then the mouths [of people] shall quarrel, and the hells shall die in their hearts!' ||33.38||

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svagatam-na jāne, janena tad varṇyamānam ākarṇya niravalambatāṃ saṃvalamānānāṃ mayy anukampā-sampātavatām ambādīnāṃ kā daśā bhavatā yā samprati ca mama hṛt-kampāya sampadyate | [71] bhavatu, prastāvāntaraṃ vistārayāmaḥ iti spaṣṭam ācaṣṭa-bhagavan ! ko' sau pañcajanaḥ ?
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [thought] to himself: 'I do not know what condition it shall be for my mother and the others, who are full of compassion and dependent upon me, when the people describe and I hear of that [feat]. And this indeed presently arises to make my heart tremble.'
[71] 'So be it — let us expand another topic!' — thus he spoke plainly: 'O venerable one! Who is that <s>Pañcajana</s>?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-jaya-vijayavat kasmāccit kāraṇāc-chaṅkhāsuratāṃ prāpto' sau prasiddhaḥ śaṅkha-viśeṣa eva | tvaṃ ca tad-aṅgam ādāsyase | kintu-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Like <s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s>, due to some cause, he has attained the state of a conch-demon — he is that well-known, special conch itself. And you shall take his body. But:

children.text: yadā yadā dhmāpayitā bhavān daraṃ
children.translated_text: 'Whenever you shall cause the conch to be blown,

children.text: netre tad-ārdre iva te bhaviṣyataḥ |
children.translated_text: then your two eyes will become as if moist;

children.text: labdhaṃ yaśodā-stana-pānajaṃ sukhaṃ
children.translated_text: the happiness obtained from drinking at <s>Yaśodā's</s> breast —

children.text: kṛpā-bhareṇa smaraṇa-prathāvataḥ ||JGc_1,33.39||
children.translated_text: from the weight of compassion, from the spreading of remembrance!' ||33.39||

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sodvegam uvāca-etad vastūddeśaṃ vinā kathāntaraṃ prastūyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with agitation: 'Let another topic be introduced, without reference to that subject!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-kiñcid anyad alpaṃ śrūyatām | vitta-vidyas tvaṃ mathurāyām āgata-mātraḥ śrīmad-vrajāya kṛta-yātras tatratya-pitrādibhiḥ kṛta-saṅkocanas tad-ājñā-laṅghanaṃ nāyatyāṃ maṅgalam iti racita-vicāratayā carita-śocanaḥ svānukūlya-kaivalya-lasad-uddhavam ativinītam uddhavam evābhinītaṃ matvā vraja-janānām āvijamānatā-jananāya niyojayiṣyasi | teṣāṃ saṅkocata eva na ca vraja-janam ātmopahṛtam āhariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Let something else, briefly, be heard! You, the knower of wealth and learning, having barely arrived in <s>Mathurā</s>, having undertaken the journey to glorious <s>Vraja</s>, being constrained by the father and others there — fashioning deliberation with the reasoning that "transgressing their command would not be auspicious in the future" — lamenting what has transpired, considering the supremely modest <s>Uddhava</s>, who shines solely in devotion to you, as the suitable one — you shall deploy him for the purpose of generating awareness in the people of <s>Vraja</s>. And from their very constraint, you shall not bring the people of <s>Vraja</s> — offered up by yourself — back [to Mathurā].'

children.text: te hy evaṃ rahasyaṃ maṃsyante, kṛṣṇasya vraja-mātra-tṛṣṇasya vraja-deśe praveśe punar lambhanaṃ vipralambhataḥ stambhanam eva lapsyate | vraja-janasyātra praveśaś ca tathāveśa eveti | atha vraja-janaḥ sa ca svayam api nayāsyati | jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmaḥ [BhP 10.45.13] iti rahasya-tvad-vacanasya bhavadbhis tu nāgamyatām iti svārasya-bhaṅga-prasaṅgaḥ syād iti |
children.translated_text: 'For they shall think thus in secret: "If <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who thirsts only for <s>Vraja</s>, gains re-entry into the land of <s>Vraja</s>, then the deception shall attain [only] the paralysis of separation. And the entry of the <s>Vraja</s>-folk there [in Mathurā] would itself be a [further] entanglement." And the <s>Vraja</s>-folk and he himself too would [eventually] come [to Mathurā]. "We shall come to see your kinsmen" [BhP 10.45.13] — regarding this secret utterance of yours, [the thought would arise]: "But let them not come" — [for] there would be an occasion for the disruption of spontaneity.'

children.text: tathā svārasyam api tādṛśa-tan-mantraṇāyantraṇayā, na tu svatantratayā | kiṃ ca, tava cetasi yaḥ ko' py anyaḥ saṅkocaḥ samprati sampratītiṃ vinārocamānatāṃ pratipannavān asti | so' pi vraja-bhūmāv āvrajanādi-varjane sāhāyakaṃ muhur nirvāhayitā |
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, the spontaneity too [is governed] by the restraint of such deliberation with them — and not by independence. Moreover, some other constraint in your heart, which at present has attained the state of being unpleasing without being understood, also exists. That too shall repeatedly serve as an aid in the avoidance of journeying to the land of <s>Vraja</s> and such.'

children.text: vraja-janaṃ prati tad idaṃ tu vedavad aparatantraṃ mantraṃ nivedayiṣyasi | samprati ca bhavatāṃ sambandhe jarāsandhādibhiḥ kṛtānusandhe tatrāpi nirb andhāt kaṭakena dhāṭī ghaṭayiṣyate iti |
children.translated_text: 'And to the people of <s>Vraja</s>, you shall convey this counsel — subordinate [to a higher purpose] like the <s>Veda</s>. And at present, since in the matter of your connection, <s>Jarāsandha</s> and others have made their investigation — even there, from insistence, an assault by an army shall be contrived.'

children.text: tathāsminn uddhava-dvārā pitrādiṣu vācika-patrikā, yathā-
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, through <s>Uddhava</s>, a verbal message to the parents and others, as follows:'

children.text: sambandhād vaḥ samantād aham api sa tathā yāmi taṃ vṛṣṇi-vṛnde
children.translated_text: 'By connection with you, I too go likewise to that <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan on all sides;

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ prāṇa-yogya-praṇaya-bhuvi tathaivāvanaṃ saṃvidhitse |
children.translated_text: and in the realm of love worthy of your life-breaths, I wish to arrange protection likewise!

children.text: kintv eṣā mūrtir atra svayam api tu bhavat-pārśva-vartī mamātmā
children.translated_text: But this form of mine here — my very Self — dwells at your side;

children.text: kiṃ vā mūrtiś ca tasmin bhavati hi bhavatāṃ sphūrtir eva pramāṇam ||JGc_1,33.40||
children.translated_text: or rather, in that [<s>Vraja</s>] is the form — indeed, your perception alone is the proof!' ||33.40||

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: āyāsyāmīti kiṃ jalped baddhaḥ praṇaya-rajjūbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'How shall he who is bound by the ropes of love say "I shall come"?

children.text: yena baddhas tu tasyecchām anicchāṃ cānuyāti saḥ ||JGc_1,33.41||
children.translated_text: He who is thus bound follows the wish and unwish of that [love]!' ||33.41||

children.text: śrī-vasudevādīnāṃ deva-dviḍ-upadravasya vidravaḥ khalu bhavad-abhimata eveti tu mayā matam eva |
children.translated_text: 'The dispelling of the affliction of the enemies of the gods upon the glorious <s>Vasudeva</s> and others is indeed your own desire — such is my view.'

children.text: atha purastād uddhava-darśana-mātreṇa ca te parama-sukhaṃ prāpsyanti | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: 'And beforehand, merely by the sight of <s>Uddhava</s>, they shall attain supreme happiness. For:'

children.text: aparicaye' py avalokād bhaktaṃ bhaktaḥ piparti kṛṣṇasya |
children.translated_text: 'Even without acquaintance, by a mere glance, a devotee nourishes a devotee of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: svaramātrāt tad-gānārambhaḥ sujanaṃ pramodayati ||JGc_1,33.42||
children.translated_text: by a mere note, the commencement of that [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] song delights the good!' ||33.42||

children.text: tataś ca tava viśleṣān nava-navārtās te tvad-vārtām eva vārtām anuvartamānāḥ śīghram iva viyanti kiyanti māsā vāsarāṇīva taṃ katicin māsān vāsayitvā paryavasāne tad-dvārā sambhāvanām evāpekṣya mudrita-mukhena svasti-mukhena sandekṣyanti, yathā-
children.translated_text: 'And then, from separation from you, suffering ever-renewed anguish, those who follow only the news of your news — they shall pass some months as if quickly, like days. And having kept him [<s>Uddhava</s>] for some months, at the end, expecting only the greeting through him, they shall behold [him] with sealed faces and faces of benediction, as follows:'

children.text: īśvaras tvam iti so' yam asmākaṃ
children.translated_text: '"You are the Lord" — thus this <s>Uddhava</s>

children.text: uddhavaḥ samupadiśya gacchati |
children.translated_text: of ours instructs and departs;

children.text: putra tat tu na vayaṃ sma man-mahe
children.translated_text: but, O son, that we do not believe,

children.text: śrīśa tā kim u sute na rocate ||JGc_1,33.43||
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Śrī</s> — does that not please you, O son?' ||33.43||

children.text: kiṃ ca-
yady aho suta bhavān adhīśvaras
children.translated_text: 'If indeed, O son, you are the supreme Lord,

children.text: tarhy api sphuratu te padābjayoḥ |
children.translated_text: then even so, let there shine at your lotus-feet

children.text: prītir atra ca paratra naḥ sadā
children.translated_text: love for us, here and hereafter, always —

children.text: kṛṣṇatām anu yataḥ satṛṣṇatā ||JGc_1,33.44||
children.translated_text: since, following [your] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-nature, there is thirst!' ||33.44||
Moreover:

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-uddhavas tu kiṃ māṃ vakṣyate ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'And what shall <s>Uddhava</s> say to me?'

children.text:
ṛṣir uvāca-
vinā candraṃ śaral-lakṣmīr vinā puṣpaṃ madhūnnatiḥ |
vinā payodaṃ varṣā-śrīr vinā tvāṃ kā vraja-sthitiḥ ||iti |
kṛṣṇaḥ sāsram uvāca-yad vraje mama vilamba-saṃvalana-kāraṇaṃ viśeṣeṇa ca varṇaya |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with tears: 'Describe in particular the reason for the delay in my prolonged [stay and] return to <s>Vraja</s>!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tatra bhaktaṃ bhajamānasya kavacaṃ bibhrāṇasya śatrūn nighnānasya tava vyāsaṅgāntaram api labdhāntaratām āpsyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'There, while you are serving your devotee, wearing your armor, and slaying enemies — even another interval of engagement shall attain an opening.'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sodvegam uvāca-hanta kiṃ tat ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with agitation: 'Alas! What is that?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-yat khalu vasudeva-svasrīyāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhirādīnāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa duṣṭa-bhraṣṭa-rāṣṭrī-kṛtānāṃ pakṣasya puṣṭīkaraṇāya bhavitā | te ca tvām eva paramātiṣṭhamānā bhakta-vaśyatāṃ vāvaśyamānasya tava kaitava-rahita-bhakti-bhāja iti | yad-arthaṃ prathamatas tāvad abhijātam abhijātaṃ cākrūraṃ dūtatayā dūram āpayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'It shall be for the strengthening of the faction of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and others — the sons of <s>Vasudeva's</s> sister — who have been made into exiles with a ruined kingdom by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>. And they, relying supremely upon you — as you who are compelled by devotee-submissiveness — are recipients of devotion free from deceit! For that purpose, first you shall send the noble-born <s>Akrūra</s>, well-born, as an emissary far [away].'

children.text: prakṛta-vyāsaṅgaḥ punar aṅgībhūtaḥ prabhūta eva | yataḥ kaṃsa-pakṣa-nirharaṇaṃ tadāpi tvayā kṛtākṛtam eva vartsyati |
children.translated_text: 'The relevant engagement, however, having become integral, shall be considerable indeed. For the elimination of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> faction shall still remain partly done and partly undone by you.'

children.text: tathā hi-varākeṣu kaṃsa-pakṣīyeṣu cānyeṣu tīrtha-kākatāṃ gateṣu yat khalv astiḥ prāptiś ceti tasya tatra kalatra-dvayam asti |
children.translated_text: 'For thus — among the wretched ones belonging to <s>Kaṃsa's</s> faction, and among others who have gone to the state of <s>tīrtha</s>-crows (merely going through the motions), there is one — "<s>Asti</s>" — and his attainment — he has two wives there.'

children.text: tat punar vaidhavyenāndhībhūtam iva sva-bandhu-jana-dattānusandhībhavat-pitṛtayā dhṛtāśvāsa-nirbandhaṃ jarāsandhaṃ gamiṣyati | yatra ca-
children.translated_text: 'Those two, as if blinded by widowhood, becoming objects of the investigation of their own kinsmen bestowing fatherly [protection], maintaining the insistence of consolation, shall go to <s>Jarāsandha</s>. And there:'

children.text: ||JGc_1,33.45|| MISSING!
children.translated_text: ||33.45|| MISSING!

children.text: visrasta-keśaveśādyos tayoḥ kaṃsasya bhāryayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even travelers shall behold — and shall laugh at —

children.text: drakṣyanti vihasiṣyanti cāṅgāni pathikā api ||JGc_1,33.46||
children.translated_text: the limbs of those two wives of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, whose hair-arrangements and attire are disheveled!' ||33.46||

children.text: tatas tat-preraṇayā jarāsandhaḥ prāpta-jarāsandha iva kāla-rūptāvantaḥ bhavantam eva trayoviṃśati-saṅkhyābhir akṣauhiṇībhir abhiyāsyati |
children.translated_text: 'Then, by their instigation, <s>Jarāsandha</s>, as if having attained a rejuvenation of his old age, time's puppet from <s>Avantī</s>, shall attack you with twenty-three <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> armies!'

children.text:
tādṛśatāṃ bhṛśam avidvān kīṭaka iva kṛpīṭa-yonim |
  abhiyāya cābhiyā mathurāṃ mathnann ivāvariṣyati ||JGc_1,33.47||tataś ca-
indv-arka-dyota-keliṃ kutuka-kalanayā nirmimāṇāv adhṛṣyau
children.translated_text: 'You two, creating the sport of moon-and-sun brilliance with the play of curiosity, invincible,

children.text: jārāsandhaṃ tad-andhaṃ tama iva kaṭakaṃ troṭayantau bhavantau |
children.translated_text: shall shatter that <s>Jārāsandha</s> army, blind [in its darkness], like darkness itself!

children.text: ekaṃ taṃ māgadheśaṃ tama iva ghṛṇayā bāḍham utsṛjya parva-
children.translated_text: Yet that one lord of <s>Magadha</s> alone, like darkness, out of contempt, you shall boldly release;

children.text: prāptaṃ sarvaṃ sva-bhaktaṃ sva-mahasi dadhatau bhāsyataḥ śaśvad eva ||JGc_1,33.48||
children.translated_text: and all your own devotees, obtained at the festival, you shall hold in your own glory — [thus] you two shall shine forever!' ||33.48||

'Not knowing such [power] at all, like a worm [approaching] a fire-pit,
having approached and attacked <s>Mathurā</s>, he shall besiege it as if churning [it]!' ||33.47||
And then:

children.text: evaṃ saptadaśa-svapyati-sampāteṣv apayāteṣu kūṭīkṛta-mleccha-koṭi-traya-prakaṭa-kaṭakaḥ samahāyavanaḥ kāla-yavanaḥ prātar evātidūrataḥ sāmudra-pūra ivālokiṣyate, yena nīvṛd eva nivṛto bhavitā |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, when seventeen assaults have come and gone, <s>Kālayavana</s> — whose army consists of revealed hosts of three crores of <s>Mlecchas</s>, marshalled in deception, accompanied by the great <s>Yavana</s> [force] — shall be seen from a very great distance the very next morning, like an ocean-flood — whereby even retreat shall become the retreat.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-bhūri-dūratayā śātrava-pātratā-rahitaḥ sa kasmād asmākam ahitatām āpsyati ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Being of exceedingly great distance, and devoid of the qualification of enmity — why would he attain hostility toward us?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-yadu-varga-vādita-gārgyārādhita-bharga-vara-sphurad-upasarga-jani-sargata eva yādava-davaṃ prati bhaya-dava-visarga-nirargale tasmin jarāsandhānusandhānād eva | sa cātrāvaśya-maraṇa-vaśatyām āpsyatīti mat-preraṇāc ca ?
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Precisely from the creation born of the emergent boon of <s>Bharga</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), worshipped by <s>Gārgya</s>, who was mocked by the <s>Yadu</s> clan — in that unstoppable conflagration of terror against the <s>Yādava</s> fire — from the very investigation of <s>Jarāsandha</s>! And that he shall attain the subjection of inevitable death there — is it not also from my own instigation?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-kathaṃ tarhi tasya garhitasya maraṇaṃ bhavitā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'How then shall the death of that despicable one come about?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-garhitatvam eva tattvataḥ khalv ahitaṃ kāraṇam | prakāraṃ cāmuṃ sahāsyam udgāsyanti-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'His despicableness itself is truly the unwholesome cause. And this manner [of his death], they shall proclaim with laughter:'

children.text: śītaṃ mahas tad anusṛtya mukunda-mūrter
children.translated_text: 'Following the cool radiance of <s>Mukunda's</s> form,

children.text: mlecchādhirāḍ adhi tamaḥ-kaṭu-kīṭa-tulyaḥ |
children.translated_text: the overlord of the <s>Mlecchas</s>, equal to a worm in bitter darkness,

children.text: eṣa jvalaj-jalanavan mucukunda-tejaḥ
children.translated_text: from contact with the blazing fire-like splendor of <s>Mucukunda</s>,

children.text: saṅgād alaṃ valita-vismiti bhasmati sma ||JGc_1,33.49||
children.translated_text: was abundantly burnt to ashes, filled with astonishment!' ||33.49||

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaḥ svagatam adhigatavān-na jāne yojana-śatakam ardati tasmin durdama-durjana-saṃmarde mat-pramada-satra-vraja-tulya-vrajaḥ parikṣiptatayā vikṣipta-cittaḥ kutra vā vrajiṣyati ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> inwardly perceived: 'I do not know — when that uncontrollable, villainous tumult burns for a hundred <s>yojanas</s> — my <s>Vraja</s>, which is like a sacrifice-enclosure of my beloveds, being surrounded [by it] — with agitated mind — where shall it go?'

children.text: ṛṣis tu tad-abhiprayan prathayati sma-kāmyakataḥ paścimāyāṃ diśi giri-taṭa-gata-gariṣṭhāṭavīm aṭiṣyati | kintu bhavatā yādavānām iva vraja-bhavanānām aritas taniṣyamāṇa-santāpa-santānābhāvāya tad idaṃ cintayiṣyate |
children.translated_text: The sage, however, understanding his intention, proclaimed: 'It shall wander in the formidable forest on the mountain-slope in the western direction from <s>Kāmyaka</s>. But you shall deliberate upon this for the sake of preventing the anguish that shall extend from enemies toward the <s>Vraja</s>-homes, just as toward the <s>Yādavas</s>.'

children.text:
samprati śaraṇāgatatayā kṛta-mad-anusaraṇānāṃ yādavānām avanāya yuktatayā niyukta ivāsmi |
[100] tatas tatra gariṣṭhaṃ prakoṣṭhāntaraṃ vidheyam | tanta yadi govardhana-dharaṇataḥ-
children.translated_text:
'At present, as if appointed by propriety for the protection of the <s>Yādavas</s> who, having taken refuge, have followed me —
[100] therefore, a great fortress-enclosure must be constructed there. If, on the basis of [the precedent of] the lifting of <s>Govardhana</s>:'

children.text: tasmān mac-charaṇaṃ goṣṭhaṃ man-nāthaṃ mat-parigraham |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore my shelter — the cow-settlement, my lord, my possessions —

children.text: gopāye svātma-yogena so æyaṃ me vrata āhitaḥ ||[BhP 10.25.18]
children.translated_text: I shall protect by the <s>yoga</s> of my own Self — this is my vow established!' ||[BhP 10.25.18]||

children.text: ity anusṛtya kṛta-rakṣāṇāṃ mat-prāṇāvali-lakṣāṇām iva vrajādhyakṣāṇāṃ yady arayas te ca rayād vighna-nighnatāṃ kariṣyanti | tadā sarvam eva kharvaṃ syāt | teṣām aṭavīṣu go-koṭi-lakṣa-rakṣakāṇāṃ rakṣā ca prakoṣṭha-ghaṭanayā durghaṭā |
children.translated_text: 'Following this, if the enemies of the <s>Vraja</s>-chiefs — who are under my protection, who are like rows of my life-breaths — shall forcibly create an obstacle-destroying [attack], then everything shall be stunted. And the protection of those who guard millions of cows in the forests shall be difficult to accomplish by the construction of a fortress.'

children.text: tathā-
children.translated_text: 'Likewise:'

children.text: rahī-bhūta-marū-bhūtaṃ cakṣū-bhūtaṃ manī-kṛtam |
children.translated_text: 'That which is one's path, one's desert, one's eye, one's mind —

children.text: yasya yat tat kathaṃ tena tyajyatāṃ vyajyatām api ||
children.translated_text: how can that be abandoned, even if it be manifested, by that one?' ||

children.text: iti nyāyena tatra samprati gamanam api tatrakīya-saṅkoca-viśeṣata eva viśeṣataḥ prasahya mahyaṃ na rocate | saṅkocāntaraṃ tu tasy anāntarīyakam eva manye | tataḥ samprati sākṣān mama tatra sthitim api na lakṣayāmi, tasmāt teṣu bahiḥ-śaśvad-udāsīnatā-vinyasanam eva mayi tad-upāsīnatāyāṃ pravīṇatām ācarati |
children.translated_text: 'By this principle, even the journey there at present, especially from the particular constraint of those there, does not forcibly please me. But I consider another constraint to be its inevitable [consequence]. Therefore, I do not at present discern even my own abiding there — hence, the placement of outward perpetual indifference toward them, while I am seated in their devotion, alone attains proficiency.'

children.text: tata eva śatravas tatra mad-bahiraṅgatāyā jānānā gṛhṇīran iti |
children.translated_text: 'For that very reason — enemies, knowing my externality there, would seize [the opportunity].'

children.text: tad evaṃ vrajata udāsīnāyamānasya tava tādṛśa-cintā-mātreṇācintya-śaktyā drāg eva dūrataḥ samudrāntaḥ-purī-viśeṣasya vyaktyā tatra ca yadūnāṃ jhaṭiti prasaktyā tam urīkariṣyasi | tad-anantaram eva kāla-yavane kālavad ācariṣyasi | mucukundaṃ ca prati mukundatvaṃ kunda-sundara-danta-kandalita-manda-hāsa-maya-samaya-racana-vacana-vilāsataḥ kṛpām ullāsayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, for you who are departing and becoming indifferent — by the mere thought of such a nature, with inconceivable power, swiftly, from afar, by the manifestation of a special city within the ocean, and by the swift attachment of the <s>Yadus</s> there — you shall accept that [city]. Immediately thereafter, upon <s>Kālayavana</s>, you shall act as <s>Kāla</s> (Death) acts. And toward <s>Mucukunda</s>, you shall cause compassion to blossom as <s>Mukunda</s>-ness — through the grace of words composed of the gentle smile blossoming from teeth beautiful as <s>kunda</s> flowers.'

children.text: atha mathurām eva rāmeṇa saha sahacara-yadu-kumāra-vṛtaḥ pratigatya patyabhāvavataḥ puruṣā mleccatas tān mleccha-yodhān nidhanam eva rodhayamānas tad-amāna-dhanāni nija-rājadhānīti dvārakāṃ hārayann api mleccha-paricchadatayā manasi nācchatāṃ maṃsyase |
children.translated_text: 'Then, having returned to <s>Mathurā</s> itself together with <s>Rāma</s>, accompanied by <s>Yadu</s> youths as companions — while those men, bereft of masters, were consigning those <s>Mleccha</s> warriors to death — even while making their wealth produce your own capital-city called <s>Dvārakā</s>, you shall not consider it pleasing in your mind, because of its <s>Mleccha</s> provenance.'

children.text: atha punaḥ punar jāta iva sa rājā jarā-jātaḥ pūrva-pūrvavad eva madhupurīm avaruddhānas tad-dhana-hartṝṇāṃ bhartṝn yuṣmān eva pratabhigamiṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'Then, that king, as if born again and again, aged <s>Jarāsandha</s>, just as before, having besieged <s>Madhupurī</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>), shall attack you — the lords and bearers of his wealth.'

children.text: tataś ca tad-dhanānām avarakṣaṇāya nija-janānāṃ rakṣaṇāya cākṣāma-śyāma-śubhra-vapuṣau parama-puruṣau kutuka-viśeṣād avyañjita-ruṣau śubhavantau bhavantau sa-dravam apadravantau tad-dharṣata iva vastutas tu tad-dharṣataḥ pravarṣaṇākhyaṃ girim ārokṣyathaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And then, for the non-protection of his wealth and for the protection of your own people, you two — of resplendent dark-and-fair forms, supreme persons — from particular curiosity, with undisplayed anger, auspicious, you two shall run away fluidly, as if fleeing from him but in truth [fleeing] from his violence, and shall ascend the mountain named <s>Pravarṣaṇa</s>.'

children.text: āruhya ca taṃ tu druhadbhiḥ prasahya dahyamānam ujjhantāv ekādaśa-yojana-samuttuṅga-śṛṅgād utplutya bhūri-dūraṃ yuvāṃ patiṣyathaḥ | patitvā ca dvārakā-patitām āgamiṣyathaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And having ascended it, when it is being forcibly burned by those assailants — abandoning it, leaping from its peak, eleven <s>yojanas</s> high, you two shall fall a great distance! And having fallen, you shall come to <s>Dvārakā</s>-fallen [state]!'

children.text: sa tu vāṃ pratāpam avidan nija-paścāt-tāpa-pāpa-pādapa-bījāyamānam abhiśāpaṃ hṛdi vāpaṃ vāpaṃ gṛham avāpsyati | gīrvāṇa-śreṇyākāśa-vāṇyā tu hasiṣyate-
children.translated_text: But he, not knowing the might of you two, shall sow in his heart the seed of the accursed tree of his own future remorse, and shall return home. And by the voice from the sky of the host of celestials, he shall be mocked:

children.text: mṛdhe tu vijitaṃ purā tvam asi yad-dvayenāmunā
children.translated_text: 'You were formerly defeated in battle by these two;

children.text: sa saptadaśa-bārakaṃ vijita eva kiṃ tad-girā |
children.translated_text: shall he who was defeated seventeen times be [restored] merely by their word?

children.text: aho sakutuka-drave prakaṭam adya cājī yathā
children.translated_text: Ah! In the curious flight, clearly, as in a [chariot] race today —

children.text: jarā-suta na yad-dhruvaṃ tam adasīyamānarcchitha ||JGc_1,33.50||
children.translated_text: O son of old age (<s>Jarāsandha</s>)! — that which you did not certainly give, you [merely] yearned for!' || (JGc 1,33.50)

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-labdha-durgāṇāṃ yadu-vargāṇāṃ balaṃ vā teṣāṃ balam eva vāvalambanaṃ vidhāya tadāpi kiṃ vrajaṃ nāvrajiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Having made either the strength of the <s>Yadu</s> groups who have obtained fortresses, or their strength alone, as my support — even then, shall I not return to <s>Vraja</s>?'

children.text: ṛṣir svagatam āha sma-aho tādṛśi saṅkoce' py etādṛg-asyotkaṇṭhā mādṛg-antabuddhiṃ kuṇṭhayati iti |
children.translated_text: The sage said to himself: 'Ah! Even in such a difficulty, his longing of this kind blunts the inner understanding of one such as me!'

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ tu spaṣṭaṃ kāraṇam ācaṣṭa-ekasmin kaṃse dhvaṃsite bahavas tat-sambandhi-bāndhavā jarāsandhavat kaṃsāyiṣyante, katham āgamanaṃ syāt ?
children.translated_text: And he spoke the reason plainly: 'When the one <s>Kaṃsa</s> is destroyed, many kinsmen associated with him — like <s>Jarāsandha</s> — shall become [new] <s>Kaṃsas</s>. How could there be a homecoming?'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-darśana-mātrārtham api na syāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Not even for the sole purpose of a visit?'

children.text: ṛṣiḥ sarūkṣa-hāsam uvāca-nahi nahi |
children.translated_text: The sage said with a rough laugh: 'No, no!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-katham iva ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'How so?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-vasudevādy-anujñāṃ vineti vijñāpitam eva |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Without the permission of <s>Vasudeva</s> and the others — this has been explained.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tarhy āgamanam eva na bhavitā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then the homecoming shall simply not happen!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-bhavitā, kintu kāla-vilambitayā | bhavāṃs tu vrajāgamanaṃ manasi-kṛtya vivāha-kṛtya-vimukhatayā sthāsyati, kintu tad api vyabhicariṣyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'It shall happen, but with the delay of time. And your honor, keeping the return to <s>Vraja</s> in mind, shall stand averse to the conduct of marriage — but even that shall be transgressed.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta kiṃ tatra kāraṇam ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Alas! What is the reason for that?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-raivata-nāmā kaścit prācīnaḥ surājā druhiṇa-vihitatayā rauhiṇeyāya yadā duhitaraṃ vitariṣyati, tadā vasudeva-devaky-ādibhir īḍitair vivāhāya bahudhā vihitāmreḍitaiḥ kṛtaḥ sa ca prayatnas tvayā sapatna iva nānumodiṣyate |
