children.translated_text: The sage said: 'A certain ancient, virtuous king named <s>Raivata</s>, through the arrangement of <s>Brahmā</s>, shall offer his daughter to the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>). Then, by <s>Vasudeva</s>, <s>Devakī</s>, and others, praised and repeatedly urged in many ways for the marriage, that effort — by you, as if [viewing it as] a rival — shall not be approved.'

children.text: tad evam eva vāsara-śate gate kadācit kaścid udvijamāna iva dvijanmā vijane santaṃ bhavantam āvrajiṣyati | āvrajya ca sa dhanyātmā pitṛ-paravatyāś ca para-sātkṛti-maya-svabhayāvṛtatayāpāvṛtāyamānāyā bhīṣmaka-kanyāyāḥ sanyāyāṃ patrikāṃ sāpatrapam iva tvayy arpayiṣyati | tasyāḥ saṅkṣepatas tv ayam artha-vikṣepaḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus, when a hundred days have passed, at some time, a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, as if troubled, shall come to you in seclusion. And having come, that blessed soul shall place in your hands — with some shyness — the letter of <s>Bhīṣmaka's</s> daughter, who — though belonging to her father — had been covered over by the nature of consecration to another, yet was [now] becoming revealed. And the summary of its meaning is as follows:

children.text:
tava svabhāvenākṛṣṭā svasya vā tvayi keśava |
  kṛṣyeya ced balād anyenāsūn madhye jahāmy aham ||JGc_1,33.51|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'Attracted by Your own nature, or if I should be attracted | to You by force by another, O <s>Keśava</s> — | then in the midst [of that], I shall abandon my life-breaths!' || (JGc 1,33.51) — thus.

children.text: tataś ca marma-spṛśā dharma-dṛśā vidharmād bhayaṃ bhāvayamānas tvam anyathā-manyamānatāṃ na lapsyase | kiṃ bahunā, vivāham api nirvāhayiṣyase |
children.translated_text: Then, your heart being touched by the core [of her words], perceiving with the eye of <s>dharma</s> the danger from <s>adharma</s>, you shall not attain the state of thinking otherwise. In short, you shall even carry out the marriage.

children.text: yathā ca loke kathā prathām āpsyati |
children.translated_text: And this is how the story shall spread in the world:

children.text: bhīṣmādri-sthita-rukmiṇī-maṇi-maya-śreṇī-viloka-spṛhāṃ
children.translated_text: 'The princes, having assumed the posture of tigers — craving to behold the

children.text: śārdūla-sthitim āśritā nṛpa-sutās tāvan madān nirmamuḥ |
children.translated_text: rows of jewels that were <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, stationed upon the mountain of <s>Bhīṣma[ka]</s> —

children.text: yāvac-chaṅkha-nināda-garja-dalita-prāgalbhya-tat-tat-sabhā-
children.translated_text: fashioned their prides — until, from the resounding blast of the conch

children.text: madhya-dhvaṃsi-nṛsiṃha-navya-taruṇaś cakre manāṅ nodyamam ||JGc_1,33.52||
children.translated_text: shattering the boldness of each and every assembly — the one like a fresh young <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, destroyer in their midst, made not the slightest effort!' || (JGc 1,33.52)

children.text: tad evaṃ paryayam āgatāyāṃ maryādāyāṃ tādṛśa-paryāyatāṃ kāścd anyāś ca dhanyāḥ kanyās tām ādhivinnāṃ praṇayan pariṇetāsi | tāś ca bhavantam antareṇa na śarīra-sthitim anusareyuḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, when propriety has reached its turn in such a sequence, you shall lovingly marry certain other blessed maidens besides her — the one [first] superseded — and they, without you, would not even maintain their bodily existence — thus.

children.text: tatra satyabhāmāṃ tāvat-pāṇau praṇeṣyasi, yatra jāmbavatīm api saṃvalayiṣyasi, yatra ca jāmbavān kukuda-mudaṃ lapsyate | tathā hi samāsena kathayiṣyanti |
children.translated_text: First, you shall take <s>Satyabhāmā</s> by the hand in marriage, in which connection you shall also bring <s>Jāmbavatī</s> into the fold, and wherein <s>Jāmbavān</s> shall obtain the delight of the hump (i.e., the joy of kinship). Accordingly, they shall narrate in summary:

children.text: prasene niḥsene nija-sahajanau divya-maṇi-bhāg-
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Prasena</s>, bereft of <s>Sena</s>, bearing the divine jewel as his own brother's [inheritance],

children.text: gale siṃha-dhvaste racayad abhiśastaṃ harim asau |
children.translated_text: [had it] destroyed by a lion at the throat — [and people] fabricated a false charge against <s>Hari</s> —

children.text: yadā satrājit-tarhy anumṛtayamāṇo maṇim amuṃ
children.translated_text: when <s>Satrājit</s> [was thus defamed], then he, following the trail of death,

children.text: sa kanyāmṛkṣendrād alabhata sa tasmād api punaḥ ||JGc_1,33.53||
children.translated_text: obtained that jewel together with a maiden from the lord of bears, and then from him [<s>Satrājit</s>] too again!' || (JGc 1,33.53)

children.text: maṇim anveṣṭuṃ cira-rātrāya kāntāraṃ gate tu tvayi parama-kānte punar nirdaratayā bhallūka-daraṃ praviṣṭe dvārakāyāṃ suṣṭhu kaṣṭam āpatiṣyati | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: And when you, the supremely beloved, shall have gone to the wilderness for a long night to search for the jewel, and then — out of utter fearlessness — having entered the bear's cave, great distress shall befall <s>Dvārakā</s>. Because:

children.text: yarhītir bhavataḥ kṛṣṇa tarhītir na tu durlabhā |
children.translated_text: 'When there is departure from You, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then departure [of well-being] is not hard to find;

children.text: akṣṇo rītistu lokānāṃ rītir eva tadā matā ||JGc_1,33.54||
children.translated_text: but the flow of tears from the eyes of the people — that alone is then considered the [natural] flow!' || (JGc 1,33.54)

children.text: prāptāyāṃ saratnāyāṃ satyabhāmāyāṃ ratnaṃ punaḥ svasminn arpite nāragītena satrā satrājitey eva pratyarpayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: When <s>Satyabhāmā</s> has arrived together with the jewel, and the jewel has been offered back to you, you shall — with a song that negates [the need for it] — re-bestow it upon <s>Satrājit</s>'s [family] alone.

children.text: yadā ca pāṇḍavānām uddaṇḍaṃ dāha-vṛttam atathyaṃ kathyamānam ākarṇya tūrṇam eva hastināpuraṃ prasthitau bhaviṣyathaḥ |
children.translated_text: And when you hear the false report of the audacious burning of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, you two shall quickly set forth for <s>Hastināpura</s>.

children.text: tadā garbhe suhitas tvad-ahitaḥ śatadhanvā tu vāṃ dūragau manvānaḥ prāpta-ratnaṃ satrājitaṃ sayatnaṃ sapatnavan nihatya ratnam apahṛtya tac ca karṇaṭiriṭirākāriṇam akrūraṃ pratyapahnutya jñāti-hatyā-bhītyā kuśasthalād avagatya vidroṣyati |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatadhanvā</s>, hostile to you yet delighted in his heart, thinking you two have gone far — shall forcefully slay <s>Satrājit</s> who had obtained the jewel, as if he were a rival, shall steal the jewel, and then — denying [its possession] to <s>Akrūra</s>, who makes a jingling sound — shall flee from <s>Kuśasthalī</s> out of fear of clan-murder, and shall rebel.

children.text: atha svapuram āgatya tad adhigatya tam evānupaditayānusṛtya nihatya ca maṇim asaṅgatya paścād akrūrāt pratipatya svam abhi durjanābhiśāpam ārjavān mārjayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Then, having come to your own city and learned of that, having pursued him following his trail and slain him — yet not finding the jewel — you shall afterward retrieve it from <s>Akrūra</s>, and thus cleanse from yourself the false accusation made by wicked persons.

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svagatm uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to himself:

children.text: saṅgaḥ kvāyaṃ vrajasthānāṃ mad-eka-prāṇatā-juṣām |
children.translated_text: 'Where is this association of those dwelling in <s>Vraja</s>, | who are devoted to me as their sole life-breath?

children.text: kva vā yadūnāṃ satrājic-chatadhanvādi-śālinām ||JGc_1,33.55||
children.translated_text: And where is the [association] of the <s>Yadus</s>, adorned with <s>Satrājit</s>, <s>Śatadhanvā</s>, and the like?' || (JGc 1,33.55)

children.text: athavā-
children.translated_text: Or else —

children.text: bhaved yaḥ proṣya-pāpīyāṃs tasya kiṃ karma śarmadam |
children.translated_text: 'For one who becomes more sinful by being away from home, | what deed would be happiness-giving?

children.text: yad yat karoti tatraiva snātvā kālaka eva saḥ ||JGc_1,33.56||
children.translated_text: Whatever he does, having bathed in that very [deed] — he is merely a spot [of impurity]!' || (JGc 1,33.56)

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ cācaṣṭa-kathāntaraṃ prathyatām | yad-anantaraṃ goṣṭhasthā mamānantarasthā bhaviṣyanti |
children.translated_text: And he spoke plainly: 'Let another narrative be spread! After which, the dwellers of the cow-settlement, my intimates, shall become [reunited with me].'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tad apy āyāsyati śrūyatām | atha bhavatā tās tat-tad-upāyam upāyaṃsateti varṇyamānam ākarṇya mṛgayāyāṃ parītā ravi-duhitā ca tvāṃ varītā | etan nirvarṇya ca janā varṇayiṣyanti | yathā-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'That too shall come — hear! Then, as you shall have employed this and that stratagem for them — and as that is being described — she who was heard of during the hunt, the daughter of the Sun-god (<s>Kālindī</s>), shall choose you. And having observed this, people shall describe it. As follows:

children.text: sūrye jīvati tat-kanyā tam anāpṛcchya paśyata |
children.translated_text: 'While the Sun is alive, his daughter — behold! — without asking him,

children.text: svayaṃ vṛtavatī kṛṣṇaṃ varākī kānyakanyakā ||JGc_1,33.57||
children.translated_text: the wretched maiden (<s>Kālindī</s>) chose <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of her own accord — what a girl!' || (JGc 1,33.57)

children.text: atha rājādhidevyā nandinīṃ mitravindāṃ svayaṃvaraṇena bhavantam anuvindamānāṃ tatra bhrātṛbhyāṃ vindānuvindābhyāṃ nindyamānāṃ yuddhena vindamānaḥ pariṇetāsi |
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Mitravindā</s>, the daughter of the paramount queen (<s>Rājādhidevī</s>), who shall find you through <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice) — being censured by her two brothers <s>Vinda</s> and <s>Anuvinda</s> — you shall win her through battle and marry her.

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-rājādhidevī khalv ānakadundubher bhāginīti bhaṇyate, satrājid api gotrajatayā tarhi katham idaṃ loka-garhitam arhiṣyati ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: '<s>Rājādhidevī</s> is indeed said to be the sister of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), and <s>Satrājit</s> too belongs to the same clan — how then would this, which is censured by the world, be worthy?'

children.text: ṛṣiḥ sa-hāsam uvāca-rājādhidevyā iva śrutakīrter api sutāṃ bhadrām upayaṃsyase |
children.translated_text: The sage said with a laugh: 'Just as [you shall marry] the daughter of <s>Rājādhidevī</s>, you shall also wed <s>Bhadrā</s>, the daughter of <s>Śrutakīrti</s>!'

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ sasaṅkoca-locanam uvāca-tad api katham ?
[137] ṛṣir uvāca-yādava-prabhavāṇām ayam eva kula-krama-samācāraḥ |
[138] kṛṣṇaḥ svagatam uvāca-na khalv idaṃ jñāteyaṃ, kintu kāpeyam eva | tathāpi bhadram evedam æ yasmād anena sambandhena vraja-bandhavas tad idaṃ maṃsyante | nāsau teṣāṃ gotratayā stotra-viṣayatām ātmani manyate, kintu gotrānta-ramitānām asmākam eva iti |
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with contracting eyes: 'And how is even that [permissible]?'
[137] The sage said: 'This is indeed the established clan-custom of those born among the <s>Yādavas</s>.'
[138] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to himself: 'This is surely not [a matter of] kinship, but of cowherdship! Nevertheless, this is indeed auspicious, since by this connection, the kinsmen of <s>Vraja</s> shall consider [that I am still bound to them]. He does not consider himself an object of their praise by clan-relation — rather, [he considers] it pertains to us alone, who are delighted within the clan's boundaries.'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-mitravindām anu cedaṃ vandiṣyante-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Following <s>Mitravindā</s>, they shall praise thus:

children.text: yathārtha-nāmnā sāmnātā mitravindā sva-bandhubhiḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Mitravindā</s>, whose name is true to its meaning, celebrated by her kinsmen —

children.text: sva-mitraṃ vindamānā yā tad-amitrān nirākarot ||JGc_1,33.58||
children.translated_text: she who, finding her own friend (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), rejected those hostile to that friend!' || (JGc 1,33.58)

children.text: bhadrām anu varṇayiṣyanti-
children.translated_text: Following <s>Bhadrā</s>, they shall describe:

children.text: śrutakīrtiḥ sutā-vyājāt kīrtim eva vyajāyata |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrutakīrti</s>, through the pretext of a daughter, gave birth to fame itself;

children.text: kṛṣṇa-sātkṛtitaḥ sā tu bhadrāpy ajani viśrutā ||JGc_1,33.59||
children.translated_text: and she, made precious by <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> acceptance — even <s>Bhadrā</s> became celebrated!' || (JGc 1,33.59)

children.text: atha nāgnajitīm apy udvakṣyasi | yatra saptānāṃ vṛṣabhāṇāṃ yugapad bandhaḥ khalu tat-pitrā paṇa-bandhatayā sthāpayiṣyate | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then you shall also marry <s>Nāgnajitī</s>. Where the simultaneous binding of seven bulls shall be established by her father as a wager-bond. And there:

children.text: yadā tvaṃ sapta-vṛṣabhān udditān ācariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: 'When you shall master the seven designated bulls,

children.text: tadā tvad-gopatāṃ smṛtvā bāṣpaṃ mokṣyāmahe vayam ||JGc_1,33.60||
children.translated_text: then, remembering your cow-herding [in <s>Vraja</s>], we shall shed tears!' || (JGc 1,33.60)

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta yuṣmabhyam api rocate khalv iyaṃ mal-līlā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Alas! Does even this sport of mine please your honors?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-āstām asmad-vārtā | bāḍham asmat-pitre' pi | yathā prārthitaṃ tad bhūri-bhāgyam [BhP 10.14.34] ity ādinā | tatra ca yā kāpi tava preyasī līlā, sā tu parama-śreyasī | yat-sambandhena bhavan-mantra-dvayaṃ mantra-rājatayā pracāritam āvābhyām | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Set aside our affairs! Indeed, even our father [<s>Brahmā</s>] [is pleased]! As he prayed: "That great fortune" [BhP 10.14.34] and so forth. And therein, whatever sport of yours is beloved — that is indeed supremely beneficial. In connection with which, the two <s>mantras</s> concerning you were propagated by us two as king-<s>mantras</s>. For thus:

children.text: nṛpo na hari-sevitā vyaya-kṛtī na hary-arpakaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A king is not one who has not served <s>Hari</s>; a spender is not one who has not offered to <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: kavir na hari-varṇakaḥ śrita-gurur na hary-āśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: a poet is not one who has not described <s>Hari</s>; one who has resorted to a guru is not one who has not taken refuge in <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: guṇī na hari-tatparaḥ sarasa-dhīr naḥ kṛṣṇāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: a man of virtues is not one who is not devoted to <s>Hari</s>; a person of rasa-filled intellect is not one who has not taken shelter of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: sa na vraja-ramānugaḥ sva-hṛdi sapta śalyāni me ||JGc_1,33.61||
children.translated_text: he is not a follower of the beloved of <s>Vraja</s> — these are seven thorns in my heart!' || (JGc 1,33.61)

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svagatam uvāca-sādhīyān mamānubhavaḥ | sa tu na savādhībhavitum arhati | yataś ca na svānubhava evāyam anubhāvaś ca | tan-mano nānyathā manyasva iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to himself: 'More excellent indeed is my experience [of this]. But it ought not become afflicted. For this is not merely his own experience but [his] influential power. Therefore, do not consider his mind otherwise.'

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ ca pṛṣṭavān-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: And he asked plainly: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tad evaṃ kāvya-śreṇīr iva nānā-deśa-veśa-bhāṣā-rasair eṇīdṛśaḥ pāṇaukṛtya pūrva-pūrvavad rāginīṃ madrādhipater api kanyāṃ sanyāyatayā varyāṃ bhāryā-varyāṃ kariṣyasi | na kevalā sā, tāsām adharāḥ ṣoḍaśa-sahasra-parimāṇāś cāparāḥ |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Thus, having taken by the hand — like rows of poetic compositions, with the <s>rasas</s> of various regional costumes and languages — the doe-eyed ones: the daughter of the king of <s>Madra</s> too, through the proper means, as the most excellent — you shall make her the best of wives. And not she alone — beneath them, sixteen thousand others.'

children.text: tatra madra-kanyāyāḥ pariṇaya-nyāyaṃ bhadram evaṃ varṇayiṣyanti-
children.translated_text: There, the manner of marrying the <s>Madra</s> princess shall be beautifully described by them as follows:

children.text: atyuccair bandha -vedhyāprakaṭa-jhaṣa-tanoś chedam ākarṇya paṇyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Hearing the wager of severing the body of a hidden fish, | pierced through exceedingly high bonds —

children.text: kanyāyā madrapātuḥ kṣitipati-niyutāsādhyam ekas tu paścāt |
children.translated_text: of the daughter of the king of <s>Madra</s>, unachievable by millions of kings — one alone, afterward,

children.text: dūrād āgamya paścād api ca viluluve tāṃ harir yaḥ sa paścād
children.translated_text: coming from afar and then afterward too, <s>Hari</s> carried her off; and he who afterward

children.text: bhūtvā tān yuktam ārdad yudhi tad api matāgrīyatā tasya citrā ||JGc_1,33.62||
children.translated_text: became [the vanquisher] — he fittingly crushed those [rivals] in battle — even that [is] the wondrous primacy of his!' || (JGc 1,33.62)

children.text: kanyānāṃ ṣoḍaśa-sahasrāṇy uddiśya ca sahasra-vaktratām eva devatāḥ prāpsyanti |
children.translated_text: And concerning the sixteen thousand maidens, even the gods shall attain the state of a thousand-mouthed one [<s>Śeṣa</s>, to describe it].

children.text: tatra dig-darśanam, yathā-
children.translated_text: There, an indication, as follows:

children.text: atha naraka-nikāyyaṃ nārakaṃ menire tās
children.translated_text: 'Then, those [maidens] considered their confinement in hell (<s>Naraka</s>) as [truly] hellish;

children.text: tad-adhikam api taṃ tu śrī-harir manyate sma |
children.translated_text: but him (<s>Naraka</s>) [himself], <s>Śrī Hari</s> considered even more [worthy of destruction];

children.text: naraka-haraṇa-nāmāpy atra yatnātiyatnaṃ
children.translated_text: for even the extraordinary effort that was made

children.text: yad akṛta yad ihāsīd vyagratā-biddha-buddhiḥ ||JGc_1,33.63||
children.translated_text: for the act named 'the removal of <s>Naraka</s>' — was [performed] with a mind pierced by eagerness here!' || (JGc 1,33.63)

children.text: naraka-vadha-prakriyāṃ caivaṃ varṇayiṣyanti |
children.translated_text: And the procedure of <s>Naraka's</s> slaying shall be described thus:

children.text: bhittvā durgāṇi kṛṣṇaḥ sasuta-mura-yutaṃ bhaumam unmukhya rājye
children.translated_text: 'Having breached the fortresses, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, confronting <s>Bhauma</s> (<s>Narakāsura</s>) together with <s>Mura</s> and his sons, in the kingdom —

children.text: tat-putraṃ sthāpayitvā sura-nara-duhitur bandhanād ujjahāra |
children.translated_text: having installed his [<s>Naraka's</s>] son [on the throne] and freed [the maidens] from the bondage of the daughter of gods and men —

children.text: devāmbā-kuṇḍalādyo maṇi-giri-varuṇa-cchatram uddhṛtya tac ca
children.translated_text: having recovered the earrings of the Mother of the Gods (<s>Aditi</s>), the <s>Maṇi</s>-mountain, the umbrella of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and [other treasures] —

children.text: pratyarpya kṣudra-vṛṣṇaḥ saha maṇi-giriṇāpy agrahīt pārijātam ||JGc_1,33.64||
children.translated_text: and having returned those, the minor <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), together with the <s>Maṇi</s>-mountain, also took the <s>Pārijāta</s> [tree]!' || (JGc 1,33.64)

children.text: tad evaṃ tava svargastha-vighna-hantṛtāṃ tatra ca vṛtraghnaḥ kṛtaghnatām avadhāya vayam evaṃ manyāmahe |
children.translated_text: Thus, having perceived your role as the destroyer of obstacles among the celestials, and the ingratitude of the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) therein, we think as follows:

children.text: tvām arcanti yadā svargyās tadā svargaḥ surālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'When the celestials worship You, then heaven is the abode of the gods;

children.text: tvāṃ nārcanti yadā svargyās tadā svargaḥ surālayaḥ ||JGc_1,33.65||
children.translated_text: when the celestials do not worship You, then [too] heaven is the abode of the gods [i.e., the name remains but the reality departs]!' || (JGc 1,33.65)

children.text: yuktam eva tat-
children.translated_text: That is indeed fitting —

children.text: ajanāśam asau naṣṭo jīvanāśaṃ nanāśa ca |
children.translated_text: 'That one did not know birth; the lost one destroyed even the destruction of life;'

children.text: ūrdhva-śoṣaṃ sa cāśuṣyat kṛṣṇa yas tvat-parāṅmukhaḥ ||JGc_1,33.66||
children.translated_text: [The river] <s>Yamunā</s> dried upward — for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she who was turned away from you, dried up!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tad evaṃ tatra sarva-svāsthya-maya-gārhasthya-caye pratiśvastanaṃ sphurad-upacaye sati suta-sampattir api matim atītya pratyahaṃ pratoṣyate | kiṃ bahunā, bhavadvad-varṣa-ṣaṭkān anantaram eva yauvana-prapañcatas teṣām api prajātāḥ prajās tāvaty eva diṣṭe dṛṣṭa-yauvanā bhaviṣyanti | bhavān punar īdṛśatayā paraṃ nava-vayāḥ sthāsyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Thus, there, when the accumulation of domesticity filled with all well-being, with its daily increase manifestly swelling — even the wealth of sons shall delight [you] beyond the mind's capacity, day after day. In short, six years after your [arrival] — from the profusion of youth — their progeny too, at that very appointed time, shall become visibly mature in their youth. But you shall remain perpetually of fresh youth.'

children.text: tathā ca paurāṇī vāṇī-nātidīrgheṇa kālena sa kārṣṇī rūḍha-yauvanaḥ [BhP 10.55.9] iti | tac ca kṛṣṇaṃ matvā striyo hrītāḥ [BhP 10.55.28]iti ca |
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Purāṇa</s>'s voice: 'Not after a very long time, that son of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> attained mature youth' [BhP 10.55.9] — thus. And: 'Seeing that [<s>Pradyumna</s>] and mistaking him for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the women became bashful' [BhP 10.55.28] — thus.

children.text: tatra ca kaimutyam idam avadhira-mātraāṇām anavadhikam avadhāna-nidhāna-pātrāyate | yathā-
children.translated_text: And therein, this argument a fortiori becomes an infinite vessel of attention for those who merely contemplate. As follows:

children.text: tatra pravayaso' py āsan yuvāno' tibalaujasaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even those of advanced age there were youthful, of great strength and vitality,

children.text: pibanto' kṣair mukundasya mukhāmbhoja-sudhāṃ muhuḥ || [BhP 10.45.19] iti
children.translated_text: drinking repeatedly with their eyes the nectar of <s>Mukunda's</s> lotus-face!' // [BhP 10.45.19] — thus.

children.text: etena śrīmad-vraje tu tad-atiśayāt sphuṭam eva tad-atiśayaḥ saṅgamitaḥ |
children.translated_text: By this, in the glorious <s>Vraja</s>, the surpassing [of that] is clearly demonstrated, on account of its surpassing [nature].

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-aho mahātman ! mahān ayam atyayaḥ sampraty api duratyayaṃ duḥkham arpayati | yat tāvad vilambaṃ tatrāvalambitāsmi | bhavatu, prakṛtaṃ prakriyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Ah, great soul! This is a great transgression — even now it inflicts suffering that is difficult to overcome! For as long as I have lingered there, I am still clinging to it. So be it — let the present [topic] proceed!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-śambareṇa janmata eva dyumnavat tava gṛhād apahṛtasya pradyumna-nāmnas tvat-putrasya samparāye sambandhaṃ tad-dhanana-caritraṃ vicitratayā gāsyanti, yathā-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'The story of the slaying of <s>Śambara</s>, relating to the fate of your son named <s>Pradyumna</s> — who was stolen from your house at birth by <s>Śambara</s>, like a celestial [stolen] — shall be sung in its marvelous character, as follows:'

children.text: kṛṣṇe' pi dhṛṣṇag-bhavitātra kaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: 'Even in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who would be the bold man

children.text: yas tu svayaṃ yoddhum amuṃ vrajiṣyati |
children.translated_text: who would go to fight him by himself?

children.text: yad adya jātaṃ khalu tasya jātakaṃ
children.translated_text: The horoscope of that one, born just today,

children.text: hṛtvā tato mṛtyum avāpa śambaraḥ ||JGc_1,33.67||
children.translated_text: having been stolen — from that, <s>Śambara</s> met death!' // [upajāti]

children.text: atha prādyumnim anu cāmnāsyanti-
children.translated_text: And after <s>Pradyumna's</s> [son], they shall also recount:

children.text: ūṣāṃ bāṇasya kanyāṃ rahasi gatam ananāniruddhaṃ niruddhaṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Aniruddha</s>, having gone secretly to <s>Ūṣā</s>, the daughter of <s>Bāṇa</s>, was captured;

children.text: yuddhe buddhā tam etaṃ drutam abhigatavān yudhyato' gryān nihatya |
children.translated_text: in battle, having perceived him, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] came swiftly, slaying the foremost [warriors];

children.text: brahmāṇḍa-dhvaṃsad-akṣa-jvalana-vaha-mahā-śūla-bhṛc-chūlapāṇiṃ
children.translated_text: the trident-bearing <s>Śūlapāṇi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who bore the great trident of the fire-bearing <s>Akṣa</s> that would shatter the cosmic egg —

children.text: tat-pakṣaṃ nirjayaṃs tad-bhuja-balam alūnād yas tu tatrānyakaḥ kaḥ ||JGc_1,33.68||
children.translated_text: conquering his faction and severing the force of his arms — who else but he could do this there?' // [sragdharā]

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-vismayaḥ khalv ayam | yad vismariṣyāmy eva vraja-vārtām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'This is truly astonishing! That I shall forget the news of <s>Vraja</s>!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-na hi na hi | sā hi tavāhite manasi rāga-mayī jāgarūkatām eva parām āgamiṣyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'No, no! For that [memory], being passion-filled, dwelling in your mind, shall indeed attain the supreme state of vigilant wakefulness.'

children.text: hanta ! yat khalu nirantaram antargatam, tat katham antargatam iva jāyeta | kintu pūrva-nirdiṣṭaṃ gurv-anādiṣṭatā-paraṃ tasmin nirdiṣṭi-viśiṣṭim ācariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'Alas! That which is continuously within — how could it appear as if it were within [i.e., hidden]? But the previously indicated [condition] — being under the supreme [obligation of] not having been instructed by the guru — shall bring about the distinction of instruction therein.'

children.text: tadā ca kadācana rāmeṇa saha rahasya-vārtā tava vartiṣyate | yatra sva-gamanam anālocya rāmaṃ śaśvad anuśocya vrajasthānāṃ smṛtitaḥ pracyavamāna-bāṣpas tvayā ca tathānuśocatā procyamānas tava sandeśaṃ praveśayan māthura-vraja-deśa-praveśaṃ gopa-veśam āveśya prāpsyati | prāpya ca sa yathā kathā-viṣayas tathā samasya varṇayiṣyati-
children.translated_text: 'And then, on a certain occasion, a private conversation between you and <s>Rāma</s> shall take place — where, without considering your own departure, constantly lamenting with <s>Rāma</s>, with tears flowing from the memory of the <s>Vraja</s> residents — and by you too, lamenting likewise — he, introducing your message, donning the garb of a <s>Māthura</s> cowherd for entry into the <s>Vraja</s> territory, shall arrive. And having arrived, he shall describe all as follows, as if it were the subject of a tale:'

children.text: vrajasthānāṃ rāmaḥ sva-sahaja-viyogārciṣi hareḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Rāma</s>, indeed, previously was born as the cause of the fire of natural separation from <s>Hari</s> for the residents of <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: purā satyaṃ jajñe punar iha tu jātaḥ sukha-kṛtī |
children.translated_text: but here again he was born as the creator of happiness!

children.text: yatas teṣāṃ jvālāṃ sphurad amṛta-vācā praśamayaṃs
children.translated_text: For, quelling their flames with manifest nectar-like words,

children.text: tadīyāṃ sphūrtiṃ dṛg-viṣayam iva cakre sva-balataḥ ||JGc_1,33.69||
children.translated_text: he made his own manifestation as if visible before their eyes, through his own power!' // [śikharinī]

children.text: kim anyad vā vinyasitavyam | tena tathā te nanditā yathā sarve' pi svayaṃ saparva-prāyatayā taṃ prārthayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: 'What more need be composed? By him, they were so delighted that all of them, of their own accord, as if it were a festival, entreated him.'

children.text: tad-upabhoga-tṛṣṇayā cira-pālita-sukumāra-kaumāra-kusumānāṃ sura-vallī-samatā-suṣamāṇām iva labdha-cara-tadīya-saṃśleṣāṇām ābhīra-kumārī-viśeṣāṇām aṅgīkārāya |
children.translated_text: 'For the acceptance of those special cowherd maidens — who had long nurtured their tender, childhood flower-like [beauty] through the thirst for its enjoyment, who possessed the loveliness equal to divine creepers, and who had obtained the embrace of him who moved among them.'

children.text: śrīmān baladevaś ca yathāvad eva tathā valayāmāsa | valayitvā ca vrajaṃ prati pravalitānujāgamana-viśvāsaḥ sva-preyasīr ihaiva vihāya dvārakām api niścinta iva caliṣyati | āgatya ca dvārakāṃ tvām api sāntvayiṣyati | yathā-kartavyāvaśeṣaṃ vidhāya vraja-śleṣam avāpsyati |
children.translated_text: 'And the glorious <s>Baladeva</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) duly enveloped [them all]. And having enveloped [them], with the confidence that his younger brother would follow toward <s>Vraja</s>, leaving his own beloveds right there, he shall depart for <s>Dvārakā</s> as if without a care. And having arrived at <s>Dvārakā</s>, he shall console you too. As follows: Having completed the remaining duties, he shall attain the embrace of <s>Vraja</s>.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-kiyān avaśeṣas tāvāṃś ca viśeṣaḥ kathyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'How much remains, and what is its distinctive character? Let it be told!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-kramaśa eva prakaramaṇīyaḥ | tathā hi-vrajaṃ prati calitavati sakala-guṇa-tantre balabhadre puṇḍraka-maṇḍala-patiḥ kṛtrima-vāsudevatayā citrita-rūpas tvāṃ spardhayā vardhamāna-garvaṃ sādhu-krodha-samudbodhanam evaṃ sandekṣyati-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'It is to be set forth gradually. For thus: When <s>Balabhadra</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), the master of all virtues, had set forth toward <s>Vraja</s>, the lord of the <s>Puṇḍra</s> territory, having fashioned himself in the false guise of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, shall challenge you with growing pride — an awakening of righteous anger. [He shall declare] thus:'

children.text: vāsudevo' vatīrṇo' ham eka eva na cāparaḥ |
bhūtānām anukampārthaṃ tvaṃ tu mithyābhidhāṃ tyaja ||[BhP 10.66.5] iti |
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for beings — you, abandon the false designation!' // [BhP 10.66.5] — thus.
'I alone am <s>Vāsudeva</s> descended [as an <s>avatāra</s>], and no other!

children.text: pratisandekṣyanti tu taṃ yadavaḥ, yathā-
children.translated_text: But the <s>Yadavas</s> shall reply to him, as follows:

children.text: puṇḍra-keśa sa bhavān abhūd dhariḥ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Puṇḍra</s>-haired one, you became <s>Hari</s>?

children.text: kāśi-rāḍ na kim ihābhavac chiraḥ |
children.translated_text: Did the king of <s>Kāśī</s> not become the head?

children.text: mitratām aśivatāṃ tathāsajann
children.translated_text: Attaching friendship to inauspiciousness,

children.text: anyathā prathitavān sa tu tvayi ||JGc_1,33.70||
children.translated_text: he proclaimed otherwise regarding you!' // [rathoddhatā]

children.text:
vṛttāntenāmunā tu tvad-vṛttāntaḥ so' yam īkṣate |
kṛtāntenācireṇa tvaṃ kṛtānta iva vartase ||JGc_1,33.71|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'By this very episode, your own affair is observed — by <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death), soon, you shall appear like Death itself!' // [anuṣṭubh] — thus.

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tatas tad-vadhānantaraṃ tvaṃ tu taṃ tan-mitraṃ kāśīrājam api prāptanāśī-kariṣyasi | tayoḥ śivādya-pacitir apy apacitim eva kariṣyati | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then, after the slaying of that one, you shall also bring the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, his ally, to destruction. The worship of <s>Śiva</s> and others by those two shall produce only disrespect. And then:'

children.text: yadā satrāyitā tatra kāśīśa-tanayas tadā |
children.translated_text: 'When the son of the king of <s>Kāśī</s> shall take to a sacrificial vow,

children.text: tasmāt kaṣṭāyamānaḥ sann aṣṭim ucciar aṭiṣyati ||JGc_1,33.72||
children.translated_text: then, afflicted by that, he shall loudly proclaim grief as his bones!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: atha rāmas tu dvividaṃ rāma-senāgrām agrāmaṇyaṃ vidann api haniṣyati | yathā ca kathayiṣyanti-
children.translated_text: 'And <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) shall slay <s>Dvivida</s>, knowing the foremost of <s>Rāma's</s> army to be incivil. And as they shall narrate:'

children.text: āśritya rāmaṃ dvividaḥ svecchayā narakaṃ śritaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having taken refuge in <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Dvivida</s> by his own will went to hell;

children.text: iti tan-niṣkṛtiṃ kurvan rāmo' nyas tam adaṇḍayat ||JGc_1,33.73||
children.translated_text: thus, effecting his punishment, the other <s>Rāma</s> did not punish him!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: śrī-rāma uddiśya ca vandi-vṛndāni vandiṣyante-
children.translated_text: And addressing Śrī <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), the hosts of panegyrists shall praise [him]:

children.text: hālālohita-locane hala-bhṛti vyākoṣa-śoṇābja-yug-
children.translated_text: 'In the plough-bearer's eyes reddened by <s>Hālā</s> (wine), [resembling] a pair of expanding red lotuses —

children.text: gaṅgā-bhrānti-bharākarā madhukarāḥ koṭir gatāḥ kūṭatām |
children.translated_text: the bees, bearing the burden of the delusion of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, have reached crookedness in their millions!

children.text: kiṃ ca kṣauṇi-śaṭhā haṭād agharipos tejaḥ prasuptaṃ yaśasy
children.translated_text: Moreover, the deceitful Earth — the radiance of the enemy of <s>Agha</s>, dormant in glory,

children.text: udbuddhaṃ kila vardhituṃ tad iti te vārdhiṃ gatiṃ saṅgatāḥ ||JGc_1,33.74||
children.translated_text: was awakened to increase it — therefore they have attained the course toward the ocean!' // [śārdūla]

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-hanta maharṣe ! bāṭa-ghaṭita-nyāyenāpi mama vraja-sambandhibhiḥ samaṃ samanvayaḥ kiṃ na bhavitā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Alas, O great sage! Even by the logic of a contrived argument, shall there not be a reunion with my <s>Vraja</s> relatives?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-bhavitā | yatas tad eva vṛttaṃ kramataḥ kramate sma |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'There shall be! For that very affair shall advance step by step.'

children.text: tathā hi-yadā rāmas tīrtha-yātrāṃ kariṣyati, yasyāś cānte bhīṣmādi-śāntatā-prānte duryodhana-vadhaḥ sampatsyate, tasyāḥ prāg yadā kadāpi sūryoparāgaḥ sāgaravat parva-garimāṇam āgantā | yaś caivaṃ varṇayiṣyate-
children.translated_text: 'For thus: When <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) shall undertake the pilgrimage — at the end of which, at the border of the pacification of <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others, the slaying of <s>Duryodhana</s> shall come to pass — before that, at some time, a solar eclipse shall arrive with the gravity of an ocean-tide festival. And that shall be described thus:'

children.text:
grasta-sūryeṇa tamasā tamasā vyāpi tad dinam |
udite hari-vaktrendau smerājani kumudvatī ||JGc_1,33.75|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'By the sun swallowed with darkness, that day was pervaded by gloom; when the <s>Hari</s>-faced moon rose, the night-lotus pond became smiling!' // [anuṣṭubh] — thus.

children.text:
tadā tu-
  kaṃsa-pratāpitāḥ sarve vayaṃ yātā diśaṃ diśam |
  etarhy eva punaḥ sthānaṃ daivenāsāditāḥ svasaḥ ||JGc_1,33.76|| iti | [BhP 10.82.21]
children.translated_text:
'And then:
"Afflicted by <s>Kaṃsa's</s> might, we all had gone in every direction; now, at this very moment, by fate, we have again attained our [rightful] place, O sisters!" // [anuṣṭubh]' [BhP 10.82.21]

children.text: śrī-vasudeva-vacanāt kaṃsa-vadhān nātivyavadhāna-kāle kuru-bhuvi suvimala-jātīyā bhāratīyāḥ prajāḥ prāyaḥ prayāsyanti | yatra yudhiṣṭhirograsenādi-saṃsaktānāṃ bhavadīya-mahiṣṭha-bhaktānāṃ samāgamaḥ parameṣṭhi-goṣṭhīm api kaniṣṭhāṃ kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'From the words of Śrī <s>Vasudeva</s>, not long after the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, in the land of the <s>Kurus</s>, the people of the supremely pure <s>Bhārata</s> lineage shall mostly come [together]. Where the assembly of your foremost devotees — connected with <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Ugrasena</s>, and others — shall make even the assembly of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) seem inferior.'

children.text: kiṃ bahunā, bhavān api tatra bhavitā | vraja-vāsi-tatir api vrajitā | yataḥ parimilanāya parasparam adhikam abhikatāṃ gatānāṃ lakṣya-mātraṃ tvad-ādikaṃ lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: 'In short, you too shall be there. The multitude of <s>Vraja</s> residents too shall come. For, seeking mutual meeting, having reached an extreme of eager desire, you and others shall be perceived merely as a glimpse.'

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sāsram uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with tears: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tataś ca-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'And then:'

children.text: yathārka-tapto jala-bindur indunā
children.translated_text: 'Just as a water-drop heated by the sun [is relieved] by the moon,

children.text: nidāgha-dagdhaṃ vipinṃ payomucā |
children.translated_text: a forest burnt by summer heat [is revived] by the rain-cloud,

children.text: viṣārditaṃ vārbhavatā vilokyate
children.translated_text: one afflicted by poison [is healed] by nectar — so it is seen:

children.text: saṅgāt tathā tvad-virahī tvayā vrajaḥ ||JGc_1,33.77||
children.translated_text: from your company, <s>Vraja</s>, separated from you, [shall be thus healed]!' // [upajāti]

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ sa-gadgadam uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a choked voice: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tataś ca-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'And then:'

children.text: mātā tātaḥ pitṛ-sahacarā bhrātaro bandhu-vargā
children.translated_text: 'Mother, father, father's companion, brothers, the circle of kinsmen,

children.text: dāsā hṛdyās tava nija-janāḥ kecid anye ca tatra |
children.translated_text: dear servants, your own people, some others too — there —

children.text: prāpsyanti tvāṃ bhavati ca bhaviṣyanti te' nanya-cittās
children.translated_text: they shall attain you, and they shall be, and shall remain, with minds fixed on none other!

children.text: teṣv āveśād bahuṣu bhavitā naika-cetā bhavāṃs tu ||JGc_1,33.78||
children.translated_text: But you, from the multitude of their emotions, shall become multi-minded!' // [sragdharā]

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: 'And then:'

children.text: tvaṃ vrajeti nija-prema gopayann iva vatsyasi |
children.translated_text: 'You shall say "Go to <s>Vraja</s>" — concealing, as it were, your own <s>prema</s>!

children.text: vrajas tu sva-guṇais tatra sarva-preyān bhaviṣyati ||JGc_1,33.79||
children.translated_text: But <s>Vraja</s>, through its own virtues there, shall become the dearest of all!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tatra ca-
yadā yadā drakṣyati tāṃ bhavāṃs tadā
children.translated_text: 'Whenever you shall see that [<s>Vraja</s>] assembly, then

children.text: pūrṇaṃ samūrṇo lavitā dṛśor jalam |
children.translated_text: you, woolly-hearted, shall spin forth full tears from your eyes.

children.text: bhavantam apy evam amī yathāmunā
children.translated_text: And they too, at you, in like manner — by that [sight] —

children.text: kaṇṭhāntam antar hṛdayaṃ nirotsyate ||JGc_1,33.80||
children.translated_text: shall raise their heart to the throat's edge, within!' // [upajāti]
'And there:'

children.text: tad evaṃ vaiśākham ārabhya varṣā yāvad atiharṣāt tvāṃ nirṇimeṣam eva nirvarṇayantas te vraja-vāsinaḥ saṃvatsyanti | tad-ante sad-anūkaṭayā labdha-mūka-sthitiṣu śrīman-nandādiṣu teṣām ānakadundubhi-prabhṛtīnāṃ parama-snigdhāntaḥ-karaṇatāṃ vilocya jāta-putra-pautrāvalokanena kṣiti-vipakṣa-pakṣa-prāyatāvakalanena ca svasminn aviśvasti-srastitaḥ samāśvastim api vilokya sarva-ślokya-caritaḥ sahāyīkṛta-balarāmoddhava-rohiṇīkatayā taiḥ saha nija-vṛndāvana-vraja-darśanam ekānte mantraṇā-pūrvakaṃ vicintya niścintya ca śrīman-nandādīn sa-sāntvaṃ māthurān eva prasthāpayiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, from <s>Vaiśākha</s> (spring) through the rainy season, those <s>Vraja</s> residents, with supreme delight, shall dwell gazing at you without blinking. At the end of that [period], when the glorious <s>Nanda</s> and others have attained a state of dumbstruck silence from devoted attachment, and when you perceive the supremely tender hearts of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) and others, and [perceive] the inspection of sons and grandsons and the nearly hostile factionalism of the earth-rulers, and even perceive reassurance in the distrust [directed] toward you — you, of universally praiseworthy conduct, having enlisted the help of <s>Balarāma</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, and <s>Rohiṇī</s>, together with them, having privately deliberated and resolved upon the sight of your own <s>Vṛndāvana-Vraja</s>, you shall dispatch the glorious <s>Nanda</s> and others, with consoling words, back to <s>Mathurā</s>.'

children.text: idam eva bādarāyaṇir apy āha tataḥ kāmaiḥ pūryamāṇaḥ sa-vrajaḥ saha-bāndhavaḥ [BhP 10.84.67] ity ādinā kṛṣṇe kamala-patrākṣe saṃnyastākhila-rādhasaḥ [BhP 10.65.6] iti pūrvoktes tvad-āgamana-tātparyā eva teṣāṃ kāmā iti | prasthāpana-samayatas teṣāṃ viśeṣāvasthā-varṇanaṃ tu tat tad asmākaṃ buddhim āstṛṇotīty alam ativistareṇa |
children.translated_text: This very thing <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>) too says: 'Then, with desires being fulfilled, together with <s>Vraja</s> folk and kinsmen' [BhP 10.84.67] — and so forth. 'In <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lotus-petal-eyed one, having placed all their wishes' [BhP 10.65.6] — as previously stated, their desires were centered solely on your arrival. But the description of their special condition at the time of dispatching — that overwhelms even our intellect — so enough with excessive detail.

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-asmad-avasthāṃ tu varṇaya |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'But describe my condition!'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-kuru-sthalāt kuśasthalam āgatya sthitaḥ sa bhavān pāṇḍava-rājena rājasūya-mantraṇāyāsmad-dvārā nimantritaṃ sann indraprasthaṃ prasthāsyate |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Having come from <s>Kuru-sthala</s> (the <s>Kuru</s> land) to <s>Kuśasthala</s> (<s>Dvārakā</s>) and having stationed yourself, you, being invited through us by the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> king for the deliberation on the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice, shall set forth for <s>Indraprastha</s>.'

children.text: tataś ca satvaraṃ gatvā bhīa-prabhṛtaye dik-sīma-vijaya-yaśāṃsi dattvā bhīma-dvārā jarāsandhaṃ hatvā tat-kṛta-bandhāni nṛpa-vṛndāni mocayitvā vijitena rāja-vrajena yudhiṣṭhiraṃ rocayitvā rājasūyena yājayiṣyasi | tatra jarāsandha-ghātanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: 'And then, having gone swiftly, having given the glories of the conquest of the directional boundaries to <s>Bhīma</s> and others, having slain <s>Jarāsandha</s> through <s>Bhīma</s>, having liberated the multitudes of kings imprisoned by him, having gratified <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> with the conquered royal host, you shall cause [him] to perform the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice. There, the slaying of <s>Jarāsandha</s>, as follows:'

children.text: bandhaṃ bandhaṃ yam anu mumuce taṃ jarāsandham enaṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Jarāsandha</s>, whom [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] freed again and again from bondage after bondage —

children.text: hanyām addhā svayam atha yadi śravyam etan na tarhi |
children.translated_text: 'I would indeed slay him myself, but then this would not be worth hearing!'

children.text: itthaṃ kṛṣṇa tvam iha kalayan bhīmasenena yuddhād
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, here, fashioning [the plan] — through the battle with <s>Bhīmasena</s>,

children.text: dharyād daitya-prakṛtim amukaṃ ghātayiṣyasy asy upetya ||JGc_1,33.81||
children.translated_text: through [his] endurance, you shall cause that demon-natured one to be slain, having approached [him]! ||33.81||

children.text: milad-artana-giri-garta-vartamāna-nṛpāṇāṃ kṛpayā mocanam, yathā-
children.translated_text: The compassionate liberation of the kings dwelling in the cave of the mountain of affliction (<s>Giridroṇī</s>), as follows:

children.text: kārāgārāndha-tāmisra-bandhād andhāyitān nṛpān |
children.translated_text: 'The kings, blinded by the dungeon's deep darkness-bondage —

children.text: svarūpa-dṛṣṭibhiḥ sṛṣṭa-dṛṣṭīn parikariṣyati ||JGc_1,33.82||
children.translated_text: he shall make them endowed with vision, [their sight] created by the sight of his own true form!' ||33.82||

children.text: rājasūyam, yathā-
children.translated_text: The <s>Rājasūya</s> [sacrifice], as follows:

children.text: nirjitya kṣitipati-maṇḍalāni pāṇḍoḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having conquered the circles of earthly kings,

children.text: putrais tāny anugamitāni saṅghaṭayya |
children.translated_text: having assembled those [kingdoms] conquered by the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: cedīśaṃ sadasi nihatya tad-viruddhaṃ
children.translated_text: having slain the lord of <s>Cedi</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) in the assembly — the one opposed to them —

children.text: teṣāṃ tad-viracayitāsi rājasūyam ||JGc_1,33.83||
children.translated_text: you shall arrange for them that <s>Rājasūya</s> [sacrifice]!' ||33.83||

children.text: yajñe tasmin nṛloko nṛpati-tad-adhipā vipra-viprarṣi-varyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'In that sacrifice — the human world, the rulers of kings and their lords, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the best of the <s>brahmarṣis</s>,

children.text: svargasthāḥ svarga-pālās tridaśa-munivarāḥ kiṃ ca vedhāḥ śivāś ca |
children.translated_text: the dwellers in heaven, the guardians of heaven, the best sages of the celestials, and moreover <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: dṛṣṭyā śrutyāpi tat tad bahuvidha-bhagavad-rūpa-vṛndasya vijñāḥ
children.translated_text: the knowers, [who comprehend] through sight and hearing the host of manifold divine forms —

children.text: paśyanto rūpam etat tava kim api muhur vismariṣyanti sarvam ||JGc_1,33.84||
children.translated_text: beholding this form of yours, shall repeatedly forget everything else!' ||33.84||

children.text: tad evaṃ rājasūyaṃ santānya kuntyāḥ santānān sammānya yadā dvārakāyāṃ gantāsi, tadā sādhūnāṃ śalyaṃ śālvaṃ lohamaya-vyoma-cāri-pūryā parāg eva tām āvārya dṛṣṭvā pūryamāṇa-pāñcajanyaḥ sannāti-prayatnatas taṃ deva-sapatnaṃ haniṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Thus, having completed the <s>Rājasūya</s> and having honored the descendants of <s>Kuntī</s>, when you shall go to <s>Dvārakā</s>, then <s>Śālva</s> — the thorn of the righteous — with his iron sky-coursing citadel, shall surround and besiege that [city] from afar. Seeing this, with the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> [conch] being filled [with breath], through great effort in armor, you shall slay that enemy of the gods.

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text: krudhyan krudhyat-saubha-puraṃ vyomādhva dvārakārudham |
children.translated_text: 'The enraged <s>Saubha</s>-city of the furious [<s>Śālva</s>], mounted upon the aerial path, toward <s>Dvārakā</s> —

children.text: dhvaṃsayiṣyasi tad yadvat tripuraṃ tripurāntakṛt ||JGc_1,33.85||
children.translated_text: you shall destroy it, just as the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) [destroyed] <s>Tripura</s>!' ||33.85||

children.text: atra ca gāyanti-
children.translated_text: And here they shall sing:

children.text: ūḍumbare kṛmis tāvan nijāḍambara-garvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'A worm in the fig-fruit, proud of its own pomp,

children.text: yāvan na danti-dantānām antaḥ patati tat-phalam ||JGc_1,33.86||
children.translated_text: [remains so] only until that fruit falls into the teeth of an elephant!' ||33.86||

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-adyāpi kati-vilambā vraja-bhū-gatiḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Even now, how much delay [remains] until the journey to the land of <s>Vraja</s>?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-āyatāv evāyātā śrūyatām |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Extended though it be, [the extension] itself has arrived — listen!'

children.text: tad etat procya maharṣiṇā manasi procyate sma-eṣā ca kalilokair viralair evāvakalayiṣyate | asyā hi bahirmukhān pratavaguṇṭhayitum antarmukhāṃs tūtkaṇṭhayituṃ maharṣibhiḥ parokṣa-prāyī-kṛtāyāḥ khalv asmad-ādi-saṃvādamayyāḥ śrī-bhāgavata-bhārata-pādmādīnām eka-vākyatā-karaṇata eva śakyā pratītir iti | tad idaṃ ca kiñcana mad-upadeśa-nidigdhaṃ madhukaṇṭha-snigdhakaṇṭhābhyāṃ prāpta-kṛṣṇopakaṇṭhābhyāṃ kṣīra-kaṇṭhābhyām api sva-kaṇṭhād eva campū-dvayam apūrva-racanayā sampūrṇaṃ kurvadbhyām uttara-campūttara-bhāgam añcadbhyāṃ tat-tac-chāstra-mata-vistāraṇayā prastoṣyate, tad eva samasya vicāryate |
children.translated_text: Having spoken this, the great sage reflected within his mind: 'And this [account] shall be perceived only by rare persons amidst the confused people. For of this [account] — rendered mostly indirect by the great sages, [so as] to cover the faces of the outward-turned and to create eagerness in the inward-turned — conviction is possible only through the harmonization of the statements of the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s>, the <s>Bhārata</s>, the <s>Pādma</s>, and others, which consist of our own such dialogues. And this [subject], dipped in some of my own instruction, by <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> and <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> — who have attained proximity to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, [though they are] but milk-throated [infants] — through their own voices, completing the pair of <s>campūs</s> with unprecedented composition, and extending the latter part of the <s>Uttara-campū</s>, shall be presented through the expansion of the doctrines of the various scriptures — that very [matter] shall be synthesized and deliberated upon.'

children.text: yadā śālva-yuddham udbuddham, tadā pāṇḍavānāṃ durodara-daṇḍa iti vana-parva-kathā | śālvasya tu prāṇān daṇḍayitvā madhu-pura-dvāri vakratā-caṇḍaṃ savidūratha-dantavakraḥ khaṇḍa-khaṇḍaśaḥ khaṇḍitaś ca, tenānena bhaviteti pādmottara-khaṇḍa-prathā | tad-anantaraṃ ca punar vrajāgamanam asya mahādeva-devyāḥ saṃvāda-rahasya-maye tatraiva spaṣṭaṃ niṣṭaṅkyate | yat khalu satya-saṅkalpatayānalpa-samajñā-vijñātānāṃ āyāsye iti dyotakaiḥ [BhP 10.41.17], āgamiṣyaty atidīrgheṇa [BhP 10.46.34] ity ādi-bahutarād bhagavad-bhāgavatānāṃ pratijñānusārāt śrīmad-bhāgavatenāpy udbhāvitam | na kevalaṃ pratijñā-mātraṃ tatra pratīti-pātrīkṛtam, kintu tad-āgatir apy adhigatīkṛtam |
children.translated_text: When the battle with <s>Śālva</s> has been aroused, then [comes] the forest-episode narrative about the punishment of the descendants of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> by wicked fate. And having punished the life-breath of <s>Śālva</s>, at the gate of the honey-city (<s>Mathurā</s>), <s>Dantavakra</s> and <s>Vidūratha</s> — fierce in crookedness — were shattered into fragments; that this shall come to pass is [attested by] the tradition of the <s>Pādma Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>. And thereafter, again, his return to <s>Vraja</s> — in the secret dialogue of <s>Mahādeva</s> and his consort — is clearly stamped in that very [text]. For indeed, through the power of his true resolve, as made known by those of no-small understanding — by the indicators 'I shall come' [BhP 10.41.17], 'He shall return after a very long time' [BhP 10.46.34], and many more such promises of the Lord and his devotees — the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> too has indicated [this]. Not merely the promise was made a vessel of conviction there, but his actual arrival too was made cognized.

children.text:
tathā hi prathame dvārakā-prajā-vacane-yarhy ambujākṣāpasasāra bho bhavān kurūn madhūn vātha suhṛd-didṛkṣayā [BhP 1.11.9] iti pratyakṣaṃ lakṣyate | na ca tat tu kālāntara-gatam | kurukṣetra-yātrāyāṃ hi sphuṭam asya vacanaṃ tasya tat-kālatām eva racayati | tathā hi-
api smaratha naḥ sakhyaḥ svānām artha-cikīrṣayā |
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first [section], in the speech of the citizens of <s>Dvārakā</s>: 'O lotus-eyed one, whenever you departed, O Lord, to the <s>Kurus</s> or the <s>Madhus</s>, with the desire to see friends' [BhP 1.11.9] — is clearly perceived. And that is not from another time. For in the pilgrimage to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, his statement clearly establishes the contemporaneity of that [visit]. Thus:

children.text: gatāṃś cirāyitāñ chatru-pakṣa-kṣapaṇa-cetasaḥ ||[BhP 10.82.41] iti |
children.translated_text:
'Do you remember us, O friends — [us who were] departed for the sake of accomplishing the purposes of our own people,
having been gone a long time, with minds intent on destroying the enemy's faction?' ||[BhP 10.82.41]||

children.text: vidūrathāntaśatruvadham evāvavadhim atra karoti nānyad iti | tad evaṃ sthite tad-anantaraṃ ca labdhāntaratayā tenānena teṣāṃ prakṛti-jāgocara-prakṛti-svapadāvirbhāvanaṃ ca tatra pādma evodbhāvaitam | tad api brahma-hrada-majjana-tad-unmajjanād anantaraṃ tad-darśitavata etasya caitadīyānāṃ cābhiprāyeṇa śrīmad-bhāgavatenābhipretam | api naḥ svagatiṃ sūkṣmām [BhP 10.28.12] iti, na veda svāṃ gatiṃ bhraman [BhP 10.28.14] iti, gopānāṃ svaṃ lokaṃ [BhP 10.28.15] iti, kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra chandobhiḥ stūyamānam [BhP 10.28.18] ity anena | ataeva skānde-
children.translated_text: The slaying of <s>Vidūratha</s> and the inner enemy alone constitutes the limit here, nothing else. This being so, thereafter, through the obtained opportunity, by him, the manifestation of their innate <s>Vraja</s>-nature and their own true abode has been indicated in the <s>Pādma</s> itself. And that too, after the immersion in the <s>Brahma-hrada</s> (the pool of <s>Brahmā</s>) and the emergence therefrom — he having shown that — is intended by the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> according to the intent of him and his devotees. [As evidenced by:] 'Our own subtle destination' [BhP 10.28.12], 'He did not know his own destination, wandering' [BhP 10.28.14], 'The own world of the cowherds' [BhP 10.28.15], and '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, being praised there by the <s>Vedas</s>' [BhP 10.28.18]. Therefore, in the <s>Skānda</s>:

children.text: vatsair vatsatarībhiś ca sarāmo bālakair vṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Surrounded by calves, cows, and boys, together with <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: vṛndāvanāntaragataḥ sadā krīḍati mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Mādhava</s> always sports!'

children.text: sadā sthiti-prayogaś cātra vaikuṇṭha-nāthasya dhruva-gajendrādy-artham anyatra gamanena vaikuṇṭha iva śrī-vrajendra-nandanasya mathurādi-gamanena sadā vṛndāvana-ramaṇam api na bādhyate |
children.translated_text: And the usage of 'always' [is explained]: Just as the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha's</s> going elsewhere — for the sake of <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Gajendra</s>, and others — does not obstruct [his perpetual presence in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>], similarly, the going of the son of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> to <s>Mathurā</s> and elsewhere does not obstruct his perpetual sporting in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.

children.text:
atredaṃ vicārayāmaḥ-
jananī-veśa-sambandhābhāsāt pūtanikāpi sā |
janaī-gatim avrājīd iti kaimutya-yogataḥ ||JGc_1,33.87||upakṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇa-ghoṣaḥ sugo-gopaṃ tad āpsyati |
children.translated_text:
Here we deliberate thus:
'Even <s>Pūtanā</s>, from the mere semblance of the connection of a mother's guise,
attained the destination of a mother — how much more so [for actual mothers], by the logic of a fortiori!' ||33.87||
'The cowherd-settlement of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, near <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with excellent cows and cowherds, shall attain

children.text: atiduḥkhaṃ duṣpratīpaṃ tad golokaṃ sa-śarma ca ||JGc_1,33.88||
children.translated_text: that <s>Goloka</s> — [transcending] extreme sorrow and resistance — with happiness!' ||33.88||

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
sāṅgaṃ yāvad vaibhavaṃ ca vrajaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ vrajiṣyati |
sa-kṛṣṇam anukṛṣṇaṃ yo dhāsyate ca sa-rāmakam ||JGc_1,33.89||sadvādaśa-skandham evaṃ śrī-bhāgavatam īkṣate |
yathā-śakti-budho' nyasya śakti-prati na vidyate ||JGc_1,33.90||
children.translated_text: the wise one [sees it] according to [the Lord's] power — for another, the power thereof does not exist!' ||33.90||

children.text: tad evaṃ vimṛṣya tu śrī-devarṣiḥ spaṣṭam ācaṣṭa- [201] yadā tvaṃ rājasūyataḥ sukhaṃ sambhūya svālaya-calanārambhaṃ sambhāvayiṣyasi, tadā vakrabhāva-cakrataḥ śakram api jigīṣur dantavakras tvāṃ kevalaṃ sarva-caṅkramaṇa-cakravalaṃ vitarkayan balena balena ca vinābhūtena tvayā kevalena gadāyuddham adhvany anivicchan madhupurīm āgantum urīkariṣyati | tām āgatya ca gatyantaraṃ cintayan man-mukhatas tava dvārakā-saṃmukha-prasthānaṃ śālva-saṃsthāpanaṃ cāsthāya sadyas tvāṃ praty eva duḥsthātmatayā prasthāsyate |
children.translated_text:
Thus, having reflected, the glorious <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>) spoke plainly:
[201] 'When you, after the <s>Rājasūya</s>, having happily reunited and beginning to contemplate the departure to your own abode — then <s>Dantavakra</s>, desiring to conquer even <s>Indra</s> through the circle of his crookedness, merely calculating you as a revolving circumference of all journeys, shall refuse a mace-fight on the road with you — [you who are] alone, bereft of both <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and [your army] — and shall consent to come to <s>Madhupurī</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>). And having come there, pondering an alternative course, learning from my mouth of your departure toward <s>Dvārakā</s> and the establishment of <s>Śālva</s> [there], he shall immediately set forth toward you alone, in a state of ill-being.'

children.text: tadaiva ca mano-juti-vibhūti-mayena mayā kathanayā nija-vraja-gamanāya tad evāspadam āspadaṃ kurval-labdha-manorathas tādṛśa-divya-rathaś ca tvaṃ tat-kṣaṇam eva mathurā-pura-dvāri prāpta-gati-prathas taṃ gadāvantaṃ niṣkrāmantaṃ drakṣyasi, srakṣyasi ca tvāṃ prati krāmantaṃ taṃ prati gadāṃ srakṣyante ca, pratyastrāṇīva tvad-ābhimukhyena karūṣa-mukhyena tena caidyenaiva sātma-jyotiṣkā niṣkāsya prāṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And at that very time, you — by me, of the power of mind-speed-glory, creating the very ground for your own journey to <s>Vraja</s> through narration — having obtained your heart's desire and a divine chariot of such a kind — at that very moment, having attained the fame of arrival at the gate of <s>Mathurā</s>-city, you shall see that mace-bearer (<s>Dantavakra</s>) emerging; you shall hurl [your weapon] and he, advancing toward you, shall hurl his mace; and the life-breaths, together with their own radiance, shall be expelled by the chief of the <s>Karūṣas</s>, by that <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla's</s> [reincarnation]) himself — as if counter-weapons — through their facing toward you!'

children.text: tatra ca ślokaḥ khalv ayam-
children.translated_text: And here, this verse indeed [applies]:

children.text: bhīmasyāhaṃ tulya-saṃvid-gadāyā
children.translated_text: '"I, of equal understanding and mace as <s>Bhīma</s>,

children.text: dvandvāghāte mādhavaṃ māgadhābham |
children.translated_text: in single combat, [shall strike] <s>Mādhava</s> who resembles the <s>Māgadha</s> (Jarāsandha) —

children.text: jitvā rājyaṃ māthuraṃ sādhayiṣyāmy
children.translated_text: having conquered, I shall establish the kingdom of <s>Mathurā</s>!"

children.text: evaṃ naṅkṣaty eṣa ko dantavakraḥ ||JGc_1,33.91||
children.translated_text: — thus shall this <s>Dantavakra</s> perish! Who is he?' ||33.91||

children.text:
tataś ca-
dantavakra-citā-vahni-prāye krodhe tava svayam |
vidūrathaś ca bhavitā dūrataḥ krūra-kīṭavat ||JGc_1,33.92||[204] tad evaṃ dantavakraṃ vidūratham api vidūratas tadā gadā-cakra-ghātaṃ ghātayitvā sva-vacana-satyaṅkāraḥ svajana-hṛd-rujām agadaṅkāraḥ svīya-mukhānām astuṅkāraḥ śrīmad-vraja-virājamāna-rāja-kumāraḥ svaka-vraja-kulam eva bhavān mathurā-bhavān anuyokṣyate | tat tu sarvaṃ pragāḍha-bhāvam avagāḍhaṃ kurukṣetrād āgater arvāg-bhavad-āgamana-maryādābhyantarīṇa-kālaṃ kālam iva cālayituṃ punar api sudināyamānatāṃ pratipālayituṃ samprati yamunā-pārīṇaṃ jātam ity avakalayyānukāmīnena nija-divya-vimānena samuttīrya diviṣadbhiḥ kusumair avakīryamāṇaḥ sahasā tad-vāsaṃ cāsat tu mud yokṣyate |
children.translated_text:
And then:
'In the fire-like rage of your own toward <s>Dantavakra's</s> funeral pyre,
<s>Vidūratha</s> too shall be [consumed], from afar, like a cruel insect!' ||33.92||
[204] Thus, having slain <s>Dantavakra</s> and <s>Vidūratha</s> from afar by the blows of mace and discus — the vindicator of your own word's truth, the healer of the heart-pains of your own people, the exclaimer of 'Hail!' from the mouths of your own [devotees] — you, the glorious prince radiant in <s>Vraja</s>, shall yoke your own <s>Vraja</s>-clan itself, [heading] from <s>Mathurā</s> homeward! And all that — deeply emotional — [you shall do], to drive forth, as if driving time itself, the time within the boundary of your arrival from before <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, and again to await the day of auspiciousness — having ascertained that [the time] has now become ripe for the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> — crossing over by his own divine aerial chariot, being showered with flowers by the celestials, he shall suddenly unite the [people of] that dwelling with joy!

children.text: uttīrṇe ca tvayi sarvataḥ kīrṇena ninitāśeṣeṇa ratha-ghargharita-viśeṣeṇa tvad-āgamanam eva manvānās tvat-parimala-valanena tu niścinvānāḥ sarva-vidhā eva tvad-ekādhvānataḥ pradhāvanam eva tanvānāḥ śrīman-nandādy-abhidhānāḥ sannidhānaṃ vināpi śikhaṇḍi-maṇḍalavad amī mārtaṇḍa-maṇḍala-stha-megha-khaṇḍam iva divya-rathārūḍhaṃ tvām agūḍhaṃ niśāmya samya-gūḍha-pramada-bahala-kolāhalaṃ kalayiṣyanti |
children.translated_text: And when you have crossed over, those named the glorious <s>Nanda</s> and others — convinced of your arrival by the distinctive rumble of chariots spread everywhere, and ascertaining [it] by the fragrance carried [toward them] — all of every kind, running headlong upon the single path toward you — even without [reaching your] proximity, like a flock of peacocks [responding to] the disc of the sun, beholding a fragment of cloud upon the disc of the sun, [i.e.,] you, mounted upon the divine chariot, undisguised — shall produce an intensely thick tumult of overwhelming delight!

children.text: kalayantaś ca stambha-sveda-romodbheda-svara-bheda-rodana-vibheda-pralaya-mayatayā spandanam apy avindamānāḥ syandanād dūratas tad-avasthā eva sthāsyanti |
children.translated_text: And producing [that tumult], from the manifestation of paralysis, perspiration, horripilation, voice-breaking, weeping-breaking, and dissolution-like [states] — not finding even the power of movement — they shall stand at a distance from the chariot, in that very state!

children.text: tvaṃ punaḥ sahasā rathād avatīrya teṣāṃ pathā yathā-vīryaṃ dhāvan sakala-gīrvāṇa-vikīryamāṇa-kusumādi-vāditrādi-kṛtamānaḥ sarvathāpy asambhāvita-samānaḥ param āsaktyā sarvān api tān anarvācīna-śaktyā ca pṛthak pṛthag eva ca yugapad eva ca saṅgacchan samāliṅgaṃs tat tad aṅga-saṅgataṃ svāṅgam apii na tato bhinnam aṅgīkariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: You, however, having suddenly descended from the chariot, running along their path with the speed befitting [your] valor — honored by the flowers, instruments, and such showered by all the celestials, altogether incomparably — with supreme attachment, meeting all of them — one by one and simultaneously — by the power of the ancients, embracing [them], you shall accept even each part of your own body that has been in contact with each of their limbs, as not different from them!

children.text: te ca tathā śokāpanudaṃ datta-mudaṃ tvāṃ labhamānāḥ sarve janyavas tvad-ananyaṃ-manyā bhaviṣyati | [209] tathā ca gāsyate-
children.translated_text: And they, obtaining you — the dispeller of sorrow, the giver of delight — all shall become people for whom there is none other [than you] to be esteemed. [209] And thus it shall be sung:

children.text: yadā yātaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ punar api yadūnāṃ nagaratas
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> went again from the city of the <s>Yadus</s>,

children.text: tadā gopāḥ so' pi prati-nijam adhur moda-nivaham |
children.translated_text: then the cowherds too, each one individually, held a heap of joy!

children.text: vyatiśliṣṭā yarhi pratijanam idaṃ nājani manāg
children.translated_text: When they were mutually embraced — for each person, not even this much was perceived:

children.text: ayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kim aham iti tarhi sphuṭataram ||JGc_1,33.93||
children.translated_text: 'This is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' or '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' or 'Who am I?' — then, most clearly!' ||33.93||

children.text: yataḥ-
yadvat kalyantimānāṃ sukṛta-virahiṇāṃ satya-dharmāvatāraḥ
children.translated_text: 'Just as for those nearing destruction, the descent of the <s>avatāra</s> of truth and <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: pṛthvī-sthānāṃ mahāvagraha-hata-vapuṣāṃ varṣukābda-pracāraḥ |
children.translated_text: for those dwelling on the earth, whose bodies are struck by the great drought — the course of a rain-bearing year;

children.text: ākūpāra-hradānāṃ muni-hṛta-payasāṃ navya-gaṅgā-prasāras
children.translated_text: for the ocean-lakes whose waters have been drunk by the sages — the expansion of a fresh <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: tadvad goṣṭha-sthitānāṃ tava viraha-rujāṃ hanta te saṅga-sāraḥ ||JGc_1,33.94||
children.translated_text: so, alas, for the pains of separation of those dwelling in the cow-settlement, is the essence of your company!' ||33.94||
Since:

children.text: atha cirāya pratimāvat labdha-tvat-pariṣvaktiṣu vraja-jana-vyaktiṣu pūrvam avyaktībhāvam āpannā madhumaṅgala-pūrṇābhyarṇā paurṇamāsī sa-vṛndā vṛndā ca samam apracchannatāṃ gacchantī tu sukha-saṃmūrcchanān mūrcchām iva gatābhyas tābhyaḥ sābhyasūyam iva kramād bahir vṛttiṃ yacchantī tad-vanikāyāṃ tan-nikāyam upaveśayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, when the people of <s>Vraja</s> — having obtained your embrace like those [who embrace] a statue — had previously attained a state of unconsciousness, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> — fully near <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — together with <s>Vṛndā</s>, going into an un-concealed state simultaneously, gradually bestowing outward awareness upon those [<s>Vraja</s>-folk] — who had gone into a swoon, as it were, from the overwhelming surge of happiness — as if with a hint of reproach, shall seat that assembly in that grove!

children.text: tathā ca kathayiṣyanti-
children.translated_text: And thus they shall say:

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ madhya-gataṃ vidhāya pitarau tad-bhrātaraḥ strī-gaṇās
children.translated_text: 'Having placed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in their midst, his parents, his brothers, the groups of women,

children.text: tan-mitrāṇi kuṭumba-saṃvalanayā cānye cirāt prāptitaḥ |
children.translated_text: his friends, and others too through the embrace of kinship, from the joy of [his] long-awaited arrival,

children.text: muñcantaḥ sphuṭam aśru tasya sukhadaṃ cārūpa-cāraṃ ciraṃ
children.translated_text: shedding tears openly — his joy-giving, beautiful, charming conduct being long

children.text: vismṛtya sthagita-kriyāḥ samabhavan mūkāś ca vaisvaryataḥ ||JGc_1,33.95||
children.translated_text: forgotten — they became paralyzed in their actions, and mute from their emotions!' ||33.95||

children.text: tvaṃ tu tatra strī-kumāraṃ putra-pautraṃ kubja-vāmanaṃ dāsī-dāsam api sarvaṃ yathāyathaṃ toṣayiṣyasi | [213] dārukas tu dāruvad eva dūrasthitas tat-prema-vaśyatayā kautukam iva drakṣyati |
children.translated_text:
'And you shall there satisfy everyone as appropriate — women, children, sons, grandsons, the hunchback, the dwarf, maidservants, and manservants.'
[213] 'But <s>Dāruka</s>, standing at a distance like a piece of wood, shall watch the curiosity [of the scene] with bewilderment, being himself under the sway of that love.'

children.text: tataś ca tatrāsīnā paurṇamāsī kupitevālapiṣyati-ahaha kim idam avidanta iva kurvantaḥ stha ? pathi pariśrāntam imaṃ katham iva na viśrāntaṃ kurutha |
children.translated_text: 'And then, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, seated there, shall speak as if angered: "Ah! What is this? Are you acting as if unaware? How can you not give rest to this one who is exhausted from the journey?"'

children.text: tad evaṃ jāta-camatkārābhyāṃ tat-pariśrama-kātarābhyāṃ mātgara-pitarābhyām ubhayataḥ sva-sva-bhajanākṛtāliṅganamaya-praṇaya-ceṣṭitaḥ sarvair eva ca parito veṣṭitaḥ sva-goṣṭha-prakoṣṭha-madhyaga-śakaṭa-ghaṭā-ghaṭita-vāṭam avāpsyasi |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, by the wonder-struck, journey-fatigue-distressed mother and father on both sides, you shall be embraced with loving gestures in the form of their respective devotional embraces, and encircled on all sides by everyone, you shall reach the enclosure of your own cow-settlement, set within the compound of cart-rows.'

children.text: tataś ca te sarve bhavat-paricaryā-maya-parisaryākṛtaḥ sambharamam evācariṣyanti, na tu kārya-kramam | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: 'Then all of them shall perform nothing but the bustle of attending to you, not the sequence of [proper] duties. As follows:'

children.text: ||JGc_1,33.96|| MISSING!
children.translated_text: ||33.96|| MISSING!

children.text: yarhy āgantāsy aghahara cirād dvārakātas tadā te
children.translated_text: 'When you shall come, O destroyer of sin, after a long time, from <s>Dvārakā</s>, then

children.text: sarve' py ete vraja-jani-janā śreṣṭha-madhyastha-nighnāḥ |
children.translated_text: all these <s>Vraja</s>-born people — the great, the middling, and the lowly —

children.text: dhāvanto' pi pratidiśam aho tat-tad-ekaika-kāryaṃ
children.translated_text: even while running in every direction, even while performing each single task —

children.text: kurvanto' pi sthagita-kṛtitām eva yāsyanti hanta ||JGc_1,33.97||
children.translated_text: alas, they shall only attain a state of paralyzed activity!' ||33.97||

children.text: yadyapi gopāḥ samyak paricarituṃ tvāṃ na tarhi śakṣyanti |
children.translated_text: 'Even though the cowherds shall not be able to serve you properly at that time,

children.text: tad api na tat-pramadāmṛta-bhogās tvāmī sadaiva pokṣyanti ||JGc_1,33.98||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, with the nectar-enjoyment of their rapture, they shall always nourish you!' ||33.98||

children.text: tad ārabhya ca-
children.translated_text: 'And from that [moment] onward:'

children.text: kiṃ bhoktavyaṃ kvāsitavyaṃ svapanīyaṃ kva vāmunā |
children.translated_text: '"What should he eat? Where should he sit? Where should he sleep?"

children.text: iti mātrādi-dhī-yātrā nātrāyāsyati tṛptatām ||98||
children.translated_text: — thus, the mental journey of his mother and others shall not attain satiation!' ||98||

children.text:
sakhāyante sukhādhīnā vismariṣyanti sarvakam |
smariṣyanti tu tāṃ tvat-kāṃ punaḥ saṃśleṣa-navyatām ||JGc_1,33.99||dāsāś ca tava dāśārha punar āśāṃ sva-mūrtiṣu |
dhāsyanti sevā-sudhayā vidhāsyanti yad āplavam ||JGc_1,33.100||gāvaḥ prāgvad bhavat-sphūrti-prabhāva-sthita-tad-daśāḥ |
tadvad eva sadaivāmūr dhāsyanti pramadaṃ tvayi ||JGc_1,33.101||śiśavaḥ paśavaś caiva vayāṃsi ca payāṃsi ca |
ye' nye hṛdyā janā hṛdyās tava teṣāṃ tu kā kathā ||JGc_1,33.102||
children.translated_text: and whatever other delightful beings — what [more] can be said of their [joy] in you?' ||33.102||

'His friends, dependent on happiness, shall forget everything;
but they shall remember that freshness of re-embrace with you!' ||33.99||
'And your servants, O <s>Dāśārha</s>, shall again place their hope in their own forms;
through the nectar of service, they shall create an immersion [of joy]!' ||33.100||
'The cows, as before, established in that state by the power of awareness of you,
just so, these shall always bestow delight upon you!' ||33.101||
'The children, the animals, the birds, and the waters —

children.text: kūrmasyeva smaraṇānubhāvena tava tena tvadīyāḥ pūrvavad eva hi te sthātāraḥ | tathaiva vrajād baladevaḥ kuśasthalīm āsādya tvayi nivedayiṣyati | yathā śrī-hari-vaṃśe-
children.translated_text: 'Like the tortoise's [nourishment of its young] through the power of mere remembrance, by that [power] of yours, your people shall remain just as before.' And likewise, <s>Baladeva</s> shall come from <s>Vraja</s> to <s>Kuśasthalī</s> (<s>Dvārakā</s>) and inform you. As in the glorious <s>Harivaṃśa</s>:

children.text: tathaivādhvaga-veśena sopaśliṣṭe janārdanam |
children.translated_text: 'And in the guise of a traveller, he embraced <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: pratyagra-vana-mālena vakṣasābhivirājatā ||
children.translated_text: resplendent with a fresh forest-garland upon his chest;'

children.text: upaviṣṭaṃ tadā rāmaṃ papraccha kuśalaṃ vraje |
children.translated_text: 'Then <s>Janārdana</s> asked <s>Rāma</s>, who was seated,

children.text: bāndhaveṣu ca sarveṣu goṣu caiva janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: about the welfare of <s>Vraja</s>, and of all kinsmen, and of the cows;'

children.text: pratyuvāca tadā rāmo bhrātaraṃ sādhu-bhāṣitam |
sarveṣāṃ kuśalaṃ kṛṣṇa yeṣāṃ kuśalam icchasi ||[HV 83.53,55-6] iti |
children.translated_text: '"All is well, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with those whose welfare you desire!"' ||[HV 83.53, 55-56] — thus.
'Then <s>Rāma</s> replied to his brother, [who had] spoken well:',

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite' pi tadā tava sadā vrajāvasthiti-pratītis tu teṣāṃ nātijaniṣyate | syandanaṃ tad atra tad-avastham eva sthāpitam astīty anāsthā-bhāvanayā |
children.translated_text: 'Even with this being so, the conviction of your constant dwelling in <s>Vraja</s> shall not fully arise in them then — through the thought of indifference: "That chariot has been left standing there in that same condition."'

children.text: kiṃ ca, tava savayasaḥ pravayasaḥ pratīdaṃ pratīpam āvedayiṣyanti | priya-vayasyasya nātiasaumanasyaṃ manasy abhyasyate | yato janitānurāga-janatāsu tāsu prāg iva nānurāgaṃ jāgaram āgamayati | tāś ca tathā dṛṣṭvā lagita-duḥkha-sthagitatayā śuṣkā iva tiṣṭhanti |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, your age-fellows, now grown old, shall report this contrary [news] to you. "The dear friend does not excessively grieve in his mind." For in those communities where love had been born, he does not generate the same wakefulness of love as before. And they, seeing this, stand as if dried up — their suffering concealed and blocked.'

children.text:
tad etad ākarṇayantaḥ prāpta-kadanāntaratayā vivarṇavadanānte tvan-mātara-pitarādayaḥ kātaratām avāpsyanti |
[222] tvaṃ tu jantu-mātra-citta-jñas tad vijñāya svayam eva tān vijñāpayiṣyasi-kathaṃ bhavanto nādyāpy ānandād udbhavanto dṛśyante | [223] sarve tu sagadgadaṃ gadiṣyanti-asmākam ānanda-kāraṇaṃ tvad-avadhāraṇa-padavīṃ vindata eva |
children.translated_text:
'Hearing this, your mother, father, and others, having attained the interstice of affliction, with pale faces at the end, shall attain distress.'
[222] 'But you, the knower of every creature's mind, perceiving this, shall yourself inform them: "How is it that you are not seen arising from joy even now?"'
[223] 'And all shall say, with faltering voices: "The cause of our joy is finding the path of ascertaining you!"'

children.text: atha tvaṃ vakṣyasi-bāḍhaṃ kintu yena bhavadbhiḥ sandihyate, so' yaṃ śatāṅgaḥ sāṅga-bhavat-kārya-saṅgamanāya saṅge rakṣitatayā lakṣyate | yathā vānyathā jñāpayatha, tathā prathayiṣyāmi | etad eva prāg eva niveditaṃ mayā-
children.translated_text: 'Then you shall say: "Certainly! But that about which you have doubt — this hundred-limbed [chariot] is seen to be kept in readiness for the assembly of your entire affair. As you indicate, whether thus or otherwise, I shall arrange [accordingly]. This very thing was previously submitted by me:'

children.text: yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān |
jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham ||[BhP 10.45.23] iti |
children.translated_text: your kinsmen — we shall come to see them, having established the happiness of friends!' ||[BhP 10.45.23] — thus.
'Go, all of you, to <s>Vraja</s>, O father! And we, the ones grieved by the affection of

children.text: jñātīn iti yuṣman-madhyata evāsau vāsaḥ sambhaviṣyati, draṣṭum iti tatra ca yuṣmad-darśanam evāsmākaṃ puruṣārtha ity arthaḥ | yad vā draṣṭum iti darśana-viṣayī-bhavitum ity arthaḥ | athāpi bhūman mahimā guṇasya te viboddhum arhaty amalāntarātmabhiḥ [BhP 10.14.6] ity atra bodha-viṣayī-bhavitum itivad etad uddhavena ca bhavatsu samudbuddhaṃ cakre-
children.translated_text: '"<s>Jñātīn</s> (kinsmen)" means that the dwelling shall be right among you; "<s>draṣṭum</s> (to see)" means that seeing you is itself our supreme goal.' Or alternatively, '<s>draṣṭum</s>' means 'to become the object of seeing.' As also [stated elsewhere]: 'Your greatness, O Supreme, of qualities, deserves to be known by those of pure inner self' [BhP 10.14.6] — here 'to be known' [means] 'to become the object of knowledge.' And <s>Uddhava</s> too shall make this realized among you:

children.text: āgamiṣyaty adīrgheṇa kālena vrajam acyutaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Acyuta</s> shall come to <s>Vraja</s> before long;

children.text: priyaṃ vidhāsyate pitror bhagavān sātvatāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s>, lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, shall create what is dear to [his] parents!' ||

children.text: hatvā kaṃsaṃ raṅga-madhye pratīpaṃ sarva-sātvatām |
yad āha vaḥ samāgatya kṛṣṇaḥ satyaṃ karoti tat ||[BhP 10.46.34-5] iti |
children.translated_text: what <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to you upon arriving — he makes that true!' ||[BhP 10.46.34-35] — thus.
'Having slain <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the adversary of all <s>Sātvatas</s>, in the arena,

children.text: sātvatāṃ patir api pūrṇa-ṣaḍaiśvarya-sampattir api pitror yuvayor vrajeśitroḥ parama-sukha-śriyaṃ sadā svalālanā-rūpaṃ priyaṃ vidhāsyate | tatrāpy acyuta evāvasthāsyate, yatas tat tato hetor adyāpi satyaṃ śapathaṃ karoti, kurvann eva vartata ity arthaḥ | tad anenaiva nayena bhavatāṃ praṇayarṇaṃ vinayeya, na tu manāg api gamanāgastvena | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: 'Even though the lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, even though possessed of the full sixfold divine opulence, he shall create what is dear — always in the form of his own cherishing — for [his] parents, the two of you, the rulers of <s>Vraja</s>. And therein, he shall remain as <s>Acyuta</s> (unfallen) itself — because, for that reason, even now he makes [his] truthful oath, and continues making it' — this is the meaning. 'By this very policy, I would discharge the debt of your love — not even slightly through the manner of coming and going.' As follows:

children.text:
pitrādi-pratirūpa-rūpa-vasudevādi-pratīghātajād-
duḥkhāt kaṃsa-vināśanārtham agamaṃ śīghrāṃ nivṛttiṃ vidan |
tatrāsīt suhṛdāṃ manoratha-tatir yuddhāyatir durhṛdāṃ
caivaṃ tad-vyasanaṃ samāpya yadi ca prāgāṃ kva vā yāmy aham ||JGc_1,33.103|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'From the suffering born of the counter-image of father and others in the forms of <s>Vasudeva</s> and others,
I went for the purpose of destroying <s>Kaṃsa</s>, knowing the return would be swift;
there, the hosts of wishes of friends and the martial efforts of enemies [arose] —
and thus, having completed that calamity — and if I then came — where indeed would I go?' ||33.103|| — thus.

children.text: tataḥ śrī-vrajeśvarānumatyā pratyāsannāḥ sarve' pi prārthayiṣyante | evaṃ ced iha ca tava dvārakā-vad eva bahala-gṛha-bṛṃhaṇāya spṛhayāmaḥ | anyathā-karaṇaṃ tu yad asmākam adhanyatāṃ vahatīti |
