children.translated_text: 'Then, with the permission of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, all who are close shall petition: "If so, then here too, just as in <s>Dvārakā</s>, we desire the expansion of abundant households for you. The alternative would carry our misfortune."'

children.text: tad etad ākarṇya bhūmiṃ nirvarṇya tvaṃ tu tasminn asantuṣṭa iva cetasi cintayitāsi-gṛha-śabdaḥ khalv ebhir gṛhiṇī-paryāyatayā paryavasāyitaḥ | tatra ca hanta mama svāntaṃ kīdṛśaṃ vāmī vidhāsyantīti |
children.translated_text: 'Hearing this and gazing upon the earth, you shall think in your heart, as if unsatisfied: "The word 'household' has indeed been concluded by them as equivalent to 'wife.' And therein — alas! — what will my inner being become?"'

children.text: atha punar vibhāvayitāsi-bhavatu, pūrṇa-jñāna-tūrṇa-vidhānā ca paurṇamāsy atra sarvaṃ śarma nirmāsyati, na tv anyathākarmatāṃ dhāsyatīti | vaktavyaṃ tu vakṣyasi | tarhi rohiṇī-mātā rauhiṇeya-bhrātā ca dvārakāgārād ākāraṇīyau | tāv eva sarvam arvāg-bhāvyaṃ nivedayiṣyataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Then again, you shall consider: "So be it — <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, of full knowledge and swift arrangement, shall here fashion all happiness, and shall not create any impropriety." What is to be said, you shall say: "Then [my] mother <s>Rohiṇī</s> and [my] brother the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) must be summoned from the house in <s>Dvārakā</s>. They shall report everything that needs to be done henceforth."'

children.text: atha punar dāruka-sārathiṃ prati prathayiṣyasi-bho sārathe ! sarathaḥ prathamānayātyantīnatayā bhavān yadu-bhavanam āsādya sadyaḥ śrīmad-bhrātaraṃ tan-mātaraṃ ca prāpayeti | punar vicārya vakṣyasi-hanta ! tam uddhavam apy ānayeti |
children.translated_text: 'Then, you shall tell the charioteer <s>Dāruka</s>: "O charioteer! With your chariot, take yourself to the <s>Yadu</s> mansion at once with utmost urgency, and bring the glorious brother and his mother!" Then, reconsidering, you shall say: "Alas! Bring that <s>Uddhava</s> too!"'

children.text:
tatas tad-vandanāruke dāruke pavanam anuharamāṇena yānena muhūrta-mātrārdhatais taiḥ sārdham āgate tasmin vismita-manasaḥ śrīman-nandādayaḥ paramānandāśayatayā sahasā bhavad-āgamanavad eva sahasā mahasā todyamānātodya-vrajaṃ tan-nijālayam āneṣyanti |
[232] gateṣu ca dineṣu tri-catureṣu rāmādayas te vrajasthābhir ucitam eva tubhyaṃ rocayiṣyanti-
children.translated_text:
'Then, when <s>Dāruka</s>, who bows [in salutation], having gone with a wind-rivaling vehicle, arrives with those [persons] in half a <s>muhūrta</s> — the wonder-minded glorious <s>Nanda</s> and the others, with supreme joy in their hearts, shall lead them to their own dwelling, as swiftly and as suddenly as your own arrival, with a suddenly-sounded festive assemblage of musical instruments.'
[232] 'And after three or four days have passed, <s>Rāma</s> and the others, along with the <s>Vraja</s>-dwelling women, shall rightly propose to you what is fitting:'

children.text: yeṣāṃ prema-guṇair yas tvaṃ baddhaḥ suṣṭhutayā hariḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those by whose qualities of love you, O <s>Hari</s>, are bound excellently —

children.text: tasya tair viniruddhā ye kuryus te katham anyathā ||JGc_1,33.104||
children.translated_text: those who are restrained by you through those [qualities] — how could they act otherwise?' ||33.104||

children.text: sarve ca militvā nirṇeṣyanti mānyāḥ kanyā-vicāram | kātyāyanyārādhikās tāḥ kanyā dhanyādayaḥ sanyāyatām arhantīti |
children.translated_text: 'And all, having met, shall determine the honorable matter of the maidens: "Those worshippers of <s>Kātyāyanī</s> — <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Dhanyā</s>, and others — those maidens deserve to be justly united [with him]."'

children.text: rāmoddhavau tu parama-niṣṇātau kṛṣṇavaj jñātvā tūṣṇīm evāvasthāsyataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'But <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>, being supremely knowledgeable — knowing as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> does — shall remain silent.'

children.text: tatas tad-artham ārambhe labdha-sambhede vraja-pati-jampatī pūrṇa-mano-gatī pūrṇimābhyarṇam āsādya sadyas tasyāṃ varivasyā-pūrvakaṃ sarvaṃ nivedayiṣyataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Then, when the endeavor for that purpose has found a meeting — the royal couple of <s>Vraja</s>, whose minds are fully resolved, having approached <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, shall immediately submit everything to her, preceded by veneration.'

children.text: sāpi vakṣyati-tad api bhadram eva, kintu varyāḥ parama-varyā rādhādayaḥ kathaṃ vā na svīkāryāḥ ?
children.translated_text: 'And she shall say: "That too is well and good — but the most excellent, supremely excellent ones — <s>Rādhā</s> and the others — how can they not be accepted?"'

children.text: tau tu sa-vailakṣyaṃ vakṣyataḥ-kāḥ khalu rādhikādy-abhidhāḥ ?
children.translated_text: 'And those two (<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>) shall say with embarrassment: "Who indeed are those called <s>Rādhikā</s> and so on?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-dhanyānāṃ vṛṣabhānv-ādīnāṃ kanyā eva |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "The very daughters of the blessed ones — <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> and the others!"'

children.text: punas tau vakṣyataḥ-sudhy-ādi-guro ! na budhyāmahe | niḥśodhyaṃ tu bodhyatām |
children.translated_text: 'The two shall again say: "O guru of the wise and such! We do not understand! Let what needs to be clarified be explained."'

children.text: sā tu sa-hāsaṃ vakṣyati-yathā kātyāyany-ārādhikānāṃ kanyātvam evam anyāsāṃ rādhikādikānām api |
children.translated_text: 'And she shall say with a smile: "Just as the maidenhood of the worshippers of <s>Kātyāyanī</s> [is maintained], so too is that of the others — <s>Rādhikā</s> and the rest."'

children.text: tau punar utphulla-nayanaṃ vakṣyataḥ-vispaṣṭaṃ kathyatām | yadi viṣaya-maye' py asmādṛśi kṛpā-viṣayatācaryate |
children.translated_text: 'The two shall again say with blossoming eyes: "Let it be stated clearly! If compassion is felt even for such worldly ones as us."'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-bhavantaḥ khalv idaṃ nānubhavanta iva santi | yat punar adyāpi kanyā eva tā dhanyāḥ | māyā-kalpita-cchāyā-prāyā evānyatra pariṇāyitāḥ | tac ca svapnavad eva | yasmān maryādālaṅghana-paryāyatayā tā eva ca śayyādau paryavasāyante iti | kiṃ tad idaṃ kiñcana bhavantāv anu sa-vedanaṃ nivedayāmi | tās tad ekānuraktā mādṛśa-sāntvanayā param adyāvadhi dhairya-sampṛktāḥ | samprati tu tyakta-mātrātirikta-prāṇa-gātrā bhaviṣyanti | tāsāṃ tad idaṃ na kevalam aham eva vidaty asmi, kintu sarvāpi vraja-janatā | tac ca pūrvam api kiñcit kiñcid viśeṣtas tu kṛṣṇa-kṛta-vṛṣṇi-sthāna-prasthāna-gata-tad-anavasthāvasthāyām | yata idaṃ munayo' pi varṇayiṣyanti |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "You indeed do not seem to experience this: that even now, those blessed ones are maidens indeed! Those who were married elsewhere were mostly shadow-like, fashioned by <s>māyā</s>. And that [marriage] was like a dream. Because, by the course of not transgressing the boundary, those very ones arrive in the bed and such." "Let me then report to you something regarding this, with feeling: Those ones, exclusively devoted [to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], have hitherto been sustained in steadfastness by consolation from the likes of me. But now, they shall become ones whose life-breaths and bodies exceed [the limit] of what can be abandoned. And this is known not by me alone, but by all the people of <s>Vraja</s> as well. And that [was known] even before, to some degree — but especially during the unsettled state caused by <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> departure to the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>-land. For this, even the sages shall describe."'

children.text: tatra pūrvaṃ yathā-kuja-gatiṃ gamitā na vidāmaḥ; kaśmalena kavaraṃ vasanaṃ vā [BhP 10.35.17] ity ādinā | uttaraṃ tu, nivārayāmaḥ samupetya mādhavaṃ; kiṃ no ækariṣyan kula-vṛddha-bāndhavāḥ [BhP 10.39.28] ity uktvā, visṛjya lajjāṃ ruruduḥ sma su-svaraṃ; govinda dāmodara mādhaveti [BhP 10.39.31] ity ādinā, kṛṣṇa-dūte samāyāte uddhave tyakta-laukikāḥ [BhP 10.47.9] ity ādinā, gata-hriyaḥ [BhP 10.47.10] ity ādinā,
children.translated_text: 'There, the earlier [descriptions], as follows: "We do not know the direction to which they were driven" [BhP 10.35.17] and so forth. And the later, as follows: having said "Shall we restrain <s>Mādhava</s> when he arrives? — what will our clan-elders and kinsmen do to us?" [BhP 10.39.28] — and then: "Abandoning shame, they wept aloud with sweet voices: '<s>Govinda</s>! <s>Dāmodara</s>! <s>Mādhava</s>!'" [BhP 10.39.31] and so forth; "When <s>Uddhava</s>, the messenger of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, arrived, they abandoned worldly conventions" [BhP 10.47.9] and so forth; "they who had lost [all] shame" [BhP 10.47.10] and so forth,'

children.text: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ bhrātṝn patīn putrān svasṝn api |
children.translated_text: 'Mother, father, brothers,

children.text: yad-arthe jahima dāśārha dustyajān sva-janān prabho ||[BhP 10.65.11] ity ādinā,
yā dustyajaṃ svajanam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā ity ādinā ca |
children.translated_text: 'She who, abandoning her own people, hard to abandon, and the path of the noble' — and so forth.

children.text: atra patīn putrān iti yad uktaṃ, tat khalu gauṇīm eva vṛttim anukramya, na tu mukhyām iti bhavat-praśnānukrameṇa prakhyāsāmi | tatra yady anyathā manyadhve, tary evam ācakṣmahe-narakādānīta-guru-kumāratayā jita-dharmarāja-dhāmā rājad-aghajin-nāmā so' yam etad anurakta-jano' py adharmasya kalayāpi spraṣṭuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca na śakyata eva | kintu lajjā-mātraṃ tasya tasya ca maryādā-paryāpakam iti vastutas tu na kevalaṃ rāgata eva tās tādṛśīṃ gati-mārgatāḥ kintv anādi-siddha-svabhāvatayā tad-vadhū-bhāvataś ceti mantra-draṣṭāro' pi niṣṭaṅkayanti | tad etad balarāmoddhavau ca suṣṭhu jānīta iti tāv api praṣṭavyau, anyathā tāsu tat-sandeśa-haratā tayor na deśa-rūpatām āsīdet |
children.translated_text: 'Here, the statement "husbands, sons" follows only a secondary usage, not the primary one — this I shall explain in accordance with the sequence of your question. Therein, if you think otherwise, then we shall state it thus: He who brought back the guru's son from the realm of the dead, who conquered the domain of <s>Dharmarāja</s> (<s>Yama</s>) — shining with the name "Conqueror of Sin" — even though loved by those people, cannot be touched or seen by even a fraction of <s>adharma</s>! Rather, mere modesty on his part and the sufficiency of propriety's boundary [explain the usage]. In reality, those [<s>gopīs</s>] were not merely led to such a path by passion alone, but by their eternally established nature and by their status as his brides — even the seers of sacred formulas confirm this! And this is well known to <s>Balarāma</s> and <s>Uddhava</s> — therefore they too should be asked; otherwise, their carrying messages to those [<s>gopīs</s>] would not have been fitting.'

children.text: punas tau vakṣyataḥ-vatsaḥ kim idam anusandadhāti ?
children.translated_text: 'The two (<s>Balarāma</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>) shall say: "What is the dear one investigating?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-sa ca pūrvaṃ kiñcid anusaṃhitavān āsīt | uttaraṃ tu samyag vidann evāste | kintu samprati lajjayā nāvadhānaṃ sajjayati |
children.translated_text: 'She (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) shall say: "He had previously investigated somewhat. But the answer, he knows well even now. However, at present, from modesty, he does not prepare attentiveness."'

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-tāsāṃ tad-artha-prāṇa-jihāsāṃ kim asau jānāti?
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say: "Does he know of their readiness to abandon their life-breaths for his sake?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-uktam eva samyag vidann āsta iti |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "It has already been said — he knows well and remains."'

children.text: yataḥ pūrvam apy uddhave tathā samudbuddhaṃ kṛtavān, yathā ca tad-vacanaṃ satya-vacasaś ca gāsyanti-
children.translated_text: 'For even previously, he had made <s>Uddhava</s> fully awakened in that regard, and the words of the truth-speaker (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) shall be sung [by them]:'

children.text: gacchoddhava vrajaṃ saumya pitror nau prītim āvaha |
children.translated_text: 'Go, <s>Uddhava</s>, to <s>Vraja</s>, O gentle one! Bring delight to our parents!

children.text: gopīnāṃ mad-viyogādhiṃ mat-sandeśair vimocaya ||
children.translated_text: And relieve the <s>gopīs</s>' anguish of separation from me with my messages!

children.text: tā man-manaskā mat-prāṇā mad-arthe tyakta-daihikāḥ |
children.translated_text: They, whose minds are fixed on me, whose life-breaths are mine, who have given up bodily [concerns] for my sake,

children.text: mām eva dayitaṃ preṣṭham ātmānaṃ manasā gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: who have taken me alone — their beloved, their dearest, their very Self — as the goal of their minds;

children.text: ye tyakta-loka-dharmāś ca mad-arthe tān bibharmy aham ||
children.translated_text: they who have abandoned worldly and religious conventions for my sake — I sustain them!

children.text: mayi tāḥ preyasāṃ preṣṭhe dūra-sthe gokula-striyaḥ |
children.translated_text: When I, the dearest of their beloveds, am far away, the women of <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: smarantyo æṅga vimuhyanti virahautkaṇṭhya-vihvalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: remembering [me], O friend, become bewildered, overwhelmed by the agitation of separation-longing!

children.text: dhārayanty ati-kṛcchreṇa prāyaḥ prāṇān kathañcana |
children.translated_text: They sustain their life-breaths with extreme difficulty, barely, somehow —

children.text: pratyāgamana-sandeśair ballavyo me mad-ātmikāḥ ||[BhP 10.46.3-6]
children.translated_text: those cowherd-women of mine, who are my very Self, [sustained] by the messages of my return!' ||[BhP 10.46.3-6]||

children.text: atra mat-sandeśaiḥ iti mayy āveśya manaḥ kṛṣṇe vimuktāśeṣa-vṛtti yat anusmarantyo māṃ nityam acirān mām upaiṣyatha [BhP 10.47.36] iti paryavasānair ity arthaḥ | mām eva dayitam iti, me vallavyaḥ ity atra tu viśeṣo' py asti, tasmāt tad eka-vrata-jīvana-vratānāṃ tad-bhāryāṇāṃ nānyā gatir nyāyyā |
children.translated_text: 'Here, "with my messages" means with messages whose culmination is "Fixing your minds on me, on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with all activities relinquished, constantly remembering me — you shall reach me before long" [BhP 10.47.36] — that is the meaning. "Me alone as their beloved" — and "my cowherd-women" — here too there is a special [emphasis]; therefore, for those whose vow of life is solely devoted to him, who are his wives — no other destiny is proper.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tatas tataḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tatas tau bhāvayiṣyataḥ | satyam asmākaṃ prakaṭatare' pi loka-dharma-ghaṭanānarha-pratikāre' pi tāsāṃ vighaṭana-duḥkhe yad adyāpi snuṣākaraṇa-spṛhā nāpayāti, pratyuta sātatyata eva tāsu snuṣābhānaṃ vibhāti | dharmānyathā-bhāve lakṣyate | yad avaśyam āyatyāṃ vidita-rahasyatām āyātīti | tad api prāpta-kālatāṃ kalayati sma |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then the two (<s>Balarāma</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>) shall contemplate: "Truly, even though this is more openly [known], even though it is incapable of being counteracted by the arrangement of worldly conventions — the sorrow of their disruption, which even now does not dispel the desire to make them daughters-in-law — rather, perpetually, the semblance of their being daughters-in-law shines forth among them. When <s>dharma</s> is perceived otherwise — [they realize] that inevitably in the future, the secret shall come to be known." And that too was being reckoned as having reached its appointed time.'

children.text: atha tau spaṣṭaṃ vakṣyataḥ-rahasyam idaṃ lokāḥ kathaṃ maṃsyante |
children.translated_text: 'And the two shall speak plainly: "How will the world regard this secret?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-māyāyāḥ svabhāva-vyāpitir iyam avyabhicāritayā lakṣyate, yad avaśyam āyatyāṃ vidita-rahasyatām āyātīti | tad api prāpta-kālatāṃ kalayati sma |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "This is observed as the unfailing nature-pervading [power] of <s>Māyā</s> — that inevitably in the future, the secret shall come to be known. And that too was being reckoned as having reached its appointed time."'

children.text: yataḥ sarveṣām api sat-saṅkalpānām upari prabhavator bhavator nigūḍhā yā tad-artham utkaṇṭhā, sā hy adhunā parāṃ koṭim ārūḍhā jhaṭiti rūḍha-kāryā bhaved eva | tau vakṣyataḥ-svīyām ananya-sambandhitāṃ tāḥ kathaṃ vidanti |
children.translated_text: '"For the concealed longing of you two, who prevail over even all auspicious intentions, for that purpose — having now ascended to the ultimate limit, shall swiftly become an accomplished deed." The two shall say: "How do they know their exclusive relationship to him?"'

children.text:
sā vakṣyati-pūrvaṃ sa vo hi svāmī bhavati iti durvāsaso vacanenāpi samyaṅ nāviduḥ kintu paścād viduḥ |
[248] tau vakṣyataḥ-katham iva?
children.translated_text:
'She shall say: "Previously, even by the word of <s>Durvāsas</s> — 'He indeed shall become your lord' — they did not fully know; but afterward, they knew."
[248] The two shall say: "How so?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati- uddhavena śrī-kṛṣṇābhiprāyam anuvyaktīkaraṇāt | ataevoktam-api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro ædhunāste [BhP 10.47.21] iti |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "By <s>Uddhava's</s> making manifest the intention of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>." Hence it was said: "Ah, in <s>Madhupurī</s>, does the noble one's son now dwell?" [BhP 10.47.21].'

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-tāsāṃ śvaśuraṃ-manyādīnāṃ ye' nugatās te prāyeṇānutāpaṃ prāpsyanti |
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say: "Those who followed them — those whom they consider fathers-in-law and such — they shall mostly attain remorse."'

children.text: atha sā tu puruṣam iva vakṣyati-tat kim āsāṃ parama-sādhvīnāṃ mādhvīkavan madhura-snigdhatāvalitānāṃ duṣkara-taraṇa-duḥkha-bhāskara-puṣkalatāpa-śuṣkatā soḍhavyā | tathā sarva-dhurīṇatā-pravīṇasya nija-kula-dhurandharasya govardhana-dharasya durdhara-lajjā-bhāra-sajjanam anumodanīyam | vastutas tu teṣām api na sukha-bhaṅga-prasaṅgaḥ yad-dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tvat-kṛte [BhP 10.14.35] iti śrī-śuka-vacanād api | tathā ca na vacana-marmābhir ācaraṇīyam, yathā sarva-sukha-sacanam eva syāt |
children.translated_text: 'Then she shall speak like a man: "Should the desiccation of those supremely chaste ones — sweet and affectionate, anointed with honeyed tenderness — [caused by] the scorching sun of the suffering of most-difficult-to-cross [separation], be endured? And should the burdening of the unbearable weight of shame upon the supreme bearer of all responsibilities, the upholder of his own lineage, the lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>, be approved? In reality, there is no occasion for the disruption of their happiness either — as the glorious <s>Śuka's</s> words declare: 'For whom home, wealth, friends, beloveds, self, sons, life-breaths, and hope are all for your sake' [BhP 10.14.35]. And so, words that pierce the vital point should not be employed — so that all may be accompanied by happiness alone."'

children.text: tad etan nirūpya sā punaḥ sahāsaṃ vakṣyati-sāmprataṃ pratataṃ kutukāntaraṃ bhavadvyāṃ kila nāvakalitam | yat khalu yuṣman-nandana ānanda-dyūte tāsāṃ patiṃmanyāṃst tat-pitrādi-paryantaṃ sarvaṃ jitavān | lajjām eva sajjan na tad-gṛham ānītavān iti |
children.translated_text: 'Having established this, she shall again say with a laugh: "At present, a continuous secret curiosity has apparently not been perceived by you two! For your dear one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), in the dice-game of delight, has won over all — those they consider their husbands, up to and including their fathers! Only producing modesty, he has not brought them to that [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] house."'

children.text: tad idaṃ guptam api kṛtam ādi-varāha-nāmā bhagavān api sva-purāṇe sākṣitayā lakṣayatīti sarvathātra nānyathā mantavyam | yathā-
children.translated_text: 'This, though done in secret, is also observed as testimony by the blessed Lord bearing the name <s>Ādi-Varāha</s> in his own <s>Purāṇa</s> — therefore this should in no way be thought otherwise. As follows:'

children.text:
dyūta-krīḍā bhagavatā kṛtā gopa-janaiḥ saha |
paṇāvahāra-rūpeṇa jitā gopyo dhanāni ca |
gopair ānīya tatraiva kṛṣṇāya viniveditāḥ ||iti |
tau vakṣyataḥ-tat-pitrādīnāṃ tan-mitrādīnāṃ vā ko vyavasāyaḥ ?
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say: "What is the intention of their fathers and such, or of their friends?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-te' pi mayopadiṣṭaṃ tattvīkṛtya pṛṣṭa-kṛtyās tad idam uddiṣṭavantaḥ-
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "They too, having accepted as true what was instructed by me, and having been asked about the matter, have declared thus:"'

children.text: aho para-sparśa-subhīru yad vapur
children.translated_text: 'Alas! The body that is supremely afraid of another's touch,

children.text: yat kṛṣṇasāra-praṇayaika-śarma ca |
children.translated_text: and whose sole happiness is in the love of the <s>kṛṣṇasāra</s> deer (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) —

children.text: tāsāṃ mṛgīṇām iva tat-paraṃ prati
children.translated_text: of those doe-women, toward that supreme [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],

children.text: praditsavo vyādha-manāṃsi bibhrati ||JGc_1,33.105||
children.translated_text: those who wish to give [them away] bear the minds of hunters!' ||33.105||

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ- rādhikādy-ārādhikānāṃ kā vārtā ?
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say: "What news of the worshippers such as <s>Rādhikā</s>?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-mat-pṛṣṭābhis tābhir apy evam ādiṣṭam-
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "When asked by me, they too have instructed thus:"'

children.text:
yathā sītā-devyā daśa-mukha-kṛtārtir vipad abhūd
yathā vā rukmiṇyā vivahana-vidhiś cedipa-kṛte |
tathā rādhādīnāṃ para-gṛha-gatir yā bata vipat
kathaṃ tasyā nityā sthitir abhimatā hanta suhṛdām ||JGc_1,33.106|| [*9]
[*9] This verse is repeated in Uttara-campū, 31.43.
children.translated_text:
'Just as the affliction wrought by the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) upon the goddess <s>Sītā</s> was a calamity;
just as the marriage ceremony of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> was performed by <s>Cedipa</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) [against her will] —
so too the going of <s>Rādhā</s> and others to another's house — that is indeed a calamity!
How can its permanence be desired — alas! — by well-wishers?' ||33.106||

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-atha rādhikādīnām ārtānāṃ kā vārtā ?
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say: "What then is the news of the anguished <s>Rādhikā</s> and others?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-
children.translated_text: 'She shall say:'

children.text: deyam adhīnaṃ kārtsnyenābhivyāptyā ca tatra kṛṣṇe svam |
children.translated_text: 'What should be given is [their] dependence entirely, with full manifestation, there upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, their own [lord];

children.text: tad-rūpaṃ racayitvā sātipratyaya-padāni tā dadhire ||JGc_1,33.107||
children.translated_text: having fashioned his form [internally], they have established supremely trustworthy footholds!' ||33.107||

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-tāḥ kiṃ sākṣād anuyuktāḥ ?
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say: "Were those [<s>gopīs</s>] directly questioned?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-atha kim ? yatas tāsāṃ marma-prakaṭana-karmaṭhatayā mayā pṛṣṭam-bho vipaścitaḥ kāścid evaṃ vadanti | tāḥ khalu kṛṣṇe prema-mātrākharva-sarvasvāḥ | premā ca balavad virodhi-sad-bhāva-milad-bhaya-prayāsa-pracchādana-paricchadatayā yathā vardhate, na tathānyathā |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "Indeed! For I, with the diligence of revealing their innermost secret, asked them: 'O wise ones, some say thus.' They are indeed ones whose entire all is nothing but the undiminished love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. And love grows in the manner of concealment — covering itself with the effort of fear born from the existence of a strong adversary — and not otherwise."'

children.text: tarhi kathaṃ tāsām apy anyāsām iva patitayā tat-sampatti-kāmanā-nikāmam antaranuvartata iti ?
children.translated_text: '"Then how does the desire for that fortune [of union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], like that of others who have fallen, silently proceed within them?"'

children.text: tad etad ākarṇya pāṭala-paṭala-savarṇa-varṇinyas tā vara-varṇinyas tad idam avarṇayanta |
children.translated_text: 'Hearing this, those excellent women, of complexion like a heap of pale-red [blossoms], described thus:'

children.text: hanta ! tāsām eva savirodhas tad-avarodhaḥ sambhavatā-dṛtīyamānā dvitīya-pati-bhāvanā ca, na punar anyasyāḥ kasyāścid api | yā khalu tad-avarodha-virodha-vāñchā | sā vā kathaṃ prema-prathana-mayī syād iti na budhyāmahe |
children.translated_text: '"Alas! The quarrel with their being his secluded ones — and the notion of a second husband, being squeezed [into existence] — that is [their condition], and not that of anyone else! And the desire for conflict with that seclusion — how could that be constituted of the spreading of love? — we do not understand."'

children.text: asmākam yadyapy asau pārśva-gato raho-gatas tathāpi tasyāṅghri-yugaṃ navaṃ navam [BhP 1.11.34] ity eva bodha-viṣayo bhavati | kintu-
children.translated_text: '"Though he is at our side, though he is with us in private, nevertheless, 'his pair of feet, ever new' [BhP 1.11.34] — this alone is the object of our awareness. But:"'

children.text: budhitāḥ paitṛka-janatā
children.translated_text: 'Those known as paternal folk have been understood;

children.text: buddhāḥ śvaśurābhimānino lokāḥ |
children.translated_text: those people who consider themselves fathers-in-law have been perceived;

children.text: mānitāḥ sarve' py asmābhir
children.translated_text: all have been honored by us;

children.text: na mato dharmas tu kenāpi ||JGc_1,33.108||
children.translated_text: but <s>dharma</s> has been accepted by no one!' ||33.108||

children.text: yad asmākaṃ bālyād eva tasmin nija-rmaṇatā-bhāvanāṃ dūrīkartum āgraham urīkurvanti, tasmād asmān mā sneha-peṣaṃ piṇḍhi, kintu svābhīṣṭam eva viśaṇḍhi |
children.translated_text: '"Since, from our very childhood, they insist on removing from us the contemplation of our own lover-hood toward him — therefore, do not grind us with the pestle of affection, but rather investigate your own desire!"'

children.text: atha tau vakṣyataḥ-bhavatyā kim udbhāvitam ?
children.translated_text: 'Then the two shall say: "What has been proposed by you?"'

children.text:
sā vakṣyati-tato mayā hasitvā śavasitvā ca tābhyaḥ pratyāśā-mātraṃ pratyāsāditam asti | yadi bhavator icchā samṛcchate, tās tu daivatas tāvan-nija-prāṇa-valalbhasya valalbhatvneālābhāl labdha-mahā-duḥkhās tatra ca svasyānya-hasta-patitatayā jugupsitaṃ-manyatā śuṣkās tatra ca priyāpriya-viprakarṣa-sannikarṣataḥ prāpta-mano-dharṣās tatra ca nirantaraṃ śaṅkamānaiḥ patiṃ-manyādibhir maṅkṣu maṅkṣu-kṛta-nivāraṇa-bhartsanādi-nikarṣās tatas tata eva ca duḥsaha-preṣṭha-viraha-tīvra-tāpa [BhP 10.29.10] ity ādy-uktatādṛg-avasthābhyo' pi mahānurāgataḥ pīḍanād bahula-dahanākāra-kārāgāra-vasatiṃ-manyatayā nigīrṇa-sarva-kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇam api kalpaṃ manvānāḥ samprati tadīya-mahā-viraha-vaha-samayam atītya cātmānaṃ tad-upekṣyatām
apy utprekṣya lajjā-mātra-paryavasānam āsajya ca dhik-kṛtaṃ-manyā daśamīm api daśāṃ tanvānāḥ | kiṃ bahunā, bahir-antaḥ-sukumāratāyām api kaumārata eva vyādhānubiddha-snigdha-kānana-pratyāsatty-aparityāgi-mṛgīvat prakhara-darāpāra-para-pāravaśya-labdha-vicitra-durgati-samplutatayā paśyatāṃ śṛṇvatām api hṛdayaṃ dhunvānā raso' yam iti manyamānena niṣkaruṇa-kautukena kenacid evopekṣituṃ śakyante, na punar anyena |
children.translated_text: 'She shall say: "Then, having laughed and having been firm, I conveyed to them merely a hope of expectation. If the wish of you two coincides — those [<s>gopīs</s>], by divine [ordainment], having obtained great suffering from the non-attainment of the status of beloved to the beloved of their very life-breaths, and therein considering themselves as having fallen into another's hands as contemptible, dried up, and therein having attained mental disturbance from the proximity and distance of what is dear and not dear, and therein [suffering] from the frequent scoldings and restraints by those who consider themselves their husbands, who are constantly suspicious — and then from all those states described as 'the fierce burning of unbearable separation from the dearest' [BhP 10.29.10] and such — and from the torment of great love, considering themselves as dwelling in a prison of the form of a conflagration, every moment swallowed [by grief], reckoning even a moment as an eon — now, having surpassed the time of his great separation, and imagining themselves as being disregarded by him, having attached themselves to merely the culmination of modesty, and deeming themselves worthy of censure, they are producing even a tenth state [of suffering]! In short — though externally and internally delicate, like a doe who from tender childhood, pierced by a disease, does not abandon her proximity to the dear forest — from the overwhelming subjection to various misfortunes obtained through the fierce, fathomless, overwhelming power of another — though they shake the hearts of even those who see and hear — can they be disregarded only by someone possessed of merciless curiosity, thinking 'this is the aesthetic savor (<s>rasa</s>)' — but not by anyone else!"'

children.text: tau sāsraṃ vakṣyataḥ-samprati tāḥ kāṃ gatiṃ matiṃ cāsādayanti ?
children.translated_text: 'The two shall say with tears: "What state and what intention do they now attain?"'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-
children.translated_text: 'She shall say:'

children.text: kurvanti maunaṃ krandaṃ vā śūnyaṃ paśyati vartma vā |
children.translated_text: 'They maintain silence, or they weep, or they gaze at the empty path,

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ vāñchanti mṛtyuṃ vā tāsām evaṃvidhā gatiḥ ||JGc_1,33.109||
children.translated_text: or they desire <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, or they desire death — such is their state!' ||33.109||

children.text:
punas tau sāsraṃ vakṣyataḥ-samprati tāḥ prati vatsasya kā vidhitsā ?
[272] sā vakṣyati-tad etat paścād api niścīyatām | yat khalu preyasāṃ premākṣemaṃ tad-bhāvanāmaya-premānurūpam eva sva-sthemānaṃ labhate | na tu svāgraha-grahilatām iti |
children.translated_text:
'Again the two shall say with tears: "What is the dear one's intention toward them at present?"
[272] She shall say: "Let that be determined later as well. For the anxiety of the beloved's love, that which is constituted of contemplation of her love-form, attains its own stability accordingly — and not the clutching of one's own insistence."'

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-manyāmahe tathāpy asmattaḥ saṅkocaṃ rocayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: Those two (<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>) shall say: 'We think nevertheless he shall be pleased to show restraint toward us.'

children.text:
sā vakṣyati-bhavatāṃ hṛdi sadā vidyotamānaḥ so' yaṃ tad api vetti, tasmān nitāntaṃ nānyathā kariṣyati | kiṃ bahunā, bhavad-āśravam anu sarveṣām eva saṃśravaḥ pratibhāti | kim uta tasya ?
[275] tau vakṣyataḥ-tarhi garga-niṣedha-vedhasya kā cikitsā ?
children.translated_text:
She (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) shall say: 'He who is constantly shining in your hearts — he knows that too; therefore, he shall certainly not act otherwise. In short, following what is heard by your honors, the hearing of all indeed appears [to be in accord]. What then of his?'
[275] Those two shall say: 'Then what is the remedy for the prohibition-arrangement of <s>Garga</s>?'

children.text: sā sa-hāsaṃ vakṣyati-sa khalu līlā-naiyatyam eva tatratya-doṣatayādhyastavān | sva-yajamāna-hita-samīhita-sahitatayā, na tu parama-śubha-niveśa-veśa-rūpāṇām āsāṃ kleśa-leśa-praveśadā sadeśatā sambhavati |
children.translated_text: She shall say with a laugh: 'He indeed superimposed the regularity of [mere] play as a fault pertaining to that [situation] — together with the well-being intended for his own patron's benefit; but there can be no locale that would introduce even a trace of distress to these [gopīs] whose appearances are of supremely auspicious nature.'

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-sampraty asmābhiḥ kim iva sopānam upeyam ?
children.translated_text: Those two shall say: 'What step should we now take?'

children.text: sā vakṣyati-sopānaṃ mayā copeyam, bhavadbhis tu sarva eva vraja-janā bhojanāya praṇayena nimantrya nimantryantām | tarhy antaḥ-paṭī-kṣepān naṭīnām ākāra iva tat prakaṭībhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: She shall say: 'A step must be taken by me also; but by your honors — let all the people of <s>Vraja</s> be invited with affection for a feast! Then, from the casting aside of the inner curtain, the true form of the actresses shall become manifest.'

children.text: tau vakṣyataḥ-yathājñāpayanti vijñānācārya-varyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those two shall say: 'As the most excellent teacher of wisdom commands!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca- tataḥ sā pratyakṣata eva tāv abhi bahulam abhivadantī gṛhāya prahāpayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then she (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), speaking abundantly before those two in their very presence, shall send them home.'

children.text: atha kathakasya manaḥ-kathā-tataś ca pūrṇimā manasi viviveca-śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlāyām anādi-siddhaṃ śrīmad-bhāgavatam eva mukhyaṃ pramāṇam |
children.translated_text: Now, the narrator's inner reflection — then <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> pondered in her mind: 'In the <s>līlā</s> of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the eternally established <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</s> alone is the primary authority.'

children.text: tatra yā khalu rāsa-yoge yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ [BhP 10.29.1] ity anena nitya-vyakti-svarūpa-śakti-vṛtti-viśeṣakā yā yogamāyā tan-nirvāhakatayā bādarāyaṇinā samudīritā, sā punar aham eva | tatra tena rāsaṃ prakāśaṃ parīkṣit-pariṣadi varṇayitvā tatra prāptam avarṇa-tritayaṃ nirasya rasyatayā samāhitam | tathā samprati vraje' pi tat-prasaktam iti jñātvā mayāpi samādheyam | tatra tejīyasāṃ na doṣāya [BhP 10.33.29] itivad atrāpi yadyapi narakād ānītā ity ādinā tal-lepa-sambhāvanāpayāpitaiva |
children.translated_text: 'Therein, the <s>Yogamāyā</s> mentioned in "at the conjunction of the <s>rāsa</s>, he took refuge in <s>Yogamāyā</s>" [BhP 10.29.1] — she who is the differentiating function of the eternally manifest intrinsic potency (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>) — was proclaimed by <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>) as the one who carries out that [rāsa]. She is none other than myself. Therein, having described the <s>rāsa</s> openly in the assembly of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, the three [potential] colorless [objections] that arose were removed, and it was established with full <s>rasa</s>. Likewise, now, knowing that the same [issue] has become relevant in <s>Vraja</s> too, I must arrange [things] similarly. Therein, just as "for the mighty, [it] is no fault" [BhP 10.33.29] — here too, even though "brought from hell" and such — the suspicion of taint has already been dispelled.'

children.text: atha para-dāra-vāra-samāhāra-kāraṇān ācāraś ca yathā gopīnāṃ tat-patīnāṃ ca [BhP 10.33.25] ity anena yaṃ parihāram āpitas tathātrāpi tāś ca na kevalaṃ rāgata eva tādṛśīṃ gatim āgatāḥ ity ādinā tāsu tadīya-nityāṅganā-bhāva-vyaṅgataḥ sa ca sāṅgī-kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And as for the custom occasioned by the congregation of another's wives — just as the solution was provided by "as [was the case] of the <s>gopīs</s> and their husbands" [BhP 10.33.25] — here too, [the statement] "those [gopīs] attained that state not merely from passion" and so forth — through the suggestion therein of their being eternally his own women — that [solution] has been adopted.'

children.text: tathāpi nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya [BhP 10.33.37] itivad asūyābhāsavattayā sambhāvitās tat-patiṃ-manyāḥ samādhātavyāḥ | tac ca tad-rahasyaṃ pūrvaṃ guptam āsīd iti māyā-dvārā yathā-guptaṃ samāhitam | sāmprataṃ tu vyaktam abhūd iti tathā tad-dvārā vyaktam eva samādheyam | yena ca sarveṣām api sarva-samādhānam ādheyaṃ bhavitā, anyathā tat-tat-karaṇaṃ vṛthā-paraṃ syāt iti |
children.translated_text: 'Nevertheless, just as "they bore no ill will toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>" [BhP 10.33.37] — those who were regarded as their husbands, being endowed with the semblance of envy, are to be reconciled. And the secret of that [arrangement] was formerly hidden — so through <s>māyā</s>, it was reconciled as hidden. But now it has become manifest — so through that very [<s>māyā</s>]-means, it must be reconciled as manifest. And by this, the complete reconciliation of all [parties] shall be accomplished; otherwise, this and that [arrangement] would be utterly futile.'

children.text: atha spaṣṭam ācaṣṭa--[287] ṛṣir uvāca-dināntare tu sarva-nimantraṇāyāṃ yathā-vṛttānte vartite sarvāḥ sādhāraṇa-mahodayāḥ śrī-rādhādayaś ca tatrāgamiṣyanti | kintu pūrvata eva jana-saṅgīta-vrajeśa-nirmitānaṅgīkāratām ātmano duḥkha-bhaṅgī-saṅgitāṃ maṃsyanta eva | tava ca rūkṣatā-vīkṣaṇena tāḥ sūkṣmāṅgatāṃ gamiṣyanti | tatra sāmpratam anyāsāṃ svasamāna-kanyānām aṅgīkāreṇa hṛt-kamale' pi bhaṅgitām āpatsyante |
children.translated_text: Then she (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) spoke plainly: [287] The sage said: 'On the next day, when the general invitation has proceeded as planned, all — the great ones of common celebration, <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and the others — shall come there. But even beforehand, they shall consider themselves to be confirmed in the non-acceptance, famous through the people's singing, established by the lord of <s>Vraja</s> — and they shall consider themselves as objects of the composition of the breaking of their own sorrow. And by your gaze of harshness, they shall become slender-limbed. And now, by your acceptance of other maidens of their own kind, they shall attain brokenness even in the lotus of their hearts.'

children.text: tathā ca bhāvī ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: And there is a future verse:

children.text: dāva-trastā mṛga-duhitaraś candrahīnāś cakoryaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Like doe-daughters frightened by a forest fire, like <s>cakora</s> birds without the moon,

children.text: srastā vṛkṣān nava-kalatikā nīra-riktāḥ śapharyaḥ |
children.translated_text: like fresh young creepers fallen from trees, like fish deprived of water,

children.text: ūrja-prāntād bahir apagatā hanta navyābja-nālyo
children.translated_text: like fresh lotus-stalks gone beyond the border of the <s>Ūrja</s> (autumn) [season] —

children.text: yadvad dṛṣṭā hari-virahitā rādhikādyāś ca tadvat ||JGc_1,33.110||
children.translated_text: alas! — just as those are seen, so too <s>Rādhikā</s> and the others, bereft of <s>Hari</s>!' || (JGc 1,33.110)

children.text: tad evaṃ tāsāṃ kṛcchrāyamāṇānām amitābhyamita-tādṛśvarī śrī-vrajeśvarī tu bāṣpa-pūrṇa-nayanā paurṇamāsīṃ nirvarṇayiṣyati | sā tu vadiṣyati-sarve sarvato' py anvicchantu | yathādyatana-nimantraṇataḥ kaścid api na paścimatām añcati |
children.translated_text: Thus, when they are becoming distressed, the incomparably sovereign queen of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>, her eyes filled with tears, shall look toward <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>. And she shall say: 'Let all seek [the answer] from all sides! By today's invitation, let no one be left behind!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tatas tad-ākarṇana-mātrataḥ sarve sarvato nirvarṇanāya saṅgatya satvaram eva cāgatya yathāvat kathayiṣyanti | teṣu kāścin mahilās tu kiñcid apy aprastutya śrī-rādhikādikāḥ pratyapūrvatāpūrvaṃ drakṣyanti | tataḥ paurṇamāsī vakṣyati-kim iva paśyatha ? kim iva ca kiñcin na kathayatha ?
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then, from the mere hearing of that, all — having come together from every side for examination and having come swiftly — shall report appropriately. Among them, certain women, without broaching anything, shall see <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> and the others for the very first time as unprecedented. Then <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> shall say: "What do you see? And why do you say nothing?"'

children.text: tā vakṣyanti-kim iva vakṣyāmaḥ, yataḥ sarvair āhataṃ manyeta |
children.translated_text: They shall say: 'What shall we say? — for all would consider it a blow!'

children.text: paurṇamāsī vakṣyati-tathyaṃ cet kathyatām, mayi kṛṣṇa-mātari ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> shall say: 'If it is true, then let it be told — to me and to <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mother!'

children.text: tās tu nīcair vakṣyanti-tatrāpy etāsāṃ rādhikādikānāṃ dhṛta-tulyatā-pūrtiīr apaśyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: They shall say in low voices: 'Even there, we see those very <s>Rādhikā</s> and the others bearing a completeness of equality [i.e., their doubles]!'

children.text: paurṇamāsī spaṣṭaṃ vakṣyati-anyāś ca punar acchaṃ gacchantu |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> shall say plainly: 'And let the others go separately to a clear [open space]!'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tato bahala-kutūhala-vahā bahulā mahilās tatra tatra gatvā jñāta-tādṛśa-tattvāḥ punaḥ paurṇamāsy-ante labdha-sattvās tadvad evāvartayiṣyanti | vārtā caiṣā vraja-rāja-sabhā-paryantaṃ paryavasiṣyati | vraja-rājaś ca paurṇamāsīm anu tūrṇam āsādya prasādya ca vakṣyati-bhagavati parama-vismāpanam idam asmān bodhaya |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then, those women — abundantly bearing abundant curiosity — having gone here and there and learned the truth of that nature, returning again at <s>Paurṇamāsī's</s> conclusion, having gained strength, shall repeat [their findings] in exactly the same way. And this news shall extend to the court of the king of <s>Vraja</s>. And the king of <s>Vraja</s>, having swiftly reached <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> and having propitiated her, shall say: "O blessed one! Explain this supremely wondrous thing to us!"'

children.text: paurṇamāsī vakṣyati-bhavat-kanyā-bhāvābhimāninyām āryāyām idam āścaryaṃ paryavasyati | bhavāṃs tu sarva-vrajasthaṃ strī-puṃsa-vrajam eka-sabhānugataṃ karotu |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> shall say: 'This wonder culminates in the noble one who holds the sentiment of being your daughter. But let your honor assemble all of <s>Vraja</s> — men and women — into a single assembly!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tad etad avadhārya jñāta-kārya-gatinā vraja-bhūpatinā tad-abhihite tathā-vihite tava hitavatī paurṇamāsī mahitāyāṃ tasyām eva sabhāyām āhita-brahmāsanam āsīnā kim api praṇihitavatī bhavitā | tad-avyavahitam eva ca siṃha-pṛṣṭhāhitam ahita-vigrahā mahāyudhāṣṭaka-veṣṭitā devī-gaṇa-sevitā devī nabhasaḥ sarabhasam avatariṣyati | avatīrṇa-mātrā ca paurṇamāsyā vrajeśvarayoḥ kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇāgrajayor anyeṣām api bhūmi-spṛśām abhūmi-spṛg-māninī yathā-nyāyam abhivādanādikam ākāśata eva prakāśayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Having ascertained this, when the king of <s>Vraja</s>, who knows the course of action, has arranged things as she directed — your well-wishing <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, in that very honored assembly, seated upon a seat arranged as a <s>Brahmā</s>-throne, shall set something in motion. And immediately following that — mounted upon a lion-throne, bearing a form hostile to adversaries, surrounded by the eight great weapons, attended by hosts of goddesses — the Goddess (<s>Durgā</s>/<s>Yogamāyā</s>) shall descend rapidly from the sky! And the moment she descends, she — considering herself as one who does not touch the ground among the earth-dwellers — shall manifestly display the proper salutation and the like to <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, the royal couple of <s>Vraja</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> elder brother, and the others — from the sky itself.'

children.text: tataḥ sāścaryaṃ paryavolokamāneṣu teṣu devī vakṣyati-kathaṃ veha sandehaḥ kriyate ? pūrvata eva tāvad ubhaya-vidhā etā nāpūrvatayā mantavyāḥ | pūrvāsāṃ sajātīyā dvitīyā hi yogamāyājñayā garga-vighnaṃ nighnatyā māyayā mayā nirmitāḥ | saṃjñāyāś chāyā-vat ratyās tan-māyā-kalpitāvac ca |
children.translated_text: Then, as those [people] were looking around in wonder, the Goddess shall say: 'Why is doubt made here? From the very beginning, these [gopīs] of both kinds should not be considered unprecedented. The second ones — of the same kind as the former ones — were fashioned by me, by my <s>māyā</s>, through the command of <s>Yogamāyā</s>, destroying the obstacle of <s>Garga</s>. Like the shadow of a name, and like a <s>māyā</s>-fashioned [imitation] of love.'

children.text: tāś cemā gṛha-gṛhāt saṃgṛhṇāmi iti tathāhnāya sāpahnavaṃ kula-vadhū-madhye vidhāya punar vakṣyati-lakṣyatāṃ kula-pālikābhir ubhaya-vilakṣaṇatā | yat parama-lakṣmī-lakṣmāṇi prāg-āgatānām eva lakṣyante nārvāg-āgatānām | tathā maṇi-tattva-dṛśām iva tādṛśāṃ dṛṣṭibhir eva netrānandaka-saundarya-viśeṣa-vṛṣṭis tābhya eva labhyā, na tv anyāsāṃ, na ca punar ābhyaś cākcikya-cikvaṇa-kāca-tulyābhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And [saying] "I shall collect these from house to house" — thus having proclaimed, and having arranged them with dissimulation amidst the family-brides — she shall again say: "Let the family-guardians observe the distinction between the two kinds. For the marks of supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s> (beauty/fortune) are visible only in the earlier-arrived ones, not in the later-arrived ones. And just as with the eyes of those who perceive the essence of jewels — the special shower of eye-delighting beauty is obtainable only from those [original ones], and not from the others — nor again from these [māyā-ones], who are like deceptive, clever glass."'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-atha sarvābhis tathā tad āścaryaṃ sākṣātkāryamāṇam avadhārya tad-āryāṇāṃ samajyāyāṃ nivedayiṣyate-hanta yathāvad eva devī vadatīti | tataḥ śrī-vraja-rāja-vacanaṃ-tarhy adhunā kiṃ vidheyam ?
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then, when all have verified that wonder being manifested directly, it shall be reported in the assembly of those elders: "Indeed, the Goddess speaks exactly as it is!" Then, the words of the king of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>: "Then what is to be done now?"'

children.text: devī vakṣyati-bhojane nirvṛtte man-nirvartitāḥ sva-sva-pati-gṛham anuvartantām | parās tu kṛṣṇa-mātra-pati-sammati-parāyaṇāḥ sva-sva-pitṛ-gṛham | mayā tu yamunā-taṭeṣṭa-praśastālaye sthāsyate, yathā yadā mātṛ-caraṇair ājñāpyate, tathā tadā vyavahartavyam |
children.translated_text: The Goddess shall say: 'When the feast is concluded, let the ones fashioned by me follow their respective husbands' houses. But the others — devoted solely to the consensus of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as their only husband — [let them go] to their respective fathers' houses. And I shall station myself in a chosen, praiseworthy abode on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, so that whenever I am commanded by [your] mother's feet, I shall act accordingly.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tad evam āpracchana-pūrvakam āpṛcchya pracchannāyāṃ devyāṃ sarveṣu ballava-valayeṣu pracchanneṣu varṇānāṃ vara-varṇinībhir varṇyamānaṃ tad ākarṇya bhavata-pativratās tu tat-kṣaṇād eva jūrit-parityakta-mūrtikā vyakta-nija-kānti-sphūrtikāś ca bhaviṣyanti | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Thus, when [the Goddess], having asked permission and taken leave, had become hidden — and when all the cowherd groups had become [aware of what was] hidden — then, as the excellent women of various castes describe what was being described — upon hearing that, your [true] devoted wives, from that very moment, shall become ones whose forms, previously abandoned by <s>māyā</s>, have manifestly departed, and whose own radiance has become manifest. Thus:

children.text: rāhu-grāsād iva śaśi-kalā vāridād ṛkṣa-mālā
children.translated_text: 'Like the moon's digit [emerging] from the eclipse of <s>Rāhu</s>, like a garland of stars [emerging] from the cloud,

children.text: varṣādharṣāt pulina-rucayaḥ sparśanād dīpa-lakṣmyāḥ |
children.translated_text: like the beauties of a sandbank [emerging] from the onslaught of rain, like the splendor of a lamp [emerging] from [being covered by] touch —

children.text: niṣkramyāmūḥ para-paribhavāt tat-kṣaṇaṃ vindamānāḥ
children.translated_text: having come forth from the humiliation of the other [doubles], those [gopīs], at that very moment, finding

children.text: kāntiṃ svīyāṃ nayana-kadanaṃ mocayeyur janānām ||JGc_1,33.111||
children.translated_text: their own radiance, shall release the torment of the eyes of the people!' || (JGc 1,33.111)

children.text: tatra ca-
tārāsu candra-valayasya kalāḥ kalāsu
children.translated_text: 'As among the stars, the digits of the moon's circle, and among those digits,

children.text: tasyāticāru dadhate sphuraṇaṃ yathā śrīḥ |
children.translated_text: the exceedingly beautiful manifestation of splendor bears its glory —

children.text: gopāṅganāhvaya-ramāsu viśākhikādi-
children.translated_text: so among the <s>gopīs</s> called <s>Ramās</s> (beautiful ones), <s>Viśākhā</s> and other

children.text: sakhyaḥ sakhīṣu ca tathā vṛṣabhānu-putrīḥ ||JGc_1,33.112||
children.translated_text: friends, and among those friends — the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>)!' || (JGc 1,33.112)
And there:

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then, from there onward?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tato devyādeśa-veśa-vaśā yathāyathaṃ te vihitavanta eva | tathāpi vidhiṃ vinā na saṅgrāhyās tā itii śrī-vraja-rājādibhir vihite ca tasmin vivāha-vicāre bhavāṃs tv agrajasya vivāhārtham āgṛhya taṃ tad-artha-rakṣita-kaumārā dvārakāta āgatya kadācit tena prasādī-kṛta-sva-vihārāḥ | kāścin nitya-kiśorikā vidhinā ca vivāhya nairapekṣyam ivāvagāhya vigata-pūrvāśaṅkaḥ parama-lalita-mādhava-samayam ālambyālaṅkṛta-pūrṇa-manorathāṅkaḥ śrī-vraja-rāja-gṛhiṇī-muhur āgraha-gṛhītatayā śanair eva sva-vivāham aṅgīkāra-saṅginaṃ kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Then, being under the command of the Goddess's arrangement — according to circumstances — they shall have acted accordingly. Nevertheless, they [the gopīs] cannot be accepted without the [proper] rite — so when the king of <s>Śrī Vraja</s> and the others have arranged that marriage-deliberation, your honor, having taken hold [of the matter] for your elder brother's marriage, shall bring those [gopīs] — whose maidenhood had been preserved for that very purpose — from <s>Dvārakā</s> at some time, and having been graciously allowed by him [<s>Balarāma</s>] to have your own festivities [as well], shall marry certain eternally-youthful [maidens] through the proper rite, and as if plunging into indifference — freed from former apprehension — taking hold of the supremely elegant spring (<s>Mādhava</s>) season, adorned with the fulfillment of complete desires — through the repeated insistence of the queen of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>, shall gradually make your own marriage an object accompanied by acceptance.'

children.text: tatra bahu-mahasā śrī-rāma-vivahane jāte taṃ jātaṃ samāsataḥ samāsāṃ samam eva tvat-kṛta-vivāham eva varṇayiṣyanti-
children.translated_text: 'There, when the marriage of <s>Śrī Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) has been accomplished with great splendor, they shall describe in summary your marriage equally together with that one. As follows:

children.text: go-dhuṅnyarbuda-geha-geha-balavad-vādyānavadya-dhvani-
children.translated_text: 'With the blameless sound of instruments — mighty as the dwellings of the ten-million cow-settlements —

children.text: prollāsita-vraja-maṇḍale diviṣadāṃ vāditra-citre mahe |
children.translated_text: with the circle of <s>Vraja</s> made joyful, with the wondrous music of the celestials at the festival —

children.text: ādāna-pratidāna-dāna-vacanodāraiḥ sadārair narair
children.translated_text: with generous men accompanied by wives, through words of giving, receiving, and bestowing —

children.text: nirvyūḍhā murajid-vivāha-paṭalī jñātā na tat-tad-bhidā ||JGc_1,33.113||
children.translated_text: the array of the marriage of the slayer of <s>Mura</s> was carried out — the distinction of each and every [detail] was not discerned!' || (JGc 1,33.113)

children.text: tad evam aṅgīkāreṇa ca-ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmy aham [Gītā 4.11] iti bhavataḥ samādhiḥ samādhīyeta |
children.translated_text: And thus, by the acceptance — 'As they surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly' [Gītā 4.11] — your contemplative equipoise shall be established.

children.text:
atra ye yathā iti ye yad-icchayetety evam eva vivikṣitam | yataś ca sādhāraṇa-janam anvanurāga-laṅghita-loka-dharma-maryādā-saṅghānām aṅganāntarāṇām apy antar-vṛttis tat-tad-gṛhiṇī-pada-spṛhiṇī dṛśyate | kim uta bhavantam anu santata-priyāṇāṃ māyā-mayātyayād eva labdhānyathā-bhāva-prāyāṇām ? [BhP 10.21.9] iti tad-vākya-vyakta-tādṛśābhiprāyāṇāṃ svatas tādṛśābhiprāyatve saty api bhramara-gītāyām api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro ædhunāste [BhP 10.47.21] ity ādau, bhujam aguru-sugandhaṃ mūrdhnyadhāsyat kadā nu ity anena tadīyaṃ prakaṭaṃ tathā svīkāraṃ prārthayamānānāṃ bhavad-gṛhiṇī-bhāva-spṛhā-bṛṃhaṇam iti sthite tathaiva tad yojayituṃ śakyata iti | sarveṣām asmākaṃ dhairya-paryāpaṇam evam eva bhavatācariṣyate
| yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Here, 'those who, as they wish' is intended to mean 'those who, by their desire.' For even the inner state of other women — those of the ordinary public whose passion-transgressed-social-convention assemblages are evident — is seen to be desirous of the status of his wife. How much more so for those who are perpetually dear to you, who have attained an altered state merely through the cessation of the <s>māyā</s>-made [illusory separation]? That their intent is such is made clear by the words [of BhP 10.21.9] — and even when their own such intent exists, in the <s>Bhramara-gītā</s> too: 'Alas, the noble husband now dwells in <s>Madhu-purī</s>' [BhP 10.47.21] and so forth, and 'When will he place his <s>aguru</s>-fragrant arm upon our heads?' — in this, they who are requesting such an open acceptance by him are augmenting their aspiration for the status of being your wives — this being established, it can be connected accordingly. The fortification of the patience of all of us shall be enacted by you precisely thus. For:

children.text: gatānām utpattyā tvayi ratim api tvad-vivahanān
children.translated_text: 'Of those who, by their birth, have attained passion for you, yet by your marriages

children.text: nirastānāṃ tvat-prāpty-abhilaṣita-saṃnyasta-jagatām |
children.translated_text: have been cast aside, who have renounced the world in the longing for attaining you —

children.text: amūṣām utkaṇṭhā yadi hata-phalā tarhi valatāṃ
children.translated_text: if their longing is of fruitless result, then let it be so!

children.text: kathaṃ vā viśvāsas tvayi muraharāsmākam abhitaḥ ||JGc_1,33.114||
children.translated_text: But how then, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, would there be trust in you among all of us?' // [śikharinī]

children.text: tad etad avadhāya madhukaṇṭhenāmukta-kaṇṭham anusandhīyate sma-aho ! tad etat-paryantaṃ phalam āgatāyā bhagaval-līlatāyā mādhurya-prasavitā | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Having perceived this, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, with unchoked throat, reflected: 'Ah! This is the fruit of the sweetness-producing nature of <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>līlā</s>, having reached this conclusion. For thus:'

children.text:
prāg-dūra-priyatā tato guru-jana-dhvasta-prayatnātmatā
tat paścāc chruti-loka-laṅghi-rabhasād guptā priyāṅgīkṛtiḥ |
tasmād dūra-mahā-viyoga-ciratā tat-prāntam udvāhataḥ
prāptaṃ cen mithunaṃ mitho hari-ramā-rūpaṃ sukhaṃ kiṃ param ||JGc_1,33.115|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'First, distance from the beloved; then, the state of self-frustration from the thwarting of efforts by elders; then, from a vehemence that transgresses both <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>loka</s> (convention), the secret acceptance by the beloved; thereafter, the long duration of the great distant separation — and at the end of that, if the couple, in the form of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), mutually attain union through marriage — what happiness is beyond that?' // [śārdūla] — thus.

children.text: atha prakṛta-tat-kartṛka-kathā |
children.translated_text: Now, the narrative of the original agent [continues].

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tataś ca sarveṣāṃ gataye duhituḥ pataye tubhyaṃ kautukāvahāni bahūni yautukāni parama-dhanyāṃ nija-nija-kanyāṃ ca prasthāpyate | gopāḥ sopādhyāyāḥ sadā tadā dhyāyaṃ dhyāyaṃ divas-pṛthivyāv api svānanda-samudra-mudrite kariṣyanti |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'And then, for the departure of all — to you, the husband of their daughter — wonder-producing abundant dowries and their own supremely blessed daughter shall be dispatched. The cowherds, together with their priests, then, meditating and meditating always, shall make even the surface of sky and earth marked with their own ocean of bliss.'

children.text: kṛṣṇa uvāca- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tatra ca kavi-lokānāṃ ślokāv etāv udeṣyataḥ-
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'There, these two verses of the world of poets shall arise:'

children.text: yarhy āyātā vraja-nṛpa-gṛhaṃ rādhikādyās tadāsāṃ
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Rādhikā</s> and the others arrived at the house of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, then

children.text: sva-jyotsnābhis tad alam abhavad dhema-dhāma-prakāram |
children.translated_text: the golden mansion-wall became sufficient through their own moonlight-radiances!

children.text: golokākhyaṃ padam udayitā yat tu tasya prakāśas
children.translated_text: The abode called <s>Goloka</s>, which has arisen — its radiance

children.text: tāsāṃ śrīṇām anugata iti dyotanaṃ yatra jātam ||JGc_1,33.116||
children.translated_text: follows [from] the splendors of those [women] — this is the illumination that was born there!' // [sragdharā]

children.text: asaṅkhya-gaṇana-snuṣā-gaṇa-nivāsam ākasmikaṃ
children.translated_text: 'How could the royal couple of <s>Vraja</s> then suddenly provide a dwelling

children.text: kathaṃ vraja-patī tadā viadadhatus tathā tac chṛṇu |
children.translated_text: for an innumerable, uncountable host of daughters-in-law? Hear that!

children.text: gṛhī iva taruṇa-vrajā yad iha bhānti yāvat-spṛhaṃ
children.translated_text: Like a householder [with] a young grove, here — fulfilling every desire —

children.text: vanāny upavana-prabhāṇy ati-sahasra-saṃsthāny api ||JGc_1,33.117||
children.translated_text: the forests, shining like pleasure-gardens, even in more than a thousand arrangements [sufficed]!' // [śikharinī]

children.text: tad etad avadhāya madhukaṇṭhenāmukta-kaṇṭhaṃ punar anusandhīyate sma-
children.translated_text: Having perceived this, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> reflected again, with unchoked throat:

children.text: bāḍhaṃvivāhādibhir asaṅkoce virocamāna eva gopa-jātibhir nārībhiḥ saha gopajāti-yogya-veśa-dhāriṇas tasya līlā-nairantaryam api tadocitatayā paryālocitaṃ pādmottara-khaṇḍe dantavakra-vadhānantara-tad-vrajāgamane yathā-
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, by the marriages and such — without any reservation — shining together with the cowherd-caste women, wearing the attire befitting the cowherd caste, the uninterrupted continuity of his <s>līlā</s> was also contemplated as fitting therein, as in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, after the slaying of <s>Dantavakra</s> and his arrival at <s>Vraja</s>, as follows:'

children.text: kālindyāḥ puline ramye puṇya-vṛkṣa-samāvṛte |
children.translated_text: 'On the beautiful bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), covered with auspicious trees,

children.text: gopa-nārībhir aniśaṃ krīḍayāmāsa keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> sported constantly with the cowherd women!' //

children.text: ramya-keli-sukhenaiva gopa-veṣa-dharo hariḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Hari</s>, wearing the cowherd's attire, with the delightful joy of charming play,

children.text: baddha-prema-rasenātra māsa-dvayam uvāsa ha ||[PadmaP 6.252.19-27]
children.translated_text: bound by the essence of <s>prema</s>, dwelt there for two months!' // [PadmaP 6.252.19-27]

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yaḥ kaumāra-haraḥ sa eva hi varas tā eva caitra-kṣapāḥ
children.translated_text: 'He who stole our childhood — he is indeed the bridegroom! Those very <s>Caitra</s> nights [are the same]!'

children.text: ity ādy apy adhiyan kayācid uditaṃ gopālikā-gīr iti |
children.translated_text: — and so forth, that which was uttered by a certain one, is called the speech of a cowherd girl.

children.text: bhāvonmādaja-gāna-nṛtya-vivaśaḥ śrī-guṇḍicā-parvasu
children.translated_text: Overwhelmed with singing and dancing born of emotional ecstasy, at the festivals of Śrī <s>Guṇḍicā</s>,

children.text: śrī-caitanya-tanur mataṃ sa bhagavān aṅgīkariṣaty adaḥ ||JGc_1,33.118||
children.translated_text: the body of Śrī <s>Caitanya</s> — he, the <s>Bhagavān</s> — shall accept that view!' // [śārdūla]

children.text: tad īdṛg eva bhāvini vidagdha-mādhava-lalita-mādhavāhvaye pūrvottara-nāṭaka-dvaye sarva-racanāyāḥ parama-phalatayā sarvānte prakārāntareṇāvakalpate-
children.translated_text: 'In precisely such a form, in the pair of earlier and later dramas named <s>Vidagdha-Mādhava</s> and <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>, the supreme fruit of all composition is fashioned at the very end, in an alternative manner:'

children.text: tavātra parimṛgyatā kim api lakṣma sākṣād iyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'What trace of yours is to be sought here? Directly, this —

children.text: mayā tvam upasāditā nikhila-loka-lakṣmīr asi |
children.translated_text: by me, you have been brought near! You are the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of all the worlds!

children.text: yathā jagati cañcatā caṇaka-muṣṭi-sampattaye
children.translated_text: Just as, in the world, when one runs for the sake of obtaining a handful of chickpeas,

children.text: janena patitā puraḥ kanaka-vṛṣṭir āsādyate ||[LalM 10.10]
children.translated_text: a shower of gold falls before one, by chance!' // [LalM 10.10]

children.text: iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyādinā,
children.translated_text: — thus, by the words of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and so forth;

children.text: sakhyas tā militā nisarga-madhura-premābhirāmīkṛtā
children.translated_text: 'Those companions met, made charming by naturally sweet <s>prema</s>;

children.text: yāmī me samagaṃs tu saṃstavavatī śvaśrūś ca goṣṭheśvarī |
children.translated_text: my mother-in-law, the queen of the cow-settlement, came to me with praise!

children.text: vṛndāraṇya-nikuñja-dhāmni bhavatā saṅgo' yaṃ raṅgavān
children.translated_text: This union with you in the bower-abode of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>) is full of delight —

children.text: saṃvṛttaḥ kim ataḥ paraṃ priyataraṃ kartavyam atrāsmi me ||[LalM 10.36]
children.translated_text: what more, dearer than this, remains to be done for me?' // [LalM 10.36]

children.text: iti pūrṇa-manorathāṅka-pūraka-śrī-rādhā-vākya-paryantena granthena |
children.translated_text: — thus, by the text ending with the words of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> that complete the act fulfilling all desires.

children.text: tad idam eva śrīmad-bhagavad-bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu-nidhi-rūpa-śrīmad-ujjvala-nīlamaṇāv api sarva-rasa-paripāṭī-pūrti-sāra-mūrti-samṛddhimad-ākhya-sambhogatayā darśitam |
children.translated_text: 'This very thing is also shown in the glorious <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> — the treasure of the ocean of the nectar of devotion to the blessed Lord — as the <s>sambhoga</s> (union) named the wealth of the perfected form that is the essence of the completion of the entire succession of <s>rasas</s>.'

children.text: teṣām upāsanā-vāsanā cedṛśy eva tadīya-ślokenāvalokyate-
children.translated_text: 'The devotional disposition of their worship is perceived through his verse, as follows:'

children.text:
gopeśau pitarau tavācala-dhara śrī-rādhikā preyasī
śrīdāmā subalādayaś ca suhṛdo nīlāmbaraḥ pūrvajaḥ |
veṇur vādyam alaṅkṛtiḥ śikhidalaṃ nandīśvaro mandiraṃ
vṛndāṭavy api niṣkuṭaḥ param ato jānāmi nānyat prabho ||iti |
children.translated_text: 'The lords of the cowherds are your parents, O lifter of the mountain! Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> is [your] beloved; <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Subala</s>, and others are [your] friends; <s>Nīlāmbara</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) is [your] elder brother; the flute is [your] instrument; the peacock-feather is [your] ornament; <s>Nandīśvara</s> is [your] abode; and <s>Vṛndāṭavī</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>) too is [your] grove — beyond this, I know nothing else, O Lord!' — thus.

children.text: atha punaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nārada-saṃvādaṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ kaṇṭhataḥ prakaṭayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> brought forth from his throat the dialogue of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Nārada</s> again:

children.text: ṛṣir uvāca-tad evaṃ māsa-dvitaye sarveṣām eva paramānandena labdha-vyatyaye datta-vrajoddhavaḥ kadācid bhavān rāmoddhavābhyāṃ samaṃ saṃmantrya śrī-vrajamahendrādīn parama-gauravād āmantrya nivedayiṣyati-adhunā yady ājñā rājñām ājñāyeta | tadā syandano' yaṃ sadāruko dvārakāṃ vindeta |
children.translated_text: The sage said: 'Thus, when two months had passed with supreme bliss for all, you, having given <s>Uddhava</s> to <s>Vraja</s>, at some time, having deliberated together with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>, taking leave of the glorious great king of <s>Vraja</s> and others with supreme respect, shall announce: "If the command of the kings is now known, then let this chariot, with <s>Dāruka</s>, find its way to <s>Dvārakā</s>."'

children.text: atha parama-hṛdayālutāmaya-dayālur asau śrī-vraja-rājas tu vakṣyati-yathā tatra śrīmad-bhrātṛ-prabhṛtīnāṃ bhṛti-bhuk-paryantānāṃ duḥkhaṃ na syāt tathā ca prathanīyam |
children.translated_text: 'And that glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, supremely compassionate and tender-hearted, shall say: "Let it be so arranged that the suffering of the glorious brother and others, down to their servants and dependents there, does not arise."'

children.text: bhavān vakṣyati-sarvathā sarveṣām ādṛtyās tatra-bhavatāṃ bhṛtyās tatra pradyumnādayaḥ pradyotanta eva | tathāpi bhavatām apūrtiś cet tadā bhavad-ārādhana-śatayāsman-mūrti-vyūham api tatra nārāyaṇaḥ pārayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'You shall say: "In every way, your servants there — <s>Pradyumna</s> and others — are already shining with respect for all of you. Even so, if there be unfulfillment on your part, then by the worship of you in a hundredfold manner, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> shall arrange even the expansion of our forms there."'

children.text: punar vraja-rājo vakṣyati-rohiṇī-rāmavad ayam uddhavaś cāsmad-eka-sampad-uddhavas tasmād ayam api tathācaraṇīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Again the king of <s>Vraja</s> shall say: "Just as <s>Rohiṇī</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, so too this <s>Uddhava</s> is one whose sole wealth is our own — therefore, he too should be treated accordingly."'

children.text: bhavān vakṣyati-yatra bhavad-icchā, tad vā kiṃ na setsyati ? kintv ājñāntaraṃ jñāpaya |
children.translated_text: 'You shall say: "Wherever your wish [goes], what would not be accomplished? But convey another command."'

children.text: vrajarājo vakṣyati-jaivātṛka ! bhavatām akrūrādi-racitenāticiraṃ bhavatā viraheṇa cirāya tarv-antimaḥ sarva eva jīvaḥ suṣṭhu durjīvanam avāpi | tato na kim api pratyeti | tatas tvad-viraha-parihārāya nānya-jana-locana-gocaraḥ syām iti prārthayate | tato niḥśalākam ālaya-viśeṣaṃ saṃśleṣaya |
children.translated_text: 'The king of <s>Vraja</s> shall say: "O <s>Jaivātṛka</s> (dear child)! Through the separation from you, contrived by <s>Akrūra</s> and others, for an exceedingly long time — every single living being, all the way to the last tree, has experienced a thoroughly wretched existence. Therefore, nothing is trusted. So, for the removal of the sorrow of your separation, let him (<s>Uddhava</s>) pray that he not become visible to the eyes of other people. Therefore, arrange a special dwelling without any public exposure."'

children.text: bhavān vakṣyati-hanta ! vṛndāvana eva tādṛśaṃ prakāśa-vṛndaṃ vartate | yat khalu brahma-hrade nimajjya punas tasmād unmajjya ca bhavadbhiḥ pūrvam apy apūrvaṃ dṛṣṭam asti | śatāṅgasyāsya kāmaṅgāmitayā tat-praveśitāpi prativeśīyate | tato yathājñāpyate prājñānāṃ rājñā |
children.translated_text: 'You shall say: "Alas! In <s>Vṛndāvana</s> itself, there exists just such an assemblage of radiance! That which, having plunged into <s>Brahma-hrada</s> (the lake of <s>Brahmā</s>) and having emerged again from it, was seen by you earlier too as unprecedented! The chariot of a hundred parts (<s>Śatāṅga</s>), by the immeasurability of its desire-form, may be entered into even there, standing next-door. Therefore, let it be commanded as the wise king [sees fit]."'

children.text: vraja-rājo vakṣyati-vatsa! tad eva pracchannaṃ vanaṃ gacchāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The king of <s>Vraja</s> shall say: "Dear child! Let us go to that very hidden forest!"'

children.text: tataḥ sa-pratiśrava-śravaṇaṃ bhavān vakṣyati-yathā mahecchānām icchā tathaiva setsyati | punaś ca tiryag avekṣya pārśva-lakṣyaṃ dārukam ādekṣyasi-sārathe ! tathā rathaṃ prathaya, yathā sarva eva vrajas tatrāntar-bhavaṃs tad-dhāma praviśaṃś ca dhāma-grāmataḥ svar-vāsinām api dṛg-ārāmatāṃ nāsīdati |
children.translated_text: 'Then, hearing the approval, you shall say: "As the great ones desire, so indeed it shall be accomplished." And then, glancing sideways at <s>Dāruka</s>, visible at your side, you shall instruct: "O charioteer! Prepare the chariot such that the entire <s>Vraja</s> enters therein, and entering that abode, the spectacle from the assemblage of luminous dwellings does not fail even the eyes of the heaven-dwellers."'

children.text: atha tena sūtena tu tathākṛta-prathe rathe sarva eva vraja-prāṇi-vrajaḥ svairaṃ nivśamānas taṃ deśaṃ praviveśa |
children.translated_text: 'And then, when that chariot had been so prepared by the charioteer, the entire community of <s>Vraja</s>'s living beings, embarking at ease, entered that realm.'

children.text: tad evaṃ sati-
children.translated_text: 'This being so:'

children.text: utsarpaj-jyotir-ālī-vibhava-vaśatayā taṃ rathaṃ tūrdhva-bhājaṃ
children.translated_text: 'By the power of the arising rows of ascending lights, that chariot [was perceived as] rising —

children.text: carmākṣā menire tarhy uparigatatayā tat-padopāsakāś ca |
children.translated_text: the leather-eyed ones (ordinary folk) deemed it so then; and the worshippers of his feet [perceived it] as having gone above.',

children.text: kṛṣṭvā brahma-hradāt prāg api murajayinā lambhitā gomino yā
children.translated_text: 'That passage which had previously been obtained by the cow-folk when drawn by the conqueror of <s>Mura</s> from <s>Brahma-hrada</s> —

children.text: tāṃ vṛndāraṇya-madhye gatim iha sugatās tadvidaś cārv apaśyan ||JGc_1,33.119||
children.translated_text: that same [passage], in the midst of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>, the wise ones who had well-gone [to liberation] beautifully beheld!' // [sragdharā]

children.text: tatra parjanya-varyāś ca ye gatāḥ prāg-adṛśyatām |
children.translated_text: 'And those foremost sons of <s>Parjanya</s> (<s>Nanda</s> and others) who had previously attained invisibility —

children.text: drakṣyante te' pi tatraiva tad āścaryaṃ bhaviṣyati ||JGc_1,33.120||
children.translated_text: they too shall be seen right there — that shall be the wonder!' // [anuṣṭubh]

children.text: tataś ca-
children.translated_text: 'And then:'

children.text: vṛndāraṇye sa-kalpa-druma-vividha-latā-mañju-kuñjādi-dhanye
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>, blessed with wish-fulfilling trees and beautiful bowers of diverse creepers,

children.text: ghoṣe cintāmaṇīndra-prathita-nilayatā-citta-vṛtti-pramoṣe |
children.translated_text: in the cow-settlement that robs the mind's activities with its reputation of being a great <s>cintāmaṇi</s>-jewel abode —

children.text: rāmādyaiḥ kāma-dhug-gavy-anugati-kutukī lakṣa-lakṣmī-prakāra-
children.translated_text: with <s>Rāma</s> and others, curious to follow the wish-fulfilling cows, with the glory of hundreds of thousands of splendors,

children.text: śrī-gopī-prāṇa-sāraḥ sa jayati nitarāṃ gopa-goptuḥ kumāraḥ ||JGc_1,33.121||
children.translated_text: that son of the cowherd-protector, the very essence of the lives of the glorious <s>gopīs</s> — may he be supremely victorious!' // [sragdharā]

children.text: atha snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tad evam anyaṃ ca vṛttāntaṃ varṇitavān | śrīmān vraja-sukha-varṣī devarṣiś ca parasparaṃ harṣitāṃ prapannaḥ sa-bāṣpa-romaharṣādhibhiḥ sampannaḥ snigdha-saṃvāda-vicchedataḥ parikhidya śanair eva ca vicchidya sva-sva-varmānuvartate sma | śrīmad-vrajendra-nandanas tu tat-kathā-paryantānandena paryāptaḥ sarvaṃ tad-duḥkha-jātam ācchannatām āpannam eva cakāra | tatra bhagavantaḥ śrī-devarṣi-caraṇā yad-yad-bhāvitayā samudbhāvitavantas tat sarvam abhūd eva |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Thus, having narrated this and other accounts, the glorious <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), the rainer of <s>Vraja</s>'s happiness, having mutually attained delight, endowed with tears, horripilation, and overwhelming emotions, being pained by the cessation of the tender conversation, gradually, gently breaking off, followed his own path. And the son of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, replete with the bliss at the conclusion of that narrative, made the entire mass of sorrow that had arisen remain concealed. And whatever the blessed Śrī <s>Devarṣi</s> had envisioned with the state of each emotion — all of that indeed came to pass.'

children.text: tad-anantaram api yathā vrajasya rājñānujñāpitam | tathā vāsudeva-prasādād vasudeva-pravīṇānāṃ tad-vartma-vīkṣādīnānāṃ dāruka-kathita-tat-tad-vṛttābhoga-bhoga-pīnānāṃ svalpa-kālatām āpakam āyādhīnānāṃ tad-āgamanāśayā bahir evāsīnānāṃ tad-iṣṭa-siddhir indhāmbabhūveti |
children.translated_text: 'Thereafter too, as was commanded by the king of <s>Vraja</s>: likewise, by the grace of <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), those expert in <s>Vasudeva</s>'s [teachings], those gazing at that path and such, those fattened by the enjoyment of the various affairs narrated by <s>Dāruka</s>, those awaiting the brief time that was approaching, those seated outside with the expectation of his arrival — the fulfillment of their desire indeed blazed forth!'

children.text: tad evam ākarṇya sarve' pi sabhāsadaḥ procuḥ- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Having heard this, all the members of the assembly said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca sarva-sukhārāmābhyāṃ śrī-rohiṇīm ābhyāṃ gopocita-veṣādy-abhiniveśa-labdha-sakhi-gaṇa-praveśoddhavenoddhavena ca sārdham asminn eva goloka-nāmake parama-duravaloke loke parama-vibhavavatāṃ bhavatāṃ madhye vibhavann eva so' yaṃ virājate |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'And then, together with the two who are the pleasure-gardens of all happiness — Śrī <s>Rohiṇī</s> — and with <s>Uddhava</s>, who had gained entry to the circle of companions through donning cowherd-appropriate attire and such — in this very realm called <s>Goloka</s>, supremely difficult to behold, in the midst of your supremely opulent selves — that very one shines forth resplendent!'

children.text: punaḥ sarve' py ūcuḥ- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: Again all said: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tataś ca sarvataḥ prasarad-amanda-bhavad-ānanda-kallola-lolan-manastayā vayam apy āgamya bhavad-bhavadīya-kṛpā-mātra-gamyaṃ ramyaṃ vāsa-varyam ajarya-saṅgamam āsādayāma |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'And then, we too — our minds tossing with the waves of the abundant bliss of your grace spreading in every direction — having arrived, we attained the delightful, supreme dwelling, accessible only through your and your devotees' grace alone — an imperishable meeting!'

children.text: śrī-vrajarāja uvāca-kathaṃ katham iti kathyatām |
children.translated_text: The glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> said: 'How so? How so? Tell us!'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-pūrvaṃ tāvad asmadīyānāṃ duṣprārabdha-vaśād adya śvaś cicaliṣa-yātrāsu yātrāyāṃ vilambanam āsīt | tatra ca sati śrīmad-vraja-prāṇasya yaduṣu saṅkramaṇam avakarṇya prāṇa-viyojanam ivāsīt | cirāya tu vraje tat-prati-saṅkramaṇaṃ cākarṇya sadyaś calitum udyame kṛta-prakrame tad-anugata-vraja-janasya tasya martya-loka-pathād antardhānam avadhārya vāridhi-praveśam udyacchatāṃ dayā-varṣi-devarṣi-caraṇācarita-nideśam upaniṣat-kṛtya jīvikākṛtya ca śrī-vṛndāvanāgamanaṃ jātam | jāte cāgamane tat-tat-padaṃ kṛṣṇa-rūpya-krīḍāspadatayā nirūpya mūrcchānantaraṃ jāgaram ṛcchatām asmākam akasmād atrānupraveśaḥ kathaṃ jāta iti na yathātathyaṃ prathayituṃ śakyate sma |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'First, there was a delay in our people's journey — in those pilgrimages of wanting to depart today or tomorrow — due to poorly commenced destiny. And when that [delay] persisted, hearing of the transference of the life-breath of glorious <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) to the <s>Yadus</s>, it was as if our life-breath was torn away. But after a long time, hearing of his return to <s>Vraja</s>, when the effort to set forth immediately was underway and the procedure was established — perceiving the disappearance of the <s>Vraja</s>-folk who had followed him from the path of the mortal world — for those who were about to plunge into the ocean — having taken as our guide and livelihood the direction followed by the compassion-raining feet of the <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), the arrival at Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s> occurred. And when that arrival happened, having perceived each and every spot as a playground of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-like sport, how our entry here suddenly occurred after the swoon and the awakening — that cannot be properly declared.'

children.text: sarve sāścaryam ūcuḥ- tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: All said with amazement: 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-tato bhagavac-caraṇa-rājīva-lokanataḥ punar-jīvana-lābhopakrameṇa krameṇa ca bhavad-upasevanāya śrī-gopāla-pūrva-campūṃ sampūrṇayantas tad idaṃ sudināham āsīdāmeti kiṃvānyat kathanīyam ?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then, by the commencement of obtaining renewed life from beholding the lotus-feet of the Lord, and gradually, while completing the glorious <s>Gopāla Pūrva-campū</s> for your service — we have arrived at this blessed day! What else need be told?'

children.text: tad etad uktvā samāpanam idaṃ padyaṃ nigadya paṇāyati sma-
children.translated_text: Having said this, he recited this concluding verse as a wager:

children.text: so' yaṃ gopendra putras tava mahita-mahīyaḥsu śaśvan-mahīyyas
children.translated_text: 'This very son of the chief of cowherds, yours — among the great, ever the greatest,

children.text: tvan-nānā-bandhutānām api vividhatayā bandhutā-baddha-buddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: whose mind is bound by the bonds of kinship through the variety of your diverse relationships —

children.text: yasmāl labdhā bhavantaḥ śiva-kamala-bhavādyantara-dhyeya-vargād
children.translated_text: from whom you have obtained — far beyond the inwardly-meditated assembly of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others —
