children.text: dūraṃ dhāma prabhāvaṃ vibhavam api mahā-prema-mādhuryam atra ||JGc_1,33.122||
children.translated_text: the abode, the power, the glory, and the great sweetness of <s>prema</s>!' ||33.122||

children.text: tad etad uktvā bhrātaraṃ praty uvāca-
children.translated_text: Having said this, he said to his brother:

children.text: gopāla-yaśasā spṛṣṭaṃ yan mṛṣṭaṃ sūta-janma ca |
children.translated_text: 'Our birth as <s>sūtas</s> (bards), touched by the fame of <s>Gopāla</s>,

children.text: tat tu sparśa-maṇer jātaṃ jāta-rūpa-mayo' pi naḥ ||JGc_1,33.123||
children.translated_text: has been refined — and that has been born of a touchstone, making even us golden!' ||33.123||

children.text: tathā hi-
atra śrī-vraja-rāja-rājita-sabhā-madhye krama-dhyeyatā-
children.translated_text: 'Here, in the midst of the assembly graced by the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: sādhye śrī-harir eṣa rāma-sahitaḥ pratyakṣatām āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Hari</s> himself, together with <s>Rāma</s>, the goal of progressive meditation,

children.text: tatrāpi sva-kathā-prathāṃ kathayituṃ naḥ samyag ādiṣṭavān
children.translated_text: has come into direct perception! And therein, he has duly instructed us

children.text: kāruṇyaṃ kim athāsya varṇyam asakṛt puṇyaṃ ca kiṃ naḥ sakhe ||JGc_1,33.124||
children.translated_text: to spread forth his own narrative — what [can be said of] his compassion? And what [of] our merit, O friend?' ||33.124||
For thus:

children.text: tad evaṃ śrī-vrajadeva-kumāra-sukumāra-mukham abhipaśyann aṅkuravat-pulaka-kula-saṅkula-kalevaratā-balena punar arjunatām arjayann iva tataś ca stambha-sambha-janam atigambhīra-kampa-sampat-sampatana-sāmpratatayā lumpan patann iva punaś ca nirnimiṣatā-nirmita-suparvatām ātmani parvan pūrvāvasthām avasthāpayann iva samanantaraṃ ca labdha-prapañca-nava-nava-dala-valaya-valita-valgu-puṭa-śobhālobhākara-kara-sampuṭam anūna-bāṣpa-navya-divya-prasūna-pūrṇaṃa kurvann upasaṃharann iva sa-snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sa madhukaṇṭhaḥ pūrvavad eva pūrva-deva-mātrā-ruci-karaṃvaraṃ varayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Thus, gazing upon the tender face of the glorious prince of <s>Vraja</s> — by the force of the body being crowded with clusters of sprout-like horripilation, as if acquiring again a silver-white [pallor] — and then, breaking the birth of paralysis through the wealth of exceedingly deep trembling befalling [him] — as if falling — and again, as if restoring the former state upon himself as a festival, through the supreme-mountain-hood fashioned by unblinking [eyes] — and immediately, making the cupped hands — beautiful with the attractive charm of the wreath of ever-new petals fashioned of full-blown emotion — full of copious tears [serving as] fresh divine flowers, as if drawing them together — he, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, together with <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, just as before, chose this supreme boon that creates the delight of the ancient divine mother:

children.text: vāṇī kaṃsaripo tavānukathanaṃ karṇau kathā-karṇanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'May the voice [be devoted to] the narration of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>; the ears, to the hearing of [his] stories;

children.text: hastau santata-sevanaṃ hṛdayam apy utkaṇṭhayā dhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: the hands, to constant service; the heart, to bearing [him] with longing;

children.text: śīrṣaṃ gokula-vastu-mātra-namanaṃ dṛṣṭī samasta-vraja-
children.translated_text: the head, to bowing before every object of <s>Gokula</s>; the eyes,

children.text: preṣṭhānāṃ sthiti-vīkṣaṇaṃ ca bhajatāṃ nau naiva tat-tad-bahiḥ ||JGc_1,33.125||
children.translated_text: to beholding the state of all the beloveds of <s>Vraja</s> — may these of ours never be otherwise!' ||33.125||

children.text:
tad evaṃ labdha-bhakti-prapañcaṃ taṃ ca taṃ ca kuñcan-manasaṃ bhūyo bhūya āhūya pramada-vraja-virājamānaḥ śrīmān vrajarājaḥ sabhājana-bhājanatayā nija-samīpam āpayāmāsa, samupaveśayāmāsa ca | tena ca sarvam api samājaṃ śarmaṇā bhrājayāmāsa |
tataś ca-
children.translated_text:
Thus, the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, radiant with the delight of the cowherd assembly, having again and again summoned both of them — whose minds were overflowing with the expanse of devotion — drew them near as vessels worthy of honor, and seated them beside himself. And by him, the entire assembly was made to shine with bliss.
Then:

children.text: puṇḍraṃ pūrvāṅga-carcā nija-maṇi-valitālaṅkṛtir divyatāmbū-
children.translated_text: 'The <s>tilaka</s>-mark, the body-anointing, the adornment set with his own jewels, the divine betel,

children.text: lāgryaṃ prāgya-sva-vastra-vratatir iti bahu svātmanaivopayujya |
children.translated_text: the finest, the foremost of his own garments and sets — having himself applied many such [items],

children.text: gantryo vāhāḥ samantāt parijana-janatāḥ spṛhya-gṛhyādivastūny
children.translated_text: conveyances, vehicles, attendant-peoples all around, and desirable household goods and such —

children.text: etāny anyaiḥ samarpya dvayam abhihitavān śrīla-goloka-rājaḥ ||JGc_1,33.126||
children.translated_text: bestowing these upon the two through others, the glorious king of <s>Goloka</s> declared:' ||33.126||

children.text: adyārabhyānupālyeta lālyena bhavator dvayam |
children.translated_text: 'From today onward, may the pair of you be cherished and fondled!

children.text: asya mātrā tathā mātā tadvat pitrā mayā pitā ||JGc_1,33.127||
children.translated_text: By his mother, [your] mother; likewise, by me, [your] father!' ||33.127||

children.text: jaya-dhvani-yutās tadā vavṛṣur uddhatāḥ sad-dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Then, with victory-cries, the elevated ones rained excellent wealth;

children.text: yathā bata sadaḥ-sadastad avagāhya bāhyaṃ gṛham |
children.translated_text: just as, indeed, the inner and outer hall of the assembly penetrated the outer dwelling;

children.text: tathāntara-gatā yataś capalam eva tat-pūritaṃ
children.translated_text: so too, the inner [beings], since that was swiftly filled —

children.text: sthalaṃ kila kṛta-kriyaṃ vyasṛjad ātma-labdhān janān ||JGc_1,33.128||
children.translated_text: the place, having its rites accomplished, released the persons obtained by itself!' ||33.128||

children.text: tad evaṃ kathā-sātau datta-sātau madhukaṇṭha-snigdhakaṇṭhau sadaiva labdha-kṛṣṇopakaṇṭhau ca tad-vilāsa-vilokanotkaṇṭhau pratikṣaṇam amanda-paramānandam anuvindamānāv eva virājete |
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> and <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, given fulfillment in the fulfillment of the narrative, always having attained proximity to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, eager for the sight of his sports, finding at every moment undiminished supreme bliss — they ever shine forth!

children.text: atra pūrvam āpātataḥ sudurbodhatāśaṅkayā yadyapi na varṇitās tathāpy asyāṃ śrī-goloka-kṛta-prabhāyāṃ sabhāyāṃ śānta-veśatayā purodhasāṃ madhya-sambadhyamānāsanaḥ sukhākṛta-sarva-svajanaḥ sarveṣām agraṇyaḥ śrīmān parjanyaḥ parjanya iva sarva-sukhaṃ varṣann āsīt | varīyasī varīyasī cāntaḥ-sabhāyāṃ tathā labdha-prabhā samavartata | śrīmān uddhavaś ca sarveṣām uddhava evājanīti sarva-janīnaṃ sukhaṃ kiyad varṇanīyam ?
children.translated_text: Here, previously, from the suspicion of extreme difficulty of comprehension at first glance, though not described — in this assembly created by the glory of Śrī <s>Goloka</s>, the glorious <s>Parjanya</s> (<s>Nanda's</s> father), with a seat placed in the midst of the priests in the garb of a peacemaker, having made all his own people happy, the foremost of all, like <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) raining all happiness, was present. And the most venerable, most venerable [<s>Yaśodā</s>] shone forth in the inner assembly, having similarly obtained glory. And the glorious <s>Uddhava</s> too became the very <s>Uddhava</s> (elevation) of all — so how much can the happiness belonging to all people be described?

children.text: rahasyaṃ punar idaṃ rasyamānaṃ vidhīyatām-
children.translated_text: But let this secret, being savored, be established:

children.text: vṛndāraṇyābhidhāne sarasi sarasija-śreṇi-lakṣmīṣu gopīṣv
children.translated_text: 'In the lake called <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>), among the lotus-splendors — the <s>gopīs</s> —

children.text: ekā rādhābhidhā sā vibhavati satataḥ divya-saugandhika-śrīḥ |
children.translated_text: one named <s>Rādhā</s> ever shines forth, the beauty of the divine fragrant lotus (<s>saugandhika</s>)!

children.text: bhrāmyan yām eva labdhuṃ vrajapati-tanayaś cāvarmūr vartama-vṛttīḥ
children.translated_text: Wandering to obtain her alone, the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, producing all present activities —

children.text: sarvā nirmāya yasyām alir iva kalayā kelim uccais tanoti ||JGc_1,33.129||
children.translated_text: fashioning all [of them], like a bee, through a mere fraction [of his attention], he mightily extends his sport in her!' ||33.129||

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
children.translated_text: 'O Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, O <s>Sanātana</s>, O <s>Rūpaka</s> (<s>Rūpa</s>)!

children.text: gopāla raghunāthāpta-vraja-vallabha pāhi mām ||1||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gopāla</s>, O <s>Raghunātha</s>, O one obtained by <s>Vraja-vallabha</s> — protect me!' ||1||

children.text: saṃvat-pañcaka-veda-ṣoḍaśa-yutaṃ śākaṃ daśeṣv eka-bhāg-
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Śaka</s> [era] joined with five-[thousand], <s>Veda</s>-[four], and sixteen [= 1516 Śaka],

children.text: jātaṃ yarhi tadākhilaṃ vilikhitā gopāla-campūr iyam |
children.translated_text: when one-portion-in-ten [was] born — at that time, all of this <s>Gopāla-campū</s> was written down,

children.text: vṛndā-kānanam āśritena laghunā jīvena kenāpi tad
children.translated_text: by a certain minor one named <s>Jīva</s>, who had taken refuge in <s>Vṛndā's</s> forest (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>) —

children.text: vṛndā-kānanam eva sambhṛti-kalāṃ dhattāṃ samantād iha ||2||
children.translated_text: may <s>Vṛndā's</s> forest itself sustain the art of nurture everywhere herein!' ||2||

children.text: prāyaḥ sarvā harer līlāḥ kramaśaḥ sūcitā mayā |
children.translated_text: 'Almost all the sports of <s>Hari</s> have been indicated by me in sequence;

children.text: yathā-svaṃ labdha-rucibhir upāsyantāṃ mahātmabhiḥ ||3||
children.translated_text: may they be devotionally served by great souls who have obtained their own taste!' ||3||

children.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gopāla-campūm anu
sarva-manoratha-pūraṇaṃ nāma
trayastriṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||33||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the thirty-third <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Fulfillment of All Desires'
||33||

children.text: kaiśora-vilāsaḥ sampūrṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Kaiśora-vilāsa</s> (Adolescent Sport) is complete!

children.text: sampūritā ceyaṃ śrī-śrī-gopāla-pūrva-campūr iti |
children.translated_text: And thus the glorious <s>Gopāla Pūrva-campū</s> is concluded!

children.text: uttara-campūḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Uttara-campū</s> (Latter <s>Campū</s>)

children.text: atha prathamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the first <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter)

children.text: śrī-śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ namaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to Śrī Śrī <s>Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa</s>!

children.text: maṅgalācaraṇam
children.translated_text: Auspicious invocation

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
children.translated_text: 'O Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, O <s>Sanātana</s>, O <s>Rūpaka</s> (<s>Rūpa</s>)!

children.text: gopāla raghunāthāpta-vraja-vallabha pāhi mām ||GC_2,1.1||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gopāla</s>, O <s>Raghunātha</s>, O one obtained by <s>Vraja-vallabha</s> — protect me!' ||UC 1.1||

children.text:
sampūrṇāsīd āśu gopāla-campūr
eṣāṃ yasmād āśrayād eva pūrvā |
eṣa tasmād uttarāpy uttarā syād
evaṃ devaṃ taṃ kamanyaṃ bhajema ||GC_2,1.2|| [svāgatā]
children.translated_text:
'The <s>Gopāla-campū</s> was quickly completed —
since the former [part] arose from the refuge of these [teachers] alone,
therefore may the <s>Uttara</s> (latter) too be even more excellent (<s>uttara</s>) —
thus, may we worship that desirable Lord!' ||UC 1.2|| [<s>svāgatā</s>]

children.text:
athānupūrvyā pūrva-kathānukathanīyā | [2] asti kila kalita-nikhila-vṛndāvanaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ nāma vanam | [3] yatra jyotiścakram iva vyomni, dharma iva dharmiṇi, tattva-nirṇaya iva vede, śukham ivābhīpsita-lābhe, rasa iva vibhāvādi-varge, ṣaḍguṇyam ivātmani, svayam iva sva-premaṇi, nārāyaṇa iva para-vyomni, śarveṣām āśryaḥ sa ca kṛṣṇaḥ sa-tṛṣṇag janānubhavanīyatayā nijāṃ
nijāśrayaṇīyatām urīkaroti |
children.translated_text:
Now, the prior narrative is to be re-narrated in sequence.
[2] There exists, it is said, a forest called <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, which encompasses the entirety of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.
[3] Therein — like the circle of luminaries in the sky, like <s>dharma</s> in the virtuous, like the determination of truth in the <s>Veda</s>, like delight in the attainment of what is desired, like <s>rasa</s> in the assembly of <s>vibhāvas</s> and such, like the sixfold [divine] attributes in the Self, like oneself in one's own love, like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> in the supreme sky — the refuge of all, that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, through his being experienceable by people eager [for him], makes manifest his own nature as the supreme object of refuge.

children.text: yatra cāntardhāna-vidyayā vidyamānam asmad-ādīnām ālokam atītaṃ dhāma goloka-nāma samāmananti | yatra ca goloke sakala-cintāmaṇīyamāna-cintā-leśaḥ keśavaḥ sarvānanda-bhāsināṃ tad-vāsināṃ prema-nāma-pañcama-pumartha-sampat-paryudañcana-prapañca-sañcaya-vyasanam amuñcaṃs tad-vaśata eva yathāyathaṃ putrāditayā vilasan na kutrāpi vyabhicarati |
children.translated_text: And therein, the abode named <s>Goloka</s> — existing by the art of invisibility, having surpassed the perception of us and others — they declare. And in that <s>Goloka</s>, <s>Keśava</s> — in whom the slightest trace of anxiety is [itself] a wish-fulfilling gem — not releasing the abundant addiction of magnifying the wealth of the fifth goal of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) named <s>prema</s> upon those bliss-radiant dwellers therein, and by their very control, sporting in the mode of son and such as it naturally occurs — never deviates anywhere.

children.text: tādṛśāt tasmād eva ca niṣkramya ramyatayā taiḥ samam asamaṃ prakāśamānaḥ sa khalu khala-nāśanas tad idaṃ jagad api kadācit pramadayati, divya-nṛtya-nāyaka iva nepathya-sthānād atha tadvat tatra praviśati ca |
children.translated_text: And emerging from that very [<s>Goloka</s>] of such a nature, manifesting with them [his associates] as incomparably charming, he — the destroyer of the wicked — sometimes delights even this world, like a divine dance-hero from the dressing-room; and then, just so, he enters there again.

children.text:
tad evaṃ sthite vāñchita-sadanta-vakra-danta-dantavakra-saṃyad-udantataḥ parataḥ punas teṣāṃ vakṣyamāṇa-pramāṇa-lakṣyatayā tat-pradeśa-praveśaḥ sa yadā babhūva, tadā kadācid anavadya-hari-bhakti-vidyā-viśārada-sarva-manoratha-pārada-śrī-nārada-kṛpā-kūpāra-taraṅga-labdha-tat prasaṅga-sārau madhukaṇṭha-snigdhakaṇṭhābhida-sūta-prabhava-nava-kumārau śrīmad-vraja-mahendra-tat-kumārādibhir
virājamānaṃ tad eva sadanam āsadatām |
children.translated_text: This being so, after the account of the desired [destruction of] the straight-toothed <s>Dantavakra</s>, whose teeth were crooked [in nature] — thereafter, when that entry into that realm occurred, verified by the evidence to be stated — then, once upon a time, two new young men — of the name <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> and <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, born of <s>sūtas</s> (bards), who had obtained the essence of that opportunity through the ocean-waves of the grace of the glorious <s>Nārada</s>, who is skilled in the art of irreproachable devotion to <s>Hari</s> and is the philosopher's stone of all desires — reached that very assembly, radiant with the glorious great lord of <s>Vraja</s>, his prince, and others.

children.text: tadā ca tad-ācarita-niyogaṃ pari tad-eka-vṛttitayā tantrī-niyantrita-gīta-yantra-tulyau parama-kulyau parasparaṃ kathakatāṃ kathaṅkathikatām api muhuḥ saṃprathayya sarva-śarma-śīlāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇasya vraja-līlāṃ kathāyām unmīlayāmāsatuḥ |
children.translated_text: And then, following the commission assigned by him [<s>Nārada</s>], with single-pointed devotion, like instruments of song controlled by strings, the two supremely well-disposed ones, repeatedly establishing even the state of questioning among each other in the narrative, began to unfurl the sport of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in <s>Vraja</s> — endowed with all happiness — in their tale.

children.text: tatra ca tasya pitṛ-paitāmahaṃ vṛttaṃ pūrvaṃ tau vṛttaṃ kurvantau tac-carita-bhavya-maya-navya-kāvyasyāpi tad ivācaritavantau janma-vṛttena ca janma-vṛttam iva |
children.translated_text: And therein, first narrating the paternal and ancestral history of his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>], the two performed [that task] as if enacting the auspicious, wonderful, new poem of his deeds — and [thus] as if [performing] a birth-narrative through the birth-narrative.

children.text: samanantaraṃ ca yad vicitraṃ tasya caritraṃ sakramatayā samavarṇayatām |
children.translated_text: And immediately thereafter, they described in sequence his wondrous exploits.

children.text: tac cettham uttara-kathā-prathanārtham anusmaryate | aho! yena khalu pūtanā pūtanārī babhūva, śakaṭaḥ sa kaṭaval-laghutayā patanam avāpa, tṛṇāvartas tṛṇāvartavad vighaṭitāṅgatāṃ gatavān, arjuna-yugalaṃ cārjunavat kṛtam anugrahaṃ jagrāha | tatra vatsakas tad vatsakaḥ, bakas tu baka eva | [11] vyomaś ca vyomavad eva bhavituṃ yuktaḥ |
children.translated_text:
And that is thus recalled for the purpose of presenting the latter narrative: Ah! By whom <s>Pūtanā</s> was made an enemy of the purified (<s>pūtanārī</s>); the cart attained its fall through cart-like lightness; <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s> attained the state of having his limbs shattered like a blade of grass; and the twin <s>Arjuna</s> trees received grace like <s>Arjuna</s> [the hero]. There, <s>Vatsa</s> [the demon] was indeed [made into] a calf; and <s>Baka</s> was indeed a crane.
[11] And <s>Vyoma</s> was indeed fit to become like the sky.

children.text: āstām apīdam, tad idaṃ tu tatrāticitraṃ, yadaho! agho'py anagha āsīt, kāliyaś ca mukta-kañcuka iva jīvann eva nirmuktatayābhidhīyata iti |
children.translated_text: Let even that be set aside — but this indeed was most wondrous there: that even <s>Agha</s> (the sinful one) became sinless (<s>anagha</s>), and <s>Kāliya</s> too, like a snake that has shed its skin, was called liberated even while alive!

children.text:
tad evam api parama-vīrya-śālī śālīnatā-vaśaṃvadatayā nija-jyāyasi yaśaḥ saṃvalayan dhenuka-pralambau tat-pratāpānala-jvālāyāṃ lambamānau yac cakāra, tena labdha-madhurācāratā-pracāraś cāyaṃ naś cetasi vikāra-sāram āsādayati |
[14] aho! nija-janeṣu sauhṛdya-hṛdyatāṃ tasya paśya, yaḥ khalu tānavan dava-hutāśanam api nijāśanam ācacāra |
children.translated_text:
Thus, even though he was endowed with supreme prowess, through submission to modesty, concealing his own elder fame — what he did with <s>Dhenuka</s> and <s>Pralamba</s>, who hung in the flame of his valor — having thereby attained the practice of sweet conduct, he reaches the essence of transformation in our hearts.
[14] Ah! Behold the heartwarming affection he has for his own people — he who indeed consumed even the forest-fire as his own meal, to save them!

children.text:
varṣa-gaṇanayā paugaṇḍo'py avikalāṅgatayā vāma-bhujaṃ giri-cchatraṃ pari pracaṇḍaṃ daṇḍaṃ cakāra | haṃho! tasya bahala-kutūhalatām api kalaya, yo'yaṃ kudarśanatāṃ prāptam api sudarśanaṃ sudarśanam eva nirmitavān | śaṅkhacūḍa-nāmnaḥ khalv asya mani-cūḍatā na yuktā syād itīva yakṣatayā vittasya yakṣa-vittasya tasya śaṅkha-mātrāvaśeṣatayā cūḍāmaṇim apajahāra,
ariṣṭaṃ riṣṭaṃ cakāra, keśinaḥ pratyayam ākṛṣya tad-arthena cātmani kṛtārthatāṃ prakṛṣya keśavatāṃ nirdeśayāmāsa |
children.translated_text:
Though a <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (pre-adolescent) by count of years, yet with unblemished limbs, he made the mountain an umbrella on his left arm — a formidable staff! Ho! Perceive also his abundant curiosity — he who rendered even <s>Sudarśana</s>, who had attained an evil appearance, into a beautiful vision (<s>sudarśana</s>) once more! As for the one named <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> — as if [thinking] 'the state of jewel-crest is not fitting for him' — being a <s>Yakṣa</s>, a guardian of <s>Kubera's</s> wealth, he stole his crest-jewel, leaving him with only the conch-shell remainder;
he made <s>Ariṣṭa</s> ill-fated, and having drawn out <s>Keśī's</s> pride and having thereby drawn from him his own fulfillment, he proclaimed his <s>Keśava</s>-hood.

children.text: kiṃ ca-
yā janma-śrīr ajani gaditā yā ca kaumāra-śobhā
children.translated_text: 'The birth-splendor that was born, the childhood beauty that was told,

children.text: yā paugaṇḍa-dyutir agha-ripor yā ca kaiśora-lakṣmīḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>paugaṇḍa</s>-radiance and the <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescent) fortune of the enemy of <s>Agha</s> —

children.text: ekā sā sā hṛdayam aharan nas tadā drāg idānīṃ
children.translated_text: that one single [beauty], at each stage, swiftly stole our hearts then;

children.text: saṃhatyāmūs tad atha balaval-lobhataḥ kṣobhayanti ||GC_2,1.3||
children.translated_text: now, having gathered all of these together, it powerfully agitates [us] with its covetousness!' ||2.1.3||
Moreover:

children.text:
pitror vātsalyam ādi-sthita-vayasi mukundasya paugaṇḍa-bhāve
sakhyaṃ teṣāṃ bahūnāṃ kim api mṛga-dṛśāṃ navya-tāruṇya-lakṣmyām |
smāraṃ smāraṃ mano naś calati na purataḥ kintu tatrātha bhūyaḥ
sambhūyāste gṛhāntar-nidhim iva vaṇijaḥ suṣṭhu dūraṃ prayātu ||GC_2,1.4|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'The parental affection for <s>Mukunda</s> in his earliest age; in the <s>paugaṇḍa</s> state,
the friendship of those many [companions]; in the novel splendor of <s>tāruṇya</s> (youth), the erotic love of the doe-eyed ones —
remembering again and again, our mind does not move forward, but remains there;
and then, having gathered [all memories], it stays like a merchant's treasure-hoard inside the house — let it go far indeed!' ||2.1.4|| — thus.

children.text:
tad evam api tat-tulayā tat-poṣārtham udyamāntaraṃ kurvantaḥ parāmṛśāmaḥ | yadyapi tatra tatra mohanatā-dhuryaṃ tan-mādhuryaṃ tau sūta-sutau yathāyogaṃ vyañjitavantau, tathāpi na vinā vipralambheṇa sambhogaḥ puṣṭim aśnute iti-rītyā vraja-satṛṣṇena śri-kṛṣṇena bhakta-duḥkha-bhāra-niḥsāra-viśāradasya śrī-nāradasya saṃvādamanu tasya yadu-nigama-gamanaṃ
punar vrajāgamanaṃ goloka-dhāma-saṅgamanam api samāsād varṇitavantau |
children.translated_text: Even so, weighing that [against something else], making another effort for its nourishment, we reflect. Although those two bard-sons duly expressed that sweetness — the foremost vehicle of enchantment — in their respective ways at each juncture, nevertheless, according to the principle 'Without <s>vipralambha</s> (separation), <s>sambhoga</s> (union) does not attain fullness' — following the dialogue of the glorious <s>Nārada</s>, expert in clearing the burden of his devotees' suffering, with the <s>Vraja</s>-thirsting glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, those two [bards] described in summary his departure to the <s>Yadu</s>-city, his return again to <s>Vraja</s>, and also his union with the <s>Goloka</s>-abode.

children.text: tat tat sarvaṃ varṇyamānam avakarṇya dināntare labdhāntare pūrvavad eva pūrvāhne śrī-kṛṣṇa-sanātha-sabhā-bhāsamānaḥ śrī-vrajanātha-pradhānaḥ sa-vraja-janas tad-gamanādikasya vyāsaṃ tāv eva papraccha-
children.translated_text: Hearing all of that being narrated, on the following day, having found an opportunity, in the forenoon as before, the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, chief among [the listeners], resplendent in the assembly graced by glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with the <s>Vraja</s> people, asked those two [bards] for the detailed account of his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] departure and the rest —

children.text: yataḥ-
yad apy antaḥ-pīḍā pratata-nija-duḥkha-śravaṇatas
children.translated_text: 'Even if the inner anguish from hearing of one's own prolonged suffering

children.text: tathāvad bhātā syāt tad api manujās tan na jahāti |
children.translated_text: should appear just as before, nevertheless, humans do not abandon it;

children.text: vraṇaṃ śuṣkī-bhāvaṃ gatam api nijaṃ te smṛtatayā
children.translated_text: even a wound that has gone dry, through the remembrance of one's own [wound],

children.text: balāt pīḍaṃ pīḍaṃ niviḍam anubhūtaṃ vidadhati ||GC_2,1.5||
children.translated_text: forcibly, pressing and pressing, makes one experience the intense [pain] closely!' ||2.1.5||
Because:

children.text: athavā-
cirād bandhau labdhe'py asukham abhito yāti na tadā
children.translated_text: 'Even when a kinsman has been found after a long time, the unhappiness does not completely go away

children.text: gṛhītvā tat-kanṭhaṃ na yadi vilapet tat-priyatamaḥ |
children.translated_text: if that dearest one does not seize his neck and weep;

children.text: sadā śālīnas tu svayam idam akurvan vraja-janas
children.translated_text: always modest, the <s>Vraja</s> people did not do this themselves —

children.text: tathā kṛṣṇas tābhyāṃ sadasi kathakābhyām akathayat ||GC_2,1.6||
children.translated_text: and so <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had those two narrators relate it in the assembly!' ||2.1.6||
Or alternatively:

children.text: atha pṛṣṭau ca tau sukha-duḥkha-spṛṣṭau śrī-rāmacandra-sabhāyāṃ kuśa-lavāv ivāsyāṃ śri-kṛṣṇacandra-sabhāyāṃ pratuṣṭuvāte | tatra prathamataḥ snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ samutkaṇṭhatayā babhāṣe |
children.translated_text: And those two, asked — touched by joy and sorrow — like <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s> in the assembly of glorious <s>Rāmacandra</s>, sang praises in this assembly of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s>. There, first, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke with longing.

children.text: tatra ca maṅgalācaraṇam-
children.translated_text: And there, the auspicious invocation:

children.text: gīr devīm anuyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: 'We follow the goddess of Speech,

children.text: sakala-śruti-sāra-bhāgavata-rūpām |
children.translated_text: who has the form of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> — the essence of all the <s>Vedas</s>;

children.text: yad-rasa-siddhāntābhyāṃ
children.translated_text: by whose <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusion)

children.text: navam api kāvyaṃ pramāṇatāṃ yāti ||GC_2,1.7||
children.translated_text: even a new poem attains the status of authority!' ||2.1.7||

children.text: atha pūrva-campūm anusmṛtya kathā-
children.translated_text: Then, the narrative recollecting the earlier <s>campū</s>:

children.text: dinaṃ dinaṃ caivam anandi sa vrajaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Day after day, thus was that <s>Vraja</s> delighted

children.text: kṛṣṇena kṛṣṇaḥ sa bhṛśaṃ vrajena ca |
children.translated_text: by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; and that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [was delighted] exceedingly by <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: sitākhya-pakṣaḥ sita-kāntinā yathā
children.translated_text: as the bright fortnight [is delighted] by the white-lustered [moon],

children.text: sitākhya-pakṣeṇa yathā sita-dyutiḥ ||GC_2,1.8||
children.translated_text: as the white-lustered [moon is delighted] by the bright fortnight!' ||2.1.8||

children.text: tad evam api-
children.translated_text: Even so:

children.text: kṛṣṇāyāsīt tasya tṛṣṇā samantāt
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> developed a thirst for her on all sides —

children.text: tṛṣṇāyai vā kṛṣṇa ity atra bhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: or was it that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> existed for the sake of thirst? — herein lies the distinction;

children.text: nābhūd itthaṃ puruṣaṃ sva-prakṛtyā
children.translated_text: but it was not thus — the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person), by his own nature,

children.text: yuktaṃ vijñās tatra dṛṣṭāntayanti ||GC_2,1.9||
children.translated_text: [was] conjoined — the wise give examples for this!' ||2.1.9||

children.text: pipāsūnāṃ nīraṃ kṣud-udayavatām annam abhitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'As water for the thirsty, as food for the hungry on all sides,

children.text: prataptānāṃ śitaṃ hima-jaḍa-hṛdāṃ tapti-nikaraḥ |
children.translated_text: as coolness for the scorched, as a mass of warmth for the frost-numbed-hearted —

children.text: yathā tadvat kṛṣṇaḥ samajani yadā gokula-bhuvām
children.translated_text: just so, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was born in the land of <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: tadā vaiyagryaṃ sa pratijana-sukhāya pratigataḥ ||GC_2,1.10||
children.translated_text: then his eagerness went forth toward the happiness of each person!' ||2.1.10||

children.text: tātas-tad bhrātṛ-vargas-tad akhila-bhaginī-bhartṛ-jāmātṛ-mukhyā
children.translated_text: 'Father, then the group of brothers, then all sisters, husbands-of-sisters, and sons-in-law foremost,

children.text: mātā mātuḥ pituś ca svasṛ-mukha-mahilās tadvad anye ca ye ye |
children.translated_text: mother, the women headed by the sisters of mother and father, and likewise whatever others —

children.text: saṛveṣām eva teṣāṃ yugapad api vasann antare vāsayaṃś ca
children.translated_text: dwelling simultaneously within all of them and causing [himself] to dwell within [them],

children.text: svāntas tān vāsudeva-śruti-bhaṇitam iva vyañjayāmāsa kṛṣṇaḥ ||GC_2,1.11||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> revealed his inner self to them, as stated in the <s>Vāsudeva</s>-<s>śruti</s>!' ||2.1.11||

children.text: surapati-maṇi-mānitāṅga-lakṣmīḥ
children.translated_text: 'With bodily splendor honored by the jewels of the lord of the gods,

children.text: śaradija-sārasa-sāra-hāri-netraḥ |
children.translated_text: with eyes of surpassing beauty like the best of autumn <s>sārasa</s> cranes —

children.text: nikhila-mati-gatiḥ kathaṃ na sa syāt
children.translated_text: how would he not be the course of all minds —

children.text: pitṛ-jananī-sukha-mādhurī-dhurīṇaḥ ||GC_2,1.12||
children.translated_text: the foremost in the sweetness of the happiness of father and mother?' ||2.1.12||

children.text: dhyāne kūrmavad īkṣaṇe śakalivad ghrāṇa-grahe dhenuvat
children.translated_text: 'Like a tortoise in meditation, like a fish in seeing, like a cow in smelling,

children.text: sparśe pakṣivad asya poṣaṇa-parau śaśvad vrajeśāv amū |
children.translated_text: like a bird in touching — always devoted to nourishing him — these two rulers of <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: nityaṃ nityam udañcad-utkalikikām āśāṃ cirād vardhitāṃ
children.translated_text: the ever-rising, ever-expanding expectation, long-nurtured hope,

children.text: kaiśore pratipadya suṣṭhu phalitāṃ jāḍyaṃ mudā jagmatuḥ ||GC_2,1.13||
children.translated_text: in [his] adolescence having borne excellent fruit — they attained a stunned delight!' ||2.1.13||

children.text: sad-bhrātṛtāṃ svamanu tasya samīksya rāmaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Perceiving his excellent brotherhood toward himself, <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: phullāṅgatāṃ pratidinaṃ gatavān yathā tu |
children.translated_text: attained a blossoming of all limbs day by day;

children.text: śeṣa-pramāṇa-tanutāṃ tanuyād asau kiṃ
children.translated_text: "Would he diminish the <s>Śeṣa</s>-measured slenderness of his body?" —

children.text: diṣṭa-kramād iti janā matim iṣṭavantaḥ ||GC_2,1.14||
children.translated_text: thus, from the sequence of destiny, the people held that opinion!' ||2.1.14||

children.text: mukhyaḥ prāṇas tad-vibhedāś ca yadvat
children.translated_text: 'As the chief life-breath and its divisions,

children.text: kṛṣṇas tadvac chrīla-dāmādayaś ca |
children.translated_text: so <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the glorious <s>Dāma</s> and others;

children.text: ekātmanaḥ śaśvad uddiśya caikaṃ
children.translated_text: being of one self, always directing toward one

children.text: kāryaṃ yat te yānti tat-tad-vihāram ||GC_2,1.15||
children.translated_text: purpose — they go to each respective sport!' ||2.1.15||

children.text: yeṣāṃ sevyaḥ samajani sa hariḥ sevakānāṃ nijānāṃ
children.translated_text: 'That <s>Hari</s> who arose as the one to be served by his own servants,

children.text: teṣāṃ prāṇa-pratikṛtir abhavad deha-sādṛśya-bhājām |
children.translated_text: for those who share bodily resemblance, he became a replica of their life-breath;

children.text: sāhāyyaṃ taṃ prati tam api vinā te na tiṣṭhanti so'pi
children.translated_text: their assistance toward him — without him they cannot stand, nor he [without them] —

children.text: nyasthāt tatra svam iti budhamatā teṣu dṛṣṭāntateyam ||GC_2,1.16||
children.translated_text: he placed himself among them: by the opinion of the wise, this is the example!' ||2.1.16||

children.text: vatsa-goṣṭha-vipinādi ced bhajed
children.translated_text: 'If the calves, the cow-settlement, the forest, and such were to enjoy

children.text: ghrāṇa-tarpaṇam aghāri-saurabham |
children.translated_text: the fragrance of the enemy of <s>Agha</s>, satisfying the nostrils —

children.text: tarhi tatra dhavalāvalir bhaved
children.translated_text: then, therein, the white herd would become

children.text: drāg ajāgara-dharā na cānyadā ||GC_2,1.17||
children.translated_text: swiftly python-holding — and not otherwise!' ||2.1.17||

children.text: śraddadhyān na jagad yad asya tu guṇair vanyāś ca te prāṇinaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The world would not believe what [he does] through his qualities — and those forest creatures

children.text: santi drāg anugāḥ parasparam api prīṇanti yad-dveṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: are swift followers, and even mutual enemies are pleased —

children.text: yady evaṃ svayam eva so'pi bhagavān śrī-yukta-vaiyāsakiḥ
children.translated_text: if the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, the glorious son of <s>Vyāsa</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>),

children.text: śrīmad-bhāgavatākhya-vajra-lipibhir niṣṭaṅkayen nāgrataḥ ||GC_2,1.18||
children.translated_text: had not stamped it previously with the diamond-script named <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>!' ||2.1.18||

children.text: tat tad yadyapi śarma-jātam abhavad goṣṭhe tathāpy acyuta-
children.translated_text: 'Although each of those happinesses arose in the cow-settlement, nevertheless,

children.text: dveṣāya prahitān muhur nija-bhaṭāt kaṃsena bhīr utthitā |
children.translated_text: from the warriors repeatedly dispatched by <s>Kaṃsa</s> for enmity toward <s>Acyuta</s>, fear arose;

children.text: tasmād atra na tarhi śānti-rajanīty unnīya līlām imāṃ
children.translated_text: therefore, since there is no night of peace here — having lifted up this pastime,

children.text: cittaṃ dhūta-bhayām ihānavarataṃ nirvaktum anvicchati ||GC_2,1.19||
children.translated_text: the mind, shaking off fear, desires to narrate it unceasingly herein!' ||2.1.19||

children.text: atha tad duḥkhaṃ smarantaṃ vrajeśvaraṃ prati sāntvanaṃ samāpanam āha sma-
children.translated_text: Then, he spoke the consolation and conclusion to the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, who was remembering that suffering:

children.text:
goṣṭhe duḥkhāgadaṅkāraḥ kulālaṅkāra eṣa te |
sarvāṃ śaṅkāṃ punar dhunvann arvāg-aṅkāgatas tava ||GC_2,1.20|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'The impression of the mark of the suffering-disease in the cow-settlement — he who is the ornament of your lineage,
shaking off all doubts again — has entered your lap!' ||2.1.20|| — thus.

children.text:
tad evaṃ śrī-vrajeśvara-sabhāntaḥ prātaḥ-kathā kathitā | yasyāṃ savyavadhāna-deśe niveśena śrī-vrajeśvaryādayaḥ śrī-rādhādayaś ca prati-nija-karṇam abhyarṇita-varṇa-varṇaṃ cakruḥ |
[23] atha pūrvavad ekānte kānte virājamāna-śrī-kānte śrī-rādhikā-niśānte niśāntas tat-
kathā-śeṣaḥ saṃśleṣam avāpa |
children.translated_text:
Thus was the morning narrative told within the assembly of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>. Wherein, at the place with an intervening screen, the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s> and the others, and glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and the others, brought the narration, letter by letter, close to their respective ears.
[23] Then, as before, in solitude, with the splendid beloved shining — in the nighttime of glorious <s>Rādhikā</s>, at the edge of the night — the remainder of that narrative attained its union.

children.text: yatra ca snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Where <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text: svayaṃ lakṣmīr apy acyuta-hṛdi gatāpy anya-vapuṣā
children.translated_text: '<s>Lakṣmī</s> herself, though entered into <s>Acyuta's</s> heart, in another body,

children.text: tapas taptvā yaṃ kvāpy alabhata na rāsādi-mahasi |
children.translated_text: performing austerities, could never obtain him in the splendor of the <s>rāsa</s> and such;

children.text: tam etaṃ govindaṃ vaśitam anuvindan vraja-ramā-
children.translated_text: this very <s>Govinda</s>, found brought under sway by the host of <s>Vraja's</s> beautiful women —

children.text: gaṇaḥ śarmāvindat kiyad iti kathaṃ kaḥ kathayatu? ||GC_2,1.21||
children.translated_text: what happiness they found — how much, and how, who can narrate?' ||2.1.21||

children.text:
prasādaṃ yaṃ svapne'py alabhata na laksmīr api hares
tam etaṃ śrī-gopyaḥ samadadhata rāsādi-mahasi |
aho yasyā bhāgyaṃ spṛhitam api tābhir na kalitaṃ
kim asyā rādhāyāḥ kavayatu kavis tan-maya-sukham? ||GC_2,1.22|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'The grace that even <s>Lakṣmī</s> could not obtain even in a dream from <s>Hari</s> —
this very [grace], the glorious <s>gopīs</s> bestowed upon her in the splendor of the <s>rāsa</s> and such;
ah! — she whose fortune is coveted even by them but not attained —
what poet could compose the bliss-filled happiness of this <s>Rādhā</s>?' ||2.1.22|| — thus.

children.text: atha kṣaṇam uṣṇībhūya tuṣṇīmbhūya ca punar āha-tathāpi bhrātar madhukaṇṭha! tad idaṃ mukta-kaṇṭhaṃ punar anuvadituṃ śaktir na prasaktībhavati | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: Then, having become heated for a moment and then silent, he spoke again: 'Nevertheless, O brother <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>! The power to repeat this once more with full throat does not become engaged — because:

children.text: kulīnānāṃ ślāghyair nija-kulaja-lokaiḥ parivṛtis
children.translated_text: 'The association of the well-born with their own praiseworthy clan-people,

children.text: tathāryāṇāṃ rītir yad api kila tāsām avicalā |
children.translated_text: and the conduct of the noble ones — though indeed unwavering for those [<s>gopīs</s>] —

children.text: tathāpy uccais tat-tad-vicalana-kṛtir dhvasta-nikhilā
children.translated_text: nevertheless, the supreme disturbance wrought by the subversion of all those [conventions] —

children.text: mukunda-premārtir mama hṛdi vimohaṃ prathayati ||GC_2,1.23||
children.translated_text: the agony of love for <s>Mukunda</s> — spreads bewilderment in my heart!' ||2.1.23||

children.text: punaḥ sāsraṃ śrī-rādhā-mukham īkṣamāṇa uvāca-
children.translated_text: Again, gazing tearfully upon the face of glorious <s>Rādhā</s>, he said:

children.text: kharāṃśor aṃśu-spṛg-vapur iva kharāṃśor maṇi-tatir
children.translated_text: 'As a body touched by the rays of the harsh-rayed [sun], as a row of jewels [reflecting] the harsh-rayed one,

children.text: vidhoḥ kānti-sparśi-sthitir iva vidho ratna-vitatiḥ |
children.translated_text: as a state touching the luster of the moon, as an expanse of gems [reflecting] the moon —

children.text: muhur jvālāṃ hanta dravam api vahantī tad abhavan
children.translated_text: alas, repeatedly bearing both flame and also fluidity — thus she became

children.text: murārer diṅ-mātrād bhramayati tad eṣā mama manaḥ ||GC_2,1.24||
children.translated_text: from the mere direction of the slayer of <s>Mura</s> — that [state] bewilders my mind!' ||2.1.24||

children.text: tad evam evāvṛtyā punar api tat-tad-viṣayam uvāca, yathā-
children.translated_text: Thus, by way of repetition, he spoke again regarding each subject, as follows:

children.text: yadā dṛṣṭiṃ yātaḥ katham api haris tāsu sa tadā
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Hari</s> somehow came into the sight of those [<s>gopīs</s>], then

children.text: paraṃ sphūrti-bhrāntiṃ racayati purāvan na tu param |
children.translated_text: he creates only a vibration-like bewilderment as before, and nothing more;

children.text: yadā spṛṣṭiṃ prāptaḥ kvacid api tadāpi prathamavat
children.translated_text: when somewhere he has attained [their] touch, even then, as at first —

children.text: tad etad vaiyagryaṃ mama hṛdayam uccair dalayati ||GC_2,1.25||
children.translated_text: this very eagerness crushes my heart mightily!' ||2.1.25||

children.text: tad etad vaiyagryaṃ vṛṣaravi-sutāyām adhigamād
children.translated_text: 'This very eagerness — when attained in the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> — from afar,

children.text: vidūraṃ yad guptaṃ hasati kim u vā roditi yadā |
children.translated_text: that which is concealed — does it laugh or does it weep?

children.text: tadā tasyā hāse sphurati nikhilaṃ hṛṣyatitarāṃ
children.translated_text: Then, when she laughs, everything manifestly rejoices exceedingly,

children.text: tathā rode glāniṃ kalayatitarāṃ ha jagad api ||GC_2,1.26 ||
children.translated_text: and when she weeps, the world too experiences excessive languor!' ||2.1.26||

children.text: yadā rāsānanda-prabhṛti-hari-līlāḥ suvalitās
children.translated_text: 'When the pastimes of <s>Hari</s>, beginning with the bliss of the <s>rāsa</s>, were beautifully unfolded,

children.text: tadā gopyaḥ satyaṃ parama-paramaṃ śarma samayuḥ |
children.translated_text: then the <s>gopīs</s> truly attained the supreme, supremest happiness;

children.text: paraṃ yātāyātaṃ racayad abhitas tad-virahajaṃ
children.translated_text: but the great suffering born of his separation, creating coming-and-going [alternations],

children.text: mahā-duḥkhaṃ tāsāṃ hṛdayam asakṛn mardayati naḥ ||GC_2,1.27||
children.translated_text: crushes their hearts — and ours — repeatedly on all sides!' ||2.1.27||

children.text: priyāṇāṃ sarvāsāṃ param upari rādhāṃ praṇayavān
children.translated_text: 'That he, full of love, above all the beloveds — <s>Rādhā</s> supremely —

children.text: asādhāraṇyena sva-hṛdi sa purā lālayati yat |
children.translated_text: previously cherished with extraordinary [devotion] in his own heart —

children.text: tad etan naḥ sarvaṃ sukham ahaha hā nātha ramaṇety
children.translated_text: that all our happiness — alas! ah! O Lord! O Beloved! —

children.text: adaḥ stoka-ślokaḥ pibati kim ahaṃ vacmi karavai? ||GC_2,1.28||
children.translated_text: that small verse drinks [it all] — what more shall I say or do?' ||2.1.28||

children.text: idaṃ smāraṃ smāraṃ jvalati mama dhīr yad vraja-mṛgī-
children.translated_text: 'Remembering this again and again, my intellect burns — that the love of the doe-eyed ones

children.text: dṛśāṃ lajjālūnāṃ harim anu ratir vyaktim agamat |
children.translated_text: of <s>Vraja</s>, the modest ones, following <s>Hari</s>, came to manifestation;

children.text: tad āstāṃ rādhyāyāḥ sa-vidham iva taṃ tat-sphuraṇa-kṛt
children.translated_text: let that remain — of <s>Rādhā</s>, [her love,] as if with method, that manifestation-maker —

children.text: pramāyās taṃ draṣṭuṃ dṛśi kuṭilatā maṃ vidahati ||GC_2,1.29||
children.translated_text: the crookedness of the eye to see him, [even] of [mere] awareness — it burns me!' ||2.1.29||

children.text: anyat paśyati kṛṣṇam anya-vacane kṛṣṇaṃ bravīty anya-vāk
children.translated_text: 'She who, in seeing one thing, sees <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; in hearing another's words, speaks of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: śrutyāṃ kṛṣṇam aho śṛṇoti satataṃ yā gopa-subhrū-tatiḥ |
children.translated_text: in hearing, always hears <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — that host of fair-browed cowherd women —

children.text: tasyāṃ kiṃ bata gopana-pravalatāṃ yady aśnuvānā sphuṭaṃ
children.translated_text: therein, alas, even while attaining the strength of concealment,

children.text: rādhāyā jaḍatā na hi prabalatāṃ yāyād amūdṛśy api ||GC_2,1.30||
children.translated_text: the stupor of <s>Rādhā</s> — it would not indeed become powerful even in such ones [as the others]!' ||2.1.30||

children.text: atha vallavī-vallabhasyāpi tathā kathā prathanīyā-
children.translated_text: Now the narrative of the beloved of the cowherd-women too must be spread forth in the same manner:

children.text: ekā śrīr yad-vaśe bhāti tad-vaśe sukha-santatiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One <s>Śrī</s> (fortune) shines under his sway, and under her sway shines a succession of happiness;

children.text: śrī-koṭīr vaśayan kṛṣṇas tat-koṭiṃ sphuṭam arhati ||GC_2,1.31||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who brings crores of <s>Śrīs</s> under his sway, clearly deserves crores of those [happinesses]!' || (GC 2,1.31)

children.text: tathāpi līlā-rasa-viśeṣa-vaśatayā tadānīm anyathā-prathayāpi santaḥ samapaśyanta, yathā-
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, due to the particular <s>rasa</s> of his <s>līlā</s>, the saintly ones at that time perceived it otherwise, as follows:

children.text: mlānau mlāniṃ rucau rociḥ
children.translated_text: 'In fading, [sharing] the fadedness; in luster, [sharing] the radiance

children.text: preyasīnām anuvrajan |
children.translated_text: of the beloved women — following [them] —

children.text: vīkṣitaḥ so'yam antarjñair
children.translated_text: he was perceived by those who know the inner [states]

children.text: vṛrttīnām vṛttimān iva ||GC_2,1.32||
children.translated_text: as one who possesses the dispositions of [their] dispositions!' || (GC 2,1.32)

children.text: gāmbhīryān mura-śatro
children.translated_text: 'Due to the depth of the foe of <s>Mura</s>,

children.text: sphuṭam abdher iva na bhāti kārśyādi |
children.translated_text: clearly, as of the ocean, emaciation and the like do not appear;

children.text: kintu tadanvayi-jīvana-
children.translated_text: but from the life-sustaining

children.text: dhārāṇāṃ tena tac ca tarkyeta ||GC_2,1.33||
children.translated_text: streams of those connected to him, that [emaciation] could be inferred.' || (GC 2,1.33)

children.text: yadyapi tāsāṃ lābhe
children.translated_text: 'Even though in the attainment of those [gopīs],

children.text: hariṇā na svairitā yātā |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> did not proceed with willfulness,

children.text: tad api svasminn abhimati-
children.translated_text: still, in the mere esteem directed toward himself,

children.text: mātre śaśvat-kṛtārthatāṃ mene ||GC_2,1.34||
children.translated_text: he perpetually considered himself fulfilled.' || (GC 2,1.34)

children.text: āstāṃ vraja-subhrūṇām
children.translated_text: 'Let alone the rendezvous, the meeting at the tryst-abode,

children.text: abhisṛti-saṅketa-dhāma-milanādi |
children.translated_text: and such [encounters] of the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: svaira-sthitir api tāsām
children.translated_text: even their spontaneous [natural] state

children.text: avakalitā kṛṣṇam unmudaṃ kurute ||GC_2,1.35||
children.translated_text: when perceived, makes <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> exceedingly joyful!' || (GC 2,1.35)

children.text: bali-muṣitā nija-lakṣmīr
children.translated_text: 'As if to recover his own <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune)

children.text: iva labdhuṃ tāḥ sadotkṛtāṃ yātaḥ |
children.translated_text: stolen by <s>Bali</s>, he was perpetually eager toward them;

children.text: kṛṣṇaś cintāmaṇivat
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, like a wish-fulfilling jewel,

children.text: tāsu ca rādhām acintayan nitarām ||GC_2,1.36||
children.translated_text: among those [gopīs], contemplated <s>Rādhā</s> most of all!' || (GC 2,1.36)

children.text: nimeṣaḥ kalpaḥ syād api nayana-pakṣmācala-varas
children.translated_text: 'A blink would become a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), and the best of the eyelid-mountains [would appear as obstacles];

children.text: tathā dṛg-vāry-abdhir vraja-vara-ramāḥ paśyati harau |
children.translated_text: likewise the eye-tears [become] an ocean — when the excellent beauties of <s>Vraja</s> behold <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: tad-īdṛg-bhāvaḥ kiṃ samacarad amūbhyas tam athavā
children.translated_text: did such a state proceed from those [gopīs] to him, or rather

children.text: tato'mūr ity evaṃ dvayam api na nirṇītim ayate ||GC_2,1.37||
children.translated_text: from him to those [gopīs] — thus both [alternatives] cannot be determined!' || (GC 2,1.37)

children.text: kim eṣā sphūrtir me vyatimilana-kartrī vanitayā
children.translated_text: '"Is this manifestation of mine the cause of the meeting with that woman,

children.text: tayā kiṃ vā sākṣāt-kṛtir iti vivekāvidura-dhīḥ |
children.translated_text: or is it her direct realization [of me]?" — thus, with a mind far from discernment,

children.text: hariḥ svānta-jvālā-valayita-vapuḥ kvāpi valavat-
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, his body encircled by the flames of his inner heart, somewhere blazing

children.text: praphullāṅgaḥ kvāpi pratimuhur udagraṃ bhramam agāt ||GC_2,1.38||
children.translated_text: with fully blooming limbs, somewhere else — wavered intensely, moment after moment!' || (GC 2,1.38)

children.text: tad evaṃ duḥkha-nigīrṇaṃ yathā-kathañcana yad varṇitam, yac cānyad ito'py atitarāṃ varṇayitum abhyarṇīkriyate, tat khalu sarvāyatyāṃ parama-sukhāgatyāḥ pratyāsattaye sampatsyate, durgama-kūpa-maru-bhū-bhuvām anūpa-gamanāya durga-laṅghanavat |
children.translated_text: Thus, what has been described — though swallowed by sorrow — in one way or another, and what else from this point draws near to be described even more — all that shall conduce, in all future time, to the nearness of the approach of supreme happiness, like the crossing of a fortress for reaching the marshy lands of an impassable well-desert.

children.text: na ca varṇanāyāṃ tasyai sampatsyata ity eva vaktavyam | paśyata paśyata, tad etad rādhā-mādhava-nirbādha-vyatimilana-nirvarṇanāyāṃ sampraty api sampadyate; yata eva ca yat kiñcit tad varṇayituṃ śakyate |
children.translated_text: Nor should it merely be said that 'it shall conduce to the description.' Look, look — this very unobstructed description of the meeting of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> is being accomplished even now; and by that very [accomplishment], whatever little of that can be described is [being described].

children.text: tac ca varṇanaṃ yathā-evaṃ kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇa-priyāṇāṃ kṛta-saṃmohena mahā-bhāvādhiroheṇa samaṃ pūrṇaṃ kaiśoram api tūrṇam āyātam | tatra śrī-kṛṣṇsya yathā-
children.translated_text: And that description is as follows: thus, along with the great ascent of <s>mahā-bhāva</s> (supreme ecstatic love) that bewildered <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> beloveds, the full <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence) too arrived swiftly. There, of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as follows:

children.text: śrī-gopādhipa-dugdha-sindhu-janitaṃ sat-kīrti-śubhraṃ sphurat-
children.translated_text: 'Born from the milk-ocean of the glorious chief of cowherds (<s>Nanda</s>), brilliant with the whiteness of true fame,

children.text: kṛṣṇābhāvalitaṃ sudīrgha-nayana-jyotir-vidhūtāmbujam |
children.translated_text: resplendent with the dark luster of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with the light of his exceedingly long eyes dispelling the lotus,

children.text: gopī-netra-cakora-jīvana-ruciṃ kāma-pracārākaraṃ
children.translated_text: the life-giving beauty for the <s>cakora</s>-bird eyes of the <s>gopīs</s>, the mine of the activity of <s>Kāma</s> (Love) —

children.text: kaiśorāmṛta-pūrṇam avyaya-kalaṃ govinda-candraṃ bhaje ||GC_2,1.39||
children.translated_text: I worship the moon of <s>Govinda</s>, full of the nectar of <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence), of imperishable digits!' || (GC 2,1.39)

children.text: tāsāṃ yathā--
children.translated_text: Of those [gopīs], as follows:

children.text: vaktrendu-sphuṭa-netra-kairava-ruciḥ pāṇḍūbhavadgaṇḍabhūr
children.translated_text: 'With the beauty of the <s>kairava</s> (night-lotus) eyes manifest in the moon-face, with the cheek-ground becoming pale,

children.text: vakṣo-janma-sahasra-patra-mukulāmandāvali-bhrājitā |
children.translated_text: with the chest-born thousand-petaled buds shining in languid rows,

children.text: navya-stavya-nitamba-bimba-pulina-śrī-kariṇī śrī-harer
children.translated_text: with the glory of the beautiful, fresh, praiseworthy, rounded hip-sandbank — a she-elephant of beauty — of glorious <s>Hari</s>:

children.text: ābhīrī-nava-yauvana-sthitir adhāj jyautsnīva netra-prathām ||GC_2,1.40||
children.translated_text: the state of the new youth of the cowherd-women spread its radiance like moonlight upon the eyes!' || (GC 2,1.40)

children.text: tad evam ubhayeṣāṃ nava-yauvana-sāgara-paramānurāga-sudhākarayoḥ parasparaṃ bhūri-paripūritā-karayoḥ sarvatra pracāraḥ sañcarati ca tasmin yad eva tāsāṃ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇa-kartṛka-pariṇayanāpanayanāya gargaḥ kila vyañjitaṃ cakāra, tad eva lokam astoka-śaṅkā-sañjitam ācacāra |
children.translated_text: Thus, of those two — the moon of supreme love in the ocean of new youth — mutually filling each other abundantly, [their love] coursed everywhere. And in that coursing, what <s>Garga</s> had earlier hinted at — for the prevention of the marriage of those [gopīs] with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — that very thing reached the people, generating no small suspicion.

children.text:
yadi kṛṣṇena samam āsām aṅga-saṅgaḥ syāt tad-ārvāg eva sarvam eva gokulaṃ tad-virahākulaṃ syād iti | [37] garga-vacanam eva ca mātara-pitarādibhiḥ kṛṣṇāya tāsāṃ vitaraṃ vighna-nighnaṃ cakāra |
[38] yatra ca sākṣād yogamāyā kṛṣṇaṃ varivasyantī svātmano gopanāya pūrṇimā nāmnā tapasyantī kṛcchra-vaśyantī gaty-antaram apaśyantī tāsām anyatra vivāhaṃ mṛṣābhāva-vaham eva nirvāhayāmāsa | sarvatrānalpa-svapna-kalpanāyām api prāyatayā jāgara-prāyatayā pracāraṇat | tathā tāsāṃ paty-ābhāsāṅga-saṅgamaṃ ca bhaṅgam āsādayāmāsa | tathaiva hi nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya [BhP 10.33.37] ityādi-rītyā
śukeneva śrī-śukena dig-darśitā |
children.translated_text:
'If there were bodily contact of these [gopīs] with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then even before that, all of <s>Gokula</s> would become agitated by the distress of their separation [from their families].' [37] And the very word of <s>Garga</s> made the mothers, fathers, and others create an extensive obstacle against the giving of those [gopīs] to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
[38] Wherein <s>Yogamāyā</s> herself, serving <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, for the concealment of her own [identity], performing austerities under the name <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, controlling with difficulty, seeing no other recourse — she arranged the marriage of those [gopīs] elsewhere, though that marriage was a bearer of mere semblance. In all [cases], even in no small dream-fabrication, [she worked] predominantly in a predominantly wakeful manner. And she also brought about the disruption of the bodily contact of those [gopīs] with the semblance-husbands. Just as indeed 'they bore no ill will toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' [BhP 10.33.37] and such — thus the direction was indicated by <s>Śuka</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>), [himself] like a parrot.

children.text: tad evaṃ sati sa ca tāś ca parama-tarṣa-kṛtākarṣatayā pracchannatayā ca parasparaṃ saṅga-maharṣam api kathañcid ācitaṃ cakruḥ |
children.translated_text: That being so, he and those [gopīs], through the attraction created by supreme longing and through concealment, somehow accumulated the great bliss of mutual companionship as well.

children.text:
atha pūrvokta-rītyā tāsāṃ sannihita-lokeṣu pratītyā mahānurāgasya kramād avagamād gurubhir manasi bhāvita-bhāvi-kṛṣṇa-saṅgamāśaṅkatayā vacasi tu vibhāvita-vadhū-jana-vana-gamana-kalaṅkatayā nirmite nirodhe milad-udbodhe balānujanmā dvi-janmānaṃ narma-priya-sakhatayānuvartamānaṃ nāmnā madhumaṅgalatayā samāmnātaṃ tat-prasaṅga-saṅgataṃ cakāra- kathaṃ rādhādīnām āgamana-vadhā
bahūny ahāny adhikṛtya dṛśyate? iti |
children.translated_text: Then, in the manner previously described, when the great love [between them] was gradually perceived by those present among the people, the restriction was fashioned by the elders — in their minds, imbued with the apprehension of the future association with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, but in their words, with the fabricated scandal of the young brides going to the forest — and when this restriction became awakened into encounter, the first-born (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), following [the situation], engaged the twice-born one (<s>Madhumaṅgala</s>) — who was attending him as a jesting dear friend, commemorated by the name <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — in connection with that matter: 'How is it that the coming of <s>Rādhā</s> and the others has been seen to be obstructed for many days now?'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca--purūṇāṃ gurūṇāṃ nirodha eva nidānatayā tatra bodha-viṣayī-bhavati |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'It is the very restriction of the many elders that is perceived as the cause thereof.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-aho! tat tad api raho-vṛttaṃ kiṃ gurūṇāṃ karṇeṣu vṛttam?
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Ah! Has even that which was done in secret reached the ears of the elders?'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said:

children.text: nāntar bahir api yasyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'In that mental transformation

children.text: sphurati jñānaṃ mano-vikṛtau |
children.translated_text: in which knowledge shines neither inwardly nor outwardly —

children.text: ekasyāpi na tasyā
children.translated_text: even of one such [woman],

children.text: na vyaktiḥ syād amūdṛśāṃ kim uta? ||GC_2,1.41||
children.translated_text: would there be no manifestation — what then of ones such as these?' || (GC 2,1.41)

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-pūrvam api purvahir antar-gamane tāsu nava-yauvanaṃ gatāsu guru-nirodha purur evāsīt | adhunā tu kīdṛg adhikaḥ?
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Even before, when those [gopīs] had attained new youth, the restriction of the elders upon their going out and coming in was extensive indeed. But now, how much greater is it?'

children.text: madhumaṅgala uvāca-yadyapi nāsman-mukhataḥ sukhatayā niḥsarati rati-pratikūlam idaṃ, tathāpi bhavat-praśna-prathāta eva kathā-viṣayīkriyate | tathā ca śrutaṃ mayā khalv idam viśrutaṃ kula-pālikānāṃ tāsu gāli-dānam avakalyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> said: 'Although this, which is hostile to love, does not issue from our mouth as something pleasant, nevertheless, by the very spreading of your question, it becomes the subject of narration. And thus I have heard this well-known abuse-giving of the household-guardians upon those [gopīs] — let it be heard:

children.text:
kiṃ dhig dhyāyasi hanta niśvasiṣi kiṃ vartmāni kiṃ prekṣase
kiṃ sakhyā mukham atra paśyasi kucau kiṃ dṛg jalaiḥ siñcase? |
mūrcchām ṛcchasi kintarāṃ kim asakṛt kṛṣṇeti varṇa-dvayaṃ
tasyāṃ jalpasi kiṃ punaḥ pulakitāṃ kampaṃ ca tantanyase ||GC_2,1.42|| iti |
children.translated_text: '"Why — shame! — do you brood? Why, alas, do you sigh? Why do you gaze at the paths? | Why do you look at your friend's face here? Why do you sprinkle your breasts with tears from your eyes? | You fall into — what kind of — swoon! Why do you repeatedly utter the two syllables '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'? | Why again, becoming horripilated, do you extend trembling?" || (GC 2,1.42) — thus.'

children.text: atha kula-pālikā-pālikānāṃ tāsāṃ dūnatākaryā nanānduḥ pratisvaṃ mātaraṃ prati vacana-caryā dig-varṇanaṃ cāvakarṇyatām--
children.translated_text: Now, the response of those [gopīs] who are the protectors of the household-guardians — the description of the course of their words to their respective mothers regarding their painful state — let it be heard:

children.text:
dṛg-vīthīṃ kula-pālikāḥ śruti-patham tāsāṃ kathā-nāsikā-
vartmāneka-sugandhi-dhūpa-racanā vavrur mayā yojitāḥ |
tasyāḥ kṛṣṇamayī daśā manasi yā sā kena yatnena vā
gacchedāvṛtatāṃ tato janani kiṃ mahyaṃ vṛthā kupyasi? ||GC_2,1.43|| iti |
children.translated_text: '"The household-guardians [block] the pathway of the eyes; the path of the ears [is blocked by] their talk; the nostrils' | path [I blocked] by arranging many fragrant incense-offerings — these were arranged by me. | But that state of hers which is fully absorbed in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — in her mind — by what effort | could that be made concealed? Therefore, O mother, why do you rage at me in vain?" || (GC 2,1.43) — thus.'

children.text: tad evaṃ varṇyamānam ākarṇya kṣaṇaṃ sa-mlāna-varṇaṃ nivarṇya ca punar asāv asyā vartāyā viśeṣānuvartanāya madhumaṅgalaṃ prasthāpya cintāṃ cāntaḥ prāpya vicārayati sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, hearing what was being described, and observing his complexion turning slightly pale for a moment, he again dispatched <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> for the further pursuit of this news, and having reached contemplation within, he deliberated:

children.text: tam etaṃ jana-ravaṃ mama guravaścānubhavamānītavantaḥ santi, prāyaśaḥ parama-yaśasaḥ pitaraś ca tatra karṇa-vitaraṃ kariṣyanti | tarhi kintarām antarāyam imam antarayitā? iti kṣaṇaṃ śūnyāyamāna-manāḥ punaś cintayāmāsa | --
children.translated_text: 'My elders too have experienced this uproar of the people, and my supremely famous parents shall likely extend their ears to that as well. Then, what kind of obstacle shall obstruct this obstacle?' — thus, his mind becoming vacant for a moment, he pondered again:

children.text: ito vyavadhānam eva khalu kaluṣatāṃ gatasya mama nidhānaṃ bhavati | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: 'From this point, separation itself becomes the receptacle for me who has attained the state of turbidity. Thus:

children.text: kalaṅko yatra syād apariharaṇīyārtha-kṛtakas
children.translated_text: 'Where there would be a stigma created by an unavoidable cause,

children.text: tato dūrād bhāvyaṃ kula-jani-janenaivam ucitam |
children.translated_text: from that, one born in a [noble] family should properly keep far away;

children.text: sa kālāl luptaḥ syād bhavati hi ca tatra pratividhis
children.translated_text: it may be erased by time, and indeed there is a remedy for that —

children.text: tad asmān me goṣṭhād vyavahitir akaṣṭaṃ prasajati ||GC_2,1.44||
children.translated_text: therefore, my separation from the cow-settlement entails no hardship.' || (GC 2,1.44)

children.text: yeṣāṃ pitrādīnāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Those fathers and others

children.text: sneho mama jīvanaṃ goṣṭhe |
children.translated_text: whose affection is my life in the cow-settlement —

children.text: ahaha ku-daivād abhitaḥ
children.translated_text: alas, alas! By cruel fate, on all sides,

children.text: saṅkocas tebhya eva sañjātaḥ ||GC_2,1.45||
children.translated_text: constriction has arisen from them alone!' || (GC 2,1.45)

children.text: atha punar anyathā cintayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then again he pondered otherwise:

children.text: prāṇās tyajantu dehaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Let the life-breaths abandon the body;

children.text: dehaḥ prāṇān api tyajatu |
children.translated_text: let the body abandon the life-breaths too;

children.text: hari-gopyas tu mithas tāḥ
children.translated_text: but <s>Hari</s> and the <s>gopīs</s> — those mutual

children.text: prāṇāḥ katham iva mithas tyājyāḥ? ||GC_2,1.46||
children.translated_text: life-breaths — how could they mutually be abandoned?' || (GC 2,1.46)

children.text: punas tad api cānyathā cakāra-
children.translated_text: And again he rendered that too otherwise:

children.text: ekasminn āvāse
children.translated_text: 'In a single dwelling,

children.text: dampatyor bhavati duḥsaho virahaḥ |
children.translated_text: the separation of husband and wife is unbearable;

children.text: tasmād dūre gamanaṃ
children.translated_text: therefore, going far away

children.text: samayaṃ gamanīyatāṃ nayati ||GC_2,1.47||
children.translated_text: leads the time [of separation] toward being passable.' || (GC 2,1.47)

children.text:
kintu hā vṛṣabhānu-bhānu-kīrtidā-kīrtidāyini! hā janmata eva man-manastayā san-manastā-dhāyini! hā kumāratām ārabhya kāya-vāṅ-manaḥ-sukumāratā-parvaṇā sarva-harṣiṇi! hā mad-vinābhāva-bhāvanā-jvālā-jāla-samutkarṣita-tarṣini! hā gaty-antara-rahitatayā kathañcit kiñcin māṃ saṅgamya ca muhur asaṅgamya duḥkha-dagdhe! hā dayite! dayite mayi visrabdhe samprati duṣṭhu-niṣṭhuratayā mayā
tyaktum iṣyamāṇā kathaṃ jīviṣyasi? hā sarva-sukhādhike! radhike! kutra vāmutra gamiṣyasi? iti |
children.translated_text: 'But — alas, O <s>Vṛṣabhānu's</s> sun, <s>Kīrtidā's</s> bestower of fame! Alas, O you who from birth nourished the good-mindedness of being my very mind! Alas, O you who from girlhood onward, by the tender festivity of body, speech, and mind, delighted all! Alas, O you who are scorched with thirst, inflamed by the net of flames born from the thought of my absence! Alas, O you who, bereft of other recourse, somehow meeting me a little and then repeatedly not meeting me, are burned by sorrow! Alas, O beloved! Beloved! You who trust in me — now, being desired to be abandoned by me with vile cruelty — how shall you live? Alas, O you who surpass all happiness! O <s>Rādhikā</s>! Where indeed shall you go then?' — thus.

children.text: atha madhumaṅgalaḥ saṅgamya tad idam aramyaṃ nivedayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, having returned, reported this unpleasant [news]:

children.text:
niracinvaṃste sarve
rādhādīnāṃ nirodha-sātatyam |
yasmād gṛha-pālyas tā
hariṇīr etā nirundhate paritaḥ ||GC_2,1.48|| iti |
children.translated_text: '"All are verifying the perpetual restriction upon <s>Rādhā</s> and the others; | for those household-guardians confine these doe-like ones on all sides!" || (GC 2,1.48) — thus.'

children.text: tad evaṃ paryag aparyavasya-didantayā cintayā labdhuṃ cāmūra-sambhāvanayā bhāvanayā samayaṃ gamayitum asamarthaḥ skhalad-arthaḥ sa-tṛṣṇaḥ sa tu kṛṣṇaḥ sa-vayobhiḥ samam eva ramamāṇas tri-yāmāṃ viramayati smeti kṛtaṃ hṛn-marma-bhaṅga-kareṇātiprasaṅgena [55] tad etad uktvā kathakaḥ samāpanam āha-
children.translated_text: Thus, unable to pass the time with a thought that was rolling about without reaching a conclusion, and with a conception incapable of imagining unlimited possibilities, faltering in purpose, full of longing — that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sporting together with his age-fellows, brought the night to rest.' — Thus was completed by the excessive elaboration that breaks the core of the heart. [55] Having said this, the narrator spoke the conclusion:

children.text: rādhe na yukta muktaṃ syān mukta-śātam athāpi vām |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>! It would not be proper to release what has been released — the mantle of your [modesty], or rather of you both;

children.text: mithaḥ prema-bharaṃ vyaktaṃ vaktum udyatavān aham ||GC_2,1.49||
children.translated_text: I was about to speak openly of the weight of mutual love between you two!' || (GC 2,1.49)

children.text: purā katheyaṃ kathitā murāre rāga-bṛṃhiṇī |
children.translated_text: 'This tale of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), which nourishes love, was told formerly;

children.text: paśya so'yaṃ prāṇa-nāthaḥ prasādaṃ tava vāñchati ||GC_2,1.50||
children.translated_text: behold — this very lord of your life-breaths desires your grace!' || (GC 2,1.50)

children.text: tad evaṃ yathā-kathā tathā līlā-prathām upalabhamānās tad-ante ca tasyāḥ samprati nāstitāyāṃ viśvasti-kṛtāśvastikā nija-nija-bhavanaṃ sarva eva sānandaṃ parvatayā jagmuḥ | śrī-rādhā-mādhavau ca nija-śayyā-gṛhaṃ sukhamayyā spṛhayā gṛhayāñcakrāte |
children.translated_text: Thus, perceiving the spread of the <s>līlā</s> according to the narrative, and at its end, when the non-existence [i.e., conclusion] of that [narrative] had been verified with trust, all went to their respective homes with joy, in great measure. And glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> too drew their own bedchamber near with a desire full of happiness.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrīmaduttara-gopāla-campūmanu
vrajānurāga-sāgara-prathanaṃ nāma
prathamaṃ pūraṇam
||1||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Uttara-Gopāla-campū</s>,
the first <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Spreading of the Ocean of Love for <s>Vraja</s>'
|| 1 ||

children.text: atha dvitīyaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the second <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter):

children.text: akrūra-krūratā-pūraṇam
children.translated_text: The Fulfillment of <s>Akrūra's</s> Cruelty

children.text: athāparedyuḥ prabhāta-virājamānāyāṃ sa-vraja-yuvarāja-vraja-rāja-sabhāyāṃ kathā | yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, in the assembly of the prince of <s>Vraja</s> and the king of <s>Vraja</s>, resplendent in the morning — the narrative [began]. As follows:

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca-atha keśi-vadhāt pūrvasyāṃ kṣapāyāṃ labdha-kṣayāyām aruṇe cārune jāte sa khalu kamalekṣaṇaś capalekṣaṇatayā kṣaṇa-katipayam idaṃ cintayāmāsa-
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: Then, on the night preceding the slaying of <s>Keśī</s>, when [the night] was coming to an end and a beautiful dawn had appeared, the lotus-eyed one, with restless eyes, pondered this for a few moments:

children.text:
aho! svapnaḥ so'yam, yatra mañcāt kṛta-sraṃsanaḥ kaṃsaḥ sa mayā samākṛṣṭa iva
 dṛṣṭaḥ | sampratyāśu ca tad eva pratyāsannam | yad adya śvaḥ keśī mad-abhiniveśī bhavan yamasya prativeśī bhavitā | tad-anantaraṃ kaṃsa-dhvaṃsanam eva prasaktam | prasakte ca tasmin mama nigama eva gamanaṃ samaya-labdhatayā yukti-visrabdham | yatas tasya mat-trastasya na khalv atra yātrā yukti-pātrāyate | tasya cādyāpi vṛṣṇiṣu tarjanāyām anāratasya mayi ca durjana-visarjanāyām avinā-kṛtasya vināśanaṃ
vinā tatra cātra ca mat-pitur ubhaya-kulaṃ bhayākulaṃ syād iti |
children.translated_text: 'Ah! That was a dream, in which <s>Kaṃsa</s>, made to fall from his platform, was seen by me as if drawn [toward destruction]. And now that very [event] is swiftly approaching. For today or tomorrow, <s>Keśī</s>, who is intent upon me, shall become a neighbor of <s>Yama</s> (Death). Immediately after that, the destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s> itself is imminent. And when that is imminent, my departure itself becomes a journey, timely and trustworthy in its logic. For he [<s>Kaṃsa</s>], terrified of me, shall not find the pilgrimage-expedition here a fit vessel [for his scheming]. And until his destruction — he who ceaselessly threatens the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and who has not abandoned the deployment of wicked ones against me — is accomplished, both the clan of my father here and there shall remain agitated with fear.'

children.text: atha punaś cintayati sma-hanta! hanta! yadi kārya-paryāyatas tatra suvilambaḥ saṃvalate, tadā man-mātrādi-prāṇānāṃ nātrāṅga-saṅga-maṅgalaṃ tarkayāmi | tataś ca,
children.translated_text: Then he pondered again: 'Alas! Alas! If, in the sequence of duties, a great delay accumulates there, then I do not envision the auspiciousness of bodily contact here for those whose life-breaths are [sustained by] my mother and the others. And thus:

children.text: mātur netra-cakora-candra-vadanas tātasya dṛk-cātaka-
children.translated_text: 'I — who am the moon for the <s>cakora</s>-bird eyes of my mother,

children.text: śreṇī-vāri-bhṛd anya-gokula-janasyāpy akṣi-padmāṃśumān |
children.translated_text: the rain-cloud for the <s>cātaka</s>-bird rows of my father's gaze,

children.text: so'haṃ tān parihṛtya hanta gamanaṃ kurvīya cet tarhy aho
children.translated_text: the sun for the lotus-eyes of the other people of <s>Gokula</s> —

children.text: candrādi-trayavan mamāpi bhavitā dhig vāta-cakra-bhramaḥ ||GC_2,2.1||
children.translated_text: if I, abandoning them, should depart — then, alas! — | like the trio of moon and the rest, mine too would be — curse it! — a whirling in the cycle of wind!' || (GC 2,2.1)

children.text: tad evam evam ambuja-locane śayyāyām eva ciraṃ racita-śocane sahasā keśī sadeśī-babhūva | asya ca nirgranthanaṃ prathama-granthata eva kathayā granthanam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: Thus, while the lotus-eyed one lay long upon his bed, fashioning lamentation in this very manner, <s>Keśī</s> suddenly appeared in the vicinity. And the narration of his destruction was woven into the tale from the very first chapter.

children.text: atha śrī-gopeśvarī-lālyas tu lālyamāna-dhavalā-kalāpa-cchalāt pālyamāna-yaśās tri-daśālaya-mune rahaḥ-sahabhāvam āsasāda | yatra ca saṃśayānuśāyātiśaya-maya-mānaṃ munis taṃ vibhāvitayā bhāvi-tat-tal-līlayā sāntvayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, the one cherished by the queen of the cowherds (<s>Yaśodā</s>) — under the pretext of tending the bright peacock-cluster, maintaining the fame of the sage of the celestial world — attained the state of secret companionship [with <s>Nārada</s>]. And there, the sage consoled him — whose mind was overwhelmed by the excess of suspicion and remorse — with the future-revealed sports of this and that.

children.text: tataḥ samasta-śasta-pālaḥ śri-gopālas taṃ visarjya prasajyamāna-manas-tāpatayāpi bahir-upahita-sarva-sukha-śrī-mukha-prakāśatayā sakhi-rāmārāmatayā ca saha-go-vrajaṃ vrajam ājagāma | yathā-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śrī Gopāla</s>, the protector of all that is praiseworthy, having dismissed him — though with a mind burning inwardly — yet displaying outwardly the radiance of a face bearing all happiness, and with the delight of his friend <s>Rāma's</s> companionship, returned to <s>Vraja</s> together with the cow-herd. As follows:

children.text: dāmnā dāmnā sura-sumanasāṃ svargibhiḥ pūjyamānaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Worshipped by the celestials with garland after garland of divine flowers,

children.text: sāmnā sāmnā druhiṇa-sadasāṃ vīthibhiḥ stūyamānam |
children.translated_text: praised by the assemblies of <s>Brahmā</s> with hymn after hymn,

children.text: nāmnā nāmnā sa-paśu-paśupāṃ saṃmukhān nirmimāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: summoning face to face the cattle and cowherds by name after name —

children.text: dhāmnā dhāmnā sukhadam akhilaḥ prāpa taṃ dṛśyamānam ||GC_2,2.2||
children.translated_text: all [of <s>Vraja</s>] attained him, seen with glory after glory, the giver of happiness!' || (GC 2,2.2)

children.text: atra ca surāṇāṃ vacanam-
children.translated_text: And here, the words of the celestials:

children.text:
indor abhyudayāt paraṃ vikasati drāk kairavāṇāṃ ganaḥ
  sindhuḥ kṣubhyati kānti-pānam ayate dūrāc cakora-vrajaḥ |
  gopāḥ paśya mudā murāri-kalanād eṣām aśeṣāṃ daśāṃ
  gacchanto'py ati-tṛptitā-vaśatayā dhāvanti yāvad gati ||GC_2,2.3|| iti |
children.translated_text: 'After the rising of the moon, the multitude of night-lotuses swiftly blossoms; | the ocean is agitated; the flock of <s>cakora</s> birds drinks in beauty from afar; | behold, O cowherds! — from the perception of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, all these states of them — | even while they are going, through the power of extreme satisfaction, they run as far as [their] capacity!' || (GC 2,2.3) — thus.

children.text: tad evam-
children.translated_text: Thus indeed:

children.text: ālokaḥ prīti-bhājāṃ kṛti-bala-nikaraḥ kiṃkarāṇāṃ hṛd-antaḥ-
children.translated_text: 'The sight for those who partake of love, the assembled might of deeds for the servants, the inner

children.text: sāraḥ sakhya-sthitānāṃ hṛdi lasad asavas tāta-mātrādikānām |
children.translated_text: essence of the heart for those established in friendship, the shining life-breaths in the hearts of father and mother and others,

children.text: ātmā rāmāntarāṇāṃ harir iha samagāt keśinaṃ ghātayitvā
children.translated_text: the very Self of the beloved women — <s>Hari</s> came here, having had <s>Keśī</s> slain;

children.text: gehaṃ yarhy eṣa tarhi prati-nijam agamaṃs te ca dehaṃ prasiddhāḥ ||GC_2,2.4||
children.translated_text: when this one [came] to his home, then each went to their respective bodies, fully realized!' || (GC 2,2.4)

children.text: svenāmbā niramañchayat tam atha dṛṅ-nīraṃ vyamuñcat pitā
children.translated_text: 'His mother wiped him with the edge [of her garment]; his father shed tears from his eyes;

children.text: sarve'nye pariphullad aṅga-valitāṃ romāñcitām āñciṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: all the others attained a state of full-blossomed, body-rippling horripilation;

children.text: anyac ca kvacana sphurad-vacanatātītaṃ tad āsīd yadā
children.translated_text: and whatever else was there, somewhere manifesting in words and beyond [words] — that happened when,

children.text: hatvā keśinam āvrajat kalakalāndoli-vrajaṃ sa prabhuḥ ||GC_2,2.5||
children.translated_text: having slain <s>Keśī</s>, that Lord returned to <s>Vraja</s>, swaying with the tumult of joyful cries!' || (GC 2,2.5)

children.text:
tataś ca prātar atulotpāta-kātaratayā nātisambhālita-lālana-vitarau matara-pitarau putraṃ pari samāśleṣitarau gṛhāpana-snehālapana-snapana-divyavāsaḥ-paṭavāsa-samarpaṇa-lepānulepa-prathanayā taṃ kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ viśramayām āsatuḥ |
[10] yatas taṃ sadā komalam eva kalayām babhūvatur yuddhādi-samaye tu nārāyaṇa-vyaktīkṛta-tātkālika-śakti-mayam iti |
children.translated_text:
Then, in the morning, the mother and father — whose anxious care was not fully extended due to the distress of extraordinary portents — embraced their son on both sides, and through the arrangement of bringing him home, affectionate speech, bathing, the offering of divine garments, fragrant powders, applying ointments and the like, they gave him rest for a few moments.
[10] For they always regarded him as tender indeed; but during battle and the like, [they understood him to be] endowed with the power made manifest at that very time by his <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-identity.

children.text: atha gavāṃ dohanāvasarāvarohaḥ syād iti sarva-sukha-pālaḥ śrīla-gopālaḥ svayam agrajena samagrībhūya tadīya-sāmagrīkara-kiṅkara-nikaram ahūya tāsām agrīya-bhū-bhāgam āgatavān | āgata-mātre ca tatra sa-rāma-śyāma-gātre-
children.translated_text: Then, thinking 'Let the occasion for the milking of the cows arrive,' <s>Śrī Gopāla</s>, the protector of all happiness, having himself assembled together with his elder brother and summoned the troop of servants who were the makers of his equipment, arrived at the foremost ground of those [cows]. And the moment he — with the body of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Śyāma</s> (dark <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — arrived there:

children.text: huṅkāra-ghoṣa-racitākhila-śabda-moṣaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The roaring bellows — the robbery of all [other] sound —

children.text: srāg-abda-kāntim amum āstṛta-dhenu-saṅghaḥ |
children.translated_text: the herd of cows surrounding him, radiant as a garland of rain-clouds —

children.text: vatsān vināpi balavat snavam eṣa tais taṃ
children.translated_text: even without calves, powerfully flowing milk — they made him,

children.text: sad vatsalaḥ saha-balaḥ śabalaṃ cakāra ||GC_2,2.6||
children.translated_text: the truly affectionate one, together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), speckled [with milk]!' || (GC 2,2.6)

children.text: tatra tu-
children.translated_text: And there:

children.text: sarvaṃ cakāra sa hariḥ paritaḥ purāvad
children.translated_text: 'He, <s>Hari</s>, did everything on all sides as before,

children.text: dadhre surarṣi-vacasā tu vidūnamantaḥ |
children.translated_text: yet his inner being was bowed by the words of the celestial sage;

children.text: yady apy adas tad api tasya nija-vrajāya
children.translated_text: although that [was the case], even so, the return to his own <s>Vraja</s>

children.text: pratyāgatir hṛdi kṛtā sthiratāṃ pupoṣa ||GC_2,2.7||
children.translated_text: that had been established in his heart nurtured steadfastness!' || (GC 2,2.7)

children.text: 12] tathā hi, tasya bhāvānām udbhāvanā-
children.translated_text: [12] Accordingly, the manifestation of his sentiments:

children.text: kaṃsaṃ hantuṃ prayāṇi sphurati pitṛ-mukha-prema tad-vighna-rūpaṃ
devarṣer vāṅ na mithyā katham atha virahaṃ hā saheya vrajasya ?
children.translated_text: the words of the celestial sage are not false — but then, how shall I endure the separation from <s>Vraja</s>?

children.text: nirṇīte'py atra jāte kṛtam asukhamayenāsya cintāmalena
children.translated_text: Even though [the matter] has been determined here, let it be done with this anxiety-jewel, which is made of unhappiness —
