children.text: smartavyaṃ tat tu nityaṃ yad iha sukha-mayaṃ vaibhavaṃ bhāvi-saṅge ||GC_2,2.8||
children.translated_text: but what should be remembered always is this: the happiness-filled glory in the future reunion!' || (GC 2,2.8)
'I go forth to slay <s>Kaṃsa</s> — but the love of my father and the others appears as an obstacle to that;

children.text: ity acintyata cānena rathaḥ kaścana caikṣyata |
children.translated_text: 'Thus he pondered, and a certain chariot was spotted;

children.text: mahatāṃ hṛdaye yāti pratibimbaṃ hi bimbatām ||GC_2,2.9||
children.translated_text: for in the hearts of the great, a reflection indeed attains the status of reality!' || (GC 2,2.9)

children.text: ratha-stha-puruṣasya darśane tu-
children.translated_text: And upon seeing the man mounted on the chariot:

children.text: rathī nirastraḥ syād dūta iti kṛṣṇena tarkitam |
children.translated_text: '"The charioteer is unarmed — he must be a messenger" — thus <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> conjectured;

children.text: kaṃsāt kasmād asāv āgād ity anyair api śaṃkitam ||GC_2,2.10||
children.translated_text: "From whom has he come — from <s>Kaṃsa</s>?" — thus the others too suspected.' || (GC 2,2.10)

children.text: tadā ca vāruṇīm anuraktaḥ patana-saktaḥ sa dina-nāthaḥ kṛta-nadī-nātha-pāthaḥ-kvāthaḥ svam ālokaṃ lokam api tamasi veśayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: And at that time, the lord of the day (the sun), attached to the western direction, prone to setting, having boiled the waters of the lord of rivers (the ocean), enveloped his own world and the world too in darkness.

children.text: satyaṃ sūryas turya-
children.translated_text: 'Truly, the sun went

children.text: praharasyāntaṃ yayau kintu |
children.translated_text: to the end of the fourth watch; but

children.text: sabala-hariḥ pratiharitaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, together with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), made

children.text: hārita-timiraṃ vyadhān nijaṃ kiraṇam ||GC_2,2.11||
children.translated_text: the repelled, parrot-like darkness his own ray!' || (GC 2,2.11)

children.text:
tata unmukhatāṃ yāteṣu gopa-jāteṣu samam unnata-karṇa-saṅghāteṣu ca go-vrāteṣu tad avalokana-satṛṣṇau bala-kṛṣṇau ratha-sthaḥ sa dūrata eva sākṣāt paricitiṃ vināpi paricitavān |
yataḥ,
children.translated_text:
Then, as the cowherd people had become attentive, together with the herds of cows whose ears were raised — the one mounted on the chariot, though without direct acquaintance, recognized <s>Bala</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who were longing to behold him, from a distance itself.
Because:

children.text: cakṣur eva paricāyakaṃ bhaved
children.translated_text: 'The eye alone would be the introducer,

children.text: rūpa-mātra iti gīḥ satāṃ matā |
children.translated_text: through form alone — this is the view held by the good;

children.text: tādṛśām anubhave tu karṇayor
children.translated_text: but in the experience of such ones [as these],

children.text: dṛṣṭi-śaktir api kṛṣṭim ṛcchati ||GC_2,2.12||
children.translated_text: even the power of sight upon the ears attains [the force of] attraction!' || (GC 2,2.12)

children.text: astu tāvad anayoh surūpatā
children.translated_text: 'Let their extraordinary beauty be set aside —

children.text: nīla-ratna-vidhu-lobhi-śobhayoḥ |
children.translated_text: of those two, whose splendors covet the blue sapphire and the moon;

children.text: aṅghri-cihnam api citra-saṃnibhaṃ
children.translated_text: even the marks on their feet, resembling a wondrous painting,

children.text: dūrato'pi tam amūmuhan muhuḥ ||GC_2,2.13||
children.translated_text: bewildered him repeatedly from afar!' || (GC 2,2.13)

children.text: tayos tādṛśa-rūpam api nirūpitavān, yathā-
children.translated_text: He discerned their such form too, as follows:

children.text: ekaḥ śyāma-dyutīnām abhimata-vibhavasyādhidevāvatāras
children.translated_text: 'One — an incarnation of the desired sovereignty of dark-lustrous things —

children.text: tat sadhryaṅ śubhra-śobhā-samudaya-subhagābhoga-sāra-prasāraḥ |
children.translated_text: and symmetrically, the other — a full spread of the essence of the aggregate of beautiful bright splendor;

children.text: tatrādir vastra-kānti-praciti-bhagavatī-kṛṣṭa-lakṣmī-pracāraḥ
children.translated_text: therein, the first — a display of <s>Lakṣmī</s> drawn by the glory of his garment's luster,

children.text: kiṃ cānyaḥ kānta-vāsaś chavi-śavalanayā sṛṣṭa-pūrvānukāraḥ ||GC_2,2.14||
children.translated_text: and moreover, the other — creating an imitation of the former through the whitening of his garment's beauty!' || (GC 2,2.14)

children.text: tathā-
ādyaḥ kṛṣṇāmbuja-śrī-vijayi-mukha-mahā-śobhayā datta-modas
children.translated_text: 'The first — bestowing delight through the great beauty of his face, victorious over the dark lotus;

children.text: tat sadhryaṅ puṇḍarīka-dyuti-paricaya-jid-vaktra-rocir-vinodaḥ |
children.translated_text: symmetrically, the other — a sport of facial luster conquering the acquaintance with the white lotus's brightness;

children.text: tatrādir netra-śobhā-viracita-rucimat-khañjana-dyotano'daḥ
children.translated_text: therein, the first — illuminating the beautiful <s>khañjana</s> birds fashioned by the splendor of his eyes;

children.text: kiṃ cānyaś cakṣur antāruṇa-kusuma-rajaḥ-piñjarāli-pratodaḥ ||GC_2,2.15||
children.translated_text: and moreover, the other — a goad to the reddish rows of red-flower-pollen-tawny inner eye-corners!' || (GC 2,2.15)
Likewise:

children.text: tathā-
ādyaḥ śrī-kuṇḍalāntar-jhaṣa-mukha-sukha-kṛd-dyota-gaṇḍa-sthalīkas
children.translated_text: 'The first — with cheek-surfaces illuminated by the happiness-giving gleam of the fish-faces within the <s>kuṇḍala</s> earrings;

children.text: tat sadhryaṅ śaśvad eka-śruti-kiraṇa-lasat-karṇikābhāvalīkaḥ |
children.translated_text: symmetrically, the other — possessing the row of the constantly-shining, radiant ear-ornament of a single ray of <s>śruti</s>;

children.text: tatrādiś cāpa-vad-bhrū-mila-tila-kusuma-ghrāṇa-vāṇac chavīkaḥ
children.translated_text: therein, the first — with nose-beauty of sesame-flower fragrance from bow-like brow-blending;

children.text: kiṃ cānyaś tad dvitīya-dyuti-jita-vilasat-kāma-ceto-gavīkaḥ ||GC_2,2.16||
children.translated_text: and moreover, the other — having the beauty of a cow-[pen] for the mind of the brilliantly-shining <s>Kāma</s> (Love-god), conquered by the luster of that second one!' || (GC 2,2.16)
Likewise:

children.text: tathā-
ādyaḥ svar nātha-ratna-dyuti-bhuja-bhujaga-dyoti-ratnair vicitras
children.translated_text: 'The first — variegated with arm-serpent-gems, gleaming on the arms with the luster of the <s>Svarṇātha</s> gem;

children.text: tat sadhryaṅ puṣpa-rāgābhida-maṇi-racita stambha-jid-bāhu-citraḥ |
children.translated_text: symmetrically, the other — wondrous-armed, pillar-conquering, fashioned with gems called <s>puṣparāga</s> (topaz);

children.text: tatrādiḥ śrīla-nīlac-chavi-nikaṣa-duraḥsvarṇa-rekhā-pavitraḥ
children.translated_text: therein, the first — sanctified by the gold-streak of the touchstone of beautiful dark-blue luster on the chest;

children.text: kiṃ cānyaś kroḍa-bhāsāśiva-giri-maṇi-bhū-kānti-sampal-lavitraḥ ||GC_2,2.17||
children.translated_text: and moreover, the other — a ladle for the prosperity of the beauty of the inauspicious-mountain-gem-ground of the bosom!' || (GC 2,2.17)
Likewise:

children.text: tathā-
ādyaḥ sāṅgādharāṅga-cchavi-kavi-kavitā-vardhi-nānardhi-yuktas-
children.translated_text: 'The first — endowed with the unsuppressed, manifold poetic-beauty-augmenting radiance of every lower limb;

children.text: tat sadhryaṅ tad vad eva prati-lava-ruciraḥ sarva-vidvadbhir uktaḥ |
children.translated_text: symmetrically, the other — equally beautiful at every moment, said by all the learned;

children.text: tatrādiḥ padma-jidbhyāṃ nija-kaṭaka-varāyeva padbhyāṃ prayuktaḥ
children.translated_text: therein, the first — having employed his feet, which conquer lotuses, as if [giving] the best boon to his own anklet-ornaments;

children.text: kiṃ cānyas tat-sahāyāv iva nija-caraṇau cālayan bhī-prayuktaḥ ||GC_2,2.18||
children.translated_text: and moreover, the other — moving his own feet as if [they were] allies of those [feet], propelled by awe!' || (GC 2,2.18)
Likewise:

children.text:
tathā-
  ādyaḥ sārdrāṅga-nīla-praguṇa-taru-latā-hastatā-śasta-khelas-
  tat-sadhryaṅ kandukārthaṃ kṛtahalatayā śākhayā labdha-melaḥ |
  tatrādiḥ saṅkucad-dhīr avayava-nicaya-vyāptaye k pta-celaḥ
  kiṃ cānyas tasya tadvan milana-kṛti-kṛte vīkṣitāgāmi-velaḥ ||GC_2,2.19|| iti |
kiṃ ca-
śitī sa-taḍid-aṃśukau sad avataṃsa-vāma-śrutī
children.translated_text: 'The two — dark and with lightning-like garments, with beautiful earrings hanging from the left ears,

children.text: puru-prabhava-rohiṇī sukha-sutau balākhyānvitau |
children.translated_text: of abundant prowess, sons giving happiness to <s>Rohiṇī</s>, bearing the name <s>Bala</s> (Strength),

children.text: sa-keli-mita-dhenukau parihṛtānya-janmāspadau
children.translated_text: with sport-companion calves, having left behind the abode of other births —

children.text: dadarśa bala-keśvau kalabhavat sa vatsāntare ||GC_2,2.20||
children.translated_text: he beheld <s>Bala</s> and <s>Keśava</s>, like young elephants amid the calves!' || (GC 2,2.20)
Moreover:

children.text: api ca-
asita-maṇi-suvarṇa-varṇa-vāsaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Of dark-gem and gold-colored garments,

children.text: kaṭi-ghaṭitāmala-śṛṅga-veṇu-saṅgau |
children.translated_text: with bright horns and flutes fastened at their waists,

children.text: kara-dhṛta-paṭu-paṭṭa-śulva-yaṣṭhī
children.translated_text: holding stout copper staffs wrapped with fine cloth —

children.text: musali-harī harataḥ sma cittam asya ||GC_2,2.21||
children.translated_text: <s>Musali</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and <s>Hari</s> were stealing his heart!' || (GC 2,2.21)
And also:

children.text: darśana-mātrataś ca niścalana-phala-yātraḥ kampa-sampat-pātra-śaṅkuvat-pulaka-saṅkula-gātratayā sahasā saha-sāraṃ rathād avatatāra | [18] avatīrya ca vikīryamāṇāṅga-tayā sāṅgam eva praṇanāma | tan-mātra-parimāṇatayā viśaśrāma ca | nija-pitṛvyatāditāyāṃ tu babhrāma | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: And from the mere sight, his journey's fruit being immobilization, his body crowded with horripilation like spikes — a vessel of the treasure of trembling — he suddenly descended from the chariot with all due form. [18] And having descended, with his limbs scattering [in agitation], he prostrated himself fully. And from the measure of that alone, he rested. But he was confused regarding the paternal-uncle relationship [to reveal]. Because:

children.text: prabhāvānubhavī yaḥ syāt prabhāvas tasya kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: 'One who is an experiencer of [another's] influence — [that] influence is the cause

children.text: guru-lāghava-bhāvāya sarvam evānyathānyathā ||GC_2,2.22||
children.translated_text: [of his behavior]; for the purpose of [determining] weightiness and lightness, everything [becomes] otherwise and otherwise.' || (GC 2,2.22)

children.text:
tad evam avirāmaṃ praṇāmam eva prasajati tasmin gavaḥ parāḥ payaḥ sa-vayaḥ-samavāyena duhyantāṃ nīyantāṃ ca tad gṛhān iti nidiśan natīvādara-saṅkaratayā saṅkarṣaṇa-sahāyaḥ kṛpā-pūrataḥ purataḥ saṃhāya sa cāyaṃ siṃhāyamāna-saṃhananaḥ sābhyutthānaṃ karābhyāṃ tam utthāpayāmāsa | [20] sa tu gadgada-gadān na tu sva-nāma gadituṃ
śaśāka |
children.translated_text: Thus, as he was continuously engaged in prostration itself, while directing that the other cows' milk — together with the assembly of those of the same age — be milked and taken to the houses, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — together with <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) as his aide, through the fullness of compassion, and through the mixture of homage and respect — having drawn [<s>Akrūra</s>] before him, he — whose build was like that of a roaring lion — raised him up with his two hands, with rising [respect]. [20] But he (<s>Akrūra</s>), with words choked by tears, was unable to utter even his own name.

children.text: tataś ca pravayaḥ-paśupa-cayeṣu viracita-tat-paricayeṣu tad vyagratā-kātarau tau
children.translated_text: Then, among the groups of senior cowherds who had arranged the acquaintance with him, as those two [brothers] — anxious with the distress of that [encounter] —

children.text: bhrātarau pitṛvyatā-vyavahāram api vismṛtya tam āliṅganenādṛtya nija-nija-pāṇinā tat prāṇī vidhṛtya svālayam evāninyatuḥ | [22] haris tu sad vyavahāraṃ samāharann agrajam eva tatra nijāgresaraṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: forgetting even the protocol of the paternal-uncle relationship, having honored him with an embrace and holding him — that living being — each by his own hand, led him to their own dwelling. [22] But <s>Hari</s>, conducting the proper courtesy, made his elder brother alone go before him as his precursor there.

children.text:
atha sa yāthātathyam ātithya-prathama-bhāgaṃ svāgatādikaṃ prathayitvā sahānu-janmā rohiṇī-janmā rasa-sampanmayaṃ bhojya-pracayaṃa tasmai balayāmāsa | bhukta-vate tu tasmai mukha-vāsanaṃ mukha-vāsa-mukhaṃ sa-sukhaṃ samarpayāmāsa | tad anantaram eva ca śrīmad vraja-rājaṃ prati taṃ bhājayāmasa |
tatra ca-
children.translated_text:
Then he (<s>Nanda</s>), having duly extended the first portion of hospitality — welcome and such — together with his co-born (<s>Balarāma</s>), the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s>, presented to him (<s>Akrūra</s>) a feast rich in flavors. And when he had eaten, he happily offered him mouth-fragrance as the chief among mouth-refreshments. Immediately thereafter, he presented him to the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>.
And there —

children.text: akrūraṃ praṇataṃ milan vraja-patiḥ kaṃsottha-duḥkhaṃ smaran
children.translated_text: Meeting <s>Akrūra</s> who bowed down, the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, remembering the suffering caused by <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: sāsrāśīr-vacasākhila-klama-haraṃ yad yad guṇais tuṣṭuve |
children.translated_text: praised him with tearful words of blessing, removing all fatigue, with [his] virtues;

children.text: sāralye'py alam asya tādṛśi manaḥ-krauryaṃ tadīyaṃ smarac
children.translated_text: [yet] even while remembering his sincerity, recalling that one's (<s>Kaṃsa's</s>) cruelty of mind,

children.text: cittaṃ kṣubhyati jājvalīti mama hā bhaṣmībhavaty adya ca ||GC_2,2.23||
children.translated_text: 'My heart is agitated, it blazes — alas! — and today turns to ashes!' ||GC_2,2.23||

children.text:
atha tena viśrāmāyādiṣṭaṃ vāsam āsajya paryaṅkopaviṣṭaṃ sammānitatayā
sukhāviṣṭaṃ punas tābhyāṃ kṛta-jananī-saṃbhṛta-bhojanābhyāṃ saha rahasi niviṣṭam akrūraṃ svayaṃ kṛṣṇas tad darśanataḥ samudbuddha-kaṃsa-vadhādi-tṛṣṇas tad idam iṣṭaṃ papraccha | yatra ca krama-cāturī mādhurībhir iyaṃ sarva-sukha-dhurīṇatāṃ vahati-
children.translated_text: Then, having assigned him a residence for rest, when he was seated on a couch, filled with comfort from being honored, and again in private with those two (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Balarāma</s>) who had partaken of food prepared by their mothers — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, his thirst for the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and such awakened by seeing him, asked this desired [question]. Wherein the skillfulness of sequence carries this sweetness to the foremost position of all happiness —

children.text: kiṃ tāta saumya sukham āgatam atra śaṃ vaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Dear father, O gentle one, have you arrived here happily? Is all well with you?

children.text: kiṃ tatra kaṃsa-hatake na hate cirasya |
children.translated_text: Has that wretch <s>Kaṃsa</s> not been slain after so long?

children.text: tau jīvataḥ kim iva vā pitarāv idānīṃ
children.translated_text: Are those two parents still alive even now?

children.text: kiṃ vā tavāgamana-maṅgala-bījam āsīt ||GC_2,2.24||
children.translated_text: And what was the auspicious seed of your coming?' ||GC_2,2.24||

children.text: athākrūra uvāca-tasya yādava-vīreṣu vairānubandhaḥ khalu bhavatā kṛtānusandha eva; viśeṣatas tu devakī-vivāha-gatāham ārabhya yaḥ sa ca bhavac chravasi sacamāna evāste | mad-vidhas tu tatra vartma-śata-parvikā-stamba-vad eva varvarti | vasudeva-sahodara-deva-bhāga-putraḥ parama-śuddhaḥ sa uddhava-nāmāpi bhavad-viraha-vyādhiḥ pavana-vyādhitayābhidhīyata ity urvarita ivāsti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Akrūra</s> said — 'His enmity toward the <s>Yādava</s> heroes is indeed already investigated by you; but specifically, the one that began from the time of <s>Devakī's</s> wedding, of which I was the starting point — that too remains ringing in your ears. One such as myself merely whirls about there like a hundred-jointed stalk on the roadside. <s>Uddhava</s> by name — the son of <s>Devabhāga</s>, brother of <s>Vasudeva</s>, supremely pure — he too, afflicted by the disease of separation from you, is called one afflicted by the wind-disease (<s>pavana-vyādhi</s>), and remains as if a remnant.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-tad etad api jñāyate | sāmpratas tu sapratīkaṃ kathyatām |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'This too is known. But now, tell it with specific details!'

children.text: akrūras tu parito nirīkṣya tad idaṃ sūkṣmākṣaram uvāca-atha śrī-nāradas tu tvādṛśi vijaya-sukha-sāradas tadṛśi durjanma-pārada iti sa tava vraja-premāvṛtasya tasya ca bhayenāstṛtasya yuyutsāyām utsāhanāya devakyāḥ saptamāṣṭama-garbhatayā yuvām anucitam iva sūcitavān |
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s>, looking around carefully, spoke these words in a low voice — 'Now, Śrī <s>Nārada</s> — who is like autumn in your joy of victory and like mercury in the evil-born's [destruction] — he, in order to inspire zeal for battle in you who are enveloped in love for <s>Vraja</s> and in him (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) who is covered with fear, indicated somewhat improperly [the news of] the seventh and eighth pregnancies of <s>Devakī</s> as being you two.'

children.text: ādau devakyā garbhaḥ khalu rohiṇyāṃ māyayā labdha-sandarbhaḥ kṛtaḥ śrī-vasudevaḥ punas tāṃ māyām api yaśodāyāṃ labdha-sambhavāṃ vijñāya devakyāḥ sambhūtaṃ tvāṃ tat-paryaṅke nidhāya tāṃ tasyāṃ labdha-sambhavāṃ cakāra iti |
children.translated_text: 'First, the embryo of <s>Devakī</s> was transferred to <s>Rohiṇī</s> through <s>Māyā</s>, having found opportunity. Then <s>Vasudeva</s>, knowing that <s>Māyā</s> too had found birth in <s>Yaśodā</s>, placed you — born of <s>Devakī</s> — on her (<s>Yaśodā's</s>) couch, and transferred her (<s>Māyā</s>), who had found birth in her (<s>Yaśodā</s>), [to <s>Devakī</s>].'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-mamedam āścaryam iva bhāti |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'This appears to me as if a wonder!'

children.text: akrūra uvāca-śrīmad ānakadundhubhi-mukhād apy advandībhavann aham anena saphalita-karṇa-dvandī-bhavann asmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s> said — 'Even from the mouth of the glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), though I did not become one who doubts, I have become one whose pair of ears has been made fruitful by this.'

children.text:
atha śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ kṣaṇaṃ vilakṣya iva nirīkṣya sahasā tad idam antaś cintitam avāpa-āṃ āṃ tad idam alupta-jñānasyāpi mama vraja-snehāveśa-vaśāt purataḥ sphurannāsīt; samprati tu vismṛta-svapnavannimittaṃ prāpya sphurati sma-[BhP 10.8.15,14] bahūni santi rūpāṇi nāmāni ca sutasya te iti, prāg ayaṃ vasudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ iti ca vrajāvitāraṃ śrīmat-pitaraṃ
prati garga-siddhānta-vargam ete na paryālocitavantaḥ santi |
children.translated_text: Then Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, gazing as if perplexed for a moment, suddenly attained this inner thought — 'Ah, ah! This very thing, though my knowledge is unobstructed, was not manifesting before me due to being overpowered by the force of love for <s>Vraja</s>; but now, having obtained a cause like a forgotten dream, it manifests — [BhP 10.8.15,14] "Many are your son's forms and names" and "Previously, this son of yours was born somewhere of <s>Vasudeva</s>" — these pronouncements of <s>Garga's</s> teachings to the glorious father (<s>Nanda</s>) regarding the descent into <s>Vraja</s>, they have not been reflected upon!'

children.text: yat khalu vrajāvitryāṃ śrīman-madīya-savitryāṃ labdha-jaṭhara-vāsayā māyayā saha dvi-bhujatayā labdha-hṛt-kamala-vāsasya mama śrī-devakyā hṛdaya-sambhavad-udayamad-rūpa-viśeṣa-caturbhuja-rūpācchādana-prārthanāyāṃ tatra sañcāraḥ sampanna ityasyāpratipannatayā tan-mātra-pratītim agatavantaḥ |bhavatu, mayā tu pitṛvyatāyāḥ pitṛtāyāś cānusartavyatayā kartavya eva tayor uddhāraḥ iti |
children.translated_text: 'For, when <s>Māyā</s>, who had obtained a dwelling in the womb of the glorious mother of <s>Vraja</s>, together with my two-armed form which had obtained a dwelling in her lotus-heart — [at the time of] the prayer of Śrī <s>Devakī</s> for the concealment of the special four-armed form arising and shining from her heart — the transfer there was accomplished. Due to the incomprehensibility of this, they have arrived at only a partial understanding. So be it — but by me, since the duty of rescuing those two (<s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>) must be pursued through both the status of nephew and the status of son — their deliverance must indeed be accomplished.'

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ cācaṣṭa-tatas tataḥ ?
children.translated_text: And he spoke plainly — 'Then what? Then what?'

children.text: akrūra uvāca-tataś ca vasudeva-vadha-samudyataṃ tam adhamaṃ sāntvataḥ śamayitvā bhramayitvā ca sa tu kratu-bhug-munir yathāyathaṃ gataḥ | tatra gate tūcchṛṅkhalaḥ kaṃsaḥ kālāyasa-śṛṅkhalayā sanirbandhaṃ tava pitarau babandha iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s> said — 'Then, having pacified that wretch who was prepared for the slaying of <s>Vasudeva</s> — through conciliation, through confusing him — that sage who feeds on sacrificial offerings (<s>Nārada</s>) departed as was appropriate. But when he had departed, the unrestrained <s>Kaṃsa</s>, with iron chains, bound your parents firmly with bonds!'

children.text: atha bhrātarāv ubhāv api sāsrāv aśrāvayatām-tarhi kiṃ pitror eva sandeśa-praveśāya bhavad āyātaṃ jātam?
children.translated_text: Then the two brothers, both tearful, made him speak — 'Then has your coming been occasioned merely for the conveyance of a message from the parents?'

children.text: akrūraḥ sa-lajjam uvāca-nahi nahi | kintu kaṃsasya tau khalu nija-yātanām api sahete | na khalu bhavac chravasi ca tat-pātanām, kintu tad idam aham eva nivedayāmi-
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s> said with embarrassment — 'No, no! But those two (<s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>) endure even their own torment. They would not cast their suffering into your ears. But this I myself report —

children.text:
bhavadbhyāṃ yadi jātābhyāṃ gatābhyāṃ yogyatām api |
  pitrārtir na nivarteta putrīyā kutra vartatām ||GC_2,2.25|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'If, even when you two, having been born and having attained capability,
the parents' suffering does not cease — then where does filial [duty] stand?' ||GC_2,2.25|| — thus.'

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇas tu tatrodvegaṃ hṛdi nigūhya sāvajñam uvāca-kaṃsaḥ kiṃ nāma śaśaṃsa ?
[38] akrūra uvāca-śaṃsanaṃ tasya kati pratiśaṃsāni | tātparyaṃ tu paryag idam eva paryavasīyatām-bhūta-rāja-dhanur-maha-vyājataḥ sva-samājaṃ sāhāyyam ānāyya durmantraṇayāsmān pratārya tat-kutūhala-kalanāya prajāntaravad bhavantāv api nija-vrajavantāv asmad-dvāraivājuhāva yad-arthaṃ tad eva iti |
children.translated_text:
Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, concealing his inner distress, said with disdain — 'What exactly did <s>Kaṃsa</s> declare?'
[38] <s>Akrūra</s> said — 'How many counter-declarations to his declarations! But the purport ultimately comes to rest in just this — on the pretext of the great bow-festival of the lord of the <s>Bhūtas</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), having summoned his own assembly and allies through wicked counsel, deceiving us, for the sake of satisfying his curiosity — like ordinary subjects — he has invited even you two, who have your own <s>Vraja</s>, through our agency alone — for that very purpose.'

children.text:
rāmaḥ sa-sahāsam āha sma-bṛṃhita-kṣudhi siṃhe matta-mataṅgaja-bṛṃhitaṃ
khalv idam |
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> said with a laugh — 'This is indeed the trumpeting of a maddened elephant before a lion whose hunger is aroused!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-bhavatu, vayam api samāgamya tam api valim arpayitvā bhūteśaṃ tarpayiṣyāmaḥ | kintu, tad bhūta-rāja-sabhā-janaṃ kadā ?
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'So be it! We too, having arrived and offering that oblation to him, shall gratify the lord of <s>Bhūtas</s>. But when is that assembly-festival of the lord of <s>Bhūtas</s>?'

children.text: akrūra uvāca-caturdaśyām iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s> said — 'On the fourteenth day (<s>caturdaśī</s>).'

children.text: tad evaṃ śeṣaṃ viśeṣam api pṛṣṭa-veṣaṃ vidhāya śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ prāha-vicārād asmākaṃ parama-maṅgalam eva yasmād idaṃ tasmāc chrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇeṣu gocaram ācarāma |
children.translated_text: Thus, having inquired into the remaining particulars in disguised form, Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'Since from deliberation this is supremely auspicious for us, therefore let us bring it within the purview of the feet of the glorious father.'

children.text: tad evam uktvā taṃ tasminn eva muktvā sa rāmas tata utthāya pitṛ-parisaram ājagāma | atha tad-ādeśād upaveśanānantaraṃ tena vīkṣita-mukha-kañjaḥ samañjad añjali vacasā tad idaṃ vyañjayāmāsa-tāta! maṅgala-vṛttaṃ kim api vṛttam asti, kintu yugapad eva parveva sarvebhyaḥ śrāvayitavyam |
children.translated_text: Having said this and leaving him (<s>Akrūra</s>) right there, he and <s>Rāma</s> arose and came to their father's vicinity. Then, by his (<s>Nanda's</s>) command, after being seated, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose lotus-face was beheld by him, harmoniously disclosed this with palms-joined words — 'Father! Some auspicious event has occurred, but it must be announced simultaneously to all, like a festival.'

children.text:
atha vraja-rājaḥ sandeha-mandehatayā sānandam ivopanandādīnān āyayāmāsa | yatra
ca kiñcid api vihitāpidhāna-vidhānāḥ śrī-vrajeśvarī-pradhānā labdhānusandhānā
jātāḥ | tataḥ sukham upaviṣṭeṣu teṣu śiṣṭeṣu śrī-viṣṭara-śravāḥ kiñcid vihasann ivācaṣṭa-asmān prati samprati bhoja-kṣiti-bhṛd-iṣṭa sandiṣṭavān asti | yat prajā-nibhāḥ prajā yūyam iha maheśa-dhanur mahāmahe saheśāḥ saha-śāvakāḥ sāvakāśam āgacchata | viśeṣatas tu nija-vīryataḥ samīryamāṇa-nija-darśana-tṛṣṇau rāma-kṛṣṇau
ca iti |
children.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, with the hesitancy of <s>Mandehā</s> (the demons of doubt), as if joyfully, summoned <s>Upananda</s> and the others. Wherein the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s>, the foremost, and others, having made arrangements of a certain concealment, obtained awareness [of the proceedings]. Then, when those dignified ones were comfortably seated, the glorious one of renowned fame (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), as if smiling slightly, declared — 'The lord of the <s>Bhoja</s> land has sent a command to us. That you, the subjects, who are like [his] subjects, should come at ease, together with your young ones, to the great festival of the bow of the great lord (<s>Śiva</s>). And specifically, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose desire for beholding [you two] is being stirred by his own valor — [he wishes them to come].'

children.text: vraja-rāja uvāca-bhavan mana idaṃ kiṃ manute; yad bhavati vasudevād bhavati cāsmiṃs tasya prītir bhavati iti |
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Vraja</s> said — 'What does your mind think about this? For what comes from <s>Vasudeva</s> — does his affection come into this?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ sa-smitam uvāca-yady anyathā syāt tathāpi vṛthā-patha eva tan manorathaḥ | yad bhavat-prabhāva-bala-saṃhitasya mama kaḥ khalv ahitam āhitaṃ kurvīta | [47] yata eva khalv ābalya-valyamāne bālye'pi mama pūtanādayas te dhūtatām āpannāḥ | kim uta tad-valataḥ eva valitāṃ valamānābhyāṃ baka-vatsaka-mukhānāṃ sukhād eva pratiritsanaṃ jātam iti |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile — 'Even if it were otherwise, that wish would be but a futile path. For who indeed could do harm to me, who am endowed with the power and might of your majesty? [47] Since even in childhood, when I was being tossed about by infancy, those <s>Pūtanā</s> and others were reduced to dust! How much more — from their very strength, the easy repelling of <s>Baka</s>, <s>Vatsaka</s>, and the rest was accomplished by us two who had grown and were growing.'

children.text: tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And there —

children.text: baka ekaṅgilas tāvad aghaḥ sarvaṅgilaḥ sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Baka</s> was a single-limbed one; <s>Agha</s> stood as an all-limbed one;

children.text: indraḥ sarvaṅkaṣas teṣu kaṃsakaḥ kaṃ samīyati ? ||GC_2,2.26||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> was an all-scratching one — among these, whom will poor <s>Kaṃsa</s> approach?' ||GC_2,2.26||

children.text: tad etan niśamya mitho niśāmya ca samyag-pratipatti-parāhateṣu teṣu mātrādiṣu ca kṛta-yātrā-bhaṅga-prāṇāliṣu punar uvāca-go-koṭibhir ghaṭita-koṭīnām asmākam anyasmin naṭitum api ghaṭanā na dṛśyate | rājñām ājñām atikramyāpayāne ca tad-āgamana-mayaṃ bhayaṃ bhavaty eva; kim uta sthāne | tataḥ saṅkocaṃ vinā tatrāsmad gamanam eva tasya śamanam upalabhāmahe |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this, looking at each other — when those mothers and others, whose resolve was struck by proper understanding, had their departure-breaking vital breaths [stifled] — he spoke again — 'For us whose millions of cows constitute millions [of wealth], the opportunity to perform elsewhere is not seen. And in transgressing the king's command, the fear constituted of his coming exists indeed; how much more so in staying. Therefore, without hesitation, we perceive our going there alone as his pacification.'

children.text: tad etad ākarṇya sa-vaivarṇyam upanandaṃ prati śrīmān nandaḥ prāha sma-kiṃ kartavyam ? iti |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the glorious <s>Nanda</s> spoke to <s>Upananda</s> with a change of complexion — 'What is to be done?'

children.text: sa covāca-tatra gamyam iti samyag evāha vatsaḥ | agatir nāma kāmaṃ tasya krodham asya ca bhayaṃ bodhayati | gatis tu taṃ tad apy apagamayati | kiṃ ca, yad-apūrvam apūrvaṃ pūrvam api rakṣāṃ kurvad āsīt tad eva sarvam arvāñcam apy āpa dvāraṃ tārayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: And he said — 'The boy speaks rightly that one should go there. Not going merely awakens his (<s>Kaṃsa's</s>) anger and fear of this one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). But going removes even that. Moreover, that which previously — unprecedented — was protecting [us] even before, that very all-encompassing [power] shall carry even the most recent [affairs] across the doorway.'

children.text: atha tad evaṃ yuktiṃ valayati gopāla-valaye prabhāva-bhāva-pūrṇa-pūrṇimā ca tūrṇam eva tatrāgatā |
children.translated_text: Thus, while this reasoning was revolving in the circle of cowherds, the full-moon lady (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>), full of the mood of influence, arrived there swiftly.

children.text: tataś ca vraja-rājena kṛte praśne sā sa-sneham uvāca-bhavan-nandanasya mathurā-prayāṇe sarvānanda eva syāt | kaṃsādayaḥ sarva eva nṛśaṃsā dhvaṃsāya sampatsyante, kintu vrajāgatāv asya vilamba-saṃvalanaṃ paśyāma iti yathā-yuktam adhyavasyantu |
children.translated_text: Then, when the lord of <s>Vraja</s> posed the question, she said with affection — 'In the journey of your son to <s>Mathurā</s>, there shall be nothing but complete bliss. <s>Kaṃsa</s> and all the others, all the cruel ones, shall meet their destruction. But we see that in his return from <s>Vraja</s> there shall be entanglement with delay — therefore let them resolve as is fitting.'

children.text: upananda uvāca-avilambāgamanam api śreya eva vairi-śamanaṃ tu yadi syād iti gamanam eva varaṃ ramaṇīyam | tataḥ sarve'pi gaty-antaram asaṅgatya saṅgatam idam ucyata iti procya kiñcid apy ananuśocya śrīman mukhaṃ vilocya śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ praśna-viṣayaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | tatra gantavyatā kadā mantavyā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Upananda</s> said — 'Even a speedy return would be auspicious, but if the pacification of the enemy occurs, then going itself is the delightful best course.' Then all, finding no other course, saying 'this is fitting,' without grieving even slightly, gazing upon the glorious face of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, made him the subject of their question — 'When should the departure be considered?'

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-gatiṃ ca prātas trayodaśyāṃ yukti-vaśyāṃ paśyāmaḥ, caturdaśyāṃ khalu mahas tan-mahanīyatām āpsyati |
[54] tad evaṃ svāntaḥ-paridevane'ham eva iha paśyati vraja-naradeve sarve'py ūcuḥ-sarvaṃ ghoṣam anughoṣanā sadya evāsādyatām, yathā prātar eva gopāḥ sopāyanā rāja-sabhām abhiyānti iti |
children.translated_text:
Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'We see the departure on the morning of the thirteenth day as amenable to reason; on the fourteenth, that great festival shall attain its greatness.'
[54] Thus, when he who alone sees the inner lamentation — the divine lord of <s>Vraja</s> — all said — 'Let the proclamation to the entire cow-settlement be made at once, so that the cowherds, bearing gifts, set forth to the king's assembly by the very morning!'

children.text: atha śrīman-nandarājaś ca samājaṃ vyājahāra-bhagavatyā sanmate bhavatāṃ mate sarvam eva maṅgalam saṅgaṃsyat iti bhadram ādiśyantām, diśyā diśyā gopāḥ prābhṛta-prabhṛti-kṛte |
children.translated_text: Then the glorious king <s>Nanda</s> addressed the assembly — 'By the consent of the blessed lady (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) and in the opinion of you all, everything shall be auspicious — let blessings be pronounced! By good fortune, by good fortune — let the cowherds prepare gifts and offerings!'

children.text: tad evaṃ labdhānumatir vṛndāvana-patir nija-paricārakān ādideśa-kathyatām idam uttāraṃ kṣttāraṃ prati iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, having obtained consent, the lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> instructed his attendants — 'Let this be announced throughout the settlement!'

children.text: tad evaṃ vijñāya vraja-rājñī tu mohenājñībhavantī na kiñcid api vaktuṃ vyaktuṃ vā śaśāka iti vadan madhukaṇṭhaś ca niruddha-kaṇṭhas tadvad eva āsīt |
children.translated_text: Thus, learning this, the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, becoming unconscious from grief, was unable to say or express anything at all — so saying, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> too became choked with emotion and fell into just such a state.

children.text: atha kathāyāḥ sabhāyām api tadvad eva mohaṃ gacchati sa-samāje vraja-rāje tasya caraṇa-rājīva-yugaṃ yugapad gṛhnan vraja-yuvarājaḥ punas tam ājīvayann uvāca-tāta ! kathaṃ kātarāyase ? yathā-pūrvaṃ kathā-mātraṃ khalv idam, so'yam ahaṃ punar bhavad-anudhyāna-ramyatayā kaṃsaṃ nirdamya cirāt purāgamya bhavad-dṛṣṭi-pathānuvartī-bhavann evāsmīti |
children.translated_text: Now, in the narrative, when the king of <s>Vraja</s> too, together with the assembly, was similarly falling into a swoon, the prince of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), simultaneously grasping the pair of lotus-feet of that one, reviving him again, said: 'Father! Why do you become faint-hearted? This is merely a story, as before. Here I am — and by the delight of meditating upon you, having subdued <s>Kaṃsa</s>, having come back to the city after a long time, I am indeed becoming one who follows the path of your sight!'

children.text: tataḥ sa-pulaka-pālitam aṅkaṃ pālayati vraja-bhūpāle sarva evākharvam ānanda-garvam uvāheti kathāyāṃ śānta-prathāyāṃ madhukaṇṭha uvāca-
children.translated_text: Then, as the king of <s>Vraja</s> protected his horripilation-guarded lap, all indeed bore undiminished pride of bliss — and when the story had reached its peaceful conclusion, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said:

children.text: kutra vā ramatāṃ putras tavānyatra vrajādhipa |
children.translated_text: 'Where else would your son find delight, O lord of <s>Vraja</s>, other than [here]?

children.text: bhaktānukampā-sampātī paśya te vaśya eva saḥ ||GC_2,2.27||
children.translated_text: He who falls [at your feet] out of compassion for his devotees — see, he is indeed under your sway!' ||2.2.27||

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇa-kṛta-mahasi rādhā-sadasi ca rātri-kathāyāṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ sa-gadgadam uvāca-ayi samprati śrī-mādhavena hṛta-viraha-bādhe ! śrī-rādhe ! purā vṛttam avadhīyatām-
children.translated_text: Now, in the nighttime narrative within the assembly of <s>Rādhā</s>, accomplished by Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said with a choked voice: 'O you whose affliction of separation has been stolen away by Śrī <s>Mādhava</s>! Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>! Let what happened before be attended to —'

children.text: sphūrjathu-pratimam ūrjitaṃ tadā
ghoṣaṇaṃ sapadi ghoṣam anvabhūt
children.translated_text: proclamation suddenly pervaded the cow-settlement,

children.text: yad babhūvur aparāḥ parāhatā
children.translated_text: by which the others were struck down

children.text: hā hatā iva ca rādhikādikāḥ ||GC_2,2.28||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rādhikā</s> and the rest became as if slain — alas, slain!' ||2.2.28||
'A thunderbolt-like, vehement

children.text: tathā sati-
children.translated_text: That being so —

children.text: kāścin mlānānanās tac-chravaṇa-dahanaja-jvālayā kāścanāsan
children.translated_text: 'Some had withered faces from the flame born of the fire of hearing that [news]; some

children.text: kṣīṇāṅga-srasta-veṣā jaḍa-nibha-vapuṣaḥ kāś ca kāścid vicittāḥ |
children.translated_text: had wasted limbs, fallen garments, and bodies like those of the insensible; and some were distracted.

children.text: tā etāḥ kena varṇyāḥ ya iha nija-hṛdi spṛṣṭa-tad-bhāva-kaṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: These — by whom could they be described? He who here has touched in his own heart the anguish of that emotion —

children.text: kiṃ vā tat-spṛṣṭi-śūnyaḥ sa ca sa ca yad alaṃ jāḍyam eva prayāti ||GC_2,2.29||
children.translated_text: or indeed he who is devoid of the touch of that [emotion] — both he and he alike merely attain stupefaction!' ||2.2.29||

children.text: atha niśi ramaṇīnāṃ mūrcchanaṃ nirmame yā
children.translated_text: 'Now, that very proclamation which at night produced the swooning of the beautiful women

children.text: cid-udayam api kalye ghoṣaṇā saiva cakre |
children.translated_text: also brought about the awakening of consciousness in the morning.

children.text: vapuṣi dahana-tapte bheṣajaṃ tena taptir
children.translated_text: For a body burned by fire, the remedy is [more] heat;

children.text: viṣam api viṣa-duṣṭe śreṣṭham iṣṭaṃ bhiṣagbhiḥ ||GC_2,2.30||
children.translated_text: even poison, for one afflicted by poison, is deemed the best [cure] by physicians!' ||2.2.30||

children.text: labdha-cetanānaṃ cāsāṃ kaṃsād aśaṅkāyām api prastutātaṅkāyāṃ devatā-kalitam iva rakṣaṇāya phalitaṃ kiñcid anyad idaṃ-bhāva-prabhāva-cetitaṃ paurṇamāsyā ca purato niścitīkṛtaṃ cetasi sphurati sma |
children.translated_text: And for those who had regained consciousness, even though there was no fear from <s>Kaṃsa</s>, in the present distress, something else — as if arranged by a deity — bore fruit for their protection: a conviction grasped by the power of their <s>bhāva</s> (emotional devotion), and previously confirmed in their minds by <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, shone forth:

children.text:
yasminn aghaḥ kāliya-kādraveyaḥ
  keśī tathāriṣṭa-vṛṣaś ca naṣṭaḥ |
  kaṃsaś ca tasmin mṛta eva sa syān
  na tatra śaṅkā-lavako'pi bhāti ||GC_2,2.31|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'He by whom <s>Agha</s>, <s>Kāliya</s> the serpent-son of <s>Kadrū</s>,
<s>Keśī</s>, and likewise the bull <s>Ariṣṭa</s> were destroyed —
<s>Kaṃsa</s> too shall surely be dead at his hands;
not even a trace of doubt shines there!' ||2.2.31|| — thus.

children.text: tad evaṃ viśvasya saṃmataṃ viśvasya punaś cintayati sma-
children.translated_text: Thus, having trusted and having resolved, they reflected again —

children.text: bakī-ripoḥ kaṃsa-jaye'pi siddhe
children.translated_text: 'Even when the victory over <s>Kaṃsa</s> by the enemy of <s>Bakī</s> (<s>Pūtanā</s>) is accomplished,

children.text: śaṅkemahi svārtha-vinaṣṭim etām |
children.translated_text: we should fear this destruction of our own interests:

children.text: bhaved asau yādava-rājadhānyāṃ
children.translated_text: he would become king in the <s>Yādava</s> capital —

children.text: rājeti goṣṭhe katham atra tiṣṭhet ? ||GC_2,2.32||
children.translated_text: so how would he remain here in the cow-settlement?' ||2.2.32||

children.text: grāmīṇā vayam iha gopa-varga-kanyā
nāgaryaḥ puram anu santi rāja-putryaḥ
children.translated_text: the city-dwellers are royal princesses following the city.

children.text: kṛṣṇas tu grahila-manā guṇeṣu tasmād
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is one whose mind is captivated by virtues — therefore,

children.text: asyāntaḥ katham iva naḥ pratismṛtiḥ syāt ? ||GC_2,2.33||
children.translated_text: how indeed could there be remembrance of us in his heart?' ||2.2.33||
'We are village folk here, daughters of the cowherd class;

children.text: nimeṣaḥ kalpaḥ syād yad apakalane yasya vipine
children.translated_text: 'A moment would become a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) in his absence from the forest;

children.text: gatau yat kṛcchraṃ tat kalayati na ātmā na tu paraḥ |
children.translated_text: the suffering of his departure — neither the self nor another can reckon it.

children.text: madhoḥ pūryāṃ tasya vrajanam atha rājyāya yad idaṃ
children.translated_text: Now, this going of him to <s>Madhupurī</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>) for kingship —

children.text: kathaṃ tad vāsmākaṃ bata kim api dhairyaṃ kalayatu ? ||GC_2,2.34||
children.translated_text: how could any patience whatsoever of ours reckon with that?' ||2.2.34||

children.text: asmākaṃ rāga-jātir vata laṣati na naḥ śarma tasyāpi rājyaṃ
kintv ekānta-stham icchaty anulavam api taṃ sevituṃ prāṇa-kāntam
children.translated_text: but it desires solely to serve him, the beloved of our lives, in solitude.

children.text: ātmāpy antardhiyā tad-dṛg-amṛta-virahaṃ mīnavac chaṅkamānas
children.translated_text: The self too, inwardly fearing separation from the nectar of his gaze, like a fish [fearing waterlessness],

children.text: tat prāg evāti śuṣyan gaṇayati na paraṃ nāparaṃ kiñcanātra ||GC_2,2.35||
children.translated_text: therefore, already drying up even before [the separation], counts neither the other nor anything else here!' ||2.2.35||
'Our inborn passion, alas, does not desire our own happiness, nor his kingship;

children.text: hā tasya smita-cāru-vaktra-valayaṃ khelāñci-netrāñcalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Alas! The circle of his smile-lovely face, the playfully arched corner of his eyes,

children.text: cittānanda-vidhāyi-gīr-vilasitaṃ līlākulaṃ lokanam |
children.translated_text: the delight of his speech that bestows bliss upon the mind, his glance agitated with <s>līlā</s> (playfulness) —

children.text: sākṣāt-kṛtya na jātu tat tad upamāṃ cāsoḍha yā vighna-dhīs
children.translated_text: she who, having directly perceived all that, and having endured its loss, with her mind [set upon] obstacles,

children.text: tyāgārtiṃ yadi sā saheta garalaṃ tatrāmṛtaṃ vetti na ||GC_2,2.36||
children.translated_text: if she could bear the agony of renunciation — she [truly] does not know poison from nectar there!' ||2.2.36||

children.text: tad evaṃ cintāturāḥ pūrāya kṛta-yātrṃ śyāma-gātraṃ vilokayituṃ niṣkalaṅkāśaṅkāḥ sarva evābhidravanti sma | yātrā-vidhānaṃ tu prātar abhidhānaṃ yāsyati |
children.translated_text: Thus, anxious with worry, all of them — with suspicions utterly dispelled — ran forth to behold the dark-bodied one who had set out on the journey to the city. The account of the journey's arrangement, however, shall be narrated in the morning.

children.text: tad etad abhidhāya madhukaṇṭhaḥ pratipatti-vipattitaḥ stabdhatāṃ labdhavati mādhave rādhāṃ tu samudyan mūrcchā-bādhāṃ nirīkṣya maṅkṣu punar āha sma-
children.translated_text: Having narrated this, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, [seeing that] <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) had become rigid from the calamity of [emotional] realization, and observing <s>Rādhā</s> being assailed by a rising swoon, quickly spoke again:

children.text: rādhe pūrva-kathā seyaṃ na tu sāmpratikī sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s>! This is the former story, not the present state of affairs!

children.text: paśya tvad-vacanaṃ mlānaṃ paśyan mlāyati so'py asau ||GC_2,2.37||
children.translated_text: See, your [present] speech is languid — and seeing [your languor], even he becomes languid!' ||2.2.37||

children.text: tad evaṃ kṣudhi bhojanam iva tad ante saṃyoga-rasam eva pariveṣya sarvān api sukhena viśeṣya kathaka-yugalaṃ nijāvāsaṃ samāsasāda | śrī-rādhā-mādhavau ca nija-mohana-mandiram iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, at the end, having served the <s>rasa</s> of union like food at a time of hunger, and having particularly delighted everyone with happiness, the pair of narrators returned to their own abodes. And Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> [went] to their own enchanting pavilion.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrīmad uttara-gopāla-campūm anu
akrūra-krūratā-pūraṇaṃ nāma
dvitīyaṃ pūraṇam
||2||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Uttara-Gopāla-campū</s>,
the second <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Fulfillment of <s>Akrūra's</s> Cruelty.'
||2||

children.text: atha tṛtīyaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, the third <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter),

children.text: śrī-mathurā-pura-prasthānam
children.translated_text: 'The Departure for the Glorious City of <s>Mathurā</s>.'

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇa-kṛtam ahasi śrī-vraja-rāja-sadasi prātaḥ-kathāyāṃ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca- ayi! śrī-vraja-rāja! rājamāna-śrī-hari-mukha-ruci-virājamāna! punar imam itihāsam avabhāsayāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, in the morning narrative within the assembly of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>, accomplished by Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'O glorious king of <s>Vraja</s>! You who shine with the radiance of the glorious <s>Hari's</s> face shining forth! Let us illuminate this <s>itihāsa</s> (narrative) once more!'

children.text:
atha rātrāv avaśiṣṭa-svalpa-mātrāyāṃ yātrā-mātrāyām api pātrācita-gātrāyāṃ rāma-bhrātrā racitena pūtanādi-vadhācaritena sambaddhā virudāvalyaḥ prābalyataḥ stutikṛtdbhiḥ prastutim āpitāḥ sarvān eva garvād utsāhayāmāsuḥ | vartatāṃ tāvad anyeṣāṃ vārtā, yatra tat-pitarau ca kaṃsa-dhvaṃsanam api siddham iti matvā nanditarau vandibhyaḥ kṛta-bahu-dhana-vitarau
babhūvatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, when only a small portion of the night remained — at the mere commencement of the journey — when their bodies were adorned for the occasion, garlands of laudatory verses connected with the exploits of <s>Pūtanā</s> and other slayings composed by the elder brother <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) were powerfully brought forward by the panegyrists and filled everyone with enthusiasm born of pride. Let the account of the others proceed — where those two parents, having reckoned that the destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s> too was as good as accomplished, becoming overjoyed, bestowed abundant wealth upon the bards,

children.text: śrī-vrajeśa-gṛhiṇī-gatiṃ gatā
children.translated_text: 'She who attained the status of the queen of the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: rohiṇī na pṛthag atra varṇyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> is not described separately here.

children.text: pratibimba-ruci-varṇanaṃ punar
children.translated_text: For the description of the radiance of a reflection

children.text: jalpatāṃ bhajati bimba-varṇane ||GC_2,3.1||
children.translated_text: is what those who speak resort to in describing the original image!' ||2.3.1||

children.text: atha prasthāna-stha-maṅgala-velāyām ārabdha-melāyāṃ punas tan-mantraṇāyā yantraṇāya labdha-vaiyagryāveśayor vrajeśayor jyotir-nipuṇāḥ śakuna-jñāna-sad-guṇāś ca dvāri saṅgamya ramya-jana-dvārā tāv ātma-gamanam adhigamayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, at the auspicious hour of departure, when the gathering had begun, the astrologers and those skilled in the knowledge of omens, having assembled at the door through the agency of pleasant people, conveyed to the two lords of <s>Vraja</s> — who had obtained eager involvement for the deliberation of that plan — the [propitious moment for] their own departure.

children.text: anantaram antaḥpura eva tān anantaritān vidhāya tadānīm ucita-dānīya-nidhāna-pātra-pāṇī śapathaṃ samprathayya tau pracchannaṃ papracchatuḥ- sarvam anubhavadbhir bhavadbhiḥ kim avadhīyate? iti |
children.translated_text: Thereupon, having secluded those unobstructed ones within the inner quarters itself, at that time, with hands holding vessels of suitable gifts, having administered oaths, the two asked them privately: 'What do all of you — who have experienced everything — discern?'

children.text: te procuḥ- katham ayaṃ nitānta-sukha-vṛttānta ekāntatayā pṛcchyate? sarveṣāṃ purata eva so'yaṃ puraskartavyaḥ | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: They said: 'Why is this account of unalloyed happiness being asked about privately? This very thing should be proclaimed before everyone! For thus —'

children.text: bhītiṃ mā kurutaṃ vraja-kṣiti-patī yuṣmat-tanūjaḥ sphuṭaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Fear not, O two kings of <s>Vraja</s>! Your son shall clearly

children.text: kaṃsaṃ dhvaṃsa-gataṃ vidhāya bhavitā trailokya-lakṣmī-patiḥ |
children.translated_text: bring <s>Kaṃsa</s> to destruction and become the lord of the prosperity of the three worlds!

children.text: yad vāṃ kīrti-kalāpa-nartita-mukhī śaśvat trilokī bhaved
children.translated_text: Moreover, the three worlds, with mouths set dancing by the array of your glory, shall become eternal;

children.text: vedaḥ pañcama-veda-tantra-sahitaḥ sākṣitvam atrāpsyati ||GC_2,3.2||
children.translated_text: the <s>Veda</s>, together with the fifth <s>Veda</s> (<s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>) and the <s>Tantras</s>, shall attain testimony therein!' ||2.3.2||

children.text: atha tebhyaś ca bahvīm aṃhati-saṃhatiṃ vidhāya hṛdi sukhaṃ nidhāya śaraṇatayā dhyāta-nārayaṇa-caraṇayor anayoḥ parivārita-bhṛtyau kṛta-prātaḥ-kṛtyau tāv etau sakhi-sametau nikāma-bhīṣi tad-anujau rāma-rāmānujau samājam ājagmatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, having bestowed upon those [priests] an abundant collection of gifts, having placed happiness in their hearts, having meditated upon the feet of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as their refuge — these two, surrounded by servants, having performed the morning rites, accompanied by companions, filled with overwhelming reverence, those two younger brothers of that elder — <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — arrived at the assembly.

children.text: samāgamya ca tayoḥ rohiṇī-sahitayoḥ padāravindāni vanditvā tad-aṅka-pāli-saṅga-śālitayā ciraṃ nayanayoḥ syanditvā sthitayor etayor eka-dvādi-krameṇa śatātikrameṇa sarve'py antaraṅgā labdha-sambhrama-taraṅgās tad-antaḥ-puram āgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: And having come together, having bowed to the lotus-feet of those two together with <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and having remained long [in their laps] by virtue of the embrace of their laps, shedding tears from their eyes — when these two had stood thus, one by one and in sequence surpassing a hundred, all the intimate ones too, having obtained waves of eager haste, arrived at that inner quarter.

children.text: ]8] atha madraṅkara-dīpa-bhadra-nipādīnāṃ madhya-madhyāsīnayoḥ sārdra-nayanayor anayor vikasad-vadanāmbujayor agrajānujayoḥ sarvataḥ kharva-vicāratayā sthiteṣu sarveṣu sa punar akrūraḥ krūras tad etad bahiḥ-pradeśataḥ sandideśa- sarva-maṅgala-saṅgataṃ katham etal lagnaṃ samyag na yātrā-lagnaṃ kriyate iti |
children.translated_text: [8] Now, when these two — the elder and younger brothers — with moist eyes and blossoming lotus-faces, were seated in the midst of <s>Madraṅkara</s>, <s>Dīpabhadra</s>, <s>Nipāda</s> and others, while everyone stood around in a state of stunted deliberation, that cruel <s>Akrūra</s> again dispatched this message from the outer grounds: 'Why is this auspicious conjunction not being properly made into the auspicious moment of departure?'

children.text:
tataś ca tāv imau śūrāṇām agrimau kaṃsa-ghātāya labdha-tṛṣṇau rāma-kṛṣṇau citrāyamāṇānāṃ pitrādīnāṃ caraṇa-vandanāyānandanāya ca madhuraṃ vidhuratā-vidhunanam api gadantau gadgada-varṇa-rāśibhir āśīr anugām anujñām ādāya prasādāyasampadā yadā tat-sthānāt prasthānāya padāravindaṃ dadānāv adṛśyetāṃ tadā tadādīnāṃ san-madālibhiḥ samam advandvatāṃ vindad divya-dundubhi-
dvandva-vṛnda-vādyam aśeṣābhivādyatayā samullalāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, these two — the foremost of heroes, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who had obtained the eager desire for the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — as their parents and others became agitated, bowing at their feet and saying sweet words that also dispelled their distress, receiving with choking streams of syllables the blessings and permission that followed — when they were seen placing their lotus-feet for departure from that place, with the grace of benediction, then, together with the bees of righteous joy, the music of the pairs of divine <s>dundubhi</s> drums, attaining non-duality [of purpose], resounded with the quality of being saluted by all.

children.text: tathā ca śrī-kṛṣṇam uddiśya ślokayanti-
children.translated_text: And they compose verses addressing Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:

children.text: kaṃsa-dhvaṃsa-kṛte yadā nija-gṛhāt kṛṣṇena yātrā kṛtā
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> set forth from his own home for the destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: tarhy ārambhata eva dundubhi-śataṃ vṛndārakair vāditam |
children.translated_text: at that very commencement, a hundred <s>dundubhi</s> drums were sounded by the celestials.

children.text: āstām anya-kathā yathā sa ca pitā mātā ca sā cintayā
children.translated_text: Let other talk remain — how even his father and that mother,

children.text: klāntātmāpi mudaṃ samasta-bhavikānandasya mūlaṃ yayau ||GC_2,3.3||
children.translated_text: though exhausted in soul by anxiety, attained joy that was the root of the bliss of all beings!' ||2.3.3||

children.text: atha ratha-sthāne sāneka-vedādi-ghoṣa-maṅgala-poṣaṃ kṛtāgamanayor anayoḥ sarvataḥ sarvam eva gokulam ākulaṃ babhūva | [12] tatra caikataḥ śrī-vraja-rājādayaḥ paratas tu tadīya-jāyādaya iti sthite prasthiter anujñāpanāya paṇāyati paritaḥ kṛtāñjali-sañjane kañja-locane sarve'py ūcuḥ- asmābhir bhavatā prasmārita-sarvaiḥ sarvair api bhavatā samam evāgamanīyam | yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, at the place of the chariot, when these two had arrived amidst the auspicious sounds of the <s>Vedas</s> and other blessings, all of <s>Gokula</s> became agitated on every side. [12] There, on one side were the glorious king of <s>Vraja</s> and others, and on the other their wives — when it was so arranged, for the purpose of requesting permission for departure, when around the lotus-eyed one — with joined palms all around — everyone said: 'We, who have all been reminded [of our bond] by you, should all come along together with you! For —'

children.text: mātā bhastreva seyaṃ baka-śamana tava tvad-vaśa-śvāsa-vargā
children.translated_text: 'This mother, O slayer of <s>Baka</s>, is like a bellows — her breath-host is under your control;

children.text: so'yaṃ tātaś ca tadvat kim aparam akhilaṃ gokulaṃ tādṛg eva |
children.translated_text: and this father too is likewise — and what more, the entire <s>Gokula</s> is just the same!

children.text: sarveṣāṃ śaśvad antar-hṛdi vasasi yatas tvaṃ tatas tvāṃ vinā kiṃ
children.translated_text: Since you dwell perpetually within the inner hearts of all, therefore without you, what

children.text: gehair arthaiḥ śarīrair asubhir api bhavet prāṇināṃ gokulasya ||GC_2,3.4||
children.translated_text: use would there be of homes, wealth, bodies, or even life-breaths for the living beings of <s>Gokula</s>?' ||2.3.4||

children.text: tad evam asra-stambhaṃ lambhayatsu gopa-sabhāsatsu tādṛśa-dṛśā śrī-kamala-dṛśā svayam uktam-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the members of the cowherd assembly were causing tears and paralysis [to arise], by the lotus-eyed Śrī [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] himself with such a gaze, it was said:

children.text: yūyaṃ me prāṇato'pi priyatama-suhṛdo yan-nimittaṃ davāgniṃ
children.translated_text: 'You are my dearest friends, more dear than life itself — on account of whom I deemed the forest-fire

children.text: mene'haṃ pānakābhaṃ tam api giri-varaṃ kanduka-prāyam eva |
children.translated_text: to be like a drink, and that best of mountains (<s>Govardhana</s>) to be like a ball!

children.text: yadyapy etan na yuktaṃ vacasi racayituṃ syād athāpi klamaṃ vaḥ
children.translated_text: Although it is not fitting to fashion this in words, yet, seeing your exhaustion,

children.text: paśyaṃs tat tad yathā prāg akaravam adhunā tadvad eva pravacmi ||GC_2,3.5||
children.translated_text: just as I acted before in those [ways], even now I declare the same!' ||2.3.5||

children.text: kiṃ ca, śrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇānāṃ pratinidhitayā tat-tat-pratividhi-racanāya tad-agraja-yugmaṃ vrajaniṣṭham eva tiṣṭhatāt; aṅga-pratyaṅga-rūpatayā tad anuja-yugman tu saṅgam eva saṅgacchatāt |
children.translated_text: Moreover, as representatives of the feet of the glorious father, let the pair of elder brothers remain stationed firmly in <s>Vraja</s> for the execution of each and every arrangement; and the pair of younger brothers, being in the nature of limbs and subsidiary limbs, let them indeed join [my] company!

children.text: atha tatra tatra yatnatas teṣu yukteṣu yathā-yathaṃ niyukteṣu yathā yathā mātṛ-tad-yātṛ-prabhṛtiṣu pitṛ-bhrātṛja-sva-bhrātṛ-pracitiṣu cānujñāpana-samāpanaṃ tathā tathā varṇanaṃ lupta-varṇa-padatām āpnotīty alam ati-prasaṅgena |
children.translated_text: Now, as those [arrangements] were carefully made and duly appointed here and there — the more the concluding requests for permission were made to the mothers, their attendants, and others, and to the father's nephews and his own brothers — the more the description loses its syllables and words — so enough with excessive digression!

children.text: kintu teṣāṃ kaṃsa-hanane'tivilambaṃ vinā pratyāgamane ca nāsambhāvanāsīd itīdam eva viṣīdan marmatām aticakrāma iti | [17] kathāṃ samāpya snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ punar uvāca-
children.translated_text: But there was no impossibility regarding his return without excessive delay in slaying <s>Kaṃsa</s> — brooding over this very thing, he exceeded the limits of anguish. [17] Having concluded the narrative, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke again:

children.text: yan mayedaṃ purā-vṛttaṃ purā vṛttaṃ pratīyatām |
children.translated_text: 'What was previously enacted by me — let what was formerly done be perceived!

children.text: rājan surāri-hantāyaṃ tava kroḍe murāntakaḥ ||GC_2,3.7||
children.translated_text: O king, this slayer of <s>Mura</s>, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods, is in your lap!' ||3.7||

children.text: tad evam āyati-ramyaṃ niśamya śrī-vraja-rājena ca taṃ parasparāsra-sārdrāṅgatayāliṅgitaṃ niśāmya sarve'py ānanda-garveṇa nija-nija-gamyaṃ jagmuḥ | yadā śrī-vraja-rājñī tam antaraṅga-dvārāhūya bhūyaḥ parirabhya navam iva labhyaṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Thus, hearing this which was beautiful in its promise of the future, and seeing him embraced by the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, their bodies moist with mutual tears, all too, with the pride of joy, went to their respective destinations. Then the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s>, summoning him through the inner door, embracing him again, made [the experience] as if newly obtained.

children.text: atha rātri-kathāyām ārabdha-prathāyāṃ śrī-rādhā-mādhavayor agrataḥ snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca-ayi samprati santata-labdha-kṛṣṇāsañjane tat-kānti-nartita-netra-khañjane sarvādhike śrī-rādhike punar idaṃ purā-vṛttaṃ karṇa-vṛttaṃ kriyatām | athavā tadā ratha-patham āgate sasamāje vraja-yuvarāje tat-preyasīnāṃ vṛttaṃ man-mati-vṛttim ativṛttaṃ kathaṃ kathayituṃ śaknomi ?
children.translated_text: Then, as the night-narrative commenced its course, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke before glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>: 'O you who have now continuously obtained the sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose eye-movement dances with his radiance, O supremely exalted glorious <s>Rādhikā</s> — let this past event again become an event for the ears! Or rather — when the young prince of <s>Vraja</s> set forth upon the chariot-path in that assembly, the conduct of his beloveds exceeded the course of my own mind — how can I narrate it?'

children.text: tathā hi-
children.translated_text: As follows:

children.text: mūrkhatvaṃ nirghṛṇatvaṃ hari-haraṇam iha krauryam akrūra-nāmnā
children.translated_text: 'Foolishness, heartlessness, the theft of <s>Hari</s> — the cruelty of the one named <s>Akrūra</s>,

children.text: sarveṣāṃ buddhi-lopaṃ śakuna-subhagatā-kalpanaṃ cātra kṛtye |
children.translated_text: the deluding of everyone's intellect, and the fabrication of auspiciousness in omens — in this matter,

children.text: dhātuḥ paśyeti śaśvad vikalita-vacasām ārya-goṣṭhī-gatānāṃ
children.translated_text: the condition born of bewilderment in those steadfast ones, members of the noble assembly,

children.text: dhīrāṇām apy amūṣāṃ bhrama-janita-daśā hanta māṃ dandahīti ||GC_2,3.8||
children.translated_text: whose speech was ever broken by the root [meaning] 'to see' — alas, it burns me!' ||3.8||

children.text: nopālabhyo vidhātā sa tu bhavati paras tadvad akrūra-nāmā
children.translated_text: 'The Creator is not to be blamed — he is beyond; likewise the one named <s>Akrūra</s> —

children.text: kintv eṣa prāṇa-nāthaḥ sva-viraha-kṛd upālabhyate nanda-putraḥ |
children.translated_text: but this lord of our lives, <s>Nanda's</s> son, who himself caused the separation, is to be reproached!

children.text: evaṃ tāsāṃ mṛdūṇām api dūta-hṛdaya-jvāla-rūpair vilāpair
children.translated_text: Thus, even of those tender ones, the lamentations in the form of flames in the messenger's heart —

children.text: adyāpi smaryamāṇaiḥ pratipadam api nas tapyate citta-vṛttiḥ ||GC_2,3.9||
children.translated_text: even now, being remembered at every step, our mental state is scorched!' ||3.9||

children.text: ābhir bhāgyaṃ vadhūnāṃ madhu-nagara-bhuvāṃ yan nutaṃ bhāvi-kṛṣṇa-
children.translated_text: 'By these [gopīs], the fortune of the women of <s>Madhupura</s> (Mathurā) was praised —

children.text: prekṣāyāṃ hanta tasmād gatir api ca nijā tatra caiṣīti śaṅke |
children.translated_text: in the prospect of seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — alas, therefore I suspect their own course led there too!

children.text: icchāṃ cāsāṃ mṛdūnāṃ svayam api rahasi prekṣyamāṇe nijāṅge
children.translated_text: And the desire of these tender ones — when their own bodies were being beheld privately by him —

children.text: lajjā-vistāra-bhājām asakṛd ahaha tāṃ cintayitvā dunomi ||GC_2,3.10||
children.translated_text: those who were pervaded by the expanse of modesty — alas, repeatedly pondering that, I am pained!' ||3.10||

children.text: tāsāṃ nāti-pratītiṃ madhu-pura-gamane śrī-hareḥ kurvatīnāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Of those who did not fully believe in glorious <s>Hari's</s> journey to <s>Madhupura</s>,

children.text: vajrāṇāṃ pāta-tulyaḥ śirasi yad abhavat tad rathāroha-jalpaḥ |
children.translated_text: like the fall of thunderbolts upon their heads was that speech of mounting the chariot;

children.text: tasmān nindā kṛtā yad vraja-pati-sadasām apy amūdṛgbhir uccair
children.translated_text: therefore, the reproach that was uttered loudly by such ones even in the assemblies of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: duḥkha-prācuryam etan mama vikalayati svāntam adyāpi hanta ||GC_2,3.11||
children.translated_text: this abundance of suffering confounds my inner being even now, alas!' ||3.11||

children.text: āyāta prāṇa-sakhyo vayam iha nikaṭāḥ koṭayaḥ prāṇa-nāthaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Come, O life-companions! Let us gather here nearby in multitudes around the lord of our lives,

children.text: prītyāvṛttaṃ vitanmaḥ kim iva guru-janā naḥ kariṣyanti nāma |
children.translated_text: and with love enfold him who has returned — what indeed will the elders do to us?

children.text: itthaṃ tās taṃ dravantīr mṛdu-caritavatīr apy alaṃ tīvra-bhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus those tender-mannered ones were running toward him — yet of exceedingly intense emotion —

children.text: kṣiptāś cakrur yad anye tad iha mama balāt prāṇa-ghātaṃ karoti ||GC_2,3.12||
children.translated_text: [but] others flung them aside — that here forcibly deals a death-blow to my life!' ||3.12||

children.text: hā hā sā rāsa-goṣṭhī nava-nava-milanollāsa-śaśvad vilāsā
tal-līlā-kalpa-vallī-samudaya-januṣām aṅkura-śrīḥ kva yātā ?
children.translated_text: the glory of sprouts born from the assemblage of wish-fulfilling creepers of those pastimes — where has it gone?

children.text: hā dhig yākrūra-nāmnā kitava-nṛpatinā dīkṣitā gopa-goṣṭhī
children.translated_text: Alas, shame! The cowherd-assembly that was initiated by the gambler-king named <s>Akrūra</s> —

children.text: seyaṃ tat-sarva-nāśiny ajani kuta iti krośikā māṃ dahanti ||GC_2,3.13||
children.translated_text: this very one became the destroyer of all that — whence [did it arise]? — the outcry burns me!' ||3.13||
'Alas, alas! That <s>rāsa</s>-assembly, with its ever-new, ever-fresh delight of meeting, its perpetual play —

children.text: āstāṃ rāsādi-līlāvalir api lalitā hā dinānte niśānte'py
children.translated_text: 'Let alone the series of <s>rāsa</s> and other pastimes, even the graceful — alas, at day's end and dawn's end,

children.text: añcan gobhir vilāsī saha-sakhi-nicayaḥ sāgrajaḥ kṛṣṇa-candraḥ |
children.translated_text: the playful <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s>, with his elder brother, with his host of companions, adorning [the scene] with the cows —

children.text: asmān netrānta-lakṣmī-vilasita-kalayā puṣṭavān suṣṭhu yas taṃ
children.translated_text: he who nourished us excellently with the beauty playing at the corners of his eyes —

children.text: gopās tūrṇaṃ nayanti kva samam iti giro gopikā māṃ tudanti ||GC_2,3.14||
children.translated_text: the cowherds quickly lead him away — to where? — these words of the <s>gopīs</s> pierce me!' ||3.14||

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite-
children.translated_text: In that situation:

children.text: rādhā yadyapi mūrchitā samabhavat tasyās tathāpi priyaś
children.translated_text: 'Although <s>Rādhā</s> had fainted, nevertheless, her beloved

children.text: cittāntaḥ sphurati sma tadvad abhito yadvac chatāṅgaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: shimmered within her inner heart, just so, as if he had entered her hundred-fold limbs;

children.text: so'yaṃ yadyapi dṛṣṭi-kṛṣṭim akarod asyāḥ sakāśān nija-
children.translated_text: although he drew the gaze from her side toward himself,

children.text: kṣobhād bibhyad iyaṃ tathāpya anudiśaṃ hā tad-dṛśi vyānaśe ||GC_2,3.15||
children.translated_text: she, fearing his own agitation, nevertheless — alas — vanished in every direction into his gaze!' ||3.15||

children.text: tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ rurudur yad etā
children.translated_text: 'In that assembly, these [<s>gopīs</s>] wept,

children.text: govinda dāmodara mādhaveti |
children.translated_text: '<s>Govinda</s>! <s>Dāmodara</s>! <s>Mādhava</s>!'

children.text: tatra smṛte'dyāpi mano mamedaṃ
children.translated_text: When that is remembered even now, this mind of mine

children.text: khedaṃ bhajat-prāṇa-bhṛtiṃ na vaṣṭi ||GC_2,3.16||
children.translated_text: embraces sorrow and does not desire the sustenance of life!' ||3.16||

children.text: evaṃ bata sudatīnāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Thus indeed, even as those beautiful-toothed ones

children.text: rudatīnām apy aruntudaḥ sa rathī |
children.translated_text: were weeping, that charioteer, the tormentor —

children.text: akrūraḥ krūra-manāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s>, cruel-minded —

children.text: dūraṃ harim ahṛta sūrajā-puram ||GC_2,3.17||
children.translated_text: carried <s>Hari</s> far away to the city of the <s>Yamunā's</s> son (<s>Mathurā</s>)!' ||3.17||

children.text: kṛṣṇas tan mukhya-vargas tad-anugata-rathas tat-patākā-tad-udyad-
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then the chief group, then the chariot following him, then the banners, then the rising

children.text: dhūlīnāṃ pālir itthaṃ kramam anu nimiṣa-projjhitaṃ vīikṣyamāṇā |
children.translated_text: dust-clouds — thus, in sequence, beheld as discarded in the blink of an eye,

children.text: pratyāvṛttau nirāśā vraja-yuvati-tatiḥ prāṇam atyakṣyad eṣa
children.translated_text: the host of <s>Vraja's</s> young women, despairing of his return, would have abandoned their life-breath —

children.text: prāk cen nātmāgati-svīkṛti-kṛti-lipibhiḥ satyam atra vyadhāsyat ||GC_2,3.18||
children.translated_text: had not the inscriptions of the acceptance of his own return previously established the truth therein!' ||3.18||

children.text: yadyapi sura-muni-kathitā
children.translated_text: 'Although it was known, as told by gods and sages,

children.text: svasyāgataye vilambitā jñātā |
children.translated_text: that his own coming would be delayed,

children.text: tad api ca valayita-tṛṣṇe
children.translated_text: even so, regarding her whose longing was entwined,

children.text: nāsyāṃ kṛṣṇena nādṛtiḥ kalitā ||GC_2,3.19||
children.translated_text: no indifference was conceived by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' ||3.19||

children.text: tatra tasya tāsāṃ ca sa-sveda-jala-kuṅkuma-rāgeṇa sāśru-kajjala-bhāgena ca muhur mitho likhitā dūtya-saṅgata-madhumaṅgala-patrikāḥ patrikā yathā-
children.translated_text: There, the letters inscribed repeatedly between him and those [<s>gopīs</s>], with perspiration-water and <s>kuṅkuma</s>-dye, and with tear-mixed collyrium, conveyed through the messenger-companion <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — the letter was as follows:

children.text: āyāsyāmy āśu hatvā tam adhi-madhupuraṃ kaṃsam apy asti dūraṃ
vatsādy-āghāta-dhāmnaḥ puram api kim adas tat priyāḥ kutra duḥkham?
children.translated_text: from the abode of the slayers of <s>Vatsa</s> and others? Then, O beloveds, where is the sorrow?

children.text: kintv anyat prārthitaṃ yad bhavadbhir ucitaṃ tad vidhatta prasattyā
children.translated_text: But as for the other thing entreated by you that is fitting — bestow it graciously!

children.text: prāṇe prāṇeśvarībhir mayi kim ayi paraṃ hanta mantavyam antaḥ ||GC_2,3.20||
children.translated_text: O mistresses of my life — what indeed, alas, should be thought of me within your hearts?' ||3.20||
'I shall come swiftly, having slain <s>Kaṃsa</s> in <s>Madhupura</s> — and is the city indeed far

children.text: gacchan neṣa tvam adya sphurasi dayita bhoḥ kaṃsa-ghātaṃ vidhāya
svīkartuṃ rājatāṃ tat katham atha bhavatād āgatis te vrajāya?
children.translated_text: [you aim] to assume kingship — then how will your return to <s>Vraja</s> come about?

children.text: tasmād asmābhir arthyaṃ tad idam iha bhavāṃs tatra nānā-virājat-
children.translated_text: Therefore, what is desired by us is this: that you, there in the various resplendent

children.text: tīrthe sarvārthade naḥ smṛtim anu dadatām añjalīnāṃ trayāṇi ||GC_2,3.21||
children.translated_text: holy places that grant all purposes, bestow upon us, following [our] remembrance, three handfuls of [sacred water]!' ||3.21||
'You who depart are not shining today, O beloved! Having accomplished the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: nālaṃ me rājya-lipsā katham api valate nirmame tatra satyaṃ
children.translated_text: 'I have no desire for kingship — how could attachment arise in one who is free from possessiveness? Truly,

children.text: kaṃsaṃ hatvā yadūnāṃ sukham abhivalayann asmi cāyāta-kalpaḥ |
children.translated_text: having slain <s>Kaṃsa</s> and having well-secured the happiness of the <s>Yadus</s>, I am ready to come!

children.text: baddhaḥ syāt kṛṣṇa-sāraḥ sapadi vidhi-vaśāt tarhi kiṃ pārthivāder
children.translated_text: If a black deer is suddenly bound by the decree of fate, then what king or such

children.text: mānas tasmin sukhāya prabhavati na vanaṃ nāpi kāntā-susaṅgaḥ ||GC_2,3.22||
children.translated_text: can his honor effect for its happiness — neither the forest nor the companionship of beloved ones?' ||3.22||

children.text: vṛndaṃ krīḍā-vanānāṃ bahu-vidham abhito'py asti tatrātha rājñāṃ
children.translated_text: 'There is indeed a multitude of pleasure-groves of many kinds there on all sides; and the daughters of kings —

children.text: kanyā bahvyo'pi kāntās tava vibhava-vaśād udbhaviṣyanti dhanyāḥ |
children.translated_text: many beloveds shall arise for you, blessed ones, by the power of your opulence;

children.text: tat-tal-lābhe manas te katham iha bhavitāsmāsu vā kiṃ tapobhir
children.translated_text: in the attainment of each of those, how will your mind be toward us? — or, when enjoyment

children.text: labdhe bhoge vicitre punar api tanum ānīhate vanya-vṛttīḥ ||GC_2,3.23||
children.translated_text: obtained through austerities is varied, does the body still long for forest ways?' ||3.23||

children.text: satyaṃ tāḥ keli-vanyā vidadhati laṣitaṃ sarvataḥ satyam eva
children.translated_text: 'Truly, those pleasure-groves produce delight everywhere — truly indeed,

children.text: kṣoṇī-pālādi-kanyāḥ parama-guṇa-gaṇa-stotra-bhājaḥ sphuranti |
children.translated_text: the princesses of kings shine as receptacles of the praise of supreme qualities;

children.text: satyaṃ kurve trilokī mama na hi ratidā nāpi tatrastha-rāmā
children.translated_text: truly, I declare — the three worlds do not give me pleasure, nor the beauties dwelling therein,

children.text: yadvad vṛndāvanaṃ me tad-anugata-ramā yadvad etā bhavatyaḥ ||GC_2,3.24||
children.translated_text: as does <s>Vṛndāvana</s> for me, as do the beauties following it, as do you!' ||3.24||

children.text: sā te sarvāṅga-śobhā bata samadhigatā yena netreṇa yena
children.translated_text: 'That all-limbed beauty of yours, alas, was apprehended — by whichever eye,

children.text: śrotreṇāśrāvi vaṃśī samagami vapuṣā yena ca sparṣa-lakṣmīḥ |
children.translated_text: by whichever ear the flute was heard, by whichever body the beauty of touch was experienced —

children.text: tenaivālakṣi dūraṃ gamanam avagataṃ tena sandiṣṭam ugraṃ
children.translated_text: by that very [sense] the distant departure was perceived, by that the harsh [command] was understood,

children.text: tena svaṃ vipralabdhaṃ racitam iti hahā jīvitaṃ dhig vidhiṃ dhik ||GC_2,3.25||
children.translated_text: by that one's own self was deceived — thus, alas, alas — fie on life! Fie on the Creator!' ||3.25||

children.text: yeyaṃ dṛṣṭir mayā vaś chavi-parikalanāt kṛṣyate yā śrutir vāg
children.translated_text: 'This gaze of mine, which is drawn to you through the perception of [your] complexion; this hearing, this voice

children.text: dūrasthā racyate yā tanur api milanād davyate sa-vyapekṣam |
children.translated_text: which is composed [even] when far away; this body too, which burns with longing from meeting —

children.text: yady etās tatra tatra pratikṛti-kṛtaye na hy adhīnā mama syus
children.translated_text: if these were not under my control here and there for producing a replica [of you],

children.text: tarhy etāḥ svairiṇīr vā katham aham ahaha prāṇa-sakhyaḥ saheya? ||GC_2,3.26||
children.translated_text: then how, alas, could I endure these, O life-companions — or would they become wanton ones?' ||3.26||

children.text: akrūra-krūra-bhāvaṃ vidhir aśubha-vidhiṃ mitram āmitra-caryāṃ
yasyām asyāṃ daśāyāṃ sarabha-samagamat tatra kānyasya vārtā?
children.translated_text: in this very condition, when [all] rushed together furiously — then what word is there of anything else?

children.text: asmaj jīvo'py ajīva-sthitim iha niyataṃ prāpnuyād evam atra
children.translated_text: Even our life-breath would certainly attain a lifeless state herein — therefore,

children.text: svāmin na vyādhivat tat-pratividhir udiyāt kāla-kalpe vilambe ||GC_2,3.27||
children.translated_text: O Lord, may the remedy for that not arise like a disease, when the cosmic-dissolution-like delay [extends]!' ||3.27||
'The cruelty of <s>Akrūra</s>, the inauspicious decree of the Creator, friends acting as enemies —

children.text:
āyāsyāmy eva śīghraṃ na khalu mama manasy anya-vārtāsti kācit
kācid vā daivataḥ syāt tad api na bhavatī-jātu dīnās tyajāni |
yā yā madhye mad-āptir muhur iha bhavitā tāṃ punaḥ svapna-rūpāṃ
mā śaṅkadhvaṃ yathā prāg asati ca virahe śaṅkamānā babhūva ||GC_2,3.28|| iti |
children.translated_text:
'I shall certainly come quickly — there is no other thought in my mind whatsoever;
if some [obstacle] should arise by divine will, even then I shall never abandon you, the forlorn ones!
Whatever attainment of mine shall occur repeatedly here in between — do not suspect that
to be dream-like, as before, in the absence [of union], you became suspicious!' ||3.28|| — thus.

children.text: etāvan mānam anyāsāṃ vācikaṃ hariṇājani |
children.translated_text: 'This much verbal pride from the other [<s>gopīs</s>] was produced by <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: rādhāyā mūkatānūkam amitaṃ yat tu nirmame ||GC_2,3.29||
children.translated_text: but immeasurable was what he fashioned for <s>Rādhā</s>, following her silence!' ||3.29||

children.text: tataḥ sva-vṛndena niśāntam āpitā
children.translated_text: 'Then, led to the end of the night by her own group,

children.text: balena bālās tad urīkṛtāgatim |
children.translated_text: and by the strength [of <s>Balarāma</s>], those young women, having accepted his coming as certain,

children.text: prācīna-tad-rīti-śatena niścitāṃ
children.translated_text: having determined [it] by hundreds of his previous customs —

children.text: vinirmāṇā muhur eva tāṃ jaguḥ ||GC_2,3.30||
children.translated_text: they sang that [assurance] again and again!' ||3.30||

children.text:
tad evaṃ snigdhakaṇthasya kathitam anu vyathita-manasi śrī-rādhikādi-sadasi
vikalaḥ kamala-locanaḥ svayam eva samavocata-
children.translated_text:
Thus, following the narration of <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, in the assembly of glorious <s>Rādhikā</s> and others whose minds were distressed,
the lotus-eyed one himself, overcome with emotion, spoke:

children.text: rādhe śravasi nāveśaṃ kuru kintu vilocane |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>! Do not place in [your] hearing — but rather in [your] eyes!

children.text: vṛttaṃ san manyase hanta vartamānaṃ na vīkṣase ||GC_2,3.31||
children.translated_text: What has happened, you consider 'past' — alas, you do not see the present!' ||3.31||

children.text:
tad etan niśamya ramyaṃ tan-mukhaṃ niśāmya śāmyat-pīḍā sa-vrīḍā tat-kāla-
valamāna-śītala-nayana-jala-bindubhis tat-padāravinda-dvandam indīvarākṣī śirasā
niṣevamāṇā suciraṃ siṣeca |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, and beholding his beautiful face, she — her suffering subsiding, bashful — with cool drops of tears flowing at that moment, the lotus-eyed one (<s>Rādhā</s>), reverently attending his pair of lotus-feet with her head, sprinkled [them] for a long time.

children.text: atha sarveṣāṃ sukha-sandohe saṃbhṛta-dohe sarve parveva labhamānā nija-nijālayaṃ sambabhūvuḥ | śrī-rādhā-mādhavau ca mohana-mandiraṃ vindataḥ smeti |
children.translated_text: Then, when the joy-flood of all was gathered and swelling, all, as if finding a festival, went to their respective abodes. And glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> reached the enchanting chamber — thus it is.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrīmad uttara-gopāla-campūm anu
māthura-pura-sthāna-prasthānaṃ nāma
tṛtīyaṃ pūraṇam
||3||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious Uttara-<s>Gopāla-campū</s>,
the third <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter), named 'The Departure to the City of <s>Mathurā</s>'
||3||

children.text: atha pañcamaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the fifth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter):

children.text: kaṃsa-vadha-kathā
children.translated_text: The Narrative of the Slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s>
