children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇena bhāsamānāyāṃ śrī-vraja-rāja-sabhāyāṃ punaḥ prātaḥ-kathā, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, in the assembly of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, radiant with glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the morning narrative [began] again, as follows:

children.text: snigdhakaṇṭha uvāca,- atha rajanir ajani; prajātāyāṃ ca yasyāṃ bahu- śivāyamānā śivā śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ prati śivā jātā, kaṃsaṃ prati sphuṭam aśiveti sthite tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ svapna-jāgarayos tasya mahā-bhaya-jananyāṃ vyatītāyāṃ sa punar dambhī gambhīraṃ malla-līlārambhaṃ sambhṛtavān | tataś cālaṅkṛtānāṃ cālaṅkṛtānāṃ ca śubhra-mañca-prapañcānām adhimadhyam-adhyastaṃ raṅga-sthalaṃ bhrājamāna-citra-viracanaṃ babhrāje | vidyud-bhrājamānād abhra-śarad-abhrāṇāṃ tārakitaṃ nabha iva |
children.translated_text: <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> said: 'Then night arose; and when it was born, she who was auspicious — <s>Śivā</s> (Night) — became auspicious toward glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and manifestly inauspicious toward <s>Kaṃsa</s>. It being thus settled, when that night — which generated great fear in both his waking and sleeping states — had passed, that deceitful one (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) again prepared the commencement of the wrestling spectacle with gravitas. Then, amidst the rows of adorned and decorated white platforms, the arena-ground, brilliant with colorful arrangements, shone splendidly — like the sky, studded with stars amidst autumn-clouds flashing with lightning.'

children.text: tatrāpy unnatatama-mañcam añcan kaṃsaḥ svayam akhila-durjana-rājāvataṃsati sma | tat tu rājādhipatā-garva-grastatayā sambhavad api trastatāyām eva paryavasyati sma | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: There too, mounting the highest platform, <s>Kaṃsa</s> himself assumed the crowning position among all wicked kings. But that [position], though arising from the arrogance of sovereignty, culminated in nothing but terror. And there:

children.text:
akrūrānakadundubhī yad akṛta sve mañcake prāntayoḥ
paurīṇāṃ gaṇa-bhāji devaka-sutāṃ nandādikān dūrage |
kiṃ ca dvāri gajaṃ dadhe kuvalayāpīḍaṃ nijāgra-sthale
mallān kūṭatayā sa bhoja-nṛpatis tasmān na kaḥ kṣubhyati? ||GC_2,5.1|| (śārdūla)
tatra ca-
children.translated_text: And there:

children.text:
kaṃsājñayāsīd yad vādyam atra malla-kalocitam |
tad eva maṅgalaṃ jajñe prasthāne rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ ||GC_2,5.2|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
The music that was, by <s>Kaṃsa's</s> order, suited to the wrestling arena here,
that very [music] became auspicious for the departure of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||GC_2,5.2|| (anuṣṭubh)

children.text: atha tayor nija-tad-anargalatā-vyañjanāya svayam anāgamya prathama-prasthāpita- sthavira-gopa-vargayoḥ kṛta-prātaḥ-kṛti-sargayor yadā raṅga-pura-dvāra-pura-pradeśa-praveśaḥ samajani | tadā tu loka-kolāhalata eva sarvas tat kalayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, when their entry into the arena-city gate-precinct occurred — the two having manifested their own unobstructedness, having themselves not come [directly] but first dispatched the group of elder cowherds, and having completed their morning rites — then, by the mere commotion of the crowd, everyone perceived it.

children.text: tataś ca sadotkaṭaṃ madotkaṭaṃ galatkaṭaṃ nago vā nāgo veti nirṇinīṣatāṃ kṛta-vrīḍaṃ kuvalayāpīḍaṃ niṣpīḍayitum aṃśukam āpīḍaṃ ca dṛḍhīkurvann agraja-sakhi-vraja-kṛtānuvrajanaḥ suretara-mardanaḥ svayam agresaratām avāpa |
children.translated_text: Then, tightening his upper garment and headpiece to crush <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, who had been made ashamed by those wishing to determine 'Is this ever-fierce, rut-dripping, streaming-rut [creature] a mountain or an elephant?' — followed by the company of friends led by his elder brother, the crusher of the enemies of the gods himself took the lead.

children.text:
snigdhā nyaṣedhan ye tatra girā svaṃ śatravas tathā |
ubhayāṃs tān smitenaiva paśyan dvipam agād dhariḥ ||GC_2,5.3|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
Those who were affectionate restrained him there with words, as did his enemies;
seeing both groups, <s>Hari</s> merely smiled and approached the elephant. ||GC_2,5.3|| (anuṣṭubh)

children.text: tataś ca śrī-hariṇā-
children.translated_text: Then, by glorious <s>Hari</s> —

children.text:
tad-vartma-prārthanaṃ tat-kupita-gajam api prārdanaṃ tan nijāṅga-
syābhīkṣṇaṃ tasya śuṇḍā-rada-pada-valanaṃ tat tato mocanaṃ ca |
tat-pucchākarṣaṇaṃ tad-bhramaṇam abhimukhībhūya tat-tāḍaṇaṃ tad
vidrutya drāk patitvā drava-bharam anu niṣpātanaṃ saṃbhramayya ||GC_2,5.4|| (sragdharā)
children.translated_text:
The demanding of its path, the pressing of that enraged elephant, the repeated twisting of his own body [to avoid] its trunk, tusks, and feet, then the freeing [of himself],
the seizing of its tail, the whirling around, the confronting and striking of it, the causing it to flee swiftly and then fall, and the making it rush about in confusion — ||GC_2,5.4|| (sragdharā)

children.text:
tad-dadbhyāṃ vañcitābhyāṃ kṣiti-hati-valanāt kṣobhaṇaṃ tat punaś ca
pratyāsadyāgra-hasta-grahaṇa-racanayā sraṃsanaṃ bhūmi-pṛṣṭhe |
tad-varṣmākramya tat-tad-daśana-vighaṭanaṃ tena tad-ghātanaṃ ca
draṣṭṝn sindhos taraṅga-pratimam anayad unmajjanaṃ majjanaṃ ca ||GC_2,5.5|| (sragdharā)
children.translated_text:
The agitation from the ground-striking whirl when deceived by its two [tusks], and then again
the toppling to the ground's surface by the stratagem of seizing the front trunk-hand,
the mounting upon its body and the breaking of each tusk, and the slaying of it thereby —
this carried the spectators through rising and sinking like waves of an ocean. ||GC_2,5.5|| (sragdharā)

children.text:
hastinaḥ kathite ghāte hastipāṃ tat-kathā vṛthā |
malle kṣuṇṇe tu tat-sthānāṃ yūkānāṃ tat kim ucyatām? ||GC_2,5.6|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
When the elephant's slaying was announced, the tale of the elephant-keepers was futile;
and when the wrestler was crushed, what need be said of those in his place — mere lice? ||GC_2,5.6|| (anuṣṭubh)

children.text: tadā cāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ,-
children.translated_text: And then this was the distinction —

children.text:
paryaṭan naṭa evāyaṃ siṃha eva sa saṃharan |
bhindan bhiduram eveti kariṇā harir aikṣyata ||GC_2,5.7|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
This one was seen as a mere actor while wandering, as a lion while destroying,
and as one splitting what is already fragile — thus <s>Hari</s> appeared with [regard to] the elephant. ||GC_2,5.7|| (anuṣṭubh)

children.text:
hatvā nāgaṃ danta-yugmaṃ gṛhītvā
bhrātre prādāt kaṃsa-śatrus tad ekam |
eko nirmāty āvayor yad yaśas tad-
dviṣṭhaṃ diṣṭaṃ syāt samantād itīva ||GC_2,5.8|| (śālinī)

kuñjaraṃ harir aghātayad balo'py
atra rakta-mada-bindubhiś citaḥ |
pāripārśvikatayā tad-antike
cchāyayeva yad asau tadābhramat ||GC_2,5.9|| (rathoddhatā)
children.translated_text:
<s>Hari</s> it was who slew the elephant, yet <s>Bala</s> too
appeared speckled with drops of blood and rut-fluid;
for he roamed nearby in the capacity of an attendant,
as though he were its shadow. ||GC_2,5.9|| (rathoddhatā)

children.text: tad evaṃ gīr-vāṇā api yad bṛṃhita-vāṇād bhayam ayamānās tata eva kila śaśvad asvapnān nāmnāpy asvapnā jātāḥ | so'yaṃ kuvalayāpīḍaḥ karī dāna-vāri-varīyān api dāna-vāri-kṛta-dānam āptavān iti te punar lekhā vismayena lekhā ivāsan | tatra ca sati kaṃsaṃ prati sahasā na kaścana bhiyā śaśaṃsa |
children.translated_text: Thus, even the gods, who were perpetually fearful of the trumpet-voiced [elephant], had become sleepless even in name — perpetually without sleep. This <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> elephant, though surpassing in rut-fluid, received a gift of rut-fluid [i.e., death-libation]. At that, those [gods] again became like painted images with astonishment. And in that situation, no one hastily reported to <s>Kaṃsa</s> out of fear.

children.text: tad anu ca-
children.translated_text: And then —

children.text:
pūrvāha-luṇṭhita-nṛpāṃśuka-śobhitāṃśū
sadyo-vighātita-mahā-gaja-danta-pāṇī |
tad-rakta-dāna-racitāṅgada-kaṅkaṇau tau
tādṛg-ganair viviśatur nṛpateḥ purastāt ||GC_2,5.10|| (vasanta)
children.translated_text:
Their limbs adorned with the garments of kings plundered the day before,
their hands holding the tusks of the great elephant just slain,
wearing armlets and bracelets fashioned from its blood-offering —
those two entered before the king with such a retinue. ||GC_2,5.10|| (vasantatilakā)

children.text:
śauryam eva puruṣasya bhūṣaṇaṃ
yatra heyam api yāti geyatām |
danti-rakta-mada-bindavas tanuṃ
kaṃsa-saṃsadi tayor arūrucan ||GC_2,5.11|| (rathoddhatā)
children.translated_text:
Valor alone is a man's ornament,
where even what is despicable attains celebration;
the drops of blood and rut-fluid of the elephant
adorned the bodies of those two in <s>Kaṃsa's</s> assembly. ||GC_2,5.11|| (rathoddhatā)

children.text:
dviṣanto bhīṣmāṅgaṃ dadṛśur ajitaṃ tarhi puratas
taṭasthā madhyasthaṃ praṇaya-manasaḥ śarma-vapuṣam |
viśeṣaṃ tatrāpi sphuṭam adhiyayus te bahu-vidhaṃ
yathā bhāvas tadvad yugapad ayam uccair vibhavati ||GC_2,5.12|| (śikhariṇī)
children.translated_text:
The hostile ones saw the unconquered one before them with terrifying form;
the neutral ones saw him as impartial; those with loving hearts saw him as an embodiment of bliss.
Moreover, each perceived a distinct [aspect] therein in many ways —
as is one's disposition, so does this [form] manifest exceedingly, all at once. ||GC_2,5.12|| (śikhariṇī)

children.text:
varṇyaṃ tad vā kiyad iha bhavet tasya mādhurya-varyaṃ
jīvat-kaṃse'py atha sadasi yad vanditaṃ loka-lakṣaiḥ |
tejas tad vā katipayam itaḥ kathyatāṃ yatra magnaṃ
prāṇantaṃ taṃ mṛtam iva surā menire bhoja-rājam ||GC_2,5.13|| (mandākrāntā)
children.translated_text:
Or how much of his supreme sweetness could be described here?
— that which was venerated by hosts of people even while <s>Kaṃsa</s> was alive in the assembly.
Or how much of that radiance can be told from here? — wherein submerged,
the gods considered the <s>Bhoja</s> king, though breathing, as if dead. ||GC_2,5.13|| (mandākrāntā)

children.text: athāgatau ca gṛhīta-mṛṇāla-nāla-hasta-hastināv iva dhṛta-danti-dantau bṛhad-urasvantau so'yam eva kim iti sāvahela-śaṃsanena kaṃsaṃ vilokya tau ślokya-caritau taṃ pṛṣṭha-deśa-parāmṛṣṭaṃ kurvantau tata ito dṛṣṭi-visṛṣṭiṃ cakratuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having arrived, the two — broad-chested, holding the elephant's tusks as if holding lotus-stalk stems — looking at <s>Kaṃsa</s> with a contemptuous declaration of 'Is this that very one?' — those two of praiseworthy deeds, making him feel touched at the back, cast their glances hither and thither.

children.text: tataś ca parivṛtya śrī-hariḥ punar aho apaśyat tri-divasya vartmārdham evānu-vartamānaḥ so'yaṃ vartate, tasmāt tatra prasthāpanam asya nātidūrāvasthāpanam iti hasitvā sakhibhir akhilaiḥ saha lasitvā ca parasparaṃ paraṃ vṛttaṃ vartayāmāsa |
children.translated_text: Then, turning around, glorious <s>Hari</s> again noticed: 'Ah, this one has been following along half the path of heaven; therefore, his dispatching is not a placing at too great a distance.' Having laughed and frolicked with all his companions, he continued the ongoing proceedings with them.

children.text: atha sva-hata-gaja-rakta-raktatayā pralaya-kāla-kāya-vyakta-nīla-lohitāyamānatā-pātrasya gātrasya vilokana-mātrataḥ prāpta-tejo-dhvaṃsaṃ kaṃsaṃ kav imāv iti śaṃsantaṃ pārśva-vartinaḥ procuḥ,- etav eva tau iti |
children.translated_text: Then, <s>Kaṃsa</s> — whose body, reddened by the blood of the elephant he had slain, had become a vessel manifesting the blue-and-red [appearance] of the dissolution-era body — whose splendor was shattered from the mere sight of them, as he was asking 'Who are these two?' — his attendants told him: 'These are those very two.'

children.text: kaṃsa uvāca,- anayoḥ karayoḥ kiṃ dṛśyate? gātraṃ vā kena citra-pātraṃ kṛtam?
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s> said: 'What is seen in the hands of these two? Or by whom was their body made into a painted canvas?'

children.text: sarve'py ūcuḥ,- kuvalayāpīḍasya dantāv ivāvakalyete gātraṃ ca tad-rakta-raktaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: All said: 'These appear to be the tusks of <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, and their bodies must be reddened with its blood.'

children.text: kaṃsaḥ sa-saṃrambha-dambham uvāca,- haṃho! aṃho-valitā dvayam api vāṅ-mātra-pātrāyamāṇam idam asambhavam |
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṃsa</s> said with concealed agitation and bluster: 'Ha! This — that both are enveloped in sin, becoming vessels of mere words — is impossible!'

children.text: atha punar adattottareṣu bhayottareṣu ca teṣu svayam eva tayoḥ prabhāvas taṃ bodhayāmāsa | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: Then, when they gave no answer and were overcome with fear, their very prowess itself enlightened him. Because:

children.text:
yadi tvaṃ re kaṃsa svayam asi balī tarhi dhig amuṃ
kathaṃ dvāre nāgaṃ kalayasi na tatra svaka-vapuḥ? |
radābhyāṃ sa śreyān iti yadi tad āvām iva kathaṃ
na tau gṛhnāsīti dhvanitam amukābhyāṃ sva-kalayā? ||GC_2,5.14|| (śikhariṇī)
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Kaṃsa</s>! If you yourself are strong, then shame on that —
how is it you station an elephant at the gate and not your own body there?
If he [the elephant] is better with his two tusks, then how is it
you don't seize those two as you would us?' — thus was suggested by those two through their own art. ||GC_2,5.14|| (śikhariṇī)

children.text: tad evaṃ sati-
children.translated_text: That being so —

children.text:
so'yaṃ pūtanikām ahan śakaṭakaṃ vyāvartayat taṃ marud-
daityaṃ prārdayad arjuna-dvayam api prārdat tad ity ādikam |
śrīmad-gokula-kelim asya kalayan lokaḥ purā paśyatas
tāṃs tarhy ārdayad adya cārdayati bhoḥ paśyāparān śṛṇvataḥ ||GC_2,5.15|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
'This very one slew <s>Pūtanā</s>, overturned the cart, crushed that wind-demon,
shattered the pair of <s>Arjuna</s> trees' — and so on.
The people, recounting his glorious <s>Gokula</s> sports,
[said:] 'He who was previously seen slaying them — behold, now he slays others too!' ||GC_2,5.15|| (śārdūlavikrīḍita)

children.text:
tatra ca nayanayor vistāraṇayā tābhyāṃ tayoḥ sakalam api rūpaṃ yugapat pātum iva varṇanā-rasa-rasanāyāś cālanayā nikhilam api mādhuryaṃ leḍhum iva tal-lābha-parva-garvataḥ sphuṭa-nāsā-puṭayoḥ phullanayā tābhyāṃ samastam api saurabhyam abhyantare praveśayitum iva muhur apy astābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ nirdeśanayā tābhyāṃ sāṅgam apy aṅgam āliṅgitum ivehamāne sukhaṃ ca sacamāne sura-nara-sarge
śabdāyamāne ca citra-vāditra-varge sarveṣāṃ mukhataḥ sarva-sukhada-stutiḥ prastutim avāpeti |
children.translated_text: And there, by the widening of their eyes — as if to drink simultaneously the entire beauty of those two — and by the movement of the tongue of descriptive <s>rasa</s> — as if to lick all sweetness — and by the blooming of their clearly flared nostrils from the pride of obtaining them — as if to draw all fragrance within — and by the repeated pointing with their unsteady hands — as if desiring to embrace every limb fully — while both striving and savoring bliss, and while the entire assemblage of divine and human creation was sounding forth, and while the array of wondrous instruments resounded — from everyone's mouth arose praise that bestowed all happiness.

children.text: sa eṣa tat-prabhāva-viśeṣaḥ śaśvad bhāvanām abhibhavan vibhavati sma | yatra kaṃsena yuddhāya pūrvam eva preritā viparīta-vāditāyām api mallāḥ stutāv eva paryavasitāḥ |
children.translated_text: This very extraordinary manifestation of their prowess, perpetually overwhelming contemplation, shone forth — wherein the wrestlers, previously dispatched by <s>Kaṃsa</s> for battle, though the instruments played discordantly, ended up in praise alone.

children.text: tathā hi- tad evaṃ sthite krūra-dhāmā cāṇūra-nāmā śaśaṃsa; yatra he nanda-sūno! he rāmeti nirādara-pitṛ-nāmnā vinā ca tan nāmnā sambodhana-dvayam anyathā-bodhanāya pravartitam api sarasvatyā tad-vāg-indriyaṃ stuty-artham eva nartitam āsīt | he pitṛ-nāmnā sva-nāmnā ca sucarita-samudācāra-kumāra-dvayatayā samānāvatāra! śrūyatām iti |
children.translated_text: Thus it was: the cruel-aboded one named <s>Cāṇūra</s> spoke; wherein the two addresses 'O son of <s>Nanda</s>!' and 'O <s>Rāma</s>!' — without the disrespectful patronymic, and with their [proper] names — though deployed for the purpose of mis-instruction — <s>Sarasvatī</s> [the goddess of speech] caused his vocal organ to dance for the purpose of praise alone. 'O pair of youths of equal descent with the well-conducted, praiseworthy clan-folk — bearing the father's name and one's own name! Listen!' — thus.

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ sa-smitam uvāca,- kāmam ājñāpyatām |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with a smile: 'By all means, command!'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- bhavator bhāga-dheyaṃ cetasi kiyad ādheyatām āpnotu |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said: 'May the fortune destined for you two find a place in your hearts!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- kīdṛśam?
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Of what kind?'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- te'mī mahārāja-caraṇā bhavator anugrahamaya-didṛkṣācaraṇā virājante iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said: 'These feet of the great king shine forth, desirous of the grace-filled seeing of you two!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- satyam, kiñcid asmat-kṛtyaṃ punar upadiśyatām |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'True. But let some task of ours be further instructed.'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- saṅgatam evedaṃ bhavataḥ saṅgīrṇam | tathāpi yuvayor itaḥ śaśvat-parāṅ-mukhatā nāsmān sukhayati |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said: 'This much is indeed consonant with your renown. Nevertheless, the perpetual turning away of you two from here does not please us.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- vayaṃ vanecarā narā na rāja-gaṇe gaṇeyānāṃ nītim unnītim ānayāmaḥ | samprati tu bhavad-upadeśam evānusarantaḥ sa-deśa-rūpam ācariṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'We are forest-dwellers — we do not elevate the policy of those countable among the king's retinue to a high position. But now, following your instruction, we shall conduct ourselves in a manner befitting this place.'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- samprati yuvāṃ prati rāja-varya-caraṇā yad ādiśanti, tat punar ācaryatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said: 'Now let what the feet of the king of kings command regarding you two be carried out.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇḥ sa-vinayam ivāha sma,- malla-tallaja! yathā-yatham ādiśyatām |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said with seeming humility: 'O champion of wrestlers! Please command as appropriate.'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- asmābhiḥ saha bhavantāv atha krīḍā-sukham anubhavantāv iha bhavatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said: 'Let you two experience the pleasure of sport with us here.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- bālānām asmākaṃ krīḍāvalocanaṃ rājñāṃ rocanam eva, kintu yuṣmābhir iti śocanam eva pratipadyate | tasmād bhavatām eva tad idam upahāsa-prakāśanam, na tu tatra-bhavatāṃ rāja-vibhavatām upapadyate |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'The watching of children's play by kings is indeed delightful, but with you [as opponents] it becomes a cause for lamentation. Therefore, this is a display of ridicule on your part, and is not befitting the royal dignity of the king.'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- rāja-caraṇebhya eva śape | rājñām eveyam ājñā |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said: 'I swear by the royal feet — this is indeed the command of the king!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- katham iva?
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'How so?'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,-
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said —

children.text:
bālas tvaṃ na hi pūtanādi-dalanād āsīr na vāvidyathāḥ
paugaṇḍaḥ kṣiti-bhṛd-vidhāraṇa-mukha-krīḍā-kula-vyāpṛte |
naivāyaṃ ghaṭase kiśora iti ca pratyakṣa-dig-dantivad
danti-prārdanatānta-karma-racanād rājñas tataḥ kautukam ||GC_2,5.16|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
'You are not a child — since you slew <s>Pūtanā</s> and the rest; you did not merely totter about.
You don't fit as a <s>paugaṇḍa</s> — being occupied with the play-community of deeds like lifting the mountain.
Nor does this [argument] — that you are a <s>kiśora</s> [mere adolescent] — apply, since like the evident quarter-elephant,
from the completion of the deed of crushing the elephant, the king therefore has curiosity!' ||GC_2,5.16|| (śārdūlavikrīḍita)

children.text: ayaṃ tu tava jyāyān pralambādyālambha-karmaṇā jyāyān eva |
children.translated_text: And this elder brother of yours is indeed greater, by the deed of seizing <s>Pralamba</s> and others — greater indeed!'

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- vṛthāsmad dveṣād eva pāpāt teṣām anyathāpattir jātā, parvataś ca labdha-makha-parvatayā śataparva-pāṇer garva-kharvaṇārthaṃ svayam eva tathā jātaḥ | svayaṃ tu vayaṃ yathāvad eva sarvathā vartāmahe | dhanur api purātanatayā purā ghuṇākīrṇam iva jīrṇaṃ vahadbhir dūrād vikīrṇatayā svayam eva dīrṇaṃ sat sparśa-mātrāt viśīrṇaṃ jātam | kuvalayāpīḍaś ca pīḍayituṃ dravann apadravantaṃ mām anāsadya sadyaḥ pṛthivyantar dantāv avagāḍhāv ācaraṃs tāv ākraṣṭuṃ na śaśāka, paraṃ tu praghaṭyamānatayā truṭy-antāv eva ghaṭayan sva-prāṇān api vighaṭayāmāseti | tatra tatra śīghratāghrātālokena lokena punar aham eva tatra kāraṇatayā ghaṭayāmāse | tathā hastipā api tad adhastād dhastim āpannā eva vipannā
iti mānyathā manyathāḥ |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'It was merely from hostility toward us — from that sin — that the misfortune of those [demons] arose; and the mountain, having obtained the greatness of a sacrifice-mountain, became so of its own accord for the purpose of humbling the pride of the hundred-jointed one (<s>Indra</s>). We ourselves, in truth, remain in every way just as we are. The bow too, being ancient, was already worm-eaten and worn; being cracked from far off, it was itself split, and from mere touch became shattered. And <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, running to torment [us] but not reaching me as I ran away, immediately drove his two tusks deep into the earth and could not extract them; rather, the tusks, being in the process of breaking, produced only fragmentation and he gave up his own life-breaths as well. In all those instances, the people, with their hastily-glimpsed perception, fashioned me alone as the cause. Likewise, the elephant-keepers too, having fallen beneath the elephant, perished — so do not think otherwise of me.'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- bhavatānucitam eva saṅkucita-cittībhavatā tad idam apalapyate | rāja-mahāśayās tu tatra tatra na jātānuśayāḥ, pratyuta cirāya nijāntika-sthāpitānāṃ garvitānāṃ garva-damanārtham eva tatra prasthāpitānāṃ teṣāṃ vṛthā-kṛta-pālana-viśeṣānāṃ parīvartād bhavantāv eva kevalāv ātma-balāya kalpayitum icchanti |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said — 'This is improperly denied by you whose mind has become contracted. The king, of great soul, has not become remorseful on this account; rather, for the very purpose of subduing the pride of those proud ones who were long stationed in his proximity and dispatched there, and whose particular protection was made futile — from their replacement, he wishes to appoint you two alone for the strength of his own self.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- tad atīvāsmākaṃ vismāyakaṃ bhāgyam | kintv ātmanātmanaḥ stutyā prastutyā lajjāmahe | yad etaṃ śrī-mahārājam indra-padam api prāpayituṃ sevāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ | tathāpi malla-vidyāyāṃ na vayaṃ kṛta-vidyā iti saṅkucati cittam |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'That is indeed an exceedingly astonishing fortune for us! However, we are embarrassed by this commendation and praise of ourselves by ourselves. We shall render service to make this glorious great king attain even the station of <s>Indra</s>. Nevertheless, the mind shrinks because we have not been trained in the science of wrestling.'

children.text: cāṇūra uvāca,- etad apy apalapitaṃ vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ | yac chrutaṃ viśrutam idam | gopāḥ khalu go-pālanaṃ kurvantaḥ sadāsmākaṃ vidyām abhyasyantīti | tasmād akapaṭatayāsmābhir yuṣmābhir api rājñām ājñā pālanīyā, na tu cālanīyā |
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṇūra</s> said — 'Do not make even this denial in vain! For this has been heard and is well known — that cowherds, while tending cows, always practice our science! Therefore, without deceit, both we and you must obey the command of kings — not evade it.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- tathāpi vanyānām asmākaṃ na dhanyā tad vidyā vidyata iti sadyas tāvad yuṣmac chiṣṭim ācarantaḥ svayaṃ rājñaḥ saṃjñapanāya ca sampatsyāmahe |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'Nevertheless, for us forest-dwellers, that science is not found to be fruitful. So for the present, following your instruction directly, we shall also be ready for the signaling of the king.'

children.text: atha tad etat paryantaṃ udantaṃ santanya danti-danta-dvayaṃ kaṃsa-puratas tad-vakṣasīva maṅkṣu śaṅkuvan nikhanya muṣṭikena muṣṭi-prahāra-hata-pralambaś cāṇūreṇa cānūru-vihagānuja-vāhanaḥ sasañja | labdha-bala-praśastinā mahā-hastinābhinavatayā dīvyad-divya-siṃha iva | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then, having spun out this discourse to its conclusion, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — as if swiftly driving a pair of elephant-tusks into <s>Kaṃsa's</s> chest before his very eyes — engaged with <s>Muṣṭika</s>, whose <s>Pralamba</s> had been struck by fist-blows, and with <s>Cāṇūra</s>, whose vehicle was the younger brother of the <s>Anūru</s>-bird (<s>Garuḍa</s>) — like a divine lion sporting with novelty, having obtained the praise of strength from a great elephant. And there —

children.text:
hastāhasti bhujābhuji prathayator aṅghry-aṅghri cābhun mahaj-
jānūjānu kaṭākaṭi prathanayā krodhaḥ samudbuddhavān |
muṣṭāmuṣṭi talātali prathamakaṃ yac cānyad āsīt tayor
yuddhaṃ tad dhari-mallayor bahu-vidhaṃ buddhaṃ kiyat kalpatām ||GC_2,5.17|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
Hand against hand, arm against arm they displayed, and foot against foot there was great [contest],
knee against knee, hip against hip — by the spreading of these, wrath was fully aroused;
fist against fist, palm against palm — first this, then whatever else there was —
that wrestling match of <s>Hari</s> and the wrestlers, of many kinds, understood [by the wise] — how much of it can be conceived? ||GC_2,5.17||

children.text:
kiṃ tu cāṇūrakaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kāmapālaś ca muṣṭikam |
hasta-rodhaṃ dadhat kaṃse śvāsa-rodhaṃ vinirmame ||GC_2,5.18|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
But <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [defeated] <s>Cāṇūra</s>, and <s>Kāmapāla</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) [defeated] <s>Muṣṭika</s>;
holding back their hands, they produced a choking of breath in <s>Kaṃsa</s>. ||GC_2,5.18||

children.text:
ekaṃ tatra babhūva citram akhila-jñānātidūraṃ yathā
sāṅgaṃ svāṅgam akarṣi yarhi hariṇā vinyāsi tad yarhi ca |
vyātyāsaḥ sphurati sma tarhi balavan malle tu kiṃ cāsphurad
dūrād apy asakṛt pari-pratinidhir ghātādikānāṃ vidhiḥ ||GC_2,5.19|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
One marvel occurred there, beyond the range of all knowledge — when
<s>Hari</s> drew back his own limb and when he deployed it,
a reversal was clearly evident; but in the wrestler — what was evident?
Even from afar, repeatedly, the method of counter-substituting blows and such [was seen]. ||GC_2,5.19||

children.text:
satyaṃ prāharatāṃ mallāv api mādhava-rāmayoḥ |
javād bṛṃhayamānau tau na tu tal lakṣyatāṃ gatau ||GC_2,5.20|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
Truly, even when the wrestlers struck at <s>Mādhava</s> and <s>Rāma</s>,
those two were swiftly increasing [in strength] — but they did not attain visibility of that [increase]. ||GC_2,5.20||

children.text: tad evaṃ sthite tat-prabhāvam ananubhavatām anubhavatām api kaṃsaṃ praty eva doṣa-śaṃsanam āsīt | tatra pūrveṣu mallānām api yathā- tatra cādau teṣāṃ bhāvaneyam,-
children.translated_text: Thus being the case, for those who did not experience their power and for those who did — there was blame directed toward <s>Kaṃsa</s> alone. Therein, among the former [group], regarding the wrestlers too — and first, this was their thought —

children.text:
etau syātāṃ suṣṭhu bālau baliṣṭhau
kiṃ tu śreṣṭhāṃ malla-vidyāṃ na vittaḥ |
tasmāt kasmād bhūbhṛd asmān mṛdhe'smiṃs
tad-vidyānāṃ pāragān vā niyuṅkte ? ||GC_2,5.21|| (śālinī)
children.translated_text:
'These two may be very youthful and strong,
but they do not know the supreme science of wrestling!
Therefore, why does the king in this battle
appoint us — who have crossed to the far shore of that science? ||GC_2,5.21||

children.text: ante tu-
children.translated_text: But at the end —

children.text:
jñātvāpy uccais tāv imau malla-vidyā
śāstra-jñānām ādi-vijñāna-vijñau |
hā dhiṅ mauḍhyād eva kaṃso'yam asmān
etad yuddhe bhīruko'pi nyayuṅkta ||GC_2,5.22|| (śālinī)
children.translated_text:
'Having fully known those two to be knowers of the original knowledge
of the science of wrestling — the science of the learned —
alas! Shame! — only from stupidity has this <s>Kaṃsa</s>
appointed us, who are cowards even in this battle!' ||GC_2,5.22||

children.text: tathānyeṣām api nārī-pracurāṇām akrūrāṇāṃ kaṃsāya doṣa-śaṃsanaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: Likewise, from the others too — the gentle ones, predominantly women — the declaration of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> fault, as follows —

children.text:
kva mallā vajrādri-pratima-vapuṣaḥ kvāti-mṛdulāv
imau bālau tasmād iha yad anumantṝn dhig adhipān |
kathaṃ vā te nindyā na khalu vayam asmin sadasi ye
satāṃ dviṣṭe dṛṣṭiṃ sakutukam ivāmī vitanumaḥ ||GC_2,5.23|| (śikhariṇī)
children.translated_text:
'Where are the wrestlers, whose bodies are like adamantine mountains — and where are these two,
exceedingly tender youths! Therefore, shame on the rulers who sanction this!
Or how are they to be blamed? — are we not the ones in this assembly who
extend our gaze with seeming curiosity upon what is hateful to the virtuous?' ||GC_2,5.23||

children.text:
dhig asmat-puṇyaṃ yat katham api harer vīkṣaṇa-lave'
py abhūd utpāto'yaṃ praṇayi-janatā-rākṣasa-nibhaḥ |
vrajan vanyāṃ prātar vrajam api viśan sāyam amukaḥ
sukhaṃ yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ vahati vara-puṇyāḥ param amūḥ ||GC_2,5.24|| (śikhariṇī)
children.translated_text:
'Shame on our merit, that even in a mere glimpse of seeing <s>Hari</s>,
this calamity has arisen — resembling a <s>Rākṣasa</s> to loving people!
He who goes to the forest in the morning and enters <s>Vraja</s> again at evening —
he carries the happiness of those women — supremely blessed are they!' ||GC_2,5.24||

children.text:
dhig asmān yāḥ kaṃsād bhayam anusṛtā nāma ca hareḥ
samarthā vaktuṃ na vraja-vara-dṛśas tāḥ kati numaḥ |
sadā yā gāyanti sva-gṛha-bahu-karmaṇy api guṇāṃs
tadīyān śaśvat tad dhṛdi ca viharanti pratipadam ||GC_2,5.25|| (śikhariṇī)
children.translated_text:
'Shame on us! Those who, having followed the fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, cannot even
utter the name of <s>Hari</s> — how many of us can praise those excellent-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>?
They who always sing his virtues even amidst their many household tasks,
and perpetually sport with him in their hearts at every step!' ||GC_2,5.25||

children.text:
kasyātulaṃ phalam idaṃ yad amuṣya rūpaṃ
lāvaṇya-sāram asamaṃ svata eva siddham |
ekānta-dhāma vibhūtāyaśasoḥ samantād
dṛgbhiḥ sadā nava-navābham amūḥ pibanti ||GC_2,5.26|| (vasanta-tilaka)
children.translated_text:
'Whose incomparable fruit is this — that his form,
the essence of beauty, unequaled, self-established by its very nature,
the exclusive abode of splendor and renown on all sides —
those women drink perpetually with their eyes, ever fresh and new?' ||GC_2,5.26||

children.text:
tāsāṃ premṇaḥ parama-mahimā śakyate kena vaktuṃ
paśyāsmākaṃ tam anugatavac cittam etad vihāya |
yad govindaḥ śrama-maya-rucāpy eṣa sarvasya cetaḥ
karṣaty arvāg api tad anugaḥ suṣṭhu saṅkarṣaṇākhyaḥ ||GC_2,5.27|| (mandākrāntā)
children.translated_text:
'Who can speak of the supreme glory of their love?
See — our minds have followed him and abandoned [everything else]!
For this <s>Govinda</s>, even with a luster born of exertion, draws everyone's heart
close — and his faithful attendant, well named <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, likewise!' ||GC_2,5.27||

children.text:
kruddhaṃ śatrum abhidravann api hariḥ smerān anābje rasol-
lāsād gharma-jalaṃ dadhad vilasati svāṃ saumyatām atyajan |
yad rāmaḥ sphuṭa-śoṇa-netra-vadnas tat-kopataḥ śobhate
tac cāsya prakṛtir yad eṣa sa hareḥ sākṣāt pratāpānalaḥ ||GC_2,5.28|| (śārdūla)

ete śrī-vasudeva-nanda-valitāḥ śrī-devakī-saṃhatāḥ
sarve sādhu-janāś ca mādṛśa-girā dīptāntara-jvālayā |
yasmāt tīvra-nibhālanaṃ vidadhataḥ kṣubhyanti kaṃse muhus
tasmād asya vināśa eva ciratā-bhānaṃ vinā setsyati ||GC_2,5.29|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
'These — the followers of Śrī <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Nanda</s>, the companions of Śrī <s>Devakī</s>,
and all virtuous people too, and those like us with our words and blazing inner flames —
since they become agitated repeatedly at <s>Kaṃsa</s> while gazing intently,
therefore his destruction alone, without delay of long duration, shall be accomplished.' ||GC_2,5.29||

children.text:
atha tat-prabhāvam anubhavatāṃ kaṃse doṣa-śaṃsaṇaṃ, yathā-
so'yaṃ mūrkhaḥ svāntare bhīta eva
nyāsthan mallān yaḥ purastān murāreḥ |
yadvad vyādhaḥ ko'pi saṅgopitātmā
siṃhasyāgre nyasyati grāma-siṃhān ||GC_2,5.30|| (śālinī)
children.translated_text:
Now, the declaration of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> fault by those who experienced their power, as follows —
'This very fool, inwardly fearful himself,
who stationed wrestlers before <s>Murāri</s> —
is like some hunter who, concealing himself,
places village-lions before a [real] lion!' ||GC_2,5.30||

children.text:
yaḥ pūtanādi-balam asya nināya nāśaṃ
yaḥ śakra-garvam api kharvayati sma sarvam |
yaḥ sarva-sarjakam amūmuhad ūha-varjaṃ
taṃ bhoja-rāḍ abhibhavan kila bāḍham īṣṭe ||GC_2,5.31|| (vasanta-tilaka)
children.translated_text:
'He who brought the forces of <s>Pūtanā</s> and others to destruction,
who humbled even the pride of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) completely,
who bewildered even the creator of all, beyond conjecture —
the <s>Bhoja</s> king thinks he can overpower him — truly!' ||GC_2,5.31||

children.text:
kva kṛṣṇaḥ sva-prakāśātmā malla-saṅghaḥ kva tāmasaḥ |
yuddhaṃ paśyānayoś citraṃ tejas timirayor iva ||GC_2,5.32|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'Where is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, self-luminous — and where is the host of wrestlers, shrouded in darkness?
Behold the wondrous battle between these two — as between light and darkness!' ||GC_2,5.32||

children.text:
saṅgharṣe'pi mithaḥ spṛṣṭir nekṣyate kṛṣṇa-mallayoḥ |
ādyasya śakti-vaiśiṣṭyāt tejas timirayor iva ||GC_2,5.33|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'Even in their mutual clash, no contact is seen between <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the wrestler —
due to the superiority of the former's power — just as between light and darkness!' ||GC_2,5.33||

children.text:
ucchūnatvaṃ kṣatajam api na prekṣyate dveṣi-gātre
daityārāter na yad udayate kaścid auddhatya-leśaḥ |
paśyāmuṣya dviṣad abhimukhaṃ vīrya-varyaṃ viṣābhaṃ
bhedaṃ bhedaṃ dviṣi nikhilakaṃ marma cūrṇaṃ cakāra ||GC_2,5.34|| (mandākrāntā)
children.translated_text:
'Neither swelling nor blood is seen on the body of the foe of the enemy of the gods;
nor does the slightest trace of arrogance arise in him.
Behold — his valor, supreme, poison-like, directed toward the adversary,
breaking every vital point of the enemy, has reduced [him] to powder!' ||GC_2,5.34||

children.text:
sūkṣāgnis tṛṇa-maṇḍale pavir age kumbhāṅgajaḥ sāgare
caṇḍāṃśus timire tathā mura-ripor nāmāpi sarvāṃhasi |
tadvan nanda-sutaḥ sa eṣa vijayī raṅga-sthalāntar mahā-
sāra-sphāra-kadaṅga-saṅgha-balite malle puraḥ prekṣyatām ||GC_2,5.35|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
'As a subtle fire in a heap of straw, as a thunderbolt before a clay-bodied elephant, as a river in the ocean,
as the fierce sun in darkness — so is even the mere name of the enemy of <s>Mura</s> against all sin.
Likewise, this very son of <s>Nanda</s>, that victorious one in the arena —
before the wrestler, fortified by the mass of formidable <s>kadaṅga</s> [weapons] — behold him!' ||GC_2,5.35||

children.text:
atra kṛṣṇasya saṃgrāme dṛśyatāṃ paramādbhutam |
cāṇūraḥ pīḍyate tena bukkā kaṃsasya bhidyate ||GC_2,5.36|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'Here behold the supremely wondrous thing in <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> battle —
<s>Cāṇūra</s> is being crushed by him, while <s>Kaṃsa's</s> chest is being split!' ||GC_2,5.36||

children.text:
mūḍhas tathāpy asau vajra-muṣṭibhyāṃ harim ārdayat |
sa tābhyāṃ hṛdi lagnābhyāṃ san-madāt pulakaṃ dadhe ||GC_2,5.37|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'Yet that fool struck <s>Hari</s> with thunderbolt-fists;
he (<s>Hari</s>), with those [fists] clinging to his chest, bore horripilation from true delight!' ||GC_2,5.37||

children.text: tad evaṃ sa-paridevanaṃ sa-devanaṃ ca loke vilokamāne,-
children.translated_text: Thus, while the world watched — with lamentation and with sport —

children.text:
athāgrahīd dharir api taṃ sakṛd dhasann
abibhraman nabhasi ca yaṃ nibhālayan |
uvāca dhiṅ mṛta iti vāḍha-rīḍhayāpy
apothayad bhuvi nṛpateḥ prapaśyataḥ ||GC_2,5.38|| (rucirā)
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Hari</s> too seized him, laughing just once,
spun him in the sky while gazing at him,
said 'Shame — die!' and with intense contempt
hurled him to the ground while the king watched! ||GC_2,5.38||

children.text:
muṣṭikenāstayā muṣṭyā tuṣtiṃ labdhavataḥ sa ca |
balasya tala-ghātaṃ yan prāṇa-ghātam apadyata ||GC_2,5.39|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
And by <s>Muṣṭika</s>, by that very fist,
<s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), having obtained satisfaction,
gave a palm-strike which became a death-blow! ||GC_2,5.39||

children.text:
agre vyagratayāṅga-saṅgham abhitaḥ samyag rayāt kampayann
ugrampaśyatayākṣi-yugmam asakṛt kṣiptī-kṛtaṃ kṣobhayan |
rāma-śyāmala-nāma-kāla-dalitaḥ kaṃsasya vartmādiśan
drāṅ mallaḥ sa sa lokam anyam agamad viśvatra citraṃ diśi ||GC_2,5.40|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
Trembling his assembled limbs on all sides with speed from the agitation of rushing forward at the enemy,
repeatedly casting and agitating his pair of fierce-looking eyes,
shattered by the name of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Śyāmala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) as [the name of] Death, pointing the way for <s>Kaṃsa</s> —
that wrestler departed to the other world, a marvel in every direction! ||GC_2,5.40||

children.text:
krīḍāṃ kṛtvātha tābhyāṃ baka-dalana-balau tatra vijñāya nāti-
pravīṇāṃ tāv avajñā-valitam akiratāṃ kṣauṇi-pṛṣṭhe yadā tu |
tarhy āgāt kūṭa-nāmā ya iha śala-yutas tośalo yaś ca taṃ taṃ
sadyo vāmāṅghri-hasta-praharaṇa-dalitī-kṛtya nṛtyaṃ vyadhattām ||GC_2,5.41|| (sragdharā)
children.translated_text:
Then, having sported, when those two, knowing the strength of <s>Baka's</s>-crusher,
found [the opponents] not very skilled and tossed them scornfully upon the earth's surface —
then came the one named <s>Kūṭa</s> ('Deceit'), armed with a lance, and also <s>Tośala</s> —
each of them was instantly shattered by the striking of [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] left foot and hand, and he danced! ||GC_2,5.41||

children.text: athāpareṣāṃ mallānāṃ samudāyena samaṃ samam api samudāyaṃ kartuṃ samudāyam eva menāte | [48] te tu,-
children.translated_text: Then, with the remaining group of wrestlers, they thought it fitting to engage the crowd simultaneously with the crowd. [48] But they —

children.text:
hateṣu teṣu malleṣu śṛgālīm āgatāḥ pare |
paśyato hāsayāmasuḥ kṛṣṇa-rāma-pradhānakān ||GC_2,5.42|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'When those wrestlers were slain, the remaining ones,
having assumed the behavior of jackals,
made the champions led by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> laugh
while they watched!' ||GC_2,5.42||

children.text:
jetuṃ prasthāpitāḥ prāk tridivam api mayā tvatka-senādhināthās
tadvat prasthāpya nāgaṃ nṛpa tava racitās tat-kṛte cādya mallāḥ |
evaṃ tad-vartma-saukhyaṃ tava viracayatā nandataḥ svīya-mitraiḥ
krīḍā kāryeti kaṃsaṃ sadasi kila diśaṃs tatra cikrīḍa kṛṣṇaḥ ||GC_2,5.43|| (sragdharā)
children.translated_text:
'Previously, I dispatched your army-commanders to conquer the triple heaven;
likewise, O king, having dispatched the elephant, and now your wrestlers fashioned for his sake —
thus arranging the ease of that [heavenly] path for you and your rejoicing friends —
"a sport must be played!" — thus addressing <s>Kaṃsa</s> in the assembly, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> sported there!' ||GC_2,5.43||

children.text:
bhrātror vikrīḍitor mitrair madhye madhye parājayaḥ |
tān hatvā paśya kaṃsasya svāntaṃ saṃkrāntavān muhuḥ ||GC_2,5.44|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'While the two brothers played with their friends, defeats occurred intermittently;
slaying those [opponents] — behold — [the defeat] repeatedly passed into <s>Kaṃsa's</s> own heart!' ||GC_2,5.44||

children.text:
tad evaṃ maitreyikayā citrīyamāṇau dhanyena cātur-varṇyena nirvaṇyamānau samāna-mānau sa-vayasaḥ saṃmānayamānau rāma-rāmānuja-nāmānau dyāv-āpṛthivy-anavadya-vādya-vidyām anuvidya-pramodād vidyotamānau divya-nṛtya-pratimallatayā labdha-malla-tālamānau tat-parvaṇaḥ sarvataḥ samāhṛta-vimānau sumanobhiḥ
sumanobhiḥ kṛtamānau ghaṭikām ekām akhilān ekāyanān nirmamatuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, while being made marvelous by friendly sport, while being extolled by the blessed fourfold assembly, the two of equal honor honoring their age-fellows — named <s>Rāma</s> and the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> — shining forth with the delight of mastering the art of music, blameless between heaven and earth, having obtained the rhythm and measure of wrestling through divine dance-wrestling, honored by flowers and by [delighted] minds, from vehicles assembled from all directions at that festival — they made all [beings] single-pointed for one <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes).

children.text: tad asahamānaḥ sahamānaḥ kaṃsas tu draviṇa-balayor eka-paryāyatayevābhedam ālaksya gopa-draviṇa-haraṇādi-lakṣaṇa-vaksyamāṇa-nija-vacaḥ-pracāraṇa-lakṣyataḥ savya-hastasya dvi-tra-vāram astatayā sva-vāditraṃ niṣiṣedha |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kaṃsa</s>, unable to bear [it yet] bearing [it], perceiving the inseparability of wealth and strength as being of one category — from the aim of propagating his own words, whose mark was the planned seizure of the cowherds' wealth and such — gestured with his left hand two or three times to silence his own musicians.

children.text: tatra ca niṣiddhe siddheśvara-vāditre tu śuddhatayā siddhe tadīddhe hitatayā sahitaṃ sakhi-varga-sahitatayā ca valgu yad avalgad yac ca vraja-devaṃ vasudevam ugrasenam apy uddiśya tasya tat tad ugraṃ vacanam aśṛṇot tad dvayam api sva-cchidra-bādhāya lakṣyaṃ vidhāya sahasā sahasānanatayā paryak plavamānaḥ svairī kaṃsa-vairī | tasmād akasmāt kaṃsa-mañcopary eva paryaikṣata |
children.translated_text: And there, when the forbidden instrument of the lord of <s>Siddhas</s> had been stopped, yet the purified one had been accomplished, and in the ardor of that [contest] — together with the company of friends in accompaniment — the charming [sport] that leapt forth, and the fierce words that he heard directed toward the lord of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>), <s>Vasudeva</s>, and <s>Ugrasena</s> too — taking both of those as the target for the obstruction of his own vulnerabilities, suddenly, with the swiftness of his own prowess surging on all sides, the independent foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — from that [point] unexpectedly — cast his gaze upon the very platform of <s>Kaṃsa</s>!

children.text: yatra kaṃsena saha tena suduḥsahaṃ śrī-harer vigraha-teja eva vigraha-karam āsīt | atha samupāgata-dhvaṃsaḥ kaṃsaś ca svaṃ parājayamānāt tasmāt parājayamāna-manā dhairyaṃ hitvā khaḍga-carmaṇī gṛhītvā yad vicacāra, tenāpi durdharṣaḥ sa-harṣa-gatiḥ sa eṣa vraja-kula-gatis tat-keśa-grāhitā-nirvāhitāṃ katham avāpa, tat khalv asāv api boddhuṃ śaśāda-vaśatāpannaḥ śaśavan na śaśāka |
children.translated_text: Where, together with <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the very battle-radiance of glorious <s>Hari</s> became the cause of the conflict — truly unbearable. Then <s>Kaṃsa</s>, whose destruction had arrived, with a mind being defeated by that one who was defeating him, abandoning courage and seizing sword and shield, when he moved about — even by that, the invincible one, moving with joyful gait, he — the refuge of the <s>Vraja</s> clan — how he attained the fulfillment of seizing him by the hair — that indeed even he [<s>Kaṃsa</s>], having fallen under the power of a hare-like [fate], could not comprehend, like a hare.

children.text: lokas tu tad idaṃ ślokayāmāsa,-
children.translated_text: And the world versified this as follows:

children.text:
śyenaḥ kapotam iva pañcamukhaḥ karīndraṃ
vajro giriṃ vikira-rāṭ kaṭukād raveyam |
kaṃsaṃ nigṛhya sahasā vaśayan sa eṣa
krīḍāṃ karoti paritaḥ pṛthum añcam añcan ||GC_2,5.45|| (vasanta-tilaka)
children.translated_text: 'As a hawk [seizes] a pigeon, as the five-faced one (<s>Śiva</s>) [seizes] the lord of elephants, as a thunderbolt [strikes] a mountain, as the king of <s>Vikiras</s> [crushes] a harsh enemy — | seizing <s>Kaṃsa</s> suddenly, subduing him, this very one sports, bounding with great leaps on all sides!' || (GC 2,5.45)

children.text: tad evaṃ loke kṛta-śloke hariṇā gṛhīta-keśaḥ sa bhojeśaḥ prāṇānām ardhaṃ pūrvaṃ mumoca, nijāghrātatayā mañcād avāñcaṃs tv ardham iti harir api tac chīghratāṃ boddhuṃ yoddhu-manastā-vaśān na śaśāka |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the world had composed its verse, the lord of the <s>Bhojas</s>, seized by the hair by <s>Hari</s>, first released half of his life-breaths, but while falling face-down from the platform due to being dragged — as for the other half — even <s>Hari</s>, due to the mental state of one eager to fight, could not perceive the swiftness of that [death].

children.text:
kaṃsasya keśā hariṇā vikṛṣṭāḥ
prāṇāś ca tan muṣṭi-gatā babhūvuḥ |
citraṃ na cedaṃ smara tasya bālye
tat pūtanā-stanya-vikarṣaṇaṃ ca ||GC_2,5.46|| (indravajrā)
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṃsa's</s> hair was pulled by <s>Hari</s>, and his life-breaths came into the grasp of that fist; | this is no wonder — remember, in his childhood, that pulling at the breast of <s>Pūtanā</s> too!' || (GC 2,5.46)

children.text:
patat-khaḍga-carmā galad-ratna-varmā
bhramat-sarva-keśaḥ skhalan-mūrdha-veśaḥ |
sa mañcād adhastāj janānāṃ purastād
anenādhirūḍhaḥ papātātimūḍhaḥ ||GC_2,5.47|| (bhujaṅga-prayātā)
children.translated_text: 'With falling sword and shield, with slipping jeweled armor, | with all his hair whirling about, with his head-ornament tumbling — | he fell from the platform, before the people, downward, | mounted upon by this one — he fell, utterly bewildered!' || (GC 2,5.47)

children.text:
prāg āsīt stabdha-pakṣmā bhayam anu sa yathā tadvad eva pramītaḥ
kaṃso'yaṃ tena mṛtyuṃ gata iti nikhilair bhīrubhir nābhyabhāṣi |
śrī-kṛṣṇas tat-pratītaṃ sapadi viracayan hastivat siṃha-varyaḥ
sāvajñaṃ taṃ visaṃjñaṃ sadasi tata itaḥ kṣmāṃ ca karṣaṃś cakarṣa ||GC_2,5.48|| (sragdharā)
children.translated_text: 'Before, he had been with unblinking eyelids from fear, and in exactly that same way he was slain — | this <s>Kaṃsa</s> has gone to death — thus it was not said by any of the frightened ones; | glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, immediately manifesting the evidence of that, like a supreme lion with an elephant, | contemptuously dragged that senseless one here and there across the ground in the assembly!' || (GC 2,5.48)

children.text:
tato jaya-jaya-dhvani-prasita-vādya-kolāhala-
prasūna-ghana-vṛṣṭi-yuk-stuti-divas pṛthivy-āspadaiḥ |
kṛta-pramada-vardhanaḥ sapadi kaṃsa-cid-vardhanaś
ciraṃ nija-ganārcitaḥ sthagita-buddhir āsīd asau ||GC_2,5.49|| (pṛthvī)
children.translated_text: 'Then, on the day resounding with cries of 'Victory! Victory!', the clamor of instruments, | showers of dense divine flowers, and hymns of praise by the earth-dwellers — | the increaser of delight, the destroyer of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> consciousness, | long worshipped by his own people, was himself stupefied [with emotion]!' || (GC 2,5.49)

children.text:
kaṃsa-dhvaṃsana-śaṃsana-prathana-bhṛd gīrvāṇa-gīr-bāndhava-
dyovādyottama-gandha-sandha-kusumāsārārcir-abhyarcitaḥ |
bhūmi-sthāpy atibhūmita-gatam aho bhūmā tadā bhūyasā-
nanda-syanda-bhareṇa bhāvitatayā hārī harir bhāvyatām ||GC_2,5.50|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text: 'Bearing the proclamation of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> destruction, worshipped by the celestials' speech-companions | with the best of divine instruments, choice fragrances, heaps of flowers, and showers of offerings and lights — | grounded on the earth yet transcending all earthly measure — ah! — with abundance | of the flood of the flow of bliss, may <s>Hari</s>, the captivating one, be contemplated!' || (GC 2,5.50)

children.text: tataś ca,
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text:
yadā kaṅkādayo bhrātur nirveśāyātra saṃyayuḥ |
sāhāyyāya tadā rāmaḥ parigheṇārdati sma tān ||GC_2,5.51|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Kaṅka</s> and the others came to avenge their brother, | then <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) tormented them with his iron mace!' || (GC 2,5.51)

children.text: atha hari-vaṃśādi-miśrībhūta-śrī-bhāgavata-mata-prabhūtatayā kathāṃ prathayiṣyāmaḥ | [56] yathā- tad evaṃ śrīmān govindaḥ svayaṃ nanditvā śrīman-nandarājena sākaṃ vindamānaṃ śrīmad-ānakadundubhiṃ vanditvā taṃ mocayitvā sarvān api rocayitvā śrī-devakīm apy anusandhāya tathā sandhāya gṛhāya bṛhan-mahilābhiḥ saha samvidhāya yathā-sandham anyān api labdha-sambandhān dhṛtānandān vidhāya kaṃsena kṛta-bandhanasya hṛta-dhanasya taj-janakasya mocanārtham api janān abhidhāya mataṅgaja-vrajenāpi kraṣṭuṃ suṣṭhu-duṣkaraṃ kaṃsa-kalevaram īṣat-karatayā vāma-kareṇa kaca-nikare vikṛṣya tad-vartma-parikhāṃ pari parihṛṣyal loka-sārthāvṛta-pitṛ-dvayānugantṛkatayā viśrānti-tīrtham anu viśrāntim avāpa |
children.translated_text: Now we shall extend the narrative in accordance with the authority of the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> intermixed with the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> and other [texts]. [56] As follows: thus the glorious <s>Govinda</s>, having himself rejoiced, having reverenced the glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) who was being found together with the glorious king of <s>Nanda</s>, having freed him, having delighted all, having also sought out glorious <s>Devakī</s> and arranged [her welfare] likewise, having provided for the household together with the great women, having duly arranged all other kinsmen who had obtained their connections and held fast to joy, having also dispatched people for the liberation of the father of that one [<s>Kaṃsa</s>] whose bondage had been made and whose wealth had been seized — with slight effort, by his left hand alone, he dragged the corpse of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, which was supremely difficult to drag even by a troop of lordly elephants, pulling it by the mass of hair, and following the path of its moat, accompanied by the caravan of jubilant people and followed by both parents, he attained rest at the place of repose.

children.text: tad anu saṅkarṣaṇādayaś ca kaṅka-mukhān saṅkarṣantaḥ sarveṣāṃ harṣaṃ varṣantaḥ kṛta-karṣa-prāṇānām amitrāṇāṃ parṣadaṃ cakruḥ |
children.translated_text: Thereupon, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and the others, dragging out the <s>Kaṅka</s>-headed ones, showering joy upon all, made an assembly of enemies whose life-breaths had been ploughed out.

children.text: paraspara-pradhane nidhanaṃ gatān bhuvar-lokāt patitān kravyādān lokān iva yān sabhyāḥ paśyanti sma | tad evaṃ sthite sādhūnāṃ manasi ca susthite |
children.translated_text: Those who had perished in mutual combat, fallen from the <s>Bhuvar</s>-world — the members of the assembly beheld them as if they were carrion-eating beings from [infernal] worlds. Thus, when matters stood thus and the minds of the virtuous were well-settled:

children.text:
śrīman-nanda-mahāśayā drutataraṃ prasthāpayan yaṃ naraṃ
goṣṭhaṃ kaṃsa-vināśa-śaṃsana-kṛte prāgād ayaṃ tad yadā |
tasmāt tarhi na kevalāḥ sukhamayā vādya-svanās tāṃ purīm
āptāḥ kintu janāś ca kecid iha ye tad yaugapadyaṃ yayuḥ ||GC_2,5.52|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text: 'The man whom the glorious great-souled <s>Nanda</s> most swiftly dispatched | to the cow-settlement for proclaiming the destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — when he went thither, | then not only did joyous sounds of instruments reach that city, | but certain people from here too arrived there simultaneously!' || (GC 2,5.52)

children.text:
tataś ca mṛta-priyatayānanusaṃhita-saṃhanana-kriyatām āpannāḥ kaṃsādi-striyas tatrāgatya gaty-antara-rahitāḥ sva-sva-paty-aṅgam āśliṣya dviṣyamāṇa-nija-prānā rodanaṃ
kurvāṇā rodanaṃ vijahus tathā tan mātaraś ca kātaratām avāpuḥ | tatra ca-
children.translated_text: Then, the wives of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and others, having attained the state of not composing their bodily arrangements due to the death of their beloved, arrived there bereft of any other recourse, and embracing the bodies of their respective husbands, despising their own life-breaths, they commenced weeping and then ceased weeping — and their mothers too attained a state of distress. And there:

children.text:
cihnāni dayita-ghnāni nihnuvānāḥ purābhavan |
kaṃsa-striyaḥ śugārtyā tad vyaktyāmārjan hriyaṃ hareḥ ||GC_2,5.53|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'The wives of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who had formerly concealed | the signs of the slayer of their beloved, | through the distress of sorrow now openly | wiped away the shame of <s>Hari</s>!' || (GC 2,5.53)

children.text:
tathāpi-
rodanaṃ sapadi rodanaṃ tathā
tan niśamya ca niśāmya cājitaḥ |
svaṃ sa-tāpam avamatya satya-kṛt
tāḥ sa-sāntvam abhito'py asāntvayat ||GC_2,5.54|| (rathoddhatā)
children.translated_text: 'Lamentation upon lamentation, and likewise | hearing that and perceiving it, the unconquered one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), | disregarding his own anguish, being true to his word, | consoled them on all sides with solace!' || (GC 2,5.54)

children.text:
sāntvayann apy amūḥ kṛṣṇo na vipade sva-sāntvanam |
iti tatra niyujyānyān ninyus taṃ yadavaḥ puram ||GC_2,5.55|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'Even while consoling them, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> did not [employ] his own consolation for [his own] misfortune; | thus, appointing others for that purpose there, the <s>Yādavas</s> led him to the city.' || (GC 2,5.55)

children.text: yatra ca puryantar-upaplavaṃ vyājam ācaritavantaḥ | yadā cākrūraṃ sva-gṛhāya ninīṣantaṃ niṣidhyan nīti-vidhy-agraṇir nijāvaraja-gṛham eva vraja-rājaḥ sāgrajaṃ taṃ nināya, upaveśayāmāsa ca; yathā-
children.translated_text: Where they enacted the pretext of turmoil within the city. And when <s>Akrūra</s>, wishing to take [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] to his own house, was refused — the foremost knower of statecraft, the king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>), led him together with his elder brother to his own younger brother's house, and seated him. As follows:

children.text:
madhye kṛṣṇaṃ rāmam apy atra kṛtvā
pārśva-dvandve śauri-nandāvabhūtām |
agre vyagrā yādava-prāgrya-lokās
te saṅgataṃ suṣṭhu sammardam āpuḥ ||GC_2,5.56|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'Having placed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s> too in the center, | <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) and <s>Nanda</s> were on the two sides; | before them, the foremost <s>Yādava</s> folk [gathered] eagerly — | they obtained a thorough meeting with great crowding!' || (GC 2,5.56)

children.text:
dvayaṃ tan-melanāyāsīd aśeṣāṇāṃ tad-agrataḥ |
jyāyasāṃ gopa-bhū-bhartā gāndineyaḥ kanīyasām ||GC_2,5.57|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'For the meeting with those two, all without exception came before them; | the king of the cowherd-land (<s>Nanda</s>) [represented] the elders, <s>Gāndinī's</s> son (<s>Akrūra</s>) the younger ones.' || (GC 2,5.57)

children.text:
atha taṃ kaṃsa-dārādi-rodanaṃ santānataḥ santaptam eva santaṃ śrīmantaṃ
putrāparādha-rāhu-kalita-mukha-vidhu-śri-rāhukaḥ saṅgatya gaty-antara-rahitaḥ sva-
hita-sahitaḥ kanaka-daṇḍa-lakṣita-kṣitipa-maṇḍana-maṇdalam agrato nidhāya
mūrdhānam avāgraṃ vidhāya tasthau |
children.translated_text: Then, him (<s>Ugrasena</s>) — continuously scorched by the lamentation of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> wives and others, being saintly indeed — <s>Rāhuka</s> (<s>Ugrasena</s>), whose moon-like glory of face was eclipsed by the <s>Rāhu</s> of his son's offense, came to meet [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], bereft of any other recourse, accompanied by what was beneficial to himself, and placing before him the circle of earth-ruling ornaments marked by golden staffs, bowing his head downward, he stood.

children.text: taṃ punar avadhāya śrīman-nanda-sahitānakadundubhir uttasthau | utthitayoś ca tayo rāma-rāmānujāv api tādṛg-avasthau babhūvatur anubabhūvatuś ca so'yam iti | anubhūya ca vidūya bhūya-sādareṇa sambhūya dareṇa dhūyamānam amūm ugrasena-nāmānaṃ praṇāma-puraḥsaratayā purata eva niveśanayā puraś cakratuḥ |
children.translated_text: And seeing him, the glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) together with <s>Nanda</s> rose. And as those two rose, <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāma's</s> younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) too attained a similar state and recognized 'This is that very one.' And having recognized him, dispelling [his grief], again joining him with heightened respect, gently, they placed this one named <s>Ugrasena</s> — whose [frame] was trembling — before them with a reverential bow as precedent, and seated him in front.

children.text: sa tu suta-sutatāparādha-sambādha-saṅkocataḥ śocann idam avocata,-
children.translated_text: And he, grieving from the constriction caused by the oppression of his son's and grandson's offense, spoke thus:

children.text:
yadyapi mantu-vidhātuḥ
svajanaḥ sujane'bhidhātum arhen na |
tarhy apy ananya-gatitā
balavaty etaṃ pralāpayati ||GC_2,5.58|| (āryā)
children.translated_text: 'Even though a kinsman of the offender | ought not to speak thus to the virtuous — | nevertheless, the powerful state of having no other refuge | makes this one prattle thus!' || (GC 2,5.58)

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- kāmam ādiśyatām |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'By all means, let your command be spoken!'

children.text: ugrasena uvāca,-
children.translated_text: <s>Ugrasena</s> said:

children.text:
sa evādhipatir bhūmyāṃ yas tāmasa-vināśanaḥ |
vidhvasta-śārvarād bhānor anyaḥ kaḥ syād aharpatiḥ ? ||GC_2,5.59|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'He alone is the sovereign on earth who is the destroyer of darkness; | other than the sun, who has dispelled the night, who else could be the lord of the day?' || (GC 2,5.59)

children.text:
vṛddho yaḥ sa tu vṛddhānām eva vartmānuvartatām |
akula-kāla-javagaḥ kaḥ kuryāt pratikūlatām ? ||GC_2,5.60|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text: 'And he who is old — let the old ones follow his very path; | who, being overcome by the velocity of untimely calamity, would commit opposition?' || (GC 2,5.60)

children.text: tasmād idaṃ chatrādikaṃ svena satrā kriyatām iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, let this umbrella and other [royal insignia] be taken up by you of your own accord!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- rājaṃs tava tanūjasya mad-vihita-vināśanatā sarvair eva niśāmitā | katham iva tām anyathayāni ? kintu mama tan nāśanatāyām upalakṣaṇatā paraṃ lakṣyate; yasmād bhavad-vidha-viṣayakāparādha-maya-kāla eva tatra paraṃ kāraṇam | mayā tu labdha-buddhi-balatayā sva-vaśāyām api daśāyāṃ jñātam api tad vairam avajñātam | bālya-daśāyāṃ tat kila na jñātam eva, tathāpi tena pūtanādi-yūthaṃ kramaśaḥ prasthāpitam, tādṛśa-kālenaiva ca saṃsthāpitam | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'O King, the destruction of your son brought about by me has been witnessed by all. How could I make that otherwise? Rather, in his destruction, it is only my role as an instrument that is observed; for the very time that was full of offenses toward one such as you — that was the paramount cause. And by me, having obtained the strength of understanding through my own power, even in a situation within my control, that enmity, though known, was disregarded. In the state of childhood, that [enmity] was indeed not even known; nevertheless, by him [<s>Kaṃsa</s>], the troop beginning with <s>Pūtanā</s> was dispatched in sequence, and by that very kind of time [i.e., fate], it was also brought to an end. Thus:

children.text:
stanyān māṃ tudatī bakī khala-marut karṣaṃś chalāt saṃharan
vatsākhyo nigiran bako mayaja-nirvicchedayan mitrakaiḥ |
bhuñjānaḥ sa-gaṇaṃ phaṇī hṛta-balaṃ kurvan pralambaḥ sa ca
ghnantu kṣmā-turago gilan svayam anaśyad dūṣaṇaṃ kiṃ mama? ||GC_2,5.61|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text: '<s>Pūtanā</s> pricking me at the breast, the evil wind-[demon] (<s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>) dragging and deceitfully destroying [me], | the one named <s>Vatsa</s> (<s>Vatsāsura</s>) swallowing [me], <s>Baka</s> (<s>Bakāsura</s>) severing [me] with friend-illusions (<s>Mayāsura's</s> kin), | the serpent (<s>Kāliya</s>) consuming [me] together with my company, <s>Pralamba</s> stealing <s>Bala's</s> strength, | the earth-horse (<s>Keśī</s>) striking, [the python <s>Agha</s>] swallowing of its own accord — yet the fault (<s>Dūṣaṇa</s>) was not destroyed — what blame is mine?' || (GC 2,5.61)

children.text:
yo'yaṃ vā tanayas tava svayam asāv akrūrakaṃ preṣayan
mām ānāyya nighātayan kuvalayāpīḍena mallaiḥ punaḥ |
yuṣmat-kutsana-bhartsana-śravaṇa-jān mantor mayā bhīruṇā
prāyaścitta-kṛtā dhṛtaḥ kaca-taṭe tasmād akasmān mṛtaḥ ||GC_2,5.62|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text: 'Or this son of yours himself, sending <s>Akrūra</s>, | having brought me here, tried to have me killed — by <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> [the elephant], and again by the wrestlers; | hearing the censure and reproach directed at you [all], by me — a frightened one — | an act of atonement was performed: he was seized by the edge of his hair, and therefore unexpectedly died!' || (GC 2,5.62)

children.text:
tasmāt tasya sa-jātīya-vijātīya-bālaṅgilasya mātulāher māraṇam api tad-udyama-kāraṇam
eva jātam, na tu mad-īhāspadī-kṛtam | tathā ca sati katham iva rājyaṃ prājyatayā mahyaṃ rocatām?
children.translated_text: Therefore, the killing even of that maternal uncle — a serpent among maternal uncles, along with his various allies and adversaries — arose as a result of his own effort alone, and was not made the object of my intention. And that being so, how could kingship be pleasing to me in its fullness?

children.text:
sa eṣa cāvyabhicāri-saṅkalpasya mama saṅkalpaḥ pratikalpaṃ satya-vacasām api jalpa-
viṣayī-bhaviṣyati | yathā-
children.translated_text: And this resolve of mine — whose determination is unerring — shall become the subject of discourse even for the truthful, age after age. As follows:

children.text: ahaṃ sa eva go-madhye gopaiḥ saha vanecaraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I, that very one, shall wander in the midst of cows, together with cowherds, a forest-dweller,

children.text: prītimān vicariṣyāmi kāmacārī yathā gajaḥ ||GC_2,5.63||
children.translated_text: delighted, moving freely like an elephant!' || (GC 2,5.63)

children.text: etāvac chataśopy evaṃ satyenaiva bravīmi te |
children.translated_text: 'This much, even a hundredfold, I tell you truthfully:

children.text: na me kāryaṃ nṛpatvena vijñāpyaṃ kriyatām idam |
children.translated_text: I have no need for kingship — let this request be carried out!

children.text: bhavān mānyostu rājā me yadūnām agrajaḥ prabhuḥ [HV 78.35-37] iti ||GC_2,5.64||
children.translated_text: Let your honor be my king, the honored elder of the <s>Yadus</s>, the lord!' [HV 78.35-37] || (GC 2,5.64)

children.text:
tad evam asya sarve'pi suśīlatām anuśīlayantas tad etan mukha-mādhurya-puryamāṇa-
salila-kalila-vilocanāḥ kṣaṇa-katipayaṃ tad-avastham eva tasthuḥ | śrīmad-ānakadundubhy-ādayaḥ katipaye bibhyati sma | śrīman-nandādayas tu nandanti smeti sthite taṃ svataḥ parataś ca bhītam ālocayan punaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ prāha sma,- virāṭ-kulam idaṃ samprati virāḍ-jātam | tato yadi bhavān patitām imām urvīm urvī-patitām urīkurvīta, tadā dina-katipayaṃ vayam api sāhāyakam āhariṣyāmaḥ | na cet sadya eva gokulaṃ prapadya tad-anavadya-sukham abhimukham ānayiṣyāmaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, all of them contemplating his good nature, their eyes overflowing with tears brimming from the sweetness of his face, stood for a few moments in that very state. Glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) and some others were afraid. But glorious <s>Nanda</s> and the others rejoiced. And in that situation, observing him (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) frightened both from within and from without, glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again spoke: 'This <s>Virāṭ</s> dynasty has now become truly sovereign. Therefore, if you would accept this earth that has fallen — and become truly earthly — then for a few days we too shall furnish assistance. If not, we shall immediately return to <s>Gokula</s> and bring that blameless happiness into our presence.'

children.text:
tad evaṃ keśavasyābhiniveśataḥ sarveṣām apy anyathā kleṣatas taṃ bhojeśaṃ tūṣñīkām
eva puṣṇantaṃ śrī-gokula-prema-tṛṣṇaḥ so'yaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ svayam eva sa-nirbandhaṃ mukuṭa-bandha-bandhuraṃ karoti sma |
children.translated_text: Thus, due to <s>Keśava's</s> insistence, though it caused all others distress in a different way — that lord of the <s>Bhojas</s>, who only nurtured silence — this very glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, thirsting with love for glorious <s>Gokula</s>, himself forcefully performed the graceful binding of the crown upon him.

children.text:
taṃ prati sarveṇa samam agarveṇa mūrdhānam ānamya svayam asāv āvedayāmāsa,-
rājaṃs tasya vīra-gatiṃ gatasya satkāra-kāraṇaṃ bhavat-puraḥ-sarāḥ sarve'pi vayam anusarāmaḥ | śrīmat-pitarau tu labdha-śrama-visarau nija-nijāvāsam evāsīdatām iti | śrīdāmādīn prati ca jagāda- āvāṃ tāvat krūra-karmaṇi pratiruddhāv iti bhavanta eva
śrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇānugatim anubhavantaḥ śakaṭāvaroha evaṃ rātriṃ kṣipantu | iti |
children.translated_text: Bowing his head before everyone together without pride, he (<s>Kaṃsa's</s> successor) himself declared to him: 'O King! We all, led by your lordship, shall follow the cause of honoring the one who has attained the hero's end. But let the glorious parents, having found rest from their exertions, retire to their own respective abodes.' And to <s>Śrīdāman</s> and the others he said: 'We two are detained by this cruel business; therefore, you yourselves, attending upon the glorious parental feet, should descend to the cart-camp and thus spend the night.'

children.text:
tatas tathā vidhāya punar viśrāntiṃ sannidhāya taraṇibhis taraṇi-duhitur uttara-tīre
mṛta-kāyān nidhāya teṣāṃ preta-kāryaṃ saṃvidhāya śrīmad-ānakadundubhi-bhavanam
eva saha-rāmaḥ samājagāma |
children.translated_text: Then, having arranged matters thus, having rested, having placed the dead bodies on the further bank of the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) by means of boats, and having performed the funeral rites for them, he came together with <s>Rāma</s> to the very house of glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>).

children.text:
āgamya ca sarveṣām agamyaṃ tad-avarodham avarundhānaḥ sāvadhānam amū mātara-
pitarau namaś cakāra | kintu sva-prabhāvānubhavāl labdha-pitṛ-bhāvābhibhavāv ata
evāsambhavantau tatra-bhavantau tāv anubhūya dūyamāna iva tathā niveśayāmāsa |
yathāsmad vraja-rāja-dvandvavad eva nirdvandva-sadayatāmaya-hṛdayatayā taṃ bala-
valitaṃ tāv āliṅgantāv aliṅgavad bahu-samayam āsāte sma | yataḥ,
children.translated_text: Having arrived and penetrating that impenetrable inner chamber of all, he reverently bowed to those two — mother and father — with great attentiveness. But due to the experience of his own majesty, the two parents, overcome by parental emotion, were thus unable to compose themselves; perceiving this, he, as if pained, arranged them such that — just as with the royal couple of <s>Vraja</s> — with hearts made of unwavering compassion, those two, embracing him who was surrounded by the strength [of <s>Balarāma</s>], sat for a long time as if they were creepers [clinging to him]. Because:

children.text:
rasayati na hi yāvan mādhurīm asya tāvan
nayati manasi bhaktas tīvra-bhāvaṃ prabhāvam |
sa katham itarathā vā śrī-śukaḥ śaśvad etat
sphuṭa-madhurima-bhājaṃ śrī-vrajaṃ suṣṭhu nauti ||GC_2,5.65|| (mālinī)
children.translated_text:
For as long as a devotee does not taste his sweetness,
so long does he not bring the intense sentiment of [his] majesty to mind.
How else would glorious <s>Śuka</s> perpetually
praise so well glorious <s>Vraja</s>, the receptacle of manifest sweetness? ||GC_2,5.65|| (mālinī)

children.text:
atha śrīmad-ānakadundubhinā samaṃ bahir āgatya svayam evānusmṛtya bhṛtya-
vatsalaḥ śrī-vatsa-lakṣmā didṛkṣayā nirnimiṣa-pakṣmāḥ sarva-śarmada-yaśāḥ saṅkoca-
vaśāt pūrvaṃ dūrata eva labdha-nijālocana-pūram uddhava-māyād anugṛhīta-jana-dvārā
sānugrahaṃ gṛhād ājuhāva | tataś ca-
children.translated_text: Then, coming outside together with glorious <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>, the bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, affectionate toward his servants, of fame bestowing all bliss, with unblinking eyes from desire to see — he who, from restraint, had previously obtained from far away the fullness of his own gaze — through the agency of persons favored by <s>Uddhava's</s> <s>māyā</s>, graciously summoned [someone] from the house. And then —

children.text:
anyo'nyaṃ milati sma yarhy abhinavaṃ tarhi svayaṃ nāvidat
ko'haṃ kutra kadā ka eta iti sa preyān sa ca śrī-prabhuḥ |
kiṃ cādūra-gatāś ca tan na vividur yat tatra siddhāntitāṃ
ko gacchen nija-tattvam etad anayoḥ premā paraṃ vetti hi? ||GC_2,5.66|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
When that beloved one and that glorious Lord met each other anew,
then he himself did not know: 'Who am I? Where? When? Who are these?'
And those standing nearby also did not understand what was concluded there.
Who could reach the essence of these two? Only their love indeed knows the supreme [truth]! ||GC_2,5.66|| (śārdūlavikrīḍita)

children.text:
atha rāmeṇa samaṃ rāmānujaḥ sa-vyājam ānakadundubheḥ kiñcid antaritam añcann
amuñca na muñcan nāsīt | añcitvā ca śītalita-viraha-maya-sva-hṛdaya-vāpyākārayā nija-bāṣpa-dhārayā muhur api tan mukha-nirīkṣaṇa-pūrvaka-tad-āliṅgana-parvaṇi tam antaraṅgatayābhiṣiñcann ivālokyata |
children.translated_text: Then, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Rāma</s>, with a pretext, moving slightly apart from <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>, would not release him — nor was he not releasing. And having drawn close, with his own stream of tears — whose form resembled a pool cooling the viraha-filled heart — he appeared as if consecrating him again and again at every juncture of gazing upon that face and embracing him, with intimate affection.

children.text:
atha saha-rāmoddhavaḥ śrī-śūrodbhavam anujñāpya bhoja-rāja-gṛhaṃ prāpya kaṃsa-
patnīnāṃ bāṣpaṃ nirvāpya rāja-sabhāyām ugrasenaṃ saha-yādava-senam ānāyya tavaiva
rājyaṃ nyāyyam iti pratyāyya siṃhāsanaṃ svīkārya punaḥ śrī-śūra-janikāyyam āgatavān |
children.translated_text: Then, together with <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>, taking leave of the glorious one born of <s>Śūra</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), reaching the house of the <s>Bhoja</s> king, drying the tears of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> wives, bringing <s>Ugrasena</s> together with the <s>Yādava</s> army to the royal assembly, persuading them that 'The kingdom is rightfully yours,' accepting the throne, he again came to the house of the son of glorious <s>Śūra</s>.

children.text:
brahmāṇḍa-kotīśvaratāti-tucchā
yasyekṣyate viṣṇūpadeśitā ca |
sā tasya goloka-mahendra-sūnoḥ
kāmyā kathaṃ kaṃsaka-rājya-lakṣmīḥ? ||GC_2,5.67|| (indravajrā)
children.translated_text:
The sovereignty over crores of universes, instructed by <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself,
is seen as utterly trivial for him.
How then could the royal fortune of petty <s>Kaṃsa</s>
be desired by that son of the great <s>Indra</s> of <s>Goloka</s>? ||GC_2,5.67|| (indravajrā)

children.text:
atha samuddhava-lasad-uddhava-sahitābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ saha mahā-ratha-mūhyamāna-
manoratham āruhya sa punar ānakadundubhir vraja-mahī-patiṃ prati milanāya viśaṅkaṭaṃ tadīya-śakaṭa-vrajam ājagāma | āgamya ca gāḍhāliṅganatayā saṅgamya ramya-svajana-saṃvalitena tena tena saha parasparaṃ labdha-dhvaṃsa-kaṃsa-kṛta-caropadrava-vārtāṃ vartayāmāsa | vartayitvā ca punaḥ prārthayāmāsa,- yāvat sthitis tāvad asmad-gṛha eva sva-gṛha iva sarvaiḥ saha bhoktavyam iti |
children.translated_text: Then, mounting a great chariot that bewildered even the wishes of great warriors — together with those two accompanied by the brilliantly resplendent <s>Uddhava</s> — that <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> came to the expansive cart-encampment of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> for a meeting. Having arrived and met through tight embraces, he exchanged with each and every one — surrounded by their delightful kinfolk — the news of the destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the removal of the affliction he had caused. And having conversed, he further requested: 'As long as this stay lasts, all together with everyone should partake in our house just as in their own home.'

children.text: tataś ca pratidinam evaṃ nirvartamāne mahā-parvaṇi sa-rāmaḥ śrī-rāmānujaḥ palāyita-yādava-caya-samācayana-maya-nava-rājya-prājya-sthāpana-karma-samaye rāja-sabhāyāṃ śrī-vasudevasya sabhāyāṃ vā virājate sma | antarāntarā ca śakaṭāvaroham āsādya śrīdāmādya-nija-mitraiḥ saha vicitraṃ krīḍati sma iti |
children.translated_text: Then, as this great festival was being conducted day after day, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Rāma</s>, at the time of the establishment of the abundant new kingdom — the gathering of the scattered <s>Yādava</s> host — was present either in the royal assembly or in the assembly of glorious <s>Vasudeva</s>. And from time to time, going to the cart-camp, he sported in various ways with <s>Śrīdāman</s> and his other personal friends.

children.text: atha dina-kathāṃ samāpayataḥ snigdhakaṇṭhasya vacanaṃ yathā,-
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> concluded the day's narrative, his words were thus:

children.text:
kaṃsaṃ nihatavān yaḥ prāk so'yaṃ kroḍa-gatas tava |
dvīpāt pratyāgataṃ vittam ivaitaṃ paśya gopate ||GC_2,5.68|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
'He who previously slew <s>Kaṃsa</s> — that very one is now in your lap;
like wealth returned from an island — behold him thus, O lord of cowherds!' ||GC_2,5.68|| (anuṣṭubh)

children.text: atha tatra gatāyāṃ kathāyāṃ samāpta-prathāyāṃ paramānandinaḥ śrīmad-vraja-vandinas tad idaṃ paṭhanti sma,-
children.translated_text: Then, when the narrative had reached its end and its fame was complete, the supremely blissful worshippers of glorious <s>Vraja</s> recited this:

children.text:
jaya kṛta-mathurā-praveśa-bhāvuka | māthura-janatā-subhagam bhāvuka ||GC_2,5.
nānā-vilasita-nandita-nāgara | nagara-vadhū-jana-mohana-nāgara |
sa-vrajaka-kaṃsaka-vasanā-dāyaka | kṛta-ruci-vāyini nija-ruci-dāyaka ||GC_2,5.
bhakta-gaṇe dhṛta-karuṇā-pūraka | mālākāra-manoratha-pūraka ||GC_2,5.
tanu-tata-kubjā-candana-citraka | kubjā-vakrima-hṛti-kṛta-citraka ||GC_2,5.
kaṃsa-makha-sthita-dhanur-anuyojaka | nagara-janānāṃ sukha-śata-yojaka ||GC_2,5.
kaṃsa-dhanur makha-dhanur anubhaṅgada | tad-asahanoddhata-yoddhṛṣu bhaṅgada ||GC_2,5.
hastipam anu nija-vartma-sa-mardaka | tasmin dhṛta-ruṣi hasti-vimardaka ||GC_2,5.
bhrātrā saha kari-danta-vibhūṣaṇa | raṅgaṃ praviśan bhoja-vibhūṣaṇa ||GC_2,5.
gaja-raktādibhir aṅgaṃ paricita | bahu-vidha-bhāvair vividhaṃ paricita ||GC_2,5.
jagati samantād apratimallaka | kaṃsāgre hata-tat-prati-mallaka ||GC_2,5.
sadasi samaste nāsti samohana | malla-naṭana-kṛta-viśva-vimohana ||GC_2,5.
kaṃsaja-guru-nindana-kampākula | dṛṣṭi-vikīrṇa-dyuti-śampākula ||GC_2,5.
pluti-līlā-kṛta-mañca-kṣobhaka | krīḍā-vikrama-kaṃsa-kṣobhaka ||GC_2,5.
sahasā mañcāt kaṃsa-nipātaka | tena dhvasta-tri-jagat-pātaka ||GC_2,5.
akhila-janānāṃ duḥkha-vimokṣada | kaṃsasyāpi ca sahasā mokṣada ||GC_2,5.
mocita-vasudevādika-bandhaka | sādhu-sukhaṃ prati dhṛta-nirbandhaka ||GC_2,5.
viśrāntiṃ prati kaṃsākarṣaka | vyañjita-nija-bala-balayotkarṣaka ||GC_2,5.
kaṃsa-pitari-jita-rājya-nidhāyaka | nija-yaśasākhila-śarma-vidhāyaka |
vrajataḥ poṣyākhila-nistāraka | punar api ca vraja-sukha-vistāraka ||GC_2,5.
jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya | jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya ||GC_2,5. vīra ||GC_2,5.69||
children.translated_text:
Victory to him who made the entry into <s>Mathurā</s> auspicious! Who became the good fortune of the <s>Mathurā</s> populace, O auspicious one!
Who delighted the city-folk with various sports! O urbane one, enchanter of the city's womenfolk!
Who gave away garments along with the <s>Vraja</s>-folk and <s>Kaṃsa</s>! Who bestowed his own luster upon the one weaving beauty!
Who bore compassion's fullness toward the host of devotees! Who fulfilled the wishes of the garland-maker!
Whose body was painted with <s>Kubjā's</s> sandal-paste! Who astonished by stealing <s>Kubjā's</s> crookedness!
Who engaged <s>Kaṃsa's</s> sacrificial bow! Who yoked hundreds of joys for the city-folk!
Who broke <s>Kaṃsa's</s> bow, the sacrificial bow! Who routed the warriors enraged by its breaking!
Who crushed in his path the elephant-keeper! Who, maintaining fury, vanquished the elephant!
Who, with his brother, was adorned with elephant-tusks! O ornament of the <s>Bhojas</s>, entering the arena!
Whose body was marked with elephant-blood and such! Who was perceived in manifold ways through varied dispositions!
Matchless wrestler anywhere in the world! Who slew his challengers before <s>Kaṃsa</s>!
Whose enchantment was not [merely] in the entire assembly! Whose wrestler-dance bewildered the universe!
Agitated by the censure of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> father's teacher! Whose scattered gaze's splendor was like <s>Śampā</s>-lightning!
Who shook the platform by his leaping sport! Who terrified <s>Kaṃsa</s> by his playful valor!
Who suddenly hurled <s>Kaṃsa</s> from the platform! By whom the sins of the three worlds were destroyed!
Who bestowed release from sorrow upon all people! Who even granted <s>Kaṃsa</s> sudden liberation!
Who freed <s>Vasudeva</s> and others from bondage! Who held firm resolve toward the happiness of the righteous!
Who drew <s>Kaṃsa</s> toward rest! Who manifested the excellence of his own and <s>Bala's</s> strength!
Who bestowed upon <s>Kaṃsa's</s> father the conquered kingdom! Who, by his own fame, ordained all happiness!
Who delivers all dependents who depart from <s>Vraja</s>! And who again expands the happiness of <s>Vraja</s>!
Victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory! Victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory, victory! O Hero! ||GC_2,5.69||

children.text:
tad evaṃ kathakayoḥ kathayā vandināṃ vandana-prathayā ca labdhāvadhāna-poṣāḥ
śrī-kṛṣṇa-lābha-santata-santoṣāḥ sarve yathāsvaṃ tad-ānukūlya-sukham arjayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, through the narrative of the two narrators and through the worship of the panegyrists, all — having obtained nourishment of attention, continuously content with the gain of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — earned the happiness of conformity to him, each in their own way.

children.text:
atha labdha-prathāyāṃ rātri-kathāyāṃ śrī-rādhā-mādhavayor agrataḥ snigdhakaṇṭha
uvāca,- tad etat pramada-vṛtte sthite pratilavam api gokulaṃ prasthite ca tat-pradeśataḥ sandeśaḥ śrīmat-keśava-sadeśam āgataḥ, tatrānyeṣāṃ prātaḥ-prastotavyaḥ | samprati tu kaṃsa-pitari rājyārpaṇasya śravaṇataḥ kiñcid avāñcita-bhayamaya-cira-viraha-klamānāṃ
vraja-ramāṇām ati-nibhṛta-svasti-mukha-saṃbhṛtaḥ so'yam ākarṇyatām,-
children.translated_text: Then, when the night-narrative had gained its renown, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> spoke before glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>: 'Now that this matter of joy stands established and [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] has departed to <s>Gokula</s> even moment by moment, a message has come from that region to the place of glorious <s>Keśava</s> — to be related to the others in the morning.
