But now, born from the hearing of the bestowal of the kingdom upon <s>Kaṃsa's</s> father, [composed] from the deeply intimate well-wishing faces of the <s>Vraja</s> women — who were weary with the fear of a long, unwished-for separation — let this be heard:'

children.text:
virahas tava gopālīr
dayita mitho yāḥ sa-patnīś ca |
rañjayati sma samastāḥ
prāṇāt katham ahaha tā virañjayati? ||GC_2,5.70|| (udgīti)
children.translated_text:
'Your separation, O beloved, which once delighted the <s>gopīs</s>
and your co-wives with one another —
how, alas, does it now drain them of their very life-breath?' ||GC_2,5.70|| (udgīti)

children.text:
vipinaṃ sadanaṃ yāsāṃ
sadanaṃ vipinaṃ babhūva gopīnām |
tāsāṃ tvad-viyujāṃ kiṃ
mṛti-jīvanayor viparyayo na syāt? ||GC_2,5.71|| (gīti)
children.translated_text:
'The forest was the home, and the home became a forest
for those <s>gopīs</s>.
For those separated from you,
would there not be a reversal of death and life?' ||GC_2,5.71|| (gīti)

children.text:
yāsāṃ candana-candra-
prabhṛti ca vastu-pratāpanaṃ bhavati |
hari-rahitānāṃ tāsāṃ
vahniḥ kiṃ bata na śītatām ayitā? ||GC_2,5.72|| (gīti)
children.translated_text:
'For those to whom sandal-paste, moonlight,
and other such substances become scorching —
for those bereft of <s>Hari</s>,
would fire, alas, not become cooling?' ||GC_2,5.72|| (gīti)

children.text:
viśleṣas tava bhadraḥ
kleśaṃ sa hared bhavann eva |
āśā seyaṃ dhṛṣṭā
tvat-sṛṣṭā tatra vighnam ātanute ||GC_2,5.73|| (udgīti)
children.translated_text:
'Your separation is blessed —
may it remove affliction, being you yourself!
This hope is bold —
created by you, it extends an obstacle there.' ||GC_2,5.73|| (udgīti)

children.text:
bhavatā maryādārthaṃ
yaḥ khalu paryāpitaḥ kālaḥ |
kālaḥ sa bhavann agha-hara
lavaśaḥ kalpāya kalpate'smākam ||GC_2,5.74|| (udgīti) iti |
children.translated_text:
'The time that was appointed by you
for the sake of propriety —
that time, O destroyer of sin, being [so appointed],
each fraction becomes an age for us.' ||GC_2,5.74|| (udgīti) — thus.

children.text: atra cedaṃ śrī-rādhā-sakhīnāṃ tad anupadyamānaṃ padyam,-
children.translated_text: Here is the verse composed in response by the friends of glorious <s>Rādhā</s>:

children.text:
agha-hara viraha-vraṇatā
na hi naḥ kṛcchrāya tādṛśe śrayati |
rādhā-lavaṇim agalanaṃ
yadi valanaṃ tatra nāpi kurvīta ||GC_2,5.75|| (gīti)
children.translated_text:
'O destroyer of sin! The state of being wounded by separation
does not afflict us so much with hardship.
[What afflicts us is] if it were not to dissolve
the salt [of <s>Rādhā's</s> tears], nor cause [her] agitation there.' ||GC_2,5.75|| (gīti)

children.text: tatra kāraṇam anyad anyad astu, tad idaṃ tu mahad eva duḥsaham,-
children.translated_text: Let other reasons be what they may — but this itself is greatly unbearable:

children.text:
ānītaṃ ghṛta-pāyasānnam anayā kṛṣṇāya kiñcit tvayā
labdhavyaṃ śuka tan-mayā ca madhuraṃ nāmnā rutaṃ tanyatām |
itthaṃ prātar anūdya nityam api tāṃ rādhāṃ muhuḥ śārikā
vṛndāraṇya-nivāsinī madhupura-kṣmā-nātha totudyate ||GC_2,5.76|| (śārdūla)
children.translated_text:
'"This ghee-and-milk-rice food was brought by her for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; take some from you too,
O <s>Śuka</s>! And that sweet sound absorbed in him — let it be extended by name!" —
Thus instructing that <s>Rādhā</s> every morning as always, the <s>śārikā</s> (myna bird),
dwelling in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, pierces the heart of the queen of <s>Madhupura</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>).' ||GC_2,5.76|| (śārdūlavikrīḍita)

children.text:
evaṃ priya-sakhī-lekhaṃ vācakasya bakī-ripoḥ |
lumpat-kalpas tadā bāṣpaḥ sthairya-kalpam acīk pat ||GC_2,5.77|| (anuṣṭubh)
children.translated_text:
Thus, while reading aloud the letter of the dear friend,
the tears of the foe of <s>Bakī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), capable of breaking forth,
assumed the semblance of steadiness. ||GC_2,5.77|| (anuṣṭubh)

children.text:
tad etat kathārambha eva tāsāṃ śvāsānāṃ bahir niṣkramaṇam iva vīkṣya snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ
sotkaṇṭhaṃ samāpayann āha sma,-
children.translated_text: Then, seeing at the very onset of this narrative what appeared to be the outward release of their sighs, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>, concluding with longing, spoke:

children.text:
rādhe yo'yaṃ dayitas
tvayi dayitaḥ katham anārdratām ayitā?
tava tanu-latikām asraiḥ
siñcati paśyāmbuda-śyāmaḥ ||GC_2,5.78|| (āryā)
children.translated_text:
'O <s>Rādhā</s>! This beloved of yours —
how could he who is beloved to you have become hardened?
Behold — dark as a rain-cloud,
he waters the creeper of your body with tears!' ||GC_2,5.78|| (āryā)

children.text:
tad evaṃ madhuropasaṃhāreṇa vyāhāreṇa sarvam ānandayan tāv amanda-premānanda-
mandiratayā vandināv amū tena saha yathā-svam āvāsaṃ vindataḥ sma, śrī-rādhā-govindau ca kandarpa-mandiram iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, delighting all with a concluding discourse of sweet conclusion, those two panegyrists, being temples of abundant love-bliss, found their respective abodes with him; and glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Govinda</s> [found] the temple of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love).

children.text:
iti śrī-śrīmad-uttara-gopāla-campūm anu
kaṃsa-vidhvaṃsanaṃ nāma
pañcamaṃ pūraṇam
||5||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Uttara-Gopāla-campū</s>,
the fifth <s>pūraṇa</s>,
named 'The Destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.'
||5||

children.text:
atha ṣaṣṭhaṃ pūraṇam
śrī-nanda-visarjanam
children.translated_text:
Now the sixth <s>pūraṇa</s>:
'The Sending-off of glorious <s>Nanda</s>'

children.text: atha śrī-govinda-kṛtam ahasi vrajendra-sadasi prātaḥ-kathā prathām āpa | yatra madhukaṇṭha uvāca,-
children.translated_text: Now the morning narrative gained its renown in the assembly of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, the day having been made [auspicious] by glorious <s>Govinda</s>. Wherein <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> spoke:

children.text: tad-evaṃ kaṃsa-māraṇānantaram uccāvaca-vāraṇāya yatra kutracid-gata-yādava-kulākāraṇāya samudbhūta-kaṃsa-pakṣa-nirhāraṇāya ca vrajāgamanāyālabdhāvasare kaṃsa-hare tat-paryanta-vṛttaṃ pratilavam api śravasi vṛttaṃ kurvatām upanandādīnāṃ sānandānām api vilambāśaṅkā-śaṅku-saṅkulānāṃ sandeśaḥ praviveśa; yathā-
children.translated_text: 'Thus, after <s>Kaṃsa's</s> slaying, the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, having found no occasion to return to <s>Vraja</s> — for the prevention of various dangers, for the sheltering of the <s>Yādava</s> clan gone here and there, and for the removal of the arisen faction of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — a message entered the hearing of <s>Upananda</s> and the others who, though blissful, were bristling with the thorns of apprehension about delay, as they made each moment's news enter their ears. As follows:'

children.text:
harer mātā bhaktaṃ tad-avadhi na bhuṅkte tad-anugās
tathā tasmin gopāḥ prati-muhur upāyātividhurāḥ |
kim anyad vaktavyaṃ vrajam anugataṃ yat paśu-kulaṃ
vanasthaṃ yad vā tan-nikhilam iha śiryad vilapati || iti || GC_2,6.1 ||
children.translated_text:
'<s>Hari's</s> mother, since that time, no longer eats the offering devoted [to him]; similarly the cowherds,
repeatedly sending messengers toward him, are distressed in that regard.
What more need be said? The herds of cattle that followed to <s>Vraja</s>,
and those in the forest — all of them here lament and waste away.' || GC_2,6.1 ||

children.text: atha kutaścin manaḥ-stha-saṃkocataḥ samprati prati-gamanād viramya bhāvi-līlā-sūcana-devarṣi-vacana-smaraṇāt tad-eva ca niyamya sahamānatāṃ vahann api tad-evaṃ niśamya samyag-utsukatayā gamyam eveti manaḥ punaḥ saṅgamya so'ayaṃ vraja-prāṇa-vrajaḥ svāgrajaṃ raho nirvyājaṃ vyājahāra,- æārya ! tatra-bhavatātra sāhāyyaṃ dhāryatām | ahaṃ punar vrajam eva vrajāni' iti |
children.translated_text: Then, desisting from going back due to some inward restraint of mind, yet curbing that very [restraint] through remembrance of the <s>Devarṣi's</s> (<s>Nārada's</s>) words hinting at future pastimes — though enduring patience — hearing this, with thorough eagerness, the life-breath of <s>Vraja</s> himself, gathering his mind that 'One must indeed go,' addressed his elder brother privately, without pretense: 'Elder brother! Let your support be maintained for those [<s>Yādavas</s>] there. I shall return to <s>Vraja</s>!'

children.text: sa punaḥ sāsram uvāca,- bhrātar bhavantaṃ vinā mama sarvaṃ vināśam āyātīti na mayā kim api syāt |
children.translated_text: He (<s>Balarāma</s>) replied with tears: 'Brother! Without you, everything of mine comes to ruin — so nothing would remain for me.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- tarhi kiṃ kāryam ?
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Then what is to be done?'

children.text: sa uvāca,- yadūnugrasenānugatān vidhāya drutam ubhābhyām evāvābhyāṃ gokulaṃ gantavyam | tad idaṃ mayāpi bhavyaṃ nivedayaitavyam āsit, diṣṭyā svayam eva diṣṭyā tad uṭṭaṅkitam |
children.translated_text: He said: 'Having established the <s>Yadus</s> under <s>Ugrasena's</s> guidance, we both should go swiftly to <s>Gokula</s>! This much I too should have submitted; by good fortune, it was by good fortune itself inscribed [in your mind].'

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇas tena sākaṃ śrī-vasudeva-vinā-kṛta-yadu-kula-virājamāna-yadu-rāja-sahāyāṃ gatvā kṣaṇād avasaraṃ ca matvā tad idaṃ nivedana-mudrayā vedayāmāsa,- æmama kiñcid vijñaptir asti' iti |
children.translated_text: Then glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with him, went to the <s>Yadu</s> king's assembly — resplendent with the <s>Yadu</s> clan assembled [but] without glorious <s>Vasudeva</s> — and perceiving the opportunity in a moment, communicated with the stamp of a petition: 'I have a certain request.'

children.text: sarve sa-sambhramam ūcuḥ,- kāmam ājñāpyatām |
children.translated_text: All said with deference: 'By all means, command!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,-æsamprati bhavantaḥ sarve sva-bhavanam eva samāgatavantaḥ, rāja-mahāśayāś ca nija-rājāsanam evāsanaṃ vidhāya yathā-pūrvaṃ bhavatāṃ parva vitanitatāraḥ | mayā pūrvam apīdaṃ nivedanaṃcakre, yan-mahyaṃ rājyaṃ na rocate, kiṃ tu mama vṛndāvanam eva sukha-vṛndāya kalpate' iti |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'Now that all of you have returned to your own homes, and the magnanimous kings have established their own royal seat, let your festival extend as before. I have already submitted this petition: that kingship does not please me; rather, my <s>Vṛndāvana</s> alone is suited for a multitude of happiness.'

children.text: tad evam avadhāya mukhāvalokanaṃ vyatividhāya satsu sabhāsatsu vikadru-nāmā yadu-bṛddhaḥ samṛddha-kṣobham ācacakṣe,- pūrvam asmākam ekaḥ kaṃsaka eva dhvaṃsaka āsīt | tad-balād anye punar asmābhir na gaṇyeṣu kṛtāḥ, bhavatā pramāpite tu tasmin pracura-pramāṇas tad-vidhā jātāḥ, yato jarāsandhādayas tat-sambandhāhita-nirbandhāḥ koṭayaḥ prasārita-śastra-koṭayaḥ santi | tasmād bhavan-mātrāśraya-praṇayanīya-prāṇa-trāṇa-yātrā yadavaḥ svayaṃ yathāvad avasthāpyantāṃ saṃsthāpyantāṃ vā |
children.translated_text: Thus, having grasped [his words] and having arranged a mutual gazing of faces — among the assembly-members who remained — an elder of the <s>Yadus</s> named <s>Vikadru</s> declared with abundant agitation: 'Previously, our sole destroyer was only petty <s>Kaṃsa</s>. By his power, others were not counted by us; but when he was slain by you, those of his kind became abundant in authority, since <s>Jarāsandha</s> and others — crores of them, with outstretched weapons — are bound by ties of relationship with him. Therefore, let the <s>Yādavas</s> — whose life-journey of protection must be sustained through sole dependence on you — be first properly established and maintained!'

children.text: kiṃ ca æasyās tvām aṣṭamo garbhaḥ' [bhā 10.1.34] iti gīr-vāṇa-vāṇī-sandarbha-sākṣitayā bhavān asmākam eva satyam apatyam, na tu go-paty-adhipānām ity asmat-pratyavasthāpanam eva bhavatā pratyham ācaraṇīyam | teṣām apakāra-kārakaś ca kaścana samprati bhātīti yathā-bhavyaṃ syāt tathā vyavahartavyam iti kim adhikaṃ marma-vyañjanayā sādhūnāṃ śatrujitsu parama-dharmavitsu |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, by the witness of the celestial voice's textual assertion "this one, your eighth embryo" [BhP 10.1.34], you are truly our offspring, not of the lord of the cattle-lords. Therefore, your settling down with us must be practiced daily. And a certain perpetrator of harm to them is now visible — so matters should be dealt with as is proper.' — What more [need be said] by way of revealing the core truth among the good, among those supreme knowers of <s>dharma</s> who conquer enemies?

children.text: atha tad etad anatikramyaṃ niśamya samyag vācaṃ saṃyamya durmanā iva tasmād apagamya śrī-vasudeva-devakībhyāṃ dharmyaṃ harmyam āgamya śrī-rāmeṇa samam eva tāv anu nivedayāmāsa,- śrī-mat-pitarāv-ājñā-vitarāyāvadhānam atrādhattām |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this which could not be transgressed, fully restraining his words, as if despondent, departing from that [assembly], coming with glorious <s>Rāma</s> together to the righteous mansion of glorious <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>, he submitted to those two: 'Let the generous parental feet attend here!'

children.text: tāv ucatuḥ,- hanta ! tat kim ?
children.translated_text: Those two said: 'Alas! What is it?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- yad vrajalokaṃ vilokaṃ vilokam āyacchāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said: 'That we wish to behold the <s>Vraja</s>-folk — beholding them again and again!'

children.text: atha tad-etad avadhārya tau tūṣñīkām evāpuṣñītām | tau hi pūrvam ugrasena-mukuṭa-bandham anu tad-vacana-pravandham ākarṇya vaivarṇyam evāsannau staḥ | yaḥ khalv avyabhicāritayā vaiśampāyanādibhir api hari-vaṃṣādiṣu pracārita evāsti; yathā darśitam,- æahaṃ sa eva go-madhyaḥ' ityādi | jānāte sma ca tāv asya manovṛttaṃ yad vraja-gamane labdha-saṅgamane sarvam asau vismaratīti |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this, those two did not nurture even silence. For those two, upon hearing that flow of his words following the binding of <s>Ugrasena's</s> crown, had already arrived at a state of pallor. For [his resolve] has indeed been promulgated by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> and others in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> and such as perfectly unwavering; as was shown: 'I, that very one, in the midst of cows...' and so forth. And those two knew his mental disposition — that upon gaining the meeting with <s>Vraja</s>, he would forget everything.

children.text: tataś cirād evam ucatuḥ,- ætataḥ parihṛtāv eva cira-labdha-śvāsa-rūpābhyāṃ yuvābhyām āvām' iti tatrākrūrasya jananyā ca vicārataḥ krūram idaṃ proktam,- æyady atra vraja-janānāṃ gamanāgamanam asti, tarhi vraja evāyam astīti gamanaṃ vāsya kathaṃ nirodha-viṣayīkriyate ?' iti |
children.translated_text: After a long time, those two said thus: 'By you two — who are like the very form of breath long-obtained — we are thus abandoned.' There, <s>Akrūra's</s> mother also, from her deliberation, spoke this cruel [word]: 'If the <s>Vraja</s>-folk have their coming and going here, then this is <s>Vraja</s> itself — so how can his departure be made the object of prohibition?'

children.text: atha sarve tasyā mukhaṃ paśyantaś ciraṃ vimṛśya tasthuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then all, looking at her face, stood deliberating for a long time.

children.text: tad-evaṃ sati punar vivikta-mitābhyāṃ rāmājitābhyām akṣīṇam aṣaḍa-kṣīṇam idaṃ nirṇiktaṃ viviktam,- tad idam āvābhyāṃ saralatayā param anayor guru-caraṇayor niveditam | tat punar amūbhāṃ svāniṣṭaṃ vitarkya pratyādiṣṭaṃ gurvājñālaṃghananṃ tu na maṅgalāya kalpeta | yad-ājñā-pālanāya parama-maryādaḥ sa khalu raghu-varyaḥ prājyaṃ rājyam api parityajya nava-bhāryayā saha rākṣasa-caryābhīṣaṇam api vanaṃ bāḍham avagāḍhaṃ cakāra | tad-ājñā-laṃghanasya parāmṛśyate ca phalam- jarāsandhādayas tv asmat-sambandhena kṛtānusandhe vraje'py utpātaṃ pātayiṣyantīti prastutam astu tāvad aprastutam anyad anyad api, tasmāc śrī-vrajeśa-caraṇa-samādhānam eva sāmprataṃ sāmpratam iti |
children.translated_text: That being so, again, in private, the two — <s>Rāma</s> and the Unconquered one — thrashed out this matter with undiminshed, unsimplistic [deliberation]: 'We two have submitted this to the parental feet with straightforwardness. But it has been rejected by them, surmising their own loss. Yet the transgression of parental command would not conduce to auspiciousness. For to fulfill his parents' command, that best of the <s>Raghus</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), the upholder of supreme propriety, abandoned even an abundant kingdom and truly entered the forest — terrifying with <s>Rākṣasa</s> activity — together with his new bride. And the consequence of transgressing that command is reflected upon: <s>Jarāsandha</s> and others, by their connection with us, will bring calamity even upon <s>Vraja</s>. So let the present topic remain for now — there are various other considerations besides. Therefore, the conciliation of the feet of the lord of glorious <s>Vraja</s> alone is what is presently fitting.'

children.text:
tad-evaṃ mantraṃ vidhāya śrī-vrajeśituranasāṃ samūha sannidhāya tābhyāṃ tasya parisaraḥ samājagme | samāgamya ca praṇamya samyagāsanam āsthitayos tayo rāma eva tasmin sadasi yad vṛttaṃ tat pravṛttaṃ cakre |
[20] tatra svayaṃ kṛṣṇas tu pitṛ-pitṛvyādīn api sa-vinayaṃ paśyan kiñcid vihasann iva tasya śeṣam āha sma,- hanta! kādācitkīm ākāśa-vāṇīṃ pramāṇīkṛtya mayi nija-devakī-putratām api te sūcayanti, tad-antargataṃ sva-mataṃ kāraṇaṃ tu nāvatārayanti iti |
children.translated_text:
Thus having resolved the counsel, having assembled the host of attendants of the lord and lady of glorious <s>Vraja</s>, those two together with him arrived at his vicinity. Having arrived and bowed, and those two having properly taken their seats, <s>Rāma</s> himself in that assembly set forth what had transpired.
[20] There, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, looking at his father and uncle and others with deference and smiling slightly, spoke the remainder: 'Ha! Having given authority to a certain casual celestial voice, they suggest that I am indeed the son of <s>Devakī</s>; but their inner motive and reason they do not bring forth.'

children.text: athaitāvat kathitavati madhukaṇṭhe snigdhakaṇṭhaś cintayati sma,- vastutaḥ khalv ayam anugatācintya-śaktitayā śrī-devakyāṃ catur-bhuja-rūpena śrĪ-yośodāyāṃ tu dvi-bhuja-rūpena sphurati sma æphalena phala-kāraṇam anumīyate' iti nyāyena | yadā tu kaṃsa-bhayāc-catur-bhuja-rūpācchādanāya devakīcchājāyata, tadā tu śrī-yośodāyāṃ sphuritaṃ dvi-bhuja-rūpam eva catur-bhuja-rūpam antarbhūtaṃ vidhāya tatrāvirbhūveti pūrva-campūm anu (3.102) śrī-bhāgavatānugata-yuktibhir uktibhiḥ sthāpitam | tat tu na pūrvam ubhayatrāpi jñātam āsīt iti |
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> had narrated this much, <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> reflected: 'In truth, he — being of inconceivable power that follows [his devotees] — manifested in glorious <s>Devakī</s> in the four-armed form and in glorious <s>Yaśodā</s> in the two-armed form, according to the maxim "the cause is inferred from the effect." But when, out of fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the desire arose in <s>Devakī</s> to conceal the four-armed form, then the two-armed form that had manifested in glorious <s>Yaśodā</s>, having subsumed the four-armed form within itself, appeared there — this was established in the <s>Pūrva-campū</s> (3.102) through arguments following the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s>. But that was not previously known in either place.'

children.text: atha spaṣṭaṃ sa-smitam ācaṣṭa,- kathaṃ te svayam api kāraṇam avatārayeyuḥ ? avatārite tu tasmin vasudevenāpahṛtāpatyasya go-paty adipasya nyāyaḥ satyaḥ syād iti | bhavatu, vraja-patinā tatra kiṃ pratipannam ?
children.translated_text: Then he (<s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s>) clearly spoke with a smile: 'How could they themselves bring forth the reason? For if that reason were brought forth, the principle of <s>Vasudeva</s> having stolen the offspring of the lord of the cattle-lords would become true!' — 'Let it be. What did the lord of <s>Vraja</s> accept in response?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭha uvāca,- tac-chrutvā tu vraja-nṛpatir bahir avihataṃ vihasya tad anyathā adhyavasyati sma, æasyās tvām aṣṭamo garbho hantā yāṃ vahase'budha' [bhā 10.1.34] iti
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said: 'Hearing that, the king of <s>Vraja</s>, laughing openly without restraint, understood it differently: "This one, your eighth embryo, will be the slayer — of the one you carry, O fool!" [BhP 10.1.34] —'

children.text: kaṃsaṃ pratyākāśa-vāṇī-
children.translated_text: the celestial voice addressed to <s>Kaṃsa</s> —

children.text: ækiṃ mayā hatayā manda jātaḥ khalu tavānta-kṛt |
children.translated_text: '"Why, by me having killed [<s>Devakī</s>]? O fool! Your destroyer has already been born!

children.text: yatra kva vā pūrva-śatrur mā hiṃsīḥ kṛpanān bṛthā ||'[bhā10.4.12]
children.translated_text: Whether the former enemy be here or elsewhere — do not slay the wretched ones in vain!" [BhP 10.4.12]'

children.text:
iti devī-vāṇyā vyavicāritā | avyalīkatā-paryavasita-bhāṣiṇānakadundhubhinā ca māṃ prati nirdvandvam ittham evoktam,
ædiṣṭyā bhrātaḥ pra-vayasa idānīm aprajasya te |
prajāīśāyā nivṛttasya prajā yat samapadyata ||' [bhā 10.5.23] iti |
children.translated_text: who were without progeny and had desisted from the desire for progeny!" [BhP 10.5.23]' — thus.

— was judged by the celestial voice of the Goddess (<s>Durgā</s>). And <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) — whose speech invariably concludes in truth — had spoken to me without duplicity precisely thus:
'"By fortune, O brother, now progeny has appeared for the aged you,

children.text: tasmān nūnaṃ æprāg ayaṃ vasudevasyakvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ' [bhā 10.8.14] iti māṃ prati vyañjita-tattva-vargasya gargasya khalv idaṃ prapañcanam evāntaḥ kāraṇam udañcati |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, surely, this fabrication of <s>Garga</s> — who intimated the true facts to me [saying] "This one was formerly born somewhere as <s>Vasudeva's</s> son" [BhP 10.8.14] — that alone rises as the hidden reason.'

children.text: bhavatu, pitroḥ punar idaṃ sukha-samvidam eva tanute, yan nija-putraṃ prati dhanyāḥ putra-bhāvanām ācarantīti |
children.translated_text: 'Let it be. This affords only happy knowledge to the parents — that they are blessed to cherish the sentiment of parenthood toward their own son.'

children.text: viśeṣataś cānakadundhubhinā mama taj-janyā ca bhavaj-jananyā na dvaitam astīti tais tad bhadram evocyate | kiṃ tu,
children.translated_text: 'And especially — <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> said that between my birth-mother and your birth-mother there is no duality — and so what they say is auspicious. But:'

children.text: yātra syād asurād bhītiḥ sā tatra viraha-jvarāt |
children.translated_text: 'The fear that existed there from demons — that here [exists] from the fever of separation;

children.text: bhāvad vayaṃ bhavaty evety ākulaṃ suta manmanaḥ || GC_2,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: "We shall certainly be with you" — [yet] my mind is agitated, O son!' || GC_2,6.2 ||

children.text: bhavatu, tathāpy eṣām eva sāhāyyaṃ kāryam, yataḥ sarvajñānāṃ matam avadhārya kāryam etad vicārya khalu mayā kaṃsa-badhāya tavāgamanaṃ na visraṃsitam | śrūyate hi - pūrvaṃ muni-hitāya daśarathenābhnava-tanayasya rākṣasa-kṣayāya prasthāpanam; yaḥ khalv anyadā tad vana-gamana-kṣaṇa eva kṣīṇa-prāṇatām avāpa iti kṣaṇaṃ rodanaṃ viṣṭabhya tam etaṃ bāhubhyām avaṣṭabhy ca tad etan mukham īkṣāmāsa |
children.translated_text: 'Let it be. Nevertheless, their assistance must be rendered, because — having ascertained the view of the omniscient ones and having reflected upon this matter — I did not prevent your departure for the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s>. For it is heard: formerly, by <s>Daśaratha</s>, for the welfare of the sages, the sending-forth of his young son for the destruction of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> [was done]; he who indeed, at the very moment of that one's departure to the forest, attained the state of having his life-breaths diminished' — and steadying his weeping for a moment and holding him by the arms, he gazed upon that face.

children.text: tataḥ sa caiṣa tam enaṃ sacamānaḥ sa-gadgadaṃ jagāda,- tāta ! duṣṭā naṣṭā eva bhaviṣyantīti na tatra sandihyatām | tathaiva hi daiva-phalaṃ mama tāta-caraṇeṣu vargaśa eva gargaḥ prati-ñātavān asti | kadācin mayi caikānte vanānte devarṣi-varya iti | tathā mama ca vāsas tāta-mahāśayānām upāsanamaya eva sampatsyate, tac ca gopānām upa-samājam eva, na tu yādavānām eva davīyaḥ | te khalv asmākaṃ jñātayaḥ, ete tu suhṛda iti jñātibhiḥ suhṛdāṃ khalv etādṛśa eva bhedaḥ | suhṛtsu tad-dhitāya kadācid vāsaḥ sadā tu jñātiṣu tad-āloka-sukhāya bhavati iti |
children.translated_text: Then he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), cherishing him, spoke with a choked voice: 'Father! The wicked ones shall indeed be destroyed — let there be no doubt about that. For <s>Garga</s> himself has pledged that divine fruit to your feet, class by class. And once, to me in private, in the outskirts of the forest, the best of the divine sages (<s>Nārada</s> too [made a similar pledge]). And my dwelling, Father, shall consist precisely of attending upon the great [parental] personages, and that too in the assembly of the cowherds, not at all at a great distance among the <s>Yādavas</s>. For they are indeed our kinsmen, while these [<s>Vraja</s> folk] are friends — and between kinsmen and friends this is precisely the distinction: among friends, dwelling is occasional, for their welfare; but among kinsmen, it is always, for the happiness of beholding [them].'

children.text: evam uktavati rāmānuje rāma-nāmāpi svaṃ tat-sadṛśam eva parāmṛśann āha sma,- pitur yuvābhyāṃ snigdhābhyāṃ poṣitau jvālitau bhṛśam āvām iti kiṃ vaktavyam; yataḥ pitror ātmano'py abhyadhikā prītir ātmajeṣu bhavati iti |
children.translated_text: When the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) had spoken thus, the one named <s>Rāma</s> too, reflecting on his own [feeling] that was similar to his, said — 'What need is there to say that we two, nourished and made to blaze greatly by a loving father? For the affection of parents toward their sons is indeed greater than toward their own selves.'

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaś ca tad eva sthāpayan prāha sma,- āstāṃ tāvan-mama tanūjasya vārtā, asya ca śrī-man-mad-agrajasya bhavān eva dharmataḥ pitā; yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, establishing that very [principle], said — 'Let the talk about me, your son, rest for now — for this glorious elder brother of mine, you yourself are, by the law of <s>dharma</s>, the father; since —'

children.text: sa pitā sā ca jananī yau puṣñītāṃ sva-putravat |
śiśūn bandhubhir utsṛṣṭān akalpaiḥ poṣa-rakṣaṇe || [bhā 10.45.22] iti |
children.translated_text: who nourish like their own sons, children abandoned by their relatives, who are incapable of their own nurture and protection.' ||[BhP 10.45.22]||
'He is the father and she is the mother

children.text: tasmāc-chrī-mad-āryasya cāsya bhavac-caraṇa-paricaryā paraṃ varyā; kiṃ tu suhṛdām eṣāṃ sukham abhimukhaṃ vidhāya śrī-caraṇam āgamisyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, the service at your feet is the supreme [duty] for this glorious elder [brother] too. But having arranged the happiness of these friends (<s>Yadus</s>), we shall come to your glorious feet.'

children.text: vraja-rāja uvāca,- vatsa ! tāvad vayam apy atra vatsyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Vraja</s> said — 'Son! Then we too shall stay here for that long.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- tāta ! tathā vidheyaṃ yathā bhavad-vyatirekād ekākitayā mātā mā tāpaṃ yāsīt |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'Father! Let it be arranged so that mother, being alone without you, may not fall into anguish!'

children.text: vraja-rāja uvāca,- tām api bhavataḥ samīpam evāpayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Vraja</s> said — 'Her too we shall bring to your very presence!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- tataḥ sarvam api gokulam utsannatām āpannaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'Then the entire <s>Gokula</s> too would have attained a state of abandonment!'

children.text: vraja-rāja uvāca,- tarhi sarvam api vrajaṃ nikaṭaṃ ghaṭayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Vraja</s> said — 'Then we shall bring the entire <s>Vraja</s> to your proximity!'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- sampraty asmākaṃ bahulāḥ pratyahaṃ saṃkhyādhikaya-pratyataḥ suṣṭhu bahulā jātāḥ | tāsām upa-nagara-vanaṃ kim upa-jīvanaṃ syāt ? gāvaś cāsmākaṃ kula-devya iti tā eva sevyatām arhanti | yadi vā mad-arthaṃ sarvaṃ bhavatām, māṃ vinā tu byartham iti samarthanīyam, tarhi ca mat-prāṇā eva tā iti tā eva prāṇanīyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'At present, our cows — very numerous, increasing in count every day, truly very many indeed — have become [a great multitude]. What sustenance would a suburban forest provide for them? And cows are our clan-deities — they alone deserve to be served! Or if all of yours is for my sake, and without me is futile — that is to be argued — then since they are my very life-breaths, they alone are to be sustained!'

children.text:
kiṃ ca, yadavo'pi nāhitaṃ vyāharanti; sphuṭam upalabdha-kaṃsa-saṃbandha-jarāsandha-nirbandhād-akṣauhiṇī-lakṣita-dur-jana-lakṣāṇi mathurām avarotsyanti; tarhi garhitam eva bhavet | tatrāstām asmat-sāmīpyam asmad-asāmīpyataś ca bhavad-avasthānaṃ yady asmat-saṃbandhaṃ vinā labdha-sandhaṃ bhavet tarhy eva kṛcchraṃ narcchet | gūḍha-puruṣa-dvāreṇa jñāte hy asmat-saṃbandhe jarāsandhādayas ta ete kaṃsa-van na bhayānubandhā iti chala-balam ekam ekaṃ na prasthāpayiṣyanti | kiṃ tv akṣauhiṇībhir dravantaḥ sarvaṃ vrajam apy upadrāvayiṣyanti | tasmād asmābhir yuṣmābhiś ca gopayitavya eva gandhaś ca vyati-saṃbandhasya; ete ca mayā yādavā durgāntare davayitavyāḥ; bhavantas tv asaṃkhyā na tathā kartuṃ śakyāḥ | saṃkhyām aticarantīnāṃ vanecarantīnāṃ gavām āvaraṇaṃ
tu sutarām eva duṣkaram; tasmāt teṣāṃ durga-vad-asmad-audāsīnyam eva bhavatāṃ rakṣāyāṃ prāvīṇyam arhati |
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, the <s>Yadus</s> too do not speak anything ill; but clearly, from the insistence of <s>Jarāsandha</s>, who has obtained the connection with <s>Kaṃsa</s>, hundreds of thousands of wicked [soldiers] marked by <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> armies shall descend upon <s>Mathurā</s>; and then it would be truly deplorable! Let our proximity there be set aside — and your staying [near us] too — if it would succeed without connection to us, only then would it not bring hardship. For when our connection is known through secret agents, <s>Jarāsandha</s> and the rest — since they would not fear [you] as they did <s>Kaṃsa</s> — would not dispatch a deceitful force one at a time, but rather, rushing with <s>akṣauhiṇī</s> armies, would harass the entire <s>Vraja</s> as well. Therefore, the very scent of our mutual connection must be concealed by us and by you; and these <s>Yādavas</s> must be sheltered by me within a fortress; but you, being innumerable, cannot be accommodated likewise. And the protection of cows — beyond counting, grazing in forests — is especially difficult to accomplish by constructing a fortress. Therefore, our feigned indifference toward you, like a fortress, deserves to serve as proficiency in your protection.'

children.text: kiṃ tu tāvad eva tad vidheyam, yāvat sarva-vipakṣa-pakṣāpakṣayaṃ vidhāya svayam eva śrī-mad-vrajam āvrajāmaḥ | āvrajite ca tasmin na punar anyatra vrajanam api syāt, yato nirupadhi-sneha-vyagra-bhavad-agrima-sva-jana-varga-darśana-sukha-mātra phala-pātratayā nirupādhir asau puruṣārthaḥ kathaṃ bādhitaḥ syāt ? tad-evaṃ vyasya yan nivedutaṃ tad tad evedaṃ samasya nivedayāmi,
children.translated_text: 'But this should be done only until, having destroyed the faction of all adversaries, I myself return to the glorious <s>Vraja</s>. And when that [return] has taken place, there shall not be departure elsewhere again — for the unconditional supreme goal of life, whose sole fruit is the happiness of beholding the foremost circle of your own people, absorbed in unconditional affection — how could it be obstructed? Thus, extending and then gathering what was submitted piece by piece, I submit it all together —'

children.text: yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān |
jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham || [bhā 10.45.23] iti |
children.translated_text: kinsmen of yours — we shall come to see them, having accomplished the happiness of our friends.' ||[BhP 10.45.23]||
'Go, all of you, to <s>Vraja</s>, dear father! And we, [wishing to see] the grief-stricken

children.text:
tad-etat-paryantaṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ procya bhrātaram avalocya prāha sma,- atra ætāta' iti nijāntaḥ-sthāpita-putratā-bhāvanāyā yogyam eva sambodhanam; æjñātīn' iti, tatrāpi æsneha-duḥkhitān' iti snehasya niravadhikatvāt prati-kṣaṇaṃ didṛkṣuṣu tan-mukhyeṣu teṣv evāvasthānaṃ prati-kṣaṇam eva sva-vīkṣaṇa-dānaṃ ca vivakṣitam | ævayam' iti æasmado dvayoś ca' iti pāṇinīya-smaraṇād astu tāvan mama vārtā, kiṃ tv āvāṃ dvāv apy eṣyāva iti vyañjitam | ædraṣṭum' iti teṣām ivātmano'pi tad-darśana-mātra-puruṣārthatā samarthitā | æathāpi bhūman mahimā guṇasya te, viboddhum arhati' [bhā 10.14.6] ity atra bodha-viṣayī-bhavitum iti-vad-darśana-viṣayī-bhavitum ity arthāntare'pi tad-vad eva siddhāntitam; æsuhṛdām' iti yadūnām ajñātitvam upakāryatva-mātraṃ ca dhvani-pātraṃ kṛtam
| tatra ca æsukhaṃ vidhāya' iti ktvā-prayogeṇa sāvadhika-nirdeśāt tad-bhayādi-nāśanānataraṃ punas tad anapekṣatvam api lakṣitam iti |
children.translated_text: Having narrated up to that point, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, glancing at his brother, said — 'Here, "father" (<s>tāta</s>) is indeed the fitting address for the paternal sentiment established within him; "kinsmen" — and therein specifically "grief-stricken" — since the love is boundless, the intention is to stay among those foremost ones who desire to see him at every moment, and to give them the gift of his own seeing at every moment. "We" — by the <s>Pāṇinian</s> recollection that it means "of us two" — let the talk about me rest, but the implication is: we two shall indeed come! "To see" — the supreme goal of life constituted of mere seeing alone is established for himself as well, just as for them. As in "But, O <s>Bhūman</s>, the greatness of your quality deserves to be known" [BhP 10.14.6], where "to become the object of knowing" is the meaning — similarly, "to become the object of seeing" is the alternative meaning, established in the same way. "Friends" — the <s>Yadus'</s> non-kinship and mere status as objects of [his] beneficence are made the vessel of suggestion. And therein, "having accomplished the happiness" — by the use of the <s>ktvā</s>-construction, from the definitive indication of something beyond, even his indifference toward that [Yadu welfare] after the destruction of their fears and such is suggested.'

children.text: tatra snigdhakaṇṭhaḥ sotkaṇṭhaṃ papraccha,- atha tatra kiṃ vyavasitaṃ śrī-vrajeśa-caraṇānām ?
children.translated_text: There <s>Snigdhakaṇṭha</s> asked with longing — 'Then what was determined there by the feet of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>?'

children.text: madhukaṇṭhaḥ prāha sma,- vraja-rājaś ca tadīya-vāco-yukti-racanam anabhirucitam api bāḍham ucitam iti matvā manasi sva-lalāṭaṃ hatvā vāṣpa-spṛṣṭam aspaṣṭam ācaṣṭa,- bhavan-mātā tu vāmā katham iyad-budhyatām ?
children.translated_text: <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> said — 'The lord of <s>Vraja</s>, considering the skillful reasoning of his (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) words as proper though not pleasing, striking his own forehead in his mind, spoke with tear-touched indistinctness — "But how shall your mother, being contrary [i.e., difficult], understand this much?"'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- tāṃ prati ca yatheṣṭa-praṇāma-pūrvakaṃ nijeṣṭa-dvārā mayedaṃ sandeṣṭavyam iti procya sva-hasta-lipibhis tat patraṃ virocya śrīdāma-hasta-vinyastaṃ kṛtavān |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'To her as well, with reverential salutation as desired and through my own desired intermediary, I shall send this message' — saying this, he composed that letter in his own handwriting and placed it in <s>Śrīdāman's</s> hand.

children.text:
śrīdāmā ca śrī-vraja-rāja-śuśrūṣāyāṃ kṛtānusandhas tan-mukhabandham atīva tad-dīnan-manyatānubandham anusandhāya taṃ vihāya nivedyam eva sa-gadgadaṃ gadati sma,- yathā samprati vayaṃ duṣṭa-janāt kaṣṭam āśaṃkya spaṣṭam eva nāyāsyāmaḥ; kiṃ tu śrīmat-pitṛ-caraṇa-paricaraṇa-prabhāvān mamāṣaḍa-kṣīṇam akṣīṇam āgamanaṃ pratyaham api vidyata eva |
tathā hi-
children.translated_text:
<s>Śrīdāman</s>, who had been attentive in the service of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s>, perceiving the conclusion of his mouth [i.e., his face-expression] as exceedingly pitiable, bound up with that very [grief], setting that aside, spoke chokingly what was to be reported — 'Just as at present we shall clearly not come [back], apprehending hardship from wicked people; but by the power of the service at the feet of the glorious father, my arrival — not diminished in six [days], undiminished — exists every day indeed.
As follows —'

children.text: ādye'hni kṣīra-bhaktaṃ ghana-dadhi-valitā roṭikā tasya paścāt-
children.translated_text: 'On the first day, rice-pudding; then thick-curd-covered bread;

children.text: tat-paścād-dugdha-pūpaṃ tad-anu bahuvidhānnādyam anyeṣu cānyat |
children.translated_text: after that, milk-cake; then many kinds of rice-foods and other [dishes] on other [days];

children.text: mātar mahyaṃ nikāyye mahati rasayate paryaveṣi tvayā yan
children.translated_text: O Mother! What you serve me at the great table with relish —

children.text: na svapnas tan na vā tat sphuraṇa-mayam iti smaryatāṃ kiṃ tu satyam || GC_2,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: that is not a dream, nor is it merely a manifestation — but remember, it is truth!' ||GC_2,6.3||

children.text: kiṃ ca,
children.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text:
yavann āśnāsi mātas tvam iti niśamaye hanta nāśnāni tāvad
yady aśnāmīva tarhy apy anubhavad asu me ye'savaḥ śoṣamīyuḥ |
goṣṭhaṃ gacchāni paśyāny api nija-jananīṃ tad-vidhām evam eva
hy udyat tejaḥ-prakāśād ripu-gaṇam acirād ut-sahiṣye vijetum || iti || GC_2,6.4 ||
children.translated_text:
'"Do not eat, Mother, until you eat" — I hear this; alas, I do not eat till then;
and if I do eat, then the life-breaths that experience through me — those very life-breaths are withered!
Let me go to the cow-settlement, let me see my own mother — one just like you —
for with the splendor of rising valor, I shall soon be able to conquer the host of enemies!' — thus. ||GC_2,6.4||

children.text: atha tad-etan niśamya samyag- asrāvilaṃ sandeśa-haraś ca vyājahāra,- satyaṃ śrī-vrajeśvarī-caraṇāś ca svapna-vad idaṃ sāmprata-bhavad-bhojanādikaṃ sa-rodanaṃ vadanti sma | bhavad-duḥkham āśaṃkya svābhojanam api gopayanti sma iti |
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this properly, the message-bearer spoke with tear-muddied [voice] — 'Truly, the feet of the glorious queen of <s>Vraja</s> too say with weeping that this present eating of yours and such is like a dream. Apprehending your suffering, they conceal even their own non-eating.'

children.text: atha tad-etad avadhārya sāścaryatayā sthiteṣu teṣu vraja-mahīkṣīd-ārdra-vīkṣitam ācacakṣe,- bhavataḥ prema-vaśyānāṃ vayasyānām eṣāṃ vartane kā vārtā ?
children.translated_text: Then, when they stood in astonishment perceiving this, the lord of the <s>Vraja</s>-land, with moist glances, said — 'What news of the conduct of all these friends of yours who are under the sway of [your] love?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- śrīman-mātṛvad eva te cāmī mamepsita-sakhi-janā vīkṣyayā mām upalapsyante; kiṃ tu mātur-vatsalatā-svabhāvatayā kadācid anyathā-prathā bhāsiṣyate, na punar amīṣāṃ praṇaya-bhājām iti |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'Just as with the glorious mother, so too these dear friend-folk of mine shall perceive me through seeing [my representatives]; but due to the maternal nature of motherly affection, a different manifestation may sometimes appear — but not in these who are vessels of loving intimacy.'

children.text: vrajeśvara uvāca,- prathamatas tāvad eta iva gāvaḥ katham etāvatīṃ prakriyāṃ śrāvaṇīṃ kurvantu ?
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Vraja</s> said — 'First of all, these very cows — how shall they produce such an audible [effect of separation]?'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca,- yady api tāsv api mama tathā-sphūrtir-jūrtim apanayet tathāpi prakārāntaram api bahir-vṛtti-samādhānāya vidhāsyāmi | yathā- tāsāṃ gandhānu-sandhānam eva pradhānaṃ rava-gaṇa-śravaṇaṃ ca; rūpa-nirūpanaṃ tu tat-pradhānakam eva | tasmāt stoka-kṛṣṇo'yaṃ tad-abhyasta-mada-stoka-saurabhya-parirabhyamāṇa-vastra-saṃvastraṇayā kṛta-man-muralī-khuralīkatayā ca tathā subalaś cāyaṃ bala-vasanāvalambatayā tadīya-śṛṃga-saṃgitayā ca tāsāṃ madyham adhyāsitaṃ kurutām | tataś ca mamākhila-guṇa-nidhaya ete sarve'py anayoḥ prati-nidhayaḥ syur yatra vanyāś ca te dhanyāḥ sarvābhi-vādyā mṛga-nagādyā mat-sphūrti-pūrtim āgaccheyur iti sarvam eva samañjasaṃ bhavitā iti |
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said — 'Although my manifestation in them too would remove their distress, nevertheless I shall also arrange another method for the settling of external functions. As follows: for them, the tracking of scent is primary, and the hearing of [my] sounds; the perception of form is subordinate to those. Therefore, let this <s>Stoka-kṛṣṇa</s>, through the garment-wrapping permeated with the slight fragrance with which he has been practiced, and through the flute made into [something resembling] my <s>muralī</s> — and also let this <s>Subala</s>, through clinging to <s>Bala's</s> garment, and through the singing of his horn — create for them a dwelling in my [presence] in the midst [of the herd]. And then, all these — who are treasuries of my every quality — may become substitutes for us two; and those blessed wild ones — the deer, birds, and such, who deserve to be greeted by all — may attain the fullness of my manifestation — thus everything shall become well-fitted.'

children.text: atha nija-paricārakān śūdrābhīra-kumārakān hata-vicārakān niśāmya vaivaśyād vaiśyābhīra-rāji śāmyad-vacana-śaktibhāji svayam eva so'yam asra-toya-dharaḥ prāha sma, ( mama sakhīyamānānām eṣām akhilānāṃ teṣām iva yadyapi gatis tathāpi tātānugatis tu viśeṣataḥ stutim āsīdati iti |
children.translated_text: Then, observing his own attendants — the <s>Śūdra</s> and <s>Ābhīra</s> boys — whose deliberation had been destroyed, and [seeing] the line of <s>Vaiśya</s>-<s>Ābhīra</s> folk whose power of speech was subsiding from helplessness — that very cloud of tears himself spoke: 'For all these who are treated as my companions, even though their path is like theirs [the <s>Yadus</s>'], nevertheless their following the father deserves special praise.'

children.text:
atha madhumaṅgalam api tad idaṃ sneha-saṅgatam āha,( hanta! Bhavantaś ca tatra yāntu | yad-bhagavatī-sevāṃ man-maṅgalāya mat-pratinidhitayā kurvāṇāḥ punas tad-apūrva-jananāt pūrvavat tad-akharva-parvaṇe sampatsyante iti |
[51] tad-evaṃ visrambhya tat-tat-aṅga-saurabhya-parirabhyamāṇa-vasanādinā tau stoka-kṛṣṇa-subalau viśeṣatas tat-tad-guṇa-vāsitau vidhāyānyān api yathā-nyāyaṃ nijālaṃkaraṇādinālaṃkṛtya sevādikāriṇaṃ ca yathāvad ādṛtya kṛtya-viśeṣān śrī-mat-pitṛ-caraṇeṣu gocaratāṃ nināya; nītvā ca tad-anujñāṃ gṛhītvā svayaṃ tatraiva sthitvā mantra-sadanād-bahiḥ sthitān māthura-vipra-janān antar-nitvā tad-dvārā sarvānn eva yadūn vjñāpayāmāsa,( ta ete vrajāya vrajiṣyanti iti |
children.translated_text:
Then he said this to <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> too, bound with affection: 'Let you all go there! Performing the service of the Blessed Lady (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) as my representative for my welfare, you shall again, by the new production of that [blessing], prosper at that grand festival as before.'
[51] Thus, having confided, having perfumed <s>Stoka-kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Subala</s> especially with the fragrance of those respective limbs through garments and such, and having endowed them with those respective qualities, and having adorned others too with his own ornaments and such as was fitting, and having duly honored the one authorized for service — he brought the particular matters to the notice of the glorious father's feet; having brought them, and having received his permission, remaining there himself, he led the <s>Mathurā</s> <s>brāhmaṇa</s> folk who stood outside the counsel-chamber inside, and through them informed all the <s>Yadus</s>: 'These are departing for <s>Vraja</s>.'

children.text: te ca śrī-vasudeva-naradeva-pramukhās tatraiva sukhād āgatāḥ, āgamya ca ramya-paricchadādinā tān abhyarcya cānuvrajya ca carcyamāna-tad-bhadratayā puramayāmāsuḥ |
children.translated_text: And they — headed by the glorious <s>Vasudeva</s> and the king (<s>Ugrasena</s>) — came there readily, and having come, honored them with lovely gifts and such, and accompanied them, and being absorbed in discussion of their welfare, returned to the city.

children.text:
sa tu yaśasvī svayam asvīkṛta-rājyatayā kim api tatratyaṃ tān praty-anapavarjya
kiṃ tu prāg-vali-valita-bali-kaṃsa-hṛta-dhṛta-kupya-bhājanāni yāni tāny eva visarjya keśavaḥ kevalatāyāṃ mithaḥ kṣubhitatā-bhītas tair eva saha śrī-vrajam ahanīyān anujñāpya manasi kayāpy avasthayā vyāpyamānaḥ puram ājagāma, rāmas tu tān dūram anu-vavrāja |
children.translated_text: But that renowned one (<s>Keśava</s>), having himself not accepted kingship and therefore not distributed anything of that [royal property] to them, but having merely released those vessels of gold and such that were seized and held by the wrinkle-bearing, wrinkle-covered <s>Bali</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) — in his state of pure simplicity, afraid of the agitation between them, bidding farewell to those very ones [departing] for the glorious <s>Vraja</s> for several days, pervaded in his mind by some [indescribable] state, came to the city. But <s>Rāma</s> accompanied them a long distance.

children.text: {54} vrajeśvaras tu pralīna-manastāyām api jīvan-mukta-vad eva saṃskāra-vaśād idaṃ jagāda,( vatsa! nijānuja-vatsala ! sa kevalatayā manobalaṃ hāsyati; tasmād anujaṃ tam evānuyāhi iti |
children.translated_text: [54] The lord of <s>Vraja</s>, though his mind had dissolved, spoke this by force of [residual] impressions, as if one liberated while yet living — 'Son! O lover of your younger brother! He (<s>Kaṃsa</s>) shall merely destroy [his own] mental strength; therefore, follow that younger brother of yours!'

children.text: atha sva-sambandhād adhika-duḥkhānubandhād āśaṃkamānaḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ sa-dhairyaṃ sarvān anujñāpya śīghra-gatyā sva-bhrātaraṃ prāpya kvacid ekāntam anuyāpya nija-nija-bāhubhyāṃ parasparaṃ grīvāṃ paridhāpya tena saha ruroda | tad alam ati-vistareṇa |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), apprehending from his own connection an even greater bond of suffering, firmly took leave of all, and with swift pace reached his brother, led him to a solitary place somewhere, and placing their respective arms around each other's necks, wept with him. But enough of excessive elaboration!

children.text: yataḥ-
kaṃsasya dhvaṃsanānte vraja-vasati-gane gacchati svīya-gehaṃ
children.translated_text: At the end of <s>Kaṃsa's</s> destruction, as the community of <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers goes to its own home,

children.text: taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ taṃ ca rāmaṃ tam api paśupati-ksmā-patiṃ tāṃś ca gopān |
children.translated_text: that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that <s>Rāma</s>, that lord of cowherds and earth, and those cowherds,

children.text: śrīdāmādyāṃś ca tāṃs tān api ca tad-anugān navya-viccheda-bhīter
children.translated_text: and <s>Śrīdāman</s> and the rest, and those various followers of his —

children.text: antaḥ smṛtvā mad-antar-virasa-vaśatayā sarvam arvāg jahāti || GC_2,6.5 ||
children.translated_text: remembering them inwardly from fear of a fresh separation, my interior, overcome by joylessness, abandons everything that follows. ||GC_2,6.5||
For —

children.text: [56} tad-evam uṭṭṃkayan-madhukaṇṭhaḥ śrī-vrajādhipādīnām ādhim avadhāya punar abhidadhe,(
children.translated_text: [56] Thus, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, stumbling [with emotion], having observed the anxiety of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s> and others, spoke again:

children.text: yaḥ svāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ purā tṛṣṇāṃ vardhayāmāsa dhṛṣṇajam |
children.translated_text: 'He, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who previously increased his own longing for the bold one (<s>Dhṛṣṇaja</s>, i.e., <s>Balarāma</s>) —

children.text: sa sākṣād bhavatām aṃke svaṃ keliṃ vahati prabho || GC_2,6.6 ||
children.translated_text: he directly bears his own sport in your lap, O lord!' ||GC_2,6.6||

children.text: atha śrī-kṛṣṇaś ca tac-caraṇāravindaṃ śirasā vindan sa-nirvedaṃ niveditavān,(
children.translated_text: Then Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, touching those (<s>Nanda's</s>) lotus-feet with his head, reported with humility:

children.text: ahaha vahalamantuṃ jantur eṣa pralāpī
children.translated_text: 'Ah! This prattling creature wishes to speak much —

children.text: racitamacita-tātaḥ kṣantum arhas tvam eva |
children.translated_text: he who has made his father without honor — you yourself must forgive!

children.text: katham api nijam aṅgaṃ vyādhinā duḥkhadaṃ syat
children.translated_text: Somehow one's own limb may become pain-giving through disease,

children.text: tad api na hi tad-aṅgī tyaktum icchet kadāpi || GC_2,6.7 ||
children.translated_text: yet the owner of that limb would never wish to abandon it!' ||GC_2,6.7||

children.text: tataś ca,
children.translated_text: And then,

children.text: āliṅgyata vrajeśitrā pitrā sa-pulakaṃ sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The son was embraced by the queen of <s>Vraja</s> and the father with horripilation;

children.text: sarvaiś cānanda-garveṇa roma-parveha sandadhe || GC_2,6.8 ||
children.translated_text: and by all, with the pride of bliss, the thrill of hair was joined here. ||GC_2,6.8||

children.text: tad-evaṃ prātaḥ-kathāṃ madhukaṇṭhaḥ samāpya śrī-mādhava-pada-sīmni rādhikā-sadasi kathayāmāsa,(
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s>, having completed the morning narrative, told it in the assembly of <s>Rādhikā</s> at the boundary of the feet of glorious <s>Mādhava</s>:

children.text: ye khalu tasya vrajāvrajanāya vyañjitā vighnās te sarve prāg-ukta-lajjā-nighnā eva mantavyāḥ | tad-eva purastād vyañjayan mathurāyāś calantaṃ subalaṃ balānujaḥ sva-vallabhārocaka-vācika-valitaṃ cakāra | yathā(
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, all the obstacles that were manifested against his return to <s>Vraja</s> should all be considered as destroyed by the aforementioned modesty. Manifesting that very [obstacle] beforehand, the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), departing from <s>Mathurā</s>, made <s>Subala</s> carry verbal messages embellished with [words] pleasing to his beloved. As follows:''

children.text: satyaṃ santyajya yuṣmān niyata-mad-anuga-prāṇanā niṣpramāṇā
children.translated_text: 'Truly, abandoning you — you whose life-breaths are of my invariable followers — is beyond all measure;

children.text: dharmyaṃ me nāsti kiṃcit tad api sa-vayasaḥ śrūyatāṃ man-nivedyam |
children.translated_text: I have no righteous [justification] for this; nevertheless, O companions, hear my submission!

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ yātisetur mayi ratir atulā sā tu māṃ hrepayantī
children.translated_text: Your love for me, surpassing all limits, is incomparable — it puts me to shame,

children.text: tat-tulyāsakti-riktaṃ hnuta-tanum akaron nāsmi dūraḥ kadāpi || GC_2,6.9 ||
children.translated_text: having made my body, devoid of equal attachment [to match yours], shrink with embarrassment — I am never far!' ||GC_2,6.9||

children.text: puryām asyāṃ yad asmi prakaṭam api hi taṃ hanta kuryāṃ kathaṃ tat
children.translated_text: 'That I am manifestly in this city — alas! — how could I make that otherwise?

children.text: kiṃ tu cchāyā-sadṛkṣaḥ sphuṭam iha viharet tatra tu svena nityam |
children.translated_text: But one like a shadow clearly plays here, while there [in <s>Vraja</s>] eternally, with his own self;

children.text: āveśo yatra yasya sphurati sa niyataṃ tatra bhāti svayaṃ yat
children.translated_text: wherever the immersion of whomever shines forth, there he himself surely shines —

children.text: sphūrtiṃ svāṃ so'yam asmīty anubhajati yathā tena nānyena tad-vat || GC_2,6.10 ||
children.translated_text: for he experiences his own manifestation as "this is I" — through that [lover], not through another — just so!' ||GC_2,6.10||

children.text: somābhe darśa-rātrāv api nija-rucibhiḥ pūrṇimā-bhrāntitas tvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O moon-faced one! Even on the new-moon night, by your own radiance you had the bewilderment of full-moon [brightness];

children.text: mad-viśleṣa-jvarārti-prathi-navama-daśā durvaśāṅgī yad-asīḥ |
children.translated_text: when you became one whose limbs were uncontrollable from the spreading ninth-and-tenth stages of the fever-agony of separation from me —

children.text: tarhi tvām aṅga-kānti-sphurad asita-maṇi-śrī-caya-vyāpta-sarvaḥ
children.translated_text: then I, pervading all with the host of radiant dark jewel-splendors flickering from your bodily luster,

children.text: so'haṃ śiśleṣa tat-tad-vinimita-daśayā yatra citraṃ jagastha || GC_2,6.11 ||
children.translated_text: embraced you in those respective states wrought by [love's] phases — wherein the wonder of the world stood!' ||GC_2,6.11||

children.text: somābhe mānam aicchaḥ pratipadi lalite mām ayāsr vanānte
children.translated_text: 'O moon-faced one, on the first day (<s>pratipad</s>) you desired amorous jealousy (<s>māna</s>); O charming <s>Lalitā</s>, you sought me at the forest's end;

children.text: pālyāsīr vāsa-sajjā paricarasi purā rādhayā mām viśākhe |
children.translated_text: O <s>Pālī</s>, you maintained the readiness of attire; O <s>Viśākhā</s>, you previously served me through <s>Rādhā</s>;

children.text: etad diṃ-mātram uktaṃ bhavad-avagataye jñeyam anyat kathaṃ vā
children.translated_text: this much only has been said for your understanding — how could the rest be known?

children.text: svapnaṃ tat tat viditvā glapayatha nijakaṃ mānasaṃ mām apīha ? || GC_2,6.12 ||
children.translated_text: Having learned that all that was a dream, do you distress your own minds — and me here as well?' ||GC_2,6.12||

children.text: padme bhadre sa-śaivye tritayam api bhavad-rūpam udbhrānta-cittaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Padmā</s>, O <s>Bhadrā</s>, O <s>Śaivyā</s> — the three forms of you, with bewildered minds

children.text: mad-viśleṣāt tamālaṃ pari viluṭhitavad yatra tatrāham āsam |
children.translated_text: from separation from me, rolled about the <s>tamāla</s> tree — wherever that was, there I was,

children.text: āliṅgan yuṣmad-aṅgāny udanamayam aho yāvad abhyasya tāvat
children.translated_text: embracing your limbs, tearful — ah! — as long as [I] practiced [this],

children.text: Kruddhā bṛddhāḥ kutaścid vata yad-upagatās tan na me yāti duḥkham || GC_2,6.13 ||
children.translated_text: then from somewhere angry elders arrived — alas! — that sorrow of mine does not depart!' ||GC_2,6.13||

children.text: ānyedyuḥ śrīla-rādhe mama pura-gamana-sphūrti-sañjāta-mūrtiṃ
tvām āliṅgyānucu mban giri-vanam anayaṃ tat kathaṃ vyasmaras tvaṃ ?
children.translated_text: you whose form had arisen from the manifestation of my thought of departing for the city — and led you to the mountain-forest — how did you forget that?

children.text: tatrāgamyātha sarvāḥ kala-kala-virutaṃ yarhi cakrus tadānīṃ
children.translated_text: When all of you then came there and raised a clamor of voices,

children.text: tatrāvāṃ hā yathāsvaṃ pṛthakad apagatau na smarasy eva tac ca || GC_2,6.14 ||
children.translated_text: then we two — alas! — each separately departed — do you not remember even that?' ||GC_2,6.14||
'The next day, O glorious <s>Rādhā</s>, I embraced and kissed you —

children.text: svapne yad rādhike tvaṃ mama śayanam ihāpy āśritā rāja-puryāṃ
children.translated_text: 'In dream, O <s>Rādhikā</s>, you have taken refuge on my very bed here in the royal city;

children.text: svapnas tan nasti nūnaṃ parimalitam abhūd yat-tvayā tasya vāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: that is not a dream at all — for your fragrance pervaded his garments;

children.text: āstāṃ tat spaṣṭam adyāpy anu mad avayavaṃ padminī-ratna-gandhaṃ
children.translated_text: let that be — even today, clearly, finding the jewel-lotus fragrance

children.text: Vindann andho'pi lokaḥ smita-śavala-mukhaḥ śīrṣam īṣad dhunīte || GC_2,6.15 ||
children.translated_text: upon each of my limbs, even the blind world, with a smile-mottled face, shakes its head slightly!' ||GC_2,6.15||

children.text: āstāṃ prāg adya sadya-stana-śaśi-kalayālaṃkṛta-śrī-rasau yad-
children.translated_text: 'Let the past be — just now, the event that was adorned by the fresh moon-crescent of your breast,

children.text: vṛttaṃ tad-yuṣmākābhiḥ sa-śapatham abhitaḥ pṛcchyatāṃ śyāmalaiva |
children.translated_text: endowed with the flavor of beauty — let that be asked about on all sides, under oath, from <s>Śyāmalā</s> herself!

children.text: yady apy evaṃ tathāpi sphuṭa-gatim acirād āgatiṃ cen-madīyām
children.translated_text: Even if it is so, nevertheless, if you desire my return, of clear course, before long —

children.text: īhadhve sarva-vighna-praśamana-racanā syād yadā tarhi kuryām || GC_2,6.16 ||
children.translated_text: when there would be a contrivance for the pacification of all obstacles — then I would accomplish it!' ||GC_2,6.16||

children.text: tad-eva etāvat-prathām eva kathāṃ samāpya punar madhukaṇṭhaḥ provāca,(
children.translated_text: Having concluded the narrative extending just that far, <s>Madhukaṇṭha</s> again spoke:

children.text: rādhe so'yaṃ satyavādī tvām alaṃkṛtya śobhate |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>! This very truth-speaker (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), adorning you, shines —

children.text: tvad-gandha-bandhanaḥ puṣpandhayaḥ svarṇābjinīm iva || GC_2,6.17 ||
children.translated_text: bound by your fragrance, a bee (<s>puṣpandhaya</s>) [seeking] a golden lotus!' ||GC_2,6.17||

children.text: ūṣā-niruddha-vad rādhe yayoḥ svāpnaś ca saṅgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rādhā</s>, the union in dream of those two — like <s>Ūṣā</s> [and <s>Aniruddha</s>] who were confined —

children.text: ṣākṣād āsīt tayor vā kiṃ viśleṣaḥ sthātum arhati ? || GC_2,6.18 ||
children.translated_text: was it direct [reality]? Or can separation endure between those two?' ||GC_2,6.18||

children.text: iti visṛmarasāndrānandaśas taṃ samastaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, with waves of intense bewildered bliss,

children.text: sapadi kathaka-varyau tāv anujñāpya yātau |
children.translated_text: having taken leave of all that, those two best of narrators departed;

children.text: harir api nija-kāntā-saṅga-sarvāṅga-śobhaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Hari</s> too, resplendent in every limb from the company of his beloved,

children.text: subhaga-śayana-lakṣmīm añjasālaṃ cakāra || GC_2,6.19 ||
children.translated_text: directly accomplished the beauty of a blessed sleeping-chamber. ||GC_2,6.19||

children.text: iti śrī-śrī-mad-uttara-gopāla-campūm anu vraja-pati-visarjana-kaṣṭaṃ
nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ pūraṇam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: the sixth chapter. ||6||
Thus, following the glorious Uttara-<s>Gopāla-campū</s>, [this is] the anguish of the lord of <s>Vraja's</s> departure,

children.text: athaikonatriṃśaṃ pūraṇam
children.translated_text: Now the twenty-ninth chapter:

children.text: bhāvi-kathā-pramāṇa-prathanam
children.translated_text: The Establishing of Authority for Future Narratives

children.text: atha bhāvi-kathāntarāvatāraṇāya kramāt pramāṇaṃ nirūpyate | tad evaṃ tatra maṅgala-bhajane sthite vraja-jane punar atra duḥsthite pūrṇimā-vṛnde'pūrṇa-manastayā viviktam anu viviktavatyau |
children.translated_text: Now, the authority for the descent of future narratives is determined in sequence. Thus, when the people of <s>Vraja</s> were settled in the worship of auspiciousness, but here [<s>Paurṇamāsī</s> and <s>Vṛndā</s>] were again ill-at-ease — in the company of <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, with unsatisfied minds — they conversed in a secluded [place].

children.text: tathā hi-yadā keśi-mathanasya vrajān mathurāgamana-samanantaram anantaram eva taj-jana-duḥkham īkṣitum akṣamatayā tad-atidūra-kṣiti-sthitiāṃ gatayor madhumaṅgala-saṅgata-vṛndā-pūrṇimayoś ciram ekānta-vana-niśāntatāsīt | tadā ca nānā-saṃvadamānayor anayoḥ saṃprati saṃvadanam evaṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: Thus: when, immediately after the departure from <s>Vraja</s> to <s>Mathurā</s> of the crusher of <s>Keśī</s>, unable to behold the suffering of those people immediately [afterward], the two — <s>Pūrṇimā</s> (<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>) together with <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> and <s>Vṛndā</s> — having gone to an exceedingly distant location, long remained in the solitude of a secluded forest. And then, the conversation of those two, who were discoursing on various subjects, came to be as follows at present.

children.text: yathā-yadā sālva-yuddham udbuddhaṃ tad-duḥkhena ca goṣṭhaṃ ruddham | tadā tat-tad-vṛttaṃ vidnamānā vṛndā sa-ruditam uditavatī-bhagavati ! kim anantaram antaraṃ bhaviteti na praviśati me hṛdayam |
children.translated_text: As follows: when the battle with <s>Śālva</s> was aroused and the cow-settlement was choked by that suffering — <s>Vṛndā</s>, knowing those various events, said with weeping — 'O Blessed Lady! That there will be no interval of respite hereafter — this does not enter my heart!'

children.text: atha pūrṇimā gadgada-pūrṇaṃ gadati sma-mama ca vigamita-sarvālokena śokena vapur api na sphurati, kiim uta puraḥ-sthitam āstāṃ tāvad apuraḥsthitam ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pūrṇimā</s> spoke, her voice choked — 'For me too, with grief that has banished all perception, even the body does not manifest — how much less what stands before me! Let alone what does not stand before!'

children.text: vṛndāha-yogamāyayā bhavatyāḥ sva-gopanārtham eva tapasvi-veṣeṇa bhavantyāḥ kathaṃ madhye madhye jñānaṃ parāhanyate ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'For you, <s>Yogamāyā</s>, who have assumed the disguise of an ascetic for the purpose of concealing your true self — how is your knowledge intermittently obstructed?'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-līlā-śakti-rūpavatyā bhavatyā yathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'Just as it is for you, who are of the form of <s>Līlā-śakti</s>.'

children.text: vṛndāha-tac ca katham ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'And how is that?'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-yā kācid ekā rati-prema-praṇaya-rāgānurāga-mahābhāva-paryanta-vṛtti-mayī prīti-nāmnī hareḥ śaktir virājate, sā sarvatra pravalāyāsmad-ādīnāṃ paramāśraya-rūpaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇam api śaśvan mohayati | yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'There shines a certain power of <s>Hari</s> named <s>Prīti</s> (Love), which is constituted of the successive stages of <s>rati</s>, <s>prema</s>, <s>praṇaya</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>anurāga</s>, and <s>mahābhāva</s>. She, being supremely powerful everywhere, perpetually bewilders even Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is the form of the supreme shelter of us and others. As [said]:''

children.text: tato vatsān adṛṣṭvaitya puline'pi ca vatsapān |
ubhāv api vane kṛṣṇo vicikāya samantataḥ || [BhP 10.13.16] iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> searched for both in the forest on all sides.' ||[BhP 10.13.16]||
'Then, not seeing the calves and coming also to the bank, not [seeing] the calf-herders —

children.text: vṛndāha-tad etad api sārvatrikaṃ na dṛśyate, kāraṇaṃ tu na parāmṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'But even this is not seen as universal; the cause, however, is not grasped.'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-sa-prema-bhaktānāṃ nikaṭībhāvata eva sā śaktiḥ śrī-kṛṣṇe'pi ruciṃ prakaṭayya prakaṭībhavati |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'It is from the very proximity of devotees endowed with love that this power, having manifested its charm even in Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, becomes manifest.'

children.text: vṛndāha-prastute kim āyātam ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'What has arrived in the matter at hand?'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-parama-premavatāṃ śrīmati vraje vasatāṃ saṅgād vayam api |kiṃ bahunā, śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ svayam api prema-gaṅgā-pravāham anu magnā unmagnāś ca bhavantaḥ saṃvidam asaṃvidaṃ ca pratipadyāmahe iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'From association with those who possess supreme love, dwelling in the glorious <s>Vraja</s> — we too [are affected]. What more need be said — Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, immersed and emerging in the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> of love, attains both awareness and non-awareness.'

children.text: vṛndāha-tarhi kāsmad āśāyā gatiḥ ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'Then from what hope does a course [of action] arise?'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-bhavatyā iva svapne'pi paridevanām eva sevamānāyāḥ kṛta-kṣapaṇāyām anantara-kṣapāyāṃ ko'pi gopitātmā puruṣaḥ pustakam idaṃ mama hasta-vinyastaṃ cakāra |vicāraya tad idam iti vadan punar avadann eva kutrāpi cacāra ca | tatas tvam atra kāca-kāmalāmala-kāra-duṣpāra bāṣpānumocana-para-locanāyāṃ mayi locanāyamānā bhava |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'For me — like you — who in dream too was devoted only to lamentation, at the conclusion of the night, in the following night, some person of concealed identity placed this book in my hand, saying "Examine this!" and then, speaking again, departed somewhere. Therefore, you — with eyes devoted to releasing irrepressible tears, clear like glass [yet blurred] by the incurable jaundice-like [condition of grief] — become the one who gazes upon me here.'

children.text: vṛndā tu tad-vandamānā provāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, honoring that [book], spoke:

children.text:
parṇeṣu svarṇa-varṇeṣv amara-pati-maṇi-prakhyatāvarṇya-varṇair
nirvarṇyair gaḍhatamyām api citam abhito ratna-saṅkīrṇa-gātram |
āmukta-svaccha-muktā guṇam idam anu yat pustakaṃ kṛṣṇa-śobhāṃ
tad-vastrādi-prayuktāṃ svayam iha sa iva prādurastīti vidmaḥ ||GC_2,3.1|| (srag)
children.translated_text:
'Upon pages of golden hue, with indescribable colors resembling the jewel of the lord of the gods,
its body studded on all sides with gems even in its deeply hidden binding,
strung with a cord of clear pearls — this book, bearing the splendor of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the splendor wrought by his garments and such — appears here as if he himself has manifested — so we know!' ||GC_2,3.1||

children.text:
pūrṇimā sānandam āha-tarhi paramam arhitam eva tad idam asman-manaḥ saṃvidaṃ viditāṃ kariṣyatīti tvaritam eva vācaya |
[17] vṛndā sa-pramada-vṛndaṃ tad-vācanāspadam ācacāra |prathamaṃ tāvad bahir vihitān nāma-varṇān nirvarṇayantī varṇayāmāsa-atra kalita-tvad-bhāga-dheyaṃ śrīmad-bhāgavata-bhāga-sambhāga-jāgarūkaṃ pādmottara-khaṇḍasya khaṇḍaṃ nidhyeyam |madhye madhye tat-tat-poṣaṇāya saṃcitaṃ kiñcid anyad anyad api iti |
children.translated_text:
<s>Pūrṇimā</s> said with delight — 'Then this is supremely worthy indeed! It shall make our minds' understanding known! Read it swiftly!'
[17] <s>Vṛndā</s>, together with a company of joyful [attendants], proceeded to the place for reading it. First, examining the letters of the names inscribed on the exterior, she described — 'Here, with the share of your destiny properly arranged, one should contemplate a section of the <s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, alert to the portions of the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s>. And interspersed within, something else here and there, compiled for the nourishment of each topic.'

children.text: atha prathamaṃ paṭhyatām iti pūrṇimā-kathanānantaraṃ vṛndā papāṭha--[19] atha śrī-bhāgavata-padyāni-
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said 'Let it be read first,' <s>Vṛndā</s> read: [19] Now the verses of the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> —

children.text: tasmin nipatite pāpe saubhe ca gadayā hate |
children.translated_text: 'When that wicked <s>Saubha</s> [-fortress] was struck down by the mace and that sinner fell,

children.text: nedur dundubhayo rājan vyomni deva-gaṇeritāḥ |
children.translated_text: kettledrums sounded in the sky, O king, beaten by hosts of gods;

children.text: sakhīnām apacitiṃ kurvan dantavakro ruṣābhyagāt || (10.77.37)
children.translated_text: <s>Dantavakra</s>, avenging his friends, rushed forward in fury.' ||(10.77.37)||

children.text: śrī-śuka uvāca-
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Śuka</s> said —

children.text: śiśupālasya śālvasya pauṇḍrakasyāpi durmatiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The evil-minded one, performing posthumous friendship

children.text: para-loka-gatānāṃ ca kurvan pārokṣya-sauhṛdam ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Śiśupāla</s>, <s>Śālva</s>, and <s>Pauṇḍraka</s> who had gone to the other world —

children.text: ekaḥ padātiḥ saṅkruddho gadā-pāṇiḥ prakampayan |
children.translated_text: alone, on foot, enraged, club in hand, causing [the earth] to tremble,

children.text: padbhyām imāṃ mahā-rāja mahā-sattvo vyadṛśyata ||
children.translated_text: he of great strength was seen, O great king!

children.text: taṃ tathāyāntam ālokya gadām ādāya satvaraḥ |
avaplutya rathāt kṛṣṇaḥ sindhuṃ veleva pratyadhāt || (10.38.1-3) ity ādi |
children.translated_text: leapt from his chariot and stood firm against him, as the shore [holds] against the ocean.' ||(10.78.1-3)|| — and so forth.
Seeing him coming thus, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, swiftly seizing his club,

children.text: tad-ante ca-
children.translated_text: And at the end of that —

children.text: kṛṣṇo'pi tam ahan gurvyā kaumodakyā stanāntare |
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too struck him with the heavy <s>Kaumodakī</s> [mace] between the breasts;

children.text: gadā-nirbhinna-hṛdaya udvaman rudhiraṃ mukhāt ||
children.translated_text: his heart split by the mace, vomiting blood from his mouth,

children.text: prasārya keśa-bāhv-aṅghrīn dharaṇyāṃ nyapatad vyasuḥ|
children.translated_text: spreading out his hair, arms, and feet, he fell lifeless upon the ground.'

children.text: tataḥ sūkṣmataraṃ jyotiḥ kṛṣṇam āviśad adbhutam |
children.translated_text: Then a subtler, wondrous light entered <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: paśyatāṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ yathā caidya-vadhe nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: while all beings watched, as at the slaying of <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>), O King. ||

children.text: vidūrathas tu tad-bhrātā bhrātṛ-śoka-pariplutaḥ |
children.translated_text: But <s>Vidūratha</s>, his brother, overwhelmed by grief for his brother,

children.text: āgacchad asi-carmābhyām ucchvasaṃs taj-jighāṃsayā ||
children.translated_text: came with sword and shield, breathing heavily, desiring to kill him. ||

children.text: tasya cāpatataḥ kṛṣṇaś cakreṇa kṣura-neminā |
children.translated_text: And as he rushed forward, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with his discus of razor-sharp rim

children.text: śiro jahāra rājendra sa-kirīṭaṃ sa-kuṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: severed his head, O chief of kings, together with crown and earrings. ||

children.text: evaṃ saubhaṃ ca śālvaṃ ca dantavakraṃ sahānujam |
children.translated_text: Thus, having slain <s>Saubha</s> and <s>Śālva</s> and <s>Dantavakra</s> together with his brother,

children.text: hatvā durviṣahān anyair īḍitaḥ sura-mānavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], unbearable to others, was praised by gods and men. ||

children.text: vṛtaś ca vṛṣṇi-pravarair viveśālaṅkṛtāṃ purīm || (10.78.8-13,15)
children.translated_text: And surrounded by the foremost <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, he entered the decorated city. || (BhP 10.78.8-13,15)

children.text: pūrṇimā prāha sma-atredam adhigatam | yadā sālva-vadhaḥ sambaddhas tadā gadām ādāya dantavakraḥ sannaddhas tatra caṅkramyate sma | śrī-kṛṣṇa-gadayāpy utkramyate sma iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'Here this is understood: when the slaying of <s>Śālva</s> was connected [to the narrative], <s>Dantavakra</s>, having taken up his mace and armed himself, was pacing there. He was also dispatched by glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> mace.'

children.text: atha tad-ante tad-antevāsinī vṛndā sandideha-bhagavati ! tad idaṃ mama matim atītam | kadā nāmāvadhāritavān vidūra-dhāmā dantavakra-nāmā tat-kṣaṇārabdha-sālva-vadhābhidhānam ? avadhārayatu vā kathaṃ tadaiva daivatam iva dūra-nija-deśāt tad-deśaṃ praviveśa | tatrāpi gadā-pāṇiḥ san padātir eva kevala eva ceti katham iva ?
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of that, <s>Vṛndā</s>, the pupil of that [<s>Pūrṇimā</s>], [said]: 'O goddess of doubts! This has gone beyond my understanding. When, pray, did the one named <s>Dantavakra</s>, of distant abode (<s>Vidūra-dhāman</s>), learn of the account of <s>Śālva's</s> slaying that had just begun at that very moment? Or even granting he learned of it, how did he enter that region from his own distant land at that very instant, as if by divine [agency]? Moreover, how is it that he was merely on foot, with only a mace in hand, and completely alone?'

children.text: pūrṇimā prāha sma-utkṛṣṭaṃ pṛṣṭam | kintu tad-anantara-vācanayāpi rocaya nija-vācam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'An excellent question! But adorn your own words also with the subsequent reading.'

children.text:
vṛndā tad api vācayati sma-atha pādmottara-khaṇḍa-gadyāni-atha śiśupālaṃ nihataṃ śrutvā dantavaktraḥ kṛṣṇena yoddhuṃ mathurām ājagāma | kṛṣṇas tu tac chrutvā ratham āruhya tena yoddhuṃ mathurām āyayau | dantavaktra-vāsudevayor ahorātraṃ mathurā-pura-dvāri yamunā-tīre saṅgrāmaḥ samavartata kṛṣṇas tu gadayā taṃ jaghāna | sa tu cūrṇita-sarvāṅgo vajra-nirbhinna-mahīdhara
iva gatāsur avani-tale papāta | iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> then read that too — the prose of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s>: 'Then <s>Dantavaktra</s>, hearing that <s>Śiśupāla</s> was slain, came to <s>Mathurā</s> to fight <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, hearing of that, mounted his chariot and came to <s>Mathurā</s> to fight him. The battle between <s>Dantavakra</s> and <s>Vāsudeva</s> raged at the gate of <s>Mathurā</s> city on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> for a day and a night. And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> slew him with his mace. And he, with all limbs crushed like a mountain shattered by a thunderbolt, fell lifeless upon the surface of the earth.' — Thus.

children.text: tad evaṃ vācayitvā vṛndā papraccha-tad idaṃ purāṇa-dvayaṃ pratyuta parasparaṃ viruddham iva buddham iti |
children.translated_text: Having thus read, <s>Vṛndā</s> asked: 'These two <s>Purāṇas</s> are understood to be rather mutually contradictory!'

children.text: etad-uttaraṃ pūrṇimāyāḥ punas tat-tad-vacana-labdha-vijñāna-pūrṇitāyā uttaram-na hi na hi ! kintu śrīmad-bhāgavatasya tāvad asaṃbaddha-bhāṣitā na sambhavati | tathā purāṇāntareṇa sambhavati caika-vākyatve vākya-bhedo na nyāyya iti vākyaika-vākyatānyathānupapattyā tad idaṃ gamyate |
children.translated_text: In reply, <s>Pūrṇimā</s> — now filled with the knowledge obtained from each of those statements — answered: 'Not at all, not at all! But the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s>, at any rate, cannot have spoken incoherently. And since it is possible through another <s>Purāṇa</s> to achieve unity of statement, it is not proper to split the statements when single-statement harmony [is achievable]. Therefore, through the principle that statements must be harmonized when no other interpretation is possible, this is understood as follows:'

children.text: yatra prathamaṃ sālvasyeva śiśupālena saha rājasūyam anāgatasya tasya pṛthvī-prakampana-gati-sampattayā prasiddhatayā mahā-sattvatayā sindhutayā vajra-nirbhinna-mahīdharatayā ca paṭhitayā sahasā prabalatamatāṃ prāptaḥ so'yam ity avagatasya smara-harārādhanaṃ tarkyate | yatra eva varābhāsena nirvāsyataḥ pāda-ghāta-pratīka-saṅghātayor anusandhānam aduḥsandhānam avadhīyate |
children.translated_text: 'Herein, first — just as <s>Śālva</s> [was associated] with <s>Śiśupāla</s> — the worship of the Destroyer of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) by this one (<s>Dantavakra</s>) who had not come to the <s>Rājasūya</s> is inferred, [given] his well-known prowess as attested by the reading of his earth-shaking gait, his great might, his [being like] an ocean, and [his body being like] a mountain shattered by a thunderbolt. Herein, the connection between the foot-stamping and the retinue-gathering of one being expelled by a seeming boon is observed to be not ill-designed.'

children.text: tatra ca sati manoratha-gati-prathakasya muramathana-rathasya ca vaibhavaṃ susambhavam avagamyate | tathā hari-lipsita-saṃprahāra-līlāṃ valayitur manojavatāṃ kalayitus tat-tad-vṛtta-saṃcāraṇāviśāradasya śrī-nāradasya ca sāhāyakam udīkṣyate |
children.translated_text: 'And that being so, the power of the chariot of the Crusher of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), which extends the range of wishes, is well understood as plausible. Likewise, the assistance of glorious <s>Nārada</s> — who is skilled in directing the course of each event and capable of arranging mind-like speed to encircle the battle-sport desired by <s>Hari</s> — is perceived.'

children.text: tad evam eva śrī-bhāgavate-
children.translated_text: Thus indeed in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> —

children.text: sakhīnām apacitiṃ kurvan dantavakro ruṣābhagāt |
children.translated_text: '<s>Dantavakra</s>, honoring his friends, rushed forward in anger,

children.text: śiśupālasya śālvasya pauṇḍrakasyāpi durmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the evil-minded one — of <s>Śiśupāla</s>, <s>Śālva</s>, and <s>Pauṇḍraka</s>.' ||

children.text: ity atra śālvo'pi gaṇitaḥ |
children.translated_text: — here <s>Śālva</s> too is counted [among his friends].

children.text: pādme ca-kṛṣṇas tu tac chrutvā iti gaditam | kintu-mahā-sattvo vyadṛśyata [BhP 10.78.2] iti yac chrī-bhāgavata-vacanaṃ tat tu dṛṣṭo'py asau śrī-nārada-vacanena vijñāta-tattva iti gamyate |
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Padma</s>: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, hearing of that' — thus it is stated. But the <s>Bhāgavata</s> statement 'he appeared as a great being' [BhP 10.78.2] is understood to mean that although he was seen, his true nature was known through the words of glorious <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text:
tathā ca sati nihata-śiśupālaṃ śrī-gopālam indraprasthād akṛta-prasthānaṃ niśamya mathurām āgamya pathi nirdvandvaṃ taṃ prati dvandva-yuddhena paripanthitācaraṇāya sthitaḥ | prāg eva taṃ dvārakāṃ prasthitam ākalayya saṃśayya kṛta-vicāra-cakraḥ sa khalu dantavakras tac cakrapāṇiḥ svayaṃ līlā-sukha-sāradena śrī-nāradena sālva-vadhādikam avadhārayāmāse | dvārakā-nāthaś ca tathā tat-kathanayā
tad-āgamana-sākṣātkāra-prathanayā ca manovad atīta-pathena tena rathena tatrāpayāmāse | nūnam iti mata-dvayam anūnam eka-mataṃ syāt | tad idam api vyaktam adya śva eva viśeṣād vyaktaṃ bhaviṣyati | punar uttaram uttara-viṣayī-kriyatām |
children.translated_text: And that being so — hearing that glorious <s>Gopāla</s> who had slain <s>Śiśupāla</s> had not yet departed from <s>Indraprastha</s>, [<s>Dantavakra</s>] came to <s>Mathurā</s> and stationed himself to obstruct him on the path with a duel, without rival. Having previously calculated that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] was departing for <s>Dvārakā</s>, and having reconsidered, this <s>Dantavakra</s> — with his deliberation-wheel — and that Wielder of the Discus himself, through glorious <s>Nārada</s> whose essence is the pleasure of sport — ascertained the slaying of <s>Śālva</s> and the rest. And the Lord of <s>Dvārakā</s>, by [<s>Nārada's</s>] narrating those events and by his manifesting the direct realization of that one's arrival, traveled there by that chariot which traverses the path-beyond-mind. Surely, thus the two views would become perfectly one view. And this too will become clear — especially clearly — today or tomorrow itself. Let the next topic be taken up next.'
