children.text: atha vṛndā paṭhati sma | paṭhantiī ca naṭantīvāsīt | tatra pūrvavat tad-gadyaṃ, yathā- kṛṣṇo'pi taṃ hatvā yamunām uttīrya nanda-vrajaṃ gatvā prāktanau pitarāv abhivādya āśvāsya tābhyāṃ sāśrukaṇṭham āliṅgitaḥ sakala-gopa-vṛddhān praṇamyāśvāsya ratnābharaṇādibhis tatrasthān santarpayāmāsa | iti |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> read. And reading, she was like one dancing. There, as before, the prose [of the <s>Padma</s>]: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too, having slain him, crossing the <s>Yamunā</s>, going to <s>Nanda's</s> <s>Vraja</s>, saluting and consoling his former parents, was embraced by them with tear-choked voices. Bowing to all the elder cowherds and consoling them, he gratified those present there with jewels, ornaments, and other gifts.' — Thus.

children.text: tad etat paṭhitvā ca vṛndā punar ucchalad-bāṣpaṃ papraccha-tad idam api kiṃ śrīmad-bhāgavata-saṃmatam ?
children.translated_text: Having read this, <s>Vṛndā</s> again asked with welling tears: 'Is this too approved by the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s>?'

children.text: pūrṇimā pūrṇa-manāḥ prāha sma-dṛśyatām uttara-vibhāgaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, with fulfilled mind, said: 'Let the later section be examined.'

children.text: vṛndā punaḥ śrī-bhāgavata iti paṭhitvā papāṭha-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> again, having said 'In the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s>,' read:

children.text: tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāne yadūttamaḥ |
sāntvayām āsa sa-premair āyāsya iti dautyakaiḥ || [BhP 10.38.35] iti |
children.translated_text: consoled them with loving messages [saying] "I shall come."' || [BhP 10.38.35] — thus.
'Seeing them thus afflicted at his departure, the best of the <s>Yadus</s>

children.text: pūrṇimovāca-mathurā-prasthāna-sthānam idaṃ vacanam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This statement pertains to the occasion of the departure for <s>Mathurā</s>.'

children.text: vṛndā punaḥ papāṭha-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> again read:

children.text: yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān |
children.translated_text: 'Go, all of you, to <s>Vraja</s>, dear ones; and we, [wishing to see] the grief-stricken

children.text: jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham || [BhP 10.45.23]
children.translated_text: kinsmen of yours filled with affection — we shall come to see them, having accomplished the happiness of our friends.' || [BhP 10.45.23]

children.text: pūrṇimā jagāda-kaṃsa-vadhād dina-katipayānantaraṃ śrī-vrajeśādi-vraja-vrāje tad idaṃśrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This is the statement of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to the <s>Vraja</s> assembly led by the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, a few days after <s>Kaṃsa's</s> slaying.'

children.text: vṛndā punaḥ papāṭha-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> again read:

children.text: hatvā kaṃsaṃ raṅga-madhye pratīpaṃ sarva-sātvatām |
yad āha vaḥ samāgatya kṛṣṇaḥ satyaṃ karoti tat || [10.46.35] iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> will truly fulfill what he said when he comes to you.' || [BhP 10.46.35] — thus.
'Having slain <s>Kaṃsa</s> in the midst of the arena, the adversary of all <s>Sātvatas</s>,

children.text: āgamiṣyaty adīrgheṇa kālena vrajam acyutaḥ |
priyaṃ vidhāsyate pitror bhagavān sātvatāṃ patiḥ || [10.46.34] iti ca |
children.translated_text: the glorious lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s> will bring joy to his parents.' || [BhP 10.46.34] — thus also.
'<s>Acyuta</s> will come to <s>Vraja</s> before long,

children.text: pūrṇimovāca-tad idam uddhava-sandeśatayā buddham | atra ca draṣṭum iti darśanam eva puruṣārtha ity arthaḥ | pitroḥ priyaṃ vidhāsyate iti tad-eka-puruṣārthatve'pi tayor abhīṣṭaṃ nitya-nija-lālanā-rūpam ity arthaḥ | [36] pūrṇimāha-punar vācyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This is understood as being in the context of <s>Uddhava's</s> message. And here, "to see" means that seeing itself is the supreme goal of life. "He will bring joy to his parents" means that even though [seeing] is the sole supreme goal for them as well, what they desire is the form of constant personal fondling.' [36] <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'Let more be recited.'

children.text: vṛndā vācayati sma-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> read:

children.text: mayy āveśya manaḥ kṛtsnaṃ vimuktāśeṣa-vṛtti yat |
children.translated_text: 'Having fixed your entire mind on me, freed from all other activities,

children.text: anusmarantyo māṃ nityam acirān mām upaiṣyatha || [BhP 10.47.36]
children.translated_text: constantly remembering me — you shall attain me before long.' || [BhP 10.47.36]

children.text: pūrṇimāha-so'py eṣa śrīmad-uddhava-sandeśa eva | atrāsmac-chabda-padānāṃ mayi ity-ādinā trir-āvṛttis tatra ca prathamataḥ kṛṣṇe iti viśiṣya śiṣyamāṇayor api mā māṃ ity anayor vibhakti-vipariṇāmenānuvṛttim abhipretya kṛṣṇākāreṇaiva sva-prāptiḥ prakaraṇa-nigamanāyām abhipretā | kintv anyad vācyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This too is part of the message of glorious <s>Uddhava</s>. Herein, the triple occurrence of the first-person words — "on me," "me," and "me" — with the alteration of case-endings of "mā" and "mām" [which could mean both 'me' and 'do not'], while being instructed as if addressed to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> specifically — [is understood as intending that] self-attainment in the very form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is intended for the conclusion of the topic. But let something else be recited.'

children.text: vṛndā prāha-asti cātra kiṃcana harivaṃśa-vacanam-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'And here there is also a <s>Harivaṃśa</s> statement —'

children.text:
ahaṃ sa eva go-madhye gopaiḥ saha vanecaraḥ |
prītimān vicariṣyāmi kāmacārī yathā gajaḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
'I, that very one, shall wander in the midst of cows, together with cowherds, a forest-dweller,
delighted, moving freely like an elephant!' || — thus.

children.text: pūrṇimā cāha-tad idaṃ kaṃsa-vadhād uttaram ugrasenaṃ prati śrī-kaṃsa-jit pratyuttaraṃ mad-vyākhyāna-sākṣitayā lakṣitam |
children.translated_text: And <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This is noted — through the witness of my commentary — as the reply of the glorious Conqueror of <s>Kaṃsa</s> to <s>Ugrasena</s>, after <s>Kaṃsa's</s> slaying.'

children.text: atha vṛndā tadaitad-ukti-viṣayī-kṛtya nṛtyantīva tad idam uktavatī-satyaṃ satya-saṅkalpasya tasya vacanaṃ nāsatyatām ṛcchet | yadi ca śrī-bhāgavatād eva punar vrajāgamana-vacanaṃ sākṣāt karṇa-sukha-racanam ālocayāmi, tadā tat-param eva rocanaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s>, making this statement the subject, as if dancing, said this: 'Truly, the word of one whose resolve is truth would not become untruth. And if I contemplate yet another direct, ear-delighting statement about the return to <s>Vraja</s> from the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> itself, then that alone would be pleasing above all.'

children.text: pūrṇimāpy utsukatā-pūrṇam uvāca-ullekhaya tad-uttara-lekham | kadācit tad api sampradāya kalpeta |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> too said, filled with eagerness: 'Point out that subsequent letter. Perhaps that too would prove authoritative.'

children.text: vṛndā sānandam ūce-asti kiṃcit | yathā śrī-bhāgavata eva-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said joyfully: 'There is something! As follows, in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> itself —'

children.text: yarhy ambujākṣāpasasāra bho bhavān
children.translated_text: 'Whenever you, O lotus-eyed one, departed, O sir,

children.text: kurūn madhūn vātha suhṛd-didṛkṣayā |
children.translated_text: for the <s>Kurus</s> or the <s>Madhus</s>, or to visit friends,

children.text: tatrābda-koṭi-pratimaḥ kṣaṇo bhaved
children.translated_text: then each moment became like a crore of years,

children.text: raviṃ vinākṣṇor iva nas tavācyuta || [BhP 1.11.9]
children.translated_text: like eyes without the sun, for us, O <s>Acyuta</s>.' || [BhP 1.11.9]

children.text: pūrṇimovāca-tad idaṃ bhāvi-bhārata-yuddhānantaraṃ śrī-dvārakā-pater dvārakā-praveśo dvārakā-prajā-vacanam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This is the statement of the <s>Dvārakā</s> citizens at the future entry of the lord of glorious <s>Dvārakā</s> into <s>Dvārakā</s>, after the <s>Bhārata</s> war.'

children.text: atra vṛndā nivedayāmāsa-padyam idaṃ viśadyatām |
children.translated_text: Here <s>Vṛndā</s> submitted: 'Let this verse be explained.'

children.text: pūrṇimātha varṇayāmāsa yathā-kurūn iti kuru-deśasya, tathā madhūn iti mathurā-deśasya samuddeśaḥ | suhṛdo'py atra dvārakā-prasthānāt parastād vrajasthā eveti vyavasthāpayan | yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> then explained thus: '<s>Kurus</s>' refers to the <s>Kuru</s> region, and '<s>Madhus</s>' refers to the <s>Mathurā</s> region. And 'friends' here are established as being those in <s>Vraja</s>, [visited] after the departure for <s>Dvārakā</s>. As follows:

children.text: balabhadraḥ kuru-śreṣṭha bhagavān ratham āsthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Balabhadra</s>, O best of <s>Kurus</s>, the glorious one, mounting his chariot,

children.text: suhṛd-didṛkṣur utkaṇṭhaḥ prayayau nanda-gokulam || [BhP 10.65.1]
children.translated_text: yearning, desirous of seeing his friends, set forth for <s>Nanda's</s> <s>Gokula</s>.' || [BhP 10.65.1]

children.text: vṛndovāca-tad idaṃ kālāntara-bhāvīti ca sambhāvitaṃ syāt | na tu paraṃ dantavakra-saṃyad-anantara-bhāvi iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'This could be considered as pertaining to a later time. But not exclusively as occurring after the battle with <s>Dantavakra</s>.'

children.text: pūrṇimā vimṛśya punar dṛśyatām ity upadideśa |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, having reflected, instructed: 'Let [more] be examined.'

children.text: vṛndā punar uvāca-āṃ āṃ punaḥ śrī-bhāgavatīyaṃ padyam ekaṃ pratipadyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> again said: 'Ah, ah! Again, one verse from the <s>Bhāgavata</s> comes to mind:'

children.text: api smaratha naḥ sakhyaḥ svānām artha-cikīrṣayā |
children.translated_text: 'Do you remember us, O friends? — those gone for a long time

children.text: gatāṃś cirāyitāñ chatru-pakṣa-kṣapaṇa-cetasaḥ || [BhP 10.82.41]
children.translated_text: with the intent of accomplishing the purpose of their own — with minds set on destroying the enemy's faction?' || [BhP 10.82.41]

children.text: tad etad vācayitvā vṛndā punar uvāca-kim anena samunneyam ?
children.translated_text: Having read this, <s>Vṛndā</s> again said: 'What is to be inferred from this?'

children.text:
pūrṇimā prāha sma-tad idaṃ kurukṣetra-yātrāyāṃ śrī-rāma-bhrātā nija-sneha-pātrāṇāṃ vraja-tanu-gātrāṇāṃ duḥkha-trāṇāya bhaṅgyā śatru-pakṣa-kṣapaṇam evāvadhitayā pratijñātam | śatru-pakṣa-kṣapaṇaṃ ca svadūratha-dantavakra-saṃyad-antam eva | tad-anantaraṃ hi svayaṃ śastra-hastatā saṃnyastā syāt | tasmād idam api sarva-sukha-sadma-padma-purāṇa-mataṃ
śrīmad-bhāgavata-bhāg avagatam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This, at the pilgrimage to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, is the brother of <s>Rāma's</s> pledge — indirectly, for the rescue from sorrow of his own objects of affection, the slender-bodied inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> — that the destruction of the enemy's faction alone was his committed purpose. And the destruction of the enemy's faction extends only up to the battle with <s>Śālva</s>, <s>Dantavakra</s>, and such. After that, the taking up of weapons would be renounced. Therefore, this too is understood as the portion of the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> concordant with the view of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, the abode of all happiness, the lotus [<s>Purāṇa</s>].'

children.text: tataḥ kaścid dantavakra-vadhaṃ kutracin manyatāṃ nāma | tad-anantaraṃ tu śrī-kṛṣṇasya vrajāgamanam avaśyam eva mantavyam | itīdaṃ procya bhagavatī punaḥ provāca-kiṃcid anyad asti ?
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let someone consider the slaying of <s>Dantavakra</s> to have occurred wherever [they wish]. But after that, the return of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to <s>Vraja</s> must necessarily be accepted.' Having declared this, the goddess (<s>Pūrṇimā</s>) again said: 'Is there anything else?'

children.text:
vṛndovāca-tathaivādhvanya-veṣeṇa ity ādinā pūrvaṃ darśitaṃ śrī-rāmasya vrajād āgatasya śrī-kṛṣṇena saṃvāda-rūpaṃ harivaṃśa-vacanam eva papāṭha |
[54] atha tad-abhiprāyaṃ pūrṇimā prāha-atra yad-vrajād āgataṃ rāmam agrajaṃ rahasi rāmānujaḥ pratyeka-vraja-jīva-kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭavān | yac ca sarveṣāṃ kuśalaṃ kṛṣṇa yeṣāṃ kuśalam icchasi iti | tasmād uttaraṃ labdhavāṃs tasmād bhāvi-nija-saṅgama-maṅgalam api tatra dvayor api bhāvitaṃ babhūva | tatrodāsīnatāyāṃ tatrāpy udāsīnatā syād iti |
children.translated_text:
<s>Vṛndā</s> said — she read the very <s>Harivaṃśa</s> statement, previously shown, in the form of a conversation of glorious <s>Rāma</s> who had come from <s>Vraja</s> with glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, beginning with 'in the guise of a traveler.'
[54] Then <s>Pūrṇimā</s> spoke the purport of that: 'Herein, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, having come from <s>Vraja</s>, asked his elder brother <s>Rāma</s> in private about the well-being of each and every person of <s>Vraja</s>. And the reply he received was: "All is well, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with those whose well-being you desire." From that, the auspiciousness of a future personal meeting between the two was also contemplated. For if there were indifference there, there would also be indifference here.'

children.text: atha tena nidigdha-dhīr api vṛndā sandigdham ācacāra-padma-purāṇam iva katham acchadma na tad vraja-pratyāgamanaṃ vacana-sadma cakāra sa ca purāṇa-sāraḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s>, though of penetrating intellect, spoke with some doubt: 'How is it that the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> — that essence of <s>Purāṇas</s> — did not make the return to <s>Vraja</s> a mere verbal dwelling [i.e., a figurative expression], but rather openly [stated it]?'

children.text:
pūrṇimā babhāṣe-śrīmad-bhāgavataṃ khalv idaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhāg-avataṃsa iti śaṃsanti | tac ca nija-rahasyam idaṃ na vyaktaṃ vaktuṃ vyavasyati | tac ca garva-sthemnā svatantraṃ-manyatayā nānānya-sampat-kāmanādhīnānāṃ tad-udāsīnānāṃ maty-avaguṇṭhanārthaṃ premṇā gokula-lokaṃ-manyatayā tam upāsīnānāṃ
viśiṣṭa-tan-nijābhīṣṭa-spaṣṭa-śravaṇa-vihīnānāṃ bāḍham utkaṇṭhanārthaṃ ca iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> spoke: 'The glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> is indeed proclaimed as the crest-jewel among the portions of glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. And it does not resolve to declare this personal secret openly. And that [reticence] is twofold in purpose: for the veiling of the understanding of those who, through the firmness of pride, consider themselves independent and do not depend on the wealth of any other — those indifferent ones; and for the intensification of longing among those who, through love, consider themselves as belonging to the people of <s>Gokula</s>, who worship him though they are deprived of a clear hearing of his specific personal wish.'

children.text: vṛndovāca-pūrveṣāṃ maty-avaguṇṭhanā samucitā | pareṣām utkaṇṭhanā tu kim arthaṃ samuditā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'The veiling of the understanding of the former is fitting. But for what purpose was the longing of the latter intensified?'

children.text: pūrṇimā vadati sma-
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said:

children.text: utkaṇṭhayā saha premā dhatte mithunatāṃ yadā |
children.translated_text: 'When longing and love assume the state of a couple,

children.text: aṅgajaṃ hari-saṅgākhyaṃ tadā bhajati nānyadā ||GC_2,3.2||
children.translated_text: then they beget the offspring called "union with <s>Hari</s>" — and not otherwise.' ||GC_2,3.2||

children.text: vṛndā viramānandān nirīhatayā smitvā prāha-janmārabhya kiyad varṣānantaraṃ kaṃsāntakasya yad-upattanād vrajāgamana-śantamam idaṃ janitā |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, smiling with effortless delight at the cessation of [her doubt], said: 'How many years after birth was this supreme tranquility of the return to <s>Vraja</s> of the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> brought about from his place of residence?'

children.text:
pūrṇimā sa-praṇidhānam āha-bhārata-rītyā bhārata-yuddhānantaraṃ yudhiṣṭhirasya prājyaṃ rājyaṃ tasya ṣaṣṭhi-varṣata eva janitā | śrī-viṣṭaraśravāś cārjuna-savayaskatā-viśiṣṭatayā yudhiṣṭhirasya varṣa-traya-kaniṣṭhas tadānīṃ sapta-pañcāśad-varṣatām āpsyatīti lakṣyate | tatra tu tad-yuddhataḥ pūrvād vanājñāta-vāsa-maya-varṣa-trayodaśakāt
pūrvaṃ sālva-dantavakra-dhūrvaṇam iti tasya vrajāgamana-samaya-vicāraṇāyāṃ varṣāṇāṃ catuś-catvariṃśad evāvaśiṣyate | tad-uttara-kālataḥ prakāśāntareṇa puryāṃ sthitasya pṛthivī-pālane tu bhāratāc chrī-bhāgavataṃ mataṃ vilakṣaṇam iti tad-eka-vākyatāyām aśakyatayākalpa-bheda-kalpanam eva kalpate | na tu tad atra prayojakam | tatas tad astu, prastutaṃ tu prastūyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said with careful consideration: 'According to the <s>Bhārata</s> tradition, the abundant reign of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> after the <s>Bhārata</s> war was generated from his sixtieth year itself. And glorious <s>Viṣṭaraśravas</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), being distinguished by his being of the same age as <s>Arjuna</s>, is observed to have been three years younger than <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, thus attaining fifty-seven years at that time. But therein, since the destruction of <s>Śālva</s> and <s>Dantavakra</s> was prior to the thirteen years of forest-dwelling and incognito exile preceding that war, in the calculation of the time of his return to <s>Vraja</s>, only forty-four years remain. After that time, regarding his dwelling in the city by another manifestation while governing the earth — the <s>Bhāgavata</s> and the <s>Bhārata</s> are understood to hold divergent views, and since single-statement-harmony is impossible in that case, the postulation of a difference in <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles) alone is appropriate. But that is not relevant here. So let that be; let the topic at hand be pursued.'

children.text: vṛndovāca-kṛṣṇo'pi taṃ hatvā iti gadyānantaraṃ pādma-padya-dvayam iti likhitvā likhitam-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — having written after the prose 'And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too, having slain him,' 'two verses from the <s>Padma</s>,' she read:

children.text: kālindyāḥ puline ramye puṇya-vṛkṣa-samāvṛte |
children.translated_text: 'On the beautiful bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), covered with auspicious trees,

children.text: gopa-nārībhir aniśaṃ krīḍayāmāsa keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> sported incessantly with the cowherd women.' ||

children.text: ramya-keli-sukhenaiva gopa-veṣa-dharo hariḥ |
baddha-prema-rasenātra māsa-dvayam uvāsa ha || [PadmaP 6.252.19-27] iti |
children.translated_text: dwelt there for two months, bound by the rasa of love.' || [PadmaP 6.252.19-27] — thus.
'With the happiness of delightful play alone, <s>Hari</s>, wearing the garb of a cowherd,

children.text: athāsya vṛndā tātparyaṃ paryanuyuktavatī |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> inquired about its purport.

children.text: pūrṇimā covāca-gopa-nārībhiḥ ity atra nṛ-narayor vṛddhiś ceti jātāv eva strī-pratyaya-vidhānād gopa-jātibhir nārībhir iti gamyam | tṛtīya-skandhe devahūtim uddiśya kardamaṃ prati śrī-śukla-vacane
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> also said: '"With the cowherd women" — here, since the feminine suffix in <s>nārī</s> is prescribed only in the sense of birth-class (according to the rule "the <s>vṛddhi</s> of <s>nṛ</s> and <s>nara</s> [applies] in birth-class"), it is understood as "women of the cowherd birth-class." In the third <s>skandha</s> (canto), in the statement of glorious <s>Śukla</s> (<s>Kapila</s>) addressed to <s>Devahūti</s> concerning <s>Kardama</s> —'

children.text: dṛśyate ca tad-anuvādi-mṛtyuñjaya-saṃhitā-vacanam-
children.translated_text: And the statement of the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya-saṃhitā</s>, which echoes that, is seen:

children.text:
smared vṛndāvane ramye mohayantam anāratam |
govindaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ gopa-kanyāḥ sahasraśaḥ |
muktāhāra-lasat-pīna-tuṅga-stana-bharānanāḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
'One should meditate on <s>Govinda</s>, the lotus-eyed one, in beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, enchanting ceaselessly,
and on the thousands of cowherd maidens, with full, high breasts adorned with pearl necklaces.' — thus.

children.text: gautamīye ca-
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Gautamīya</s>:

children.text:
gopa-kanyā-sahasrais tu padma-patrāyatekṣaṇaiḥ |
arcitaṃ bhāva-kusumais trailokyaika-guruṃ param || iti |
children.translated_text:
'Worshipped with devotion-flowers by thousands of cowherd maidens with lotus-petal-wide eyes —
the one supreme guru of the three worlds.' — thus.

children.text:
brahma-rātra upāvṛtte ity ādy-uktād vilakṣaṇena aniśaṃ ity anena ca tat-patiṃmanyādiṣu vāstavābhīrīṇāṃ vivāhādi-vañcanārthaṃ nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya ity ādy-ukta-diśā yā mayā yoga-māyayā sṛṣṭās tāsu punar vyaktī-kriyamāṇāsu pūrvāsāṃ para-dāratva-bhramāpakramānantaraṃ saṅkoca-mocanaṃ gamyate | tac cāvaśyaṃ tatrāvagantavyam | tatra hi sarve guṇā lajjānuguṇā eva kīrtyante
| tathā hi hari-vaṃśe śrī-nāradena tasya praśaṃseyaṃ yādava-saṃsadāṃ karṇāvataṃsavad ācarati sma |
children.translated_text: By the word 'incessantly,' which differs from [the Bhāgavata's] statement beginning with 'when the <s>Brahmā</s>-night had ended,' the removal of inhibition after the removal of the misconception of the real <s>Ābhīra</s> women's status as wives of others is understood — in the direction stated by [the verse] 'they did not indeed reproach <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — [explaining that] those [gopīs] whom <s>yogamāyā</s> had manufactured as 'considering him their husband,' etc., when they were again being made manifest, after the prior removal of the delusion of being wives of others, the release from inhibition is understood. And this must necessarily be understood there. For therein all virtues are praised as being in accordance with modesty. Thus, in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, this praise by glorious <s>Nārada</s> functioned as an ear-ornament for the assemblies of the <s>Yādavas</s>:

children.text: yatra hrīḥ śrīḥ sthitā tatra yatra śrīs tatra sannatiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Where modesty abides, there <s>Śrī</s> (fortune) stands; where <s>Śrī</s> stands, there is humility;

children.text: sannatir hrīs tathā śrīś ca nityaṃ kṛṣṇe mahātmani || [HV 2.101.73]
children.translated_text: humility, modesty, and <s>Śrī</s> — eternally [dwell] in the great-souled <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' || [HV 2.101.73]

children.text:
tad evam eva ramya-keli-sukhenaiva ity anena, bahu-prema-rasena ity anena cātra vraje tat-keli-sukhasya sarva-manorathatvaṃ nānā-prema-rasadatvaṃ ca darśitaṃ syāt | tad evam eva ca pūrvaṃ yad asūyā-rāhityaṃ teṣu māyayā sampāditam, tac ca mahā-viraheṇa vyakta-rahasyāsv apy etāsu nirvyūḍhaṃ syāt | kiṃ ca yā śrī-bhagavataḥ pratikalpam avaśyambhāvi-tādṛśatā-svabhāvāvatāra-līlāt
preyasī-prema-prabhāva-vyañjanāya tat-priya-jana-rañjanāya ca khelantī janaka-kanyāyām iva gopa-kanyā-śreṇyāṃ tasya nitya-kāntāsmīti jñānaṃ yadyapy āvṛtavatī, tathāpi premāṇām avarītuṃ na śaktavatī |
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, by 'with the happiness of delightful play alone' and by 'with abundant rasa of love,' the fact that the happiness of his play in <s>Vraja</s> fulfills all desires and bestows manifold rasas of love is shown. And thus, the absence of envy in them that was previously accomplished through <s>māyā</s> — that too, through the great separation, would be fully accomplished even in these [gopīs] whose secret was now manifest. Moreover, the <s>yogamāyā</s>, which — from the necessarily-occurring sport of his descent in every <s>kalpa</s> — while playing to manifest the power of the love of his beloveds and to delight his dear ones, as in the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), so too in the host of cowherd maidens — though she had veiled the knowledge 'I am his eternal beloved,' she was nevertheless unable to veil their love.

children.text:
yaḥ khalu premā tādṛśa-tal-līlā-paravaśatayā tasyā iva tasyāḥ para-hasta-patanāvasthāyām api tat-pātivratyaṃ pratipālayitā, sa evāyatyām api tāṃ duḥkha-rūpāṃ śamayitvā melayitā syād eveti māsmānyathā manyathāḥ | tathā hi, ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmy aham iti tat-tad-vacanaṃ prasiddham | tat khalu para-dāratāpa-krama-racanā-pūrvaka-tan-milanārtham eva tāsāṃ
sacate | bhaktānāṃ yādṛṅ-manoratha-prakāratā, tādṛg eva mad-ākāratāviṣkāra iti hi tatra vivakṣitam | tat-prakāratā ca tac-chreṇīnām ittham eva-aho kadācid evaṃ bhāgyam asmākaṃ bhavitā | yad anya-patnītva-pratītir ayatnībhūya duḥsvapnatayā mithyā syāt tat-patnītvam eva jāgaratayā tvarayā satyaṃ syād iti |
children.translated_text: The very love that — through submission to such play of his — would maintain her fidelity to him (<s>pātivratya</s>) even in the condition of falling into another's hands, as with her (<s>Sītā</s>), so with those (<s>gopīs</s>) — that very [love] in the future too, having pacified that sorrow-form, would bring about union. So do not think otherwise. For thus, the well-known statement of his is: 'As they surrender to me, so do I reward them.' That indeed serves the purpose of uniting with them through the procedure of first establishing the anguish of being wives of others. For what is intended there is: 'As is the manner of the devotees' desire, so is the manifestation of my own form.' And the manner of those hosts [of gopīs] was precisely this: 'Ah! Some day such fortune will be ours — that the perception of being another's wife, becoming effortless, would become false as a nightmare, and being his wife alone would become true with urgency, as wakefulness!'

children.text: āstām iha para-puruṣe rāgi-strīṇāṃ tathā rītiḥ | anyatra ca tat-sadṛśāṃ gṛhiṇī-bhāvaḥ sadāpīṣṭaḥ | tathā ca tābhir evābhipretam | gopyaḥ kim ācarad ayaṃ kuśalaṃ sma veṇur dāmodarādhara-sudhām api gopikānām bhuṅkte svayam iti |
children.translated_text: Let us leave aside the matter of the conduct of women enamored of another's husband. Elsewhere too, the status of being a housewife of those similar to them is always desired. And thus was intended by them themselves: '<s>Gopīs</s>! What has this flute done — the well-born one! — that it drinks for itself the nectar of <s>Dāmodara's</s> lips, even [the share] of the <s>gopikās</s>?'

children.text: api bata madhu-puryām ārya-putro'dhunāste
children.translated_text: 'Does the noble husband now dwell in <s>Madhu's</s> city?

children.text: smarati sa pitṛ-gehān saumya bandhūṃś ca gopān |
children.translated_text: Does he remember, O gentle one, his father's homes and the cowherd kinsmen?

children.text: kvacid api sa kathāṃ naḥ kiṅkarīṇāṃ gṛṇīte
children.translated_text: Does he ever speak of us, his maidservants?

children.text: bhujam aguru-sugandhaṃ mūrdhny adhāsyat kadā nu || [BhP 10.47.21]
children.translated_text: When will he place his arm, fragrant with <s>aguru</s>, upon our heads?' || [BhP 10.47.21]

children.text: atra yaḥ khalv asmākam ārya-putra-śabda-vācyasya pratyutas tasya svīyāḥ smaḥ ity abhimānas tatra guptam asti | tadaiva tāḥ kiṅkarya iti matyāpi kadā svayaṃ vyaktam aṅgīkāriṇā tenāsmān aṅgīkariṣyata iti | ity atra ārya-putraḥ ity anena tatra patitvaṃ vyajya naḥ kiṅkarīṇām ity ādinā tathā tadīya-svīkāraḥ prakaṭam eva syād iti vyañjitam |
children.translated_text: Herein, the self-regard 'We are his own' — expressed by the word '<s>ārya-putra</s>' (noble husband) — is secretly present there. At the same time, by the expression 'us, his maidservants' — [they ask] 'When will he, who of his own accord openly accepts, accept us?' Thus, by '<s>ārya-putra</s>' their wifehood [to him] is suggested, and by 'us, his maidservants' and so forth, the disclosure that such acceptance by him would become manifest is indicated.

children.text: tad etad ātmanaḥ śrīmad-vrajāgamanam | vrajāgamanam anu ca tāsu svīyatāprakṭī-karaṇam eva śubhaṅkaraṇam iti śrīmad-vrajendra-nandanena svayam eva vyañjitam |
children.translated_text: Thus, this is his return to glorious <s>Vraja</s>. And following the return to <s>Vraja</s>, the making manifest of their own-ness [to him] in those [<s>gopīs</s>] is itself the auspicious act — as indicated by the glorious son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> himself.

children.text: dhārayanty ati-kṛcchreṇa prāyaḥ prāṇān kathañcana |
children.translated_text: 'They sustain their life-breaths with extreme difficulty, somehow, barely,

children.text: pratyāgamana-sandeśair ballavyo me mad-ātmikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: through messages of my return — those cowherd women who have me as their very self.' ||

children.text: iti tad-vacanaṃ hi tāsu svīyatām | svīyatāyām api tad-eka-svarūpatāṃ, tathāpi vidūra-sthitatayā visūrita-pūritatāṃ tat-pratyāgamanam api pratyāyayati | tathā ca sati yathā tāsu virahasya duḥsahatā tathā parakīyatākhyāteś ceti khyāpayati | athavā, tām imāṃ tato'py adhikām adhigamayati | tatas tām avaśyam eva naśyantīṃ kariṣyāmīti paryavasāyayati |
children.translated_text: For this statement of his conveys their own-ness to them; and within that own-ness, their identity with him alone; and yet, because of being situated far away, the state of being deeply distressed — and also [conveys] his return. And that being so, just as the unbearability of separation for them, so too the renown called <s>parakīyā</s> (being another's) — this it proclaims. Or rather, it causes one to understand this [suffering] as even greater than that. Therefore, it concludes: 'I shall certainly destroy that which is inevitably perishing.'

children.text: vṛndā prāha-yuṣmad-bhāvitam evāyuṣmad bhavitā |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'What you have contemplated — that very thing, O long-lived one, shall come to be!'

children.text: pūrṇimāpy āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> also said:

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇāsvāditādharāsu vijita-śrīṣu vraja-strīṣu sā
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Vraja</s> women — conquered in splendor — whose lips have been tasted by glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: māyā-mātra-mayī bhaved vivahanādy-utthā parocchiṣṭatā |
children.translated_text: the state of being another's leavings, arising from marriage and such, would be merely <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: manyantām ubhayatra bhakti-rahitāḥ satyeti tāṃ durdaśāṃ
children.translated_text: Let those devoid of devotion in both camps consider that wretched state to be true —

children.text: hā dhik tāṃ kim u tat-parāḥ sthiratayā vāñchanti śṛṇvanti ca ||GC_2,3.3||
children.translated_text: alas, shame on it! Would those devoted [to him] desire or even listen to it with steadfastness?' ||GC_2,3.3||

children.text: vṛndā papraccha-māsa-dvayam iha vāsaś cet kathaṃ evaṃ saubhaṃ ca sālvaṃ ca [BhP 10.78.13] ity-ādi-vīkṣayā tasya pratīkṣayā raṇa-raṅga-saṅgatair yadu-saṅghaiḥ sahaiva dvārakāntaḥ-praveśaḥ sadeśa-rūpaḥ syāt ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> asked: 'If the sojourn here was two months, then how — by the observation of [the verse] "<s>Saubha</s> and <s>Śālva</s>" [BhP 10.78.13] and such — could his entry into <s>Dvārakā</s> together with the <s>Yadu</s> hosts gathered at the battlefield in anticipation of him be in accordance with the [Vraja-]region?'

children.text: pūrṇimā sahāsam ivāha sma-na jānāmi | tā imās tasya yogamāyāḥ prakriyāḥ | yathā brahma-mohanānantaraṃ tad idaṃ darśitam-
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said, as if laughing: 'I do not know! These are the procedures of his <s>yogamāyā</s>. Just as, after the <s>Brahmā-mohana</s> (bewilderment of <s>Brahmā</s>), this was shown:'

children.text: ekasminn api yāte'bde prāṇeśaṃ cāntarātmanaḥ |
kṛṣṇa-māyā-hatā rājan kṣaṇārdhaṃ menire'rbhakāḥ || [10.14.43] iti |
children.translated_text: the boys, struck by <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> <s>māyā</s>, O King, considered it but half a moment.' || [BhP 10.14.43] — thus.
'Even though a full year had passed, and the Lord of their life-breaths [had been absent] from their inner selves,

children.text: vṛndāha-tarhi vrajam āgatya hariṇā cirāya yad yat kṛtam | tat kiṃ dvārakā-vāsibhir na jñātam ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Then, was what <s>Hari</s> did for a long time after coming to <s>Vraja</s> not known by the inhabitants of <s>Dvārakā</s>?'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-pūrvam ajñātam api dāruka-mukhād avadhārya jñātam anubhūtaṃ ca yena tat-prajābhiḥ yarhy ambujākṣāpasasāra iti proktam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'Though previously unknown, it was ascertained and known through <s>Dāruka</s> and others, and also experienced — whereby those citizens spoke: "Whenever you, O lotus-eyed one, departed..."'

children.text: atha vṛndā sānandāpi samutkaṇṭhayā tataḥ kaṇṭakam uddhartum icchati sma | yathāha yarhy ambujākṣāpasasāra ity-ādi-rītyā māsa-dvayam uvāsa ha iti nītyā ca punar vrajād vrajanaṃ vrajarāja-sūnor upalabhyate |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s>, though joyful, wishing with longing to extract a thorn from that [joy], said: 'By the manner of "whenever you, O lotus-eyed one, departed" and by the manner of "he dwelt for two months" — a departure of the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> from <s>Vraja</s> again is perceived.'

children.text: pūrṇimovāca-vāci śeṣaya | yad pādma-vācāṃ śeṣaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'Keep the rest in your mouth. For the remainder of the <s>Padma</s> statements will answer.'

children.text: vṛndā ca vācayati sma- atha tatrasthā nandādayaḥ sarve janāḥ putra-dāra-sahitāḥ paśu-pakṣi-mṛgādayaś ca vāsudeva-prasādena divya-rūpa-dharā vimānam ārūḍhā parama-vaikuṇṭha-lokam avāpur iti | kṛṣṇas tu nanda-gopa-vrajaukasāṃ sarveṣāṃ paramaṃ nirāmayaṃ sva-padaṃ dattvā divi deva-gaṇaiḥ saṃstūyamāno dvāravatīṃ viveśa || [PadmaP 6.252.28-29] iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> then read: 'Then, all the people stationed there — <s>Nanda</s> and the others — together with their sons and wives, and the cattle, birds, deer, and other creatures, by the grace of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, assuming divine forms, ascending a celestial vehicle, attained the supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> world. And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having bestowed upon <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd, the <s>Vraja</s>-dwellers, and all others his own supreme, imperishable abode, praised by the hosts of gods in heaven, entered <s>Dvāravatī</s>.' || [PadmaP 6.252.28-29] — thus.

children.text: punar nibhālya vṛndā tad etad āha-tad etat padam eva mahā-golokākhyaṃ tac ca sarvordhvam eva vartata iti brahma-saṃhitā-vacanaṃ cātra dṛśyate | yathā-
children.translated_text: Gazing again, <s>Vṛndā</s> said this: 'This very abode is named great <s>Goloka</s>, and it exists above all — and the statement of the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> is also seen here. As follows:'

children.text: goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya
children.translated_text: 'In his own abode named <s>Goloka</s>, and at the base of that —'

children.text: devi maheśa-hari-dhāmasu teṣu teṣu |
children.translated_text: O goddess, in each of those abodes of <s>Maheśa</s> and <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: te te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena
children.translated_text: by whom those respective arrays of power have been bestowed —

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||
children.translated_text: I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval person!' ||

children.text: tathā mokṣa-dharmasya nārāyaṇīyopākhyāna-vacanaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Likewise, the statement from the <s>Nārāyaṇīya</s> episode of the <s>Mokṣa-dharma</s> —

children.text:
evaṃ bahu-vidhai rūpaiś
carāmīha vasundharām |
brahma-lokaṃ ca kaunteya
golokaṃ ca sanātanam || [Mbh 12.330.68] iti |
children.translated_text: and in the eternal <s>Goloka</s>.' ||[Mbh 12.330.68]||

'Thus, in many forms,
I wander on this earth,
O son of <s>Kuntī</s> — and in <s>Brahmaloka</s>,

children.text: atha punaś ca nirūpya vṛndā savismayam āha-aho ! harivaṃśe govindābhiṣekaṃ racayitum āgatasya śacīpater vacanam idam iti likhitam | tasya sarvagatatām api śaṃsad dṛśyate, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, having examined further, <s>Vṛndā</s> said with wonder — 'Ah! In the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, the statement of <s>Śacīpati</s> (<s>Indra</s>), who had come to perform the consecration of <s>Govinda</s>, is written here. It is seen to declare his all-pervasiveness as well, as follows —'

children.text: tasyopari gavāṃ lokaḥ sādhyās taṃ pālayanti hi |
children.translated_text: 'Above that is the world of cows; the <s>Sādhyas</s> protect it indeed;

children.text: sa hi sarva-gataḥ kṛṣṇa mahākāśa-gato mahān ||
children.translated_text: he is all-pervading, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, great, abiding in the great ether;

children.text:
upary upari tatrāpi gatis tava tapomayī |
yāṃ na vidmo vayaṃ sarve pṛcchanto'pi pitāmaham || [HV 2.19.31-2| iti |
children.translated_text:
above and beyond even that is your abode, constituted of <s>tapas</s>,
which not even all of us know, though we ask the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>).' ||[HV 2.19.31-32]||
But let this be elucidated!'

children.text: kintu tad idaṃ viśadyatām |

pūrṇimā prāha-sādhyāḥ iti sarveṣām asmākaṃ prasādanīyā ity arthaḥ | sarva-gataḥ iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-vigrahavad acintya-śaktitayā vibhur ity arthaḥ | tathāpi sarvordhvatā tādṛg-upāsakānāṃ tathaiva sphuraṇād iti gamyate | mahākāśo brahma ākāśas tal-liṅgāt [Vs 1.1.22] iti nyāyāt | tad-gataḥ iti tad-anubhavopary apy anubhavanīya ity arthaḥ | tapomayī iti pāramaiśvaryamayīty arthaḥ | yāṃ
na vidmaḥ iti brahmāpi durjñeyatayā na samyak prakāśayatīti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — '<s>Sādhyas</s>' means 'those who should be propitiated by all of us.' 'All-pervading' means that, like the form of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he is all-encompassing through inconceivable power. Even so, his being supreme over all is understood from the fact that he manifests as such to such worshippers. 'Great ether' means <s>Brahman</s>, by the principle 'ether, from that indicator' [<s>Vedānta Sūtra</s> 1.1.22]. 'Abiding in that' means 'to be experienced even beyond the experience of that.' 'Constituted of <s>tapas</s>' means constituted of supreme sovereignty. 'Which we do not know' means even <s>Brahmā</s> does not fully illuminate it, due to its being difficult to know — such is the purport.'

children.text: atha vṛndā punar vācitavatī śrī-bhāgavate-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> again read from the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> —

children.text: nandas tv atīndriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s>, seeing the superhuman, great exaltation of the world-protectors,

children.text: kṛṣṇe ca sannatiṃ teṣāṃ jñātibhyo vismito'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and their submission before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, told his kinsmen in amazement:' ||

children.text: te cautsukya-dhiyo rājan matvā gopās tam īśvaram |
children.translated_text: 'Those cowherds, O king, with curious minds, considering him the Lord,

children.text: api naḥ svagatiṃ sūkṣmām upādhāsyad adhīśvaram ||
children.translated_text: [wondered:] "Will he bestow upon us his own subtle abode, the supreme Lord?"' ||

children.text: iti svānāṃ sa bhagavān vijñāyākhila-dṛk svayam |
children.translated_text: 'Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the all-seeing, understanding this of his own people,

children.text: saṅkalpa-siddhaye teṣāṃ kṛpayaitad acintayat ||
children.translated_text: for the fulfillment of their resolve, compassionately reflected:' ||

children.text: jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'People indeed in this world, through ignorance, desire, and action,

children.text: uccāvacāsu gatiṣu na veda svāṃ gatiṃ bhraman ||
children.translated_text: wandering in higher and lower destinations, do not know their own destination.' ||

children.text: iti sañcintya bhagavān mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Thus having reflected, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Hari</s>, the supremely compassionate,

children.text: darśayāmāsa lokaṃ svaṃ gopānāṃ tamasaḥ param ||
children.translated_text: showed his own world to the cowherds — that which is beyond darkness.' ||

children.text: satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ yad brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam |
children.translated_text: 'That which is truth, knowledge, infinite — the eternal effulgence of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yad dhi paśyanti munayo guṇāpāye samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which the sages, concentrated, behold when the <s>guṇas</s> are dissolved.' ||

children.text: te tu brahma-hradaṃ nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'They, led to the lake of <s>Brahman</s>, immersed, and lifted out by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: dadṛśur brahmaṇo lokaṃ yatrākrūro'dhyagāt purā ||
children.translated_text: beheld the world of <s>Brahman</s> — where <s>Akrūra</s> had gone before.' ||

children.text: nandādayas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramānanda-nirvṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s> and the others, seeing that, were filled with supreme blissful contentment;

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra cchandobhiḥ stūyamānaṃ suvismitāḥ || [10.28.10-17]
children.translated_text: and seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> being praised there by Vedic hymns, they were greatly amazed.' ||[BhP 10.28.10-17]||

children.text: atha vṛndā vadati sma-kim atra sukha-satram āyātam ?
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'Has a festival of happiness arrived here?'

children.text:
pūrṇimovāca-tad evaṃ yan-nija-padaṃ teṣām evāspadatayā teṣām eva dṛṣṭi-padam akārṣīt tad eva paścād vyatārīd iti tatra parāmṛśyate | tatra te tu brahma-hradaṃ nītāḥ ity atra yatrākrūraḥ stutavāṃs taṃ brahma-hradaṃ kṛṣṇena tat-tīrtha-mahimānaṃ lakṣyaṃ vidhātuṃ nītā magnāś ca punaḥ kṛṣṇenaivoddhṛtya vṛndāvanam ānītās tasminn
eva narākṛti-para-brahmaṇas tasya lokaṃ dadṛśur na tv akrūravaj jala-madhya iti na cānyatheti ca gamyate | purā ity etat-prasaṅgād bhāvi-kāla ity arthaḥ | purā purāṇe nikaṭe prabandhātīta-bhāviṣu iti hi koṣa-kārāḥ | lokaḥ sa ca sūkṣmam iti tamasaḥ param iti | satyaṃ jñānam ity ādi-svarūpa iti ca prakṛti-guṇāspṛṣṭatayā cic-chakti-vilāsa eveti labhyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'Thus, his own abode — which he made the object of their vision precisely because it was their own station — that very [abode] he later bestowed. This is reflected upon therein. In the statement "They were led to the lake of <s>Brahman</s>" — to the lake of <s>Brahman</s> where <s>Akrūra</s> had offered praise, they were led by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to establish the glory of that <s>tīrtha</s>, and immersed, and again by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself lifted out and brought to <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. There, they beheld the world of that <s>Para-brahman</s> in human form — but not, as in <s>Akrūra's</s> case, in the midst of the water — this is understood, and not otherwise. "Before" here, from the context of this future-oriented passage, means in future time. For the lexicographers state: "<s>purā</s> [means] formerly, in the <s>Purāṇa</s>, nearby, in a connected narrative, in past or future." "World" — that it is subtle, is indicated by "beyond darkness." From "truth, knowledge" and so forth — it is understood as the <s>svarūpa</s> (essential nature), and as the sport of the <s>cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-power), untouched by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>prakṛti</s>.'

children.text:
tathā api naḥ sva-gatim iti, na veda svāṃ gatim iti, gopānāṃ tamasaḥ param iti, kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra iti ca | na parama-vyomādi-rūpaḥ | kintu brahma-saṃhitādi-kṛta-ślokaḥ sphuṭam aprākṛta-goloka-svarūpa evāyaṃ śrīmad-vrajeśa-śloka iti paryavasīyate | tatra chandobhiḥ stūyamānam iti taj-janmādi-līlā-varṇanīnāṃ śruti-vara-varṇinīnāṃ sākṣitā tu tatrāpi puraḥ sphurati
kṛṣṇe teṣāṃ nija-sutatādi-mātratā-jñānāya pārṣadāntara-darśanānuktis teṣāṃ gopānām eva tatratya-tat-parikaratā-vyañjanāyeti jñeyam | yata eva tad-eka-rucīnāṃ śrī-nandādīnāṃ paramānanda-nirvṛtir vismitiś ca ghaṭate |
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, "his own subtle abode," "does not know his own destination," "beyond darkness for the cowherds," and "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> being praised there" — [all indicate that] it is not of the form of the supreme sky and such, but rather, by the verse composed in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> and such, the conclusion is reached clearly that this verse of the glorious lord of <s>Vraja</s> pertains to the essential nature of the transcendental <s>Goloka</s>. Therein, "being praised by Vedic hymns" — the fact that the <s>Śrutis</s>, the excellent descriptors that narrate his birth-pastimes and such, are witnesses — this shines forth there too first. The non-mention of seeing other associates [in <s>Goloka</s>] serves to indicate to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> that those cowherds themselves possess only the awareness of his being their son and such, [and] that they are his attendants in that very place — this should be known. For precisely this reason, the supreme blissful contentment and amazement of Śrī <s>Nanda</s> and the others — who have exclusive delight in him — is consistent.'

children.text: sva-lokatāyām apy avatārāvasare teṣāṃ tasyādarśane kāraṇaṃ jano vai iti | sālokya-sārṣṭi ity ādi-padye janā itivaj-jana-śabdo'yaṃ tadīya-svajana-paraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The reason for their not seeing that [<s>Goloka</s>] even though it is their own world, at the occasion of the <s>avatāra</s>, is [expressed in] "People indeed" — here the word "people" (<s>jana</s>), as in the verse "liberation of equal status and equal opulence," refers to his own people. —'

children.text: tasmān mac-charaṇaṃ goṣṭhaṃ man-nāthaṃ mat-parigraham |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore my shelter — the cow-settlement, my lord, my possessions —

children.text: gopāye svātma-yogena so'yaṃ me vrata āhitaḥ || [BhP 10.25.18]
children.translated_text: I shall protect by the <s>yoga</s> of my own Self — this is my vow established!' ||[BhP 10.25.18]||

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇasyaiva tatra ca manasaiva sva-niṣṭhā-pratiṣṭhā-racanād vacanād atra sa tu vraja-janaḥ parama-svajana eva spaṣṭaḥ | sādhāraṇa-jana-vācitve tat-kṛpā sarvasyāpi janasya vyāpiny abhaviṣyat | svāṃ gatim ity api na samagaṃsyata | tataś ca parama-svajano'yaṃ mama vraja-vāsi-janaḥ prāpañcike loke yāḥ svāvidyādibhir deva-tiryag-ādi-rūpā tgatayas tāsu bhramaṃs
tan-nirviśeṣatayātmānaṃ manvānaḥ svāṃ gatiṃ goloka-lakṣaṇāṃ na jānātīty arthaḥ | atra kāraṇaṃ tu--
children.translated_text: 'By Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> own establishing of his commitment there through the mind alone and through speech — the <s>Vraja</s>-people are clearly his supreme own people. If the word "people" referred to common people, then his compassion would have been all-pervasive for all people [equally]. "His own destination" too would not have been consistent. Therefore, this <s>Vraja</s>-dwelling people is my supreme own. In the empirical world, wandering in the various destinations — divine, animal, and such — produced by their own ignorance and the rest, considering themselves as undifferentiated from those, they do not know their own destination characterized as <s>Goloka</s> — this is the meaning. The cause here is —'

children.text: iti nandādayo gopāḥ kṛṣṇa-rāma-kathāṃ mudā |
kurvanto ramamāṇāś ca nāvindan bhava-vedanām || [BhP 10.11.58] iti |
children.translated_text: narrating the tales of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, sporting, did not experience the suffering of worldly existence.' ||[BhP 10.11.58]||
'Thus <s>Nanda</s> and the other cowherds, joyfully

children.text: ity anusāreṇa madīya-laukika-līlā-śaktir eveti bhāvaḥ | tad-ajñānād eva ca nandas tv atīndriyam ity ādikaṃ ghaṭata iti | tasmād yad eva khalv idaṃ darśitam | tad eva tebhyaḥ paścād dattam iti gamyate |
children.translated_text: '— Following this, the purport is: it is my own mundane <s>līlā-śakti</s> (pastime-power). And from their non-awareness of that very [power], the passage beginning with "<s>Nanda</s>, seeing the superhuman" is consistent. Therefore, what was indeed shown [to them] — that very thing is understood as having been subsequently given to them.'

children.text: vṛndā prāha-hanta ! kathaṃ ta ete mad-vanād antarhitatām āpsyanti | śrī-kṛṣṇena punar viyogaṃ ca lapsyante ?
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'Alas! How will they disappear from my forest? And they will obtain separation from Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again?'

children.text: pūrṇimā prāha-kiṃcid anyad asti ced vācyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'If there is something else, let it be read!'

children.text: vṛndā prāha sma-atha vārāha-vacanam iti kiṃcid anyad api saṃcitam asti | tad yathā-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'Now there is also a statement from the <s>Vārāha Purāṇa</s> compiled with something else. As follows —'

children.text:
tatrāpi mahad āścaryaṃ paśyanti paṇḍitā narāḥ |
kālīya-hrada-pūrveṇa kadambo mahito drumaḥ |
śata-śākhaṃ viśālākṣi puṇyaṃ surabhi-gandhi ca |
sa ca dvādaśa-māsāni manojñaḥ śubha-śītalaḥ |
puṣpāyati viśālākṣi prabhāsanto diśo daśa || iti |
tathā-
children.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: tatrāścaryaṃ pravakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu tvaṃ vasundhare |
children.translated_text: 'Here I shall declare a wonder — hear this, O Earth!

children.text: labhante manujāḥ siddhiṃ mama karma-parāyaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mortals devoted to my deeds attain perfection.

children.text: tasya tatrottare pārśve'śoka-vṛkṣaḥ sita-prabhaḥ |
children.translated_text: On its northern side is an <s>aśoka</s> tree of white radiance;

children.text: vaiśākhasya tu māsasya śukla-pakṣasya dvādaśī ||
children.translated_text: on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>,

children.text:
sa puṣpati ca madhyāṅge mama bhakta-sukhāvahaḥ |
na kaścid api jānāti vinā bhāgavataṃ śucim || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
it blossoms at its central limb, bringing happiness to my devotees;
no one knows [this] except the pure <s>Bhāgavata</s> devotee.' — and so forth.

children.text: atra tasya iti brahma-kuṇḍasyety arthaḥ ity uktvā punaḥ pūrṇimovāca-kiṃcid anyad apy asti ?
children.translated_text: Here, 'of that' means 'of the <s>Brahma-kuṇḍa</s>' — having said this, <s>Pūrṇimā</s> again said — 'Is there anything else?'

children.text: vṛndā sānandam uvāca-asti cānyat skānda-mathurā-māhātmye-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said joyfully — 'There is also another, in the <s>Skānda</s>-<s>Mathurā-māhātmya</s> —'

children.text:
tato vṛndāvanaṃ puṇyaṃ vṛndā-devī-samāśritam |
hariṇādhiṣṭhitaṃ tac ca brahma-rudrādi-sevitam || iti |
children.translated_text:
'Then the sacred <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, sheltered by the goddess <s>Vṛndā</s>,
presided over by <s>Hari</s>, served by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others.' ||

children.text:
vatsair vatsatarībhiś ca sadā krīḍati mādhavaḥ |
vṛndāvanāntara-gataḥ sa-rāmo bālakair vṛtaḥ || iti ca |
children.translated_text:
'<s>Mādhava</s>, together with calves and young cows, always plays
within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, accompanied by <s>Rāma</s>, surrounded by boys.' ||

children.text: athādi-vārāha-vacanaṃ ca-
children.translated_text: And now a statement from the <s>Ādi-Vārāha</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] —

children.text: kṛṣṇa-krīḍā-setu-bandhaṃ mahā-pātaka-nāśanam |
children.translated_text: 'The bridge of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> sport, destroyer of great sins,

children.text: valabhīṃ tatra krīḍārthaṃ kṛtvā devo gadādharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a fort there, made for sport by the god who bears the mace (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),

children.text:
gopakaiḥ sahitas tatra kṣaṇam ekaṃ dine dine |
tatraive ramaṇārthaṃ hi nitya-kālaṃ sa gacchati || iti |
children.translated_text:
together with cowherds there, for one moment each day,
he goes there perpetually for the purpose of enjoyment.' ||

children.text:
vṛndāvane vased dhīmān yāvat kṛṣṇasya darśanam || iti |
[92] athātra vṛndā papraccha-samprati cirāya proṣitatvena parāmṛśyamānasya tasya sadā krīḍanam atra katha ghaṭate ?
children.translated_text:
'Let the wise one dwell in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> until the vision of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [is attained].' ||
[92] Then <s>Vṛndā</s> asked — 'At present, when he is being considered as one who has been absent for a long time, how is his perpetual playing here consistent?'

children.text: pūrṇimā prāha-vaikuṇṭhād gajendra-dhruvādi-kṛpārthaṃ madhye madhye pṛthviīm āgatasya ca yathā tan-nāthasya tatra nityāvasthānaṃ procyate | tadvad atrāpi sacyate | anādy-ananta-kālaṃ tatra viharatas tasya nimeṣa-mātram eva tat-tat-kāla iti | ataḥ paraṃ kiṃcid asti, tat tu vada |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'Just as it is said that the Lord, who comes to earth from time to time for the sake of compassion toward <s>Gajendra</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, and others, nevertheless has his eternal abode there — so too it is stated here. For him who sports there from beginningless and endless time, each of those intervals is merely the blinking of an eye. If there is something beyond this, tell it.'

children.text: vṛndā prāha-etad-anantaraṃ bṛhad-gautamīya-padyāni pratipadyante |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'After this, verses from the great <s>Gautamīya</s> [Tantra] are set forth.'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-vācyantām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'Let them be read!'

children.text: vṛndā ca vācitavatī | yathā, nārada uvāca-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> read. As follows — <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: kim idaṃ dvādaśābhikhyaṃ vṛndāraṇyaṃ viśāmpate |
children.translated_text: 'What is this called the twelve[-forests] <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>, O lord of the people?

children.text: śrotum icchāmi bhagavan yadi yogo'smi me vada ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear, O Blessed One — if I am worthy, tell me!' ||

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca-
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said —

children.text: idaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ mama dhāmaiva kevalam |
children.translated_text: 'This charming <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is nothing but my own abode;

children.text: atra ye paśavaḥ pakṣi-vṛkṣā kīṭā narāmarāḥ |
children.translated_text: those animals, birds, trees, insects, humans, and gods here,

children.text: ye vasanti mamādhiṣṇye mṛtā yānti mamālayam ||
children.translated_text: who dwell in my domain — upon dying, they go to my abode.' ||

children.text: atra yā gopa-kanyāś ca nivasanti mamālaye |
children.translated_text: 'Those cowherd-maidens who dwell here, in my abode —

children.text: kālindīyaṃ suṣumnākhyā paramāmṛta-vāhinī ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) is called <s>Suṣumnā</s>, carrying supreme nectar.' ||

children.text: atra devāś ca bhūtāni vartante sūkṣma-rūpataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Here gods and beings exist in subtle form;

children.text: sarva-deva-mayaś cāhaṃ na tyajāmi vanaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: and I, who contain all gods, never abandon this forest.' ||

children.text:
āvirbhāvas tirobhāvo bhaven me'tra yuge yuge |
tejo-mayam idaṃ ramyam adṛśyaṃ carma-cakṣuṣā || iti |
children.translated_text:
'My manifestation and disappearance occur here in every age;
this [realm], constituted of splendor, charming, is invisible to the physical eye.' ||

children.text: pūrṇimā prāha-āyātam atra ca prakaṭāprakaṭa-līlāvakāśatām ayaṃ prakāśa-dvaividhyam | atra me paśavaḥ iti, tejomayam iti coktavān |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'There has arrived here the scope for both manifest and unmanifest pastimes — this duality of manifestation. Here he has said "my animals" and also "constituted of splendor."'

children.text: tad evaṃ jāta-sukha-vṛndā vṛndā punaḥ papraccha-tad idaṃ ca sarvaṃ paryak tātparyāya-paryālocyatām |
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Vṛndā</s>, having obtained a host of happiness, again asked — 'Let all this be thoroughly considered to its ultimate purport!'

children.text:
pūrṇimovāca-anenedaṃ gamyate | golokākhyaṃ tad vaibhavaṃ sadaiva vṛndāvana-bhavam | kintu tvaṃ vraja-vāsin-janavad eva samprati na tad avagacchasi | yathā pṛthvyā api tad-ajñānaṃ vārāha-vacanāl labhyate | tad etad eva ca nitya-dhāma tebhyas tena darśitaṃ, tad eva ca teṣāṃ nitya-prāpyatayā varṇitam | akke cen madhu vindeta kim arthaṃ pravataṃ vrajet iti-nyāyena dūre teṣāṃ gamanaṃ
ca vyartham iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said — 'By this, it is understood that the glory called <s>Goloka</s> is eternally born of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. But you, like the <s>Vraja</s>-dwelling people, do not presently comprehend that. Just as even the Earth's non-awareness of that is obtained from the <s>Vārāha</s> statement. This very [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>] is the eternal abode that was shown to them by him, and this very [abode] is described as their eternal attainment. By the maxim "If one can find honey in the <s>akka</s> plant, why would one go to the mountain?" — their going far away is also futile.'

children.text: vṛndāha-satyaṃ satyam | dvayor abhedenaiva vyavasthā-racanaṃ harivaṃśa-stha-tat-prasaṅga-saṅgata-śakra-vacanaṃ cātra dṛśyate-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said — 'True, true! The arrangement establishing the non-difference of the two [<s>Vṛndāvana</s> and <s>Goloka</s>] — and <s>Śakra's</s> (<s>Indra's</s>) statement found in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, concordant with that topic — is seen here too:'

children.text: sa tu lokas tvayā kṛṣṇa sīdamānaḥ kṛtātmanā |
children.translated_text: 'That world of yours, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which was sinking — by you, the self-composed one,

children.text: dhṛto dhṛtimatā vīra nighantopdadravān gavām || [HV 2.19.35]
children.translated_text: the steadfast hero, it was upheld — destroying the calamities of the cows.' ||[HV 2.19.35]||

children.text:
kintu, atha tatrasthā nandādayaḥ ity ādi-pādma-gadya-dvayaṃ viśadyatām |
[102] pūrṇimā vyācacakṣa-śrīman-nandādyā vraja-sthitāḥ sva-sva-putraiḥ svayaṃ kṛṣṇādibhiḥ sva-sva-dāraiḥ śrī-yaśodādibhiḥ sahitā vasudevād āgatasya tasya kṛta-nijāgamana-saṅkalpa-saṃvādena prasādena pūrvato'pi paramāpūra-rūpa-dharāḥ parasapara-dṛk-sukha-karā sarvatra manoratha-patha-prāpaka-tadīya-ratham ārūḍhās tattva-mātrānabhijñeṣu tattvāntara-vijñeṣu ca tat tejasā gūḍhāḥ
|mahasādhaḥ-kṛtāśeṣaṃ śrī-vṛndāvanasya pūrvokta-prakāśa-viśeṣaṃ parābhir mābhir akuṇṭhaṃ golokākhya-vaikuṇṭhaṃ tatra ca gokula-kamalaṃ yamunāyā uttara-pārād dakṣiṇa-pāram avāpya prāpuḥ iti |
children.translated_text:
'But now, let the two prose passages from the <s>Padma</s> [Purāṇa] beginning with "Then <s>Nanda</s> and others stationed there" be elucidated.'
[102] <s>Pūrṇimā</s> explained: 'The glorious <s>Nanda</s> and other inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s>, together with their respective sons — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the others themselves — and their respective wives — glorious <s>Yaśodā</s> and the others — through the grace concordant with the resolution of his own coming, communicated from <s>Vasudeva</s>, bearing a form of supreme fullness even greater than before, causing mutual delight to each other's eyes, mounting his chariot — which conveys [them] to the path of [their] heart's desire — everywhere concealed by that radiance from those who know only the superficial truth and from those who know a different truth, having made all things subordinate by [his] majesty, attaining the particular splendor of glorious <s>Vṛndāvana</s> previously described, with the transcendent <s>Māyā</s>-powers, without obstruction, [they reached] <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> called <s>Goloka</s>, and therein, having traversed from the northern bank to the southern bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, they reached the lotus of <s>Gokula</s>.'

children.text:
tac ca nirāmayaṃ kuta-punar-viraha-vyādhi-vilayaṃ sva-padaṃ nija-nityāspadaṃ putra-dāra-sahitāḥ iti pūrva-sūcita-tat-putratocita-rūpeṇātra sthitir eva yadu-pura-samucita-svarūpeṇa tu dvāravatī-praveśa iti sarvam eva sadeśa-rūpam | kintu gopanārthaṃ lokeṣu camatkriyāropaṇārtham eva ca seyaṃ vimāna-prakriyā | pāre'vāre vā vasatu | sa tu ghoṣas tāṃ vināpi brahma-hrada-majjanānataravat tatra sajjanaṃ
labheta |
children.translated_text: 'And that wholesome [abode] — the dissolution of the disease of "whence-again-separation" — their own station, their eternal dwelling — "together with sons and wives" — their standing there in the form appropriate to the previously indicated sonship, while the form appropriate to the city of the <s>Yadus</s> [serves for] entry into <s>Dvāravatī</s> — all this is in its proper place and form. But for the purpose of concealment among the people, and for the purpose of imposing wonder — this very aerial-chariot procedure [was employed]. Whether he dwells on the near bank or the far bank — that cow-settlement would find good people there even without the immersion in the lake of <s>Brahman</s> and such.

children.text: nādhyātiṣṭhed yadi yadu-purāt prāpya goṣṭhaṃ sa bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'If, having reached the cow-settlement from the city of the <s>Yadus</s>, he did not remain there again,

children.text: sarvaṃ tarhi pratihata-rasaṃ sarvathā syād vṛthā ca |
children.translated_text: then everything would be bereft of <s>rasa</s> and entirely futile;

children.text: janmānandaḥ pratilava-vayaḥ śrī-citiḥ sneha-vṛddhir
children.translated_text: the joy of birth, the glory of progressive ages, the increase of affection,

children.text: līlā-pūrtir viraha-mathitaḥ sāntvanaṃ cātra tasya ||GC_2,3.4||
children.translated_text: the fulfillment of pastimes, the consolation of those churned by separation — [all depend on] his [presence] here.' || (GC 2,3.4)

children.text:
atha vṛndā papraccha-yady evaṃ paścād api sarva-vraja-prāṇas tat-trāṇam ācaritavāṃs tadā purā mathurā-prasthāna eva na kathaṃ vā racitavān ?
[105] pūrṇimā prāha-rasa-poṣāya pratikalpam īdṛśam eva labdha-sātatyena līlā-naiyatyena sthāpitam api tad idaṃ pṛcchatyā bhavatyā nijam utkaṇṭhitam eva mac-chrotrayor upakaṇṭhīkṛtaṃ vādarāyaṇādibhir api kṛta-lālasā-saṃkramasya śrī-bhagaval-līlā-kramasya vaiyarthyaṃ tu na samarthanīyam |
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Vṛndā</s> asked: 'If this is so — if afterward too, the life-breath of all <s>Vraja</s>, he carried out their protection — then why did he not arrange the same at the very time of the departure for <s>Mathurā</s>?'
[105] <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'For the nourishment of <s>rasa</s>, this very [arrangement] has been established with continuity in every <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle), through the regularity of his pastimes. But by your asking, you have merely brought your own eagerness close to my ears. The futility of the sequence of the glorious Lord's pastimes — for which even <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) and others have created longing's transmission — is not to be justified.

children.text: punar udayaja-śarma-poṣa-dharma
children.translated_text: 'The mere sojourn of <s>Hari</s> [away from <s>Vraja</s>] is itself

children.text: svayam upaśarma hareḥ pravāsa-mātram |
children.translated_text: a principle that nourishes the happiness born of reunion;

children.text: vrajam api tad-ṛte rasasya pūrtir
children.translated_text: if the fulfillment of <s>rasa</s> could encompass <s>Vraja</s> without that [separation],

children.text: yadi valayeta tadā tad eva na syāt ||GC_2,3.5||
children.translated_text: then that very [fulfillment] would not exist.' || (GC 2,3.5)

children.text: tasmād vraja-rasa-sampad-arthaṃ tad apy arthanīyam iti | tad evam eva svayam uktam-nāhaṃ tu sakhyo bhajato'pi jantūn [BhP 10.32.20] iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the sake of the wealth of <s>Vraja's</s> <s>rasa</s>, that [separation] too is to be valued.' Thus indeed it was said by him: 'I do not [reciprocate], O friends, [even] to those who worship [Me]' [BhP 10.32.20] — thus.

children.text: tad etad vyākhyāya pūrṇimā papraccha-kiṃcid asti vānyat ?
children.translated_text: Having explained this, <s>Pūrṇimā</s> asked: 'Is there anything else?'

children.text: vṛndā sānandam uvāca-bhagavati śrī-bhāgavatīyam ante kiṃcid añcitaṃ dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said joyfully: 'O blessed one! At the end of the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> [Tenth Canto], something notable is seen.'

children.text: purṇimā prāha-kāmaṃ vācyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'By all means, let it be recited!'

children.text: vṛndā tac ca vācayāmāsa, yathā-
children.translated_text: And <s>Vṛndā</s> recited it. As follows:

children.text: jayati jananivāso devakī-janma-vādo
children.translated_text: 'Victorious is he whose abode is the people [of <s>Vraja</s>], [though] famous as the son of <s>Devakī</s>,

children.text: yadu-vara-pariṣat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam |
children.translated_text: dispelling unrighteousness with his own arms amidst the assembly of the best of <s>Yadus</s>;

children.text: sthira-cara-vṛjina-ghnaḥ susmita-śrī-mukhena
children.translated_text: the destroyer of the sins of all moving and stationary beings, with his beautifully smiling glorious face

children.text: vraja-pura-vanitānāṃ vardhayan kāma-devam || (10.90.48)
children.translated_text: augmenting the god of love for the women of the town of <s>Vraja</s>!' || (BhP 10.90.48)

children.text: pūrṇimovāca-tad ittham ākhyātā mama vyākhyā | yat khalv ayaṃ daśama-skandhāntarvartī śrī-śuka-siddhāntas tatra cātra ca tasya viccchedaṃ nirasya nita-vihāram eva vyāharati |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'Thus has my commentary been declared. For this conclusion of glorious <s>Śuka</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>), situated within the Tenth <s>Skandha</s>, repudiating any discontinuity therein and herein, proclaims nothing but eternal sport.

children.text: yataḥ sva-dos-tulyair yadukulyair adharma-bahula-rāja-kula-vyākulatārthaṃ devakī-janma-prasiddhim urīkṛtya kṛta-kṛtyaḥ susmita-śrī-mukhena vrajasya purasya ca vanitānāṃ kāma-prāya-prema-vardhana-sukhena sarvato'pi śaśvad utkarṣeṇa sadā virājata iti labhyate | tatra hetuḥ-tatra tatra sthāvara-jaṅgama-mātrāṇāṃ viraha-duḥkha-hantā tat-tad-upāsaka-svajana-hṛdaye tathā sphuraṃś ceti |
children.translated_text: For, having assumed the fame of being born from <s>Devakī</s> — for the purpose of removing the disturbance of the wicked royal dynasties — with his arms equal to those of his <s>Yadu</s> clansmen, being accomplished, with his beautifully smiling glorious face, by the happiness of augmenting the love bordering on <s>kāma</s> of the women of <s>Vraja</s> and of the city [<s>Dvārakā</s>] — he ever shines with supreme excellence everywhere.' The reason for this: 'The destroyer of the separation-sorrow of all moving and stationary beings in each and every place, shining thus in the hearts of his own people who are worshippers of those respective [forms].'

children.text: tad etad-ukti-kauśalād bhāvi-mausalādi-līlānām api māyikatvam eva pratyāyitam | kṣīra-nīra-nidhi-śāyina eva tad etad-rūpāvatāra ity ādi-vyavahāraś ca tādṛśa-nitya-vihāra-gopanārtha eveti ca |
children.translated_text: 'By the skill of this very statement, the merely illusory nature of even the future <s>mausala</s> (mace-battle) and other pastimes is established. And the conventional designation "this is an <s>avatāra</s> (descent) of the very form of the one who reclines on the milk-ocean" — that too is solely for the purpose of concealing [his] eternal sport.'

children.text: atha śrī-bhāgavatīyaṃ padya-dvayaṃ sā paṭhati sma-
children.translated_text: Then she (<s>Vṛndā</s>) recited two verses from the <s>Bhāgavata</s>:

children.text: dvārakāṃ hariṇā tyaktāṃ samudro'plāvayat kṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: '<s>Dvārakā</s>, abandoned by <s>Hari</s>, was instantly flooded by the ocean,

children.text: varjayitvā mahārāja śrīmad-bhagavad-ālayam ||
children.translated_text: with the exception, O great king, of the glorious abode of the Lord.' ||

children.text: smṛtyāśeṣāśubha-haraṃ sarva-maṅgala-maṅgalam |
children.translated_text: 'Destroyer of all inauspiciousness merely by remembrance, the auspiciousness of all auspiciousness —

children.text: nityaṃ sannihitas tatra bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ || (11.31.23-24)
children.translated_text: the Lord <s>Madhusūdana</s> is eternally present there.' || (BhP 11.31.23-24)

children.text: atra viṣṇu-purāṇīyaṃ tu kiṃcid viśiṣṭam api-yadu-deva-gṛhaṃ tv ekaṃ nāplāvayat iti | viṣṇu-krīḍānvitaṃ sthānam iti ca |
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> statement is somewhat more specific as well: 'But the one house of the Lord of the <s>Yadus</s> was not flooded.' And: 'The place endowed with the sport of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'

children.text: pūrṇimā prāha-tad idaṃ vṛndāvana-nitya-vihārasya dṛṣṭāntatayāpi ghaṭitam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'This too is consistent even as an illustration of the eternal sport in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.'

children.text: atha vṛndā śrī-bhāgavatīyaṃ (10.14.35) padyaṃ punaḥ papāṭha, yathā-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vṛndā</s> again recited a verse from the <s>Bhāgavata</s> (10.14.35). As follows:

children.text:
eṣāṃ ghoṣa-nivāsinām uta bhavān kiṃ deva rāteti naś
ceto viśva-phalāt phalaṃ tvad-aparaṃ kutrāpy ayan muhyati |
sad-veṣād api pūtanāpi sakulā tvām eva devāpitā
yad dhāmārtha-suhṛt-priyātma-tanaya-prāṇāśayās tvat-kṛte || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Of these dwellers of the cow-settlement — are you, O God, [their very own]? — thus our | mind, from the fruit of all the worlds, is bewildered regarding any other fruit than you. | Even <s>Pūtanā</s>, by the disguise of a virtuous one, together with her family, obtained you alone, O God — | [you who are] their home, wealth, friend, beloved, Self, son, life-breath, and refuge — for your sake!' || (BhP 10.14.35) — thus.

children.text: pūrṇimā pūrṇam idam uvāca-tad etat kaimutya-vidhinā prastutya vraja-vāsināṃ tena saṃvāsaṃ satya-loka-parivṛḍhaḥ parama-dṛḍhaṃ cakāreti sarvaṃ śāntam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> spoke this as the fulfillment: 'This, by the method of the a fortiori argument, having introduced the topic, the elder of <s>Satya-loka</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) made the cohabitation of the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> with him supremely firm — thus all is at peace.'

children.text: punaḥ pūrṇimā prāha-kim apy anyad vacanam asti ?
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> again said: 'Is there any other statement?'

children.text: vṛndāha-tad api śrūyatām-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said: 'Let this too be heard:'

children.text: tad bhūri-bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'That great fortune here — of some birth in the forest —

children.text: yad gokule'pi katamāṅghri-rajo'bhiṣekam |
children.translated_text: that even in <s>Gokula</s> [receives] the ablution of the dust of some [person's] feet;

children.text: yaj jīvitaṃ tu nikhilaṃ bhagavān mukundas
children.translated_text: for whose entire life is the Lord <s>Mukunda</s> —

children.text: tv adyāpi yat-pada-rajaḥ śruti-mṛgyam eva || (10.14.34)
children.translated_text: the dust of whose feet is sought even now by the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas)!' || (BhP 10.14.34)

children.text: pūrṇimā saharṣam āha-pūrva-nirṇayād eva tad idaṃ brahmā sva-puruṣārthatayā varṇayāmāsa | punar dṛśyatām-
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said with delight: 'From the very determination established before, <s>Brahmā</s> described this as his own supreme goal of life.' Again, let this be seen:

children.text: aho bhāgyam aho bhāgyaṃ nanda-gopa-vrajaukasām |
children.translated_text: 'Oh, the fortune! Oh, the fortune of <s>Nanda</s>, the cowherd, and the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s>!

children.text: yan-mitraṃ paramānandaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahma sanātanam || (10.14.32)
children.translated_text: Whose friend is the supreme bliss, the complete, eternal <s>Brahman</s>!' || (BhP 10.14.32)

children.text: vṛndā sānandam āha [BhP 10.26.25]-
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> said with joy [BhP 10.26.25]:

children.text: deve varṣati yajña-viplava-ruṣā vajrāśma-varṣānilaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'When the god (<s>Indra</s>) rained with the fury of disrupted sacrifice, with thunderbolts, stones, rain, and winds,

children.text: sīdat-pāla-paśu-striy ātma-śaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭvānukampy utsmayan |
children.translated_text: seeing the herdsmen, cattle, and women afflicted, [taking] refuge in himself, compassionate, smiling,

children.text: utpāṭyaika-kareṇa śailam abalo līlocchilīndhraṃ yathā
children.translated_text: uprooting a mountain with one hand — the powerless one! — as easily as a mushroom,

children.text: bibhrad goṣṭham apān mahendra-mada-bhit prīyān na indro gavām ||
children.translated_text: holding it, he protected the cow-settlement — the crusher of great <s>Indra's</s> pride — may the lord of cows be pleased!' ||

children.text: atha pūrṇimā varṇayāmāsa-tad evaṃ śrī-bādarāyaṇir api tasya gavendratāṃ nijāśrayatayā śrāvayāmāsa | so'yaṃ yatra gopālādīnāṃ tenāparityājyatāṃ vyañjayāmāsa | tathaiva hi tatra śrī-gavendrasyāntaḥ-pratijñā tasmān mac-charaṇaṃ goṣṭham ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pūrṇimā</s> described: 'Thus, the glorious son of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>) too made heard his [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] state as the lord of cows as his own foundation. This is where he indicated the non-abandonability of cowherds and others by him. Just as therein, the inner vow of the glorious lord of cows: "Therefore, my refuge — the cow-settlement" and so forth.'

children.text: atha punar vācyatām |
children.translated_text: 'Now, let more be recited!'

children.text: vṛndā tāṃ vandamānā prāha-granthanā pūrṇatayā mayā pūrṇīkṛtāsmīti kiṃvānyad vācyatā yācyatām āsīdatu ? kintu samājñāpayantu tatrabhavatyas tad idaṃ pustakaṃ nāyakam iva hāra-vinyastaṃ karomi iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>, bowing to her, said: 'I have been made complete by the completeness of the compilation — so what else should be asked to be recited? But let your grace command: I shall place this book, like a necklace upon the hero [of the narrative]!'

children.text: pūrṇimāha-sāmpratam |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇimā</s> said: 'It is timely.'

children.text: atha vṛndā ca tathā kṛtavatī |
children.translated_text: And <s>Vṛndā</s> did accordingly.

children.text:
iti śrī-śrīmaduttara-gopāla-campūmanu
bhāvi-kathā-pramāṇa-prathanaṃ nāma
ekonatriṃśaṃ pūraṇam
||29||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the glorious <s>Uttara-Gopāla-campū</s>,
the twenty-ninth <s>pūraṇa</s> (chapter) named
'The Spreading of the Authority for the Future Narrative'
|| 29 ||
